text: "" is a Main Quest in . Overview "A Mystery in the Depths" becomes available after one of the Main Quests associated with "Regional Phenomena" has been completed. At Lookout Landing, Link will find Josha while Tauro arguing about whether he should be involved in Chasm Research. Tauro wants to help Josha, but she thinks that he should finish investigating the Ring Ruins first. When the two of them notice Link nearby, Tauro decides to give up and return to Kakariko Village. Josha explains that although she admires Tauro, she is afraid he would abandon her Chasm Research if something more interesting came along, and she thinks Link would fit her needs perfectly. If Link agrees to help her, Josha will thank him and invite him into her lab. Following this, "A Mystery in the Depths" will start. When Link speaks to Josha, she reveals that the Zonai Survey Team found more Slates that she was able to piece together into a complete mural. She observes that the Statues That Point the Way appear to be leading to an unknown structure associated with the Zonai. By following it, Josha thinks one could find something associated with the Ancient Powers of the Zonai. Since Josha is too young to go into the Depths, she asks Link to investigate the structure on her behalf, and she gives him 10 Giant Brightbloom Seeds and a bundle of 10 Arrows to help him. She believes that investigating for her could provide Link with both clues to Zelda's location and a new Ancient Power. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Link's Right Arm as he receives the power of Autobuild.|Link receiving Autobuild By following the Statues That Point the Way in the Depths, Link will eventually come upon the Great Abandoned Central Mine. There, he will find two Researchers investigating an inactive Steward Construct, which they have been unable to figure out. Using his Right Arm, Link is able to restore the Steward Construct, which also activates the Mine's Travel Point. The Steward Construct then grants Link the ability to Autobuild. The Researchers are shocked that Link was able to receive the Ancient Power. They ask for a demonstration, and after consulting a text that describes Autobuild, they request that Link repair their broken vehicles. First, Link must reattach the Small Wheel to the vehicle on the Round Pedestal. When he does so, he will be able to use Autobuild to recreate the vehicle from the pieces left on the Square Pedestal. After both vehicles have been repaired, the Researchers will be shocked express their satisfaction. thumb|right|250px|alt= A screenshot of Master Kohga at the Great Abandoned Central Mine. Two Yiga Footsoldiers are at either side of him. Text on-screen displays his name, along with the title "Leader of the Yiga Clan".|Master Kohga's introduction Suddenly, the Researchers call for their master before teleporting away, revealing that they were Yiga Footsoldiers. A voice can then be heard, noting that the rumors about an Ancient Power appear to be true.

Text on-screen displays his name, along with the title "Leader of the Yiga Clan".|Master Kohga's introduction Suddenly, the Researchers call for their master before teleporting away, revealing that they were Yiga Footsoldiers. A voice can then be heard, noting that the rumors about an Ancient Power appear to be true. From behind Link, Master Kohga appears alongside the Yiga Footsoldiers, and he commends both Link and his subordinates for confirming the rumor as part of Operation Steal the Ancient Power. After looking at Link, however, Master Kohga recognizes him from their encounter at the Yiga Clan Hideout, which resulted in him entering the Depths and swearing vengeance on Link. With a dance, he reintroduces himself to Link as the leader of the Yiga Clan. He accuses Link of cheating, claiming that it is not fair that he can Autobuild while they have to build their vehicles by hand. Since they were planning to offer the ability to the Magnificent One, Master Kohga declares that he will take it back. He teleports into the nearby courtyard and summons a massive vehicle, where he challenges Link to a fight. After Link defeats Master Kohga, he complains about his strength. He decides to leave Link alone for now, gloating that he has already found many other Abandoned Mines in the Depths. Having seen Link use his Right Arm to receive Autobuild, he plans to try and get it from a Steward Construct at another Mine, which he will use to destroy the world with the Magnificent One. Master Kohga summons a Wing with four Fans and a Steering Stick attached, using it to retreat. A stone Treasure Chest containing a Huge Crystallized Charge then appears in front of Link, and the "Master Kohga of the Yiga Clan" Side Adventure will begin. When Link returns to Josha at Lookout Landing, she notices that he appears pleased and asks what happened. Upon hearing about Autobuild, she is shocked, and she decides to search for anything relevant to it among her artifacts. She is able to find a Schema Stone, which grants Link the Schematic for a Hot-Air Balloon. She suggests that he test it out by repairing Robbie's broken Hot-Air Balloon. After she removes the chains holding down the Balloon and the Basket, she asks Link to demonstrate Autobuild for her. Using Autobuild, Link is able to reassemble Robbie's Hot-Air Balloon, much to Josha's surprise. She shouts to Robbie to get his attention, and he is shocked to see his Hot-Air Balloon has been fixed. Josha is happy to have been able to see the Ancient Power of the Zonai, giving Link a piece of Large Zonaite as a reward. Although she does not know its uses, she believes Link could make use of it, since he is able to use Ancient Powers. Josha has been inspired to continue her Chasm Research, and she hopes that Link will tell her anything else he discovers about the Depths. Following this conversation, "A Mystery in the Depths"

Josha has been inspired to continue her Chasm Research, and she hopes that Link will tell her anything else he discovers about the Depths. Following this conversation, "A Mystery in the Depths" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview Inside Zelda's Secret Well in Hateno Village, Link can find Zelda's Diary on her desk. Within her Diary, Zelda reveals that she has commissioned a new Champion's Tunic for Link, since she has noticed his old one has become worn. In order to keep him from discovering it during their expedition Beneath Hyrule Castle, Zelda hid the new Champion's Tunic in the Throne Room of Hyrule Castle. She also wrote that the Throne Room's Torches are the key to revealing its hiding place. After reading Zelda's Diary, the "A New Champion's Tunic" Side Quest will begin. The remaining throne in Hyrule Castle's Throne Room is flanked on either side by a pair of stationary Torches. Striking the Torches with Flint, Fire Fruit, or Red Chuchu Jelly will ignite them. Once both Torches have been lit, the statue behind the throne will move to the side, revealing an Iron Treasure Chest in the base of its pedestal. Using Ultrahand, Link can pull out the Chest and open it, receiving the Champion's Leathers from inside. Immediately afterwards, "A New Champion's Tunic" will be completed. Objectives

page_title: A Picture for Dueling Peaks Stable
text: "" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link inspects the Empty Frame at Dueling Peaks Stable, its owner Tasseren will take note of him. He explains that it was given to him by the Stable Association so that he can display a Picture for his patrons. Tasseren wants to decorate it with a scene depicting the sunrise, as seen from the summit of Tuft Mountain. While he is unable to see the view for himself, Tasseren claims he would be able to paint it if he saw it. Afterwards, "A Picture for Dueling Peaks Stable" will begin. From Tuft Mountain, Link will be able to use his Camera to take a Picture of the sunrise, which he can then show to Tasseren. Upon seeing the Picture, Tasseren is amazed and asks for permission to copy it. If Link agrees, Tasseren thanks him for bringing the Picture He then proceeds to recreate the Picture for himself, promising he is talented enough to do so. Once the Picture of Hyrule's Finest Sunrise is complete, Tasseren declares that it is perfect. Tasseren informs Link that he is willing to replace it with another Picture of Hyrule's Finest Sunrise if he is provided with another reference. He then rewards Link will one Pony Point. In addition to this, he gives Link a Hasty Apple Pie, which is a specialty of Dueling Peaks Stable. Tasseren once again thanks Link for the Picture, inviting him to visit the Stable whenever he wants to. Following their conversation, "A Picture for Dueling Peaks Stable" will be finished. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link examines the Empty Frame at Foothill Stable, the owner Ozunda will notice him. He reveals that it was given to him by the Stable Association so he can hang up a Picture for his patrons. Since the Stable is a common stopping point on the way to Goron City, Ozunda wants to display a Picture of the statue of Daruk that can be found there. Although he is unable to leave the Stable to go paint it, he claims he would be able to replicate a Picture of it. After this, "A Picture for Foothill Stable" will start. Using his Camera, Link can take a Picture of the Goron Stone Memorial in Goron City, which contains the statue of Daruk. He can then take the Picture back to Foothill Stable to show Ozunda. Once he sees the Picture, Ozunda claims it is what he needed to see, and he asks for Link's permission to copy it. If Link agrees, Ozunda thanks him, claiming that the Picture captures Daruk's strength. He asks for a moment to create his own Picture, promising he has the talent to recreate it faithfully. After the Picture of the Daruk Sculpture is finished, Ozunda expresses his pride at how it turned out, and he is happy to have been able to paint again. Due to how much he enjoyed painting the Picture of the Daruk Sculpture, Ozunda offers to paint any more Pictures of the Goron Stone Memorial that Link takes. He then proceeds to reward Link with one Pony Point. In addition to this, he gives Link a Fireproof Lizard, which he believes will help him during his travels. Once again, Ozunda thanks Link, inviting him to make use of the Stable whenever he wants. Following their conversation, "A Picture for Foothill Stable" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link examines the Empty Frame at Highland Stable, Padok will notice his interest. He reveals that the Stable Association has given it to the Stable in order to display a Picture. Having heard a rumor about the Giant White Stallion, Padok wants to display a Picture of it. Although he has heard it can be found near the Lake of the Horse God to the southeast, Padok is hesitant to leave the Stable based on only a rumor. However, he claims he would be able to create a painting from a Picture of the Giant White Stallion. If Link has already registered the Giant White Stallion, Padok will recall that they are looking after such a Horse for him. Afterwards, "A Picture for Highland Stable" will start. After taking a Picture of the Giant White Stallion with the Camera, Link will be able to show it to Padok. Once he sees the Picture, Padok claims it is what he needed to see, and he asks for Link's permission to copy it. If Link agrees, Padok will imagine riding the Giant White Stallion across the plains. He then proceeds to paint the Picture, assuring Link that he is talented enough to replicate it. Upon completing the Picture of the Giant White Stallion, he will declare that it is perfect, and he looks forward to displaying it proudly. Should Link want to replace the Picture of the Giant White Stallion, Padok offers to do so, as long as a new reference Picture is provided. To reward Link for his assistance, Padok gives him one Pony Point. He also gives Link an Energizing Honey Crepe, which is a specialty of Highland Stable. Padok thanks Link for the Picture, inviting him to use the Stable's facilities whenever he needs. Following this, "A Picture for Highland Stable" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link inspects the Empty Frame at Lakeside Stable, the owner of the Stable, Anly, will notice him doing so. He explains that it was sent to him by the Stable Association so he could display a Picture for guests. After much thought, Anly has decided he would like to hang up a painting of the Floria Falls during clear Weather. However, Anly is unable to leave the Stable for long periods of time, and it is rare for the Weather in the area to remain clear. Anly claims that if someone brought him a Picture of this setting, then he would be able to recreate it for the Frame. Following this conversation, "A Picture for Lakeside Stable" will begin. Using the Camera, Link is able to capture an image of Floria Falls when the Weather is clear, which he can then show to Anly. When he sees the Picture, Anly claims it is exactly what he needed, and he asks for Link's permission to make a copy. Should Link agree, Anly states that he is moved by the Picture, and he believes it will make travelers happy they came to visit. He then proceeds to make his own copy, which he assures Link he is capable of doing. Once the Picture of Floria Falls on a Clear Day is completed, Anly declares that it is perfect. If Link ever wants to replace the Picture of Floria Falls on a Clear Day with a new version, Anly offers to repaint it so long as he is provided with a new reference. As a reward, he gives Link one Pony Point. He also gifts him a Tough Tomato Seafood Soup, which is a specialty of Lakeside Stable. Once again, Anly thanks Link for the Picture, and he invites him to visit the Stable whenever he needs. Afterwards, "A Picture for Lakeside Stable" will be finished. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link examines the Empty Frame at Outskirt Stable, Embry will notice. Embry explains that after the Stable owners decided to display Pictures to their patrons, the Stable Association provided them with Empty Frames. Since the Upheaval has caused people to become anxious, Embry wants to display a Picture of Mother Tree, the Cherry-Blossom Tree on Satori Mountain, to put them at ease. While Embry is too busy to venture to Satori Mountain and paint it himself, he believes he would be able to recreate a Picture of one. After their conversation, "A Picture for Outskirt Stable" will begin. Using the Camera, Link can take a Picture of Mother Tree, which he can then show to Embry. Upon seeing the Picture, Embry claims that it is exactly what he needed, and he asks Link permission to paint a copy of it. Should Link agree, Embry will be grateful. He is shocked that something as lovely as Cherry-Blossom Tree's petals can exist in the world, and he feels warm being able to see it bloom. He assures Link that he is talented enough at painting to create a copy of his Picture. Once the Picture of a Cherry-Blossom Tree is completed, Embry declares that it is perfect for Outskirt Stable, claiming it is as heartwarming and he thought it would be. If Link brings him another Picture featuring Mother Tree, Embry offers to paint a new version of it. To reward Link for his help, Embry gives him one Pony Point. He also gifts him a Egg Tart, which he claims is a specialty of Outskirt Stable. Embry thanks Link for his help, inviting him to visit the Stable whenever he needs to. At this point, "A Picture for Outskirt Stable" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link inspects the Empty Frame at Riverside Stable, Ember will notice him doing so. He explains that it was provided by the Stable Association so that he could display a Picture for visitors to enjoy. Ember has decided that he wants to hang a Picture of a Great Goddess Statue. While he does not know where many of them are, but he has heard that one is located in a nearby temple southwest of Hyrule Field. Since he has been unable to find it, he suspects it is somewhere that a Horse cannot easily reach. Ember claims that if he were able to see a depiction of a Great Goddess Statue, he would be able to copy it for his own Picture. Following their conversation, "A Picture for Riverside Stable" will begin. To complete this Side Quest, Link will need to use his Camera to take a Picture of one of these Great Goddess Statues: The Temple of Time Statue, located within the Temple of Time Ruins on the Great Plateau. The Great Goddess Statue, located within the Temple of Time on the Great Sky Island. The Spring of Courage Statue, located at the Spring of Courage in the Faron Grasslands. The Spring of Power Statue, located at the Spring of Power in Deep Akkala. The Spring of Wisdom Statue, located at the Spring of Wisdom on Mount Lanayru. After taking a Picture, Link will be able to present it to Ember. Upon seeing the Picture, Ember claims it is exactly what he has been searched for, and he asks permission to paint a copy. If Link agrees, Ember will be shocked by the Great Goddess Statue's size, though he assures Link that he is talented enough to produce a copy. Once the Picture of a Great Goddess Statue is completed, Ember declares that it is perfect for Riverside Stable, and he feels blessed having it watching over them. Should Link ever want to bring him a new Picture depicting a different angle or Great Goddess Statue, Ember offers to paint a new one. As a reward, he gives Link one Pony Point. He also gifts Link an Energizing Crab Stir-Fry, which he claims to be a specialty of Riverside Stable. Thanking Link once again, Ember invites him to visit the Stable whenever he needs. Afterwards, "A Picture for Riverside Stable" will be completed. Objectives

page_title: A Picture for South Akkala Stable
text: "" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link examines the Empty Frame at South Akkala Stable, Dmitri will notice. He explains that the Stables are hanging up Pictures for their patrons, and they are making use of Empty Frames provided by the Stable Association. After discussing it with his wife and daughters, Dmitri decides he wanted to display a Picture of the Unity Bell, which can be found in Tarrey Town. Though he is too busy to leave the Stable to paint it himself, Dmitri claims he would be able to copy a reference Picture. Afterwards, "A Picture for South Akkala Stable" will begin. Using the Camera, Link can take a Picture of the Unity Bell, which he can then show to Dmitri. When he sees the Picture, he claims that it is exactly what he needed before asking permission to make his own copy. If Link agrees, Dmitri recalls that he and his wife once rang the Unity Bell together, and they are still happy together. He then proceeds to make his duplicate, assuring Link that he is talented enough to do so. Once the Picture of the Unity Bell is complete, Dmitri claims he can almost hear it ringing, revealing that many couples hold wedding ceremonies in front of the Bell. Should Link ever capture a new Picture of the Unity Bell, Dmitri offers to make a new painting for him. As a reward, he gives Link one Pony Point. He also gives Link Prime Meat Stew, which he claims is a specialty of South Akkala Stable. Thanking Link for the Picture, Dmitri invites him to stay at the Stable whenever he needs. Following this conversation, "A Picture for South Akkala Stable" will be finished. Objectives

page_title: A Picture for the Closed Stable I
text: "" is a Side Quest in . Overview At the end of the "Piaffe, Packed Away" Side Quest, Piaffe claims it would be nice to decorate the Empty Frames at Gerudo Canyon Stable before it closes for good. When Link examines one of the Frames, Piaffe asks if he is interested. He explains that he forgot about them due to how busy he was cleaning out the Stable. Feeling indebted to the role Gerudo Canyon Stable played in his life, he wants to decorate them before he leaves. Piaffe recalls a Rito traveler once told him that when they looked down at Spectacle Rock while flying overhead, it appears to be smiling. Piaffe believes that a smile would be the best way to say goodbye to the Stable, and so he wants to frame a Picture of this sight. Although he is unable to take a Picture of this for himself, he believes that he would be able to copy one that someone else took. Objectives

page_title: A Picture for the Closed Stable II
text: "" is a Side Quest in . Overview At the end of the "Piaffe, Packed Away" Side Quest, Piaffe claims it would be nice to decorate the Empty Frames at Gerudo Canyon Stable before it closes for good. The second time Link examines one of the Empty Frames, Piaffe will notice his interest. He reveals that the Stable Association accidentally sent him two Frames, but he has decided to use both to say goodbye to the Stable. For the second Empty Frame, Piaffe wants to display a Picture of the Forgotten Sword near Gerudo Summit. However, Piaffe is unable to visit it himself since he needs to clean, and he dislikes the Freezing Climate of the Gerudo Highlands. Piaffe is willing to copy a Picture of the Forgotten Sword so he can display it in the Stable. Afterwards, "A Picture for the Closed Stable II" will begin. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link examines the Empty Frame at Wetland Stable, Lawdon will notice his interest. He explains that it was provided to him by the Stable Association so that he can hang up a Picture for his guests. Lawdon wants to display a painting of the Ring Ruins, since they are popular among the patrons of his Stable. Although he can see the Ruins from the Stable, he is not close enough to paint them. Following their conversation, "A Picture for Wetland Stable" will begin. At Kakariko Village, Link is able to take a Picture of the Large Ring Ruin using the Camera, which he can then show to Lawdon. When he sees the Picture, Lawdon asserts that it is just what he needed, and he asks for Link's permission to make his own copy. If Link agrees, Lawdon expresses his shock at how large the Ring Ruins are. He then proceeds to make his painting, assuring Link that he is talented enough to do so. Once the Picture of the Ring Ruins is complete, Lawdon states that he is proud of it. Lawdon offers to replace the Picture of the Ring Ruins if Link brings him a new reference. As a reward, Lawdon gives Link one Pony Point. He also gifts Link an Electro Elixir, which he believes will be helpful for his journey. Thanking Link, Lawdon invites him to visit Wetland Stable whenever he wants to. Afterwards, "A Picture for Wetland Stable" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link examines the Empty Frame at Woodland Stable, Kish will notice him doing so. He reveals that the Stable Association sent it to him after the Stable owners decided to display Pictures for their patrons. Kish wants to hang up a Picture depicting a Goron soaking in the Goron Hot Springs. While he does not have the time to make a trip to the Hot Springs, Kish claims he would be able to recreate a reference if provided with one. Following this, "A Picture for Woodland Stable" will begin. At the Goron Hot Springs, Link can find Grapp relaxing and take a Picture of him. He can also take a Picture of Axyl, Bohrin, or Jengo in the Hot Spring in Goron City. He can then present the Picture to Kish. Seeing the Picture, Kish proclaims that it is exactly what he needs, and he asks permission to copy it. When Link agrees, Kish jokes that he should abandon the Stable so he can go visit the Hot Springs. He then promises that he is talented enough to copy the Picture. Upon finishing the Picture of a Goron Soaking in Hot Springs, Kish declares that is is perfect. Kish offers to switch out the Picture if Link brings him a new one to copy. As a reward, he gives Link one Pony Point. He also gifts him Hasty Vegetable Curry, which he claims is a specialty of Woodland Stable. Once again, Kish thanks Link, inviting him to visit the Stable whenever he is in need. Afterwards, "A Picture for Woodland Stable" will be completed. Objectives

page_title: A Pretty Stone and Five Golden Apples
text: "" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview After defeating the Phantom Ganon inside the Great Deku Tree, Damia can be found with a Mysterious Crystal near the eastern entrance to Korok Forest. When spoken to, he expresses how pretty the Crystal is. If Link asks for it, Damia will initially refuse, but he reveals he will give it up should Link do something for him. If Link agrees to help, Damia claims he will relinquish the Crystal if he brings him five Golden Apples. To help, Damia points Link toward Mido Swamp, where Golden Apples are known to grow. He warns Link of both Monsters and the Swamp's Bottomless Bog. However, he does not care whether the Golden Apples come from Mido Swamp or not. Following this conversation, "A Pretty Stone and Five Golden Apples" will begin. Once Link is in possession of at least five Golden Apples, he can return to give them to Damia. Upon receiving the Golden Apples, Damia will allow Link to take the Mysterious Crystal. The next phase of "A Pretty Stone and Five Golden Apples" is activated by either interacting with the Mysterious Crystal or activating the Travel Point of the Pupunke Shrine. Doing so will cause him to hear a Mysterious Voice, which offers him a Light of Blessing if he can bring the Crystal to the Shrine of Light. A beam of Light then appears connecting the Mysterious Crystal and the Shrine. After bringing the Crystal to the Shrine, the Mysterious Voice will acknowledge Link and honors its promise. The Mysterious Crystal will then grow in size, revealing itself to be the entrance to the Pupunke Shrine. Afterwards, "A Pretty Stone and Five Golden Apples" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview Following the completion of "Sidon of the Zora", Link can find Yona overlooking the Zora's Domain Square. When spoken to, she once again thanks him for saving Zora's Domain. She reveals that she wanted to give him the Zora Greaves as a reward, which was inspired by Jiahto finding an ancient text describing them. Since they grant their wearer an easier time Swimming, Yona thinks that they could be useful for finding Zelda. Although Yona has been unable to find the Zora Greaves, the texts suggest that they were offered at the Ancient Zora Waterworks as a symbol of friendship between the Zora and the Hylians. After their conversation, "A Token of Friendship" will begin. When Link returns to the Ancient Zora Waterworks, he will find that the Water has been drained from its central chamber. On the north side of the Waterworks is a hole, which he can jump down to discover another chamber. Behind a Waterfall at the back of this chamber is a stone Treasure Chest, from which Link can obtain the Zora Greaves. Afterwards, "A Token of Friendship" will be completed. Objectives

page_title: A Way to Trade, Washed Away
text: "" is a Side Quest in . Overview After completing the "Village Attacked by Pirates" and "Lurelin Village Restoration Project" Side Adventures, Link can find Garini at the dock in Lurelin Village. He seems defeated, and he tells Link that with his Boat gone, he cannot open the Lurelin Village Store. Unfortunately, he cannot borrow one, because all the Boats in the village got washed out when the Monsters attacked. Usually, things that float out from their Village tend to wash up on Tenoko Island,. But he cannot get there himself, so his store will have to stay closed. Link then has to bring a Boat back from Tenoko Island. When he is close enough, Garini will call to him and Link will be transported to the dock. He thanks Link for his help and takes a moment to put the Lurelin Village Store back together, before offering Link a Star Fragment. Then, "A Way to Trade, Washed Away" will be completed. Objectives

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Abandoned Kara Kara Mine is an Abandoned Mine in the Gerudo Desert Depths. It is located directly beside the Tatayam Lightroot. Along the grounds of the Mine, Link can find Decayed Constructs which can be searched for Zonai Charges. Link can also find Crystallized Charges, Poes, Large Poes, and a Grand Poe. A Forge Construct can be found in the southeastern building of the Mine. This Construct will open a Shop that processes Zonaite once spoken to. A Steward Construct can also be found near the center of the Mine, awaiting activation. Once Link has obtained the Autobuild Ancient Power, the Steward Construct will grant him a Schema Stone with the Schematic for an Instant Scaffold. The Steward Construct will also add four Stone Slabs to the platform behind it so that Link can test the new Schematic. There is a Yiga Footsoldier disguised as a Researcher near the western side of the Abandoned Kara Kara Mine. This Yiga Footsoldier can be found alongside a lit Campfire and a machine fashioned from a Wing, a Fan, and a Steering Stick. When spoken to, the "Researcher" will inform Link that the Abandoned Kara Kara Mine contains Crystallized Charges and Constructs, but remarks that they cannot allow him to take anything. They then announce that they will kill Link and drop their disguise to attack. This "Researcher" will not attack Link if he is wearing the Yiga Clan Gear, instead asking him to look around for resources. Areas Forge Construct's Shop Enemies Materials Treasure Chests

are recurring Items in . Accessories go unnamed in . Location and Uses Accessories are a type of Armor Set consisting of Circlets and Earrings. They are traditionally crafted by Gerudo artisans, which is why they are sold by Isha at the Starlight Memories Jewelry Shop in Gerudo Town. All Accessories are head Armor, meaning only one can be worn at a time. They also make use of the natural powers of Gems in order to provide specific protections to their wearers. At the end of the "Tools of the Trade" Side Quest, Isha offers to make an Accessory for Link in return for the Flint he gave her. The options that she gives him are a Ruby Circlet, a Sapphire Circlet, and Topaz Earrings. List of Circlets List of Earrings Accessories can be worn to grant specific effects to Zelda. List of Accessories Other Appearances Accessories are a type of Fairy Clothing that can be worn by Companion Fairies. List of Accessories

are recurring Items in . Locations and Uses Acorns are common throughout Hyrule Kingdom, often found at the base of Trees. They may also drop when a Tree is cut down. They can also be obtained by killing Bushy-Tailed Squirrels. Acorns can be eaten raw to restore a quarter of a Heart. As Acorns are flammable, they will ignite when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate, which will result in Roasted Acorns. When added to a Cooking Pot, each Acorn will provide half a heart to the resulting meal. The first Acorn used will provide a 10 second boost to the duration of effects obtained from eating meals. Any further Acorns added will not provide any benefits to Foods or Elixirs. Acorns are also used as an ingredient for Brown Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop in Hateno Village. Acorns are required when Cooking the following meals: Acorns are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Acorns can be Fused to Arrows to increase their damage by one. They can be used to make the following Meals: Acorns are Items collected in the Acorn Gathering Mini-Game. Other Appearances Acorns are worth 3 Rupees, though the Merchant Bena takes them for 7 Rupees.

are recurring Objects and Korok Seed Puzzles in . Acorn Jars go unnamed in . Overview Acorn Jars are a type of Archery-based Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. They are often found hanging from Trees or below Bridges. They are also occasionally located in the hollows of Trees. Link can destroy them by either shooting them with an Arrow or using Remote Bombs. When he does so, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Like in , Acorn Jars are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle that can be solved using Archery. They can be found hanging from a variety of surfaces, such as Bridges or Sky Islands, in addition to being hidden inside of Tree hollows. Another type of Acorn Jar can be found floating in small bodies of Water. They can be destroyed by shooting them with Arrows or setting off an explosion nearby. As a result of this, a Korok will appear and grant Link a Korok Seed.

, also known as , are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Added Effects are a type of buff that Link can acquire by consuming Meals and Elixirs, or by equipping various pieces of Armor. They can buff Link in a variety of ways, from increasing his movement speed, to augmenting his combat prowess. Most Added Effects obtained through Meals or Elixirs will have a limited duration, determined by the Ingredients of the dish, while Added Effects obtained via Armor will be available for as long as the Armor piece is equipped. Some Added Effects can have different levels of potency, increasing their effectiveness. Certain Added Effects can stack to up to three total levels of potency, while others cap at one or two levels. When active, most Added Effects will be shown in the Inventory to the left of Link's model. The current level of potency, the max possible level, and the Added Effect's name and icon will all be displayed. Outside of the Inventory, active Meal or Elixir buffs will be shown below Link's Life Gauge, provided that the Pro HUD option is disabled. Some Added Effects are not shown directly in the Inventory when active, but their existence may be indicated by an Item's description. Link can only have one type of duration-based Added Effect from Meals or Elixirs active at a time. However, Added Effects can stack between Meals or Elixirs and Armor. This means that Link can have up to four different active buffs shown in the Inventory at a time, or if he has two pieces of Attack Up Armor equipped, he can consume a Meal or Elixir that grants a level one Attack Up Effect for a total of three levels. Set Bonuses Set Bonuses are a rarer type of Added Effect obtained exclusively through certain Armor Sets. In , there are 18 Added Effects that are visible in the Inventory when active and 13 that are hidden, totaling to 31 different Added Effects. In the Memory "Silent Princess", Zelda finds a Hot-Footed Frog and tells Link about its special properties, referencing the Speed Up Effect that an Elixir made with a Hot-Footed Frog can provide. List of Added Effects List of Hidden Added Effects Of the 31 Added Effects available in , 28 of them return in . With the addition of new Armor pieces and Ingredients, there are 17 new Added Effects, eight of which are hidden. The glowing effect of the Radiant Set also received the name NightGlow. The Effects "Guardian Resist Up", "AncientPowUp", and "See Enemy HP" are no longer available within . With 27 visible Effects and 19 hidden Effects available, there are 46 different Added Effects present in . Several Added Effects were renamed or received small changes, such as the new mobility options for the Swim Up Waterfalls Effect. Aerocudas are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Aerocudas are yellow, spotted, wyvern-like Enemies with large, red eyes, a pair of long, thin horns resembling antennae, orange wings with dark spotting, and a tail with a pair of wing-like structures at its tip. Upon sighting Link, they will fly after him, occasionally attempting to charge into him. They are capable of making high-pitched screeches that alert other nearby Enemies to Link's presence. They are also able to carry other enemies such as Bokoblins and Moblins in their talons in a manner similar to Kargaroks. Some Aerocudas may carry Treasure Chests; these will not attack Link and will focus on keeping their cargo out of his reach. While swift, they are very easily defeated with most Weapons, only having 2 health points. A single Arrow from most Bows will dispatch them. Link can also Parry an Aerocuda while it is charging at him to instantly kill it, a trait shared with Keese. Aerocudas will also drown if they make contact with Deep Water. Other Appearances Aerocudas serve as Powerful Enemies. In addition to the standard version, Electric, Fire, and Ice Aerocudas appear as Elemental variants.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Afromsia Coast is located along the Lanayru Sea, on the eastern side of Mount Lanayru. It is populated by Razorclaw Crabs and Ironshell Crabs. Several Ore Deposits are also available in this area. When Link speaks to Clavia in Hateno Village, she tries to decipher a message she found, stating that turning towards the sea could refer to heading to Afromsia Coast. During the "Secret of the Cedars" Shrine Quest, walking towards Afromsia Coast after lining up the Cedar Trees on Madorna Mountain will lead Link to Tahno O'ah Shrine. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Afromsia Coast. On the southern end of the Coast, Link can find a Korok hidden in a Natural Hiding Spot, which is disguised as a Rock. When Link lifts the Rock, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Agraston is a recurring character in . Biography In the Era of Foundation, Agraston was the Goron Sage of Fire and one of the Six Sages. He was a leader to the Gorons, and during the Imprisoning War, he fought alongside the King of Hyrule, Rauru, as a Sage. Agraston can be seen in the Forgotten Temple during the Memory "The Sages' Vow". When Rauru reveals the room containing the Secret Stones, Agraston recognizes them. Rauru grants the four remaining Stones to Agraston, Raphica, Qia, and Ardi, intending to increase their power before facing Demon King Ganondorf. Agraston's Stone turns into a Secret Stone of Fire, and he becomes the Sage of Fire. Once this is done, the Six Sages make a vow of loyalty to Rauru. thumb|left|320px|Agraston during the Imprisoning War In flashbacks to the Imprisoning War, Agraston wields a Boulder Breaker. Despite their strength, Rauru and the Sages were unable to overcome Demon King Ganondorf, and Agraston appears wounded by Gloom during the Memory "The Imprisoning War". To distract the Demon King, the Sages throw their Weapons toward him, which Princess Zelda returns to them using Recall. This allows Rauru to get closer to Ganondorf, and he subsequently sacrifices himself to seal the Demon King away. The Sage of Fire witnesses this event. Following the Imprisoning War, Zelda came to visit Agraston at the Fire Temple. She warned that Demon King Ganondorf would one day break free from his seal, and she asked him to ensure the Gorons would support Link when the time comes to oppose him. As a result, he vowed that a new Sage of Fire will awaken when the Demon King returns and fight alongside Link. Afterwards, during the Memory "Tears of the Dragon", Agraston can be seen with the Raphica, Qia, and Ardi, watching as the Light Dragon disappears into the Sky. Throughout the Main Quest "Yunobo of Goron City", Yunobo and Link hear Agraston's voice calling to them from the Depths. Once they reach the Fire Temple, Agraston instructs them to ring the Gongs to release the five Locks, which will allow them to access the Temple's innermost chamber. After Marbled Gohma has been defeated, a Secret Stone will appear before them. When Yunobo touches it, Agraston appears before them, introducing himself as Yunobo's ancestor. He expresses his pride in Yunobo's Power of Fire, and he reveals that Demon King Ganondorf sent Marbled Gohma to prevent Yunobo from finding his Secret Stone. Hearing Yunobo's confusion, the Sage proceeds to tell him the story of the Imprisoning War. Following his retelling, Agraston warns that, although Goron City has been saved, Demon King Ganondorf still poses a threat to all of Hyrule. Therefore, he asks Yunobo to honor the vow he made to Princess Zelda and fight alongside Link, at which point he disappears. is a recurring character in . Biography Agus is a Merchant who lives in Hateno Village in East Necluda, where he grows vegetables to sell at Dueling Peaks Stable in West Necluda. As such, he can be found traveling the roads between these locations with his Donkey. He uses the Rupees from his vegetable sales to purchase meat at the Dueling Peaks Stable, which he exchanges to the people of his home town. He will offer to sell his stock to Link or purchase items from him, as well. When Agus arrives in the Midla Woods, he will rest below a cliff near the edge of Hateno Village. He laments the fact that he is unable relax in his hometown, since he has to gather fresh vegetables to bring back to Dueling Peaks Stable. After a while, he will get up and start to head back towards the Stable. Agus prefers Donkeys to Horses, claiming they are more his style. He claims that, while people talk about horsepower, they tend to forget about "donkeypower", which is the power to be friends. He calls his Donkey his buddy, which Link is apparently confused by. On his journey, Agus will pass by Kakariko Village, explaining that he has not had luck selling his wares there. While passing Lake Siela, Agus will grow nervous, being frightened if Link approaches him. He will be relieved so see Link is a regular person and apologize. Agus explains that a while ago, he was scared by a Tree ghost on the other side of the Lake, so he ends up being a bit jumpy in this area. He keeps an eye on this Tree, asking Link if it is actually moving or if his eyes are playing tricks on him. To make something delicious, Agus suggests Cooking Goat Butter and Tabantha Wheat together. There is apparently a third item that should be used, but he is unable to remember what it was. This recipe lines up with Salmon Meunière, Porgy Meunière, and Seafood Meunière. If Link saves Agus from an Enemy attack, he might ask if Link is a famous swordsman and say he should be one. He may also wonder what would have happened to him if Link had not come along, but soon dismisses this thought as something he does not want to worry about. He can also comment that he thought Link was strong the first time he saw him, and he ended up being proven right. In all scenarios, he will give Link a Sneaky Elixir as a reward. On subsequent rescues, he gives Link Cooking ingredients. If Link buys from him while it is Raining, Agus will note that that many Merchants sell their best wares or cut deals when the Weather is bad. However, Agus himself has no special offers during such scenarios. He reveals that he does not mind the rain, since it gives one a good excuse to stay put for a while. Wares and Pricing In the

is a character in . Biography Aja is Hylian who resides at Lookout Landing. During the day, he practices with a Dummy, hoping to one day become a swordsman. He carries a Soldier's Broadsword and a Soldier's Shield. He does not appear until Link has started the Main Quest "Crisis at Hyrule Castle". When Link tries to speak to Aja, he claims to be busy and says he can only talk between swings of his Soldier's Broadsword. He believes it is important to be prepared for Monster attacks, and he suggests trying out a variety of Swords to get used to how they handle. Through practice, he has found that Decayed Weapons can still be useful. Should Link need to train, Aja tells him to do so elsewhere. If Link examines the nearby Swords, Aja will explain what they are and allow him to take them. When asked about the Soldier's Broadsword, Aja reveals that they were used by the Soldier of Hyrule Castle, and he believes they can be used to unleash Charged Attacks more quickly. When asked about the Knight's Broadsword, he explains that they were used by Knights of Hyrule, and he recalls that he was able to unleash a strong attack against a Monster using one. Lastly, when asked about the Royal Broadsword, he claims it was used by the Royal Guard and has a high counterattack power, though he is not yet skillful enough to make use of it. After Link has learned about each type of Sword, Aja will give one to him. He then suggests that Link make sure to practice with and take care of his new sword. If Link does not have enough space in his Inventory for another Weapon, Aja tells him to come back for it later. Once Link has taken all three Swords, Aja stops training and introduces himself. When he realizes he has been talking to Link, he apologizes for not noticing sooner and is honored to meet him. He is motivated to become a master swordsman like Link, and so he returns to his training. When Link talks to Aja again, he asks how he has found the Sword he received. He then asks Link if he wants to learn more about Swords. He comments that he likes the Soldier's Broadsword's mobility, which allows users to quickly unleash Charged Attacks. Although Knight's Broadswords increase in power if their users are weakened, he suggests avoiding such situations. Finally, when talking about the Royal Broadsword, he reiterates that he is not yet able to make use of its counterattack ability. After the Main Quest "Sidon of the Zora" has been completed, Aja can be found training with the Zora soldiers at Lookout Landing. He plans to work with them if reinforcements are ever needed.

is a recurring character in . Biography Aji is a Goron who runs the Protein Palace General Store in Goron City. He sells a small selection of Roasted Foods that were Cooked upon a heated stone slab. If Link asks about the Protein Palace, Aji explains that he grills Roasted Food. He admits that since Gorons normally only eat Rocks, the General Store mainly serves tourists. However, because it is possible to create Roasted Foods just by placing them on the ground in the Scorching Climate, he has been losing customers. If Link decides to buy from him, Aji becomes extremely shocked, since he has not had a customer in a very long time. When Link repeats this desire, Aji appreciates it, since it is very easy to create Roasted Food outside of the Protein Palace. He claims not to be worried about this, though, and he encourages Link to take what he wants. When Link buys a piece of Roasted Food, Aji remarks that he is sold out. Should Link buy all of Aji's wares, he will promise to restock soon. Like other General Store owners, Aji will buy Items from Link. Throughout the process, he encourages Link to sell to him. Whenever he makes a purchase from Link, Aji will thank him. He also remarks that he is doing good business. If Link stands on Aji's Cooking platform, he looks visibly surprised and asks him to stop. Speaking to him in this state has him beg Link to get down. He may also question Link's upbringing, implying that he lacks manners.

The , also known as the Yiga Clan's Akkala Branch, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Akkala Ancient Tech Lab is located on the North Akkala Foothill in Deep Akkala. It was converted from an abandoned lighthouse near East Akkala Stable, and it currently houses Robbie and Jerrin. The pair of them operate the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab together. It is one of two successors to the Ancient Research Institute, the other being the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. Following the Great Calamity, Robbie and Purah discovered two sources of Ancient Energy in Necluda and Akkala. After a game of rock, paper, scissors, it was determined that Robbie would make use of the Energy in Akkala, where he would continue his research into Ancient Technology. With him, he took a Guidance Stone. When he came upon the ruined lighthouse, he decided to settle there, turning it into the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab. At the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab, Robbie focused his research on Ancient Soldier Gear. The Ancient Furnace in Akkala is located on Tumlea Heights, which is on the opposite side of the North Akkala Foothill. In order to expedite the process of smelting Ancient Materials, Robbie refined his Guidance Stone into the Ancient Oven, which he refers to as "Cherry." When Robbie was 90, Impa sent Jerrin to work at the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab. She took over the duties of lighting the Lab's Furnace with the Blue Flame, in addition to remodeling the Ancient Oven. After some time, the two of them ended up married. They had a son together, Granté, who they raised at the Lab. As Granté grew, he took over retrieving the Blue Flame, but he eventually left after Robbie encouraged him to travel. As part of the "Robbie's Research" Side Quest, Purah tells Link to bring Ancient Materials to either her or Robbie. This tasks Link with finding Robbie at the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab. When he arrives, the Furnace outside the Lab will be extinguished, and Link must reignite it in order to restore the Ancient Oven's manufacturing of Ancient Soldier Gear. Once Link lights the Furnace, the Travel Gate at the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab will be activated, allowing him to Warp there directly. As thanks, Robbie gives Link three Ancient Arrows. Following this, Link will be able to purchase Ancient Soldier Gear and the Ancient Set from the Ancient Oven, in exchange for Rupees and Ancient Materials. When Link speaks to Jerrin at the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab, she informs him that through her research, she has discovered an Ancient Shrine on the left eye of Skull Lake. This begins "The Skull's Eye" Shrine Quest. If Link returns to Jerrin after locating Zuna Kai Shrine, she is unable to give him a reward due to the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab being short on funding. Equipment Inhabitants Korok Seeds Inhabitants

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Akkala Bridge Ruins are located in the Akkala Highlands. They are the remains of a bridge that once lead to the Akkala Citadel Ruins. Both ends are littered with the deactivated remains of Guardian Stalkers, which Link can scavenge for Ancient Materials. On the western side of the Akkala Bridge Ruins, Link will find Nell fighting off a Blue Moblin. When Link helps him, Nell will offer his thanks and gift him Food as a reward. He explains that he wanted to go to the Akkala Citadel Ruins to pray for his ancestors who fell there, but since the Guardians surrounding the Ruins are still active, he has decided not to progress past the Akkala Bridge Ruins. Enemies Inhabitants Treasure Chests

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview In , the Akkala Citadel Ruins are the remains of a fortress built to protect the Akkala Region from all conceivable threats, and to protect Hyrule as a whole from invaders coming from the sea to the east. However, the events of the second Great Calamity forced the remains of Hyrule's leaderless army to retreat to the Akkala Citadel, where they were assailed by Guardians under Calamity Ganon's control. Unable to match the sheer power of the ancient Sheikah technology, the soldiers fell in battle, marking the decisive end to the Kingdom of Hyrule. A century later, a traveler named Nell decided to visit the Akkala Citadel Ruins to pay respects for his relatives who fell during the battle. However, as the Akkala Citadel Ruins are still inhabited by Guardians, Nell is unable to complete his journey. Atop a broken balcony on the northern side of the Ruins, Link can find several Arrows as well as a metal door covering a Rock under which a Korok can be found. On the wall above this point, a second Korok can be found hiding under a Rock beneath a pile of dead leaves. A third Korok can be found underneath a Rock beside a row of Cannons south of the Akkala Tower. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests In the years following Calamity Ganon's defeat, the Malice that covered the top of the Akkala Citadel Ruins has vanished, making the top area more explorable. Two Caves have become accessible as a result, these being the Akkala Citadel Ruins Cave at the Ruins' base and the Akkala Citadel Ruins Summit Cave near where the Akkala Tower used to be. The latter Cave is one of three key locations to completing the "Misko's Treasure: The Fierce Deity" Side Quest. At the top of the Ruins lies Domizuin Shrine, which serves as a new Warping point. A Gloom Spawn also resides in the immediate area. The Ancient Underground Fortress in the Depths is a counterpart to the Akkala Citadel Ruins. The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Akkala Highlands are a densely-wooded area in the northeast of Hyrule. It is bordered by the Akkala Sea to the east, Deep Akkala to the north, Eldin Canyon to the west, and the Lanayru Great Spring to the south. As with the rest of the Akkala Region, the Trees in the Akkala Highlands possess a permanent Autumnnal coloration. The Akkala Highlands have historically been a defensive region for Hyrule Kingdom, defending it from attacks from the Akkala Sea with the Akkala Citadel. Ironically, the Akkala Highlands are where the Kingdom fell during the second Great Calamity, after it was attacked by Guardians originating from the Kingdom's center, Hyrule Field. A century after the Great Calamity, the Bolson Construction company attempts to reconstruct civilization in the Akkala Highlands by dispatching Hudson to build a new settlement. Hudson settles on a rock island in the northern part of Lake Akkala, naming the new village Tarrey Town. At some point prior to this, Epona Co. established the South Akkala Stable near the base of the Akkala Citadel Ruins to assist travelers in the region. Climates Areas Areas Other Appearances

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Akkala Parade Ground Ruins are located on the South Akkala Plains in the Akkala Highlands, south of the Akkala Citadel Ruins. The Ruins consist of rows of planted Trees and an abandoned fountain. A Blue Hinox sleeps in the center of the Akkala Parade Ground Ruins. It has a single wooden brace around one of its ankles, which is capable of blocking attacks from Link. However, this brace can be burned away with Fire. Around the Hinox's neck is a Royal Broadsword, a Royal Bow, and a Royal Halberd, which Link can pick up upon its defeat. Creatures Enemies Materials

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Akkala Span is located in the Akkala Highlands between Cephla Lake and Akkala Falls. The bridge connects the Akkala Highlands to the Lanayru Great Spring. It is a short bridge made out of stones with 3 stone pillars leading to the ground below. Next to the Akkala Span, a Monster Stronghold can be found among some small ruins. In Master Mode, two platforms held aloft by Sky Octoroks are located near the Akkala Span. left|40px On one of the Akkala Span's broken pillar, Link can find a Rock underneath a stone slab. This slab can be moved by attaching Octo Balloons to it or hitting it while it is under the effect of the Stasis Rune. If Link picks up the Rock, it will be revealed to be a Natural Hiding Spot. A Korok will then appear and gift Link a Korok Seed as a reward. Creatures Enemies

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Akkala Wilds are located in Deep Akkala, west of Tumlea Heights. They span all the way to the edge of Eldin. Several Ore Deposits, including Rare Ore Deposits, are found along the cliffs on its southern border. There are several small forests among the Akkala Wilds, which are filled with Mushrooms and other Materials. In addition, many Fallen Guardians are found in the area, which can be scavenged for Ancient Materials. Dinraal will fly over the Akkala Wilds on occasion. While it does not get close enough to the ground for Link to reach, it does cause a strong Wind to sweep over the area. A single Monster Stronghold, filled with a variety of Bokoblins, is found in the Akkala Wilds. If Link defeats all of the Enemies, he will be able to open their Treasure Chest, which contains a Drillshaft. A Blue-Maned Lynel also patrols the eastern side of the Akkala Wilds. While the "[Xenoblade Chronicles 2]" Side Quest is active, Link can stand on the left eye of Skull Lake, causing a Treasure Chest to fall from the sky and land in the Akkala Wilds. This Chest contains the Salvager Vest. left|40px A total of six Korok Seed Puzzles can be found hidden among the Akkala Wilds. When Link solves each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear, which then proceeds to give Link a Korok Seed as a reward. They are in the following locations: Under a Natural Hiding Spot, located in a dead Tree on the western side of the Akkala Wilds. A Rock Pattern, south of the Monster Stronghold. Under a Natural Hiding Spot, which is concealed by a Boulder southeast of the Monster Stronghold. Under a Natural Hiding Spot, hidden by a rock slab east of Skull Lake. Hitting a Boulder from Tumlea Heights into a hole in the Akkala Wilds. This task may cause Link to pass through the territory of the Blue-Maned Lynel At the end of a Flower Trail, east of the ruins. is a recurring character in . Biography Akrah is one of three Hylians who can be found at Serenne Stable debating the cause of the Leviathans' extinction, the other two being his brothers Onya and Garshon. He theorizes that the Leviathans went extinct to a volcanic eruption. However, while of the three scientists have been able to locate any Leviathan Bones, they do have an idea of where to find them. Akrah will ask Link if he's willing to travel to these locations to find the bones and return with a Picture. He also asks that these Pictures include the heads of the animals. He will offer a reward of 300 Rupees, and accepting will activate the "Leviathan Bones" Side Quest. The specific Leviathan Akrah wants to see is the Eldin Great Skeleton, which is located in the region of Eldin. Link can take a photo of it with the Camera Rune. When he shows the picture to Akrah, he will be shocked at the quality. With the Picture, he believes he'll be able to prove his theory about the volcanic eruption. If Link hasn't delivered Pictures to Onya or Garshon by the time he speaks to him, Akrah will ask Link to assist in their research as well. If Akrah is the last scientist to have his photo delivered, he will be the one to give Link his reward. After the quest is completed, Akrah will continue to debate the Leviathans' extinction with his brothers. He will explain that he's using the Picture Link provided to his theory about the Leviathans. At night, he mutters about heat in his sleep. On rainy days, he and his brothers stay inside the stable, and Zumi joins in on their conversations. He says they like to stay inside during rainy days, but quietly admits that it gives him a chance to talk with Zumi. Akrah and his brother Onya now reside at New Serenne Stable, where they argue about what goals to pursue next. He wants to find a rumored beast, and he thinks that the legendary weapon is just a story.

is a recurring character in . Biography Aliza is a resident of Outskirt Stable. She can be found standing beneath a large Tree just east of the Stable, which she refers to as sacred. There, she diligently waits to meet the hero of legend, whom she is smitten with. Until Link speaks with her, she will stand beneath the Tree regardless of the Weather or Time of day. If Link approaches her, she will preemptively speak to him. When Link first speaks with Aliza, she initially believes him to be the legendary hero. Regardless if Link confirms or denies this, she will backtrack on her assertion and doubt his status when she notices he is not carrying the Master Sword. Once she realizes her mistake, she asks Link to send the hero her way if he ever encounters him on his travels. Even if Link tries to stop talking to her without acknowledging her belief, she will still make this request. After speaking to Aliza, Link receives the "My Hero" Side Quest, prompting him to return to Aliza once he has found the Master Sword. Link can further interrogate Aliza about the "legendary hero" and the Master Sword. When asked about the hero, Aliza explains that he appears with the Master Sword whenever Calamity Ganon threatens Hyrule Kingdom. If Link inquires about the Master Sword, she will inform him that the stories she heard of it say that it was put to rest in a forest, awaiting its owner's return. After acquiring the Master Sword, Link can return to Aliza and state his status as the hero. She states that the Master Sword he carries is proof of this. As a gift, she gives Link a Star Fragment. Though Aliza is truly excited about meeting Link, her mood completely drops after rewarding their encounter, having lost her excitement over meeting him. If Link talks to Aliza later on, she scolds him for talking to random strangers instead of doing his job. During the evening, she sits beside Outskirt Stable's Cooking Pot. At midnight, she heads inside the Stable to sleep in one of its Beds. Aliza is one of the tailors that Link rescues from the Yiga Clan. After she is rescued, Aliza walks from Kara Kara Bazaar to Gerudo Town and back again. She spends some of the morning outside Fashion Passion, Kara Kara Bazaar's Armor Shop, before walking to Gerudo Town at about 8:00AM. She waits in the market square for about an hour in the evening, then walks back in the night. She shows interest in finding both Misko's hidden treasure and the Gerudo Secret Club, frequently making reference of the latter while in Gerudo Town.

is a recurring character in . Biography Amali lives in Rito Village with her five daughters Kheel, Notts, Kotts, Cree, and Genli, and she is the wife of Kass. Before the Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been appeased, Amali can be found on the platform near the Akh Va'quot Shrine with Kheel. Amali muses that Kheel insists on worrying her. If Link asks what is the matter, Amali explains that her youngest daughter Kheel wants to go to Warbler's Nest and will not stop talking about it. Her five daughters have been getting needier by the minute ever since the "beast", Vah Medoh, appeared. At times like this she wishes Kass was around. Amali wishes she could be a kid again and think only of herself, but acknowledges that as a parent she has to be bigger than her children. Amali tells Kheel to watch her language when she calls Divine Beast Vah Medoh a big jerk. At night, Link can encounter Amali by the Cooking Pot in the Village's Kitchen. She asks him who he usually cooks for. If Link says he cooks for himself, Amali hopes she did not ask too personal of a question. When she cooks, Amali wonders about the future of the village and her family. Her thoughts are dark, but they are lighter once she eats. She encourages him to use the Cooking Pot. After Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been appeased, Amali is still on the platform, this time calling for Kheel. She turns to Link and says that she cannot find Kheel anywhere and wonders where she could be. Amali considers the possibility that she could have gone to Warbler's Nest to practice her singing. However, it is far away and Amali worries whether she could have made it there on her own. This initiates the Side Quest "Find Kheel." Once Kheel has been found, Amali is relieved that she is at Warbler's Nest after all. She gives Link 50 Rupees as thanks for letting her know. Amali feels much better now that she knows where Kheel is and thanks Link again. It sets her mind at ease to know where her children are. Her daughters are gathering the ingredients necessary to make Salmon Meunière, since Genli will not sing with her sisters until she has some. She hopes they stay safe as they are all out gathering ingredients. When Amali's daughters finish their recital at Warbler's Nest, they return to her in Rito Village. She can be found in the Kitchen, where she hopes her children are not causing Link too much grief. Upon Kass's return to Rito Village, Amali is inside her home and thanks Link for bringing her husband back. She says he is singing with his daughters at his usual place and that they could use an audience if Link has some time to spare.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Ambers are Materials that can be found in various Treasure Chests. The Gems can also often be found inside broken Ore Deposits, and they sometimes appear inside Snowballs when they shatter. Stone Taluses and Stone Pebblit occasionally drop them as well. They are sold by Kairo, who travels between Foothill Stable and the Maw of Death Mountain. 10 pieces of Amber can be used at Starlight Memories to create the Amber Earrings, which use the Amber to harness the power of the land and increase defense. The Kochi Dye Shop accepts Ambers as an ingredient to make Orange Dye. When speaking to Ramella in Goron City, she will explain that if Link brings her 10 Ambers, she will pay more for them than a store will. This will begin the Side Quest "The Jewel Trade". Afterwards, Link may sell batches of 10 Gems to Ramella in exchange for an increased payment. Ambers are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Ambers return as Materials in . They are much sharper than they appeared in . Ambers are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances Ambers as they are depicted in are featured in . They can be earned from Treasure Chests or as a reward for completing Scenarios and Challenges. As Materials, they can be used to fulfill Quest requirements. Ambers return in , utilizing the sharp design featured in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Amber Earrings are a type of Accessory, specifically Earrings that can be clipped onto Link's ears. They can be purchased at the Starlight Memories Jewelry Shop in Gerudo Town for 100 Rupees and ten pieces of Amber. The Amber in the Earrings harnesses the land's power, giving them increased defense compared to most other Armor. Amber Earrings can be enhanced by a Great Fairy at a Great Fairy Fountain. However, they cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Earrings have no other use than to increase Link's defense. Enhancing Enhancing Other Appearances Amber Earrings are a piece of Attire that can be worn by Link. The Amber Earrings are unlocked after completing the Quest "Not a Light Meal", and cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop.

is a recurring character in . Biography Ami is a child who lives at the Wetland Stable on the edge of the Lanayru Wetlands. His brother Izra will direct Link to him for directions, stating it is great to have a little brother who pulls his weight. During the day, Ami can be found watching Yolero practice with his Master Torch by the Cooking Pot. If it rains, Ami will seek shelter in the Stable. At night, he sleeps in one of the Beds inside. The first time Link speaks to Ami, he will sigh. When asked what is wrong, Ami explains that while his older brothers get to play all day long, he is forced to stay by the Wetland Stable and give directions. Link inquires further, at which point Ami reveals that the Stable Association requires each Stable to have an individual ready to give directions to visitors. Since Ami is the only resident of Wetland Stable with a grasp on geography, this job has fallen to him. On subsequent visits, Ami proclaims that his life is a joke, before he asks Link what he wants to know about the surrounding area. When asked what is to the east, Ami will explain that Zora's Domain is about the only thing in that direction. If Link asks about the west, Ami mocks Link and explains Hyrule Castle is that way. He also shares that he has heard about a hidden escape route from the Castle called the East Passage, which was supposedly made for the Royal Family of Hyrule. To the north, he explains that there is Death Mountain and other things. When Link tries to leave, Ami will ask if he wants to know what is to the south. If Link denies him, Ami says that he will see him around. If Link agrees, Ami reveals that he wishes he knew but he has never been able to leave Wetland Stable. He tells Link to ask around at Riverside Stable if he wants to know.

is a recurring character in . Biography Amira is a rather unfriendly, gossip loving woman who resides in Hateno Village with her family.. At 9:00 PM, Amira heads to sleep on the top floor of the East Wind with her children. She is clearly tired and sighs when Link attempts to converse with her, irritated with the company. She is an uneasy sleeper, often grunting or mumbling as she dreams. If Link tries to speak with her in the morning, she asks him to leave her alone. During the day, Amira be found chatting with fellow villager Nikki at the Well next to the East Wind. However, she despises others who try to listen in on her conversation and will harshly tell Link off if he tries to speak with her. If Link attempts to speak to Nikki instead, Amira admonishes him for trying to eavesdrop. Should Amira make it to the Well before Nikki, she will say that she is waiting for someone and ask Link to leave. To listen to their conversation, Link must hide out behind the Well. They talk about a little girl who has been spotted at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. Amira thinks that perhaps the people living in the Lab adopted her, but Nikki disagrees. Like most residents of Hateno Village, Amira will have a reaction if Link speaks to her while carrying the Blue Flame. She notes that it is dangerous and says that he should not run around with it. If Link speaks to her again, she scolds him for carrying something so dangerous and tells him to put it away.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview At Wetland Stable, Link can encounter Ami staring into the nearby woods. He warns Link not to enter the forest during the night, since a Blue Moblin and several Lizalfos have set up a Monster Outpost inside. He complains that he is now unable to use the Wetland Stable South Well that he built due to its proximity to the Outpost. However, he did make the new Wetland Stable Well to replace it. Ami is so scared of the Monsters that he is having trouble sleeping and talking straight. He claims that he tried to sneak up on them from behind, but he failed. If the Blue Moblin was gone, Ami thinks he would feel much safer, and he reiterates his warning to stay away from the forest. Following their conversation, "An Uninvited Guest" will begin. From the bottom of the Wetland Stable Well, Link is able to exit from the Wetland Stable South Well right next to the Monster Outpost. After defeating the Blue Moblin, Link must return to Wetland Stable to inform Ami. He asks Link if he was the one who defeated the Blue Moblin, expressing his amazement and gratitude. Since he does not have any Rupees for a reward, Ami gifts Link two Pony Points. Ami thanks Link once again, stating he will be able to greet customers now. He then runs away, and "An Uninvited Guest" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring character in . Biography Anche is a Gerudo Soldier who manages the Northern Icehouse. She is often seen counting the Ice in the Icehouse, and she carries a Gerudo Shield and a Moonlight Scimitar on her person. If Link speaks to her, she explains that the Icehouse stores the Ice that is collected from the Gerudo Highlands. Anche explains that the Ice is important for the Gerudo people. If Link speaks to Anche while she is in Bed during the night, she tells him to come back tomorrow and that her work is done for the day. During "The Perfect Drink" Shrine Quest, Furosa will ask Link to talk to Anche about obtaining Ice for Pokki's drink. She also mentions that Anche goes to bed early, so Link should speak to her while it is bright out. When the situation is explained, Anche will allow Link to bring the Ice to Furosa. She reminds him to move quickly due to the heat, since Furosa can not do anything with Water. Anche will be disappointed if the Ice melts, though she accepts Link's mistake and allows him to take another block. After completing the Shrine Quest, speaking to Anche will cause her to ask Link to once again deliver Ice to Furosa for her. While she usually delivers the Ice herself, she explains that the nearby monsters are preventing her from leaving the Icehouse. Anche charges Link 50 Rupees for the Ice and explains that Furosa will reimburse him. Once Link has paid the fee, the Carry the Ice! Mini-Game will begin. Link is timed while delivering the Ice and will be rewarded with extra Rupees if he delivers it quickly enough. If Link accepts the task, Anche expresses joy and reiterates that Furosa will be waiting for him at the end of the North Gerudo Ruins nearby. If Link attempts to melt a formation of Ice inside the Northern Icehouse or if Anche detects any Fire inside the Northern Icehouse, Anche will scold him for damaging her supply before kicking him out. If Anche detects Fire but cannot find the culprit (such as if Link sets the Fire while she is asleep and then leaves), she will angrily ask who is responsible for putting it there. If Link is caught enough times, she will inform Link that she will not be held responsible for the punishment being brought to him and demands that he leave.

Ancient Blades are Items in . Location and Uses Ancient Blades are Materials. They can be Fused to a weapon or arrow to increase its attack power by 50, but will break after the first hit, and will disintegrate normal Enemies on contact in the same way as Ancient Arrows in . Ancient Blades can be found in various Treasure Chests across Hyrule, as well as bought from a Mining Construct in the Spirit Temple once the "Ancient Blades Below" Side Quest has been completed. They can also be found in Iron Treasure Chests that spawn after scanning the series Link (Archer) and Guardian amiibo, which can be done using the amiibo Ancient Power.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Ancient Columns are a set of Ancient Hylian Ruins located on the Rayne Highlands in the Tabantha Frontier. Dozens of ruined stone columns litter the area, some of which have fallen over. There is a small pond in the center of the area, which contains Chillfin Trout. The Columns are also home to Tena Ko'sah Shrine. Prior to the second Great Calamity, Zelda attempted to investigate the Ancient Shrine using the Sheikah Slate, but she was unable to gain access. When Link approached her, Zelda reiterated her annoyance at having an escort and ordered him to stop following her. During the "Captured Memories" Main Quest, Link can claim the "Zelda's Resentment" Recovered Memory outside of Tena Ko'sah Shrine, which depicts these events. The is an Item in . Location and Uses The Ancient Hero's Aspect is a piece of Armor and an Armor Set. It is obtained from the Treasure Chest that appears behind the Goddess Statue in the Temple of Time as part of the "The Shrine Explorer" Side Quest. The Quest begins when Link receives the final Light of Blessing after completing every Shrine of Light. Unlike other Armor, the Ancient Hero's Aspect is by itself a complete Armor Set and cannot be worn alongside any other pieces of Armor; the Rupee cost to upgrade it is tripled (30, 150, 600, 1500) due to this. When the Ancient Hero's Aspect has been upgraded at least two times by a Great Fairy and is worn, it provides the Master Sword Beam Up Set Bonus. Enhancing

The is the title given to a recurring character in . The Ancient Hero goes unnamed in . The Ancient Hero was born with the spirit of the hero and defeated Calamity Ganon with the help of Ancient Technology 10,000 years prior to the events of , as memorialized on the Calamity Ganon Tapestry. depicts the Ancient Hero as having a connection to the Zonai, with a similar though distinct appearance and wearing their armor. However, the details of this relation and the Ancient Hero's species are unknown. Biography thumb|left|The Calamity Ganon Tapestry depicting the Ancient Hero sealing Calamity Ganon 10,000 years before the events of , the Ancient Hero united with an incarnation of the Princess, the four Divine Beasts, and numerous Guardians, using the Sword That Seals the Darkness to seal Calamity Ganon away beneath Hyrule Castle. This legend is told upon completing the Great Plateau by King Rhoam and retold to Link separately by Impa and Kass. The Ancient Hero is never seen directly, but he appears in artistic form on the Calamity Ganon Tapestry. The artwork depicts him with green eyes, fiery red hair, and a light blue outfit, similar to the Champion's Tunic his successor wears in the distant future. Upon first meeting Link, Kass claims that his Ancient Songs commemorate the actions of the Ancient Hero. He also mentions the Ancient Hero during the Side Quest "The Hero's Cache", supposing that the treasure hidden in Kitano Bay may have belonged to the Hero who defeated the Calamity 10,000 years ago. Furthermore, at a Stable where he plays , Kass will inform Link that while the Song's origins are uncertain, his teacher the Court Poet believed the Ancient Hero used it to call to his Horse. After completing every Shrine of Light, Link is instructed to visit the Temple of Time, where he can receive the Ancient Hero's Aspect. When worn, it envelops Link in the aura of the hero's spirit and gives him the appearance of the Ancient Hero. The Ancient Hero is shown to be similar to a Zonai, with similar animalistic traits and Zonai markings and armor. However, his appearance still significantly differs from the two known Zonai, Rauru and Mineru, as he has green skin, shorter stature and ears, and a tail. Given this difference, the lack of knowledge about variation in the Zonai's appearance, and Ganondorf's claim that the other Zonai no longer exist in their world, it remains unclear if the Ancient Hero is actually a Zonai or related to them. The Ancient Hero's actual armor is also near-identical to the Zonaite Waistguard and Zonaite Shin Guards, though Hylians are seen wearing this type of clothing in the time of Rauru. If spoken to by Link when wearing the Ancient Hero's Aspect, several characters will recognize the Ancient Hero. Impa will be amused and note that Link appears similar to the figure on the Screen of the Ancient Hero; Purah will compliment Link but remark that she didn't recognize

of Rauru. If spoken to by Link when wearing the Ancient Hero's Aspect, several characters will recognize the Ancient Hero. Impa will be amused and note that Link appears similar to the figure on the Screen of the Ancient Hero; Purah will compliment Link but remark that she didn't recognize him at first; Tauro will believe the Ancient Hero had been resurrected, before realizing it was Link and wishing to try on the outfit; and Symin will inquire as to where Link found the clothing. At the Hateno School, Symin recounts the story of the Ancient Hero and the 10,000-year-old Great Calamity to the children of Hateno Village. Azu also has a comment about Link having shown the class "ancient hero getup", though this is tied to the lesson on the Calamity and not Link actually having worn the Ancient Hero's Aspect, appearing to be a mistranslation.

are recurring locations in . Ancient Hylian Ruins go unnamed in . Features and Overview Ancient Hylian Ruins are decrepit, typically small structures made of a light stone. They are considered Hylian cultural relics and were in ruins far before the Great Calamity. Some speculate that such ruins may have been built at a similar time to the sacred springs. Pillars within Ancient Hylian Ruins are often fluted, and floors have a distinct geometric pattern. Most ruins are located within the Hebra and Akkala Regions, though some are also found within Central Hyrule and Lanayru.
