is a location in . Ancient Hyrule goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Ancient Hyrule is the version of Hyrule that existed during the Era of Foundation. After cleansing the land from Demons, Rauru and Sonia founded Hyrule Kingdom atop the Great Plateau in Ancient Hyrule. They settled the Ancient Hyrule Castle at the base of Mount Hylia. They gathered support from the various tribes across the land, incorporating the Gorons, Hylians, Rito, and Zora into their Kingdom. Eventually, the Gerudo also swore fealty to the Kingdom under Ganondorf's rule. However, this was a ploy from Ganondorf to steal a Secret Stone and begin what would come to be known as the Imprisoning War to wrest control of the land for himself. thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of the Forgotten Temple's Floor Map.|The Floor Map depicting Ancient Hyrule's geography from The geography of Ancient Hyrule was slightly different to its present day counterpart. Notably, Central Hyrule featured several large lakes and bodies of Water which covered the land north of the Great Plateau. The Sacred Ground Ruins do not exist as a result of this. A gazebo used by the Royal Family of Hyrule was built in between the rivers surrounding Lake Kolomo. Certain landmarks such as the Bridge of Hylia are present, indicating their age. A ring of smoke encircled the peak of Death Mountain. Because Ancient Hyrule existed before the 10,000-Year-Old Calamity, the Hebra Peak remains intact with no damage, and the Dueling Peaks exist as a single mountain. The Fir River and Squabble River are both absent. The Forgotten Temple bore a different style of architecture and lacked its characteristic Mother Goddess Statue. At this point in history, Zora's Domain had not been settled by the Zora. The walls surrounding the Great Plateau are different in design, although ruined portions of the contemporary design used in the Era of the Wilds can still be seen. Shrines of Light stand in the spots where Ancient Shrines would eventually be built atop the Plateau, indicating that they were moved or deconstructed at some point. The Temple of Time atop the Great Plateau was raised into the Sky by Mineru following the Imprisoning War, and a structure that later came to be known as the Temple of Time Ruins was built in its place to fulfill religious purposes by the Kingdom. thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of Hylians atop the Great Plateau's outer wall.|The people of Ancient Hyrule from Hylians in this time period were heavily influenced by the Zonai and made use of Zonai Technology. They also featured much longer ears than their contemporary counterparts. Hylian Soldiers wore feathered headpieces and jewelry. They made use of Old Wooden Bows and Spears. Hylian men typically wore white togas and a covered the left side of their torsos with colored cloth that ended with triangular tassels which evoked the Triforce. Hylian women were shown wearing simplistic layered dresses. Other Appearances Ancient Hyrule is the setting for .

The Ancient Tree Stump is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Ancient Tree Stump is located in Hyrule Field. It is the remains of a giant, ancient Tree at the northern base of Mount Daphnes. A small village was situated at the roots of the Ancient Tree Stump, but it has since been submerged in an unnamed lake. A Garbage Dump now sits at the top of the Stump, which is connected to Mount Daphnes by a simple bridge. Creatures Enemies Equipment Korok Seeds As in , the Ancient Tree Stump is located just north of Mount Daphnes in Hyrule Field. Areas

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Ancient Tree Stump Cave's entrance is located at the center of the Ancient Tree Stump's top. Inside the Cave, there are several sprawling roots above a pool of Water. There are several small chambers along the walls of the Cave. The southernmost chamber at the base of the Cave is blocked by small roots that can be cut. Beyond these roots, there is a tall vertical chute where Misko hid their treasure. Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits can be found throughout the Cave. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests

The are a location in . Overview The Ancient Zora Waterworks are a Cave located at the bottom of East Reservoir Lake in the Lanayru Great Spring. After Mucktorok is defeated in the Water Temple, the Water will drain from the main chamber of the Ancient Zora Waterworks and reveal a tunnel at the bottom. Once the Main Quest "Restoring the Zora Armor" is complete, Yona will ask Link to investigate a rumor that the Zora Greaves can be found somewhere in the Waterworks. This begins the Side Quest "A Token of Friendship", which ends once Link explores the new tunnel and retrieves the Armor. Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Anly is a Hylian and the owner of the Lakeside Stable in West Necluda. He can be found at the front of Lakeside Stable. If Lakeside Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Anly will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Anly explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Anly then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Anly instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Anly suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Anly to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Anly tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Lakeside Stable, Anly will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Anly thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Anly will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Anly asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Lakeside Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Anly asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Anly will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Anly insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Anly refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Anly starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Anly gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will

Anly gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Anly gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside Lakeside Stable, Anly once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by Lakeside Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Anly tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Anly wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

The , designated by the trial name Wings on the Wind, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Apogek Shrine can be found on the southern edge of Ja'Abu Ridge in the Lanayru Great Spring. It corresponds to the Kegopa Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation The Shrine is a two-room traversal shrine built around the Wing. The first room sees Link using a Wing to move an Ancient Orb across a gap. The second room sees Link crossing a large gap using the wing. The Shrine has infinitely generating Wings and four Fans. Treasure Chests

Apples are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses In , Apples are a health-restoring item that can only be obtained by dashing into Trees with the Pegasus Shoes. Apples are also the answer to one of the Lumberjack's Riddles in . In , Apples are found growing on certain Trees scattered on the Overworld of Koholint Island. Link can perform a Dash Attack into these Trees to make them fall on the ground. He can then pick them up and eat them to restore some Hearts. In , Apples are found in the stalls of Hyrule Castle Town's South Road. However, Link cannot actually obtain or use them. In , Apples can recover one Heart. They can also be stored in Bottles by catching them with the Net. Next to Link's House, an Apple tree grows Apples with every StreetPass encounter, starting with three and reaching a maximum of 20. In , Apples are Materials that can be used in Cooking Food. This red fruit can be found growing on various trees throughout Hyrule. They're also sold by the General Shoppe and the travelling Merchant Gartan near Gerudo Town. Regular Hinox also drop Apples when defeated. Apples can be eaten fresh to heal half of a Heart. They can also be made into Baked Apples by exposing them to Fire, which heal three-quarters of a Heart. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Apples can be used to create Red Dye. During the Side Quest "Riddles of Hyrule", Walton will ask Link to bring him something small, red, round, and sweet. If Link drops an Apple on the leaf in front of Walton, he will cheer before moving on to the next riddle. Apples are required for the following Meals: They can also be used to make the following Meals: Apples can be found growing on Trees throughout Hyrule. They can also be found among Yiga supplies at Abandoned Mines in the Depths. A special variety of Apples known as Golden Apples may also appear on Trees. Apples and Golden Apples can be used interchangeably when Cooking. They are required for the following Meals: They can also be used for most Fruit-based Meals: Apples appear as Objects inside crates. They cannot be interacted with. Other Appearances left|50px The fifth puzzle in the How to Play Picross series depicts an Apple. Apples can be found by breaking Objects such as Wooden Boxes. They can be consumed to heal a Warrior's Life Gauge. There is an initial capacity limit of three Apples, though it is possible to increase this capacity to hold four Apples instead. If an Apple makes contact with Fire, it will turn into a Baked Apple, which heals more Hearts. Apples are Materials in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Apple Pies can be made in Cooking Pots by combining Tabantha Wheat, Cane Sugar, Goat Butter, and an Apple. Their flaky pie crusts and sweet Apples are thought by many people throughout Hyrule to be a match made in heaven. Misa's Recipe Book at the Slippery Falcon in Rito Village contains a recipe for Apple Pie. Misa first suggests buying Tabantha Wheat, Goat Butter, and Cane Sugar from the Slippery Falcon. She then tells the reader to cook them with an Apple until the crust is a flaky golden brown and the insides are gooey. Finally, she tells the reader they can substitute the Apple with another Ingredient for an added kick. Apple Pies made with the base recipe sell for 30 Rupees. However, they can sell for up to 70 Rupees depending on the additional Ingredient added. Eating a basic Apple Pie will restore three of Link's Hearts. They will restore four Hearts if an additional Apple is added, or five Hearts if another Tabantha Wheat is added. A fifth Ingredient can be added to Apple Pie, which will result in it having different effects: Chilly Apple Pie: They can be eaten to temporarily increase Link's Heat Resistance by one level. They also restore four of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 50 Rupees. Electro Apple Pie: Eating one will grant Link Shock Resistance for a short period of time. They also restore four of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 50 Rupees. Enduring Apple Pie: Eating one will completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. They also restore eight of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 50 Rupees. Energizing Apple Pie: Eating one will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. They also restore seven of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 50 Rupees. Hasty Apple Pie: They will grant Link a speed boost when they are eaten. They also restore four of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 70 Rupees. Hearty Apple Pie: They can be eaten to temporarily increase Link's maximum Hearts. They also fully restore all of Link's Hearts and sell for 60 Rupees. Mighty Apple Pie: When eaten, they will grant Link a small boost to his attack-power. They also restore five of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 50 Rupees. Spicy Apple Pie: Eating one will increase Link's Cold Resistance by one level. They also restore three of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 50 Rupees. Sneaky Apple Pie: Eating one will increase Link's Stealth. They also restore four of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 50 Rupees. Tough Apple Pie: If they are eaten, they will temporarily boost Link's Defense. They also restore four of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 50 Rupees. Apple Pie returns in , where it has a similar Recipe to the one it had in , which involves Cooking either an Apple or a Golden Apple alongside Cane Sugar, Goat

temporarily boost Link's Defense. They also restore four of Link's Hearts and can be sold for 50 Rupees. Apple Pie returns in , where it has a similar Recipe to the one it had in , which involves Cooking either an Apple or a Golden Apple alongside Cane Sugar, Goat Butter, and Tabantha Wheat in a Cooking Pot or Portable Pot.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Applean Forest is located in Hyrule Field. It is an Apple orchard located in a small field of flowers along the bank of the Hylia River. An unmarked road runs through the southern ends of the Forest, ending near the middle of the Forest's depths. Near the start of this road, skid marks from a wagon can be found leading off the trail to an edge. The remains of this wagon can be found atop the edge and can be searched for Materials. A second wagon can be found along the slope beneath the edge, near the base of a monster camp. A Blue Hinox rests in a clearing in the northeastern portion of the Applean Forest. In Master Mode, it is replaced with a Black Hinox. At the end of the unmarked road leading into the Applean Forest, Link can find three Apple Trees. Two of these Trees are identical, each bearing one Apple on branches facing the southeast, while the third bears five. Reducing the Apples on the third Tree so that it is identical to the other two will cause a Korok to appear. As thanks for finding him, the Korok will gift Link a Korok Seed. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Aquame Bridge spans over Aquame Lake in Hyrule Field, connecting the Coliseum Ruins to the main portion of Hyrule Field. In Master Mode, a wooden Treasure Chest containing a Sapphire can be found east of the Bridge atop a platform held aloft by Sky Octoroks. A metallic Treasure Chest containing a Knight's Shield can be found also atop a platform suspended by Sky Octoroks west of the Bridge. Hanging just under the bridge lies an archery Puzzle, disguised as a Jar shaped like an Acorn dangling from a chain. If Link breaks the Jar, the Korok will reveal itself and reward him with a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds

Aquame Lake is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Aquame Lake is located in Hyrule Field. It is fed by the Regencia River to the north and partly surrounds the Coliseum Ruins. A stone bridge, the Aquame Bridge, crosses over the Lake from the north and connects to the Coliseum Ruins. Close to the Lake's eastern shore are the ruins of a dilapidated village. In the waters near the point where the Regencia River meets Aquame Lake, Link can find a metallic Treasure Chest containing an Opal. A Korok can be found by lifting a Rock on the cliff just west of the Aquame Bridge. Creatures Enemies Aquame Lake is located in Hyrule Field. The Aquame Lake Well is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Aquame Lake Well is situated among a set of ruins along the eastern end of Aquame Lake in Hyrule Field. Before the Great Calamity, it was part of an unnamed Hylian settlement, which now consists of Ruined Houses. The Aquame Lake Well returns in , and it is still located east of Aquame Lake in Hyrule Field. The Well now has an interior chamber, which Link can access using a Ladder leaning against its rim. Inside the Aquame Lake Well is a Traveler equipped with a Traveler's Sword and a Hunter's Shield. They are practicing fighting against a Dummy that has Arrows and Weapons stuck into it, counting as they do so. If Link asks them why they are counting, they claim that they are tallying the grievances they have against an individual who has defeated many of their brethren in combat. Alternatively, if Link requests to count with them, the Traveler says doing so would be difficult, before telling the same story about the harm their family has been subjected to. In either scenario, they identify Link as the individual responsible, at which point they reveal themself to be a Yiga Footsoldier and attack. During future interactions, the Traveler will battle Link immediately after being spoken to. Creatures Enemies Equipment Materials

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Arbiter's Grounds are a sparse group of Gerudo Ruins in the southern part of the Gerudo Desert. A majority of the ruins are buried beneath the Sand, but their architectural style indicates they were created by the Gerudo. What can be seen are the remains of several doorways and walls, some of which have scaffolding or a Ladder appended to their sides. At the center of the Arbiter's Grounds is a natural rock formation, at the base of which are Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits. Due to the intense Heat in the area, Link requires at least two levels of Heat Resistance in order to traverse the Grounds without taking damage. At night, Link needs two levels of Cold Resistance, since the Gerudo Desert becomes a Freezing Climate. Among the Arbiter's Grounds, a Molduga swims through the Sand. Link can stand on the ruins to avoid its detection. If it senses Link is nearby, it will rush towards him and attack. left|40px A single Korok Seed Puzzle can be found at the Arbiter's Grounds. On top of the natural rock formation at their center, Link will find a Rock. If he picks it up, it will be revealed as a Natural Hiding Spot. A Korok will then appear and give Link a Korok Seed as a reward. Creatures Materials

is a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Archery goes unnamed in Location and Uses In both and , Archery refers to three different types of Korok Seed Puzzles. The first are Hidden Balloons, which are lone Balloons located in hard-to-reach spots. The second is Pinwheels & Balloons, which summon a group of Balloons for Link to shoot when he stands next to a Pinwheel. The last type involves Acorn Jars, which Link must shoot as well. There are also Archery puzzles that do not fall into any of these three categories, where a unique or out-of-place Item or Object is intended to be shot. Whenever Link solves one of these puzzles, a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed.

Ardi is a recurring character in . Biography In the ancient past, Ardi was the Sage of Lightning and a leader of the Gerudo. After the Chief of the Gerudo, Ganondorf, transformed into the Demon King, she allied herself with the first King of Hyrule, Rauru, to oppose him. In the Forgotten Temple, Rauru entrusted the remaining Secret Stones to Ardi, Agraston, Qia, and Raphica, strengthening them before the battle against Demon King Ganondorf. Ardi's became a Secret Stone of Lightning. As one of the Six Sages, she swore a vow of loyalty to Rauru. thumb|left|320px|alt= Ardi in a flashback.|Ardi during the Imprisoning War from Ardi fought in the Imprisoning War alongside Rauru and her fellow Sages. She wielded the Arms of the Seven, which consist of Daybreaker and the Scimitar of the Seven. During "The Imprisoning War" Memory, she appears weakened by Demon King Ganondorf's Gloom. To distract the Demon King, she throws her Scimitar of the Seven towards him, which Zelda sends backwards using Recall. Ardi was then a witness to Rauru sacrificing himself to seal Demon King Ganondorf. Following the Imprisoning War, Zelda came to visit Ardi at the Lightning Temple. She revealed that Demon King Ganondorf would one day break from his seal, and she asked Ardi to ensure the Gerudo will help Link defeat him. Feeling guilty that the Gerudo brought Ganondorf into the world, Ardi promised that her successor would awaken to fight with Link. In the "Tears of the Dragon" Memory, Ardi and the remaining Sages can be seen watching as the Light Dragon flies into the Sky. During the "Riju of Gerudo Town" Main Quest, Riju and Link repeatedly hear a voice calling to them from somewhere in the Gerudo Desert. This reminds Riju of the Mural in the Underground Shelter, which states that the owner of the voice is awaiting them. Inside the Lightning Temple, they again hear Ardi's voice, who directs them to activate the Temple's four Batteries to reach the Lightning Temple 7F. After defeating Queen Gibdo, Link and Riju will be able to access the Secret Stone on the Lightning Temple 7F. When Riju touches the Secret Stone, the two will be engulfed in Light, and Ardi will appear before them. She reveals that she is Riju's distant ancestor, using her Lightning to serve the King of Hyrule. She expresses her pride in Riju's Power of Lightning, and she claims that Queen Gibdo was summoned by Demon King Ganondorf to prevent Riju from finding her Secret Stone. Riju reacts with confusion, which prompts Ardi to recount the Imprisoning War and her promise to Zelda. Following her story, Ardi states that Demon King Ganondorf is still a threat, and she asks Riju to face him alongside Link. When Ardi disappears, Riju states that fighting the Demon King sounds fun, and she accepts the Secret Stone and her new role as a Sage. Other Appearances thumb|right|320px|alt= Closeup of Ardi's face.|Ardi from Ardi is a benevolent Gerudo warrior clad in green.

She follows Ganondorf according to the ancient Gerudo tradition which recognizes him as their leader. is a recurring character in . Biography Ardin is a Gerudo who manages a Stall in Gerudo Town. Her Stall specializes in Mushrooms. If spoken to, Ardin will tell Link that Gerudo use Mushrooms to keep their skin beautiful. Depending on the time of day, she will also remark that Link has a lot of energy being awake this early, if spoken to in the morning, or she will comment on the Temperature if spoken to around noon or in the evening. As a Merchant, Ardin is very keen to sell her wares, with her tactics ranging from persuasion to telling tall and implausible lies in order to make some money. If Link purchases all of the Mushrooms from her stall she will pretend her stall is full of rare and mysterious Mushrooms, that are only visible to the most beautiful. If Link talks to her about this, she will admit that after he bought all her Mushrooms she had nothing left to restock her stall with, but she think people will fall for this. However, she promises to restock her Mushrooms soon. She does in fact manage to convince both Jules and Nellie, although the latter requires Link’s help. Despite her trickery, Ardin is genuinely interested in Mushrooms and will tell Link facts about them, such as that they enjoy the cool weather. She encourages Link to take an interest in them despite not being an expert herself, quietly admitting that although there is lots of interesting information about mushrooms she does not understand a lot of it. When Link makes a purchase from Ardin, she may encourage him to use the nearby kitchen for Cooking. She might also tell him to eat a lot of Food so he can grow big. Like other Merchants, Link can sell his own Items to Ardin. When she buys an Item from Link, Ardin will thank him.

is a recurring character in . Biography Ariane is a Stable Worker at Rito Stable, just outside of Rito Village. During the day, she will sweep the ground in front of the Stable, and she will sit inside at night. On sunny mornings, she greets Link and says that the Weather looks nice. When spoken to, Ariane will ask Link if he needs a Bed. If Link says he does, she directs him to Galli at the counter. If Link does not want a Bed, Ariane will appear disappointed. Link can also ask her where he is, and she will ask if he is lost, saying he is at Rito Stable and explaining the services they can provide. She will also reveal that the Stable's name comes from the Rito, who live nearby. Due to the Extreme Cold Snap in Hebra, Rito Stable was closed, resulting in Ariane coming to work at New Serenne Stable. On occasion, she accidentally refers to New Serenne Stable by the wrong name. When Link talks to her, she gives him a Spicy Elixir, as she does not need it anymore. She also complains during Rain.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Aris Beach is located along the Necluda Sea in East Necluda. It is south of Ubota Point and North Aris Beach. In Lurelin Village, Link can receive the "Take Back the Sea" Side Quest. Sebasto explains that Monsters have taken over many of the Village's best fishing spots, including Aris Beach. Since Link appears tough, he asks him to clear out the Monsters. The Monster Stronghold he is referring to is located just off the eastern coast of Aris Beach. The Monsters that inhabit it are Bokoblins, Blue Bokoblins, a Black Bokoblin, and a Blue Moblin. To access it, Link can either Swim or take the Raft that can be found on the Clarnet Coast. After all of the Monsters have been defeated, Link will be able to access the Stronghold's Treasure Chest, which contains a Knight's Halberd. Sebasto will reward Link with a Silver Rupee for completing his request. A smaller Monster Stronghold can be found on the western end of Aris Beach, consisting of a Lizalfos and two Blue Lizalfos. The Campfire here has four Boko Spears staked into the ground surrounding it, three of which bear Roasted Basses. The Treasure Chest at this Stronghold contains five Bomb Arrows. Several other Treasure Chests can be found in the sand and waters surrounding Aris Beach. The contents of these Chests are a Sapphire, two Topazes, a Giant Boomerang, a Soldier's Broadsword, and a Silver Rupee. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

Armes is a recurring character in . Biography Armes is a Hylian resident of Lurelin Village, who can be seen carrying a Boat Oar. He resides in his House on the eastern side of the Village. He is a fisherman, but he claims that he is unable to go fishing when it Rains. This is due to the strength of the Wind making it difficult to control Boats. During such times, he says all he can do is gamble at Cloyne's Lucky Treasure Shop. On days with sunny Weather, Armes can be found at the Campfire on the beach near the Merchant Boat. He will tell Link that the Fish roasting there look delicious, explaining that he is the one who caught them. If Link speaks to him after examining the Fish, Armes will allow Link to take some, stating that he Cooked too many for himself. Afterward, he asks Link if he enjoyed the Fish. Should Link say yes, Armes states that they are the pride of Lurelin Village. Armes will also ask Link if he has ever been sailing on a Raft. If Link replies that he has not, Armes explains that the Wind direction is critical to controlling a Raft. He also reveals he heard of an Item called a Korok Leaf that can help people control the Wind. If Link says he has sailed a Raft before, Armes comments that he never would have guessed based on his appearance. He reminds Link to be careful at sea, as the Wind can leave one stranded quickly.

are recurring Items in . Armors go unnamed in . They are pieces of Clothing and protective covering that Link can wear. Location and Uses Suits of Armor can be found in Hyrule Castle. They are equipped with Spears. Armor serves a variety of purposes, primarily to provide Link with defensive padding, allowing him to endure more damage. Damage numbers are shown numerically in , albeit indirectly. Each unit of damage normally deals a quarter of a Heart to Link. For example, an attack with a power of 4 will damage Link by one full Heart. By wearing Armor, Link can decrease the amount of damage he takes. Each piece of Armor has a numeric rating that contributes to Link's overall Defense. The higher Link's Defense, the less damage he will take from Enemy attacks. Wearing Armor subtracts the attack's strength value by Link's total defense value. Wearing Armor with a defense rating greater than or equal to the strength of the attack will reduce that damage to a quarter of a Heart, and no matter his defense, Link takes at least a quarter of a Heart of damage from any attack. Armors often pair with other pieces to form Armor Sets. Certain pieces of Armor also provide Added Effects that can boost Link's attack, movement speed on Snow, Sand, through Water, or while Climbing, boost his stealth capabilities, or protect him from the environment. Environmental hazards include Lightning, Fire, heat, Ice, and the cold. Most clothing can be enhanced up to four times by the revived Great Fairies, with the number of available upgrades dependent on how many Great Fairies have been restored. Each upgrade comes with a certain cost of Materials. Armor Sets that have been enhanced at least twice may provide Set Bonuses. If Link has no Armor on, some characters make a passing comment or directly acknowledge this. Extra pieces of Armor were added in the Expansion Pass DLC, and some pieces can also be gained by scanning certain amiibo on the Wii U and Nintendo Switch consoles. There are 107 pieces of Armor available to collect overall, of which Link can carry a maximum of 100 pieces in his Inventory at any one time. Armor and damage calculations to Link works the same way as it did in . However, the Strength of Weapons used against Link is now calculated differently.

They can typically be found in major settlements across Hyrule Kingdom. Certain merchants and Jewelry Shops such as Starlight Memories may also sell Armor, but they do not qualify as Armor Shops. Armor Shops usually sell specific Armor Sets, such as Ripped and Shredded, which sells the Fireproof Armor. List of Armor Shops Merchants who sell Armor Some Hylians will also sell Link Armor directly, even though they do not appear on the Sheikah Slate's Map. In , all Armor Shops remain except for the Rhondson Armor Boutique, as Rhondson has gone on to co-operate Hudson Construction instead. Fashion Passion has been relocated to the Kara Kara Bazaar and the Ventest Clothing Boutique has been taken over by Sophie's sister Cece, but the Shops are otherwise mostly unchanged. List of Armor Shops Merchants who sell Armor In there are still individual Merchants selling Armor pieces.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Armoranths grow on Hyrule Ridge and in the Akkala Highlands. They are plentiful near Mija's Great Fairy Fountain, which is located outside of Tarrey Town. When an Armoranth is Cooked into a Meal in a Cooking Pot, the resulting dish will grant Link Defense Up when eaten, which increases his defense. Armoranths can be roasted by a Fire to create Roasted Armoranths. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Link can use Armoranths to create Purple Dye. In order to start the "Little Sister's Big Request" Side Quest, Link must find common ground with Jana, or else she will not speak to him. If he has an Armoranth, Jana will notice and ask for it. If Link gives it to her, she will state that it is her favorite plant and that she may get along with him after all. Like other Flowers, Armoranths can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Like other Flowers, Armoranths can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Other Appearances Armoranths can be sold for five Rupees.

Large deposits of calcium within their scales cause them to be as hard as armor. Because of this, Cooking them into a dish will grant the consumer a boosted defense. Once caught, they can be eaten raw to heal one Heart, or they can be cooked into Roasted Carp or frozen into Frozen Carp. The , also known as the , are recurring Items in . The Arms of the Seven go unnamed in . Location and Uses The Champion's Arms refer to the pairing of Scimitars of the Seven and Daybreakers. Both pieces belong to the Gerudo Gear archetype. Prior to the Great Calamity, which occurred 100 years before the events of , the Gerudo Champion Urbosa wielded a pair of Champion's Arms. After she was killed by Thunderblight Ganon, her Arms became heirlooms to the Gerudo, and they eventually ended up in the possession of Riju. During the EX Recovered Memory "Champion Urbosa's Song", Urbosa uses her Champion's Arms to defend Zelda against a pair of Yiga Footsoldiers. When Link returns to Gerudo Town after reclaiming Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Riju gives him Urbosa's Champion's Arms as a reward for saving the Gerudo. If either the Scimitar of the Seven or Daybreaker are ever broken, Buliara will be able to create new ones for Link. In , it is revealed that the Arms of the Seven can only be created for chosen individuals. Sometime prior to the start of the Upheaval, Isha chose to make the Arms for Riju. An ancestor of hers was also responsible of making those that belonged to Urbosa. In addition, the former Sage of Lightning Ardi can be seen wielding the Arms of the Seven during flashbacks to the Imprisoning War. According to Isha, the Arms of the Seven create a bond with their owner, and they can only be remade if it is impossible to recover them. As part of the Side Quest "Pride of the Gerudo", Isha chooses to make a new set of Arms of the Seven for Link. She tasks Link with gathering the supplies to create the Arms, since that is the responsibility of the one who will wield them. Once Link brings her the Materials, she will be able to make the Arms for him. Should Link break either the Scimitar of the Seven or the Daybreaker, Isha will be able to make a new one for him. Other Appearances Urbosa's default Weapon, a Scimitar of the Seven, is paired with a Daybreaker when equipped. Ardi can be seen wielding the Arms of the Seven.

The is a recurring General Store in . Features and Overview The Arrow Specialty Shop is a Stall located between the Royal Palace and Hotel Oasis in Gerudo Town. It is run by Danda, who claims to have the best selection of Arrows available. One of Danda's granddaughters, Kalani, advertises the different Arrows available to travelers. She also makes recommendations as to which Arrows to make use of. At night, both Kalani and Makure sleep beside their grandmother at the Arrow Specialty Shop. When Link makes a purchase at the Arrow Specialty Shop, Danda will ask Link if he is pleased with her Arrows. If Link buys the entire stock of a single Arrow type, Danda will consider him to be strange. Lastly, should Link buy all of the Arrows at the Arrow Specialty Shop, Danda will promise to restock soon. When spoken to afterwards, Danda claims no one has ever bought so many Arrows before, and she plans to use the proceeds to purchase new toys for Kalani and Makure. is a recurring ability in . Overview Ascend is an Ancient Power that Link can use while underneath terrain or buildings so long as the targeted surfaces of both where Link enters and exit are relatively flat, he is close enough to the surface where he enters, and nothing would obstruct him on the other side. This is indicated via the portal turning green. When Link uses the ability, he will rise upward through the material above him and appear on the other side. During this sequence, everything else will freeze. Ascend can be used to quickly gain altitude or escape from dangerous situations. Link will have an opportunity to confirm if he wishes to Ascend through an Object after seeing what is on the other side of the selected Object. However, he will automatically complete the ascent after 30 seconds. If the view of Link becomes obstructed while he Ascends, the world around him will render as a green void, similar to being inside of a Shrine of Light. This will also happen if the area where Link will appear needs to be loaded. Climbable Bosses, such as Stone Taluses and Marbled Gohmas, can be Ascended through. In the Depths, Ascend Access Points can be found, which will take Link to the Surface when he Ascends through them. Link can also ascend to the surface from the alcove in the Deku Tree Chasm. Link cannot Ascend anywhere else in the Depths to the Surface. Other Appearances During the Movie "Fated Adversary", which plays at the beginning of the Scenario "The Counterstrike", Rauru reveals his plan to ambush the Monsters in the Seres Scablands. Agraston asks if he will be using a Zonai ability, which Rauru confirms. He then directs the Six Sages to make for a Cave system nearby, so they can launch their attack from beneath the Monsters. Once the Scenario starts, Rauru can be seen Ascending through the ground holding Agraston and Qia's hands. Upon exiting the ground, they are able to take a Fire Boss Bokoblin and its Black Bokoblin followers by surprise.

are locations in . Features and Overview Ascend Access Points are Zonai Ruins found throughout the Depths. There are sixteen Ascend Access Points in total. Each Ascend Access Point consists of a slightly raised square stone platform with stairs on each side leading up to it. On each corner, there is a pillar with a light source on top. In the middle of the platform, there is a pile of Sand, which is patterned with concentric circles in a manner similar to that seen in a Zen garden. Above the platform, there is a large stonework pillar that makes up the majority of the structure. Each edge of the pillar is decorated with light sources and a depiction of Dragons, with the heads of the Dragons ending at the wider base of the pillar. The pillar extends upward into the ceiling of the Depths, through any terrain that may be in the way. On the bottom face of the pillar is a design of concentric circles, with Zonai runes in the center. Each Ascend Access Point is also rotated so their sides are aligned with the cardinal directions, with the exception of the one in Korok Grove. The primary purpose of Ascend Access Points is to function as locations where Link can use Ascend to leave the Depths and reach the Surface. This is because using Ascend to pass through the ceiling of the Depths is blocked everywhere else, except at the bottom of the Deku Tree Chasm. Utilizing the Ascend Access Point within Korok Grove is also the only method of reaching Korok Forest for the first time. When Link uses Ascend at the majority of the Ascend Access Points, he will emerge at a location on the Surface within eyesight of a Geoglyph. Ascend Access Point Locations

is a recurring location in . Ash Swamp goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Ash Swamp is located in West Necluda. Like the adjacent Blatchery Plain, Ash Swamp is composed of generally flat land with tall Grass and ruined buildings. During the second Great Calamity, Guardians made their way through Ash Swamp on their way to Fort Hateno. After Link fell in battle to a Guardian in Ash Swamp, Zelda's powers awoke and she destroyed most of the surrounding Guardians. Consequently, several Fallen Guardians litter the Plain and can be searched for Ancient Materials. The events of the Great Calamity can be retrieved in the final Recovered Memory, "Zelda's Awakening", near the southern part of the Swamp. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests Ash Swamp reappears in . The Fallen Guardians littering the Swamp have been cleared. Numerous damaged Trees and Logs can be found surrounding the Water, and it is still covered in ruins. Large Boulders are scattered across the Swamp. Ruins Rubble occasionally fall from the Sky onto the area. An encampment of Constructs can be found next to the northern pond amongst some Fallen Debris. Addison can be found holding up a Sign on a small rock formation in the south of the Swamp. If Link props up the Sign so that it can stand up on its own, Addison will reward him with a Red Rupee, Sneaky Mushroom Rice Balls, and a Bomb Flower. Creatures Enemies Materials Zonai Devices Treasure Chests Korok Seeds Other Appearances Ash Swamp appears as part of the Fort Hateno Stage. During the "Across Time" Movie, Zelda can be seen awakening her sealing powers to save Link from a Guardian. During this time, she wishes to protect everyone.

is a recurring character in . Biography Ashai is a Gerudo who lives in Gerudo Town and teaches two classes to young girls before they depart from Gerudo Town. In the past, she and Isha were involved in a love triangle with Aurie Taamu, though both of them remained single in the end. If Link speaks to Ashai while she is walking through Gerudo Town, she introduces herself and asks Link if he is interested in taking her class, "Voe and You". Ashai explains that she teaches a relationship class during the day and a Cooking Class at night. Ashai encourages Link to attend the Cooking Class at her home during the night and her relationship class in the barracks during the day. When speaking to Ashai in the Relationship Classroom before "Voe and You" begins, she asks if Link is interested in sitting in. She then assures Link that there is no hurry and that class does not begin until everyone arrives. If Link speaks to Ashai during her relationship class, she invites Link to observe if he is interested. If Link rejects her offer, Ashai asks if Link already has a loved one, to which Link scratches the back of his head in embarrassment. Ashai then explains that the young girls in her class have never even met a man before and that it is her duty to prepare them for the world outside of Gerudo Town. Should Link agree to observe the class, Ashai instructs everyone to demonstrate what they have been learning. Ashai then asks the class what to do when a "handsome voe" approaches them on the street. Pasha stands up and answers that she would wave casually yet remain prepared in case he is a distraction for a bandit ambush. Ashai praises Pasha for her solution and then reminds the class that sometimes men only look suspicious from being intimidated by a Gerudo. Dina then stands up to share her solution, saying that she would enthusiastically greet the man and approach with her hands empty. Ashai praises Dina for her optimistic approach, adding that friendliness is a great way to relax others. Lastly, Risa stands to share her solution, saying that she would attack the man when he least suspects it. Ashai dismisses Risa's solution and tells her that it is a crime. Ashai also asks her students what they would do if they encountered an injured voe lying on the ground. Pasha responds that she will lift him over her shoulder and take him to the nearest person who can treat him. Ashai will praise this answer, but she will remind Pasha to check for non-visible injuries before she moves someone. Next, Dina says she would figure out what is wrong with him and then make a medicine to treat him. Once again, Ashai will say Dina has a great answer, but she tells her to make sure he does not have any allergies to the ingredients she uses. Finally, Risa will say

says she would figure out what is wrong with him and then make a medicine to treat him. Once again, Ashai will say Dina has a great answer, but she tells her to make sure he does not have any allergies to the ingredients she uses. Finally, Risa will say that she would secretly take the voe back to her home, where she would help him recover. Ashai says that while Risa's sentiment is sweet, her plan is basically kidnapping. For her third question, Ashai asks her students what they will do when they are approached and spoken to by a voe whose attention they have sought. Pasha says she would pretend not to speak his language. Ashai comments that her approach is interesting since it could inspire curiosity, and she explains it is unrealistic that he will know the language she pretends to. Dina claims she will take the opportunity to examine his clothes to determine his social status. Ashai commends Dina on her good thinking, but reminds her that sometimes, if someone's nice clothes are dirty, they may wear something more casual. Lastly, Risa says she would grab his hand and twist his wrist until he agreed to marry her. Ashai is left without words, and she tells Risa to speak to her after class. Before her Cooking Class begins, she tells Link one might as well learn if there is more to learn. If Link agrees with her, she comments on Link's innocent expression. Ashai also explains to Link that she was planning a lesson on Creamy Heart Soup, but she forgot the name of the heart-shaped vegetable in the Recipe. Ashai assures herself that she will remember eventually.

is a recurring character in . Biography Ashe is an old man who works at the Woodland Stable. During the day, he watches over the Stable's White Goats in their pen. At night, he can be found looking over his grandchild Shamae as she sleeps. When Link speaks to him, he'll identify he's not from the area due to the look on his face. He assists new travelers by telling them about the surrounding areas and giving directions to them, including the Eldin Region, Hyrule Field and the Great Hyrule Forest. If Link asks, Ashe will tell him about Eldin, describing Death Mountain at its center. He tells Link that one can see the back of Death Mountain from the stable. Though he doesn't know why anyone would do so, he recommends climbing to the Maw of Death Mountain from Foothill Stable in Akkala. He also recommends Link figures out how to deal with the Scorching Climate before he heads up. Ashe also talks about Hyrule Field, saying it's just south of the stable past Crenel Hills. He describes it as a beautiful place to live with no shortage of nature. He mentions Hyrule Castle Town and Hyrule Castle are both north of the field, and they used to be the center of culture or commerce in Hyrule. However, he warns Link to stay away from both the castle and the field, as he considers both to be dangerous. Ashe says he's sure Link has a family who cares about him, and he's seen too many people head into Hyrule Field and never come back. When asked about the Great Hyrule Forest, Ashe will indicate that it's north of the stable, and it's the largest forest in Hyrule. He recounts a time where he had left to gather firewood at the Lost Woods as a young boy. He remembers venturing deep into the Woods when the wind suddenly started blowing in several directions. He ran away then, only to find himself outside the Woods as the fog lifted. He believes that there is something dangerous in the Lost Woods and warns Link to stay away. His story is actually a clue to navigating the Lost Woods, by following the wind's direction. still resides at Woodland Stable in . During the day, he can be found standing next to the Signboard across the road from the Stable. When Link speaks to Ashe, he will greet him. Assuming that Link is heading to Goron City, Ashe warns him to avoid any Gorons with Marbled Rock Roast. If Link asks about his wording, Ashe reveals that he directed another traveler to the Bedrock Bistro along the New Road, but he has not returned yet. If Link asks about Marbled Rock Roasts, Ashe explains that travelers have been attacked by Gorons who were holding them. At the end of their conversation, he claims it is Woodland Stable's duty to keep its guests safe, and he invites Link to return if he is ever in

yet. If Link asks about Marbled Rock Roasts, Ashe explains that travelers have been attacked by Gorons who were holding them. At the end of their conversation, he claims it is Woodland Stable's duty to keep its guests safe, and he invites Link to return if he is ever in trouble.

is a recurring character in . Biography Aster is a young Hylian girl who resides in Hateno Village with her father, Medda. She is usually found running about in front of The Great Ton Pu Inn, laughing to herself. Aster is a big fan of the Bolson Construction dance, and she will ask Link if he knows it. Link can claim to recognize it and please the child, or he can admit that he does not know it and allow her to teach it to him. If Link speaks to her again later, he can ask about either Bolson himself or the dance. Aster will tell the hero that Bolson is a carpenter and how he can find him behind the East Wind. Apparently, Bolson is also a "luminary in his field," but Aster does not fully understand that title. She also says she heard he was a construction company, but she is not sure how that is possible. In addition, Aster may share she heard that Bolson is a famous president or designer. No matter what she says, Aster will direct Link to Bolson so he can see the dance for himself. Asking about the dance will prompt Aster to demonstrate it to Link. However, telling her to stop will upset Aster, and she will call him lame. When it Rains, Aster will run to the nearby Shared Cooking Space and pretend to Cook. She plays with a mound of material as though kneading it like dough. At 8:00 PM, Aster goes home to go to bed. She will also remark that if she does not get home soon, she will get in trouble. As she sleeps, she dreams about her absent mother. Should Link approach Aster with a Torch lit by the Blue Flame, she will excitedly follow him around, commenting on how pretty the Flame is. Aster is a resident of Hateno Village.

is a character in . Biography Atmus is a Hylian who works in Lookout Landing. He can be found in front of the large Map in the Emergency Shelter, where he helps manage the deployment of the Monster-Control Crew. He is an expert in Hyrule's geography, including the different peoples and settlements. When Link first approaches Atmus, he apologizes for not noticing him sooner, since he tends to focus on his Map. He then asks Link if he is interested in his research, explaining that it comes from examining Maps while out with the Monster-Control Crew. If Link asks about the peoples of Hyrule, Atmus reveals that they are the Hylians, the Rito, the Gorons, the Zora, and the Gerudo, all of whom live in their own Region and bear unique traits. He also mentions the Sheikah, who are known for their wisdom. Should Link ask about the settlements of Hyrule, Atmus uses his Map point out Lookout Landing, Rito Village, Gerudo Town, Goron City, Tarrey Town, Zora's Domain, Kakariko Village, Hateno Village, and Lurelin Village. He then reveals that many of them have been suffering the effects of the Upheaval, and he hopes that the Monster-Control Crew will be able to help them. Lastly, if Link asks about Atmus himself, Atmus explains that since he is not skilled with combat, he helps the Monster-Control Crew figure out where they should be deployed. At the end of their conversation, Atmus warns Link about new types of Monsters that have been sighted.

It has a maximum potency of level three. In , the following Materials and Armor pieces grant Attack Up: In , the Attack Up Effect now applies twice multiplicatively to thrown Weapons. This means that with a level three Attack Up Effect active, instead of a thrown Weapon dealing 1.5x damage against Enemies, it will deal 2.25x damage. Features and Overview thumb|right|alt= A screenshot of Ganondorf kneeling to Rauru.|Ganondorf swearing fealty to Rauru The Audience Chamber is a room within the Ancient Hyrule Castle atop Ancient Hyrule's Great Plateau. It is where the Zonai king Rauru receives guests and hears appeals from the people of Hyrule. The Audience Chamber is divided into two levels. The top level features mezzanines that flank the central hall to the east and west while the bottom level features a pathway to a pair of Thrones that face north. Beneath the mezzanines at each side of the pathway, there are side chambers that house dining tables. A Stained Glass window featuring an abstract design sits along the wall just above the Thrones. This window is complemented by deep blue cloth banners which in turn hang beneath a smaller Stained Glass window of a lotus. The entrance to the north and the central walkway are guarded by a detail of 12 Hylian Soldiers. thumb|right|alt= A screenshot of Ganondorf kneeling to Rauru.|Ganondorf swearing fealty to Rauru Ganondorf visits the Audience Chamber after his attempted assault on Hyrule Kingdom is thwarted through the combined efforts of Rauru, Sonia, and Zelda. Here, he falsely swears loyalty to the Kingdom as he plots to steal one of the Kingdom's treasured Secret Stones. Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . He does not ever actually appear in either game, but is detailed through his own writings and descriptions by other characters. Biography Aurie Taamu is a famous chef and the author of Chef Aurie Taamu, Vol. 1 and Chef Aurie Taamu, Vol. 2, which are studied in the cookery class held by Ashai. At some point after he was 35, Aurie Taamu's first book was published, documenting his knowledge of Cooking Meals with special effects, Elixirs and Fairies. His second book was published an unknown period of time later and expanded on his knowledge of Cooking special effects, as well as covering Monster Extract and Cooking for monetary gain. In this book he also explained that he learnt all he knew from someone he described as a dear friend, although he was unable to recall the person's name. During his life, Aurie Taamu was involved in a love triangle involving Ashai and Isha. It is unknown exactly what happened between the three of them, except that it ended badly and that both Ashai and Isha remain single to this day. Not much else is known about Aurie Taamu, other than that he went to bed early, was afraid of Insects, and considered himself to be a pure soul. He was, by his own admission, an impatient man and always kept some hasty foods on hand as a result. Notes left by Aurie Taamu can be found in Wells across Hyrule. Like his books, each one gives different tips and advice in regards to Cooking Meals with special effects. Following the Upheaval, he became interested in the many new Caves that opened across Hyrule. At some point, he ended up in the Carok Bridge Well, where he seems to have been stuck for an unknown period of time. However, his note explains that he actually found it quite comfortable in there thanks to the stable Temperature. His note in the Tabahl Woods Well distinguishes Materials dropped from Construct Enemies from regular Monster Parts, detailing that they are inedible even if made into Elixirs.

is a recurring ability in . Location and Uses Autobuild is an Ancient Power that Link can use with his Right Arm, which can be found in the Great Abandoned Central Mine. It allows Link to generate Objects constructed with Ultrahand automatically, expending Zonaite should the component parts needed to build the Object not be available in his nearby surroundings. Creations constructed with Autobuild using Zonaite rather than existing Objects can be identified by their uniquely green appearance, showing that they were created synthetically. Objects built using Zonaite will be destroyed if detached from the rest of the creation. Creations made using Autobuild can be built based on the most recently constructed Objects Link has made. Alternatively, they can be made using pre-built Schematics from Schema Stones and Yiga Schematics. While older designs will automatically be cleared from Autobuild's memory as Link creates new Objects, Link can designate a design as a Favorite to prevent it from being erased and make it more easily accessible. Up to eight Favorites can be saved in this fashion. Other Appearances During combat, Mineru uses Autobuild to summon designs made using Zonai Devices and other pieces of Zonai Technology. This can be done rapidly as she fights Enemies during her regular attacks and Strong Attacks. Her Unique Skills Construct Launch, Spherical Strike, and Repelling Gust also utilize Autobuild creations. Mineru uses Autobuild to summon Small Wheels and a large Iron Ball during her default Sync Strikes. In her Sync Strike with Rauru, she creates Autobuild duplicates of Rauru's Spear of Light. Lastly, she outfits the Knight Construct with Zonai Devices during their Sync Strike.

Axes are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Axes are exclusively used by various type of Dairas; Orange Dairas slash with their axe and Red Dairas throw their Axes. All Axes cannot be blocked by Link's Magic Shield, unless the Reflect Spell is cast. Large, two handed Axes are wielded by Iron Knuckles. Attacks from the Iron Knuckle's Axe take off four Hearts from Link and can destroy pillars. Hand Axes with a crescent shaped blade are wielded by Dinolfos. The King Bulblin wields a massive two handed Axe. Dynalfos wield hand Axes in tandem with steel Shields, both decorated with Eye Symbols. In , five different kinds of Axe Weapons appear throughout Hyrule. These include the Woodcutter's Axe, the Ancient Battle Axe, the Ancient Battle Axe+, the Ancient Battle Axe++, and the Double Axe. Axes are One-Handed and Two-Handed Weapons that can be made by Fusing sharp Materials or Objects onto One-Handed or Two-Handed Weapons. Axes are Weapons wielded by Darknuts. How they are used differs based on the type of Darknut wielding them; while regular Darknuts wield a single-bladed Axe used only for slashing attacks, Darknuts Lv. 2 and Lv. 3 both wield double-bladed Axes that they can perform spin attacks with. The Axes wielded by standard Darknuts have a burgundy handle and a gray blade, those wielded by their Lv. 2 counterparts have a gold handle with silver blades, and the Axes of Darknuts Lv. 3 have a blue handle and gold blades. Non-interactable Axes can be found in the environment at locations such as Link's House. Axes of this variety cannot be Learned by Zelda as an Echo. Other Appearances In , the spell Short Axe throws a small Axe. In , both a Double-Sided Axe and Battle Axe appear as Items. In , Destructor Axes can be found dropped by Axe Oinkers.

is a recurring character in . Biography Axyl is a Goron child who resides at the Southern Mine in the Eldin Canyon. While the adult Gorons work during the day, Axyl will roll around the Mine's Pickaxe statue, in which he is joined by Pelison before the latter leaves for Tarrey Town. At night, he mumbles in his sleep about his father, Dorill, and not being able to eat another bite. When Link first approaches Axyl, he will be scared to see a Hylian in the are. Link then asks why, and Axyl explains that there are Magma Bombs falling further up the Mountain Road. If Link informs Axyl of his plans to continue on to Goron City and up Death Mountain, Axyl tries to convince him not to, warning him of the intensity of the Scorching Climate there. If Link acts ignorant to the danger, Axyl reminds him that they should listen to adults, since they know what is best. After Divine Beast Vah Rudania has been calmed, Axyl will ask Link if he has been to Goron City. If Link confirms that he has, Axyl becomes dismissive and end their conversation. However, if Link claims he has not been there, Axyl encourages him to dig up Gems on the far end of Death Mountain Summit, though he tells him to keep it a secret.

is a recurring character in . Biography Aya is a Stable Worker at the East Akkala Stable. She sits on a stool under the Tree next to a Blue Flame Pedestal at all hours of the day. When spoken to, she will seem depressed. If Link asks her what is wrong, she quietly mutters about the Blue Flame. Upon questioning, she will explain that her life has been dull since she got married, and she previously used to pass the time by staring at the Blue Flame. However, she reveals that the director of the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab, Robbie, has not lit the Blue Flame Pedestals in a while. Link can offer to relight the Blue Flame, at which point Aya asks if he can retrieve it in under three minutes. This initiates the Restoring the Blue Flame Mini-Game, in which Aya will charge Link 20 Rupees as a Horse-handling fee. She does this because she does not see how else he could complete the challenge within the time limit. She also makes a joke before sending Link out, pretending to count down and then telling Link this is what she will say before he leaves. If Link returns the Blue Flame, Aya will be excited and give him a Purple Rupee as a reward. The next time the Blue Flame goes out, Aya will ask Link to bring it back in one minute. After this is done, Aya will reward Link with a Silver Rupee. When the Blue Flame goes out a third time, Aya asks Link to relight the Blue Flame Pedestal in less than twenty seconds. The reward for doing this is a Gold Rupee. On subsequent visits, however, she will only be able to give Link 20 Rupees. If the Blue Flame is extinguished while it is Raining, Aya will remark that Link should not retrieve it due to the poor weather. Aya is happier while the Blue Flame is lit. She asks Link if there is anything as pretty as the Blue Flame, but she does not think there is. She also finds the Blue Flame to be soothing, and wants to know if Link thinks the same. In addition, she will warn Link against putting it out, grumbling angrily if he does so.

is a recurring character in . Biography Azu is a curious child who spends most of his time spying on the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab from a distance with his friend Sefaro. He has heard from Karin that a girl was seen around the Lab, but he is growing frustrated with the lack of evidence. Still, he is hoping to eventually catch sight of her. If Link speaks to Azu in the morning, he tells him to keep his space, as he could potentially blow their cover. Upon further prompting, he will explain that he and Sefaro are playing spies. While Sefaro would like to go up to the Lab, Azu admits that his mother has told him not to get too close. During the Rain, Azu claims that while he would like to go visit the girl, he hates walking through the rain. If Link stands between Azu and the Lab, he will quietly tell him that he is in the way. However, should Link show an interest in what he is doing, Azu will perk up and explain his actions. Link can apologize for getting in the way and Azu will be pleased. When Link speaks to Azu while holding the Blue Flame, he will recognize it, as he has seen Purah holding it before. He then wonders how Link knows Purah. At 8 o'clock, Azu decides it is time to stop playing and go home for the night. He sleeps above the East Wind with his mother, Amira, and his sister, Ivee. Even in his dreams, he mumbles about the Sheikah girl.

is a recurring character in . Biography Babi is a Gerudo Soldier who wields a Gerudo Spear, and she can be found in the Barracks of Gerudo Town. She trains some of the other soldiers. When Link speaks to her, she warns him that they are on high alert and that outsiders must stay out of their way. If Link speaks to Babi while Malena is asking her for help, Babi is exasperated that Link and Malena still wander into the barracks, despite her warnings. She warns Link that they would be in pieces if they were not busy. After Link receives permission from Captain Teake to hear what happened from the soldiers, Babi says that she and her soldiers are busy spear training and that Link cannot interfere, even with Teake's permission. If Link speaks to Babi after recovering the Thunder Helm, she proclaims that she must prevent a crime like that from happening again. She believes that her diligence will inspire others. Due to her strong appearance, Babi claims to feel the gazes of those weaker than her. Marta remarks that once their spears are repaired, she believes Babi will have more special training from them. She also claims that Babi is working too hard, even though the heirloom has been returned, hoping to never be as intense as she is. Smaude also makes similar comments, wondering if Babi thinks training without rest proves her discipline and wishing Babi could feel how tired she is. She thinks Babi would train for days on end if no one stopped her. In addition, Smaude tries to avoid eye contact with Babi so she does not get dragged into her training.

is a recurring character in . Biography Baddek is a Hylian who rides a Horse, carrying a Wooden Shield and Traveler's Sword. He travels along the Hilltop High Road from Serenne Stable all the way to Tabantha Bridge Stable and back. Once he reaches a Stable, he will rest nearby with his Horse for a moment before leaving again. When spoken to, Baddek will reveal that he has a great appreciation for Horses, claiming he sees the world through "horse-tinted glasses". He also tells Link that he only talks about Horses. While he has difficulties speaking with others, he finds that Horses love him. Due to how much he talks about Horses, his wife left him for one. He does not mind, though, as it gives him more time to talk about Horses. To Baddek, taming wild Horses is like adopting a new family member that you can sit on. He says that registered Horse companions will always be by your side, until they die. Baddek's Horse is the one thing he cannot travel without. As long as he has his Horse, Baddek says he does not need anything else, and he believes the Horse is more important than he is. In addition, he states that his Horse's saddle fits both him and the Horse perfectly. The Horse's bridle is also easy to grasp and elastic. Occasionally, Baddek will give Link tips for handling Horses, saying to pet them when they follow directions and work hard, as praising them reinforces good behavior. In addition, he tells Link that he cannot expect a horse to ride hard for him without a meaningful connection, and that he should spend time with his Horse to form a bond. He also recites Horse facts, stating that Horses can swim if they need to. After this, he will ask Link to name another animal that swims, but says it is a trick question as there are none. He also informs Link that Stables fit registered Horses with saddles and bridles. One type of Horse Baddek likes the most is the White Horse, claiming he has heard of a special Horse in the Sanidin Park Ruins fit for a king. While girls dream about princes on White Horses, Baddek only cares about the White Horse. Though Horses come in many colors, White Horses take his breath away. Baddek has also ridden a Stalhorse in the Hebra Mountains. Since he could never be afraid of a Horse, Baddek claims he was not scared of it. He describes the Stalhorse as running well and being surprisingly comfortable. Baddek tells Link that there are four different Stables that have different Bridle and Saddle styles, these being Woodland Stable, Highland Stable, Outskirt Stable, and South Akkala Stable. This, however, is false, and these are simply the Stables where Link can have a worker change the gear of his Horses. When it is Raining, Baddek will seek shelter for himself and his horse, comparing the Weather "like stallions and mares". During

Stable, Outskirt Stable, and South Akkala Stable. This, however, is false, and these are simply the Stables where Link can have a worker change the gear of his Horses. When it is Raining, Baddek will seek shelter for himself and his horse, comparing the Weather "like stallions and mares". During this time, he'll give Link a quiz on Horses. He lists four different types of Horses—the White Horse, the Giant Horse, the mechanical horse, and the bone Horse—and asks Link which one does not exist. He says that the answer will be revealed someday, somewhere, and that Link may already know it. Occasionally, Baddek will make dismissive comments about the existence of mechanical horses. Despite his addiction to Horses, he also wonders about Paragliders and Carrots.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Baked Apples are a type of Roasted Food that results from Apples making contact with Fire or a Scorching Climate. They are softer and sweeter than regular Apples. By eating one, Link can heal three quarters of a Heart to his Life Gauge. When Link first meets the Old Man at his Campfire, he can steal his Baked Apple and have the Old Man lecture him. The Old Man will then tell Link he was only teasing him, and he welcomes him to help himself to his Baked Apples. If Link speaks to Juney, who can be found in Rito Village, she will explain that she is upset with her husband, Jogo, for bringing her there for her honeymoon, and they only way she will not divorce him is if he brings her a Baked Apple. This initiates "The Apple of My Eye" Side Quest. Returning to Juney with a Baked Apple in Link's Inventory will be able to smell it. She then asks if she can have one, promising a present for Link in return. If Link decides to give her one, she rewards him with a Silver Rupee. Juney laments that her husband does not Cook Baked Apples for her very often. She also asks Link to bring her more Baked Apples if he can. When Link brings Baked Apples to Juney, she will pay a greater amount per Apple depending on how many are available. She buys Baked Apples in groups of one, five, 10, 30, 50, and 100.

are recurring Items in . They have a hard rind on the outside and steamy flesh on the inside. By eating one, Link can heal three-quarters of a Heart. In , Baked Fortified Pumpkins are identical to their counterpart. They are a type of Roasted Food, and they are the result of Fortified Pumpkins that have been exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They have a hard rind on the outside and steamy flesh on the inside. By eating one, Link can heal three-quarters of a Heart.

are recurring Objects and Items in . Location and Uses A Balloon can be found in North Clock Town being shot at by Jim with a blowgun. Another appears in the Astral Observatory, blocking the ladder leading out of the sewers. It must be destroyed for Link to continue. Balloons first appear in Stage 1 of the second Level, Buzz Blob Cave, where they demonstrate the Balloon-popping power of the Bow. Each of the Links must fire an Arrow at one to lower a small bridge, allowing access to the Level's main area; then, working together with the Totem ability, one of the Links can reach a high-up ledge and pop a final Balloon containing the Key to the Triforce Gateway. Balloons can also be popped with the Sword, any other weapons, thrown objects, or even by Enemies. The main use of Balloons thereafter is in the Drablands Challenges "Pop all balloons!", in which every Balloon in each Stage must be popped before the Triforce Gateway will activate, and "Don't pop any balloons!", in which popping a single Balloon results in an instant KO, restarting the Stage. In these challenges, numerous Balloons appear in preset locations around the Level. Some are stationary, while some float around a given area. Elevated Balloons often bare a number, indicating the height of a Totem required to reach it. The challenge "Pop all balloons!" can be selected in Buzz Blob Cave, Moblin Base, Secret Fortress, Blazing Trail, Hinox Mine, Frozen Plateau and Palace Noir. "Don't pop any balloon!" can be selected in Hinox Mine, Desert Temple and Deception Castle. Balloons are found throughout Ancient Shrines. They are commonly attached to platforms, allowing for movement through the air. They can also be attached to Bomb Barrels, creating portable Bombs. Balloons also act as Korok Seed Puzzles throughout Hyrule, revealing Koroks when they are popped. Balloons are Zonai Devices. When a heat source is placed underneath them, they will rise into the air. They can be merged with other Objects with the Ultrahand ability to create vehicles that can reach high altitudes with relatively little drain on Link's Energy Cell. Balloons cannot remain aloft indefinitely and will blink green for a few seconds before their duration expires, at which point they will disappear. Balloons also appear as part of the Pinwheel & Balloons and Hidden Balloon types of Korok Seed Puzzles. Other Appearances The Balloon is a class of Weapon used by Tingle. It is associated with Fire. Variations The default Balloon is the Rosy Balloon. Bamitok Shrine, designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Bamitok Shrine can be found within the Mount Dunsel Cave in East Necluda.
