is a character in . Biography Bandaga is a Gerudo soldier. After the Main Quest "Riju of Gerudo Town" is completed, Bandaga will appear at Lookout Landing, where she guards the eastern entrance at all hours with Mondi. She wields a Decayed Gerudo Spear. When Link first speaks to her, she thanks him for helping Gerudo Town. After that, she tells Link that if he is looking for Gems that Goron City is a great source for ones that are not too expensive. She claims to know this because Gerudo have a sharp eye for quality Gems and reveals that most of the Gerudo's Gems are originally from Death Mountain. She then muses that she might travel to Death Mountain herself after the Demon King is defeated. Like all Gerudo guards, Bandaga has unique dialogue if Link speaks to her while wearing the Yiga Clan Attire, believing him to be from the Yiga Clan.

is a recurring character in . Biography Banji is a resident and worker of the Tabantha Bridge Stable, where she will greet travelers as they come by. During the day, she does several chores for the stable with Ena, such as tending to the White Goats, cataloging the cargo, and caring for the Horses. She believes that the White Goats at the Stable are the cutest in Hyrule. At night, she watches her children while they sleep in the Stable's Beds, as it makes her happy. When it Rains, Banji will run inside and comment on the Weather. Banji offers directions to travelers who pass through Tabantha Bridge Stable. If asked about the east, Banji speaks about Ludfo's Bog. If Link has not yet completed the trials on Thundra Plateau, she will explain that it is an area with constant Thunderstorms. She considers the storm clouds to be a sign from Hylia to stay away. If Link has completed the trials, she notes that the Thunderstorms recently disappeared after many years. She believes this to be the doing of Hylia. Banji tells Link that she is thinking of taking the Horses from the Stable on a trip to Ludfo's Bog soon, since the storms have cleared. When asked about the south, Banji tells Link about the Tamio River and Satori Mountain, claiming there is a legend about a "lord" over all living things as well as a god who watches over the Stables, which their aunt told them stories about. For the west, she tells Link that beyond the Tabantha Great Bridge lies Rito Village, and she also warns him about the Divine Beast Vah Medoh that recently appeared above it. Finally, when she is prompted about the north, Banji tells Link about Konba, a man north of Tabantha Bridge Stable who loves to race. She asks Link to visit him, since he must be bored on his own.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Bank of Wishes is located along the Zora River in the Lanayru Great Spring. According to legend, if someone sends a letter down the Zora River from the Bank of Wishes, the person who replies will be theirs forever. These wishes are supposedly granted by a Water Fairy. Before Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, the Rain that it generates will constantly fall over the Bank of Wishes. Prior to Link arriving in Zora's Domain, Finley would go to the Bank of Wishes to communicate with her pen pal, Sasan. However, once Divine Beast Vah Ruta started its rampage, her mother Kodah forbade her from visiting. After Link has completed the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" Main Quest, he can find Finley at the Bank of Wishes with her Love Letter. When Link approaches her, she asks if he also has a wish for the Water Fairy, but she dismisses this idea when she notices he does not have a letter. She then wonders if he is a servant to the Water Fairy. Once Finley realizes that he is a traveler, she asks him if he could follow her Love Letter down the Zora River to see who picks it up. Finley herself is unable to, as she promised her mother that she would not stray far from Zora's Domain. If Link agrees to her request, Finley will thank him before preparing to throw the Love Letter into the Zora River. Once she does, the "Special Delivery" Side Quest will begin. If the Love Letter is broken or lost, Link can return to the Bank of Wishes to inform Finley. Having predicted this would happen, she made an extra one. Finley will also push this Love Letter into the Zora River, and Link will still have to follow it.

, also known as the Wayfaring Island, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Bannan Island is an Island found in the northwestern portion of the World of the Ocean King in . It is here that Romanos' father, the Old Wayfarer, decided to begin his search for the mermaid after navigating the foggy passage north of Molida Island and living for months on the Isle of Gust. Bannan Island is split into two main parts by a long cavern that runs the length of it. The left side of the Island is split into two smaller sections, connected by a bridge. A small island that can only be accessed with the Grappling Hook is located south of the lower section, and is home to a Treasure Chest containing a Power Gem. The cavern in the middle of the island contains a wall that can only be destroyed with Bombs, and Link therefore cannot access the right side of the Island until he obtains the Bomb Bag in the Temple of Wind. The right side of the Island is made up of one section. However, two smaller islands, that can only be accessed with the Grappling Hook can be found to the north. The island on the right is home to two Treasure Chests containing 100 Rupees and a Courage Gem. The island on the left is home to some stone tablets that inform Link of a Treasure Map buried between the two chests on the lower island. The island's Dock is located in the very southwest corner of the island. From there, a path leads to the bridge that connects the two sections of the left side of the island. To the right of the bridge is the island's Mailbox, and further right of that is the entrance to the cave separating the two sides of the island. On the other side of the cave, on the right side of the island, is the Cannon Game Stand, run by Salvatore. Here, Link can play the Cannon Game for 20 Rupees. Link can win many prizes from this game, the most notable being a Bomb Bag upgrade. thumb|left|Inside the Old Wayfarer's house In the north section of the island's left side is the Old Wayfarer's house. Here, Link can find the Old Wayfarer, who asks Link to tell him if he sees a mermaid. He also tells Link that the mermaid will not appear if there are any monsters in the area. After Link finds the mermaid, who turns out to be Joanne, a human in a mermaid costume, she will pay a visit to the Old Wayfarer's house. She stays there for the rest of the game in a pool which the Old Wayfarer had purchased in order to keep her. For uniting the two, Link receives a Fishing Rod from the Old Wayfarer. Link can then return to the Old Wayfarer's House and speak to him (or Joanne if Link has reached the final stage of

in a pool which the Old Wayfarer had purchased in order to keep her. For uniting the two, Link receives a Fishing Rod from the Old Wayfarer. Link can then return to the Old Wayfarer's House and speak to him (or Joanne if Link has reached the final stage of the trading sequence, as the Old Wayfarer will be travelling the sea) to show him what fish he has caught. If Link shows him a Loovar, he will receive a Big Catch Lure, and if he shows him a Neptoona, he will receive a Heart Container. A Treasure Map can be found buried in front of the sign outside the Old Wayfarer's house, which Link is told about by a Gossip Stone on the Isle of Frost. Later on in the game, Link must return to the Old Wayfarer's house for two reasons. Firstly, after receiving Jolene's Letter, he must return here to deliver it to Joanne, who will thank him and reward him with a Wisdom Gem. Secondly after completing the Trading Sequence, Link must return to the Old Wayfarer's house in order to get his reward, which was left inside a large treasure chest. However, when Link attempts to dock at the island, he is attacked by a Giant Eye Plant. After defeating it, Link is able to dock at the island and receive his reward; a Swordsman's Scroll which teaches the Great Spin Attack. Areas Bannan Island is located in the Lanayru Wetlands with a wooden House its center. Two Rusty Halberds can be found in the ground. Like many of the islands that surround it, the dry land sits just above the wetland. Shrine Island is connected by wooden bridge to the southwest where Daka Tuss Shrine can be found.

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Barbarian Armor is a piece of Armor located in the Dila Maag Shrine at South Lomei Labyrinth. After obtaining it, Granté will begin selling the piece of Armor for 4,000 Rupees. According to its description, the Armor was worn by the warriors of an ancient warlike tribe from the Faron Region. When worn, it provides one level of Attack Up. The Barbarian Armor can be enhanced by a Great Fairy and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Barbarian Armor, alongside the Barbarian Helm and Barbarian Leg Wraps, compose the Barbarian Set. When each piece of the Set has been enhanced at least two times by a Great Fairy and the full Set is worn, it provides a Charge Atk. Stamina Up Set Bonus. Dye Options Enhancing The Barbarian Armor is found in a Treasure Chest in Crenel Hills Cave. Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances The Barbarian Armor is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and it is obtained by completing the Challenge "Coliseum: Expert". It can also be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Dye Options

The is a recurring Armor Set in . Location and Uses The Barbarian Set is an Armor Set consisting of the Barbarian Helm, Barbarian Armor, and Barbarian Leg Wraps. Each piece must be obtained from a Treasure Chest in the following Ancient Shrines respectively: Tu Ka'loh Shrine at Lomei Labyrinth Island. Dila Maag Shrine at South Lomei Labyrinth. Qaza Tokki Shrine at North Lomei Labyrinth. Each piece increases Link's Attack Up by one when worn. If all three pieces are worn and have been Enhanced at least twice by a Great Fairy, they provide the Charge Atk. Stamina Up Set Bonus. Dye Options Enhancing Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances The Barbarian Helm is acquired upon completing the "Anti-Element Training" Quest. The Barbarian Armor is acquired upon completing the "Coliseum: Expert" Quest. The Barbarian Leg Wraps are acquired upon completing the "Hair Width Trial: Expert+" Quest. Dye Options

Bargainer Statues are characters in . Biography Bargainer Statues are sapient Statues that are predominantly found in the Depths. Their purpose is to deliver Poes to the afterlife. Link can speak with most of them to trade Poes for rare Materials, Armor, and Equipment. The Bargainer Statue at the entrance to the Great Plateau cannot be traded with. When Link speaks to it, the Great Abandoned Central Mine Bargainer Statue will speak through it, instructing him to go to the Temple of Time Ruins where he can start the Side Adventure "A Call from the Depths". Afterwards, it will fall silent. List of Bargainer Statues There are eight Bargainer Statues in , six in the Depths, one in Lookout Landing, and one at the entrance to the Great Plateau. Each Bargainer Statue in the Depths corresponds to a Great Goddess Statue on the Surface or in the Sky. Wares and Pricing The wares the Bargainer Statues offer are expanded each time Link opens a new Bargainer Statue's Shop. Until Link has interacted with all of them, the Bargainer Statue in Lookout Landing will mark the location of a Bargainer Statue in the Depths that Link has not yet visited on his Map in exchange for 100 Poes. Additionally, rare Armor and Equipment will become available for purchase from the Bargainer Statues in the Depths after Link has obtained them at least once.

is a recurring character in . Biography Bargoh is a Goron who stands watch between Goron City and the Abandoned North Mine near the Shae Mo'sah Shrine. As a guard, he carries a Cobble Crusher with him and wears a Forehead Protector. He is tasked with making sure that monsters do not enter the City, as they have started to appear following the emergence of the Divine Beast Vah Rudania. If Link tells Bargoh he is lost, he will suggest climbing up high to get a feel for his surroundings. As part of his job, Bargoh stops people from heading to the Abandoned North Mine due to its danger. However, he allows Link to go through, as Bludo sent him. Link may speak with Bargoh to learn the whereabouts of Yunobo, who passes him several times over the course of the "Divine Beast Vah Rudania" Main Quest. At first, he will direct Link to the Abandoned North Mine. Later, he tells Link that Yunobo is at the Boss's House. Once Yunobo leaves, however, Bargoh will tell Link that he is at the Bridge of Eldin, which he gives him directions to. After Divine Beast Vah Rudania has been calmed, Bargoh tells Link that Yunobo has returned to Goron City. He also asks Link if something happened on Death Mountain, since it looked like Yunobo had been through something.

The are a recurring location in . The Barracks go unnamed in . Features and Overview The Barracks are located in the western corner of Gerudo Town. They house the Gerudo soldiers, who can be seen training within. From the Barracks, Ashai's Relationship Classroom can be accessed through a doorway at the bottom of a staircase. At the top of this staircase, Link can enter the Royal Palace of Gerudo Town. When Link initially enters the Barracks, the soldiers are on high alert due to a recent theft of the Thunder Helm, which they refuse to discuss with outsiders. Two soldiers, Smaude and Marta, are being subjected to intense training by Babi since the thieves managed to slip past them. While meeting with Riju, Buliara suggests that Link prove himself by recovering the stolen Thunder Helm. To this end, she allows the Gerudo soldiers in the Barracks to speak freely about the theft to Link. In the Barracks, the captain of the guard, Teake, will explain the details of the theft once Link reveals that Buliara sent him. She then commands her soldiers to offer whatever information they have to Link. Turning back to Link, she tells him to consider himself part of their unit, and he should ask the soldiers any questions he has. When Link approaches Liana during this time, he will overhear her wondering where Barta has gone. Leena reveals that Barta went to scout out the Yiga Clan Hideout two days prior, leaving before anyone could stop her. Liana is shocked that Barta has been gone for so long without anyone informing her. Leena apologizes, recalling that Barta claimed she would be careful. Liana expresses her frustration that they have to search for both the Thunder Helm and Barta, and she is afraid of Teake punishing them if she hears about what happened. Realizing the gravity of the situation, Kotta asks what they should do. Liana yells that she is thinking about it. After the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest has been completed, Link can return to the Barracks to find that Barta has disappeared again. Kotta explains that she left to investigate the Gerudo Great Skeleton, southwest of Gerudo Town. Leena claims she tried to stop her, but Liana points out that this obviously did not work. After witnessing their exchange, "The Search for Barta" Side Quest will begin. When Link saves Barta from her exhaustion, she considers resting at the Gerudo Great Skeleton longer before she returns to the Barracks. However, when she hears how angry Liana is, she decides to leave right away. Back in the Barracks, Liana will commend Link for helping Barta, giving him a Silver Rupee as a reward. Malena frequents the Barracks during the day, where she begs the guards for help. When spoken to, she reveals that her husband has fallen ill, and he can only be cured with Molduga Guts. She returned to Gerudo Town to ask the Gerudo soldiers for help, but they were unable

She returned to Gerudo Town to ask the Gerudo soldiers for help, but they were unable to offer her any. After speaking to her, the "Medicinal Molduga" Side Quest will begin. Equipment The Barracks are located in Hyrule Castle Town to the northwest of the fountain. It is inhabited by a lone Soldier who is attempting to motivate himself while training against a dummy. is a recurring character in . Biography Barta is a Gerudo Soldier who protects Gerudo Town, wielding a Gerudo Spear. When Link first enters Gerudo Town, however, she will be absent. If Link approaches Liana, Leena, or Kotta in the Barracks after speaking to Riju for the first time, Liana will ask where Barta is. Leena explains that she went to the Yiga Clan Hideout two days ago and wonders what happened to her. Angered, Liana asks why she let Barta go by herself, which Leena apologizes for. Liana is upset that they now have to retrieve both the Thunder Helm and Barta. She expresses concern about Captain Teake finding out about it, Kotta asks what they should do. This causes Liana to yell that she is thinking about it. Link can find Barta imprisoned in a cell within the Yiga Clan Hideout. She is surprised that he has entered the Hideout, as they will call in reinforcements if they notice him. Barta has only ever seen them patrol and eat Mighty Bananas, neither of which she can see a weakness in. She tries to convince Link to leave, as she can take care of herself. After Link recovers the Thunder Helm, Barta returns to the Barracks in Gerudo Town and tells Liana how helpful Link was. Barta will recognize Link from the Yiga Clan Hideout, explaining she was able to escape because they spread their forces thin looking for him. If Link was not wearing the Gerudo Outfit when she saw him, she promises not to tell anyone that he is a voe. Barta disappears again after Link frees Divine Beast Vah Naboris. Speaking to the soldiers, Liana is shocked to find Barta has not come back. Kotta explains that she went to investigate the Gerudo Great Skeleton, and Leena claims she tried to stop her this time. When Liana points out that this obviously did not work, Leena and Kotta try to rationalize their decisions, saying everyone knows the area is dangerous and to avoid it. This only angers Liana further, who remarks that Barta would not realize she was walking right into danger. She wonders why Barta has to get in trouble all the time. Witnessing this conversation activates "The Search for Barta" Side Quest. Link will find Barta on the brink of death, kneeling on the ground in the Gerudo Desert near the Gerudo Great Skeleton. Barta wishes she could have eaten a Hearty Durian one last time. After Link gives her a Hearty Durian, Barta will stand up and thank Link for saving her life. She laments heading out into the heat without the proper gear. If Link is wearing the Gerudo Outfit, she notices he is not wearing the proper gear either and is amazed he made it out so far. If Link is not wearing his disguise and Barta has not yet seen him without it, she will realize he is a man, mentioning that he seemed muscular for a Hylian woman. Barta

he is not wearing the proper gear either and is amazed he made it out so far. If Link is not wearing his disguise and Barta has not yet seen him without it, she will realize he is a man, mentioning that he seemed muscular for a Hylian woman. Barta promises to keep it a secret, especially because Link saved her life. At first, Barta is so tired that she wants to rest just a bit longer before she returns to Gerudo Town. However, when Link informs her that Liana was furious, Barta realizes she is in trouble and decides to head back. Upon returning to the Barracks, Liana has heard that Link saved Barta. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Batrea Lake is a shallow lake in West Necluda that can be found just east of the Owlan Bridge. Near the center of Batrea Lake sits a giant, hollow stump. Link can find a thin, stone tower at the end of a peninsula which cuts into the Lake. Three giant, metallic blocks can be found throughout Batrea Lake: one near the stone tower and two more which rest inside the giant, hollow stump. An enemy Platform can be found near the base of the aforementioned peninsula, atop which Link can find several Bomb Barrels. A stone Treasure Chest can be found atop the tower, which contains a bundle of five Bomb Arrows. A wooden Treasure Chest, which contains a Traveler's Bow, can be found atop the enemy Platform. Creatures Enemies

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Batteries are Zonai Devices. When used alongside other Zonai Devices, the other Zonai Devices will use Energy from any connected Batteries before they begin to drain Link's Energy Cell. Each Battery has a limited energy supply and will disappear once it is depleted. As Objects, Batteries can be found throughout the Gerudo Desert. They activate when struck by Riju's Power of Lightning. During the "Riju of Gerudo Town" Main Quest, Riju must charge four Batteries in the Lightning Temple, allowing the platform in the Room of Ascension to rise to the Lightning Temple 7F. Other Appearances Batteries can be used to instantly refill the Energy Gauge.

is a recurring character in . Biography Baumar is a Hylian who travels with his Horse, Bamboo, while carrying a Fisherman's Shield and a Traveler's Sword. The pair travel a portion of the Hilltop High Road between Serenne Stable and Snowfield Stable. When Baumar was a child, he almost got lost up in the Hebra Mountains. While a shield surfer saved him, Baumar has trouble recall his name. Falmark was the shield surfer, and he claims that surfing down the mountain with a child on his back was difficult. Baumar shows a lot of appreciation for Bamboo. He refers to his Horse with a lot of affectionate terms, such as "totally gnarly", "radical", and "most excellent". He also offers directions as the two of them travel. If Link overhears him talking to Bamboo, he will explain that he is not good at conversing with people. Baumar enjoys Shield Surfing, finding it difficult to go long times without doing so. His plan for his journey is to stop at Snowfield Stable, at which point he will head to the Hebra Mountains to Shield Surf. Ocassionaly, he will say that he has no time to chat with Link. He claims to be talented, though he describes his process as climbing the Mountains and Surfing. When he makes it to Snowfield Stable, Baumar is excited to head up the Hebra Mountains and finally go Shield Surfing. On the way to the Hebra Mountains, Baumar mentally prepares himself for Shield Surfing, and he becomes annoyed if Link interrupts him. The legendary Shield Surfer, Selmie, supposedly had all of her routes memorized. There is a rumor Baumar has heard that Selmie is waiting on the Hebra Mountains for a worthy opponent. If he is caught in the rain, Baumar will be disappointed disappointed that he can not shield surf. While it is storming or snowing, Baumar wonders if professional shield surfers head out in this type of weather, confessing he would break his neck if he wiped out. Occasionally, Baumar will give Link a Shield Surfing tip. For example, depending on the type of Shield used, one's surfing will be different. He knows of a Shield that is supposed to be good for Shield Surfing, which is the Knight's Shield, but he can not remember what it is called. Additionally, he has heard of the Hylian Shield within Hyrule Castle, which is supposed to be durable.

is a recurring character in . Biography Bayge is the eldest of the Goron Blood Brothers, a group consisting of himself and his brothers, Heehl and Kabetta. Bayge and his brothers are passionate about training in difficult feats of strength and endurance. He lives with his brothers in a house in southern Goron City, which is now abandoned and left with a Sign saying they have gone to Gut Check Rock to train. Bayge is involved in two Shrine Quests. One is the "Test of Will" at Mount Nabooru in the Gerudo Highlands. Bayge and the other Goron Blood Brothers have traveled to their ancestral training ground to train themselves to withstand the rising heat of Goron City. Bayge and the others challenge Link to join them by sitting in a ring of fire to see who can withstand the longest. When Link joins them in the ring, Bayge will start the contest of endurance. Though Bayge claims that it is easy, he is the last of the three to collapse. Afterwards, he declares Link the winner. The brothers then challenge Link to a harder contest, which would require him to stand on an even hotter platform. Bayge warns Link that he will catch on Fire if he looses his focus. However, he also comments that clearing this challenge is said to reveal an Ancient Shrine. During this challenge, Bayge will notice if Link is wearing Armor from the Fireproof Armor, Gerudo Outfit, or Desert Voe Set, and he refuses to start until he takes them off. After enough time passes, Bayge will stop the contest to declare that Link has beaten it. Once this is done, Joloo Nah Shrine will emerge from the ground nearby. Bayge praises Link for being able to overcome the challenge, and the Shrine Quest will be completed. Bayge is also involved in "The Gut Check Challenge" Shrine Quest at Gut Check Rock in northern Eldin Canyon. Bayge is found sitting on the steps to Gorae Torr Shrine atop tits pinnacle. He refuses to let Link approach, as the Shrine's platform is a sacred place to the Goron Blood Brothers. However, Bayge decides to let Link through if he can clear their training exercise, the Gut Check Rock Challenge, wherein Link must climb the pinnacle while collecting enough Rupees. Upon clearing the Challenge, Bayge happily appoints Link as an honorary Goron Blood Brother and allows him to approach the Shrine. Bayge will then offer a much harder course called the Super Gut Check Challenge. When Downloadable Content Pack is active and Link is pursuing the "EX Champion Daruk's Song" Main Quest, the Goron Blood Brothers can be found at Darb Pond. If Link has already completed "The Gut Check Challenge", Bayge recognizes him as their fourth brother. He explains that Daruk used to train at this spot, and while he does not know why, he believes it was part of his training as a Champion. Therefore, the Goron Blood Brothers are training at this spot

He explains that Daruk used to train at this spot, and while he does not know why, he believes it was part of his training as a Champion. Therefore, the Goron Blood Brothers are training at this spot to become mighty Gorons like Daruk, claiming it is their only path. Kabetta points out the Glowing Ring on the Lava and directs Link to stand on it. Bayge points out that choosing this spot makes Daruk hard-core. Due to the intensity of this training, he decides to take the time to strategize with the other Goron Blood Brothers. He is disappointed that he can no longer attempt the training. After this, the Goron Blood Brothers will return to Gut Check Rock.

is a recurring character in . Biography Bazz is a Zora and the captain of the guard of Zora's Domain. He wields a Silverscale Spear. He is the son of Seggin, and when he was a child, he was the leader of the Big Bad Bazz Brigade. Link taught Bazz swordsmanship when he was young. When Link first speaks to Bazz, he will welcome him to Zora's Domain and explain that they have been looking for a Hylian like him. He mutters to himself that Link seems familiar, believing that they have met a long time ago. If Link speaks to Bazz a second time, he is certain that he remembers who Link is. However, due to the shorter lifespan of Hylians, Bazz decides to test him in order to be sure. He asks Link if he knows the Bigg Badd Bazz Brigade password, starting with, "Fluffy white clouds! Clear blue..." After Link successfully guesses the word "Zora", Bazz will be convinced that the person he is speaking to is Link. If Link confirms that he is, Bazz excitedly proclaims that he knew it. If Link denies this, Bazz refutes him, saying only a member of the Big Bad Bazz Brigade could know the password. Noticing that Link looks the same as he did 100 years ago, Bazz asks Link what he has been doing. If Link tells him that he was sleeping, Bazz refuses to believe anyone could sleep so long. If Link is unable to come up with an answer, Bazz assumes he was doing something important. Either way, he repeats that Zora's Domain is in need of the help of a Hylian, and he urges Link to meet with King Dorephan. Once Bazz has confirmed Link's identity, he will answer questions for him. When asked about King Dorephan, Bazz explains that he is located upstairs. He is certain that Link must remember him, revealing that he is the father of Mipha. When asked this question after Link has met with King Dorephan, Bazz reminds him that King is the father of both Mipha and Sidon. He also reveals that things have been difficult for the Zora since Mipha was defeated by Calamity Ganon. After hearing her name from Bazz, Link is able to ask him about Mipha. Bazz is shocked to hear that Link has forgotten Mipha. He shares that Mipha was a princess who was admired and beloved by the Zora. He starts to elaborate on Mipha and Link's relationship, but he decides it would be better if he heard it from King Dorephan, instead. Asking who Bazz is causes him to introduce himself, revealing that Link trained him when he was younger. He credits his father Seggin surviving the Great Calamity to Link. He also laments that Seggin has not changed much, revealing that he has begun training to increase his resistance to Electricity for Mipha's sake. Bazz reminds Link that the Zora typically avoid Electricity, and he is afraid that Seggin may reach his

father Seggin surviving the Great Calamity to Link. He also laments that Seggin has not changed much, revealing that he has begun training to increase his resistance to Electricity for Mipha's sake. Bazz reminds Link that the Zora typically avoid Electricity, and he is afraid that Seggin may reach his limit soon. When Link asks this question after speaking to King Dorephan, Bazz reveals that he was able to become the captain of the guard due to Link's training. He considers himself to be in Link's debt because of this. After the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" Main Quest has been completed, Bazz thanks Link for saving Zora's Domain. While he believes that calming Divine Beast Vah Ruta should have been his job as the captain of the guard, he is unable to handle Shock Arrows. However, even though the trouble has passed, he plans to continue protecting Zora's Domain. He can also be seen in the Throne Room as King Dorephan thanks Link. During "EX Champion Mipha's Song", which is a Main Quest exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Bazz can be found in Upland Zorana alongside his father, Seggin. When Link approaches him, he remarks how rare it is to encounter a Hylian where they are. Upon recognizing Link, Bazz warmly greets him, and he thanks him again for calming Divine Beast Vah Ruta. He warns Link that blue-eyed Guardians have appeared in Upland Zorana, which he has heard were last seen during Mipha's trial. Though Seggin claims that they are harmless, Bazz has decided to remain alert. After Link has defeated the Guardians, Bazz notices the emergence of Sato Koda Shrine, which confirms to him that they were related to the trial. Bazz can first be encountered at the Upland Zorana Skyview Tower, where he is stuck in a pool of Sludge.

is a recurring character in . Biography Bedoli is a citizen of Rito Village, located on the Tabantha Frontier. She and her sister Laissa live together in a House near Akh Va'quot Shrine. During the day, she can be found walking around Revali's Landing. When spoken to initially, Bedoli asks if Link has seen Divine Beast Vah Medoh, admitting everyone in Rito Village is unsure what to do. Every time she looks up, she cannot help but sigh, and she wonders when the Village will be able to relax again. After Vah Medoh has been appeased, Bedoli becomes so excited she does not realize that she has started singing an old song. She asks Link if he heard her sing. If Link asks Bedoli to teach him, she claims to be embarrassed. While Bedoli sings the song for Link, she is unable to remember all of it. She directs Link to find Laissa, which initiates the Shrine Quest "The Ancient Rito Song". Speaking to Laissa, she comments that Bedoli's memory is terrible. Once Link has learned the second half, he can return to Bedoli, who claims to remember the rest of the lyrics. She is then able to recite the whole song, and she's not sure what it means. At any time afterwards, Link can approach Bedoli to have her recite the song again.

are Room Units in . Location and Uses Bedrooms are a type of Room Unit. They are sold by Grantéson as part of Hudson Construction's Dream Home service for 400 Rupee. In addition, during the Side Quest "Home on Arrange", Link's contract with Hudson Construction includes both a Bedroom and a Foyer. After being purchased, Link can use Ultrahand on Bedrooms to orient them and attach them to other Room Units. Any Bedrooms that are left unused by the end of construction will be stored by Grantéson. Bedrooms feature a single Bed, which Link can Sleep in to fully restore all of the Hearts in his Life Gauge.

is a recurring character in . He is a small-time businessman, seen working operating his various Shops. Like other Shops and Business Scrubs, Beedle sells, and sometimes even buys back, quest-specific items, such as All-Purpose Bait and Picolyte, both of which are not plot-required, but add extra interest to the games. Unlike the other entrepreneurial businesses in The Legend of Zelda series, Beedle incorporates memberships into his line of work, rewarding Link with increased price discounts if he becomes a frequent, repeat customer. Biography In , Beedle is a local sea merchant who travels the Great Sea in search of profit. He is located in Beedle's Shop Ship, a floating shop located near various islands of the Great Sea. There are a total of 11 Beedle Shop Ships on the Great Sea, not including the Rock Spire Shop Ship which Beedle runs under the guise of an "Assistant Manager". Beedle hopes to one day open a chain of trading posts. Bugs, especially beetles, are his favorite thing. Beedle will buy any item in Link's Spoils Bag. He calls Link "Mr. Customer". Link's first opportunity to meet Beedle is on Outset Island at the beginning of the game. At this time, Beedle's wares are the Bait Bag, All-Purpose Bait, and Hyoi Pears. Beedle later sells Bombs, and Arrows once Link has obtained the Hero's Bow and the initial set of Bombs, respectively. Until then, Beedle does not carry Arrows due to circumstances beyond his control, nor Bombs due to Bomb-Master Cannon's monopoly on the product. Beedle's wares vary by location. Some locations sell Red Potion, though Link can only buy it once he has a Bottle. After Link obtains the Bombs from Tetra's Ship, he receives a Letter from Beedle informing patrons of Bombs becoming available Beedle's Shop Ship. In the Letter, Beedle advertises the shop's "semi-annual Big Chance Extravaganza" and claims to have a special limited-time sale for Bombs. In reality, Beedle sells Bombs at the same price throughout Link's adventure. Enclosed with the Letter is Beedle's Chart, which marks the location of all Beedle Shop Ships including the Rock Spire Shop Ship. When Link purchases his first item, Beedle will make him a Member's Card so he can collect loyalty points. Link earns one point for each purchase. At 30 points, Beedle grants Link a Silver Membership and sends him the Complimentary ID via the Island Postal Service. Link can give the Complimentary ID to Beedle in exchange for a verbal compliment which refills Link's Life Energy. At 60 points, Beedle grants Link a Gold Membership and sends Link a Fill-Up Coupon, which can be redeemed for a full refill of Link's Arrows, Bombs, Life Energy, and Magic Meter. After Link obtains his first Wallet upgrade, he receives another Letter advertising the Rock Spire Shop Ship's wares: a Bottle, a Piece of Heart, and Treasure Chart 4, which also leads to another Piece of Heart. The Letter is signed "Asst. Manager, Rock Spire Shop Ship". Enclosed is a single

After Link obtains his first Wallet upgrade, he receives another Letter advertising the Rock Spire Shop Ship's wares: a Bottle, a Piece of Heart, and Treasure Chart 4, which also leads to another Piece of Heart. The Letter is signed "Asst. Manager, Rock Spire Shop Ship". Enclosed is a single Green Rupee. At the Rock Spire Shop Ship, Beedle wears a face-covering helmet and pretends not to know Link. If Link shows him something from his Spoils Bag, he refuses to buy it and denies being Beedle. Letters Beedle first appears in Hyrule Town during the Picori Festival in , selling fruits. After Princess Zelda is turned to stone and Link obtains the Earth Element from Deepwood Shrine, he returns to Hyrule Town. In Hyrule Town Square, he can use the Gust Jar to clear off the dust covering one of the stalls; if Link does this, after he obtains the Fire Element from the Cave of Flames, Beedle will set up his shop in the stall. Beedle sells Picolyte, and his available selection will expand as Link brings different liquids to the Forest Picori Inside the Barrel House of Minish Village. Beedle's initial selection includes Green, Red, and White Picolyte, and has three empty bottles to hold more. After Link gives the Forest Picori Inside the Barrel House Lon Lon Milk, Mt. Crenel Mineral Water, and a Red Potion, Yellow, Blue, and Orange Pico Blooms will grow, and Beedle will begin selling Yellow, Blue, and Orange Picolyte. In , Beedle operates Beedle's Shop Ship as in , except that he has only one ship that appears in random locations in the World of the Ocean King. From 10am to noon on weekends and 10pm to midnight on weekdays (according to the Nintendo DS clock), the Masked Ship appears instead, manned by his alter ego Beedle's Assistant. Beedle sells a Bomb Bag and a Wisdom Gem. Beedle's Assistant sells a Piece of Heart and a Courage Gem. Both sell Potions, Ship Parts, and Treasure. Their ships are unaffected by cyclones. The concept of memberships was expanded to include two more levels of membership and member discounts. A Silver Membership gives a ten percent discount on all items, a Gold Membership gives a twenty percent discount, Platinum Membership gives thirty percent and the VIP Membership forty percent.Discounts or points do not apply to the Masked Beedle's items. Along with Link, Tetra and Salvatore, as well as Tetra's Pirate Crew to some extent, Beedle is one of the few characters from to actually reappear in . In , Beedle runs Beedle's Air Shop. Link can see his Hot-Air Balloon flying around the Overworld prior to actually being able to enter it. At a certain point, Link receives a Letter stating that his Shop just opened. Link can get Beedle's attention from then on by blowing the Spirit Train's Train Whistle when he is nearby. He will then land, allowing Link to stop by it like any other Station. Link can get Beedle's

a certain point, Link receives a Letter stating that his Shop just opened. Link can get Beedle's attention from then on by blowing the Spirit Train's Train Whistle when he is nearby. He will then land, allowing Link to stop by it like any other Station. Link can get Beedle's Club Membership Cards, allowing him to save up a point for every ten Rupees spent. After passing certain point milestones, Beedle will grant Link rewards. Saving up 500 points awards Link the Heart Container sitting at the back of the Shop. Beedle appears again in , this time selling wares in a flying house, Beedle's Airshop. He operates this ship by pedaling a bicycle which powers an electric generator that drives some gears. He sells Medals, additional Wallets, and his most valuable item, a Piece of Heart. Asking Beedle about his Piece of Heart before buying it will yield the response that he does not actually know what it is, and picked it up from somewhere nearby and decided to sell it. Should Link look at something of Beedle's and attempt to leave without purchasing anything, Beedle will rant at Link about how much effort he needs to exert to hold Link's weight and decides to punish him by activating a trap door under his feet. During the night, Beedle and his ship retire to an island in the sky called Beedle's Island. Falling asleep in his ship will allow Link to visit the shopkeeper on his island during the night, and if the young hero falls asleep in his ship during the night, it will return him to Skyloft. While resting on his island, Beedle will sit and talk with Link whilst admiring the Horned Colossus Beetle caged in his lap. Here, his diction makes a dramatic change with an above average vocabulary and without the joyful yells he is known for. Link can ask about his altered demeanor, but Beedle does not appear to notice any difference, and will dismiss the question as unimportant. After Strich settles in the Bug Rock, Beedle will inform Link that his Horned Colossus Beetle has gone missing and asks the young hero to help him look for his prized possession. If Link flies to Bug Rock, he will find out that Strich has discovered a Horned Colossus Beetle. Upon learning that the Bug belongs to Beedle, he states that he will only let Link have the legendary bug after he plays Bug Heaven, which requires the young hero to catch 10 Bugs in under 3 minutes. If Link succeeds, he will obtain the rare beetle from Strich, and can return the Horned Colossus Beetle to Beedle to receive 5 Gratitude Crystals. As an additional reward, the shopkeeper allows the hero to buy any item from his Airshop at half price. In , Beedle can be found walking around Hyrule, mostly close to Stables. He travels Hyrule on foot instead of by boat or airship like in previous titles. His backpack is shaped

an additional reward, the shopkeeper allows the hero to buy any item from his Airshop at half price. In , Beedle can be found walking around Hyrule, mostly close to Stables. He travels Hyrule on foot instead of by boat or airship like in previous titles. His backpack is shaped like a Beetle, which customers can remember him by. Beedle stocks items such as Arrows and Materials, claiming to carry many "special Bugs." He also offers to buy things from Link, mentioning that gemstones are valuable for earning rupees. If Link speaks to Beedle with a beetle in his inventory, Beedle will ask for it in exchange for a random Food or Elixir. His favorite is the Energetic Rhino Beetle, which he says is rare. If Link denies his request, he claims his deal was good and the beetle wants to be with him. He mutters to himself that he'll sneak into Link's inventory and replace it with a regular beetle, but quickly decides to hire someone else to do it. He's surprised to see Link is still there. Wares and Pricing Beedle can be seen selling his wares outside of Dueling Peaks Stable. Wares and Pricing Other Appearances Beedle makes a minor cameo on a sign near the village in the Hyrule Circuit track with the sign having Hylian on it that translates to “Item Shop”. Beedle is a Master Spirit who owns and operates Beedle's Tent in . Beedle will excitedly greet anyone who enters his Tent, praising anyone who purchases from him. If all of Beedle's stock is purchased, he will announce that he is going to retrieve new wares. 's appearance in Beedle's Spirit Battle is a reference to Beedle's attire, whereas Toon Link's appearance is an allusion to the Hero's Clothes worn by Link in and , as well as the Recruit Uniform in . The presence of is likely an allusion to the Forest Realm of New Hyrule. Beedle is a merchant who hid himself away in order to protect himself from the sudden influx of monsters in Hyrule. He wants to make a profit off the Diamonds that monsters drop, selling Weapons and other equipment to adventurers in exchange for Diamonds in the hopes of cashing in on them. The location of his shops are random, but there will always be two hidden throughout the land either in the Grassland, Cliffs, or Desert biomes. His shops are always hidden in caves behind mounds of dirt, which must be dug away by a Shovel or blown up with an explosive. The goods that he sells are also randomized but he will always sell an Bottle in each shop for four Diamonds. Once his goods are bought, they will never restock.

The is a recurring location in . The Bell Tower goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Bell Tower is a part of the Sanctum of Hyrule Castle. It is located above the Sanctum Observation Room, and its Bell was designed to ring when a chain is pulled. Inside the Bell Tower, Link can find a stone Treasure Chest. Once it is opened, he will receive five Ancient Arrows. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found in the Bell Tower. When Link uses Archery to shoot the Balloon near the Bell Tower's ceiling, a Korok will reveal itself and give him a Korok Seed. As in , the Bell Tower sits above Hyrule Castle's Sanctum in Hyrule Field. Equipment Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

is a location in , serving as both the first and final area of the game. Features and Overview Beneath Hyrule Castle is a forbidden zone that descends into the very deepest part of Hyrule's Depths. A Stone Tablet in the Royal Hidden Passage indicates that the area beneath the castle was originally accessible through the passage. As the entrance evidently collapsed during the Upheaval, it can now only be reached through the Hyrule Castle Chasm. Prologue After Gloom started to seep out from below Hyrule Castle and made nearby people fall ill, Purah tasked Link and Zelda with investigating the source, which originated in a tunnel system deep Beneath Hyrule Castle. Entry to the tunnels below the castle is forbidden to all, including the Royal Family of Hyrule, though the reason why has been lost to history. Upon arrival to the area known as the Forgotten Foundation, Zelda notes that the concentration of Gloom found Beneath Hyrule Castle is relatively mild in spite of the effects it has on the people of the Surface. As they travel deeper, the Master Sword begins to glow, reacting to something dangerous in the area. While investigating, Zelda discovers signs of Ruins belonging to the ancient Zonai people and excitedly documents her findings with the Purah Pad. She eventually comes across a series of murals in the Forgotten Foundation, which she deduces must be about the origin of Hyrule Kingdom and the Imprisoning War that followed. Once again, she uses the Purah Pad to take Pictures of their discoveries. A series of murals to the right of the central relief are concealed by rocks, and so they cannot be viewed. thumb|left|250px|Zelda and Link enter the Imprisoning Chamber As they descend further down Beneath Hyrule Castle, the Gloom grows thicker. Eventually, they enter the Imprisoning Chamber, where they stumble upon the mummified body of Demon King Ganondorf held in place by a Right Arm. This Arm releases its grip on the body when Zelda approaches, causing the Secret Stone on the back of its hand to fall to Zelda's feet. When she picks it up, Demon King Ganondorf awakens and attacks with tendrils of Gloom. While defending her against the Gloom, Link's Master Sword is heavily damaged and breaks. Before they can muster a counterattack against the Demon King, he launches a burst of Gloom upwards, tearing the earth surrounding most of Hyrule Castle and sending it into the Sky. This also causes the ground beneath the three of them to give way, sending them all into freefall. The Secret Stone in Zelda's possession begins to glow, causing her to disappear. Link is saved by the Right Arm, which Warps him away to the Room of Awakening atop the Great Sky Island. The Imprisoning War thumb|250px|Rauru seals the Demon King Beneath Hyrule Castle is seen again in "The Imprisoning War" Memory. In the distant past, Rauru leads the Six Sages in a battle against Demon King Ganondorf to bring an end to the Imprisoning

Room of Awakening atop the Great Sky Island. The Imprisoning War thumb|250px|Rauru seals the Demon King Beneath Hyrule Castle is seen again in "The Imprisoning War" Memory. In the distant past, Rauru leads the Six Sages in a battle against Demon King Ganondorf to bring an end to the Imprisoning War. With no other choice but to sacrifice himself, Rauru relies on the Six Sages to distract the Demon King long enough to grab hold of his chest and bind his heart, simultaneously draining his Magic in the process. This sacrifice traps both of them in place for millennia while Rauru waits for Link and Zelda to arrive in the Era of the Wilds, where they can destroy Ganondorf with the Master Sword. The room in which this occurs later comes to be known as the Imprisoning Chamber. The entire area beneath the castle is sealed off throughout the ages with access forbidden to all, including the Royal Family of Hyrule. Entrance to Beneath Hyrule Castle Beneath Hyrule Castle is revisited for the final Main Quest, "Destroy Ganondorf". Demon King Ganondorf is convalescing Beneath Hyrule Castle in the Central Hyrule Depths, and can be faced here at any point after returning to the surface from the Great Sky Island. However, Link will only learn of the Demon King's location after defeating Master Kohga at the Abandoned Hebra Mine during the "Master Kohga of the Yiga Clan" Side Adventure. The destruction wrought by the Upheaval has collapsed the entrance in the Royal Hidden Passage, making it impassable. The only way to access the location is through the Hyrule Castle Chasm that has opened directly below the castle. A cave at the base of the chasm known as Gloom's Approach leads to the ruins and tunnels that make up the passage to the Forgotten Foundation. Themes and Navigation The Upheaval appears to have had a profound impact on the area; many passageways are blocked, Zonai-built structures have entered states of extreme disrepair, and an extremely high concentration of Gloom is prevalent all throughout. The Gloom has corrupted the many Monsters that now inhabit the passage, turning the area Beneath Hyrule Castle into a long and dangerous gauntlet to its deepest depths. As Link gets close to the Forgotten Foundation, any Sage Avatars he has unlocked will disappear, being unable to reach him. In the central chamber of the Forgotten Foundation, the rocks covering a series of murals can be blown apart to reveal three additional depictions: the final battle of the Imprisoning War between the Sages and Demon King Ganondorf, Zelda with the Master Sword, and her transformation into the Light Dragon. A passage descends further to Imprisoning Chamber, where the ground has since given way leading to Gloom's Lair. A stone platform reaches over the void, and Link can dive from it to begin the final confrontation. Rising out of the void is an enormous Tree-like structure made out of Suspicious-Looking Red and Black Roots. The front of the Tree bears

has since given way leading to Gloom's Lair. A stone platform reaches over the void, and Link can dive from it to begin the final confrontation. Rising out of the void is an enormous Tree-like structure made out of Suspicious-Looking Red and Black Roots. The front of the Tree bears a demonic face, with a mouth covered in brightly glowing, pulsing Gloom. When Link reaches a platform at the base, an all-out war will break out with Monsters forming the Demon King's Army being summoned in several waves. If Link has acquired the vows of any Sages, they will physically appear in-person to assist him in the battle. Following the battle, the mouth will open to reveal a passageway and Colgera, Marbled Gohma, Mucktorok, Queen Gibdo, Seized Construct, and Phantom Ganon are summoned to confront Link. At this point, the only way to move forward is to confront Demon King Ganondorf in the very deepest of the Depths, Gloom's Origin. is a recurring character in . Biography Benja is a Hylian man who is the leader of a group of Merchants, one of them being Robsten. Link finds Benja in the Gerudo Desert sands outside of Gerudo Town, watching the entrance closely. When Link speaks to him, Benja asks if Link has business with him. Link asks if he is spying and Benja immediately rejects the idea, saying that he is a Merchant and the leader of a caravan. Benja explains that he traveled all the way to Gerudo Town, but they do not allow men inside. Again, Link asks him if he is spying, and Benja defensively exclaims that it is just research and explains that he found out key information on how to sneak into Gerudo Town. Link can ask about the information, causing Benja to share his "heroic tale" with him. He says that he has been there for more than a week and that the guards have kicked him out of Gerudo Town more times than he can count. He explains that he has heard about a man who frequently travels between the Kara Kara Bazaar and Gerudo Town. Therefore, Benja has been waiting to spot this man to ask him how he is able to sneak into the town. After he finishes speaking, Link receives the "Forbidden City Entry" Main Quest. If Link speaks to Benja while wearing the Gerudo Outfit, Benja will scream and mutter that this "young lady" is just his type. Link again asks Benja if he is spying, causing Benja to nervously stutter that he is only investigating. Benja mutters to himself that this conversation seems very familiar. After Link calms the Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Benja can be found at the Kara Kara Bazaar Barracks with Robsten. He was never able to find the man who was able to sneak into Gerudo Town, and he comments about how hard it is to wait around in the unpleasant desert.

is a recurring character in . Biography Benny is a Hylian woman who can be found on a small mesa on the Mabe Prairie, which is in northeastern Hyrule Field. If Link speaks to her, she is surprised by his appearance and comments that it is rare to run into another person there. Link then asks Benny who she is, and she explains that she is a traveling adventurer. Benny continues to talk about how it is dangerous in Hyrule Field because of the Monsters, but she feels that it is worth it because of the treasure she finds. She then tells Link that high vantage points are great for spotting things of interest, encouraging him to survey the area from the top of the rock behind her. If Link talks to Benny again, she again reminds him that looking from somewhere high up is the best way to find something. She then tells Link that he can take any of the nearby Cooking ingredients he wants and use her Cooking Pot. In the Gerudo Highlands, Benny can be found in a remote area being attacked by a red Bokoblin. If Link talks to Benny after she has been defeated by the Bokoblin, she asks for space and eventually moves to her nearby shelter to rest.

is a recurring character in . Biography Bertri is a Gerudo Soldier who can be found in the Royal Palace of Gerudo Town. She guards one of the entrances to Riju's Bedroom upstairs, and she carries a Gerudo Spear. When Link initially tries to go past her, Bertri stops him and tells him that he better leave if he does not want to be skewered. After Link has recovered the Thunder Helm from the Yiga Clan Hideout, Bertri is shocked that Link has permission to enter Riju's Bedroom and asks who he is. After clearing the Sand Shroud, Bertri is found guarding Kara Kara Bazaar. When talking to Link, she will mention his skill in battle and thank him for helping.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Big Hearty Radishes are flora that are found in various grassy areas of Hyrule, characterized by their forked and flowering stalk. The Vegetable itself cannot be seen until it is picked, as it is a root. As their name implies, Big Hearty Radishes are larger versions of the Hearty Radish. Big Hearty Radishes can be eaten raw to restore four Hearts. If a Big Hearty Radish is roasted over a Campfire, it becomes a Roasted Big Radish. If a Big Hearty Radish is Cooked in a Cooking Pot, the resulting Food will grant Link Extra Hearts. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Big Hearty Radishes are one of the ingredients that can be used to make Peach Dye. Making Creamy Heart Soup in a Cooking Pot requires Link to use either a Hearty Radish or a Big Hearty Radish: Big Hearty Radishes, among other Vegetables, can also be used to make the following Meals: Big Hearty Radishes are Vegetables that can be found growing on Sky Islands. They can also be grown by Uma at the School's Field in Hateno Village, though due to her inexperience in growing them, she can only raise two at a time. Big Hearty Radishes are marked by Flowers growing off of them. They restore all of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge and grant him several Extra Hearts when Cooked into Meals. When exposed to Fire or Scorching Climates, they become into Roasted Big Radishes. Either Big Hearty Radishes or Hearty Radishes are required as part of the recipe for Creamy Heart Soup: They can also be used to make the following Meals: Other Appearances Big Hearty Radishes can be sold for 15 Rupees. Big Hearty Radishes are Materials in .

, also known as White Hearty Truffles, are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Big Hearty Truffles are a more rare yet more effective version of the regular Hearty Truffle. Though they were once regular Hearty Truffles, being left unpicked for years and has caused them to grow larger. They can be found growing at the base of Trees in the Hebra Mountains and the Great Hyrule Forest. Like all hearty-type foods, Big Hearty Truffles can be Cooked in a Cooking Pot to restore Link's Life Gauge and increase his maximum health, though it increases the Heart count more than a regular Hearty Truffle. They can be eaten for three Hearts, which is more than the normal Hearty Truffle. Big Hearty Truffles exposed to Fire become Toasted Big Hearty Truffles. They can be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to create Black Dye. Big Hearty Truffles, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Big Hearty Truffles, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Other Appearances Big Hearty Truffles can be sold for 15 Rupees. Big Hearty Truffle are Materials in .

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Big Twin Bridge is one of two bridges that cross Squabble River to the east of Dueling Peaks. The second bridge is the Little Twin Bridge. The Big Twin Bridge is mostly dilapidated and has pieces missing. Debris has also built upon the eastern side, including dead Trees, stone wreckage, and a stone slab. A traveler named Mezer can be seen crossing the Bridge. A stone Treasure Chest containing an Opal can be found under the rock slab off the eastern side of the Bridge. In Master Mode, there is a platform held aloft by Sky Octoroks that holds a Treasure Chest containing a Soldier's Spear. Creatures Enemies Equipment

The Biggoron's Sword is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses In , the Biggoron's Sword is a far sturdier version of the Giant's Knife, which Biggoron crafted for the Master Craftsman, and is a very powerful sword. It can be obtained completing the Trading Game. The blade is much longer than the Master Sword and deals twice as much damage. Its handle also changes from yellow to blue. However, it must be wielded with two hands, meaning that Link cannot defend with a Shield while equipped. If the Shield button is pressed, he attempts to protect himself with the blade. Despite being the strongest Weapon, the Biggoron's Sword is incapable of defeating Ganon as only the Master Sword can deliver the final blow. However, it can be useful during the final battle, as Ganon knocks the Master Sword out of reach before getting it back. left The Biggoron's Sword is the strongest Sword in . It can only be acquired in a Linked Game by using Secrets. The Biggoron's Sword is obtained from Biggoron himself. While every other Item in these games is assigned to one hand and can be used in conjunction with another, the Biggoron's Sword takes up both slots as it is held with both hands. Link swings it in a whole 180-degree arc, as opposed to the other Swords' 90-degree slash. The Biggoron's Sword is 67% stronger than the Noble Sword and 150% stronger than the Wooden Sword. Excluding the 180-degree arc, the only other difference from the Master Sword is that it can kill Armos in one hit. The Biggoron's Sword is the strongest Sword in , as it works exactly as Seasons. It can only be acquired in a Linked Game by using Secrets. The Biggoron's Sword is obtained from the Goron Elder who resides at the Goron Shooting Gallery, after telling him the Elder Secret and scoring 300 points at the Shooting Gallery. The Biggoron's Sword is 67% stronger than the Noble Sword and 150% stronger than the Wooden Sword. Excluding the 180-degree arc, the only other difference from the Master Sword is that it can kill Armos in one hit. In , the Biggoron's Sword is an amiibo exclusive two-handed Weapon. The Weapon will rarely appear in a Treasure Chest after scanning the Link amiibo using the amiibo Rune, but only after freeing one of the Divine Beasts. It is noted to have been forged by a Goron craftsman for a hero who travelled through time, with a cutting edge that speaks to its creator's mastery. It has a base attack power of 50. Biggoron's Sword is made of metal, and will therefore attract Lightning if it is equipped during a Thunderstorm and conduct Electricity. It will also sink in Water, but since it is magnetic, it can be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, it will not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Biggoron's Swords reappear in . is a character in . Biography Billson is an employee of Hudson Construction. He is responsible for working on Skyview Towers, which takes him to several locations throughout Hyrule. Billson can initially be found at a campsite north of the Hyrule Field Skyview Tower. He explains what it is to Link and advises him to visit Purah at Lookout Landing for more information. After the Lookout Landing Skyview Tower is activated, he can be found at the Sahasra Slope Skyview Tower and the Thyphlo Ruins Skyview Tower. After both of the Skyview Towers have been activated and Lurelin Village has been restored, Billson heads to Lurelin Village so her can eat Fish. He can be found next to a single Palm Tree east of the Fishing Resort with Frita. When spoken to, he expresses how glad he is to relax, and he also notes how different Lurelin is from Rito Village.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Bird Eggs are Materials that can be found in Birds' nests atop Trees throughout Hyrule. They are also sold at the East Wind and High Spirits Produce, as well as by the travelling Merchant Agus. They can be eaten raw to restore a Heart or used as a Cooking Ingredient to make various Foods. Bird Eggs become Campfire Eggs when exposed to Fire and Hard-Boiled Eggs when dropped in Hot Springs. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Bird Eggs can be used to make Yellow Dye.
