The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Biron Snowshelf is located in the Hebra Mountains, overlooking Lake Kilsie between the Hebra Peak and the Hebra West Summit. The area is a large, flat plateau covered with Snow and a few hills, though the Snowshelf also includes the slope leading down to Sturnida Basin. This slope is crossed by a natural rock formation known as the Big Bridge. Two Koroks can be found in the Biron Snowshelf, and they are both underneath rocks. The first one is around the middle of the Snowshelf, a small crevasse digs into the Snowshelf from the west. Down in this ravine, the first Korok hides under a rock. The Second Korok is southeast of the first one, under a rock on a small platform of bigger rocks. Creatures Enemies Normal Mode Master Mode Materials Treasure Chests Sub-Bosses

are recurring Enemies in the . Characteristics Black Bokoblins are a stronger variant of Bokoblin, and they are considered to be one of the most dangerous. They are much more resilient and are usually armed with stronger Weapons than their common counterparts, including Dragonbone Boko Clubs and Dragonbon Boko Bats. Black Bokoblins can be found in Monster Strongholds and occasionally on roads, where they may attack passing travelers. Black Bokoblins can also sometimes be found going on hunts while riding Horses. Black Bokoblins share an attack pattern with other Bokoblin counterparts. On the ground, Black Bokoblins mainly attack by swinging and slamming their held Weapons. In the event that their Weapons is lost or stolen, they will search for any other available Weapons nearby and use them instead. In some Monster Strongholds, Black Bokoblins may also be found standing on top watch towers, where they may alert other Monsters to Link's presence by blowing a horn. These Black Bokoblins may also be equipped with Bows that they use to snipe intruders with Arrows. When defeated, Black Bokoblins may drop Bokoblin Fangs, Bokoblin Horns, or Bokoblin Guts. Drops Black Bokoblins reappear in , acting mostly the same as they did in . They are now capable of wearing backpacks to carry Materials and wearing Rock Armor to protect themselves. Black Bokoblins will use a variety of attacks depending on what weapon they have equipped. They are able to ram Link with their new Black Bokoblin Horns. They also swing or spin One-Handed Weapons, and they can guard themselves with Shields. Black Bokoblins can sometimes be found in Monster Outposts and Monster Strongholds. In these camps, they can be found guarding Treasure Chests, which may contain a Weapon or Gem. They sleep during the night and are awake during the day. Sometimes, Black Bokoblins can be seen eating Meat by their Campfires. Sometimes, Black Bokoblins may guard their camps from a small watchtower. Black Bokoblins may be found in camp, or on patrol with Blue Boss Bokoblins or Black Boss Bokoblins. In these cases, Black Bokoblins will follow the commands of their Boss Bokoblin. Other Appearances left Black Bokoblins appear as enemies in where they move to the beat of the music. They're stronger than the Green Bokoblin and Red Bokoblin, but share the same beat pattern as they raise their arms up for one beat before moving on the following beat. In , Black Bokoblins appear as the second strongest type of Bokoblin, first appearing in the Scenario "Calamity Strikes." They may drop a Bokoblin Fang, a Bokoblin Horn, or Bokoblin Guts. At the end of a Battle, a Bokoblin Trophy will be awarded for each defeated. Black Bokoblins as they appeared in are featured in .

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Black Boss Bokoblins are the second-most powerful version of Boss Bokoblin. They drop Black Boss Bokoblin Horns upon defeat, as well as the usual Fangs and Guts. In battle, they command a troop of Black Bokoblin to do various attacks. However, if Link gets too close, they will not be afraid to join the fight themselves. They can wield Fused weapons such as a weapon with a Hylian Shroom on it. Outside of battle, they will patrol a set route with their troop. Other Appearances Black Boss Bokoblins serve as Powerful Enemies in .

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Black Lizalfos are a stronger variant of Lizalfos. They are known to carry stronger pieces of Lizalfos Gear, resulting in them being regarded as more dangerous. Like most Lizalfos, Black Lizalfos can be found swimming in bodies of Water, such as lakes or seas. They can also be found within Monster Strongholds. Drops Black Lizalfos appear in with largely the same appearance as they have in . The primary distinction is that they have larger, upright horns resembling notched blades. Other Appearances In , Black Lizalfos are stronger than Blue Lizalfos and Green Lizalfos, possessing more health and attack power than their weaker counterparts. Unlike the Green Lizalfos, they wield spears that can hit Cadence, Link, Yves and Zelda at a farther distance. However, they do share the same beat pattern as other Lizalfos, standing still until the player walks in front of them, prompting them to charge forward. When attacking, they move in a straight line on every single beat until they collide into something, becoming stunned for three music beats and therefore vulnerable. If not slain within that period of time, they will regain consciousness on the fourth beat and either resume standing in one place or repeating their attack pattern. Black Lizalfos as they appeared in return as Enemies in .

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Black Moblins are tall and heavy Monsters that can be found all over Hyrule. They are stronger, more resilient variants of Moblins, and they are known to carry the stronger Moblin Gear or other Weapons. When defeated, they drop Moblin Horns, Moblin Fangs, and Moblin Guts. Drops Black Moblins reappear in , acting similarly to how they did in . They have new Black Moblin Horns, which they slam into the ground while attacking. It is possible to encounter Gloom-Wreathed variants of Black Moblins. Other Appearances left Black Moblins are stronger than Red Moblins, possessing more health and attack power, along with having more powerful spears that they can throw at Cadence, Link, Yves, and Zelda. They move to the beat of the music and share the same beat pattern as the other Moblins, moving on every other beat, having to crouch for one beat before hopping to an adjacent tile on the second beat. When they're close enough, they will throw a spear at the heroes, stopping on one beat to aim, throwing it on the second, and letting it land on the third beat. Afterwards, they will try to retrieve their weapon until it is either destroyed or picked up by another Moblin or even the hero if they are using the Power Glove. Once they lose their spear, they will try to look for another one or if there are none, try to attack the heroes head on. Their spears are the second-strongest, dealing 3 Hearts of damage to any enemy that get hit by them, being second to only the Purple Moblin spear in terms of power. During the events of Symphony of the Mask, Black Skull Moblins appear but otherwise act the same as in the main game. Black Moblins reappear as Powerful Foes in , first appearing in the Scenario "The Road Home, Besieged". During certain Challenges added in the Downloadable Content pack, some carry containers holding Bomb Barrels on their backs. A variant utilizing Sky Octoroks appears during the Scenario "EX Liberate the Ancient Lab". Two Black Moblins are also absorbed by Harbinger Ganon to recover its health after taking a beating from Terrako. Defeated Black Moblins most often drop Moblin Fangs and Horns, but may also rarely drop Moblin Guts. Slaying one awards a Moblin Trophy at the end of a Battle. A Treasure Chest containing a Weapon may also appear. Black Moblins can be encountered as Powerful Enemies.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Locations and Uses Bladed Rhino Beetles can be found on Trees in the Region of Necluda. They can be combined with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot to make a Mighty Elixir, which increases attack damage when consumed. The Kochi Dye Shop accepts Bladed Rhino Beetles as an ingredient to make Navy Dye. If Link approaches Beedle with at least one Bladed Rhino Beetle in his Inventory, Beedle will offer to trade it in exchange for a Mighty Elixir. If Link agrees to the trade, Beedle promises to cherish it for the rest of his life. Beedle will also be happy, remarking that he is adding it to his Beetle collection. When Link speaks to Beedle afterwards, he claims to still be excited about the Beetle. He claims that if Link has another, he should give it to him tomorrow, as he is going to be focusing on his new Beetle for the rest of the day. If Link refuses, Beedle states that he misjudged Link's character. Bladed Rhino Beetles are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Bladon is a Goron who lives in Goron City with his younger brother Gonguron. Bladon is furious with his brother because he had left to find the "secret of the hero," a mystery believed to be hidden in Gorko Tunnel. Bladon believes that his brother is just using it as an excuse to slack off. Speaking with him begins the first phase in the "A Brother's Roast" Shrine Quest. Upon finding Gonguron in Gorko Tunnel, it is discovered that he has collasped from hunger and is unable to continue excavating the Tunnel. Bladon then shortly arrives. He instructs Link to bring back a Rock Roast from Gortram Cliff, claiming that he cannot do it himself as he has a chronic condition called Goron shoulder. Bladon cooks the Rock Roast that Link brings back, which invigorates Gonguron and gives him the needed strength to continue. It is then revealed that the hero's secret is actually the Kayra Mah Shrine. After finding the Ancient Shrine, Bladon and Gonguron return to their home in Goron City. The finding of the hero's secret has inspired Gonguron and he now digs in their home while Bladon cheers on. Bladon says that he is proud of him and must train harder to keep up. However, he is also concerned that Gonguron's digging will ruin their house. Bladon also claims that discovering the hero's secret has cured his shoulder, though he also admits how similar it is to the Ancient Shrine near Goron City.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Blatchery Plain is located in West Necluda between the Dueling Peaks and Fort Hateno. Blatchery Plain is a flat section of land covered in tall Grass that is surrounded by high cliffs and the Squabble River. In the center of the Blatchery Plain, a Monster Encampment sits near some pillars and ruins. Celessa can be found walking the Road through the Plain, talking about the battle that took place in the Plain years before. Another traveler, Agus walks along the road with her Donkey. She will sell various things to Link if he talks to her. Two travelers, Joute and Toma, can be seen riding along the road on horseback. During the second Great Calamity, Blatchery Plain was overrun with Guardians that were making their way to Fort Hateno. After Link fell in battle to a Guardian, Zelda's powers awoke and she destroyed most of the surrounding Guardians. Consequently, several Fallen Guardians litter the Plain and can be searched for Ancient Materials. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests Blatchery Plain reappears in .

are Room Units in . Location and Uses Blessing Rooms are Room Units that feature a shrine and a Goddess Statue. As part of Hudson Construction's Dream Home program, Link can buy Blessing Rooms from Grantéson for 400 Rupees each. While constructing his House, Link can use Ultrahand to manipulate Blessing Rooms and attach them to other Room Units. If a Blessing Room is unused and left outside of Link's housing plot following construction, Grantéson will store it for him. Link is able to pray to the Goddess Statue inside of a Blessing Room, allowing him to exchange four Light of Blessing for either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. He can also trade four Sage's Will to deepen the bond he has with any Sage.

are a recurring Weather mechanic in . Blizzards go unnamed in and . Overview Blizzards occur in certain areas of Frozen Hyrule. While present, Snow falls and harsh gusts of Wind that cover the screen and damage the Links if they are not in a Cave intermittently appear. Blizzards are a common Weather event in Freezing Climates, particularly on Mount Lanayru, the Hebra Mountains, and the Gerudo Highlands. During a Blizzard, heavy amounts of Snow fall from the sky. Visibility is reduced during this time, though they are not impossible to navigate. Blizzards are still frequent within Freezing Climates, especially in relation to Mount Lanayru, the Hebra Mountains, and the Gerudo Highlands. As a result of Colgera's presence in the Hebra Mountains Sky, a large Blizzard has appeared over a majority of the Hebra Region. Blizzard also occur when Link faces a Frost Gleeok. Blizzards occur on Hebra Mountain, causing Freezing Climates as a result of their presence. Initially, the entire Mountain is subject to a Blizzard, but it eventually shifts to only cover its lowest level during the Main Quest "Rift on Holy Mount Lanayru".

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Blizzrobes are a variant of the Ice Wizzrobe. They attack by using their Blizzard Rods to dispel a huge freezing blast of air, in addition to summoning Monsters such as Ice Chuchus or Ice Keese. They also cause blizzards that decrease the surrounding area's temperature, making it too cold for Link without cold-resistant Armor and Elixirs. Like other Wizzrobes, Blizzrobes will turn invisible after attacking, leaving ripples in the air with each footstep. Striking them in the head with an Arrow will stun them, allowing Link an opportunity to attack. Hitting them with Fire-based attacks, such as those from a Fire Arrow or a Flameblade, will immediately evaporate a Blizzrobe. When defeated, Blizzrobes drop their Blizzard Rod. Instead of a Blizzard Rod, Blizzrobes now carry a Magic Rod that has been Fused to a Sapphire. Link can defeat them in one hit by Fusing Fire-type Materials to an Arrow, such as Fire Fruits or Red Chuchu Jelly. Other Appearances Blizzrobes appear as Powerful Foes in the Downloadable Content pack for .

Blood Moons, also known as Red Moons and the Nights of the Red Moon, are a recurring event in . Overview Blood Moons occur at midnight on nights when Calamity Ganon's power reaches its peak and escapes from Zelda's control within Hyrule Castle, dyeing the night sky and the Moon red with Malice. The effects of this Malice revive any fallen Monsters and Enemies, returning them to where they once were prior to being slain. The effects of the Blood Moon begin around 11:30 PM, though the Blood Moon itself can usually be seen as early as 10:00 PM when the Moon rises into the sky. At 11:30 PM, Malice will rise from the ground, like when Link is aboard a corrupted Divine Beast, around Pools of Malice, or on the grounds of Hyrule Castle. At 11:50 PM, the sky will turn red, and the clouds will begin to fly by very fast. When midnight hits, a cutscene begins where the Blood Moon has risen, and Monsters are seen respawning across Hyrule. Princess Zelda telepathically informs Link that the Blood Moon has risen and urges Link to be careful. After that, the Blood Moon dissipates. Hino of the Dueling Peaks Stable is the primary source of information on Blood Moons, and can be seen acting strangely during the time period that it affects the overworld. Link can determine if that night will be a Blood Moon, as if he asks Hino what moon will be out tonight, he will say; "I'm getting that feeling again... Something is going to happen tonight. I can taste it". For the time from 11:30 PM to 12:15 AM when Malice lingers in the air for, certain other effects of the Blood Moon can be seen. Hino will seemingly be inflicted with lunacy and begin to run in circles shouting. Cooking during this time gives Food an effect boost, as noted in Chef Aurie Taamu, Vol. 2. This time period is also when standing on the Pedestal at Washa's Bluff will allow Mijah Rokee Shrine to appear. These effects wear off at 12:15 and will not occur again until the next regular Blood Moon. Blood Moons are always represented by a full Moon regardless of which phase the Moon is in. Blood Moons reappear in where they serve the same function, though as a result of Ganondorf's power rather than Calamity Ganon. Correspondingly, Gloom fills the air and revives Monsters rather than Malice. Unlike in , if a Blood Moon occurs while Link passes time, the Gloom lingers and fades from the air afterwards, no matter the time of day. The first time the Blood Moon occurs, a cutscene plays depicting it reviving Monsters, while Zelda narrates an explanation of the Monsters rising just as they did in the Imprisoning War. A shorter version of this cutscene plays every subsequent time. After it is revealed that Zelda was actually a Phantom Ganon impostor, the cutscene will play but without narration. The Blood Moon also appears

Zelda narrates an explanation of the Monsters rising just as they did in the Imprisoning War. A shorter version of this cutscene plays every subsequent time. After it is revealed that Zelda was actually a Phantom Ganon impostor, the cutscene will play but without narration. The Blood Moon also appears in certain Memories, where it is shown to be a direct result of Ganondorf's power. In "Birth of the Demon King" after Ganondorf steals Sonia's Secret Stone, Gloom comes forth from his body and creates armies of Monsters under the glow of an unnaturally giant Blood Moon. It is seen again when he and his army attack in "The Demon King's Army". During the "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" Main Quest, a large Blood Moon rises when the puppet Zelda appears to lure Link to Hyrule Castle. Similarly, when the Demon Dragon's final weak point is revealed, the sky shifts to red as an enormous Blood Moon looms. Hino reappears, now a dedicated researcher of the Blood Moon. He can be found in a cage in several Monster Strongholds in need of rescue. When Link saves him, he will explain he was attempting to study the Blood Moon by getting close to Monsters but got captured. He will then tell Link the current phase of the Moon, and still displays signs of lunacy if it is a Blood Moon. Mechanics The function of the Blood Moon is to revive slain Enemies and respawn Weapons. Contrary to what it may seem, the Blood Moon does not act as a "world reset" mechanic (Materials and other objects are not respawned), nor does it serve to clear the game's memory. The statuses of slain Enemies and obtained Weapons are always kept in memory. However, if certain, specific conditions are met regarding memory usage, a "forced Blood Moon" (see below) can occur to reload the game world in order to clear the game's memory. The Blood Moon is simply the game mechanic used to execute this. Scheduling and prohibition The Blood Moon is not dependent on in-game days such as the Moon's cycle nor the amount of Enemies killed, but rather a running timer of real time spent in-game (not in menus or loading screens). When this timer is checked, a Blood Moon is scheduled for the next midnight. This is why the Blood Moon can occur if Link passes the night using a Bed or Campfire on such a night; but continually doing so will not speed up the arrival of the Blood Moon if one is not scheduled– in fact, this only serves to effectively delay it since the timer does not run during cutscenes. If certain conditions are met on a night when the Blood Moon is scheduled, it will be pushed to the next night. Taking advantage of these conditions every night means that a Blood Moon can technically be indefinitely postponed, unless one is forced. In In , the Blood Moon timer is 168 minutes (2 hours 48 minutes, or 7 days in-game) begins upon leaving the Shrine of Resurrection. This timer is checked every night at midnight, and if it exceeds 2 hours 48 minutes, a Blood Moon is scheduled for the following night. In , conditions that prohibit a scheduled Blood Moon include: Link has not yet left the Great Plateau, i.e. before landing when "Hyrule Kingdom" appears on screen Link is not in the main overworld (i.e. inside an Ancient Shrine, a Divine Beast, or the Sword Monk's Shrine) Link is in Hyrule Castle The story events battling Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Vah Ruta or Vah Naboris are ongoing Link is in the Yiga Clan Hideout Dark Beast Ganon is being fought The One-Hit Obliterator section of the "EX The Champions' Ballad" Quest is active Saving and Warping are disabled: i.e. Link is in a cutscene, a Mini-Game is active, or the Yiga Blademaster in "The Stolen Heirloom" Shrine Quest is being fought Note that unlike with the other three Divine Beast battles, Blood Moons can occur during the Vah Rudania battle with Yunobo. If this happens, the Sentries will not be revived, but the Black Moblins in the area will. In In , the Blood Moon timer is reduced to only 144 minutes (2 hours 24 minutes, or 6 in-game days). This timer begins upon receiving the Main Quest "The Closed Door" from Rauru at the Temple of Time. The timer is checked every frame instead of only at midnight as in , and if the time is exceeded and it is before 9 PM (so as to allow the Moon to rise), the Blood Moon will appear that night. Both of these mean Blood Moons are scheduled to happen more frequently in than in . In , the following conditions are known to prohibit a scheduled Blood Moon: Link has not yet completed the Great Sky Island Link is in the Depths Link is inside a Shrine of Light Link is in a Temple or Hyrule Castle Link in the progress of building a Dream Home Link is assisting a Monster-Control Crew squad in battle A Mini-Game is active Forced Blood Moons have different checks; see below. Forced Blood Moons If certain conditions are met in regards to the game's memory allocation, a so-called "forced Blood Moon" (also known as a "panic Blood Moon", and internally referred to as having the reason ForMemory as opposed to Schedule) may be induced regardless of the usual timer and time of day. This is not influenced by killing Enemies, postponing regular Blood Moons, or any other player actions, nor is it a generic fallback mechanic for errors; it simply occurs because something in the current game state is causing trouble with certain subsystems for loading and handling resources. Forced Blood Moons reset the entire "game scene", effectively the same as when going through a loading screen (e.g. when Warping, or going from a Shrine to the overworld). This is why certain Objects' positions are reset, and notably Enemies will regain any health they lost. Because a forced Blood Moon uses the normal cutscene, it will revive Enemies and Weapons. However, this has no effect on the regular Blood Moon timer, and does not have the other properties of regularly scheduled Blood Moons, such as Cooking boosts, affecting Hino, or enabling Mijah Rokee Shrine to appear. While forced Blood Moons do not rely on the prohibitions that apply regularly, Link still must be in the overworld with no event in progress, as well as several other technical checks. However, this does allow for a rare chance for a Blood Moon to occur in places it normally would not, one notable example being a forced Blood Moon occurring while Link is battling Calamity Ganon, replenishing the Boss's health. However, in , a forced Blood Moon cannot happen during the War in the Depths of Hyrule (fighting the Demon King's Army and subsequent boss rush), or while battling Demon King Ganondorf and the Demon Dragon. In , there are also four circular areas surrounding the locations of the "Regional Phenomena" Main Quest (Rito Village, Goron City, Zora's Domain and Gerudo Town) that force an immediate Blood Moon when entered if Link has not experienced one before. The reason for this being implemented is unknown. Moon remains in the sky until Calamity Ganon is sealed again. Following the completion of the last Scenario and the start of the postgame, Blood Moons start appearing. They turn Scenarios into Blood Moon Battlefields. These Blood Moon Battlefield events enhance the Enemies of past Scenarios, one Scenario per waxing, changing the icon of the boosted Scenario into a Blood Moon icon, raises the recommended levels by up to sixfold, and colors the map with a red filter. It also improves the quality of Weapon drops, and increases their frequency. When a Blood Moon rises, it changes the map theme to its "Amid the Calamity" version. Other than doubling the Rupee counts after completing the Scenario battles, including the Divine Beast combat segments, nothing else changes. It is up to random chance which Scenarios becomes a Blood Moon Battlefield, and the frequency of the Blood Moon waxing is erratic, ranging from a Blood Moon rising immediately after clearing a Blood Moon Battlefield to after several battles. Potentially, a Blood Moon could rise over the same Scenario twice in a row. If players go to Challenge maps or other Scenario maps, it resets the Blood Moon Battlefield.

is a recurring character in . Biography Bludo is the Chief of the Gorons in the Eldin Region and the founder of the Goron Group Mining Company. He lives in Goron City in the Boss's House. Bludo has a number of Cannons around Eldin that only he is able to operate. Whenever the Divine Beast Vah Rudania starts terrorizing the Gorons, he and his partner, Yunobo, leave to drive it away. Working in tandem, Bludo operates the Cannons while Yunobo acts as the cannonball using Daruk's Protection. Despite their many attempts, though, Vah Rudania always returns. When Link arrives at Goron City, he will find Bludo cursing Divine Beast Vah Rudania in frustration. He explains that the Divine Beast's rampage have worsened the eruptions from Death Mountain. There is a legend that, 100 years ago, it used to protect the Gorons, but Bludo states that times have changed since then. Rudania has disrupted the Goron Group Mining Company's operations, leading to suffering for all of the Gorons. In his anger, Bludo accidentally throws out his back, though he dismisses it when Link asks if he is alright. At this point in the conversation, Bludo realizes he does not know who Link is. When Link reveals that he is a traveler, Bludo is honored that he came so far to pay his respects to him. He then properly introduces himself to Link. Bludo was planning to drive away Vah Rudania again, but he is unable while his back hurts. He quietly wonders where Yunobo went, explaining that he is a young Goron who helps him with the task. However, he has not returned after setting out to the Abandoned North Mine to retrieve Bludo's painkillers. Believing that Yunobo is slacking off, Bludo asks Link to tell Yunobo to return if he sees him. With this, the "Divine Beast Vah Rudania" Main Quest will begin. After Link rescues Yunobo and returns to Goron City, Bludo reveals that Yunobo told what happened. Since Hylians need rewards, Bludo gives Link three Fireproof Elixirs. Now that he has taken his painkillers, Bludo is ready to meet up with Yunobo to face Divine Beast Vah Rudania. While he does not wish to disrespect the legacy of Daruk, he is eager to send the Divine Beast back again. At Link's confusion, Bludo is shocked to hear that he does not know who Daruk is. He points out the Goron Stone Memorial, explaining that it depicts Daruk. Seeing the statue triggers the "Daruk's Mettle" Recovered Memory. Although Bludo is confused by Link's reaction, he adds that Yunobo is a descendant of Daruk, and is thus able to use his ability. Bludo reveals that Yunobo uses it to stay safe while they fire him at Divine Beast Vah Rudania, as it is the only way to scare it off. Just as Bludo is about to leave to meet up with Yunobo, his back flares up again. When Link asks if he is alright, Bludo grumpily replies that he is

safe while they fire him at Divine Beast Vah Rudania, as it is the only way to scare it off. Just as Bludo is about to leave to meet up with Yunobo, his back flares up again. When Link asks if he is alright, Bludo grumpily replies that he is not. With no other choice, he is forced to cancel his plans. He asks Link to find Yunobo at the Bridge of Eldin and inform him of the news. Ater Link has freed Divine Beast Vah Rudania, he meets with Yunobo in Goron City, who tells him that Bludo wants to see him and should not be kept waiting. At the Boss's House, Bludo thanks Link for all he has done and admits that he is impressed. However, Bludo is teases Link about the fact that he did so just when his back pain went away, as now it looks like he was faking it to avoid the battle. He is also relieved that the experience has helped Yunobo mature, crediting Link with the achievement. Finally, Bludo points out Divine Beast Vah Rudania on top of Death Mountain, which has now returned to its peaceful self. Now, the Goron Group Mining Company will be able to return to mining near the volcano. Suddenly, Bludo remembers that he still needs to reward Link. He allows Link to keep the contents of the Treasure Chest in his House, which he claims is a blade once used by Daruk. Inside the Chest, Link will find the Boulder Breaker. If Link does not already have the Master Sword, Bludo will recount the legend that states it is sleeping in a forest. He suggests that Link try to search for the Sword. When Link speaks to Bludo, he will remark that it is scorching out. Link will be able to ask him about the Master Sword, Boulder Breaker, or Divine Beast Vah Rudania. Bludo explains that the Master Sword, known as the Sword that Seals the Darkness, once belonged to the Hylian Champion. That Sword was supposedly stronger than the Boulder Breaker. If Link has the Master Sword, Bludo will notice the sharp blade he carries and wonders where he got it. If Link asks about the Boulder Breaker, Bludo explains that he should seek out Rohan if he ever loses it. He repeats that it once belonged to Daruk, sharing a rumor that Daruk used to fan himself with it. Finally, if Link asks about Divine Beast Vah Rudania's location, Bludo tells him it is still where he left it. He is grateful that Link defeated the Divine Beast, as that meant he did not have to do it himself. If Downloadable Content Pack is downloaded, Link can ask Bludo about Daruk during the "EX Champion Daruk's Song" Main Quest. are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Blue-Maned Lynels are a stronger variation of regular Lynels that have inhabited Hyrule since ancient times. They carry the "Mighty" set of Lynel Gear, which includes the Mighty Lynel Sword, Mighty Lynel Shield, Mighty Lynel Bow, Mighty Lynel Spear, and Mighty Lynel Crusher. In Master Mode, they carry the regular Lynel Gear set. Though facing them is dangerous, it is recommended to be prepared if one must fight them. Like other Lynels, Blue-Maned Lynels will often refrain from attacking for a short period of time after spotting Link, instead opting to stare down its opponent. Though they commonly wield Shock Arrows, certain Blue-Maned Lynels may carry Ice Arrows or Fire Arrows. Though most Lynels will Progress past Blue-Maned Lynels as the World Level increases, the Blue-Maned Lynel in the First Gatehouse of Hyrule Castle will always remain as such. Drops Blue-Maned Lynels reappear in . Other Appearances Blue-Maned Lynels reappear in as Powerful Foes, first appearing in the "Akkala Tower" Scenario. More can be encountered later on during various Challenges. They may drop Lynel Guts, Hooves, or Horns. For each Blue-Maned Lynel slain, the Warriors will be awarded a Lynel Trophy and a Wooden Chest containing a Weapon. Blue-Maned Lynels are Powerful Enemies in .

are recurring Enemies in . Blue-colored Bokoblins appear in and , but they are unnamed and known as their default color variants. Characteristics In , Blue Bokoblins are much stronger than a Red Bokoblin. Their skin and clothing differs depending on the different environments, but they still have the same fixation with exotic undergarments. Blue Bokoblins wear chainmail vest and shorts, also adorning a bandana similar to Red Bokoblins (Leader) and gold ringers on their fingers. The Blue Bokoblin swords are black scimitars contrasting the Machetes used by Red Bokoblins and the hammers used by Green Bokoblins. They fight the same way as their weaker variants, but can also do a Jump Attack. During the Horde Battle, the Blue Bokoblin found near the final entrance can do a charging attack similar to Ghirahim in his first fight. In , Blue Bokoblins are stronger a stronger variation of Bokoblins, as they have more health and wield stronger Bokoblin Gear and Weapons. They are more clever than regular Bokoblins, knowing to kick away Remote Bombs to avoid an explosion. In Master Mode, they are the first type of Bokoblin encountered in . During the Recovered Memory "A Premonition", one Blue Bokoblin can be seen amongst the Monsters that have been defeated by Link. As part of the "Missing in Action" Side Quest, Blue Bokoblins can be found attacking Canolo, Flaxel, Oliff, and Palme on the Koukot Plateau Path. When Link defeats the Blue Bokoblins, the will leave for Gerudo Canyon Stable to meet with Sesami. Drops Blue Bokoblins appear as Enemies in . They resemble their counterparts, but with longer, forked Horns. Some Blue Bokoblins wear Rock Armor, which protects them from damage. This Rock Armor displays a yellow health bar and can be broken with blunt Weapons and explosions. Other Appearances In , Blue Bokoblins appear as an upgrade to Bokoblins and just like their weaker counterparts, can act as standard troops and large Powerful Foes. Both types of Blue Bokoblin can toss their Weapons at the Warriors and then immediately take out a duplicate Weapon after finishing their ranged attack. When defeated, Blue Bokoblins may drop Bokoblin Fangs, Guts, or Horns. They will always award a Bokoblin Trophy.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Blue Lizalfos are a stronger variation of the regular green Lizalfos, as they are knwon to have more health and carry stronger Lizalfos Gear and other Weapons. Like other Lizalfos, they can be often be found in or around bodies of Water, such as lakes and rivers. However, they also inhabit much of the Gerudo Desert. Drops Blue Lizalfos reappear in , acting mostly the same as they do in . However, they have new horns known as Blue Lizalfos Horns, which they can attack Link with. Other Appearances In , Blue Lizalfos are not stronger than Green Lizalfos, but they do wield Spears, giving them a much farther reach when they attack. While their movement is bound to the beat of the music, they typically stand still until one of the heroes crosses their path. Once they have a hero within their sights, they will proceed to charge at them within a straight line, moving on every beat until they collide into something or the hero stops their attack with their Weapon, stunning them for three beats. While stunned, they are rendered completely defenseless until they regain consciousness on the fourth beat, returning to their original stance to look for targets.

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Blue Moblins first appear in , being seen in forest areas like the Lost Woods. They act the same as Moblins, but can withstand more hits. Blue Moblins later reappear in as the strongest variety of Moblin. Like other Moblins, they attack by throwing their Spears or jabbing Link with them, while also draining his experience points if they land a hit on him. In , Blue Moblins are first found as a Miniboss in Dragon Roost Cavern, then appearing as a common Enemy afterwards. They are fought the same way as regular Moblins, but do not wield Lanterns. In , Blue Moblins are found all over Hyrule, being a stronger variation of the regular Moblin. They are known by their tall and heavyweight stature, and they carry stronger Moblin Gear and other Weapons than their weaker counterparts. When defeated, Blue Moblins drop Moblin Horns, Moblin Fangs, and Moblin Guts. Drops Blue Moblins reappear in . They drop Blue Moblin Horns upon defeat. Other Appearances Blue Moblins reappear in , first seen in the Scenario "The Yiga Clan Attacks!". Like Moblins, they attack with either their fists or weapons like Moblin Spears, Moblin Clubs, and any metal weapons, which can be Countered with the Stasis, Cryonis, and Magnesis Sheikah Runes, thus exposing their Weak-Point Gauge. When defeated, Blue Moblins drop Moblin Fangs, Moblin Horns, and, rarely, Moblin Guts. A Treasure Chest containing a Weapon may also appear in their place. One Moblin Trophy will be awarded at the end of a Battle for each slain Blue Moblin. Blue Moblins are Powerful Enemies.

is a recurring character in . Biography Blynne is a Hylian who works at Highland Stable. He grew up taming Horses in the area, making him confident he is the best rider in Hyrule. When Link first approaches him, Blynne asks if he is a nomad and supposes he has already seen the Horses nearby. To prove his superiority with Horses, Blynne has developed a test to see who is better at riding Horses, and he never loses. He will ask Link if he has the grit to challenge the master. His test is a horseback Obstacle Course with ten different obstacles, and whoever has the best time wins. He guarantees that his race will help people master riding Horses. However, Blynne notes that the difficult part is controlling one's Horse. He promises Link horse gear if he can beat his time. During the Rain, Blynne will retreat into the stable. He will not feel like running his course, and he tells Link to come beat his time when the sun is out. If Link tries to start the challenge without a Horse, Blynne will stop him. He tells Link to come back with a Horse when he is serious. Entering the Obstacle Course requires a 20 Rupees fee. Before the race, he will explain that Link must jump all of the obstacles before crossing the finish line. He also forbids Link from dismounting his horse. When Link finishes but does not beat Blynne's time, Blynne will say he is impressed and gift Link a Swift Carrot for his Horse. He will yell at Link if he gets off his Horse during the race. He notices something is eating at Link and says he will need an attitude adjustment. Blyne first suggests that Link aims to complete his race in less that one minute and thirty seconds. Once Link beats this time, he will admit that he gets better every time he rides. As a reward for this, he will give Link the Extravagant Bridle. Blynne's own record is one minute and fifteen seconds. If Link beats his record, Blynne states he never thought he would see the day. He will give Link the Extravagant Saddle as a reward.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Boat Oars are found in East Necluda and along the Necluda Sea. They are particularly common around Lurelin Village, but they are also used as Weapons by Monsters in the area. Though they were originally made to paddle boats, they may be useful for self-defense. Since they are made of wood, Boat Oars will float if they are dropped on Water. However, they will also burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity, and they are unable to be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Boat Oars are part of the Daily Use Goods equipment archetype, a series of tools used by the residents of towns throughout Hyrule. Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Bohrin is an elderly Goron who works as a miner at the Southern Mine in the Eldin Canyon. In the past, he was young and strong, but even though he's older now, he still has a lot of fight. Bohrin works the night shift; during the day he can be found asleep beneath a tarp while the other Gorons work, before waking up at night and working the entire shift alone. By the following morning, he is much too tired and goes straight back to sleep. Bohrin may be spoken to while he is working. When asked, he'll explain that the ore from the Southern Mine is sold, which Goron City profits from. He explains that the Gorons used to mine at the Death Mountain Summit, until the Divine Beast Vah Rudania appeared and made the area too dangerous. As a result, the Gorons now work at the Southern Mine. He also gives directions to Goron City, and warns Link that the road ahead is dangerous.

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Boko Bows are basic wooden Bows that are used by regular Bokoblins throughout Hyrule Kingdom. They are made by tying a string to either end of a tree branch, so they are not considered to be very effective in combat. Being made by Bokoblins, they belong to the Bokoblin Gear equipment archetype as a result. If scanned using the amiibo Rune, the Series Bokoblin amiibo has a chance of spawning a Treasure Chest containing a Boko Bow, along with other Bokoblin Gear. Being made from wood, Boko Bows will burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will also float if dropped in Water, but they are unable to be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Boko Bows do not conduct Electricity, nor do they attract Lightning during Thunderstorms. Boko Bows appear in . Other Appearances Boko Bows are wielded by Bokoblins. They cannot be used by any Warriors.

are recurring Items in . Boko Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Boko Shields are Bokoblin-made Shields that are made by attaching a handle to a flat piece of bark. Due to the low level of craftsmanship that went into them, they do not last very long in combat. They are commonly wielded by regular Bokoblins in Hyrule Field, particularly on the Great Plateau, as well as in West Necluda. These Shields are part of the Bokoblin Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Weapons created by Bokoblins. Boko Shields are made of wood and will consequently burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They also float when dropped in water, and they do not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms like metal Shields do. If scanned with the amiibo Rune, the Series Bokoblin amiibo has a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Boko Shield. Boko Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Boko Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Boko Clubs.

are recurring Enemies in the . They are common infantry units used by antagonists such as Ganon. Characteristics Bokoblins first appear in . They have snouts, arrow-shaped tails, three fingers and a single horn. Bokoblins come in three variants: Blue, Green, and Pink. The most common is the blue-skinned, Boko Stick-wielding combat form. Green-skinned elites carry Machetes and wooden Shields. Pink Bokoblins carry Telescopes, which they use to scan their surroundings and to attack. Unarmed Bokoblins will combat Link hand-to-hand until they can find an available weapon. They can wield any kind of Enemy Weapon as needed. They are even strong enough to wield Weapons such as Moblin Spears and Darknut Swords with one arm. The attack power remains the same, however. Bokoblins are more intelligent than their Moblin counterparts. Blue Bokoblins man the Searchlights in the Forsaken Fortress, demonstrating an understanding of machinery. Pink Bokoblins act as scouts on the Great Sea. They use their telescopes to scan the sea from Lookout Platforms and rafts tied to Submarines. Bokoblins also recognize the danger of Bombs and will run away if Link pulls one out. One Green Bokoblin in Forsaken Fortress serves as the first Miniboss of the game. It guards Link's Sword which he dropped entering the fortress. Bokoblins attack by swiping their Weapons at Link. Occasionally, Bokoblins will jump back and attempt to swing their Weapons at Link, which can send the young hero flying backwards if they make contact. Green Bokoblins are a little more versatile as they are able to defend themselves with their Shields. However, they are not particularly tough Enemies and can be defeated by most conventional Items in the game, especially Link's Sword. If they are knocked back, they may drop their Weapons, which Link can use against them. Unarmed Bokoblins will resort to jumping and kicking at Link to hurt him. Bokoblins, even the seafaring pink ones, cannot swim. Sometimes, when walking on a bridge, Bokoblins lose their balance and nearly fall, but manage to hang onto the edge. When this happens, a single hit of the Sword or some other Weapon causes the Bokoblin to fall and drown. All Bokoblins carry one Joy Pendant, which may be dropped after they are defeated. These are easily stolen using the Grappling Hook. They are common in the southern and parts of the eastern areas of Hyrule Field, and are prominent in Faron Woods, but are driven out by Link as he is traversing the Forest Temple. They come in a blue-skinned variant, which carry a wooden club, and, later in the game, a stronger and more durable purple variant that wield Swords. Red Bokoblins appear as a common type of Enemy in , appearing in many places throughout the Surface. Their appearance resembles that of a Japanese more so than their previous incarnations. Red Bokoblins have floppy ears as opposed to pointy ones, and noses instead of snouts. They are much bigger and stouter than previous Bokoblins (slightly larger than Link himself), and have an extra edge of difficulty. They can block attacks with their Weapons, and in order to defeat them, Link must slash around the Weapon. The Red Bokoblins in appear to be somewhat more intelligent and sociable than their past incarnations, even establishing small Monster Strongholds while conflicting with the native Mogma throughout Eldin Volcano. They defend these villages with the aid of lookout towers and large boulders, which they can roll downhill to hinder Link. is a recurring character in . Biography Boldon is a Goron traveler who carries a Traveling Pack. He can be found walking along Ternio Trail, stopping at Foothill Stable along the way. Boldon is the ambassador of tourism for Goron City, and while he recommends that everyone visit it, he also admits that it has its share of problems. Boldon adds that because of the Divine Beast Vah Rudania, the Goron Hot Springs have seen fewer tourists lately. He also tells Link that if he plans on visiting Goron City or other Scorching Climates, he should wear Fireproof Armor or make a Fireproof Elixir. In the Lanayru Region, Boldon notes that there is a noticeable difference to the east and west of their location, which is why places like Woodland Stable are too cold for Gorons. He also comments about the ruined Hyrule Castle, saying that the treasure hunters who plunder it are crazy. If an Enemy attacks him, Boldon assumes a defensive position and tells the threat to come and get him. After being saved, Boldon says that if they put their together their heads as well as their muscles, the two can "stomp 'em flat." He will then reward Link with Food or Rupees.

is a recurring character in . Biography Bolson is the president of Bolson Construction, a company that only hires people whose names end in "-son". If Link asks Bolson who he is, he will recite Bolson Construction's signature theme and dance, only to be disappointed by the realization that Link does not recognize it. Bolson initially appears behind the vacant house in Hateno Village, where he is working with Hudson and Karson to demolish it. Should Link comment that the work sounds boring, Bolson realizes that someone Link's age would not understand. If Link offers to buy the House instead, Bolson will explain to him that the cost of the operation is 50,000 Rupees, which Link would need to pay for in order to stop the demolition. Whether Link agrees to the price or not, Bolson will sympathize with him and decide to lower the price. He offers a revised deal to Link for the house in exchange for 3,000 Rupees and 30 bundles of Wood. Afterwards, he orders his crew to cease demolition as they wait under a Tree nearby for Link to pay for the House. This initiates the Side Quest "Hylian Homeowner", tasking Link with the responsibility of fulfilling his side of the bargain in exchange for the House. If Link tells Bolson that he cannot afford the cost, Bolson will become angry and lecture to him about the hardships of life. However, if Link presents the 30 bundles of Wood to Bolson, he will accept the offer and conclude that Link is serious about the offer. If Link provides the 3,000 Rupees, Bolson will offer a Weapon Mount as a housewarming gift. Bolson then tells Link to speak to Hudson before he leaves to carry out a business expansion in Akkala. Now that they no longer have to demolish Link's House, Bolson and Karson will sit by the Cooking Pot nearby. Starting at 9:05 PM each night, Bolson and Karson will cross the bridge over Firly Pond and sleep inside one of the pre-constructed homes. There, he will recite Bolson Construction's theme in his sleep. After Hudson leaves to establish Tarrey Town, Bolson will offer to furnish Link's House for 100 Rupees per refurbishment. Link can request various additions to his House, such as Weapon Mounts, Bow Mounts, and Shield Mounts, as well as a Bed, lighting and a front door. Link can also request that Bolson decorates the property surrounding his House, adding a Sign with Link's name, a flower bed and Trees. Once Link has fully decorated his property, Bolson will call him a "housing monster" and leave additional furniture inside Link's House before taking a break. If spoken to again, Bolson will declare the House to be perfect and bring Link's attention to Hudson once more, wondering how the Bolson Construction expansion is coming along. During the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, Hudson will ask Link to invite Bolson and Karson to his wedding in Tarrey Town. Bolson is shocked to hear

the House to be perfect and bring Link's attention to Hudson once more, wondering how the Bolson Construction expansion is coming along. During the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, Hudson will ask Link to invite Bolson and Karson to his wedding in Tarrey Town. Bolson is shocked to hear that Hudson is getting married, and he and Karson will depart together. Once they arrive in Tarrey Town, Bolson urges Link to speak to Hudson to start the ceremony. When Rhondson reacts negatively to the vow to name her and Hudson's children in accordance with the Bolson Construction naming policies, Bolson interjects and claims they are traditional. After the wedding, Bolson remarks that Rhondson and Hudson make a lovely couple. He wishes them both well in the future, He decides that it is time for himself and Karson to return to Hateno Village. The pair of them will depart from Tarrey Town together. Back in Hateno Village, Bolson reveals to Link that he has come to a decision. With prompting from Link, he admits that he is planning to retire from Bolson Construction. He wants to go on a journey where he will find someone to marry. When Link shows his support, Bolson advises him not to waste any time, as youth does not last forever. He tells Link to go do what he needs to. While Bolson is sitting outside of Link's House, Link is able to ask him questions. If Link how he is doing, Bolson will reiterate his plans to retire and begin his travels. If Link does not have a reason to speak to him, Bolson will ask if he can make sure that the Bolson Construction theme song catches on. He will then demonstrate the dance for Link. When Link comments on the charm around Bolson's neck, he explains that it is an heirloom that has been passed down through his family for generations that is said to bring happiness. He then asks Link if he noticed the flower petals at the end of Hudson's wedding, which he claims can only be seen by those who are not vapid or disenchanted. They represent endless love, which Bolson considers to be beautiful.

Bomb Flowers are recurring Enemies, Items, and Objects in . Location and Uses Bomb Flowers are plants with an explosive fruit that serve as a substitute for Bombs. In most games, the fruit of the Bomb Flower will explode after a short time once picked from the plant. Just like Bombs, they flash red when near the point of detonation. Bomb Flower fruits detonate automatically in the presence of fire or when caught in an explosion, which may cause a chain reaction should there be other Bomb Flowers nearby. Slashing it with Link's Sword or piercing it with an Arrow also cause its explosion. Earlier versions of the Bomb Flower are sensitive to light, and only grow in darker places. In later reincarnations, Bomb Flowers seem to have become more tolerant of sunlight, as they are more common throughout the world. In certain appearances, Bomb Flowers are considered a special token of the Gorons, who tend the flowers in the mountainous region in which they appear. Bomb Flowers first appear in , appearing exclusively on Death Mountain. Referred to by the Gorons as their "special crop," Bomb Flowers are said to be "mining plants," and the fruit of the flower is the raw material for regular Bombs. When Link is a child, Bomb Flowers are too heavy for him to lift without the aid of the Goron's Bracelet. Although very rare on the mountain itself, Bomb Flowers grow wildly within Dodongo's Cavern, as the warmth and dim lighting presents ideal conditions for their growth. Therefore, it causes some distress among the Gorons when Dodongo's Cavern becomes infested with "ancient creatures", the Dodongo, making the caverns a dangerous place and affecting the Goron's Bomb Flower harvest. Above the entrance to the cavern, near Goron City, stands a lone Bomb Flower, and a Goron devotedly protecting this rare flower from the sun. With the Goron Bracelet, young Link is able to throw the fruit of the Bomb Flower down to the entrance of Dodongo's Cavern, which has been blockaded by boulders. The Bomb will destroy the boulders, allowing Link to enter. Additionally, Bomb Flowers can be found next to most doors and in hallways in Goron City, where they are required to blow up the rocks blocking the warp to the Lost Woods. They are also seen growing in the Fire Temple, suggesting they can even survive in volcanic temperatures. Their fibers are claimed to be one of two materials from which Goron Tunics are made, the other being Dodongo scales, in order for them to be heat-resistant. In , Bomb Flowers act in exactly the same way as in , except Link no longer requires the Goron Bracelet to pick them up. They make a minor appearance in the Woodfall Temple and Snowhead Temple, where they can be used to solve puzzles if Link has not obtained the Bomb Bag or Blast Mask. The is a recurring location in . The Boss's House goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Boss's House is the residence of Bludo, the boss of the Goron Group Mining Company. Goron City's Goddess Statue is located outside of the building, at which Link can exchange Spirit Orbs for Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels. Bludo can be found either inside the House or just outside. Since it is located within Eldin Canyon's Scorching Climate, Link requires at least one level of Flame Guard to avoid catching on Fire while at the Boss's House. When Link first arrives in Goron City, he can speak to Bludo outside of his House. Bludo expresses his frustration towards Divine Beast Vah Rudania, explaining that it has worsened the eruptions from Death Mountain. In his anger, Bludo ends causing his back pain to flare up. He sends Link to fetch Yunobo from the Abandoned North Mine, which begins the "Divine Beast Vah Rudania" Main Quest. Once Link helps Yunobo, he must return to the Boss's House to receive three Fireproof Elixirs from Bludo. He decides to go meet Yunobo at the Bridge of Eldin to deal with Divine Beast Vah Rudania, but his plans change when his back pain returns. Instead, he has Link find Yunobo to cancel their plans for the day. After Divine Beast Vah Rudania has been calmed, Yunobo will bring Link to the Boss's House at Bludo's request. To thank him, Bludo allows Link to keep the contents of a Treasure Chest found inside his House. Inside, Link can retrieve the Boulder Breaker.

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Boss Bokoblins are large, red, pig-like Monsters that lead teams of Bokoblins by blowing their war horns and whistling. They are more powerful than their Bokoblin counterparts, and easily tower over them. Atop their heads are sword-like Horns sharp enough to cut through large trees. In battle, they are capable of digging up and throwing boulders. These boulders can be sent back to their point of origin with the Recall ability. They are always accompanied by a group of Bokoblins, which they will lead in coordinated attacks. Like Moblins, they can attack by throwing their underlings at Link. are locations in . Features and Overview Boss Rematches are structures scattered across the Depths. They are circular arenas where Link can battle already-defeated Bosses. Upon defeating them again, he will be rewarded with a Treasure Chest containing a Huge Crystallized Charge. There are twelve Boss Rematch arenas in total. Each Boss has three dedicated arenas. Two of Colgera's arenas are located in the Hebra Mountains Depths, near the Nupisoyuat Lightroot and Narusis Lightroot, respectively. The third one is in the Gerudo Highlands Depths next to Granajh Canyon Mine and Daval Canyon Mine. Mucktorok has one arena near the Uoyoyuik Lightroot, one near the Uinoj Lightroot, and one near the Ancient Underground Fortress. Marbled Gohma's three arenas are near Takaruk Lightroot, Uasnoj Lightroot, and Muzasu Lightroot. Interestingly, only one of Queen Gibdo's arenas is in the Gerudo Highlands Depths; the other two are in the Hyrule Ridge Depths and in the Lanayru Wetlands Depths between Korakut Lightroot and Korom Lightroot, respectively. If Link has not yet defeated a particular Boss, its Boss Rematch arena will be empty until he does so.

is a recurring character in . Biography Botrick is a Hylian traveler who patrols the area surrounding the Outskirt Stable. He is equipped with a Traveler's Sword and a Wooden Shield. He is a self-described watchman who protects the southwestern corner of Hyrule Field from Monsters. Botrick travels along the road that passes by the Outskirt Stable. Depending on where he is spoken to along the road, he will offer various kinds of advice and insight to Link. At the Outskirt Stable, Botrick will point out Hyrule Castle, informing Link that powerful weaponry can be found there, though the danger of retrieving them is too high. At night, Botrick will go inside the Stable to rest. Inside the Stable, Botrick will share a rumor about the Lord of the Mountain that appears on Satori Mountain. While traveling south from the Stable, Botrick will talk about the Coliseum Ruins and mention how dangerous they are due to large amount of monsters in the Ruins. At the fork in the road, Botrick will head west towards the Digdogg Suspension Bridge. As he approaches the ruins of some wooden buildings, he will stop and watch for monsters. He will also warn Link that the desert to the southwest is plagued by monsters, counseling him to properly equip himself. When he begins his return to the Stable, Botrick will share the history of the Coliseum Ruins with Link, stating that it was once used for people to engage in combat. He also muses that the Ruins still serve that purpose, though only for combat with deadly monsters. After traveling south, Botrick will take the road north. As he passes the Stable, he will mention that the north side is relatively safe but that he is determined to patrol them anyway. Once Botrick reaches the crest of the knoll where the road leads, he informs Link that the road continues into the Tabantha Frontier where Rito Village can be found. He also warns Link that Guardians patrol the road along the way and suggests approaching Rito Village from the east instead. Here, Botrick will stop and look towards Satori Mountain, attempting to catch a glimpse of the Lord of the Mountain's presence. While watching for the Lord of the Mountain, Botrick will inform Link that when it appears, a migration of various Creatures will occur as a result of its presence. Afterwards, Botrick will return to the Outskirt Stable. Upon returning, Botrick will mention that the sudden rise of the Sheikah Towers seemingly corresponds with an increase in the monster population, and that Link must equip himself properly in order to account for this change. If Botrick is attacked by monsters, he will stand his ground and attempt to fight them. If he is knocked unconscious by a monster, he will remain unconscious until the threat has passed. Afterwards, he will begrudge the fact that Link did not assist him in time. If Botrick is saved by Link, he will sheathe his Sword and return

ground and attempt to fight them. If he is knocked unconscious by a monster, he will remain unconscious until the threat has passed. Afterwards, he will begrudge the fact that Link did not assist him in time. If Botrick is saved by Link, he will sheathe his Sword and return to his patrol. If Link speaks to him after saving him, he will thank Link for his help and offer to repay him with Food. If Botrick is saved a second time, he will be embarrassed to have needed Link's help and offers more Food as a bribe. Upon being rescued a third time, Botrick will express his disbelief and either resolve to repay Link in kind or that even watchmen require their own protection. Though none appear along the road that he travels, if a Guardian approaches Botrick, he will frantically warn Link to distance himself from it, claiming that neither of them have a chance against it. Whenever he is spoken to, Botrick will offer to sell gear to Link for his adventure. Though he only carries Arrows, they can be purchased from Botrick at a cheaper rate than from Beedle. If Link attempts to purchase something from Botrick without the necessary funds, Botrick will tell him to stop shopping. Additionally, if Link attempts to buy something without the available Inventory space, Botrick will offer to buy from Link instead. If Link attempts to sell Armor that he is currently wearing, Botrick will call the situation weird and refuse. During Rain, he will offer a special selection of Arrows and offer some at a discounted price to reward Link's determination. If Link speaks to Botrick while he is resting, he will comment on the fact that Link smells like a traveler. If Botrick is resting while it begins to Rain, he will comment about how Rain inhibits a traveler's abilities and cautions Link to wait it out. Botrick will also make various comments under certain conditions. He will passively announce when he returns to his work, and recite his duties when approached. He will comment when sunset approaches, and begrudge having to patrol at night. He will also shout and run for cover when it begins to Rain. At 9:00 PM, the Lantern on Botrick's backpack will turn on. Wares and Pricing

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Bottomless Bogs are quagmires of marshy Water found in various locations throughout Hyrule. If Link steps into a Bottomless Bog, he will begin to sink. If he sinks too deep, he will become fully submerged and, if he has any hearts left, will reappear outside of the Bog. Enemies that fall into a Bottomless Bog will die, although Lizalfos can swim in these bogs. Similarly, any Materials, Weapons or Rupees that fall into a Bottomless Bog will sink to the bottom and become inaccessible, unless they can be retrieved with Magnesis. Due to being a body of water, Cryonis will work on Bottomless Bogs, providing one the means of safely traversing the marshy terrain. Bottomless Bogs reappear in . A Bottomless Bog appears on the northern end of the Great Plateau. Inside this Bog, Link can find a wheel that is used to construct a four-wheel vehicle.

The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Bottomless Swamp is located in Hyrule Field, along the bank of the Hylia River. The Bottomless Swamp features a hostile landscape, with various hazards such as Bottomless Bogs, Pools of Malice, and several primitive . Furthermore, several dead Trees, large skulls, and large rib bones dot the Swamp as well. In the center of the Swamp is a giant skull that serves as a Monster Stronghold, which a number of Enemies patrol around. At the southeastern reaches of the Swamp, the charred remains of a couple buildings can be found. Ore Deposits can be found inside the highest of the cluster of skulls. In the southernmost skull, a metallic Treasure Chest containing a Soldier's Broadsword can be found submerged in a Bottomless Bog. Inside the largest of the skulls is a wooden Treasure Chest containing a Silver Rupee. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment The Bottomless Pond reappears in , now filled with Water and Lily Pads of varying sizes. It is located directly beneath the Temple of Time on the Great Sky Island, and is where Link lands when Skydiving off the platform behind the Temple during the "To the Kingdom of Hyrule" Main Quest. The Pond, despite its name, is actually relatively shallow. A dense, unnamed forest lies to the northeast of the Pond, filled with vegetation, while several Trees can be found southeast of the Pond. The Bottomless Pond Well can be found in a Deserted House near these Trees, along with a Monster Outpost inhabited by a Bokoblin and Moblin and littered with Garbage Dumps. Fallen Debris can be found around the Pond, with Materials from the Sky Islands growing near them. Ruins Rubble occasionally fall from the Great Sky Island, landing on its shores. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Boulder Breakers are Weapons that are part of the Goron Gear equipment archetype. They are the strongest variant of the Cobble Crusher. Just like the other Goron crushers, they are Two-Handed Weapons that can be used for both mining and combat. They also have a hidden property which causes their damage output to be doubled when used on the Ore Deposit atop a Stone Talus. They are capable of immediately destroying Stone Pebblits. Despite Bludo describing Boulder Breakers as sharp Weapons, they do not act as such and cannot cut Grass or Trees. Prior to the Great Calamity, a Boulder Breaker was wielded by the Goron Champion, Daruk It was made for him by a blacksmith based out of Goron City. Daruk supposedly made swinging this Weapon around look easy, while others who used it would need a large amount of strength. According to Bludo, Daruk used his Boulder Breaker to carve the valley at Gortram Cliff in one night to make it easier for the Gorons to reach their Rock Roast. In addition, there is a rumor that Daruk used to use it to fan himself. During the EX Recovered Memory "Champion Daruk's Song", Daruk can be seen using his Boulder Breaker to fight off a group of Bokoblins harassing a Hylian Retriever. After appeasing the Divine Beast Vah Rudania, Bludo will allow Link to take Daruk's Boulder Breaker from a Treasure Chest in his House as a reward. If Link ever misplaces or breaks the Boulder Breaker, Rohan will be able to craft him a new one in exchange for a Cobble Crusher, five pieces of Flint, and a Diamond. However, he will not make if the Boulder Breaker is still recoverable. Boulder Breakers are made of metal, and they will therefore conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. However, they are unable to burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They sink if dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated using the Magnesis Rune. Boulder Breakers reappear as Weapons in . They are one of the few Weapons that remain Intact on the Surface, while the rest have Decayed as a result of the Upheaval. The creation of Boulder Breakers is considered to be an honor among the Gorons, and only a select few are taught how to make them. According to Fugo, there is only one Spirit that can be forged into a Boulder Breaker, and as a result, multiple Boulder Breakers cannot be made when one already exists. According to Zelda, Daruk's Boulder Breaker was originally twice as heavy compared to normal, and he had its weight increased further when he was appointed as a Champion. In the present, Yunobo now wields a Boulder Breaker of his own. After Link frees him from the Weird Mask's influence during the Main Quest "Yunobo of Goron City", he will begin to use his Boulder Breaker to fight Enemies

weight increased further when he was appointed as a Champion. In the present, Yunobo now wields a Boulder Breaker of his own. After Link frees him from the Weird Mask's influence during the Main Quest "Yunobo of Goron City", he will begin to use his Boulder Breaker to fight Enemies that the two of them encounter, such as Marbled Gohma. His Sage Avatar also carries a projection of a Boulder Breaker, which Link is still able to take a Picture of for his Hyrule Compendium. If Yunobo has been awoken as a Sage, he will appear during the War in the Depths of Hyrule to fight Monsters with his Boulder Breaker. The Goron smith Rohan was prepared to teach his apprentice Fugo how to make a Boulder Breaker prior to the Upheaval, but he gave up after Fugo was mind-controlled to focus on Marbled Rock Roast. A Boulder Breaker can be found leaning against Rohan's House, but if Link tries to pick it up, he will yell at him and state that it is incomplete. During the Side Quest "Soul of the Gorons", Fugo attempts to convince Rohan to let him finish the Boulder Breaker, but Rohan is still angry with him for abandoning it in the first place. Rohan eventually relents, but they are unable to afford the necessary supplies due to Fugo spending all of their Rupees. To finish the Boulder Breaker, Fugo requires a Cobble Crusher, five pieces of Flint, and three Diamonds. The Cobble Crusher can be either Decayed or an Intact Cobble Crusher✨, but it cannot have any Objects or Materials Fused to it. Once Link provides Fugo with what he needs, he will proceed to complete the Boulder Breaker. After it is finished, Rohan declares that the Boulder Breaker is one of the best he has ever seen. To thank Link, Fugo gifts him the Boulder Breaker. He also offers to make a new Boulder Breaker for him if this one ever breaks, so long as he provides the necessary supplies again. However, he will refuse to make another if Link's Boulder Breaker is not broken, as its Spirit is not available to be forged again. In flashbacks to the Imprisoning War during the Era of Foundation, the Sage of Fire Agraston can be seen wielding a Boulder Breaker. Other Appearances Boulder Breakers are a type of Weapon used by Daruk, which he is able to use when he is available as a Warrior in Scenarios and Challenges. In both Narrations and Movies, Daruk is seen carrying his Boulder Breaker with him. For example, he wields it when the Yiga ambush the party in "Assassination!", when Monsters begin an attack in "A Song from the Past", and when he is fighting Fireblight Ganon in "Rescue Across Time: Water and Fire". In , Agraston can be seen wielding a Boulder Breaker while in combat.

, also known as , and , are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Bow allows Link to fire Arrows as its main ammunition, allowing him to snipe Enemies and faraway objects such as Switches. Being a staple item in , the Bow is almost always found in a Dungeon. Typically the item is often guarded by a Sub-Boss, most commonly within the console Zelda games with a few exceptions. In the top-down styled Zelda games, the Bow can shoot Arrows at any cardinal direction. In the 3D console games, the Bow instead switches to a first-person view and can fire Arrows at any angle. Since its debut, the Bow has been expanded to be equipped with and fire other varieties of Arrows, such as the Fire and Ice Arrows, among a few others. The Bow of Light is a recurring upgraded form of the Bow, which fires Arrows of sacred light. The Crossbow is a variant of the regular Bow, which instead fires Arrows from a wide angle, and has only appeared in ambiguous and non-canon media. In , the Bow is found in Level 1 of the First Quest and in Level 5 of the Second Quest. In order to use the Bow, Link must purchase an Arrow from a Shop for 80 Rupees. After Link has done so, he will be able to shoot the Bow by consuming one Rupee per Arrow shot. The Bow and Arrow deals 2 damage to Enemies that can be inflicted by them. Pols Voices are weak to Arrows and will be defeated by them in one hit. Gohmas can only be defeated with the Bow and Arrow. Link can also shoot Silver Arrows from the Bow, which must be used as the final blow on Ganon to destroy him. In , the Bow is found in the Eastern Palace. Arrows are now introduced as ammunition items, allowing the Bow to fire Arrows without using Rupees. The Bow is a powerful weapon whose Arrows inflict piercing damage to most Enemies, making it a stronger weapon than the starting Sword. In some situations it is the only weapon that can damage certain Enemies, namely the Eyegores. Aside from attacking Enemies at a distance, it can also be used to hit and activate Switches that are out-of-reach. While mostly used to solve puzzles, the Bow is also necessary to defeat Ganon by shooting a Silver Arrow when he is weakened. The Bow is also used to play the Shooting Gallery game in the Village of Outcasts. In , the Bow is not found in any dungeon but is instead bought from the Town Tool Shop in Mabe Village for 980 Rupees, making it one of the most expensive items in The Legend of Zelda series. It can, however, simply be stolen. The Bow becomes available once Link has bought the Deluxe Shovel from the store. Like the Bow in , the Bow is able to inflict heavy damage onto most Enemies, and

it one of the most expensive items in The Legend of Zelda series. It can, however, simply be stolen. The Bow becomes available once Link has bought the Deluxe Shovel from the store. is a recurring character in . Biography Bozai is a Hylian man who spends his days outside of Gerudo Town in the Gerudo Desert. He's the giver of two Side Quests, "The Eighth Heroine" and "The Forgotten Sword". Bozai is 35 years old and loves jogging on sand. He believes that Link is a woman when he is wearing the Gerudo Outfit and has a strong romantic affinity for him. Bozai behaves rudely to Link if he is not disguised as a woman, saying that he would only consider giving him his Sand Boots if he were a girl. Link can first find Bozai sometimes running around the Gerudo Desert in front of Gerudo Town if the Camera Rune has already been unlocked as it will be required for completing his quest. If he's spoken to while wearing the Gerudo Outfit, Bozai will introduce himself to Link, making note that he is single and loves jogging on sand. When Link asks for Bozai's Sand Boots, he agrees to give them to Link in exchange for a favor. Bozai then explains that while everyone has heard of The Seven Heroines, there is also a legend of an Eighth Heroine in the northern Gerudo Highlands that has been wiped from history. Bozai promises to give Link his Sand Boots if he shows him a Picture of the Eighth Heroine. Before he finishes speaking, Bozai lends Link his pair of Snow Boots for faster traversal through the northern Gerudo Highlands. This begins the Side Quest "The Eighth Heroine". After taking a Picture of the Statue of the Eighth Heroine in the Gerudo Highlands with his Sheikah Slate, Link returns to Bozai to show him the Picture. Bozai is glad to see Link is safe after starting to worry he would never return. Bozai then admits that the Eighth Heroine does not exist and only used it as an excuse to get close to Link. Bozai vows not to put Link in danger anymore and be his protector, before Link interrupts him to tell him he found the Statue. Thinking Link is merely trying to console him, Bozai says that Link is kind, but that there is no need to coddle him. Link interrupts Bozai again to show him the Picture of the Statue and Bozai is shocked that the Eighth Heroine exists. Bozai promises not to tell anyone and that it will be their little secret. Bozai begins to ask Link for romantic involvement before Link interrupts him, asking for the Sand Boots he was promised. Bozai takes the Sand Boots off and gives them to Link, telling him to treat them tenderly. Bozai then requests for his Snow Boots back and Link returns them. Before leaving, Bozai invites Link to join him later at the nearby tent. Link says bye without answering the question and the Side Quest is completed. After the completion of "The Eighth Heroine", Bozai can be found at a tent outside of the front of Gerudo Town. Speaking

returns them. Before leaving, Bozai invites Link to join him later at the nearby tent. Link says bye without answering the question and the Side Quest is completed. After the completion of "The Eighth Heroine", Bozai can be found at a tent outside of the front of Gerudo Town. Speaking to Bozai here will begin "The Forgotten Sword" Side Quest. Like "The Eighth Heroine", Link must be wearing the Gerudo Outfit to initiate the Quest. When Link speaks to him, Bozai is surprised that Link arrived. After Bozai asks him if he wants to "hang out," Link immediately asks for Bozai's Snow Boots. Bozai mocks Link for a "boot thirst that cannot be slaked." While Bozai does not like the idea of being stuck without footwear, he admits that he cannot resist a request from Link. Bozai tells Link that he will give him the Snow Boots if he is able to surprise him again. Bozai then explains that the Statue of the Eighth Heroine is not holding a sword like the other Seven Heroines. Bozai believes that the Statue once had a sword and feels that evidence of its existence would be a great surprise. Link agrees to go look for it to Bozai's surprise and Bozai says that it could not have been carried off too far, likely residing on the steppes of the Gerudo Highlands. Before he finishes speaking, Bozai is sorry that he cannot lend Link his Snow Boots this time and tells Link to find him if he needs anything beyond footwear. After taking a Picture of the sword in the Gerudo Highlands with his Sheikah Slate, Link returns to Bozai at the tent. Bozai says that a traveler swore he saw Link in the Gerudo Highlands, which made him worry because he did not think Link would really go to the Highlands without Snow Boots. To Bozai's shock, Link shows him the Picture of the sword. Stating that Link risked his life for the Picture, Bozai admits that it would be uncouth of him to break his promise and gives Link the Snow Boots. Although stuck barefoot, Bozai is happy that Link is happy. Before Link ends the conversation, Bozai confesses that all of this has endeared him even closer to Link and the Quest is completed. If Link talks to Bozai directly after the Quest, he will ask permission to gaze at Link until he leaves and wishes to never forget Link's appearance. If Link speaks to Bozai again without wearing the Gerudo Outfit, he claims to feel dumped. If Link returns to the tent later, Bozai will not be there and is never seen again.
