is a recurring character in . Biography Branli is a Hylian who wears a Snowquill Tunic and Snowquill Trousers. He can be found at the top of Ridgeland Tower, which he has been stuck on since it rose from the ground. He runs the Bird-Man Research Study Mini-Game. Branli is a researcher dedicated to discovering the flying capabilities of the Rito. According to him, their flight is seemingly inexplicable, due to their heavy weight and relatively short wingspan. Now that he is trapped on top of Ridgeland Tower, he realizes it gives him the perfect vantage point to observe the Rito in Rito Village. When Branli realizes that Link is also on the Tower, he assumes that Link is stuck as well and is unable to get down without hurting himself. After learning that Link can glide down, he is excited as he thinks this could help his research. Through his research, he wants to one day himself be a bird, capable of flight. Branli asks Link to participate in a study to see how far he can glide, agreeing to compensate him based on how far he flies. However, he charges Link a liability fee of 20 Rupees in the event of any accidents. If Link agrees, Branli asks him to keep several things in mind while he glides. Based on the distance Link flies, Branli will have different reactions. If he flies less than 450 meters, Branli will be upset and refuse to give Link a reward. He encourages Link to think of himself as a Rito, free from gravity. In addition, he suggests that Link make adjustments to preserve his Stamina. If Link glides between 450 and 600 meters, Branli considers it a small step towards his goal. He initially offers 21 Rupees as a reward, though he relents and gives Link a Purple Rupee instead. Should Link make it more than 600 meters, Branli notes that, while he did not flap his arms, his methods were still effective. As a reward, he gives Link a Silver Rupee. If Link returns to Branli at any point after first participating in the Research Study, he will refer to him as his research assistant.

is a location in . Features and Overview Bravery Island is a towering Sky Island that is part of the North Hyrule Sky Archipelago in the Great Hyrule Forest Sky. It was the site of a Dive Ceremony for young Zonai to test their courage in ancient times. Zonai would prove themselves in this rite of passage by diving through a set of rings leading to a pool at the bottom of the Island. Link can participate in the Dive Ceremony by speaking to the facilitator of the Dive Ceremony, a lone Steward Construct, at the bottom of Bravery Island. Before Link can undergo the Ceremony, he must pass a trial run by passing through the rings without a time limit. When Link completes the trial run, the Simosiwak Shrine will appear at the bottom of the Island and he will be allowed to attempt the Dive Ceremony for the price of one Zonai Charge. In order to complete the Dive Ceremony, Link must pass through all of the rings in 35 seconds or less. If Link successfully does so, he will be given the Glide Tights as a reward. By beating the current record of 25 seconds in the Dive Ceremony, Link will also receive a Large Zonai Charge and be registered as the new record holder. Every time Link beats his own record, he will be given an additional Large Zonai Charge. Every time he beats the Island's record of 25 second but not his own, he will be given either five Portable Pots, Rockets or Springs. The is a recurring Armor Shop in . Features and Overview The Brazen Beak is the resident Armor Shop of Rito Village. It is operated by Nekk, who stands at the front desk and sells wares. In addition to this, Huck beckons in customers from outside the Armor Shop, where he advertises the Snowquill Set sold inside. The Brazen Beak makes its Armor pieces with the feathers that Rito molt when seasons change. When Link makes a purchase from the Brazen Beak, Nekk will thank him for doing so. Should Link buy the Armor Shop's entire stock, Nekk remarks that he is going on a shopping spree. If Link speaks to Nekk after buying the entire Snowquill Set, Nekk suggests that he buy another to Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop. Wares and Pricing Since the blizzard over Rito Village started, Kheel has taken over the Brazen Beak. The Armor Shop sells warm Armor to travelers intending to traverse the Hebra Mountains. After Link has completed the Main Quest "Tulin of Rito Village" and the adult Rito return to the village, Nekk is able to come back to the shop. Kheel will stick around the Shop to help out, even though she is not in charge of sales anymore. Wares and Pricing

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Breach of Demise is located in Central Hyrule. A crossroad between the north, east, and west runs through it. The travelers Baddek, Nazbi, and Savelle ride their Horses through the Hilltop High Road, which runs to the north and west. To the far reaches of the eastern road is a monster camp, consisting of an outdoor encampment with a Cooking Pot and a couple of watchtowers, along with three skull structures where more Enemies are taking shelter. Inside the westernmost skull structure, Link can find a metallic Treasure Chest containing a Silver Rupee embedded in the ground. A Korok can be found by standing on a Tree stump atop the southernmost spire and racing to the ring that appears atop a spire further north before it disappears. Creatures Enemies Materials Other Appearances The Breach of Demise is the main setting of the "Road to the Ancient Lab" Scenario. Link, Zelda, and Impa make their way through the Breach of Demise to reach the Royal Ancient Lab.

is a recurring character in . Biography Breen is a Stable Worker of the Woodland Stable whose job is to help travelers change their Horse's Gear and Mane. If Link approaches her with a Horse, she will offer to change its Gear, though she is only interested in Horses that have developed a strong bond with their riders. If Link's Horse does not have a full bond, she will refuse and tell him to spend more time caring for it. However, if Link's bond with his Horse is fully realized, she will become excited and agree to change the Horse's Gear. From then on, she will change that Horse's Gear without needing to check its affection. If Link attempts to change the Giant Horse's Gear, she will apologize and inform Link that she does not have any Gear large enough to fit the Horse and that it would not like for its Mane to be handled. Similarly, if Link attempts to change Epona's Gear, she will claim that Epona is too lovely and graceful to change her Gear.

The , also known as , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview In , the Bridge of Eldin is a bridge found north of Kakariko Village. It crosses a deep gorge where Zora's River runs through, essentially connecting the Eldin Province to a path leading to the Lanayru Province. It also serves as the main access road to the Hidden Village. After King Bulblin suddenly kidnaps Colin from Kakariko Village, he makes his way to the Bridge of Eldin, with Link in pursuit. Here, the two engage in horseback combat in which Link comes out victorious and rescues Colin from the Bulblin's grasp. Once the young hero clears the Goron Mines and crosses this Bridge en route to the next province, a significant portion of the Bridge is removed by Zant's Shadow Beasts, thus blocking the path. Defeating the beasts causes a Twilight Portal to be created, but it cannot be used due to the Bridge's removal. Link eventually finds what appears to be the removed section of the Bridge of Eldin in the of the Gerudo Desert, right on the Gerudo Mesa. With the aid of Midna, the young hero warps back to the area where the Bridge of Eldin was removed, taking the section with them. However, if Link did not defeat the Shadow Beasts that appeared after the Bridge was removed, the portal will not appear and thus they will be unable to warp the missing section of the Bridge. Once the portal is created, Midna will place the section back where it belongs, allowing Link to cross the Bridge again. Once Link receives the Ancient Sky Book from Shad, he will have to return to the Bridge of Eldin in order to receive a Sky Character from the Owl Statue situated in the northern section of the bridge. Moreover, by transporting the statue to the other side of the Bridge and situating it exactly below a certain ledge will allow Link to jump over and obtain a Piece of Heart. A male Golden Phasmid can also be found in the northern portion of the Bridge of Eldin. In , the Bridge of Eldin is a bridge that crosses over Death Mountain's lava moat in the Eldin Region, connecting Death Mountain with Eldin Canyon. It is denoted as Death Mountain Marker #8. A road leading from Goron City paves the way to the Bridge through the Abandoned North Mine and Stolock Bridge. On the western side of the Bridge of Eldin is a Cannon, one of many stationed around Death Mountain that the Gorons use to drive away Divine Beast Vah Rudania. The Bridge is initially inaccessible as Bludo, the Gorons' Boss, has drawn the Bridge to prevent Vah Rudania from crossing over. After Link saves Yunobo a second time from a pair of Black Moblins at the Bridge's Cannon, and informs him of Bludo's inability to come and use the Cannon, the two decide to attack Vah Rudania themselves so that Link can

the Bridge to prevent Vah Rudania from crossing over. Yunobo uses Daruk's Protection and instructs Link to fire him at the Bridge using the Cannon to lower it. From there on, the Bridge becomes accessible. The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Bridge of Hylia is a bridge that spans across Lake Hylia, connecting Hyrule Field from the north to the Faron Grasslands in the south. It is a massive stone structure that bears 15 piers and 13 pedestrian recesses per side. The center of the Bridge of Hylia features a disused fountain and several Wooden Boxes, which may contain Materials and Arrows when broken. Beside the fountain sits a ruined Wagon, which can be searched for Gems. When Ralera married her husband, Rhodes, the two of them crossed the Bridge of Hylia on their way to Hateno Village. On occasion, Link can encounter Yiga Footsoldiers disguised as Travelers on the Bridge. At midnight, Farosh will begin to fly around Lake Hylia. It passes over the Bridge of Hylia three times: at 1:20 AM, 2:30 AM, and 4:20 AM. Several Treasure Chests are located on the Bridge of Hylia. A stone Chest under the Bridge's fifth pier contains five Shock Arrows. A Soldier's Broadsword is hidden inside a metallic Treasure Chest in the Water between the seventh and eighths piers. In the Water beneath the arch of the eighth pier, Link can find two metallic Chests containing an Edge of Duality and five Shock Arrows, respectively. On the north and south springing lines of the Bridge's central pier, two stone Treasure Chests can be found, both of which contain a bundle of five Arrows. A metal Chest resting on the Bridge of Hylia's fountain contains a Zora Spear. Finally, a Phrenic Bow can be found inside a stone Treasure Chest on the Bridge's 11th pier. In Master Mode, a wooden platform held aloft by Sky Octoroks is located above the Bridge of Hylia. On this platform is a metallic Treasure Chest containing a Knight's Halberd. left|40px A total of eight Korok Seed Puzzles are present on the Bridge of Hylia. The first can be solved by igniting the unlit stationary Torches that at the northern end of the Bridge. A second can be found by throwing Rocks off the eastern refuge on the Bridge's northern pier into a Circle on the surface of Lake Hylia. A third can be found by picking up a rock hidden under a stone slab on the Bridge's fourth pier, which reveals it to be a Natural Hiding Spot. Using Archery, Link can destroy a Balloon to solve a fourth Puzzle. The fifth is another Natural Hiding Spot, which takes the form of a Tree Branch on the wall of the seventh pier. The sixth Puzzle can be located by examining the Leaves with Fairy Dust on top of the fountain. A Flower Trail is found on the eastern side of the Bridge's ninth refuse, which must be followed to solve the seventh Puzzle. The eighth and final Korok Seed Puzzle is solved by lifting the Natural Hiding Spot Rock at the base of the 12th pier. Once these Puzzles have been solved, a Korok will

on the eastern side of the Bridge's ninth refuse, which must be followed to solve the seventh Puzzle. The eighth and final Korok Seed Puzzle is solved by lifting the Natural Hiding Spot Rock at the base of the 12th pier. Once these Puzzles have been solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Normal Mode Master Mode Equipment The Bridge of Hylia is guarded by a three-headed Flame Gleeok. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Brightcaps are rare Mushrooms found in dark environments such as Caves and Wells. They contain luminescent enzymes that, when Cooked, create Food that causes Link to faintly Glow. Brightcaps can be roasted in Fire or Scorching Climates to create Toasty Brightcaps. is a recurring character in . Biography Brigo is a Hylian who is found patrolling Proxim Bridge in West Necluda to protect it from monsters, as the bridge is an important route. He wields a Traveler's Spear. Despite being used to bad omens, Brigo feels as though they have been getting worse. When he notices Link, Brigo does not recognize him and asks if they have met before. However, he says it does not matter who Link is because he is tired of talking to himself, stating that Link has come at a good time. He continues by asking Link if he has seen the Sheikah Towers that have popped out of the ground all over the place. Since the long deserted Ancient Shrines have also started glowing, Brigo believes the end is here. Because of these events, he is keeping his eye on "that thing", referring to the nearby Decayed Guardian, in case it starts moving. Brigo describes the broken down Guardian as being shaped like an overturned . Closer to Hyrule Castle, a Guardian Stalker had chased down Brigo and shot blue beams of light to kill him, but he managed to escape into the nearby woods. Brigo asks Link if he thinks his lightning fast reflexes saved him. However, he laughs off the comment and says he just got lucky. Since Guardians are said to still wander around Hyrule Castle, Brigo tells Link to be careful. If Link asks for directions to Kakariko Village, Brigo points to Dueling Peaks and says that on the other side there is a stable where he can ask for further directions. Brigo exclaims in surprise if asked for directions to Hyrule Castle, stating that no matter how many lives Link has, it is not enough to face the many Guardians there. Despite this, he points Link in the right direction, although he believes it would be better to view the Castle from Proxim Bridge. Brigo is confused when Link asks for directions to the abandoned Great Plateau, which is surrounded by a high cliff. Brigo points in the Great Plateau's direction and tells Link to be careful of monsters. Should Link go to climb or jump off the side of Proxim Bridge, Brigo will stop him and tell the hero to think about what he is doing. He says Link will not change the world by jumping carelessly to his doom. It would only cause Brigo himself shock at seeing such a thing. Brigo ends the conversation by telling Link he is fine and not to be careless, as there are too many enjoyable things in the world to gamble with his life. If spoken to after this, Brigo tells Link he almost gave him a heart attack and not to do something like that again, at which point he offers to chat with him for a while. Brigo is a friendly traveler and member of the Chasm Investigation Team who is searching for a Chasm near Mount Daphnes. If spoken

he almost gave him a heart attack and not to do something like that again, at which point he offers to chat with him for a while. Brigo is a friendly traveler and member of the Chasm Investigation Team who is searching for a Chasm near Mount Daphnes. If spoken to before reporting in to Purah at Lookout Landing, he points Link toward Hyrule Castle in order to help him get his bearings. He travels with a Donkey at his side. Brigo's journey begins with him resting underneath Fallen Debris before he travels along an unmarked road through the Exchange Ruins. At Mount Daphnes, Brigo asks Link whether he has seen any such Chasm. Despite Link's efforts, Brigo is unable to find the Chasm at Mount Daphnes Well and begins to talk about giving up his search, as he believes word of it was likely an embellished story from someone who found themself stuck in a hole. Brigo also briefly muses about whether the Surface is actually what lies below the Depths. Brigo turns south from the Exchange Ruins and passes the east side of Aquame Lake, walking through the Gatepost Town Ruins and the Forest of Time. When walking near the Hyrule Field Skyview Tower, he informs Link that it has been taken over by Monsters and turned into a Monster Fort. Around the Forest of Time, Brigo explains that Ring Ruins have fallen onto Kakariko Village to the east and that he eventually intends to visit them. From the Forest of Time, he travels around the eastern side of Whistling Hill to stop beneath a large Tree north of the Riverside Stable. If spoken to while it is Raining or during a Thunderstorm, Brigo warns Link that despite his young age, he should be careful while Climbing slippery surfaces. Brigo rewards Link with Food if saved from Enemies.

is a recurring character in . Biography Brokka travels between Dueling Peaks Stable and Kakariko Village, carrying a Hunter's Shield and a Traveler's Sword. When she reaches Kakariko Village, Brokka will rest at the Shuteye Inn before continuing her journey. At Dueling Peaks Stable, she sits at the table inside before heading out. Brokka is very passionate about Gems, often singing Gem-themed lyrics while walking. She wonders if she should think about things that can help others, informing Link that placing a Bird Egg in a Hot Spring will make a Hard-Boiled Egg. During her travels, Brokka also has a tendency to zone out. Though she considers owning something as beautiful as a Gem important, she also highly values money. In general, she enjoys things that sparkle, but she loves Gems and Rupees in particular. If spoken to, Brokka will give Link advice on collecting Gems from the Ore Deposits near the Dueling Peaks. According to her, the mountains are rich in Gems, and she dreams about selling the Gems she mines from there. She also notes that Bombs can be used to break Ore Deposits, but she asks that Link not set any off near her. Despite this, Brokka prefers using Hammers for mining over Bombs. Brokka may also notice Link's pouch, reminding him to sell any Gems he has due to their value. In particular, she suggests selling Rubies and Sapphires, since they are worth a lot. She believes that the amount of Rupees that Gems sell for can be a great motivator. According to Brokka, the value of a Gem comes from its beauty, and she herself has sold several beautiful Gems. In addition, Brokka will give Link directions if she thinks he looks lost, and she suggests that he use his Map for help. However, she laments the fact that there is not a Map for life. She will also direct him to Kakariko Village, saying that since she sells Gems there, she knows it well. When it is Raining, Brokka may not feel like talking. She may also inform Link that Bomb Arrows will not ignite in such Weather. Brokka then asks about the look on Link's face, stating that she is allowed to talk about things aside from Gems. When Link saves Brokka from Enemies, she will be grateful for his help. She may comment on his strength, swearing to never forget that he saved her. She will give him Rupees, meals, or Elixirs as a reward.

Bubbul Gems are Items in . Location and Uses Bubbul Gems are Key Items that are dropped by defeated Bubbulfrogs, which are Creatures found in the Caves scattered throughout Hyrule. Each Cave has only one Bubbulfrog, meaning only one Bubbul Gem can be acquired per Cave. If a Bubbulfrog is defeated and its Bubbul Gem is not picked up before Link leaves the area, then the Bubbulfrog will need to be defeated again in order to acquire the Bubbul Gem. Upon acquiring the Bubbul Gem within a Cave, any discovered entrances for that Cave will receive a checkmark on the Purah Pad's Map. Bubbul Gems can be traded to Koltin for Monster Parts and Armor. The first trade is part of the "The Hunt for Bubbul Gems!" Side Adventure which can be started by interacting with Koltin outside the Pico Pond Cave in the Eldin Region. Link will be tasked with entering the Cave and retrieving the Bubbul Gem from the Bubbulfrog inside. Upon speaking with Koltin, Link will be able to trade the Bubbul Gem for a Bokoblin Mask. After completing the Side Adventure, Koltin can be found in various locations across Hyrule. As part of the "Bubbul Gems" Additional Adventure, he will make the following trades: Once Link has traded 46 Bubbul Gems to Koltin and obtained the Mystic Headpiece, Koltin will ask Link to find the remaining 101 Bubbul Gems even though he has no rewards left to give him. If Link collects the remaining Gems and gives them to Koltin, he will give Link the Koltin's Fabric and ask him to show it to his brother, Kilton. Koltin then transforms into a Blupee and disappears.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Bubinga Forest is located in West Necluda, just east of the Dueling Peaks Stable and south of Blatchery Plain. A majority of the Forest grows on sloped terrain, with the Squabble River curving around its southern base. The Forest's western part consists of open woodland with trees separated by wider grassy spaces, while the eastern part is denser. The forest as a whole has little undergrowth. One Korok is found using a Natural Hiding Spot under a Rock at the top of a large Tree in the northwest corner of the Forest. Another Korok is found near the center of the Forest, by stepping on a rock with a pinwheel on it and shooting the three Balloons that appear. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Bubinga Forest reappears in . A Hinox lives in the forest's northern edge where it borders the Ash Swamp and Blatchery Plain. When Link sleeps in a Malanya Bed, Malanya may advise him that many Horses are present at the Forest, and would serve as excellent mounts. Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials Equipment

is a recurring character in . Biography Bugut is a traveling Hylian Merchant who appears on the path between Kakariko Village and the Dueling Peaks Stable. At Kakariko Village, he will sit inside Shuteye Inn to rest before he leaves. When he reaches Dueling Peaks Stable, he will sit at the table inside for a moment. When spoken to, Bugut frequently makes reference to his old age. In his youth, he was a mountain-climber, and he used the Dueling Peaks Stable as a base for Climbing the Dueling Peaks. He occasionally remarks that Climbing is difficult in the Rain, suggesting the one should wait until it passes before continuing to Climb. Bugut enjoys mornings and bright days. When he travels during the night, he will comment that he is awake past his bedtime. He also shows an interest in Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain near Kakariko Village, recommending Link prepare before he investigates it. Claree, the owner of Enchanted, is the object of Bugut's affections, but he considers her to be out of his league. He also wants to buy a Stealth Chest Guard from her, as he hears it makes it harder for Monsters to find you. Bugut thinks he is too old for Claree, and he does not have enough Rupees to afford the Stealth Chest Guard. Bugut will offer advice at various points on his journey. At the intersection of the road between Kakariko Bridge and Fort Hateno, he offers directions to Hateno Village. While in direct proximity to the Dueling Peaks Stable, Bugut remarks upon the look in Link's eyes, claiming that he knows that Link will not stay there for long due to the call for adventure. While resting inside, he talks about how Kakariko Village is a good shopping destination due to its food and fashion. When Link saves Bugut from Enemies, he will be grateful. He may also comment that Link is tough despite his youth. He will give Link meals and Rupees as a reward. Bugut will also advertise his wares and their ability to boost Link's Stamina. He suggests having Stamina-boosting Foods on hand when Climbing and running. Everything he sells are Items that he found on his travels, and he sells specialty Items when it's raining. When Link agrees to buy from him, Bugut guarantees that his ingredients will be able to boost his vigor. Bugut also agrees to buy from Link. He thanks Link for every purchase he makes. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring character in . Biography Buliara is the Gerudo captain of the guard who accompanies Lady Riju, the Gerudo Chief. Throughout the day, she can be found in the Royal Palace of Gerudo Town. She is known as the best spear master in Gerudo Town. Despite this, she carries a Golden Claymore. Riju notes in her diary that Buliara was the one who informed her of her mother's passing and her new role as Gerudo Chief. When Riju left Gerudo Town to investigate Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Buliara was the one who rescued her when she got too close. Since then, she has not left Riju's side, blaming herself for the theft of the Thunder Helm. Link first meets Buliara at the start of the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest when he first enters the Royal Palace disguised as a woman. Buliara will stop Link when he approaches Riju on her throne and demands him to explain his business here. After Riju speaks to Link for some time, she will mention to Buliara that she recalls her mother speaking of a fallen swordsman that was placed into a deep sleep by the Princess of Hyrule when the Great Calamity happened. She also recalls that the swordsman's name was Link, hesitantly wondering if the Link before her is that same swordsman. If Link is not carrying the legendary sword, Buliara will point out that Link is not carrying the sword from those same legends. After more conversation, Buliara suddenly notices that Link is actually a man. Riju states that it is a great crime for a man to enter Gerudo Town, but she dismisses this due to Link's status as a Champion. Riju soon reasons that if Link truly is a Champion, then he may be able to enter Divine Beast Vah Naboris and calm its anger. Buliara urges Riju not to trust a stranger with such an important task, suggesting that he prove himself worthy by recovering the stolen Thunder Helm. Riju agrees with this suggestion, and Buliara assures her that recovering the Thunder Helm should be an easy task for Link if he is truly a Champion. Buliara tells Link that Captain Teake in the Barracks nearby can tell him about the thieves who stole the Thunder Helm. If Link speaks to Buliara again, she asks him what is wrong and says that if he is truly the Champion of legend, the task should be simple. She then reiterates that he should see Captain Teake to learn more about the thieves and comments that this is his chance to show them what he is capable of. When Link returns with the Thunder Helm, Buliara will direct him to Riju, saying she is on the second floor. She notes the special permission he has received to be able to enter Riju's Bedroom, and she reminds him to be on his best behavior. During this time, Riju notes in the Chief's Diary how Buliara trusts in Link's abilities

him to Riju, saying she is on the second floor. She notes the special permission he has received to be able to enter Riju's Bedroom, and she reminds him to be on his best behavior. During this time, Riju notes in the Chief's Diary how Buliara trusts in Link's abilities and does not mind that he is a man, which is a surprise to her. After Link calms Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Buliara tells him that they are indebted to him. She also informs Link that Gerudo Town is his ally now, but she warns him that he should still hide that he is a man. When Downloadable Content Pack is active, Link can ask Buliara about the Sacred Orb, an Ancient Orb guarded by the Gerudo. Though she is shocked he knows about it, Buliara admits that it has been stolen by the Yiga. She also shares rumors that the Yiga have begun regrouping at the Yiga Clan Hideout. Link can recreate the Champion's Arms if they are broken by speaking to Buliara. She will make a new Scimitar of the Seven if Link can supply her with one Diamond, five pieces of Flint, and a Gerudo Scimitar. To make a new Daybreaker, Buliara requires one Diamond, five pieces of Flint, and a Gerudo Shield. Other Appearances At the end of the "Gerudo Fury" Challenge, Riju notes how popular Hot Springs are amongst the Gerudo Soldiers, and she plans to discuss this with Buliara upon her return home.

is a character in . Biography Burmano is a Hylian who resides at Lookout Landing. He carries a Soup Ladle. As the newest member of the Emergency Shelter, he has been tasked with Cooking for all of the other inhabitants. According to Scorpis, Burmano has been struggling to come up with daily menus. In the Emergency Shelter's Kitchen, Burmano can be found contemplating Cooking healthy Meals. When Link approaches him, Burmano recognizes that he is also new to Lookout Landing and introduces himself. He wants to make a Fruit and Mushroom Mix due to how fancy it sounds, but he needs an Apple in order to complete the Recipe. Following this conversation, the Side Quest "Today's Menu" will begin. Should Link already have an Apple when he speaks to Burmano, he will be able to smell it. When Link returns to Burmano, he once again complains about having no Apples. If Link chooses not to give an Apple to Burmano, he reiterates that he would be able to make his Fruit and Mushroom Mix if he had one. If Link gives Burmano an Apple, Burmano offers his Meal to Link. After Cooking a Fruit and Mushroom Mix, Burmano dubs it his special mix and gives some to Link. Afterwards, he admits that all one needs to make it is an Apple, a Mushroom, and a Cooking Pot, and he encourages Link to try making it himself. Following the Side Quest, Burmano will again thank Link for bringing him the Apple. He is happy that he will be able to provide energy to the Monster-Control Crew. Burmano then allows Link to use the Kitchen's Cooking Pot. When Link next visits the Emergency Shelter, Deon will inform him that Burmano left for Hyrule Castle.

is a character in . Biography Burwar is a Hylian who, alongside Drozer, guards the Southern Gate of Lookout Landing. He wields a Rusty Halberd. When Link first approaches Burwar, he will be distracted. If Link tries to enter Lookout Landing for the first time from the Southern Gate, both Burwar and Drozer will be surprised by his appearance. They tell him that he should report to Purah at the Research Lab. If Link speaks to Burwar after he has already entered Lookout Landing, he claims that he saw something fall from the Great Sky Island, but he forgets about it when he realizes Link has returned. He immediately sends Link to speak with Purah. If spoken to again, he theorizes that what he saw falling from the Great Sky Island could have been Link, though he dismisses this thought and once again directs Link to Purah. Even after Link has spoken to Purah, Burwar is still distracted by the Great Sky Island. He is now convinced that what he saw falling was a person, and he has not been able to stop thinking about it. He wants to find an expert on Sky Islands among the Zonai Survey Team, but he is not sure when he will be able to leave his post.

are recurring Enemies and Objects in . Cacti go unnamed in , , , , , , and . Characteristics In , Cacti can be found in the Yarna Desert. When Link touches them, he takes half a Heart of damage, or a quarter of a Heart with the Blue Mail. Cacti can be found in the Samasa Desert in . Cacti can be found in the Lanayru Desert in . When struck with Link's Sword, the struck area of their skin falls off and they bounce back and rebound at him. If Link is hit by a Cactus with skin in the area that hits him, he takes a quarter of a Heart of damage. If he is struck by an area without skin, it will only bounce off him without dealing damage. Cacti may either have Bomb Flowers or closed red Flowers growing off them. When red Flowers are struck, they open and reveal either Deku Nuts or a Heart. Cacti in sometimes have Voltfruits growing from them. Cacti can be found in the Gerudo Desert. Other Appearances Cacti are Objects found in the Valley of Seers Stage. Cacti are stationary plants found in the Desert. When the current hero walks into one, they inflict half of a Heart in damage. They cannot be moved or destroyed. Cacti appear throughout the Gerudo Desert.

is a recurring character in . Biography Cado is a member of the Sheikah Tribe who lives in Kakariko Village with his beloved Cuccos. He is separated from his ex-wife, Rola, but both remain in the Village. He is a talented archer who normally wears his Phrenic Bow on his back in addition to the Eightfold Blade he wears on his hip. In the Journal of Various Worries, Cado recounts the end of his relationship with Rola. She asked him to choose between herself and his Cuccos, and he chose the Cuccos. Within, he signs his name as "The Bow Master". When Link first approaches Impa's House in Kakariko Village, Cado and his fellow guard Dorian will take a defensive stance and demand he identify himself. However, he then notices the Sheikah Slate on Link's belt and realizes who the young hero must be. The two relax their stances and Dorian apologizes, inviting the young hero inside to see Impa. Cado and Dorian will step aside to allow Link passage, and Cado will again apologize. Cado admits they are on high alert due to the Yiga Clan. Link can ask about them to learn the history of both the Sheikah and the Yiga. Cado will describe how their Ancient Technology was once used against Calamity Ganon, but then was considered too dangerous and forced the Sheikah into exile. Cado explains that while some were able to move on and lead normal lives, others were embittered and formed the Yiga Clan. He declares that he and Dorian are stationed to protect Impa against a possible attack from them. Cado asks that Link take caution in his travels, as the Yiga are likely to wish him harm. He reminds the hero not to underestimate them as an opponent. After Link has had his first meeting with Impa, Cado and Dorian will begin to take shifts guarding her home. At noon, Cado will head home to his Cuccos, whom he refers to very affectionately. However, Cado is utterly shocked and horrified to find that most of the birds have flown away. He is so dismayed by their absence that he breaks down into tears, explaining that his wife has left him and the Cuccos are all he has. Cado has difficulty holding himself together, startling Link with his sudden sobbing. Link can try to reassure him that they will return, but he replies that he has been waiting for his wife to return as well. Speaking to him again has him despairing over the idea that his Cuccos have decided to leave him the way his wife did. Cado breaks down into sobs again, but Link can volunteer to search for them to cheer him up. He explains that he has 10 Cuccos in total, at which point the "Flown the Coop" Side Quest begins. When Link returns all of the Cuccos, Cado will excitedly inform him that they have all returned. He thanks Link for his help and gives him a Purple

cheer him up. He explains that he has 10 Cuccos in total, at which point the "Flown the Coop" Side Quest begins. When Link returns all of the Cuccos, Cado will excitedly inform him that they have all returned. He thanks Link for his help and gives him a Purple Rupee as a reward. With his Cuccos back at his side, Cado asserts he is ready to face the world again. However, he still wishes that Rola would come back to him. This completes the Side Quest. After the Side Quest, Cado will continue to watch over his Cuccos until late into the night. He admits that while he is nervous about leaving them alone, he knows he needs his sleep. Even is his sleep, Cado mutters to his Cuccos, begging them not to leave. Any other time Link comes by to see him, Cado is okay with his Cuccos hopping the fence and exploring, mentioning that they can be used to fly. Link can ask him about the fact, and Cado will proudly declare that it is true. He happily describes the feeling of flying with a Cucco as the greatest joy in his life. At the outset of "The Stolen Heirloom" Shrine Quest, Cado explains to Link that something awful happened, despite the fact that he and Dorian were standing guard the whole time. He is shocked that they allowed someone to sneak past them. During the Shrine Quest, Cado is angry that the Sheikah Heirloom was stolen and wonders how the thief made it past him and Dorian. He reveals that the only let through known villagers, as they're able to come and go as they please. The only people he remembers visiting around the time of the theft are Lasli and Mellie. When Dorian leaves his post, Cado wonders why he has not returned yet. He recalls that Dorian said he was going to the forest above the village, but Cado believes he is taking longer than expected.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Slices of Cake are sold at the Bakery for 60 Rupees. Eating them will heal one of Link's Hearts and has a chance to give him a Kinstone Piece. Link is able Cook a variety of Cakes. All Cakes require both Tabantha Wheat and Cane Sugar in their creation, while all but Fruitcakes also utilize Goat Butter. When Link eats these Cakes, several of his Hearts will be healed. The exact number is dependent on the type of Cake he eats and what ingredients were used to make it. List of Cakes All varieties of Cakes that were present in return in . In addition, Link is able to Cook two new types of Cake. List of Cakes Other Appearances Two types of Cake can be made. Both of these Cake require Cane Sugar and Tabantha Wheat to create. List of Cakes

is a recurring character in . Biography Calip is a researcher who lives in a cabin at Fort Hateno. He spends his time researching Ancient Shrines while boasting about his accomplishments in the field of research. He demands that people address him by his professional title, Doctor Calip, claiming that he spent too much effort to simply be called by a standard honorific. He highly values his work to the degree that he refused to tell his family where he conducts his archaeological research. If Link indulges in his desire to be honored with the title "Doctor," he will change his attitude towards Link and share some of his findings, directly quoting from the worn book on his table, An Ancient Text. This initiates the Shrine Quest "The Cursed Statue" as he dismisses Link to continue his research. Starting at 6:00 AM, Calip rushes to the site of his fieldwork. He stays there until 5:00 PM, at which point he begins to return home to avoid the monsters that appear at night. If rain strikes as he is out, he will rush home, explaining that his metallic glasses are a conductive hazard for lightning. If a rain shower hits before he leaves for fieldwork, he cancels his trip until the rain passes. If Link speaks to him while he is out of his cabin, he will allow Link to observe him work provided that he stays out of his way. After completing "The Cursed Statue", Calip will become determined to solve the mystery of Kam Urog Shrine and continues to take trips out to his research site. There, he will comment on the timing of the Shrine's appearance. Calip is an archaeologist for the Zonai Survey Team who can be found in Kakariko Village. According to Calip's Journal, at the start of the Upheaval, Calip observed ruins falling from the sky west of his home and was grateful that neither he nor his home were harmed. A member of the Zonai Survey Team visited Calip and told him about the Ring Ruins. He was attracted by the idea of many inquisitive types like Tauro gathering at Kakariko Village to investigate the ruins. He prepared to depart for Kakariko Village, hoping that the members of the Zonai Survey Team will address him as a doctor and a genius. In addition, he left his Journal behind at his home to let any wandering traveler know they may use the supplies he has left behind. Upon joining the Zonai Survey Team, Calip admired Tauro for his dedicated focus and willingness to make discoveries even without credit. Calip, on the other hand, wishes to receive credit and have landmarks named after him. Calip guards the Floating Ring Ruin, believing the site to be off-limits by the Order of Princess Zelda. If Link attempts to get too close to the Floating Ring Ruin, Calip will stop him. Calip is curious about the contents of the Floating Ring Ruin and desires for Princess Zelda to call

the Floating Ring Ruin, believing the site to be off-limits by the Order of Princess Zelda. If Link attempts to get too close to the Floating Ring Ruin, Calip will stop him. Calip is curious about the contents of the Floating Ring Ruin and desires for Princess Zelda to call him Doctor Calip. He does not know why Princess Zelda has forbidden the site, but he speculates it is for villagers' safety. During the Main Quest "Secret of the Ring Ruins", Link informs Paya and Tauro that the Princess Zelda's order was given by a Phantom Ganon impostor. Paya then gives Link permission to open the Floating Ring Ruin. Using Ascend, Link is able to enter the Floating Ring Ruin and take a Picture of the Ring Ruins Stone Slab inside. When Link shows his Picture to Tauro, he is shocked, calling over Paya and Calip to see it. As they examine the Picture, Tauro is able to decipher the words "Mineru" and "southeast". Calip notes that Mineru could be the name of a Sage. Although Tauro is excited, he notices that Paya appears to be thinking. She is able to translate more of the Zonai writing, referring to a Dragon land in the southeast. Fearing Paya is upstaging him, Calip points out that the Ring Ruins Stone Slab could be referring to the Zonai Ruins. Tauro praises Calip for this, which he appreciates. Looking back on what they have learned, Tauro determines that they can find out more by visiting the Zonai Ruins. He asks Calip to accompany him, which he agrees to. They plan to established their base camp near the Popla Foothills Skyview Tower. Tauro and Calip then depart for the Faron Grasslands. At the Popla Foothills Skyview Tower, Link can find Calip near a makeshift Tent. He welcomes Link to his base, revealing that Tauro has already left to see the Zonai Ruins near Dracozu Lake. If it is daytime, Calip expresses his hope to find more clues, though he claims he needs to rest before joining Tauro. At night, Calip is worried that Tauro has yet to return, wondering if he is caught up in his investigation. Later, when Link drops a Zonai Charge or Large Zonai Charge on the altar inside a Tall Dragon Pillar while wearing the entire Charged Set, the eyes of the Tall Dragon Pillars begin to glow and their horns start to spark. All of them are simultaneously stuck by Lightning. Drawn by the Lightning, Tauro and Calip arrive at the altar. They are shocked to find Link inside, though Calip is relieved that he is unharmed. Tauro asks Link if he knows what happened. He is impressed by Link's findings, though Calip laments that they are unable to visit the Sky Islands themselves. Since he needs to make a report to Purah, Tauro leaves Calip in charge of investigating the Zonai Ruins further. Though Calip is hesitant at first, Tauro's assurances convince him to stay.

is a recurring character in . Biography Calisa is a Gerudo who travels throughout the Gerudo Region carrying a Gerudo Scimitar and a Gerudo Shield. She can be found at the Gerudo Canyon Stable and the Kara Kara Bazaar, and she also traverses the Gerudo Desert. Calisa is a legendary treasure hunter, searching for both treasure and men. She has been treasure hunting for twenty year, so she is sure she can acquire any treasure she sets her eyes on. While at the Gerudo Canyon Stable, Calisa tells Link that she is looking for men at the Stable. She says that she would not rate any of the men as treasure except for Link. Calisa also mentions that she aims to dig up the buried Treasure Chests in the Gerudo Desert and find out what is inside them. Calisa wishes that she had a Sand Seal to cross the desert with ease. Calisa also asks Link how he has such strength and endurance from his runty body. She tells Link to keep an eye out for the leviathan bones in the desert as well. While at the Kara Kara Bazaar, Calisa comments that the whole town has been talking about the Yiga Clan. While in the Gerudo Desert, Calisa tells Link about a rumor of a great treasure buried in the sands. Calisa is also surprised that a runt like Link wants to cross the desert. If Enemies approach Calisa, she will exclaim that she could defeat the monsters if she was a few years younger. If Link defeats the monsters, she rewards him with a Spicy Meat and Seafood Fry.

are a recurring mechanic in . They are sounds that summon a character, enemy, or Animal, typically a Mount or Bird. A Call may also refer to the Instrument used to make the sound. In some games, Bokoblins blow horns to call for reinforcements, or to alert their camp when they spot Link. Calls made indoors fail to summon the callee, as they cannot hear them. Appearances Link can play a tune on the Whistle to summon the Flute Boy's Bird, who can Warp Link across Hyrule. Once Link escapes from Lon Lon Ranch with Epona, he can play "Epona's Song" to summon Epona from anywhere in Hyrule (but only as an adult). Link can play the "Scarecrow's Song" to summon Pierre. Link can play "Epona's Song" to summon Epona from anywhere in Termina. As in , he can play the "Scarecrow's Song" to summon Pierre. He must play the "Oath to Order" to summon the Guardians to Clock Town. and Link gains the ability to summon one of the three Animal Companions based on whose Flute he obtains. Playing Dimitri's Flute summons Dimitri the dragon Playing Moosh's Flute summons Moosh the bear Playing Ricky's Flute summons Ricky the Kangaroo In , Link can Call nearby characters to have them follow him. This applies only to the characters on which he can use the Command Melody: the Servants of the Tower, Medli, and Makar. Link can play a Note on the Ocarina of Wind to summon Zeffa, who can Warp Link across Hyrule. Link can pick Grass Whistles and use them on-the-spot to summon an Animal – he cannot carry the grass with him. He whistles "Epona's Song" with Horse Grass to summon Epona. Hawk Grass summons a Hawk. Hanch is also seen using Hawk Grass. At Lake Hylia, a Shadow Bulblin archer uses Horse Grass to summon the Twilit Carrier Kargarok. After Wolf Link defeats the Shadow Bulblin, he can summon the Twilit Carrier Kargarok by sitting at the Hawk Grass spot and mimicking the Call with a howl. Once Link dispels the Twilight at Lake Hylia, howling at the Hawk Grass summons a Kargarok used to play Fruit Pop Flight Challenge. Once her memory is restored, Ilia gifts a Horse Call which allows him to play "Epona's Song" anywhere. When Princess Zelda or Phantom Zelda is following Link, he can Call her to his current location. He can also play the "Song of Birds" to attract nearby Birds, including: Whip Birds, Doves, Crows, and Cuccos. Residents of Skyloft use finger whistling to call their Loftwing. On the Surface, Fi can use a telepathic signal to call LD-301S Scrapper. The signal registers as short piercing noise. Red Bokoblin leaders can summon more Red Bokoblins by blowing their Monster Horn.

The , also known as the Calora Lakefront Cave, is a recurring location in . The Calora Lake Cave goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Calora Lake Cave is a small Cave located on an island, which is part of a pond north of Calora Lake in West Necluda. Seven Ore Deposits and one Rare Ore Deposit are embedded in the Cave's ceiling. The Calora Lake Cave system has expanded since , and it now spans the area north of Calora Lake in West Necluda. It has two entrances: one along the northern shore of Calora Lake, and another that is located on the rock formation within an unnamed pond to the north. Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Calyban is a Gerudo woman who can first be found eating Hydromelons on top of the walls of Gerudo Town. If Link speaks to her, she will tell him that she cannot eat with Link staring at her and tells him to go away. Calyban plays a role in the Side Quest, "The Mystery Polluter", which begins with the Gerudo child, Dalia, crying because a water trough is unusable due to a flow of Trash in it. Link will find Hydromelon rinds flowing down into the trough through the upper waterway and must follow where they are coming from to find the source of the pollution. This leads Link to Calyban, who is throwing the rinds into the waterway. When Link talks to Calyban, she rudely insists that she can do what she wants. Stating that altruism is for suckers, Calyban refuses to stop eating melons unless Link brings her ten Wildberries. Wildberries are often found in cold places, such as the Gerudo Highlands and Hebra Mountains. Once Link has collected ten Wildberries and returns to give them to Calyban, she is amazed at how delicious they are. Calyban says that she may stop eating other fruit entirely if she has Wildberries. She then realizes how selfish she has been and leaves to go help Dalia clean up the melon rinds. When Link returns to Dalia, Calyban has already cleaned up her Trash and left. Dalia gives Link a Hydromelon that was given to her by "the lady who cleaned it up" as a thank you for caring about her. After the Side Quest, Link can find Calyban sitting in the shade nearby with Hydromelons and Hydromelon rinds. She says that she gave the Wildberries to Dalia to apologize and because she will always prefer Hydromelons.

is a recurring character in . Biography Cambo is a Hylian traveling merchant who travels between Wetland Stable and Kakariko Village with his Donkey. He does this to sell his wares and purchase products at Kakariko Village to sell before traveling back to Wetland Stable. At Kakariko Village, he rests under the tree at the Village's western entrance. When he reaches Wetland Stable, he sits under a tree behind the Stable. He carries a Hunter's Shield and a Traveler's Sword. Cambo has a habit of launching into explanations that, when finished, he realizes Link never asked for in the first place. He may also offer Link directions to Kakariko Village and Riverside Stable. When it's late in the day, he plans on stopping at Wetland Stable for dinner and a couple of Elixirs. Occasionally, Cambo speaks directly to his Donkey. The story as to how the two of them met is long, but since Cambo can't do it justice, he doesn't share it. When they have a potential customer, he'll calm it down or ask it to wait for him. He believes it understands him, and he reminds it of how clever it is. He agrees to give it a "vegetal delight". Despite all the Horses that pass him, he prefers his Donkey due to its strength and stuborn nature. Cambo gives Link tips for Cooking. He suggests thoroughly thoroughly Cooking Food before eating to avoid food poisoning. In addition, he warns Link against putting any Insects in his Food. However, he acknowledges that Insects and Monster Parts must be used when making Elixirs. Cambo is apologetic to his Donkey after being saved from Enemies, as he abandoned it in his fear. He also delights in the destruction of monsters. He'll give Link meals and Raw Meats as a reward. When Link approaches Cambo, he notices him eying his donkey's packs and asks if he wants to see his merchandise. He also allows Link to sell to him, and he'll thank him for his business after every purchase. If Link leaves, Cambo suggests the possibility of doing business later. With his whole stock bought, he thanks Link for being an enthusiastic customer. During rainy weather, he sells higher quality Meats and Mushrooms. Wares and Pricing

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses In , the Camera is given to Link by the Photo Bro at the Miiverse Gallery. The Camera is used to take screenshots of Levels of the Drablands by pressing the 'X' button; after the Level's completion, the most recent screenshot to be taken is saved to the Miiverse Gallery's photo album. Up to 99 photos can be saved to the photo album; the photos can be posted onto Miiverse from the Miiverse Gallery, and unwanted photos can be deleted from the photo album. The Camera cannot be used outside of the Drablands or in Download Play. Any Status Reports visible when the photo is taken will not appear in the saved screenshot, though other on-screen indicators including the Life Gauge, the Energy Gauge, and Communication Icons, will be retained. If the 3D slider is turned on when the photo is taken, then the screenshot will be viewable in 3D. In , the Camera appears as a Rune on the Sheikah Slate. It is an ancient piece of Sheikah technology. It is obtained in the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab from Purah after bringing Blue Flame to the Ancient Furnace outside of the Lab. Link must place the Sheikah Slate into the Guidance Stone in the Lab to repair the Slate and restore missing files. Doing so will add the Camera Rune, the Album, and the Hyrule Compendium to the Sheikah Slate. With the Hyrule Compendium, Link also receives the Sheikah Sensor +. After obtaining the Camera Rune, Purah asks Link to try it out by taking a Picture of her. The Camera Rune allows Link to take a Picture by pressing the 'A' button, which is saved to the Album. Link can aim the Camera with either the right analog stick or the gyroscope. Link can zoom in and out by pressing up and down on the D-pad. Link can also quickly access the Album by pressing the minus button and take a Self-Portrait by pressing the 'X' button. While taking a Self-Portrait, Link can position himself in eleven poses by using combinations of the left analog stick (up, down, left and right), the ZL button (ZL + up and ZL + down) and different types of weapons (one handed, one handed + shield, two handed, spear and bow). If Link takes a Picture of certain creatures, monsters, Materials, Treasure Chests, Ore Deposits, or pieces of equipment, it will be logged in the Hyrule Compendium. After being logged, Link can view information about the subject in the Compendium or track it with the Sheikah Sensor +. The Camera's Album comes with twelve Old Landscape Photos that were taken by Princess Zelda 100 years ago. After obtaining the Camera Rune and speaking to Impa, she will instruct Link to go to each location in all of Zelda's Pictures to recover his Memories. By visiting these locations, Link will experience a flashback of a Memory with Zelda where the Picture was taken. The Camera

years ago. After obtaining the Camera Rune and speaking to Impa, she will instruct Link to go to each location in all of Zelda's Pictures to recover his Memories. By visiting these locations, Link will experience a flashback of a Memory with Zelda where the Picture was taken. The Camera is unlocked during the "Camera Work in the Depths" Main Quest. As part of the Quest, Robbie discovers that the Purah Pad's Camera and the Hyrule Compendium have both been locked, though he is able to fix this. Once this has been done, Link can take a Picture of a Statue That Points the Way for Josha. Other Appearances The Camera Rune is featured as a crucial part of Zelda's Special Attack when she is using her starting weapon class, which is Sheikah Runes.

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview After Link starts the "Regional Phenomena" Main Quest, Josha will go to meet Robbie at her lab in Lookout Landing. The two can then be found arguing with each other. When Link approaches them, Robbie comments on how nice the day has been. Noticing Link, Robbie makes a remark about his Purah Pad and its development. At this point, Josha becomes annoyed and accuses Robbie of not listening to her, which draws his attention back to her. Josha reveals that she wants to investigate the Depths herself, but Robbie insists it is too dangerous for someone as young as she is, fearing what Purah would do to him if something happened to her. Despite this, Josha claims that she needs to know more about a "figure" in order to understand the Depths. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Josha in her lab at Lookout Landing. Text on-screen displays her name, along with the title "Head of Depths Research".|Josha's introduction When Link asks about the figure, Josha apologizes for leaving him out of the conversation. Josha explains that she has become interested in a Slate, which was brought back by the Zonai Survey Team after an investigation of the Depths. She theorizes that it could be evidence of a civilization in the Depths, and she wants to search for more clues. She laments that because of the danger, Robbie will not let her go. To cheer Josha up, Robbie offers to investigate the Slate with Link on her behalf. He claims that they will search for a figure resembling the one of the Slate, and if they are successful, they will use the Camera to take a Picture of it to show Josha. When Link expresses confusion, Robbie explains that he can use the Camera to capture a Picture of nearby scenery, which is then stored in his Album. He promises to teach Link how to take Pictures in the Depths. Since there are many Monsters in the Depths, Robbie also asks Link to protect him. Robbie then leaves for the Hyrule Field Chasm, asking Link to meet him there when he is ready. Josha tries to ask Robbie to wait, but he leaves anyway. She apologizes to Link for getting him involved in her Chasm Research, revealing that Robbie can be overly eager when it comes to helping her. To help Link in the Depths, Josha gives him 10 Brightbloom Seeds and a bundle of five Arrows. She suggests that in order to navigate the Darkness, he attach the Brightbloom Seeds to Arrows he shoots, which will light up the surrounding area. She then directs Link to go through the Southern Gate to reach the Hyrule Field Chasm. Josha expresses her excitement to see Link's Picture, and she asks him to take care of Robbie as well. Following this conversation, "Camera Work in the Depths" will begin. At the Hyrule Field Chasm, Link will discover that Robbie has already descended into the Depths. At

the Hyrule Field Chasm. Josha expresses her excitement to see Link's Picture, and she asks him to take care of Robbie as well. Following this conversation, "Camera Work in the Depths" will begin. At the Hyrule Field Chasm, Link will discover that Robbie has already descended into the Depths. At the bottom of the Chasm, he will find Ponnick looking for Robbie. When Link approaches him, he reveals that Robbie instructed him to guide Link to his location. However, Ponnick did not bring enough Brightbloom Seeds to keep up with Robbie, and now he has lost him. He claims that Robbie was initially only visiting the Nisoij Lightroot nearby, but he kept walking past it, Ponnick then asks Link if he has any Brightbloom Seeds. If Link says that he does not, Ponnick impresses upon him the danger of exploring the Depths without Light. If Link claims to have Brightbloom Seeds, Ponnick will be relieved. Either way, Ponnick tells him that they can be found in Caves on the Surface, and he can throw them or shoot them on Arrows to cause them to bloom into Brightblooms. Before Link leaves, Ponnick once again expresses his sadness about not having enough Brightbloom Seeds. Once Link reaches the Nisoij Lightroot, he can find a Note on the Table written by Robbie, in which he reveals that he is heading toward the Iayusus Lightroot to the west. Along the way is another Note on the Table, wherein Robbie claims to have spotted something resembling the figure on Josha's Slate. Robbie can be found near a Campfire at the Iayusus Lightroot, where he points out the Statue That Points the Way that resembles Josha's Slate. However, he complains about the Darkness making it difficult to see. He wishes that the Iayusus Lightroot was able to give off more Light. After Link activates the Iayusus Lightroot, Robbie is surprised and states that he feels refreshed, comparing it to being on the Surface. He then decides to begin examining the Statue That Points the Way. Recalling that Link has not yet used his Camera, Robbie asks to see the Purah Pad. He then discovers that the Camera and Hyrule Compendium have been locked, though he is able to fix this for him. After doing so, Robbie instructs Link to take a Picture of the Statue That Points the Way, noting that this is an opportunity to learn how to use it and test that it is still working. Once the Picture has been taken, Robbie asks to see it. When he sees it, Robbie is pleased with the results, and he is certain Josha will be too. Robbie claims that in the future, there will be more for them to investigate in the Depths. He then decides to return to Lookout Landing, telling Link to join him there soon. more for them to investigate in the Depths. He then decides to return to Lookout Landing, telling Link to join him there soon. At Lookout Landing, Robbie tells Link to show Josha the Picture he took. The roasting process is said to retain water within the Egg's shell, which causes a chewy consistency. Link can restore one and a half Hearts to his Life Gauge by eating a Campfire Egg. Campfire Eggs reappear in and are again a variety of Roasted Food. They can be made by exposing Bird Eggs to Fire or a Scorching Climate. The roasting process is said to retain water within the Egg's shell, which causes a chewy consistency. Link can restore one and a half Hearts to his Life Gauge by eating a Campfire Egg.

At the Kochi Dye Shop, Cane Sugar is an ingredient that can be used to make Green Dye. When Cane Sugar is boiled, it becomes a sweet juice that can be used to make cake. When Cooking, Cane Sugar is required for the following Meals: Cane Sugar reappears in . It is one of the few Ingredients that can only be purchased from Shops or Merchants, since it does not naturally appear in Hyrule. It is required for the following Meals: Other Appearances Cane Sugar can be sold for 3 Rupees each, but Bena accepts them for 7 Rupees.

is a recurring character in . Biography Canni is a Stable Worker at the Outskirt Stable whose job is to help travelers change their Horse's Gear and Mane. If Link approaches her with a Horse, she will offer to change its Gear, though she is only interested in Horses that have developed a strong bond with their riders. When Link and his Horse do not have a full bond, she will refuse and tell him to spend more time caring for it. However, if Link's bond with his Horse is fully realized, she will become excited and agree to change the Horse's Gear. From then on, she will change that Horse's Gear without needing to check its affection. If Link attempts to change the Giant Horse's Gear, she will apologize and inform Link that she doesn't have any Gear large enough to fit the Horse and that it wouldn't like for its Mane to be handled. Similarly, if Link attempts to change Epona's Gear, she will claim that Epona is too lovely and graceful to change her Gear.

are recurring Items, Objects, and Enemies in . Cannons most commonly appear as either stationary weapons or as weapons that can be equipped to a vehicle, such as a boat or Train, which can then be used to fire either Bombs or cannonballs. Location and Uses In , Cannons are dangerous traps that appear in some locations. They are connected to the walls of certain rooms; the room containing the Big Key in the Desert Palace, and a room in the third floor of Ganon's Tower known as the Corridor of Cannons. They move along the wall in a predictable back-and-forth motion, firing cannonballs at regular intervals. They are placed on either side of the room, so the cannonballs will assault Link from both directions, making it hard to pass. Link has to time his movements carefully to get beyond these traps, as they cannot be destroyed. After Link obtains Bombs from Tetra's Ship, the King of Red Lions facilitates the use of the Cannon. The cannon has a large range for such a small boat, and is a useful item when fighting off Gyorgs, Seahats, Octoroks and other sea-based enemies. When Link's Bomb stock is depleted, the Cannon cannot be used. Small, floating Cannons known as Air Cannons can be found in some stages in . They are used to blast all of the four Links to higher areas, but are also present to return to the top once the Links fall through a hole in the ground. Often, there are Large Force Gems for the Links to collect in these areas. Cannons are also found in . In Snowpeak Ruins, there are Cannons spread throughout the dungeon. In order to use them, a cannonball must be found and brought to the Cannon. To fire, Link must put the cannonball into the Cannon, then place a Bomb into the Cannon for ignition. This will send the cannonball flying and destroying any ice object in its path, including Freezards. The Cannon Manual in the Snowpeak Ruins explains how Cannons are used. Two Cannons can be found in the overworld which are used to transport Link between places. The first of these is Fyer's cannon, used to launch Link to Gerudo Desert, and the Sky Cannon, used to shoot him up the City in the Sky. In , Cannons are weapons which can be attached to the SS Linebeck. Link buys his first Cannon from Eddo's Garage for 50 Rupees, when he finds that the route to Northwestern Sea is blocked by Boulders. The Cannon has infinite ammunition and is fired by tapping the desired target with the stylus. A variety of Cannons with different appearances can be obtained in the same manner as other Ship Parts; most commonly from Shops, Treasure Chests and Mini-Games. The Cannon can also be used to get the attention of Golden Frogs by hitting them with a cannonball. List of Cannons A Cannon appears in as part of the Spirit Train. This Cannon has infinite

same manner as other Ship Parts; most commonly from Shops, Treasure Chests and Mini-Games. The Cannon can also be used to get the attention of Golden Frogs by hitting them with a cannonball. The first Cannon that Link acquires is the Practical Cannon, given to him by Alfonzo after the pair are attacked by Bulblins en route to the Snow Realm. The young Goron Yunobo offers to act as a Cannon ball to chase the Divine Beast Vah Rudania into Death Mountain. With Daruk's Protection, he is able to do so without being hurt. Cannons are the only means to break Metal Chests, dropping the Item inside. Cannons appear as Zonai Devices in . They can be found throughout the Sky Islands and near Zonai Ruins on the Surface. Cannons can be Fused to Weapons and Shields, which results in the Cannon firing when drawn. Shots from Fused Cannons deal the Weapon or Shield's base damage plus one. The Cannon is last used to keep Bellum at bay until Link slays the monster. The pirate Jolene uses Cannons on her ship to attack the SS Linebeck. These Cannons are also used on Bellum so Link can defeat him.

is a recurring character in . Biography Canolo is a Hylian traveler who can be found in Gerudo Canyon. She was previously traveling with her friends Sesami, Oliff, Flaxel, and Palme. However, the five of them were attacked by Bokoblins along the Koukot Plateau Path and ended up separated. At Gerudo Canyon Stable, Link can find Sesami, who managed to escape. He asks Link to let Canolo and the rest of his friends know that he is waiting for them at the Stable. This initiates the "Missing in Action" Side Quest. Canolo can be found on the northern part of the Koukot Plateau Path, which bridges the Koukot Plateau and Mount Nabooru together. There, she will be under attack by a Blue Bokoblin, which Link must defeat. Initially, Canolo is hesitant to believe that she has been saved. After being informed of Sesami's whereabouts, Canolo expresses her anger towards him for abandoning her. She agrees to go to the Gerudo Canyon Stable, though she is still upset. When she makes it to the Gerudo Canyon Stable, Canolo calls Sesami a Cucco and thanks Link for saving her. She admits that she did not know traveling could be so dangerous, as it was not mentioned in the guidebook she read. Having decided traveling is not for her, Canolo plans on heading back home after she rests. However, she has a feeling Link does not have the option to go home, so she wishes him well. Canolo and the rest of her friends chip in to give Link a Gold Rupee as thanks for saving them. After the Side Quest is completed, Canolo and her friends, with the exception of Sesami, disappear from the Gerudo Canyon Stable.
