are recurring Enemies and Bosses in . Characteristics Captain Constructs I are an advanced type of Construct that command Soldier Constructs. They can be found on Sky Islands and in the proximity of Zonai Ruins that have fallen to the Surface. Captain Constructs I are capable of Fusing nearby Items and Objects onto their Weapons, which makes their attack damage vary. Captain Constructs can wield Wooden Sticks, Long Sticks, Thick Sticks, Bows, and Zonaite Swords. They can also rarely attack with their horns, which deals two Hearts of damage. Upon their defeat, Captain Constructs I may drop Zonai Charges and Captain Construct I Horns. Other Appearances Captain Constructs I can be encountered as Powerful Enemies.

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Captain Constructs II are a moderately powerful type of Construct that command Soldier Constructs. They can be found on Sky Islands and around Zonai Ruins dotted throughout Hyrule. They are capable of Fusing nearby Items and Objects onto their Weapons, which makes their attack damage vary. Captain Constructs can wield Construct Bows, which deal a minimum of two and a half Hearts of damage. They also carry Strong Zonaite Swords, which deal a minimum of three and three-quarters of a Heart of damage. They also rarely attack with their horns, which deals five Hearts of damage. Captain Constructs II be seen with a variety of Shields. Upon death, they may drop Zonai Charges and Captain Construct II Horns. Other Appearances Captain Constructs II can be encountered as Powerful Enemies.

are recurring Bosses, Enemies, and characters in . Characteristics Captain Constructs III are an elite type of Construct that command Soldier Constructs. They can be found on Sky Islands and in groups surrounding Zonai Ruins scattered about Hyrule. Captain Constructs III are capable of Fusing nearby Items and Objects onto their Weapons, which makes their attack damage vary. Captain Constructs all wield Mighty Zonaite Swords, the attacks of which deal around 12 and a half Hearts of damage. A few use various Bows to attack. They also have a rare horn attack, which deals 10 Hearts of damage. Upon death, Captain Constructs III may drop Zonai Charges and Captain Construct III Horns. Other Appearances Captain Constructs III can appear as both allied fighters and Powerful Enemies in .

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Captain Constructs IV are an elite type of Construct that command Soldier Constructs. They can be found on Sky Islands, and in groups around Zonai Ruins scattered about Hyrule. Their identifying feature is their gold colour and the single red eye. Captain Constructs IV are capable of Fusing nearby Items and Objects onto their Weapons, which makes their attack damage vary. Captain Constructs IV wield Mighty Zonaite Swords, attacks dealing around 50 damage (12.5 hearts.) A few use various Bows to attack, dealing 48 damage. As the mightiest Construct, Captain Constructs IV can perform a wide variety of attacks such as windmill swings and ground slams. They may also attack with their horn; this attack is quite rare, but it does 48 damage (12 hearts.) Upon death, Captain Constructs IV may drop a large amount of Zonai Charges and Captain Construct IV Horns. Other Appearances In , Captain Constructs IV appear as Powerful Enemies.

is a recurring character in . Biography Cara is a Gerudo who, alongside Isha, owns the Starlight Memories Jewelry Shop in Gerudo Town. When Link first speaks to Cara, she apologizes and says that the Shop is not open right now. She goes on to explain that with the Divine Beast Vah Naboris around and the theft of the Thunder Helm, Gerudo Town has been facing many problems lately. After Link completes the "Tools of the Trade" Side Quest, Cara will tell him secrets about Isha as thanks. One secret is the fact that Isha's name is actually "Jewel", but she thought it was embarrassing to be a jeweler named Jewel. However, Cara thinks it is a fine name. She has also heard that Isha sleeps wearing nothing but Accessories, and she wonders whether she gets cold. Cara also shares that, despite Isha's claims that she does not do anything special with her looks, she visits the Hotel Oasis once a week. She teaches Link that people who make such claims are usually lying. She also describes Isha's past love triangle with Ashai, noting that both are still single.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Carok Bridge is a wooden bridge in Hyrule Field that spans the Regencia River east of the Breach of Demise. The ruins of an unnamed Hylian village sit just east of the Bridge, which includes the Carok Bridge Well. In Master Mode, two Treasure Chests can be found at Carok Bridge. A Wooden Chest containing a Diamond is found atop a platform held aloft by Sky Octorok south of the Bridge. A Metal Chest containing a Royal Guard's Claymore can be found on a similar platform north of the Bridge. A Korok can be found by breaking the Pot suspended by a chain underneath Carok Bridge's northern side. A second Korok can be found beneath a Rock atop a rock formation near the eastern side of the Bridge. Creatures Enemies Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials

The is a recurring location in . The Carok Bridge Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Carok Bridge Well is situated on the southeastern side of Carok Bridge in Hyrule Field. Alongside the Mount Gustaf Well, it was part of an unnamed Hylian settlement one century prior to the events of . This town was destroyed by Guardians during the Great Calamity. The Carok Bridge Well returns in , and it is still part of Hyrule Field. Link is now able to enter its interior, which is a small chamber containing several potted Brightblooms, two Barrels, a Wooden Box, and a Cooking Pot with an unlit Campfire. Additionally, there is a Note on the Table written by Aurie Taamu, wherein he claims to have been living and farming inside the Well due to its Stable Climate. However, when new Caves appeared as a result of the Upheaval, he left to explore the new Materials he could Cook with. Creatures Materials

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses and left In and , a meter consisting of six Carrots appears while riding a Horse. The number of remaining Carrots represents the number of times Link can whip the Horse to make it gallop. Carrots successively regenerate 3 seconds after the last whipping. If all 6 Carrots are exhausted, they regenerate simultaneously after roughly 7 seconds. In , Carrots appear only in "The Field", in the Bucking Bronco Mini-Game in Tingle's Tower, and in Shadow Battles. Touching a Carrot instantly puts the Links on Horses. Additional Carrots collected on horseback increase the Horses' speed. In "The Field", Talon invites the Links to use the Carrots in the farm area of Lon Lon Ranch after they safely return his daughter Malon to him. A Carrot encased in a Crystal Ball can be obtained by reading the Stone Slab at the farm entrance. Additional Carrots can be found moving back and forth over the ground, and in certain tufts of Grass. The Horses disappear after approximately 10 seconds—obtaining another Carrot resets the timer. In Bucking Bronco, the Links start on horseback and remain so even without additional Carrots, which serve only to increase speed in this case. In Shadow Battles, Carrots are one of the random items obtained from Crystal Balls. The Horses last only about 5 seconds. left|32px In , Carrots appear in two different varieties, Swift Carrots and Endura Carrots. Uncooked Swift Carrots restore half of a heart each. When cooked into a dish, they add a "Hasty" bonus which temporarily increases Link's movement speed. Uncooked Endura Carrots restore two hearts each and when cooked into a dish, grant Link a "Enduring" bonus which gives him extra maximum Stamina. Swift Carrots look like ordinary orange Carrots, while Endura Carrots are bifurcated with a lighter orange hue. Endura Carrots will also temporarily grant Horses three extra yellow Spurs with a carrot icon next to them. These extra "Carrot" Spurs act similarly to Link's extra Stamina Wheels granted via "Enduring" dishes and Enduring Elixirs as they are lost once used and can only be used after other Spurs have been used up including those granted by the Ancient Bridle. Roasted Endura Carrots have the same effect if eaten off the ground by Horses. Horses can also eat Swift Carrots but this only increases their Bond. Additionally the Giant Horse can eat both types but Endura Carrots only increase its Bond as it has no Stars in Stamina thus no Spurs. List of Carrots By creating an Echo of a Carrot, Zelda is able to summon her Horse to her location. When summoned an Echo, Carrots have an Echo cost of one. Other Appearances 64px|left In , Carrots appear as Plant-type Food. They are imbued with the Lightning Element. When consumed by a Companion Fairy in the Dining Room of the My Fairy mode, Carrots can increase the Fairy's Trust level and personality traits.

Carrot Cakes are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Carrot Cakes are a type of Cake made by combining Tabantha Wheat, Cane Sugar, Goat Butter, and either a Swift Carrot or an Endura Carrot in a Cooking Pot. Their mild sweetness makes them enjoyed by even those who dislike Carrot. Regular Carrot Cake can be made by using one of each carrot, which can be eaten to restore seven Hearts in Link's Life Gauge. Two other variations of Carrot Cake also exist, depending on which kind of Carrot is used to make them: Hasty Carrot Cake: Made by using a Swift Carrot. Eating one will grant Link a mid-level speed boost. They restore three of Link's Hearts and can also be sold for 40 Rupees. Enduring Carrot Cake: Made using an Endura Carrot. Eating one will restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. They restore five of Link's Hearts and can also be sold for 100 Rupees. Carrot Cake returns in with an identical Recipe. It can be made in either a Cooking Pot or a Portable Pot. A Carrot Cake appears in a House in Kakariko Village. A slice of the Cake can be seen on the Table inside the House, while the rest of the Cake sits on a cutting board in the rear left corner of the House.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Carrot Stews are made in Cooking Pots using Tabantha Wheat, Fresh Milk, Goat Butter, and either a Swift Carrot or an Endura Carrot. Regular Carrot Stew is made by either using both types of carrots or by using a filler as a fifth Ingredient. Consuming one will restore eleven of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. They sell for 70 Rupees if a carrot and an additional Ingredient are used and for 120 Rupees when both carrots are used. These stews are left to simmer for a long time, which brings out the carrots' sweetness. Using either type of carrot will result in one of two different variations of Carrot Stew: Enduring Carrot Stew: Made using an Endura Carrot. Eating one of these will completely replenish and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. They also heal seven of his Hearts and sell for 100 Rupees. Hasty Carrot Stew: Made using a Swift Carrot. When consumed, Link's speed will temporarily increase. They also restore four of his Hearts and can be sold for 40 Rupees. Other Appearances The Recipe for Carrot Stew is earned by completing the Quest "A Balm for the Soul". It is made using four Endura Carrots, four Tabantha Wheat, four Fresh Milks, and four Goat Butters. Through the completion of "Hungry Hunches", the amount of each ingredient used can be lowered to three. When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warrior's Special-Attack Gauge will charge slightly for every Enemy KO.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Castle Town Prison is a set of ruins located on the island of Hyrule Castle West in Hyrule Field. It is a desolate area with many charred Trees and building supports. The inactive remains of two Fallen Guardians, which can be searched for Ancient Materials, can be found near the northern and southern ends of the Prison. A Raft is tied to the end of the Dock on the north side of the ruins. At the start of the second Great Calamity, the Castle Town Prison and its prisoners were destroyed by Guardians, as they did not have enough time to react to being attacked. Most of the structure was burned, but its stone walls survived despite being severely damaged. As part of the "EX Treasure: Fairy Clothes" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link reads Misko's EX Journal to learn the location of Tingle's Outfit. The Book claims that one of the Armor pieces can be found "at the ruins where sinners were imprisoned." At the center of the Castle Town Prison, Link can locate a metal EX Treasure Chest embedded in the ground, which can be pulled free using the Magnesis Rune. Inside, Link will find Tingle's Shirt. Two additional Treasure Chests can be found within the Castle Town Prison. The first is a stone Chest atop the Prison's southern wall, which contains an Ancient Arrow. Atop the northern wall, Link can find another stone Treasure Chest containing a Knight's Bow. left|40px There are a total of two Korok Seed Puzzles in the Castle Town Prison. The first is an Offering Spot at the center of the ruins, marked by three Stone Statues. Link must place a Rusty Shield in the empty Spot. The second is a Cube Pattern on the north end of the Prison. When Link completes each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Equipment

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Castle Town Watchtower is located in the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins in Hyrule Field. An unlit Campfire can be found in the northern part of the wreckage and is accompanied by a red cloth marker. A metal door covers a Rock acting as a Natural Hiding Spot for a Korok in the eastern part of the ruins. A second Korok can be found by examining the Leaves with Fairy Dust atop the flagpole in the northeastern section of the ruins. Creatures Enemies The Castle Town Watchtower remains in ruins but features an abandoned campsite with an unlit Campfire. A single dead Tree sits near the center of the keep, and a Big Flag sits on its northeastern corner. Creatures Materials Treasure Chests

are a recurring type of location in . Features and Overview Dodongo's Cavern is the second Dungeon in , located part-way up the Death Mountain Trail. Originally used as a source of food for the Gorons, it has been infested with Dodongos and sealed off by Ganondorf. Once Link gets inside the Cavern and defeats King Dodongo, Darunia makes him a sworn brother of the Goron tribe and entrusts him with the Goron's Ruby. The Ice Cavern is a mini-Dungeon accessed from Zora Fountain, where Link obtains the Iron Boots and learns the Serenade of Water, both of which allow him to enter the Water Temple. It is filled with falling Icicles, Ice Stalagmites, and Ice-based Enemies. Other Caves include the Forest Stage in the Lost Woods, Death Mountain Crater, and the numerous Dig Caverns found throughout Hyrule. The second Level of the Woodlands in is the Buzz Blob Cave, where the Links use Bows to battle Blobs, pop Balloons, and activate Shock Switches. At they end of the Level, they reach a large pit area where they face off against the Electric Blob King. The Ice Cavern is the fourth Area of the Drablands. It contains four Levels set in an open-air, mountainous region, filled with slippery surfaces and rolling Boulders. Its Mini-Boss is Freezlord, and its Boss is Blizzagia. Several Caves appear throughout Hyrule in . Most of them are unnamed, but they would later reappear and gain names in . List of Caves As a result of the Upheaval, a number of Caves have opened throughout Hyrule. They feature unique Creatures and Materials that cannot be found anywhere else. Each Cave also contains one Bubbulfrog, which drops a Bubbul Gem upon its defeat. List of Caves The following locations meet the criteria of being Caves, but they are not listed as such on the Map and do not contain Bubbulfrogs: Caves can be found throughout Hyrule, a majority of which are unnamed. List of Caves Other Appearances Entering a Cave is an objective of the "Fire in the Hole" challenge.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Cave Under Zora's Domain can be found behind the Waterfall beneath the Great Zora Bridge in the Lanayru Great Spring. Its main feature is the Chasm Under Zora's Domain, which provides access to the Abandoned Lanayru Mine in the Depths. As part of the Side Quest "Secret Treasure under the Great Fish", Sidon shares a passage from an ancient text about the Zora royal family, which described a treasure being found beneath Zora's Domain's giant Fish Statue. Following his instructions leads Link to the Cave Under Zora's Domain. Behind the Waterfall at the back of the Cave, Link can find a Stone Chest containing the Vah Rudania Divine Helm, completing the Side Quest. Areas Creatures Materials

is a character in . Biography Cece is a famous fashion designer in Hateno Village who has taken over her family's clothing store, the Ventest Clothing Boutique. Cece's designs are known for incorporating the use of Mushrooms, which now adorn the Village. Cece aims to refresh the Village's old-fashioned focus on its produce, as championed by Mayor Reede, and aims to challenge him for mayor in the village's next election. In addition to those sold by Ventest Clothing Boutique, Cece herself has a private collection of rare clothing she will personally sell Link (though she does not enjoy parting with it), serving the same purpose as Granté in . Cece will not stock a particular item until Link has obtained it himself. Cece also does not stock the outfits worn by past legendary heroes, which are instead exchanged with Bargainer Statues. Cece is the only means of reobtaining the Hylian Shield if it breaks. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring character in . Biography Cecili is a Rito who manages the Swallow's Roost Inn at Rito Village. She greets Link as he enters and will thank him for stopping by. If Link speaks to her at night, she will remark that only Stalkoblins have a reason to be up so late. If Link refuses a bed at the Inn, she tells him to stop by whenever he is feeling tired. Swallow's Roost offers two options for visiting travelers: the standard Bed or the Rito-down Bed. When asked, Cecili explains that a Rito-down Bed is made using Rito feathers, and she claims if Link sleeps on it, he will never want to sleep on a Stable Bed again. She guarantees that she will eat her own tailfeathers if Link does not wake up full of energy. When Link agrees to sleep at the Inn, Cecili will ask when he wants to be woken. If Link asks to be woken in the morning or at noon, she wishes him sweet or pleasant dreams. If he wants to be woken at night, though, she tells him to rest up. Cecili will proceed to greet Link when he wakes up. In the morning, she hopes he slept well. At noon, she informs him that the sun has been up for some time. During the night, she asks how he slept and wonders what his reason for getting up in the middle of the night is. However, if Link purchased the Rito-down bed, she asks how it was and if he is feeling fully rested. She then tells Link to take care as he leaves.

is a recurring character in . Biography Celessa is a Hylian adventurer, and she can be found between Dueling Peaks Stable and Hateno Village. At Dueling Peaks Stable, she sits at the foot of one of the beds. She carries an Emblazoned Shield on her back, in addition to a Traveler's Sword. Previously, Celessa has met Impa, calling her a wonderful woman and suggesting Link meet her as well. She praises her lovely personality, having learned history from her. Celessa is currently on a pilgrimage to the Spring of Wisdom on Mount Lanayru. It is the final location on her journey. This pilgrimage is her attempt to recreate Zelda's steps. She wonders what she might have found at the Spring. However, she seems surprised by the fact she has made it this far safely, and she believes she is moving slower than Zelda did. Celessa asks Link if he has heard of Zelda before, revealing that she is not just a fairy tale and was once a real person. The reason for Celessa's pilgrimage is her love and respect for Zelda. When she does arrive at the Spring of Wisdom, she hopes to feel Zelda's presence. According to her, the princesses of Hyrule have visited it for generations. At Fort Hateno, Celessa will explain to Link that it was built to stop the Guardians. She describes an ancient battle once took place there, referring to the events of the Great Calamity. She laments the tragic battle where many Hyrulean soldiers lost their lives protecting Hateno Village from the onslaught of Guardian Stalkers, wishing to honor their sacrifice. She hopes that the souls of those who lost their lives have found peace. During her stop at Hateno Village, Celessa pays a visit to the East Wind. She remarks that, while Hateno Village escaped the brunt of the Great Calamity, its peace feels precarious. As a fellow traveler, she asks Link if he can feel it as well. When Celessa is caught in the Rain, she wonders if it is also Raining at Hyrule Castle. She also wishes for the spirit of King Rhoam to be at peace. As she travels at night, Celessa warns Monsters to stay away. If Link saves Celessa, she apologizes to him for having to look out for her. She will thank him and give him Mighty Meaty Rice Balls as a reward. On subsequent rescues, Celessa will reward Link with Rupees.

is a recurring Region in . Features and Overview Central Hyrule is the central Region of Hyrule, containing the Great Plateau and Hyrule Field. The Region was severely damaged in the Great Calamity a hundred years prior to the events of . Link begins his quest in this Region after waking up in the Shrine of Resurrection on the Great Plateau. Another major feature of Central Hyrule is Hyrule Castle, where Calamity Ganon has been sealed since the Great Calamity. During the time of Calamity Ganon, Central Hyrule is known as one of the most dangerous Regions in Hyrule. This is due to vast amounts of Guardians being present there and myriad Monsters, such as Bokoblins. Areas Central Hyrule reappears in , located underneath the Central Hyrule Sky. Areas Other Appearances

The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . The Central Square goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Castle Town Central Square is the busiest section of Hyrule Castle Town in . A fountain bearing the Hylian Crest rests in the middle, while a cafe bar can be found in the portion of the Square. Near the cafe is an entrance to the Goron Trading Post with a viewing platform, where Link can view the entire Central Square as well as buy a variety of wares from Gorons. Some musicians are situated near the entrance to Hyrule Castle, and farther back is a young Hylian, Soal, who will polish Link's shoes for just 10 Rupees, thus allowing the young hero to enter Chudley's Fine Goods and Fancy Trinkets Emporium. The cafe bar is one of Castle Town's oldest shops, so most of its customers are regulars. The cafe bar does not play an important role in Link's journey, but he can visit the cafe bar to hear the latest gossip from its customer. The customers at the cafe will also advise Link on which places to visit, such as the viewing platform to the side of the cafe or Fanadi's Palace. Areas The Central Square is located at the center of the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins in Hyrule Field in . It was once a place for rest, but became the starting grounds of the Guardians' rampage across Hyrule at the advent of the second Great Calamity. The ruins of a large stone fountain featuring three large birds sits in the middle, marking the center of the Square and the surrounding Town Ruins. A Korok Seed is given to Link for finishing a race that begins along the southern wall of the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins and ends just above the decimated fountain. Creatures Enemies Equipment The Central Square can be found at the center of the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins. Areas Creatures Korok Seeds Other Appearances

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Cephla Lake is a large body of water in the southeastern portion of Eldin Canyon, located along its border from Akkala. Cephla Lake sits at the bottom of a tall range of cliffs. Unlike many other bodies of water in Eldin, which are heated by the region's volcanic activity, Cephla Lake's water is kept at a cool temperature. Cephla Lake is largely featureless, having no islands or any other distinguishing landmarks with the exception of a monster camp in the Lake's south. This camp is watched over by Lizalfos, both guarding an unprotected Treasure Chest housing a Drillshaft. Enemies Areas Other Appearances At the start of the "Relentless as a Waterfall" Scenario, Mipha and Sidon come upon a fork in the road while piloting Divine Beast Vah Rudania to Akkala Citadel. The eastern path takes them through Cephla Lake, which is a longer journey with the advantage of abundant Water. Both pathways lead Vah Ruta to Akkala Citadel. As part of the "Defending Cephla Lake" Challenge, Sidon notices a horde of Monsters while piloting Divine Beast Vah Ruta. Fearing for the safety of Akkala Citadel, he takes it upon himself to fight off the Monsters using Vah Ruta.

is a recurring character in . Biography Chabi is a Hylian traveler who can be found throughout Hyrule. She carries a Hunter's Shield and a Traveler's Sword. Link can save her from Bokoblins that regularly attack her as she camps. She always gives Monster Extract as a reward. The first time Link saves her, Chabi asks him how much he knows about Kilton and the Fang and Bone. She gives Link a Monster Extract and explains that it was made by Kilton. It makes Food taste better, and despite being made of monsters, Chabi considers it to be good. She also shares rumors about Kilton, such as the fact that he is obsessed with monsters and does research with them. Chabi wants to meet Kilton to see if the stories are true, but he is difficult to track down. She has heard from a trusted source that he is often found at a skull-shaped lake in Akkala. According to her, Kilton is more interested in researching monsters than any normal person. After Link has visited the Fang and Bone for the first time, Chabi notes that Kilton has been spotted all over Hyrule Kingdom, not just in Akkala. She shares stories of his shop popping up out of nowhere when night falls. Because of this, she is beginning to doubt whether she wants to meet him. When Link saves Chabi again, she might insist that she did not need his help. However, she might thank him for making the situation simpler. She is embarrassed she had to have Link save her again. Though she has not gotten anywhere in her search for Kilton, she has not given up. She swears to find him someday. Chabi camps at the following locations: The fork in the road on the West Hyrule Plains near Ludfo's Bog. Here, she is attacked by a Blue Bokoblin. The ruins of a house south of Serenne Stable on Rowan Plain. She is found fighting a Black Bokoblin. The road east of the Akkala Parade Ground Ruins, where she fights a Blue Bokoblin. In the Shadow Pass forest south of the Shadow Hamlet Ruins. She is attacked by a Blue Bokoblin at this location.

The are an Item in . Location and Uses The Champion's Leathers serve as a replacement for the Champion's Tunic, which is destroyed during Link and Zelda's encounter with Ganondorf Beneath Hyrule Castle. Upon reading Zelda's Diary in her Secret Well in Hateno Village, Link learns that she was planning to surprise him with the Champion's Leathers, having noticed that his original Tunic had become worn during their travels. To keep the Leathers a secret, she hid them in the Throne Room of Hyrule Castle, with a pair of Torches being the key to reveal them. Reading this Book starts the "A New Champion's Tunic" Side Quest. When Link lights both of the Torches in the Throne Room, the statue behind the thrones will shift to the side, revealing a metallic Treasure Chest inside its pedestal. Upon opening the Chest, Link will receive the Champion's Leathers. When worn, the Champion's Leathers gives Link the ability to shoot sword beams from the Master Sword regardless of current hit points. The Champion's Leathers has the highest potential defense of any Armor present in the game, with a maximum defense of 32. Enhancing

is a recurring location in . Champions' Hall goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Champions' Hall makes up the second floor of the Sanctum of Hyrule Castle. Previously, the Throne Room could be seen from the center of the Hall, but that view is now blocked by Ganon's Cocoon. As a result of this, it has also been covered in Malice. Despite this, spiral staircases on either side still allow Link to access the Throne Room. During the "EX Royal Guard Rumors" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack, Link can read in Super Rumor Mill V4 that a part of the Royal Guard's equipment can be found on the second floor. At Champions' Hall, he will find a Hidden Chest at the foot of a statue of a knight. After opening it, he will receive the Royal Guard Cap. As in , the Champions' Hall is located above Hyrule Castle's Throne Room in Hyrule Field. Following the Upheaval, it became infested with Gloom. Enemies Equipment Treasure Chests

The is an Armor Set in . Location and Uses The Charged Set is made up of the Charged Headdress, the Charged Shirt, and the Charged Trousers. Each can be found inside a Treasure Chest, located in rooms along the Dracozu River that are marked by Tall Dragon Pillars. Wearing the entire Armor Set grants Link the Stormy Weather Charge Set Bonus. During the "Secret of the Ring Ruins" Main Quest, Tauro is able to translate the Zonai writing in one of the rooms for Link, which instructs the reader to wear the Charged Set and offer a Zonai Charge to an altar. If Link follows the instructions and places a Zonai Charge to the altar at the end of Dracozu River, Lightning will simultaneously strike all of the Tall Dragon Pillars, which disperses the Thunderstorm that has been hiding the Thunderhead Isles. Dye Options Enhancing

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Charred Peppers are a type of Roasted Food, being the result of Spicy Peppers that have made contact with Fire or a Scorching Climate. The roasting process is said to remove some of the spiciness of the Pepper. Link can heal three quarters of a Heart by eating a Charred Pepper. Charred Peppers reappear in and are again a variety of Roasted Food, which are created when Spicy Peppers come into contact with Fire or a Scorching Climate. Following the roasting process, the Pepper's spiciness is reduced. When Link eats a Charred Pepper, he heals three quarters of a Heart.

is a recurring character in . Biography Chessica is the proprietor of the Fishing Resort, an Inn in Lurelin Village. She welcomes Link as he arrives and, figuring he is tired, asks if he wants to stay. She offers a regular Bed for 20 Rupees and a fluffy Bed for 40 Rupees. If Link declines to stay at the Inn, Chessica is disappointed but reminds him to stay another time. When Link does decide to stay, she asks him how long he wants to sleep. Once Link chooses when to wake up, Chessica sends him off to sleep. When Link wakes up, Chessica asks if he slept well. For staying at the Inn, she allows Link to use the Raft at the Dock, and she encourages him to come again.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Chichim Shrine can be found in the Ancient Prison Ruins in the Gerudo Desert. It corresponds to the Mihcihc Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Chichim Shrine The Chichim Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Chichim Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can obtain Chickaloo Tree Nuts by killing any Sparrow, searching Trees and the floors of forests, or in the waterways of Zora's Domain. Chickaloo Tree Nuts are commonly used as Food and can be eaten raw to restore a quarter of a Heart. They can be roasted in Fire to create Roasted Tree Nuts, or they can be used in a Cooking Pot as part of a Recipe. Chickaloo Tree Nuts are also used in the Kochi Dye Shop as an ingredient for Crimson Dye. When Cooking, either Chickaloo Tree Nuts or Acorns are needed to make the following Foods: Meal Ingredients Acorn or Chickaloo Tree Nut Cane Sugar Goat Butter Tabantha Wheat Acorn or Chickaloo Tree Nut Other Appearances Chickaloo Tree Nuts can be sold for 3 Rupees. Chickaloo Tree Nuts can be obtained as Materials in .

are recurring characters in . Biography In , Child Gorons reside on Goron Island, where they are almost as numerous as their adult counterparts. Child Gorons exhibit the same tribal pride and manners of speaking as grown-up Gorons, but they have a predilection toward playing as well as a variety of personality traits. One Child Goron seems annoyed by his father's obsession with Linebeck's Ship, and another one rewards Link with Treasure Map #14 for defeating a group of Yellow Chuchus which have appeared on a nearby hill. Some readily welcome Link to their homeland, with several even willing to call the young hero "Brother" before he has officially joined the tribe, while others are more hesitant to trust him, including the island chief Biggoron's son, Gongoron. Child Gorons also appear on Dee Ess Island, where they help to set up and manage the Goron Game. While the average maturation period of a Child Goron is unknown, one particular Child Goron is shown to grow into a full-sized Goron by the time Link has completed the Goron Temple, thanks to a healthy diet of Wood Hearts. Several Child Gorons appear in . One is the Goron Elder's grandson, who is known simply as the Goron Child. After Link completes the Fire Temple, the Goron Child asks Link to take him to Castle Town, as he would like to experience life in the "big city" and hopefully meet a Princess in-person. A different Child Goron manages the Goron Target Range just west of Goron Village. Another is held captive at the Pirate Hideout, while his friend waits outside the Hideout's entrance to request help from Link; these two Child Gorons appear to perpetually swap places whenever the captive one is rescued. Several Child Gorons appear in , including Axyl, Dugby, Offrak, Pelison, and Slergo. All of the Child Gorons from reappear in , along with the new character Tule, the younger brother of Barin.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Chillfin Trout can be caught by Link in the waters of the Tabantha Frontier and Hebra Mountains. The Coral Reef in Zora's Domain also sells them. They can be eaten raw to restore one Heart to Link. Similar to other trout, Chillfin Trout become Roasted Trout when exposed to Fire and Frozen Trout when chilled by Ice. When Cooked, Chillfin Trouts provides Heat Resistance. Like other Fish and seafood, Chillfin Trouts can be Cooked to make the following Foods: Meal Ingredients Any Seafood Any Vegetable, Herb, or Flower Fresh Milk Rock Salt Any Fish Any Mushroom Any Seafood Goat Butter Rock Salt Tabantha Wheat 1-3 Fish Any Seafood Courser Bee Honey Any Seafood Raw Gourmet Meat or Raw Whole Bird Any Seafood Raw Meat or Raw Bird Drumstick Any Meat Any Seafood Monster Extract Any Seafood Spicy Pepper Any Seafood Raw Prime Meat or Raw Bird Thigh Any Fish Rock Salt Any Seafood (except porgy or salmon) Goat Butter Tabantha Wheat Any Seafood Hylian Rice Any 4 different Seafood Any Seafood Any Vegetable, Herb, or Flower Chillfin Trouts are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances Chillfin Trouts can be sold for 6 Rupees.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Chillshrooms are found at the base of Trees in the Hebra Mountains and on Mount Lanayru. They can also be bought in Gerudo Town from Ardin's Stall. When eaten, they restore half of a Heart. A Chillshroom that is exposed to Fire will turn into a Toasty Chillshroom. Food made using a Chillshroom will grant Link Heat Resistance. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to create Blue Dye. Chillshrooms, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Chillshrooms, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Chillshrooms are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances Chillshrooms can be sold for five Rupees. Chillshrooms can be obtained as Materials in .

, also known as Elixirs That Stave off the Heat, and Cooling Elixirs, are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Drinking Chilly Elixirs will grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. They do this by providing a cooling effect, making them important for travelling through the Gerudo Desert. When spoken to, Guy the Rito will complain about the heat at Kara Kara Bazaar. He explains that he's heard of an Elixir that can help with the heat, but it isn't sold at the Bazaar. However, despite knowing that he can find the insects needed in the Gerudo Highlands, Guy isn't motivated due to the monsters up there. This initiates the Side Quest "An Ice Guy". Link can make a Chilly Elixir for Guy, who will be happy he can cross the Gerudo Desert during the day. He'll give Link 50 Rupees as a reward. Chilly Elixirs can be made by Cooking any of the following critters with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot: Cold Darner Winterwing Butterfly By adding any of these chilly ingredients, Link can make a Chilly Elixir that will also heal him: Hydromelon Chillshroom Cool Safflina Chillfin Trout

is a recurring character in . Biography Chio is a Korok that can be found underneath the Great Deku Tree in the Korok Forest. When Link first speaks to him, Chio recognizes him as the hero. He explains to Link that the mushroom on his head suddenly sprouted that day, so he had expected something to happen. Chio reveals that the Koroks all prepared a series of Korok Trials for Link. If Link has not yet pulled out the Master Sword, Chio says the trials will help him do so. However, if Link already has the Master Sword, Chio asserts that the trials will help him become stronger. He goes on to tell Link that he designed an extra-tough trial himself, as the elder of Korok Forest. He asks Link if he is ready to test his mettle. Accepting his challenge initiates the Side Quest "The Korok Trials". When Link asks, Chio informs him what the Korok Trials are before he gets started. He explains that the goal is to visit all of the Ancient Shrines in the Korok Forest to be considered a grown-up. According to him, it is a ceremony based on the ancient hero that every Korok must undertake. Chio and Hestu have both participated, as have several other Koroks. The first Trial that Chio shares is the "Trial of Second Sight", which is found in the southwest of Korok Forest. He then shares the location of the second Trial, "The Lost Pilgrimage", in the northwest Forest. Finally, he tells Link the third Trial, "The Test of Wood" is in the eastern Forest. He reiterates that overcoming the Korok Trials means one can overcome anything. The Koroks have also prepared prizes for Link when he completes the Trials. Once Link completes all of the Trials, Chio will be impressed. Recognizing that Link wants a reward, Chio has no choice but to give Link his most treasured item, three Big Hearty Truffles. He suggests eating a dish made with Big Hearty Truffles, as it will soothe all of his pain. After this, the Side Quest will be completed. Chio feels privileged to have witnessed Link pulling out the Master Sword. Without any additional Trials for Link, he encourages him to go and save Hyrule. Meanwhile, Chio says the Koroks will be cheering for him from the Korok Forest.

is a recurring character in . Biography Chork is a worker at the Tabantha Bridge Stable. He spends his mornings drinking at the table inside. In the afternoons, he takes care of the White Goats outside the Stable. When Link first speaks to Chork, he mentions the Pedestal at Washa's Bluff, south of the Stable. Previously, he investigated the Pedestal with Geggle, but neither of them could figure it out. If spoken to again, he will tell Link that a Rito Bard flew to Washa's Bluff to observe it himself. Link can return to Chork after completing the "Under a Red Moon" Shrine Quest. Chork is surprised to hear an Ancient Shrine was hidden by the Pedestal. He decides that his new goal is to solve the mystery of Mijah Rokee Shrine. He mutters to himself about how the Shrine only deepens the mystery.

, also known as , and , are recurring Enemies in . They are gelatinous creatures of living slime or jelly, often depicted with facial features. Chuchus come in a wide variety of colors and types, with some having different traits and behaviors depending on their color. Red, Green, Blue, Yellow and Purple Chuchus are among some of the most common types of Chuchus in the series. Beginning with , some Chuchus are capable of producing electricity as a defense mechanism, making them similar to Buzz Blobs in both appearance and behavior. Chuchus are relatively simple enemies to defeat; most varieties can be felled by a simple slash with the Swords, while some types must first be stunned with another item. In several games, Chuchus also leave behind Chuchu Jelly when defeated. Chuchu Jelly is valued as an ingredient that can craft restorative Potions that can replenish health or other vitals depending on its color, and in some cases can even act as a substitute for the Potions themselves. Characteristics Chuchus debut in . They appear as bottom-heavy blobs of transparent jelly with large, grinning mouths full of crooked teeth and round eyes on stalks. They move around by slowly oozing along the ground, but once they see Link, they attack by hopping towards him in an attempt to knock him down. However, they can be easily defeated with one or two hits with the Sword. Chuchus are characterized as appearing either Green, Red, Yellow or Blue. Depending on their color, they contain various items inside their bodies which are dropped as they are defeated. Chuchus will shortly respawn after being destroyed, making fighting them a quick means of restocking on supplies in little time. Red and Green Chuchus are commonplace to Termina Field, and carry Hearts and Magic Jars, respectively, in their bodies. Yellow Chuchus contain Arrows, and usually appear near puzzles or enemies that require the Bow. Blue Chuchus are the rarest, and only appear in the Great Bay Temple. They hold no items inside them; instead they can be frozen and used as a stepping stone by freezing them with the Ice Arrows, allowing Link to reach higher places. Tatl explains this by stating they are "just blob(s) of water." In , the Blue Chuchus sparkle, further indicating that they can be frozen. In , ChuChus take on a much different form that would become their most common depiction: they are top-heavy blobs of jelly with bulbous, yellow-green eyes that move by crawling or hopping on their pseudopod-like feet at their base. This appearance greatly resembles Buzz Blobs, an earlier slime enemy with a similar shape. When they appear, they make a distinctive chattering sound. If left alone, ChuChus melt into a tiny, slow-moving puddle, but immediately start hopping after Link when he approaches. Some ChuChus will ambush Link by dropping from above. alone, ChuChus melt into a tiny, slow-moving puddle, but immediately start hopping after Link when he approaches. Some ChuChus will ambush Link by dropping from above. ChuChus in come in various colors, each with their own traits and sometimes unique Chu Jelly. They come in Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, and a newer type called a Dark ChuChu, which is dark purple in color and its eyes glow a deep yellow. ChuChus live on many islands across the Great Sea, including dungeons and most notably, Pawprint Isle, an island famous for its ChuChu population. The Savage Labyrinth also contains Chuchus, among various other enemies encountered throughout the game; the only Chuchus that aren't found there are the Blue ones. Several ChuChus drop Chu Jelly when defeated, which can also be stolen from them with the Grappling Hook. Chu Jelly can be given to Doc Bandam on Windfall Island, a man studying ChuChus and their jelly, to craft new Potions as well as make free servings in exchange. Blue ChuChu 80px|right Blue ChuChus are an extremely rare type of ChuChu, with only 23 Blue ChuChus appearing in total throughout the Great Sea. They are found scattered on various islands. Blue ChuChus are highly electrified, and will shock Link if he attempts to attack one. However, these Chuchus will not pursue and try to attack Link like the other Chuchus do; rather, they'll try to flee from Link if he approaches. As they are constantly electrified, they must first be stunned before being attacked, with items such as with the Deku Leaf or the Boomerang. Alternately, they can be attacked with Bombs or Arrows. They drop the most valuable and rarest kind of Jelly: Blue Chu Jelly. If Link gives 15 Blue Chu Jellies to Doc Bandam, Blue Potions will become available for purchase. This type of Potion is a cure-all, being a mix of the Red and Green Potions, but it costs the most Rupees to purchase. Blue ChuChus, however, will only ever drop their Jelly Spoils once. Yellow ChuChu 100px|right Yellow ChuChus are another type that possess the ability to electrify themselves, but unlike Blue ChuChus, they do not keep their bodies electrified at all times and will periodically drop their electric guard. They are even rarer than Blue ChuChus (technically), as they only appear on Pawprint Isle and in the Tower of the Gods. Like all Chuchus except Dark Chuchus, they can be stunned with the Boomerang or the Skull Hammer to make defeating them easier, or attacked with Bombs or Arrows. Additionally, defeating Chuchus with the Skull Hammer shows an alternate death animation, where they're reduced to small blobs of jelly, then they dissolve and the Chuchu is defeated. Yellow ChuChus yield Red Chu Jelly when defeated or hit with the Grappling Hook (despite being yellow), and they may alternatively drop Green Chu Jelly in the same manner. Dark Chuchu alt=|left|82x82px Dark Chuchus are a unique type distinguished by their dark, purple coloration. They inhabit dark areas devoid of light, namely the Earth Temple and Ganon's Castle. These Chuchus are defeated differently compared to other Chuchus; Link cannot use the sword to defeat them, as they will just reform if struck this way. Instead, they have to be stunned with light, which turns them to stone. Then, the Skull Hammer can be used, or they can be picked up and throw them to break them in this state, thus defeating them. Tingle mentions that they cannot be defeated until Link obtains the Mirror Shield, but this technically is not true. Instead, it will just be harder to do so. If the Mirror Shield has not been obtained yet, Link has to lure Dark Chuchus into beams of light coming from the ceiling, then defeat them in the manner mentioned above. In , Chuchus have an identical appearance and behavior to those in . Most Chuchus emerge from the ground as small puddles, then pop up to leap at Link to attack. They also come in a variety of colors, each with different traits and characteristics. They are among some of the most common and weakest enemies, and can be found all over Hyrule. Blue Chuchus, like those in , have bodies that are constantly electrified. They can be attacked with Bombs or Arrows from afar, or alternately stunned with other items, such as the Boomerang. They are much rarer and are not native to any particular region. Spiny Chuchus are purple Chuchus that possess a unique trait: they shoot out thorns from their body when Link is near. These spikes protect them from a wide assortment of attacks, and will remain in this state until Link backs away, whereupon the Spiny Chuchu will pursue him. To defeat them, Link must either be quick to attack or stun them first. A Bomb is powerful enough to penetrate their defenses. Arrows can also be shot at them from afar. They appear at Mount Crenel, and also act as the Sub-Bosses of the Cave of Flames. Red Chuchus also come in an additional variant called a Rock Chuchu, which wear rock helmet over their faces. They appear in Veil Falls. These Chuchus do not jump, and their mask protects them from almost any attack. Their helmets can be destroyed by various attacks, including the Rock Breaker technique, turning them into regular Red Chuchus. A Bomb can also be used to defeat them instantly. Link also encounters two giant Chuchus in Dungeons. These enemies are normal Chuchus, but appear much larger as Link is Minish-sized when they are encountered. instantly. Link also encounters two giant Chuchus in Dungeons. These enemies are normal Chuchus, but appear much larger as Link is Minish-sized when they are encountered.
