These large Chuchus attack by jumping at Link periodically, and are fought by sucking up their jelly with the Gust Jar, though this does not work on other Chuchus when Link is normal-sized. When the Big Chuchus have enough of their jelly sucked up by the Gust Jar, they'll lose their balance, and then fall over after a few seconds; Link can then hit the Chuchus with his Sword and deal damage. When the big Chuchus are low on health, they'll jump around much more often. The Big Blue Chuchu will occasionally electrify itself, just like regular Blue Chuchus; it will be immune to the effects of the Gust Jar while it's electrified, but it won't electrify itself when it falls over. In , Chuchus are simply known as Chus, and are little more than large, amoeba-like blobs of opaque jelly. They slide and powerfully leap to move and attack. Like previous incarnations, Chus come in various colors, including Red, Blue, Yellow, Purple, and a very rare variant called a Rare Chu. While little else sets apart between them, Chus have the ability to split and merge. A large Chu will split into two smaller Chus when attacked, similarly to a Zol dividing into Gels when struck, and will keep splitting until they are too small to do so. Chus appear in several places, including the entrance way of the Lakebed Temple, the Snowpeak Ruins, and in hidden Caves. When Chus are defeated, they dissolve into a puddle which can then be scooped up into a Bottle to collect Chu Jelly. Unlike Chu Jelly of , their remains can be used immediately as a drinkable solution. They have various different effects depending on the color of the Jelly. Red and Blue Chu Jelly act as their respective Potions, Yellow Chu Jelly is used like Lantern Oil, thus cannot be consumed, and Purple Chu Jelly has one of four different effects, determined randomly: restore or take away one of Link's Hearts, fully restore Link's Hearts, or drain Link's health to one quarter of a heart. When two Chus of different colors collide, they will merge together and form a single, larger Chu. The new Chu will retain the color of the more common one (from least to most common: Rare, Blue, Red, Yellow, Purple). The exception to this is when a Blue and a Yellow Chu merge—which is only possible in the Cave of Ordeals—which creates a Green Chu in the Wii and HD versions; the Green Chu Jelly has no effect when drunk. Green Chu Jelly was meant to restore a Magic Meter that was scrapped during Twilight Princess's development; the HD Edition has messages when scooping up and

in the Cave of Ordeals—which creates a Green Chu in the Wii and HD versions; the Green Chu Jelly has no effect when drunk. Green Chu Jelly was meant to restore a Magic Meter that was scrapped during Twilight Princess's development; the HD Edition has messages when scooping up and viewing the description of Green Chu Jelly mentioning that it does absolutely nothing when consumed. These messages are not present in the original Wii Version. Rare Chus are a significantly rare variety that are pearl-colored and sparkle. They appear anywhere where Chus are, but the chances of finding one are incredibly slim. The only certain places to find them are the Cave of Ordeals, inside a small cavern in Death Mountain, and inside three hidden Caves accessed via a dig spot (one under a tree at Snowpeak, another in the Gerudo Desert, and another beneath the barn in Ordon Ranch). Rare Chus are highly valuable as they leave behind Rare Chu Jelly, which has the same effect as Great Fairy's Tears. However, not only are they hard to find, but they are also the first to be targeted by Purple Chus to merge. If a Rare Chu and any other Chu merge, the new Chu will become the other color, canceling out the Rare Chu. Additionally, if Link already has Rare Chu Jelly, any Rare Chus set to appear will be replaced with Yellow Chus. There's also data for Black Chus in the game. These Chus were scrapped in the final game, but are fully functional if added into the game. Black Chu Jelly has the same effects as the Nasty Soup, but if a Black Chu merges with any other Chu color, it'll turn into a Rare Chu; this is why the Black Chu was removed from the final game. Even so, Black Chu Jelly has fully functional messages in the Wii and GameCube Versions, stating that drinking it is a bad idea. In , ChuChus appear similarly to their and incarnations. They are a common sight throughout the World of the Ocean King and can be found on many islands and inside dungeons. Generally, ChuChus are slow-moving enemies that pop out of the ground when Link is near. Most can be easily defeated with just the Sword or the most basic items. They come in Red, Green, Blue and Yellow colors, as well as the Rock ChuChu variant. Yellow and Blue ChuChus, like previous incarnations, are electrified and will shock Link if he strikes one. Yellow ChuChus will periodically drop their electrical barriers, but Blue ChuChus remain electrified. They can be stunned with items such as the Boomerang to disable their barriers, or alternately attacked with Arrows or Bombs from afar. Rock ChuChus are similar to their incarnation, as they wear rock helmets that protect them from most attacks. This ChuChu variety likes to hide beneath large rocks, busting out whenever Link draws near. It can be destroyed with a Bomb, its helmet pulled off with the Grappling

Bombs from afar. Rock ChuChus are similar to their incarnation, as they wear rock helmets that protect them from most attacks. This ChuChu variety likes to hide beneath large rocks, busting out whenever Link draws near. It can be destroyed with a Bomb, its helmet pulled off with the Grappling Hook, or smashed with the Hammer. In , ChuChus appear mostly the same as in , but come in a few different variants. ChuChus in this game come in Red and Yellow colors, as well as three new variants called Ice ChuChu, Helmet ChuChu, and Metal Chuchu. As with the previous game, ChuChus are basic enemies that pop out of the ground and move slowly. They are among some of the most common and weakest enemies found throughout New Hyrule, and can be found in all four of its regional Realms. With the exception of the Ice ChuChu, all other ChuChus can be found in the Ocean Temple. Yellow ChuChus are an electrified variant, and must be stunned first to interrupt their electric field before attacking. The Whirlwind, Boomerang and Whip can all be used to stun them. Ice ChuChus are white ChuChus that produce an icy mist. Their mist prevents them from being attacked directly as it will freeze Link instantly, requiring the screen to be rubbed with the stylus to thaw him out. Like Yellow ChuChus, they can be stunned first to remove their defense mechanism, rendering them safe to attack. They appear in the Snow Realm. Metal Chuchus are another electric variant, but are more dangerous as their electricity is not disabled when they are stunned, and most items such as the Boomerang and Whip do not affect them. They can only be defeated with Arrows, Bombs, Sword Beams, Phantom Zelda's sword, or a by throwing a sharp object grabbed by the Whip, such as a thorn or a Helmet ChuChu's helmet. Metal Chuchus appear in the Ocean Temple and the Tower of Spirits. Helmet ChuChus are Red ChuChus that are similar to Rock ChuChus as they wear protective helmets, only except now their helmets are made of iron and have three horns. Their helmets are not easily destroyed, and must be pulled off using the Whip. The helmet can then either be thrown back at the ChuChu to defeat it or thrown away to finish it off with the Sword. Its helmet can also be thrown to damage other enemies as well. They appear in the Ocean Temple. In , Chuchus appear as blobs of jelly with dripping mouths and bulging eyes. They slowly crawl after Link when they spot him, and sometimes emerge from the ground. Chuchus come in various sizes, ranging from large to very small. Like Zols and the Chus of , when they are struck with the Sword, they will split into smaller Chuchus. Although similar, the enemies are not as simple as previous incarnations, and must be dealt with accordingly - if struck horizontally with the Sword, a Chuchu will split

very small. Like Zols and the Chus of , when they are struck with the Sword, they will split into smaller Chuchus. Although similar, the enemies are not as simple as previous incarnations, and must be dealt with accordingly - if struck horizontally with the Sword, a Chuchu will split horizontally, only for the top Chuchu to fall right on top of the other, causing them to merge back into their larger size. As such, they must be attacked with a vertical slash to split and distance them from each other to prevent them from merging. Bombs are also very effective, as they are absorbed into any Chuchu that touches them and will destroy any size of Chuchu upon exploding. If two Chuchus merge, they will form a Chuchu one size larger than the bigger of the two, regardless of the size of the smaller. Like Gels, small Chuchus can also grab a hold of Link's foot and slow him down until they are shook off. Four variations of Chuchus exist in , with some found in both Skyloft and various regions of The Surface. These include Green, Blue, Red, and Yellow Chuchus. Although they share the common colors of previous incarnations, the traits of each Chuchu are now slightly different. Green and Blue Chuchus do not have any particular abilities, although the green ones are found on land while the blue kind are found underwater. Yellow Chuchus are native to the Lanayru Desert region and retain their electrified bodies. They are capable of releasing an electric discharge, a defense which they tend to use after being split. While Chu Jelly does not appear in , Chuchus may sometimes drop Jelly Blobs after being defeated, which can be used to craft certain items. According to Fi, Chuchus are believed to reproduce asexually in a process similar to cell division, though this is only seen when Link purposefully divides a large Chuchu. In , Chuchus are common Enemies throughout Hyrule. They often hide in Trees or underground in order to ambush their prey. Standard Chuchus are blue, and they will drop Chuchu Jellies when defeated. However, when they are defeated by an elemental attack, such as Magic Gear or other elemental Weapons, Arrows, or environmental factors, they will drop Yellow Chuchu Jellies, Red Chuchu Jellies, or White Chuchu Jellies, depending on the elements used to kill them. Three size variations of Chuchus can also be encountered, which will drop more Chuchu Jellies when defeated. However, they are also stronger than their smaller counterparts. Three additional variations of Chuchus appear, known as Fire Chuchus, Ice Chuchus, and Electric Chuchus. These variants can be found naturally in certain Regions, but they can be summoned by their respective elemental Wizzrobe. These Chuchus will inflict their respective elemental effect when they attack Link, though they are also capable of releasing elemental blasts. A similar, larger blast is also triggered when the elemental Chuchu is killed. After releasing these blasts, elemental Chuchus enter a "powered-down" state,

summoned by their respective elemental Wizzrobe. These Chuchus will inflict their respective elemental effect when they attack Link, though they are also capable of releasing elemental blasts. A similar, larger blast is also triggered when the elemental Chuchu is killed. After releasing these blasts, elemental Chuchus enter a "powered-down" state, marked by darker and duller colors. In this form, they lack their elemental coatings and thus cannot utilize their elemental abilities. After a few seconds, a powered-down Chuchu will restore its coating and abilities. Drops Chuchus reappear in . The Jelly they leave behind can be altered into different types by exposing it to elemental attacks or extreme weather conditions. Other Appearances right|80px Chuchus appear as enemies in , taking on their appearance from . They come in Green, Red and Yellow varieties. Unlike other enemies, normal attacks are ineffective against them. They can be defeated instantly by using the Hammer or by being caught in a Special Attack. If they are hit by the shockwave from the Hammer instead of the Hammer itself, they will be stunned briefly, allowing normal attacks to damage them. They attack by swinging around their head after deflecting base attacks. When defeated, ChuChus will drop items based on their color. Yellow ChuChus will drop a Force Fragment, Green ChucChus will drop a Magic Jar, and Red ChuChus drop Hearts. Chuchus in have the exact same shape and color as the ones in . This is because Age of Calamity occurs at about the same time as the Great Calamity which means the Chuchus will be the same. The Giant Chuchus from Breath of the Wild reappear as enemies during the Pulse of the Ancients DLC Missions, attacking by slamming down into the ground, firing out Chuchus, spinning their bodies, and rolling into enemies.

, also known as , are recurring Items in . They are items retained from defeating Chuchus, and have restorative properties. Depending on the game, they can either be used as an ingredient to make Potions or can be scooped up and used in their current states in an Empty Bottle. Location and Uses Link can obtain Chu Jelly either by defeating a ChuChu or stealing it from the ChuChu with the Grappling Hook in . The Chu Jelly is then kept in the Spoils Bag. It cannot be used as an item but must be given to Doc Bandam on Windfall Island to brew into Potions. Doc Bandam already has the Red Potion available, while Green Potions and Blue Potions must first be created by giving him fifteen Chu Jellies of the respective color. Once Doc Bandam has made one Potion from the first batch of Chu Jellies and has given Link a free sample, that Potion will then be available for purchase from his store. Link can also continue to give Doc Bandam five additional Chu Jellies of any color to receive a free Potion. The Jellies can also be sold to Beedle. Chu Jelly can be found by defeating Chus in . Unlike in , once a Chu is defeated, its dissolving remains can be scooped up into an Empty Bottle and be used as drinkable Chu Jelly. There are several different types of Chu Jelly available: Purple Chu Jelly: obtained from Purple Chus. It has a random effect when drunk. Usually it drains one Heart, but it can occasionally restore one or all of Link's Hearts. Purple Chu Jelly can also drain Link's health down to a quarter of a Heart. Yellow Chu Jelly: obtained from Yellow Chus. It has the same use as Lantern Oil and can be used to refuel the Lantern. It can also be scooped with the Lantern to instantly refill it as well. Red Chu Jelly: obtained from Red Chus. It has the same effect as Red Potions and restores eight Hearts. Blue Chu Jelly: obtained from Blue Chus. It has the same effect as Blue Potions and restores all Hearts. Rare Chu Jelly: obtained from Rare Chus. It has the same effect as Great Fairy's Tears, which restores all Hearts and grants Link double attack power for 16 seconds or until harmed. This Jelly has to be obtained quickly, as if the Rare Chu merges with another kind of Chu, it will become that Chu's color. If Link has Rare Chu Jelly already, Yellow Chu will appear instead of the rare one. Green Chu Jelly: obtained from Green Chus. It has no effect when drunk. Green Chus only appear when a Blue Chu and Yellow Chu merge in the Wii and HD versions of the game (they create a Purple Chu in the GameCube version), which can only occur in the Cave of Ordeals. In the Wii version, the Green Chu Jelly has no description on the item subscreen and

a Blue Chu and Yellow Chu merge in the Wii and HD versions of the game (they create a Purple Chu in the GameCube version), which can only occur in the Cave of Ordeals. In the Wii version, the Green Chu Jelly has no description on the item subscreen and no text appears when it is obtained; in , text was added in both cases, even referencing the fact that is has no effect when drunk. Black Chu Jelly: An unused item intended to appear from a hypothetical Black Chu, which does not appear in the final game. It is fully functional in the code, and depletes one of Link's hearts when consumed, similarly to Nasty Soup. Chuchu Jellies can be found by defeating Chuchus. Chuchu Jellies exhibit mutagenic properties when exposed to elemental attacks (e.g. setting them on fire changes them to Red Chuchu Jelly), and will burst if struck. Chuchu Jellies comes in four colors: Chuchu Jelly: Appears light blue in color. Drops from normal Chuchus. Harmless if struck but will cause Link to receive the "wet" condition. Red Chuchu Jelly: Drops from Fire Chuchus or exposing other Chuchu Jelly to fire. Explodes if struck by physical attacks. White Chuchu Jelly: Drops from Ice Chuchus or exposing other forms of Chuchu Jelly to ice. Releases a freezing mist if struck by physical attacks. Yellow Chuchu Jelly: Drops from Electric Chuchus or exposing other forms of Chuchu Jelly to electricity. Releases an electric burst if struck by physical attacks. As a Monster Part, Cooking with Chuchu Jellies will result in Dubious Food. However, if Link Cooks them with critters, he can make a variety of Elixirs. They can also be sold to Kilton at the Fang and Bone for Mon or used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Light Blue Dye. Five Chuchu Jellies are used to upgrade each piece of the Soldier's Set to its first tier at a Great Fairy Fountain. Chuchu Jellies return as Items in . Like in , five Chuchu Jellies are used to upgrade each piece of the Soldier's Set to its first tier at a Great Fairy Fountain. Other Appearances 64px|left Chu Jellies appear as Weird-type Food in . It is imbued with the Lightning Element. When consumed by a Companion Fairy in the Dining Room of the My Fairy mode, Chu Jelly can increase the Fairy's Trust level and personality traits. Chuchu Jellies are Materials that can be obtained by defeating Chuchus in battle. They can commonly be sold for 5 Rupees, though Segimo will buy them for 12 Rupees. They are required to complete certain Quests such as "Strange and Unusual Monsters" and can also to be used to Octo-Polish a Weapon, remove a Weapon's seals, or raise its Weapon-level limit.

is a recurring character in . Biography Chumin is a traveling Hylian Merchant from Lurelin Village who travels with his Donkey along the Faron Highroad, where he sells fruits and Fish to other travelers. He can be encountered walking back and forth from Lurelin Village to the Highland Stable to sell his products. He sporadically rests under a tree near the Fishing Resort or at the Lakeside Stable as he travels. When he sits under an awning at Highland Stable, he attempts to attract customers. When spoken to, Chumin describes Lurelin Village as a simple, sleepy town. He also makes reference to Lucky Treasure Shop, calling it a traditional Treasure Chest game and saying it reminds him of his childhood. When he is at Lurelin, he restocks his wares and claims to have won at the Treasure-Chest Game. Chumin spends a lot of time traversing trade routes, where he sells his wares. He has been traveling on the roads for years, and he thinks he could even be a tour guide. According to him, a lot of monsters hang around Highland Stable, so the area should be avoided. Occasionally, Chumin will give Link directions to Lake Hylia and the Finra Woods. Chumin claims to have made many Rupees from satisfied customers. The first time he entered the Faron Woods, he didn't have a map and ended up getting lost. Chumin also mentions that, if he ever lost his Donkey, he is not sure if he could go on. He takes rain as a sign to rest. Link can save Chumin from Enemies. As a reward, he will give him Rupees. As he walks, Chumin tries to attract customers. He assures his customers that he has a lot of top-choice merchandise. When it is raining, he offers Hearty Blueshell Snails among his other products. Not only does Chumin sell his own wares, he also purchases Items from Link. He thanks Link whenever he makes a purchase. When Link buys his whole stock, Chumin thanks him for doing business. Wares and Pricing After being rescued by Link during the Side Quest "A Bottled Cry for Help", Chumin can be found wandering the road between Hateno Bay and Hateno Village. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring character in . Biography Cima is a Hylian Stable Worker at Lakeside Stable in West Necluda. She tends to the Horses that reside at the Stable during the day. At night, she sleeps in one of the Stable's beds. When Link first speaks to Cima, she complains about how nervous Lightning makes her when it strikes the Stable. Since she can not figure out the reason, she asks Link to figure out why it is struck so often. Cima will be happy if he accepts, which initiates the "Thunder Magnet" Side Quest. On top of Lakeside Stable, Link can find a Woodcutter's Axe. After taking it, Link can return to Cima to inform her of his discovery. She realizes that the Axe must have been drawing the Lightning to the Stable and wonders if it was put up there on purpose. She thanks Link for his help, giving him a Rubber Helm as a reward. Cima is relieved to finally be able to relax. This completes the Side Quest. Afterwards, if Link speaks to Cima, she will ask if he has seen the Waterfalls leading into Lake Floria. She claims each one is unique and worth seeing. While she is going to sleep, she tells Link to wait for whatever he needs until tomorrow.

are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Circles go unnamed in . Location and Uses Circles are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. There are two different varieties. The first is a Circle of Rocks jutting out of a body of Water. Several Rocks that Link is able to carry will always be found nearby. If Link throws one of these Rocks so that it lands in the middle of the Circle, a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed. The second type of Circle is known as Dive Through the Ring. It takes the form of a Circle of Lily Pads or seaweed floating on top of Water. They will always appear underneath a ledge overlooking the Water, which Link can jump off of. If he dives into the middle of the Circle, this will also cause a Korok to appear. A total of two Circles can be found in Akkala. A total of 17 Circles can be found in Central Hyrule. A total of five Circles can be found in Eldin. A total of five Circles can be found in Faron. A total of four Circles can be found in Hebra. A total of two Circles can be found in Lanayru. A total of 19 Circles can be found in Necluda. Only one type of Circle remains in , those being of the Dive Through the Ring variety. Like in , if Link dives through the ring of Lily Pads or seaweed, a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed.

is a recurring character in . Biography Claree is a shopkeeper and a member of the Sheikah Tribe who lives in Kakariko Village, where she owns the Armor Shop, Enchanted. When Link first steps into her store, she will proudly declare that all of her items belong to a brand named the "Claree Collection" and recommends one of the pieces. If Link asks what the Claree Collection is, she will explain that the collection is curated by none other than herself. She points out that certain items have specific features. Claree is very upbeat and tells Link he can ask her about anything. Claree is also willing to buy items from the hero. She cheers whenever Link sells her anything. She's very excited to see items from beyond Kakariko, as she doesn't get to leave the Village. When Link decides to sell her something, Claree can react in a few different ways. She can be in shock over the item, end up thrilled, admit that she was eyeing what he sold, or proclaim that she has been looking for that particular item. She will claim to buy anything, and even suggests that Link sell anything he does not need anymore. If Link approaches the Stealth Set, Claree says the pieces are exclusive to the store. She points out the use of its stealth capabilities, but quietly admits that its defense is lacking.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Clarnet Coast is located along the Necluda Sea in East Necluda. Clarnet Coast is a narrow beach stretching across the Necluda Sea. It features many Palm Trees as well as a Monster Stronghold. At this Monster Stronghold, Link can find an unlit Campfire as well as Barrels and Wooden Boxes that contain Apples, Hearty Durians, Hydromelons, Mighty Bananas, Palm Fruits, and Voltfruits. A dock sits at the far western side of Clarnet Coast. Around this dock, Link can find a lit Campfire as well as Barrels, Jars, and Wooden Boxes containing Arrows, Apples, Hydromelons, Palm Fruits, and Voltfruits. A metallic Treasure Chest containing a Silver Rupee can be found inside the aforementioned Monster Stronghold. A second metallic Treasure Chest containing an Amber sits in the water beside the western dock. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

is a recurring character in . Biography Clavia is a Hylian resident of Hateno Village. She can often be found on the dock behind the Kochi Dye Shop, thinking to herself. At night, she sleeps in the Village Chief's House with her family. During Rain, she can be found taking stock in her House. She greets Link when they speak, and she occasionally remarks on her life in Hateno. When Link first meets Clavia, it takes her a moment to realize that he is a traveler. She is eager to share something with him, but if Link decides to leave instead, she considers it a shame. If Link decides to listen to her, Clavia will point to the cliffs of Mount Lanayru and explain that she found a note in an old Book at her House. The note holds cryptic instructions to a trial. Although Clavia admits that she does not understand the words, she guesses that the note refers to Afromsia Coast and excitedly thinks of the possibility of treasure waiting there. However, she is quick to recall with dismay that she has parental responsibilities and must remain in Hateno Village. Instead, she enlists Link to venture out and collect the reward for her, beginning the "Secret of the Cedars" Shrine Quest. Link can return to Clavia later after completing the Shrine Quest. She will hesitantly ask if he has found the treasure the note spoke of. Realizing that it was rude to push this errand on Link, she asks if he might be open to sharing the reward. Regardless of Link's response, Clavia will admit that she was only joking with him and that she is satisfied without it. She is disappointed by the "treasure" being an Ancient Shrine, as there is already one in Hateno Village. As with other villagers in Hateno, Clavia will react to the Blue Flame if Link speaks to her while carrying it. She recognizes it as the one Purah uses, and she suggests he hurry along with his delivery.

is a recurring character in . Biography Cleff is a Zora shopkeep that runs the Coral Reef at the Marot Mart in Zora's Domain. He is known to have a serious demeanor, in contrast with his sister Tona's excitable personality. When he is first spoken to, Cleff will welcome Link and explain that the General Store sells Swift Violets, which can help one run faster. He also shares that they sell Arrows, encouraging Link to grab whatever he wants to buy. If Link asks about the Coral Reef, Cleff explains that it is a General Store where one can buy fresh Fish. While they do sell Arrows, due to the Zora's weakness to Electricity, they do not stock Shock Arrows. When asked about business, Cleff will admit that things have not been great. He initially tells Link that he is worried about the Coral Reef's business, since there are not many travelers coming to Zora's Domain to make purchases. After Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, Cleff will remark that business is improving, and he no longer believes that he will have to close his General Store. Cleff will accept any Items that Link wants to sell to him, encouraging him to take his time choosing what to sell. As they do business, Cleff will be grateful and ask Link if he wants to sell more Items. When Link ends their business at night, Cleff warns him to be careful going out after dark.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Cliffs of Quince are located in East Necluda. The Cliffs of Quince overlook both Fort Hateno and the Fir River, the latter of which runs directly beneath the northern portion of the Cliffs. On the southern side of the cliffs, Link can find Wild Horses, which are being ridden by Bokoblins. A second herd of Wild Horses can also be found on the eastern side of the Cliffs, without Bokoblin masters. On the underside of the highest Cliffs, Link can find a Magnesis puzzle, which can be solved to uncover a Korok who will give Link a Korok Seed for finding him. The Cliffs of Quince form an alcove, under which a group of Bokoblins have formed a camp at the bank of the Fir River. This camp contains several Bomb Barrels and a Treasure Chest, holding an Opal, which can only be unlocked by clearing the camp of its inhabitants. A spit in the middle of the camp holds a Seared Steak. A Stone Talus can be found at the top of the Cliffs of Quince. Enemies The Cliffs of Quince reappear in , retaining an almost identical array of geographical features and Trees from its appearance in . Areas

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Cliffs of Ruvara are the northernmost section of Gerudo Highlands and serve as the transition between Gerudo Highlands and the Tabantha Frontier. The Cliffs are sections of mesa that become less vertical as the altitude increases. Along the sides of the cliffs are multiple scaffolds and evidence of architectural involvement. The Cliffs are where the ancient Sheikah technology was uncovered, including the Divine Beasts and the Guardians. There are also multiple geothermal vents which cause Updrafts that allow Link to Paraglide up the sides of the Cliffs. Link can find multiple Korok puzzles along the cliffs, including a puzzle where Link must follow a flower that teleports away when he is near it. Once Link follows the flower for long enough, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Climber's Bandanna is a piece of Armor located in the Ree Dahee Shrine at Dueling Peaks. After obtaining it, Granté will begin selling the piece of Armor for 4,000 Rupees. It is infused with ancient technology, despite what its plain appearance would suggest. When worn, it provides one level of Climb Speed Up. The Climber's Bandanna can be Enhanced by Great Fairies and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Climber's Bandanna, alongside the Climbing Gear and Climbing Boots, compose the Climbing Set. When each piece of the Set has been Upgraded at least two times by a Great Fairy and the full Set is worn, it provides a Climb Jump Stamina Up Set Bonus. Dye Options Enhancing Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances The Climber's Bandanna is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and is obtained by completing the Challenge "Mountain Rescue". It can also be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Dye Options

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Climbing Boots are a piece of Armor located in the Tahno O'ah Shrine at Mount Lanayru. After obtaining them, Granté will begin selling the piece of Armor for 4,000 Rupees. According to their description, they are infused with ancient technology. When worn, they provide one level of Climb Speed Up. The Climbing Boots can be Enhanced by a Great Fairy and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Climbing Boots, alongside the Climber's Bandanna and the Climbing Gear, compose the Climbing Set. When each piece of the Set has been Enhanced at least two times by a Great Fairy and the full Set is worn, it provides a Climb Jump Stamina Up Set Bonus. Dye Options Enhancing Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances In , the Climbing Boots are a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link and are obtained when the Warriors complete the Quest "Perils of Mount Hylia". They can also be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Dye Options

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Climbing Gear is a piece of Armor located in Chaas Qeta Shrine on Tenoko Island. After obtaining it, Granté will begin selling the piece of Armor for 4,000 Rupees. According to its description, it is infused with ancient technology. When worn, it provides one level of Climb Speed Up. The Climbing Gear can be Enhanced by a Great Fairy and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Climbing Gear, alongside the Climber's Bandanna and the Climbing Boots, compose the Climbing Set. When each piece of the Set has been Enhanced at least two times by a Great Fairy and the full Set is worn, it provides a Climbing Jump Stamina Up Set Bonus. Dye Options Enhancing The Climbing Gear can be found as one of Misko's treasures in the North Hyrule Plain Cave. It is hidden behind a Waterfall. Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances The Climbing Gear is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and it is obtained by completing the Quest "The Hope of Necluda". It can also be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Dye Options

The , also known as the Climber's Set, is a recurring Armor Set in . Location and Uses The Climbing Set is an Armor Set consisting of the Climber's Bandanna, Climbing Gear, and Climbing Boots. Each piece must be obtained from a Treasure Chest in the following Ancient Shrines respectively: Ree Dahee Shrine at Dueling Peaks Chaas Qeta Shrine at Tenoko Island Tahno O'ah Shrine at Mount Lanayru After acquiring a piece of the Climbing Set, Granté will begin to sell it in Tarrey Town. Each piece increases Link's movement speed while climbing. If all three pieces are worn and have been upgraded at least twice by a Great Fairy, they provide the Climbing Jump Stamina Up set bonus, significantly reducing the stamina cost for jumping during a climb. Despite what the equipment description implies however, this armor set will not prevent Link from slipping when climbing during rainy weather. Dye Options Enhancing Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances The Climber's Bandanna is acquired upon completing the "Mountain Rescue" Quest. The Climbing Gear is acquired upon completing the "The Hope Necluda" Quest. The Climbing Boots are acquired upon completing the "Perils of Mount Hylia" Quest. Dye Options

is a recurring character in . Biography Cloyne is a Hylian resident of Lurelin Village. He runs the Treasure-Chest Game Mini-Game at his Shop, the Lucky Treasure Shop, that he inherited from his father after he passed away. He is known to have gained a variety of knowledge from the Books he keeps in the Shops, resulting in him having a unique outlook on life. When Link first speaks to Cloyne, he beckons him to come closer. He then asks if Link would like to be rich without working for it. Though Link reacts with shock, Cloyne assures him that what he is talking about is not illegal. He goes on to explain that Link can put a wager on the Treasure Chests in the Shop. Then, he can open any Chest he picks and get all of the Rupees inside. However, Cloyne reveals that only one will allow a profit. Link is not allowed to play until he bets, and Cloyne claims the more he bets, the more he could win. He reasons that Link since must have expenses, getting some quick cash could be beneficial. When asking if Link wants to play, Cloyne says the only thing he could lose is his pride and his Rupees. He gives Link the option to bet 10, 50, or 100 Rupees. With a 10 Rupee bet, Cloyne states that it s smart to start low. If Link chooses to bet 50 Rupees, Cloyne remarks that he is ready to make real money. Should he bet 100 Rupees, Cloyne congratulates him on living on the edge, stating that he reminds him of himself. After Link's bet, Cloyne then sets up the Treasure Chests, telling him not to look. Once he is done setting up, Cloyne tells Link to step up and take his chances. If Link tries to speak to him during the game, Cloyne reminds him to pay attention. Should Link not win the Treasure-Chest Game, Cloyne is unsympathetic and says he will win next time. He then asks Link if he is going to keep going or admit defeat. If Link decides to stop, Cloyne will be understanding and respect that he knows when to walk away. If Link wins, Cloyne comments on his luck.

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview During "The Broken Slate", Jiahto translates the ancient Slate for Link, which reveals that the Sky can be accessed by shooting the "mark of the king" through a "droplet" on the "land of the sky fish". Believing that Dorephan may soon return from his investigation, Jiahto suggests that Link consult with him. Following this statement, "Clues to the Sky" will begin. When Link enters the Throne Room of Zora's Domain, he will find Tumbo, Keye, and Laruta reenacting what happened to Dorephan through play. According to them, Dorephan was injured while fighting a Sludge Monster, and he went to heal in a secret location. However, they refuse to keep playing when they notice Link nearby, so Tumbo tells him to leave. By hiding in the Water of the Throne, Link is able to eavesdrop on the children's game. At first they attempt to continue playing, but Keye struggles playing both the Monster and Muzu. Laruta then wonders aloud what Dorephan's hiding spot is like. Tumbo recalls asking him about it once, and it was called the "pristine sanctummy." Since it is supposedly pristine, Keye reasons that the Water must be clean there. Tumbo claims that clean Water flows between Ploymus Mountain and Zora's Domain, and he heard there is a secret entrance behind a Waterfall there. Laruta is impressed by the concept. Keye suddenly remembers that Muzu warned them not to tell anyone, but Tumbo insists that it is fine since no one is listening. He then decides that they should go through their game one more time, but Keye wants to play something else. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Dorephan in the Pristine Sanctum. He is visibly sickened by Sludge. Text on-screen displays his name, along with the title "King of the Zora".|Dorephan's introduction Link can enter the Pristine Sanctum from either Lulu Lake or Mikau Lake. Inside, he will find Muzu caring for Dorephan, who is suffering from the effects of Sludge. Though Muzu is initially hostile toward Link, Dorephan stops him, claiming his is only causing confusion. Dorephan greets Link and asks what has brought him to Zora's Domain, since he last heard that he and Zelda went missing. Despite Dorephan's shock, Muzu still refuses to believe Link, claiming he saw Zelda right after the Upheaval began. Seeing no betrayal in Link's eyes, Dorephan declares that he is still an ally to them. After Hyrule Castle began to float, Dorephan and Muzu left Zora's Domain to investigate the Sludge, but they were caught off-guard by Zelda appearing from the Sky and ordering a sludge monster to attack them. Although Dorephan was able to defeat the Monster, he was injured, and he hid himself in the Pristine Sanctum to avoid word of Zelda's betrayal spreading. Noting how their story contradicts Link's, Dorephan states that they may find answers in the Sky. Recalling that Jiahto was meant to be studying the ruins from the Sky, Dorephan wonders if he has found anything

he hid himself in the Pristine Sanctum to avoid word of Zelda's betrayal spreading. Noting how their story contradicts Link's, Dorephan states that they may find answers in the Sky. Recalling that Jiahto was meant to be studying the ruins from the Sky, Dorephan wonders if he has found anything yet. When Link relays the writing on the Slate, Dorephan reveals that the "mark of the king" refers to one of his scales, though he does not know anything about the ritual in which it is used. Since Link is in need of it, Dorephan gives him five King's Scales, inviting him to take more if he runs out. Due to recent events, Dorephan considers whether it may be time to pass on his title as King of the Zora to Sidon. While this concerns Muzu, Dorephan puts off his decision until after the Sludge crisis has ended. He then asks Link to inform Sidon of both his condition and the King's Scale. Link can reach Floating Scales Island by Swimming up its Waterfall while wearing the Zora Armor. Once there, he must look to the southwest, from where the floating rocks surrounding the Island appear to form a drop of Water. From this angle, Link can Fuse one of the King's Scale to an Arrow and shoot it through the droplet, which causes it to land in East Reservoir Lake. A green Pillar of Light will then rise up to the Sky, completing "Clues to the Sky". Objectives

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Cobble Crushers are two-handed Weapons created by Gorons. They are very thick but do not possess a cutting edge. Therefore, they are consequently used as crushing Weapons, due to the weight of their component metal. They belong to the Goron Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Weapons that are made by Gorons. They are most commonly found around Goron City in the Eldin Canyon and throughout the Eldin Mountains. In addition to this, they have a chance to appear in Treasure Chests found from scanning the Series Daruk amiibo with the amiibo Rune. Should Link ever lose the Boulder Breaker, he can ask Rohan in Goron City to make him a new one in exchange for a Cobble Crusher, a Diamond, and five pieces of Flint. Cobble Crushers have a hidden property which causes their damage output to be doubled when used on the Ore Deposit atop a Stone Talus. In this vein, they will immediately destroy Stone Pebblits when used against them. As Cobble Crushers are made out of metal, they will sink if they are dropped in Water, and they do not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. This also means that they can be manipulated through the Magnesis Rune. Finally, they will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if Link has one equipped during a Thunderstorm. Cobble Crushers reappear in . Other Appearances

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Cold Darners can be found in cold regions of Hyrule, such as Hyrule Ridge and the Tabantha Frontier. They can also be purchased from traveling merchants, such as Maypin and Beedle at the Kara Kara Bazaar and Woodland Stable. When Cooked, Cold Darners can be made into Elixirs that provide Heat Resistance. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Cold Darners can be used to make Blue Dye. As part of the "Little Sister's Big Request" Side Quest, Link must ask Gleema what the insect she wants to see is. She will reveal that she once saw a dragonflies in a book and when she grows up, she wants to travel and see dragonflies in real life. Gleema was unwilling to tell her sister Jana that she wanted to see them because of Jana's distaste for them. However, because it is Gleema's birthday wish, Jana will ask Link to bring her the dragonflies. However, Jana grows disgusted by them asks Link to deliver them instead. As a reward for completing this quest, Jana will give Link a Silver Rupee. Cold Darners are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Cold Pool is a large pool of Cold Water located inside Talonto Peak Cave in the Hebra Mountains. It is surrounded by Icy walls, and has a wooden Raft in the Water at its northern edge. It is thought to have formed as a result of the Blizzard affecting the Hebra Region. During the "Crossing the Cold Pool" Side Quest, Verla explains that he came to the Cave to forage the large population of Chillshrooms growing in it, but found the Cold Pool blocking the path to them and could not cross it due to his injured wing. Link can retrieve the Chillshrooms for him by crossing the Pool. Enemies

is an Added Effect in . Overview Cold Weather Attack is an Added Effect that, when in Freezing Climates, causes Link's charge attacks and combo finishers to generate an Ice-based area of effect. In addition to the damage the Enemy will receive by default from the element, the area of effect has a bonus attack power of five, which can be increased by the Attack Up Effect. Level two increases the size of the area of effect by 50% for combo finishers and 33% for charge attacks, while level three increases the size of the area of effect by 100% for combo finishers and 66% for charge attacks. Level three is the maximum possible potency for this Effect. The following Materials and Armor pieces grant Cold Weather Attack:

Colgera is a Boss in . Characteristics Colgeras are massive worm-like creatures reminiscent of Molgera, with a jagged layer of ice serving as armor for them. They have five eyes, large pincers, and a pair of wings on three of their body segments. One is responsible for the Extreme Cold Snap affecting the Hebra region. After Colgera's defeat in the Wind Temple, three Colgeras can be found in arenas throughout the Depths, east of Narusis Lightroot in the Hebra Mountains Depths, east of Nupisoyuat Lightroot in the Hebra Mountains Depths, and east of the South Lomei Depths Labyrinth in the Gerudo Highlands Depths. If Colgera is not defeated in the Wind Temple, Link fights it at Gloom's Origin during the War in the Depths of Hyrule. It appears after the Demon King's Army and before Marbled Gohma. When defeated in the Depths, Colgeras drop a Colgera Jaw, and unlock a Treasure Chest containing a Huge Crystallized Charge. In battle, Colgera flies through the air, firing icicle spikes at Link if he gets too close. It will also open portals that it will pass through to try and confuse Link about where it will be, sometimes appearing directly underneath him to perform a biting attack. The use of Tulin's Power of Wind is necessary to dodge this attack, and will generally come in handy for repositioning throughout the battle. Colgera's weaknesses are the purple glowing spots on its body, which are protected by a layer of ice on its underside and the spiky shell on its top. The ice can be broken with Arrows (preferably ones that have been Fused with Fire Fruits, Fire Chuchu Jelly, or Bomb Flowers) or by Skydiving onto it from above; despite Colgera's jagged exterior Link will not take damage from contact with it but he will be knocked back if his dive is not fast enough or if he hits the shell. Colgera takes a moment to regrow its spikes after shooting them and exposes its ice layer from above when it does so, making that moment ideal for Link to dive into it. Colgera harnesses wind to create powerful updrafts around it, which allow Link to glide up to it; using them will also fully restore his Stamina. After half its health is depleted, Colgera will begin to summon tornadoes to attack Link and will behave more aggressively.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Coliseum Ruins are located in Central Hyrule, northwest of the Great Plateau. The Ruins were once an arena for combat but have since become run-down and overrun by Monsters. Pools of Malice coat the outer walls while several monsters patrol the interior. A Lynel can also be found in the center of the Coliseum. Weapons wielded by these enemies and the Lynel both scale up depending on how many Divine Beasts have been freed. If the four Beasts are released, all the enemies inside will carry elemental weapons. Due to the danger it poses, only scavengers such as Dai approach the Ruins in search of Weapons and treasure, though he hides behind a wall among the rubble outside them. Bomb Barrels can also be found among the rubble and Malice. A metallic Treasure Chest containing a bundle of five Bomb Arrows can be found on the northern wall. A metallic Chest containing an Amber is located on the southern wall. In the "EX Treasure: Phantasma" Side Quest exclusive to The Master Trials DLC Pack, the Phantom Helmet can be found inside a metallic Treasure Chest stuck in the ground at the northwest side of the Coliseum. A Korok can be found under a Rock on the northern wall of the Coliseum. Another Korok can be found by completing the Race puzzle activated by standing on the Tree stump on top of a dead Tree surrounded by Malice northwest of the main Ruins entrance. Creatures Enemies Equipment The Coliseum Ruins are home to a secret underground location known as the Coliseum Ruins Cave. To enter the Cave, Link must return a Soldier's Claymore to one of the Soldier Statues. The Coliseum Ruins have a counterpart in the Central Hyrule Depths known as the Floating Coliseum. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Equipment Korok Seeds Materials Zonai Devices

The is a recurring location in . The Common Cooking Area goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Common Cooking Area is a part of Kakariko Village in West Necluda. It features a Cooking Pot, the Campfire under which can be lit in order to prepare Food. Two Jars at the side of the structure can be broken for supplies. In the evening, Olkin and Mellie will head to the Common Cooking Area to make dinner. Their meals are made using many Fortified Pumpkins, which Olkin finds to be better than Swift Carrots. During the "Flown the Coop" Side Quest, one of Cado's Cuccos can be found in and around the Common Cooking Area. It can easily be picked up and returned to the Cucco Coop. Afterwards, it will continue to appear in this location during the day. Creatures

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Construct Factory is a large tower situated in the Faron Grasslands Depths deep beneath the Tobio's Hollow Chasm. The Muokuij Lightroot is located directly in front of it. It is operated by a lone Caretaker Construct who sits at its top chamber and reviews schematics for Crafter Constructs. The eastern and western rooftops are gardens with a gazebo on each side. The western gazebo houses a Decayed Construct while the eastern gazebo contains a Large Poe. The entire building is littered with Poes, and two Grand Poe can be found on its central rooftop. An assembly mold for Crafter Constructs can be found at the entrance to the Construct Factory, and additional molds can be found in a closed-off chute behind it. The purpose of the Construct Factory is to assemble Crafter Constructs for shipment to Dragonhead Island. The parts for the Crafter Constructs are supplied from the nearby depots, which have stopped production for unknown reasons. Because of this, the Caretaker Construct was left with nothing to do but await further shipments. Link must visit the Construct Factory under Mineru's guidance to assemble Mineru's Construct and provide her with a new body so that she can resume her work as the Sage of Spirit. Enemies Materials Zonai Devices Treasure Chests

is a recurring mechanic in . Overview While in previous games in Link would need to pick up Hearts to replenish his Life Gauge, in he has to forage or hunt in order to collect Materials, Ingredients, and critters. While some can be eaten raw to replenish the Life Gauge, Cooking them can unlock their greater potential as a tool for combat and exploration. There are two primary avenues of Cooking in the games: using extreme environment conditions and implementing a Cooking Pot. Cooking returns in . Although some Materials can no longer be found throughout Hyrule since the events of , namely Hearty Durians, Hearty Blueshell Snails and Ancient Materials, the base mechanics are the same and there are a number of new Ingredients Link can Cook with. Other Appearances

page_title: Cooking in Tears of the Kingdom
text: This article details the Cooking mechanisms specific to . For the Cooking mechanisms of , see Cooking in . __TOC__ Overview Cooking is a mechanic in that allows Link to combine Ingredients in order to make Meals. Although Cooking remains mostly unchanged from how it was in , new Ingredients can be found around Hyrule, most of them with their own Added Effects. Roasted Food Since Death Mountain has become dormant and the whole Region has cooled down, Link is no longer able to Roast Food there. However, Caves within that Region remain Scorching, along with the Death Mountain Depths and surrounding areas. Frozen Food At the start of Link's adventure, most of the Hebra Region is affected by an Extreme Cold Snap, which Freezes Meat and Seafood left outside. After completing the Main Quest "Tulin of Rito Village" the Extreme Cold Snap dies down. Link is still able to Freeze Food in the Region afterwards, but only during Blizzards. Cooked Food Like in , most dishes are still made by putting up to five Ingredients in a Cooking Pot. In addition to the ones he can find in the wild or in Villages, in Link is able to Cook from anywhere by using Portable Pots. Life Recovery While most Meals have a predictable amount of Hearts recovered based on how much each Ingredient heals when cooked on its own, some recipes will heal more or less than what would be expected from the Ingredients themselves: Some Materials will also change the total amount of expected Heart recovery: Critical bonus When Link uses a Cooking Pot, there is a chance for a bonus to be applied to one of the dish's properties. The bonuses from remain, with the addition of Gloom Recovery. The bonuses are as follow: extra life recovery 5:00 added duration Increased Effect strength For time-based Effects, the level increases by one. For the Extra Hearts Added Effect, the extra amount increases by one. For the Extra Stamina and Stamina Recovery Effects, the Stamina Wheels increase by two ⅕ notches. For the Gloom Recovery Effect, the amount repaired increases by two. If there is no Added Affect or duration tied to an Effect then the irrelevant bonus will never be chosen. However, Gloom Recovery is unique in that duration can be chosen even though the Effect has no duration. If life recovery is already at maximum, either from the Extra Hearts Effect or from reaching forty. Hearts, then it will not be chosen. If an Effect's strength is already at maximum, it will not be chosen. If an Effect has duration, it can be chosen even if it is already at 30:00. Critical bonuses can happen naturally with a base 5% chance to occur per unique Material in the dish. Some Materials will further increase the rate on top of that, but it will only be calculated in once and only by the highest chance present. Cooking between 11:30 and 12:15 on the night of a Blood Moon will guarantee a bonus. Critical bonus chance caps at 100%; no more than one bonus can be gained per Recipe. If Monster Extract is present or the dish is Dubious or Rock-Hard Food, you cannot gain a critical bonus. Dubious and Rock-Hard Food There are certain Materials that cannot be used in Recipes or certain combinations that do not work together. When that happens, the result is a failed Meal that restores very little Hearts and will not have any added Effects. Rock-Hard Food will only restore . It occurs when any of the following Materials are present, even taking precedence over Dubious Food: Dubious Food will always restore at least . The base life recovery of the Materials is added together for the total but only if there are two or more unique Materials. Material recovery bonuses are not activated. Dubious Food occurs when any of the following conditions are met: One of these inedible Materials is present: A Recipe contains a critter but not a Monster Part, or vice versa. An Elixir contains Materials that provide different Added Effects. An invalid combination of supplemental Materials is made: Some can be Cooked on their own for a valid Recipe: these include Courser Bee Honey, Bird Egg, Fresh Milk, and any combination of Acorn or Chickaloo Tree Nut. Fresh Milk and Bird Egg can be successfully Cooked with any other supplemental Ingredient. There are preset combinations that do produce a valid combination, such as Tabantha Wheat with Rock Salt or Hateno Cheese. For more Recipes, refer to its section (see below). Selling To calculate the Sell Price of Meals and Elixirs, first take the sum of the prices of the Materials, then multiply it by a modifier determined by the number of Ingredients; values with decimals are rounded down to the next whole number. Fairy Tonics, Dubious Food, and Rock-Hard Food will only sell for 2 Rupees regardless of Materials used. 1.2x for one Ingredient 1.3x for two Ingredients 1.4x for three Ingredients 1.6x for four Ingredients 1.8x for five Ingredients Dragon Parts and Star Fragments are considered as having a base sell price of 1 Rupee when Cooked. For the other Material values, see Materials in . Roasted and Frozen Food do not follow the conventional selling rules and rather have a set price. For Sell Prices for these Foods, see Food in . Added Effect Materials The following Materials are categorized by which Added Effect they give. Each Material grants a certain amounts of points (represented here by ★) towards its Added Effect. If the total points contributed by all the Materials reaches certain thresholds, it will increase the level of the Added Effect provided. If Materials from

If the total points contributed by all the Materials reaches certain thresholds, it will increase the level of the Added Effect provided. If Materials from multiple are present, the dish will remove all Added Effects. Neutral Materials Neutral Materials are comprised of Food and other supplemental Ingredients that do not give any Added Effect. The full duration added by neutral Materials is only given once per unique Material; duplicates will be reduced to 0:30 each. They are the only Ingredients where this occurs. Monster Part Materials Monster Parts are to be combined with at least one critter to make an Elixir. They extend Added Effect duration and some can increase the chance for a critical bonus. Monster Parts do not add life recovery to the Elixir, nor do they increase the Added Effect strength. Monster Parts are divided into three tiers based on the time and critical bonus chance they add: high-grade, mid-grade, and low-grade. For more information on critical bonus chance, refer to its section (see above). With the exception of Gibdo Guts, which guarantee a critical bonus, the only mechanical difference between Monster Parts of the same grade is Sell Price. Lynel Guts provide just as much added duration and critical bonus chance as a Bokoblin's. Elemental Monster Parts offer no special benefits to elemental Added Effects. Dragon Parts and Zonai Materials are not considered Monster Parts. Monster Extract Monster Extract will remove any chance of a critical bonus and instead have random changes on expected properties of a dish. Effect duration will be set to 1:00, 10:00, or 30:00. Only neutral Materials can add more, but their duration will reduced by 0:30. Between life recovery and Effect strength, one will be chosen to receive either a positive or negative change. If one property is not present, then the other is guaranteed to be changed. The Extra Hearts Effect will always have the strength changed by Monster Extract, never life recovery. The negative change reduces the affected property to its lowest value: Life recovery is set to . Effect strength is set to one ★. The positive change increases the affected property by an amount dependent on what was chosen: Life recovery increases by . For time-based Effects, its level increases by one if half of the ★ required for level 2 is reached, rounded up (e.g., an Attack Up dish would need at least ★★★ to be able to increase in level). For the Extra Hearts Effect, the extra amount increases by one. For the Extra Stamina and Stamina Recovery Effects, the stamina wheels increase by two ⅕ notches. For the Gloom Recovery Effect, the recovered amount increases by two. Even if life recovery is reduced, recovery bonuses from Recipes and Materials will still be applied.
