are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Cool Safflinas can be found growing in the snow of the Hebra Mountains and Gerudo Highlands. They also sprout near Tera's Great Fairy Fountain in the Gerudo Desert. Cooking Cool Safflinas in a Cooking Pot will result in Meals that grant Link Heat Resistance when eaten. At the Kochi Dye Shop in Hateno Village, Cool Safflinas can be used to create Light Blue Dye. Like other Flowers, they can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Like other Flowers, Cool Safflinas can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Cool Safflinas are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances Cool Safflinas can be sold for three Rupees.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Copious Fried Wild Greens are made by Cooking four different Vegetables, herbs, or Flowers together in a Cooking Pot. When eaten, they will restore several Hearts to Link's Life Gauge. They are known to be healthy Meals made by cooking mixed greens over a strong flame. Due to the variety and number of ingredients needed to make Copious Fried Wild Greens, only their default version is available. It is impossible to add any effects to this dish. Copious Fried Wild Greens reappear in . Due to the addition of Korok Fronds acting as a neutral Cooking Ingredient, it is possible to make five variations of the Meal. Other Appearances The recipe for Copious Fried Wild Greens is earned by completing the Quest "A Feast of Greens". It is made using one Hyrule Herb, one Swift Violet, one Mighty Thistle, one Armoranth, and one Blue Nightshade. When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Perfect-Dodge timing window increases by 5% for the Warriors.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Copious Meat Skewers can be made by Cooking a minimum of four different types of Meat together. If consumed by Link it will restore between ten and twenty of his Hearts, depending on the quantity and quality of the Ingredients that were used to make it. The preparation of Copious Meat Skewers is simple, consisting only of shoving Meat onto a skewer. A fifth Ingredient can be added to Copious Meat Skewers, which can result in the following variations: Chilly Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding a chilly Ingredient. When these skewers are eaten, Link gains one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding an electric Ingredient. Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance when he eats them. Enduring Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding an enduring Ingredient. They completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel when consumed. Energizing Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding an energizing Ingredient. Eating these skewers will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding a hasty Ingredient. Link's movement speed will be increased by eating these skewers. Hearty Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding a hearty Ingredient. When eaten, Link's Hearts will be completely healed and he will gain temporary Hearts. Mighty Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding a mighty Ingredient. When eaten, Link will receive a boost to the power of his attacks. Sneaky Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding a sneaky Ingredient. They can be eaten to temporarily increase Link's Stealth. Spicy Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding a spicy Ingredient. Eating them will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Copious Meat Skewers: Made by adding a tough Ingredient. If consumed, Link's defense will be temporarily boosted.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Copious Mushroom Skewers can be made by Cooking at least four different types of Mushrooms together in a Cooking Pot. Due to the variety of Added Effects granted by Mushrooms, it is impossible to create any different types of Copious Mushroom Skewers aside from their default. These Skewers are popular among fans of Mushrooms. Copious Mushroom Skewers return in . Their Recipe is the same as in , requiring at least four different types of Mushrooms to be Cooked together. Since Skyshrooms are now available as a neutral Ingredient, one variety of Copious Mushroom Skewers can be made that grants an Added Effect. Other Appearances Copious Mushroom Skewers boost the Warriors' movement speed by 15% when cooked before the start of a Challenge or Scenario, and is made using four Endura Shrooms, four Stamella Shrooms, four Rushrooms, four Hearty Truffles, and four Big Hearty Truffles, but this can be lowered to three of each Mushroom through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". The Recipe for Copious Mushroom Skewers is obtained by completing the Quest "Stumped by Shrooms".

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Copious Seafood Skewers can be made by Cooking four different types of Seafood in a Cooking Pot. When eaten, they heal some of Link's Hearts. Despite being a heap of random Items shoved onto a skewer, they are known to be a tasty dish. Because of their specified recipe, very few variations of Copious Seafood Skewers exist. They can only be made by combining a Hyrule Bass, a Sanke Carp, and two different types of seafood that grant the same effect. These variations are as follows: Hearty Copious Seafood Skewers: Made by using any combination of Hearty Salmons, Hearty Blueshell Snails, or Hearty Bass. When eaten, it will fully heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Energizing Copious Seafood Skewers: Made by using Staminoka Basses and Bright-Eyed Crabs. If they're eaten, they refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Mighty Copious Seafood Skewers: Made using any combination of Mighty Carp, Mighty Porgies, or Razorclaw Crabs. Eating one will grant Link a temporary boost to his attack power. Tough Copious Seafood Skewers: Made using any combination of Armored Carp, Armored Porgies, or Ironshell Crabs. When they're eaten, Link's defense will be temporarily boosted. Sneaky Copious Seafood Skewers: Made using Stealthfin Trouts and Sneaky River Snails. Eating them increases Link's Stealth for a short period of time. Much like their counterparts, Copious Seafood Skewers can be made by Cooking four different types of Seafood together. When eaten, they restore some of Link's Hearts. They have also retained their reputation as delicious Meals. Variations of Copious Seafood Skewers can be made using any combination of Hyrule Basses, Sanke Carps, or Ancient Arowanas, and any other type of Seafood. The addition of Ancient Arrowanas as a neutral ingredient allows for new variations that were not available in . These variations are as follows: Hearty Copious Seafood Skewers: Made by using Hearty Salmons and Hearty Bass. When eaten, it will fully heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Energizing Copious Seafood Skewers: Made by using Staminoka Basses and Bright-Eyed Crabs. If they are eaten, they refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Mighty Copious Seafood Skewers: Made using any combination of Mighty Carp, Mighty Porgies, or Razorclaw Crabs. Eating one will grant Link a temporary boost to his attack power. Tough Copious Seafood Skewers: Made using any combination of Armored Carp, Armored Porgies, or Ironshell Crabs. When they are eaten, Link's Defense will be temporarily boosted. Sneaky Copious Seafood Skewers: Made using Stealthfin Trouts and Sneaky River Snails. Eating them increases Link's Stealth for a short period of time.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can make Copious Simmered Fruits by Cooking four different Fruits together in a Cooking Pot. Their default version can be made by using at least two Fruits with differing Added Effects. Eating them will heal some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. The flavors of the Fruits used in these Meals exist in perfect harmony. If Link uses an Apple, a Wildberry, and a Palm Fruit when making Copious Simmered Fruits, the fourth Fruit that he uses will grant the dish a status effect. This can result in the following variations: Hearty Copious Simmered Fruit: Made using Hearty Durians. When eaten, they'll heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him temporary Hearts. Hasty Copious Simmered Fruit: Made using Fleet-Lotus Seeds. Link's movement speed will receive a boost when he eats these. Spicy Copious Simmered Fruit: Made using Spicy Peppers. These fruits will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance if he eats them. Electro Copious Simmered Fruit: Made using Voltfruits. By eating them, Link can gain one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Copious Simmered Fruit: Made using Mighty Bananas. If they're eaten, they'll grant Link a boost to the power of his attacks. Chilly Copious Simmered Fruit: Made using Hydromelons. These meals can be eaten to provide Link one level of Heat Resistance. Copious Simmered Fruits can be made by Cooking at least four different types of Fruit together. Their default versions can be made by using a combination of Apples, Golden Apples, Hylian Tomatoes, Palm Fruits, and Wildberries, all of which grant no Added Effects. Variations can be made by using Fruits that grant an Added Effect. Alternatively, Link can use a fifth ingredient to create variations as well.

is a character in . Biography Coppora is a Hylian who guards the western entrance of Lookout Landing. He carries a Rusty Halberd. If Link attempts to enter Lookout Landing for the first time from the west, Coppora is shocked to see him and reveals that everyone has been worried. He directs Link to the Research Lab, where he can meet with Purah. If Link speaks to Coppora after he has already entered Lookout Landing, he is shocked to see him and asks where Zelda is. Dismissing his own question, Coppora instead tells Link to meet with Purah at the Research Lab. After Link has spoken to Purah, Coppora can be found thinking about reading the Newspaper, He is surprised to see Link if they have not met, revealing that he wanted to come and see him. In future conversations, Coppora asks Link if he had read the Newspaper. He shares information about the Extreme Cold Snap afflicting Rito Village, and he suggests bringing Spicy Foods or Spicy Elixirs when traveling to Hebra

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Cora Lake is located south of the Lake Tower in the Faron Sea. It is surrounded by cliffs on all sides, leaving lower than the Faron Grasslands nearby. The Lake is the source of the Menoat River, which feeds into the Faron Sea. During the "EX Treasure: Garb of Winds" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link is tasked with finding the Hero of Winds' garb, which was stolen from Hyrule Castle. After reading Misko's EX Journal 2, he learns that it is located "where the Menoat River was born". In the cave opening on the west side of Cora Lake, Link can find an EX Treasure Chest containing the Island Lobster Shirt, which can be pulled from the Water using the Magnesis Rune. Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds As in , Cora Lake is located in the Faron Sea.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Coral Reef is a General Store that has been in business for over 100 years, and it is currently operated by Cleff. Alongside the Hammerhead, it is part of Marot Mart in Zora's Domain. The first time Link speaks to Cleff, he will advertise the Store's Swift Violets and Arrows. The Store is unable to sell Shock Arrows, however, due to the Zora being vulnerable to Electricity. The Coral Reef also sells fresh Fish, many of which are caught by Mei. When Link asks Cleff how the Coral Reef's business is doing, he admits that they are struggling due to a lack of visitors coming to Zora's Domain, and he is afraid that he will have to close the General Store. After Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, Clef} claims that business has improved, and he does not think he will have to close the Coral Reef. Douma also arrives in Zora's Domain, planning to purchase rare Items from the Coral Reef to sell elsewhere. She suggests buying the Chillfin Trouts and Sizzlefin Trouts, since they can only be found in Zora's Domain. If Link makes a purchase at the Coral Reef, Cleff will thank him and ask him to return again. Should Link buy the entire stock of a single Item, Cleff promises to restock soon. When Link buys all of the Items in the Coral Reef, Cleff invites him to come back once he has replenished his stock. Wares and Pricing The Coral Reef reappears in , but it will not stock any items until Link has completed the Main Quest "Sidon of the Zora". Wares and Pricing Other Appearances As part of the Quest "Imported Goods", the owner of the Coral Reef wants to provide goods from all across Hyrule to his customers, but he needs ideas about what to look into. Once he is shown a variety of Materials, the owner decides to procure them for the Coral Reef.

are Objects and Korok Seed Puzzles in . Overview These types of Korok Seed Puzzles involve a pair of Corks chained together. One of these Corks is wedged into a Tree Stump, though the other is not. To solve these Puzzles, Link must manipulate the free Cork so that its counterpart is pulled out of the Stump. One way he can do this is by attaching heavy Objects, such as Boulders, to the Cork, which weighs it down. He can also attach Rockets to these Corks. In certain cases, Link is able to submerge the free Cork beneath Water and release it, causing it to launch into the air. After Link solves the Korok Seed Puzzle, a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Corta Lake is located on the southern foothills of Mount Floria in West Necluda. It is the origin point of several of the Waterfalls that make up the Floria Falls, which eventually flow south into Lake Floria. The remains of two small Zonai Ruins can be found within the Lake. As Farosh flies over the Floria Falls, strong Winds and Updrafts will appear around Corta Lake. During the "EX Treasure: Dark Armor" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link reads Misko's EX Journal 2 and discovers that part of the Phantom Ganon Set is hidden "at the highest of three waterfalls north of Lake Floria." This correlates to the Waterfall that flows south from Corta Lake, where Link can find a metallic EX Treasure Chest containing the Phantom Ganon Skull. A total of five Treasure Chests can be found within Corta Lake. One at the center of the Lake is made of metal, and it contains a bundle of five Fire Arrows. The other four are made of wood and located within the Zonai Ruins. However, Boulders have been placed on top of them, which prevent them from rising to the Water's surface. When Link moves the Boulders, he will be able to open the Treasure Chests and retrieve an Opal, a Purple Rupee, a Silver Rupee, and a Gold Rupee. Creatures Enemies Materials Areas

is a recurring location in . Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain is located on top of the East Hill, which is located at the edge of Kakariko Village in West Necluda. As its name implies, it is home to the Great Fairy named Cotera. The Great Fairy Fountain is located in an unnamed forest, and it is surrounded by a shallow pool of Water. 10,000 years ago, the peaceful Sheikah founded Kakariko Village near Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain. As a result, Cotera is considered a guardian Spirit of the Village, and its residents are wary of giving out the location of her Fountain. When Link first comes upon Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain, it will be withered into a bud. Cotera speaks to him from inside, begging that he listen to her story. If Link agrees to listen, Cotera explains that since travelers have stopped visiting her Fountain and offering Rupees, her power has dwindled. To restore her power, she needs Link to give her Rupees. Depending on how many other Great Fairy Fountains have been activated, Cotera requests that Link pay either 100 Rupees, 500 Rupees, 1,000 Rupees, or 10,000 Rupees. After Link gives the correct amount of Rupees to Cotera, her Great Fairy Fountain will bloom as her power is restored. Following this, Cotera will be able to enhance Link's Armor when provided with the proper Materials. The degree to which she can enhance his Armor depends on how many other Great Fairy Fountains have been opened. In search of Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain, Pikango has come to Kakariko Village. During the "Find the Fairy Fountain" Main Quest, Pikango shares that he has a lead on the Fountain's location, and he asks Link if he would like to come with. However, Pikango becomes too tired to finish the journey, so he requests that Link go ahead and take a Picture of Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain if he finds it. If Link returns to Pikango with a Picture of the Fountain, he will be shocked, but he notes that it is not as sacred and elegant as he thought it would be. As a reward, Pikango offers to guide Link to locations he has been unable to find. Creatures Materials Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain is located next to the Little Twin Bridge in West Necluda.

is a recurring character in . Biography Cottla is a young Sheikah girl residing in Kakariko Village with her sister Koko and their father Dorian. Cottla and her sister Koko wake up at 5:00 AM, with Cottla claiming her mother is hiding. When Link initially asks Cottla if she would like to play, she will refuse, claiming that she and her mother are already in the middle of a game. She will then head up to the Ta'loh Naeg Shrine on the East Hill to search for the her mother. By 8:00 AM, Cottla gives up and goes to meet with the rest of her family. At 8:30 in the morning, Cottla will sit at the base of a Tree near a fork in the road, wondering if her other family members will come by. At around 9:00 AM, Koko will join her. After Link speaks with Impa for the first time, Dorian will start to join them at this time. While they sit together, Dorian shares stories with his children. Dorian tells them about how one can hear a woman sobbing in the woods past the Ancient Shrine, but he is actually just trying to scare them away from the woods, which have become full of Monsters. However, Cottla only becomes excited by the story instead of being fearful. At 11:00 AM, Koko and Cottla will get up and go their separate ways, running through Kakariko Village as Dorian returns to work. Even in the Rain, Cottla can be found running about. If Link speaks to her during this time, she will declare that she is bored and wonder when dinner will be. Should he immediately say goodbye, she will be disappointed. If Link asks Cottla if she would like to play with him, she will be excited at once, causing her to ask what he would like to play. For games, Link can choose between Tag or Hide-and-seek. Choosing Tag excites Cottla further and she begins to run in place. Choosing Hide-and-seek makes Cottla declare that she will hide while Link seeks her. Before she leaves, she lets Link know that they will have to stop the game at dinnertime. Selecting a game and agreeing to play begins the "Playtime with Cottla" Side Quest. When Link catches Cottla, she will pout. However, she is excited to have had so much fun. As a reward, she gives Link her secret treasure, which is Rock Salt. At around 4:30 PM, Cottla will sit at one of the tables near Impa's House, where Koko has been Cooking at a Cooking Pot. While sitting, she will complain about wanting dinner. Link can still ask if she would like to play, but she is too focused on dinner to want to. During the "Cooking with Koko" Side Quest, Koko mentions that Cottla loves Hot Buttered Apples. 7:00 PM is when both Cottla and her sister Koko head home for the night. While asleep in her Bed, Cottla dreams about her parents.

is a location in . Features and Overview Courage Island is a tall Sky Island located in the Hyrule Ridge Sky. In the distant past, it was the site of the Dive Ceremony for Zonai youth to test their courage and prove their adulthood. This was done by diving from the top of the Island through a set of rings to the pool at the lowest part of the Island. It has since been abandoned and is home to a lone Steward Construct. By speaking to the Steward Construct, Link can undergo the Dive Ceremony himself. If Link has not performed the dive beforehand, the Steward Construct will require him to undergo a practice run first. This practice run does not have a time limit and the sole goal is to pass through all of the rings of light in the dive. If Link agrees, he will be taken to the top of Courage Island and the practice run will begin once he activates the terminal there. When Link successfully completes the practice run, the Taunhiy Shrine will appear to the west of the pool. Upon Link completing the practice run, the Steward Construct will allow him to perform the Dive Ceremony at the cost of one Zonai Charge. The Dive Ceremony must be completed by passing through all of the rings of light in 35 seconds or less. By completing the Dive Ceremony in the specified amount of time, Link will be given the Glide Shirt as proof of his courage and status as an adult. If Link takes longer than 20 seconds to complete the Ceremony, he will be invited to beat the current record at the cost of another Zonai Charge. If Link also beats the record of 20 seconds on his first attempt, he will be given a Large Zonai Charge as well. Beating this record after his first attempt will also result in the same reward. After Link beats the 20 second record, the Steward Construct will ask for his name to register him as the new record holder. A Device Dispenser can be found on the lowest part of the Island where the Steward Construct waits. Areas Device Dispenser Creatures Inhabitants Materials Korok Seeds

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses In , Courser Bee Honey resembles beehives and can be found on various Trees throughout Hyrule Kingdom. It can be found in various Regions, but it appears more commonly in Necluda. Each hive is guarded by a swarm of Courser Bees that will do a quarter Heart of damage and take two hits to scare off. Their Honey can be eaten to restore two Hearts. When Cooked, they provide Link with Meals that grant him Stamina Restoration. Courser Bee Honeys can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Orange Dye. The Side Quest "Koko's Specialty" requires Link to retrieve Courser Bee Honey for Koko so she can make a Honeyed Apple. After Link delivers the Courser Bee Honey and Koko makes her desert, she will thank Link and give him an Energizing Honeyed Apple. Courser Bee Honey is required for the following Meals: Courser Bee Honeys are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. Courser Bee Honeys can be found attached to Trees. When they are Fused to a Weapon, they will cause Courser Bees to appear, which will attack Link or nearby Enemies. Courser Bee Honey is required for the following Meals: Other Appearances Courser Bee Honeys can be bought for 24 Rupees at the Mabe Ranch Co-op from Makimi. Unlike many other Materials, they are not Battle-Specific Materials of any Scenarios or Challenges. They are needed for Cooking Glazed Mushrooms, Honey Candies, Honey Crepes, and Honeyed Fruits. They can also be sold at most locations for 10 Rupees and specifically to Bena for 25 Rupees.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Crab Omelets with Rice are made by combining Hylian Rice, a Bird Egg, Rock Salt, and any Crab in a Cooking Pot. Regular Crab Omelets with Rice can only be made by using two different types of Crabs in the recipe or by using an ingredient with a differing effect. These types of omelets restore eight of Link's Hearts}. Alternatively, they can be sold for 70 Rupees. The fluffy Crab legs are known to pair perfectly with the rice. Three different variations of Crab Omelets with Rice exist, correlating with all three different types of Crabs: Energizing Crab Omelet with Rice: Made using a Bright-Eyed Crab. Consuming one will partially refill Link's Stamina Wheel. They restore six of his Hearts and sell for 50 Rupees. Mighty Crab Omelet with Rice: Made using a Razorclaw Crab. When eaten, they will temporarily boost Link's attack power. They also restore nine of his Hearts and sell for 40 Rupees. Tough Crab Omelet with Rice: Made using an Ironshell Crab. If they are consumed, they increase Link's Defense for a short period of time. They heal Link for seven Hearts and sell for 60 Rupees.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Crab Risottos are made in Cooking Pots using Hylian Rice, Goat Butter, Rock Salt, and any type of Crab in . Regular Crab Risotto can only be made by either using two different types of Crabs or by using a fifth Ingredient with a contradictory effect. Eating one will restore six of Link's Hearts, but they can also be sold for 70 Rupees. They are known to be a staple of seaside villages, and the secret to their delicious flavor comes from Crab fat. Due to the three different types of Crabs available, there are three variations of Crab Risotto: Energizing Crab Risotto: Made using a Bright-Eyed Crab. When eaten, they refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. They also heal four of his Hearts and sell for 50 Rupees. Mighty Crab Risotto: Made using a Razorclaw Crab. If eaten, Link's attacks will be more powerful. They also heal seven of his Hearts and are worth 40 Rupees when sold. Tough Crab Risotto: Made using an Ironshell Crab. Consuming one will temporarily boost Link's defensive abilities. In addition, they heal four Hearts and sell for 40 Rupees. are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Crab Stir-Fries are made by Cooking Goron Spice and any type of Crab together in a Cooking Pot. A regular Crab Stir-Fry can be made by either using two different types of Crabs or by adding a third Ingredient with a contradictory effect. When eaten, it will restore seven of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. Alternatively, they can be sold for 50 Rupees. The Goron Spice used is known to pair perfectly with the flavor of the crab meat. Three different variations of Crab Stir-Fry exist, correlating with the three different types of Crabs available: Energizing Crab Stir-Fry: Made using Bright-Eyed Crabs. Eating one will replenish a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. They heal five Hearts, but they sell for 30 Rupees. Mighty Crab Stir-Fry: Made using Razorclaw Crabs. When consumed, Link's attack power will be temporarily boosted. They heal two Hearts and sell for 30 Rupees. Tough Crab Stir-Fry: Made using Ironshell Crabs. If eaten, Link will have a higher Defense for a short period of time. They also heal for five Hearts and can be sold for 30 Rupees. Crab Stir-Fry reappears in . It has the same Recipe that it did in , which is to Cook either a Bright-Eyed Crab, Ironshell Crab, or Razorclaw Crab with Goron Spice.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Cream of Mushroom Soups are made by Cooking any Mushroom, Fresh Milk, Rock Salt, and any vegetable, herb, or flower in a Cooking Pot. They are worth 30 Rupees when sold. These soups are known to be so chunky that they're as filling as a full meal. Several different variations of Cream of Mushroom Soups exist, depending on the type of Ingredients used: Hearty Cream of Mushroom Soup: Made by using Hearty Truffles, Big Hearty Truffles, or other hearty Ingredients. When eaten, they completely restore all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum hearts. They also sell for 50 Rupees. Energizing Cream of Mushroom Soup: Made using Stamella Shrooms or other stamina-increasing Ingredients. Eating one will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. They restore seven of his Hearts and they sell for 40 Rupees. Enduring Cream of Mushroom Soup: Made using Endura Shrooms or Endura Carrots. Consuming this soup will completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. They heal for five Hearts and sell for 40 Rupees. Hasty Cream of Mushroom Soup: Made using Rushrooms or other speed-increasing Ingredients. These soups will temporarily increase Link's speed when eaten. They also restore four Hearts to Link, and they sell for 30 Rupees. Spicy Cream of Mushroom Soup: Made using Sunshrooms or other heat-related Ingredients. Electro Cream of Mushroom Soup: Made using Zapshrooms or other electricity-related Ingredients. Eating them will grant Link one level of Shock Resistance for a short time. are Meals in . Location and Uses Creamy Heart Soups are made by Cooking a Hydromelon, a Voltfruit, Fresh Milk, and either a Hearty Radish or Big Hearty Radish together in a Cooking Pot. Soups made with a regular Hearty Radish heal eight Hearts to Link's Life Gauge and sell for 50 Rupees. Soups made with Big Hearty Radishes heal eleven Hearts and sell for 70 Rupees. Unlike many other Foods, there are no variations of Creamy Heart Soup that grant additional affects. These soups are known to be sweet, and sharing them is believed to bring two people closer together. During her Cooking Class in Gerudo Town, Ashai will mention that she was planning on making Creamy Heart Soup. However, when reciting the recipe to Link, she will name every ingredient but the Hearty Radishes, claiming she cannot remember them. Other Appearances The Recipe for Creamy Heart Soup is earned by completing the Quest "Needs a Splash of...". It is made using four Hydromelons, four Voltfruits, four Hearty Radishes, and four Fresh Milks, but the Recipe can be lowered to three of through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warrior will recover health every 10 seconds.

is a recurring character in . Biography Cree is a Rito child who lives in Rito Village. She is the fourth child of Amali and Kass. When Link first visits Rito Village, Cree can be found crying in her home. If he asks what is wrong, she explains that she is upset that Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been causing so much chaos in the Village and that she is unable to help. According to Amali, Cree and her sisters have been getting needier since Vah Medoh appeared. While she sleeps, Cree wishes for her father to return. After Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been calmed, Link can find Cree's sister, Kheel, at Warbler's Nest. Kheel is angry that none of her sisters have showed up to their planned rehearsal. Their song is supposed to be performed for Kaneli, the elder of Rito Village, and Kheel is worried that they will be laughed off the stage. She asks Link to find her sisters for her, since they would likely listen to a scary Hylian. This initiates the "Recital at Warbler's Nest" Shrine Quest. During this Quest, Cree can be found in The Slippery Falcon, where she has bought all of the Goat Butter. When Link reminds her of her rehearsal, she admits to forgetting. She gives Link her Goat Butter on the condition he makes Salmon Meunière for Genli in the Kitchen. She will also tell Link that Notts is probably singing somewhere high up and Kotts went to catch Hearty Salmon at the pond near the Village's entrance. Once all the sisters are at Warbler's Nest, Cree will tell Link it is fun to sing together. However, she admits that she does not know the lyrics to the song. After Link uses their song to unearth Voo Lota Shrine, Cree and her sisters will be shocked by its sudden appearance. She calls it a weird-looking house and wonders if it was always there. At Notts' suggestion, the five sisters fly off to tell their mother. Cree trips on a rock before taking off with the rest of her sisters. After they have returned to Rito Village, Cree and her sisters can be found singing together near Akh Va'quot Shrine. Due to Link bringing all the sisters together, Cree notes that they are all happy and singing together again. Kass joins his daughters upon his return to Rito Village, playing his bandoneon along with their songs. Cree is so happy to sing his songs with him that she does not hear Link when he speaks to her. She also expresses that she does not care what they sing, so long as everyone has fun together. Kass admits that his daughters refuse to leave him alone throughout the whole day. At night, she and her sisters run to go to sleep in their home. During the blizzard in Rito Village, Cree temporarily takes control of The Slippery Falcon General Store.

The are a recurring location in . The Crenel Hills go unnamed in . Features and Overview The Crenel Hills are located in Hyrule Field. They are a series of rocky hills that are surrounded on either side by the Hylia River. In addition to this, it is covered in giant, hollow Tree Stumps. The Namika Ozz Shrine is located within one of these Stumps, and Thims Bridge and Orsedd Bridge both connect the display=Hills to other parts of Hyrule. The Crenel Hills also feature the remains of many smaller Trees, and a Raft is beached on its northern shore. Ore Deposits, Rare Ore Deposits, and Luminous Stone Deposits can all be found on the Crenel Hills. In the northern part of the Crenel Hills, there is a Stone Talus (Luminous) embedded in the ground. It will initially be inactive, but it will rise up and begin to attack Link if he approaches it. Several Treasure Chests can be found among the Crenel Hills. In total, these Chests contain one Purple Rupee, one Silver Rupee, one Ruby, one Thunderstorm Rod, one Soldier's Shield, 10 Fire Arrows, five Shock Arrows, and five Bomb Arrows. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials Korok Seeds Other Appearances The Crenel Hills appear as part of the Crenel Peak Stage. They are also the setting of the Movied "A Song from the Past" and "Zelda's Wishes".

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Crenel Peak is located in Hyrule Field. It makes up the southern part of the Crenel Hills, and at its very top, there are two Ore Deposits and one Rare Ore Deposit. It features a small hollow with a pond, Cedar Trees, and an alcove. On the western side of Crenel Peak, there is an abandoned Monster Stronghold. When Link enters it, however, Chuchus will drop down and attack him. One Treasure Chest is located on Crenel Peak, which contains a Purple Rupee. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Crenel Peak. The first is a Balloon northwest of the top of the Peak, which Link must use Archery to destroy. The second Puzzle is a Rock Pattern, which surrounds one of the Cedar Trees in the hollow. Link can complete this Pattern using a nearby Rock. Once each of these Korok Seed Puzzles are solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Overview Upon hearing Link's story during the "To the Kingdom of Hyrule" Main Quest, Purah determines that the events of the Upheaval must be connected to the mummy he and Zelda encountered Beneath Hyrule Castle. Since Link heard Zelda's voice, Purah believes that she could still be trapped below Hyrule Castle. As a result, she tasks Link with meeting up with Squad One and Squad Two of the Monster-Control Crew led by Hoz at Hyrule Castle, who have been searching for both him and Zelda. Despite the fact that the mummy may be in the area, Purah decides it is important to keep up the Search for Princess Zelda. Afterwards, "To the Kingdom of Hyrule" will end, and "Crisis at Hyrule Castle will begin. At the First Gatehouse, Link can find Hoz directing his squad members to continue the search. When Link approaches him, Hoz initially tries to dismiss him, claiming to be busy. He is shocked when he realizes it is Link, believing that means Zelda is safe as well. Although Hoz is confused by Link's clarification, he declares that continuing to search for Zelda is more important. He expresses how relieved he is to have Link's help, since they have been overwhelmed by the Gloom surrounding Hyrule Castle. Suddenly, Toren shouts, claiming to have spotted Zelda. On a ruined wall in the distance, a figure resembling Zelda can be seen staring towards the group. Hoz is happy to see that she is safe. However, she then floats into the air and bursts into Light, much to his confusion. Hoz declares that they are in an emergency situation, wondering why Zelda left without speaking to them. When Link steps onto the Platform, mechanical arms will emerge from the ground, outfitting him with a coil of wire that plugs into the Purah Pad. She is relieved that the Purah Pad's Map is functioning, and she tells Link that he should try to get scans from all of the Skyview Towers in Hyrule. Switching topics to the Upheaval, Purah reveals that there have been reports of strange happenings all throughout Hyrule. In particular, she points out troubles in the Regions of Hebra, Eldin, Gerudo, and Lanayru. She believes that they may find clues about Zelda by looking into the Upheaval. Sidon states how dangerous his return is, which causes Yunobo to panic. However, Riju reasons that they still have time until he returns to his full strength, since he chose to leave instead of continuing to fight them. She tells the other Sages to regroup at Lookout Landing, asking Link to join them. After they leave, a Heart Container appears for Link. Back at Lookout Landing, Link can find the Sages gathered outside the Research Lab. When Link approaches Purah, she greets him and asks what he found. After Purah hears Link and the Sages' story, Tulin points out how all of the strange occurences throughout Hyrule happened because of Demon King Ganondorf. are locations in . Features and Overview Two separate Crystal Refineries can be found in . The first is near Nachoyah Shrine on the Great Sky Island, and the second is situated between Lookout Landing and the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins. Each is staffed by a Steward Construct, which is capable of exchanging Crystallized Charges for Energy Wells. It costs 100 Crystallized Charges to create one Energy Well. Once Link can no longer expand his Energy Cell, the Steward Constructs at both Refineries will offer to trade Crystallized Charges for Zonai Devices instead. Both Refineries stock ten of each Zonai Device each, and restock at midnight in-game. Devices cost three Crystallized Charges each, except for Big Batteries which cost thirty Charges. Wares and Pricing

are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Location and Uses Cube Patterns are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. They take the form of two separate structures made entirely of Cubes, with one structure having a Cube that the other lacks. To rectify this, Link must find a nearby Cube, which he can lift with the Magnesis Rune. He must then place this Cube in the correct space on the structure that is missing one. Doing so will cause a Korok to appear, who then gives Link a Korok Seed. List of Cube Patterns A total of four Cube Patterns can be found in Akkala. A total of nine Cube Patterns can be found in Central Hyrule. A total of eight Cube Patterns can be found in Eldin. A total of four Cube Patterns can be found in Faron. A total of 19 Cube Patterns can be found in Gerudo. A total of six Cube Patterns can be found in Hebra. A total of five Cube Patterns can be found in Lanayru. A total of 10 Cube Patterns can be found in Necluda. In , Cube Patterns consist of of a Cube-based structure and an Object made of several cubes. Using Ultrahand, Link must pick up the Cube Object and manipulate it so that it fits into the structure. Upon successfully completing the structure, a Korok will appear to give Link a Korok Seed.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Cuho Mountain is located in the western portion of the Tabantha Frontier, where it overlooks Gisa Crater to the south, Passer Hill and Lake Totori South to the north, and Strock Lake to the east. Its peak is composed of three separate rock spires, with enough space between them for Link to walk through. Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits can be found along the slopes of Cuho Mountain. After Link completes the four Ancient Shrines on the Great Plateau during the "EX The Champions' Ballad" Main Quest, a Monument will emerge from the ground on Cuho Mountain. When Link travels to the Monument, he will find Kass playing his bandoneon nearby. The voice of a Monk then speaks to Link, instructing him to undertake the Divine Beast Tamer's Trial depicted on the Monument. Following this, Kass sings a portion of the Court Poet's Unfinished Song, which describes the Trial Revali undertook 100 years ago. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Korok Seeds Cuho Mountain is located in west Tabantha Frontier. Like its counterpart, it borders Passer Hill to the northwest, Lake Totori South to the north, Strock Lake to the east, and Gisa Crater to the south. Its peak remains split into three rock spires, though the south spire's east side has been struck by a large piece of Fallen Debris, more of which litters the rest of the Mountain. As a result of the Blizzard enveloping Hebra, a thin layer of Snow has formed across all of Cuho Mountain save for a small Grassy plateau overlooking Strock Lake, though the Blizzard and associated Freezing Climate is only present in the north foothills. Once the "Tulin of Rito Village" Main Quest is completed, the Blizzard dissipates and the Freezing Climate encompassing the foothills disappears. Creatures Enemies Materials Korok Seeds

, also known as , is a recurring mechanic in . The Currency mechanic goes unnamed outside of and . Overview Rupees are the primary Currency in Hyrule in , used by Hylians and Business Scrubs to purchase items from one another. Trade and bartering are occasionally used for simple goods like food, and Carlov accepts Mysterious Shells as a Currency to exchange for Figurines. Although Rupees can be obtained in the Minish Realm, the Minish are never shown to use them. Instead, they give the people of Hyrule the nectar of their Pico Blooms, and leave Items (including Rupees) scattered around the land for travelers to find with Kinstones. Other Appearances

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Curry Pilaf is made by Cooking Hylian Rice, a Bird Egg, Goat Butter, and Goron Spice in a Cooking Pot. They restore four of Link's Hearts when eaten, but they can also be sold for 40 Rupees. The Goron Spice used to make these pilafs gives them a rich, spicy aroma. By adding a fifth Ingredient, several different variations of Curry Pilaf can be made: Hearty Curry Pilaf: Made by adding hearty Ingredients. Eating this will completely restore all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. They are also worth 60 Rupees when sold. Energizing Curry Pilaf: Made by adding energizing Ingredients. When eaten, these pilafs will replenish a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. They heal four of Link's Hearts, and they sell for 50 Rupees. Enduring Curry Pilaf: Made by adding either Endura Carrots or Endura Shrooms. Consuming these Meals will completely replenish and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. They restore nine of Link's Hearts, but they can also sell for 60 Rupees. Hasty Curry Pilaf: Made by adding speed-related Ingredients. Eating one will temporarily boost Link's movement speed. They heal for five Hearts, and they can be sold for 50 Rupees. Spicy Curry Pilaf: Made by adding spicy Ingredients. When eaten, they will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance for a short period of time. They heal eight of his Hearts and sell for 50 Rupees. Electro Curry Pilaf: Made by adding electricity-related Ingredients. If they are eaten, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance. They heal eight of Link's Hearts, but they can be sold for 50 Rupees. Mighty Curry Pilaf: Made by adding attack-boosting Ingredients. Eating one of these pilafs will temporarily boost Link's attack power. They restore five Hearts and sell for 50 Rupees. Tough Curry Pilaf: Made by adding defensive Ingredients. When consumed, Link's Defense will be temporarily increased. They replenish five Hearts in Link's Life Gauge, and they sell for 50 Rupees. Sneaky Curry Pilaf: Made by adding Stealth-boosting Ingredients. Eating one will increase Link's Stealth abilities for a short time. They heal five of Link's Hearts and sell for 50 Rupees. Chilly Curry Pilaf: Made by using cold Ingredients. When eaten, Link will temporarily gain one level of Heat Resistance. They restore five Hearts and sell for 50 Rupees.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Curry Rices are made by Cooking Hylian Rice and Goron Spice together in a Cooking Pot. They can be eaten to restore two Hearts to Link, and they also sell for 20 Rupees. They are a favorite all over Hyrule, noted to be a simple dish with a flavor people do not get tired of. Curry Rice is mentioned as part of the "Curry for What Ails You" Side Quest. Lester, a Stable Worker at Rito Stable, enjoys spice, specifically Curry Rice. While he has Hylian Rice, he does not have any Goron Spice. He will request Link bring him Goron Spice, which begins the "Curry for What Ails You" Side Quest. As a reward for completing the quest, Lester will give Link 50 Rupees. Only fruits (and Courser Bee Honey) can be added to Curry Rice. Otherwise, the resulting dishes will be different Meals. Using additional Ingredients will create the following variations: Hearty Curry Rice: Made by using Hearty Durians. They heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum number of Hearts when eaten. They are worth 50 Rupees when sold. Energizing Curry Rice: Made by adding Courser Bee Honey. When eaten, they restore a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Curry Rice: Made by using Fleet-Lotus Seeds. When eaten, Link's speed will be temporarily boosted. They heal three of Link's Hearts and sell for 30 Rupees. Spicy Curry Rice: Made by using Spicy Pepper. Eating one will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. They restore three Hearts and sell for 30 Rupees. Electro Curry Rice: Made by using Voltfruit. If they are eaten, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance. They heal six of Link's Hearts and can also be sold for 30 Rupees. Mighty Curry Rice: Made by using Mighty Bananas. Eating these will temporarily boost the power of Link's attacks. They will also restore three of Link's Hearts, and they sell for 30 Rupees. Chilly Curry Rice: Made by using Hydromelons. When they are eaten, Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance for a short period of time. They heal three Hearts and sell for 30 Rupees. Curry Rice returns in with an identical base recipe. It can be made in either a Cooking Pot or a Portable Pot. Other Appearances Curry Rice appears in as an unlockable Recipe. The Recipe is unlocked after completing the Scenario "All Hyrule, United". Like in and , it is made with Hylian Rice and Goron Spice. If made, Warriors will start the battle with an extra two Hearts.

is a recurring character in . Biography Dabi is a Hylian and the owner of the Tabantha Bridge Stable on Hyrule Ridge. He can be found at the front of Tabantha Bridge Stable. If Tabantha Bridge Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Dabi will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Dabi explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Dabi then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Dabi instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Dabi suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Dabi to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Dabi tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Tabantha Bridge Stable, Dabi will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Dabi thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Dabi will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Dabi asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Tabantha Bridge Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Dabi asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Dabi will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Dabi insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Dabi refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Dabi starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Dabi gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated

Link to name her Epona. Dabi gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Dabi gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside Tabantha Bridge Stable, Dabi once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by Tabantha Bridge Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Dabi tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Dabi wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

is a recurring character in . Biography Dai is a Hylian traveler who can be found outside the Coliseum Ruins. He is equipped with a Traveler's Sword and a Fisherman's Shield. Link can initially find him trembling near the entrance to the Coliseum Ruins, looking on in terror at the Lynel inside. If it is Raining, Dai will blame his trembling on the Rain. Upon speaking to Dai, he will be spooked by Link's presence and consequently chide him for scaring him. Afterwards, Dai will explain that he is attempting to slay the monsters inside the Ruins for the treasure and Weaponry they guard. If Link speaks to him a second time, Dai will boast about his skills in battle or suggest that Link scouts out the area first. However, Dai will not actually go into the Coliseum Ruins. At midnight, Dai will fall asleep against the wall that he hides behind, dreaming of defeating the monsters inside the Ruins. Dai will wake up and resume his activities at 05:00 AM. If Link defeats the Lynel inside the Coliseum Ruins and returns to Dai, he will give Link a Silver Rupee, valued at 100 Rupees, for his trouble. He will then tell Link that he can handle the situation on his own and bids him farewell.

is a recurring character in . Biography Dalia is a Gerudo child who lives in Gerudo Town. At night, she sleeps at Lorn's Fruit Stand, which is a Stall owned by her mother, Lorn. According to Lorn, Dalia loves Fruitcake, so she makes it every once in a while. When Link first enters Gerudo Town, he can find Dalia and the other three children speaking to each other as a group as the sun sets. Kalani asks them if they are in love. Makure then responds that she wants to attend Ashai's class when she grows up and get married. Pearle then comments that Ashai is unmarried and wonders what that means. Lastly, Dalia says that she heard being in love is the sweetest thing in the world, but she does not think she can handle something sweeter than berries. After this, Link can find Dalia in the empty plot near The Noble Canteen. She asks what someone from out of town is doing in a place like this. When Link asks what she is doing, Dalia reveals that she is planning on starting a fruit garden in the plot, though she is keeping it from her mother for now. Once the garden is made, she will be able to eat as mush fruit as she wants. However, she has not yet decided what she will plant. Despite this, Dalia promises to share some of what she grows with Link. After Link has calmed Divine Beast Vah Naboris and started "The Thunder Helm" Side Quest, he can find Dalia crying in the empty plot. Dalia explains that she wanted to plant an orchard in the plot, going so far as to pick up the Trash, pull the weeds, and till the ground. Unfortunately, the Water from the nearby trough is unusable due to a flow of Trash into it. Without the Water, her orchard will not be able to flourish. After she is finished speaking, Link will receive "The Mystery Polluter" Side Quest. Link finds out that the source of the Trash is a Gerudo named Calyban, who enjoys eating Hydromelons on the walls of Gerudo Town and throwing the rinds into the waterway. This pollutes the water trough that Dalia for her orchard. Link convinces Calyban to stop by giving her 10 Wildberries. Once Calyban receives her Wildberries, though, she feels bad for Dalia, so she helps clean up the trash. When Link returns to Dalia, Calyban has already cleaned up her Trash and left. Dalia gives Link a Hydromelon that was given to her by "the lady who cleaned it up" as a thank you for caring about her. Dalia claims that Calyban also gave her some Wildberries, which has inspired her to make her garden into a Wildberry patch. She tells Link he can come eat the Wildberries anytime he likes, after which "The Mystery Polluter" Side Quest will be complete. Link can come back later to find that three Wildberry plants have grown there. According to

which has inspired her to make her garden into a Wildberry patch. She tells Link he can come eat the Wildberries anytime he likes, after which "The Mystery Polluter" Side Quest will be complete. Link can come back later to find that three Wildberry plants have grown there. According to Dalia, when she planted the first Wildberry, more began to sprout from the ground. Despite her work clearing up the garbage and preparing the garden, she thinks the first Wildberry must have been magic. In her sleep, she even talks about eating Wildberries and other fruit.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Dalite Forest is located in the Hyrule Ridge. It is a large forest that is bisected by a road that leads to Nima Plain. A pond sits along the southwestern reaches of the Forest, separated by a small rock hill. Along the path that divides the Forest, two Koroks can be found. The first one is found by offering an Apple at the statues on the roadside, while the second one can be found by hitting an Acorn-shaped Jar suspended by a chain on a tall Tree further on the path. Two additional Koroks can be found near the pond by lifting a Rock atop a Tree and by hitting a second Acorn-shaped Jar suspended on the inside of a hollow Rock formation. Creatures Materials Equipment Dalite Forest is located on Hyrule Ridge.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Damel Forest is located in the Faron Grasslands. It lies north of both the Zonai Ruins and Harker Lake. Approaching from the south, the entrance to the Damel Forest is flanked by two large, carven stone pillars. An ancient road of flagstone and dirt passes through these into a wide clearing, where several Enemies are camped. There are a handful of Wooden Boxes present in the clearing, gathered together on its western flank. On nearly all sides, the forest is thick with vegetation. To the west lie the tall Farosh Hills, forming a natural barrier. It is often overcast or rainy in this particular environment; the ground is saturated as a result, evidenced by the presence of many puddles. Northward and then east, past the first Monster Stronghold and the clearing sits a second clearing space. Here is another Monster Stronghold, coupled with a handful of metal Wooden Boxes strewn on the ground. This second camp boasts a Cooking Pot near a small pond. From here, the old forest road veers to the southeast, where it meets the winding Dracozu River. Its path is watched over by several stone Dragon statues. Another wooded hill encircles from the north and boasts similar fare. From this vantage point, the grand ruins at Dracozu Lake are visible. In a small cave blocked with a breakable rock wall on top of the wooded hill, on its eastern flank, are two regular Ore Deposits and one Rare Ore Deposit. The first aforementioned Monster Stronghold has a wooden Treasure Chest containing a bundle of Fire Arrows, as well as a remote, metallic Treasure Chest on a raised platform containing a Soldier's Spear. The second camp has a raised platform housing a metallic Treasure Chest, which contains a single Silver Rupee. Creatures Enemies Materials Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Damia is a Korok that lives in the Korok Forest. Link can meet with Damia by following the eastern path out of the Forest. Damia has been expecting Link and asks if he is ready for the Test of Wood, since it is the hardest of the Korok Trials. He explains that the only thing Link needs to do is equip the Korok Gear and reach the Ancient Shrine. Damia asks Link if he is ready to attempt the Trial. Agreeing initiates "The Test of Wood" Shrine Quest. Once Link completes the Shrine Quest, Damia congratulates him. He then offers Link another trial, the Test of Wood Mini-Game, which has a shorter time limit. If Link can make it to Maag Halan Shrine within five minutes, Damia promises him a prize. However, he requires a security deposit of 20 Rupees, which covers the cost of gear rental. If Link agrees, Damia explains that the rules are the same as before. He then goes to set everything up. When Link reaches the Shrine, Damia shouts that he reached the goal. The prize for making it in under five minutes is a Silver Rupee, which Damia hopes Link likes. When Link breaks his record, Damia asserts that he knew Link would be good at the Test of Wood. He asks Link to let him know if he wants to come back and break his record. If Link is done playing, Damia will take his Korok Gear back and return him to the start.

is a recurring character in . Biography Danda is an elderly Gerudo who manages the Arrow Specialty Shop Stall in Gerudo Town. She boasts that she has the best selection of Arrows available. Danda's daughter works all of the time, which means Danda has to look after her grandchildren, Kalani and Makure. As Link shops, Danda asks what he thinks about her selection of Arrows. If Link buys all of one type of Arrow, Danda calls him strange for needing so many. After buying the last of her Arrows, Danda promises to restock soon. When spoken to after this, she comments on how long it took her to procure all of her products. Danda will remark that she has never seen her selection cleared out so completely, before she thanks Link and tells him that she should now be able to buy her grandchildren some new toys. While she does sell Items herself, Danda will also buy them from Link. On occasion, she will wonder why Link would sell such high quality Items. She may also remark that she believes one of her grandchildren will be excited to see what she has bought.

is a recurring character in . Biography Danton is a Hylian who resides at Snowfield Stable. During the day, he will sit beside his Cooking Pot outside of the Stable. He warns Link that he should make Cold Resistant Food before heading into the Hebra Mountains. He allows Link to use his Cooking Pot, as leaving for such a journey unprepared would be unacceptable. If it starts to snow, Danton will retreat inside the Stable. When Link first approaches Danton, he will talk about how great something must be before asking if he knows what he is talking about. If Link explains that he does not know, Danton reveals he is talking about the Sword that Seals the Darkness, which legends state has been hidden somewhere in Hyrule. He is enamored by the Sword and dreams of owning it. Should Link speaks to him again, Danton will imagine what it would be like if he found the Master Sword, claiming he would use it to defeat every monster in the Hebra Mountains. Even while sleeping, Danton dreams about the Sword. After obtaining the Master Sword, Link can show it to Danton. Once he calms down, Danton will note that the Sword is not as big or extravagant as he thought it would be, but he still finds it amazing and says that he will never forget the day he saw it. If Link speaks to Danton again, he will state that according to legend, Link is the chosen hero. In that scenario, Danton makes Link promise he will never give up, despite all of the challenges he will have to face.

is a recurring character in . Biography Dantz is a Hylian who works at Hateno Pasture in Hateno Village. He carries a Farmer's Pitchfork, which he uses to move hay. When Link first approaches him, Dantz asks if he is a wanderer. He mutters to himself that this could work, noting Link looks like he can use a Bow and asking if he could help. If Link agrees, Dantz remarks that he is the answer to his prayers. He explains that he needs Link to hunt the Mountain Bucks in Retsam Forest, since they are overpopulated and destroying the environment. He gives Link a time limit of one minute. Should Link accept thos, Dantz wants to know if he can start hunting right away. When Link asks if there is a trick, Dantz suggests using a strong Bow so that he will only have to take one shot. He also advises sneaking up to Deer without them noticing. If Link decides to head out, Dantz calls him a trooper and asserts that he is counting on him. Before the Deer Hunting Mini-Game starts, Dantz says he will call for Link once the minute is up. When Link runs out of time, he will be transported back to Dantz. If Link fails to get a single Deer, Dantz refuses to give him any reward. He gives him one Rupee for getting one to three Deer as thanks for doing his part. If he gets four to six deer, Dantz calls Link vicious and rewards him with a Blue Rupee. For seven to nine Deer, Dantz admits it is more than he thought Link would get and gives him a Red Rupee. Dantz is shocked if Link gets all 10 Deer, saying there is such a thing as being too good at hunting and giving him a Purple Rupee. Like all residents of Hateno Village, Dantz will notice if Link speaks to him while carrying the Blue Flame. He recalls that Purah used to carry a similar flame, and while he does not know why a stranger has it, he sends Link along anyway. Afterwards, he will encourage Link to continue on his delivery for Purah.

Darb Pond is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Darb Pond is a small body of Lava south of Death Mountain in Eldin Canyon. It is connected by a strait that flows from the Mountain's Lava moat. Darb Pond itself flows into Medingo Pool further south through another, narrower strait. Several Ore Deposits line the Pond's shores. Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Korok Seeds Darb Pond has solidified into igneous rock, and no longer contains any Lava, revealing a skeletal ribcage. A Fire Wizzrobe can be found wandering above the western area of the Pond, and the central spire of rock now contains a Ore Deposit and a Luminous Stone Deposit. Several pieces of Fallen Debris have fallen from the Sky, bringing Fire Fruits with them. Creatures Enemies Materials

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Dark Hood is a piece of Armor that can be purchased from Kilton at his Fang and Bone shop after all Divine Beasts have been freed. It cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy, nor can it be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Dark Hood, alongside the Dark Tunic and Dark Trousers, compose the Dark Series. When the full set is worn, it provides a Night Speed Up bonus. Also, characters get scared when they see Link wearing it. Other Appearances The Dark Hood is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and it is obtained by completing the Challenge "Questionable Escort Mission". Unlike most other pieces of Attire, it cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop.

The is a recurring Armor Set in . The Dark Series goes unnamed in and . Location and Uses The Dark Series is a set of Armor that can be purchased from Kilton at Fang and Bone after all four Divine Beasts have been freed. The set cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy, nor can it be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Dark Set is comprised of the Dark Hood, Dark Tunic, and Dark Trousers. When the full set is worn, it provides a Night Speed Up bonus. Additionally, characters get scared when they see Link wearing it. Enhancing The Dark Series can be purchased from Bargainer Statues in the Depths and at Lookout Landing. Enhancing Other Appearances The Dark Hood is acquired upon completing the "Questionable Escort Mission" Quest. The Dark Tunic is acquired upon completing the "Unnatural Disaster" Quest. The Dark Trousers are acquired upon completing the "Fire Hazards" Quest.

is a recurring character in . Biography Darton is a Hylian child who lives at Dueling Peaks Stable with his family. During the day, he can be found near the Horses with his twin brother, Shibo. At night, Darton will go inside the Stable to sleep. While asleep, Darton will count one-colored Horses. When he wakes up, Darton will attempt to beat Shibo to the Horse pen. According to Sagessa, Darton and Shibo will collect more Apples if the Stable runs out. When approached, he begins speaking to his brother in hushed words about whether or not Link may be interested in Horses. He decides that Link has the look of a Horse enthusiast, and concludes that he must be a customer. Darton believes that Link's passion for Horses is apparent in his eyes. Because of this, Darton encourages Link to ask the pair of them for information about steeds. Darton and Shibo will tell Link various facts about Horses if he asks. They will teach him how to sneak up behind a Horse to catch it off guard, essentially teaching him how to crouch. If questioned about which Horses are good for riding, they will explain how the color indicates their temperament: gentle Horses have spots, while more wild Horses are solid in color. They also point out the differences between the two temperaments. Darton and Shibo's father, Rensa, also gave them advice on what kind of Horse is difficult to train, and which to start with. When asked about how to train a Horse properly, the twins point out that a Horse will not be obedient at first and must be soothed. Darton mentions that their father says constantly soothing a Horse will not help, so the rider must only do it when the Horse is doing what it is being told. Whenever the twins are finished answering a question, Darton will ask if Link understood everything. When Link decides to leave, Darton and Shibo will say goodbye the same way. is a recurring character in . Biography Daruk was the Goron Chief and Champion, one of the appointed members tasked with piloting a Divine Beast in the fight against Calamity Ganon 100 years ago. He was the pilot of the Divine Beast Vah Rudania. He was described as being generally calm, but becomes wildly excitable in battle. He possessed the ability known as Daruk's Protection, a red crystal polyhedric barrier that can deflect any attack or incoming damage to the user. When Daruk was a small child, Dogs would chase him around when they saw him. This started when he stepped on the tail of one, which made it angry at him. Even as an adult, he still panics when he meets a Dog. Daruk carried a Weapon known as the Boulder Breaker, which he could easily swing around despite its heft. According to Bludo, Daruk used the Boulder Breaker to carve the valley at Gortram Cliff in a single night. This was done so the Gorons could more easily attain Rock Roast. There is also a rumor that Daruk would fan himself with the Boulder Breaker. Daruk wrote his thoughts down in a Book known as Daruk's Training Journal. In his first entry, he writes about the Rock Roast he ate that day. In the next entry, Daruk recounts meeting a group of Hylians at the base of Death Mountain who spoke about Calamity Ganon. He recalled that the Sheikah dug up Divine Beast Vah Rudania from Death Mountain several years prior, and he was told by the Hylians that is was a weapon that needed someone to control it. In the past, Daruk claimed that Gorons only cared about relics that they could eat, which inspires him to search for Rock Roast for dinner. One day, while Daruk was searching for lunch, he saw a Hylian being attacked by Monsters. He rushed to help them, but by the time he arrived, the Hylian had already defeated his opponents. Daruk was so surprised that another Monster almost ambushed him, but the Hylian ended up saving him. He later learned that the Hylian was named Link, and while Daruk respected his appetite, he was appalled by the organic Food he would eat. Since Link enjoyed Cooking, Daruk offered him some Rock Roast to grill, and he took Link's silence to mean that he enjoyed it. Daruk was also pleased that Link had a similar level of strength to himself. Link explained that when he focused, he felt as though time slows down, which Daruk was impressed by. As he could share a meal with Link and trust him to watch his back, Daruk declared that Link was officially his brother. When Princess Zelda came to Goron City to ask Daruk to become a Champion, he immediately accepted. Daruk and the other Champions take the opportunity to open fire as the Divine Beasts lasers weaken Ganon, but the Blood Moon rises, and revives the fallen monsters. the armies persevere as they charge into Hyrule Castle to take it back and confront Astor and Harbinger Ganon. In The Future of Hyrule Scenario, Princess Zelda leads the ground army and Revali, alongside Teba, leading the Rito forces from the air. The Blight Ganons attempt to hold them back but are ultimately destroyed forever and they defeated Astor and the Harbinger as well. Astor is completely unstable as he orders Ganon to destroy the warriors that stand against him, but he is absorbed by Ganon's Malice to take on a new form and some of its Malice takes control of Terrako, forcing Link and Zelda to duel it. With Terrako damaged, Daruk and the others join her as they mourn for it. The now angered Zelda becomes determined to stop Ganon by any means possible as they head upstairs into the Sanctum where Ganon awaited them. The dark beast proved to be too powerful for them and their attacks don't work against it and Zelda used her power to try and seal it, but it indirectly powers up Terrako,

In the "Terrako's Return" Quest, with Hyrule at peace, the warriors decide to repay Terrako for its miracles that significantly changed their fates for the better and Daruk takes part in finding fifty of its components and brings them to the Lab where Terrako is being rebuilt. Terrako isn't working right, and they became worried. Revali insists that it's likely still waking up, and Impa tries to wake it up herself, before Zelda stops her and stands in front of it. Within a full minute, Terrako became responsive, much to their relief, and reunites with the princess once more. During the end credits following these events, Terrako visits each of its allies and even paid Daruk a visit and he jumps for joy in greetings as it moved on. Daruk is seen with everyone and pulls the Champions and Terrako in for a group hug. During the DLC ending, Daruk and Yunobo sit at a cliff as they enjoy their Prime Rock Roasts together. In another scene, Daruk and Yunobo are then seen with the present and future Champions as they talk among themselves and smile at Terrako. After that, Daruk and the Champions are at the Sheikah Tower, having already returned to their original attires, and they watched as Princess Zelda floats away on a paraglider with Terrako coming along.
