Darunia Lake is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Darunia Lake is a large body of Lava in northwestern Eldin Canyon. The Lake is an extension of Lake Darman to the east, which flows from Death Caldera. Darunia Lake itself flows into the Golow River south, which further extends to the Goronbi River and finally Goronbi Lake. Darunia Lake is a significant part of the Abandoned North Mine, which forms a large part of its southern shore and several scattered islands over the Lake. The Isle of Rabac is also an important landmark of the Lake, and sits close to its northern shore. This Isle can be reached via Mine Cart Tracks that curve over Lake Darman from the Abandoned North Mine's shore. An Igneo Talus is buried in the Lake's western shore. This Igneo Talus is involved in the Side Quest "The Road to Respect", and its defeat is crucial to fulfilling Fugo's request. Areas Enemies Sub-Bosses As a result of Death Mountain's eruption ending, the Lava making up Darunia Lake has dried up, revealing its bed. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Dauntless is a Horse belonging to the Hylian treasure hunter Nazbi. Together they can be found traveling along the Hilltop High Road, making stops at Serenne Stable, Tabantha Bridge Stable, and Snowfield Stable. Dauntless is equipped with a Stable Saddle and a Stable Bridle. Nazbi claims to have become dependent upon Dauntless, being unable to run a few steps on his own without getting winded. He shows a great deal of affection toward Dauntless, who he describes as his "beloved Dauntless," "dear horse," "noble steed," and "equal partner." Even in the face of cold weather, Nazbi encourages Dauntless to continue forward. Although Dauntless does not appear in , they are mentioned by Nazbi, who claims that they have grown so big that he lacks the budget to feed them. As a result, he has begun searching for treasure throughout Hyrule so that he will be able to buy Carrots for Dauntless. After calling himself a "dauntless adventurer", Nazbi clarifies that he should not be confused with Dauntless.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Daval Peak is located on top of Mount Granajh in the Gerudo Highlands. It is the smaller of two peaks located on the mountain, and it can be found at its southern end. A Pedestal is affixed to the Peak's northern side. Due to Daval Peak being part of a Freezing Climate, Link will require at least two levels of Cold Resistance in order to traverse it without taking damage. According to the Mountain Peak Log, an unnamed individual attempted to use the Pedestal on Daval Peak to reveal an Ancient Shrine in the past. However, they were unable to achieve their goal, and they were forced to leave Mount Granajh after running out of rations. During the "Secret of the Snowy Peaks" Shrine Quest, Link must cast the shadow from either a Cryonis block or a Snowball onto Daval Peak's Pedestal. Doing this will cause Suma Sahma Shrine to rise from the ground on Mount Granajh. A Treasure Chest can be found on the southern end of Daval Peak. When Link opens the Chest, he will receive a Purple Rupee. Creatures Materials

are recurring Items in . Daybreakers go unnamed in . Location and Uses Daybreakers are the most durable and protective variant of the Gerudo Shield, adorned with a jeweled Crest of the Gerudo. Paired with Scimitars of the Seven, they make the Champion's Arms. They were designed to be both lightweight and durable, and the gold used to make them is handpicked to ensure this. They belong to the Gerudo Gear equipment archetype. Before the Great Calamity, a Daybreaker was beloved by the Gerudo Champion Urbosa. Both it and her Scimiat of the Seven were made by a Gerudo jeweler. During the EX Recovered Memory "Champion Urbosa's Song", Urbosa can be seen performing a Parry with her Daybreaker. After Urbosa's death, her Daybreaker and Scimitar became treasures of the Gerudo. After defeating Thunderblight Ganon and calming Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Riju will offer Link both pieces. She believes it is right he should have them, as he was friends with Urbosa. Both Items can be found in Stone Chests behind Riju's Throne in the Royal Palace of Gerudo Town. If either Item breaks, Buliara will offer to remake them for Link. To create a Daybreaker, she needs one Diamond, five pieces of Flint, and a Gerudo Shield. Selmie will take note of a Daybreaker if Link has one equipped when he speaks to her. She will ask if she is dreaming, explaining that she has wanted a Daybreaker so badly that she has seen it in her dreams. Being made of metal, Daybreakers will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. They will also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can still be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune if it happens. In addition, they will not burn like wooden Shields when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Daybreakers reappear in . They are part of the Arms of the Seven alongside Scimitars of the Seven, which can only be created by select individuals. These Weapons form a bond with their owners, which is only broken when they are permanently lost. According to Isha, an ancestor of hers was responsible for making Urbosa's Daybreaker and Scimitar of the Seven. Additionally, the Sage of Lightning Ardi can be seen wielding her own Daybreaker and Scimitar in flashbacks to the Era of Foundation's Imprisoning War. During the Side Quest "Pride of the Gerudo", Isha chooses to make a Daybreaker and Scimitar of the Seven for Link. She tasks Link with gathering the supplies she needs to make them, which is his responsibility as the person who will wield the Arms of the Seven. To make a Daybreaker, Isha needs one Diamond, five pieces of Flint, and a Gerudo Shield. Once Link has brought her all of the Materials, Isha proceeds to make the Daybreaker and Scimitar for him. When she is done, she gives them to him, saying they are a representation of the gratitude the Gerudo feel for him. She

five pieces of Flint, and a Gerudo Shield. Once Link has brought her all of the Materials, Isha proceeds to make the Daybreaker and Scimitar for him. When she is done, she gives them to him, saying they are a representation of the gratitude the Gerudo feel for him. She also offers to make a new Daybreaker for Link if his ever breaks. However, she will refuse to do so if his Daybreaker can still be recovered, as his bond with it has not been broken. Whenever Isha makes a Daybreaker for Link, she comments on its vibrant colors and her pride in her own work. Other Appearances Daybreakers are wielded by Urbosa in conjunction with Scimitars of the Seven, which she uses to defend herself against frontal attacks. During several Narrations and Movies, a Daybreaker is featured as Urbosa's default Shield. Ardi uses a Daybreaker alongside the Scimitar of the Seven in battle.

is a recurring character in . Biography Dayto is a Hylian traveler who can be found walking the Mountain Road from Foothill Stable and through the Maw of Death Mountain before heading back. At Foothill Stable, he sits at the table inside, where he asserts that he does not need to make a choice about whether he goes east or west. He carries a Hunter's Shield and a Traveler's Sword. Dayto is a very indecisive man who cannot decide on what he wants to do. He struggles with whether he should check his map, his method of travel, and whether he can obtain a Fireproof Elixir. He looks back on his past choices occasionally and wonders whether he made the right decisions. One of Dayto's many worries is whether he should traverse Death Mountain. If there are other people up there, though, he believes he could sell to them. He is unsure if he should try to withstand the heat, since he will end up sweating either way. Dayto is also unsure of when to end his journey. At the end of the Maw of Death Mountain, he asks himself whether he should fight the Enemies ahead or flee. He also debates whether to continue, quit, or take a nap. During the night, Dayto struggles with whether or not he should sleep. Even then, he has difficulties choosing a spot to rest. Dayto is troubled by the current state of Hyrule, calling it bleak and noting the cause of his worries cease when he takes a break. He can only find respite when it is Raining, and he asks not to be bothered during this time. If Link saves Dayto from Monsters, he initially has difficulty believing the danger is over. He's scared of Monsters, even describing himself as drenched with sweat after seeing Monsters. He will give the hero Tough Poultry Curry and Rupees as thanks. Along his journey, he encounters the Guardian Stalker by Gero Pond, which he runs from in terror. Dayto now works for YunoboCo. He can be found on the first floor of YunoboCo HQ selling the Flamebreaker Armor. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring character in . Biography Daz is a Korok that runs the General Shoppe, a General Store located in the Great Deku Tree's Navel in the Korok Forest. He gathers his wares himself, from both within and outside the Forest. When asked, Daz explains that the General Shoppe sells Arrows and Foods that he thought would be useful to Link. He recommends using Shock Arrows while it's raining to deal extra damage to enemies. In addition to selling his wares, Daz will purchase Items from Link. He asks Link to sell whatever he doesn't need, since he enjoys seeing Items from outside of the Korok Forest. He's very pleased to see Link's Inventory. Daz is grateful when Link sells to him, occasionally demanding more Items.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Dazzlefruits are Materials that grow on the Sky Islands, as well as from bushes on Fallen Debris from the Sky. They can be manipulated with the Ultrahand and Fuse Ancient Powers. Throwing them or Fusing them to and firing Arrows creates a flash of blinding Light that temporarily disorients nearby Enemies. They are ineffective on Enemies without Eyes, such as Evermeans and Like Likes. When set off, they will instantly defeat any Stalkoblins, Stalizalfos, and Stalmoblins in a small area. Dazzlefruits can also be used to trigger Light Switches if enough are broken at once, or to make Yellow Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop. Dazzlefruits do not attract Lightning nor conduct Electricity. When Fused to a Weapon or Shield, a Dazzlefruit will be consumed after only one use unless it is Fused to a Weapon that is part of the Korok Gear, in which case it can be used continuously. Like other Fruits, they can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Dazzlefruits are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

is a recurring location in . It is a tall, often volcanic mountain that can be found in Hyrule, the Dark World, and Lorule. Features and Overview In , Death Mountain is the northern region of Hyrule. It is a large sprawling expanse of rock covering the northern border of the map. The mountain range is usually home to some of the stronger enemies, such as Lynels, who are said to be the guardians of the Mountain. Occasionally, Boulders will fall from the hills. The Mountain also has a few streams and ponds that are home to Zoras. Death Mountain also has two distinctive landmarks. The first being Lost Hills, a mountainous counterpart of the maze-like Lost Woods. Beyond this maze is the fifth Labyrinth, Level 5, in the First Quest. The mountain also contains Spectacle Rock, which houses Level-9 and the location of Ganon. This Dungeon is a huge labyrinth found underneath the Mountain itself. It is the largest Dungeon in the game and is filled with lava pools and a large number of enemies such as Lanmola and Wizzrobes. Princess Zelda is held captive deep inside until Link rescues her. Areas In , Death Mountain can be found south of Western Hyrule. This area, located south of the Water Town of Saria, is comprised of many different tunnels that house many enemies, such as Dairas, several of which lead to dead ends if the wrong paths are taken. A few tunnels also have pools of lava, usually with a bridge suspended above them. Only a few paths lead to the southern region of Hyrule, where Link can find the Hammer hidden in a cave beneath Spectacle Rock. Areas Enemies In , Death Mountain can be found on the northern border of Hyrule. It is home to many Deadrocks and numerous caves filled with Keese and Mini-Moldorms among other enemies. At the very peak of mountain, the Tower of Hera can be found beyond Spectacle Rock. Without traveling to the Dark World, Link cannot scale this peak to reach the dungeon and the final Pendant of Virtue. Here, the hero also meets the Lost Old Man, and by saving him, he is able to start the game from his hideout in the Mountain Cave. Later on in his quest, he is able to obtain the Ether Medallion from a Hylian Monolith and gain access to the Secret Store. Death Mountain is covered by constantly-tumbling boulders. Its Dark World counterpart is home to Turtle Rock and Ganon's Tower, found where the Tower of Hera is in the Light World. Ganon's Tower itself is guarded by Lynels. The Dark World counterpart is volcanic, with rocks constantly dripping with magma. The Cane of Byrna can also be found hidden in its caves. Areas In , Death Mountain is home to the Gorons, a peaceful race who eat rocks and are exceptionally good at forging blades. It can only be reached via a gate in Kakariko Village. Sticking to the Gorons' reputation as skilled metalsmiths, metal structures have been erected around the face of the mountain to provide access to areas which are otherwise unreachable. The Gorons themselves can give each other and Link a leg-up to unscalable surfaces. The Gorons also have a mine inside the volcanic interior of the mountain, where materials are mined and transported with the assistance of magnetic cranes. Link eventually reaches the main area of Death Mountain, where a giant rock from the mountain's volcano falls. After successfully evading the Gorons and using them to launch himself higher up the mountain, Link enters the Gorons' home. There, he is informed by Gor Coron that he will not allow him to enter the Goron Mines, which are sacred to the Gorons, unless he beats him in a match of sumo. Successfully defeating the Goron Elder allows Link to enter the mines and obtain the second Fused Shadow, saving Darbus and obtaining the Gorons' respect along the way. saving Darbus and obtaining the Gorons' respect along the way. Spectacle Rock is now near the Tower of Hera. As the Dark World is not present in , going through it is not necessary to reach the Tower of Hera. The cave system on the eastern side of Death Mountain is complex, containing several moving platforms that Link must fall on in order to reach the exits. One of the exits leads to Rosso's Ore Mine, which contains a portal to Lorule. Lorule has its own Death Mountain that is not an active volcano. It is covered in snow, thus many of the enemies adapted ice-themed powers. The cave system of Lorule's Death Mountain contains similar jumping puzzles in the eastern section. This version is split in half, with one half containing the Treacherous Tower, and the other half containing the Ice Ruins. Areas In , Death Mountain is a an enormous volcanic mountain in eastern Eldin. It is surrounded by a large moat of lava known as Death Caldera, which flows into other parts of Eldin as rivers and forms smaller bodies of lava. The Bridge of Eldin is the only means of crossing the moat. Death Mountain has a higher temperature than the rest of Eldin, requiring Link to possess two levels of Flame Guard in order to explore the Mountain without being lit aflame and taking damage. Link can acquire enough Flame Guard either by wearing at least two pieces of Flamebreaker Armor or wearing one piece and using a Fireproof Elixir. The Divine Beast Vah Rudania walks along the side of Death Mountain, causing its eruptions to worsen. Bludo of the Gorons, along with Yunobo's help, use Cannons stationed at the mountain to drive away Vah Rudania, but it always returns. Bludo had also raised the Bridge of Eldin to prevent Vah Rudania from crossing over, thereby making the Bridge and Death Mountain inaccessible until Link progresses in the "Divine Beast Vah Rudania" Main Quest. After Link defeats Fireblight Ganon and frees Vah Rudania, the Divine Beast climbs to the Death Mountain Summit, where it takes aim at Hyrule Castle. Climates Areas Death Mountain has become dormant, causing the Lava flows that were present in to solidify and the surrounding terrain to become safe to travel without Flame Guard. However, some of its Caves still feature Scorching Climates. Its Crater is now a Chasm leading to the Death Mountain Depths, in addition to being the location where Link and Yunobo battle Moragia. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Death Mountain Chasm is a Chasm that opened on top of the Death Mountain Summit at the peak of Death Mountain when the Upheaval began. It connects directly to the Death Mountain Depths below. When the Death Mountain Chasm first appeared, Yunobo went to investigate it to ensure Death Mountain would not erupt again. While he was there, he encountered a Phantom Ganon disguised as Zelda, who gave him the Weird Mask to wear. After Link frees Yunobo from the Weird Mask's influence during the "Yunobo of Goron City" Main Quest, they decide to investigate the Chasm for signs of Zelda. When they approach the Chasm, they catch sight of the impostor Zelda again. However, they are interrupted by Moragia rising from within the Death Mountain Crater, which they must defeat before proceeding. Afterwards, Yunobo becomes concerned that Zelda fell through the Death Mountain Chasm, and so he beckons Link to join him as he jumps into the Death Mountain Depths. Enemies

The is a recurring location in . The Death Mountain Crater goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Death Mountain Crater is the heart of Death Mountain. The Crater is accessible from the top of Death Mountain, or through an ancient Goron pathway from Darunia's room in Goron City. The heat of the crater is too intense to be in for very long unless the Goron Tunic is being worn. Without this tunic, Link only has a limited amount of time to stay in the crater, otherwise he will burst into flames and die as soon as the timer runs out. The amount of time Link can remain in the crater is dependent upon how many Heart Containers Link possesses. Also as a child link, the bridge to Fire Temple is blocked by three gray rocks, that he cannot destroy with bombs alone. After Link receives the Goron Tunic from Darunia's son and enters Death Mountain Crater for the first time, Sheik will appear in front of him and teach Link the Bolero of Fire, which allows him to immediately transport back to the crater's Triforce Warp at any given time. The Bolero of Fire is needed to access the middle portion of the crater as young Link. The Great Fairy of Wisdom also resides in the Great Fairy Fountain on the western portion of the volcanic area, but its entrance is blocked by giant Boulders that can only be removed with the Megaton Hammer. Once Link enters the fountain, he meets the Great Fairy within it who doubles his Magic Meter. The Death Mountain Crater contains Divine Beast Vah Rudania and several streams of Lava pooling into the center of the Crater. After Link defeats Fireblight Ganon, Divine Beast Vah Rudania climbs out of it. Areas Enemies Death Mountain Crater is the interior of Death Mountain. The Lava in the Crater has solidified into large streams of volcanic rock following the end of Death Mountain's eruption. During the Upheaval, a haze of Gloom began rising through the Crater from the Death Mountain Depths. The Crater is initially covered in a layer of rock with patches of Gloom on it. During the "Yunobo of Goron City" Main Quest, after Yunobo's Weird Mask is shattered, the Goron directs Link to Death Mountain to look for Zelda after he remembers her giving him the Mask when he went to investigate the Gloom spouting from the Crater. When they arrive at the Summit, they see what appears to be Zelda entering the Chasm and Moragia erupts out to block the Crater. Once Moragia is defeated, the surface of the Death Mountain Crater is shown to have been destroyed, revealing the Death Mountain Chasm in its place. Passing through the Chasm allows the two to enter the Death Mountain Depths. Areas Enemies Bosses

The , also known as the Summit of Death Mountain, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Death Mountain Summit is the top of Death Mountain. Travelers are advised to stay away from the Summit due to how dangerous it is. The Death Mountain Summit leads into the Death Mountain Crater and houses a Great Fairy's Fountain where Link can obtain the Spin Attack from the Great Fairy of Power. In the Child Era, Link can speak to Kaepora Gaebora atop a Sign, who offers to bring him down the Mountain. If Link accepts, Kaepora Gaebora will drop him on the roof of Impa's House in Kakariko Village. In the Adult Era, Link can find Biggoron here. By showing Biggoron the Broken Goron's Sword, Link can receive the Prescription. Later, Link can deliver the prescribed World's Finest Eye Drops in exchange for a Claim Check. After waiting for three days, Link can exchange the Claim Check for Biggoron's Sword. Enemies Death Mountain Summit is the highest point of Death Mountain. Its location is marked by a Sign denoting it as one of Hyrule's one hundred famous mountains. After Link has defeated Fireblight Ganon and activated Divine Beast Vah Rudania's Main Control Unit, Daruk operates Vah Rudania to climb up to the Summit and take aim at Hyrule Castle. From there on, the Summit becomes a new Travel point via Vah Rudania's icon on the Map. Link will not be able to approach Vah Rudania, however, due to it being too dangerous. Bohrin states that the Gorons used to mine at the Summit, but were forced to relocate to the Southern Mine when Vah Rudania began launching Magma Bombs.

After Zelda falls and is transported through Time, Link is brought to the Great Sky Island's Room of Awakening by Rauru, who also transports the now Decayed Master Sword and transplants his Right Arm onto Link to save him from the corruption of Darkness. It is necessary to use the Sword to cut Vines in the doorways of the Room of Awakening. As Link approaches it, the Decayed Master Sword speaks to him and instructs him to put it into the sphere of light. Upon Link doing so, it is transported to the distant past just after the conclusion of the Imprisoning War to find itself in Zelda's hands. Realizing what she must do to heal the Sword, Zelda swallows her Secret Stone and transforms into the Light Dragon while holding the Sword, embedding it within herself as she carries it through the millennia. With her sacred powers, she infuses the blade with even more strength so that it will not break against the Demon King's attacks.

are Items in . Overview Decayed Weapons are Weapons that have been weakened as a result of the Upheaval. They exhibit reduced durability, lower attack power and general stats compared to their Intact counterparts. Many of the residents of Hyrule have been attaching Monster Parts to the ends of Decayed Weapons so they can continue to use them. Decay affects most handheld Weapons, including One-Handed Weapons, Two-Handed Weapons, and Spears. A majority of the Weapons encountered on the Surface are decayed. The exceptions to this are Boulder Breakers, Lightscale Tridents, and Scimitars of the Seven, including those used by the Sages. In addition to these, one Intact Eightfold Blade✨ can be found on the Surface. Shields and Bows are not susceptible to decay.

, also known as , is a recurring mechanic in . Overview In , Link can acquire two rings that enhance his defensive abilities: 14px The Blue Ring reduces damage Link takes in half and turns Link's tunic blue. Link can find it beneath an Armos in the overworld or buy it from the Merchant for 250 Rupees. 14px The Red Ring reduces damage to a quarter of its original amount and turns Link's tunic red. It is found in Level-9. 20px|left In , Link can use the Shield Spell to enhance his defense, reducing the damage he takes by half. Link's tunic turns red, and the effect of the spell will wear off as soon as Link leaves to another area. It can be found in Rauru Town. In addition, every time Link's life level goes up via experience points, it will decrease the damage he takes permanently. In , Link's defense is enhanced by his tunics. left The Blue Mail reduces the damage taken from enemies by 1/2. It is found in the Ice Palace. left The Red Mail reduces the damage taken from enemies by 1/4. It is found in Ganon's Tower. left|Guardian Acorn Once Link defeats twelve enemies without being hit, the twelfth will drop a Guardian Acorn, which temporarily doubles Link's defense. left In , after completing the Color Dungeon, Link can choose either the Blue Clothes, or the Red Clothes as a reward. The Red Tunic doubles attack power, while the Blue Tunic halves the damage Link takes. In , Link's Defensive Power can be enhanced by the Great Fairy of Courage who lives in a hidden cave by Ganon's Castle in Link's Adult time. The entrance is blocked by a Monolith which can only be removed by the use of the Golden Gauntlets. In , if Link is able to collect all 15 Stray Fairies in the Great Bay Temple and return them to the Fairy's Fountain on the Zora Cape, the Great Fairy of Courage rewards him with enhanced Defense. In , if Link collects 10 or 20 Wisdom Gems, he can use them to power up the Spirit of Wisdom which when equipped increases his defense. In , Link can purchase Guardian Potions from the Potion Shop at the Bazaar. This Potion, when drunk, halves the damage dealt to Link by half for three minutes. By upgrading it to the Guardian Potion +, the Potion will make Link completely invincible for three minutes. In , like in , Link's Defense is enhanced by his tunics. The Blue Mail is found in the Swamp Palace. The Red Mail is found in Lorule Castle. Defense in reduces the damage that Link takes from Enemy attacks. It is calculated as the raw damage value subtracted by the defense rating, in units of a quarter Heart. Damage cannot be reduced to less than a quarter Heart.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Deku Tree Chasm is a Chasm that opened within the Great Deku Tree's Navel in Korok Forest when the Upheaval began. It leads to an isolated portion of Korok Grove in the Great Hyrule Forest Depths. When Link first arrives in Korok Forest, he will find the Great Deku Tree suffering from the effects of the Deku Tree Chasm's Gloom. At the bottom of the Chasm, he will find a mass of Gloom Spawn, which will proceed to attack him. After they have been defeated, a Phantom Ganon will appear to fight him as well. Following their fight, the Gloom will disappear from the Deku Tree Chasm, and a group of Koroks fly down to thank Link for saving the Great Deku Tree. At the bottom of the Chasm is an alcove that Link can Ascend through to return to Korok Forest.

is a recurring character in . Biography Deltan is a Gerudo who can be found depressed and hunched over at a table in The Noble Canteen in Gerudo Town. She is a graduate of Ashai's Cooking Class. Presumably intoxicated from drinking, Deltan mutters about "stupid voe" to herself if Link tries to speak to her. She's attempted to charm some voe with her newfound knowledge, yet all her attempts proved unsuccessful. Deltan complains about a man who told her that he is engaged but claims that she cannot be angry about it. She also complains about a man who only told her that he likes to cook after she took Ashai's Cooking class. Another man said that he does not like girls twice his height, which Deltan is confused by since she's only eight feet tall. Deltan grew her hair out because a man told her he liked long hair, but he then informed her that he liked short hair.

The is the final Boss in . It is the form attained by Demon King Ganondorf when, in a final attempt to destroy Link, he sacrifices himself by swallowing his Secret Stone of Darkness to irreversibly transform into a Dragon. By permanently losing his own self through the transformation, no trace of Ganondorf's original form remains. Biography Link defeats Demon King Ganondorf in Gloom's Origin, Beneath Hyrule Castle. In a last, desperate attempt to survive, Ganondorf declares that he will sacrifice himself to destroy Link, losing his body and mind in the process. He wrenches the Sacred Stone embedded in his forehead and swallows it, causing a huge explosion as he transforms into a Dragon. After the transformation, the dragon swoops down to pick up Link and launches itself upward through the ceiling, crashing through the earth as it makes its way to the Surface. Emerging from the Hyrule Castle Chasm, it causes considerable damage to the castle itself as it flies high up in the Central Hyrule Sky. The Light Dragon suddenly appears to try and intercept the the Demon Dragon, and rescues Link as he falls from it during the confrontation. If Link has not yet obtained the Master Sword, he will notice it embedded in the head of the Light Dragon and automatically retrieve it to use during the final battle. Characteristics The Demon Dragon is a large Dragon with jet-black scales immune to all attacks, red spike protrusions in its back, and oozing with Gloom. Along its back are also several pits in its scales containing vulnerable, glowing pustules of Gloom with eyes. To defeat the dragon, Link must attack these pustules with the Master Sword. The Light Dragon supports Link during the battle by allowing him to ride it through the Sky to gain altitude for skydiving and gliding onto the Demon Dragon. Once Link rises above the Demon Dragon's position, it will look upwards and spew large balls of Gloom toward the hero. Link will sustain Gloom damage if he touches any part of the Demon Dragon, other than the pits along his back, or the dragon's head. During the battle the Light Dragon will attempt to quickly swoop in to catch Link as he falls, though it's possible for it to miss him. Link is unable to fall to the surface however, as if he falls too low a cutscene will play where the Light Dragon catches him regardless of their distance from one another. When all of the Gloom pustules on the Demon Dragon's back are destroyed, Link must deliver a final killing blow to the Secret Stone of Darkness embedded in the Demon Dragon's head, destroying both the Secret Stone and the Dragon in the process.

The Demon King's Army is a Boss in . Characteristics The Demon King's Army is a large group of Gloom-Wreathed Monsters. They can first be seen during "The Demon King's Army" Memory, which plays when Link and the Sages encounter Demon King Ganondorf in Hyrule Castle. In the ancient past, the Demon King can be heard commanding his Army to attack Hyrule and its citizens. Their invasion can be seen on one of the murals in the Forgotten Foundation. As part of the "Destroy Ganondorf" Main Quest, Link encounters the Demon King's Army at Gloom's Lair, which starts the War in the Depths of Hyrule. The Demon King's Army takes up the first four waves of the War. If Link has awakened any of the Sages, they will appear to help him fight against the Army. Waves

are Items in . Location and Uses Demon King's Bows are dropped by Phantom Ganons when they are defeated. Their attack power increases by two for every Heart in Link's maximum Hearts, up to 60 damage. Any Hearts under the effects of Gloom damage are not counted towards this maximum. For example, if Link has a total of 20 Hearts, with five of them Gloom damaged, the attack power of a Demon King's Bow would be 30. Demon King Ganondorf also uses this Bow during the final battle at Gloom's Origin. Demon King's Bows cannot be directly repaired by or receive Weapon Bonuses from Rock Octoroks.

Demon King Ganondorf is a recurring Boss in . Biography Demon King Ganondorf is the form assumed by Ganondorf after obtaining his Secret Stone, stolen from Sonia. After becoming the Demon King, he created a swarm of Monsters and attacked Hyrule Kingdom and its allies, which started the Imprisoning War. At the end of the War, the Six Sages confronted him. However, Ganondorf's overwhelming power made the Sage of Wind unable to slip past his defenses, the Sage of Fire's strongest blows unable to break him, the Sage of Water's strongest defenses unable to stop his attacks, and he endured the Sage of Lightning's Lightning strikes. After Mineru fell ill to Ganondorf's Gloom and the rest of the Six Sages were exhausted, Ganondorf was caught off-guard by King Rauru, who sacrificed himself to seal the Demon King in the Imprisoning Chamber, binding his heart and stealing his Magic. Ganondorf was intrigued of the coming of Link, wielder of the Sword that Seals the Darkness who Rauru spoke of shortly before the seal's Magic was complete. After the seal was cast, Hyrule Castle was built to keep the Imprisoning Chamber undisturbed. Although Ganondorf remained sealed Beneath Hyrule Castle, a form of Ganon known as Calamity Ganon appeared to plague Hyrule multiple times. According to King Rhoam and Impa, Calamity Ganon was originally the "Demon King" born in the distant past who resurrected and transformed into a being made of pure Malice and hatred manifest. Beyond this potential connection to a Demon King from ancient times, the exact nature of the relationship between the imprisoned Ganondorf and Calamity Ganon as distinct entities is unclear. After thousands of years, the seal's Magic weakened due to the damage done to Hyrule Castle from the most recent Great Calamity. This led to Ganondorf's power steadily increasing. His Gloom began to seep from Beneath Hyrule Castle, making people who came across it sick. Zelda and Link went to investigate the Gloom and discovered Ganondorf's mummified body. When they approached the body, Rauru's Right Arm and Secret Stone fell down, awakening Ganondorf. He injures Link's Right Arm and shatters the Master Sword with his Gloom. He is disappointed by the capabilities of the Master Sword, Zelda, and Link and uses his Gloom to cause an Upheaval in Hyrule. As Hyrule Castle rises, the platform he was sealed in begins to collapse, making him fall to the bottom of the Depths of Hyrule. He uses a Phantom Ganon disguised as Zelda to send several Hyruleans into confusion and mislead Link throughout his journey. Four of his Servants are also sent to cause the Regional Phenomena. After Link clears the four Temples, Ganondorf uses his Phantom Ganon disguised as Zelda once more to lead Link into Hyrule Castle's Sanctum, where Ganondorf reveals the true form of the impostor Zelda and sends Phantom Ganon to end Link's life. After Link defeats Phantom Ganon, Ganondorf notices that there is more to Link's powers than Rauru's Right Arm has gifted, he dissolves

Zelda once more to lead Link into Hyrule Castle's Sanctum, where Ganondorf reveals the true form of the impostor Zelda and sends Phantom Ganon to end Link's life. After Link defeats Phantom Ganon, Ganondorf notices that there is more to Link's powers than Rauru's Right Arm has gifted, he dissolves Phantom Ganon into tendrils of Gloom but the Six Sages defend Link from them. Ganondorf is surprised that the Six Sages don't recognize him, noting that there's limits to the knowledge that Secret Stones give. He gives the Six Sages and Link a vision of him and his army from the past, saying that the world will be like this once more when his power will be restored. He then tells them that they can only await the inevitable end and vanishes. He later uses his Gloom to possess a Construct in the Spirit Temple to use it as a pawn against Link and Mineru. Upon meeting Link in Gloom's Origin in the Central Hyrule Depths after the hero faced his Army within Gloom's Lair, Ganondorf expresses his disappointment that the world is not yet covered in Darkness and that those he deems as weak still remain. He then slams his fist into the ground, using his Gloom to transform into a more healthy version of himself. He vows to reshape the world and act as its uncontested king. After battling Link in his Gerudo form, Ganondorf revels in the feeling of battle without even using his full power. He further envelops himself in Gloom and takes his second, demonic form, taunting Link in certainty that he will kill him. When the Demon King's second form is ultimately defeated by Link, he refuses to give up his goal of ruling the world in Darkness and swallows his Secret Stone, becoming the Demon Dragon. Characteristics First Form thumb|right|320px|Link confronting Demon King Ganondorf In his first phase, Demon King Ganondorf takes on his original Gerudo form. Similar to Phantom Ganon, Demon King Ganondorf wields a variety of Weapon types. He starts out the fight with a Gloom Sword, but during the battle, he can switch his Weapon to a Gloom Spear, Gloom Club or Demon King's Bow. While he is wielding a Gloom Club, Ganondorf is capable of kicking Link with his left foot when Link is close enough. If any of these Weapons hit Link, then his Hearts will be temporarily damaged by Gloom. Two of his attacks can permanently reduce Link's maximum number of Hearts if they connect. Both of these are projectile attacks, one originating from the Gloom Club that spawns three columns of Gloom that travel along the ground, and the other being bursts of Gloom spawned by shots from the Demon King's Bow. If Link has the Master Sword, it can be used to deflect Gloom projectiles, while any other Weapon will be destroyed immediately if they connect with the Gloom. Ganondorf also has the ability to Perfect Dodge, even against Link's Parries. The Demon King is

shots from the Demon King's Bow. If Link has the Master Sword, it can be used to deflect Gloom projectiles, while any other Weapon will be destroyed immediately if they connect with the Gloom. Ganondorf also has the ability to Perfect Dodge, even against Link's Parries. The Demon King is also capable of knocking Arrows away if Link attempts to repeatedly shoot him in the head with a Bow. If Link shoots his bow while airborne, Ganondorf will be unable to avoid his shot. Ganondorf will sometimes berate Link whenever he performs a Perfect Dodge, knocks away Arrows, or deals damage to Link. After Ganondorf's health is depleted, he comments on how he had forgotten the thrill of battle, revealing that he has not expended most of his power. The Demon King then proceeds to use his Secret Stone to transform into the more demonic form that he had during the Imprisoning War, increasing his health to twice the amount he had previously. After the transformation, he threatens to take more than Link's arm. Second Form Demon King Ganondorf, also known as Demon King Ganondorf (2nd Form), is the second phase of the fight. In this phase, he is stronger and faster, and he is accompanied by four Phantom Ganons. If Link has made a vow with a Sage, they will join this part of the battle to fight alongside Link. When his health is reduced by half, he will absorb the Gloom of each Phantom Ganon to increase his strength, before unleashing a wave of Gloom that renders the Sages unconscious. His ability to Perfect Dodge and Flurry Rush have intensified, and he will counter a Perfect Dodge or Parry followed by a Flurry Rush with a Dodge of his own. He also no longer gets stunned when shot by Arrows. He alternates between using Gloom projectiles and dashing towards Link to strike him. Upon the defeat of his second form, Demon King Ganondorf will swallow his Secret Stone and transform into the Demon Dragon, carrying Link into another, final battle in the Sky. Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Dento is a Zora can be found at his workshop, the Hammerhead, which is located in Marot Mart in Zora's Domain. According to the History of the Zora, Part Four, he made the Lightscale Trident for Mipha when she was born, which he maintains in the present day. He has two apprentices, Fronk and Ledo, who he has tasked with making repairs to Zora's Domain. Like all elder Zora, Dento is initially hostile and untrusting towards Link due to the loss of Mipha. When Link speaks to him, Dento is short and curt with his answers. Eventually, his annoyance at Link becomes too much, saying there is no reason for him to be there without the Lightscale Trident. After Divine Beast Vah Ruta is calmed, Dento will be relieved that Mipha can rest in peace. He offers to repair both the Lightscale Trident and the Ceremonial Trident if Link ever breaks them. Repairing the Lightscale Trident costs a Zora Spear, a Diamond, and five pieces of Flint. A new Ceremonial Trident can be made from a Zora Spear and five pieces of Flint.

is a character in . Biography Deon is a Hylian member of the Zonai Survey Team. He can initially be found resting on one of the Beds at the Emergency Shelter at Lookout Landing. When Link first approaches Deon, he is able to recognize him. Link confirms his identity, and Deon notes that his face matches the one on his missing poster. He allows Link to take one of the empty Beds though he suggests staying away from Nappin due to his sleep talking. He explains that Nappin has been sick since he visited a Chasm, even though it has been a while since he returned. If Link asks Deon about the Chasms, he explains that they were created as a result of the Upheaval. The two nearest are the Hyrule Castle Chasm to the north and the Hyrule Field Chasm to the south, but Deon warns that the Depths below them are filled with dangerous Gloom. He then expresses his admiration for Josha, who has been leading the Chasm Research despite her young age. If Link ends their conversation, Deon invites him to make use of the resources in the Emergency Shelter. After the Side Quest "Today's Menu" is completed, Deon will sit near the Cooking Pot in the Emergency Shelter's Kitchen. He will inform Link that Burmano has departed to Hyrule Castle to investigate a new recipe, and he wonders if he should be worried about him.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Deplian Badlands are a barren landscape in the Eldin Mountains range. The Deplian Badlands are littered with dead Trees and volcanic soil, leaving the land unfit to bear any significant vegetation. The Deplian Badlands lead eastward up a slope. At the top of this slope rest some unnamed ruins, which bear several dead Trees and one large, living Tree. Atop the lone Tree is a Pinwheel, which will spawn five Balloons throughout the surrounding ruins when approached. Destroying these Balloons will cause a Korok to appear. Ore Deposits can be found north and south of these ruins. At the base of the slope at Deplian Badlands' eastern border, Link can find a Magnesis-themed Korok puzzle. Completing the puzzle will cause a Korok to appear, who will then grant Link a Korok Seed for finding him. Creatures Enemies

The Depths are a location in . Features and Overview The Depths are a colossal network of caverns extending deep underneath Hyrule. They are accessed via the Chasms present on the surface, which are easily identified by the Gloom surrounding them. The Depths are extremely dark, making items that create light such as Brightbloom Seeds, Giant Brightbloom Seeds, or Lights valuable when exploring them. Additionally, Gloom covers most of the Depths, forcing Link to watch his step or else have his maximum hearts reduced. Alternatively, he can cross it safely if he finds a Stalhorse or builds a vehicle using Ultrahand and the numerous Zonai Devices that can be found at Supply Sites. Lightroots can be found that light up large areas around them and reverse Gloom damage with their Light; activating them will also activate them as Travel Points and reveal their surroundings on the Map. Each Lightroot is located directly beneath a Shrine of Light on the Surface, whose names are s of each other, allowing them to be used as a method of locating Shrines. In addition to the Lightroots, most other major terrain features on the Surface of Hyrule have an equivalent in the Depths: Bodies of Water on the Surface are mirrored by walls stretching to the top of the Depths. Mountains on the Surface are mirrored by Canyons in the Depths. Forests on the Surface are mirrored by Groves in the Depths. Villages on the Surface are mirrored by Abandoned Mines in the Depths. Stables on the Surface have Lynels near their locations in the Depths. Great Goddess Statues on the Surface and in the Sky are mirrored by Bargainer Statues in the Depths. Hot Springs on the Surface are mirrored by Waterfalls of Flowing Lava in the Depths. The Shrine of Resurrection on the Surface is mirrored by the Secret Spring of Revival in the Depths. For the most part, there is no weather in the Depths but some areas require Flame Guard to safely traverse. These can be recognized by the presence of Lava in the environment. Most minor Enemies and Sub-Bosses encountered in the Depths are Gloom-Wreathed, and will temporarily reduce Link's maximum Hearts capacity upon striking him. Unlike from the Gloom in the environment, Gloom Resistance from Armors and Foods will not apply to their effects. Additionally, Gloom-Wreathed Enemies will take an additional 15 damage from the Master Sword. The Depths are home to a number of legendary artifacts, mostly corresponding to previous titles in . The presence of these artifacts is not explained, although they can be found within Zonai-style Stone Chests in Abandoned Mines. Old Maps found on Sky Islands contain the coordinates of these Items. The Depths are also the main source of Zonaite, which is present in large Zonaite Deposits that appear throughout the Depths. The Zonaite can then be brought to Forge Constructs to buy Zonai Charges and Crystallized Charges, or expended to create devices with Autobuild. Poes can also be found in the Depths,

is a character in . Biography Derbos is part of Flaxel's Monster-Control Crew squad who is initially seen in Lookout Landing. He wields a Wooden Shield and a Traveler's Sword. When Link first arrives in Lookout Landing, Derbos can be seen receiving orders about searching Hyrule Castle from Gralens. If Link tries to speak with Derbos before he meets Gralens, he will apologize, claiming that he will be scolded if he does not pay attention. Afterwards, Derbos will remark on how tough Link appears. They are then interrupted by Gralens, who tells Link to meet with Purah. After Link has spoken to Purah, Derbos expresses an interest in having Link teach him about combat.

Deserted Houses, also known as Ruined Houses, are recurring locations in . Features and Overview Ruined Houses are the remains of homes once belonging to Hylians before the return of Calamity Ganon. Due to this, they are most common among ruins in Central Hyrule, though they can also be found among all destroyed Hylian settlements in other Regions. Since their destruction during the Great Calamity, these buildings have fallen into further disrepair, leaving only portions of their walls and foundations. Ruined Houses come in two varieties: wood and stone. Deserted Houses are damaged or destroyed Houses found throughout Hyrule. Some Monsters have constructed Outposts inside of certain Deserted Houses.

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview When Link speaks to Purah after completing "Crisis at Hyrule Castle", "Find the Fifth Sage", and "Recovering the Hero's Sword", she comments how useful it is that the Mineru is helping him and the other Sages fight Demon King Ganondorf. After hearing that Link has found the Master Sword, she is shocked to hear that it was on the head of the Light Dragon. She thanks Link for finding it, reminding him that Zelda sacrificed herself so that it could be restored. She remarks that without the Master Sword, Link does not look like himself. Since Link is ready to face Demon King Ganondorf, Purah declares that they must figure out his location. She discerns that he must be somewhere in the Depths, as Hyrule Castle and anywhere else on the Surface seem unlikely. For more information, she suggests that he speak to Josha, who has been leading Chasm Research. She informs Link that she is relying on him. At this point, the "Destroy Ganondorf" Main Quest will begin. When Link faces Master Kohga at the Abandoned Hebra Mine during the "Master Kohga of the Yiga Clan" Side Adventure, he reveals that he serves Demon King Ganondorf, who is dwelling in the Depths beneath Hyrule Castle. This portion of the Central Hyrule Depths is only accessible through the Hyrule Castle Chasm. There, the first wave of the Demon King's Army will appear as part of the War in the Depths of Hyrule, which consists of several Gloom-Wreathed Bokoblins and Boss Bokoblins that charge towards him. However, they are deterred by a single Arrow shot towards them. Tulin tells Link that he does not need to fight alone as he and the other Sages arrive. He activates his Secret Stone of Wind and continues, saying that they are unstoppable when they fight together. Yunobo's Secret Stone of Fire activates as well, and he claims he will make his ancestors proud by fighting with Link. Sidon activates his own Secret Stone of Water, promising to protect Hyrule alongside Link. Riju's Secret Stone of Lightning is also activated, revealing that since the Gerudo owe him, she is here to help him as well. Lastly, Mineru activates her Secret Stone of Spirit, vowing to atone for her past failure during the Imprisoning War by defeating Demon King Ganondorf now. All five Sages gather behind Link, drawing their Weapons. As Link and the Sages fight the Demon King's Army, waves consists of Gloom-Wreathed Lizalfos, Gibdos, and Moblins will appear in succession. He is disappointed that he has yet to destroy the world, and he believes that since Link is fighting for peace, he in an unworthy opponent. The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Deya Village Ruins are the half-sunken remains of Deya Village, a village that once existed in West Necluda. They are found in the northern portion of Deya Lake, and they are bordered by the Hills of Baumer to the north and west. The Deya Village Ruins are set mostly on marshland, with little vegetation remaining. A Monster Stronghold can be found among the Ruined Houses along the hill to the south. A Barrel containing a Chuchu can be found inside a Ruined House. Several Busted Wagons litter the Deya Village Ruins, which can be searched for Materials. A Stone Talus rests in the northern section of the Deya Village Ruins. In Downloadable Content pack, Misko's EX Journal 2 can be found under a collapsed roof in one of the easternmost Ruined House. The Journal contains the locations for six priceless relics stolen from Hyrule Castle by Misko. The relics are linked to four Side Quests: "EX Treasure: Merchant Hood", "EX Treasure: Garb of Winds", "EX Treasure: Usurper King", and "EX Treasure: Dark Armor". When set as Link's objective, all four Side Quests will mark the Journal's location on the Sheikah Slate's Map until Link reads the relevant page of the Journal. The is a recurring location in . The Deya Village Ruins Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Deya Village Ruins Well is a stout stone Well, located near a Ruined House on an island in the Deya Village Ruins. It has no roof, and an Iron is chained to its base. Before the Great Calamity, it was part of Deya Village. Equipment Korok Seeds The Deya Village Ruins Well returns in , still being part of West Necluda. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Diamond Circlets are a type of Circlet Accessory that serve as head Armor. One can be found inside a Treasure Chest located in a chamber under the Lomei Labyrinth Island. Once obtained, all of the Decayed Guardians inside the chamber will activate. Link can also purchase Diamond Circlets in the Starlight Memories Jewelry Shop at Gerudo Town for 1,500 Rupees and three Diamonds. When worn, Diamond Circlets provide one level of Guardian Resist Up. They also boasts a hidden stat of increasing damage done by Ancient Soldier Gear and Guardian Gear by 20%. Diamond Circlets can be enhanced by a Great Fairy at a Great Fairy Fountain. However, they cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Enhancing Enhancing Other Appearances The Diamond Circlet is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and it is obtained by completing the Challenge "Hunting for Gemstones". Unlike most other pieces of Attire, it cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop.

The , also known as Digdogg Bridge, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Digdogg Suspension Bridge is a bridge spanning the Regencia River, connecting the Three-Way Intersection in Hyrule Field with the Gerudo Canyon Pass in the Gerudo Highlands Beneath the Bridge, Link can find the Dah Kaso Shrine and a Raft. A Traveler can occasionally be seen walking along the Digdogg Suspension Bridge. If spoken to, they will reveal themselves as a Yiga Footsoldier and attack Link. Additionally, a Blue Hinox sleeps at the center of the Bridge. It wears a single wooden brace around one of its ankles, but this can be burned away with Fire. In Master Mode, it is replaced with a Black Hinox. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Treasure Chests Korok Seeds Due to the presence of the Massive Zonai Ruin at the entrance to the Gerudo Canyon Pass, the Digdogg Suspension Bridge has become a base of operations for the Zonai Survey Team. A Mini Stable run by Pirou has also been established along the Bridge. A Device Dispenser that produces Zonai Capsules sits on top of a large piece of Fallen Debris on the south side of the Water. Areas Device Dispenser Materials Other Appearances As part of the Quest "The Lazy Guards", Merchants are scared of crossing the Digdogg Suspension Bridge due to its guards slacking. Once the Warriors provide the guards with gifts, they become motivated to do their jobs, and the Merchants will feel safe to cross the Bridge.

is a recurring character in . Biography Dillie is a Hylian traveler who can be found in the West Barrens of the Gerudo Desert with his friend, Jora. The pair can be found being attack by two Bokoblins. He is grateful if Link saves him, and he gives him a Hearty Durian as a reward. After being saved, Dillie explains that he and Jora are going to Gerudo Town. They have heard it is a city of "foxy ladies" and think that the women will treat them like kings. He asks Link if he is jealous of their plan and warns him not to copy their idea. He then questions what woman would be interested in a "skinny twig" like Link anyway. He also wonders what the women in Gerudo Town do all day and fantasizes about being the only man in the Town. Once Dillie and Jora are saved, they will stand beside each other while scouting out the Desert. Dillie wonders to himself whether they are lost. If Link speaks to Dillie, he asks Jora if he is alright and reminds him that they are headed to Gerudo Town in an attempt to cheer him up. As consolation, he offers to let Jora lead the way, shocking Jora and prompting him to ask when they decided that fact. Exasperated, Dillie hunches over in disappointment and remarks that he has to be kidding. When Link speaks to Jora, he explains that Dillie knows the way out of the Gerudo Desert and to Gerudo Town. However, Dillie reveals that he thought Jora knew the way and was following him, much to Jora's surprise.

is a recurring character in . Biography Dina is a teacher at Funday School in Hyrule Town in , along with her twin Tina. Throughout the game, she stands in front of the School and will not let Link through, citing the important lessons going on inside, such as Hyrulean literature and math. After Link obtains the Water Element from the Temple of Droplets and sees the spirit of Gustaf for the first time, Funday School lets the children out for recess and the building becomes accessible. Dina is a young Gerudo who attends Ashai's classes in Gerudo Town in . She considers all the learning she does to be a pain in a neck but asks Link not tell anyone she said so. One her way to the Cooking Class, she insists that she needs to pay attention this time. She also asks Link to try attending their classes with them. If Link speaks to Dina in the Relationship Classroom before the "Voe and You" class begins, she asks Link for his opinion of her lipstick. Dina then explains that the color of lipstick is important in bringing good luck. If Link asks how the color affects luck, Dina stutters nervously and says that she is learning that next. If Link says it looks good on her, Dina exclaims that she can feel the lipstick working already. During the "Voe and You" class, Ashai asks her students what to do when a "handsome voe" approaches them on the street. Dina is the second to stand up and share her solution, saying that she would enthusiastically greet the man and approach with her hands empty. Ashai praises Dina for her optimistic approach, adding that friendliness is a great way to relax others. Next, Ashai asks her class what they would do if they found an injured man lying on the ground. Once again, Dina stands second, claiming she would make a medicine to treat him with. Ashai considers this a great answer, though she reminds Dina to check for allergies. Ashai's final scenario for her class is what they would do if they're approached by a man whose attention they have sought. Dina states she would try to determine his social standing based on his clothing. Ashai thinks this is a good idea, but she reminds her that people may wear more casual clothes if their good ones are dirty. If Link speaks to Dina while she is attending Ashai's Cooking Class at night, she complains that she is only able to make Dubious Food. If Link asks her about Dubious Food, she explains that adding Insects or Monster Parts when Cooking a Meal causes it to become Dubious Food. She feels that there is nothing dubious about how inedible Dubious Food is. Dina has learned in Class that the quickest way to someone's heart is through their stomach. If Link attempts to read Chef Aurie Taamu, Vol. 2 while Dina is at the Class, she will notice that the

If Link attempts to read Chef Aurie Taamu, Vol. 2 while Dina is at the Class, she will notice that the Book is too high up for him to read and offer to read it for him.

The Dining Hall is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Dining Hall is a spacious room that previously hosted guests of Hyrule Castle. The entrance to the Dining Hall can be found on a break in the main road to the Sanctum just before the Second Gatehouse. On the Dining Hall's northwestern wall stand three wooden doorways, which lead into the Hyrule Castle Corridors. A Campfire and an unlit Cooking Pot can be found on the southern end of the Dining Hall. Numerous Jars, Wooden Boxes, and Barrels can be found along the walls of the Dining Hall. Enemies Equipment Materials The Dining Hall is devoid of life after the Upheaval. There is a lone, unlit Cooking Pot in the southwestern corner of the room and an unlit Campfire nearby. Along the northwestern wall there is a poster with a Recipe for Crunchy Fried Rice using Oil Jar, Hylian Rice, Raw Meat, and a Bird Egg. The grate to the fireplace has been removed and now leads to a small, featureless chamber. Like in , the candles along the walls and on the tables can be lit with a source of Fire, although this does nothing beyond creating light sources. Enemies Equipment

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Dinraal's Claws can be collected from the Dragon Dinraal, who typically flies around the Eldin Mountains and the Tabantha Frontier. Link must shoot its hands with an Arrow. The Claws in question will fall onto the land in the form of light. Dinraal's Claws that are used in a Cooking Pot will make Dubious Food. However, when used with critters, the result will be Elixirs. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Dinraal's Claws are one of the ingredients that can be used to make Crimson Dye. They also count as Monster Parts, which means they can be exchanged for Mon at the Fang and Bone. Dinraal's Claws are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Dinraal's Claws are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: In addition, one Dinraal's Claw is required to complete the Goddess Statue of Power Side Quest.

, also known as Sacred Articles, or Sacred Relics, are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Dinraal's Scales can be collected from the Dragon Dinraal, who typically flies around the Eldin Mountains or Tabantha Frontier. Link can shoot anywhere along the main body that is not the horns, teeth, or claws to receive the Scales. Dinraal's Scale will fall somewhere on the land in the form of a light. Additionally, the first time Link shoots Dinraal, he will always receive this item, regardless of what part he hit. A Scale can also be found in a Treasure Chest in Hyrule Castle. Meals made using Dinraal's Scales will result in Dubious Food. However, if they are Cooked with a critter, the result will be an Elixir. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Crimson Dye. Kilton at the Fang and Bone will also accept them in exchange for Mon. During "The Spring of Power" Shrine Quest, Link will hear a legend about offering a "sacred article" to the Spring of Power. There, Hylia will task Link with retrieving one of Dinraal's Scales and placing it into the Spring. When Link does so, the doorway behind the Goddess Statue will open, revealing Tutsuwa Nima Shrine. is a recurring Dragon Spirit in . Characteristics Dinraal is one of three roaming Dragons in Hyrule, the others being Naydra and Farosh. She can be found roaming the Eldin Region, the Great Hyrule Forest, Akkala, and Hebra. Dinraal guards the Spring of Power. While she cannot be defeated, she does not actively try to harm Link. Despite this, if Link gets too close, he will be seared by the Fire emanating from her body. Link can avoid her Fire by drinking Fireproof Elixirs or wearing the full Fireproof Armor that has been enhanced twice by a Great Fairy. Dinraal will drop different Materials if Link shoots her with a Bow. Depending on what part of Dinraal is hit, she will drop a Shard of Dinraal's Horn, Shard of Dinraal's Fang, Dinraal's Claw or Dinraal's Scale. Dinraal's Scale can be offered at the Spring of Power to unlock a hidden Ancient Shrine. Schedule Note that these times will vary, but the difference between the timestamps are always the same. Dinraal generally appears between 11:00 PM and 5:00 AM.

are recurring mechanics in . Overview Disguises are used by Link to avoid detection among Enemies or hide his identity, allowing him to avoid combat or enter areas that he would not be allowed in otherwise. In , Link can wear a variety of Armors to Disguise himself. By wearing the full Gerudo Outfit, he can enter Gerudo Town without being thrown out. Once he obtains the Thunder Helm, the Sand Boots, or the Snow Boots, he can wear them in place of the Gerudo Veil and Gerudo Sirwal while maintaining the effects of the Disguise. Link can also wear Armor with a Disguise Added Effect or Set Bonus to remain hidden among different types of Enemies, preventing them from attacking him unless he attacks them first. Enemies affected by Link's Disguise will follow him around and study him, making it difficult to perform Sneakstrikes on them. If an Enemy that is not affected by Link's Disguise begins to attack him, Enemies that were fooled by the Disguise will see through it and attack him as well. While using certain Disguise Effects, Link adopts a new idle pose to mimic the Enemy he is disguised as. Much like in , Link can wear different Armors to disguise himself. The Gerudo Outfit is no longer available, but Link can now obtain and wear the Yiga Clan Attire to infiltrate the Yiga Clan Hideout and other strongholds of the Yiga Clan. Once he obtains the Lightning Helm, Link can use it in place of the Yiga Mask without revealing his identity. Many friendly characters will chide Link's poor taste if he wears the Yiga Mask around them, and wearing it within Gerudo Town will result in Link being locked up in the local Jail until he takes it off. Yiga Footsoldiers and Yiga Blademasters will not immediately attack Link while he is wearing this Disguise, but Master Kohga is not fooled by it. Link can wear Armor with a Disguise Added Effect or Set Bonus to prevent certain types of Enemies from attacking him. Disguise Effects will end early if Link attacks an Enemy, or if an Enemy not fooled by the Disguise starts to attack Link. In addition to the special idle poses available in , Link has a new idle pose while wearing the Horriblin Mask.

is a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Dive Through the Ring goes unnamed in . Overview Dive Through the Ring is a variety of Korok Seed Puzzle found on bodies of Water throughout Hyrule. They involve a Circle of plants, such as Lily Pads or seaweed, located below a ledge. When Link dives through this Circle, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. List of Circles A total of one instance of Dive Through the Ring can be found in Akkala. A total of nine instances of Dive Through the Ring can be found in Central Hyrule. A total of three instances of Dive Through the Ring can be found in Eldin. A total of four instances of Dive Through the Ring can be found in Faron. A total of four instances of Dive Through the Ring can be found in Hebra. A total of 14 instances of Dive Through the Ring can be found in Necluda. In , Dive Through the Ring is the only type of Circle-based Korok Seed Puzzle. They can be found on the Surface of Hyrule and on Sky Islands. In some cases, Fallen Debris serves as a ledge hanging over the Circle. As is the case in , when Link dives through a Circle, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed.

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses The Divine Helms are Ancient Technology of the Sheikah. They resemble the Divine Beasts and are obtained by scanning corresponding amiibo figures. There are four kinds of Divine Helms in total: the Vah Medoh Divine Helm which is obtained with the Revali amiibo, the Vah Naboris Divine Helm which is obtained with the Urbosa amiibo, the Vah Rudania Divine Helm which is obtained with the Daruk amiibo, and the Vah Ruta Divine Helm which is obtained with the Mipha amiibo. Each Divine Helm confers the Guardian Resist Up Added Effect as well as a secondary Added Effect to complement traversal in their corresponding region. Cold Resistance is granted by the Vah Medoh Divine Helm, Shock Resistance is given by the Vah Naboris Divine Helm, Flame Guard is granted by the Vah Rudania Divine Helm, and Swim Speed Up is given by the Vah Ruta Divine Helm. These Divine Helms have a Set Bonus compatibility with the Ancient Cuirass and the Ancient Greaves, granting them Ancient Proficiency when all worn together and Enhanced by a Great Fairy. The list of obtainable Divine Helms is as follows: The Divine Helms are Ancient Technology of the Sheikah hidden throughout Hyrule. There are four Divine Helms to be found in total, with surviving records held by their respective cultures. Each Divine Helm has a corresponding Side Quest which can be unlocked after awakening its associated Sage. Ancient equivalents of the Divine Helms were worn by the Sages of Rauru's time. Like the Sheikah Divine Helms, they each resemble their associated Animals. When worn by Link, Divine Helms grant Added Effects and can alter the appearance of their corresponding Sage's Avatar, increasing its base attack power. These Sage Avatars change to wear their ancestral Divine Helms while Link is wearing their associated Sheikah Divine Helm. While not a Divine Helm, this effect can also be seen with Mineru's Construct, whose Zonai Relic changes to match the Zonaite Helm when it is worn.
