Rauru is seen presenting one to Agraston in the Audience Chamber of the Ancient Hyrule Castle. These Divine Helms are granted before their appointments to become Sages, as they are shown wearing these Helms without their corresponding Secret Stones.

is a mechanic in . Overview Once Link slays the Demon Dragon high in the Central Hyrule Sky, his arm is restored to normal and Zelda's Draconification is undone, leaving the pair to fall to the Surface. As Zelda is rendered unconscious by the transformation, Link must catch her as she falls by Diving to Zelda. In doing so, he Grabs her hand, and guides their descent into the Bottomless Pond. Diving to Zelda is distinct from standard Skydiving in that the two can fall for an infinite amount of time; they will never get closer to, or land on, the Surface until Link has successfully Dove to Zelda.

is a recurring character in . Biography Dmitri is a Hylian and the owner of the South Akkala Stable in the Akkala Highlands. He can be found at the front of South Akkala Stable. Dmitri is also the father of Kaifa, Jana, and Gleema. If South Akkala Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Dmitri will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Dmitri explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Dmitri then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Dmitri instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Dmitri suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Dmitri to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Dmitri tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the South Akkala Stable, Dmitri will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Dmitri thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Dmitri will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Dmitri asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that South Akkala Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Dmitri asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Dmitri will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Dmitri insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Dmitri refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Dmitri starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Dmitri gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing

that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Dmitri gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Dmitri gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside South Akkala Stable, Dmitri once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by South Akkala Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Dmitri tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Dmitri wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

The are a recurring location in . The Docks go unnamed in . Features and Overview The Docks are located inside a Cave on the northern end of the grounds of Hyrule Castle. Link can access the Docks via the Hyrule Castle Moat. The pathway out of the Docks leads into the Library. Many Wooden Boxes, Barrels, and Bomb Barrels can be found throughout the Docks. Above the mouth of the Cave is a grassy ledge with a pair of Torches on it. There is a thin path leading up to this ledge on the north side of the Docks. In between the Torches sits a pedestal with a Great Flameblade embedded in it. On the higher level of the Dock, Link can find several lit stationary Torches surrounding a single unlit one. If Link ignites this stationary Torch, Saas Ko'sah Shrine will emerge from the ground nearby. Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment Inhabitants Korok Seeds Treasure Chests As in , the Docks connect Hyrule Castle to the Hyrule Castle Moat in Hyrule Field. Creatures Enemies Equipment Treasure Chests Other Appearances The Docks are part of the Hyrule Castle Stage in . They appear similar to their counterpart, but with fast-flowing Water that has four defeated Guardians partially submerged in it. Broken Barrels and intact Wooden Boxes sit inside the Cave, and some of the Braziers have been broken, lighting parts of the ground on Fire. The ledge at the entrance is inaccessible and covered in green Grass. The upper layer remains mostly the same apart from two broken Braziers. During the "Calamity Strikes" Scenario, a Warrior and Zelda arrive in the Docks through the Hidden Passage in the Sanctum mid-Calamity, following the fleeing King Rhoam. After Zelda reaches the Hyrule Castle Corridors through the Library, two of the four inactive Guardians in the upper layer of the Docks activate to pursue her. Once these two are defeated, the remaining Guardians activate as well.

is a recurring character in . Biography Domidak can be found at the Dueling Peaks Stable with his twin brother, Prissen. Domidak considers himself a premiere treasure hunter, and is often praised for his skills by his younger brother. Both he and Prissen are part of the Treasure-Hunting Brothers. When Link approaches them, he will find that the two of them are busy discussing a bandit by the name of Misko and the location of their supposed treasure. However, Domidak will quiet his brother when he notices Link standing there. As Prissen explains who they are, Domidak immediately chides him for giving out information. Domidak is quick to dismiss Link and any attempt at conversation. Should Link choose to drop the subject, Domidak will state that Misko's treasure is for seasoned treasure hunters and promptly rules Link out of the competition. He then mutters to himself that he is grateful for the lack of rivals. If Link is persistent, Domidak will give up his attempts to pass off Prissen's slip as rambling. When Prissen suggests telling Link the riddle they found to get him to leave, Domidak agrees. Domidak explains that they are seeking the treasure of Misko, a legendary bandit. However, Domidak refuses to tell more without proper compensation and requires 100 Rupees, though he claims the price for the exclusive information is a steal. If Link agrees, but does not have enough Rupees, Domidak will scoff and turn him away. Once Link agrees to the deal and gives up the Rupees required, Domidak will tell him the riddle they discovered. He explains where he got this information from and claims it is unmistakable. At the end of the conversation, the "Misko, the Great Bandit" Side Quest begins. Link can still talk to the pair to overhear Domidak musing over the riddle. If Link tells them to keep at it Prissen will snap at him, causing Domidak to tell his brother to quiet down and let him think. Link can let the pair know that he already solved the riddle, but Domidak does not believe him. Prissen declares that Link could never solve the puzzle before his brother and Domidak goes back to mulling the riddle over.

Domizuin Shrine, designated by the trial name A Prone Pathway, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Domizuin Shrine can be found on top of the Akkala Citadel Ruins in the Akkala Highlands. It corresponds to the Niuzimod Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of the cage inside the Shrine.|The box cage within the Shrine Domizuin Shrine consists of a single gigantic chamber with several floating platforms. Beyond the entrance, the floor extends forward over an abyss. Above the end of this floor is a tall structure that Link can Ascend through. Above this structure, there is a staircase that leads down into a bridge further into the Shrine's abyss. At the end of this bridge is a gigantic floating box cage and a Shock Switch with a circular, horizontal arrow hinting at its function. When struck, this Shock Switch will rotate the cage 90 degrees counter-clockwise, allowing entry into the cage. There are a number of platforms built along the walls of this cage. At the bottom of the cage there is a platform that does not move along with the cage. A second Shock Switch with a circular, vertical arrow sits atop this platform. When struck, it rotates the cage by 90 degrees in the direction that it points. By utilizing both of these Shock Switches, Link is able to access all sides of the cage. In order to reach the end of the Shrine, Link can strike the horizontal Shock Switch once, enter the cage, then strike the horizontal Shock Switch a second time. From this point, the horizontal Shock Switch will be blocked by a tall platform. By standing in the gap between the tall platform and the wall before striking the vertical Shock Switch once, Link can position himself near the top of the cage where he can Ascend and walk toward the end of the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Domizuin Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

, also known as , is a recurring character in . He is the ruler of the Zora and, by the time of , has been for up to 200 years. Biography King Dorephan is the reigning monarch of Zora's Domain. In addition to this, he is the father of Mipha and Sidon. He presides over the Domain from his Throne in the Throne Room. He is a historian, collecting stories about Zora's Domain that have been passed down in the Zora royal family. As the King of the Zora, it is his job to watch over the Water level of the East Reservoir Lake. King Dorephan greatly cherished his daughter Mipha. As the threat of Calamity Ganon rose, he eventually gave her permission to pilot Divine Beast Vah Ruta, though he made her promise to return to him safely. Following the Great Calamity, he grew to regret allowing her to join the fight against Ganon. Since then, he has prayed every day that Mipha's soul will rest in peace. According to the History of the Zora, Addendum 1, a Guardian Stalker approached Zora's Domain through Upland Zorana approximately 100 years after King Dorephan became its ruler. When the Zora soldiers were unable to stop the Guardian, King Dorephan decided to face it on his own. He threw the Guardian into a ravine and destroyed it, which increased the trust and respect his citizens had for him. He still has a scar on his forehead from this encounter. The Stone Monuments scattered throughout the Lanayru Great Spring were originally a single monument commissioned by King Dorephan. However, due to the length of the writing he gave to the stonemason, the commission was split among seven Monuments. Three additional Monuments were crafted, one of which honors the achievements of King Dorephan. After Link follows Sidon to Zora's Domain during the "Reach Zora's Domain" Main Quest, Sidon beckons Link to meet King Dorephan. In the Throne Room, Link will find King Dorephan and Muzu, the former of whom identifies Link as the Hylian that Sidon has recruited. He congratulate Link for being able to make it to the Domain. He introduces himself as the ruler of the Zora. Upon noticing the Sheikah Slate, King Dorephan is able to recognize Link as the Hylian Champion. King Dorephan informs Link that they have met many times before. Thinking back to such memories brings a wave of nostalgia upon him. Having heard a rumor that Link fell in battle, King Dorephan is relieved to see that he has survived. Despite how Link responds to him, King Dorephan will realize that Link has lost his memories. Upon hearing this, King Dorephan asks Link if he remembers his daughter, Mipha. He is shocked to hear that Link is unable to recall her, since the two of them were close friends. He encourages Link to look upon Mipha's Statue in the Zora's Domain Square in an attempt to jog his memory. King Dorephan hopes that Link's memory will

is a recurring character in . Biography Dorian is a Sheikah who guards Impa's House in Kakariko Village. He carries an Eightfold Blade. Before Link meets with Impa, Dorian will stay at his post at all hours of the day. In the past, Dorian was a member of the Yiga Clan, but he gave this up when he met his wife and had his daughters, Koko and Cottla. Dorian tried to change his ways and leave the Yiga for the Sheikah Tribe, but the Yiga killed his wife in retaliation. With the lives of his children on the line Dorian continued to serve as an informant within the Sheikah for the Yiga Clan. In the Journal of Various Worries, Dorian expresses concern over Pikango's arrival in Kakariko Village. Dorian fears that, in his search for Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain, Pikango will discover the Ancient Shrines near it. Dorian signs the Journal as "Anonymous Father of Two" in an attempt to remain anonymous. When Link first approaches Impa's House, Dorian and his fellow guard Cado will take a defensive stance and demand he identify himself. However, once they notice the Sheikah Slate in Link's possession, the two relax their stances and apologize. He will explain that Impa informed them about the swordsman and asks that Link head inside to meet with her. Cado and Dorian will step aside to allow Link passage and Dorian reveals that for ages Impa has been waiting for his return. While he wishes to speak to Link as well, he asks that the hero first see the elder. Dorian implores Link to use the Sheikah Village's resources to his advantage. He also mentions the Ta'loh Naeg Shrine on the East Hill, as well as the Great Fairy Fountain, which he refers to as the location of Kakariko Village's Guardian Spirit. Dorian admits that does not dare to try and contact the Great Fairy himself, but recommends that Link search for her. If Link speaks to him at night, he asks what he's doing up so late and tells him to spend the night at the Shuteye Inn. Following Link's meeting with Impa, Dorian told the Yiga Clan about his awakening. Filled with grief, Dorian eventually decided to cut ties with the Yiga Clan completely, but the Yiga Clan threatened the lives of Impa and Paya as well. Once Link has spoken to Impa, Dorian and Cado will begin to take shifts guarding the her House. Cado will return to his post at 11:00 in the evening, allowing Dorian to go home at midnight to his daughters, Koko and Cottla. At home, Dorian will take a seat and remove his umbrella hat. He explains that his wife was murdered by the Yiga. He mourns her death and admits his great displeasure as his inability to protect her. Eventually, Dorian will fall asleep in his chair. is a recurring character in . Biography Dorill is a Goron miner who works at the Southern Mine in Eldin Canyon. He is the head of the Goron Group Mining Company, and he takes direct orders from the boss, Bludo. He spends the whole day mining, and at night he sleeps nearby with his son, Axyl. When Link first arrives at the Southern Mine, Dorill explains that his happiness is Bludo's, and is therefore the rest of Goron City's. He is highly motivated to dig and sell the Ore he finds. If Link asks about Goron City, Dorill will give him directions and warn him to take care not to get burned along the way. He comments that Goron City is prosperous because of their work, though he expresses that he would much rather mine at Death Mountain Summit if not for the Divine Beast Vah Rudania there. Dorill is driven to find as many Gems as possible in a day, his target being one thousand pieces. He has a great admiration for Bludo, as everything they do at the Southern Mine is for him. He encourages the other Goron miners to work just as hard as he does. He is especially eager to sell their Gems for a profit. While he works, Dorill encourages the other miners. He also laughs when Link speaks to him.

is a recurring character in . Biography Dorrah is a Gerudo soldier who guards the front entrance of Gerudo Town with her fellow guard, Merina. She wields a Gerudo Spear. When Link tries to enter Gerudo Town without a disguise, the guards will stop him. Dorrah will tell him that no "voe" are allowed in Town. She apologizes if Link speaks to her and says that it is a strict tradition that "voe" are not permitted into the Town, suggesting that Link instead go to the Kara Kara Bazaar if he needs to prepare for a journey. When Link mishears "voe" as "boe," Dorrah corrects him, explaining that "voe" means "man" in the Hylian language. Dorrah also explains that the Gerudo word for "woman" is "vai". When Link finishes speaking to Dorrah, she tells him that "Good-bye" is "sav'orq" in Gerudo. If Link tries to sneak into Gerudo Town without being disguised or removes any piece of his disguise while inside, Dorrah will yell that a man has been detected and commands the soldiers to capture him at once. Link is then thrown out to the front entrance of Gerudo Town, where Dorrah points her Gerudo Spear at him and tells him that men are forbidden by Gerudo law. Once Link obtains the Gerudo Outfit, he can speak to Dorrah again. She explains that Gerudo Town is Hyrule's largest trade hub and that only "vai" are permitted to enter. When Link mishears "vai" as "bai," Dorrah corrects him and explains that "vai" means "woman" in Hylian. She also explains that the Gerudo word for "man" is "voe." Dorrah recommends learning the Gerudo language if Link plans to stay in Gerudo Town. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Dorrah says that Riju has calmed the Divine Beast and, if he is wearing the Gerudo Outfit, Link can now relax in Gerudo Town. She expects there to be more traffic in and out of Gerudo Town, which means she will have to be more diligent to keep men from entering.

is a recurring character in . Biography Douma is a Hylian who can be found in the Lanayru Region of Hyrule. She is a self-described peddler and traveling Merchant, who goes wherever she feels. Initially, Douma is found at the fork in the road near the mouth of Zora River in the Lanayru Wetlands. She beckons Link over when she sees him, where she remarks how strange it is to find another Hylian in the area. She introduces herself and says it is nice to meet him. Douma then wonders if Link spoke to the Zora nearby and if they asked him to head to Zora's Domain and meet Prince Sidon. If Link says yes to both these questions, Douma reveals that she met Sidon, and the first thing he said to her was "I've been watching you!" and "What's your name?!" Creeped out, she ran away, though she tells Link to visit if he wants to see a freak show. However, she does not think he will go for Link, since he is not as much of a looker as she is. After Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, Douma returns to Zora's Domain. She will recognize Link if they have spoken before. She explains that, since the Rain has stopped, she was able to reach the Domain. Her plan is to buy rare goods from the Coral Reef, and she tells Link not to get in her way. She is also relieved to take a break and enjoy the sights. During the day, she sleeps at the Seabed Inn. Douma thinks that Mipha's Statue in the Zora's Domain Square is cute. When Link tells her Mipha's name, Douma is annoyed and asks how she was supposed to know. She becomes irritated when Link tells her this more than once. Douma's work is purchasing Items from the Coral Reef. However, she considers it boring, so she suggests Link does not follow her. She enjoys going sightseeing when she takes her breaks. Within the Coral Reef, Douma remarks that Sasan was planning on stocking up on Hylian Rice. Due to its abundance, however, she does not see it as a good purchase. She instead suggests buying Chillfin Trouts or Sizzlefin Trouts, since they are not as common.

, also known as Mouth of the Dragon, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Dracozu Lake is located in the Faron Grasslands. It is the northernmost terminal of the Dracozu River, and it is overlooked by ancient ruins. The lake opens up into a small plaza where a massive stone structure in the form of a Dragon—evidently the centerpiece—rests only a short distance away. Inside of this structure is the Spring of Courage, complete with a Goddess Statue and an Ancient Shrine. The lake is surrounded by the Farosh Hills to the west, the Popla Foothills to the north, the Damel Forest to the south, and to the east by the rim of Tobio's Hollow. The plaza is heavily defended by many powerful enemies. Within the Dragon structure, just before the Spring of Courage proper, one can find a Metal Chest containing a Gold Rupee. There are a few Korok to be found here. One hides in a Block Puzzle arrangement above the right hand of the Dragon structure. The block needed to complete this puzzle can be found on a matching block arrangement present on the left hand—immediately across the plaza. Another can be found at a small shrine around a large boar head statue on the hill to the west. Here a stone boulder, found atop one of the four pillars found there, must be moved into the corner to match the arrangement of the other three corners, prompting the Korok to appear. The last can be located at the very top of the enormous tree, which grows up and out from the aforementioned Dragon structure in the central plaza. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Dracozu River is located in the Faron Grasslands. It is most easily accessed from the Damel Forest. It is a meandering river typified by the presence of numerous, serpentine Dragon statues along its banks, and by its dense, tropical forest surroundings. The location is tied to the Shrine Quest, "The Serpent's Jaws", given to Link by Kass, who is found in Pagos Woods, in the form of an Ancient Song. The River itself is shaped like a Dragon. A metallic Treasure Chest containing a Purple Rupee sits submerged at the southernmost tip of the River. A second Treasure Chest rewards the same prize; this one can be found upriver, underwater, at the river bend nearest to Dracozu Lake. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Dragon Bone Mire is located directly to the west of Warbler's Nest on the Tabantha Frontier. It consists of the remains of a giant, skeletal rib cage, which has been surrounded by several Bottomless Bogs. A pair of Ore Deposits can be found on the Mire's southwestern end. There are four Treasure Chests at Dragon Bone Mire, all of which are made of metal and have been submerged in the Bottomless Bogs. Using the Magnesis Rune, Link can pull the Chests to the surface, allowing them to be opened. These Treasure Chests contain a Feathered Edge, a bundle of five Shock Arrows, a Sapphire, and a Diamond. left|40px There is only one Korok Seed Puzzle within the Dragon Bone Mire. It is a Natural Hiding Spot, which takes the form of a Rock under a Pile of Leaves in the Mire's northwest corner. When Link picks up the Rock, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

are a recurring class of Item in . Dragon Parts go unnamed in . Location and Uses Dragon Parts are a type of Material that can be obtained from shooting Dragons with Arrows. Depending on where Link shoots, he will obtain either a Scale, a Claw, a Fang Shard, or a Horn Shard. Dragon Parts can be given to a Great Fairy in order to Enhance pieces of Armor. They may also be used as Cooking Ingredients in a Cooking Pot to enhance Meals. List of Dragon Parts Dragon Parts reappear in , with the addition of Spike Shards. Like other types of Materials, they can be Fused to Weapons, Shields, or Arrows and used to perform elemental attacks, although this depends on which Dragon they belong to. Dinraal for Fire, Naydra for Ice and Farosh for Electricity. There is a new Dragon, the Light Dragon, who also drops Dragon Parts when hit with an Arrow. When Fused to a Weapon or a Shield, her Parts allow Link to heal when hitting Enemies. Like in , Dragon Parts can be be given to a Great Fairy in order to Enhance pieces of Armor or used in a Cooking Pot to enhance Meals. List of Dragon Parts

, also stylized as , are recurring Items and Objects in . Dragonbone Boko Bows go unnamed in . Location and Uses Dragon Bone Boko Bows are Bows used by high-tier Bokoblins on Hyrule Ridge and in Hyrule Field. They are Boko Bows that have been reinforced with fossils that were handpicked by Bokoblins. Because of this, they are known to have a respectable firepower. They belong to the Bokoblin Gear equipment archetype, which is a series of Weapons created by Bokoblins. Due to being made of wood, Dragon Bone Boko Bows will burn and eventually disintegrate if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will also float if dropped in Water. Unlike metal Weapons, they do not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, nor do they conduct Electricity. If scanned with the amiibo Rune, the Series Bokoblin amiibo has a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Dragon Bone Boko Bow, along with other Bokoblin Gear. Other Appearances Dragonbone Boko Bows are wielded by Black Bokoblins and Silver Bokoblins. They cannot be wielded by any Warriors.

are recurring Items in . Dragonbone Boko Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Dragonbone Boko Shields are Boko Shields that have been upgraded and reinforced with fossilized bone. They belong to the Bokoblin Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created and maintained by Bokoblins. Though they provide a respectable defense, the poor craftsmanship used to make them leaves them with low Durability. They are used by Black Bokoblin, Silver Bokoblin, and Golden Bokoblin. High-tier Moblins also make use of these Shields. As they are made of wood, Dragonbone Boko Shields will burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will float if they are dropped in Water, and unlike metal Shields, they will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity. Finally, they cannot be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. If scanned with the amiibo Rune, the Series Bokoblin amiibo has a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Dragonbone Boko Shield. Dragonbone Boko Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Dragonbone Boko Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Dragonbone Boko Clubs.

is a recurring character in . Biography Drak is a Goron miner who can be found at the Abandoned North Mine in the Eldin Canyon. He carries a Cobble Crusher, and he noticeably speaks with a slur where his vowels extend. Drak helps Link by explaining the area to him. He tells him that the Abandoned North Mine used to be active, until it grew too hot and dangerous due to the Divine Beast Vah Rudania and the infestation of monsters. Because of that, Bludo had appointed him to keep watch of the area. When Link first speaks to Drak, he wonders why so many people are out and about. He warns Link that the Scorching Climate gets hotter past him and there are more monsters. At the beginning of the "Divine Beast Vah Rudania" Main Quest, Link can ask Drak about Yunobo. Drak is at first suspicious and asks why a stranger is asking about Yunobo. When Link explains that Bludo asked, Drak tells Link that Yunobo went into the Vault to retrieve painkillers, but he has yet to return. Due to its danger, Drak suggests that Link does not go after him. When Link approaches the Cannon closest to them, Drak warns him not to touch it. He discourages Link from putting any explosives inside. Throughout "Divine Beast Vah Rudania", Link is able to keep asking Drak where Yunobo is. Once Link has rescued him from the Abandoned North Mine, Drak tells Link that Yunobo went back to Goron City. He will also inform Link of Yunobo's location after he departs for the Bridge of Eldin.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Drenan Highlands are a stretch of land along the western range of the Eldin Mountains. They lie at the northern flank of Hyrule at the Mountains' base. The Highlands may be entered through a passage in the western Mountains, which lies at the northern road between the Hebra Mountains and Great Hyrule Forest. The Drenan Highlands shares its landscape with the Deplian Badlands further east, in that it is largely barren and has rugged terrain. Very little vegetation grow here aside for a few patches of grass, flowers, and shrubs; the latter of which can be cut down to produce Tree Branches. In spite of its scarce landscape, the Highlands, along with the entire Eldin Mountains stretch, is home to numerous Creatures. Most of the Highlands' greenery is condensed in its core, where a small meadow lies. To the east of the meadow is a dirt path lined by several stone monuments. The path leads to the entrance of the Thyphlo Ruins in the Great Hyrule Forest. A small wood south of this pathway bears a fallen log, which hides a nut at one end. Destroying the nut will reveal a Korok. Along the cliffside east of the Lynel prowling the Highlands, Link can find an orange Pinwheel. Upon approaching the Pinwheel, three Balloons will spawn and fly around. Destroying the Balloons will reveal a Korok, who will give Link a Korok Seed for finding him. Creatures Enemies

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Dronoc's Pass is located in the Hebra Mountains. It is a short pathway that branches off from the main road to Rospro Pass, instead directing travelers to the Flight Range nearby. The Pass eventually ends at the Flight Range's hut. Sha Warvo Shrine is situated along Dronoc's Pass, just outside of the Flight Range. Since it is located within a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance in order to traverse the Pass without taking damage. During the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, Saki directs Link to Dronoc's Pass, where he can access the Flight Range and find Teba. left|40px A single Korok Seed Puzzle can be found at Dronoc's Pass. A small well with a metal Boulder chained to it is located at the start of the Pass. Using the Magnesis Rune, Link can place the Boulder into the well, which causes a Korok to appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures

The is a recurring location in . The Dronoc's Pass Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Dronoc's Pass Well is a stout stone Well, which is located at a fork in the road at Dronoc's Pass in the southern Hebra Mountains. It is located within a Freezing Climate, and so Link must have at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit it without taking damage. The Well has no roof, and an Iron is chained to its base. Korok Seeds Returning from its appearance in , the Dronoc's Pass Well is still found at the southern end of Dronoc's Pass in the Hebra Mountains. Link can now access its interior, which is a Stable Climate. This is in contrast to its Freezing surroundings, which will damage Link unless he has at least one level of Cold Resistance. The inner chamber features two levels. The lower level consists of a pool of Water and a Luminous Stone Deposit. The upper level is illuminated by two potted Brightblooms, and it contains two Barrels and a Cooking Pot with an unlit Campfire. Near the Cooking Pot is a Note on the Table written by Aurie Taamu, who recounts his encounter with the Mountains' cold Temperatures. He claims that he ate Sautéed Peppers for Cold Resistance, but he accidentally replaced it with Heat Resistance when he drank a Cooling Elixir afterwards. Creatures Equipment

is a character in . Biography Drozer is a Hylian who guards the Southern Gate of Lookout Landing alongside Burwar. He carries a Traveler's Spear. If Link attempts to enter Lookout Landing from the Southern Gate, Drozer and Burwar will both be shocked to see him. The pair then direct him to meet with Purah, who can be found in the Research Lab. If Link speaks to Drozer after already entering Lookout Landing, Drozer will initially be in disbelief. He is relieved to see that Link has returned, revealing that after he and Zelda disappeared, Purah began to panic. If Link asks about Lookout Landing, Drozer explains that Purah has been using it to observe the Gloom rising from Beneath Hyrule Castle. Since Zelda has gone missing, it is also where the search for her has been based out of. Drozer directs Link to the Research Lab so he can show Purah that he is safe. Should Link speak to Drozer again, he recalls how terrible the day of his and Zelda's disappearance was. After Link has met with Purah, Drozer will begin to greet him whenever they speak. He encourages Link to make use of the facilities at Lookout Landing, and he promises to protect Lookout Landing until Zelda has been located. If Link asks about Lookout Landing again, this time Drozer will offer his support in the effort to find Zelda. If Link ends their conversation, Drozer warns him about the Hyrule Field Chasm and the Hyrule Castle Chasm, both of which are located in the vicinity, as well as Monsters.

Dubious Food is a recurring Meal in . Location and Uses Dubious Food can be made from several different Cooking combinations: Food with Monster Parts or critters, but not both Monster Parts on their own Critters on their own Any recipe that would produce an Elixir without an effect (e.g. Monster Part + Chilly critter + Spicy critter) Seasonings without Food Dubious Food is noted to be too gross to look at and emits a bizarre smell. However, it can restore a random amount of Link's Hearts depending on the ingredients used. Moza, who can be found near Ishto Soh Shrine, will give Link three recipes, two of which result in Dubious Food. One is her ancient Meat dish, which involves Cooking Meat with an Ancient Material from a Guardian. When Link calls this gross, she will scold him, saying the only way to Cook Meat is something with history. She asks Link how else she is supposed to make her ancient meat dish. However, Moza admits to Link that her only results have been Dubious Food. For her other dish, the ultimate survival dish, Moza tells Link to defeat Monsters and to put their parts in a Cooking Pot. This time, if Link calls her recipe gross, she will insist that one has to be willing to eat anything to survive in the wild. Though she always ends up with Dubious Food, she asserts she will not achieve her goal unless she makes some sacrifices. She also admits to Link that she is unsure what is so dubious about using Monster Parts. Other Appearances The recipe for Dubious Food is earned by completing the Quest "Extreme Survival Cuisine". It is made using two Hearty Durians, two Rock Salts, and two Hot-Footed Frogs. However, it can be lowered to one of each ingredient through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warriors will gain twice as many Rupees, including those earned after the mission, but they will have 20% less total Hearts. Nomeclature

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Dueling Peaks are a large mountain located in West Necluda that has been split in half. The Squabble River flows between the two Peaks, alongside which trails the only road connecting most of Necluda to the rest of Hyrule. The Peaks are also bordered by Dueling Peaks South and North Dueling Peaks. Ree Dahee Shrine, Shee Venath Shrine, and Shee Vaneer Shrine are all situated on the Dueling Peaks. The Peaks are the namesake of both Dueling Peaks Tower and Dueling Peaks Stable, which sit near the mountain's base. The tops of the Peaks become a Freezing Climate due to their high altitude, requiring at least one level of Cold Resistance for Link to traverse the area without taking damage. According to legends, the Dueling Peaks were split by a Dragon Deity in order to create a path between them. In modern times, the Peaks are known for their abundant Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits, which makes them a popular spot for miners. Bugut, a former mountain Climber, recounts scaling the Dueling Peaks in his youth. Two Treasure Chests can be found on top of the Dueling Peaks. The first is a metal Chest, located along the southern edge of the northern Peak, and it contains a Traveler's Bow. The second Chest is also made of metal, and it can be found on the southeastern corner of the northern Peak. This Chest holds a Boomerang. left|40px A total of four separate Korok Seed Puzzles are located at the Dueling Peaks. The first is a Natural Hiding Spot, which takes the form of a Rock on top of the northern Peak. The second is an Offering Spot, situated on the southern Peak. The third Puzzle is another Natural Hiding Spot Rock, this time on the northwestern end of the southern peak. The final Puzzle is marked by a large pair of Trees, which Link must roll a Boulder between. Whenever one of these Puzzles is solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials The Dueling Peaks return in . Several pieces of debris have fallen onto the Peaks, which Link can use Recall on in order to reach the Sky Islands above. During the "An Unfamiliar World" and the "Zelda and Sonia" Memories, the Dueling Peaks can be seen joined together as a singular mountain in the ancient past. The Floor Map also depicts the Dueling Peaks as one mountain. Areas Other Appearances The Dueling Peaks are located on the western end of the Fort Hateno stage.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Dueling Peaks South is a rocky hill located along the southern slope of the Dueling Peaks in West Necluda. Tobio's Hollow and the Jia Highlands can be found at its southern border. Unlike the rest of the slope, Dueling Peaks South is flat, allowing Link to walk across it without needing to Climb. The Stone Talus (Junior) resides on Dueling Peaks South. It is initially dormant, but if Link approaches it, it will stand up and begin to attack him. Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Dueling Peaks South returns in . Enemies Sub-Bosses

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Dueling Peaks Stable is a Stable located in West Necluda, situated beside the road running north from the Big Twin Bridge, east of the Dueling Peaks themselves. The Ha Dahamar Shrine is in a shallow pool of Water between the Stable and the Dueling Peaks, providing a convenient Travel Gate to the Stable when activated. Link can find Wooden Boxes surrounding the Stable that contain Apples and Arrows. A Cooking Pot can be found outside of the Stable. The Dueling Peaks Stable's uniqueness comes from the fact that most of its inhabitants are twins, including the workers. The Dueling Peaks Stable is run by Tasseren, who mans both its Horse-boarding services and Inn. Tasseren's brother, Rensa, offers directions to points of interest in the area, such as Kakariko Village and Hateno Village. His children Shibo and Darton can be found in front of the stabled Horses during the day, and will give Link tips about catching and training Horses. Hino, Sagessa, Domidak, and Prissen are all permanent residents of the Stable. Hino can be found near the Stable's entrance, studying the mystery of the Blood Moon. Sagessa can be seen sitting next to the Cooking Pot, talking about Elixirs. She will also stand across from Ha Dahamar Shrine, remarking on the Ancient Shrine's new glowing feature. As with all other Stables, Beedle at Dueling Peaks Stable as well. The Hylian travelers Agus, Brokka, Bugut, Joute, Toma, and Mezer all stop at the Stable during their travels. When staying at Dueling Peaks Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Tasseren explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Tasseren offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Tasseren will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Tasseren will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. Link can receive the "Misko, the Great Bandit" Side Quest by talking to Domidak while he converses with Prissen inside Dueling Peaks Stable. After Link overhears them discussing Misko's treasure, Prissen accidentally reveals that they know how to find it. When Link asks about the treasure, Domidak offers to sell him the information they have for 100 Rupees. Once Link makes the payment, Domidak shares the riddle they have heard with him. As part of the "Wild Horses" Side Quest, Rensa challenges Link to a tame-off of Wild Horses in the area. Link is tasked with taming a Horse and bringing it back to the Stable within two minutes. If Link is able to do so, Rensa will give him a Purple Rupee as a reward. By befriending the Hylian Retriever behind the Dueling Peaks Stable, Link can be led to a

Link is tasked with taming a Horse and bringing it back to the Stable within two minutes. If Link is able to do so, Rensa will give him a Purple Rupee as a reward. By befriending the Hylian Retriever behind the Dueling Peaks Stable, Link can be led to a metal Treasure Chest containing a Silver Rupee, which is embedded in the ground beneath the Tree to the northeast. Link can use the Magnesis Rune to pull the Chest from the ground. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found at Dueling Peaks Stable. It takes the form of Leaves with Fairy Dust located on the nose of the Horse figure on top of the Stable. When Link interacts with the Leaves, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Materials Equipment Dueling Peaks Stable returns in . Beedle, Darton, and Shibo can all be seen outside of the Stable. Areas Creatures Materials Equipment Treasure Chests

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Dueling Peaks Stable Well can be found in the White Goat pen behind Dueling Peaks Stable in West Necluda. It has a Ladder leading into its interior, which is comprised of three different levels. Each of these levels is separated by another Well structure that leads to the floor below. The first level contains Mushrooms, the second level has multiple Ore Deposits and Luminous Stone Deposits, and the third level features several pools of Water inhabited by a variety of Creatures. Although the first two levels' walls are easily Climbable, the third level's walls are Wet Walls. The Dueling Peaks Stable Well is one of several Wells that Fera can be found in prior to beginning the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?". She rates the Well's Water quality as fair and its moss growth as extensive, in addition to confirming the presence of Brightcaps. Once her Side Quest has started, she leaves for the Lookout Landing Well. Creatures Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Dugby is a Goron child who can be found at the Goron Hot Springs in the Eldin Canyon. During the day, he can found sitting in one of its Hot Springs. When he's sitting in the Spring, Duby's mouth is underwater, which gargles his words. If Link swings his weapon around Dugby, he will be yelled at for doing something dangerous. At night, he sleeps nearby. Dugby competes with his grandfather, Grapp, to see who can stay in the Spring the longest. However, he's unable to do so, and decides to go to sleep and beat his grandfather another day. When Dugby is in the water, he'll tell Link about the treasure that he buried near the Bridge of Eldin, with the promise that Link can keep it if he finds it. However, because Dugby's mouth is submerged underwater when spoken to, his directions to the treasure come out as gurgles. This initiates the Side Quest Death Mountain's Secret. If visited during the night, Dugby mutters clearer directions to the treasure in his sleep. The treasure turns out to be a Drillshaft. Although amazed that Link found the treasure, Dugby is skeptic about it and checks the Weapon to determine if it is the same Drillshaft he buried, and confirms that it is the same one. True to his word, he lets Link keep the Drillshaft as a reward for finding it.

right|thumb|Link exploring a Dungeon from , also known as Levels, are locations in . They form the "Underworld" of the worlds which Link visits and contain Items and treasure to collect, Enemies to overcome, and Puzzles to solve. Purpose The main reason for the existence of Dungeons is to house a prize that Link must collect. Throughout the series these Items have been different; Link collects fragments of the Triforce in the original , Pendants and Crystals in , musical instruments in , and other Items throughout the other games. In , the goal is not to collect, but to return gems to magical statues in the Dungeons. Items 70px|right|Big Key in The Wind Waker The Dungeons that Link visits are home to valuable items and treasures for Link to collect, ranging from Item upgrades to unique tools and Weapons. Many of these Items will prove to be essential to the completion of Link's goals. With the exception of , almost every Dungeon that Link encounters contains a set of items usable only in that Dungeon. These include a Dungeon Map, which displays the layout of the Dungeon (but may still omit certain secret rooms). The original use of the Compass was to display the location of the boss of the Dungeon, but as the games moved into a 3D style it has come to also pinpoint hidden secrets within the Dungeon. The Big Key is used to open specially locked doors (and sometimes chests). It is sometimes called the Boss Key since its use usually signals that the boss fight is about to occur. History thumb|Link searching for secrets in a Dungeon from In , the Dungeons retained the same format as the rest of the game: Link maneuvers each area from a top-down perspective, facing everything from dead ends to invincible and usually strong enemies to complex traps, puzzles, and maze-like passages. From this game to , there is a trend revolving around almost all the Dungeons sharing a common audio theme. Unlike most of the other games in the series, the Dungeons can be completed in any order. This entry is also one of but a few in the franchise to feature a special Second Quest after the challenges of the first one are overcome, or by the player entering "ZELDA" as the file name. In either case, the Second Quest proves more challenging, offering nine Dungeons similar to those in the original quest. However, not only are some of the Dungeons' locations mixed up in the Second Quest, but they are generally more difficult, with a different layout, the items being hidden more carefully and stronger Enemies and Bosses introduced sooner. The general layout of Hyrule remains the same, but the locations of items scattered across the overworld are also hidden in different places. Its series-new 3D graphics allow the game's Dungeons to be far more individual. More unusual settings are used, such as the humongous insides of both a tree and a giant fish. Though not included in the original release of the game for the Nintendo 64, the GameCube release of carries a , which is a similar revisiting of the game to that of the Second Quest from the original . One major difference of note between the Second Quest and the is that, in the Second Quest from , both the overworld and Dungeons undergo radical changes, but in , only the Dungeons change. These altered Dungeons offer new puzzles and traps, as well as different locations for the Items within and stronger Enemies introduced sooner. For , is implemented with the same cartridge. It is made even more difficult due to it being mirrored east-west and making Enemies inflict twice as much damage as before. The following is a list of Dungeons in : Inside the Deku Tree Dodongo's Cavern Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly Forest Temple Fire Temple Water Temple Shadow Temple Spirit Temple Ganon's Castle employs the same game engine used for , but has not offered a Second Quest. In fact, the game's Dungeons are the lowest in number in the series: four main Temples, with two mandatory mini-Dungeons. However, they are more complex in various aspects, and they are thematically unique. The Great Bay Temple, for example, serves as a waterwheel factory, while the [[[Woodfall Temple]] is made of stone and wood used by the Deku for their worship. One of the new elements is the game's Time-based gameplay device, which makes it possible to reset Dungeons. As a result, all the puzzles solved, Enemies defeated, and Keys obtained in a Dungeon are reverted every time Link travels back in time, although he retains the Dungeon Map and Compass. However, after a Dungeon has been cleared for the first time, they allow Link to directly confront the Bosses through the warp spots that activate in their entrance rooms. Likewise, Stray Fairies can be collected in these Dungeons so that Link can return them to the Fairy's Fountains they belong to, in exchange for special rewards. The game's first three Dungeons require Link's new respective forms (Deku Link, Goron Link, and Zora Link) to be completed. In the fourth Dungeon Stone Tower Temple, Link makes use of all of them to reach Twinmold; all main temple items in this game also pertain to the Bow. The following is a list of Dungeons in : Suthorn Ruins Gerudo Sanctum Jabul Ruins Hyrule Castle Eldin Temple Lanayru Temple Faron Temple Null's Body Classification There are several criteria to classify a Dungeon, including the following: thumb|right|The interior of the Lakebed Temple, a water-themed Dungeon in Architecture A Dungeon can be classified according to its architecture. Some types include labyrinths, palaces and temples. Not infrequently, several games have portrayed common types of building (for example, the labyrinths are exclusive to the original , the temples are mainstream for the 3D games, etc.); and depending on this, the Dungeons themselves may be crafted for a specific quest purpose. Besides the aforementioned types of Dungeons, there are also Caverns (characterized for having little, if any, artificial architecture within), towers (large buildings that have a more prominent purpose, such as guarding a pearl that bring protection to the user from dark influences, or guarding the entrance to the ruins of an ancient kingdom), or organic entities,

Themes The Dungeons in series cover a wide variety of elements, themes and environments. Among the most well-known types of Dungeons, according to these criteria, are forest, fire and water Dungeons. Depending on the element present in the Dungeon, there may be a determined type of puzzles, bestiary and obstacles to conquer; added to this are the unique mechanics or themes that make the Dungeon different from the others. Not all Dungeons convey elemental themes, however, and some of them show a heavy ambiguity that makes them more difficult to classify (for instance, none of the Dungeons in the NES games can be distinguished this way). Certain Dungeons in the series are of mixed category, meaning that they can cover two or more themes simultaneously. Some of the final Dungeons (such as the recurring Ganon's Tower, which encases the elements of most Dungeons in the games where it appears) are of this type, as are regular Dungeons like the Arbiter's Grounds (shadow, desert) in and the Sword & Shield Maze (fire, ice) in , among others. Rank Some Zelda games may feature main Dungeons and mini-Dungeons. The main Dungeons are the most important, as they are directly related to the game's plot, and are usually the largest and most difficult to conquer, not to mention the mandatory presence of a boss in each of them. The mini-Dungeons are mid-way stages that show one of these two characteristics: They may be required to complete for reasons not as prominent as those that motivate the young hero to complete the main Dungeons. They are optional. thumb|left|Pirate Stronghold, a mini-Dungeon in Having either condition, they may not house a boss or even a map and compass, or they are smaller in size. For example, the Ice Cavern in has the Iron Boots, which are required in a future Dungeon, but it is pretty small in comparison to the temples, and no boss is found. A Dungeon lacking a map and compass is the Ancient Castle of Ikana in . An example of an optional Dungeon is the Gerudo's Training Ground in . As mentioned above, both Phantom Hourglass and introduce the "master" Dungeons, which have an even more significant role and must be visited numerous times so that Link can achieve success in his quest. Partial examples of master Dungeons include the earlier Hyrule Castle in and Forsaken Fortress in , as they are only visited twice each, but they are still heavily plot-critical and are places for twists in the storyline. Though similar in various aspects to the regular Dungeons, they also show new characteristics that accommodate to their role as the ultimate test for Link and his adventure. In addition to housing the Final Boss, they show puzzles, obstacles and enemies that will test each of the young hero's skills. So far, there have been three types of final Dungeon. For the first type, it is simply longer and more imposing that any of the main Dungeons, often consisting of a very high number of rooms, and even sporting new enemies and features. is a recurring character in . Biography Dunma is a guard of Zora's Domain who wields a Zora Spear. She is the daughter of Rivan and the granddaughter of Trello. Though she is offended when Link asks her age, she will clarify that she is less than 100 years old. When Rivan gets carried away speaking to Link, Dunma will interrupt to remind him that they are on duty. She later notes how excited Rivan was to see him. Since it is their first time meeting, she introduce herself to Link. If Link asks if she is female, Dunma comments on how observant he is. Dunma believes herself to be less formal than the Zora elders. She explains to Link that Zora's Domain is looking for a Hylian and instructs him to meet with King Dorephan for more information. Link can ask Dunma about King Dorephan, who she reveals is the ruler of Zora's Domain and the father of Sidon and Mipha. She gives him directions to the Throne Room and reminds him to mind his manners. According to her, Sidon is very sociable and popular among the younger Zora. However, this demeanor is not understood by the Zora elders. After Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, Dunma tells Link that it has been some time since Zora's Domain has seen the sun. She wonders if the Divine Beast has stopped spouting water. Once Link has received the Lightscale Trident, Dunma calls him no ordinary man and proclaims that he will always be welcome in Zora's Domain. In , Dunma can be found on a rock next to Toto Lake keeping watch over Jiahto while he examines the Zora slate. When Link talks to her, she will remark that she wishes Jiahto would do his studies more carefully and will also tell Link about how Jiahto was sent there by Sidon.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Duplex Bows are Bows used by skilled archers of the Yiga. They belong to the Yiga Clan Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Weapons used by the Yiga. They can be found by only two methods. The first is to infiltrate the Yiga Clan Hideout in the Gerudo Highlands, where they are both abandoned and in use by several Yiga Footsoldiers. The second is to defeat the random Yiga Footsoldiers assassins that appear and take their Duplex Bow from them. Unlike other Bows, Duplex Bows have been engineered to fire two Arrows in order to ensure targets are stunned. Nebb, as part of the "The Weapon Connoisseur" Side Quest, will ask Link to show him a Duplex Bow. If Link brings one back to Hateno Village for him, Nebb will be excited and thank Link with a Purple Rupee. Being made of wood, Duplex Bows will burn if they touch Fire or are exposed to a Scorching Climate. They will also float if they are dropped in Water, and they will not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms like metal Weapons do. Finally, they cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune.

is a recurring mechanic in . Overview Durability causes Link's equipment to wear down with repeated use, eventually shattering when worn down too much. In , the Giant's Knife will break after 8 hits or upon striking a wall, as it is a less durable version of the Biggoron's Sword. In , Shields' Durability is measured on the Shield Gauge. The Wooden Shield and Iron Shield will lose durability upon blocking a hit. They can be repaired by bringing them to Gondo in Skyloft's Bazaar or by using a Restoration Potion. The Goddess Shield will automatically restore itself over time, and the Hylian Shield has unlimited durability. If Link Parries an attack, no Durability will be consumed. In , all Weapons, Shields, and Bows have a limited number of uses before they shatter. If thrown at an Enemy, Weapons will break immediately. The last attack performed by a Weapon before it breaks will always be a Critical Hit that deals twice the Weapon's normal damage. This also applies to attacking while mounted on Lynels, since no Durability is lost while doing so. If a Weapon, Shield, or Bow has full Durability, a sparkle can be seen on the top right of their Inventory icons. If the Item has three or less uses left, their icons will flash red, and a message will appear stating that they are badly damaged. The Durability of Weapons and Shields is restored when they are inhaled and spat out by Rock Octoroks. For Shields, Durability is lost when struck by an Enemy attack and by Shield Surfing on rough terrain. The latter can be avoided by only Shield Surfing on Snow or Sand. Lynel Shields, Mighty Lynel Shields, and Savage Lynel Shields also lose Durability when Parrying an Enemy. The Master Sword will not permanently break, instead losing energy on each hit and having a 10-minute recharge period upon depletion. When the Master Sword has three or less uses left, a message appears that states it is low on energy. For Weapons, Durability will not be consumed if no contact is made, unless it is a melee Weapon that shoots projectiles. This includes swinging at nothing, cutting Grass, hitting Switches, hitting the terrain, and striking Trees with a blunt Weapon. For the most part, Durability is unchanged from . However, the Fuse ability can be used to unlock the "bonus" Durability of Weapons. Activating Zonai Devices or hitting any movable Object that does not take damage, such as a Mine Cart, will also consume no Durability. Durability will still be drained when a Weapon generates a projectile that can deal damage to Objects or Enemies. This can be done by Fusing a a Gem or certain Zonai Devices to a Weapon or using Sidon's Power of Water. If a Shield has a damaging Object Fused to it, such as something sharp, Durability will decrease when Link Parries an Enemy to deal damage to it, much like a Lynel Shield. The , also known as the , is a recurring Item and Object in . The Dusk Claymore goes unnamed in , , and . Location and Uses Prior to the events of , the six Sages forged the Dusk Claymore to execute the Demon King, Ganondorf. When this execution took place, the six Sages gathered at the Mirror Chamber with Ganondorf in chains. The Sage of Water thrust the Dusk Claymore into Ganondorf's chest. However, the attempt was in vain, as the Triforce of Power kept him alive. Ganondorf withdrew the Sword from his body and broke free from his chains to kill the Sage of Water. Despite failing to kill him, it did inflict a glowing wound on Ganondorf that never healed. The wound later acts as Dark Beast Ganon and Ganondorf's weak point. During the final sword battle between Link and Ganondorf, Link plunges the Master Sword into the wound, defeating him. Even though the Sages banish Ganondorf to the Twilight Realm, he manages to keep the Dusk Claymore and use it against Link in the final battle. Ganondorf wishes to blot out the light forever with this blade. Link never wields the Dusk Claymore in . The Sword of the Six Sages appears in as an exclusive amiibo Item. It has a rare chance of appearing in a Treasure Chest after scanning the Series Ganondorf amiibo with the amiibo Rune, although only after Link has tamed at least one of the Divine Beasts. The Sword of the Six Sages functions as a two-handed Weapon, and its description refers to it as a longsword. Additionally, its sheath is the same one used by Ganondorf in . It shines with a holy luster that causes it to glow in dark areas such as the Thyphlo Ruins. Link can acquire replacements via using the Ganondorf amiibo if it breaks or if it is lost. Being made of metal, the Sword of the Six Sages will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if it is equipped during a Thunderstorm. It will also sink if dropped in Water, but it can be picked back up and manipulated using the Magnesis Rune. If it is exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate, it will not burn as wooden Weapons do. In contrast to , the Dusk Claymore's damage has been reduced to 32 and its Durability has been reduced to 50. It can be obtained as a reward for completing all four stages of the "Investigate the Thyphlo Ruins" Side Quest. It can also be found from scanning the series Ganondorf amiibo. Once it has been obtained, it can be purchased from any Bargainer Statue for 140 Poes. Other Appearances In , Ganondorf shows the Sword during one of his taunts. In , Ganondorf shows the Sword as a taunt. He can also attack with it by using the Warlock Blade, a custom neutral special move that replaces the Warlock Punch.

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview On Quatta's Shelf, Link can find a Steward Construct that claims to have information among a group of Sky Island ruins. When spoken to, the Steward reveals that a Shrine of Light can be found in the area, and it is the Shrine's keeper. To find the Shrine, Link must follow a riddle, which states, "Dye the white pattern black when the sun awakens in the sky. Then will the sacred shrine appear." After speaking to the Steward Construct, "Dyeing to Find It" will begin. Near the Steward Construct is a level, which will rotate a rock structure when pushed. At 6:00 AM, the structure's shadow will be cast onto a white pattern on the ruins below. By orienting the structure correctly and inserting Boards into its slots, Link can shape its shadow to match the white pattern. When the pattern is completely covered by the shadow, Zonai writing will appear on top of it, and Kurakat Shrine will take form. Once the Shrine of Light appears, "Dyeing to Find It" will be completed. Objectives

Features and Overview East Akkala Stable is a Stable located on the North Akkala Foothill in Deep Akkala, It is managed by Rudi, and the Katosa Aug Shrine can be found across the road. Due to increased rumors of danger in the area, the Stable has hired Hoz as a guard. The East Akkala Stable is also home to the area-exclusive Akkala Bun, which Link must consume immediately after purchasing one from Khini for 10 Rupees. Inside East Akkala Stable is a poster on the wall, which details a Recipe for a Meat and Rice Bowl, as well as the Rumor Mill: Volume 4. When staying at East Akkala Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Rudi explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Rudi offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Rudi will send him off to sleep. When Link wakes up, Rudi will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. If Link has already completed the "Find the Fairy Fountain" Main Quest, Pikango can be found painting at East Akkala Stable. When spoken to, he is able to identify the location of ninth Picture in Link's Album, which is the Spring of Power. A resident of the Stable, Nobo, also shares rumors about the Spring of Power with Link, which starts "The Spring of Power" Shrine Quest. When Link speaks to Hoz about the dangers of the area, Hoz shares that he has heard about a suspicious individual called Kilton, who runs a Shop called Fang and Bone and has been making people uncomfortable. As part of the "A Shady Customer" Side Quest, Hoz asks Link to bring him a description of Kilton. If Link returns to Hoz with a Picture of Kilton, he will be rewarded with a Silver Rupee. After completing the "Robbie's Research" Side Quest, Link will be able to partake in the Restoring the Blue Flame Mini-Game at East Akkala Stable. When Link offers to light the Stable's Blue Flame Pedestal for Aya, she challenges him to do so in under three minutes. In order to participate, Link must pay a 20 Rupee Horse-handling fee. As Link continues to play the Mini-Game, Aya will challenge him to relight the Blue Flame Pedestal in under one minute with a reward of a Silver Rupee. Her final challenge is to relight the Pedestal in under 20 seconds, and she gives him a Gold Rupee as a reward.
