The is a location in . Features and Overview The East Akkala Stable Well can be found behind East Akkala Stable in Deep Akkala. Its interior is accessible via a Ladder that leads into a pond of Water in its first chamber. The second chamber can only be entered by breaking the Cracked Wall on the Well's north side, revealing a small passageway that Link must Crouch through. This chamber contains a Goddess Statue, which is the only of its kind to be located within a Well. Link can interact with the Goddess Statue to exchange Lights of Blessing for either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. He is also able to give it four Sage's Wills to deepen his bond with any Sage. The East Akkala Stable Well is one of several Wells that Fera can be found in prior to beginning the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?". She rates the Well's Water quality as good and its moss growth as limited, in addition to confirming the presence of Brightcaps. She leaves for the Lookout Landing Well once her Side Quest has started. Creatures Materials

, also known as , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview West Nabi Lake is located to the west of Nabi Lake and South Nabi Lake in West Necluda It is a large plain featuring several Big Flags and Ruined House, the latter of which make up the remains of an unnamed Hylian village that was destroyed during the Great Calamity. The South Nabi Lake Well was part of this town. A Stone Talus is located at the center of West Nabi Lake. In addition to this, two Monster Strongholds can be found on the plain. The first is just to the south of Nabi Lake, within which are two Treasure Chest containing Ambers. There is also a Campfire where Roasted Basses are impaled on Boko Spears. The second Monster Stronghold is located along the shore of South Nabi Lake. West Nabi Lake contains one additional Treasure Chest, which is located at the western base of the hill near the Stone Talus. It is a Stone Chest hidden behind a pile of rocks, which Link must destroy. When he opens the Chest, he will receive a Purple Rupee. left|40px Three Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on West Nabi Lake. The first is a series of Horse Hurdles between the Ruined House, which Link must direct a Horse to jump over. The second involves pushing a large Boulder downhill into a hole near the Stone Talus. The final Puzzle is Leaves with Fairy Dust located on top of the Big Flag on the south end of the field, which Link must interact with to solve. When Link completes each of the Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Equipment

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview East Castle Town is the eastern portion of Hyrule Castle Town, making up roughly a third of the Town's area. However, the only part of it that Link can explore is the Hyrule Castle Town East Road. East Castle Town's exit to the majority of Hyrule Field is at first rendered untraversable by a broken Bridge. In order to carry through their Townspeople-Relief Plan, Malo Mart repairs the Bridge with monetary assistance from Link. Areas East Castle Town is located on the eastern side of the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins in Hyrule Field. It is an area that features many ruined buildings, dead Trees, and is covered in Malice. Near the center of the Town ruins, an unlit Cooking Pot can be found sitting near a wall. Deactivated Guardians can be found scattered through the ruins and can be searched for Ancient Materials. A Stone Chest containing a Knight's Bow can be found in the southern bastion. A second Stone Chest containing an Amber can be found sitting in a small puddle, covered by a large stone slab. A third Stone Chest containing a Knight's Shield can be found inside the bastion along the eastern wall. The bastion along the northern tip of the wall contains a Stone Chest with a bundle of five Bomb Arrows. A fifth Stone Chest containing a Purple Rupee is hidden in the remains of a small decayed tower to the west of the Town, surrounded by Pools of Malice. Within the walls of a Ruined House near the southern part of the Town ruins, a sixth Stone Chest containing a Topaz can be found. A Korok Pinwheel can be found on the southwestern wall, and if Link stands near it, five Balloons will appear and spin in a spiral, each a farther distance from Link. If Link shoots these five Balloons, a Korok will appear and gift him a Korok Seed. Areas Creatures Enemies East Castle Town remains largely untouched, with some Fallen Debris littering its grounds. There are seven Hyrule Restoration Material stations scattered among East Castle Town and additional Restoration Materials in the southwest as signs of a reconstruction effort. A ruined tower west of the ponds has a Cracked Wall that can be destroyed to create a passageway. Zelda has established a monument to those lost during the Great Calamity near the entrance to the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins. As part of the dedication, a single Silent Princess was placed atop it. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials Equipment Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The East Gerudo Ruins are located in the Gerudo Desert. The East Gerudo Ruins are the ruins of a temple near the entrance to Gerudo Desert. The temple is a circle of giant statues of the seven heroines who once protected the region of Gerudo. Link must solve a puzzle here in the Shrine Quest, "The Seven Heroines", given by Rotana. There is a Korok hidden in a balloon between the arms of one of the statues and another Korok hidden under a rock atop the southernmost statue. In the time between the Calamity's defeat and the Upheaval, the Ruins have become filled with sand, with several of the statues no longer being visible.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The East Gerudo Sky Archipelago is located in the Gerudo Highlands Sky. It is a cluster of Sky Islands that are particularly abundant with Accented Pigeons. The southwestern Sky Island features a pool of Water and an eastward-facing ramp. A couple Vehicles and spare Zonai Devices can be found here, with one Vehicle loaded onto the ramp. A cluster of Sky Islands with varying elevations can be found in the center of the Archipelago. The lower set of Sky Islands is home to three Air Platforms and a set of Rockets. The Sky Island above is separated into two connected masses, with the eastern mass housing the Rakashog Shrine. On the western mass, Link can find a Decayed Construct, a Tilted Platform, and a Device Dispenser. The northwestern Sky Island in the Archipelago is a three-tiered structure. The top level is littered with Decayed Constructs. A broken staircase on the eastern side leads to an opening in the middle level. The middle level is composed of several guarded rooms, which are also blocked by roots that can be cut. Zonai Devices can be found throughout these rooms. The bottom level features a lone cage controlled by a Light-sensitive Switch. Areas Device Dispenser Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Zonai Devices Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

is a recurring location in . East Gut Check Rock goes unnamed in . Features and Overview East Gut Check Rock is located northeast of Gut Check Rock in the Eldin Canyon. It is a series of shallow Hot Springs, which will heal Link if he stands in them. Several dead Trees can be found on the surrounding land. A Black Hinox is situated on a small piece of land at the center of East Gut Check Rock. It will initially be asleep, but if Link disturbs the Hinox, it will wake up and begin to attack him. Enemies Creatures Materials

East Hyrule Castle is a recurring location in . Features and Overview East Hyrule Castle is an island located east of Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field, surrounded by the Hyrule Castle Moat and Hylia River. It is bisected by a path which leads to Boneyard Bridge and Helmhead Bridge. Hyrule Forest Park can be found on the island, in addition to one of the five Giant Columns surrounding the Castle. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests As in , East Hyrule Castle is located in Hyrule Field. The Sepapa Shrine can be found on East Hyrule Castle. In addition to this, the Hyrule Castle Moat East Chasm is hidden in a Cave on East Hyrule Castle. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Equipment Materials Treasure Chests

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The East Passage is a sprawling cavern situated in the Hyrule Castle Underground. Inside the entrance of the Passage are Wooden Boxes and Barrels, which can be broken for supplies. Link can use a Mine Cart to traverse through the tunnel. Further along in the East Passage is a room containing a Cooking Pot. A Stone Talus (Rare) can be found in the chamber where the rails end, beneath a vertical tunnel shaft. If it is defeated, an Updraft will appear where it once rested, allowing easy travel up the shaft. The shaft itself continues into a tunnel leading north, connecting to a break in the southern wall of the first floor of the Library. However, this gap is filled by Malice connected to a Glowing Eyeball, which Link must defeat in order to progress further into Hyrule Castle. Near the entrance of the East Passage, Link can find a stone Treasure Chest containing five Bomb Arrows. A ledge on the southern side of the shaft holds a Treasure Chest which contains a Shard of Farosh's Fang. Interspersed through the Passage are Ore Deposits and a Rare Ore Deposit. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found within the East Passage. If Link melts the Ice in the Water of the East Passage, he will uncover Leaves with Fairy Dust. When he interacts with them, a Korok will appear and reward him with a Korok Seed. Enemies As in , the East Passage composes part of the Hyrule Castle Underground in Hyrule Field. Due to the Upheaval, it is now a dead-end. Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The East Post Ruins are the remains of an outpost located between the Outpost Ruins and Proxim Bridge in Hyrule Field. Various pieces of furniture can be found among the wreckage of the buildings, and a Wagon that can be searched for Gems is situated along the road that runs through the Ruins. A Yiga Footsoldier may occasionally pass through the Ruins disguised as a Traveler. 100 years ago, the East Post was a settlement with a high Hylian population. Alongside Gatepost Town and Hyrule Outpost, it was used as a place to rest for travelers heading to the Great Plateau, Lanayru, or the Gerudo Desert. During the Great Calamity, the East Post was destroyed along with the rest of Hyrule Field. After passing through the Ruins, evacuees would travel through the East Post, though few survivors successfully reached Necluda. Though the buildings closer to the road have remained relatively intact, structures that are further away have been partially reclaimed by nature. Three Treasure Chests are located within the East Post Ruins. The first is a stone Chest containing an Opal can be found by moving aside two metal doors in the northeastern building with Magnesis. A second stone Chest holding a Traveler's Bow is located in a corner of a ruined structure near the center of the Ruins. Lastly, a third stone Chest lies in the south of the westernmost building, and it contains a bundle of 10 Arrows. In Master Mode, a wooden platform held aloft by Sky Octoroks appears due west of Proxim Bridge, atop which is a metal Treasure Chest which containing an Iron Sledgehammer. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles can be found at the East Post Ruins. The first is a group of Leaves with Fairy Dust atop the Big Flag northwest of Proxim Bridge. The second is an Archery Puzzle, taking place at a Tree Stump marked by a Pinwheel on the north end of the Ruins. When Link solves each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Equipment

is a recurring location in . East Reservoir Lake goes unnamed in . Features and Overview East Reservoir Lake is located in the Lanayru Great Spring, which is part of the Lanayru Region of Hyrule. Its southern end is secured by the Rutala Dam, and it feeds Water into both the Zora River and the Rutala River. Before Divine Beast Vah Ruta is calmed, its Rain will constantly fall over East Reservoir Lake. Every 10 years, Lanayru faces heavy Rainfall that would previously wash away the Zora of Zora's Domain. During the Era of Prosperity 10,000 years before the events of , the Zora and the Hylians joined forces to create East Reservoir Lake in a single year, which would protect Hyrule Kingdom from floods. Ever since then, the Kings of the Zora have maintained the promise to manage its Water level, making East Reservoir Lake a symbol of the bond between Zora's Domain and the rest of Hyrule. The Zora have appointed monitors to alert their king if the Water ever exceeds acceptable levels. When Divine Beast Vah Ruta was reactivated following the second Great Calamity, it took up residence in East Reservoir Lake. Its ability to generate Water caused heavy Rain to fill up the Lake. King Dorephan began to fear that it would soon burst, which would put the lives of the Zora and the Hylians downstream of the Lake in danger. As a result, Sidon left Zora's Domain in search of a Hylian to help them. During the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" Main Quest, Sidon tells Link to meet him at East Reservoir Lake once he has gathered at least 20 Shock Arrows. Once Link arrives, Sidon will ensure that he is prepared before they face Divine Beast Vah Ruta. When Link confirms that he is ready, the pair of them will jump into the Lake to begin their attack on the Divine Beast. After Link has halted the flow of Water from Divine Beast Vah Ruta, it will remain dormant in East Reservoir Lake until it is reclaimed. Once this has been done, Mipha will pilot the Divine Beast out of the Lake through the Rutala Dam. The northern dam of East Reservoir Lake has bedroom that is intended for visitors to use. It includes a Bed and Jars. It also houses a Treasure Chest that contains a Knight's Shield. Creatures Treasure Chests Areas Other Appearances As part of the "Regulating the Reservoir" Quest, it is revealed that the Zora have been using Divine Beast Vah Ruta to manage the Water levels of East Reservoir Lake. When the Warriors bring provisions to the workers, they are able to finish work on the Reservoir earlier than anticipated, allowing them time to upgrade the Divine Beast.

East Rutimala Hill is a recurring location in . Features and Overview East Rutimala Hill is situated between Rutimala Hill and Meadela's Mantle in the Gerudo Highlands. It is part of a Freezing Climate, and so Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit it without taking damage. At its center is a large Updraft, which allows Link to Glide to nearby landmarks like Rutimala Hill, Meadela's Mantle, and the Risoka Snowfield. Creatures Materials East Rutimala Hill returns in . It is still located within the Gerudo Highlands' Freezing Climate, requiring Link to have at least two levels of Cold Resistance to traverse it without taking damage. Enemies Sub-Bosses

is a recurring General Store in . Features and Overview East Wind is a General Store located in Hateno Village. The Store is run by Pruce and Ivee. Pruce sells goods inside the Store, while Ivee stands outside sweeping and calling people inside. Three Beds can be found on the second floor, which is where Ivee, Amira, and Azu sleep at night. Ivee's Diary also rests on a table by the side of her Bed. Celessa, a Hylian traveler, stops at East Wind while visiting Hateno Village. The produce sold by East Wind is supplied by the farmers of Hateno Village. Pruce himself makes the Store's Arrows and Bomb Arrows. As Link enters East Wind, he will be welcomed by Pruce. However, when Link first visits the General Store, Pruce will be turned away from the shop desk. If Link approaches him, he will be shocked, apologizing for not hearing him come in. Pruce then asks if his stock is where he left it. On subsequent visits, Pruce will greet Link and ask what he needs. At the end of their conversations, Pruce tells Link to come back in the future. To make a purchase from East Wind, Link must select one of the Items laid out in the Store. Whenever Link buys Items from East Wind, Pruce will be excited and thank him. If Link buys the entire stock of one Item, Pruce will compliment his choices, even remarking on how many Rupees he seems to have. Wares and Pricing Ivee can be seen sweeping outside of the East Wind. Wares and Pricing

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Eastern Abbey is a ruin surrounding the Ja Baij Shrine on the eastern edge of the Great Plateau. The Eastern Abbey contains several Fallen Guardians, which can be looted for Ancient Materials. The formal entryway to the Ja Baij Shrine is blocked by a Cracked Wall. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests Korok Seeds The Eastern Abbey can be found on the eastern end of the Great Plateau. The Abbey has been heavily affected by the Upheaval, which caused the Great Plateau East Chasm to open up and Fallen Debris to fall from the Sky onto the Surface. The Decayed and Fallen Guardians have disappeared, though the mounds of dirt that they were placed on remain. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Korok Seeds

is a recurring location in . Eastern Daval Peak goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Eastern Daval Peak is located east of Daval Peak in the Gerudo Highlands. It is part of Hyrule's southern border, and as a result, Link cannot travel south beyond it. The Oseira Plains and Nautelle Wetlands can be found directly to the west of Eastern Daval Peak. A Stalnox resides on Eastern Daval Peak. It will be inactive during the day, but at night, it will patrol the area and attack Link if he approaches. A Moonlight Scimitar, a Great Thunderblade, and a Knight's Halberd are lodged into the Stalnox's body, and they will drop upon its defeat. Creatures Materials

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Egg Puddings are made by combining Fresh Milk, a Bird Egg, and Cane Sugar in a Cooking Pot. When eaten, they heal six of Link's Hearts. They also sell for 20 Rupees. They are made by cooking eggs and milk in a special mold, and they are known to have a soft texture that melts in one's mouth. Link can find a recipe for Egg Pudding written in Ivee's Diary. In it, Ivee lists the ingredients as some Bird Eggs, a few bottles of Fresh Milk, and several servings of Cane Sugar. Though she knows Cane Sugar is difficult to come by, she states that the dish will not work without it. By using additional ingredients, different variations of Egg Pudding can be made: Hearty Egg Pudding: Eating one will heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum number of Hearts. Additionally, they sell for 40 Rupees. Energizing Egg Pudding: When eaten, Link's Stamina Wheel will be refilled. They also heal him for four Hearts and sell for 40 Rupees. Enduring Egg Pudding: Not only will these restore Link's Stamina Wheel when eaten, they will also overfill it. They heal Link for five Hearts and sell for 40 Rupees. Hasty Egg Pudding: If eaten, these will temporarily increase Link's movement speed. They restore three Hearts to Link's Life Gauge, and they'll sell for 50 Rupees. Spicy Egg Pudding: Eating one will temporarily increase Link's Cold Resistance by one level. They also heal four Hearts in his Life Gauge, and they can be sold for 30 Rupees. Electro Egg Pudding: They grant Link one level of Shock Resistance when consumed. They also heal him for four Hearts, but they sell for 40 Rupees. Mighty Egg Pudding: When eaten, they'll temporarily boost Link's attack power. They also heal for four Hearts, and they can be sold for 40 Rupees. Tough Egg Pudding: Eating one will temporarily increase Link's defense. In addition, they'll heal four Hearts in his Life Gauge, and they sell for 40 Rupees. Sneaky Egg Pudding: When eaten, they'll grant Link a temporary Stealth boost. They also restore four Hearts to his Life Gauge, and they're worth 30 Rupees when sold. Chilly Egg Pudding: Eating one increases Link's Heat Resistance by one level. They also heal Link for seven Hearts and sell for 40 Rupees. Other Appearances

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Egg Tarts can be made in a Cooking Pot by combining Tabantha Wheat, a Bird Egg, Cane Sugar, and Goat Butter. When eaten, they will restore four of Link's Hearts, though they can also be sold for 30 Rupees. It is said that one knows when this dish is done baking due to its delightful smell. By adding a fifth Ingredient, different variations of Egg Tarts can be made: Hearty Egg Tart: Eating one will completely restore Link's missing Hearts, in addition to temporarily increasing his maximum Hearts. They can be sold for 50 Rupees. Energizing Egg Tart: If eaten, these will restore a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. They will also heal him for five Hearts and are worth 50 Rupees when sold. Enduring Egg Tart: Eating one of these dishes will completely refill Link's Stamina Wheel and temporarily increase his maximum Stamina. They also restore six of his Hearts and sell for 50 Rupees. Hasty Egg Tart: These tarts temporarily boosts Link's movement speed. They will also heal him for five Hearts, and they can be sold for 50 Rupees. Spicy Egg Tart: When eaten, they will temporarily increase Link's Cold Resistance for one level. They will also heal him for five Hearts and sell for 50 Rupees. Electro Egg Tart: If they are eaten, they will temporarily increase Link's Shock Resistance. They also heal him for five Hearts, and they sell for 50 Rupees. Mighty Egg Tart: Eating one will temporarily boost Link's attack power. They will also heal five of his Hearts, and they sell for 50 Rupees. Tough Egg Tart: They grant a temporary Defense boost when eaten. They restore five of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge and are worth 50 Rupees when sold. Sneaky Egg Tart: Eating them will temporarily increase Link's Stealth. They also heal him for five Hearts and sell for 50 Rupees. Chilly Egg Tart: If they are eaten, these tarts will temporarily increase Link's Heat Resistance by one level. They will also heal four of his Hearts, and they sell for 50 Rupees. Egg Tarts return from . Their Recipe remains unchanged, requiring Link to Cook a Bird Egg, Cane Sugar, Goat Butter, and Tabantha Wheat together. Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Eightfold Blades are kodachi forged with Sheikah Ancient Technology, thought to be among the sharpest Weapons ever made. These swords belong to the Sheikah Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created by the Sheikah. They can be found in West Necluda and around Lake Hylia, particularly near the Sheikah town of Kakariko Village. They can also be found in Treasure Chests that spawn after scanning the Series Sheik amiibo with the amiibo Rune. Since Eightfold Blades are made of metal, they can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate. They also attract Lightning when equipped during a Thunderstorm, and they conduct Electricity. Eightfold Blades will not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Eightfold Blades deal bonus damage when performing Sneakstrikes. Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Eightfold Longblades are two-handed Weapons passed down through the Sheikah tribe. This makes them part of the Sheikah Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Weapons created by the Sheikah. They have a sharp edge that makes them ideal for slicing. They are commonly found in West Necluda and the Lanayru Great Spring, particularly around Kakariko Village. They also have a chance to appear in Treasure Chests spawned after scanning the Series Sheik amiibo with the amiibo Rune. Like the Yiga-made Windcleaver, the Eightfold Longblade has a charged attack distinct from other two-handed Weapons. Rather than spinning, Link will draw the Longblade back before slashing forwards with considerable speed, knocking large Enemies over and sending smaller ones flying. Since they are made of metal, Eightfold Longblades will attract Lightning when equipped during Thunderstorms and conduct Electricity. They can also be picked up using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate, and they will sink if dropped in Water. Finally, they will not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Eightfold Longblades are capable of generating gusts of Wind. Unlike in , they are the primary Weapon used by Yiga Blademasters. Other Appearances

The is a recurring character in . Biography The Eighth Heroine is a rumored eighth member of the Seven Heroines. The Heroines are known as the divine protectors of the Gerudo people. The Eighth Heroine is still worshiped by those faithful to her. Although massive statues of the Seven Heroines can be found at the East Gerudo Ruins, the Statue of the Eighth Heroine is found in the northern Gerudo Highlands. This Statue plays a role in the Side Quest, "The Eighth Heroine", given by Bozai. Though the Eighth Heroine was wiped from history and is not proven to exist, Bozai sends Link in search of its Statue. After Link shows Bozai a picture of the Statue, he can receive another Side Quest from Bozai titled "The Forgotten Sword", where Link must find the Statue's missing Sword on the southeastern section of Gerudo Summit.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Eldin's Flank is an expansive cliff in the northern part of Eldin Canyon. It sits at the very edge of northern Hyrule, bordering a vast pit that serves as the end of the kingdom. The Flank sits on the other side of a mountain range that slopes downward from Death Mountain. The area is largely a mountainous wasteland that is deserted of life and has very little substance. The cliff stretches further to the west and extends to the Eldin Mountains. To the west of the Flank is a bombable wall that conceals a lone Rock inside. Lifting the Rock will reveal a Korok who will then give Link a Korok Seed. Further west are a pair of block formations. Pushing the missing piece into one of the formations causes another Korok to appear, who also gives Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

, also known as the Eldin Region, is a recurring Region in . Features and Overview Eldin is a vast Region in northeastern Hyrule. The Region is split into two distinct halves. The eastern side is a largely mountainous stretch of land that consists densely of foothills, deep gorges, and volcanic activity. It consists of two areas: Eldin Canyon and Death Mountain. The Eldin Mountains run north of Eldin Canyon and west into northern Central Hyrule. The Eldin Canyon is the largest of all these areas, covering almost the entirety of southern and eastern Eldin. The Eldin Region initially starts off as a partially wooded and even road furthest to the south. Further to the northeast and closer to Death Mountain, the land grows increasingly perilous with harder terrain and volcanic activity, particularly beginning in the Mountain Road. As Link nears this area, the Temperature grows exceedingly hot and causes Link and any wooden Gear equipped to catch on fire. Link can withstand the high Temperatures by consuming Food or Elixirs that grant Flame Guard, or by wearing any of the Flamebreaker Set, allowing him to safely travel through the hotter climate. Some areas such as Death Mountain and the Abandoned North Mine, are even hotter and require Link to either wear at least two Flamebreaker pieces, or to wear one and consume a Flame Guard Food. The northernmost area of Eldin is a barren, dead wasteland that sits along the ends of Hyrule. This area extends to the northwest through the Eldin Mountains. Due to its hotter climate, eastern Eldin hosts a number of Hot Springs that will gradually recover Link's health as he swims through them. Certain items will begin to burn as they are placed on the ground in the Region's volcanic areas as well. Through this, it is possible to grill certain Food. As very few people can naturally withstand the intense heat without the aid of Food or Armor, eastern Eldin is home almost exclusively to the Goron Tribe, who live in Goron City in east-central Eldin. Creatures well adapted to the climate, such as Fireproof Lizards, Hotfeather Pigeons, and Eldin Ostriches, also inhabit the Region throughout. Eldin is also a major resource of Gems which are found inside Ore Deposits, and also has a high abundance of Luminous Stone Deposits. During present events, eastern Eldin is plagued by the Divine Beast Vah Rudania. As Link enters the Region to quell Vah Rudania from Calamity Ganon's influence, he eventually meets the Gorons Bludo and Yunobo as part of the "Divine Beast Vah Rudania" Main Quest. Link and Yunobo band together to scale Death Mountain to weaken the Divine Beast, allowing Link to board it and regain control of Vah Rudania after defeating Fireblight Ganon. Areas Areas Other Appearances

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Eldin Canyon is a vast area within Eldin, comprising of almost the entirety of the Region. The Canyon primarily covers southern and central Eldin, and stretches to the far northeast along the ends of Hyrule. The southern portion of the Canyon is a valley with rolling foothills that borders along Great Hyrule Forest, Hyrule Field, and northern Lanayru. A road paves through this section before forking between Eldin proper and Lanayru. This winding road then leads to the Foothill Stable before continuing into central Eldin. The valley is initially even and partially wooded, especially toward the west, however, further north it increasingly turns more rugged and mountainous closer to central Eldin. The central portion of Eldin Canyon has harder terrain with steep cliffs and deep gorges. Further to the north and closer to Death Mountain, the landscape turns more perilous due to the area's high volcanic activity. Eruptions caused by Death Mountain have formed multiple bodies and rivers of lava around the area, as such as Darunia Lake and the moat that surrounds Death Mountain. Due to the intense climate, the Temperature grows exceedingly hot here, and puts Link in danger of catching fire along with any wooden Gear that is equipped. The high Temperature can be remedied either by consuming Food or an Elixir that grants fire resistance, or by wearing any one of the Flamebreaker Set. The road that paves through central Eldin Canyon eventually leads to Goron City, the home of the Gorons, before continuing to the Abandoned North Mine and finally Death Mountain. The northernmost portion gives way to a mountainous, barren wasteland that has little to no substance. This area borders along the very edge of Hyrule as a steep, bottomless cliff known as Eldin's Flank. Eldin Canyon shares much of this landscape with the Eldin Mountains to the west. Throughout Eldin Canyon, a number of bodies of water close to Death Mountain are Hot Springs, and will gradually recover Link's health as he stands or swims in them. Climates Areas Following the dormancy of Death Mountain, the Lava flows formerly present throughout Eldin Canyon have solidified into igneous rock and the majority of the Canyon is now safe to travel through. Only the Caves are hot enough to require Flame Guard. Areas Materials Treasure Chests Other Appearances

is a location in . Features and Overview The Eldin Canyon Skyview Tower is a Skyview Tower in Eldin Canyon. When Link uses the Tower, he will be launched into the Sky, allowing him to Scan Map data for a majority of the Eldin and the Eldin Sky. Following this, Link can launch himself into the Sky from the Tower at any time. After activating the Tower, he will also be able to Warp to its Travel Point. When Link first arrives at the Eldin Canyon Skyview Tower, he will find Sawson standing outside of its closed doors. If Link speaks to Sawson, he apologizes for the mess in the area. He goes on to explain that the Tower was hit by a piece of Fallen Debris, which caused the lid on top of it to fall off and jammed the doors. He theorizes that using the Terminal inside would fix the doors, but he is unsure how to reach it. He also advises Link that Ruins Rubble commonly falls in the area and warns him to be careful. By using Recall on the Ruins Rubble from the Eldin Canyon Sky, Link can gain enough altitude to reach the open hole on top of the Skyview Tower. Alternatively, he can Climb the Tower. Once inside the Tower, Link can try to open the doors, and although he will fail, Sawson will be shocked by his presence. After activating the Skyview Tower with his Purah Pad, the doors will finally open. Sawson thanks him for his help, resolving to take a break before moving on to his next job. Afterwards, Link will be able to freely use the Eldin Canyon Skyview Tower.

The Eldin Great Skeleton is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Eldin Great Skeleton is a giant skeletal landmark in the Eldin Mountains. The skeletal remains are of an extinct Leviathan. The remains consist of a flat skull and a ribcage that are partially buried underground. A small Monster Stronghold is located beneath the Skeleton. The Eldin Great Skeleton becomes a point of interest during the "Leviathan Bones" Side Quest, where Link is sent by Akrah and his brothers to take pictures of the three Leviathan skeletal remains around Hyrule. Akrah requests a photo of the Eldin Great Skeleton. Creatures Enemies Normal Mode Master Mode Equipment Korok Seeds The Eldin Great Skeleton now features eye sockets, with one stone eyeball present. The Monster Outpost that was here is no longer present, and more varieties of Creatures can be found here as well. Additionally, Spiny Bones can be found along the ground surrounding the Eldin Great Skeleton. During the Side Quest, "Eldin's Colossal Fossil", the traveler Loone sets up a Tent east of the Eldin Great Skeleton while on a tour to visit the Fossils of Giant Leviathans. However, she is disappointed that the Skeleton's left eye is missing from its socket. This stone eye can be found in a pile of Hard Sediment beneath the skull of the Skeleton. Link can receive a Purple Rupee, valued at 50 Rupees, from Loone by placing it back into its socket. Creatures Enemies Materials

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Eldin Mountains are a mountain range in far northwestern Eldin. Its mountains stretch to the far west of northern Hyrule toward Hebra, directly north of the Great Hyrule Forest. The range extends as far as Mount Drena and the Forgotten Temple. The range is a highly mountainous area, consisting densely of tall peaks, steep foothills, and difficult terrain. The Mountains border along the northern ends of Hyrule, where a vast, bottomless cliff, an extension of Eldin's Flank of the Eldin Canyon, runs beside it. The eastern range consists largely of a dead and barren wasteland, characterized by its dead trees and scattered skeletal remains. This landscape is also shared with northern Eldin Canyon. Further towards the west, the Eldin Mountains gradually turn more lively with grassy foothills and a few trees, but remains rugged for most of the entire stretch. Mountain Goats and Maraudo Wolves inhabit the Mountains throughout. Climates Areas Areas Other Appearances

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Electric Chuchus are a variation of Chuchu most commonly found in the Gerudo Desert and East Necluda. Electric Wizzrobes and Thunder Wizzrobes are also able to summon them. They are known to have an aura of Electricity. If Link touches or is attacked by an Electric Chuchu, he will be shocked. Electric Chuchus will emit an Electrical blast when they lunge towards Link, which can shock him if he is within range. Should Link have any metallic Weapons equipped, he will drop the Weapons and receive double the damage. After releasing their shock, Electric Chuchus will temporarily enter a "powered-down" form, marked by a darker yellow color. During this period, they cannot release additional shocks and can be struck without Electrocuting Link. After a few seconds, Electric Chuchus will re-charge themselves and return to their electrified state. If they are defeated while in their powered-up state, they will explode in an electrified blast that will electrocute any vulnerable entities within its range. As a result, the Hyrule Compendium recommends fighting them with ranged Weapons, such as Spears or Arrows. Electric Chuchus will drop Yellow Chuchu Jellies upon being defeated. Drops Electric Chuchus are a greenish-yellow variety of Chuchu imbued with Electricity. Small, medium, and large Electric Chuchus are found throughout Hyrule, primarily in Faron, the Gerudo Desert, and both East and West Necluda. They also appear on the Thunderhead Isles in the Sky. Gloom-Wreathed Electric Chuchus of all three sizes can be found in the Depths. In addition, they can be summoned by Electric and Thunder Wizzrobes. Electric Chuchus are immune to damage from Electrical sources, such as from Shock Emitters, Due to being covered in Electricity, Electric Chuchus damage Link by electrocuting him when he touches them or attacks them with a metal Weapon. They can also electrocute the area around them in any body of Water they touch, damaging anything inside. They attack by jumping at their target, discharging a burst of Electricity when they land and then turning a darker shade of yellow with brown spots. In their inactive state, they will not attack and can be safely touched. Upon death, they explode in a burst of sparks that can damage other Enemies. If they go into Water that reaches up to their Eyes, they will spasm and then explode in a burst of Electricity. Concentrated Light from Dazzlefruits or Mirrors causes them to leap up into the air and temporarily lose their Electrical charge. While being exposed to this Light, their gel churns violently. Muddle Buds make them attack nearby Enemies, while Puffshrooms cause them to lose the ability to see Link. Electric Chuchus drop Yellow Chuchu Jellies in varying amounts, based on their size. Electric Chuchus in the Depths drop Zonaite. Other Appearances Electric Chuchus reappear in , acting the same way as in . The Giant variants reappear in the game through the Downloadable Content missions, attacking by rolling towards the player, slamming down, and releasing the small

amounts, based on their size. Electric Chuchus in the Depths drop Zonaite. Other Appearances Electric Chuchus reappear in , acting the same way as in . are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Electric Darners can be found on Hyrule Ridge and in the Gerudo Desert. Beedle also sells them at Riverside Stable. They can be used with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot to make an Electro Elixir, which will temporarily provide Shock Resistance to Link. The Kochi Dye Shop accepts Electric Darners as an ingredient for Yellow Dye. During the "Little Sister's Big Request" Side Quest, Link finds out that Gleema likes dragonflies, despite her sister's fear of them. When Jana hears this, she asks Link to obtain an Electric Darner and other dragonflies for Gleema's birthday on her behalf. Upon delivery, however, Jana will become disgusted by the dragonflies and asks Link to give them to Gleema for her. Gleema will be excited about her dragonflies and rush to show Jana, which causes her sister to shriek in terror. Afterwards, she will give him a Silver Rupee as a reward. Electric Darners are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

, also known as , are recurring Enemies in . They are an electrified variant of Keese. Characteristics Thunder Keese are similar to the fiery variant of Fire Keese, but differ as they have electrified bodies as their main form of defense. They inhabit the Lanayru Desert area, and like other electrified enemies in that region, they produce small bursts of electricity that will stun and harm Link if he strikes one while it is shrouded in electricity. Though Thunder Keese are weak, they can be dangerous in large groups as they may constantly electrocute Link, giving him little opportunity to defend himself. A safe and effective way to eliminate them is to use the Shield Bash technique, knocking them to the ground, then finishing them with the Fatal Blow. Electric Keese appear in , most commonly is Regions such as East Necluda, the Lanayru Great Spring, and the Gerudo Desert. They can be found hanging from the ceilings of caves at all hours of the day, but they also fly around at night. In addition to this, Electric Wizzrobes on Thunder Wizzrobes are capable of summoning Electric Keese. Their Electric bodies are noted to make them more dangerous than regular Keese. When attacking Link, they have the ability to shock him, which will stun him and cause him to drop any metal Weapons he may be holding. Upon their defeat, Electric Keese can drop Keese Eyeballs or Electric Keese Wings. Drops Electric Keese in are identical those in . They can be found most commonly in the Gerudo Desert, with Gloom-Wreathed variants also appearing throughout the Depths. Electric Keese attack similarly to regular Keese, but they also have the ability to shock Link. Such attacks will stun him momentarily and cause him to drop metallic Weapons, Bows, and Shields he has equipped. Each strike from an Electric Keese deals two Hearts of damage to Link. Upon defeat, Electric Keese may drop Electric Keese Eyeballs and Electric Keese Wings. Electric Keese are Electricity-surrounded Keese that appear in areas with heavy Rain. When summoned as an Echo, Electric Keese have an Echo cost of four. Other Appearances left|100px Electric Keese appear as Enemies in . Electric Keese appear as Enemies in . They often drop Electric Keese Wings or Keese Eyeballs upon defeat. Killing one also rewards the Warriors with a Keese Trophy at the end of a Challenge or Scenario. Electric Keese can often be found in Challenges or Scenarios that are electric-themed or take place in the Yiga Clan Hideout.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Electric Keese Wings are dropped by Electric Keese upon their defeat. Like other Monster Parts, they can be Cooked with critters in a Cooking Pot to make Elixirs. They can also be sold to Kilton at the Fang and Bone for Mon or used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Yellow Dye. Electric Keese Wings are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: The Climbing Set requires Electric Keese Wings to be Enhanced to its second tier by a Great Fairy. Other Appearances right|100px Electric Keese Wings can often be obtained by defeating Electric Keese. They can be used to raise the Weapon-level limit of a Weapon, remove any or all Seals on a Weapon, Octo-Polish a Weapon, or complete certain Quests. They can also be commonly sold for 6 Rupees and sold specifically to Segimo for 15 Rupees.

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Electric Wizzrobes are a type of Wizzrobe that are often found skipping around Ruined Houses throughout Hyrule Kingdom. They are most common on Hyrule Ridge and in West Necluda. They have yellow eyes and wear white robes with a yellow hood. Electric Wizzrobes wield a Lightning Rod, which can shoot balls of Electricity or summon Electric Chuchus and Electric Keese. When an Electric Wizzrobe spots Link, it waves to him before initiating battle. They will often become invisible and reappear before attacking Link with their Lightning Rod. When invisible, they can be tracked by the trail they leave with each step. If Link is struck with the Lightning Rod's Electricity, he will drop any metal Weapons he has equipped. This can be avoided by using Weapons made from wood or Ancient Technology. Electric Wizzrobes drop their Lightning Rods upon their defeat. Instead of a Lightning Rod, Electric Wizzrobes now carry a Zonaite Sword that has been Fused to a Topaz. Electric Wizzrobes are Electricity-using Wizzrobes. They attack by shooting blades of Electricity at their targets, then teleporting in a puff of smoke to a nearby location. Electric Wizzrobes are vulnerable to being set on Fire and drowning in Deep Water. When summoned as an Echo, they have an Echo cost of five. Other Appearances left Electric Wizzrobes appear as enemies in where they move to the beat of the music. They tend to act as medium- to long-range combatants for Cadence, Link, Yves, and Zelda, teleporting towards them whenever they are nearby and attempt to cast magical projectiles in their direction. However, they appear for a total of seven beats between each teleport, taking two beats to fully appear and will begin charging their attack on the third. On the fourth beat, they release their magic in a straight line, with it flying on every single beat until it makes contact with something. After attacking, they will remain stationary until the seventh beat, raising their orbs to the sky in order to teleport themselves and then disappearing on the following beat. Once gone, they will remain invisible for five beats or if there is significant distance between them and the heroes, won't reappear at all until they return to the Wizzrobe's last known location. Despite their appearance, they can still be attacked while fading in and out of teleportation. During Symphony of the Mask, they are known as Skull Electric Wizzrobes and wear masks that resemble plague doctors. In , Electric Wizzrobes can cast attacks involving shocking the Warriors with electricity. Electric Wizzrobes are strong foes and they have a weak-point gauge, which can be weakened significantly by the Remote Bomb Rune of the Sheikah Slate function when Electric Wizzrobes start doing a dance midair, preparing to shock the area around them. When defeated, Electric Wizzrobes will drop greenish-yellow pellets, which can be used as Lightning Rods after collected.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can drink Electro Elixirs to gain one level of Shock Resistance. They're known to be useful against electrical attacks. Before parting at Inogo Bridge, Sidon will gift Link an Electro Elixir to show his faith in him. He notes that they have no effect on Zora, which he theorizes is due to them being made for Hylians. Electro Elixirs can be made by Cooking any of the following critters with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot: Electric Darner Thunderwing Butterfly By adding any of these electric ingredients, Link can make an Electro Elixir that will also heal him: Voltfruit Zapshroom Electric Safflina Voltfin Trout

Elements are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Other Appearances In , Elements determine the strengths, resistances and effects of Warriors and their class of Weapon. Elements are divided into five types: Fire, Water, Lightning, Light and Darkness. Elements affect certain values in battle which determine how much damage a Warrior can inflict onto an enemy, and how much damage they will receive after being attacked. Each class of Weapon belongs to its own Element as indicated by a colored symbol, which determines its inherent strengths and effects. Some Weapons, such as Sheik's Harp, can hold more than one type of Element based on the attack. Enemies and enemy Warriors in turn have their own Elemental strengths and weaknesses, and thus may receive more or less damage when attacked by a Weapon of a particular Element. How effective an Element is against an enemy depends on the type of Element they innately have; Lizalfos, for example, are of the Fire Element, and are thus weak to Water and resist Fire. In certain battles, a particular Element of a Weapon may be recommended over others, as indicated by a thumbs-up symbol next to its Element. Using a Weapon of the recommended Element will allow the Warrior to inflict more damage onto the enemies in that battle. In addition, Badges that increase a Warrior's defense in battles of a recommended Element can also be crafted at the Bazaar. In certain Adventure Mode battles, a Keep may be covered by an Elemental barrier. These barriers will continuously inflict damage onto a Warrior inside the Keep so long as the barrier remains active. These barriers can either be dispelled by rescuing an Elemental Fairy of the corresponding Element from another Keep and releasing it within the protected Keep, or by simply claiming the Keep by defeating its Keep Boss at the cost of taking damage. Elemental Effects Elemental Effects are secondary effects of a particular Element added to Weapons, each with a unique purpose. When a Warrior performs a combo attack with their Weapon, there is a chance that an Elemental Effect may occur. Elemental Effects may either boost the power of an attack or create a secondary effect that temporarily afflicts enemies hit. These secondary effects can range from continuously damaging enemies or having a longer attack range. Certain Skills can also be applied onto individual Weapons to give it a stronger bonus to the effect, such as the Fire+ or Water+ Skills. The Elemental Skills a Weapon can have will usually be of its inherent Element, although some Weapons, such as Sheik's Harp and Agitha's Parasol, can have different Elemental Skills applied to it. The Fire Element causes foes to create a small explosion when they hit the ground, damaging other nearby foes.Applying Fire+ to a weapon will increase the blast radius. The Water Element forms a bubble of water around foes' heads, causing them to take damage periodically over time.The Water+ Skill will cause the bubble to stay for longer, thus

small explosion when they hit the ground, damaging other nearby foes.Applying Fire+ to a weapon will increase the blast radius. The Water Element forms a bubble of water around foes' heads, causing them to take damage periodically over time.The Water+ Skill will cause the bubble to stay for longer, thus dealing more damage. The Lightning Element will cause the enemy to take extra damage from miniature lightning strikes with each hit until they once more land on the ground.Electricity+ makes it easier to keep enemies from hitting the ground. The Light Element increases damage the more that groups of enemies are attacked by consecutive attacks.Light+ increases the length of time the effect remains, allowing the Warrior to pick up more easily from one string of attacks to the next. The Darkness Element increases damage the more a single enemy is attacked by consecutive attacks.Darkness+ allows the Element to affect more than one enemy at a time.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Elixirs can be created by Cooking at least one Critter with at least one Monster Part in a Cooking Pot. Other Materials can also be added when Cooking to create Elixirs that can restore Hearts. All Critters and some of the other Materials are divided into Categories that determine the Elixir's effect. If the Materials used share the same Category, the Elixir produced match that Category and the strength of its effect is determined by the Potency of the Materials used. Cooking Materials from multiple Categories will produce Dubious Food instead of an Elixir. The duration of the Elixir depends on the Materials used when Cooking with each Material increasing the duration by a fixed amount. A critical success when Cooking also increases the Elixir's duration by 5:00. Elixirs can have a duration of up to 30 minutes. Materials List of Elixirs List of Elixirs

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Elma Knolls are a plateau in the Great Hyrule Forest that is situated south of Aldor Foothills and east of Lake Mekar. The Knolls create a series of flat rocks leading to a top plateau. On top of the Knolls are two Koroks. The first is located in the center of the plateau and requires Link to stand on a Tree stump with a small pinwheel placed on it. Once he does so, he must then shoot three Balloons flying around the surrounding Trees. Upon successfully doing so, the Korok will reveal himself and give Link a Korok Seed for finding him. The second Korok, in an eastern, lower section of the plateau, is simply hiding under a Rock within a ring of dead Trees.

The is a recurring location in . The Elma Knolls Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Elma Knolls Well is situated between North Hyrule Castle and the Elma Knolls in Hyrule Field. It is directly next to a Ruined House, which was inhabited by Hylians prior to the Great Calamity. Materials The Elma Knolls Well returns in , located in the same position in Hyrule Field. Its interior is comprised of two levels. The first is small, with its only features of note being a large hole in the ground and an unlit Campfire. This hole leads to the second level, which is clouded by Darkness. However, it is sparsely illuminated by Luminous Stone Deposits and a variety of glowing Materials. Much of this layer is also flooded by Water, which Link must Swim through. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Ember is a Hylian and the owner of the Riverside Stable in Hyrule Field. He can be found at the front of Riverside Stable. If Riverside Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Ember will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Ember explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Ember then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Ember instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Ember suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Ember to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Ember tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with his Horses in this way, they will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Riverside Stable, Ember will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Ember thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Ember will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Ember asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Riverside Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Ember asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Ember will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Ember insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Ember refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Ember starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Ember gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause

gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Ember gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside Riverside Stable, Ember once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by Riverside Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Ember tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Ember wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

are Items in . Location and Uses Emblazoned Shields are Shields featuring a traditional design from the Necluda Region. This design has lead to the Shield finding popularity, even though they do not provide much protection when compared to Wooden Shields. They can be found in many locations, particularly within East Necluda and the Hebra Mountains. One can be located in a Treasure Chest in the Gatepost Town Ruins near Oman Au Shrine. Alternatively, there is one at the Equestrian Riding Course. An Shield can also be obtained from Selmie if Link completes the Shield-Surfing Mini-Game between 3:00 and 3:15. Several travelers also carry an Emblazoned Shield on their journeys. Being made of wood, Emblazoned Shields will burn and eventually disintegrate if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They also float if they are dropped in Water, and they will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity. Finally, they cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Emblazoned Shields reappear in .
