is a recurring character in . Biography Emri manages a small Fruit-based General Store in the Kara Kara Bazaar. She is an elderly Gerudo with a grumpy attitude. She sells Mighty Bananas, Hydromelons, and Palm Fruits. Emri tells Link that she offers more Hydromelons than one could find in Gerudo Town. She also says that it is foolish to cross the Gerudo Desert without cooling Food. She does not see what is so amazing about the Desert. If Link speaks to Emri with the Gerudo Outfit on, she calls him an oddball for wanting to wear Gerudo outfits. Emri complains when Link buys a small amount of produce, saying he should buy them all at once. However, when Link buys out one of Emri's products, she complains that she will have to get more. If Link declines to make a purchase, Emri tells him to leave if he is going to jerk her around. Link can sell Items to Emri, though she complains about it and tells him to hurry up. She continuously asks if he is done yet. After Link is finished selling, Emri says that she wishes he would sell his Items somewhere else next time. If Link speaks to Emri while searching for the man who discovered a way into Gerudo Town, Emri will note that Link has a look on his face like he needs to talk to her. If Link exits the conversation, she asks what his deal is, but she is glad that she is not getting dragged into the drama. When Link asks about suspicious merchants, Emri thinks for a moment and says that every merchant that is not a Gerudo is suspicious to her. Emri then remembers a particular person, and she tells Link of a female merchant who frequents the General Store in the Kara Kara Bazaar Inn. However, Emri says that she is not going to poke her nose in someone's business and finishes speaking.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The En-oma Shrine can be found within the Lake Hylia Whirlpool Cave on the bed of Lake Hylia. It corresponds with the Amo-ne Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of En-oma Shrine The En-oma Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of En-oma Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Ena is a Hylian child who lives at Tabantha Bridge Stable. Throughout the day, Ena follows her mother, Banji, around and assists her with chores. In the morning, they tend to the Stable's White Goats, where she encourages one of the Goats, Mr. Goat, to eat. While Ena helps Banji with the cargo, she wants to know if Link keeps his own cargo in his pouch. She then informs Link of a rumor that the forest people can expand one's Inventory and asks if he has heard of this. If Link has heard of it, Ena declares the two of them to be friends, and she shares that people can collect the things forest children leave behind. On the contrary, if Link denies hearing the rumor, Ena claims to have heard it from a Fairy that told her to be nice to a big forest child to receive a bigger Inventory. Despite not knowing what an Inventory is, Ena believes that bigger is always better. She wonders if the big forest kid ever leaves the forest. Ena sings songs as she takes care of Tabantha Bridge Stable's Horses, one about Horses and one about poop. She learned the song about Horses from a man who came through the Stable with a Horse that she thought was cool. He also told her about a secret tunnel in the western part of Hyrule Castle that leads inside. However, the man warned her against going due to the danger of Hyrule Castle, which she relays to Link as well. Despite the speed of his Horse, Ena tells Link to avoid the Castle. During the Rain, Ena flees inside the Stable, where she sits at the end of one of the Beds with Kenyo. She considers bringing Mr. Goat inside. At the end of the day, Ena admits she is tired before she heads to sleep. Banji watches Ena as she sleeps in one of the Beds.

is a recurring character in . Biography Endai is a Hylian who travels on his Horse back and forth between Riverside Stable and Wetland Stable. He carries a Emblazoned Shield and a Traveler's Sword. At Wetland Stable, Endai briefly pauses under the tree across the road before leaving. He and his Horse rest under the shelter when they reach Riverside Stable. If it Rains during Endai's journey, he may seek refuge under the Tree on the southern side of Eagus Bridge. At Wetland Stable, Endai tries to decide whether he should head back south or continue north. Due to the danger presented by heading north, he decides to return to Riverside Stable. As he travels, Endai will sometimes speak to himself. He thinks about putting Bird Eggs in Hot Springs and how much he likes Dogs. He also reminds himself to shoot Chuchus in the eye and that Fairies can be found by cutting grass. When Link speaks to Endai, he recognizes him as a courageous adventurer from his look. He reasons that Link's "roguish look" makes him appear as though he would try to infiltrate Hyrule Castle. Getting into the Castle is one of many things Endai considers a possibility in life, among catching Insects, swimming, and sleeping. In fact, he encourages Link to do so and find that lost treasures of the Royal Family of Hyrule. Endai occasionally shares tips with Link. He mentions that Frogs and snails, which are useful for Elixirs, often come out before it rains. He tells Link to avoid Lightning by putting away metal gear during thunderstorms, though he suggests throwing metal Weapons at Enemies. He also informs Link that Fish will be attracted to ingredients that share similar properties with them, giving the example of Staminoka Basses eating Stamella Shrooms when they are thrown into the Water. According to Endai, shopkeepers sell their best wares during rain because they get less customers. Climbing during rain also isn't something he recommends, since it makes the rocks slippery. Endai also has a bit of knowledge on the Yiga Clan. He knows that their leader, Master Kohga, loves Mighty Bananas more than anything.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Endura Carrots are found at Malanya Spring, near the peak of Satori Mountain, and at the edges of Great Fairy Fountains. Eating an Endura Carrot will heal Link for two Hearts. Endura Carrots can also be roasted by a Fire to make Roasted Endura Carrots. They can also be Cooked into a Meal using a Cooking Pot to temporarily grant Link Extra Stamina. Like Apples and Swift Carrots, Endura Carrots can be fed to Horses to increase their Bond. Unlike other Foods that Horses can eat, Endura Carrots will temporarily increase the Horse's number of speed boosts granting them three extra yellow speed boosts which have a carrot icon next to them. After using up normal speed boosts and any granted by the Ancient Bridle, these extra speed boosts can be used. However, they are lost afterwards. Roasted Endura Carrots have the same effect if eaten off the ground by a Horse. If the Giant Horse eats an Endura Carrot, only its Bond will be increased, as it has no speed boosts. An Endura Carrot is required to revive a Horse via the Horse God, Malanya. If Link decides to give him an Endura Carrot, Malanya will agree to revive one of his Horses. Endura Carrots can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop as an ingredient for Light Yellow Dye. Endura Carrots are not required to upgrade any pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. Endura Carrots and Swift Carrots can be used interchangeably when Cooking. In some cases, they can also be replaced by Pumpkins. They are required for the following Meals: Like other Vegetables, Endura Carrots can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Endura Carrots reappear in , roughly the same as in . Endura Carrots are still not required to upgrade any pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. However, one must be given to Malanya in order to restore his strength. Endura Carrots and Swift Carrots can be used interchangeably when Cooking. In some cases, they can also be replaced by Pumpkins. They are required for the following Meals: Like other Vegetables, Endura Carrots can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Other Appearances Endura Carrots are a type of Material in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Endura Shrooms are a rare type of Mushroom that are dotted around the various small forests within and outlining Hyrule Field. More concentrated amounts can be found in Hyrule Ridge within the Dalite Forest and at the base of the Trees in the Seres Scablands. They can also be found in an unnamed forest behind Wetland Stable. Endura Shrooms can be purchased at the East Wind General Store in Hateno Village. Link can eat an Endura Shroom raw to restore one Heart Life Gauge. Alternatively, he can roast them near a Fire to create a Toasty Endura Shroom, which increases the amount of Hearts restored to one and a half. When used in Cooking, they grant the Extra Stamina Added Effect, which gives Link extra Stamina on top of replenishing his Stamina to full. Endura Shrooms are also one of the Materials used by Sayge to create Orange Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop in Hateno Village. Endura Shrooms, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Endura Shrooms can be found on the Sky Islands. Endura Shrooms, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Other Appearances Endura Shrooms appear as Materials in .

are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Enemies appear within the Overworld and Dungeons in . However, they do not appear until after Din is kidnapped by Onox. Many of the Enemies in also appear in . Enemies appear both in the Overworld and inside Dungeons in . Many of the Enemies from reappear in , though some of their appearances have been altered. Enemies do not appear at all in the game until Vaati opens the Bound Chest at the Picori Festival, releasing monsters into Hyrule. After Vaati is defeated by Link at Dark Hyrule Castle and Princess Zelda uses the Mage's Cap to undo the damage he caused to Hyrule, all the Enemies disappear from across the land. In , Monster is the name given to the category of most animals who harm and are hostile towards Link. Most types of Monsters have different variants that differ in strength or attacks. Color variants consist of the basic Monster and then blue, black, and silver variants of that Monster, each with an increase in attack strength and health. While playing in Master Mode, a fifth color variant is added, gold Monsters, which are even stronger than silver Monsters. When just starting the game, the Monsters encountered would consist mainly of basic Monsters with occasional blue-variant Monsters; a hidden tally of the Monsters defeated is kept by the game, and when certain milestones are hit, the Monsters scale-up to stronger color variants. For example, Link would encounter regular Bokoblins and occasional Blue Bokoblins when just barely awakening from the Shrine of Resurrection, but by the time he frees a Divine Beast, he is most-likely encountering Blue Bokoblins more often and is now encountering new Black Bokoblins. On top of color variants, elemental variants separate different Monsters by elemental abilities; the three elemental variants include Fire, Ice, and Electricity. Fire and Ice are the opposites of each other, and hitting a Fire-type Monster with an Ice-type Weapon (or vice-versa) will instantly kill the Monster. For example, hitting an Ice Wizzrobe with a Flamespear will instantly kill the Monster. Furthermore, many Monsters also have a skeletal variant that randomly appears at night to attack Link called stal monsters. These include Stalkoblins, Stalizalfos, Stalmoblins, and Stalnoxes. Their bodies are counted as a separate entity from their skull, with the latter bearing the Monsters's health bar. Generally speaking, skeletal Monsters only drop first and second tier Monster Parts and drop an arm in addition to their held Weapons upon death. Bosses In addition to regular Monsters, Bosses can be encountered anywhere throughout Hyrule at any time. Bosses that can be encountered in Hyrule include Stone Taluses, Hinoxes, and Molduga. Two elemental variants of Stone Taluses, Frost Taluses and Igneo Taluses, reside in very cold and very hot climates, respectively. Stone Taluses and all the color variants of Hinoxes can be found in the grassy plains that take up most of the Hyrule Kingdom. Unlike the other two bosses, Molduga can only be found in

Taluses, Frost Taluses and Igneo Taluses, reside in very cold and very hot climates, respectively. Stone Taluses and all the color variants of Hinoxes can be found in the grassy plains that take up most of the Hyrule Kingdom. Unlike the other two bosses, Molduga can only be found in the Gerudo Desert. The rest of the Monsters that make up the Boss category are encountered in one-time only battles; Fireblight Ganon, Thunderblight Ganon, Waterblight Ganon, Windblight Ganon, and Monk Maz Koshia are fought in each Divine Beast, Master Kohga is fought in the Yiga Clan Hideout, and Calamity Ganon is fought in Hyrule Castle. Monster Parts All Monsters drop Monster Parts when defeated, which are a class of Material. Monster Parts are grouped into three tiers, with the higher tiers only being dropped by Monsters in higher color variant tiers. (i.e. Bokoblin Horns, a first-tier Monster Part, can be dropped by any Bokoblin, but Bokoblin Guts, a third-tier Monster Part, can only be dropped by Blue Bokoblins or higher.) Monster Parts can be used to create Elixirs, upgrade Armor with a Great Fairy, or sold for Rupees. They can also be sold as the only way to obtain Mon, the currency that Kilton uses in his shop, Fang and Bone. Other Appearances (TV Series) (Ishinomori) ‎ ‎

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Energetic Rhino Beetles can be throughout the Akkala Highlands and West Necluda, particularly on Trees near South Akkala Stable and on pillars in Kakariko Village. They are also sold by the traveling merchant Bugut, who travels between Dueling Peaks Stable and Kakariko Village. Combining them in a Cooking Pot with Monster Parts will result in an Energizing Elixir. The Kochi Dye Shop can use Energetic Rhino Beetles as ingredients for Yellow Dye. When Link speaks to Beedle with at least one Energetic Rhino Beetle in his Inventory, Beedle will notice and beg to have it. He offers Food or Elixirs as a trade. If Link accepts, Beedle will be happy, as he considers finding an Energetic Rhino Beetle to be a good omen. When Link speaks to Beedle afterwards, he claims to still be excited about the Energetic Rhino Beetle. He claims that if Link has another, he should give it to him tomorrow, as he is going to be focusing on his new Energetic Rhino Beetle for the rest of the day. If Link refuses the trade, Beedle cannot understand his reasoning, as he believes the Energetic Rhino Beetle wants to be with him. Beedle then quietly schemes to have someone sneak into Link's Inventory and replace his Energetic Rhino Beetle with a more common one. Noticing Link is still listening, he asks Link to let him know if he changes his mind. Energetic Rhino Beetles are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Energetic Rhino Beetles can be found on Trees on both the Sky Islands and on the Surface. Energetic Rhino Beetles are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

The is an Item in . Location and Uses Once Link completes the In-isa Shrine, the Steward Construct that previously gave him the Purah Pad will approach him. It will explain that it forgot to give Link the Energy Cell earlier, and will present it to him. The Steward Construct will then direct Link to other Constructs on the far side of Pondside Cave, who will instruct him on its use. The Energy Cell is a device used to power Link's Zonai Devices. It is fueled by installed Energy Wells, and carried on Link's hip. Energy from the Energy Cell is consumed whenever a Zonai Device is activated, and they will restore automatically when the Zonai Device is deactivated or is too far away. If Link's Energy Cell is depleted, it will need to fully recharge before it can be used again. Zonai Charges can be used to both restore and add charge. The Energy Cell will always take the same amount of time to regenerate regardless of how many Wells Link has. The Energy Cell can be recharged by using Zonai Charges and Large Zonai Charges. If a Battery is present when a Zonai Device is activated, the energy from the Battery will be consumed until it is expended instead.

are Items in . Location and Uses Energy Wells are Zonai technology that can be made at Crystal Refineries. Link can give Crystallized Charges to the Steward Construct stationed there, and it will refine them into Energy Wells at a rate of 100 Charges per one Well. The produced Energy Wells are then added to Link's Energy Cell, with one Well filling up one third of one of the eight slots on the Energy Cell. Link first obtains the Cell with three Wells installed, and can add an additional 45. Once a total of 24 Energy Wells have been installed and the Energy Cell has run out of space, added Wells will instead add power to already-installed ones, turning them blue and allowing them to be used twice without stopping. Energy Wells are what extend the capacity of Link's Energy Cell, allowing Zonai Devices to be powered for longer. Consuming a Zonai Charge will restore exactly one Energy Well's worth of charge, and a Large Zonai Charge will restore exactly three.

is a recurring mechanic in . Overview The four Great Fairies can enhance Link's Armor once Link pays a certain amount of Rupees to restore their Great Fairy Fountains. The restorations cost 100, 500, 1,000, and 10,000 Rupees, increasing with each Great Fairy Fountain that Link unlocks. Each Enhancement requires a certain amount of Materials. Each Enhancement increases the Defense value of the Armor. The progression is consistent across Armors—all Armor with the same initial Defense value will also have the same Defense any any given Enhancement level. The progressions are as follows: At any given level, all Armor pieces in an Armor Set have the same Defense value. Most require the same Materials to upgrade and have the same Sell Price as well—these Armor pieces are listed under the name of their Armor Set. Each Enhancement requires a certain amount of Materials and Rupees. The required Rupees are 10 Rupees for ★, 50 Rupees for ★★, 200 Rupees for ★★★, and 500 Rupees for ★★★★ for all Armor except the Ancient Hero's Aspect, which requires triple the amount of Rupees for each Enhancement (30, 150, 600, 1500). At any given level, all Armor pieces in an Armor Set have the same Defense value. Most require the same Materials to Enhance and have the same Sell Price as well—these Armor pieces are listed under the name of their Armor Set.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Equestrian Riding Course is located in East Necluda. It was once used for riding Horses and practicing archery, as evidenced by the many Targets located among the ruins, though it has since been inhabited by monsters. Among the ruins in the center of the track, there is a lit Campfire, which the monsters sleep around at night. Southwest of the Riding Course's track is a small hut which houses a wooden Treasure Chest containing 10 Arrows. In Master Mode, a metal Treasure Chest containing an Eightfold Longblade appears atop a wooden platform held aloft by Sky Octoroks above the Riding Course. Destroying all of the Targets on the track will cause a Korok-themed Balloon to appear over the hut. If this Balloon is destroyed, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed for finding him. A second Korok can be found on the portion of land located furthest south of the track. Here, Link must move a large, metal door with Magnesis and lift a Rock to uncover the Korok. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Enemies

is a recurring character in . Biography Eryck is a Hylian traveler in search of self-discovery. He can be found beside a Campfire on Rabia Plain. When Link first speaks to Eryck, he asks if he heard him humming. Eryck explains that he was intending to travel to Zora's Domain, but he became lost and almost gave up. Before this could happen, however, he heard a voice coming from the Lanayru Tower, reigniting his interest. Despite this, he is unable to cross Rutala River. Link is able to ask Eryck about the locations on his journey. When asked about Zora's Domain, he shares that it is a town in Lanayru, but he is unable to reach it due to needing to cross the Rutala River. Due to how hard reaching Zora's Domain is, he decided to give up on visiting it. If Link asks about Lanayru Tower, Eryck explains that if one crosses Rutala River, they will be able to see it on the opposite bank. He claims that he heard a voice coming from the top of it, and he wonders if someone is up there. Finally, if Link asks about Rutala River, Eryck reveals that it is the widest river in Lanayru. Since it is dangerous to swim across it, Eryck suggests that Link pass it by way of Linebeck Island. Eryck has become a Wandering Merchant, and he can be found traveling between Highland Stable and Faron Woods. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring character in . Biography Essa is a Gerudo woman who works for Frelly at the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth in Gerudo Town. She can often be found sweeping the ground with her Broom. When Link speaks to Essa, she tells him that all of the Sand Seals there were trained by Frelly, making them faster and preventing them from abandoning the rider. Wild Sand Seals, on the other hand, will run off when their rider dismounts them. She feels that it is worth renting a trained Sand Seal, informing Link that Frelly puts her heart into training them. Essa also reveals that Frelly trained the Sand Seals that are used in the Sand-Seal Races. If Link asks about the Sand-Seal Races, Essa explains that Sand-Seal Racing is a Gerudo tradition where people race around a course with a Sand Seal to see who is the fastest. She tells Link to exit from the Southeast Gate of Gerudo Town and head to the right to find the Sand-Seal Rally. Though it is off topic, she adds that Frelly has been talking strangely lately and wonders why. Essa's job at the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth is part-time. Though it is difficult, she finds enjoyment in how happy the Sand Seals Sue, Nah, and Zarashi get when she puts out their food. However, she admits to feeding them too much sometimes. At midnight, Essa considers her work for the day to be done. With everything she does for the Sand Seals, the day just seems to fly away from her. According to her, whenever she lays out food for the Seals, they rush over as quickly as they can to eat it. If Link speaks to Essa while she is sleeping, she asks to be left alone. During the "EX Champion Urbosa's Song" Main Quest, Link can find Essa to the northwest of Gerudo Town with a group of wild Sand Seals. She explains that Frelly asked her to go recruit some wild Sand Seals. While the Sand Seals in Gerudo Town are faster and will wait for the rider, Essa's wild Sand Seals will run away when dismounted. She recommends renting a trained one, as she believes them to be worth it. Link can use one of her Sand Seals to ride through the Glowing Rings in the West Barrens.

Essences are recurring Items in . Location and Uses In , Essences include Heart Containers and Stamina Vessels. Link can obtain either by spending four Spirit Orbs at a Goddess Statue. Heart Containers can also be obtained by defeating Waterblight Ganon, Fireblight Ganon, Windblight Ganon, and Thunderblight Ganon. Excluding Link's intial Heart Containers and Stamina Vessels, a total of 34 Essences can be acquired in . In Downloadable Content pack, one additional Essence is available from completing the four Ancient Shrines added to the Great Plateau and obtaining their Spirit Orbs. Link can have a maximum of 30 Heart Containers and 15 Stamina Vessels in , though he cannot normally have both at the same time. Link can speak with the Horned Statue at Hateno Village to sell each of his Essences for 100 Rupees each. He may then buy his Essences back at 120 Rupees apiece, allowing him to exchange a Heart Container for a Stamina Vessel or vice versa for 20 Rupees. The initial trade that takes place as part of the Side Quest "The Statue's Bargain" does not cost any Rupees. The Horned Statue cannot reduce Link's Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels below their minimums, nor can he increase them beyond their respective maximums. In , Essences are nearly identical to their appearance in . At the start of , Link has 30 Hearts and three Stamina Wheels. However, they are destroyed by Ganondorf's Gloom and reduced to their minimums during the events of "The Awakening", requiring him to obtain Lights of Blessing and defeat Bosses to regain his Heart Containers and Stamina Vessels. Link can spend four Lights of Blessing at any Goddess Statue to acquire either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. During the Main Quest "Find Princess Zelda", Link is required to obtain a fourth Heart Container in order to open the Challenge Door in the Temple of Time. In , the total Essences that Link can acquire has been increased to 45, and Link's maximum Heart Containers have been increased to 40. Link can again speak with the Horned Statue, now located in the Royal Hidden Passage, to sell and buy back his Essences for 100 Rupees and 120 Rupees respectively. The trade made during "A Deal With the Statue" does not cost any Rupees. The Horned Statue cannot reduce Link's Essence below their minimum values, nor can he increase them beyond their maximum values.

is a recurring character in . Biography Estan is a Gerudo who manages a Stall in Gerudo Town. She sells a variety of cooked Meat. According to Maike, a merchant at the Kara Kara Bazaar, Estan is her little sister. Maike tells Link that Estan knows Hylian well, and she recommends that he stop by and meet her. When Link speaks to Estan, she greets him and asks what he eats for breakfast, lunch, or dinner depending on the time of day. If Link says that he eats Meat, Estan comments that he has good taste. If Link says that he eats vegetables, she insists that he must have meant Meat. Estan wonders if Frita, the Rito woman who stands near her General Store, has something against Meat, but she mutters that this is impossible. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Estan is very grateful and thanks Link. Estan tells Link that she once traversed across Hyrule Kingdom in search for the best Meats, which allowed her to learn common words in the Hylian language. Although Estan knows some words in Hylian, she usually mispronounces them, such as saying "tank you" instead of "thank you." When Link buys Estan's Meats, she calls it a good purchase. If Link has bought all of her stock, she thanks him for doing so. Not only does Estan sell her wares, she will also buy Items from Link. When she accidentally says "sarqso" instead of thank you, she appears disappointed. She is grateful for Link's patronage.

The , designated by the trial name Proving Grounds: Infiltration, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Eutoum Shrine is located at Goflam's Secret Hot Spring in the Hebra Mountains. It corresponds with the Muotue Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation Upon entering the Shrine, all of Link's equipment is removed (except for his Paraglider and Ancient Powers). Right inside, a Long Stick, Wooden Stick, and Old Wooden Shield is provided to Link. He is intended to defeat every Construct in the Shrine which will return his equipment and open the door to the Light of Blessing. If Link is noticed by any of the Constructs, they will sound an alarm to the other Constructs and a boss bar will appear. Treasure Chests

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Eventide Island is a small island located in the southeastern portion of the Necluda Sea. It is notable for being the site of the "Stranded on Eventide" Shrine Quest which begins once Link reaches the Island. Areas Enemies Eventide Island is an island located in the southeast Necluda Sea. A Monster Stronghold has been built upon Toronbo Beach North, and the Eventide Island Chasm has opened up on Toronbo Beach as a result of the Upheaval, leading down into the Necluda Sea Depths. At the Back of the Island, Eventide Island Cave has formed and become a hideout for the Pirates laying siege to settlements along the shores of the Necluda Sea. Fallen Debris litters the Island, having fallen from the Sky Island patrolled by a King Gleeok in the Sky above. During the "Seeking the Pirate Hideout" Side Quest, the Monster-Control Crew scout Sesami asks Link to locate and clear out the three Monster Strongholds on Eventide Island. Areas Other Appearances The Quest "Searching Eventide Island" appears on Eventide Island upon completion of the Scenario "The Future of Hyrule". To complete it, the Warriors must provide a search party with 25 Mighty Thistles, 25 Armoranths, 20 Big Hearty Truffles, 125 Wood, and 3 Hinox Trophies to help them search Eventide Island for parts that can be used to revive Terrako. When the Quest is finished, the search party successfully finds five Terrako Components.

Evermeans are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Evermeans are Monsters that disguise themselves as Trees until their prey comes within range, at which point they jump from the ground and walk on their roots to approach. They can be told apart from normal Trees because of their occasional fidgeting, though they can also be detected with the Purah Pad's Camera. Like Trees, Evermeans are weak to Fire and explosions and can be cut with bladed Weapons. Some Evermeans carry Apples or Courser Bee Honeys on their branches. Despite not having any apparent eyes or ears, Evermeans are capable of seeing and hearing Link. They are susceptible to Muddle Buds and Puffshrooms, but not Dazzlefruits. When defeated, an Evermean will drop any Materials attached to its body, as well as an Evermean Log. Additionally, they may drop Materials such as Monster Extracts and Golden Apples regardless of whether they were growing on them. They can drop Weapons such as Sturdy Thick Sticks or Gnarled Thick Sticks upon defeat. If Link tries to Climb on their trunks, they will jerk around and deal at most three quarters of a Heart's worth of damage. Evermeans in the Depths can be found primarily in large groves beneath named forests and woods on the Surface. A small group of Evermeans can also be found near the Construct Factory, far away from any named groves. When defeated, Gloom-wreathed Evermeans will drop Zonaite and may drop Dark Clumps. Other Appearances

The , also known as the , is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Phantom Ganon Armor is a piece of Armor exclusive to Downloadable Content pack. Obtaining the Phantom Ganon Armor is one part of the objective of the "EX Treasure: Dark Armor" Side Quest. The Armor was stolen from Hyrule Castle by Misko and a clue to its location can be found in Misko's EX Journal 2 at the Deya Village Ruins. The metallic Treasure Chest that hides the Phantom Ganon Armor can be found submerged in Floria River underneath Sarjon Bridge. Link must use the Magnesis Rune to pull the Chest from the River to retrieve it. When worn, the Armor provides one level of Stealth Up. The Phantom Ganon Armor cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy nor can it be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Phantom Ganon Armor, alongside the Phantom Ganon Skull and Phantom Ganon Greaves, compose the Phantom Ganon Set. When the Phantom Ganon Armor is worn with the Bokoblin Mask, Flamebreaker Helm, Salvager Headwear, Zant's Helmet, Hylian Hood, or Ravio's Hood, its cape will be removed. According to its description, it is believed that the Phantom Ganon Armor is infused with a dark entity that resembles the Great King of Evil. After obtaining the Phantom Ganon Armor, Granté in Tarrey Town will begin selling it for 50 Rupees.

Obtaining the Phantom Ganon Greaves is one part of the objective of the "EX Treasure: Dark Armor" Side Quest. The Greaves were stolen from Hyrule Castle by Misko and a clue to their location can be found in Misko's EX Journal 2 at the Deya Village Ruins. Link must use the Magnesis Rune to dislodge the Chest from the ground to retrieve the Greaves. When worn, the Greaves provide one level of Stealth Up. The Phantom Ganon Greaves cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy nor can they be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Phantom Ganon Greaves, alongside the Phantom Ganon Skull and Phantom Ganon Armor, compose the Phantom Ganon Set. According to their description, it is believed that the Phantom Ganon Greaves are infused with a dark entity that resembles the Great King of Evil. After obtaining the Phantom Ganon Greaves, Granté in Tarrey Town will begin selling them for 50 Rupees.

The , also known as the , is an Armor Set in . Location and Uses The Phantom Ganon Set is an Armor Set comprised of the Phantom Ganon Skull, Phantom Ganon Armor, and Phantom Ganon Greaves. They can be obtained through the Side Quest "EX Treasure: Dark Armor", which is available after reading Misko's EX Journal 2 in the Deya Village Ruins. The pieces of the set can be found in the following locations in the Faron Woods. Within Corta Lake Under Sarjon Bridge In Ebara Forest Each individual piece of the Phantom Ganon Set will increase Link's Stealth when worn. The full set can be worn to give Link the Disguise Set Bonus against Stalkoblins, Stalmoblins, and Stalizalfos. He'll also receive the Bone Atk. Up Set Bonus, which will increase his attack when using bone weaponry. The Phantom Ganon Set is unable to be enhanced by a Great Fairy. Similarly, it can't be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Characters who see Link wearing the Phantom Ganon Set will be temporarily frightened. It is modeled after Phantom Ganon from . Enhancing The Evil Spirit Set can be found at the end of the three Lomei Labyrinths spread across Hyrule. Enhancing

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Exchange Ruins are located in Hyrule Field. They are the remains of the Exchange, which was destroyed during the second Great Calamity. Atop a keep in the southwest portion of the Ruins, Link can find a stone Treasure Chest containing a Soldier's Claymore. A metallic Treasure Chest containing a Purple Rupee can be found embedded in the pond east of the aforementioned keep. Link can find a second stone Treasure Chest containing a bundle of 10 Arrows inside the ruined building in the northern portion of the Ruins. In the "EX Treasure: Fairy Clothes" Side Quest exclusive to The Master Trials DLC Pack, Tingle's Hood can be found inside a metallic Treasure Chest stuck in the ground at the center of the Ruins. is a recurring Added Effect in . Overview Extra Hearts is an Added Effect in and that fully restores Link's health and provides him with extra yellow Hearts that absorb damage. These Hearts cannot be restored once used, but they can be replaced by reapplying the Effect. In , the total amount of Hearts in Link's Life Gauge cannot exceed 30. The following Materials grant Extra Hearts when cooked in Meals or Elixirs: Hearty Durian Big Hearty Truffle Hearty Truffle Big Hearty Radish Hearty Radish Hearty Salmon Hearty Bass Hearty Blueshell Snail Hearty Lizard In , the total amount of Hearts in Link's Life Gauge cannot exceed 40. This figure includes Hearts that have been affected by Gloom. If Link receives Gloom damage from any source, any extra Hearts he has will all be consumed at once, after which his Heart Containers will be damaged as normal. Furthermore, if Link has Gloom-stricken Hearts when he is granted Extra Hearts, any Gloom Recovery will convert them into regular Hearts. The following Materials impart Extra Hearts in : Big Hearty Truffle Hearty Truffle Big Hearty Radish Hearty Radish Hearty Salmon Hearty Bass Hearty Lizard

is a recurring Added Effect in . are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Extravagant Bridle is a type of Bridle that can be obtained from Blynne by completing the Obstacle Course Mini-Game in less than one minute and thirty seconds. These Bridles are often utilized in festivals. They are also decorated with feathers, making them great for adding a splash of color to Horses. The Extravagant Bridle is a piece of Extravagant Gear, which is a set of Horse Gear. Link can have the Extravagant Bridle equipped onto his Horses by one of the workers at Highland Stable, Outskirt Stable, South Akkala Stable, or Woodland Stable. However, as is the case with other Bridles, they are unable be worn by Epona or the Giant Horse.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Extravagant Saddle is one of several Saddles that Link can obtain. They can be won by beating Blynne's record of one minute and fifteen seconds at the Obstacle Course. This type of Saddle is commonly used in festivals. Its delicate embroidery and Gem arrangements leaves a lasting impression, making it perfect for standing out. The Extravagant Saddle is a piece of Extravagant Gear, which is a set of Horse Gear. Link can equip the Extravagant Saddle to his Horses by speaking to workers at Highland Stable, Outskirt Stable, South Akkala Stable, or Woodland Stable. Similar to other Saddles, they are unable to be worn by Epona or the Giant Horse.

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Gohma Eyes serve as Weak Points that can be attacked using the Bow. Swarms of Eye-like creatures called Patras can be found in Level 9. Arrows fired by Link into the Eyes of certain Enemies will deal Critical Hits to them. Formations of Malice known as Glowing Eyeballs can be found near Pools of Malice throughout Hyrule. Keese and Octoroks drop Monster Eyeballs when killed. When an Arrow is fired into a Stalnox's Eye while the Stalnox is at half or less of its health, the Eye will detach from its socket, rolling around on the ground before the Stalnox picks it back up. Stalnox Eyes can be picked up and carried around by Link. The following Enemies suffer Critical Hits when struck in the Eyes by an Arrow: During the "A Call from the Depths" Side Adventure, the Great Abandoned Central Mine Bargainer Statue requests that Link return four of its Eyes to it the Depths. A large yellow Eye is found on Gohma, the Boss of the Faron Temple. It is the only part of the Boss that can be damaged, though it can only be harmed while Gohma is stunned. The Eye cannot be Learned as an Echo, but can have Bind used on it. While Bind will not move the Eye, it will hold Gohma in place until the Boss shakes off its effects. Other Appearances The Boss of the Lost Swamp, Gohmaracas, has a single Eye with a vertical slit pupil, which is the only part of its body that can be damaged. After it has been struck, Gohmaracas will close it for the next seven beats. This Eye varies in color based on how many of the Four Champions have been defeated. If Gohmaracas is the first or second Champion fought, it will be a bright yellow; if it is the third or fourth, it will instead be bright red. Defeating Gohmaracas while having only damaged its Eye with a Bow or Great Bow will grant the Achievement "The Eye of Gohma".

Fabrics are Items in . Location and Uses Fabrics are Key Items that are obtained throughout Hyrule. They are typically received as a reward for Link's endeavors, but they can also be found in Treasure Chests and as amiibo rewards. Fabrics can be given to Sayge at the Kochi Dye Shop in Hateno Village, at which point Link will be able to use the Fabric Reworking Service in exchange for 20 Rupees. They disappear from the Inventory when they are given to Sayge, though they can be chosen as a style option any time at the Kochi Dye Shop. The default Fabric style is the Ordinary Fabric. It does not appear as its own item in the Inventory and therefore does not need to be given to Sayge in order to set its design. List of Fabrics

Fairies, also known as Faeries, are a recurring race of creatures in . Most Fairies are small creatures with healing powers, and they usually fly by means of delicate, insect-like wings. Their appearances vary from game to game: in some games, such as , they resemble small orbs of light with four wings, while in others they take the form of tiny, winged humanoid females. Overview Fairies usually have one of two roles in the series. Most Fairies possess healing powers; they can restore some of Link's Hearts when he is wounded. From onwards, these Fairies can usually be caught in Empty Bottles for later use. If Link falls in battle while carrying a bottled Fairy, it will automatically come out to revive him. Groups of Fairies can be commonly found in Fairy Fountains scattered through the land, although some may also occasionally be found by breaking Pots or cutting grass. In some games such as , Bubbles and Sparks can be turned into Fairies by using Magic Powder or the Boomerang. In , Fairies can be summoned by drawing the Triforce on a Goddess Wall. In and , Link is able to pick them up and store them despite the lack of Empty Bottles, though he needs to sneak up on them to avoid detection. The second role held by Fairies is that of a traveling companion. In several games, beginning with , Link has been accompanied on his travels by Fairy companions. Although in many cases they are used to facilitate gameplay (allowing Z-Targeting, for example), they also provide advice on what to do next or how to defeat certain enemies. In other games, such as , companion Fairies also serve as the cursor for guiding Link. Fairies occasionally appear after Enemies have been defeated. Fairies fly around the screen until they make contact with Link, fully healing him upon doing so. Fairies are depicted in the game's manual as blonde-haired humanoids with red dresses. However, both their clothes and hair are depicted as red in-game due to palette limitations. Fairies sometimes appear when Monsters have been defeated. They will fully heal Link upon making contact with him. Link is also able to Transform into a Fairy using the Spell of the same name. Doing so allows him to fly past Enemies and through Locked Doors. Fairies are depicted as pink-haired humanoids in blue dresses that congregate within Fairy Fountains throughout Hyrule. In addition to appearing from slain Enemies, Fairies can emerge from bushes, Pots, and Rocks. Link can capture Fairies in Empty Bottles by using a Bug Net. Once captured, a Fairy will revive Link if he runs out of health, acting as an extra life. The Fairy then disappears, requiring him to either capture another one or have other bottled Fairies on hand to repeat the process. Link can also release the Fairy back into the overworld, allowing him to either recapture it or consume it to heal a large chunk of his health. Fairies occasionally

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can make Fairy Tonics by using at least one Fairy on a Cooking Pot. These elixirs harness the power of Fairies, making them able to heal some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. Therefore, the more Fairies used, the stronger their effects will be. Their fragrance is known to be sweet. Fairy Tonics are Foods that can be Cooked with Fairies at a Cooking Pot or Portable Pot. They harness the healing power of the Fairies used in their recipe to restore Hearts to Link's Life Gauge. They are known to have a sweet fragrance. Other Appearances The recipe for Fairy Tonic is earned by completing the Quest "Unexpected Discovery". It is made using one Fairy. When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warrior will be automatically revived once after being KO'd.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Falcon Bows are highly refined Bows made by master Rito craftsmen. These Bows belong to the Rito Gear equipment archetype. They have a quick rate of fire, which Rito warriors favor for use in aerial combat. Falcon Bows are found both in Treasure Chests and in the hands of Enemies on the Tabantha Frontier and in the Hebra Mountains. During the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, Teba will allow Link to take a Swallow Bow he has modified from a nearby Treasure Chest for their fight against Divine Beast Vah Medoh. The following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Falcon Bow when they are scanned with the amiibo Rune: Series Link (Archer) amiibo Series Revali amiibo Being made of wood, Falcon Bows will burn if they are exposed to Fire or equipped in a Scorching Climate. In addition, they will float if they are dropped in Water, and they will not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms. Finally, they cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Falcon Bows appear in . Other Appearances The Falcon Bow is primarily used by Teba. When he arrives in the past, he uses it to shoot Arrows at Windblight Ganon's cannons to intercept its attack on Revali. He also uses it against the Guardians that were aiming at Revali.

is a recurring character in . Biography Falmark is a Hylian who travels between Rito Stable and Snowfield Stable. He carries a Wooden Shield. At both Stables, he momentarily sits at the tables inside. At Rito Stable, Falmark will admit that Rito Village is too much for him, since he is afraid of heights. However, this fear does not apply to mountains, as he knows he can Shield Surf down. At Snowfield Stable, Falmark claims he is staying there while he prepares to head up the Hebra Mountains. A former Shield Surfing champion who lives in the Mountains told him not to make light of his journey. When Link seems worried about him, Falmark assures Link of his plan. He offers to share stories from when he was young as Link walks with him. He also asks Link to Shield Surf with him. Falmark is a Shield Surfer, claiming to be a rather famous one. He takes it upon himself to give Link some tips for Shield Surfing. For example, he informs Link that Shields will not break if he surfs on Snow or Sand, but they will on any other terrain. Baumar, another traveler, refers to Falmark. He claims that Falmark saved him in the Hebra Mountains, though he has difficulties remembering his name. Falmark himself may comment on this event, saying that he was around Link's age and Surfing down the Mountain with a kid on his back was tougher than he expected. Originally, Falmark got into Shield Surfing to impress ladies. Since then, he has become obsessed with it and wants to participate in the competition at Hebra East Summit. Falmark wants to see the Hebra Great Skeleton on the Hebra North Summit. He claims that Shield Surfers consider seeing the Skeleton to bring happiness. There is a competition he hears is held in Hebra that he also wants to enter. When he is encountered on the road, Falmark will ask Link if he is planning to go to the Hebra Mountains. He recommends imagining the feeling of surfing down the hill while climbing up, it makes the journey easier. According to him, the tougher the climb is, the better the ride back down. Along his journey, Falmark may be attacked by not only Enemies, but Wolves as well. When this happens, he wishes someone would take care of them and remarks how this ruins his plans. If Link saves him, Falmark may thank him or comment on his strength. He gives him Enduring Veggie Rice Balls initially, later giving him Rupees. Falmark is a Hylian traveling between South Akkala Stable and Bloodleaf Lake on Horseback. While he is riding toward Shadow Pass, he speaks to himself about wanting Misko's Treasure. If approached by Link, he asks if he would like to hear about the Treasure. He then admits he does not currently have anything to share about the Treasure, and explains that he went west of Akkala to visit the Treasure-Hunting Brothers at Cephla Lake Cave,

about wanting Misko's Treasure. If approached by Link, he asks if he would like to hear about the Treasure. He then admits he does not currently have anything to share about the Treasure, and explains that he went west of Akkala to visit the Treasure-Hunting Brothers at Cephla Lake Cave, but they refused to speak to him. Then, he tells Link, he traveled to Malanya Spring to wish for help from the Horse God Malanya, adding that if his wish is not granted, he can simply return and ask again. are recurring Items and Objects in . Fans go unnamed in and . Location and Uses Fans appear inside the Shadow Temple and Inside Ganon's Castle. They operate on timed intervals and when active, they generate strong gusts of wind that can push Link in whichever direction they are facing. Link can resist Fans by wearing the Iron Boots, or he can gain additional distance from them by wearing the Hover Boots. Several rooms in the House of Gales contain large Fans built into the floor, which allow Link to be blown to a higher level of the Dungeon. Several rooms of the Dungeon contain wall-mounted Fans that can either hinder Link by blowing him off of his path, or help him by allowing him to cross gaps or reach other areas. In some instances, Link must use the Tornado Rod to enter the path of the Wind emanating from a Fan. Two of the Treasure Hunter Caves feature Fans as well. In the cave near the Haunted Grove, Link must descend into a deep pit by floating with a Cucco, while avoiding the blasts of Wind from several wall-mounted Fans. In the cave near Misery Mire, he must again use the Tornado Rod to traverse the cave's upper sections after activating the Fans by stepping on Floor Switches. Fans appear in several Levels of the Sky Realm, where they create Updrafts that lift the Links into the air, allowing them to reach higher ledges or cross gaps. Some Fans are always active, while others must be turned on with a Switch or temporarily activated by firing the Gust Jar at them. The Mini-Boss of the Sky Realm, Gigaleon, can be stunned by activating a Fan as it flies overhead. Gigaleon can then be attacked by throwing a Bomb into the Updraft, and later, by throwing one of the other Links to launch him up to the Mini-Boss to strike it directly. Fans are Zonai Devices that originate from the Sky Islands. However, they can also be found on the ground below. When they are struck, Fans will activate and generate strong gusts of wind that can propel Link in whichever direction they are pointing. However, Fans require energy from Link's Energy Cell or a Battery, or it will stop operating if it runs out of power. Fans can be deactivated by striking them once more. Fans can often be found near Logs to build Rafts or near Mine Carts to power them.. They can be bonded to Objects with the Ultrahand ability, creating a larger Object that will be propelled forward. On its own, an active Fan will not fly in a straight line. However, attaching two Fans together gives them a stable flight path. A single Fan generates enough thrust to propel Link plus a Steering Stick into the air, and a Battery is able to power a Fan for about 25 seconds.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Farmer's Pitchforks are sharp, light tools used to easily collect hay. However, Link can use them as Weapons against Enemies. They are most common around villages, such as Hateno Village, and Stables in East Necluda and West Necluda. With their metal prongs, Farmer's Pitchforks will attract Lightning when they are equipped during a Thunderstorm and conduct Electricity. They will also sink in Water, but they can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate. Finally, they will not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Farmer's Pitchforks reappear in . Link can Fuse Farmer's Pitchforks with other Weapons to create long range Weapons. Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Farming Hoes are a tool used by farmers to till their fields, and as a result are found near Hylian settlements and ruins in East Necluda and Hyrule Field. Regular Bokoblins may also wield them as Weapons. They can be used as two-handed Weapons by Link, though their application in battle is untested. Farming Hoes belong to the Daily Use Goods equipment archetype, which is a series of tools that double as Weapons for Link. Due to their metallic components, Farming Hoes will attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms and conduct Electricity. This also makes them magnetic, which means they can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. They sink if they are dropped in the Water, but they will not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Other Appearances

The , also stylized as the Faron High Road, is a recurring location in . The Faron Highroad goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Faron Highroad is an expansive road that begins in the Taobab Grassland in the Gerudo Highlands, continues into the Faron Grasslands and West Necluda, then ends at Lurelin Village in East Necluda. It passes through the Oseira Plains, Nautelle Wetlands, Darybon Plains, Harfin Valley, Fural Plain, Faron Woods, Pagos Woods, Floria River, Sarjon Bridge, Sarjon Woods, Floria Bridge, Ebara Forest, and Atun Valley before ending at Lurelin Village. Several encampments can be found along the Faron Highroad, such as the Mounted Archery Camp, Highland Stable, and Lakeside Stable. The travelers Chumin, his Donkey, Letty, Spinch, and his Horse who is also named Spinch frequent the Faron Highroad between Highland Stable and Lurelin Village. Other travelers can be found on smaller portions of the Highroad. Between Highland Stable and Lakeside Stable, Link can encounter Meeshy and Totsuna. Beedle can also be found along the Faron Highroad near Highland Stable and Lakeside Stable. Finally, Regan is found along the Faron Highroad near a broken down Busted Wagon in Atun Valley, where he is being attacked by a Blue Bokoblin. When Link saves him, he will receive Meals and Rupees as a reward. Kass can be encountered playing his bandoneon along the Faron Highroad in the Pagos Woods. When Link approaches, Kass will greet him. He reveals that he knows an "Ancient Song" pertaining to the area, which he offers to play for Link. The "Ancient Song" describes a Dragon in the forest, where an Ancient Shrine can be found. After listening to Kass, the Shrine Quest "The Serpent's Jaws" will begin. After the Main Quest "Seek Out Impa" has been completed, a Traveler can be found along the Faron Highroad in Atun Valley. As Link passes by, they will beckon him closer with the promise of wares to buy. When Link speaks to them, they claim to have Mighty Bananas for sale. If Link agrees to shop, the Traveler will speak highly of their wares. One bundle of Mighty Bananas costs 99 Rupees. When Link makes a purchase, the Traveler will thank him and encourage him to buy more. Link can also choose to buy all 99 bunches of Mighty Bananas in stock, for a total of 9,801 Rupee. Should Link agree to this deal, the Traveler calls him a Banana fan. Afterwards, Link will be unable to buy Mighty Bananas. Following their transaction, the Traveler says they would like for Link to come back later, though they reveal this to be a lie. Alternatively, if Link refuses to buy any Mighty Bananas, the Travele} will be shocked and demand that he make a purchase. If Link again refuses, the Traveler accuses him of hating Bananas. , also known as the Southern Wood, and the Skulltula Forest, is a recurring location in . As its name suggests, Faron Woods is part of and makes up a large majority of the overall Faron Province. It is home to one of the province's two protectors, Faron the Spirit of Light. The other protector from , Faron the Water Dragon, is located in the nearby Lake Floria. Faron Woods was known as the Kokiri Forest in . Features and Overview Link first enters Faron Woods looking for Talo, who ran off chasing a Monkey. Talking to Coro will result in Link obtaining a free Lantern as part of a special offer, which serves to aid the young hero on his way through a cave that leads to the northern section of Faron Woods. Link eventually makes his way to the entrance of the Forest Temple, where he rescues Talo and a Monkey from Bokoblins. However, the next time Link enters Faron Woods, it is covered in Twilight, and he is pulled in by a Shadow Beast. The Triforce symbol on his hand shines, causing the beast to drop him. Link turns into Wolf Link for the first time and falls unconscious shortly after, leaving him to be dragged to Hyrule Castle by the Shadow Beast and imprisoned. When he returns to the Twilight-covered Woods, he is tasked by Faron the Spirit of Light to restore light to the Woods by collecting its Tear of Light. After doing so, Link is restored to his Human form. Faron tells Link that he must obtain the Fused Shadow in the Forest Temple to counter Zant. Since more monsters have begun appearing around the Woods, Link will have to talk to Coro to obtain the Small Key that will open up the cave's gate that leads to North Faron Woods. After Link obtains all three Fused Shadows, Zant ambushes him at Lanayru Spring, cursing him to be trapped in his Wolf form and gravely injuring Midna. Link takes Midna to Princess Zelda, who heals Midna and tells Link that the only way to break the curse placed on him is to obtain the Master Sword, located in the Sacred Grove deep within Faron Woods. The entrance to the Sacred Grove is located near Trill's Shop, where Link must stand on a ledge and jump through various Tree roots with the help of Midna From there, the young hero must continue to jump around various obstacles and eventually reach the hidden Sacred Grove. Obtaining the Mirror Shard from Snowpeak will force Link to once again return to Faron Woods and make his way to the Sacred Grove to retrieve the next Mirror Shard in the Temple of Time. Faron Woods is connected to the Ordon Woods via the Ordon Bridge, built over a large chasm between the two regions. The woods are comprised of southern and northern portions, the latter being the location of the Forest Temple. The northern section of the Woods is

the Temple of Time. Faron Woods is connected to the Ordon Woods via the Ordon Bridge, built over a large chasm between the two regions. The woods are comprised of southern and northern portions, the latter being the location of the Forest Temple. The northern section of the Woods is largely uninhabited, with its only residents being Coro and Trill. To get to the northern section, Link must pass through a cave in the southern section of the Woods that leads to a bigger section of the Woods infested by Deku Babas, Keese, and Bokoblins. Areas Faron Woods is the first place Link visits on the Surface after departing from Skyloft. While on Zelda's trail, Link searches for members of the Kikwi race using the Goddess Sword's Dowsing ability, finding them hiding from the invading Red Bokoblins in many places throughout the forest. Upon discovering each one of these plant-like creatures, the large Kikwi elder Bucha gives Link the Slingshot. With the slingshot, Link is able to continue on to the deeper part of the forest known as Deep Woods, and later the Skyview Temple. Link visits Faron Woods for the second time while on his quest for the three Sacred Flames to temper his blade. The Woods are now infested by stronger and deadlier demons, including Blue Bokoblins and Moblins, suggesting that the seal on The Imprisoned is weakening. Link completes Farore's Silent Realm Trial and receives the Water Dragon's Scale as a reward. It allows Link to dive deep beneath the water for a limited time and gives him special maneuvering abilities in the water. Link is able to enter the Great Tree and proceeds to climb to the top of the large canopy towering over the surrounding Faron Woods. It is there that Link meets a Kikwi hermit named Yerbal. Yerbal reveals the location of the entrance to Lake Floria to Link. Lake Floria, despite being sealed off from the outside world, seems to be in a troubled time. Ghirahim, leading a group of large fish known as Cranioc, attacked the Water Dragon Faron, mortally wounding her and scaring many of the local Parella into hiding. After venturing with a Parella known as Jellyf through the underground tunnels of the lake, Link meets Faron, who is recuperating from her wounds in a Water Basin. Faron asks Link to return to Skyview Spring through the Skyview Temple to retrieve some Sacred Water to heal her wounds. After Link does so, Faron is healed and reveals the entrance to the fourth dungeon, the Ancient Cistern behind the Floria Waterfall, where Farore's Sacred Flame is found. Link visits Faron Woods for the third and final time to find Faron in order to learn one of the four parts of the "Song of the Hero". However, the Woods are completely flooded. order to learn one of the four parts of the "Song of the Hero". However, the Woods are completely flooded. Link locates Faron inside the Great Tree and learns that she flooded the Woods to clear out the monsters in the area. As a final test, she makes Link search the flooded Woods for her musical notes, called Tadtones, so that he can learn her part of the Song. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Farosh's Scales can be collected from the Dragon Farosh, who typically flies around Lake Hylia, Lake Floria, and the Gerudo Highlands. The first time that Link strikes Farosh, it will yield a Scale regardless of where it was struck, whereas after that he must strike the main portion of its body to receive the Scale. is a recurring Dragon Spirit in . Characteristics Farosh is one of three roaming Dragons in Hyrule Kingdom, the others being Naydra and Dinraal. She is the servant of the Spring of Courage, and she has been described as a Spirit of Lightning that takes the form of a Dragon. According to old legends, Farosh flies into the sky when the sun begins to set, but no modern accounts of such an occurrence exist. While she cannot be defeated, Farosh does not actively try to harm Link. However, if Link gets too close, he will be damaged by the Electricity surrounding her body. This can be avoided by wearing the Thunder Helm or the full Rubber Armor Set that has been enhanced twice by a Great Fairy, both of which grant Link the Lightning Proof Set Bonus. Farosh will drop different Materials if Link shoots her with a Bow. Depending on where Farosh is shot, she will drop a Shard of Farosh's Horn, Shard of Farosh's Fang, Farosh's Claw or Farosh's Scale. After being shot, the Dragon will disappear until the next in-game day. Farosh's Scale can be dropped into the Spring of Courage to reveal a hidden Ancient Shrine. is a recurring Armor Shop in . Features and Overview Fashion Passion is the local Armor Shop of Gerudo Town. The Shop sells the complete, Gerudo Outfit is sold here at a total of 540 Rupees, which is 60 Rupees cheaper than what Vilia sells them for. The Gerudo Outfit here has also been Dyed white, as opposed to the regular coloring that Vilia sells. According to Saula, this is because it is currently trendy for Gerudo women to dye their clothes. She explains that one can do so at the Kochi Dye Shop in Hateno Village. Though Link already has a Gerudo Outfit, Saula suggests that he buy more sets in order to have different colors. Through the doorway behind Fashion Passion is a curtain, which conceals an entrance to the Gerudo Secret Club. If Link attempts to enter, Saula stops him, telling him that the doorway is not for customers. She then whispers that he should use the door on the side of the building if he is a member of the Club. As Link passes by Fashion Passion, Saula will beckon him over. When Link makes a purchase from the Armor Shop, Saula will thank him. She will also give Link fashion advice, which includes wearing all pieces of an Armor Set together and Dyeing clothes. If Link buys the entire Gerudo Outfit that Saula is selling, she will once again suggest Dyeing. Wares and Pricing Fashion Passion has moved outside the Kara Kara Bazaar Barracks in the Kara Kara Bazaar. Wares and Pricing

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Feathered Edges are lightweight, double-edged swords forged by Rito craftsmen, designed so that Rito warriors can soar into battle unaffected by their weight. They belong to the Rito Gear equipment archetype, a grouping of Weapons with Rito origins. Feathered Edges are primarily found on the Tabantha Frontier. A Feathered Edge can be found inside Treasure Chests in Rota Ooh Shrine and at Dragon Bone Mire. In addition, two Blue Lizalfos on the Tabantha Frontier equip a Feathered Edge. One can be found just south of Kolami Bridge at a Monster Stronghold, while the other is hiding in a path north of Kolami Bridge. The Lizalfos and the swords reappear every Blood Moon. In Master Mode, another Treasure Chest can be found containing a Feathered Edge at the Waterfall in Hebra Plunge. Being made of metal, Feathered Edges will attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms, and they are capable of conducting Electricity. They will not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate, but they will sink if they are dropped in Water. They can be picked up and manipulated using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate. When swung, Feathered Edges create a gust of wind that launches Enemies back. Other Appearances An ancient version of the Feathered Edge appears as a One-Handed Weapon. One is wielded by Vence as his default Weapon. The Knight Construct is also able to utilized Feathered Edges during combat.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview At Riverside Stable, Link can find Teli looking into the Cucco pen, panicking about how much trouble he is in. If Link asks what is wrong with him, Teli initially fears that he has been caught, but he tells Link off after realizing his mistake. He recognizes that Link was the one who saved him and his friends during the "Gourmets Gone Missing" Side Adventure, and as a result, he wonders if he is willing to help him again. Teli reveals that he wanted to eat the Bird Eggs laid by the Stable's six Cuccos, but he accidentally scared away five of them. Although they are still in the vicinity, they run away whenever Teli gets close to them. He claims that he needs to return them before a Stable Worker notices, at which point "Feathered Fugitives" will begin. Riverside Stable's Cuccos can be found at the following locations: The stage where the Stable Heroes perform. On top of a large Tree south of the Stable. On top of a piece of Ruins Rubble in the Hylia River. Inside the Stable. On top of the Stable's Horse head. Once all of the Cuccos have been returned, Teli will be shocked to see them. He is relieved that Link managed to retrieve them all, though he is embarrassed to have been saved by him yet again. To ensure Link's silence on the matter, Teli gives him a Silver Rupee. Afterwards, "Feathered Fugitives" will be completed. Objectives

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Feathered Spears are Weapons created by Rito craftsmen. These spears belong to the Rito Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Rito-made Weapons. They are lightweight and made of sturdy materials, which allow Rito warriors to use them in aerial combat. The guards of Rito Village, Gesane and Mazli, wield them. They are also used by Enemies on the Tabantha Frontier and in Hyrule Field. Being made of metal, Feathered Spears will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms. They will sink if they are dropped in the Water, but they can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. If they are exposed to a Fire or a Scorching Climate, they will not burn like wooden Weapons do. Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Fegran is a Gerudo woman who can be found standing just past the front entrance of Gerudo Town. If Link speaks to Fegran, she congratulates him on making it to Gerudo Town with the Divine Beast Vah Naboris roaming the Gerudo Desert. Fegran goes on to explain that the Gerudo chief assures the Town that everything is alright, but the Divine Beast still makes her feel uneasy. If Link asks about the chief, Fegran explains that Lady Riju became chief after her mother, the previous chief, passed away. Fegran says that Riju inherited the throne because she was their previous chief's only child. Fegran heard that the Town's troubles have been causing Riju and her advisors to worry. If Link asks about the Divine Beast, Fegran says that Link must have seen it on his way there. She explains that it suddenly appeared a few weeks ago and that it strikes lightning at those who come near it. Fegran also recounts a story that Naboris was once a god who protected the Gerudo Desert 100 years ago, but she is not sure whether to believe the story or not. Before finishing speaking, Fegran warns Link not to get too close to the Divine Beast Vah Naboris. After Link calms Naboris, Fegran will say that she is relieved that the Divine Beast is calmed, but she is still worried that it will start stomping around again.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview "Fell into a Well!" is begun when Link speaks to a Hylian named Dillie inside the Rebonae Bridge Well. He explains that he had previously dropped something in the Well and used a Ladder to retrieve it, which broke when he tried to Climb back up. Additionally, he says that his friend, Jora, failed to realize that he was stuck, and that it would be possible to reattach the broken part of the Ladder if the upper half was not out of reach. Link can reconnect the broken part of the ladder using Ultrahand, although Dillie will be unable Climb it if it is still too high off the ground. When the Ladder reaches low enough, Dillie and Link will leave the Well. Dillie will reward Link afterward with a Purple Rupee, and he warns Link not to fall into any Wells in the future. He will also tell Link of his plans to apply for the Zonai Survey Team with Jora. The Side Quest will then be completed. Objectives

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Fierce Deity Armor is an Outfit that was added in the Ver. 2.0.0 update of . It is obtained by completing the Den of Trials for the first time. When worn, the Fierce Deity Armor will double the power of Link's Sword and also allow Link to shoot four Sword Beams in a cross shape when the Sword is swung, provided his Hearts is full. The Sword Beams can be alternatively be fired from the Sword when performing a Spin Attack, even when the Hearts is not full. Additionally, Link will remain steadfast at all times and won't get knocked back from Enemies while wearing the Fierce Deity Armor. Any Links who join the game through Download Play will be unable to obtain the Fierce Deity Armor. The Fierce Deity Armor is a piece of Armor in . It is obtained by scanning the Link amiibo with the amiibo Rune. According to its description, the Fierce Deity Armor is the same armor as the one worn by Fierce Deity Link in the Era of the Hero of Time. When worn, the Fierce Deity Armor provides one level of Attack Up. The Fierce Deity Armor can be enhanced by a Great Fairy, but it cannot be Hateno Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Fierce Deity Armor, alongside the Fierce Deity Boots and Fierce Deity Mask, compose the Fierce Deity Set. Enhancing Enhancing

The , also known as the , is a powerful recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Fierce Deity's Mask is one of five Masks that transforms Link when worn. It transforms Link into Fierce Deity Link, where Link has a unique, very tall adult form and voice, and allows him to manifest the Fierce Deity Sword. His attack power and range is greatly increased (roughly the same as the Great Fairy Sword), and his sword can release Sword Beams at the cost of Magic. When obtained, it is suggested to be as dangerous as Majora's Mask. Link can obtain the Fierce Deity's Mask by trading the twenty non-transformation Masks to the four Moon Children. Since the Deku Mask, Goron Mask, and the Zora Mask cannot be traded, Link must have in his possession all of the other Masks before being able to receive the Fierce Deity's Mask. Once this has been done, the young hero obtains the Mask from the child wearing Majora's Mask. He gives him the Mask so that the two of them can "play" together. It is said to possess the merits of all Masks. The Fierce Deity's Mask can only be used during Boss battles, and, in , Fishing Holes. However, its combat capabilities are disabled inside Fishing Holes, and the Fishing Hole Men will forbid Link from leaving while wearing it. The Fierce Deity Mask is a piece of Armor in . It is obtained by scanning the Link amiibo with the amiibo Rune. According to its description, the Fierce Deity Mask is the same Mask as the one worn by Link in the Era of the Hero of Time, although it no longer retains its powers that it once had. When worn, the Fierce Deity Mask provides one level of Attack Up. Like Majora's Mask, the eyes of the Fierce Deity Mask glow allowing them to be seen in dark areas such as the Thyphlo Ruins. The Fierce Deity Mask can be enhanced by a Great Fairy, though it cannot be Hateno Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Fierce Deity Mask, alongside the Fierce Deity Armor and Fierce Deity Boots, compose the Fierce Deity Set. The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses When Link equips the Fierce Deity's Mask in , he manifests the Fierce Deity Sword—a powerful blade that is able to focus Link's magical power into a disk of light and release it during an attack. As well as possessing this useful ability, the Fierce Deity Sword inflicts great physical damage — equal to that of the Great Fairy's Sword. If Link strikes an enemy while Targeting and has any magic remaining, the enemy will take damage both from the Sword itself and from the energy blast, for a grand total of eight times the destructive power of the Kokiri Sword. However, this doesn't always work on normal enemies because the sword was only ever intended to be used against Bosses. Some of these enemies will resist the secondary damage from the energy disk because its ability to break through the defenses were not programmed into these enemies. The energy beams can, however, be used against objects (i.e. Gossip Stones, Signs, etc.). Due to its double helix shape, it is sometimes referred to as the "Double Helix Sword" or "Double Helix Blade." The Fierce Deity Sword appears in as an exclusive amiibo Item. It has a rare chance of appearing in a Treasure Chest after scanning the Link amiibo with the amiibo Rune, but only after Link has completed at least one of the Divine Beasts. It functions as a two-handed Weapon and its description refers to it as a "peculiar greatsword" allegedly used by a hero from a world in which the moon threatened to fall. The Fierce Deity Sword slashes wildly in battle as if possessed by a fierce deity. It can be wielded by Link even when he is not wearing the Fierce Deity Set acquired using the same amiibo. Link can acquire replacements of the Fierce Deity Sword by using the amiibo again. Like other two-handed Weapons, it can be thrown and can also be displayed on the Weapon Mount in Link's House. It has a base attack power of 60, making it equal to the Master Sword's full Power, but its durability is at a 35, making it inferior to the Master Sword in that aspect. The Fierce Deity Sword is made of metal, and it will therefore conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if it is equipped during a Thunderstorm. It will sink if dropped in Water, but due to its magnetic nature, it can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. It also will not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. The Fierce Deity Sword reappears in .

is a recurring character in . Biography Fin is a Hylian who can be found camped out on Trilby Plain, just off the road. He is a member of the Shield Breakers, a Shield Surfing gang. Initially, he is seen scoping out a hill nearby, where he believes Russ is slacking off. Upon talking to Fin, he asks Link if he is up for Shield Surfing. Fin points him to his best friend, Russ, under a Tree on top of the hill. He then wants to know if Link will head up. If Link agrees to head up, Fin is excited and remarks that Shields were made for surfing. However, if Link refuses, Fin accuses him and cramping his vibe and says to come back after he chills out. Link will be automatically transported to the top of the hill when he agrees. Once there, Russ apologizes for Fin pressuring him into Shield Surfing, and he offers him Shields to buy. After several rounds of Shield Surfing, Fin calls Link a Shield Surfing junkie. Fin and Russ went to Selmie's Spot the receive Shield Surfing training from her. Due to a blizzard over Hebra Mountains, they can't go outside though. When Link arrives there, he informs him, that Selmie doesn't take any more students at the moment and that he should return once the weather conditions improved. He wields a Wooden Shield.

The Final Boss, much like in any video game, is the last obstacle standing in the way of the lead protagonist's mission. Often, the final Boss is the mastermind behind the plot of the game, much like the role Ganon recurringly plays in . Whether their plan is to take over the world, gain the true force of the Triforce, or rid the land of peace and serenity, this final showdown is the antagonist's ultimate chance to destroy the hero. Ganon is the most popular Boss of the Zelda franchise, but the games have seen a variety of different lead antagonists. The final Boss often has a puppet, or minion who precedes him, like Zant in or Agahnim in , who appeared to be the primary antagonist of the game until the plot took an unexpected turn storyline-wise, revealing the main antagonist to be a larger, more influential figure, such as Ganon himself. Recurring Final Bosses Ganon right|200px Ganon is the most frequently recurring final Boss of the series, namely because his ties to the Triforce and to Hyrule itself outweigh any other antagonist in any other Zelda title. As the wielder of the Triforce of Power, Ganon assumes an incredible strength, not only physically, but magically as well; his ability to transform the land and its atmosphere to suit his dark desires is a power used in a more positive light by his representative goddess, Din. Throughout the series, Ganon exists in human form as Ganondorf, in pig form (weilding a Trident in some incarnations), and even in beast form in , using different aspects of the Triforce of Power to morph into stronger, more menacing monsters. Ganon is the Final Boss in: and (In the Linked Game) (As Yuga Ganon) Other Appearances 's attraction Vaati right|200px Vaati is the second-most recurring antagonist in the Zelda series, only after Ganon, appearing in a total of three games. Vaati is a Minish wind mage who uses his dark magic to get his way, in his search for the Light Force of Hyrule through selfish motives. Like Ganon, Vaati also can change form, last of which being his intimidating "Wrath" phase. Vaati only appears as an antagonist, however, whenever Link is forced to pull the Four Sword from its pedestal in the Elemental Sanctuary, releasing his spirit, only to be sealed back into the sword during the game's finale.
