Overview thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of a Steward Construct on the Great Sky Island.|The Steward Construct As Link explores the Great Sky Island after leaving the Room of Awakening, he will come across a Steward Construct that reactivates when he approaches it. It recognizes him, claiming that Princess Zelda left something for him with it. A compartment within the Steward Construct slides open, revealing the Purah Pad. It claims that the Purah Pad will be useful for navigation. When Link takes it into his hands, it opens to a Map of the Great Sky Island. The Steward Construct informs Link that Princess Zelda is waiting at the Marker indicated on the Map. Link then asks where they are, and the Steward Construct explains that they are in the Garden of Time. It points out the Temple of Time nearby, which it claims hosted rites for Hyrule in the ancient past. However, it reveals that no one has visited recently. The nearby Terminal activates, and the Main Quest "Find Princess Zelda" will begin. By following the Marker, Link will find himself in front of the Temple of Time. He apologizes for startling Link, and he introduces himself as Rauru, the source of Link's new Right Arm. "" is a Main Quest in . Overview After facing Phantom Ganon during the "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" Main Quest, Link and the Sages return to Purah and Lookout Landing, who is able to determine that Princess Zelda was making preparations for their fight against Demon King Ganondorf in the ancient past. She believes that they could be missing a hint that she left for them. Sidon agrees with her, claiming it is important for them to act now. However, Riju is concerned by their lack of leads. Purah remembers that in all of their stories, Six Sages were involved in the Imprisoning War, and excluding Zelda, only four of them are accounted for. Riju and Tulin are amazed, though Yunobo is confused. Sidon then voices that they are missing one Sage. In a flashback, Mineru can be seen fighting alongside her fellow Sages. Back in the present, Purah states that this is a lead they must follow, wondering if the final Sage could be within ruins from the ancient past. Riju decides that they should start by searching these ruins. Purah directs the Sages to search for clues in their respective Regions, while she asks Link to find leads on his own. After they leave, "Find the Fifth Sage" will begin. At Kakariko Village, Link can inform Paya and Tauro of the Phantom Ganon pretending to be Zelda. Tauro realizes that the Floating Ring Ruin may be a threat to Demon King Ganondorf in some way, and since the Order of Princess Zelda no longer stands, they are now able to investigate. Following this revelation, "Secret of the Ring Ruins" will start. During "Secret of the Ring Ruins", Link opens a Challenge Door and enters a chamber on Dragonhead Island. Inside, he finds the Zonai Relic, which shoots a beam of light toward Tobio's Hollow when interacted with. He will then hear the voice of Mineru, telling him to take the Relic and follow the light. Afterwards, "Secret of the Ring Ruins" will be completed, and "Guidance from Ages Past" will begin. During "Guidance from Ages Past", Link reawakens Mineru as the Sage of Spirit, which he must then report to Purah. Though she is initially shocked, Purah is excited to hear they have gathered all five Sages. She is also relieved to hear of Zelda's actions in the distant past, which have restored the Master Sword in the modern day. To find the Master Sword, Purah suggests that Link visit the Great Deku Tree in the Great Hyrule Forest. Afterwards, both "Find the Fifth Sage" and "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" will be completed. is a recurring character in . Biography Finley is a Zora from Zora's Domain. She can be found running around the Domain, upset that her mother Kodah will not let her go to the Bank of Wishes to send a letter, because of Divine Beast Vah Ruta. Finley says it is condescending for her mother to still treat her like a child. She is at that awkward Zora age where she is a young woman but still has not had her growth spurt yet. Finley believes she will never grow taller and laments that it is awful to be herself sometimes. She doubts that Hylians have to deal with such nonsense since they age so fast. If Link asks who she is, Finley introduces herself and says all the other girls are "head over flippers" for Sidon, but she believes everyone has their own special prince out there waiting for them. When asked about the Bank of Wishes, Finley explains that it is a location halfway down Zora River. She goes on to say that if a letter is sent down the Zora River from the Bank of Wishes and there is a reply, that person will be theirs forever. When questioned about the letter, Finley reveals that she has a pen pal who she communicates with by tossing a letter in a bottle down Zora River. After the Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been appeased, Kodah is unable to find Finley, who apparently told her mother that she was going to find a prince of her own. Because of this, Finley can be found at the Bank of Wishes, where she asks her Love Letter to carry her thoughts. When she notices Link, she asks if he has a wish for the Water Fairy too, before realizing he does not have a letter. Finley then wonders if Link is a servant of the Water Fairy. If he agrees with Finley's statement, she will tell him not to make fun of her just because she is a cute girl. If Link says he is a traveler, Finley will express excitement. Either way, Finley will request Link's help. She asks Link to follow her Love Letter when she releases it down the River to know whoever picks it up. Finley says to report back to her so she can find out what kind of person received it. She explains that she cannot do it herself because her mother does not want her to venture too far. Finley begs Link to find the person who picks up the letter. Finley then throws the Letter into the Zora River and asks if he is ready, warning Link that the Letter container breaks easily. This initiates the "Special Delivery" Side Quest. After following the Love Letter, a Hylian man named Sasan receives it. He reveals to Link that he was traveling to Zora's Domain when he received the first Letter from Finley. Ever since, he has been corresponding with her by having travelers take

This initiates the "Special Delivery" Side Quest. After following the Love Letter, a Hylian man named Sasan receives it. He reveals to Link that he was traveling to Zora's Domain when he received the first Letter from Finley. Ever since, he has been corresponding with her by having travelers take his replies to Zora's Domain. Sasan admits that he lied to Finley in his responses, claiming to be a buff traveler, and he cannot meet her without revealing the truth. If he knew that he would fall for her, he claims he never would have lied. With Link's encouragement, Sasan decides to pursue the sender. Afterwards, Finley can then be found back in Zora's Domain listening to Sasan tell her his traveling stories. She tells Sasan that Link was the one who helped make sure her Love Letter arrived safely. Finley thanks Link for introducing her to her soul mate. After discussing it, the two decided they would thank him when they next saw him, and so they give him a Gold Rupee. Finley tells Sasan to be sure to Swim, Climb, and lift so he can build up the muscles he promised her. Finley laughs while she talks with Sasan. When Link speaks to her during this time, she claims to be discussing important things with him, such as how many siblings he has and his favorite Foods. She also encourages him to Swim so he can build up his muscles. Sasan agrees, saying he will Swim as fast as he can for her. On her own, Finley tells Link about how gorgeous and great Sasan is. She reminds Link to say hello to Sasan when he arrives. At night, she tells Link it is time for kids like him to go to Bed and that he should sleep soon. She sleeps in the lowest pool in the Sleeping Chamber.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Fir River is located in East Necluda. The Fir River is fed by Lake Jarrah and flows into the Squabble River. Along its banks, Link can find several Ore Deposits. A cluster of boulders has landed over the body of the Fir River in one segment, and though this doesn't inhibit the flow of the River, it does prevent Link from sailing down the River with the Raft from Lake Jarrah. The Fir River runs beside the Equestrian Riding Course and eventually cuts into the Cliffs of Quince, where it becomes the Squabble River. Enemies

are recurring Enemies in . They are visually distinct from other types of Lizalfos due to their red and orange coloration. Incarnations of normal, green-colored Lizalfos from previous Zelda games can breathe fire, but in , only this variety can do so. Characteristics Fire-Breath Lizalfos are one of the elemental variants of the Lizalfos race. They most commonly reside in the Gerudo Desert and Eldin Canyon, though they have also been spotted in certain areas of Akkala. Like other Lizalfos, Fire-Breath Lizalfos are also capable of disguising themselves to blend in with their surroundings. In addition to the agility typical of Lizalfos, Fire-Breath Lizalfos can breathe a stream of Fire. Hitting them with Ice-based attack, however, will result in them being instantly defeated. If they are defeated, Fire-Breath Lizalfos will drop Lizalfos Talons, Lizalfos Horns, and Red Lizalfos Tails. Drops Other Appearances

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Fire Chuchus are flaming Chuchus that appear in hot places, such as the Eldin Region. Fire Wizzrobes and Meteo Wizzrobes are also capable of summoning them. They leave trails of Fire behind them as they move, igniting flammable materials such as Grass. Fire Chuchus come in three different sizes, with their strength correlating to how large they are. Fire Chuchus attack by dashing forward and emitting a blast of Fire around them. If hit by their attack, Link will be temporarily set on Fire, but this can be avoided by wearing the full Fireproof Armor for the Fireproof Set Bonus. After attacking, Fire Chuchus temporarily lose their fiery coating and become a darker color, leaving them vulnerable. If they are defeated while on Fire, they will explode with a fiery blast. As a result, the Hyrule Compendium suggests fighting them at a distance by utilizing Spears or shooting Arrows. Fire Chuchus drop Red Chuchu Jelly after being defeated. Drops Fire Chuchus reappear, acting the same as in . Gloom-Wreathed variants are also present in the Depths, typically appearing in fiery locations such as the Eldin Canyon Depths. Other Appearances Fie Chuchus reappear in , first appearing in. They act the same as in and drop Red Chuchu Jelly upon their defeat once again. The Giant variants reappear during the Downloadable Content Missions, attacking players by rolling around, spinning their bodies, slamming down into the ground, and releasing small Fire Chuchus.

Fire Keese are recurring Enemies in . They are a variation of Keese that are enveloped in fire. Fire Keese behave identically to their regular counterparts, but are significantly more dangerous as they can potentially set Link on fire upon contact. They inhabit volcanoes, dungeons, and other fiery environments. In some games, Fire Keese can revert into an ordinary Keese when their flames are extinguished, most often by an item that produces wind. This may also prompt them to intentionally fly into fire, such as a Torch or another source of fire, thereby turning them back into a Fire Keese. Characteristics and Fire Keese made their first appearance in and . They are most commonly found within dungeons, and often near Torches. Fire Keese fly around the area in small colonies, and attack by swooping down at Link when they spot him. However, Fire Keese are dangerous as they can set Link on fire for a short period of time upon contact, and can destroy wooden items such as Deku Shields and Deku Sticks if they are equipped. Inadvertently, this will also turn the Fire Keese back into a normal Keese, prompting it to seek out a Torch and set itself on fire as it flies through. Link can also turn regular Keese into Fire Keese using Din's Fire. Like normal Keese, they can be defeated with any conventional weapon. and In and , Fire Keese possess a much different strategy of attack than normal Keese, being much more aggressive. Fire Keese fly at a much higher altitude, and actively pursue Link when he is nearby to swoop down in attack. While in flight, they cannot be attacked, and become vulnerable only when they dive. Like the Fire Keese of and , they will burn Link as their bodies' flames pass to him, reverting them into a fireless Keese in the process. They will then seek out the nearest Torch to set themselves aflame. Even without their flames, the Keese will still fly at a high altitude to avoid Link's attacks. They inhabit the Skull Dungeon in , the Sword & Shield Maze in , and the Hero's Cave in both games. In , Fire Keese appear as bright orange Keese with flaming wings. They are often found in areas with high volcanic activity, such as the Dragon Roost Cavern and Fire Mountain. However, unlike in , none of Link's equipment can be burned away by their flames. The flames of a Fire Keese can be blown away by waving the Deku Leaf at them, turning them into normal Keese as they fall to the ground. are Enemies in . Characteristics Fire Like are Like Likes that can be found in volcanic Caves and Wells with Scorching Climates, as well as in the Eldin Canyon Depths. They attack by spitting fireballs at Link. Like other Like Likes, their hides are too tough to damage, but their bulbous, reddish-purple tongues are extremely sensitive, and striking them leaves Fire Likes vulnerable to attacks. Fire Likes intermittently reveal their tongues, swallowing Link if he remains in front of them for several seconds. If they swallow Link, they steal one of his Bows, Shields, or Weapons before spitting him out. If stunned in the few seconds they take to chew the stolen Item, they will drop it. They are vulnerable to being frozen by Ice- or Water-based Weapons and Arrows, which stun them, allowing their tongues to be attacked. They can also briefly be shocked by Electrical Weapons and Arrows. As with other Like Likes, Fire Likes can eat Crabs, Fish, Frogs, Fruits, Insects, Lizards, Meats, and Mushrooms. When defeated, they may drop one or two bundles of five Arrows, one to three Fire Fruits, and a Fire Like Stone, as well as any Bows, Shields, or Weapons they may have stolen. If they have not stolen any Equipment, they will instead drop an Iron Treasure Chest with contents varying based on the Fire Like's location. Fire Likes in the Depths may also drop one or two pieces of Zonaite.

The , also known as the Mountain Temple, is a recurring Dungeon in . Overview Entrance to the Temple The Fire Temple is located deep within the Death Mountain Crater. It is only accessible to Link by use of the Goron Tunic, which is given to him by Darunia's son, Link, in the hopes that he will rescue the other Gorons. Being in an active volcano, the Fire Temple is filled with many lava pits including the boss room. In the boss room is a giant rock platform where the battle takes place. Themes and Navigation thumb|left|The maze of the rolling rocks on the third floor Link's progress in the Fire Temple is based on opening jails so that the imprisoned Gorons can be freed. When a Goron is released, he gives Link a clue or tip regarding the use of the so-called special crop, although some offer other facts; Link also receives keys to open locked doors. Throughout the Temple, there are bridges and platforms over magma that must be crossed, as well as complex mazes (one of them consisting of Flame Walls). Once the Megaton Hammer is found, after defeating the mini-boss Flare Dancer, Link may use it to break obstacles or create new paths. thumb|right|The Flame Wall maze on the third floor The dungeon as a whole is notable for having a nearly-symmetrical architecture: From floor three upwards, the interior of the temple is divided into two, although Link only needs to visit the western territory to succeed on his quest (in fact, the other portion can only be accessed from the third floor by using the "Scarecrow's Song"). The Temple is home to an ancient dragon, Volvagia, who is known to have eaten Gorons in the past. Defeated by an ancient hero with the Megaton Hammer, he was resurrected by the evil Ganon. The only real defense against the dragon is the aforementioned Hammer, which Link can put in practice as soon as the dragon is hesitating in one of the fire holes placed in the battle arena's floor. Similarly to the rest of the dungeons, the Fire Temple was altered in the version of . Honoring the name of the dungeon, the first rooms require Din's Fire to light several torches. Compared to the original version of the dungeon, the redesigned layout features a lesser focus on enemies and a stronger focus on puzzles. Additionally, most make use of the Hookshot. Some invisible walls and time blocks are found in the dungeon. Also, some switches need the Spin Attack to be activated, including one that is hidden inside a crate and can't be seen. There are fewer Gorons than in the normal version as well. Most doors are blocked with iron bars, and the Big Key and Megaton Hammer come very early. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Fire Temple 1F is the base floor of the Fire Temple. Its entrance hall is blocked by a Gloom Rock, which can only be destroyed with Yunobo's assistance. When Link and Yunobo first arrive, they spot Zelda advancing to the center of the floor, which is barred by a gate. This gate is controlled by five padlocks with stone lizard heads that resemble Divine Beast Vah Rudania. Near this gate, there is a Terminal that will activate a Travel Point nearby. This Terminal also releases the gate, though the gate cannot open unless the five padlocks are released remotely from various points throughout the Temple. From its center, the Fire Temple 1F branches into the north and south. To the south, there is a room containing a river of Lava with an active Hydrant pouring into it to create moving Lava Slabs. Beyond this river, there is a larger pool of Lava blocking access to the far end of the room where a Mine Cart station sits. Two Mine Carts with Fans can be found in this station. Mine Cart Tracks lead to the south out of this room. By default, the Tracks are arranged in a loop, though a Rail Switch beside them can be struck to change the path and allow Link to access the southernmost room. In this room, there is a barrier controlled by a nearby Shock Switch. This barrier blocks Mine Carts from continuing forward along the Tracks until the Shock Switch is pressed, opening the path back north and up to the Fire Temple 2F. Another Gloom Rock sits atop the tracks leading to the next floor. When this Gloom Rock is destroyed, the barrier containing one of the Soldier Constructs on the floor above is released, allowing it to patrol the Tracks on the second floor in a circular fashion. South of these tracks, there is a Lava pit blocking access to a chamber where one of the padlocks is housed. However, this chamber is blocked by a Gloom Rock that can only be destroyed if Yunobo has a pathway across the Lava. The northern branch of the floor is barred off, and can only be accessed by Paragliding from the equivalent room on the Fire Temple 4F. Inside this enclosure, there is a Gong that releases one of the padlocks. There is also a Shock Switch that opens the enclosure, allowing for Link to enter and leave at will. Upon successfully releasing all five padlocks, Link can use the Terminal to lower the gate and create a bridge to the western room. Due to the hemispherical shape of the room, Yunobo is capable of rolling up the sides of the room to strike the Gloom Rocks on its ceiling. By doing so, the duo will reveal Marbled Gohma, the Boss of the Fire Temple. After Marbled Gohma is defeated, the Fire Temple's Secret Stone will descend from the ceiling to be claimed

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Fire Temple 2F is the second floor of the Fire Temple. It can be accessed via Mine Cart Tracks from the southern room of the Fire Temple 1F. These Tracks lead into a central room with a turntable. Opposite this turntable, there is a Rail Switch that can redirect Mine Carts northward to a barrier atop a spire of rock. This spire leads to two branching paths to the north and the west respectively. The northern path is blocked by the barrier, which can be lifted by striking a nearby Bell that controls a larger turntable in the middle of the tracks. When struck, the barrier lifts and the turntable rotates 90 degrees, allowing Link to proceed north. To the west, there is a stone suspension bridge with additional Mine Cart Tracks beyond it. Like the other Tracks, these are blocked by a barrier controlled by a corresponding Bell. When struck, this Bell lowers the Tracks from the floor above and releases the barrier to allow Mine Carts to enter a second room to the north. By following the eastern track, Link arrives at a northeastern supply room. The western track instead leads to a larger room with a pool of Lava. A ledge on the western side of this room houses an active Hydrant, which ineffectually pours Water onto a Gloom Rock. By destroying this Gloom Rock, Link can cause Lava Slabs to appear, creating bridges across the Lava. On the northern side of this room, there is a Gong that releases one of the Fire Temple's padlocks. By striking the Bell to the south while riding a Mine Cart southward from this room, Link can access the Fire Temple 3F. Enemies Equipment Zonai Devices Treasure Chests

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Fire Temple 3F can be accessed from the Fire Temple 2F by striking a Bell that controls elevating Mine Cart Tracks. The central room of the floor is a crossroads with several paths leading outward. On the eastern side of the room, there is a Shock Switch that controls an elevator platform. When struck, this Shock Switch will permanently turn on and move the elevator platform between the third floor and the Fire Temple 1F's entrance hall. This hub room also contains several Mine Carts and Zonai Devices. The southwestern Tracks provide a one-way path from the Fire Temple 4F's southwestern room, while the broken set of Tracks beside them lead into it. By striking a Switch in that room, Link can create a two-way passage between the floors. The northeastern track leads to the northern room, which in turn leads to the western room. In the western room, there is a Gloom Rock concealing a Bell that controls a turntable that connects to the central room. On the north side of the central room, there are two Bells. The western Bell controls a turntable leading to the northern room, and redirects it to connect the western and eastern rooms instead. By redirecting the Tracks, Link can access the eastern room, which houses a single Treasure Chest. Alternatively, by traveling north from the central room and striking the eastern Bell, Link can raise himself up to the Fire Temple 4F's northern rooms. By utilizing both Bells, Link can raise himself to the Fire Temple 4F's central room by traveling along the northwestern Tracks instead. Enemies Zonai Devices Treasure Chests

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Fire Temple 4F is divided into several areas connected by Mine Cart Tracks. The southwestern room can be accessed from a broken set of Tracks leading from the central room of the Fire Temple 3F. In this room, there is a Bell-shaped Switch that controls a nearby barrier and lowers a set of Tracks that bridge the gap between another set of Tracks between the Fire Temple 3F. In the entry chamber of this room, there is a ramp leading to another set of Mine Cart Tracks. Beneath these Tracks, there are two Mine Carts bonded to two Hooks, which can be used to create a long chain of Mine Carts that can cross the broken segment of the Tracks and reach the south side of the central room. Northwest of these Tracks, there is a broken suspension bridge with missing segments. To the southeast of this bridge, there is another broken suspension bridge that can be mended in order to reach a higher level of the room where Lattices can be found. These Lattices can be used to bridge the gaps in the first suspension bridge that connects to a Gloom Rock. This Gloom Rock hides three Zonai Devices capsules. When used with the Lattices, these capsules provide the necessary components to create a Hot-Air Balloon that can raise Link to the floor above. By striking the eastern Bell in the Fire Temple 3F's central room, Link can access the northern rooms. In the northernmost room, there is a large pool of Lava with a Gong at its center. There is also a Lava Slab that can be used to destroy a Gloom Rock in the pool of Lava. Atop this Gloom Rock, there is an active Hydrant. By using a second, square-shaped Lava Slab, Link can create a ramp to strike the Gong from afar. By pointing this ramp southwest, Link can also destroy a Gloom Rock obstructing the northwestern room, which in turn leads to a Gong on the Fire Temple 1F. Link can access the north side of the central room by striking both Bells in the central room of the Fire Temple 3F and riding the northwestern Tracks into the eastern side. On this side of the room, there is a second set of Mine Cart Tracks that lead to the Fire Temple 5F's northern room. Enemies Zonai Devices Treasure Chests

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Fire Temple 5F is the highest floor of the Fire Temple. It consists of just two rooms. The northern room can be accessed via Mine Cart Tracks from the Fire Temple 4F's central room. This northern room contains an enclosed area that features a Treasure Chest, though this room cannot be entered from the fifth floor. Instead, Link must first break the nearby Gloom Rock and drop down to the newly-created entrance on floor below. From there, he can Ascend into the enclosure. The northern room on the fifth floor also contains a pathway around the side of the enclosure. Along this pathway, there is a partially-broken suspension bridge that leads to a drop to the floor below. On this floor, Link can strike a Bell to lower a set of Mine Cart Tracks leading to the northern room of the Fire Temple 4F. The southern room can be accessed by creating a Hot-Air Balloon from the floor below with the Zonai Devices capsules provided there. This room bears a Gong, which releases the center padlock on the Fire Temple 1F. Along the floor of this room, there is a Gloom Rock with a Metal Mesh Block sitting atop it. On the eastern side of this room, there is a broken set of Mine Cart Tracks which do not lead anywhere. Enemies Zonai Devices Treasure Chests

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics In , Fire Wizzrobes appear inside Vaati's Palace. They will vanish and appear in a random location and attack with a fire attack before vanishing again. Fire Wizzrobes make their first 3D appearance, first appearing in the Tower of the Gods in , after Link obtains the Hero's Bow. They repeatedly teleport and shoot three fireballs each time they reappear. In , Fire Wizzrobes appear as a fiery variant to the green Wizzrobes and Ice Wizzrobes. Like the others, they will teleport to random locations throughout the area in which they appear, shooting their fire attack before vanishing again. In , Fire Wizzrobes appear in Turtle Rock alongside their Ice variants. Like previous incarnations, they will randomly appear around the area and attack with a fire attack before vanishing again. Rushing to attack them as they appear will ensure their demise. Fire Wizzrobes also appear on the 24th floor of the Treacherous Tower's advanced level. In , Fire Wizzrobes can be found all throughout Hyrule Kingdom, particularly in the ruins of former Hylian settlements. They attack by using their Fire Rods to conjure fireballs or by summoning flaming Monsters such as Fire Chuchus and Fire Keese. They are also able to increase an area's Temperature, making it too hot for Link without Flame Guard. Fire Wizzrobes, like their other Wizzrobes, will become invisible after attacking, leaving ripples in the air with each footstep. Striking their heads with an Arrow will stun them, giving Link time to attack. Hitting Fire Wizzrobes with Ice-based attacks will immediately evaporate them. Upon their defeat, Fire Wizzrobes drop their Fire Rods. Instead of a Fire Rod, Fire Wizzrobes now carry a Traveler's Sword that has been Fused to a Ruby. Link can defeat them in one hit by Fusing Ice-type Materials to an Arrow, such as Ice Fruits or White Chuchu Jelly. Fire Wizzrobes are Fire-wielding Wizzrobes found in Eldin Volcano. When summoned as an Echo, they have an Echo cost of five. Other Appearances left Fire Wizzrobes appear as enemies in where they move to the beat of the music. Here, they act as medium- to long-range combatants for Cadence, Link, Yves, and Zelda, teleporting towards them whenever they are nearby and attempt to cast fiery projectiles in their direction. They appear for a total of seven beats between each teleport, taking two beats to fully appear and charging their attack on the third. On the fourth beat, they release their magic, letting it fly in a straight line on every single music beat until it makes contact with something. If any of the heroes, flammable objects, or even another monster gets struck by the projectile, they will burn for a few beats before cooling off. After attacking, they will remain stationary until the seventh beat, raising their crystal orbs to the sky in order to teleport themselves away, fading until they finally disappear on the eighth beat. Once gone, they will remain invisible for five

they will burn for a few beats before cooling off. After attacking, they will remain stationary until the seventh beat, raising their crystal orbs to the sky in order to teleport themselves away, fading until they finally disappear on the eighth beat. Once gone, they will remain invisible for five beats or if the heroes are too far away, won't reappear at all until they return to the Fire Wizzrobe's last known location. Despite their appearance, they can still be attacked while fading in and out of teleportation. Fire Wizzrobes shoot out mini fireballs and teleport in . They also use heavy attacks, such as a giant fireball, or making fire rain from the sky, which both can make the Weak Point Gauge appear. They drop a Fire Rod, if not already obtained, when defeated, and will drop pieces of Fire elemental energy that can be used to recharge a Fire Rod if the character already has a Fire Rod. They are particularly weak to Ice elemental attacks, such as the Ice Rod.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Fireproof Elixirs will grant Link Flame Guard when drunk, preventing him from catching fire in a Scorching Climate. They're useful when traversing Death Mountain. Two merchants sell Fireproof Elixirs. Gaile, a worker at Foothill Stable, has them available for travelers heading to Goron City. She suggests taking at least three, as this is what regular Goron City travelers do. One elixir costs 60 Rupees, two cost 110 Rupees, and three cost 150 Rupees. If Link refuses to buy, Gaile advises him to give up on Goron City. Once Link has at least three, she'll tell him he's ready to head to Goron City. In Goron City, Link can speak to Offrak, who will ask if he needs a Fireproof Elixir. If Link admits that he does, Offrak will offer to sell him one for 60 Rupees. Link can refuse, causing Offrak to become angry and say he shouldn't come crying to him when he's on fire. Offrak will attempt to coerce Link into buying more, saying a Hylian will need it. Once Link stops buying, Offrak comments under his breath that Link could easily make his own. Fireproof Elixirs can be made by Cooking any of the following critters with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot: Smotherwing Butterfly Fireproof Lizard

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Fireproof Lizards can be found in the Scorching Climates of Hyrule, particularly Death Mountain and the nearby Eldin Canyon. They can be combined with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot to make a Fireproof Elixir, which will provide Link with temporary Flame Guard when consumed. However, if they are Cooked with other ingredients, the result will be Dubious Food. The Kochi Dye Shop also accepts Fireproof Lizards as an ingredient for Gray Dye. If Link speaks to Kima at the Southern Mine, he explains that he is returning from Goron City and forgot to buy a souvenir. He says that he wants some Fireproof Lizards and offers Link Fireproof Armor if he can catch 10. This begins the "Fireproof Lizard Roundup" Side Quest. When Link brings the Fireproof Lizards, Kima will reward him with Flamebreaker Armor. Afterwards, Link can deliver three Fireproof Lizards to Kima for 20 Rupees. Fireproof Lizards are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

When Link enters the First Gatehouse, a Blue-Maned Lynel will drop from the ceiling and portcullises will cover both of its entrances to trap him inside. However, the upper floors of the First Gatehouse contain several archways that Link may exit from. Defeating the Blue-Maned Lynel will cause the portcullises to raise and a Metal Chest will then appear. Enemies Korok Seeds Treasure Chests The First Gatehouse is separated from the higher portions of Hyrule Castle during the Upheaval. are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Fish and Mushroom Skewers are made by Cooking any Mushroom with any Fish. Eating one will restore some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. The Fish used in these skewers are fresh, while the Mushrooms are fragrant. Several different variations of Fish and Mushroom Skewers exist, depending on both the Ingredients are used and whether any additional Ingredients are added: Hearty Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Hearty Salmons, Hearty Bass, Hearty Truffles, Big Hearty Truffles, or Hearty Durian. When eaten, will heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Enduring Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Endura Shrooms. Eating them will refill and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Staminoka Basses, Stamella Shrooms, or Bright-Eyed Crabs. If eaten, Link's Stamina Wheel will be partially refilled. Hasty Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Rushrooms or Fleet-Lotus Seeds. Eating one will grant Link a temporary boost to his movement speed. Spicy Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Sizzlefin Trouts or Sunshrooms. Link will gain one level of Cold Resistance when these are eaten. Electro Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Voltfin Trout, Zapshrooms, or Voltfruits. Eating these Skewers will give Link one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Mighty Carp, Mighty Porgies, Razorshrooms, or Mighty Bananas. Eating them will boost Link's attacks for a short time. Tough Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Armored Carp, Armored Porgies, or Ironshrooms. If eaten, Link's Defense will increase. Sneaky Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Stealthfin Trouts or Silent Shrooms. Eating one will temporarily increase Link's Stealth. Chilly Fish and Mushroom Skewer: Made using Chillfin Trouts, Chillshrooms, or Hydromelons. When eaten, Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance temporarily.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview Following the end of the Blizzard in Rito Village, Link can find Bedoli watching over a shipment of supplies. She recognizes Link as the person who aided Tulin in stopping the Blizzard, and she explains that the Rito are working on replenishing their stockpiles. Bedoli's job is the manage the process of searching for supplies, while other adults focus on scavenging. She notes that Huck has yet to return from Snowfield Stable, and she hopes he is fine. Bedoli apologizes, before asking Link if he has any Food he would be willing to trade with her. She offers him a bundle of 10 Arrows if he can bring her three Glowing Cave Fish. If Link does not have enough Fish, Bedoli tells him the offer will still stand if he returns. Following their conversation, "Fish for Fletching" will begin. When Link speaks to Bedoli with at least three Glowing Cave Fish in his Inventory, she will ask if he is willing to trade with her. If Link agrees, Bedoli will give him the bundle of 10 Arrows. Bedoli then asks if Link has more food, revealing that the Rito children enjoy Chillfin Trouts and Brightcaps. She promises to give him more Arrows if he can bring them to her. Afterwards, "Fish for Fletching" will be completed. Objectives

Mighty Fish Skewer: Made using Mighty Carps, Mighty Porgies, or other attack-boosting Ingredients. Consuming one of these will increase Link's attack power for a short period of time. Tough Fish Skewer: Made using Armored Carps, Armored Porgies, or other defensive Ingredients. When eaten, Link's Defense will be temporarily increased. Sneaky Fish Skewer: Made using Stealthfin Trouts or other Stealth-boosting Ingredients. Eating one increases Link's Stealth abilities. Chilly Fish Skewer: Made using Chillfin Trouts or other cold Ingredients. If they are eaten, Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance. Based on the types of Ingredients used, several different variations of Fish Skewers exist: Biting Fish Skewer: Made by adding Ice Fruits. If they are eaten, Link will deal increased damage when in Freezing Climates. Bright Fish Skewer: Made using Glowing Cave Fish or other bright Ingredients. If they are eaten, Link will emit a faint Glow. Chilly Fish Skewer: Made using Chillfin Trouts or other cold Ingredients. If they are eaten, Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Fish Skewer: Made using Voltfin Trout or other electricity-related Ingredients. Eating one grants Link one level of Shock Resistance. Energizing Fish Skewer: Made using Staminoka Basses or other energizing Ingredients. Eating one of these Skewers will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Fish Skewer: Made by adding speed-boosting Ingredients. If they are eaten, Link's movement speed will be boosted temporarily. Hearty Fish Skewer: Made using Hearty Bass, Hearty Salmons, or other hearty Ingredients. When eaten, they will replenish all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Mighty Fish Skewer: Made using Mighty Carps, Mighty Porgies, or other attack-boosting Ingredients. Consuming one of these will increase Link's attack power for a short period of time. Rapid Fish Skewer: Made by adding Splash Fruits. Consuming one of these will temporarily increase

Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Mighty Fish Skewer: Made using Mighty Carps, Mighty Porgies, or other attack-boosting Ingredients. Consuming one of these will increase Link's attack power for a short period of time. Rapid Fish Skewer: Made by adding Splash Fruits. Consuming one of these will temporarily increase Link's Swimming speed. Scorching Fish Skewer: Made by adding Fire Fruits. If they are eaten, Link will deal increased damage when in Scorching Climates. Sneaky Fish Skewer: Made using Stealthfin Trouts or other Stealth-boosting Ingredients. Eating one increases Link's Stealth abilities. Spicy Fish Skewer: Made using Sizzlefin Trouts or other spicy Ingredients. They grant Link one level of Cold Resistance when eaten. Stormy Fish Skewer: Made by adding Shock Fruits. If they are eaten, Link will deal increased damage when in Thunderstorms. Tough Fish Skewer: Made using Armored Carps, Armored Porgies, or other defensive Ingredients. When eaten, Link's Defense will be temporarily increased. Warding Fish Skewer: Made by adding Dark Clumps. Eating one grants Link a single additional Heart to shield him from Gloom. Other Appearances The recipe for Chilly Fish Skewer is earned by completing the Quest "Superb Fish Dish". It is made using four Stealthfin Trouts. However, it can be lowered to three through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warriors will take 50% less damage from Fire.

are recurring Shields in . Location and Uses Fisherman's Shields are semi-rare Shields, similar to the Hunter's Shield. They are often carried by fishermen for their Fish design, which is said to represent hope for a great catch. This is aided by their light wooden construction, which makes them easier to take onto a boat. There are five areas where a Fisherman's Shield can be found. Two are in Lurelin Village. One is near Tawa Jinn Shrine in the Rabella Wetlands. Another is in a Treasure Chest in an enemy camp north of Parache Plains. There is also in a Treasure Chest on a cliff near Brynna Plain on the shores of Lanayru Bay. Finally, Selmie gives one out as a reward for completing the Shield-Surfing between 2:45 and 3:00. Being made of wood, Fisherman's Shields will burn to a crisp if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will also float in Water, and they will not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms like metal Shields would. Finally, they cannot be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. Fisherman's Shields reappear in .

The is a recurrng location in in . Features and Overview The Fishing Resort is an Inn located in Lurelin Village. Like other buildings in Lurelin, it has been constructed around a large Palm Tree. It is operated by Chessica. The Gerudo traveler Flavi is temporarily residing at the Inn while visiting Lurelin Village, resting in one of the Beds during the night. Chumin, Letty, and Spinch all rest within or near the Resort during their journeys on the Faron Highroad. When Link chooses to stay at the Fishing Resort, he has the choice to Sleep in a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a fluffy Bed for 40 Rupees. The fluffy Bed will provide Link will Extra Hearts when he wakes up. If Link decides to Sleep at the Resort, Chessica will offer to wake him up in the morning, afternoon, or evening. Once Link makes his selection, Chessica will send him off to Bed. When he wakes up, Chessica greets him, and she reveals that he can use the Raft at the nearby as a bonus for staying at the Resort. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found at the Fishing Resort. Where the Resort's Palm Trees stick out of its roof, Link is able to locate the start of a Flower Trail. After following the Trail to its end at the top of the Palm Tree, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed.

page_title: Fishpond in Front of the Village
text: The is a recurring location in . The Fishpond in Front of the Village goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Fishpond in Front of the Village is a shallow pond on the island east of Rito Village that is stocked with Hearty Salmons, along with small, uncatchable Fish. The Water inside reaches up to Link's shoulders. During the "Recital at Warbler's Nest" Shrine Quest, Kotts can be found fishing for Hearty Salmons in the Fishpond. After all of her sisters are found, Kotts leaves the Fishpond to head to Warbler's Nest. Creatures As a result of the Blizzard, the Fishpond has been covered in a thin layer of Ice that breaks when Jumped on repeatedly. Its stock of Hearty Salmons have disappeared, though the tiny Fish still reside in the Fishpond. After the Blizzard ends, the Ice film over the Water disappears and Staminoka Basses populate it. Creatures

is a character in . Biography Flahva is a Hylian member of Hoz's Monster-Control Crew squad. He carries a Wooden Shield and a Boko Reaper, which is made of a Tree Branch and a Bokoblin Horn. As part of the search party at Hyrule Castle, Flahva can be found looking into the Hyrule Castle Chasm near the front of the First Gatehouse. He claims that it is intense to look into a Chasm, and he believes seeing one is better than hearing about it. If Link responds to Flahva, he will be startled, and he scolds Link for scaring someone so close to a Chasm. He is frightened by the idea of falling into a Chasm, especially due to how deep they are. If Link chooses to leave Flahva alone, he reveals that although he is scared, he is unable to stop staring into the Chasm. Should Link speak to Flahva again, he wonders if Zelda could have fallen into the Chasm. They later prepare for an attack on a Monster Stronghold south of the Hyrule Garrison Ruins. He uses a Wooden Shield and a Bokoblin Horn attached to a Tree Branch during the attack. If approached during the fighting he brushes Link off. Squad one plans to head southeast towards Fort Hateno in Necluda after the fight.

The , also known as the , the Flame-Resistant Armor, the Fire-Resistant Clothes, and the Fireproof Gear, is a recurring Armor Set in . The Flame-Resistant Equipment goes unnamed in . Location and Uses The Fireproof Armor consists of the Flamebreaker Helm, Flamebreaker Armor, and Flamebreaker Boots. All three pieces can be bought at Ripped and Shredded armor shop in Goron City, though a Flamebreaker Armor is awarded from completing the "Fireproof Lizard Roundup" Side Quest. Each piece grants protection from volcanic temperatures, similar to Fireproof Elixirs. If all three pieces of the set have been upgraded twice at a Great Fairy Fountain, wearing the set grants Link complete immunity to being set on fire. Confusingly, the trait on the armor pieces that protects against scorching climates is called Flame Guard, while the set bonus granting protection from burning is called Fireproof. Dye Options Enhancing Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances The Flamebreaker Helm is acquired upon completing the "Fighting Fire With..." Quest. The Flamebreaker Armor is acquired upon completing the "Daruk, the Goron Hero" Quest. The Flamebreaker Boots are acquired upon completing the "Tough Bulwark of the Gorons" Quest. Dye Options

are recurring Enemies in . Flame Fountains go unnamed in , , , and . Characteristics The Flame Fountain is found only in one Cave in the Western Tal Tal Mountains. This Cave leads to Turtle Rock and first needs to be blown open with Bombs. After Link enters the Cave, he encounters the Flame Fountain at the end of a narrow corridor, spewing a constant stream of Fire into the passageway. Link cannot get past the flames at all: they not only cause a huge amount of damage (two and a half hearts worth), but the strength of them forces him back. The Fountain cannot be destroyed. Link can only bypass the Flame Fountain with the Mirror Shield from the Eagle's Tower in the Eastern Tal Tal Mountains. Using the Shield, he can force the flames back and pass the Fountain unharmed. It is possible to bypass the Flame Fountain (and thus skip the Mirror Shield) by taking enough damage from the flames while being in possession of Tracy's Secret Medicine. Once the Medicine kicks in and starts restoring Link's Hearts, he can run through the flames unharmed for a brief period of time. Flame Fountains appear inside the Fire Temple, releasing bursts of Fire if Link approaches. Flame Fountains cannot be destroyed. Flame Fountains appear in the Tower of Spirits, Fire Temple, and the Lost at Sea Temple. They periodically spew Fire. Flame Fountains shoot Fire in a single direction.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Flamebreaker Armors are pieces of Armor that can be purchased in the Ripped and Shredded shop at Goron City. One can also be received from Kima by completing the "Fireproof Lizard Roundup" Side Quest at the Southern Mine. When worn, they provide one level of Flame Guard. Flamebreaker Armors can be enhanced by a Great Fairy and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Flamebreaker Armor, alongside the Flamebreaker Helm and Flamebreaker Boots, compose the Flamebreaker Set. When each piece of the Set has been enhanced at least two times by a Great Fairy and the full Set is worn, it provides a Fireproof Set Bonus. Dye Options Enhancing Flamebreaker Armors appear as pieces of Armor in that can be purchased at the Ripped and Shredded Shop in Goron City, like their incarnation. Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances Dye Options

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Flamebreaker Boots are pieces of Armor that can be purchased in the Ripped and Shredded shop at Goron City. When worn, they provide one level of Flame Guard. Flamebreaker Boots can be enhanced by a Great Fairy and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Flamebreaker Boots, alongside the Flamebreaker Helm and Flamebreaker Armor, compose the Flamebreaker Set. When each piece of the Set has been enhanced at least two times by a Great Fairy and the full Set is worn, it provides the Fireproof Set Bonus. Dye Options Enhancing The Flamebreaker Boots reappear as Armor in , providing one level of Flame Guard once again. Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances Flamebreaker Boots are a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and they are obtained by completing the Challenge "Tough Bulwark of the Gorons". They can also be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Dye Options

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Flamebreaker Helms are pieces of Armor that can be purchased in the Ripped and Shredded shop at Goron City. When worn, they provide one level of Flame Guard. Flamebreaker Helms can be enhanced by a Great Fairy and can be Hateno Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Flamebreaker Helm, alongside the Flamebreaker Armor and Flamebreaker Boots, compose the Fireproof Armor. When each piece of the Set has been enhanced at least two times by a Great Fairy and the full Set is worn, it provides a Fireproof Set Bonus. Dye Options Enhancing Flamebreaker Helms are Armor pieces that provide Flame Guard. Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances In , the Flamebreaker Helm is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and is obtained by completing the Quest "Fighting Fire With...". It can also by Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Dye Options

is a recurring character in . Biography Flavi is a Gerudo traveler who can be found in Lurelin Village. She sleeps in the Fishing Resort during the night. When Link speaks to her, Flavi remarks on the Weather, the warmth being nice when compared to the Heat of the Gerudo Desert. She then asks if Link is visiting Lurelin on vacation. If Link asks about the Desert, Flavia explains that she's from Gerudo Town, which is surrounded by the Desert. Flavi came to Lurelin Village out of interest in Eventide Island. During the day, she camps out on a hill just outside of the village and looks upon the Island. However, she's had difficulties in reaching it by sea and wonders if one needs wings to reach it. During the rain, Flavi takes shelter under the umbrellas outside the Fishing Resort. When Link speaks to her during this time, she admits to hating the rain as it makes her miss home. If Link says he likes the rain, she calls him a weirdo. It never rains in Gerudo Town, so while she was initially intrigued by it, it now annoys her.

is a recurring character in . Biography Flaxel is a Hylian traveler who is found in the Gerudo Canyon. She carries a Hunter's Shield and Traveler's Sword. She was previously traveling with her friends Sesami, Oliff, Canolo, and Palme. However, the five of them were attacked by Bokoblins on the Koukot Plateau Path and ended up separated. At Gerudo Canyon Stable, Link can find Sesami, who managed to escape. He asks Link to let Flaxel and the rest of his friends know that he is waiting for them at the Stable. This initiates the "Missing in Action" Side Quest. Flaxel is found on the northern end of the Koukot Plateau Path, defending herself from a Blue Bokoblin. When Link saves her, she thanks him for his help. She remarks on how sore she will be tomorrow, calling the Bokoblins filthy bottom-feeders. Flaxel is angry when she finds out Sesami has been at the Gerudo Canyon Stable the whole time, at which point she decides to give him a piece of her mind. She then leaves for the Stable. Back at the Gerudo Canyon Stable, Flaxel admits that she was going to yell at Sesami for leaving her, but she stopped once she noticed he looked like he was going to cry. She is unable to bring herself to be mad at him for being scared, since that is the way he is. Flaxel and the rest of her friends chip in to give Link a Gold Rupee as thanks for saving them. After the Side Quest is completed, Flaxel and her friends, with the exception of Sesami, disappear from the Stable, as they have all decided to part ways. Flaxel has become the captain of Monster-Control Crew, Squad Three. Initially, Link can find Flaxel and her squad at Lookout Landing, where they are receiving orders from Gralens about searching Hyrule Castle for Zelda. If Link tries to speak to her before he has met Gralens, Flaxel dismisses him. Afterwards, she is able to identify that Link is the famous swordsman they have been looking for, and she expresses her pleasure at meeting him. She offers to talk to him about his status as a hero when she is off-duty. Gralens then interrupts their conversation, telling Link that they are busy and he should instead meet with Purah.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Fleet-Lotus Seeds can be found growing in wetlands across Hyrule, such as near the Ne'ez Yohma Shrine and throughout the Lanayru Wetlands. Stamm, a Wandering Merchant, sells them for 20 Rupees. They restore half of a Heart for Link when eaten. They can also be Cooked into Meals to grant Link Speed Up. When they are burned by Fire, they turn into Roasted Lotus Seeds. At the Kochi Dye Shop, they can be used to make Green Dye. Fleet-Lotus Seeds can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Fleet-Lotus Seeds can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Other Appearances Fleet-Lotus Seeds can be obtained as Materials in .

is a character in . Biography Flesi is a Hylian who serves as a guard for Lookout Landing. He has been positioned on the Second Floor, despite his fear of heights. He wields a Soldier's Spear. When meeting Link for the first time, Flesi is surprised to see him, noting that Lookout Landing felt different. Since Link is Zelda's swordsman, Flesi was confident that he would return. He then asks where Zelda is, wanting to welcome her back as well. Although Flesi is disappointed to hear that she is still missing, he is relieved that Link is safe and assures him that Lookout Landing will support him. After Link has met with Purah, Flesi claims that he wants to save Zelda, but he does not know how to reach Hyrule Castle while it is floating in the air.

The , also known as the Rito Flight Range, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Flight Range is a Rito training ground located at the end of Dronoc's Pass in the Hebra Mountains. Rito warriors use the Flight Range to prepare for aerial battles due to its consistent Updrafts. As such, the Range features a number of Targets, as well as a House containing a Cooking Pot and a good amount of Rito Gear. The bottom of the Range is covered in a pool of Water. Since it exists within a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit the Flight Range without taking damage. 100 years ago, the Flight Range was built at Revali's request as a reward for winning an archery tournament, since he required training grounds to improve his skills at. When the Rito children expressed interest in training there too, Revali decided to open the Flight Range to the public, hoping it would nurture the next generation of warriors. thumb|left|250px|Princess Zelda and Revali at the Flight Range Prior to the second Great Calamity, Zelda visited the Flight Range in search of Revali, seeking to appoint him as a Champion and pilot of Divine Beast Vah Medoh. There, she witnesses Revali practicing his Gale, but he gets caught up in the whirlwind and is thrown back to the ground. After noticing Zelda, Revali officially accepts her offer. He then attempts his Gale once more, this time successfully launching himself off of the ground and destroying all of the Flight Range's Targets with Bomb Arrows. Landing by the House, Revali asserts that he will play the biggest role in helping seal Calamity Ganon, and he says not to come crying to him if Link loses his confidence after seeing his skills. These events can be seen as part of the "Champion Revali's Song" EX Recovered Memory that appears during the "EX Champion Revali's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack. After failing to defeat Divine Beast Vah Medoh when it reactivated, the Rito warrior Teba fell back to the Flight Range to prepare for another attack. When Link arrives at the Flight Range during the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, he will find Teba working on a Falcon Bow. Though Teba is initially distrusting of Link, he eventually accepts his help. However, he first needs to test Link by having him destroy five of the Flight Range's Targets within three minutes. When Link completes the Flight Range, Teba commends his skills. To help Link against the Divine Beast, Teba directs him to a stone Treasure Chest on the landing, which contains a Falcon Bow that he was modifying. Teba also gifts Link a bundle of 20 Bomb Arrows to use on the Cannons. Following the fight against Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Teba will retreat to the Flight Range to deal with his injured leg. If Link visits the Flight Range before appeasing Vah Medoh, Teba

he was modifying. Teba also gifts Link a bundle of 20 Bomb Arrows to use on the Cannons. Following the fight against Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Teba will retreat to the Flight Range to deal with his injured leg. If Link visits the Flight Range before appeasing Vah Medoh, Teba will express his frustration that he got hurt after he was so close to defeating the Divine Beast. Once Link receives the Great Eagle Bow, Teba will take his son, Tulin, to practice at the Flight Range. While there, he will ask Link to demonstrate his archery skills for Tulin. Tulin also asks Link to show him his skills as part of the Flight Range Mini-Game, challenging Link to destroy as many Targets as he can in a limited amount of time. During the "EX Champion Revali's Song" Main Quest, the Targets at the Flight Range start to glow with the Crest of the Sheikah. As part of the Divine Beast Tamer's Trial, Link must shoots four of these Targets. Doing so causes Noe Rajee Shrine to emerge from the ground at the bottom of the Flight Range. A total of two Treasure Chests are hidden at the Flight Range. Both are made of metal and are submerged in the Water at the bottom of the Range, though Link can use Magnesis to pull them to the surface. These Chests contain a Knight's Broadsword and a Gold Rupee. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found at the Flight Range. It takes the form of a group of Leaves with Fairy Dust on the roof of the Range's House. When Link examines the Leaves, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed as a reward. Equipment After retiring as chieftain of Rito Village, Kaneli operates the Flight Range as a training center for young Rito warriors. Equipment Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Flints can be found after breaking Ore Deposits, Luminous Stone Deposits, and Rare Ore Deposits. Striking pieces of Flint with metal Weapons causes the former to ignite. This can be used to create Campfire by dropping a piece near some Wood before striking it. It can be used to relight extinguished Campfires as well, including those under Cooking Pots. The Kochi Dye Shop accepts Flints as an ingredient for Black Dye. The Champions' Weapons, if broken, can be reforged by special craftsmen, with Flint as a requirement. If the Ceremonial Trident ever breaks, Link can have Dento at the Hammerhead recreate it for him in exchange for five pieces of Flint and a Zora Spear. If the Lightscale Trident ever breaks, Dento will make another one in exchange for a Zora Spear, five Flints, and a Diamond. If the Scimitar of the Seven ever breaks, Buliara in the Royal Palace will require one Diamond, five Flints, and a Gerudo Scimitar to make a new one. If the Daybreaker ever breaks, Buliara requires a Diamond, five pieces of Flint, and a Gerudo Shield to remake it. If the Boulder Breaker ever breaks, Rohan in Goron City will make a new one in exchange for a Cobble Crusher, a Diamond, and five pieces of Flint. Flints are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Flints reappear in . When Fused to a Weapon or Arrow, they increase its attack power by one. Gomo is in search of a rare variety of Flint known as Ripened Flint. It is indistinguishable from regular Flint, though Gorons are able to tell it apart by its taste. As part of the Side Quest "Cash In on Ripened Flint", Gomo offers to pay Link 1,000 Rupees if he can provide him with Ripened Flint. Both during and after this Side Quest, Link can give Gomo pieces of Flint in groups of 20, 50, or 100, which he will taste-test for Ripened Flint. Flints are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances In , pieces of Flint can be obtained as Materials during Scenarios or Challenges. They can be used to fulfill the requirements of certain Quests. In , Flint can be earned as Materials during certain Challenges. It can be supplied to Camps to enhance the effects of any Fish or Ores that have also been supplied.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Floating Coliseum is a huge structure located in the Central Hyrule Depths, and it is situated directly beneath the Coliseum Ruins. Like other coliseums in the Depths, the Floating Coliseum's door is automatically closed when Link approaches the Treasure Chest in the middle. Waves of Lynels are then released, which Link is tasked with defeating. Once all of the Lynels are defeated, the Gloom surrounding the Treasure Chest will disappear, and Link will be able to retrieve Majora's Mask from inside. Enemies Wave 1 Wave 2 Wave 3 Wave 4 Wave 5 Treasure Chests

The , also known as the Ring Ruin That Floats, is a location in . Features and Overview The Floating Ring Ruin is one of the five Ring Ruins that fell onto Kakariko Village when the Upheaval began. Uniquely, a portion of this Ruin floats in the air above the rest. Shortly after it fell, a Phantom Ganon posing as Zelda appeared in Kakariko Village and gave the Order of Princess Zelda, which forbids anyone from entering the Floating Ring Ruin. Initially, Paya and Tauro believe this is to protect the villagers should the Ruin crash. When Link first arrives in Kakariko Village, he can find Paya and Tauro looking up at the Floating Ring Ruin. Tauro theorizes that, like the other Ring Ruins, there could be a Ring Ruins Stone Slab inside, but because of the Order of Princess Zelda, he is unable to see for himself. If Link gets too close to the Floating Ring Ruin, Calip will stop him. During the "Find the Fifth Sage" Main Quest, Link reveals to Paya and Tauro that the Order of Princess Zelda was given by an impostor, allowing them to reopen the Floating Ring Ruin for investigation. At the start of the "Secret of the Ring Ruins" Main Quest, Tauro reveals that he has no way to access the suspended portion of the Floating Ring Ruin, so he is unable to check if there is a Ring Ruins Stone Slab inside. Using Ascend, Link can enter the interior of the Floating Ring Ruin, where he can then use his Camera to take a Picture of the Slab inside. Paya and Tauro are able to decipher the Zonai script, which refers to a "dragon land" to the southeast.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Floret Sandbar is a small island in the middle of the Hylia River in West Necluda, located west of Eagus Bridge. It is the home of a flower maze, grown by Magda. If Link speaks to Magda, or steps on or damages the flowers, she will warn him not to hurt them, initiating the "Watch Out for the Flowers" Shrine Quest. At the end of the flower maze sits the Hila Rao Shrine. Along the western bank of the Sandbar, Link can find a Raft. Hidden in the water near the raft is a metallic Treasure Chest, which contains a Purple Rupee. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Floria Bridge is a wooden structure built upon three large Trees in West Necluda. It spans the entirety of Lake Floria, and it connects the Faron Highroad between the Ebara Forest and Sarjon Woods. On either end of the Bridge are the remains of masonry laid down by the ancient Zonai, including small sets of Zonai Ruins. From a platform about midway, one can take in the sight of all ten of the Floria Falls. The travelers Chumin, Letty, and Spinch all pass over Floria Bridge on their journeys. On occasion, Farosh will fly under Floria Bridge while passing by Lake Floria. When she does this, Updrafts and Winds will appear in the surrounding areas. Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds Treasure Chests Creatures Korok Seeds Other Appearances As part of the Quest "Floria Bridge Protection", the Warriors are tasked with providing supplies that would protect travelers from Farosh as it travels over Floria Bridge. Once 10 Electric Keese Wings, 20 Yellow Lizalfos Tails, five Yellow Chuchu Jellies, 50 Keese Trophies, and five Wizzrobe Trophies have been supplied, word spreads that the Bridge is safe to cross, and Merchants will begin to utilize it.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Floria Falls are located in West Necluda. They are a series of 10 multi-tiered Waterfalls that flow south into Lake Floria. The Waterfalls originate from Corta Lake, Riola Spring, and Rodai Lake. Shoda Sah Shrine is hidden in a cave behind the Waterfall that flows directly from Riola Spring. Several Zonai Ruins are also scattered amongst the Falls. As part of the Side Quest "EX Treasure: Dark Armor", which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link reads Misko's EX Journal 2 and learns that a piece of the Phantom Ganon Set can be found "at the highest of three waterfalls north of Lake Floria." Following these directions, Link can find a metallic Hidden Chest beneath the Waterfall that flows south from Corta Lake, from which he can recover the Phantom Ganon Skull. After emerging from Riola Spring, Farosh will fly alongside the Floria Falls as she descends towards Lake Floria. She follows the same path on her way back up towards the Spring. When this happens, strong Winds and Updrafts will appear around the Floria Falls. A large number of Treasure Chests are situated among the Floria Falls. In total, they contain one Soldier's Broadsword, one Double Axe, one Soldier's Bow, 10 Ice Arrows, one Amber, three Opals, and two Purple Rupees. In addition to this, during Master Mode, several more Treasure Chests can be found on wooden platforms held in the air by Sky Octoroks. These Chests contain one Giant Boomerang, one Great Thunderblade, one Forest Dweller's Bow, one Forest Dweller's Shield, and one Sapphire. left|40px In total, three Korok Seed Puzzles can be found in and around the Floria Falls. The first is a Cube Pattern on either side of the Waterfall flowing south from Corta Lake. The second is a Natural Hiding Spot, which takes the form of a Rock on a ledge between the two Waterfalls from Rodai Lake. The last Puzzle is a Flower Trail among the Zonai Ruins at the center of the Falls. Whenever Link solves one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Floria River is located between the Faron Grasslands and West Necluda. It flows east from Lake Floria, ending between the Zonai Ruins and Pagos Woods. Two bridges connect the Faron Highroad as it passes over the Floria River, one of which being the Sarjon Bridge. A single Raft can be found on the Floria River, east of Sarjon Bridge. During the Side Quest "EX Treasure: Dark Armor", which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link must read Misko's EX Journal 2 to learn the location of the Phantom Ganon Set. The Journal describes one of the Armor pieces to be between two small Waterfalls in the Floria River. Beneath the Sarjon Bridge, which is located between two Waterfall, Link will find a metallic Hidden Chest containing the Phantom Ganon Armor. Several Metal Chests are submerged within the Water of the Floria River, which can be retrieved using the Magnesis Rune. These Chests contain a total of one Gold Rupee, one Silver Rupee, one Purple Rupee, one Amber, one Opal, one Knight's Claymore, one Soldier's Broadsword, five Fire Arrows, and five Shock Arrows. In Master Mode, another Metal Chest containing a Royal Shield can be found west of Sarjon Bridge. Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Flowers appear in both as Materials and Objects found throughout Hyrule Kingdom. The Armoranth, Blue Nightshade, Mighty Thistle, Silent Princess, and Swift Violet, as well as the Cool, Electric, and Warm Safflinas are all usable in Cooking and in making Hateno Dyes at the Kochi Dye Shop. Additionally, the locations of Hearty Radishes and Big Hearty Radish are revealed by their distinct pink Flowers. A Flower garden is featured prominently in the Shrine Quest "Watch Out for the Flowers". List of Flowers List of Flowers Flowers are set to reappear in . Other Appearances Flowers appear as Materials in .

are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Location and Uses Flower Trails are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. There are two varieties, and the first is a series of Flowers that Link must follow. The second is a set of Flower groupings, which Link must touch in rising order. Once |Link reaches the end of a Flower Trail, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. List of Flower Trails A total of seven Flower Trails can be found in Akkala. A total of 14 Flower Trails can be found in Central Hyrule. A total of one Flower Trail can be found in Faron. A total of four Flower Trails can be found in Gerudo. A total of nine Flower Trails can be found in Hebra. A total of five Flower Trails can be found in Lanayru. A total of 16 Flower Trails can be found in Necluda. In , only one variety of Flower Trail can be found. These are the series of Flowers that Link is tasked with following. When Link reaches the end of a Flower Trail, a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed.

The is an Item in . Location and Uses After completing the Side Quests "WANTED: Hinox", "WANTED: Molduga", "WANTED: Stone Talus", "Unknown Huge Silhouette", "Unknown Sky Giant", and "Unknown Three-Headed Monster", Link will be able to talk to Gralens about Flux Constructs. If he has defeated all 35 Flux Constructs, Gralens will reward him with the Flux Construct Monster Medal. He explains that it was meant for someone who is capable of fighting every Flux Construct, but he thought it would be impossible until Link did so. Alternatively, should there be any remaining Flux Constructs that Link has not defeated, Gralens will instead tell him how many are left.

, also known as Enemy Bait, is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses Food is an item that Link can purchase from Shops in . It normally costs 100 Rupees, but the Shop that also sells the Blue Ring sells Food for 60 Rupees. Link can equip and use Food to place it on the ground. This will attract certain enemies to the Food, allowing Link to attack or walk past them while distracted. The only enemies that are attracted to Food are Octoroks, Moblins, Vires, and Goriyas. Link can only place down one piece of Food at a time. However, after about 10 seconds, the Food will disappear and Link is able to place down another one. In certain Dungeons, Link will encounter a hungry Goriya who will not let him pass to the next room until given Food. These Goriyas are found once in the First Quest within Level 7 as well as Level 3 and Level 8 of the Second Quest. In Level-7, Link must pass the hungry Goriya in order to reach the end of the Dungeon. The Goriya in Level-3 of the Second Quest guards a room full of hostile red Goriyas. If Link defeats all of them, he is rewarded with the Magical Boomerang. The Goriya in Level-8 of the Second Quest guards a path that is the only way of reaching the room that contains the Magical Key. After giving Food to a Goriya, it is gone from Link's inventory until another is purchased. Apples can be found by using the Pegasus Boots to crash into certain trees, such as one between Kakariko Village and Lost Woods. They are functionally identical to Hearts, but as a high number of them are guaranteed to drop each time you enter the screen they are a convenient way to replenish Link's health when reloading a save file. In , Food is a type of consumable item that Link uses to restore health and receive special Added Effects. Edible Materials can be eaten raw, heated up, or frozen. Up to five Materials can also be combined together and cooked in a Cooking Pot. Only certain Materials combined can yield useful Food, and the potency of a Food's effects (e.g. the amount of Hearts or Stamina recovered) differs based on how many Materials Link used in the recipe. Failed combinations yield Dubious Food or Rock-Hard Food, which only restore minimal Hearts. Fruits, vegetables, nuts, mushrooms, meats, and other cooking materials should be combined together to create successful dishes. Combining Monster Parts or Critters with normal food items will usually result in Dubious Food unless the recipe contains both Critters and Monster Parts. Adding Wood or Ores will always result in Rock-Hard Food regardless of what other ingredients are used. If a Fairy is used as an "ingredient" when cooking a Meal, it will use its magic to aid the cooking process, significantly increasing the amount of Hearts recovered. Elixirs will also provide Link with Added Effects

If a Fairy is used as an "ingredient" when cooking a Meal, it will use its magic to aid the cooking process, significantly increasing the amount of Hearts recovered. Elixirs will also provide Link with Added Effects and can replenish health. They are made by cooking critters together with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot. Each Meal or Elixir made in a Cooking Pot, including duplicates, occupies its own slot in the Inventory. Roasted Food is created by directly subjecting Ingredients to high heat. Roasted Foods have 150% the heart restoration value over the raw Material but do not provide any Added Effects or buffs. Likewise, Frozen Food is created by directly subjecting raw Meat to freezing temperatures. A one-minute Low-level Heat Resistance boost is added to all Frozen food. Unlike Meals cooked in Cooking Pots, Roasted and Frozen Foods can stack in Link's Inventory up to a maximum of 999. Food Effects In , certain ingredients carry different effects that are applied to food when it is cooked in a Cooking Pot. These effects are granted to the player at the time when food is consumed. Most of these effects have a time limit before they run out. These timed effects cannot be stacked, meaning that when a player has one effect active and eats a food with a different, or even the same effect, the previously active effect will be replaced. Hearty and Enduring effects do not stack either, but if multiple meals are consumed, instead of cancelling the previous effect, the strongest one will remain active (for example, consuming a +4 Hearty meal and then a +3 will only grant 4 temporary hearts instead of 7) until the extra hearts/stamina sections are used up. Finally there is the Stamina-recovering Energizing effect, which, like Heart recovery, is an instantaneous effect only. While effects from Food do not stack, they can be combined with the Added Effects granted by certain pieces of Armor.
