Adding more than one of the same ingredient or multiple different ingredients with the same non-timed effect to the cooking pot causes the resulting food to have a stronger effect than it would have had with just one ingredient with that effect. In general, having a variety of ingredients with the same effect produces stronger bonuses than using all of the same ingredient with that effect. Combining ingredients with different effects will not cause the resulting food to have multiple effects. Instead, the resulting food will have only the most prominent effect present. If all ingredients cancel each other out, the resulting food won't have any special effect at all. If this happens in an Elixir recipe, Dubious Food will be created instead. Ingredients Ingredients are a type of Material that can be used to create Food and Elixirs. The only Materials excluded from this category are Wood and Ores, which will result in either Rock-Hard Food or Dubious Food. Effect Duration Materials with matching Effects (i.e. "Chilly") will stack duration, and may increase the effect level (from low to mid or high). Adding Materials without Effects will add to the duration. For example: Ingredient Dish Effect and Duration Hydromelon (2:30) Chilly Simmered Fruit Heat Resistance (2:30) Hydromelon (2:30) + Hydromelon (2:30) Chilly Simmered Fruit Heat Resistance (5:00) Hydromelon (2:30) + Apple (0:30) Chilly Simmered Fruit Heat Resistance (3:00) Other Appearances In and , Food can be dropped by Enemies and found inside Jars within Keeps. They are used to feed Companion Fairies, which will grow to a higher level depending the quality of the Food. Like Materials, they can be found in three different qualities. Regular Food is obtained from bronze-colored bags, Tasty Food is obtained from silver-colored bags and Delicious Food is obtained from gold-colored bags. The 8-Bit Food, based on the Food from , appears as the 8-Bit Weapon for Darunia's Hammer. It was added to with the Pack DLC and in replaces the Darkfire Hammer when the "8-Bit Weapons" setting is turned on. In , Food serve as the replacement for the Apothecary's Mixtures from the games. By using specific Materials to prepare these meals within the Cooking submenu after selecting a Scenario or Challenge map, they grant stackable passive effects that help Warriors in combat maps. They last until deployment, and are not consumed if players have to reset the battle. The menu options can be expanded by either clearing Cooking Quest or beating Scenario battles. Certain Quests can also expand how much slots for food players can make, up to three.

, also known as , are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Location and Uses Offering Spots are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. They are often marked by Stone Statue, but in Kakariko Village and Karusa Valley, these are changed to Traveler's Guardian Deities. In addition, Offering Spots utilize Zonai Owl Statues in southern West Necluda. To solve them, Link must place the Item present in other nearby Offering Spots into an empty one. Doing so will cause a Korok to appear and give Link a Korok Seed. List of Offering Spots A total of one Offering Spot can be found in Akkala. A total of six Offering Spots can be found in Central Hyrule. A total of one Offering Spot can be found in Faron. A total of five Offering Spots can be found in Gerudo. A total of four Offering Spots can be found in Hebra. A total of 11 Offering Spots can be found in Necluda. Food Offerings in operate the same as they did in . A line of Stone Statues, Frog Statues, or Zonai Owl Statues while have trays in front of them, most of which have a certain Item inside. In these types of Korok Seed Puzzles, Link must place a matching Item inside the empty trays. A new variety of Food Offerings involves multiple Statues surrounding a single tray, in which Link must place Items matching to the number of Statues. When either type of Puzzle is solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Foothill Stable is nestled along Ternio Trail in eastern Trilby Valley, right at the entrance to Eldin Canyon. The Stable is surrounded by rugged hills and cliffs, giving it its name. On the eastern cliff stands the Mo'a Keet Shrine, which when activated, can be used as a convenient Travel Gate to the Stable. The Foothill Stable contains every amenity characteristic to Stables, including Horse services, providing lodging, and a Cooking Pot for Cooking. Several Wooden Boxes are left outside which can be broken for small Items. As with all other Stables, Beedle can be found within or in front of Foothill Stable, where he sells his wares. Kass the Rito bard can be found at the Stable, who when spoken to, will offer to sing Link an "Ancient Song". The travelers Boldon, Dayto, Kairo, Karsh, and Zorona all stop at Foothill Stable on their journeys. A worker at Foothill Stable named Gaile sells Fireproof Elixirs to travelers who are intending to brave the Scorching Climate of Eldin Canyon. She will sell one Elixir for 60 Rupees, two for 110, and three for 150. In addition to this, a poster inside the Stable depicts a Recipe for Fireproof Elixirs. Inside the Stable is a large Painting depicting Trilby Valley and the Foothill Stable. One of the Stable's regulars, Mayro, can be found admiring the Painting. Mayro states that it was painted by Ozunda. He believes that the Stable depicted in the Painting was painted from the southern direction. The Painting provides a clue to the location of the Tah Muhl Shrine, and speaking with Mayro initiates the "A Landscape of a Stable" Shrine Quest. The Foothill Stable is run by Ozunda, who mans both its Horse services and lodging. When staying at Foothill Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Ozunda explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Ozunda offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Ozunda will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Ozunda will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Foothill Stable Well is located behind Foothill Stable within Eldin Canyon. A Ladder can be found inside its stone rim, which allows Link to access its interior. A majority of the Well's inner chamber consists of a pond, though there is a small shore along the southwestern wall that bears an Ore Deposit and a Luminous Stone Deposit. There are also two pieces of Lumber and a Metal Plate within the Well's Water. The Foothill Stable Well is one of several Wells that Fera can be found in prior to beginning the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?". She rates the Well's Water quality as good and its moss growth as limited, in addition to confirming the presence of Brightcaps. She leaves for the Lookout Landing Well once her Side Quest has started. Creatures Materials Treasure Chests

are Items in . Location and Uses Forest Dweller's Bows are Bows made by Koroks for use by Hylians. As a result, they can commonly be found in the Korok Forest, but they can be found in Treasure Chests on the Tabantha Frontier and Hyrule Ridge as well. These Bows belong to the Korok Gear equipment archetype. They are crafted from flexible wood, and the bowstring is made from sturdy vines. Forest Dweller's Bows are capable of firing three Arrows at once in trade for only dealing a smaller amount of damage per hit. They have a slightly slowed Arrow flight speed compared to other Bows, with Arrows fired from them travelling roughly 11% slower. A Forest Dweller's Bow is one of the Weapons given to Link during "The Test of Wood" Shrine Quest, with which he must fight his way to the Maag Halan Shrine. The other two weapons are the Forest Dweller's Shield and Forest Dweller's Sword. If any of these Items are switched out or break, the trial is over and must be restarted. Being made of wood, Forest Dweller's Bows will burn if they touch Fire or if they are equipped in a Scorching Climate. They will also float if they are dropped in Water, and they will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity. Finally, they cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune.

are recurring Items in . Forest Dweller's Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Forest Dweller's Shields are Shields made by Koroks specifically for Hylians to use. This is common among Korok Gear, which includes all Weapons created by Koroks. They are only found in three locations in and around the Great Hyrule Forest, though an additional one can be found in a Treasure Chest at Floria Falls. They are made from the finest hard wood in the Korok Forest, making them deceivingly sturdy. As part of "The Test of Wood" Shrine Quest, Damia will give Link a Forest Dweller's Shield, Forest Dweller's Sword, and Forest Dweller's Bow he must use to fight his way to the Maag Halan Shrine. If he switches out or breaks any of these Items, the trial must be restarted. Being made of wood, Forest Dweller's Shields will burn to a crisp if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. If Link drops them in Water, they will float. They also do not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning in Thunderstorms like a metal shield would. Forest Dweller's Shields reappear in Other Appearances Forest Dweller's Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Forest Dweller's Swords.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Forest Dweller's Spears are Weapons made by Koroks to be used by Hylians. They belong to the equipment archetype known as Korok Gear, which consists of many Weapons created by Koroks. They are entirely made of wood, and they are both easy to use and strong. They are commonly found in Treasure Chests in and around Hyrule Ridge and the Great Hyrule Forest. Being made of wood, Forest Dweller's Spears will float when dropped in Water. While they will not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, they will burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. The Magnesis Rune is incapable of picking up Forest Dweller's Spears. Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Forest Dweller's Swords were made by the Koroks for the Hylians to use. They belong to the Korok Gear equipment archetype. It is likely they were intended to clear paths through forests. They are mostly commonly found in and around Hyrule Field and the Great Hyrule Forest. "The Test of Wood" Shrine Quest requires Link to use a Forest Dweller's Sword, as well as a Forest Dweller's Shield and Forest Dweller's Bow, to fight his way to the Maag Halan Shrine. The trial is failed and must be restarted if Link switches his Weapons or one of them breaks. As a wooden weapon, Forest Dweller's Swords are flammable and will burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. If dropped in Water, they will float. They also will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, nor can they conduct Electricity. They also are unable to be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Forest Dweller's Swords have been decayed as a result of the Upheaval. Other Appearances

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Forest Octoroks are a type of Octorok that have adapted to live in forests. They hide underground and disguise themselves as shrubbery, jumping out if a person wanders close enough. If a Forest Octorok spots Link, it will spit rocks at him from afar. These can be deflected by a performing a Perfect Guard, which defeats the Forest Octorok in the process. If their shrubbery is cut, Forest Octoroks will pop out of the ground in confusion, leaving themselves open for an attack. Similar to Forest Octoroks in , Forest Octoroks in are found in certain Forests throughout Hyrule. They jump out of the ground and shoot Rocks at Link when he walks by. Cutting off the Grass on top of their head will cause them to pop up in confusion and look around, giving Link the opportunity to defeat them. Other Appearances Forest Octoroks appear as Enemies in , and often drop Octorok Eyeballs or Octo Balloons upon defeat. Killing one also rewards the Warriors with a Octorok Trophy at the end of a Challenge or Scenario. Forest Octoroks can be found as some of the main Enemies in Challenges such "Sidon vs. the Octoroks" and "Hair-Width Trial: Expert+", and are often also found in grassy areas.

The Forest of Spirits is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Forest of Spirits is a heavily-wooded area in the north of the Great Plateau that encircles Hopper Pond. It is lush with wildlife, inhabited by various Creatures as well as a plethora of plant-based Materials. In particular, the Forest is home to large numbers of Woodland Boars. Various ruins sit within the forest. A Zonai Tower can be found at the Forest's northwestern reaches. An uninhabited camp containing a Campfire and a Cooking Pot can be found in the eastern reaches of the Forest of Spirits. An enormous hollow log with the top rotted away can be found near the center of the Forest of Spirits. North of this log, Link can find a Monster Encampment. A Stone Talus can be found in the rocky clearing in the eastern portion of the Forest. During "The Isolated Plateau" Main Quest, Link can find the Old Man hunting in the Forest. He cautions Link to crouch in order to not disturb his prey. Link can ask him for advice with hunting, and he will respond accordingly to Link's current equipment. If Link does not yet have a Bow, the Old Man explains that he may have difficulty hunting prey as it runs away. Otherwise, he advises Link to get as close as possible to prey and aim carefully in order to kill it quickly. After this, he goes to sit in the camp nearby to rest his back. While at the camp, the Old Man invites Link to Cook with the Cooking Pot should he ever find himself hungry. If Link presents a Spicy Meat and Seafood Fry to the Old Man, he will be surprised that Link was able to make his signature dish that he had long forgotten. As thanks for sharing Link's Recipe with him, he gives Link a Warm Doublet and assures Link that he will be fine without it because the Food will be able to keep him safe from the Freezing Climates. However, he will not be able to do this if Link has already obtained the Warm Doublet from the Old Man at the Old Man's Cabin or at the peak of Mount Hylia. During the "EX The Champions' Ballad" Main Quest, Link must visit the Forest of Spirits and defeat certain Enemies in order to make the Yowaka Ita Shrine appear. As part of the requirements of the Quest, Link must also do this with only a quarter of a Heart left and the One-Hit Obliterator as his only melee Weapon. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Equipment Inhabitants Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests The Forest of Spirits is geographically identical to its incarnation, though the Stone Talus has become a Battle Talus after having a Monster Stronghold built on top of it. The is a recurring location in . The Forest of Time goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Forest of Time is the region in Labrynna where Link begins his quest. The first person he meets is Impa, who was sent by Princess Zelda to look for Nayru. It is in this area that Link meets Nayru, Ralph, and Veran, the antagonist of the game, for the first time. Link also witnesses the possession of Nayru by Veran here. Nayru's House is also located in a Tree in the northeastern corner of the Forest of Time. During his quest Link will pass through this area to reach Yoll Graveyard and Rolling Ridge. In the southwestern corner of the Forest is a rocky area where Link will meet Tingle. However, to reach Tingle, Link will require Ricky's assistance, as his path is blocked by holes and cliffs. Tingle will give Link the Island Chart which is necessary if Link is to reach Crescent Island. Later on, Tingle will upgrade Link's Seed Satchel, allowing him to carry 50 Mystical Seeds. In a Linked Game of , Link will receive a secret which can be told to Tingle, who will then upgrade his Satchel again, allowing him to carry a maximum of 99 Seeds. The Forest of Time is a wooded area northeast of the Great Plateau in . A monster-infested camp is situated toward the south in a small clearing. A Chuchu hides inside one of two Barrel at the camp. A wooden Treasure Chest containing 10 Arrows sits next to a pair of crates within the camp, adjacent to two decayed Wagons. A metallic Treasure Chest containing a bundle of five Fire Arrows sits atop a platform in a clearing in the south of the Forest. A Barrel containing a Roasted Bird Drumstick and two Bomb Barrels can also be found on the platform. A stone Treasure Chest containing an Amber can be found atop a tower at the northern base of the small plateau at the southern portion of the Forest. Creatures Enemies Normal Mode Master Mode Materials Equipment The Forest of Time is now dotted with Fallen Debris. A road passes through the center of the Forest, which is now used by travelers such as Brigo. The road forks at the east, continuing on north toward Whistling Hill while an unmarked branch leads south to the East Post Ruins. At this fork, Link can find Hyrule Restoration Materials. are characters in . Biography Forge Constructs are responsible for converting Zonaite into energy resources. A majority of them can be found at Abandoned Mines in the Depths. However, one is stationed within the Mining Cave on the Great Sky Island. The Forge Construct in the Mining Cave serves to explain what Zonaite is to Link. If Link speaks to it or attempts to pick up a piece of Zonaite from the forge, prompting a warning, it will explain that Zonaite is a precious mineral found typically beneath the Surface as well as trace deposits in the Mining Cave, and that the Zonai civilization utilized the material by processing it. It then explains this processing is done through smelting, and provides several of the resulting materials for Link. The Construct presents Zonai Charges and Crystallized Charges and offers to explain them. Link can purchase these with Zonaite, which the Forge Construct will use to create more for later stock. Forge Constructs in the Depths remain dormant until Link activates them with the Right Arm, some of whom have done so to avoid intruders from the Yiga Clan until Link defeats them. After greeting Link, these Forge Constructs display a wider array of materials for trading, and will then appear as a Shop on the Map. Link may also ask them to re-explain the concepts of Zonaite and processing it. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Fort Hateno is located in East Necluda, demarcating the border between East and West Necluda. The surrounding cliffs, Cliffs of Quince to the east, make Fort Hateno a small enclosure. Ore Deposits can be found on the lower levers of the cliffs. Much of the ground level is covered in Trees, with a lone Lodge hiding among their shade, and a Cooking Pot at the entrance to the Fort. The Squabble River hugs the cliff in the south, and the broken remains of a Wagon can be found along the road leading through the Fort. Near this Wagon sits a small camping spot with a Wooden Box, a Barrel, and a Garbage Dump. A lone Chuchu can be found hiding inside the Barrel. During the second Great Calamity, Fort Hateno served as a tactical defense point for the Hylian army. Link and Zelda attempted to flee to Fort Hateno but were met with Guardians at Blatchery Plain. Fort Hateno was ill-equipped for serious combat, but the surrounding terrain impeded the Guardians' attacks upon the Fort. The combined efforts of Link, Zelda, the militia from the citizens of Hateno Village and the Hylian forces stationed at Fort Hateno led to the successful defense of the Fort, narrowly sparing those living east of its walls. Following the victory at Fort Hateno, minor repair efforts were carried out to restore its fortifications, however these repairs were in a very limited capacity as those trained in stonemasonry were lost during the Great Calamity. Despite the successful defense of Fort Hateno, a small number of Guardians still roamed the land west of the Fort for 40 or 50 years. After developing the Ancient Arrows, Robbie used them to rid the territory of the Guardians to atone for his failure to sufficiently support Link during the Great Calamity. As a result of the battles with Guardians, the remains of Guardians that can be found at Fort Hateno can be searched for Ancient Materials. The Hylian travelers, Agus, Celessa, Joute, Teli, and Toma, can be found traveling along the road leading through the Fort. Calip and Garill can be seen living at the Fort. A stone Treasure Chest containing an Iron Sledgehammer sits atop a Zonai Tower behind Fort Hateno's wall. Two more stone Treasure Chests can be found under some Rocks, one containing Opal, the other an Emblazoned Shield. To the northern part of the area hides a Korok in a Natural Hiding Spot, where Link must move a metal door with Magnesis or Stasis before removing the Rock to get the Korok Seed. Another Korok puzzle can be found on top of the stone gates. Standing next to a Pinwheel, Link must successfully shoot two Acorn-shaped Jars that are seemingly being thrown above the wooded area before he is rewarded. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Fortified Pumpkins are one of three foodstuffs favored by the Sheikah, with the others being Swift Carrots and Mighty Bananas. They are primarily and exclusively cultivated by the Sheikah farmer Olkin, who sells 8 from his field in Kakariko Village. Olkin sells the Fortified Pumpkins he grows from Olkin's Pumpkins because his rival, Steen, refuses to have them stocked at his wife's shop. There are nine Pumpkin plants in the patch, yet only eight bear fruit. During the evening, Olkin's wife Mellie Cooks him dishes containing many Fortified Pumpkins, which Olkin feels is better than Swift Carrots. Some may also be purchased from the Wandering Merchant Cambo, and Hinoxes have a chance to drop them upon their defeat. Eaten raw, Fortified Pumpkins restore half of a Heart. They can also be roasted by a Fire or Scorching Climate to create Baked Fortified Pumpkins. When Cooked in a dish, the resulting Meal temporarily provides Link with Defense Up. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Fortified Pumpkins can be used to create Orange Dye. As part of the Side Quest "Riddles of Hyrule", Walton will ask Link to bring him Kakariko Village's specialty Fruit, which has rock-hard flesh. If Link returns with a Fortified Pumpkin, Walton will be excited he figured the riddle out and move on to the next one. When Cooking, Fortified Pumpkins can be replaced by a Carrot in some cases. They are required for the following Meals: Like other Vegetables, Fortified Pumpkins can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Fortified Pumpkins and Sun Pumpkins can be used interchangeably when Cooking. In some cases, they can also be replaced by a Carrot. are Room Units in . Location and Uses Foyers are Room Units that cost 300 Rupees, and they are sold by Grantéson through Hudson Construction's Dream Home program. In addition, Link will receive both a Foyer and a Bedroom through the contract he makes with Hudson Construction during the Side Quest "Home on Arrange". Foyers can be manipulated and attached to other Room Units through the use of Ultrahand, but only while construction is taking place. If a Foyer is left outside of Link's plot when construction concludes, it will be stored on his behalf by Grantéson. They are the only Room Units that feature doors, allowing them to serve as an entryway for Link's House.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Fragrant Mushroom Sautés are a meal that can be made by Cooking Goron Spice with Mushrooms together in a Cooking Pot. Regular Fragrant Mushroom Sautés can be made by using a Hylian Shroom in the recipe or by using multiple mushrooms with differing effects. Eating them will heal some of Link's missing Hearts. The aroma of these dishes make mouths water. Fragrant Mushroom Sautés are favored by Nellie, a resident of Gerudo Town, who makes it whenever she is feeling tired. Based on the types of Mushrooms used, several different variations of Fragrant Mushroom Sauté exist: Hearty Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Hearty Truffles or Big Hearty Truffles. Eating them will heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum hearts. Energizing Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Stamella Shrooms. When eaten, they will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Enduring Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Endura Shrooms. They completely refill Link's Stamina Wheel when consumed. Hasty Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Rushrooms. If they are eaten, they will temporarily boost Link's movement speed. Spicy Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Sunshrooms. Consuming one will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance for a short period of time. Electro Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Zapshrooms. Eating them gives Link one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Razorshrooms. When eaten, they will temporarily increase the damage of Link's attacks. Tough Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Ironshrooms. If they are eaten, Link's defense will be boosted for a short period of time. Sneaky Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Silent Shrooms. Eating one increases Link's Stealth for a time. Chilly Fragrant Mushroom Sauté: Made using Chillshrooms. When consumed, Link will temporarily gain one level of Heat Resistance.

, also known as Cold Weather, are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Freezing Climates are located in snowy locations, such as Mount Hylia, the Hebra Mountains, Mount Lanayru, and the Gerudo Highlands. Other Freezing Climates can be found at high elevations, such as the tops of the Akkala Tower, the Wasteland Tower, and Hyrule Castle. When Link is in one of these Climates, he will begin to shiver and take damage. This can be avoided by wearing the Snowquill Set or Warm Doublet or drinking a Spicy Elixir, all of which will grant Cold Resistance. When Meat Materials are dropped in Freezing Climates, they will harden into Frozen Food. Much of the Water will also be Cold Water, which causes Link to take damage when he Swims in it. In , the entirety of Hebra Mountain is a Freezing Climate as the result of a Blizzard. During the Main Quest "Rift on Holy Mount Lanayru", the Blizzard and its Freezing Climate shift, only covering the Mountain's lowest levels. When Zelda is in a Freezing Climate, the screen becomes frosted with Ice, and she gradually begins losing Hearts. The effects of Freezing Climates can be avoided by consuming drinks that provide the Chill-Proof Added Effect, such as Warming Potions or Warm Smoothies. Zelda can also avoid damage by staying close to sources of Fire, including Braziers and Ignizols.

is a recurring character in . Biography Frelly is a Gerudo who manages the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth in Gerudo Town. The Northwest Booth is managed by Frelly's mother, Kohm. Link can first encounter Frelly in the Gerudo Desert just outside the front gate of Gerudo Town. When Link speaks to her, Frelly asks if Link crossed the Desert on foot. If Link tells her that he came on foot, Frelly comments that it must have been difficult and that it is common sense to travel the Gerudo Desert with a Sand Seal. If Link says he rode there, Frelly is impressed that a Hylian man has mastered Sand Seal surfing. Frelly is speechless, pausing for a moment before saying that it must have been a challenge to catch a Sand Seal. Frelly then introduces herself and explains that she rents out trained Sand Seals for people who do not have the time to train their own. She assures Link that she can answer any questions he has about Sand Seals and that she is skilled at training them. When Link asks about Sand Seals, Frelly explains that they are native to the Gerudo Desert Gateway. She then says that it is dangerous to cross the Gerudo Desert on foot, but one would breeze along by crossing with a Sand Seal. This has made them very important to the Gerudo. If Link asks Frelly how to catch a Sand Seal, she tells him that they are sensitive to sound and that they must be approached very slowly. However, she points out that most Gerudo simply rent a Sand Seal to avoid the hassle of catching one. If Link asks how to ride a Sand Seal, Frelly tells him that he only needs a Shield, since Sand Seals will simply go in whatever direction he steers them. She recommends that the best way to learn is to try it. Frelly also tells Link to come by her shop in Gerudo Town to rent a Sand Seal if he has trouble catching one, but quickly remembers that men are not allowed inside the Town's walls. If Link is wearing the Gerudo Outfit, Frelly tells him to look for the big Sand-Seal Statue to find her shop in Gerudo Town. If Link speaks to Frelly at the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth, she says that Sand Seals are the best way to cross the Gerudo Desert. She offers Link a Sand Seal rental for 20 Rupees, but if he does not have any Shields, she will include a Wooden Shield for a total of 50 Rupees. If Link wishes to rent a Sand Seal, he will tell Frelly to "seal the deal", which is a pun that confuses her. After hearing this, Frelly herself will start to use Sand Seal puns, such as telling Link that it would be a "sealious mistake" to travel the Gerudo Desert without a Sand Seal and saying "seal you another time" when Link makes a rental.

is a recurring character in . Biography Frita is a traveling Rito woman that is visiting Gerudo Town. She can always be found standing by Estan's Stall, which sells a variety of Roasted Meats. If Link speaks to Frita, she greets him and explains that she wants to use the Gerudo greeting. However, she is worried that she will embarrass herself and feels that it would seem like she is bragging. Frita then asks Link}if he gets many visitors where he is from, commenting that Gerudo Town is drastically different from her home, Rito Village. She explains that she wanted to try the Meat in Gerudo Town, but she is disappointed that they do not have any poultry. Despite this, she is still interested in the Meat, staring at it all day and night and believing she would eat three servings if it was her dinner. Frita also comments that she does not see any other Rito in Town and wonders if she is the only one visiting. Estan notices Frita's dissatisfaction with the wares in her General Store and wonders if she has something against Meat. However, she thinks that would be impossible. If Link talks to Frita at night, she explains that Rito do not have good night vision, but Gerudo Town's brightly lit environment allows her to see everything. She comments that if Rito Village was brighter, they would be able to go out at night like the Gerudo do. After the Sahasra Slope Skyview Tower and Thyphlo Ruins Skyview Tower have both been activated and the Side Adventure "Lurelin Village Restoration Project" has been completed, Frita can be found in Lurelin Village. She and Billson are relaxing under a Palm Tree in the eastern part of the Village. When spoken to, she senses that she and Billson are similar to each other.

Side Adventure, Traysi offers the Armor Set to Link as an incentive for his help investigating the disappearance of Zelda. Wearing pieces of Froggy Armor will reduce how often Link slips when Climbing a wet surface. is a recurring character in . Biography Fronk is a Zora who can be found at Zora's Domain. Alongside Ledo, he is working on repairing the Domain as an apprentice under the smithy Dento. When Link initially approaches Fronk, he will be distant from him. He may ask Link to get out of his way. He might also be quiet for a moment, before he apologize to Link and explains that he was lost in thought. After the Divine Beast Vah Ruta is appeased by Link, Fronk can be found hammering a pillar in Zora's Domain while conversing with himself. If Link speaks to him, Fronk will apologize and explain that he was talking to himself. Fronk says that after Ruta started rampaging, his wife Mei went out to go fishing. Even though the Divine Beast is appeased, she still has not returned. Fronk wishes he had made her stay and wonders what he should do. If Link offers to find Mei, Fronk expresses his gratitude and apologizes for placing this burden on him. This unlocks the "A Wife Washed Away" Side Quest. Fronk says he will help Link however he can to find Mei. If Link asks about Mei, Fronk again says she is his wife and the mother of his children, Tumbo and Keye. He says she spends her days catching Fish and selling them at the Coral Reef General Store. Fronk describes Mei as being very lively and cheerful, believing Tumbo gets that from her. Fronk recalls that she was fishing in the Zora River, which began to swell from Divine Beast Vah Ruta's Rain. He believes that the worst case scenario is that she was carried to Lake Hylia. Once Mei has returned to Zora's Domain, Fronk scolds his wife and tells her that she should not go wandering anymore for a while. Fronk is overwhelmingly appreciative towards Link and thanks him multiple times. If Link speaks to him again, Fronk calls him a true Champion and thanks him in a more composed manner.

are recurring Enemies in . They are miniature versions of the Frost Talus. Characteristics Frost Pebblits are juvenile Frost Taluses. They are mainly found in snowy areas, such as the Hebra Mountains and Gerudo Highlands. Due to their young age, Frost Pebblits' bodies are light and fragile, leaving them vulnerable to Remote Bomb blasts. As they mature, Frost Pebblits will toughen up, eventually becoming entirely composed of Ice. Due to their coloring, Frost Pebblits often blend in with their surroundings, being somewhat difficult to spot until they become active. Their primary attack is moving toward Link and attempting to swipe at him with one arm. Coming into contact with one will cause Link to become frozen for a short period of time. This can be avoided by throwing Remote Bombs from a distance or melting the Frost Pebblit's icy coating with a heat-based Weapon, such as Fire Arrows or Flameblades. Alternatively, wearing the entire Snowquill Set will grant Link the Unfreezable Set Bonus, so long as has been enhanced twice by a Great Fairy. This allows the Pebblit to be picked up and thrown in order to defeat it. Frost Pebblits will explode when they are thrown or if Link holds them for too long. Drops Other Appearances

They can be made by exposing Hyrule Basses or Staminoka Basses to a Freezing Climate or Cold Water. Link can eat a Frozen Bass to restore two Hearts to his Life Gauge and receive one minute of Heat Resistance.

Nutcake and Sautéed Nuts also specifically require an Acorn or a Chickaloo Tree Nut. List of Fruits List of Fruits Other Appearances Fruits are a type of Material that appear in the Spoils menu. The , also known as , is a recurring General Store in . Features and Overview Lorn's Fruit Stand is a Stall located near the front gate of Gerudo Town, directly next to the entrance to Starlight Memories. It is operated by Lorn, who advertises that her Fruits are fresh and ready to be eaten. She also claims that her wares are as sweet as her daughter, Dalia. At night, Dalia sleeps at the Stand beside her mother. Emri, who sells Fruits in Kara Kara Bazaar, states that her General Store has more Hydromelons that Lorn's Fruit Stand. Oftentimes, Lorn tries to provide Fruits for Patricia to eat. After Link frees Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Lorn remarks on how Patricia was involved in the act, and she begins to work on rebranding her Stall to associate it with the heroic Sand Seal. Whenever Link purchases Fruit from Lorn's Fruit Stand, she will thank him for his business. If Link buys the entire stock of a single Fruit, Lorn will promise to restock for him soon. Lastly, if Link buys all of Lorn's Fruits, she claims that they were so fresh that her Stall still smells like them. Wares and Pricing Wares and Pricing

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Fruitcakes are a type of Cake made by Cooking either an Apple or a Wildberry, any Fruit, Tabantha Wheat, and Cane Sugar together in a Cooking Pot. Regular versions of Fruitcake can be made by only using ingredients that do not grant any effects. They can be eaten to restore some Hearts to Link's Life Gauge. Fruitcakes make use of fruits found all over Hyrule Kingdom, and they are commonly used in celebrations. The first Castle Library Book outlines the recipe for Fruitcake, noting it to be a secret of the Royal Family of Hyrule and Princess Zelda's favorite food. The Book suggests boiling two or more pieces of Fruit with Tabantha Wheat and Cane Sugar for a while. This dish is known to help clear one's head and help with focus, which Zelda apparently took advantage of while she researched Ancient Technology. As part of the "A Royal Recipe" Side Quest, Link can give Gotter at Riverside Stable a Fruitcake. After eating it, he at first describes it as having a refreshing aroma, reminiscent of galloping across the planes on horseback. However, he states that undersells the complexity of the dish, saying it fills him with the intensity of being seen by a Guardian. Gotter calls Fruitcake an elegant dish and explains he never thought he would taste something so thrilling. As a reward, he will give Link a Silver Rupee. Several different variations of Fruitcake can be made, based on both the kind of Fruit used and whether any additional ingredients are added: Chilly Fruitcake: Made using Hydromelons or other chilly ingredients. They grant Link one level of Heat Resistance temporarily if they are consumed. Electro Fruitcake: Made using Voltfruits or other electric ingredients. They grant Link one level of Shock Resistance when eaten. Enduring Fruitcake: Made using enduring ingredients. If they are eaten, they will completely refill and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Fruitcake: Made using energizing ingredients. When eaten, they will replenish a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Fruitcake: Made using Fleet-Lotus Seeds or other hasty ingredients. Eating them will increase Link's movement speed for a short period of time. Hearty Fruitcake: Made using Hearty Durians or other hearty ingredients. Eating these cakes will completely heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him temporary Hearts. Mighty Fruitcake: Made using Mighty Bananas or other mighty ingredients. If eaten, they increase the power of Link's attacks for a short time. Sneaky Fruitcake: Made using sneaky ingredients. When eaten, these Cakes will increase Link's Stealth for a short period of time. Spicy Fruitcake: Made using Spicy Peppers or other spicy ingredients. When consumed, they grant Link one level of Cold Resistance temporarily. Tough Fruitcake: Made using tough ingredients. is a recurring character in . Biography Fugo is a Goron who lives in Goron City. He can be found outside of the blacksmith Rohan's House. Fugo is training under Rohan as his apprentice so that he may one day be his successor. Even when he is tired, Fugo will answer any questions. According to Fugo, Rohan is a blacksmith who keeps the ancient arts alive. However, while Rohan is working, he warns Link to approach him carefully. When Rohan is sleeping, Fugo suggests that Link come back the next day to speak to him. As part of his training, Rohan tasked Fugo with defeating every Igneo Talus around Goron City. He later explains that Rohan fought every Igneo Talus to grow stronger when he was young, and he hopes to also reach that same goal. However, Fugo laments that he cannot get to the Igneo Talus at Darunia Lake, and openly wishes that someone else could go in his stead. This starts "The Road to Respect" Side Quest. Upon defeating the Igneo Talus and returning to Fugo, he is surprised to learn that Link defeated the monster. Fugo then decides to offer Link 100 Rupees in exchange for the achievement, and gives him a Silver Rupee. in return. Fugo eagerly plans to tell Rohan about his false success. However, he cannot work up the courage to tell him nor confide his secret. He realizes that he has a long way to go before he learns Rohan's secrets.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Fural Plain is located in the Faron Grasslands between Harfin Valley and Guchini Plain. The Fural Plain is a large plain that is surrounded by many small cliffs, and also sprouts many clumps of Trees throughout the landscape. In the southwest corner of the Fural Plain, the Haran Lake rests between a few Trees, and in the southeastern corner of the Fural Plain, the Highland Stable sits between two small cliffs. A small path runs through the middle of the Plain, and along the path, Totsuna can be found running across it. A Korok can be found by jumping into a Circle of Lily Pads in the Lake of the Horse God. is a recurring character in . Biography Furosa is a Gerudo who manages The Noble Canteen in Gerudo Town. When Link speaks to Furosa, she greets him and is surprised to see a "Hylian vai" in Town. Furosa comments that Link seems too young for the special adult drinks that she mixes. If Link asks about the special drinks, Furosa explains that they make the drinks with the Ice from the Northern Icehouse. If Link asks for drink recommendations, Furosa tells him about their featured cocktail, the Noble Pursuit. She describes the taste of the Noble Pursuit as a light, sweet and cool sensation and that it is like drinking "distilled motivation." When asked if they serve Milk, Furosa is appalled by the idea of serving something so childish. She then complains, thinking that Greta sent Link to say that as a prank and criticizes the Gerudo Secret Club for only drawing young people's attention. When Link ends the conversation, Furosa comments that she has not seen Pokki in a while, explaining that she used to come to The Noble Canteen every day to drink a Noble Pursuit. Furosa cuts herself off and apologizes after realizing that there is no reason to talk to Link about this. During "The Perfect Drink" Shrine Quest, Link can try to order a Noble Pursuit from Furosa. However, she needs a huge amount of ice to make the drink and she is all out. In addition, due to its strength, she refuses to sell it to Link. After Link informs her that it is for Pokki, she laments that she can not carry the Ice from the Northern Icehouse. Link can offer to retrieve the Ice on Furosa's behalf. Since Pokki is her best customer, Furosa is grateful that Link wants to help. She tells Link that if he explains the situation to Anche, she will allow him to take the Ice, but he should get there while the sun is up since Anche goes to bed early. Once she realizes the distance Link would have to carry the Ice, Furosa offers to take it from him at the entrance to the North Gerudo Ruins. Upon arriving to the Northern Icehouse, Link gets permission from Anche to take some Ice once she finds out it is for Furosa. She warns Link to take the heat into account as he moves, as Furosa has no use for water. After this, the Carry the Ice! Mini-Game will begin. Link must now carry the block of Ice to Furosa, who is waiting for Link past the North Gerudo Ruins. If Link is not wearing the Gerudo Outfit, Furosa realizes that he is a man but decides it does not matter. She confirms that he has brought her Ice from the Northern Icehouse and that it is in good shape. She tells him that she may be able to make the best Noble Pursuit she has ever made with the Ice he brought. Furosa asks Link to inform

She tells him that she may be able to make the best Noble Pursuit she has ever made with the Ice he brought. Furosa asks Link to inform Pokki that the "best drink ever" is waiting for her, and she believes Pokki will come running when she hears about it. When Pokki has returned to The Noble Canteen, she and Furosa can be found speaking to each other at the bar. Pokki asks if there is any better than the taste of a Noble Pursuit. Furosa is shocked Pokki ran all the way from Misae Suma Shrine when she was at death's door and asks if she has given up investigating the Ancient Shrine. When Pokki calls the work dull, Furosa reveals that she never thought it would be her thing. Pokki declares that her thing is drinking. Furosa is thankful that Link was able to help Pokki, claiming that while she heard people outside of Gerudo Town are cold, Link does not seem to be. She tells Link to come back to The Noble Canteen when he is of age, at which point they will celebrate with a Noble Pursuit. If Link talks to Anche again, she will ask him to deliver more Ice to Furosa for her. Anche charges Link 50 Rupees for the ice and explains that Furosa will reimburse him. Link is timed during this delivery. Furosa will reward Link depending on how quickly he delivered the Ice. If Link takes more than two minutes to reach Furosa, she will call him a professional at delivering Ice. She considers a Silver Rupee an ample payment for his services. Furosa also remarks that managing the Northern Icehouse seems to suit Anche and makes her happy. If Link reaches Furosa in under two minutes, she will be shocked with his time. She claims that he has gone beyond her expectations and calls him a savant, rewarding him with a Gold Rupee. Furosa also states that Anche must be happy, since the Ice seems to be happy as well. After giving Link his reward, Furosa asks Link if he is willing to make another delivery. Once again, Link will have to pay Anche the 50 Rupee fee. If Link accepts, Furosa tells him that she will be waiting for his delivery. However, if Link refuses, she tells him to talk to Anche when he feels up to it.

is a recurring ability in . Overview Fuse is an Ancient Power that allows Link to bond any Items and most Objects and Weapons with his equipped Weapon or Shield. Items from the Inventory can also be attached to Arrows. Internally, the two parts of a fused weapon are distinguished as the "base" and the "attachment". Different attachments grant the base special Fuse Properties, as well as other effects depending on what is used. An Item that has been Fused with a Weapon or Shield can be removed in the Inventory to let the base equipment be Fused with something else, but doing so will destroy the Fused Item in the process. However, Pelison's Break-a-Part Shop in Tarrey Town can do so while preserving the Fused Item so it can be re-Fused with other equipment. Weapons Using Fuse on melee Weapons has by far the most range of effects. Any Fused material will increase the attack power of the Weapon, and usually change its shape and thus its hitbox/reach. Base Weapons retain their Weapon Traits and Weapon Bonuses. Almost every Object or Item fused to a Weapon grants it a new ability, known as a Fuse Property. Durability Using Fuse on a Weapon in effect increases its Durability. The actual effect of this is that the base weapon gains access to a certain amount of "bonus" durability, which is 25 for most Weapons. Any strike that lands with the Fused Weapon depletes this bonus Durability, with the base Weapon's Durability not being depleted until either all bonus Durability is used up or the attachment is removed or broken. However, this bonus value is saved but not consumed when the attachment is removed or broken. Weapons attached to the end of another will use their own durability alongside the base Weapon's, and they will break if it is depleted. If the base Weapon is Fused again, it can utilize any remaining "bonus" Durability. Any attachment, regardless of its own Durability, will break when the base Weapon's Durability is depleted. As an example, if a Fierce Deity Sword (base) is Fused with a Gloom Sword (attachment), the fusion will last for 15 hits without depleting any of the Fierce Deity Sword's base 35 Durability. This corresponds with the Gloom Sword's Durability. However, 15 of its 25 "bonus" Durability will be depleted. After the Gloom Sword breaks, the Fierce Deity Sword will use up its base Durability until another fusion is made, which allows the 10 remaining bonus Durability to be used. While a Weapon's base Durability is used when it is an attachment, simply Fusing it restores its "bonus" Durability. This means Fusing a Weapon to the end of another and detaching it at Pelison's Break-a-Part Shop effectively gives it more Durability, as long as the Weapon itself now has something else attached to it. However, Fusing also removes any Weapon Bonus modifier the attachment may have had, though these can be regained at random with Rock Octoroks. Additionally, allowing a Rock

it at Pelison's Break-a-Part Shop effectively gives it more Durability, as long as the Weapon itself now has something else attached to it. However, Fusing also removes any Weapon Bonus modifier the attachment may have had, though these can be regained at random with Rock Octoroks. Additionally, allowing a Rock Octorok to swallow a Weapon will completely restore the base and "bonus" Durability of both pieces. This can be used to repair Weapons that Rock Octoroks normally refuse to when they are a base, such as the Champions' arms or Weapons sold by Bargainer Statues. The sparkle at the top-right of a Weapon's icon indicates that it still has full Durability. Thus, any use of the Weapon with or without the Fuse will make the spark disappear. The icon flashing red indicates that a Weapon has three or less Durability points. Possibly due to an oversight, the "bonus" 25 fusion durability of the Master Sword is never recharged alongside its base Durability, and because the Master Sword cannot be dropped or Fused with anything, it cannot be repaired with the above methods. This means the Master Sword will never again show the "sparkle" indicating full durability in Link's Inventory. The Decayed Master Sword also cannot have anything Fused to it in the first place, though it technically has a bonus Durability of 25 that cannot be utilized without glitches. Shield Fusions do not increase durability or Shield Guard, with the exception of the long Lava Slab which increases Shield Guard by 1. This means Fusions with no special properties, such as most other Shields, do not do anything aside from modifying the Shield's hitbox and friction when Shield Surfing. Depending on the Object being Fused to the Shield, Shield Surfing may also be enhanced or outright disabled. Arrows Arrows can be Fused with Materials to imbue them with more attack power or other special effects. This is done using the quick menu instead of actually utilizing the Fuse ability. As such, only Materials from the Inventory can be fused to Arrows, and not Objects from the overworld. For example, unique to arrow fusion, Keese Eyeballs that are Fused with Arrows can home in on Enemies and Creatures that would normally be too fast for Link to hit reliably, and Arrows Fused with icy Materials such as White Chuchu Jellies can freeze targets upon impact. Using a multi-shot Bow will also apply the Fused material to all arrows while only consuming one. is a recurring character in . Biography Fyson is a Rito who is initially found in Rito Village. When Link first speaks to him, he asks if he has noticed Divine Beast Vah Medoh. Even though everyone in Rito Village is concerned about it, Fyson believes he has bigger problems. He helps his mother, Misa, with her shop, The Slippery Falcon, which she wants him to take over some day. However, this is not what he wants, as Fyson's dream is to open his own General Store. He does not want to compete with his mother's shop, so he is found searching for a new place to open it. Even after Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been calmed, he is still plagued by his sorrows. During the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, after asking for 30 pieces of Wood to build more homes, Hudson will ask Link to find someone who would like to open a General Store in Tarrey Town. When Link asks if he should look for a traveling trader, Hudson suggests looking for a Rito, as their flight could help with transporting supplies. Link can head to Rito Village to find Fyson, who is intrigued by the prospect of Tarrey Town. While he is excited to hear they need a General Store, he is worried about the distance Akkala is from Rito Village. However, he reasons that he needs to leave the nest and this is the only way to open his own Store. In the end, Fyson decides to head to Tarrey Town, planning to gather Items on the way that he will sell there. He thanks Link for helping him and says to come visit him. On Fyson's journey, a group of bandits attempted to mug him, but he was able to fly away. Once he reached Tarrey Town, he established the Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch). He finds the Town to be great, appreciating the Weather and that his mother can no longer annoy him. He is glad to be able to run his General Store and sell what he wants to. He encourages Link to shop as much as he wants. Fyson can be seen in the crowd gathered for Hudson and Rhondson's wedding. Afterwards, Fyson is happy that all went well. He comments on Rhondson's beauty and hopes to find a wife as pretty as her one day. Due to his responsibility, he decides to go back to manning his General Store. When Link speaks to him, Fyson asks how he is and claims to be doing great. Since Link is an adventurer, Fyson realizes that he need to carry a lot of supplies with him. He encourages him to buy anything he needs at the Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch). If Link stands on Fyson's table, he asks him not to do so. Fyson thanks Link whenever he makes a purchase. When Link buys the entirety of one product, Fyson claims he will restock soon. He will also purchase Items

anything he needs at the Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch). If Link stands on Fyson's table, he asks him not to do so. Fyson thanks Link whenever he makes a purchase. When Link buys the entirety of one product, Fyson claims he will restock soon. He will also purchase Items from Link. He asks Link to keep selling to him, continuously asking if he has anything else.

, designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Ga-ahisas Shrine is located inside Lightcast Island. In order to enter the Shrine, Link must first drain the Island's pool by using the northwestern terminal and enter the cave at its center. From there, Link must use the Mirrors to carry the Light Beam to a light-sensitive Switch to open the way to the Shrine. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Ga-ahisas Shrine The Ga-ahisas Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Ga-ahisas Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Gaddison is a Zora guard for Zora's Domain who can be found guarding the eastern bridge, wielding a Zora Spear. In her youth, Gaddison was part of the Big Bad Bazz Brigade with Bazz and Rivan. Before the Great Calamity, Link would play with her and her friends. When Link first approaches Gaddison, she reports that the east gate to Zora's Domain is clear. However, she quickly recognizes Link, calling him a sight for sore eyes. She realizes that Link must be the Hylian that Sidon brought to the Domain. However, Gaddison notes that Link has not changed at all in 100 years, but she dismisses it as she does not have time to chat. She is supposed to watching the East Reservoir Lake as part of her job, but she asserts that she can talk to Link later. Once Link has calmed Divine Beast Vah Ruta, Gaddison notices the clear sky wonders whether Sidon managed to stop the Divine Beast. She is still wary of the water level of the Reservoir, even after Ruta has stopped spouting water. She shares some of the history of Divine Beast Vah Ruta, such as Mipha being its 100 years ago, and wonders if Seggin managed to fire Shock Arrows at it. Gaddison is seen in the crowd of Zora in the Throne Room who watch as King Dorephan praises Link. She is grateful for all that Link has done, as she can return to her work and Zora's Domain can receive tourists again. During the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, Link can ask Gaddison about her name. When Link tells her that is looking for someone like her, she asks what he needs. However, since he is looking for someone who can act as a priest, Gaddison will refuse him. She considers herself a blood-stained soldier who could never be a priest, but says that Kapson could help him. After Kapson has left, Gaddison will inform Link that he departed for Akkala. She suggests a shortcut to Akkala to Link, telling him to climb the Waterfalls of Mikau Lake and Lulu Lake. However, she is concerned for Kapson to be crossing the mountains at his age, though his good health puts her at ease.

is a recurring character in . Biography Gaile is a Hylian Stable Worker who resides at the Foothill Stable. During the day, she is sweeping the outside of the Stable. At night, she can be found sitting in front of its Cooking Pot. When spoken to, Gaile asks Link if he is planning on heading to Goron City. She becomes concerned when she sees that he is not dressed for the Scorching Climate, and she warns him that it gets so hot past the Mountain Road's second checkpoint that he will catch on Fire. She decides that she likes Link enough to sell him Fireproof Elixirs that will protect him from the Scorching Climate, recommending that he buy at least three. Gaile will sell one Fireproof Elixir for 60 Rupees, two for 110 Rupees, and three for 150 Rupees. When Link buys one Elixir, Gaile recites the saying "hope for the best, prepare for the worst." If Link buys two or three Elixirs, Gaile declares that he could make it to Goron City. If Link refuses to buy any Fireproof Elixirs, Gaile decides she will not waste her time and suggests he give up on Goron City. However, if Link is already dressed in at least one piece of the Fireproof Armor set, she states that he can make it. Wares and Pricing

are Room Units in . Location and Uses Galleries are Room Units sold by Grantéson for 400 Rupees. After purchasing one, Link can use Ultrahand to add it to his House as part of Hudson Construction's Dream Home service. If a Gallery goes unused following construction, Grantéson will store it for Link. Galleries feature an Empty Frame, which Grantéson can decorate with any Picture from Link's Album. Once Link decides on a Picture, Grantéson will ask him to confirm his choice. After finishing his painting, Grantéson declares it a masterpiece and tells Link to enjoy it. It is impossible to remove Pictures in the Empty Frames once they are painted.

is a recurring character in . Biography Galli is a Hylian and the owner of the Rito Stable on the Tabantha Frontier. He can be found at the front of Rito Stable. If Rito Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Galli will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Galli explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Galli then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Galli instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Galli suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Galli to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Galli tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Rito Stable, Galli will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Galli thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Galli will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Galli asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Rito Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Galli asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Galli will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Galli insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Galli refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Galli starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Galli gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling

Epona. Galli gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Galli gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside Rito Stable, Galli once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by Rito Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Galli tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Galli wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

Gama Cove is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Gama Cove is located in East Necluda. Located north of Gogobi Shores at the foot of Mount Dunsel, it is a circular area with Sandy ground surrounded by high cliffs. Seven Ore Deposits and one Rare Ore Deposit sit on rocky outcrops protruding from the cliff face. Enemies Sub-Bosses Gama Cove is located in East Necluda, below the southern entrance to Mount Dunsel Cave and north of Gogobi Shores. A Monster Outpost consisting of a single tower and fortifications built on a Battle Talus has been established here, and the area consequently contains several Garbage Dumps and piles of bones. Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials Treasure Chests

, also stylized as , refers both the mechanic of dying and the menu shown when the player dies and or when they fail their quest in . Overview In , whenever Link's Life is fully depleted, Link begins to spin around in circles before fading away completely. The Game Over screen then appears, giving the player the choice to continue playing or to Save the game and return to the File Select screen. If the player chooses to respawn, Link will start from the Origin if Link died in the Overworld or at the beginning of a Dungeon if he was defeated inside one. The game will also count the number of times that the player has Game Overed. In , the Game Over screen appears whenever Link loses a life. The screen will flash red and Link will turn into a silhouette and then disappear. If Link runs out of all his lives, a different Game Over screen appears, stating that Ganon has returned. The player can choose to respawn at the North Castle or save and return to the Title Screen. If Link dies inside the Great Palace, selecting "Continue" will respawn him at from the entrance to the Great Palace instead of the North Castle. Getting a Game Over resets Link's Experience to zero. In , the Game Over screen appears when Link's Life Gauge completely runs out. Link will spin in circles and then collapse face-first onto the ground, then being focused to the middle of the screen and disappearing as the words "GAME OVER" appear with a few options for the player. The menu allows the player to Save and continue playing, Save and quit the game, or don't save and respawn from the last saved point. Choosing the respawn will make Link respawn in a predetermined location, depending on where Link Game Overed. If Link died in a Dungeon, he will respawn at the entrance to that Dungeon. Link can avoid a Game Over if he has a Fairy with him, as the Fairy will appear and heal seven Hearts from his Life Gauge after it runs out. If Link died anywhere else in the Light World, he can choose to respawn in Link's House, the Sanctuary, or the Mountain Cave. In the Dark World, Link will respawn atop the Pyramid. The game also counts the number of times that Link has Game Overed and displays them next to the save file after completing the game. During the credits, a breakdown of how many times Link died at various locations in Hyrule is shown. When Link's Life Gauge is fully depleted in , Link will spin in circles and fall. The Game Over menu appears and gives the player the options to either Save and continue playing, respawn without Saving, or Saving and quitting to the Title Screen. A secret ending to the game can be earned if Link awakens the Wind Fish without ever getting a Game Over. In , a winged

menu appears and gives the player the options to either Save and continue playing, respawn without Saving, or Saving and quitting to the Title Screen. A secret ending to the game can be earned if Link awakens the Wind Fish without ever getting a Game Over. In , a winged Marin can be seen flying across the screen. In , Marin's image appears in the sky and then slowly fades, revealing a Seagull. In , it's similar to , although Marin's image is animated briefly to have her close her eyes and shudder slightly in an apparent giggle before fading away. In , Link gets a Game Over after his Life Gauge is fully depleted. He grunts weakly, falling to one knee (both knees in the 3DS remake), before collapsing face-first onto the floor. All other moving objects freeze in place, and the screen darkens so that only Link and Navi are visible as Link collapses. If Link dies from drowning, he chokes and thrashes about before his body goes limp and floats to the surface of the water (if he is wearing the Iron Boots underwater when he drowns, the standard collapsing death animation is used instead). The Game Over menu has the options to either Save the game and respawn, respawn without Saving, or to save and go to the Title Screen. Link can avoid death if he has a Fairy, where after losing all the Hearts in his Life Gauge, he will die as usual, but the Fairy will appear and restore Link's life, saving him from a Game Over. In , the "Game Over" text looks different, featuring simple, white lettering rather than the bolded, fiery text of the original. In there are two Game Over scenarios: one when Link's Life Energy depletes fully, which uses the dying animation from Ocarina of Time, and a second where the Moon crashes into Termina. The "Game Over" text does not appear in either scenario. For the latter, a cutscene plays that shows the Moon slowly approaching Clock Town as the clouds in the sky spin uncontrollably, before touching down on the tower and spreading a fiery inferno across all reaches of the land. Link is seen standing in a black void against a dark red sky at the horizon, as the fiery shockwave begins to approach him. Link braces himself and is swept away. Afterward, Majora's Mask is shown, followed by someone speaking of Link's "terrible fate" while the Happy Mask Salesman's laugh is heard in the background. The Happy Mask Salesman then saves Link by resetting the three-day cycle, though all progress he made within the doomed cycle is lost. adds a passage of text, which reads "And so the angry moon fell from the sky, annihilating this world and its many inhabitants. All items and such gained these last three days are lost." If Link is atop Clock Tower, and plays the "Oath to Order" without having freed all four Guardian Deities, they will still attempt

"And so the angry moon fell from the sky, annihilating this world and its many inhabitants. All items and such gained these last three days are lost." Ganondorf Dragmire is a recurring character and boss in . The original Gerudo form of Ganon, he shares the role of the main antagonist of the series. First mentioned in and formally introduced in , Ganondorf has made fewer appearances than his bestial counterpart but tends to have a more substantial role in the games he appears in. Biography Ganondorf is not seen in , though he is mentioned by the Maiden in the Swamp Palace and in the Super Nintendo Entertainment System instruction booklet for . The Maiden explains that Ganondorf discovered the location of the Golden Land, the resting place of the Triforce, though he allegedly couldn't find a way to return to the Light World once laying his hands on the completed Triforce and being sealed in the Sacred Realm. In reality, Ganondorf managed to manipulate the Hero of Time to enter his way into the Sacred Realm, but was unable to collect the complete Triforce and unwittingly caused Link and Princess Zelda to come into possession of their respective pieces. After kidnapping Princess Zelda and stealing her Triforce of Wisdom, Ganondorf was confronted in a final battle with the Hero of Time. Ganondorf was able to defeat Link after using the Triforce of Power to transform into Ganon, claiming Link's Triforce of Courage for his own. This left the Six Sages and their leader, Princess Zelda, with no choice but to seal Ganon in the Sacred Realm with the complete Triforce. Ganondorf is not known to have returned to his Human form after this, though his legacy as a thief who turned into a Demon King with the power of the Triforce remained. Because of this legacy, Ganondorf inspired others to seek out the Sacred Realm to claim the Triforce, only to cause them to transform into Monsters upon entering the Dark World. With an army of Monsters at his disposal, Ganon launched an attack on Hyrule from within the Dark World. This eventually became known as the Imprisoning War because it resulted in the total sealing of the Sacred Realm. However, the cost of this War severely weakened the Kingdom of Hyrule and paved the way for Ganon's return in the Era of Light and Dark. Ganondorf was born as the only male in a century among the Gerudo, which according to their customs meant that he was fated to be their king. He was raised by his surrogate parents, the evil witches Kotake and Koume. The two witches groomed Ganondorf into becoming an evil and wicked man in the hopes of him becoming their Demon King. After the Hyrulean Civil War, the Gerudo lands became part of the Kingdom of Hyrule and Ganondorf swore his loyalty to the King of Hyrule. However, Ganondorf secretly plotted to use this opportunity to find a way into the Sacred Realm where the Triforce rests. Upon discovering the nature of the three Spiritual Stones as keys to the Door of Time, Ganondorf threatened the people responsible for keeping

his loyalty to the King of Hyrule. However, Ganondorf secretly plotted to use this opportunity to find a way into the Sacred Realm where the Triforce rests. is a recurring character in . Biography Garill can be found living underneath a Tree at Fort Hateno in East Necluda. Each day, he goes to observe the ruins of Fort Hateno. Garill is struck by the tragedy at Fort Hateno when he sees the ruins and is boggled by how many Guardians there are. He reasons that the Champion must have been a great threat to the forces of darkness. He attributes the existence of Hateno Village, and by extension his own life, to the sacrifices made at Fort Hateno and vows to pass this knowledge on. Garill fancies the idea that he would have fought alongside the Hylian Champion if he were present during the Great Calamity, and expresses wonder at the Champion's skill to have been capable of felling the Guardian Stalkers. attacking the Fort. If Link wakes Garill up at night, he says that while he'd love to keep talking with him, he's observing a moment of silence for everyone who fought against the Guardians. He tells Link that they can continue speaking in the morning.

is a recurring character in . Biography Garini is a resident of Lurelin Village who can be found examining the ruined monument in the Palmorae Ruins. When Link first speaks to him, he will initially be startled, but he will then apologize and ask if he needs something. If Link asks him what he is doing, Garini explains that he was investigating the stone monument at the center of the Ruins, having noticed that it bears writing upon it. If Link offers to help with deciphering the text, Garini will inform him that the stone monument was once a complete discoid object that broke apart due to a recent earthquake. He then asks Link to locate the Monument Shards and return with Pictures of the text on each one's face. To help with Link's search, Garini mentions that the text will glow at night and that one Shard should be near their location. This begins the Shrine Quest "A Fragmented Monument". When Link returns to Garini, he will ask if he has found the Monument Shards yet. If Link replies that he is still looking, Garini reiterates his previous advice. If Link says that he has found the Shards but does not have any Pictures, Garini asks him to draw one. When Link returns with a Picture of the first Monument Shard, Garini hints that the next one may have been washed away and pulled underwater. Once Link returns with a second Picture, Garini will wonder if the waves from the Necluda Sea could be powerful enough to carry a Monument Shard further away, such as to Cape Cresia. or Soka Point. Once Link returns with Pictures of all three Monument Shards, Garini will begin work to decipher their text. He finds that the completed monument held directions for two people to "kneel in reverence," but does not know what this means. If Link crouches atop one of the two pedestals at the Palmorae Ruins, Garini will follow suit, causing the Kah Yah Shrine to rise from the ground. In his excitement, Garini compliments Link's capacity for solving riddles before allowing him to explore the Ancient Shrine. Afterwards, Garini will continue to explore the Palmorae Ruins and, when spoken to, comment on how extraordinary Link is. Garini is a Hylian who initially resides at Lookout Landing. When pirates attacked Lurelin Village, Garini and his wife Mubs fled to Lookout Landing. Garini can first be encountered in the Emergency Shelter of Lookout Landing. He admits to being starstruck as a result of meeting Link, claiming that not many celebrities come to visit Lurelin Village. If asked about Lurelin Village, Garini recalls that it was a fishing village known to be a popular resort destination. However, the Pirate attack forced all of its residents to flee. Despite being saddened by this, Garini decides to look on the bright side and enjoy Lookout Landing. He points out how, in Lurelin Village, Beds could only be found at the local Inn, the Fishing Resort.
