is a recurring character in . Biography Garshon is a Hylian found at Serenne Stable, where he debates the cause of the Leviathans' extinction with his brothers. However, their search for the Leviathan Bones has not been lucky, so they have decided to rest at the Stable. He wonders why they are wasting time at the Stable, when it would be better to go out and find the skeletons. When Link speaks to Garshon's brother, Akrah, he can hear the three brothers discussing their theories on the Leviathans' extinction. Garshon's theory is that the Leviathans went extinct due to a sudden drought. Akrah reveals to Link that they have a general idea where the three skeletons can be found, and he asks Link to locate them and bring Pictures back. Accepting his request begins the "Leviathan Bones" Side Quest. Garshon requires a Picture of the Gerudo Great Skeleton, located in the Gerudo Desert. When Link shows him a picture, he is shocked at how good Link is at drawing. He believes it is the evidence he needs to prove his theory about the drought. He encourages Link to help Akrah and Onya with their own pictures. If Garshon is the last one that Link shows the picture to, he will give Link his reward. He asserts that Link's pictures will be valuable for his and his brothers' research. Garshon is very invested in his theory, even panting in his sleep. When Link speaks to him, he reiterates how useful the picture will be to him. He doesn't like rain, but he likes to stay inside and think about Leviathans during such times. Garshon initially resides at New Serenne Stable with his brothers Akrah and Onya. Due to their constant arguing about where to go next, he leaves the location on his own. Link can meet him again in Kakariko Village, where Garshon went to follow his passion in exploring Caves and ruins. He still thinks about his brothers and sometimes misses to have people to talk to.

is a recurring character in . Biography Gartan is a Hylian Merchant that can be found traveling on foot in the Gerudo Desert. He carries a Wooden Shield and a Traveler's Sword as he travels between Gerudo Canyon Stable and the entrance to Gerudo Town. Along the way, he passes through Kara Kara Bazaar. Gartan is very interested in Gerudo women. He is very defensive of this, claiming that business is his top priority. He is disappointed that he is not allowed to move into Gerudo Town. Gartan enjoys being a Merchant because it gives him an excuse to talk to the Gerudo. At Kara Kara Bazaar, Gartan is excited about making small talk with the Gerudo there. Gartan then says that it is just part of his job to make friends and asks Link if he wants some Apples. However, he admits that he gets nervous around Gerudo ladies. While Divine Beast Vah Naboris is still active, Gartan reveals that it makes traveling to Gerudo Town from Kara Kara Bazaar dangerous. However, he refuses to let it stop him from meeting Gerudo women. He is also very worried about the presence of thieves in Gerudo Town. Gartan considers the term "wasteland" to be accurate when describing the Gerudo Desert, as there are many Monsters and Sandstorms. However, he does not know how else someone is supposed to meet Gerudo women. Gartan can also be found at the Gerudo Canyon Stable, where he tells Link that he wishes more Gerudo ladies would come by. Gartan sometimes mutters about his determination to get into Gerudo Town and get close to the women. When he notices Link listening, he tells him that he was just muttering about "important business secrets." Gartan journeyed to Gerudo Town to get to know the Gerudo better, but he did not find out men were not allowed until he got there. Link can catch him muttering to himself that there must be a way into the Town. When he notices that Link is listening, he is startled and nervously explains that he was just thinking out loud to nobody. If Link saves Gartan from Monsters, he may say how close of a save it was to himself. He considers the only thing scarier than Monsters to be Gerudo women. His strategy for surviving attacks is to run away. He gives Link Rupees as a reward for saving him. Link can buy Items from Gartan. He thanks Link for his purchases. When Link buys all of one of his products, he apologizes that he has run out. He is grateful for Link's business when all of his stock is bought out. In addition to selling his wares, Gartan will also purchase Items from Link. He is appreciative of the products he is able to buy, and he asks if Link has more for him. Wares and Pricing Gartan is a traveler who has set up a Tent at the Digdogg Suspension Bridge, which he rests in at night.

will also purchase Items from Link. He is appreciative of the products he is able to buy, and he asks if Link has more for him. Wares and Pricing Gartan is a traveler who has set up a Tent at the Digdogg Suspension Bridge, which he rests in at night. During the day, he can be seen near the Massive Zonai Ruin. When Link speaks to Gartan, he will warn him about Naia's quiz. If Link questions him about the quiz, Gartan reveals that all of the questions are based on extreme Heat and Freezing Climates, and he has been studying so he can enter Gerudo Canyon. He also explains that it never Rains in Gerudo Canyon, and he wonders how one is supposed to splash themself with Water. While he is asleep at night, he complains about the test. After Link has passed Naia's quiz, he is able to inform Gartan. Upon hearing this, he is jealous and accuses Link of boasting.

Gatanisis Shrine, designated by the trial name A Well-Timed Bounce, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Gatanisis Shrine can be found on the eastern side of the Akkala Highlands, on a cliff that overlooks the Lanayru Sea west of Knuckel Island. It corresponds to the Sisinatag Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation Gatanisis Shrine opens into a spacious chamber with a bottomless pit at the bottom. Opposite the entrance, there is a wide spring device that sits beneath a Target Switch on its right side. High above the left side of the spring device, there is a dispenser that releases a gigantic Iron Ball onto a ramp which rolls the Iron Ball along the length of the spring device. An extension of the floor leads to the left side of the spring device, granting Link access to the device, which has a small platform jutting from its side allowing Link to safely stand on it outside of the path of the Iron Ball. In order for Link to hit the Target Switch with the Iron Ball, he must make timely use of the Ancient Power Recall on the spring device as the Iron Ball travels along it. With the Target Switch activated, a portcullis along the wall opposite the entrance will raise, granting Link access to the end of the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Gatanisis Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Gatepost Town Ruins are located in Hyrule Field, close to the former entrance to the Great Plateau. They are situated at a crossroads at the western end of the Forest of Time. Lake Kolomo borders the Ruins to the north, and the Outpost Ruins and East Post Ruins can be found nearby. 100 years ago, Gatepost Town was a predominately Hylian settlement. Alongside the East Post and Hyrule Outpost, Gatepost Town was used as a waypoint for those traveling to the Temple of Time on the Great Plateau, Lanayru, or the Gerudo Desert. Prior to the Great Calamity, the Town's population was increasing, but influxes of Monsters in the area drove out its citizens. When Calamity Ganon returned, Gatepost Town was destroyed. Soldiers from the Hyrule Garrison fled to Gatepost Town, where they joined the civilian evacuation to Necluda. Though the Ruins have been worn over time, travelers often use them for shelter. The Hylian traveling duo, Mina and Mils, can be found searching for the valuables left behind by the Town's former inhabitants. When Link initially comes upon them, they will be fighting off a pair of Bokoblins at the Gatepost Town Ruins. They will reward Link with Food, Materials, or Rupees if he saves them. A stone Treasure Chest can be found at the center of the Gatepost Town Ruins. If Link opens it, he will find an Emblazoned Shield. is a recurring character in . Biography Geggle is a Hylian worker at Tabantha Bridge Stable. Sometime prior to Link's arrival at the Stable, he and Chork went to investigate the Pedestal at Washa's Bluff, but they were unable figure out its secrets. Link can find Geggle on the cliff behind the Stable, staring up at the Gerudo Highlands. When Link first speaks to him, he asks what he needs. If Link wants to know what he is looking at, Geggle points out a section of the cliff face that appears to be man-made. He asks if Link can see it too, and while he would check it out if he could, he can not make it there on his own. This initiates the "Cliffside Etchings" Shrine Quest. When spoken to again after this, Geggle recognizes Link. Once more, he points out the strange section of the cliff, claiming he would investigate if he had the energy of an adventurer. Geggle returns to the cliff even after Link has finished the Shrine Quest, where he looks for something to pique his curiosity. However, he is disappointed at the end of the day when nothing has happened, and he admits that he is simply trying to pass the time. Throughout the night, Geggle sits inside the Tabantha Bridge Stable. He wonders when he got so old, and he claims if he would be off exploring if he was still young. He feels trapped by his age, as the only thing he can do is stare off into the distance.

Gems are generally found by breaking Ore Deposits, with Rare Ore Deposits more likely to yield rarer varieties. Gems can also sometimes be found inside Treasure Chests, as well as dropped by Stone Taluses, Stone Pebblits, and Silver and Golden Enemies. After Pelison moves to Tarrey Town, he will open a stall there that sells a few Gems at a high price. Gems are most notably used to purchase and craft accessories at the Starlight Memories shop in Gerudo Town. The respective Gem is also used to upgrade these accessories as well. After completing the Side Quest "The Jewel Trade", Ramella will offer to buy ten pieces of a randomly chosen Gem at a higher price than at stores. Gemimik Shrine, designated by the trial name Turbine Power, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Gemimik Shrine is located on the tip of Rist Peninsula in the Akkala Sea. It corresponds to the Kimimeg Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of the interior of the Shrine.|The interior of Gemimik Shrine The Shrine opens into a large chamber with eight unlit Zonai-style Torches arranged in a circle at its center and a portcullis opposite the entrance barring entry into the rest of the Shrine. Above each of these Torches, there are custom Hydrants hanging from floating pillars. If any of the Torches are lit, these Hydrants will activate, dousing them in the process. At the center of this circle, there is a Motor connected to a partial circuit that leads to the left outside of the circle's space. After a short gap, a second circuit continues along this line to an Electricity Generator. A long Metal Plate can be found near the Electricity Generator, providing a means to connect the circuits and activating the Motor. To the right of the circle, there is a Propeller situated on a small pedestal. If this Propeller is lost or Fused onto one of Link's Equipment, a replacement will appear on this pedestal. Beside the Propeller, there is a short staircase to a grated platform leading over the circle of Torches. In order to lift the portcullis, Link must attach the Propeller onto the Motor with Ultrahand and connect the circuit to the Electricity Generator. This will cause the Propeller to act as a fan, creating an Updraft toward the upper reaches of the chamber. From this point, Link can use the platform to catch the Updraft and Paraglide to a high ledge on the far left side of the wall opposite the entrance. On this ledge, there are three pedestals holding Flame Emitters, with the central Flame Emitter already active. As with the Propeller, these Flame Emitters will reappear if they are lost or Fused. By bringing these Flame Emitters down to the base floor, Link can attach one of them onto the top of the Propeller to create a spinning source of Fire that will light all of the Torches in quick succession. With all of the Torches lit, the portcullis raises, granting access to the end of the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Gemimik Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests Zonai Devices

The is a recurring General Store in . Features and Overview The General Shoppe is a General Store located within the Great Deku Tree's Navel in Korok Forest. The Shoppe was established by Daz in order to provide Materials and Arrows for Link after waking up from his Slumber of Restoration. Whenever Link enters the General Shoppe, Daz will advertise how useful their wares are. If Link makes a purchase from the General Shoppe, Daz will thank him for doing so. He can also be excited about helping Link. Should Link buy the entire stock of a single Item, Daz expresses his gratitude for being able to help save Hyrule, and he promises to gather more Items to sell soon. Lastly, if Link buys all of the Items at the General Shoppe, Daz will instead offer to buy Link's own Items. Wares and Pricing The General Shoppe is a General Store operated by Daz in the Great Deku Tree's Navel. Because of the Gloom infesting the Great Deku Tree, the General Shoppe is initially closed and can only reopen after the Phantom Ganon below the Deku Tree Chasm has been defeated. Wares and Pricing

are recurring locations in . Features and Overview The General Store is a Shop near the eastern entrance to the Village of Outcasts. Wares and Pricing General Stores are Shops that sell various things ranging from Arrows, Foods, and Materials. General Stores can be found at every major settlement in Hyrule Kingdom, though traveling Merchants who act as de facto General Stores can also be found traveling the roads between towns and Stables. In Gerudo Town, all General Stores take the form of Stalls. The Spore Store, located in the Korok Forest, is a Shop that functions like a General Store, but it is not designated as one on the Sheikah Slate's Map. List of General Stores List of General Stores

is a recurring character in . Biography Genli is a Rito child who lives in Rito Village. She can initially be found in the Village's Kitchen, where she asks who Link is and if he has come to stop Divine Beast Vah Medoh. Genli is upset if Link confirms he has, as Kheel will make her go to singing practice if everything returns to normal. She feels bad that Molli's father, Harth got hurt, but she does not want to practice. According to Amali, Genli and her sisters have become needier since Divine Beast Vah Medoh started flying around. After the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest has been completed, Link can find Kheel at Warbler's Nest. She is angry that Genli and the rest of her sisters have not arrived for their rehearsal. They are supposed to perform for Kaneli, the elder of Rito Village, but Kheel thinks are not prepared to do so. Since Link is a scary Hylian, Kheel asks him to find her sisters and remind them of rehearsal. However, she thinks Genli will be difficult, as she is probably in the Kitchen demanding Salmon Meunière. This begins the "Recital at Warbler's Nest" Shrine Quest. Back in Rito Village, Genli can be found in the Kitchen, where she is begging for Salmon Meunière. She refuses to practice with Kheel until she gets it. The rest of her sisters have already left to gather ingredients for her, though she did not expect them to listen to her. Genli does not want to practice her singing, but she still does want Salmon Meunière. She wonders what is taking them so long, as they were only supposed to go to The Slippery Falcon. When Link speaks to Notts, Kotts, and Cree, they will each give him one ingredient on the condition he makes Salmon Meunière for Genli. In the Kitchen, Genli can smell Salmon Meunière if Link has it on him. She frantically asks Link to let her have it. She is very excited when Link allows her to have some, and she eats it immediately. Reminded of her promise to her sisters, Genli realizes she should uphold her word. While she enjoys singing, she gets nervous doing so in front of others. She thinks that her stage fright might be cured if she practices with her sisters. Genli thanks Link for the Salmon Meunière, claiming it was soft, flaky, and delicious. Deciding to give the rehearsal her all, she asks Link to come visit. At Warbler's Nest, Genli is found happily singing with the rest of her sisters. All the singing she is doing is making her hungry, and she asks Link if he wants to hear her stomach's song or a song about Warbler's Nest. When Link asks to hear the Warbler's Nest song, the sisters will recite the song together. Once Voo Lota Shrine rises from the ground, Genli will remark that it is cool that Warbler's Nest had such a secret. The sisters decide to

stomach's song or a song about Warbler's Nest. When Link asks to hear the Warbler's Nest song, the sisters will recite the song together. Once Voo Lota Shrine rises from the ground, Genli will remark that it is cool that Warbler's Nest had such a secret. The sisters decide to leave to inform their mother, and the five of them race back to Rito Village. Afterwards, Genli practices singing with her sisters near Akh Va'quot Shrine. She shows off her singing to Link, admitting that she never would have realized how much she likes to sing if Link had not helped Kheel. Now, she is having fun with her sisters. After Link has completed all of the Ancient Shrines, Genli notices that he looks cooler. She congratulates him and calls him a good boy. If Link speaks to her again, she notes he looks like he is hungry. Once Kass has returned to Rito Village, Genli and her sisters spend all time singing with him. On her way home at the end of the day, Genli reveals that Kaneli likes the way she sings. She decides to eat some Salmon Meunière, as she can practice more tomorrow.

, also known as , are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Golden Bows are Gerudo-made Bows popular for their ornamentation. They belong to the Gerudo Gear equipment archetype. When Link uses these Bows, the camera zooms in much more than normal to provide extra range, making it easier to hit far away targets. They are commonly found in the Gerudo Desert, particularly around Gerudo Town, as well as in the Gerudo Highlands. Being made of metal, Golden Bows will attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms and conduct Electricity. They will also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. In addition, they will not burn if they touch Fire or if they are exposed to a Scorching Climate.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Gerudo Canyon is located in the Gerudo Highlands. It contains the Kay Noh Shrine and the Gerudo Canyon Stable. Areas Enemies Following the Upheaval, the climate within Gerudo Canyon has shifted drastically. The sudden change in Weather inside caused Extreme Temperatures which led to Gerudo Canyon Stable closing down. During the daytime, the Canyon becomes an Extremely Hot Zone and at night, a Freezing Climate envelops the region. Many Caves have formed throughout the area, granting shelter against the extreme Temperatures outside to travelers and Monsters. A Waterfall now flows down from Taafei Hill into Mount Nabooru Cave, leaving the bend in the Canyon flooded. The Water flowing down from the Gerudo Highlands wards off the extreme heat present during the day. If Link attempts to enter Gerudo Canyon from the Gerudo Canyon Pass, he will be interrupted by a Gerudo Soldier named Naia. Before granting him passage through the Canyon, she tests his knowledge of how to survive in the extreme Temperatures within through a quiz. If he answers the four questions she poses correctly, she allows him to proceed into the Canyon freely. She refuses to allow him to ride Horses or other Animals through it, commenting that it would be too dangerous for them. As part of "The Yiga Clan Exam" Side Quest, a Yiga Blademaster in the Station behind the Waterfall instructs a Disguised Link to find and offer Mighty Bananas to five Frog Statues hidden around Gerudo Canyon, both in Caves and on the Surface. Areas Materials Other Appearances

is a location in . Features and Overview The Gerudo Canyon Skyview Tower is a Skyview Tower in the Gerudo Highlands. Link can use the Tower to launch himself into the Sky. The first time he does so, he will be able to Scan the area with his Purah Pad, which grants him Map data for the Gerudo Desert, the southern portion of the Gerudo Highlands, the Gerudo Desert Sky, and the southern part of the Gerudo Highlands Sky. It also features a Travel Point that Link can Warp to. After all Skyview Towers are activated by Purah and Josha, lights will appear around the Gerudo Canyon Skyview Tower. When Link first arrives at the Tower, he will find that it is malfunctioning. Nearby, Sawson is trapped on the lower end of a rudimentary Elevator. He explains that he came to fix the Skyview Tower, but the Elevator he needs to reach it is broken as well. Using Ultrahand, Link can attach Objects to the end of the Elevator's pulley system, which will cause the platform Sawson is standing on to rise up. Once there, he thanks Link for fixing the Elevator and proceeds to fix the Tower. Sawson recognizes that one of the mechanisms has become stuck due to the Heat in Gerudo Canyon, so he replaces several parts with heat-resistant counterparts. As a reward for his help, Sawson gives Link Chilly Steamed Mushrooms. He also warns Link about the heat of the Gerudo Desert. Following this, Link will be able to use the Gerudo Canyon Skyview Tower.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Gerudo Canyon Stable is a Stable located at the western end of Gerudo Canyon in the Gerudo Highlands. The Stable is managed by Piaffe, with Pirou being employed as a worker. The Kay Noh Shrine sits on a cliff south of the Stable, and the main entrance to the Gerudo Desert, the Gerudo Desert Gateway, can be found to the west. A Sign at eastern end of Gerudo Canyon directs travelers to stop by the Stable before entering the Desert. Like most Stables, Beedle can be found in front of or inside of Gerudo Canyon Stable, where he sells his wares. It is also one of the Stables that Kass visits, offering to play an "Ancient Song" for Link. Maypin, Hylian Merchant, travels to and from the Stable alongside his Donkey. During the "Captured Memories" Main Quest, Pikango appears at Gerudo Canyon Stable, where he is able to identify the fourth Picture in Link's Album as featuring Kara Kara Bazaar. Several travelers also stop at Gerudo Canyon Stable during their journeys, those being Lukan, Calisa, and Gartan. A poster demonstrating a Recipe for Chilly Mushroom Risotto can be found on the Stable's wall. When staying at Gerudo Canyon Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Piaffe explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Piaffe offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Piaffe will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Piaffe will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. As part of the "Rushroom Rush!" Side Quest, Pirou asks Link to bring him 55 Rushrooms, offering a Diamond as a reward. When Link returns with the correct number of Rushrooms, Pirou will direct him to a Treasure Chest behind Gerudo Canyon Stable, within which he can find his promised Diamond. At Gerudo Canyon Stable, Link can meet Sesami, who was separated from his friends while they were traversing the Koukot Plateau Path. During the "Missing in Action" Side Quest, Link is tasked with finding Sesami's friends and telling them where Sesami is. After Link saves each of Sesami's friends, they will join him at Gerudo Canyon Stable. Once all four of them have been saved, they pool their Rupees to give Link a Gold Rupee as a reward. They also decide that caring for one another creates emotional liabilities, and when Link returns to the Stable in the future, only Sesami will remain. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Gerudo Canyon Well can be found beside Gerudo Canyon Stable in the Gerudo Highlands. It has an interior that Link is able to access, which consists of a small pond. There is a pile of Hard Sediment along the eastern wall that, when broken, reveals a second chamber infested by Monsters. In the past, the Gerudo Canyon Well was utilized by Stable Workers, Horses, and visitors as a source of Water and Mushrooms. Its construction also brought an increase of Monster sightings in the surrounding area. Upon hearing that there were Monsters inhabiting the Well, Princess Zelda had the entrance to their den sealed away. To prevent anyone being harmed by the Monsters until they could be permanently dealt with, she also told the proprietor of Gerudo Canyon Stable, Piaffe, to avoid the Well. However, she neglected to tell Piaffe the reason why the Well should not be used. When Zelda failed to return after the Upheaval began, the closure became one of the reasons that the Stable went out of business. During the Side Adventure "Potential Princess Sightings!", Link can find Penn standing in front of the Gerudo Canyon Well. If spoken to, he explains the rumors he heard about Zelda forbidding access to the Well, though he is unable to investigate them due to his size. This starts the Side Adventure "The Blocked Well". When Link discovers the den inside the Well, he must defeat all of the Monsters to protect Gerudo Canyon Stable. After doing so, Link can return to Penn to share his findings. Penn realizes that Zelda must have been aware of the Monsters, and he speculates that she never told anyone to prevent people from panicking. Creatures Enemies Materials

, also known as , are recurring Weapons in . Location and Uses Golden Claymores are two-handed Gerudo Weapons that are commonly wielded by talented sword fighters. They belong to the Gerudo Gear equipment archetype. Due to being lighter than they appear, they are easy to wield. They are found in the Gerudo Highlands and Hyrule Ridge, either abandoned in Treasure Chests or being used by Enemies. They also have a chance to appear in Treasure Chests that spawn after the Series Ganondorf amiibo is scanned with the amiibo Rune. Buliara carries one as she guards Riju's Throne. As metal Weapons, Golden Claymores will attract Lightning during Thunderstorms and conduct Electricity. They are unable to be burned by Fire or a Scorching Climate. They can also be picked up using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate, which is useful as they sink in Water. Other Appearances

The , also known as the Western Desert, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Gerudo Desert is found in the Desert Province in , located in the corner of Hyrule. Although called Gerudo Desert, the Gerudo themselves do not appear in . The Gerudo Desert is completely cut off from the rest of Hyrule after being abandoned years ago. At first, Link can only reach it by being shot out of Fyer's cannon and can only leave by Warping out. According to Auru, the Desert once held a prison to hold Hyrule's worst criminals. The Gerudo Desert covers a vast territory, but most of its surface is a barren wasteland with no signs of life other than enemies like Moldorms, Shadow Beasts, Bulblins and Leevers. The Gerudo Desert holds the Arbiter's Grounds Dungeon, the aforementioned prison. On top of it lies the Mirror Chamber, a large circular temple where the Sages reside. It houses the Mirror of Twilight, which is the only way to access the Twilight Realm. The Mirror of Twilight can create a portal inside a gigantic rock that leads to the Palace of Twilight. The mirror was shattered into four pieces by Zant, but the three missing pieces are recovered by Link and Midna. After the defeat of Ganondorf, Midna departs to the Twilight Palace and shatters the mirror completely. The Gerudo Mesa can also be found in the Gerudo Desert. It holds the Cave of Ordeals, an optional 50-floor dungeon. Areas Animals Enemies Treasure Chests In , the Gerudo Desert is a vast desert wasteland located in the southwest section of Hyrule in the Gerudo region. It is plagued by sandstorms that disrupt Link's Sheikah Slate Map, rendering it unusable. Four Moldugas can be found throughout the desert. Stalizalfos appear all over it during the night. Climates Areas Areas The Gerudo Desert is located in the southwest of Hyrule. It is home to the Gerudo tribe, who have begun suffering from the formation of Rifts across the Desert. Due to the arid environment, the climate of the Gerudo Desert is afflicted by Heat. Areas Animals Echo Objects Enemies Sub-Bosses Might Crystals Pieces of Heart Stamps Treasure Chests Other Appearances In , the Gerudo Desert appears in two stages. In the first appearance, during Stage 1, Link faces a constant onslaught of Stalfos rising from the sand. The skeletal warriors approach slowly and several Automatic Crossbow upgrades can be obtained by defeating enemies that glow green. Bonus point items are much less common in this barren setting. The second appearance, during Stage 5, is the same as Stage 1 but with different enemies. Moldorms will circle Link from under the sand, jumping occasionally, which is the opportunity to shoot them. Between swarms of Moldorms, a group of Leevers will encircle Link before attacking. In , the Gerudo Desert appears as a stage where Warriors must defeat Ghirahim and Zant.

The are a location in . Features and Overview The Gerudo Desert Depths are an area in the Depths located below the Gerudo Desert on the Surface. They are generally flat, featuring no major hills or valleys. They are also noted by Master Kohga to be Sandy. There are a total of eight Lightroots spread throughout the Gerudo Desert Depths. Although no regular mines can be found within the Gerudo Desert Depths, they are home to two Abandoned Mines, the most of any other portion of the Depths. Link can find the Abandoned Kara Kara Mine and the Abandoned Gerudo Mine near the center of the Gerudo Desert Depth. These mines correspond to Kara Kara Bazaar and Gerudo Town on the Surface, respectively. The Gerudo Underground Cemetery sits in the Depths beneath the Arbiter's Grounds. To its immediate west is the Desert Coliseum. Beginning north of the Coliseum, the Gerudo Dark Skeleton wraps around to the west. South of the Skeleton's head, there is an Ascend Access Point which leads just outside the entrance to the Gerudo Great Skeleton's Cave on the Surface. A total of four Yiga Clan Relay Bases can be found within the Gerudo Desert Depths. The Yiga Clan Notebooks at these Bases describe following Statues That Point the Way to Abandoned Mines, a legend from Gerudo Town about a treasure hidden beneath the site of the arbiter, the damage that can be caused by contact with Gloom, and the healing properties of Lightroots. Additionally, 41 Monster Outposts can be found scattered throughout the Gerudo Desert Depths. Nine of these contain Stone Chests with supplies. These Outposts tend to contain Bomb Barrels, Campfires, Iron Boxes, monstrous Time Bombs, Skull-shaped Torches, Wooden Boxes, and Zonaite Deposits. Areas Relay Bases Spectral Figures Supply Sites Enemies Sub-Bosses Treasure Chests Zonai Devices

The is a recurring archetype of Weapon in . Location and Uses Gerudo Gear is weaponry crafted by the Gerudo and used by both travelers and soldiers. It is characterized by its highly ornate designs. Gerudo swords are distinguished by their distinctive curved blades. All forms of Gerudo Gear are constructed with metal, meaning they will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning when they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. They sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, pieces of Gerudo Gear will not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. List of Equipment Gloom has caused most Gerudo Gear Weapons to have significantly reduced Durability, but some uncorrupted Weapons can be found in the Depths. All melee Weapons from the Gerudo Gear also gain a new property that doubles the attack bonuses they receive when Fused, but reduces the Durability boost from Fusion. Other Appearances List of Equipment

The , also known as Gerudo's Colossal Fossil, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Gerudo Great Skeleton is located in the southwest reaches of the Gerudo Desert. The Skeleton is one of the three remaining sets of Bones of the now extinct Leviathans. Link must take a Picture of these Bones for the Side Quest "Leviathan Bones". Tera's Great Fairy Fountain is nestled within the Great Skeleton's ribs, and the Hawa Koth Shrine is located under the fossil's head. Areas Creatures Materials Korok Seeds The Gerudo Great Skeleton is located inside of a Cave in the southwest Gerudo Desert. Alongside with the gargantuan Leviathan Bones seen in , a smaller Leviathan Skeleton thought to be the larger Leviathan's child can be found scattered throughout the Cave in parts. A small pond with three Fairies fluttering over it sits under the ribcage of the Great Skeleton, and Ore Deposits are scattered throughout the Cave. The Gerudo Dark Skeleton can be found in the Gerudo Desert Depths beneath the Gerudo Great Skeleton. As part of the Side Quest "Gerudo's Colossal Fossil", Loone asks Link to reassemble the baby Leviathan's Skeleton and place it next to the remains of its parent. Once Link finds the baby's torso and tail hidden in the Cave, he can attach them to the Skull using Ultrahand. For doing this, Loone rewards him with a Purple Rupee. Creatures Materials Treasure Chests

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Gerudo Highlands surround the Gerudo Desert and isolate the area from the rest of Hyrule. Its cliffs sit to the east of the Desert and its tall, snowy mountains overlook the Desert to the north. Link needs protection from the cold to navigate the northern and southeastern Highlands unharmed. Gerudo Highlands is the location where the ancient Sheikah technology was first uncovered. Nine Stone Taluses can be found throughout the Highlands. Climates The Gerudo Highlands contain two distinct climates, "Gerudo frost" and "Gerudo plateau." The two climates are unique to the Gerudo Highlands, and do not appear in other map areas. The Gerudo frost climate is split into two sub-areas. The northern portion spans from Mount Agaat to Zirco Mesa, with the middle bounded by the Cliffs of Ruvara and Birida Lookout. The canyon housing the Yiga Clan Hideout forms a noticeable intrusion into the area. The southern portion of the Gerudo frost climate surrounds Mount Granajh and Daval Peak. Comparatively, it has a noticeable lack of Wildberries and cutting Grass can spawn Hot-Footed Frogs instead of Restless Crickets. The Gerudo plateau climate is a dominant, contiguous climate. In the north, the area surrounds the base of Mount Agaat and is split by the Gerudo frost climate. It stretches southeast to the Oseira Plains and Nautelle Wetlands. Areas Areas Other Appearances

are recurring locations in . Features and Overview Gerudo Ruins are the remains of ancient Gerudo civilization found within the Gerudo Region. Their architectural style is noted to be different from other ruins throughout Hyrule due to the relative isolation of the Gerudo. Many of these Ruins contain homages to the Seven Heroines, who the Gerudo worship. List of Gerudo Ruins The following locations are classified as or contain Gerudo Ruins: Gerudo Ruins return in . Prior to completing the "Riju of Gerudo Town" Main Quest, they are all subject to the Sand Shroud over the Gerudo Desert. Several new sets of Ruins are now accessible due to the appearance of Caves. List of Gerudo Ruins

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Gerudo Scimitars are one-handed Weapons made by the Gerudo. They are commonly wielded by Gerudo women, especially travelers that journey through the Gerudo Desert. They belong to the Gerudo Gear equipment archetype. People who carry Gerudo Scimitars are often seen carrying Gerudo Shields as well. They are common in the Gerudo Desert, particularly around Gerudo Town and the Kara Kara Bazaar, as well as in the Gerudo Highlands. Gerudo Scimitars can be found inside Gerudo Town. They may also be wielded by Enemies throughout the Gerudo Desert, such as Electric Lizalfos. The Series Urbosa amiibo also has a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Gerudo Scimitar when it is scanned by the amiibo Rune. A Gerudo Scimitar is required to remake the Scimitar of the Seven, along with five pieces of Flint and a Diamond. Due to being made of metal, Gerudo Scimitars will attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm, and they can also conduct Electricity. They will sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated using the Magnesis Rune. In addition, Gerudo Scimitars are unable to burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Gerudo Scimitars appear in . Other Appearances Ancient versions of Gerudo Scimitars are Weapons in . They are the default Weapon of Sholani. They can also be wielded by the Knight Construct, Typhan, Lago, and Vence, all of whom can fight with One-Handed Weapons as well. If Typhan is equipped with a Gerudo Scimitar, he will carry a Gerudo Shield as well.

The , also known as the GSC, is a recurring secret Shop in . Features and Overview The Gerudo Secret Club is a hidden Shop run by Greta in Gerudo Town, located in the building behind the Fashion Passion Armor Shop. Despite the fact that it is illegal to sell men's clothing in Gerudo Town, the Gerudo Secret Club sells the Desert Voe Set and Radiant Set, since there is a demand for such Armor. The Club is also the only place in Gerudo Town where Link can remove the Gerudo Outfit without being kicked out, since Greta is able to tell he is a man and does not care. If Link tries to enter the Gerudo Secret Club through the door at Fashion Passion, Saula will stop him from doing so, instead quietly directing him to the side door if he is a member. When he first tries to use the side door, Greta will ask him for a password. This starts "The Secret Club's Secret" Side Quest. At The Noble Canteen, Link is able to overhear Yaido share the Club's password, which is "GSC♦". Upon hearing the correct password, Greta will allow Link to enter the Shop. When Link does so, she notices that she has not seen him before and welcomes him as a member. Whenever Link makes a purchase from the Gerudo Secret Club, Greta will thank him and promise to restock the Armor piece soon. She may also instruct Link to take care of his new Armor, since it is a precious item. When Link leaves the Shop after buying all of its Armor, Greta will not be surprised. Wares and Pricing Wares and Pricing

are recurring Items in . Gerudo Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Gerudo Shields are Shields made by the Gerudo. This is consistent with all other pieces of Gerudo Gear, the equipment archetype to which the Gerudo Shield belongs. They are commonly wielded by Gerudo, especially Gerudo Soldiers and travelers. Their design has changed over the years to match the fighting styles of the Gerudo. They can be found in Treasure Chests throughout the Gerudo Region. Additionally, Gerudo Shields may also be wielded by Enemies in the Gerudo Region. One also spawns on a rock pillar in the Great Cliffs area east of the Dako Tah Shrine. They have a chance to appear in Treasure Chests that spawn when the Series Urbosa amiibo is scanned with the amiibo Rune. A Gerudo Shield, as well as a Diamond and five pieces of Flint can be given to Buliara to remake the Daybreaker, should it ever be broken. If Link speaks to Selmie with a Gerudo Shield equipped, she will take note of it. She reveals that the Gerudo are famous for this Shield, and remarks that they put thought into making it useful for Shield Surfing. Being made of metal, Gerudo Shields will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms. They will also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, Gerudo Shields do not burn like wooden Shield will when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Gerudo Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Gerudo Shields can be wielded by Urbosa in conjunction with Gerudo Scimitars.

They belong to the Gerudo Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created and used by the Gerudo. Due to this, Gerudo guards commonly wield this Gerudo Spears to keep out intruders. Their center of gravity is in their tips, making them difficult for anyone other than skilled Gerudo warriors to use. The following Gerudo wield Gerudo Spears: Babi Barta Bertri Dorrah Katta Kotta Laine Lashley Leena Marta Merina Ploka Reeza Ripp Smaude Being metallic Weapons, Gerudo Spears will attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity. Gerudo Spears reappear in . Other Appearances

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview thumb|right|320px|The North Gate of Gerudo Town Gerudo Town is the primary settlement of the Gerudo Desert, and it consequently serves as the home of the Gerudo people. Since the Gerudo are a solely female race, they only allow women to enter the Town. When inside Gerudo Town, Link will not be subjected to the Heat or Freezing Climate of the Gerudo Desert. The Daqo Chisay Shrine resides right outside Gerudo Town's walls. Gerudo Town also houses a Goddess Statue near the Southeast Gate, where Link can exchange Spirit Orbs for Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels. In the past, Gerudo Town was constructed around the largest oasis in the Gerudo Desert. The Town's Water is sourced from the Royal Palace, where it then flows throughout the town within waterways. Being isolated from the rest of Hyrule, Gerudo Town's culture developed independently and is considered to be unique. During the Great Calamity 100 years prior to the events of , Gerudo Town was spared any damage from the Guardians' assault, though their chief at the time, Urbosa, was killed while fighting Thunderblight Ganon. In modern times, the chief of Gerudo Town is Riju, who inherited the position at a young age due to her mother's untimely demise. When Divine Beast Vah Naboris became active in the East Barrens, the Gerudo began to fear that it would trample their Town. When Link normally tries to enter Gerudo Town, he will be stopped by the guards. As part of the "Forbidden City Entry" Main Quest, Link is tasked with finding a man who was supposedly able to enter Gerudo Town. After receiving the Gerudo Outfit from Vilia, Link will be able to pass through the gates of Gerudo Town. In addition to other pieces of the Gerudo Outfit, Link can wear the Sand Boots, the Snow Boots, and the Thunder Helm in Gerudo Town without being thrown out by the guards. During the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Link offers Riju and Buliara his help in calming the Divine Beast. Before he can do so, he must first prove himself by retrieving the Thunder Helm, which was stolen by the Yiga Clan. Once he returns to Gerudo Town with the Thunder Helm, he will be directed to meet with Riju outside of her Bedroom, which is located on the second floor of the Royal Palace. There, she tells him to meet her at the Lookout Post when he is ready to face Divine Beast Vah Naboris. After Link successfully appeases the Divine Beast, Riju will allow him to take the Scimitar of the Seven and the Daybreaker as a reward for saving Gerudo Town. Initially, a total of three Side Quests can be found in Gerudo Town, those being "Medicinal Molduga", "The Secret Club's Secret", and "Tools of the Trade". "The Seven Heroines" Shrine Quest can also be obtained after Link is able to enter Gerudo Town. After the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main

Initially, a total of three Side Quests can be found in Gerudo Town, those being "Medicinal Molduga", "The Secret Club's Secret", and "Tools of the Trade". "The Seven Heroines" Shrine Quest can also be obtained after Link is able to enter Gerudo Town. After the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest has been completed, three new Side Quests become available, which are "The Mystery Polluter", "The Search for Barta", and "The Thunder Helm". Two separate Treasure Chests are located within Gerudo Town. The first is a wooden Chest can be found in the storage area northeast of Fashion Passion, and it contains a Silver Rupee. A second Treasure Chest made of metal is buried in the Sand near the Southeast Gate, which Link can find a Golden Bow inside of. Areas Creatures Equipment Inhabitants Materials Following the Upheaval, Gerudo Town was covered by a Sand Shroud that made it almost impossible for anyone to navigate the Gerudo Desert, and soon came under attack by a horde of Gibdos that could not be harmed by the soldiers' Weapons. The majority of Gerudo Town's inhabitants took refuge in an underground shelter until the situation can be resolved, while Gerudo Town itself is nearly deserted and occupied by Gibdos. Link no longer needs Gerudo clothing to enter. Areas Gerudo Town is located in the west of the Gerudo Desert in southwestern Hyrule. It is led by the chief of the Gerudo, Seera. Areas Animals Echo Objects Inhabitants Might Crystals Other Appearances Gerudo Town is the setting for the "Urbosa, the Gerudo Chief" Scenario.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Gerudo Underground Cemetery is located in the Gerudo Desert Depths, near both the Desert Coliseum and Kasari Lightroot. It corresponds to Arbiter's Grounds on the Surface. There is an ancient Gerudo legend about the Underground Cemetery. This legend is retold through a Yiga Clan Notebook in a Relay Base for the Yiga Clan in the Gerudo Desert Depths. According to the Notebook, a great treasure can be found at the Cemetery. However, the person who goes to look for it must hold fast to their courage or risk facing the "wrath of the executed". In the Voice Memory "The Cemetery's Secret", Master Kohga appears to stumble upon the fabled treasure by accident. After failing to open a rusted Treasure Chest, Kohga finds an ancient Notebook left behind by Mineru. This Notebook details a wide range of information about the Depths and the Zonai who inhabited them. By using the images detailed in the Notebook, Kohga explores the Depths to assemble his Ultimate Weapon in service of Demon King Ganondorf. Enemies Materials Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Gesane is a Rito guard who patrols the lowest entrance of Rito Village. He carries a Feathered Spear and continuously paces the bridge closest to Rito Stable. When Link first speaks to Gesane, he greets him and asks if he needs something. Link asks who he is, so Gesane introduces himself. When Link asks about the Rito, Gesane recites a saying about the Rito and is surprised Link has never heard it. He encourages Link to visit Rito Village, should he have a chance. Once Link has obtained the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, he can ask Gesane about Teba's whereabouts. Gesane reveals that Teba left for the Flight Range to prepare to avenge Harth. He explains that, since the Flight Range is where Rito warriors train, Teba went there to stock up on Bows and Bomb Arrows. If asked about the Flight Range, Gesane directs him to Dronoc's Pass on the other side of Lake Totori. Due to the difficulty of traveling around Lake Totori, Gesane suggests Link take the western path. After Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been calmed, Gesane will note that Link has come at a good time now that the trouble is gone. He asks if Link needs something, which Link replies to by asking how Gesane is. He has nothing to complain about in his life, but then he reveals that he saw a Frost Talus when he went on a walk earlier. He clarifies that it is a giant monster made of enchanted Ice, and he thought it was both incredible and terrifying. He thinks he saw it in Coldsnap Hollow, but he ended up fleeing very quickly. Despite its size, Gesane believes a Champion could take it down easily. This begins the "Face the Frost Talus" Side Quest. When Link speaks to Gesane again, he can ask about the Frost Talus. Gesane explains that it is made of enchanted Ice, and he says that Coldsnap Hollow should be avoided because of it. Though he is good at fighting, Gesane would not want to face a Frost Talus. After Link has defeated the Frost Talus, he can return to Rito Village to share the news with Gesane. He would not have thought that a Hylian could take down something of that size. Ultimately, Gesane is relieved, since Rito Village could have been in danger if it had wandered towards the town. As a reward, he gifts Link a Silver Rupee. When spoken to afterwards, Gesane is still very shocked that Link managed to defeat the Frost Talus. However, the world is still full of other dangerous creatures, so he remains vigilant.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Giant's Forest is located in Hyrule Field. A Road cuts through the east of the Forest, running north towards Mount Gustaf and south between the Central Tower and Mount Daphnes. A Black Hinox sleeps in a clearing at the center of the Giant's Forest. A Korok can be found by following the Flower Trail that starts on top of a Tree stump in the south of the Forest. Creatures Enemies Materials The Giant's Forest reappears in . Its layout is the same as in , except a Stalnox is now found in the clearing. It is inactive during the day, and it will only awaken when Link enters the area at night.

are Items in . Location and Uses Giant Boomerangs are massive metallic Boomerangs that require two hands to wield. They were originally used for hunting, but they have been modified to be used as Weapons. They can be used to deal melee damage in front of Link, or they can be thrown to hit distant targets. Giant Boomerangs will curve after traveling a short distance and will travel back to Link, which he can catch in mid-air. If something obstructs the Giant Boomerang mid-air or if Link fails to catch it in time, the Giant Boomerang will bounce and land somewhere for Link to retrieve himself. Giant Boomerangs are commonly found wielded by certain Lizalfos in the Hebra Mountains, primarily around Goflam's Secret Hot Spring. They can also be found in West Necluda. Since Giant Boomerangs are made of metal, the Magnesis Rune can be used to move them. The metal will also attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, striking Link if he equips one for too long. However, this also means that they conduct Electricity They will sink in Water, but they will not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Gibdos are undead, mummified corpses commonly appearing within Graveyards and Dungeons. They are one of the more resilient enemies in as they are weak to few weapons and are not knocked back when hit with a Sword in most games. In some games, they are able to use a petrifying gaze to stun Link, identically to that of the similar ReDeads. They are very susceptible to fire-based attacks, and take great damage from items such as the Fire Rod and Din's Fire. Burning away a Gibdo's bandages in will even reveal it to be a ReDead, while in other games, burning a Gibdo's bandages instead reveals a Stalfos. Gibdos first appear in . When defeated, Gibdos may drop a Heart, one Rupee, four Bombs, or a Clock. Gibdos first appear in Skull Woods, and deal three hearts of damage with each attack. They are also found later in Ganon's Tower. Gibdos are weak to the Lantern and Fire Rod, the latter also found in Skull Woods. Gibdos appear in the Bottom of the Well, Shadow Temple and the Spirit Temple in . They also appear in the Master Quest variant of Inside Ganon's Castle. They are susceptible to the "Sun's Song", which will stun them for a period of time after being played. Unlike ReDeads, which walk around in circles, thereby making them briefly harmless when one is killed in the same room, Gibdos are not affected by this therefore making them more dangerous. Sentient Gibdos can be found Beneath the Well in , requesting that Link bring them certain items when he wears the Gibdo Mask. They also appear in Ikana Canyon. They have an intense dislike for the song "Farewell to Gibdos", composed by Pamela's Father, and will retreat into the ground when they hear it. Wearing the Gibdo Mask will keep Gibdos from attacking Link. Interestingly, neither Gibdos nor ReDeads are able to harm Deku Link or Goron Link, as the former and latter are too small and large respectively for them to attack. Both forms are still vulnerable to Gibdos' paralyzing gaze. Using Fire Arrows against them will result in their bandages being burnt off, revealing a ReDead. However, they will not begin to dance if Link is wearing Garo's Mask or the Captain's Hat, unlike other ReDeads. Gibdos in appear in the Desert of Doubt and the Pyramid, acting the same as in . Gibdos appear in the Royal Crypt, the Palace of Winds, and Dark Hyrule Castle. If their bandages are burned away using the Flame Lantern, they will reveal a Stalfos underneath. Some Gibdos hold items such as Small Keys. Gibdos appear in Arbiter's Grounds and the Cave of Ordeals in . They lay motionless on the ground until Link approaches, then they rise and drag their sword towards him. When Link is within their attack range, Gibdos will release a paralyzing scream before attacking with their sword. 12 Arrows, two Bomb Arrows, the Ball and Chain,

Cave of Ordeals in . They lay motionless on the ground until Link approaches, then they rise and drag their sword towards him. When Link is within their attack range, Gibdos will release a paralyzing scream before attacking with their sword. 12 Arrows, two Bomb Arrows, the Ball and Chain, a Jump Strike, and a Mortal Draw can all be used to defeat Gibdos. As Wolf Link, they can be defeated by targeting and continuously biting them twice. A Back Slice can be used if Link is caught in a Gibdo's scream by pressing the A button and tilting the control stick left or right. When it brings down its sword, Link will roll around it and slice at it, leaving the Gibdo vulnerable. Gibdos appear in the Gerudo Desert and the Gerudo Desert Depths alongside the Sand Shroud, emerging from Hives in the sand to attack Gerudo Town and Kara Kara Bazaar. Gibdos have a skeletal appearance, with distinctly inhuman body proportions and insectoid mandibles. While highly resistant to physical attacks, they are vulnerable to Electricity, Fire, Ice, and Water-based attacks, which will cause them to turn white and temporarily disable their resistance to physical attacks. Additionally, concentrated light will kill them outright. Some Gibdos may lie motionless on the ground to ambush Link. They also sometimes have Weapons or Arrows stuck in their bodies. A new variation called Moth Gibdos also appear, which are able to fly and move more quickly than the standard Gibdo. They can also attack from long range by spitting acid. They are seemingly led by the Queen Gibdo. Gibdos are mummified Enemies. When summoned as an Echo, they have an Echo cost of three. is a recurring character in . Biography Giro is a Hylian Merchant who camps out in the woods along the Squabble River, between Proxim Bridge and Dueling Peaks Stable. He greets Link based on the time of day, such as noticing how hard he must be working if he is staying up late or how early he is. During rain, he decides to rest under his tarp until it starts. When Link first approaches him, Giro is worried and asks who is there. Realizing that Link is a traveler, he invites him to sit by the Campfire with him. He introduces himself and says that it is nice to meet him. Even though it is dangerous, Giro gathers his wares himeself. However, he also offers to buy off of Link, since it is much safer. He asks Link if he has anything rare he would want to sell. On subsequent visits, Giro will call Link over and comment on him coming back. When Link offers to sell to him, Giro wants to see what he has. He is grateful whenever Link offers him Items, though he encourages him to take his time and come back for more. Giro is proud of the wares he has collected and asks Link to look. He admires Link adventuring in rainy weather, so he decides to offer his special wares. When Link makes a purchase, Giro is thankful. However, if Link wants a product that he is all out of, he apologizes. With his whole stock bought out, Giro thanks Link for all of his purchases. Wares and Pricing

is a character in . Biography Gladis is a Hylian adventurer who can initially be found spelunking at the entrance of the North Hyrule Plain Cave. If Link asks him what a Bubbulfrog is, he will be startled. When Link shows interest in them, he explains that at Woodland Stable, Koltin and Kilton had asked him to retrieve Bubbul Gems from Cave-dwelling Bubbulfrogs. If Link has found at least one Bubbul Gem, he is able to tell Gladis about this. When doing so, he is shocked by his bravery. Now knowing that Bubbulfrogs inhabit every Cave in Hyrule, Gladis suggests that he should find another one by himself, although he doubts he will find one that is not dark or scary. He also suggests that Link should visit Koltin and Kilton to exchange Bubbul Gems for treasure, recalling that he overheard them talking about a Mystic Robe.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Glazed Meats are meals that can be made by Cooking predominantly Meat with Courser Bee Honey. Their regular version can only be made by adding a third ingredient that differs in effects from the Courser Bee Honey. They heal seven of Link's Hearts and sell for 60 Rupees. The sweetness of the honey permeates the Meat, giving it a complex taste profile. Only one variation of Glazed Meat exists: Energizing Glazed Meat: Made by only using Meat and Courser Bee Honey. Eating these will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. They heal seven of Link's Hearts, and they are worth 50 Rupees when sold.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Glazed Mushrooms are meals made by Cooking any Mushroom together with Courser Bee Honey in a Cooking Pot. Their default version can only be made by using a Mushroom that has a differing effect to the Courser Bee Honey. Eating this meal will heal a few Hearts to Link's Life Gauge. The Courser Bee Honey gives the Mushrooms a sweet and complex taste with a savory finish. Only one variation of Glazed Mushrooms exists: Energizing Glazed Mushrooms: Made using either Hylian Shrooms or Stamella Shrooms. If eaten, they will replenish a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Other Appearances Glazed Mushrooms boost the Warrior's movement speed by 10% and are made using two Stamella Shrooms and one Courser Bee Honey.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Glazed Seafood is a dish that can be made by Cooking any Seafood together with Courser Bee Honey. The default variation can be made by using seafood that has a different effect than the Courser Bee Honey. When eaten, they will some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. Glazed Seafood is known to be a meal that can be eaten in one sitting. Only one variation of Glazed Seafood is available: Energizing Glazed Seafood: Made using Hyrule Basses, Sanke Carp, Staminoka Basses, or Bright-Eyed Crabs. Eating these Meals will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Glazed Veggies are made by Cooking any Vegetables, herb, or Flower in a Cooking Pot with Courser Bee Honey. Regular Glazed Veggies can be made by using Ingredients with a different effect than the Courser Bee Honey. When eaten, they will restore some of Link's Hearts. Glazed Veggies are Veggies sautéed with Honey for a salty-sweet flavor, which makes them ideal for those who dislike the taste of vegetables. Due to the limitations of their Recipe, only one variation of Glazed Veggies exists: Energizing Glazed Veggies: Made using Hyrule Herbs, which doesn't have any effects. Consuming these Veggies will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel.

is a recurring character in . Biography Gleema is a Hylian child who lives at South Akkala Stable. She is the youngest of Dmitri's three daughters and a fan of Insects. As she walks around the Stable, she sings to herself. During the night, she sleeps in one of the Beds inside the Stable. When Link first speaks to Gleema, she greets him excitedly. If Link asks what is up, she admits that she has a secret and asks if he wants to know what it is. She shares that her older sister, Jana, loves Armoranths. However, she suddenly remembers that was a secret and realizes Jana will be mad at her. She was not supposed to reveal Jana's love of Armoranths to anyone. If Link speaks to Jana with an Armoranth in his Inventory, she will ask for it. Once Link gives one to her, she decides that the two of them could get along. Hearing that Link is a traveler, Jana reveals that she has a request for him. Gleema is a fan of Insects, and there is apparently one that she wants to see that she will not tell Jana about. She thinks it is something Gleema can not talk about with the people she is closest to. Jana asks Link to talk to Gleema about the Insect, so she can get it for her birthday. This begins the "Little Sister's Big Request" Side Quest. During the Side Quest, Gleema will have another secret to share with Link. She shares that Jana hates dragonflies. While reading a book, Gleema saw pictures of a Warm Darner, a Cold Darner, and an Electric Darner, but Jana thought their eyes were creepy and got mad when Gleema showed them to her. Once again, she realizes that was a secret she was not supposed to share. She thinks Jana's fear came from how close the pictures were and that real dragonflies are cuter. When she grows up, Gleema wants to travel and meet dragonflies. When Jana finds out that Gleema wants to see dragonflies, she is shocked. She reasons that Gleema kept her love of them to herself since Jana despises them so much. For Gleema's birthday, Jana asks Link to obtain the three dragonflies. Since it is a surprise, she asks Link to say nothing to Gleema. Once Link has the three types of dragonflies, Jana becomes grossed out and has Link deliver them to Gleema for her. Gleema is intrigued to hear that Link has something for her. Finally seeing actual dragonflies, Gleema asks if they are really for her. In her excitement, she calls out to Jana to show her the dragonflies However, Jana shrieks as her sister approaches. As a reward, Jana gives Link a Silver Rupee. After receiving the dragonflies, Gleema thanks Link. She then gives Link an update on Jana, Kaifa, and the Stable's Highland Sheep, saying they are all doing well. She also starts referring to Link as "the dragonfly guy".

are Items in . Location and Uses Gleeok Thunder Horns are Materials that are dropped by Thunder and King Gleeoks. They resemble crowns, and are imbued with the Electricity of the Gleeoks they once belonged to. Due to the Electricity they are imbued with, Weapons Fused with Thunder Horns will shock Enemies they strike, to the point where common Monsters are said to stand no chance against them. When thrown or attached to a fired Arrow, Gleeok Thunder Horns explode on impact, shocking any nearby Enemies. When Fused to Shields, they cause Link's Parries to deal damage and Electrify struck Enemies. They can be Cooked with critters in a Cooking Pot or Portable Pot to create Elixirs. Gleeok Thunder Horns are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain:

is a recurring character in . Biography Glendo is a Hylian who travels on horseback from the Outskirt Stable to the Sanidin Park Ruins. He bears a Traveler's Sword and a Fisherman's Shield. He thinks of himself as a cautious man, and avoids traveling at Night. He even goes so far to warn Link of monsters that appear at night. When Glendo returns to the Outskirt Stable, he may dismount his Horse and wait underneath a Tree behind the Stable. There, he will inform Link about his daily visit to the Ruins. Depending on where he is spoken to on his daily ride, he will offer various kinds of advice and insight to Link. If he is spoken to while leaving the Outskirt Stable, he will inform Link that the terrain along his path is hilly, so travel by Horse is recommended. He also informs Link that he can Whistle to call his Horse. Any time that he is traveling along the road between the Outskirt Stable and the Manhala Bridge, he will take a brief detour off of the road near a broken wagon to gaze at Hyrule Castle, remarking how the sight of it fills him with dread. He also mentions an abandoned rest area along the high road which travelers once frequented. While traveling from the broken wagon to the Sanidin Park Ruins, Glendo will talk about the rumors he has heard about Shooting Stars, and how one can find an item of value where they land. Atop Safula Hill, Glendo will state that he is cautious and avoids traveling at night as to not encounter monsters. When Glendo reaches the Ruins, he will stop and stay on his Horse while looking out towards Hyrule Castle. If Link talks to him at the Ruins, Glendo will mention feeling uneasy when looking at the Castle but is unable to explain why. On his return trip from the Sanidin Park Ruins, Glendo will inform Link about the fabled Lord of the Mountain and speculates on the form that the spirit takes. Once he reaches the Manhala Bridge again, Glendo will warn Link that monsters appear at night. Between the broken wagon and the Stable, Glendo will clarify the threat of monsters, mentioning Keese and Stal creatures. If it begins to Rain while he is resting at the Outskirt Stable, he will comment on how nice it is, but state that he does not wish to ride through it. If it Rains while his is on the road, he will take shelter and wait it out. Glendo will also make various comments under certain conditions. In the morning, he will comment on the morning's beauty. During the daytime, he will state his unease, claiming that something feels "off" to him. At night, he will consider taking a nap. If it begins to Rain, he will state that he expected the unfortunate Weather. If Glendo is attacked by monsters, he will panic and flee the area. If he is knocked unconscious

are a type of Enemy in . Characteristics Gloom-Wreathed Enemies are variations of Monsters found exclusively in the Depths. They are distinguished from their Surface counterparts by the Gloom emanating from their bodies. When Link is attacked by a Gloom-Wreathed Enemy, Link's maximum amount of Hearts will be reduced by Gloom damage. The amount of damage taken is 0.3x of the damage they would normally do, rounded up to the nearest whole Heart. A majority of the Enemies in the Depths are Gloom-Wreathed, with the only exception being the Bosses within the Fire Temple, the Spirit Temple, and Boss Rematches. All varieties of Froxes and Constructs that can be found in the Depths are exempt from being Gloom Wreathed as well. When Link and the Sages face the Demon King's Army, all of the Monsters they encounter will be Gloom-Wreathed. List of Gloom-Wreathed Enemies Bokoblins Boss Bokoblins Chuchus Gibdos Hinoxes Keese Like Likes Lizalfos Lynels Moblins Stone Taluses

is an Added Effect in . Overview Gloom Recovery is an Added Effect that restores Hearts that have been damaged by Gloom. This effect can be obtained by Cooking Sundelions or Sun Pumpkins. For each Sundelion included, the resulting Meal will heal an additional three Gloom-damaged Hearts, while Sun Pumpkins restore one Heart each. Critical cooks that improve the potency of the Effect will cause it to heal two more Hearts. Gloom Recovery itself does not automatically refill Link's Life Gauge, unless the Meals include ingredients that would normally provide a healing effect. If Link has Extra Hearts when he gains Gloom Recovery, the Extra Hearts will be converted into regular Hearts.

is an Added Effect in . Overview Gloom Resistance is an Added Effect that provides Link with fake, teal Hearts that take Gloom damage before the Heart Containers in his Life Gauge do. These fake Hearts automatically heal over time when Link is safe from Gloom, even in the Depths. They only protect Link from the Gloom found in the environment or damage dealt by Gloom Spawn, not from Enemy attacks that deal Gloom damage on hit. When the Effect is first applied or when loading a save with the Effect active, the fake Hearts will start out damaged before healing as normal. This Effect's potency is capped at level three, but an additional fake Heart can be obtained from the Gloom Attack Resist Set Bonus. are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Gloom Spawn consist of a group of long, corpse-like arms, resembling the arms of the mummified Demon King Ganondorf. Each hand has an eye on its palm, and the group is surrounded by a moving patch of Gloom. Gloom Spawn appear in fixed locations across Hyrule's Surface and Depths, remaining hidden until Link approaches their spawn location. Once Link is nearby, they will appear and begin to patrol the area. If they spot Link or are struck, they will shriek and begin pursuing him. The moving Gloom patch drains Link's maximum Hearts on contact, and if he is grabbed by a hand, it will continue to drain his life until he is able to escape its grasp. Unlike the attacks from Gloom-Wreathed Enemies, damage from Gloom Spawn can be blocked with the Gloom Resistance Added Effect. Gloom Spawn will pursue and surround Link quickly, making escape difficult. Gloom Spawn cannot climb up sheer walls, making Climbing out of their reach an effective escape strategy. The hands will be temporarily stunned if set on fire, including from explosions. Bomb Flowers and other explosives are effective tools against them, particularly from high vantage points, as each hand can be damaged by the area of effect. They can also be frozen, shocked, or stunned with Dazzlefruits. The hands will temporarily go limp if struck in the eyes by an Arrow. Gloom Spawn do not hear any noise Link makes, which means that sprinting and whistling will not catch their attention. They are not affected by Majora's Mask's Disguise. If Link does not defeat all the hands quickly enough, the defeated hands will re-emerge from the Gloom at half of their maximum health until every hand is defeated. Once defeated, Gloom Spawn will coalesce and transform into a Phantom Ganon. Unlike Phantom Ganon, Gloom Spawn do not drop any Items and do not appear in the Hyrule Compendium. However, they can be detected by the Sensor + if it is set to track Phantom Ganon. The Master Sword does not awaken in the presence of Gloom Spawn. When Gloom Spawn or Phantom Ganon appear, all other Enemies in the vicinity will vanish until they either dissipate or Phantom Ganon is defeated. If they cannot reach Link for a certain amount of time, most Gloom Spawn will dissipate into several Dark Clumps without transforming into Phantom Ganon. However, some Gloom Spawn, such as the one found at the bottom of the Deku Tree Chasm, will never wither away on their own. If a Gloom Spawn dissipates, it will not appear again until the next Blood Moon. Some instances of Gloom Spawn are set only to appear if a "random" flag is set, which is randomized when their spawn point is loaded in. Some of these "random" Gloom Spawn are grouped within a general area, such as three at the Great Cliffs or two at Seres Scablands, allowing one of them to spawn at any given time. Other

Other Appearances A set of Gloom Spawn appears as a Powerful Enemy at the end of the Scenario "Purging the Shadows". Upon being defeated, they summon a Phantom Ganon.

are Items in . Location and Uses Gloom Spears are Spears dropped by Phantom Ganons. While powerful, they cause Link to take Gloom damage with each attack chain. This effect can be negated by Fusing the Spear to a Shield or Weapon. Gloom Spears strike fear into the hearts of people due to their menacing appearance. Being partially metallic, Gloom Spears conduct Electricity and attract Lightning in Thunderstorms. They do not burn when exposed to Fire or Scorching Climates, and sink in Water. When Fused to Shields, they cause Parrying to deal damage. Shield Surfing with one Fused to Link's Shield makes him move more slowly. Demon King Ganondorf wields one in Gloom's Origin and the "The Demon King's Army" Memory. Another is wielded by a Gerudo in "The Gerudo Assault" Memory.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview Once "Sidon of the Zora" has been completed, Link can speak to Dento at the Hammerhead workshop. To thank Link for saving Zora's Domain, he wants to craft him a Lightscale Trident, a Weapon passed down by the Zora. In order to do so, however, he needs a Zora Spear, three Diamonds, and five pieces of Flint. Following this conversation, "Glory of the Zora" will begin. After gathering the necessary supplies, Link must bring them back to Dento, who then proceeds to craft the Lightscale Trident. Once it is completed, Dento gifts the Lightscale Trident to Link. Should Link ever lose or break it, Dento offers to make a new one for him. Afterwards, "Glory of the Zora" will be completed. Objectives

The Effect's intensity and radius increase at higher levels, and it has a maximum potency of level three. The Light has no effect on Enemies or Objects, nor can it restore Hearts that have been damaged by Gloom.
