are Creatures and Items in . Characteristics Glowing Cave Fish are bioluminescent, purple-colored Fish that can be found in pools of Water in Caves, the Depths, and Wells throughout Hyrule. Their fins and the spots on their scales on them glow lavender. The enzymes they produce can be used to Cook bright Foods, which cause Link to Glow. When exposed to Fires or Scorching Climates, they become Roasted Cave Fish, whereas Glowing Cave Fish exposed to Ice become Frozen Cave Fish. They restore one Heart to Link's Life Gauge when eaten. When edible or Roasted Mushrooms are dropped in Water containing Cave Fish, any nearby Cave Fish will swim over to them. When exposed to Electricity, they die, rolling over onto their sides and floating to the Water's surface. Deceased Glowing Cave Fish can be manipulated using Ultrahand and Recall, though their bodies can only be Recalled to a point they were present at after their death. They cannot be Fused to Weapons, Shields, or Arrows. Glowing Cave Fish are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain:

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Goat Butters are made from the Fresh Milk produced by White Goats. They can be purchased at High Spirits Produce and The Slippery Falcon, though the Merchant Agus also sells them. While they cannot be eaten, they can be used as an Ingredient in a Cooking Pot to make certain dishes. Goat Butters can also be used to make Yellow Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop. As part of the "What's for Dinner?" Side Quest, Kiana asks Link to bring her a Goat Butter and a Hearty Blueshell Snail to make Seafood Paella. When Link brings them to Kiana, she will give him a Purple Rupee and a serving of Seafood Paella as a reward. Similarly, the "Cooking with Koko" Side Quest requires Link to retrieve Goat Butter for Koko, who wants to make a Hot Buttered Apple. Once she has the Goat Butter, Koko will give him a Hot Buttered Apple as a reward. When Cooking, Goat Butter is required to make stews and meunière. Specifically, it is needed to make Apple Pie, Carrot Cake, an Egg Tart, Fish Pie, Carrot Stew, Crab Risotto, Curry Pilaf, Fruit Pie, Gourmet Meat Stew, Gourmet Poultry Pilaf, Hearty Clam Chowder, Hearty Salmon Muenière, a Hot Buttered Apple, Meat Pie, Meat Stew, Monster Cake, Monster Soup, a Mushroom Omelet, Mushroom Risotto, Nutcake, a Plain Crepe, Porgy Meunière, Poultry Pilaf, Prime Meat Stew, Prime Poultry Pilaf, Pumpkin Pie, Pumpkin Stew, Salmon Risotto, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Paella, a Vegetable Omelet, and Vegetable Risotto. Other Appearances

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link prays to the Spring of Courage Statue at the Spring of Courage, she reveals that she can no longer sense the presence of the Mother Goddess Statue, which can be found at the bottom of a "vast canyon". She asks Link to investigate the Mother Goddess Statue's status. Afterwards, "Goddess Statue of Courage" will begin. At the Forgotten Temple, Link can find the Mother Goddess Statue has fallen over. When Link informs the Spring of Courage Statue, she becomes concerned, and she asks him to help her restore the Mother Goddess Statue. To do this, she asks him to find the Dragon Farosh and offer one of her Claws to the Spring of Courage. When Link drops Farosh's Claw into the Spring of Courage, the Water surrounding it will begin to glow. The Spring of Courage Statue states that his offering gave her enough power to send her strength to the Mother Goddess Statue. As a reward, she gives Link a Topaz. If Link has already completed "Goddess Statue of Power" and "Goddess Statue of Wisdom", the Spring of Courage Statue asks him to make a pilgrimage to the Mother Goddess Statue, which starts "The Mother Goddess Statue". If not, she then requests that Link help the other two Goddess Statues who guard springs. Following this, "Goddess Statue of Courage" will be completed. Objectives

" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link prays to the Spring of Power Statue at the Spring of Power, she claims that she can no longer sense the presence of a Goddess Statue known as the Mother Goddess Statue, which supposedly located within a "vast canyon". As a result, she asks Link to check on the Mother Goddess Statue and return with news of her condition. Following this request, "Goddess Statue of Power" will begin. Inside the Forgotten Temple, Link finds that the Mother Goddess Statue has been knocked over. Upon returning to the Spring of Power Statue, she is shocked to hear this, and she asks Link to help her restore the Mother Goddess Statue. She needs Link to find the Dragon Dinraal and offer one of her Claws to the Spring of Power. After obtaining Dinraal's Claw, Link can drop it into the Spring of Power, which causes the Water surrounding it to glow. The offering allows the Spring of Power Statue to send some of her strength to the Mother Goddess Statue. As a reward, she gives Link a Ruby. If "Goddess Statue of Courage" and "Goddess Statue of Wisdom" have already been completed, the Spring of Power Statue suggests that he visit the Mother Goddess Statue, which starts "The Mother Goddess Statue". If not, she asks him to help the other Goddess Statues that guard springs. Afterwards, "Goddess Statue of Power will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link prays to the Spring of Wisdom Statue at the Spring of Wisdom, she expresses her concern that she can no longer sense the presence of the Mother Goddess Statue, who is situated within a "vast canyon". As a result of this, she asks Link to find the Mother Goddess Statue and report her condition. Following this request, "Goddess Statue of Wisdom" will begin. At the back of the Forgotten Temple, Link discovers that the Mother Goddess Statue has fallen over. When he returns to the Spring of Wisdom Statue and informs her, she is saddened and asks for his help to restore the Mother Goddess Statue. In order to do so, she needs Link to find Naydra and offer one of her Claws to the Spring of Wisdom. When Link drops Naydra's Claw into the Spring of Wisdom, the surrounding Water will begin to glow. The offering gives the Spring of Wisdom Statue the strength to send some of her power to the Mother Goddess Statue. As a reward for his help, she gives Link a Sapphire. If "Goddess Statue of Courage" and "Goddess Statue of Power" have already been finished, she suggests that he visit the Mother Goddess Statue, which starts "The Mother Goddess Statue" Side Quest. If not, she tells him to aid the other Goddess Statues that guard springs. Afterwards, "Goddess Statue of Wisdom" will be completed. Objectives

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Gogobi Shores are located by the Necluda Sea in East Necluda. It consists of a lush green plain with scattered Palm Trees and many beaches. In the eastern Gogobi Shores, near a cluster of rocks, there is a metallic Treasure Chest containing an Amber underwater. Near that Chest, a wooden Chest containing a Red Rupee floats on the water's surface. Nearby the aforementioned rocks, a Korok can be found hiding in a circle of Lily Pads. Another Korok can be found in the southwestern Gogobi Shores hiding among a cluster of Palm Trees. Link must follow a Flower Trail to a rock to make the Korok appear. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

, also known as Huge Rupees, are recurring Items in . Gold Rupees go unnamed in . Location and Uses Link can find a Gold Rupee by playing the "Song of Storms" atop the platform near the entrance to Goron City in . This creates a hole leading to a grotto which houses a Treasure Chest containing a Gold Rupee. Link can also kill the Skull Kid as an adult in order to retrieve a Gold Rupee. When playing the Diving Game after obtaining the Silver Scale, on rare occasions, a Gold Rupee worth 500 Rupees can be collected during the Mini-Game. Link can find a Gold Rupee by killing the Takkuri in Termina Field in . He can also earn a Gold Rupee by trading the Ocean Title Deed to the Business Scrub just outside of Sakon's Hideout, thus completing the "Business Scrub Scramble" Event. There is only one Gold Rupee that Link can find in Hytopia. He is awarded the Gold Rupee, valued at 300 Rupees, by King Tuft after clearing all Levels and Drablands Challenges for every Area. Gold Rupees are worth 300 Rupees. They can be found in Treasure Chests located in the North Gerudo Ruins and Hyrule Castle's Sanctum. Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Gonguron is a Goron who lives in Goron City with his older brother Bladon. Prior to Link's arrival, Gonguron had left the City to find the "secret of the hero," a mystery that is believed to be in Gorko Tunnel. He can be found excavating the Tunnel. Bladon however, is furious with him for leaving. Speaking with Bladon begins the first phase in the Shrine Quest "A Brother's Roast". Upon finding Gonguron, it is discovered that he has collapsed from an overbearing hunger and cannot continue. Bladon, who shortly arrives after, then tells Link to bring a Rock Roast from Gortram Cliff. The Rock Roast he brings is then Cooked, which invigorates Gonguron as he eats the now Deliciously Grilled Rock Roast. The Roast gives Gonguron enough energy to finish excavating the Tunnel, and it is revealed that the hero's secret is actually the Kayra Mah Shrine. Gonguron comments that the secret looks familiar, referring to the Shae Mo'sah Shrine near Goron City. After finding the Ancient Shrine, Gonguron and Bladon return to their home in Goron City. Gonguron's finding of the secret inspires him to keep digging, and he begins digging in their house while Bladon cheers him on.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Goponga Village Ruins are located on the northeastern side of Goponga Island in the Lanayru Wetlands. The ruins of Goponga Village, they consist mainly of Ruined Houses made of wood, though they also contain the remains of fences and a well. 100 years ago, Goponga Village was heavily inhabited by Hylians. However, the Village was destroyed by the onslaught of Guardians during the Great Calamity. Since it was located along the trail Soldiers used to evacuate to Akkala Citadel, the Village was a site of conflict. Surviving residents of Goponga Village potentially fled to Kakariko Village in West Necluda, which is to the south. Inside one of the Ruined Houses in the Goponga Village Ruins, Link can find a Treasure Chest. Inside of it is a Purple Rupee. Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment Areas

The is a recurring location in . The Goponga Village Ruins Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Goponga Village Ruins Well is a part of the Goponga Village Ruins, which are located on Goponga Island in the Lanayru Wetlands. A shallow puddle of Water can be found inside of it. Before the Great Calamity, which occurred 100 years prior to the events of , the Well was part of Goponga Village. The Goponga Village Ruins Well returns in , and it is still part of the Goponga Village Ruins in the Lanayru Wetlands. It now has an interior that Link can explore, though most of it is filled with Water. A Cooking Pot and Barrel can be found on its dry land. There is also a Note on the Table written by Aurie Taamu, wherein he considers making an Elixir using Sticky Frogs. Creatures Material

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Gorko Tunnel is an underground passage located in the northeastern end of the gorge between Gortram Cliff and Gorko Lake, in Eldin Canyon. The Tunnel is said to conceal the "secret of the hero." Gonguron, the brother of Bladon, can be found inside the Tunnel excavating it to uncover its secret. A lit Cooking Pot for Cooking can also be found inside. As part of the Side Quest "A Brother's Roast", Bladon asks Link to go to Gorko Tunnel to find his brother. There it is discovered that Gonguron has collapsed from hunger and cannot continue excavating. Bladon, who arrives shortly after, asks Link to bring back a Rock Roast from Gortram Cliff so he can cook it for his brother. After Gonguron eats the cooked Rock Roast, he finishes excavating the Tunnel, and it is discovered that the secret is the Kayra Mah Shrine. Areas Areas Other Appearances As part of the "Fine Goron Dining" Quest, the Goron miners at Gorko Tunnel have stopped working due to hunger. Once they are provided the proper seasoning for the Rock Roasts, they will continue to work on digging out the Tunnel.

The is a title belonging to multiple characters in . Overview Darunia is the Goron Chief for the duration of . He is a sworn brother to the King of Hyrule. When Link arrives at Goron City, Darunia will have shut himself in his Room with the Spiritual Stone of Fire to wait for a messenger from the Royal Family of Hyrule. Link can meet with him by playing "Zelda's Lullaby" outside of his door. However, Darunia is already angry about the lack of food caused by the infestation of Dodongo's Cavern, and he is offended when he sees that Link is a child. If Link plays "Saria's Song" for him, Darunia will calm down and begin dancing, after which he asks Link what he needs. He then tasks Link with defeating the Dodongos within Dodongo's Cavern to prove himself worthy of the Spiritual Stone. Upon leaving Dodongo's Cavern after defeating King Dodongo, Darunia appears to congratulate Link. He realizes that Ganondorf likely blocked the Cavern's entrance after being denied the Spiritual Stone of Fire. Since Link put himself in a dangerous situation to save the Gorons, Darunia offers to become his sworn brother. He gives him the Spiritual Stone as a symbol of their connection. After Link awakens from his seven-year slumber, he learns that Ganondorf's forces took most of the Gorons to the Fire Temple so that they could be eaten by Volvagia. As the Goron Chief, Darunia has left Goron City to save them. Darunia recognizes Link when the reunite at the Temple, and he explains that his goal is to defeat Volvagia to not only save the Gorons, but to protect the rest of Hyrule as well. While he is not in possession of the Megaton Hammer that his ancestor used to defeat Volvagia in the past, he feels as though he has no choice but to face it. He requests that Link free the captured Gorons while he fights Volvagia. Once Link defeats Volvagia himself, Darunia appears before him in the Chamber of Sages. He thanks him for his help saving the Gorons, and he reveals that he has awakened as the Sage of Fire. Darunia then gives Link the Fire Medallion. As Link leaves, Darunia states that they are now true brothers. Darbus serves as both the Goron Chief and Patriarch during the events of . One of the Village Elders, Gor Coron, was the previous Chief. 100 years prior to the events of , Daruk was the Goron Chief. He was appointed as a Champion and piloted Divine Beast Vah Rudania. When the Great Calamity occurred, Daruk was separated from his Divine Beast, allowing it to be overtaken by Fireblight Ganon. He was killed while trying to reclaim Vah Rudania, causing his Spirit to be trapped within it for a century. In ancient times, Gorons who wished to become Chief would have to face the Crater Shortcut's trials and cleanse themselves in the Crater itself. This custom is no longer practiced. The current Goron Chief is Darston, who recently succeeded his father after he passed away. Darston's father was supposedly serious when it came to his responsibilities, and Darston is said to resemble him. The Chief had a portrait of himself hung up in his quarters in Goron City to block the entrance to the Crater Shortcut. However, he made Darston promise to take it down and hang up his own portrait once he inherited his title. When he passed, he left Darston the Goron Chief's 56 Nuggets of Wisdom, which are a series of mottos intended to help him lead the Gorons. Other Appearances Darunia reprises his role as the Goron Chief in . Agraston is the Goron Chief during the events of .

, also known as the Home of the Gorons, is a recurring location in . It is the home of the Goron Tribe. It is located nearby Death Mountain. Features and Overview Goron City is the main gateway to Death Mountain Crater which leads to the Fire Temple. There is also a portal to the Lost Woods, but its entrance is blocked by rocks that Link must destroy with Bombs. Paintings of Gorons, Dodongos, and other abstract shapes can be seen all around the city walls. The city consists of four floors, with the entrance on the top floor. The lowest floor has two important points of interest: the Goron Shop and Darunia's chamber, which is initially closed off until Link proves his connection with the Royal Family. Within the chamber is a heavy stone monument blocking off the entrance to Death Mountain Crater. Link can move this obstacle once he is an adult. Also on the bottom floor is a giant vase which spins once Link lights up all of the city's torches. Situated at the center of the city is a platform suspended by ropes where the Spiritual Stone of Fire, also known as the Goron's Ruby, was once displayed; it used to light up the city before Darunia took it away. When young Link arrives at Goron City, he finds the source of the Goron's troubles: their source of food, Dodongo's Cavern, has been blocked by a giant boulder thus endangering their lives. Their leader, Darunia, locks himself up in his chamber and won't let anyone in unless they are connected to the Royal Family of Hyrule. Once Link shows his proof of connection with the Royal Family, the door opens, allowing Link to speak to the Goron chief. Darunia, though reluctant at first, lets Link help them by having him destroy the Dodongos in Dodongo's Cavern. After Link defeats King Dodongo and clears the infested cavern, Darunia gives him the Goron's Ruby and calls him a Sworn Brother. Seven years later, after retrieving the Master Sword, Link returns to Goron City to find that all of its citizens are gone. He notices a lone Goron rolling around the third floor and stops him with a Bomb. Link discovers the Goron is Darunia's son who informs him about the revival of Volvagia, an ancient Dragon who eats Gorons. Due to this situation, Darunia went to the Fire Temple to try and defeat Volvagia; however, while he was gone, all the Gorons were taken by Ganondorf as prisoners into the temple where they would be fed to Volvagia as a warning to those who might oppose him. Darunia's son pleads for Link to go and save Darunia. So, Darunia's son gives him the Goron Tunic, a tunic which lets Link endure the heat of Death Mountain Crater and the Fire Temple indefinitely, so long as it is worn. Once Link rescues all the Gorons from the Fire Temple, they will return to the city and thank Link for

It consists of a series of rocky buildings, with several bridges providing safe passage over a pool of Lava below the City. The Mountain Road cuts through the City before continuing on to the Abandoned North Mine. After Link calms Divine Beast Vah Rudania, Bludo will reward him with the Boulder Breaker, which he can take from a Treasure Chest in the Boss's House. is a recurring archetype of Weapon in . Location and Uses Goron Gear is a group of Weapons crafted by the Gorons. Most of these items are powerful two-handed Weapons made from thick, hard metal; these lack cutting edges, and instead rely on their weight and the force of the swing to crush opponents. All pieces of Goron Gear are made of metal. This means that they will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, and they will sink if they are dropped in Water. They do not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate, and they can be picked up and manipulated using the Magnesis Rune. List of Equipment List of Equipment

The is a recurring General Store in . Features and Overview The Goron Gusto Shop is a small General Store located in Goron City, next door to the Protein Palace. Its motto is "From the kitchen to the battlefield, we've got the right tool for you to wield!". The Shop is operated by Tanko, who always makes sure to open it early. As Link enters the Goron Gusto Shop, Tanko will advertise he wares. Whenever Link makes a purchase from the Goron Gusto Shop, Tanko will thank him for doing so. Should Link buy the entire stock of a single Item, Tanko may promise to restock soon. Alternatively, Tanko will express his hope for Link's purchases to serve him well. Wares and Pricing The Goron Gusto Shop imports all of its products. Wares and Pricing

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Goron Hot Springs are a small collection of Hot Springs that are situated along the Mountain Road between Stolock Bridge and the Bridge of Eldin in Eldin Canyon. They are denoted as by the seventh Death Mountain Marker, which describes them as world-renowned. At their eastern end, there is another Sign pointing travelers towards Death Mountain and the Bridge of Eldin. The Goron Hot Springs are heated by the Lava flow from Death Mountain, though Gorons consider them to be too cold. As Hot Springs, the Water is warm and will gradually recover Link's Hearts as he sits in it. If Link stands in the Goron Hot Springs, he will be able to avoid catching on Fire due to the Scorching Climate. To safely traverse the Scorching Climate, Link requires one level of Flame Guard. Two Gorons inhabit the Goron Hot Springs. One is Grapp, an elderly Goron who complains that the Water only feels lukewarm to him. He also suggests that Link stay away from the Divine Beast Vah Rudania lest he get burned. However, he also reveals that the Bridge of Eldin is currently unavailable, since Bludo raised it to prevent Vah Rudania's advance. Grapp's grandson, Dugby, can also be found at the Goron Hot Springs. During the day, Dugby sits in one of the Springs, but due to his mouth being submerged underwater, his spoken words come out as gurgles. Dugby tells Link that he has hidden a treasure near the Bridge of Eldin, initiating the "Death Mountain's Secret" Side Quest. At night Dugby sleeps nearby, and he will mutter more coherent directions to the treasure. If Link retrieves the Drillshaft that Dugby hid, he will allow him to keep it as a reward. Other Appearances The Goron Hot Springs appear as part of the Death Mountain Stage. In the "Daruk's Wishes" Movie, Daruk leads Zelda, Impa, Link, and Terrako through the Goron Hot Springs. While there, he formally accepts Zelda's offer to be the pilot of Divine Beast Vah Rudania. Noticing that Link might be hungry, he gives him a Prime Rock Roast, which Link proceeds to eat after hearing his encouragement. During the "Defend the Goron Hot Springs" Quest, a group of Monsters begin threatening the Goron Hot Springs, and the Gorons need supplies to create a defense crew. The crew requires 10 Fortified Pumpkins, 10 Ironshell Crabs, 250 Bokoblin Trophies, and 10 Moblin Trophies. When they receive these Materials, the Gorons are able to keep the Goron Hot Springs and their visitors safe.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Goron Spice can be purchased from the Goron Gusto Shop in Goron City. Alternatively, it's sold by the travelling merchant Yammo near the Tabantha Great Bridge. It is made of several different spices, and the initial wave of spiciness turns into sweetness. While it can't be eaten, it can be used to make certain Foods at a Cooking Pot. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Goron Spice is one of the ingredients that can be used to make Red Dye. As part of the "Curry for What Ails You" Side Quest, Link must give a bottle of Goron Spice to Lester at the Rito Stable so he can make Curry Rice. Upon obtaining Goron Spice, Lester will ask Link to trade it for 50 Rupees. Afterwards, Link can trade Goron Spice with him at any time for Hylian Rice. While Cooking, Goron Spice is required to make the following Meals: Goron Spice reappears in . It is one of the few Ingredients that can only be purchased from Shops or Merchants, since it does not naturally appear in Hyrule. It is required to Cook the following Meals: Other Appearances

The is a recurring location in . The Goron Stone Memorial goes unnamed in . Location and Uses The Goron Stone Memorial is a Statue overlooking Goron City. It depicts four Gorons: Daruk at the top, Darmani III carrying the Elder's Son, and Gor Coron. Originally, it only depicted the latter three, but Daruk was added in memoriam of his sacrifice during the Great Calamity. When Link returns to the Boss's House after rescuing Yunobo, Bludo mentions that, while he means no disrespect to Daruk's legacy, he is eager to send Divine Beast Vah Rudania away from Goron City. Link expresses confusion over who Daruk is, which causes Bludo to tell him to look up at the Goron Stone Memorial. Seeing the Statue causes Link to remember the "Daruk's Mettle" Recovered Memory. Korok Seeds Korok Seeds

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Goronbi River is a long river of lava in western Eldin Canyon. It is an extension of the Golow River north, which itself flows from Darunia Lake. The Goronbi River flows slightly southeast and eventually ends at Goronbi Lake. The River is bordered by a mountain range on its western side. On the eastern side is the main road paving the way to Goron City. A fort camp guarded by monsters sits on a ledge overlooking the Goronbi River at its half point, north of the Southern Mine. The camp is watched by monsters who guard three Treasure Chests containing a Cobble Crusher, a Knight's Shield, and a Topaz. Close to the River's half point is a giant rib cage partially submerged in lava. A Korok is hidden at the southern point of the rib cage, and will give Link a Korok Seed for finding it. Enemies Areas

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Goronbi River Cave is a Cave on the west side of the dried-up Goronbi River. Its chambers contain flowing Lava with Stone Slabs flowing with it. At one end of the Cave is one of Misko's Treasure Chests, containing an Ember Shirt. Once Link opens this Chest, a wall opens, revealing a Stone Tablet. Reading this Stone Tablet starts the Side Quest "Misko's Treasure of Awakening I". The Bubbulfrog is located in another end of the Cave. The Goronbi River Cave contains a Scorching Climate, and Link needs at least one level of Flame Guard to avoid catching on Fire. Creatures Enemies

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Gortram Cliff is a cliffside that is part of a large gorge that runs between Goronbi River and Gorko Lake in the Eldin Canyon. The Cliff itself designated by a Sign at the southwestern end of the gorge, where a tiny pool of Lava is found. At the opposite end of the gorge in the northeast is the entrance to Gorko Tunnel. The path to the Tunnel is an upward slope of uneven terrain, including steep areas with poor traction. Since Gortram Cliff is located in a Scorching Climate, Link needs at least one level of Flame Guard to traverse the area without taking damage. During the "A Brother's Roast" Shrine Quest, Bladon sends Link to retrieve a Rock Roast from Gortram Cliff so that he may Cook it for his fatigued brother, Gonguron. During this time, Rock Roasts can be found at the base of Gortram Cliff. As Link makes his way back to Gorko Tunnel, Monsters will appear in the area, including archer Black Moblins and rolling Boulders. In addition to contending with obstacles, Link must also carefully plan his path ahead, as the steep slopes will make him slip and drop the Rock Roast, causing it to roll down into the Lava pool below. Creatures Enemies

is a recurring character in . Biography Gotter is a man who works at the Riverside Stable. Though Gotter works the Stable, he dreams about consuming a Recipe once favored by the Royal Family. When Link speaks with Gotter, the latter will tell him that the Riverside Stable's Inn is exemplary for its beauty. Afterwards, Gotter will recommend that Link visit the Millennio Sandbar, noting its pleasant environment. He will also compliment Link's appearance, claiming that he has beautiful features and asking the Hylian Champion to indulge in a request of his. If Link agrees to hear his request, Gotter will praise his inner beauty. He explains that, in the past, Hyrule Castle used to be a wondrous beauty, and during that time an ancestor of his worked as a chef.. He is interested in learning what kinds of food was enjoyed within the Castle. Even when he was a child, he would imagine the meals served in the Castle when he ate his less-spectacular food. As an adult, he continues to pursue his childhood dreams. He enjoys his work at the Riverside Stable, as it allows him to share stories with travelers. Even so, he wonders about what could have been. Seeing Link has rekindled his desire, and so he asks Link to keep an eye out for any cookbooks inside Hyrule Castle. This begins the Side Quest, "A Royal Recipe". Afterwards, Gotter will wait outside the Stable beside its Cooking Pot and muse to himself about delicious cuisine. Though it is not necessary to complete the Quest, if Link returns to Gotter after reading either Castle Library Book in Hyrule Castle, he will ask Link to prepare it for him. To complete the Quest, Link must give Gotter either a Fruitcake or a Monster Cake. If Link gives Gotter a Fruitcake, Gotter will pause to muse that Zelda herself once enjoyed the same Recipe before eating it. Gotter compares its refreshing aroma to galloping across the plains on a Horse. However, he believes this undersells the dish's complexity, so he instead says it fills him with the adrenaline of being spotted by a Guardian. Alternatively, if Link gives Gotter a Monster Cake, Gotter will mention that the minister of Hyrule favored it before eating it. Gotter will then compare the experience to biting into a Chuchu. Since that is disgusting and dangerous, Gotter instead says it is like being attacked by a Hinox. In return for recreating either Recipe, Gotter will praise the Food and gift Link a Silver Rupee, valued at 100 Rupees. This completes Gotter's Quest. Afterwards, Gotter will mention that he would like to try any other Recipes that might be found in Hyrule Castle. If Link returns with the other cake after giving Gotter one, Gotter will ask Link to prepare it for him. If Link complies, Gotter will give Link a second Silver Rupee. Gotter decides to continue practicing his culinary skills, offering his Food to patrons at Riverside Stable. He remarks that

If Link returns with the other cake after giving Gotter one, Gotter will ask Link to prepare it for him. If Link complies, Gotter will give Link a second Silver Rupee. Gotter decides to continue practicing his culinary skills, offering his Food to patrons at Riverside Stable. He remarks that there are still many Recipes he does not know yet, comparing their number to the ostensibly endless horizon of Hyrule. Gotter reappears in , still working at Riverside Stable. He is seen behind the stable by one of the pens, looking south towards Owlan Bridge. When Link approaches him during the Side Adventure "Gourmets Gone Missing", Gotter will mention that his friend Agus and fellow gourmets usually cross the bridge on their way to Riverside Stable, but they are running late. Once the Side Adventure is over, Gotter will roam around the Stable, caring for the Horses and standing by the Cooking Pot. At 6:00 AM, he will be by the Cooking Pot, where Agus teaching him how to make a Meat And Rice Bowl. While being taught, Gotter will mention how excited he is to experiment with different kinds of Meat. He will also hope that Princess Zelda will teach a Cooking class at the Stable someday.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowls are Meals made by Cooking Raw Gourmet Meat, Hylian Rice, and Rock Salt together in a Cooking Pot. They can be eaten to restore several of Link's Hearts. The Meats used in this dish are carefully selected to ensure their quality. Additional Ingredients can be used when making Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowls, creating several different versions of the Meal. These versions are: Chilly Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding cold Ingredients. Eating them will grant Link a low-level of Heat Resistance. Electro Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding electric Ingredients. If they are eaten, they grant link a low-level Shock Resistance. Enduring Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding enduring Ingredients. They both refill and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel when consumed. Energizing Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding energizing Ingredients. If eaten, they will replenish a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding hasty Ingredients. When eaten, they will grant Link a boost to his movement speed for a short time. Hearty Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding hearty Ingredients. Eating them will heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Mighty Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding mighty Ingredients. Eating this Meal will temporarily boost the power of Link's attacks. Sneaky Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding sneaky Ingredients. When eaten, they increase Link's Stealth temporarily. Spicy Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding spicy Ingredients. They grant Link low-level Cold Resistance when eaten. Tough Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl: Made by adding tough Ingredients. They increase Link's defensive abilities if they are eaten. Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowls return in . Like in , they can be made by Cooking Raw Gourmet Meat, Hylian Rice, and Rock Salt together.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fries are meals made by Cooking either Raw Gourmet Meat or a Raw Whole Bird with any Seafood together in a Cooking Pot. Their default version can be made either by using Seafood that lacks any effect, such as Hyrule Basses and Sanke Carp, or by using multiple pieces of Seafood with different effects. Eating these dishes will heal several of Link's Hearts. Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fries are made using the best cuts of Meat and Seafood and are considered to be as delicious as they are filling. is a character in . Biography Gralens is the leader of the Monster-Control Crew who can initially be found in Lookout Landing. When Link arrives at Lookout Landing, Gralens can be seen giving orders to Flaxel, Derbos and Landi, who are supposed to join the search for Zelda at Hyrule Castle. If Link tries to speak to them, Gralens will interrupt. He initially dismisses Link, but he is shocked when he realizes who he is speaking to. He expresses how relieved he is to see Link well and introduces himself. Though he wants to keep talking with Link, he tells him to report to Purah so she knows he is safe. If Link tries to ask about the Monster-Control Crew, Gralens tells him to talk to Purah instead. If Link ends their conversation, Gralens urges him to hurry. Should Link try to speak to Flaxel, Derbos, or Landi, Derbos will once again redirect him to Purah. After Link has met with Purah, Gralens will express how concerned he is about Zelda, and he hopes that the Monster-Control Crew will be able to find her. If Link asks about the search at Hyrule Castle, Gralens reveals that Purah recruited the Monster-Control Crew to help with finding Zelda. If Link asks about the Monster-Control Crew, Gralens explains that they are a group of volunteers dedicated to defending the people of Hyrule from Monsters. Gralens has been considered sending reinforcements to the members who are currently searching Hyrule Castle, though he wants to keep them on standby now that Link is joining the effort. He predicts that Hoz will be surprised to see Link. After Purah asks the Monster-Control Crew to suspend the search for Zelda, they resume their primary mission to hunt down monsters. He informs Link about the locations and tasks of their three squads and asks that he help them. Hoz's squad hunts monster in Hyrule Field south of Lookout Landing. Toren's squad is on the north side of Death Mountain in Eldin to take out monster nesting in a cave. Flaxel's squad wants to subdue a pirate ship on the Menoat River in Faron to the south.

, also known as , is a recurring character in . Biography Granté is a half-Hylian, half-Sheikah merchant, who is the son of the researchers Robbie and Jerrin. Robbie recalls that Granté grew quickly, and he used to train his body by carrying the Blue Flame from Tumlea Heights. Before Granté left the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab, Robbie wrote to Purah to ask if he could study with her at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab, but she refused any guests. Seeing Granté's curiosity, Robbie encouraged him to travel. On the day his father suggested he should explore the outside world, Granté left his home. During this time, he traveled the world whilst studying ancient civilizations. Granté appears on the porch of one of the Houses in Tarrey Town after the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest is complete. When Link first meets Granté, he asks if he is also traveling throughout the world. If Link says he is doing something like that, Granté is excited to meet someone else like him. Granté sells Armor Sets to Link that have no other method of being replaced after Link loses them, such as Expansion Pass Armor Sets or those found within Ancient Shrines. However, he is unable to sell Armors that Link has not previously obtained. He will also sell Link a new Hylian Shield for 3,000 Rupees if the original is lost or broken. Link can also sell Items to Granté. He asks to see what Link has, in addition to warning him not to make a mistake when choosing what to sell. Wares and Pricing Grantéson now works for Hudson Construction, having changed his name to get a job with the company. He helps Link build his House during the "Home on Arrange" Side Quest by selling him rooms to use for House building, as well as verifying the House meets the construction guidelines.

is a recurring character in . Biography Grapp is an elderly Goron who is found at the Goron Hot Springs sitting in one of its pools. He dislikes being disturbed while taking he is taking his bath. His grandson Dugby competes with him to see who can stay in the Hot Springs the longest. Grapp expresses that he feels the water there is only lukewarm and would like to bathe in much hotter water, but is unable to due to the Magma Bombs ahead. Grapp warns Link to stay away from the Bridge of Eldin, as the area past that point is incredibly hot. However, he also admits that the Bridge is inaccessible anyway as Bludo lowered it to prevent the Divine Beast Vah Rudania's advance. If Link is wearing at least two pieces of Armor from the Fireproof Armor, Grapp will be impressed with him. However, he warns him to stay away from Vah Rudania regardless. After Link has completed the "Divine Beast Vah Rudania" Main Quest, Grapp will encourage him to spend as much time in Hot Spring as he would like.

, also known as , are recurring locations in . They are locations where the deceased are buried, often in tombs with marked headstones. They are frequently haunted by ghosts and other undead enemies. Features and Overview In , the Graveyard is first accessed by correctly navigating through the Lost Woods. It is a bleak, desolate, gray area characterized only by the white tombstones marked with blue crosses. Touching these tombstones will cause Ghinis to emerge from their graves. The lone Ghini floating outside is a "ring leader"; slaying that one will slay all others that appear. The Magical Sword can be obtained here after Link has twelve Heart Containers in his possession. In the Second Quest, Level 6 can be found beneath a tombstone. Areas In , the Graveyard is located in the Western Hyrule portion near the coast. Among the regular graves, the King's Tomb is also present. A grave a few steps south from the King's tomb holds a secret entrance to the Island Palace. A smaller, more desolate Graveyard can be found just south of Death Mountain, which represents the Graveyard from the original . Another Graveyard can be found in Eastern Hyrule, leading to where the Valley of Death is. Before the first defeat of Agahnim, the graves are patrolled by Soldiers, and when Link pushes some of the graves, Poes will rise from the bones of the dead. Later, after Agahnim has been defeated the first time, Poes will freely haunt the Cemetery. A hole can be found under the westernmost grave that leads to part of the Sewer Passageway. A lone grave surrounded by stones that Link cannot move without the Titan's Mitt hides a secret tomb that contains the Magic Cape. Link cannot push this grave open, so the Dash Bash must be used. The cave to the north of the Cemetery cannot be reached without first travelling to the Dark World and using the Magic Mirror. Deep within a Piece of Heart can be found. The Dark World counterpart of the Hyrulian Cemetery is the Ghostly Garden, a corrupted version of the Golden Land Cemetery. In the northwest portion, a Giant Ghini can be found. In , the Color Dungeon can be found beneath a tombstone in the southwest section. The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Great Cliffs are located north of the Kara Kara Bazaar in the Gerudo Desert. Link can complete the Shrine Quest, "The Eye of the Sandstorm", by finding the Dako Tah Shrine among the Great Cliffs. A large Sandstorm plagues the area, making it difficult to navigate and interfering with the Sheikah Slate's Map. However, the Sandstorm clears up during the night between 9:00 PM and 4:00 AM. The Sandstorm begins to return at 3:00 AM, but is not fully blown until 4:00 AM. A Korok resides on the southern edge of the cliffs.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Great Deku Tree's Navel is the hollow center of the Great Deku Tree in Korok Forest. The Navel consists of a single central room, where a Cooking Pot and the Goddess Statue of Korok Forest can be found. At the Goddess Statue, Link can exchange Spirit Orbs for Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels. Three side rooms also exist within the Navel, each of which hosts a Store created by the Koroks to help Link after his Slumber of Restoration. The Shops are the General Shoppe, the Spore Store, and an unnamed Inn. At the Inn, Link is able to Sleep in a Bed for free. Areas Equipment The Great Deku Tree's Navel is similar to its incarnation, though the Deku Tree Chasm has opened up on the former site of the Spore Store, forcing Natie to relocate. Before Link defeats the Phantom Ganon beneath the Deku Tree Chasm, the Koroks within the Navel will be unresponsive, not replying if interacted with. After the Phantom Ganon is defeated, Pepp will reopen their Inn, allowing Link to stay free of charge. Natie and Daz will then also reopen the Spore Store and General Shoppe, respectively. Tasho can be found here looking for Oaki. Tasho suspects that Oaki may be inside the Great Deku Tree's mouth, which is located directly above the Spore Store and can be accessed by Ascending from there. An unlit Cooking Pot sits at the heart of the Great Deku Tree's Navel. Along the wall nearby, there is a Goddess Statue. Areas

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Great Eagle Bows are Bows belonging to the Rito Gear equipment archetype. They are powerful Bows for aerial combat that can fire three Arrows at once, similar to the Lynel Bow and its counterparts. Prior to the Great Calamity, the Rito Champion Revali wielded a Great Eagle Bow. During the EX Recovered Memory" Champion Revali's Song", the Bow is missing the blue cloth resembling Revali's Champion Garb. In this Memory, Revali can be seen practicing shooting Targets with his Great Eagle Bow at the Flight Range. It is said that Revali could fire Arrows from his Bow with the speed of a gale, making him adept at aerial combat. Teba claims that they too heavy for the average Rito to wield, as they would end up losing all their speed. However, he states that Revali's strength and speed allowed him to counter the detriments of the Weapon. Kaneli will gift Link Revali's Great Eagle Bow in Rito Village as a reward for calming Divine Beast Vah Medoh. This is done at the suggestion of Teba, who was impressed by how Link handled his own Bow against the Divine Beast. It can be retrieved from inside a Stone Chest in Kaneli's House. If Link's Great Eagle Bow breaks or becomes irreversibly lost, Harth can make a new one for him if he provides a Swallow Bow, five bundles of Wood, and a Diamond. If it was dropped somewhere but can still be re-obtained, Harth will instead recommend trying to find it first, as it is expensive to make. Being made of wood, Great Eagle Bows will burn if they touch Fire or are equipped in a Scorching Climate. They will also float if dropped in Water, and they will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity. Finally, Great Eagle Bows cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Great Eagle Bows reappear in . By tradition, Revali's Great Eagle Bow is bestowed to the best warrior among the Rito. Initially, Teba is in possession of this Great Eagle Bow, as evidenced by the blue cloth tied around its limb. According to Tulin, having this Bow means a lot to Teba. At the end of the Main Quest "Tulin of Rito Village", Teba passes his Bow down to Tulin, acknowledging that he has proven himself as a warrior. From this point on, Tulin will wield this Great Eagle Bow in place of his Swallow Bow, and he expresses a desire to keep it in prime condition. His Sage Avatar will also carry a projection of a Great Eagle Bow, which Link is able to take a Picture of for the Hyrule Compendium. During the War in the Depths of Hyrule, Tulin appears and fights with his Bow if Link has awakened him as a Sage. After giving his Great Eagle Bow away, Teba expresses a desire to craft a new one for himself. He offers to make one for Link as well, though

the War in the Depths of Hyrule, Tulin appears and fights with his Bow if Link has awakened him as a Sage. After giving his Great Eagle Bow away, Teba expresses a desire to craft a new one for himself. He offers to make one for Link as well, though he requires a Swallow Bow, five bundles of Wood, and three Diamonds from him. This starts the Side Quest "Legacy of the Rito". Upon receiving the proper supplies, Teba will proceed to make new Bows for himself and Link, claiming that the Harth, the Rito's best craftsman, vouches for his skill. When he is finished, he will give Link his own Great Eagle Bow, telling him to use it in health. He also offers to make a replacement Bow should Link's be broken or lost. However, he will not do so if Link's Bow is still retrievable. Teba and Link's new Bows do not have the same blue cloth wrapped around it that Tulin's does. Following this, Teba will take pride in the fact that he and Tulin are using the same type of Bow. Tulin will also comment on Link's Great Eagle Bow if he equips it will speaking to him. During flashbacks to the Era of Foundation's Imprisoning War, the Sage of Wind Raphica can be seen wielding a Great Eagle Bow. Other Appearances Great Eagle Bows are a type of Weapon used by Revali. He is able to wield one when he is chosen as a Warrior for Scenarios and Challenges. After he is officially appointed as a Champion following "The Road Home, Besieged", a blue cloth will be tied around Revali's Great Eagle Bow. A Great Eagle Bow is Revali's default Weapon that he uses in Movies and Narrations. For example, he uses his Great Eagle Bow against Link during "Peacemaker", aims it at ambushing Monsters in "A Song from the Past", fights with it against Windblight Ganon in "Rescue Across Time: Air and Lightning", and uses it to shoot arrows at Guardian Skywatchers threatening Teba during "Vah Medoh's Pilots". , also known as Guardian Spirits, are recurring characters in . They are large humanoid Fairies.https://zelda.com/about/ Their main purpose is to heal Link whenever he is wounded. , also known as , is a recurring character in . Biography Cotera is a Great Fairy living in West Necluda. Her Great Fairy Fountain is located on the East Hill near Kakariko Village. Like the other Great Fairies, Cotera will upgrade Link's Armor in exchange for Materials. According to Dorian, Cotera is also said to be a guardian spirit of Kakariko Village, though few remain in the village who know of her. Cotera is at least 10,000 years old, as she was around during the first Great Calamity. Soon after, she watched over the construction of Kakariko Village. When first meeting Cotera, she is cocooned in a thorny flower bud and begs Link to listen as she explains her sad state. If he agrees, she introduces herself and tells him about her home. A lack of travelers and offerings have left her utterly drained, giving her no choice but to ask for Link's help. She requests several Rupees from Link. The number changes based on how many Great Fairies Link has already helped. Cotera assures Link that she will aid him once she is back to her old self and extends a hand from the bud to accept his offering. Should Link refuse to help her, she retracts her hand with disappointment. Once Link gives her the appropriate amount of Rupees, Cotera thanks him and is able to regain her power. She bursts from the renewed Great Fairy Fountain completely refreshed, expressing her joy. To thank him for his part in her rejuvenation, Cotera offers her assistance to Link in the form of enhancing his Armor. How much Cotera will be able to enhance Link's Armor depends on how many of her sisters have been assisted. Whenever Cotera uses her power, she urges Link to allow her to handle the work. Cotera will occasionally mention set bonuses when she enhances Link's clothing, pointing out how they work. Once Link decides to stop, Cotera will mention her sisters and request that he help them as well. Other Appearances Cotera appears as a Boss in the Challenge "Fairy Fountain: Grassy Plains" after completing the Quest "Offering Help on the Road". Once the Warriors have also completed "Fairy Fountain: Deep Snows", "Fairy Fountain: Desert Sands", and "Fairy Fountain: Battlefield", Cotera will be unlocked as a playable Warrior alongside her sisters and Malanya.

At the Tabantha Bridge Stable, Link can encounter Toren, who is determined to locate Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain and meet her. He has heard that the shadow of the Tabantha Tower points towards the Fountain in the afternoon. However, he is unable to reach the top of the Tower on his own, so he asks Link to make an offering to Kaysa for him on his behalf. If Link agrees, Toren will give him 500 Rupees to give to Kaysa. When Link arrives at the Great Fairy Fountain, he will hear the voice of Kaysa inside, asking him to listen to her story. If Link agrees to listen, she introduces herself and explains that there was once a spring in this location. Over time, the number of travelers visiting to offer Rupees to Kaysa dwindled, and thus her power weakened. Without her power, she asks Link to give her Rupees. Depending on how many Great Fairies Link has already given offerings to, Kaysa will ask for either 100 Rupees, 500 Rupees, 1,000 Rupees, or 10,000 Rupees. She promises to help him after her power has been restored. Her hand will then emerge from the bud, and she asks Link to hand over his Rupees. If Link agrees to give her an offering, Kaysa will thank him for his kindness. Her power returns to her, causing her Great Fairy Fountain to bloom once again. She then emerges from the pool. Finally able to see Link, Kaysa notes that she was correct in assuming that he is handsome. She jokingly asks him if he would like to live at the Great Fairy Fountain with her. Revealing that she was kidding, Kaysa remarks that Link is cute when he blushes. To thank Link for his assistance, she offers to enhance his Armor if he brings her the correct Materials. The degree to which she will be able to enhance Link's Armor depends on how many other Great Fairies have received offerings. When Link selects a piece of Armor to upgrade, Kaysa will tell him to close his eyes as she upgrades it. Should Link lack the materials for a requested upgrade, Kaysa will playfully chide him for being impatient, whereas declining an available upgrade has her accuse him of attempting to tease her with the prospect. Other Appearances

, also known as , is a recurring character in . Biography Mija is a Great Fairy who resides in her Great Fairy Fountain in the Akkala Region. Like the other Great Fairies, Mija will upgrade Link's Armor in exchange for Materials. When Link comes across Mija's Great Fairy Fountain, it will be closed. If Link approaches the Fountain, he will hear the voice of Mija asking him to listen to her story. Should Link agree, Mija introduces herself, explaining that her Fountain was once a spring. However, when travelers stopped offering Rupees to her, she lost her power. To restore her power, Mija requires Rupees. Depending on how many out Great Fairies Link has made offerings to, Mija will ask for either 100 Rupees, 500 Rupees, 1,000 Rupees, or 10,000 Rupees. Mija promises to help Link once he makes an offering to her. Mija's hand will then emerge from her closed Fountain, and she requests that Link hand over his Rupees. If Link refuses, Mija will be disappointed. If Link agrees to give her Rupees, Mija will snatch them from Link and thank him. Mija then proclaims that her power is overflowing, and her Great Fairy Fountain will bloom. With her power restored, Mija will emerge from the Water of her Great Fairy Fountain. She is surprised by Link's appearance, having expected him to be bigger than he is. Since Link helped restore her power, Mija decides to offer him a reward. She informs Link that she is capable of enhancing his Armor if he provides the correct Materials. The degree to which Mija can enhance Armor depends on how many Great Fairies have had their power restored. If Link agrees to enhance his Armor, Mija will ask him to choose a piece to enhance. Once Link makes a selection, Mija will ask him to wait for a moment. To enhance the Armor, she will either blow a kiss, kiss Link, hug him, or drag him into her Great Fairy Fountain. Following this, she will occasionally explain Set Bonuses to Link. She then asks Link if he has other pieces of Armor he would like to enhance. Should Link run out of Materials or reach the limits of Mija's power, she will invite him to come back once he has rectified this. If Link approaches Mija without the supplies to enhance his Armor, she will notice. However, she will allow Link to view his Armor enhancements to see what Materials he needs. If not all of the Great Fairy Fountains have been opened, Mija notices when Link ends their conversation that her not all of her sisters' powers have been restored. She tells him that if they all regain their powers, they will be able to enhance his clothing more than she can currently. Following these encounters, Mija will instead invite Link to return when he has more pieces of Armor he wants to upgrade. When Link finishes enhancing his Armor, Mija will dive back into her Great Fairy

, also known as , is a recurring character in . Biography Tera is a Great Fairy who can be found within her Fountain in the Gerudo Desert. She is the oldest of the four fairy sisters in . Like the other Great Fairies, Tera will upgrade Link's Armor in exchange for Materials. When Link first visits Tera's Great Fairy Fountain, it will be closed, and he will hear Tera asking him to listen to her story. If Link agrees, Tera introduces herself, explaining that her Great Fairy Fountain was once a spring, but it has dried up now that travelers no longer offer Rupees to her. To restore her power, Tera requests that Link make an offering. Depending on how many of Tera's sisters Link has already helped, she will ask for either 100 Rupees, 500 Rupees, 1,000 Rupees, or 10,000 Rupees. In return, she promises to use her power to help Link. Sticking her hand out of her Fountain, Tera then demands the Rupees from Link. Once Link pays her, Tera will thank him for his kindness. The Great Fairy Fountain will then bloom as Tera's power is returned to her. She will then emerge from the Water. Clearing her throat, Tera introduces herself to Link as the eldest of the Great Fairies, admitting that she has witnessed his adventures from her Fountain. To prove that she can see all, Tera predicts that Link wants her to enhance his Armor. She then asks to see the Armor that Link wants enhanced, revealing that she will need the proper Materials in order to do so. The degree to which Tera can enhance pieces of Armor depends on how many of her sisters have had their power restored. If Link chooses to have Tera enhance his Armor, she will ask him to choose a piece from his Inventory. Following Tera's first enhancement, she informs Link that certain Armor Sets will receive a Set Bonus if they have been enhanced twice. Following their first meeting, Tera will loudly greet Link whenever he visits her Great Fairy Fountain. On occasion, she will use a Gerudo greeting. Afterwards, Tera coughs, claiming it is due to swallowing Water or that she set a deep-diving record. When Link ends his conversation with Tera, she states that she is returning to her home, at which point she dives back into her Great Fairy Fountain. Other Appearances

are recurring characters in . Great Goddess Statues go unnamed in . Biography Great Goddess Statues are a larger variation of the standard Goddess Statue. They are functionally the same as regular Goddess Statues, offering to exchange four Spirit Orbs for a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. When Link speaks to the Great Goddess Statues at the Spring of Courage or the the Spring of Power, they will instruct him to offer the scale of their respective Dragon. Doing so will unlock the path to an Ancient Shrine. At the Spring of Wisdom, the Spring of Wisdom Statue will instruct him to free Naydra from the Malice that has corrupted her. List of Great Goddess Statues Great Goddess Statues are unique Goddess Statues known for their immense size. Like typical Goddess Statues, they are able to exchange four Lights of Blessing for a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. They also accept four Sage's Wills to deepen the vow of a Sage. Each Great Goddess Statue has a corresponding Bargainer Statue located below its position in the Depths. An additional Great Goddess Statue can be found in the Temple of Time on the Great Sky Island. Unlike the other Great Goddess Statues, it does not have a unique name. During the "Find Princess Zelda" Main Quest, Rauru suggests that Link receive the final Light of Blessing on the Great Sky Island. Once he does so, he can give all four to the Great Goddess Statue in exchange for a Heart Container, which should restore enough of his strength to open the nearby Challenge Door. When Link returns with all four Lights of Blessing, he is able to request a Heart Container from the Great Goddess Statue. This Great Goddess Statue's counterpart, the Plains Bargainer Statue, can be found below its position in the Depths. As part of the "A Picture for Riverside Stable" Side Quest, Ember wants to display a Picture of a Great Goddess Statue at Riverside Stable, but he has been unable to find one. If Link takes a Picture of a Great Goddess Statue and shows it to him, he will be able to create the Picture of a Great Goddess Statue. List of Great Goddess Statues

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Great Hyrule Forest is a large wooded area in northern Hyrule, consisting of the vast majority of north Central Hyrule. The area is characterized by its woodlands and rolling hills that extend to the Eldin Mountains further north. Its most notable landmark is the Lost Woods in its center, a dense forest that is surrounded by a gorge known as Lake Mekar. Along with the Lost Woods, the Great Hyrule Forest consists of multiple smaller woodlands that together make up the entire Forest. The area borders Hyrule Field to the south, Hebra to the west, and the Eldin Canyon directly east. A trail paves between the Forest and Hyrule Field, connecting the Forest to Eldin, and, further east, the Akkala and Lanayru Regions. The Woodland Stable sits between the Forest, Hyrule Field, and Eldin Canyon. The trail going north leads through its smaller woodlands before finally reaching the Lost Woods. These enchanted Woods are covered in a dense fog that causes travelers to lose their way. The Lost Woods themselves surround the Korok Forest, where the Koroks and the Great Deku Tree thrive. The Korok Forest also houses the Master Sword, left there by Princess Zelda after the losing battle against Calamity Ganon 100 years ago. The woodlands end at the Lost Woods, and give way to rolling hills and mountains further north before eventually reaching the Thyphlo Ruins; the Forest's final stretch. The is a recurring Region in . Features and Overview The Great Plateau was the birthplace of the Hyrule Kingdom. It is a sacred place where rites were once held by the Kingdom, particularly at the Temple of Time. However, during the second Great Calamity, its entrance was destroyed, making travel to and from the Great Plateau impossible for normal people without the use of tools such as Paragliders. After Link's Slumber of Restoration in the Shrine of Resurrection, the only person to be found on it is the Old Man, a mysterious fellow with a deep knowledge of the Sheikah. Though Monsters are not meant to step foot on the sacred Plateau, they have since occupied it. Guardians under Calamity Ganon's control also found their way atop the Plateau, though they are now rendered as immobile Decayed Guardians. The Great Plateau's architecture mirrors that of Hyrule Castle, with the Great Plateau featuring more feminine statues and the Castle featuring more masculine designs. The Great Plateau undergoes several changes in Master Mode. A White-Maned Lynel occupies the forest north of the Old Man's Cabin and several Treasure Chests appear on platforms held by Sky Octoroks. A total of four Chasms have opened, all in the locations of the Ancient Shrines from . thumb|right|320px|The Great Plateau during the Era of Myth During the Era of Myth, the Great Plateau was the seat of Hyrule Kingdom. Its step pyramid castle was located at the site of the River of the Dead, which did not exist yet. The Temple of Time, which is now rotated to face south and found in the Sky as part of the Great Sky Island, sat over a nameless lake which no longer exists. This lake fed a river that passed between the Temple of Time and the site of the Eastern Abbey. However, as this lake no longer exists, only the wetlands surrounding the Old Man's Cabin and a dry riverbed can be found in the present time. The walls of the Great Plateau featured a different design, and there was once a road leading through Mount Hylia to an observation point at the south of the Plateau. Two unidentified Shrines of Light once stood at the sites where Keh Namut Shrine and Owa Daim Shrine were later built, and ultimately where the Great Plateau West Chasm and Great Plateau South Chasm formed during the Upheaval. After the Temple of Time was raised into the Sky by the Six Sages, a new Temple of Time, later christened the Temple of Time Ruins, was built in its place. In the Era of Myth, the Great Plateau featured a much warmer climate. However, a Freezing Climate formed around Mount Hylia at some point. It is initially blocked by a thick wall of Hard Sediment, behind which there is a tunnel with Ore Deposits, a Luminous Stone Deposit, and two more sets of Hard Sediment. The Great Sky Island is a location in . Features and Overview The Great Sky Island is a large mass of land composed by several Sky Islands found in the Central Hyrule Sky. It is home to many Constructs who protect and tend to its grounds. On its northern end sits a large tower known as the Temple of Time. According to a Steward Construct, the Great Sky Island and its surrounding environment were once located on the Surface. The site was raised into the Sky long ago by the sages to keep it safe from the Demon King in anticipation of Link's eventual awakening there. The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Great Zora Bridge is a bridge that spans Ruto Lake in the Lanayru Great Spring. It starts on a large, pillar-like island on the Lake, and it ends at the entrance to Zora's Domain directly to the north. Until Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, Rain will constantly fall on the Bridge. When Link reaches the end of the Great Zora Bridge during the Main Quest "Reach Zora's Domain", Sidon will run out to greet him. He welcomes Link to Zora's Domain before inviting him to meet with King Dorephan in the Throne Room. Creatures Equipment
