is a recurring character in . Biography Greta is the proprietor of the Gerudo Secret Club, located in the building behind Fashion Passion in Gerudo Town. When Link initially tries to enter the Gerudo Secret Club, Greta will speak from behind the door and ask for the password. If Link guesses the password wrong, he will not be able to try again until the next day. Greta will then tell Link to go drink Warm Mlik at The Noble Canteen in an attempt to get him to go away. This begins "The Secret Club's Secret" Side Quest. Once Link provides the correct password to Greta, he is allowed entry to the Gerudo Secret Club. Upon entering the Secret Club, Greta notices that she has not seen Link before. She comments that he is a rare visitor and promises not to ask any questions if he does the same. Greta then accepts Link as a member to the Club and the Side Quest is completed. If Link speaks to Greta, she comments that it is always "good evening" in the Gerudo Secret Club. If Link asks what the place is, she explains that it is the Gerudo Secret Club, or "GSC" for short. She sells the Desert Voe Set and the Radiant Set and tells Link that it is the only Shop in Gerudo Town that sells men's clothing. Despite being illegal in Gerudo Town, there is a high demand for men's clothing that Greta recognizes. Greta then comments that she has never seen a man disguise himself as a woman like Link has. When Link reacts with shock, she mentions that they both have something to hide and suggests they move on to business. When Link is done speaking with her, Greta assures him that his secret is safe with her. Greta admits to Link that the sunlight does not agree with her, as she has not been out in the day for years. If Link ends the conversation, Greta asks if he has ever noticed how beautiful light is in the dark. When examining the Radiant Set, Greta will tell Link that it is made using Luminous Stones. She then informs Link that he must also trade her Luminous Stones when buying the Armor Set, in addition to a handling fee. When Link asks to sell his Items to Greta, she agrees, though she will refuse to pay more than another trader would. However, she is still interested in finding something rare, should Link have any. She has not done much traveling, so she appreciates being sold rare goods. Greta appreciates a good deal, and she is glad to purchase unique Items from Link. She may occasionally mention how she wanted the product that Link just sold to her.

is a recurring character in . Biography Greyson is a Goron miner who works at the Southern Mine in Eldin Canyon. During the day, Greyson mines alongside Dorill and Jengo while his younger brother, Pelison, plays with Axyl. Greyson rests for the night in front of the Mine's Cooking Pot while Bohrin resumes his night shift. However, he expresses to Link that he is tired of digging and wishes he could find a job where he could use his strength to make a difference in people's lives. When Link meets with Hudson in Tarrey Town during the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, he is eventually asked to find a Goron who would be able to remove boulders to clear the land for further development. However, due to the strict naming policy of Bolson Construction, the Goron's name must end in "son." Link can approach Greyson during his break and offers him the job, who is interested to hear that there is a place out there that needs him. Deciding that Akkala is not too far, he decides to embark to Tarrey Town with Pelison. The two brothers then walk out of the Southern Mine together. At Tarrey Town, Link finds that Greyson has accepted the job and is much happier now. As the boulders he breaks contain Gems, his brother Pelison has also opened Ore and More to sell the Gems they find. Greyson will continue to break the boulders in Tarrey Town as Link proceeds with the Side Quest. A house will replace a boulder every time Link refers another person to the Town. Once all of the rocks have been cleared, Greyson will stand in the center of Tarrey Town as he was told to. Greyson is one of the guests present at Hudson and Rhondson's wedding. He agrees with the vow that Rhondson should name her children in accordance to the Bolson Construction naming policy. Greyson later comments that he did not know there was a wedding planned, and voices his disappointment that he was never told despite having known Hudson for a long time Since the wedding was nice, though, he decides everything is alright. After the wedding, Greyson will no longer have any work to do and decides to relax. He can be found in front of the Tarrey Town's Goddess Statue and sitting beside Ore and More at night.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Grinnden Plains are located at the base of Mount Faloraa in the Faron Grasslands. It is a flat stretch of land covered by groupings of Cedar Trees and the occasional rocky outcropping. Zokassa Ridge is situated along the southern border of the Plains. left|40px A single Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on the Grinnden Plains. Link can find a Jar in a fallen log on the west side of the Plains. Using Archery or Remote Bombs, Link can break the Jar, which causes a Korok to appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

is a character in . Biography Grunyon is a Hylian member of the Zonai Survey Team. Alongside Gagaim, he can be found outside the northern exit of Lookout Landing, where they are examining the fallen Crystal Refinery. If Link approaches Grunyon and Gagaim, he is able to eavesdrop on their conversation. Gagaim is shocked by the age of the Zonai Ruins that have fallen from the Sky. In response, Grunyon tells him that their appearance is due to the Upheaval, and if it had not happened, the Zonai Survey Team would have nothing to study. Gagaim then comments that Purah has been studying the Upheaval in hopes of finding Zelda. Grunyon quietly wonders whether their research is important in a time when the princess is missing. He also states that Zelda's safety must come first.

is a recurring character in . Biography Gruve is a member of the Zora tribe who was employed by Sidon in his search for a Hylian warrior. However, during his search, Gruve neglected his duties and fell asleep on the spot where the Lanayru Tower was buried. When Link activated the Great Plateau Tower, the Lanayru Tower rose in unison with it, causing Gruve to be carried to the top of the Lanayru Tower. If Link speaks to Gruve atop the Lanayru Tower, he explains that he is too high up to make it down safely. He points Link toward Inogo Bridge, saying that while Prince Sidon is there, he has not been able to get his attention. Having found a Hylian, Gruve will call down to Sidon. Unfortunately, Sidon is unable to hear him. Gruve weighs the option of jumping down into the waters surrounding the Lanayru Tower, believing that Sidon must be worried about him. He decides that such an attempt would be fatal and gives up on it. Gruve apologizes to Link, saying he must go on ahead without him. Speaking to Gruve again will lead him to accuse Link of trying to push him off of the Sheikah Tower, but he dismisses the idea. Gruve hopes to find a way to get Sidon to hear his cries for help. After Link speaks to Sidon for the first time, Gruve will return to Zora's Domain and stand over the waterfall to the northwest of the Goddess Statue, peering down into the water below. If Link speaks to him after previously meeting him atop the Lanayru Tower, Gruve will reintroduce himself and explain that he managed to jump from the Sheikah Tower and into the Zora River. If Link did not speak to Gruve prior to meeting to Sidon, Gruve will then explain that he previously worked for Sidon trying to find a Hylian, but it is lucky that Link found Sidon on his own. He then relays his plight atop the Sheikah Tower to him. In either event, Gruve will explain that he saw his reflection during his jump from the Tower and later developed a philosophy that a person is at their most beautiful when diving into water. Gruve will then invite Link to return to him to show his beautiful diving form after he has learned to ascend waterfalls. If pressed further, Gruve will explain that when equipped with Zora Armor, Hylians are capable of climbing waterfalls much like a Zora, and that the Zora Armor made by Zora princesses are far superior. Gruve will also explain that his favorite diving spot is Shatterback Point, though the Lynel patrolling Ploymus Mountain makes it a dangerous trip. Laflat considers him to be a fool for this, as his words encourage others to follow his actions. Upon receiving the Zora Armor from King Dorephan, Gruve asks Link to dive down the waterfall. This initiates the "Diving is Beauty!" Side Quest. If Link jumps from the waterfall, Gruve

trip. Laflat considers him to be a fool for this, as his words encourage others to follow his actions. Upon receiving the Zora Armor from King Dorephan, Gruve asks Link to dive down the waterfall. This initiates the "Diving is Beauty!" Side Quest. If Link jumps from the waterfall, Gruve will exclaim in excitement before asking Link to return by means of the waterfall. If Link returns without climbing the waterfall, Gruve will reassert his desire to see him ascend via the waterfall. After successfully fulfilling Gruve's request, Gruve will give Link five Fleet-Lotus Seeds as a reward. If Link's inventory space for Fleet-Lotus Seeds is full, Gruve will tell him to return when he has space for them. Bidding goodbye, Gruve will inform Link that he hopes to see his next dive.

The Guards' Chamber is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Guards' Chamber is a multi-leveled room on the western side of Hyrule Castle. It is situated beneath the First Gatehouse. The top floor of the Guards' Chamber is split into two sections, with the southeastern portion serving as entry and exit points and the northwestern segment being used for storage. The southeastern side features a Floor Switch near the entrance, which can be held down to release a wooden portcullis leading to a small courtyard on the southwestern side of the Castle. The northwestern side of the top floor of the Guards' Chamber is inaccessible by foot as the stairway from the middle floor has broken, though Link can climb the walls to reach it. The middle floor of the Guards' Chamber is the most spacious, featuring the remains of several wooden dummies and archery targets, as well as a small cluster of Bomb Barrels scattered around the floor. Loosely-rigged shelves along the northern wall of this floor also hold multiple Bomb Barrels, and a long, metal slab can be used to cross the gap on the northwestern stairs. A Campfire sits beneath these shelves, placed evenly between two stationary Torches. The stone stairs on this level have an alcove underneath them that is covered by dead leaves. The bottom floor of the Guards' Chamber holds a small sparring square. Near the square are three knight statues, all of which hold Weapons. Three Wooden Boxes hide a small alcove underneath the second stone staircase. During the "EX Royal Guard Rumors" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link must read Super Rumor Mill V4, which mentions that part of the equipment used by the Royal Guard is hidden in the Guards' Chamber. Enemies Equipment Treasure Chests As in , the Guards' Chamber is connected to the Hyrule Castle Corridors and Hyrule Castle Courtyard in Hyrule Field. It is one of the parts of Hyrule Castle that was not lifted into the Sky during the Upheaval. Enemies Equipment Treasure Chests

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Guchini Plain Barrows are an eastern subsection inside the Guchini Plain located in the Faron Grasslands. The barrows are a lush, plain with many small hills, rocks and trees. Throughout the Guchini Plain Barrows, Totsuna can be found walking through the plain. In the eastern Barrows, a large flat rock sits between two short pillars. If Link moves this rock out of the way, a Stone Chest holding a Royal Halberd can be found sitting underneath the rock. In an area near Herin Lake, there is a tall stone pillar that extends into the sky. If Link climbs up this stone pillar, he can find a stone chest containing a Boomerang at the top. The stone pillars and the structures around their bases are typical architecture of Zonai origin. Creatures Enemies Materials

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview When Link interacts with the Zonai Relic on Dragonhead Island, he hears the voice of Mineru, who tells him to take it and follow the beam of light it emits. By doing so, he will complete the "Secret of the Ring Ruins" Main Quest and start "Guidance from Ages Past". In Tobio's Hollow, Link is lead toward a large owl statue with a pedestal in front of it. When he brings the Zonai Relic to the pedestal, the owl statue will raise, revealing the entrance to the Tobio's Hollow Chasm. The Zonai Relic then shoots another beam of light toward the pedestal at its center. Placing the Zonai Relic on the pedestal causes the surrounding platform to descend into the Depths. As they move, Mineru speaks to Link again, urging him to meet with her as soon as possible. The platform lands in front of the Construct Factory, and the Zonai Relic shoots a final beam of light toward the mold at its entrance. Using Ultrahand, he can place the Relic into the head slot. When he does so, Mineru formally introduces herself to him as the Sage of Spirit. She reveals that she has lost her original body and is therefore unable to speak with him in person. In order to create a new body for herself, she asks Link to retrieve parts from the Left-Arm Depot, the Left-Leg Depot, the Right-Arm Depot, and the Right-Leg Depot. As Link places the parts into the mold, Mineru will count how many are left. After Link assembles Mineru's Construct, it will activate itself and emerge from the mold. Mineru thanks Link, revealing that they now must recover her Secret Stone. Opening the Map, Mineru points Link towards its location and asks him to accompany her. Due to the danger of their journey, she tells Link to use a nearby platform to explore the uses of the Construct. She beckons Link to hurry. When they reach the Spirit Temple, Mineru's Construct is unable to pass crumbled stairs. By Fusing a Rocket from the nearby Supply Site to the Construct, Link is able to bring it to the Temple's entrance. When they approach the statue at its center, Mineru's Construct fires a beam at it, which activates the nearby Travel Point and causes the platform they are standing on to descend. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of the Seized Construct crying out in the Spirit Temple. Text on-screen displays its name, along with the title "Scourge of the Spirit Temple".|The Seized Construct's introduction The Secret Stone of Spirit can be seen across a stretch of Gloom, requiring Link to ride Mineru's Construct in order to reach it it. However, they are stopped by Electric fences rising from the ground, and the Seized Construct appears. Mineru recognizes it as her own creation, but she is able to tell it is being controlled. Since it is being controlled by Demon King Ganondorf, Mineru declares that they must defeat the

it. However, they are stopped by Electric fences rising from the ground, and the Seized Construct appears. Mineru recognizes it as her own creation, but she is able to tell it is being controlled. Since it is being controlled by Demon King Ganondorf, Mineru declares that they must defeat the Construct. Once the Seized Construct has been defeated, the Gloom inside the Spirit Temple will dissipate and the fences will drop. A Heart Container will also appear for Link. As Link examines the Secret Stone of Spirit, his Purah Pad will suddenly begin to glow. Mineru's Spirit emerges from the Pad and enters the Secret Stone, which shrinks and embeds itself into her Construct. A purple light then engulfs Link. thumb|right|250px|alt= A screenshot of Mineru appearing before Link in another realm. Text on-screen displays her name, along with the title "The Sage of Spirit".|Mineru's introduction When the light fades, Link can see Mineru standing in front of him. Once again, she introduces herself to him, this time revealing that she is a Zonai. She expresses her happiness to finally meet Link, thanking him for helping recover her Secret Stone. Mineru reveals that she originally planned to contact him when he first acquired the Purah Pad and take over the Seized Construct, but she did not realize they would have to fight it instead. Expressing her gratitude, she asks Link to give her his hand. Once he does so, she makes the Vow of Mineru, Sage of Spirit, which engraves itself on the middle finger of his Right Arm. She claims that this has formed a bond between her and Link, swearing to help him however she can. Returning to reality, Mineru continues to speak to Link from her Construct. She reveals that she lived through the founding of Hyrule, and during that time, she lost her body and became a Spirit. Since then, she waited in the Purah Pad for Link to awaken her, and she blames Demon King Ganondorf for delaying their meeting. In her era, Zelda appeared after awakening as the Sage of Time, and she was involved in a tragedy. She decides to tell Link about Zelda's resolve, which starts "The Imprisoning War" Memory. Although Demon King Ganondorf was sealed during the Imprisoning War, Mineru reveals that she was injured and would soon die. In that time, Zelda came to her with the Decayed Master Sword, which is where it went after it disappeared from the Temple of Time. This starts the "Critical Decisions" Memory. Following Mineru's meeting with Zelda, the two of them began to prepare to guide Link in the future, which involved Mineru residing in the Purah Pad as a Spirit. Using a forbidden process, Zelda was able to restore the Master Sword, which Link must use to defeat Demon King Ganondorf. Mineru believes that the restored Master Sword can be found somewhere in Hyrule, and she tells Link to see out the Great Deku Tree to find it. She then urges Link to

process, Zelda was able to restore the Master Sword, which Link must use to defeat Demon King Ganondorf. Mineru believes that the restored Master Sword can be found somewhere in Hyrule, and she tells Link to see out the Great Deku Tree to find it. She then urges Link to continue his journey to defeat Demon King Ganondorf. Afterwards, "Guidance from Ages Past" will be completed, and "Trail of the Master Sword" will begin. Objectives

is a character in . Biography Guspar is a Hylian and a member of the Zonai Survey Team. He is one of the researchers who can be found on Digdogg Suspension Bridge investigating the Massive Zonai Ruin, which he encourages Link to look at. He states that Zonai Ruins have been falling over since the Upheaval, giving the reason for them to set up camp. He describes Digdogg Suspension Bridge having a harsh environment. However, the Survey Team finds interesting discoveries every day, so he believes it is worth it. He also encourages Link to visit the Ring Ruins in Kakariko Village. Guspar also provides information about the Gerudo Canyon, which leads to the Gerudo Desert. He describes that lately, the days in the Canyon have been very hot, and the nights have been freezing. This could lead unprepared travelers to collapse. He has also been maintaining a careful diet so he can deal with Extreme Temperatures. He directs Link to Fenlin to learn more. Guspar advises Link to keep an eye out for other investigators or travelers.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Gut Check Rock is a colossal pinnacle in northeastern Eldin Canyon, in close proximity to Eldin's Flank. The pinnacle stands in the middle of a Hot Spring river moat. Its body is sectioned into two halves, consisting of a much broader base and another pinnacle on top. Otherwise, its entirely smooth, making Climbing the Rock difficult and strenuous. A number of wooden platforms are built along its side as rest stops between Climbing. Gut Check Rock has two Updrafts along its sides, which can be ridden using the Paraglider. At the very top of the pinnacle is Gorae Torr Shrine, alongside a Cooking Pot. A metal archway serves as the entrance to Gut Check Rock, and a nearby Sign asks travelers if they have what it takes. The Goron Blood Brothers have taken up residence at Gut Check Rock in order to train. When Link first approaches Gorae Torr Shrine, Bayge will be sitting on its Travel Gate, which he claims only Goron Blood Brothers are allowed to access. The other two Goron Blood Brothers, Heehl and Kabetta, can be found at the base of Gut Check Rock. Heehl is standing next one of the Updrafts, while Kabetta is laying down in exhaustion from failing his training. However, Bayge agrees to move if Link can clear the Gut Check Rock Challenge, Mini-Game, in which Link must climb Gut Check Rock while collecting 100 Rupees. This initiates "The Gut Check Challenge" Shrine Quest. After Link has successfully completed the Gut Check Rock Challenge, Bayge will declare him the fourth Goron Blood Brother and allow him to enter Gorae Torr Shrine. Following this, Link can retry the Gut Check Rock Challenge at any time, though Bayge also begins to offer the Super Gut Check Challenge. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle is located at Gut Check Rock. A Rock Pattern can be found spread out among the five pillars on top of the Rock. When Link moves the northernmost Rock to match with the other four, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed as a reward. Creatures Materials Other Appearances As part of the "Gut-Check Challenge" Quest, Daruk must complete the Gut Check Challenge, requiring Materials to help him climb up Gut Check Rock in a limited amount of time. After receiving the Materials, Daruk is able to complete his climb, which inspires spectators to attempt the same.

, designated by the trial name The Ability to Rise, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Gutanbac Shrine is located in the eastern part of the Garden of Time on the Great Sky Island between the entrances to the Bottomless Cave. In order to enter the Shrine of Light, Link must interact with the Gutanbac Shrine's entrance. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of Link receiving the power of Ascend.|Link receiving Ascend Once Link enters Gutanbac Shrine, he is greeted by the Spirit of Rauru, who grants him the Ascend ability. The Gutanbac Shrine is heavily built around the use of the Ascend ability, with multiple ledges placed jutting out from higher areas. On its second level, a stone slab held up by two Ropes acts as the entry point to the third level once it is cut loose. The third level contains a floating platform that moves along a wall, testing Link's ability to use the Ascend ability in time with its motion. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Gutanbac Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Enemies Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography } Guy is a Rito who can be found resting next to the oasis in the Kara Kara Bazaar. He is originally from Rito Village, but he left his home for the Gerudo Desert in order to earn money. When Link first speaks to Guy, he asks if they have met before. If Link asks about Rito Village, Guy describes it as a modest village on the Tabantha Frontier. Alternatively, if Link says that he has been to Rito Village before, Guy remarks that he must have found it cold. Due to the Heat of the Gerudo Desert, Guy has been unable to continue on his journey. Despite not being allowed inside, he would like to see what Gerudo Town looks like. He then mentions that he has heard of a cooling Elixir that is made from Insects with cooling effects and Monster Parts. Guy says that they are not selling the Elixir anywhere and he is not good at Cooking. However, Guy has heard that insects with cooling effects live in the cold parts of the Gerudo Highlands, but because of how rough the monsters are there, he has had a hard time motivating himself to gather the After speaking with Guy, Link receives the Side Quest "An Ice Guy". If Link speaks to Guy again, he will mutter under his breath that he is allergic to "monster punches". He regrets coming to the Desert without a cooling Elixir and wishes someone had mentioned the Heat before he came all the way there. He also feels that the nights in the Gerudo Desert are a nice break from the Heat, but that the night is also scary. Guy admits that he is afraid of the dark. When Link returns to Guy with a Chilly Elixir, he will thank Link, as he can now leave the Gerudo Desert during the day. He rewards him with a Purple Rupee. He will also teach Link that the Gerudo word for "thank you" is sarqso. When Guy is finished speaking, the Side Quest is completed. Although Link gives him the Chilly Elixir, Guy never leaves Kara Kara Bazaar. At night, his excuse is that the Desert is not safe during this time. However, he does not leave during the day either, saying that there is no rush and that he might leave tomorrow. Guy also says that he never understood how hot the Desert was before he experienced it. He also mentions his son, saying he will have to get him to travel as well. Guy greets Link based on the time of day, correcting himself with the Gerudo word along with it. When he says "good morning" to Link, Guy amends his words and says that the Gerudo word is "sav'otta". In the evenings, Guy shares that the Gerudo word for "good evening" is "sav'saaba". In , Guy can still be found at Kara Kara Bazaar. He will greet Link with a partial Gerudo greeting,

"good morning" to Link, Guy amends his words and says that the Gerudo word is "sav'otta". In the evenings, Guy shares that the Gerudo word for "good evening" is "sav'saaba". In , Guy can still be found at Kara Kara Bazaar. He will greet Link with a partial Gerudo greeting, noting that he has picked up the language by spending so much time in the desert. If the Sand Shroud has not yet been cleared up, Guy informs Link about it, noting that as a Rito he could simply fly over it. Guy then bids farewell to Link with another mixed-up Gerudo term, "goodvorq." After "Riju of Gerudo Town", Guy will admire the clear view and safety now that the Sand Shroud has disappeared. He notes he has grown fond of his spot at the oasis, intending to bring his family to live there with him. If Link inquires about his family, he will reveal that his wife, Misa, is the proprietor of the general store in Rito Village, and that his son, Fyson, opened a shop of his own in a new town in northeast Hyrule. However, Guy laments that due to their businesses it will be a long time before they can join him. Guy once again uses "goodvorq" to say goodbye to his hometown.

is a recurring character in . Biography Hagie is a Hylian who moves to Tarrey Town with his family after the completion of the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest. During the day, he sits at the edge of town, overlooking Lake Akkala and the Torin Wetland. When Link first speaks to him, Hagie asks what his deal is. If Link responds that he is a traveler, Hagie remarks that he does not normally speak with "commoners" and that Link is an exception. Based on his clothing, Hagie guesses that Link is in need of money. If Link says he does not need Rupees, Hagie grunts and the conversation ends. However, if Link says that he is, Hagie appreciates his honesty. Immediately, Hagie offers Link a down payment of 100 Rupees. When Link is confused by this, Hagie forces him to take the money. By taking the money, Link accepts Hagie's request. Hagie reveals that there are two Guardian Stalkers in the Torin Wetland. Hagie asks Link to defeat both of them, which begins the "Hobbies of the Rich" Side Quest. If Link asks him who he is, Hagie mutters to himself that he must engage with the common folk to get things done. He assumes that Link has heard of him before, saying that he got everything he wanted in life. His days have felt empty as of late, his only thrill coming from seeing people risk their lives. Once Link has defeated both Guardian Stalkers, he can return to Tarrey Town and talk to Hagie. He saw Link destroy both Guardians, and so delivers the rest of the reward. When Link is upset to only receive a Red Rupee, worth 20 Rupees, Hagie acts pretentiously. He insists that the concept of a down payment being less than a reward is one that comes from the "common folk". With their business finished, Hagie tells Link to leave him alone. This concludes the Side Quest. Hagie also plays a small role in the Side Quest "A Parent's Love". During the night, Link can hear Hagie and Ruli discussing their daughter Hunnie. Hagie looks back on their search for a cake that would please Hunnie, wondering how much money they have spent. Ruli becomes angry at him, asking whether money or his daughter is more important to him. When Ruli says she will sell her soul to a monster for a cake that could cure Hunnie, Hagie calls her insane. After "Hobbies of the Rich" is complete, Hagie continues to look out on the Torin Wetland. He claims to be sunbathing with his family and tells Link to leave. During the sunset, he notes that his soul feels cleansed because of its beauty. At night, he wonders to himself whether his family needs to remain in Tarrey Town, as Hunnie's health has improved.

is a recurring character in . Biography Haite is a young Hylian child who lives at the Outskirt Stable, which is located on the southwestern edge of Hyrule Field. She runs around the Stable during the day. If Link speaks to her during this time, she will politely respond. When he inquires about what she is up to, Haite will remark that she is playing tag and asks Link if he wants to join. Alternatively, if Link chooses to end the conversation instead of asking her a question, Haite will be annoyed a blow a raspberry at him. If it begins to Rain while Haite is out, she will run indoors to get out of the bad Weather. She will then sit on the floor, hoping for the Rain to stop. As soon as the Rain lets up, she will bolt outside and continue her game of tag. In the evening, Haite joins Myti at the Cooking Pot for dinner. She will explain to Link that she eats her vegetables so that she can grow big and strong. At night, Haite sleeps in the Bed that is second from the right. While asleep, she mutters about being full and tired.

, also known as , are recurring Items in . Hammers go unnamed in Vermin. They can be used to press Switches, destroy certain obstacles such as Boulders, or as a weapon. Location and Uses The Hammer is found within the Death Mountain region of western Hyrule in . It is used to smash large Boulders that are occasionally found in Hyrule's overworld, often unblocking pathways and revealing new objects underneath. It can also be used to cut Trees down in the overworld. The Magic Hammer is found in the Palace of Darkness in . It can remove obstacles from Link's path, allowing him to pass into otherwise inaccessible areas. It can be used to dispatch enemies such as Helmasaurs, and is essential in defeating Terrorpins in the Palace of Darkness. The Magic Hammer is also capable of shattering the faceplate of the Helmasaur King. Against most enemies, it deals as much damage as the Master Sword Lv2, but its reach is much shorter. Freezing enemies with the Ice Rod and then breaking them with the Magic Hammer instantly defeats them, often yielding a Magical Decanter. The Magic Hammer can smash stakes, stumps, and several other obstacles in . By holding the A Button, the Links can charge the Magic Hammer which, upon release, sends out a shockwave which dazes enemies momentarily. It can be upgraded to the level 2 Magic Hammer, which makes it more powerful, sending much larger shockwaves. The Magic Hammer can also knock Force Gems from their hiding spot beneath the soil. Shadow Link can also use the Magic Hammer to interrupt the Links by sending unavoidable but harmless dazes. The Hammer can be found in Mutoh's Temple in , where it is used to defeat the temple's boss, Eox. It is also used to pound at objects, including Switches and Springboards that will propel Link into the air if he stands on it and pounds it with the Hammer. It is also one of the most powerful weapons in the game. The Hammer is controlled by holding and moving the Stylus on the Nintendo DS screen, which will drag Ciela around as she aims it and prepares to smash it. It is possible to pound on objects and enemies that are far away from Link. When held for a while longer, the Hammer will grow to a gigantic size and will make a much stronger pound. It cannot be used while on stairs. The Hammer is an effective weapon against certain enemies. Stalfos can be defeated with the Hammer in a single hit. By using it in conjunction with the Phantom Sword, it is also possible to defeat a Phantom without being seen by hiding in a Safe Zone. The Hammer can be rented or purchased from Ravio's Shop in . It is needed to progress through the Tower of Hera. The Hammer can be used to pound Moles into the ground, which then launch Link up to higher grounds, and it is essential to

in a Safe Zone. The Hammer can be rented or purchased from Ravio's Shop in . It is needed to progress through the Tower of Hera. The Hammer can be used to pound Moles into the ground, which then launch Link up to higher grounds, and it is essential to defeat enemies such as Deadrocks and Terrorpins. If Link buys the Hammer, he can upgrade it to the Nice Hammer by returning 10 or more Lost Maiamais to Mother Maiamai. This form does more damage to enemies and sends out a shockwave to stun them. The Magic Hammer deals twice the damage to enemies as Swords in . It creates a shockwave when used, which can destroy Grass and Rocks and stun enemies. The Magic Hammer can be used to pound down stakes, destroy ice crystals, defeat Deadrocks, and make use of Moles. Magic Hammers first appear in Silver Shrine, in which all three Links acquire one. They reappear in Ice Temple (two Hammers), Desert Temple (two Hammers), Dragon Citadel, and Sky Temple. They also appear in the Scorching Zone, Frozen Zone and Baneful Zone of the Den of Trials, as well as the Coliseum's Ice Cavern and The Ruins arenas. The use of Magic Hammers is required to defeat the Bosses Blizzagia and Stalchampion. The effects of the Magic Hammer are improved while wearing Hammerwear. This Outfit doubles the item's shockwave size and damage output, while allowing it to be swung quicker. Two different Hammers can be obtained in . The first is the Iron Sledgehammer, which can be used both as a Weapon and for mining Ore. The second is the Spring-Loaded Hammer. It can only be purchased at the Fang and Bone for 199 Mon, and it is capable of knocking back Enemies on its fourth hit. Other Appearances In , the Hammer is a Spell that Zelda can cast as a projectile with her Wand. It is a slow-moving Spell, but can potentially inflict a lot of damage onto enemies. It is dropped by Warbane after encountering him for the first time in the Shrine of Fire. It costs two Rupees to use. In , the Hammer is a class of Weapon used by Darunia. It is associated with Fire. A different Hammer also appears as an item in and . This item is mainly used to smash objects, but can also be used as a weapon to attack enemies. It is also used to weaken the Helmaroc King. Additionally, two Hammer Item Cards appear in and . The first Hammer Item Card, based on the Skull Hammer from , appears in the Great Sea and Master Wind Waker Maps. It can be used on Hammer Switches to reveal hidden Enemies. The second Hammer Item Card appears in the Lorule Map, based on the Hammer from . Using this Item Card adds increased attack to the Ravio Board and reveals hidden rewards when used on posts. Ravio also uses a unique Hammer as his class of

Switches to reveal hidden Enemies. The second Hammer Item Card appears in the Lorule Map, based on the Hammer from . Using this Item Card adds increased attack to the Ravio Board and reveals hidden rewards when used on posts. Ravio also uses a unique Hammer as his class of Weapon, referred to as the Rental Hammer. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Haran Lakefront Well can be found directly north of Haran Lake on Fural Plain, which is part of the Faron Grasslands. The Well's interior includes an area of dry land alongside a pool of Water. Due to the acoustics in this chamber, Sagessa has decided to use it to practice her singing, though she only does so at night. During the day, Sagessa can be found asleep in the Well. At the beginning of the Side Adventure "An Eerie Voice", Penn tells Link about rumors concerning Zelda, whose voice can be heard telling people to "leave the...rms..." on Fural Plain. As he approaches the Haran Lakefront Well, Link hears this voice singing a warning for people to abandon their Weapons or face harm. Upon approaching Sagessa, however, he can hear the song's true lyrics from her, and she realizes this is the reason people have been throwing their Weapons through the Well's opening. She has gathered all of the Weapons together in nearby Buckets, and she welcomes Link to take them for himself. Creatures Materials Equipment

is a recurring character in . Biography Harlow is a Stable Worker at the Snowfield Stable in the Tabantha Tundra. When Link speaks to her, she suggests that he rest in one of their Beds before journeying into the snow. At night, Harlow will scrub the Stable floor, as she can only clean when it is dark out. During the day, she will sit beside Danton at the Cooking Pot next to the Stable. However, she will retreat inside if it starts to snow. Harlow is annoyed by the pursuit of power and thinks that there is more to being a hero than having the Sword that Seals the Darkness, which Danton is fascinated by. If Link agrees with her, she says that she hopes a kind swordsman like him will be the one to wield the Master Sword, if it exists. Alternatively, if Link tells her that he loves adventure, she notes that he willingly ventured all the way to Snowfield Stable. Harlow overhears Link when he shows the Master Sword to Danton, which she will later admit to. While she can not do much to help, she promises to keep Snowfield Stable clean if Link ever needs a place to rest.

is a recurring character in . Biography Harth is a young Rito man who serves as Rito Village's Bow craftsman. He has been friends with Teba since they were children. When he was young, Harth dreamed of being a warrior, but he ended up inheriting his family's Bow-crafting business. From this business, he learned how to recreate the Great Eagle Bow. Harth is the father of Molli. Prior to Link's arrival in Rito Village, Harth refused to listen to Kaneli when he told them only a Champion could enter Divine Beast Vah Medoh. He and Teba attempted to face the Divine Beast on their own, which resulted in Harth becoming injured. Harth was forced to retreat because of this. Link can find him in his home, where he is in much pain. Though he initially welcomes Link, he dismisses him when he asks what is wrong with him. Afterwards, he curses Medoh. If Link speaks to Harth again, he will still welcome him. When asked who he is, Harth introduces himself as the Bow craftsman. Due to his injury, however, he is unable to raise his arm, so his business has halted. Once again, Link can ask him if he is alright, but this time Harth admits that he is not. He regrets not listening to Kaneli's warnings about the Divine Beast. After Link speaks to Kaneli, Harth decides to tell Link about what happened when he faced Divine Beast Vah Medoh. Harth reveals that the wound on his wing came from Medoh, which was supposedly once a protector of Rito Village. However, when he and Teba approached the Divine Beast, it unexpectedly shot at them. Though Harth tried to fight back, he was too slow and ended up being hit. Teba managed to catch him before he fell out of the sky, and the pair ended up retreating. Harth is frightened when he thinks of what would have happened had Teba not been there to save him. Now that Link knows the story, Harth asks if he is going to find Teba and promises to tell him everything he knows. Link can then ask Harth about Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Teba, or himself. When Link asks about the Divine Beast, Harth shares the legend that it protected Rito Village before it disappeared 100 years ago, though he does not believe this to be true. His injury occurred when he and Teba went to investigate it. As soon as he is able, Harth plans on taking a lot of Bomb Arrows up to it and destroying its Cannons. When Link asks about Teba, Harth explains that they have known each other for a while and that Teba is the best at flying in Rito Village. While Teba is reckless, temperamental, and rude, he and Harth look out for each other. However, Harth was disturbed by the way Teba was speaking before he left. He is angered that Teba intends to face Divine Beast Vah Medoh alone, especially since he has

at flying in Rito Village. While Teba is reckless, temperamental, and rude, he and Harth look out for each other. However, Harth was disturbed by the way Teba was speaking before he left. He is angered that Teba intends to face Divine Beast Vah Medoh alone, especially since he has a wife and a child. If Link asks Harth who he is, he will explain his trade and his childhood dream. He also reveals that he is the father of Molli, and since she is close in age with Tulin, his family spends a lot of time with Teba's. However, he stops his explanation when he realizes nothing he said was helpful to Link. After Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been calmed, Harth will begin to work on a Swallow Bow. Harth is willing to do Link the service of crafting him a new Great Eagle Bow, should he ever lose or break the one he receives from Kaneli. In this scenario, Harth will need a Swallow Bow, five bundles of Wood, and a Diamond in order to craft a new one. As they are expensive to make, Harth suggests Link try to find the Bow if he has lost it somewhere. When Link tries to take the Swallow Bow from the table near Harth, he will call him out. If Harth is still injured, he will tell Link to keep it, as he is unable to use it. After freeing Divine Beast Vah Medoh, however, Harth allows Link to keep it as a reward.

The , also known as the Purah Pad Research Lab, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Hateno Ancient Tech Lab is located on a hill on the northeastern end of Hateno Village, overlooking the Necluda Sea. It is a three-story tower, with the main Lab taking up the first floor. The second floor consists of Symin's room, while Purah's Room is located on the third floor. The remains of a Guardian Stalker are strapped down to the roof. Several Signs leading to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab warn against visitors and suggest caution. The Lab is one of two successors to the Ancient Research Institute, the other being the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab. Following the second Great Calamity, a source of Ancient Energy was found in Necluda. After playing rock, paper, scissors with Robbie, it was decided that Purah would continue her research in Hateno Village. At Purah's insistence, Robbie escorted her there, carrying her Guidance Stone in a cart. However, the pair became separated at Fort Hateno, and Purah continued on her own. Purah's research at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab focuses on the Sheikah Slate and its Runes. The Lab also boasts a collection of all known Books on ancient civilizations. Two of these Books are the Camera Manual, Sheikah Sensor Notes, and Sheikah Slate Manual, all of which were written by Purah and Symin. Over the years, three research assistants are known to have resided at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab with Purah. The first is Nanna, who describes Purah as having a strange personality. The next known assistant is Jerrin, who was later sent to the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab by Impa. Finally, Purah's current assistant is Symin, and while he struggles with the disorganized state that Purah keeps the Lab in, he is still honored to work with her. Sometime prior to Link's arrival at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab, Purah began development of an anti-aging Rune. Her goal was to reverse the aging process, bringing older warriors out of retirement to fight Calamity Ganon upon his return. Purah tested the Rune on her, and over time, she regressed to the age of six. Once she developed an age-boosting Rune to reverse its effects, though, she discovered that the Furnace's Blue Flame had been extinguished, thereby deactivating her Guidance Stone. Symin attempted to retrieve the Blue Flame from the Ancient Furnace, but a combination of his clumsiness and Rain caused him to fail. When Purah herself tried to go, she was seen by Karin. As a result of this, Purah has not left the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab, and the residents of Hateno Village have not seen her. As part of the "Locked Mementos" Main Quest, Impa sends Link to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab to repair his Sheikah Slate. When Link first speaks to Purah, she points him towards Symin, who she claims is the director. However, Symin reveals that Purah is actually the Lab's director, despite her youthful appearance.

are Items in . Location and Uses Hateno Cheese is a dairy product produced from the Milk of Hateno Cows in the Hateno Pasture. Koyin begins producing the Cheese after Link recovers a letter from Lake Sumac in the Side Adventure "A Letter to Koyin". The letter was left by Koyin's great-grandfather and contains a recipe for Cheese developed by him and Reede's grandfather. Once Koyin has begun production, she begins selling Hateno Cheese at the Pasture and allows Link to trade Milk for Hateno Cheese. Merchants and General Stores across Hyrule also begin to stock Hateno Cheese. Hateno Cheese becomes the new "signature dish" of Hateno Village and is the solution to the Side Adventure "A New Signature Food". Hateno Cheese has the price of 20 Rupees, and is called a delicacy by numerous travelers and vendors. This high price is consistent, but the cheese produces multiple new recipes. There are no special healing effects besides heart recovery. Meals made with Hateno Cheese

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Hateno Pasture is a ranch located on the eastern end of Hateno Village. It features a single House, where Tokk sleeps at night. Koyin, who is a shepherd, can always be found in front of the Pasture, while Dantz works in a stall behind the House. The largest part of Hateno Pasture is its field, which borders Lake Sumac and Retsam Forest. Several Blue Flame Pedestals and Apple Trees are placed along the Pasture's western fence. Fresh Milk originates from the Hateno Cows and Highland Sheep kept at Hateno Pasture. However, it has recently had issues with the Monsters on Hateno Beach, which have been stealing the Sheep from Koyin. Searching for help, Koyin posted a notice on Hateno Village's bulletin board asking for someone to defeat the Monsters. When Link first meets Koyin, she will explain the Hateno Pasture's troubles with Monsters to him. This begins "The Sheep Rustlers" Side Quest. After the Monsters on Hateno Beach have been defeated, Koyin notices that the Highland Sheep have calmed down. She then asks Link if he was the one who defeated the Monsters. If Link confirms that he did, she will give him 10 bottles of Fresh Milk as a reward. Afterwards, the notice on Hateno Village's bulletin board will change to a message thanking Link. Dantz operates the Deer Hunting Mini-Game from the Hateno Pasture. In order to manage the Deer population in Retsam Forest, Dantz asks Link to hunt as many Deer as he can within one minute. As a reward, he gives Link Rupees depending on how many Deer he kills. A single Treasure Chest can be found within Hateno Pasture. If Link befriends the Pasture's Hylian Retriever, it will lead him to a metal Chest embedded in the ground, which contains a Silver Rupee. Creatures Materials Equipment Other Appearances As part of the "Helping Out at Hateno Pasture" Quest, the family at Hateno Pasture wants a new wheat supplier for feeding their livestock and stuffing their pillows. Once Impa introduces them to Tabantha Wheat, they strike a deal with the farmer that grew it in Tabantha Village.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Hateno School was founded in Hateno Village by Zelda as part of reconstruction efforts in Hyrule. Bolson was commissioned to construct the School itself, which was his final job in the Village. Zelda appointed Symin as the School's teacher, believing his experience as Purah's assistant gave him the experience to do so. Prior to the Upheaval, Zelda observed the classroom, which resulted in many of the children becoming close to her. The School Notes can be found on the second floor of the Hateno School. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Hateno Village is a permanent Hylian settlement located in East Necluda. It is rumored to be the hometown of Link. The Myahm Agana Shrine is located on the southern end of the Village, next to Bolson Construction's model homes. To the east, the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab overlooks the Village, and pathways to Hateno Beach and Hateno Bay can be found nearby. The peaceful Village contains an Inn and a few shops, including the East Wind, the Ventest Clothing Boutique, and the Kochi Dye Shop. A total of three Silos can be found throughout the town, two of which have had windmills attached in order to grind flour. Blue Flame Pedestals also dot the landscape, and Hateno's Goddess Statue can be found at the Village Chief's House. During the Great Calamity 100 years ago, Hateno Village was the larger of only two Hylian settlements to remain. Its survival is owed largely to the successful defense effort at Fort Hateno, as well as the awakening of Zelda's sealing powers on Blatchery Plain. Following the Calamity, the Age of Burning Fields began in Hateno Village, wherein the destruction of Necluda left Hateno unable to farm. Eventually, the Region was able to recover, and Hateno Village became self-sufficient. Purah also founded the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab nearby, due to the source of Ancient Energy discovered on the High Ground. Since it is located so close to Mount Lanayru, Hateno Village has a chilly environment, and most residents wear long sleeves as a result. The villagers primarily make their living through agriculture, and most Houses have either a field or a ranch of some kind. Dyeing clothes is also a traditional craft of the village. Though Hateno Village is relatively peaceful when compared to the rest of Hyrule Kingdom, travelers such as Celessa note that it feels precarious. As part of the "Locked Mementos" Main Quest, Link is sent to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab in Hateno Village to repair his Sheikah Slate. Two Shrine Quests, "The Spring of Wisdom" and "Secret of the Cedars", can be started by speaking to residents of Hateno Village. A total of six Side Quests can be obtained throughout Hateno, these being "Hylian Homeowner" at Link's House, "From the Ground Up" at Link's House, "The Statue's Bargain" at Firly Pond, "The Weapon Connoisseur", "A Gift for My Beloved" at The Great Ton Pu Inn, and "The Sheep Rustlers" at Hateno Pasture. Two additional Side Quests, "Slated for Upgrades" and "Sunshroom Sensing", are available at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. Areas Creatures Equipment Inhabitants Materials Hateno Village reappears in . A variety of large Mushrooms decorations are now spread across the village, and many residents wear similar clothing and hats. Cece introduced the mushroom fashion to the village, making it a popular destination for fashion-inclined people across Hyrule. In the time between games, Zelda had Bolson build the Hateno School for the children of Hateno Village, with Symin as the

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Hateno Village East Well is the easternmost Well in Hateno Village, which is part of East Necluda. Its chamber is comprised of a single pool of Water. This Well and Hateno Village's other Wells are connected underground by a series of tunnels. The two tunnels branching out from the Hateno Village East Well connect to the inner chambers of the Hateno Village West Well and Hateno Village South Well, though these passageways are infested by Monsters and occasionally blocked by Hard Sediment. As part of the Side Adventure "Reede's Secret", Clavia asks Link to enter the locked Shed and learn what her husband Reede has been doing inside it. Link can access the Shed by Ascending through its floor from the tunnels connecting Hateno Village's Wells. The position to do so is in the tunnel between the Hateno Village East Well and the Hateno Village West Well. Creatures Materials

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Hateno Village North Well is the northernmost Well in Hateno Village in East Necluda. It is situated on the High Ground between the Village Head's House and the Hateno School. Inside the Well is a small pond and several Boulders, the latter of which are positioned along the western wall. When Link moves these Boulders with Ultrahand, he reveals a tunnel leading to the Hateno Village West Well's underground chamber. From here, two other tunnels connect to Hateno Village's remaining Wells. During the Side Adventure "Reede's Secret", Clavia asks Link to investigate her husband Reede's locked Shed. Link can enter the Shed by Ascending into it from the tunnel system below Hateno Village, which the Hateno Village North Well provides access to. Creatures Materials

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Hateno Village South Well is situated in the southern portion of Hateno Village in East Necluda. It has an interior that Link can enter, which consists of a pond of Water and two branching tunnels. The northeastern tunnel leads to the Hateno Village East Well, while the northwestern tunnel connects to the passageway between the East Well and the Hateno Village West Well. In the past, Zelda pointed out to Aster that many Frogs reside in the Hateno Village South Well, in addition to showing her how to catch them. Since she has moved into one of Hudson Construction's model Houses nearby, Aster has found joy in living close to the Well and its Frogs. During the Side Adventure "Reede's Secret", Clavia requests that Link investigate Reede's locked Shed. To do so, Link must Ascend into the Shed from the tunnel system below Hateno Village. The point to do so is located in the tunnel between the Hateno Village East Well and West Well, specifically where it meets with the end of the Hateno Village South Well's northwestern tunnel. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Hateno Village West Well is located near the School's Field in northwestern Hateno Village, which is part of East Necluda. Its underground chamber consists of a small pool of Water. It is connected to Hateno Village's other Wells by a series of tunnels, two of which branch off from the West Well. The northeastern tunnel leads to the Hateno Village North Well, while its southeastern tunnel leads to the Hateno Village East Well. As part of the Side Adventure "Reede's Secret", Clavia asks Link to investigate her husband Reede's Shed. However, the Shed is locked, and so Link must Ascend into it from the tunnels below Hateno Village. He can do so in the tunnel between the Hateno Village West Well and the East Well, near where the Hateno Village South Well's northwestern tunnel ends. Creatures Materials

, also known as Recovery Hearts, and Blood, are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Hearts aid Link by replenishing his life energy by one Heart at a time. They can be found anywhere in Hyrule, Koholint Island, Termina, Labrynna, Holodrum, the Great Sea, the World of the Ocean King, New Hyrule, and Skyloft. Hearts are uncovered in Pots, Jars, tall Grass, defeated enemies, under rocks and, in many instances, they can even be purchased from shops. They appear as small, floating, red Hearts. In , Hearts cannot be found in the world; life energy can only be replenished by consuming Food, using Fairies or Mipha's Grace, or standing in hot springs. Hearts are found by defeating Enemies or breaking Objects such as Pots. Life Meter The Life Meter is a gauge indicating how much life Link has. Whenever Link takes damage from an enemy attack or hazard, he loses health in increments of full Hearts, half Hearts, or in and all games from then on, quarter Hearts. Losing all Hearts in the Life Meter causes Link to collapse, resulting in a Game Over. In various The Legend of Zelda games, Link can extend his life energy from three to twenty hearts. In others, the maximum is either 14 or 16. The only game where Link does not have his health represented by Hearts is , where it is instead represented by rectangular segments (the game still features Heart Containers to increase the Life Meter, however). and introduces Green Hearts. These replenish the endurance of SS Linebeck's Hull in , and the Spirit Train in . These Hearts can only be found while traveling on the overworld of their respective games. Initially the vehicle start out with four Hearts, and can obtain more by assembling matching parts of the vehicle. When the vehicle runs out of Green Hearts, it becomes destroyed, resulting in a Game Over. In , Link can store Hearts in a Bottle by using his Bug Net. left introduces Temporary Hearts, which are yellow in color and temporarily increase Link's total life energy. Temporary Hearts can be gained by consuming cooked Food or Elixirs that have this effect. Once depleted, Temporary Hearts are lost and cannot be recovered, however more can be gained by consuming another item with the effect. introduces an unnamed variety of Heart, which is gray and visibly cracked. These represent Hearts that have been lost to Gloom exposure and cannot be recovered without either eating specific types of cooked Food, being near a Lightroot, or going to the surface. Oxygen In both and , oxygen is measured according to Link's life meter. When he is exposed for too long underwater, or enters a very hot environment, a timer appears. Before it runs out, the young hero must either rise to surface or exit from the hot area, depending on the area; otherwise, he will die. How long the time will be depends on the current life meter (not only the maximum capacity,

Another moment occurs in : as Link and Zelda reach specific floors in Ganon's Castle, Zelda becomes trapped in a ring of fire and two Stalfos appear. The only way to free Zelda is to defeat both foes; once this occurs, she thanks Link and drops a few Hearts. After Link receives a Piece of Heart from the Stylish Woman in Kakariko Village in , she will give him normal Hearts after every time he visits.

Heart Containers, also known as Bowls of Hearts, Heart-Shaped Stones, Life Hearts, and Crystal Hearts are recurring Items in . They increase Link's Life Gauge, which is represented by a set of Hearts, excluding , where his health is symbolized by a life bar. Collecting enough Pieces of Heart assembles a Heart Container and increases Link's maximum health. Location and Uses As Link progresses through the games, he will require more and more health in order to survive the greater challenges. This additional health is acquired in the form of Heart Containers, with each Heart Container adding one whole heart to the amount of hearts Link has, in addition to fully recovering his Life Gauge. A Heart Container is awarded after every major boss in most games. The maximum number of Heart Containers is typically 20 or 16; see below. In , only full Heart Containers are available, not Pieces of Heart. 8 Heart Containers are obtained from bosses, one each in Level 1 to Level 8. A single Heart Container can be found on Hyrule's eastern coast, requiring the Stepladder to collect. The remaining 4 Heart Containers are offered as gifts in caves, in locations that vary between the First and Second Quest. In these caves, Link is offered the choice of a Heart Container or a Red Potion; if Link takes the potion, the Heart Container is permanently lost. In the Second Quest, it is possible to permanently lose a Heart Container in specific rooms, one in Level 4, and two in Level 7, where Link is required to pay either 1 Heart Container or 50 rupees. In , Link's life is represented by a gauge, which starts with 4 segments. 4 Bowls of Hearts are found throughout the game. Each permanently increases length of the life gauge by 1 segment, up to a maximum of 8, and fully refills the gauge. In , the first additional Heart Container can be found in the Sanctuary after the first visit to Hyrule Castle; this Heart Container uniquely fully restores Link's health. An additional 10 Heart Containers are obtained by defeating the Bosses of the first three Light World Dungeons and the first seven Dark World Dungeons. Unlike most games, Heart Containers dropped by Bosses are mandatory, as Link remains locked in the arena until he picks up Container. Agahnim does not drop a Heart Container when fought in either Hyrule Castle or Ganon's Tower. This game introduces Pieces of Heart, 4 of which are required to form a Heart Container. 6 Heart Containers are formed this way. In , eight Heart Containers are obtained by defeating Bosses. Three can be obtained by collecting four Pieces of Heart each. As in , Boss Heart Containers are mandatory, though this was removed in . Starting in this game, collecting any Heart Container fully restores Link's health. In , eight Heart Containers are obtained by defeating Bosses, and nine are obtained by collecting four Pieces of Heart each. Boss Heart Containers return

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Characteristics Hearty Bass are a type of Fish that can be found in the Waters of West Necluda and the Akkala Highlands. Schools of Hearty Bass can be found in ponds located on Firly Plateau and Mount Rhoam. Their large bodies are able to store a lot of nutrients. Exposing Hyrule Basses to Fire results in Roasted Hearty Basses, while chilling it with Ice results in Frozen Hearty Basses. They can be eaten raw to heal two Hearts. Meals made using Hearty Bass will grant Link Extra Hearts when eaten. Hearty Bass are among the Fish that can be used to cook a Fish Skewer, a Fish and Mushroom Skewer, and Salt-Grilled Fish. They're also counted among the seafood that can be used to make Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Seafood Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. In order to upgrade the Zora Set to its third tier at a Great Fairy Fountain, Link needs to collect five Hearty Bass for each piece. Other Appearances
