are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Hearty Lizards can be found resting on Palm Trees in the Gerudo Desert and on the shores of the Necluda Sea. They can be Cooked with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot to make a Hearty Elixir, which will temporarily increase Link's maximum Hearts when consumed. However, Cooking them with other ingredients will result in Dubious Food. The Kochi Dye Shop also accepts Hearty Lizards as an ingredient to make Blue Dye. Hearty Lizards are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Hearty Radishes are found in the ground in Hyrule Ridge and East Necluda, their location indicated by their stalk. Hearty Radishes are also sold by Beedle at the East Akkala Stable and the General Shoppe. Hearty Radishes can be eaten raw to restore two and a half Hearts. If a Hearty Radish is roasted over a Campfire, it becomes a Roasted Radish. If a Hearty Radish is Cooked in a Cooking Pot, the resulting Food will grant Link Extra Hearts, which temporarily increases Link's maximum Hearts. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Hearty Radishes are one of the ingredients that can be used to make Peach Hateno Dye. Hearty Radishes are not required to upgrade any pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. Making Creamy Heart Soup in a Cooking Pot requires Link to use either a Hearty Radish or a Big Hearty Radish: They can also be used to make the following Meals: Hearty Radishes appear in , where they play a similar role to Hearty Radishes in . They are still not used to upgrade any pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. They are not sold in any Shops anymore. Making Creamy Heart Soup requires Link to use either a Hearty Radish or a Big Hearty Radish: Hearty Radishs can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Other Appearances Hearty Radishes are Materials in that can only be used as supplies for Camps.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Characteristics Hearty Salmons inhabit cold bodies of water within the Hebra Mountains and the Tabantha Frontier. Their bodies accrete layers of fat in response to this, insulating them from their cold surroundings. Eating them raw restores four Hearts to Link's Life Gauge. Exposed to fire, Hearty Salmons become Roasted Hearty Salmons. Alternatively, they can be exposed to Ice to become Frozen Hearty Salmon. Meals made using Hearty Salmons will grant Link temporary Hearts when eaten. During the Shrine Quest "Recital at Warbler's Nest", Kotts can be found fishing for Hearty Salmon just outside Rito Village. When reminded of the recital, she will give Link a Hearty Salmon for Genli. Hearty Salmons are required to use while Cooking to create Hearty Salmon Muenière and Salmon Risotto. As with other fish in the game, Hearty Salmons can be used to make a Fish Skewer, a Fish and Mushroom Skewer, and Salt-Grilled Fish. Hearty Salmons are also among the seafood that can be used to make Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. Hearty Salmons reappear in . They are found in cold bodies of water and can also be bought from the Coral Reef once Link has completed the "Sidon of the Zora" Main Quest. Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Hearty Truffles can be found below Trees in the Great Hyrule Forest and Hyrule Field. They can be purchased from establishments such as the Spore Store and the East Wind or from the Wandering Merchant Cambo. They can be eaten to restore two Hearts. When Cooked in a Cooking Pot, the resulting food will grant Link Extra Hearts. Hearty Truffles that are exposed to Fire turn into Toasted Hearty Truffles. At the Kochi Dye Shop, they can be used as an ingredient to create Black Dye. Hearty Truffles, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Hearty Truffles can now be found exclusively in clumps of dirt in Caves and Wells instead of on the Surface, and they are significantly more valuable due to their newfound rarity. When eaten, they restore two of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge, whereas when Cooked into Meals, they restore all of his Hearts and temporarily grant him Extra Hearts. Due to their black coloration, they are difficult to spot in the dark environments they are found in. When exposed to Fires or Scorching Climates, they become Toasted Hearty Truffles. At the Kochi Dye Shop, they can be used to make Black Hateno Dyes. When Fused to Weapons, Hearty Truffles impart Bouncy properties onto them, causing the Weapons to launch struck Enemies back slightly. Shields with Truffles Fused to them cause Enemies who are Parried to stumble slightly. Hearty Truffles, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Other Appearances Hearty Truffles are Materials in .

, also known as Extreme Heat and , is a recurring mechanic in . Overview Heat occurs during the daytime in the Gerudo Desert. When the Temperature rises above 104°F, Link will experience one level of Heat and slowly take damage. When the Temperature rises above 122°F, as in Extremely Hot Zones, he will experience two levels of Heat and take damage more quickly. Link can avoid taking damage from Heat by taking shelter within shade, submerging himself in a body of Water, equipping certain pieces of Armor, consuming Chilly Cooking, or drinking Chilly Elixirs. Both Gerudo Town and Kara Kara Bazaar provide constant protection from Heat. The Rito traveler, Guy, can be found in the Kara Kara Bazaar, waiting for the daytime Heat to pass in order to visit Gerudo Town. The Side Quest "An Ice Guy" involves giving a Chilly Elixir to Guy so that he can cross the Desert. The Gerudo Desert and its settlements, Gerudo Town and the Oasis, are subject to intense Heat. Whenever Princess Zelda is idle in the Desert, she will begin to sweat and fan herself. However, she will not take damage as a result of the Heat. Other Appearances Desert Heat appears in the "Enduring Resolve" Scenario. Warriors caught within the Desert portion of Gerudo Desert will occasionally sustain minor damage from Desert Heat. In order to curb the effects of the Desert Heat, the Hyrulean Forces must seize the North and South Oasis for the northern and southern portions of the Desert, respectively.

, also known as the Hebra Region, is a recurring Region in . Features and Overview Hebra is a vast Region covering the northwestern corner of Hyrule. The Region is very mountainous but also has vast expanses of flat terrain. Hebra is made up of three smaller areas: Hebra Mountains, Tabantha Frontier, and Tabantha Tundra. Both areas are roughly similar in size with Hebra Mountains covering most of the northern portion and Tabantha Frontier covering the southern portion of the Region. The vast majority of northern Hebra is extremely cold, with Temperatures requiring 2 levels of Cold Resistance at all times. The Weather is often snowy and rarely sunny. Link can withstand the cold by consuming Spicy Elixirs or other spicy Food, or by equipping multiple pieces of Armor that grants Cold Resistance such as the Warm Doublet or the Snowquill Set. Areas Areas Other Appearances

The , also known as the Leviathan in Hebra, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Hebra Great Skeleton is located in the Hebra Mountains in the Ice Cave. It is one of the three remaining skeletons of the now-extinct Leviathans. Link must take a picture of the remains for the "Leviathan Bones" Side Quest. The Hebra Great Skeleton remains where it was in Breath of the Wild and is the subject of the Side Quest "Hebra's Colossal Fossil". After Link completes the previous Side Quest, "Eldin's Colossal Fossil", Loone travels to the Ice Cave to see the Leviathan for herself. However, its skeleton is missing two large pieces, which she will lament if Link speaks to her. The missing piece of its spine can be found frozen in a giant chunk of Ice, and the missing Fin Bone is stuck inside a large patch of breakable Rock. Link can piece the remains back together to complete the Side Quest. Two Koroks are hidden inside the skeleton's eye sockets.

The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview In , the Ice Cave is a Cave in the Hebra Mountains below the Hebra North Summit. It contains the Hebra Great Skeleton and To Quomo Shrine. The Cave has bluish-purple Ice with dark patches running through it along the walls and in spikes along its floor. A deep pool of Water which the Great Skeleton is partially submerged in is located at the Cave's lowest point, with short Grass around its shore. The Ice Cave is located behind a Giant Stone Door southeast of the Hebra North Summit, which can be knocked down with a Snowball rolled from the top of a nearby hill. Areas The Hebra Great Skeleton Cave returns in . It is located in the same position in the Hebra Mountains. Areas Creatures Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Hebra North Summit is located in the Hebra Mountains overlooking the Sturnida Basin between the Hebra West Summit and the Hebra East Summit. The Hebra North Summit is a steep incline up to a small flat peak. At the top of the Summit, a Pinwheel can be found sitting at the top. If Link stands near this pinwheel, a Balloon will appear and fly around the peak, stopping every few seconds. If Link shoots the balloon with an Arrow, the Korok will appear and grant Link a Korok Seed for finding him.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Hebra Peak is located in the Hebra Mountains. It features a unique hole in the mountain causing it to form a crescent shape, which was apparently formed by a giant beam in a battle during the 10,000-Year-Old Calamity. The inside of the crescent shape has a polished, glassy texture. Hebra Peak can be seen in scenes set in the Era of Myth without its characteristic hole. Additionally, in the present day, it lacks the crystalline texture it once had. Creatures Enemies Materials Treasure Chests Korok Seeds Other Appearances At the end of the "Goron Rations" Quest, the amount of Rock Roasts in the Gorons' stockpile is compared to the size of Hebra Peak.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Hebra Plunge is a lake located northeast of Rito Village and south of Hebra Peak in the Tabantha Frontier. The lake is located on the border between the Tabantha Frontier and the Hebra Mountains, making the Lake's Water cold enough to hurt Link if he swims in it, but close enough to still be in the Tabantha Frontier. The top area of the Lake is freezing and will damage Link if he Swims in it, but the bottom area is not. This allows Link and Fish to swim in it. Hebra Plunge starts as the river Hebra Falls feeds into and, when it gets wide enough, turns into a lake and switches to Hebra Plunge. In the lower area of the Lake, a small flat-topped pillar can be seen sticking out of the water. In the top section of the lower area in Hebra Plunge, a small dock and Raft can be found next to a Monster Stronghold. On a small island on the eastern side of the lake, a lone Tree stands high into the air. If Link climbs this tree, an invisible Korok is found hiding at the top. Creatures Enemies Normal Mode Master Mode Materials Treasure Chests Normal Mode Master Mode

is a location in . Features and Overview The Hebra South Summit Cave is located on the north side of Rospro Pass in the Hebra Mountains. Its lower entrance is marked by a Bonfire. Inside the Cave, there is a large Updraft that can be used to advance to higher ground. At the ground where this Updraft can be found, there is a thin sheet of Ice, which can be broken to reveal a small chamber housing Ore Deposits. On the upper level of the Cave, Link can find Rare Ore Deposits and more Ore Deposits. Its upper entrance leads to the base of Talonto Peak on the Hebra South Summit. Creatures Enemies Materials

The , also known as the Evacuation Hut or the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Hebra Trailhead Lodge is located at the southern end of Rospro Pass in the Hebra Mountains. A Campfire can be found outside the Lodge, and a nearby Ladder marked by a Sign leads to Rospro Pass. Inside the hut is a Cooking Pot and a Bed where Link can rest to restore his Hearts. Selmie's Notes, which offer guidance to those attempting to scale the Hebra Mountains, can also be found on the table to the left of the entrance. Due to the Lodge being situated within a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit the cabin without taking damage. As Link approaches the Hebra Trailhead Lodge, a Traveler sitting at the Campfire outside the cabin will call out to him. When Link speaks to the Traveler, they notice they he appears to be troubled and offer to show him his future. If Link accepts their offer, the Traveler claims to see Link's death. If Link refuses, the Traveler declares that some things are better left unknown, claiming that today is the day Link will die. With either answer, the Traveler then reveals that they are a Yiga Footsoldier and proceeds to attack Link. Inside the Hebra Trailhead Lodge is a stone Treasure Chest. When Link opens the Chest, he will receive a Meteor Rod. Materials Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Heehl is one of the Goron Blood Brothers, a group consisting of himself and his brothers Bayge and Kabetta. Heehl and his brothers are passionate about training in difficult feats of strength and endurance. They live in a house in southern Goron City, which is now abandoned and left with a Sign saying they have gone to Gut Check Rock to train. Heehl is involved in the "Test of Will" Shrine Quest at Mount Nabooru in the Gerudo Highlands. Heehl and the other Goron Blood Brothers have traveled to their ancestral training ground to train themselves to withstand the heat in Goron City. They challenge Link to join them by sitting in a ring of fire to see who can withstand the longest. When Link accepts their challenge, Heehl remarks that he has a fiery passion. Heehl is the second Goron to collapse, at which point he appears to be hallucinating. After Link is declared the winner, Heehl allows him to attempt a harder contest, which involves standing on an even hotter platform. When Bayge asks Link if he thinks it is a bad idea, Heehl says that he is right. When Link passes this challenge, Heehl will be impressed by his display. Joloo Nah Shrine will then emerge from the ground, and the Shrine Quest will be completed. Heehl also appears at the base of Gut Check Rock in northern Eldin Canyon, standing next to one of the Updrafts near the main gateway. He recognizes that a need to build up his strength must have brought him there and welcome him. He encourages Link to talk to Bayge to attempt their training. After completing Bayge's Gut Check Rock Challenge, he commends Link on his success. During the "EX Champion Daruk's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, the Goron Blood Brothers can be found at Darb Pond. They have decided to train at this location like Daruk did, since they believe it will allow them to be more like him. Heehl explains that the goal of this training is to stand on the Glowing Ring atop the Pond's Lava. Before attempting it, however, the brothers decide to strategize. When spoken to afterwards, Heehl says that this training is intense. After Link manages to pass through the Glowing Ring, Heehl wonders if someone managed to complete the training. However, he thinks this is impossible, as only Daruk or one of the Goron Blood Brothers could have done such a thing.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Herb Sautés are dishes made by Cooking any Vegetable, herb, or Flower together with Goron Spice in a Cooking Pot. Their neutral versions are made by using Hyrule Herbs, which offer no status effects. When eaten, they will replenish some of Link's Hearts. Herb Sautés are fragrant mixtures of herbs and spices that have a unique aroma. Different variations of Herb Sautés can be made, depending on the type of Ingredients used: Chilly Herb Sauté: Made by using Cool Safflinas. Eating them grants Link one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Herb Sauté: Made by using Electric Safflinas. If eaten, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance temporarily. Enduring Herb Sauté: Made by using Endura Carrots. These Sautés completely refill and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel when consumed. Hasty Herb Sauté: Made by using Swift Carrots or Swift Violets. Link gains a temporary boost to his movement speed when he eats them. Hearty Herb Sauté: Made by using Hearty Radishes or Big Hearty Radishes. Eating one will completely heal all Link's Hearts and grant him temporary Hearts. Mighty Herb Sauté: Made by using Mighty Thistles. They can be eaten to increase the power of Link's attacks. Sneaky Herb Sauté: Made by using Blue Nightshades or Silent Princesses. When eaten, they increase Link's Stealth for a short period of time. Spicy Herb Sauté: Made by using Warm Safflinas. When eaten, they grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Herb Sauté: Made by using Armoranths. They increase Link's Defense if he eats them. Herb Sautés return in . Due to the addition of Stambulbs, it is now possible to Cook their energizing variety. Other Appearances An Herb Sauté widens the timing window for Perfect Dodging by 5%. It is made using three Warm Safflinas and three Goron Spices.

is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses Hestu's Gift is received from Hestu at the Korok Forest after collecting all 900 Korok Seeds and maxing out all the stashes. It serves no purpose, however, Link can visit Hestu at any time to see him dance. Hestu's Gift returns in , where it is received from Hestu after all collecting all 1,000 Korok Seeds and fully upgrading Link's Inventory. Its sprite has been updated to include four layers instead of 's three. It still has no gameplay function, but it allows Link to visit Hestu at any time to watch him dance. Link can also ask to see Hestu's "classic" dance, wherein Hestu performs the version of his Inventory expansion dance.

is a recurring character in . Biography When Link first encounters a Korok, it will believe that it has been found by Hestu before realizing that it is mistaken. The Korok will then give Link a Korok Seed ask him to return it to Hestu. From this point forward, Koroks will continue to give Link Korok Seeds once he finds them. Initially, Hestu can be found on the road between Kakariko Bridge and Kakariko Village. Hestu is surprised that Link can see him, saying that the last time anyone was able to see him was 100 years ago. He introduces himself and asks Link for assistance. He will tell Link that his Maracas were stolen from him by a group of monsters. Hestu explains that he is powerless without them, and so he asks Link to retrieve them in his stead. This dialogue will trigger "The Priceless Maracas" Side Quest, in which Link will have to retrieve Hestu's Maracas from a Treasure Chest in a nearby Monster Stronghold. If spoken to again, Hestu will ask if he completed the task and hopes the monsters have not been using them. Once Link retrieves Hestu's Maracas, he is overcome with joy and asks for them back. When Link returns them, Hestu can tell something is wrong and realizes that the Korok Seeds inside them are gone. Hestu will then explain that if he had even one Korok Seed, he would be able to sing, dance, and use his powers to expand Link's Inventory. Hestu can upgrade Link's Weapon stash, Bow stash, or Shield stash. Hestu states that the other Koroks must have taken the Seeds, and he is surprised to find that he was the target of such a prank. If Link has Korok Seeds with him, Hestu will be able to smell them. For the first expansion of Link's Inventory, Hestu asks for a single Korok Seed. Should Link refuse, Hestu will respond with a dejected sound. If Link agrees to the trade, Hestu will ask which stash he would like to upgrade. Every time Hestu upgrades a stash, he will sing the tune that plays with it. Hestu will only allow Link two upgrades before announcing that he needs to return to the Korok Forest. Hestu thanks Link for his help and promises to see him off before leaving. Before he leaves, Link can talk to him to learn more about the Koroks. If asked about the Korok Forest, he will recite the directions he was told: follow the Hylia River north. Asking about Hestu himself will have him reintroduce himself and state that he is the most celebrated musician in the Korok Forest. Should Link ask about Korok Seeds, Hestu will hesitate in his explanation before giving an excuse to not continue, saying his voice is blown out. Hestu does travel north, but he becomes lost along the way. While Hestu is lost, Link can find him Riverside Stable, Wetland Stable, and Woodland Stable. During these encounters, Link can

Hestu will hesitate in his explanation before giving an excuse to not continue, saying his voice is blown out. Hestu does travel north, but he becomes lost along the way. While Hestu is lost, Link can find him Riverside Stable, Wetland Stable, and Woodland Stable. During these encounters, Link can obtain four more stash upgrades before Hestu remembers the way back. If Link makes it into the Korok Forest before getting these four upgrades, Hestu will appear there straight away and will no longer appear at any Stables. Once Link has located all 900 Koroks hidden throughout Hyrule Kingdom, he will be instructed to share the news with Hestu. Hestu excitedly informs Link that the Koroks have all returned to Korok Forest. He claims that Link must have had a lot of people helping him search for the Koroks. When Link instead explains that he found them all on his own, Hestu will be impressed. Since Link has already maximized his Inventory, he will be given Hestu's Gift as a reward. Hestu asks Link if he likes his Gift. He invites Link to keep visiting him to watch his dances. are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Hidden Balloons go unnamed in . Overview Hidden Balloons are a variety of Korok Seed Puzzle that can be solved using Archery. They involve singular Balloons, which are located in various hidden spots throughout Hyrule. Link can use a Bow to shoot these Balloons with an Arrow. Whenever he does so, a Korok will appear to grant him a Korok Seed. Like in , Hidden Balloons are Korok Seed Puzzles that take the form of Balloons located in hard-to-reach or hidden places. When Link pops one of these Balloons, a Korok will appear, and he will receive a Korok Seed as a reward.

The is a recurring location in . The High Ground goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The High Ground is a cliff located behind the Village Chief's House in Hateno Village. It is the site of the Village's Ancient Furnace. It also houses many of the Village's crop fields, as well as the Scarecrows that guard them. During the day, Reede tends to one of these fields. After Link has spoken with Kilton for the first time, the Fang and Bone will start to appear on the High Ground during the night. During the "Locked Mementos" Main Quest, Purah will send Link to the High Ground to retrieve the Blue Flame from the Ancient Furnace. After igniting a flammable Weapon with the Blue Flame, Link can light the Blue Flame Pedestals found around the High Ground. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on the High Ground. It is a Natural Hiding Spot, taking the form of a Rock in the large Tree next to Zelkoa Pond. If Link lifts this Rock, a Korok will appear. As a reward for finding it, it gives Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Materials Equipment

, also known as the Materials Shop, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview High Spirits Produce is a General Store located in Kakariko Village. It is run by Trissa, and its products are sourced from within the Village. High Spirits Produce sells the Swift Carrots that have made Kakariko Village famous, which are grown by Trissa's husband Steen. In spite of their popularity, High Spirits Produce is unable to sell Fortified Pumpkins due to the rivalry between Steen and Olkin. When Link enters High Spirits Produce, Trissa will be pleased to receive a customer. If Link makes a purchase, Trissa may claim that the Item will be delicious. Trissa may also state that Steen will also be happy about Link's purchase, or she will claim that they are in the perfect season for fresh produce. Finally, she might also Link to continue shopping for other products. If Link buys the entirety of one product, Trissa will initially be shocked, after which she expresses her gratitude. If Link buys all of the stock in High Spirits Produce, Trissa believes that Steen will be pleased to hear it, but she also claims she needs him to grow more Swift Carrots soon. At 3:00 PM, Steen will visit High Spirits Produce to check in on Trissa. In response, Trissa tells him to stop worrying about her. When Link speaks to her during this time, she says to ignore him and continue shopping. However, she will quietly admit that she enjoys when he visits. If Link has bought everything in High Spirits Produce, Trissa remarks that he does not even notice the General Store is empty. Wares and Pricing Wares and Pricing Other Appearances After the Road to the Ancient Lab Scenario is completed, the "Pumpkin Burglars" Quest will become available in Kakariko Village. Beni, the proprietor of High Spirits Produce, is unable to work due Fortified Pumpkins being stolen from his supplier. Once the Quest is completed, the field will be protected, allowing Beni to return to work. As a result, High Spirits Produce will become available. Once High Spirits Produce is open, Warriors will be able to purchase Materials from Beni. Warriors can also sell their Items to Beni. The prices at High Spirits Produce can be reduced by 10% by completing the "Floria Bridge Protection," "Lighting the Way," "Rebuilding Akkala Bridge," and "Goods on the Move in Hyrule!" Quests. In total, prices can be discounted by 40%. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Highland Stable is a Stable that is located along the Faron Highroad on Fural Plain, which is part of the Faron Grasslands. Padok, Phanna, Perosa, and Blynne are all workers at the Stable. The traveler Suzuna also resides here. As is the case with all Stables, Beedle visits as well; Beedle is found sitting outside the entrance to the Stable, but will retreat inside by the main post while it is raining. In downloadable content pack, the Super Rumor Mill V3 Book can be found atop the table inside, advancing the "EX Ancient Horse Rumors" Side Quest. Phanna can be found tending to Horses and is one of the four Stable hands who will offer to customize Link's Horse, provided it has a sufficiently high enough bond and is not too big. When staying at Highland Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Padok explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Padok offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Padok will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Padok will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. Perosa can be found outside tending to the Horses with Phanna, mumbling to herself. When spoken to, Perosa will complain about the horseback Bokoblins that terrorize the northern road. If Link offers to help with dispatching the monsters, he will begin the "The Horseback Hoodlums" Side Quest. Blynne runs the Obstacle Course Mini-Game from the Stable. He gives Link a Swift Carrot for each run he does where he does not beat his record. If Link completes the course in one minute and thirty seconds, Blynne will give him the Extravagant Bridle. When Link breaks Blynne’s record of one minute and fifteen seconds, Blynne gives him the Extravagant Saddle. When "Captured Memories" is active and Link has already completed "Find the Fairy Fountain", Pikango can be encountered at the Stable. While there, he paints a view Fural Plain. He is happy to meet Link again and offers to identify any of his Pictures. If Link decides to show him a Picture, he will look at the seventh on in the Album, which depicts the Bridge of Hylia from a distance. He declares that the Picture was taken along the northeast shore of Lake Hylia, possibly on Scout's Hill or east of it. While that is all he knows, Pikango encourages Link to go out and search for himself. On a final note, he believes the statues look like a married couple embracing each other, which he finds charming. Link can befriend the Hylian Retriever behind the Highland Stable. Once it has been fed enough times, it will lead him

encourages Link to go out and search for himself. On a final note, he believes the statues look like a married couple embracing each other, which he finds charming. Link can befriend the Hylian Retriever behind the Highland Stable. Once it has been fed enough times, it will lead him to a Treasure Chest buried behind the Stable, which contains a Silver Rupee. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Highland Stable Well is situated on the northern side of Highland Stable in the Faron Grasslands. It has a Ladder that allows Link to Climb into its interior. The Well's underground portion connects to the Komo Shoreline Cave, though this entrance is initially covered by a pile of Hard Sediment. The Highland Stable Well is one of several Wells that Fera can be found in prior to beginning the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?". She rates the Well's Water quality as good and its moss growth as limited, in addition to confirming the presence of Brightcaps. She leaves for the Lookout Landing Well once her Side Quest has started. Materials

Hightail Lizards are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Hightail Lizards are common Lizards that can be encountered in warm and temperate areas throughout Hyrule. They can be found basking on Trees or Rocks, and they can also be startled out of hiding when Grass is cut. They often take a moment to register Link's presence, but they flee quickly once they do. To catch them, Link can chase after them, use Stealth to approach them without being noticed, or stun them with an Arrow or Remote Bomb. Hightail Lizards can be Cooked with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot to make a Hasty Elixir, which will temporarily increase Link's speed when consumed. Cooking them with other ingredients, however, will make Dubious Food. The Kochi Dye Shop will also accept them as ingredients for Brown Dye. Hightail Lizards are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Hightail Lizards can be found throughout the Surface of Hyrule. Hightail Lizards are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances Hightail Lizards are Materials that can be earned during Scenarios and Challenges. The Warriors are able to use them to complete certain Quests. Hightail Lizards appear in .

The is a recurring location in . The Hills of Baumer Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Hills of Baumer Well can be found on the Hills of Baumer, which are part of West Necluda. It is situated among an isolated portion of the Deya Village Ruins. Prior to the Great Calamity, it was part of Deya Village. The Hills of Baumer Well returns in , still within the limits of West Necluda. Link is now able to enter the Well and explore its interior. Initially, the chamber is empty, and there is a pile of Hard Sediment at its center. If Link breaks this Hard Sediment, the chamber will partially flood, creating a pool of Water. The is a recurring location in . The Hilltop High Road goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Hilltop High Road is a winding path that runs from the Tabantha Tundra to Hyrule Ridge, passing through the western edge of Hyrule Field. It starts at Snowfield Stable and follows the edge of the Tanagar Canyon to meet Serenne Stable. The Road continues south through the Breach of Demise, along the southern side of the Seres Scablands, and ends at Tabantha Bridge Stable. From this point, the Westbound Road continues northwest. The travelers Baddek, Nazbi, his Horse Dauntless, and Savelle all follow the entirety of the Hilltop High Road. The Wandering Merchant Yammo also wanders the route with her Donkey, and Beedle may be found along the road near Stables. Other travelers frequent a portion of the Hilltop High Road, such as Baumar, his Horse Bamboo, Ronn, and Kanny. Two of Chabi's camps can be found at along the Hilltop High Road, one being at the fork in the Road between the Breach of Demise and Tabantha Bridge Stable, while the other is between Rowan Plain and Irch Plain. She will be under attack by Bokoblins, and if Link saves her, she will give him Monster Extract as a reward. Near the Seres Scablands, a Sign on the Hilltop High Road warns travelers about bandit attacks and says they can find safety at Tabantha Bridge Stable. Near this Sign, Link can encounter a Traveler claiming to be lost. When Link approaches them, they ask if he knows the way to the Gerudo Desert. If Link says that he does, the Traveler will be relieved, since they were unsure if he would tell them. Alternatively, if Link says that he does not know, the Traveler swears they saw him near the Desert in the past. No matter how Link responds, the Traveler will then identify him. They then reveal that they are a Yiga Footsoldier and will proceed to attack Link. Other Travelers also have a chance to randomly appear along the Hilltop High Road. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Hino is an inhabitant of Hyrule who resides at Dueling Peaks Stable. He is a researcher focused on the phenomenon of the Blood Moon. Each night, he stays up until 3:00 AM in order to observe the moon, at which point he decides to sleep. Should Link reveal that he knows nothing about the Blood Moon, Hino will tell him that in some nights, the moon rises blood-red and, at midnight, revives all monsters that have been defeated thus far. Due to it being a common occurrence, there is not much research into why it happens, but this does not dissuade Hino. However, he admits that he has no idea why this is happening. He asks Link to tells him if he finds any information on what exactly causes the Blood Moon to rise. While he is watching for the moon, Hino will make comments on where it is in the sky if Link approaches him. During the day, Hino asks Link if he is interested in his research. Before the moon rises, he will be awaiting its arrival. While the moon is up, Hino remarks that it is beautiful. After the moon sets for the night, Hino will be disappointed that it is gone. In addition to information on the Blood Moon, Hino is able to tell Link what phase the moon will be in that coming night. On the night of a new moon, Hino says that even though it can't be seen, he is happy to know the moon is there. He comments that the shape of the crescent moon makes him hungry. Hino compares the seven-day moon to a Bow aiming towards the land, which he thinks is beautiful. On the 13th-day moon, Hino anticipates it expanding in the coming nights. When the full moon rises, Hino says it looks as though it could fall at any minute, and he has a hard time taking his eyes off of it. The day after the full moon, Hino remarks that though it is smaller, it is nice in its own way. Similar to the seven-day moon, Hino compares the third-quarter moon to a Bow aiming towards the heavens. The 26th-day moon has a sloping line that Hino considers to be wonderful. Finally, leading up to the Blood Moon, Hino will reveal that he has a feeling something is going to happen. When it is Raining, Hino will flee inside Dueling Peaks Stable. He complains that he is unable to see the moon during this weather, a point which he reiterates if Link asks what phase it will be in that night. During a Blood Moon, Hino will grow agitated and begin to run around Dueling Peaks Stable screaming. If Link talks to him during this time, he may witness him growling, basking in the color of the moon, claiming that his blood is boiling, or reveling in the revival of the monsters. He calms down at 12:30 AM, and when

begin to run around Dueling Peaks Stable screaming. If Link talks to him during this time, he may witness him growling, basking in the color of the moon, claiming that his blood is boiling, or reveling in the revival of the monsters. He calms down at 12:30 AM, and when Link speaks to him during this time, he asks if he was also observing the Blood Moon. Now that the Blood Moon has passed, Hino states that it is time to wait for the next one. Hino is now an adventurer, and can be found trapped in a cage in various Monster Strongholds throughout Hyrule. After being rescued by Link, he'll reward him with various types of Food.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Hinox Guts are dropped by all three varieties of Hinoxes when defeated. As is the case with other Monster Parts, they can be cooked in a Cooking Pot with critters to make Elixirs. They can also be used to make Yellow Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop or exchanged for Mon with Kilton at the Fang and Bone. Hinox Guts are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Hinox Guts are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

The is an Item in . Location and Uses After completing the Side Quests "WANTED: Hinox", "WANTED: Molduga", "WANTED: Stone Talus", "Unknown Huge Silhouette", "Unknown Sky Giant", and "Unknown Three-Headed Monster", Link will be able to talk to Gralens about Hinoxes. If he has defeated all 68 Hinoxes, Gralens will reward him with the Hinox Monster Medal. He explains that it was meant for someone who is capable of fighting every Hinox, but he thought it would be impossible until Link did so. Alternatively, should there be any remaining Hinoxes that Link has not defeated, Gralens will instead tell him how many are left.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Hinox Toenails are Monster Parts that are dropped by all types of Hinoxes when they're killed. They're as thick as a plate of armor and can be cooked with critters in a Cooking Pot to make Elixirs. Alternatively, they can be sold to Kilton at the Fang and Bone for Mon or used as an ingredient for Brown Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop. Each piece of the Fierce Deity Set requires five Hinox Toenails, as well as a dragon scale, to be upgraded to their first tier by a Great Fairy. Like other Monster Parts, they can be used in a Cooking Pot to make Elixirs. They can also be used as an ingredient for Brown Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop or exchanged for Mon at the Fang and Bone. The Fierce Deity Set requires Hinox Teeth in order to be upgraded to its second tier at a Great Fairy Fountain. Hinox Teeth are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

Since they are composed entirely of Courser Bee Honey, there is no default version of Honey Candies, as all results grant the energizing effect. Honey Candies can be sold for 20 to 140 Rupees, depending on how many Courser Bee Honeys were used. When eaten, Energizing Honey Candies will instantly refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel, as well as replenish two to 18 Hearts in his Life Gauge.
