are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Honey Crepes are dishes made by Cooking Fresh Milk, a Bird Egg, Tabantha Wheat, Cane Sugar, and Courser Bee Honey together in a Cooking Pot. They can be eaten to refill two fifths of Link's Stamina Wheel and restore ten Hearts of his Life Gauge. The Courser Bee Honey drizzled over them brings out their natural sweetness and flavor. Since five ingredients are necessary to make Honey Crepes, only their energizing version can be made. Honey Crepes return in with an identical Recipe. They can be made in either a Cooking Pot or a Portable Pot. Other Appearances Honey Crepes appear in as an unlockable Recipe. The Recipe is unlocked after completing the Scenario "The Great Plateau". Like in and , they are made with Cane Sugar, a Bird Egg, Courser Bee Honey, Tabantha Wheat, and Fresh Milk. If made, Warriors will earn 30% more Rupees in the battle.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Honeyed Apples are a Meal that can be made by Cooking Courser Bee Honey together with Apples. Their regular version can only be made by adding a Fruit or Vegetable to the recipe that has a differing effect than the Courser Bee Honey. They restore six of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge, but they can also be sold for 40 Rupees. These dishes are noted to be a juicy combination of sweet and sour flavors, since they combine newly ripened Apples with Honey. In Kakariko Village, after completing Koko's first three Side Quests, she will decide to make Honeyed Apples for dessert. Her mother loved them, and she notes how they melt in one's mouth. However, when going over the ingredients, she realizes she is missing Courser Bee Honey. This activates the Side Quest "Koko's Specialty". If Link returns with Courser Bee Honey for Koko, she will be ecstatic and thank Link, asking him to wait while she makes dessert. When the Honeyed Apple is made, Koko becomes emotional after remembering how her mother used to always make it for her. She thanks Link, rewarding him with a Honeyed Apple. There is one variation of Honeyed Apples: Energizing Honeyed Apple: Made using only Apples and Courser Bee Honey. When eaten, they will instantly refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. They heal five Hearts and sell for 30 Rupees.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Honeyed Fruits are dishes made by Cooking Courser Bee Honey with any Fruit, aside from Apples, in a Cooking Pot. The regular version can be made by using Fruits with an effect that counteracts that of the Courser Bee Honey. When eaten, they will restore some Hearts to Link's Life Gauge. This Meal combines the sweetness of Courser Bee Honey with the sourness of Fruits. Only one variation of Honeyed Fruits can be made: Energizing Honeyed Fruits: Made by using neutral Fruits, such as Palm Fruits or Wildberries. Eating them will refill a part of Link's Stamina Wheel. Other Appearances Honeyed Fruits boost the amount of Rupees the Warrior gains by 30% when prepared before a Scenario or Challenge. They are made using two Hearty Durians, two Hydromelons, two Voltfruits, and two Courser Bee Honeys. However, it can be lowered to one of each ingredient through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". The recipe can be earned by completing the Quest "Bee Very Careful".

The is a recurring character in . Biography The Horned Statue is found along the path to Firly Pond in Hateno Village. Link can speak to Teebo to be guided to the Horned Statue's exact location, though Teebo has no knowledge of what the Statue is meant for. If Link prays to the Horned Statue, he will note that there are still people who pay him homage. When Link reacts with shock, the Horned Statue is surprised that he is able to be heard. If Link denies hearing his voice, the Horned Statue says he makes bargains with those who can hear him. He asks Link if he was praying for a long life or wealth, promising that he can grant these requests. The Horned Statue explains that he was once a person who made bargains by trading people's Essences. The Goddess, Hylia, disapproved of his heinous dealings and smote him by trapping him inside the Horned Statue. Since then, he has been neglected by the residents of Hateno Village. Despite this, the spirit of the Horned Statue remained headstrong and chose to bide his time waiting for another person to make a deal with him. He asks Link if he would like to strike a bargain. Without waiting for an answer, he steals either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel from him. This initiates "The Statue's Bargain" Side Quest, tasking Link with the responsibility of recovering his stolen Essence. In speaking to the Horned Statue once again, he at first pretends not to understand why Link is upset. When Link demands his stolen Essence back, the Horned Statue is offended that Link believes he was deceived. He promises Link that they will have a profitable relationship, and he explains that for a price, he will give him either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. When Link chooses which one to receive, the Horned Statue tells him to stay still as he returns his Essence to him. Afterwards, the Horned Statue notices that Link is skeptical, and he explains that he sees money and life as the same thing.He explains that Link can sell either of his Essences to him for 100 Rupees and buy it back for 120 Rupees. However, he allows Link to choose whether he receives a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. Link can begin this process by praying to the Horned Statue again. After this, the Side Quest will be completed. When Link approaches the Horned Statue, he asks if he has come to tamper with his Essences. If the Horned Statue is not currently holding any Essences, he will ask Link if he is willing to sell them. The Horned Statue will only take the Essence that Link asks him to. Through this process, Link is able to transfer the upgrades that he has received from Goddess Statues from Heart Containers to Stamina Vessels, or vice versa. If Link attempts to sell his Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels beyond their default limitations

only take the Essence that Link asks him to. Through this process, Link is able to transfer the upgrades that he has received from Goddess Statues from Heart Containers to Stamina Vessels, or vice versa. If Link attempts to sell his Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels beyond their default limitations (3 Hearts and 1 full Stamina Wheel), the Horned Statue will reject his request. Additionally, if Link tries to speak to the Horned Statue before he has received any blessings from Hylia, he will be turned away and instructed to return with something to trade. The Horned Statue reappears in . He can be found in the Royal Hidden Passage.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Horon Lagoon is located in the Lanayru Sea. It is bordered by Brynna Plain to the west and Lodrum Headland and Talus Plateau to the east. Many rocky outcroppings can be found throughout the Water of the Lagoon, three of which are particularly large. The northernmost outcropping bears a Pedestal. The central outcropping contains many bombable walls, as well as small tidepool with Crabs and Luminous Stone Deposits. On Horon Lagoon's eastern beach, there is an abandoned campsite. Horon Lagoon is the subject of an "Ancient Song," which prompts Kass to travel to the area. Link can find Kass on the Lagoon's western shore. When spoken to, Kass will offer to play the "Ancient Song" associated with Horon Lagoon for him, which describes breaking the bombable walls in order to glide onto the Pedestal. Listening to it begins the "Master of the Wind" Shrine Quest. When Link destroys the bombable walls on the Lagoon's central outcropping, Wind will begin to flow through it towards the northern outcropping. If he uses the Paraglider to ride the Wind and land on the Pedestal, Shai Yota Shrine will emerge from the ground nearby. One Treasure Chest is located on Horon Lagoon. It is made of metal, and it is submerged in one of the tidepools in the southernmost outcropping. Link can pull it to the surface using the Magnesis Rune, and when he opens it, he will receive a Ruby. left|40px There is a single Korok Seed Puzzle on Horon Lagoon. To the east of the central outcropping, Link will find a stone Circle. On top of the outcropping, there are several Rocks that must be thrown into the Circle. When this is successfully done, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

The Horriblin Mask is an Item in . Location and Uses The Horriblin Mask is a piece of Armor that can be obtained from Koltin's Stall for four Bubbul Gems after trading a total of 25 Bubbul Gems for the prior rewards. Subsequent Horriblin Masks can be purchased from Cece for 4,000 Rupees. When worn, the Horriblin Mask grants Link the Disguise Added Effect, allowing him to blend in with Horriblins. However, the Horriblin Mask does not prevent other Enemies in the same area from attacking Link. It also makes quiet Horriblin sounds as Link moves around. While wearing the Horriblin Mask, Link adopts a new idle pose to match that of a Horriblin.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link arrives in New Serenne Stable, Zumi stands in front of it and talks about her latest investment, a horse-drawn wagon. Unfortunately, she isn't able to use it, as two wheels and a carthorse are missing. If Link uses the Fuse-ability the attach one of the scattered wheels to the wagon, she realised he is helping, but points out, that two wheels are necessary. After attaching another wheel, the cart is able to roll and Zumi overjoyed. Now the only missing objective is a suitable carthorse. Zumi earlier told Link that there are lots of wild horses around, but in order to catch them, one has to sneak up on them and after catching one, it needs to be soothed. Link sets out to catch a wild horse. He is not able to give one of his own to her, since she won't react to them. After catching and soothing a wild Horse, he gifts it to her. She is thankful and explains that a harness is required for a horse to pull a wagon and uses one to attach the horse to the cart. To show her gratefulness she give Link 100 Rupees, names the wagon "Zunk" - a combination of hers and his name - and shares her knowledge of horses with him on later visits. Objectives

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Horwell Bridge is a wooden bridge that spans the Hylia River between Hyrule Field and West Necluda. It is connected by roads to Eagus Bridge and Owlan Bridge. During the Great Calamity 100 years prior to , any survivors from Mabe Village and the nearby Ranch would have used Horwell Bridge to evacuate to Necluda. The travelers Endai, Kazul, and Spoone will also occasionally cross the Horwell Bridge on their way between Riverside Stable and Wetland Stable. Another traveler, Leekah, can be found being attacked by Bokoblin at the Bridge. If Link rescues her, she will give him a Meal or Rupees as a reward. Creature Enemies Treasure Chests

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Hot-Footed Frogs are a type of Frog that can be located near bodies of Water, either Swimming or hopping along the bank. Link can Crouch to sneak up and catch them, or alternatively, he can quickly Spring to capture them before they startle and disappear. Otherwise, Hot-Footed Frogs will run away once they spot him. They can be Cooked alongside Monster Parts to create Hasty Elixirs. The Kochi Dye Shop also accepts them as an ingredient for Green Dye. A Hot-Footed Frog appears in the ninth Recovered Memory, "Silent Princess", wherein Zelda captures one to show Link. She excitedly shares that it is a delicacy known to have potent effects. She then states that Hyrule Castle's research shows that eating one can enhance certain abilities, going on to add that while they are not in a controlled environment, Link's high level of physical fitness would make him perfect for the study. She presses him to taste it, to which Link reacts poorly. Hot-Footed Frogs are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Like in , Hot-Footed Frogs can be found in and around various bodies of Water. Other Appearances Hot-Footed Frogs are Materials that the Warriors can obtain during Scenarios and Challenges. Certain Quests require that they be supplied in order to be completed. Hot-Footed Frogs appear in .

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Hot Buttered Apples are made by Cooking an Apple and Goat Butter together in a Cooking Pot. When eaten, they will heal several of Link's Hearts. The sweetness of the Apple has been enhanced by smothering it with Goat Butter and baking it. During the Side Quest "Cooking with Koko", Koko decides to make Hot Buttered Apples, since her mother used to make them and her sister Cottla loves them. However, she realizes that she has run out of Goat Butter, and therefore cannot make the Meal. When Link brings her Goat Butter, Koko will be excited, thanking him and making sure he means it. She then makes a Hot Buttered Apple, which she gives to Link as a reward. Additional Ingredients can be added when making Hot Buttered Apples, which can result in one of the following variations: Chilly Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding cold Ingredients. If eaten, Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding electric Ingredients. They grant Link one level of Shock Resistance when eaten. Enduring Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding enduring Ingredients. They completely refill and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel when consumed. Energizing Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding energizing Ingredients. If eaten, they will replenish a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding hasty Ingredients. When eaten, they temporarily increase Link's speed. Hearty Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding hearty Ingredients. Eating them will heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him temporary Hearts. Mighty Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding mighty Ingredients. Link gains a boost to the power of his attacks when he eats these apples. Sneaky Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding sneaky Ingredients. When eaten, they grant Link a boost to his Stealth temporarily. Spicy Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding spicy Ingredients. Eating these apples will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Hot Buttered Apple: Made by adding tough Ingredients. They can be eaten to increase Link's Defense for a short period of time. A Tattered Notebook written by Cottla's mother can be found in the Secret Base, providing instructions on how to Cook the family's favorite Foods. Inside, Cottla's mother noted that her daughter had a particular fondness for Hot Buttered Apples and listed the Ingredients used to make them.

are recurring locations and Objects in . Features and Overview In , three Hot Springs can be found. The first one is located in the Goron Graveyard. After obtaining the Goron Mask, Link can pull Darmani III's grave to reveal the spring. Link can use an empty Bottle to scoop some Hot Spring Water and unfreeze one of the Gorons outside the graveyard, the Goron Elder, and the entrance to the second Hot Spring. The second one is located inside a Secret Grotto in the second of the Twin Islands. The last spring can be found Beneath the Well in Ikana Canyon. It is protected by a Dexihand and can be used to get some Hot Spring Water for one of the Gibdos inside. In , there is a Hot Spring in Kakariko Village known as the Kakariko Hot Spring and another one in Death Mountain. The Kakariko Hot Spring is located atop the Elde Inn and is merely a small pond. Link can only reach it via the Elde Inn. The Hot Spring from Death Mountain is a popular spot for Gorons. There is also a Goron Store located in the far end of the Hot Spring. Link is able to scoop Hot Springwater from them using an Empty Bottle. He can also recover his Hearts by standing in Hot Springs. In , a number of Hot Springs can be found across the Eldin Region and the Hebra Mountains. The Spring's warm waters will gradually replenish Link's Hearts at a rate of half a Heart every two seconds, so long as he is at least waist-deep in the water. A number of Hot Springs in Eldin are named, including Gero Pond, the Goron Hot Springs, Lake Ferona, and Lake Intenoch. Unnamed Hot Springs can also be found around the region. The various Hot Springs in Hebra are all named, including Goflam's Secret Hot Spring, Sherfin's Secret Hot Spring and Sturnida Secret Hot Spring. There is also an isolated unnamed Hot Spring in West Necluda just south-southwest of Mount Rozudo, and another located beneath Hyrule Castle. Link can also make Hard-Boiled Eggs by throwing Bird Eggs into Hot Springs. List of Hot Springs Hot Springs appear atop the Eldin Volcano.

is an Added Effect in . Overview Hot Weather Attack is an Added Effect that, when in Extremely Hot Zones or Scorching Climates, causes Link's charge attacks and combo finishers to generate a Fire-based area of effect. In addition to the damage the Enemy will receive by default from the element, the area of effect has a bonus attack power of five, which can be increased by the Attack Up Effect. Level two increases the size of the area of effect by 50% for combo finishers and 33% for charge attacks, while level three increases the size of the area of effect by 100% for combo finishers and 66% for charge attacks. Level three is the maximum possible potency for this Effect. The following Materials and Armor pieces grant Hot Weather Attack:

is a recurring Inn in . Features and Overview Hotel Oasis is an Inn located within Gerudo Town. Its owner, Romah, works behind the Inn's counter, while Olu attempts to attract customers from the street. In addition to regular Inn services, the Hotel features a unique Spa Plan, which is so popular throughout that there is typically a line leading outside the Inn. The Hylian traveler, Tauma, stays at the Inn, where she can be found waiting for her own Spa Plan. While staying in Gerudo Town, Malena will also Sleep in one of the Hotel's Beds during the night. Hotel Oasis offers a regular stay for 20 Rupees, though Link can add the Spa Plan to his stay for a cost of 80 Rupees. When Link first enters the Hotel Oasis, Romah will allow him to cut to the front of the Spa Plan line, claiming to sense something special about him. If Link decides on the Hotel's standard plan, Romah will be disappointed, but she still allows him to choose when he wants to be woken up. Once Link makes his selection, Romah will send him off to sleep. When Link wakes up, Romah will greet him, but she also warns him of how dangerous the Gerudo Desert can be. If Link chooses the Hotel Oasis's Spa Plan, Romah will become excited, asking when he would like to wake up. While performing Link's Spa Plan, Romah may note that Link has a masculine figure for a Hylian. She might also state that he has an unusual amount of scars for a Hylian woman, reasoning that he must be a warrior. When Link wakes up, he will receive Extra Stamina and three Extra Hearts. Romah claims that he appears relaxed, though she still warns him about the dangers of the Gerudo Desert. By speaking to Tauma afterwards, she states that his skin is shiny and that he appears carefree. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been appeased, Romah hopes that Hotel Oasis's business will increase as a result.

are Items in . Location and Uses Hover Stones are Zonai Devices that resemble square-shaped platforms. When activated they levitate in the air without any need for external support as long as they are powered and are resistant to any force save for Ultrahand, allowing Link to use them as stable footholds or as anchors for other Zonai Devices. They can be obtained from Device Dispensers, but can also be found inside Shrines of Light and around the Water Temple. The Zonai are theorized to have used these Devices to create the Sky Islands. The Yiga utilize Hover Stones to create devices that defend their Relay Bases.

is a recurring character in . Biography Hoz is a soldier who works to fend off monsters from East Akkala Stable in the Akkala Highlands. He carries a Soldier's Spear and wears a Soldier's Helm. He patrols the Stable throughout the day and night. If it begins to rain, he will flee inside. If Link agrees that it has become dangerous in the area, Hoz shares a rumor he has heard of a suspicious individual known as Kilton. The rumors say that he runs a shop called Fang and Bone, which he operates during the night. Kilton's behavior has reportedly been making people uncomfortable. Hoz asks Link if he knows Kilton. If Link replies that he does not, Hoz will be disappointed. Alternatively, if Link says that he does, Hoz is shocked that he is aware of him. Despite Link's answer, Hoz asks him for a detailed description of any suspicious people that he encounters, especially if he meets Kilton. This begins the Side Quest "A Shady Customer". Once Link has taken a Picture of Kilton, he can return to the East Akkala Stable to show it to Hoz. Though he thinks the Picture is strange, Hoz believes it will help him track Kilton down. As a reward, he gives Link a Silver Rupee. He bids Link farewell so that he can return to his mission. After completing the Side Quest, Link can continue to speak to Kilton. Now that he has seen Kilton, he wonders what he sells at the Fang and Bone. He believes it could be fangs, bones, or "evil things", but thinking about it creeps him out. Hoz became a captain of his own Monster-Control Crew squad, and he continues to wear a Soldier's Helm. After Princess Zelda and Link disappeared at the start of the Upheaval, Hoz and his squad were dispatched to Hyrule Castle by Purah to search for them. Initially, Hoz can be found on top of the First Gatehouse alongside Toren, from where he is directing the search. At first, Hoz attempts to dismiss Link, but he is relieved when he realizes he is speaking to Link and assumes that Zelda is also safe. If Link has not yet met with Purah, Hoz is confused by Link's story, and he tells him to find Purah while they continue to search for Zelda. When Link approaches Hoz during the "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" Main Quest, he is still confused by Link's explanation, but he decides it is more important to continue searching for Zelda. Due to how overwhelming the amount Gloom surrounding Hyrule Castle has been, Hoz is relieved to have help. Their conversation is interrupted by Toren, who spots a figure resembling Zelda. Hoz is happy to see she is safe, but he is confused when she begins to float in the air and disappears into Light. Declaring that they are now in an emergency situation, Hoz sends Link back to Purah while he withdraws the Monster-Control Crew, since it will take

Zelda. Hoz is happy to see she is safe, but he is confused when she begins to float in the air and disappears into Light. Declaring that they are now in an emergency situation, Hoz sends Link back to Purah while he withdraws the Monster-Control Crew, since it will take them some time. Link can meet him again south of the Hyrule Garrison Ruins where Hoz leads his squad in an attack on a Monster Stronghold. Squad one then heads southeast on towards Fort Hateno in Necluda.

is a recurring character in . Biography Huck can first be found talking with Verla about Divine Beast Vah Medoh outside The Slippery Falcon in Rito Village. He tells Link that Revali, the Champion of the Rito, once tamed Vah Medoh and used it to protect Rito Village. He continues, saying that all males from the Rito tribe are encouraged to be formidable warriors like Revali, though he considers this expectation is nearly impossible. Huck can later be found outside of Rito Village's Armor Shop, the Brazen Beak, advertising the products inside. He advises Link to purchase the Snowquill Set if he wishes to head to the Hebra Mountains or go to any elevation higher than Rito Village. When asked about the Brazen Beak, he pitches their gear, which is made from Rito plumage. He quickly adds that the feathers used in the Armor are not simply taken from Rito and glued to shirts, rather they are crafted from the soft, molted feathers from baby Rito as they mature. If Link agrees to buy his clothing, Huck becomes excited and invites Link to enter the store. After the Upheaval, Huck investigates the Blizzard that forms over the Hebra Mountains. Upon spotting Link there, he remarks that he did not expect to find a Hylian. To find its cause, he wants to find a higher vantage point, but cannot fly due to strong gales.

is a recurring character in . Biography Hudson is a carpenter who works for Bolson Construction, a company situated in Hateno Village in East Necluda. He can initially be found attempting to demolish Link's House under Bolson's orders. When Link asks why he is doing so, Hudson explains that the building has been abandoned since its owner left town, though he does not know the reason they had for leaving. Once Hudson confirms that he has answered all of Link's questions, he reveals that Hateno Village is finally recovering in the wake of the Great Calamity. He wishes both himself and Link luck in the future. If Link offers to buy the House, Hudson will direct him to Bolson instead. Once Link and Bolson strike a deal on the House, Hudson will take a break underneath a Tree nearby. There, he mentions that Link would be a great hire for Bolson Construction, but retracts the offer upon learning that his name does not end in "-son." According to Hudson, Bolson maintains this hiring requirement for team unity. After Link pays for his House, Bolson mentions that he has plans to send Hudson to Akkala. He advises Link to speak to Hudson before he leaves. When Link approaches Hudson, he will explains that he is leaving to work on expansions for Bolson Construction. He decides to leave after Link wishes him luck, and he invites him to visit in the future. This begins the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest. Hudson can be found again on an island in Lake Akkala. As Link does not recognize him, Hudson will reintroduce himself. He has decided to create a village in Akkala called Tarrey Town. However, Hudson is lacking in supplies to make a town. Link can offer to retrieve supplies for Hudson, who is confused as to why he would help. When Link insists, Hudson will accept his offer. He asks Link to bring him 10 bundles of Wood. Once Link has enough bundles of Wood, he can return to give them to Hudson. Hudson then complains that he is having difficulty clearing out the boulders on the island, and he asks Link if he could find someone with brute physical strength, like a Goron, to assist. He also requests that this individual's name ends in "-son" in accordance with Bolson Construction policy. After Link recruits Greyson and Pelison, Hudson will be pleased that they meet his requirements. He also informs Link that Pelison set up a Jewelry Shop called Ore and More. For his next request, he asks that Link bring him 20 bundles of Wood. When Link makes this delivery, Hudson notes that his clothes have become worn, so he tells Link to find a tailor. He suggests looking among the Gerudo for such an individual. Like before, he also wants this person's name to end in "-son." When Rhondson arrives in Tarrey Town, Hudson thanks Link for finding her. Hudson approves of her name, and since she was able

tells Link to find a tailor. He suggests looking among the Gerudo for such an individual. Like before, he also wants this person's name to end in "-son." When Rhondson arrives in Tarrey Town, Hudson thanks Link for finding her. Hudson approves of her name, and since she was able to patch up his clothes, he is enamored with her. She also opened an Armor Shop, the Rhondson Armor Boutique, which Hudson encourages Link to visit. Next, he asks Link to bring him 30 bundles of Wood. After this delivery, Hudson informs Link that they need someone to set up a General Store in town. When Link reasons that they need a traveling trader, Hudson suggests looking among the Rito for someone who qualifies. As has been the case before, Hudson reminds Link that this individual needs to have a name that ends in "-son." Once Fyson lands in Tarrey Town, Hudson will inform Link that he has already established the Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch). He is content with Fyson's name, and he tells Link to check out the General Store. Before people can start moving in, Hudson needs 50 bundles of Wood so he can make more houses. When Link brings the Wood to Hudson, he admits that he has something personal to tell him. Link expresses his concern, so Hudson clarifies that he has gotten engaged to Rhondson. He asks Link to find someone priest-like for his wedding, explaining that such an individual might be found among the Zora. He also wants this person's name to end in "-son." After Kapson arrives in Tarrey Town, Hudson will approve of both his occupation and his name. Before the wedding can begin, Hudson requests that Link invite Bolson and Karson to attend the ceremony. Once they are in attendance, Hudson and Rhondson will be ready to move forward with their wedding. As Kapson begins the ceremony, he asks Hudson if he will take Rhondson to be his wife, which he accepts. He asks the same thing of Rhondson, with the added stipulation that they name their children in accordance with the Bolson Construction naming policies. When Rhondson objects that these are not traditional vows, Hudson will be confused. He begs Rhondson to think of their future descendants, and so she agrees. Kapson then declares the couple to be married. After the ceremony, Hudson will thank Link for attending. He proclaims that Link has helped make Tarrey Town into a real town, and so he gives him three Diamonds as a token of his appreciation. He explains that they were found while clearing away the rocks, and he and Rhondson have no use for them. If Link approaches Hudson later, he will recognize him. He explains that he and Rhondson are very happy to be in Tarrey Town. However, he asks Link if there is something important he should be doing instead. If Link confirms that there is, Hudson encourages him to get to it, as there are many other

he will recognize him. He explains that he and Rhondson are very happy to be in Tarrey Town. However, he asks Link if there is something important he should be doing instead. If Link confirms that there is, Hudson encourages him to get to it, as there are many other people in the world that need his help. If Link denies needing to be anywhere else, Hudson invites him to stay as long as he would like.

is a recurring character in . Biography Hunnie is a young Hylian girl who lives with her parents, Hagie and Ruli. After Link completes the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, she and her family will move to Tarrey Town together, as they believe it could improve her health. While Hunnie has started to improve, her parents have had difficulty finding something that she will eat, which leaves her stuck in bed most days. When Link speaks to Hunnie while she is weak, she will excitedly greet him and ask if he is a traveler. When Link confirms that he is, she then asks if it is fun. If Link tells her that it is, Hunnie reveals that she wants to travel on her own when she grows up. After this initial encounter, Hunnie will ask Link to tell her a story if he approaches her. When Link asks how she is feeling, Hunnie will respond that she is fine. If Link asks Hunnie what she likes to eat, she reveals that while she hates most Foods, she will eat cake if he offers some to her. If Link asks if she has heard of the Great Calamity, she becomes annoyed and calls it boring. When Link leaves her, she tells him that she does not want him to be there anyway. At night, Link can listen in on Ruli and Hagie discussing Hunnie through an open window. Hagie recounts that they have looked all over the world for a cake that Hunnie could eat, but they have yet to find anything so far. Ruli declares that she would sell her soul to a monster if it meant finding a cake to cure Hunnie. This activates the "A Parent's Love" Side Quest. To complete the Side Quest, Link needs to bring a Monster Cake to Ruli. She gives the cake to Hunnie right away, after which Hunnie can be seen running through her front door. Ruli reveals that she ate the entire Monster Cake and that she is finally healthy again. As a reward, she gives Link a Gold Rupee. Once she has regained her energy, Hunnie wakes up at 8:00 AM every day. She immediately runs outside and sits with Hagie on the cliff overlooking the Torin Wetland. At 8:00 PM, she gets up and slowly walks back to her house with her father, and she goes to sleep at around 9:00 PM.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Hunter's Shields are wooden Shields similar to the Emblazoned Shield and Fisherman's Shield. They are favored by hunters for their rabbit designs, which are said to bring luck. Hunter's Shields, like Wooden Shields, have low defensive power, but they are known to be easy to use. There are three places to find Hunter's Shields. One is in a Treasure Chest near a lake below Lanayru Tower. There is another in the east side of the North Lomei Labyrinth, and it will respawn after some time. Finally, Selmie gives one out as a reward for completing the Shield-Surfing Mini-Game in between 3:15 and 3:30. Female Hylian travelers are known to wield them as well, allowing Link to take a Picture of them for the Hyrule Compendium. Hunter's Shields are made of wood, and they will therefore burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will float if they are dropped in Water, and they will not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms like metal Shields do. Finally, they cannot be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. Hunter's Shield reappears in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Hydrants are a type of Zonai Device capable of generating an endless supply of Water when active. As a result, they can be used to wash away Sludge. They were supposedly used to save the Sky Islands from a drought in the distant past. Other Appearances Hydrants can be obtained from a Treasure Chest that appears upon defeating the Sludge Like in the Scenario "Lanayru Defiled". They have an attack power of 45. When they are activated, they supply an infinite amount of Water in front of the Warrior holding them, expending Energy as it does so. Hydrants are effective when used against Enemies covered in Sludge and Fire-related Enemies.

are recurring Items in . Locations and Uses Hydromelons are found growing from vines in the Gerudo Desert, as well as on certain parts of Satori Mountain. They are also available being sold by Emri at Kara Kara Bazaar and Lorn's Fruit Stand in Gerudo Town. They can be used by Link to restore half of a Heart. When Hydromelons are cooked into food, it will give Link Heat Resistance when eaten. If a Hydromelon comes into contact with Fire, it will turn into Roasted Hydromelon, which restores three-quarters of a Heart. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Hydromelons can be used to make Green Dye. Hydromelons are not required to upgrade any pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. Hydromelons are required to make Creamy Heart Soup in a Cooking Pot: They can also be used in regular Fruit-based Meals: Hydromelons are similar to their versions, and are still not used to upgrade any Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. Hydromelons are required to make Creamy Heart Soups and Noble Pursuits. They can also be used in regular Fruit-based Meals: Other Appearances

is a location in . Features and Overview The Hylia Canyon Mine is an ancient Zonai Mine in the Depths, situated far below Mount Hylia on the Surface. It features Mine Cart Tracks that pass through its southern part, connecting to sister sites in the northwest and east. These sites are located directly beneath the Great Plateau West Chasm and the Great Plateau South Chasm, respectively. A supply station with Zonai Devices can be found along the tracks here. Though it is abandoned, there are still several Zonaite Deposits littered throughout the Mine, including those in the form of Hard Sediment deposits. Enemies Materials Equipment Zonai Devices Treasure Chests

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Hylia Island is a large landform partially submerged by Water in the western part of Lake Hylia. In total, 11 points can be seen peeking out of the Lake. The central point is the largest and is surrounded by 10 smaller ones. The Ya Naga Shrine can be found in the crater of the central point, and a Raft can be seen tied to the dock on the western side of the central point. A Zora named Mei can be found catching Fish on one of the eastern points of the Island before the Side Quest "A Wife Washed Away" is completed. Two metallic Treasure Chests, each containing a Purple Rupee, can be found set in the ground on the northernmost and southernmost points of Hylia Island. A third metallic Treasure Chest containing a Phrenic Bow can be found in the water on the eastern side Hylia Island. A fourth metallic Treasure Chest containing a bundle of five Shock Arrows can be found in the water north of the aforementioned Chest. A fifth metallic Treasure Chest containing a Knight's Halberd can be found in the water nestled between the two westernmost points of the Island. A Korok can be found atop a Tree on the northwestern part of Island, who will give Link a Korok Seed in return for finding him. Areas Creatures Enemies Areas Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Hylia River runs between Hyrule Field, the Lanayru Wetlands, and West Necluda. It begins on the east side of the Hyrule Castle Moat near Boneyard Bridge, and it flows into Nabi Lake and the Squabble River. It ends as a Waterfall that pours its contents into Lake Hylia. Orsedd Bridge, Rebonae Bridge, Eagus Bridge, Horwell Bridge, Owlan Bridge, and Proxim Bridge all span portions of Hylia River. The Floret Sandbar is also located within the River. At Wetland Stable, Link can find Izra staring into the Water of Hylia River. When spoken to, he explains that there is a Metal Chest at the bottom of the River, but he has no way to retrieve it. Hearing this initiates the Side Quest "Riverbed Reward". Using the Magnesis Rune, Link can pull the Chest from the Water to receive a Knight's Broadsword. Several Treasure Chests are located within Hylia River. Metal Chests can be pulled out of the Water using the Magnesis Rune, while wooden Chests can be lifted using Cryonis. In total, these Treasure Chests contain four Purple Rupees, three Ambers, three Opals, one Traveler's Sword, one Soldier's Claymore, ten Fire Arrows, and five Shock Arrows. In Master Mode, a Knight's Halberd can be found in a Treasure Chest at the end of the River. Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds Hylia River reappears in . Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Zonai Devices Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Hylian Hood is a piece of Armor that can be purchased at the Ventest Clothing Boutique in Hateno Village or Enchanted in Kakariko Village. According to its description, it is made from a sturdy material to protect travelers from the harsh sun and weather. It can be enhanced by a Great Fairy and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Hylian Hood, alongside the Hylian Tunic and Hylian Trousers, compose the Hylian Armor Series. Dye Options Enhancing The Hylian Hood can be purchased from Mubs's Armor Shop at Lookout Landing. After the mayoral election in Hateno Village, Link can speak to Cece to customize the Hylian Hood by wearing it down. Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances Dye Options

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Hylian Rice can be found by cutting grass in East Necluda. It is also sold by establishments like the Coral Reef, the East Wind, the General Shoppe, and The Slippery Falcon and the travelling merchant Yammo. Eating it restores one of Link's Hearts. After completing the Side Quest "Curry for What Ails You", Link can give Lester Goron Spice at any time to receive Hylian Rice. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Hylian Rice can be used to make White Dye. When Cooking in a Cooking Pot, Hylian Rice is required to make Crab Risotto, a Crab Omelet with Rice, Curry Pilaf, Curry Rice, Fried Egg and Rice, a Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl, Gourmet Meat Curry, Gourmet Poultry Curry, Gourmet Poultry Pilaf, a Meat and Rice Bowl, Meat Curry, Meaty Rice Balls, Monster Curry, Monster Rice Balls, Mushroom Rice Balls, Mushroom Risotto, Poultry Curry, Poultry Pilaf, a Prime Meat and Rice Bowl, Prime Meat Curry, Prime Poultry Curry, Prime Poultry Pilaf, Salmon Risotto, Seafood Curry, Seafood Fried Rice, Seafood Paella, Seafood Rice Balls, Vegetable Curry, Vegetable Risotto, and Veggie Rice Balls. Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . The Hylian Shield goes unnamed in the Zelda HD Experience and . Location and Uses It is the traditional Shield bore by the Knights of Hyrule and is commonly used by Link in 3D Zelda games alongside the Master Sword. Unlike Wooden Shields, the Hylian Shield will not burn upon contact with fire. Though it is made of steel, it is light and sturdy, an optimal weight for a fighter with a one-handed weapon. Throughout the Zelda games, the Hylian Shield has changed little in terms of overall appearance, always bearing the symbol of the Triforce and, beneath it, a red Hylian Crest representing the goddess Hylia and the Crimson Loftwing that helped Link at the founding of Hyrule. The first Hylian Shield was a legendary Shield guarded by the Thunder Dragon Lanayru, who created the Lightning Round to judge whether someone would be worthy of wielding the Shield. While the Hylian Shield did not appear in the original or DX versions of , the Shield was given the appearance of the Hylian Shield in . It it received from Tarin after Link wakes up on Koholint Island. The Hylian Shield can either be purchased or found by Link as a child in . Emblazoned with Hylian artwork, complete with a Crimson Loftwing and the Triforce, the Hylian Shield is much too large for young Link to wield on his arm and functions more like a turtle's shell. After his seven year sleep, Link became able to use it as his standard Shield. The Hylian Shield becomes almost necessary to survive a visit to the Great Fairy in Death Mountain, as child Link's 'turtle shell' use of the Shield protects from recurrent flaming rock eruptions. It is also not prone to the risk of being burnt by particular fire-borne enemies, such as the Fire Keese. However, the Hylian Shield can be consumed by the Shield-eating Like Likes if Link is swallowed by one. Child Link's use of the Shield limits mobility while defending and does not provide as much adequate protection from the front as the Deku Shield (and the Hylian Shield as an adult) and is similarly unable to reflect Deku Scrub and Octorok attacks, but it can defend Link from the Boulders that rain from Death Mountain. The guard at the gates of Kakariko Village (leading to Death Mountain) can offer Link a discount in correspondence with the owner of the Bazaar in Hyrule Castle Town. If Link speaks to the guard and then attempts to purchase the Hylian Shield at normal price at the Bazaar in the Market, the shop owner will give Link a discount of random values in intervals of 5 Rupees between a total price of 45 to 75 Rupees. However, the Shield cannot be bought even with the discount if Link does not have 80 Rupees. Despite the discount, a free Hylian Shield can be found if Link opens a certain grave at night in the Kakariko Village

5 Rupees between a total price of 45 to 75 Rupees. However, the Shield cannot be bought even with the discount if Link does not have 80 Rupees. Despite the discount, a free Hylian Shield can be found if Link opens a certain grave at night in the Kakariko Village Graveyard. In , the Hylian Shield becomes available before entering the Goron Mines in the newly established Malo Mart in Kakariko Village for 200 Rupees. It can also be bought (for a slightly higher price of 210 Rupees) from a Goron in Hyrule Castle Town. Unlike the Wooden Shield and Ordon Shield, the Hylian Shield is indestructible as it is made of metal. However, it is unable to catch Arrows that strike it, merely deflecting them instead. Its appearance is largely similar to its appearance, with some minor design changes. Unlike , the metal frame is thinner and the numerous rivets are replaced by three large bolts. The Triforce symbol has become smaller, now with metal framing it. In contrast, the Royal Crest is noticeably bigger and takes up the entire bottom half of the Hylian Shield. The inverted triangle at the bottom has been removed and two metal decals take its place. As with all other Shields in , the Hylian Shield is controlled by using the Nunchuk: by quickly thrusting the Nunchuk forward, Link will raise his Shield and use it to defend himself against enemy attacks. Unlike other Shields in the game, this Hylian Shield is imbued with heroic power, making it indestructible, with its durability bar permanently filled with a glowing blue color to signify this. Unlike its past appearances, the Hylian Shield cannot be obtained early on in the game, due to the nature of normal Shields as potentially temporary items with limited durability. It is the reward from the Thunder Dragon Lanayru's Lightning Round if Link wins eight fights consecutively and then quits. The Hylian Shield's design originally was largely similar to that of , albeit with brighter colors more akin to the original design. Sometime prior to E3 2011, the design was altered, removing the silver rim around the Triforce and the metal ornamentation beneath the Crimson Loftwing design. The Hylian Shield is found in Turtle Rock in , by killing all four Fire Wizzrobe on the first floor. When obtained, it replaces the standard Shield once obtained. Unlike the standard Shield, it can block magical attacks such as the beams fired by Beamos, as well as block the Lynels' fire breath, although it cannot reflect them back. Although the Shield is referred to as a Hylian Shield and bears the Hyrulean Triforce, it is not known or explained how it came to be housed in a Lorulean dungeon. be housed in a Lorulean dungeon. The Hylian Shield is located in a Treasure Chest in the Lockup Back Room within Hyrule Castle, guarded by a Stalnox. It is said to have been passed down through the Royal Family of Hyrule along with legends of the hero. The defensive capability and Durability of this Shield are known to outshine all others. It is the strongest and most durable Shield in the game, having a Durability of 800 (up to 1160 with Durability Up +) and Defense rating of 90 (up to 144 with Guard Up +). Unlike , the Hylian Shield is capable of breaking like other Shields. Once obtained within Hyrule Castle, it can be purchased from Granté in Tarrey Town for 3,000 Rupees, provided Link does not have one already. However, when purchased here, it does not come with a chance of being granted modifiers. When spoken to at Trilby Plain, Russ of the Shield Breakers will explain that all Shield Surfers have heard of and covet the Hylian Shield. He believes it to have been commissioned by the Royal Family, and its Durability makes it perfect for Shield Surfing. The traveler Baumar has also heard about the Hylian Shield's durability. The Hylian Shield, being made of metal, will attract Lightning if it is equipped during a Thunderstorm and conduct Electricity. It will also sink if it is dropped in Water, but it can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, it will not burn if it is exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. The Hylian Shield is located in a Treasure Chest in the Docks of Hyrule Castle, where the Saas Ko'sah Shrine was located in . This chest will appear once the nearby torch was lit, similar to said shrine in the previous game. As per before, it is the most durable shield in the game, with a Durability of 800 (up to 810 with Durability Up +), and a Defense rating of 90 (up to 100 with Guard Up +). If it is broken, a replacement can be bought from Cece in Hateno Village, assuming Link does not already have one in his inventory and "The Mayoral Election" Side Adventure has been completed. Link uses a Hylian Shield while rescuing Zelda from Ganon. When Zelda activates her Swordfighter Form, she carries a semblance of a Hylian Shield which can protect her from enemy attacks. , also known as the Land of the Gods, and the Lesser Kingdom of Hyrule, is the name of the land that serves as the iconic setting for a majority of the games in the Zelda series. It is usually depicted as a beautiful and prosperous land blessed with deep forests, tall mountains, vast lakes, a barren desert, great cities, villages, and many ancient temples hidden throughout. Once ruled by the goddess Hylia as an unnamed land in ancient times, it became established as the Kingdom of Hyrule by the descendants of her mortal incarnation. The sacred bloodline that was started by the Zelda of would go on to become known as the Royal Family of Hyrule. At the northern center of Hyrule is seated Hyrule Castle, where the family reside, and a bustling town surrounded by a stonewall, populated mostly by the Hylians and a variety of shops. To the west of the kingdom can often be seen a desert, forests to the south and south-east and a mountain range to the east and north-east. The kingdom has its own long and unique history with many wars and conflicts over the Triforce, deities, legendary relics, historical heroes and villains. It is connected to a variety of different realms or universes via magical artifacts and portals, including but not limited to the Sacred Realm, the Twilight Realm, its own direct parallel world Lorule and, to a lesser extent, Termina. The story of the Sacred Realm and the Triforce would shape Hyrule's future in the centuries that followed its establishment, becoming the basis of its providence. It is also home to a multitude of different races and tribes, each inhabiting a different part of the country and sometimes protecting its legendary relics and guarding its temples. After the birth of the Gerudo thief from the western desert, Ganondorf, who wishes to conquer the kingdom for himself using the Triforce's tremendous power, a young hero clad in a green tunic and armed with the legendary Master Sword will often rise up to save the land from destruction and defeat him. The hero is often assisted in this effort by the kingdom's young princesses, traditionally named Zelda. This would become a repeated history that would doom Hyrule on several occasions, one account resulting in its sealing during the Great Flood. Many years after the flood, it was succeeded by a new kingdom named after it. Appearances by Game Hyrule has appeared multiple times throughout the series as the setting for most installments in one form or another. The geography of the land has changed in each appearance, sometimes drastically. History Hyrule's history is long and storied, beginning with the Golden Goddesses transforming the Emptiness where Null resided into the larger world that Hyrule resides in; which begins a history spanning three separate timelines. Major Conflicts Several of the wars in Hyrule's history were fought over possession of the Triforce or dominion over the Sacred Realm, others were fought over ownership of the kingdom and its sacred artifacts, or simply desire to destroy it in spite and hatred. Ancient Battle: After the three Golden Goddesses finished creating the realm which would come to be known as Hyrule, they trusted the Triforce in the hands of the Goddess Hylia and her chosen hero. The Demon King Demise, wanting to make the world his own, gathered an army of monsters and together launched an attack against the people of the surface, murdering them and causing misfortunes in an attempt to get their hands on the power guarded by Hylia. The goddess gathered the surviving humans on a piece of land and sent it to the heavens, beyond the clouds and out of reach from the evil plaguing the land. In order to keep it from falling into the hands of Demise, Hylia also sent the Triforce to The Sky and hid the portals to three pieces of the Triforce within Sky Keep, and enshrined the Goddess Sword inside the Statue of the Goddess, to be found by her next chosen hero when the time was right. This new temple contained the only sealed entrance to the Sacred Realm. The Triforce was placed in the Temple of Light, located in the center of the Sacred Realm, which was now isolated from Hyrule. With the chaotic era at an end, the land entered an era of prosperity and Hyrule was established by the descendants of Zelda, the mortal incarnation of the goddess Hylia. Governance Hyrule's form of government has remained relatively consistent throughout its history, with an ancient monarchy, the Royal Family of Hyrule, ruling over the lower-class citizens of the kingdom from Hyrule's capital city, Hyrule Castle Town. The Royal Family itself rules from the seat of government in the land of Hyrule, Hyrule Castle, the namesake of the capital. The government is typically headed by the King of Hyrule, and his heir in most depictions of Hyrule is his daughter or descendant, Princess Zelda. In some cases, Zelda herself has ruled over the land as matriarch of the Royal Family as well, such as during the Twili invasion of Hyrule. Hyrule is typically divided into various provinces and most of the various races pledge their allegiance to the central government headed by the Royal Family. Each race has its own local government and the individual tribal leaders, but all races pledge their overall allegiance to the Royal Family as kingdom of Hyrule citizens. Hyrule has faced many coups throughout its history, but ultimately the Royal Family is usually restored to power through the efforts of Hyrule's hero, Link. Despite their duty to protect the peace, the guards have a poor reputation and a tendency towards cowardice, they will shrink in fear whenever Wolf Link passes by them. Due to their minor inefficiencies, they often are unable to prevent infiltration of even Hyrule Castle. However, these guards were also very wary of when evil took over their kingdom. When Vaati impersonated King Daltus, the guards who dissented were turned to stone. When the guards would not follow an evil ruler, they were brainwashed into doing so. In , the dark wizard Agahnim took over the country through much cunning and deceit; one of the first things he did was take over Hyrule's military force using his powerful magic. The guards are shown to be freed of this spell when Link destroys Agahnim and returns the Royal Family to power. Although the guards are mostly concentrated in the Hyrulean capital city Hyrule Castle Town, they are seen spread out all across the kingdom as well. Geography Like many of the other lands depicted in The Legend of Zelda series such as Termina, Holodrum and Labrynna, Hyrule's geography varies greatly from region to region. In most depictions of Hyrule, the land is shown to be a collection of regions with varying geographies and climates usually linked by a great open expanse of land known as Hyrule Field. Hyrule Castle Town and by extension Hyrule Castle are usually located near the central part of the country and not far away from Hyrule Field. The other regions of Hyrule as stated before vary greatly in their composition and appearance. For example, the region most associated with the rock-loving Gorons is the sweltering and rocky Death Mountain, which has little to no vegetation and is for all intents and purposes a large volcano. On the other hand, there are parts of the country covered by deep forests that have a more hospitable climate and atmosphere, where plant-life and vegetation are much more common and provide a means to live for such forest-dwellers as the child-like Kokiri race. Hyrule is also usually shown to be home to a vast lake usually named Lake Hylia as well as a watery grotto named Zora's Domain, both being more hospitable and suitable to the aquatic Zora race. Hyrule is also known to have snowy regions as well, such as the Snowpeak Mountain Range, which is the preferred home region of the Yeti race. Finally, Hyrule is also usually shown to be home to a vast desert (usually to the west), more commonly known as the Gerudo Desert amongst other names, which is home to such desert-dwelling tribes as the Gerudo or the Zuna. Taken altogether, Hyrule is shown to be a melting pot of sorts in regards to its geography as it has been shown to possess nearly every kind of climate and terrain, and the implied ages that span between each game are more than sufficient to erode and shift the land, and for temples and cities to be moved and rebuilt. Population Races of Hyrule Hyrule is home to numerous races which are scattered all across the land, each inhabiting a different part of the kingdom. The main distinction between Hyrule's inhabitants is that of Hylians and Hyruleans. Hylian refers to the specific race prominently appearing throughout Hyrule. Hyrulean refers to the many humanoid and non-humanoid races that have inhabited Hyrule. With the exception of the Hylians, most of the races have preferred environments and primarily reside among members of their own race. Moreover, few of Hyrule's races are limited to residency in just this one kingdom. Other lands of The Legend of Zelda series have featured these, and even more exotic races. , also known as the Castle of Hyrule, is a recurring location in . It is the seat of Hyrule's monarchical government and the home of the Royal Family of Hyrule, which usually includes Princess Zelda and the normally unseen King of Hyrule. The castle first debuted in , the third game in the series. Each game that contains Hyrule Castle features a different layout. Near the castle is Hyrule Castle Town, which serves as the city's marketplace where Hyruleans come to engage in business and trade. Hyrule Castle is usually directly in the center of Hyrule's geographical layout in each game, serving as the crown jewel of the kingdom. It is often one of the most important places for Link during his numerous adventures in Hyrule and many times is the site of the final confrontations, usually serving as a level or dungeon of sorts. As the seat of Hyrule's government, the Castle has been the location of multiple conflicts and has been the subject of invasion more than once throughout its depiction in . , also known as the Castle of Hyrule, is a recurring Dungeon in the . Overview Hyrule Castle is visited twice by Link throughout his adventure: first to rescue Princess Zelda from her cell, and later to battle Agahnim before being transported to the Dark World. The main Item obtained is the Boomerang. Entrance to the Castle After Link is telepathically contacted by Princess Zelda to rescue her from Agahnim's clutches in Hyrule Castle, the young hero uncovers a hidden hole beneath a bush northeast of the Castle that leads him into a secret passage. He then finds his Uncle has been mortally wounded and receives his Fighter's Sword and shield before passing away. Guarding Princess Zelda's cell is the Ball and Chain Trooper, whom Link must defeat in order to free Zelda from her prison. Together, they head towards the King's chamber to reveal a path that takes them to the Secret Passage, which eventually leads them into the Sanctuary. At this point, Agahnim makes the upper levels of the Castle inaccessible by creating an electrical barrier that cannot be bypassed. This area of the Castle requires Link to defeat various enemy Soldiers in order to reach the top of the Castle. Although he can evade some of the foes, some of the rooms will require that Link defeat all the enemies before proceeding. After reaching the top of the Castle, Link witnesses Agahnim as he sends Princess Zelda to the Dark World. The young hero must then burn the middle curtain with the use of his Lamp to enter another room and battle against the evil wizard who, upon his defeat, sends Link to the Dark World. An unmarked branch of this road continues left, down a flight of stairs into the northern entrance of the Library. However, it is possible for Link to simply walk around the rubble and continue along the side road. Beyond the landslide sits a pool of Water beside the road. A metallic Treasure Chest containing five Bomb Arrows is hidden underwater. A Guardian Skywatcher patrols the road near the pool. Beyond the pool of Water, the side road continues to another landslide. When Link approaches the landslide, an inactive Guardian will fall from above. Link can walk along the narrow strip of land around the landslide to continue along the side road which passes the Dining Hall. The road continuing from the Bridge beyond the Dining Hall meets back with the main road, on the other side of the massive collection of Malice. road which passes the Dining Hall. The road continuing from the Bridge beyond the Dining Hall meets back with the main road, on the other side of the massive collection of Malice. An Glowing Eyeball can be found on this side of the Malice, and destroying it will clear the main road for Link to travel between his position and the First Gatehouse. From here, the main road continues along to the Second Gatehouse nearby. The main road beyond the Second Gatehouse curves around a series of stone walls. Features and Overview thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of the Great Plateau during the Era of Myth.|The Ancient Hyrule Castle visible on the horizon behind the Temple of Time from The Ancient Hyrule Castle is located at the base of Mount Hylia atop the Great Plateau in Ancient Hyrule. It is set roughly where the River of the Dead is during the Era of the Wilds. It is a step Pyramid built in the style of Zonai architecture and is home to the Zonai king Rauru and the Hylian queen Sonia. It features several draped cloth banners and carpets in deep red and blue colors. When Zelda transports back to the Era of Foundation, she is met by Rauru and Sonia who welcome her into their Castle and attempt to help her harness her powers over Time so that she can return to the distant future. Following Ganondorf's thwarted assault on Hyrule Kingdom with a swarm of Molduga, Ganondorf visits the Audience Chamber of the Ancient Hyrule Castle under the guise of swearing his fealty to Rauru. Despite Zelda's concerns, Rauru accepts his vow of loyalty under the belief that he can more closely monitor Ganondorf's actions this way. Ganondorf in turn uses this opportunity to send his Phantom Ganon disguised as Zelda to sneak throughout the Castle and find an opportunity to steal a Secret Stone. Because of the strange sightings of Zelda's doppelganger, Zelda and Sonia eventually confront Phantom Ganon atop the balcony of the Castle, where Ganondorf launches a surprise attack. In this moment, he kills Sonia and steals her Secret Stone before Rauru arrives. He uses the power of the Secret Stone to augment his own Dark power, taunting Rauru for his arrogance and transforming into Demon King Ganondorf. Zelda and Rauru flee with Sonia's corpse to the Forgotten Temple as Demon King Ganondorf summons an army of Monsters to attack Hyrule in the start of the Imprisoning War. Though the Ancient Hyrule Castle still stands after the Imprisoning War, it does not endure the ages and its traces cannot be found in the future. A new Hyrule Castle is built atop the site where Rauru sealed Demon King Ganondorf as a measure to contain and safeguard the seal. Areas Inhabitants As in , the Ancient Hyrule Castle is located atop the Great Plateau during the Era of Myth.

The are a recurring location in . The Hyrule Castle Corridors go unnamed in and . Features and Overview The Hyrule Castle Corridors are located throughout the interior of Hyrule Castle. They connect the Dining Hall, Reception Room, Square Spiral Staircase, Library, and Guards' Chamber together. A Cooking Pot can be found in the Corridors near the Guards' Chamber. During "EX Royal Guard Rumors," a Side Quest exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link can read Super Rumor Mill V4, which mentions that a piece of equipment worn by the Royal Guard can be found near the Dining Hall. In the Hyrule Castle Corridors west of the Dining Hall, Link can find an EX Treasure Chest behind a bombable wall. When he opens this Chest, he will receive the Royal Guard Uniform. Another stone Treasure Chest can be found behind a bombable wall in the Corridors near the Guards' Chamber, which contains three Ancient Arrows. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles can be found behind bombable walls in the Hyrule Castle Corridors. One is between the Dining Hall and the Square Spiral Staircase. The other is outside of the Guards' Chamber. Link will find an Acorn Jar hanging from the ceilings in each of these newly revealed rooms. Using Archery, he can shoot the Jars, which causes the Koroks to appear and give him Korok Seeds. Enemies Equipment As in , the Hyrule Castle Corridors compose the hallways of Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field. Enemies Sub-Bosses Equipment Other Appearances The Hyrule Castle Corridors appear as part of the Hyrule Castle Stage. In the Movie "An Uneasy Heart", Zelda, Impa, and Terrako can be seen walking through the Hyrule Castle Corridors. After a discussion about King Rhoam with Impa, Zelda sends her to inform Mipha and Daruk of their training the next day. Zelda begins to confide her worries to Terrako, but they are interrupted by Link's arrival.

The Hyrule Castle Courtyard, also known as the Castle Courtyard, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Castle Courtyard is a small, open enclosure inside Hyrule Castle. In order to speak to Princess Zelda, Link must infiltrate Hyrule Castle, make his way through the Castle Gardens, and visit her within the Courtyard. There, Princess Zelda explains that she had a prophetic dream warning of a dark force attempting to corrupt Hyrule. She then shows Link a window where he can spot Ganondorf, who intends to steal the Triforce from its resting place in the Sacred Realm, the Temple of Time. thumb|right|320px|alt= Screenshot of Link looking into Hyrule Castle from the Courtyard.|Link spying on Ganondorf In order to counter Ganondorf, Princess Zelda devised a plan to keep the tools necessary to enter the Sacred Realm, the Ocarina of Time and the Spiritual Stones, out of his reach. To this end, she tasks Link with the responsibility of retrieving the remaining two Spiritual Stones. Princess Zelda then gives him a Letter granting him permission to ascend Death Mountain Trail. Afterward, she orders Impa to teach Link her Lullaby and help escort him out of the Castle. If Link strikes the western window with a Deku Seed, a Soldier appears and berates him before throwing a Bomb in his direction. The eastern window contains scenery from . Striking this window with a Deku Seed will release a Red Rupee. The Castle Courtyard is only accessible during the day, since Soldiers that cannot be bypassed will be stationed just in front of the secret entrance at night. After Princess Zelda flees from the Castle, the aforementioned Soldiers will be stationed at the secret entrance at all times, rendering the entire area inaccessible. The Hyrule Castle Courtyard composes the majority of the exterior of Hyrule Castle in . It follows a sprawling and branching road that connects to key locations within the Castle. The primary road leads through three major compounds: the First Gatehouse, the Second Gatehouse, and the Sanctum. It begins at the Hyrule Castle Gate, which winds around to the entrance to the Guards' Chamber before passing through the First Gatehouse. After the First Gatehouse, the road splits twice. The first split of the road leads through a garden beneath the tower containing Princess Zelda's Room, continuing on to the Dining Hall on the southeast side of the Castle before reconnecting with the primary road a short distance after it initially splits. The main road continues through the Second Gatehouse before wrapping around and leading up into the Sanctum. The road between the First and Second Gatehouse is obstructed by a Pool of Malice, which can be partially dispelled by destroying a Glowing Eyeball on the eastern side of the Malice. thumb|right|320px|alt= Screenshot of Sheikah beside a Guardian Stalker.|Sheikah researchers operating a Guardian Stalker in the Courtyard Prior to the second Great Calamity, the Hyrule Castle Courtyard was used by Sheikah scientists to research and control the Guardians they excavated

destroying a Glowing Eyeball on the eastern side of the Malice. thumb|right|320px|alt= Screenshot of Sheikah beside a Guardian Stalker.|Sheikah researchers operating a Guardian Stalker in the Courtyard Prior to the second Great Calamity, the Hyrule Castle Courtyard was used by Sheikah scientists to research and control the Guardians they excavated from beneath Hyrule Castle, as seen in the Recovered Memory, "Father and Daughter". After Calamity Ganon escaped its seal beneath Hyrule Castle, it spread its Malice to the Guardians populating the Courtyard, seizing control of them and using them to assail Hyrule Castle, initiating the second Great Calamity that spread to the rest of Hyrule Kingdom. Areas Enemies With Hyrule Castle risen into the Sky, the Hyrule Castle Courtyard has been split in two. The larger portion is still located on the Surface, while a small part is now situated in the Sky. Areas Other Appearances thumb|right|320px|alt= Promotional screenshot of King Rhoam and several Hylian Soldiers.|King Rhoam receiving the Hylian Soldiers in the Courtyard The Hyrule Castle Courtyard appears as part of the Hyrule Castle Stage. In the "Reunited" Movie, King Rhoam can be seen congratulating a Hylian Captain and a group of Soldiers on their success in a recent battle. When Zelda enters the Courtyard, she meets with Impa and Link. They are interrupted by the arrival of Terrako, which Link stops from reaching Zelda. This causes Zelda and Impa to realize that the noises Terrako makes have an effect on the Sheikah Slate.

The Hyrule Castle Gate is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Hyrule Castle Gate divides Hyrule Castle from the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins. It features a bridge that spans that Hyrule Castle Moat. The metallic doors on the Gate can be moved with Magnesis or by hitting them while they are under the effect of Stasis. The Hyrule Castle Courtyard begins past the Gate. left|40px Three Korok Seed Puzzles are located on and near the Hyrule Castle Gate. One can be found on top of the Gate by picking up a Natural Hiding Spot. A second can be found by shooting the jar hanging underneath the bridge by using Archery. The third and final one can be found by following the Flower Trail that starts underneath the bridge. When Link discovers these Koroks, they will give him a Korok Seed. Enemies As in , the Hyrule Castle Gate is located between Hyrule Castle and the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins in Hyrule Field. Before Link reports the news of Zelda's sighting at Hyrule Castle to Purah, Raseno stands stationed at the north end of the Gate. Oliff later takes up a position on the south end of the Gate after Raseno leaves. Creatures Inhabitants Korok Seeds Other Appearances The Hyrule Castle Gate is part of the Hyrule Castle Stage. During the Movie "Duty", Zelda and Link attempt to escape Hyrule Castle through its Gate, but they are stopped when a Guardian spots them and begins to attack. However, they are saved by King Rhoam, who ambushes the Guardian. Link starts to run to his aid, but King Rhoam reminds him of his responsibility as Zelda's knight. As a result, Link takes Zelda's hand and drags her through the Hyrule Castle Gate despite her protests.

The Hyrule Castle Gazebo is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Hyrule Castle Gazebo is located on the premises of Hyrule Castle. It is situated above the Round Spiral Staircase in the Hyrule Castle Courtyard. Like the rest of Hyrule Castle, it suffered massive amounts of damage during the Great Calamity, and most of its structure has been destroyed. During the Recovered Memory "The Champions' Ballad", which is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack, the Champions visit the Hyrule Castle Gazebo after their official appointment. Daruk complains to Link about being tired after the ceremony, while Princess Zelda shows the Sheikah Slate to Urbosa, Mipha, and Revali. After hearing about the Camera Rune, Mipha asks Zelda if they can use it to take a Picture. As in , the Hyrule Castle Gazebo is part of the Hyrule Castle Courtyard in Hyrule Castle. It is located on Hyrule Castle B1 and is within the part of the Castle that rises into the Sky at the beginning of the Upheaval, which can be seen during the Memory "The Awakening". Equipment Other Appearances The Hyrule Castle Gazebo is part of the Hyrule Castle Stage. In the Movie "After the Ceremony", Zelda and the Champions visit the Hyrule Castle Gazebo following the latter's official inauguration.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Hyrule Castle Moat is a body of Water that surrounds Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field. Hyrule Castle Moat is a deep, fast-flowing Water body encircling Hyrule Castle, located in northern Hyrule Field. It feeds into the Hylia and Regencia Rivers to the east and west respectively. A large bridge crosses the south of the Moat, providing access to the Hyrule Castle Gate. The Moat's northern side connects to an entrance to the Castle's Docks, and following the Upheaval, a Cave containing the Hyrule Castle Moat East Chasm has opened up on its eastern side. Creatures Korok Seeds

The is a recurring location in . The Hyrule Castle Town Gate goes unnamed in and . Features and Overview The Hyrule Castle Town Gate is the entrance to the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins in Hyrule Field. The Gate features a multi-level interior, which can be traversed using the Ladders located inside. Two worn Big Flags have been planted at both of its sides, and a Fallen Guardian can be found atop the wall nearby. 100 years ago, the Hyrule Castle Town Gate served as both an entryway and a guard post for Hyrule Castle Town. However, it was destroyed alongside the rest of the settlement during the second Great Calamity. Enemies Korok Seeds The Hyrule Castle Town Gate remains standing in . Lookout Landing has been established on its southern end. Its doors are open by default, but Link is able to manipulate them using Ultrahand. Korok Seeds Other Appearances King Rhoam stands on the Hyrule Castle Town Gate while giving a speech to the Hylian Soldiers during the "King on the Eve of Battle" Movie. He rallies the Soldiers to defend Hyrule Castle from the incoming horde of Monsters.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Hyrule Castle Town Ruins are located in Hyrule Field at the southern base of Hyrule Castle. They are the ruins of Hyrule Castle Town, Hyrule Kingdom's largest city before the second Great Calamity. As it had the highest concentration of Hylians and was built in Central Hyrule, it was both a shopping hub and travel destination for the people of Hyrule. At their center is the Central Square, a former thoroughfare with a large fountain. The Hyrule Castle Town Ruins are filled with Ruined Houses and desolate terrain that is covered in Malice. There is little vegetation to be found except for Grass. A Cooking Pot can be found in one of the Ruined Houses to the northwest. A stone Treasure Chest containing a Luminous Stone rests in the Ruined House to the south. Another stone Treasure Chest containing a Purple Rupee can be found in the Ruined House to the southeast. A third stone Treasure Chest containing a Purple Rupee can be found inside the tower that is surrounded by Pools of Malice in the road in the southwest. A fourth stone Chest containing a Sapphire can be found in a Ruined House in the west. A fifth stone Treasure Chest containing a Purple Rupee can be found in a Ruined House north of the previous Chest. Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment By the time Link first arrives at the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins, a group of Tents have been set up in the Central Square. These Tents belong to the Monster-Control Crew, who are searching for Zelda after her disappearance during the Upheaval. After Link speaks to Hoz at Hyrule Castle and reports their findings to Purah at Lookout Landing, the Monster-Control Crew leaves the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins, taking their camp equipment with them. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Hyrule Castle West is an island located west of Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field. It is completely surrounded by the Hyrule Castle Moat, but it retains a connection to the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins by the Moat Bridge. The rest of the island is covered by two hills and an unnamed forest. The ruins of the Castle Town Prison can be found on the eastern end of Hyrule Castle West, and Noya Neha Shrine is in a Cave on the island's southwestern corner. There are Wooden Boxes in this Cave, as well as along the island's southern shore. A Stone Talus (Rare) can be found atop the plateau in the center of Hyrule Castle West.
