is a recurring large, grassy area of Hyrule in . Hyrule Field goes unnamed in . Hyrule Field is the central region of Hyrule that leads to many of the prominent locations of the kingdom and beyond. As such, it is typically a major area that the hero must traverse repeatedly throughout the course of the game. Features and Overview Hyrule Field is a large round area that acts as the hub or crossroads of Hyrule in . All other areas of the game branch out from this region. However, there is little activity, and besides a few side-quests, it serves little purpose other than maintaining the illusion of a vast land. Located in the center of Hyrule Field is Lon-Lon Ranch, and all other areas dwell on its outskirts. At the northmost section of the field rests Hyrule Castle Town, the main center of activity of Hyrule which also serves as the location of Hyrule Castle. To the northeast is Kakariko Village, the primary settlement for Hyruleans, and just north of the village is Death Mountain. Zora's River and ultimately Zora's Domain reside in the east, while the Kokiri Forest is situated in the southeast. Directly to the west of Kokiri Forest is Lake Hylia, a deep, pure lake that is home to the Water Temple. Lastly, Gerudo Valley is located to the west, where one the other side of the valley the gang of female thieves have established their hideout, the Gerudo's Fortress. All of the waterflow in Hyrule is a direct source from the waters in Zora's Fountain, located in the northeast. This water flows through Zora's River and makes its way past Castle Town, continuing its path through the bottom of Gerudo Valley and eventually reaching its final destination: Lake Hylia. As young Link, Stalchildren burrow out of the ground during the nighttime and attack the young hero. They can be avoided by sticking to the dirt road or by wearing the Bunny Hood. Peahats can also be found in the southern and northern corners of the field, and will attack anyone who gets too close to their territory during the day; however, if Link attacks the Peahats during the night, they will send out Peahat Larva to chase after him. Once Link turns into an adult by retrieving the Master Sword from its Pedestal, the Stalchildren and the Peahats will disappear; instead, Big Poes as well as ordinary Poes will roam the field, although they will only appear at certain spots. Areas In , Hyrule Field is divided into two parts on the map: North Hyrule Field and South Hyrule Field, with Hyrule Town between the two locations. Other places linking to the two parts of Hyrule Field include Hyrule Castle, Lon Lon Ranch, Trilby Highlands, the Eastern Hills, and the Western Wood. Areas thumb|right|300px|Hyrule Field's northern portion from In , Hyrule Field is almost five times larger than in and spans three Provinces: Lanayru, Eldin, and Faron. It sports more landscape variety than its previous incarnation, including bridges, rocky cliffs, woods, and ancient ruins, and unlike , Hyrule Field in is not one huge area, but several areas connected by pathways. Due to its immense size, it is easier to traverse the field with either the help of Epona or by warping through a Portal. Hyrule Field surrounds Hyrule Castle and is full of shortcuts and entrances to many other areas, including: Faron Woods in the south Kakariko Village and Kakariko Gorge in the Zora's Domain in the north Lake Hylia in the Hyrule Castle Town in the center Various enemies roam the field, including Bokoblins, Bulblins, Deku Babas, Bomskits, Guays, Leevers, Poes, Stalhounds (at night), Kargaroks, Tektites, Helmasaurs, Lizalfos, Chuchus, and Bullbos. Several important game events occur in the field. After Colin gets kidnapped by King Bulblin, Link follows him to the portion of Hyrule Field, where the young hero defeats King Bulblin at the Bridge of Eldin. Link must once again journey through Hyrule Field as Telma, Ilia and Ralis are riding in a caravan on their way to Kakariko Village from the Hyrule Castle Town while the young hero defends Telma's caravan from enemy attacks during the ride. The last event is the final two fights against Ganondorf which take place on Hyrule Field. When riding Epona through Hyrule Field, a remixed version of the theme music is played, which adds brass instruments to the melody. Unlike in previous Zelda games, Hyrule Field in is completely open; all parts of the overworld are accessible with no interruptions, whereas in previous games, different parts of the overworld were separated by loading screens. There are also enemies roaming the field such as the one shown in the game's reveal trailer. Central Hyrule houses Hyrule Field's location in the game. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Hyrule Field Chasm is a Chasm that opened along the path between the Passeri Greenbelt and Windvane Meadow in Hyrule Field when the Upheaval began. It leads to the Central Hyrule Depths below. The Monster-Control Crew and the Zonai Survey Team have set up campsites in the area, and the Jiosin Shrine can be found nearby. The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Hyrule Garrison Ruins are located in Hyrule Field. They were formerly ruins of an outpost that Hyrule Kingdom adapted into a military base known as the Hyrule Outpost in preparation for the Great Calamity to come. However, as they could not predict that Calamity Ganon would wrest control of the Guardians away from them, the Hyrule Garrison was again destroyed. Some Fallen Guardians can be found around the Ruins and can be searched for Ancient Materials. Similarly, a Busted Wagon can be found on the southeast side of the Ruins, which can also be searched for Materials. Areas Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests The Hyrule Garrison Ruins remain occupied by Monsters in . The Central Tower is now gone, and the Susuyai Shrine now sits near where it was. Despite its population of Monsters, people still travel along the roads that pass through the Ruins. Along the southeastern road of the Ruins, Link can find Hyrule Restoration Materials as well as a Busted Wagon that can be searched for Materials. West of the fountain area, the Monsters have constructed a Monster Stronghold. This Stronghold is fortified with Barricades and Bomb Barrels. A lit Cooking Pot can be found beneath this Stronghold. Between this Stronghold and the Susuyai Shrine, more Hyrule Restoration Materials can be found. Following the defeat of Calamity Ganon, Zelda visited the fountain in the Ruins to examine the damage done to it by the Guardian attacks. In the "Unshaken Bravery" Voice Memory, she remarks that most of the Soldiers that were posted here were deployed to help in other regions. She believes that the Soldiers who remained fought bravely against the assault, but ultimately could not repel the invading force. , also stylized as Ice ChuChus, are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Ice Chuchus are white Chuchus that produce an icy mist in . They are native to the Snow Realm of Hyrule. Their mist prevents them from being attacked directly as it will freeze Link instantly, requiring the screen to be rubbed with the stylus to thaw him out. Like Yellow Chuchus, they can be stunned first to remove their defense mechanism, rendering them safe to attack. Ice Chuchus appear in more frigid climates, such as Mount Hylia and the Hebra Mountains. They are lightweight and can be pushed about with gusts of wind from the Korok Leaf. If they touch Link, he becomes temporarily frozen due to the frigid air they emit. Ice Chuchus attack by leaping at Link and creating an icy blast around them. After attacking, Ice Chuchus temporarily lose their icy coating and are vulnerable to attack. If they are defeated while they have their icy exteriors, they will explode into a cloud of frost, freezing anything in range. Ice Chuchus drop White Chuchu Jellies upon their defeat. Drops Ice Chuchus in can, once again, be found in snowy regions. They emit frigid air that temporarily freezes Link if he touches them. Ice Chuchus attack by leaping at Link and creating bursts of frost that freeze anything caught in them. They are temporarily thawed after attacking, allowing Link to safely strike them. When defeated with their icy coatings active, they explode into a cold mist that freezes anything nearby. When defeated, Ice Chuchus drop White Chuchu Jellies. Other Appearances Ice Chuchus reappear in , first appearing in Revali, the Rito Warrior. They act the same as in , and once again drop White Chuchu Jelly upon defeat. The giant variants make a reappearance during the Downloadable Content missions, attacking by rolling into the player, spinning around, slamming down into the ground, and firing off small Ice Chuchus.

are recurring Enemies in . They are a variation of Keese that are exposed to the cold, and are enveloped in a frigid, icy mist. Ice Keese otherwise behave identically to their regular counterparts, but are significantly more dangerous as they can potentially freeze Link upon contact. They inhabit frozen Caves and mountains, Ice-themed Dungeons, and other cold locations. In some games, Ice Keese can revert back into an ordinary Keese when their mists are extinguished. They may also intentionally fly into a source of cold substance, such as Blue Fire, to turn back into an Ice Keese. Characteristics and Ice Keese made their first appearance in and . They are encountered only in snowy and icy areas, such as the Ice Cavern in and Snowhead in . Like normal Keese, they fly around the area and attack Link by swooping down at him. Coming into contact with one will immediately freeze Link on the spot, damaging him as well as rendering him immobile for a few seconds until he breaks free. Although hazardous, they can be defeated by any conventional weapon in Link's arsenal. Ice Keese in appear as chilled Keese fully engulfed in mist. They mainly appear in frigid locations, most notably around Snowpeak and the Snowpeak Ruins, but also appear in the Cave of Ordeals and the Cave of Shadows in . Ice Keese have an identical behavior to their other variants, but whose bodies are able to freeze Link upon contact. As with all Keese variations, they can be forced onto the ground and stunned whenever Link uses the Shield Attack on them. The mist of the Ice Keese can be removed with the Gale Boomerang, but they can still freeze Link upon contact without it. and Ice Keese in and appear as light blue Keese with a stream of icy mist trailing behind them. Like other variants, they simply fly in circular and erratic patterns. Touching one will instantly freeze Link, requiring the Stylus to be rubbed on the screen to thaw him out. They can be defeated by most Weapons in Link's arsenal, but long-range weapons such as the Bow are recommended to keep Link at a safe distance. They appear in frozen regions. In , ordinary Keese can fly into a light blue fire turning into Ice Keese. In , Ice Keese appear in Levels of the Drablands' Ice Cavern region. They resemble blue Keese enveloped in mist. Like the other Keese variants in the game, Ice Keese will attack the Links by diving at them from afar. They can only be defeated either with the Fire Gloves or by first stunning them with an item. Ice Keese appear in . They are typically found on icy mountaintops, such as Mount Lanayru. They can potentially drop Ice Keese Wings when defeated. are Enemies in . Characteristics Ice Likes are Like Likes that are capable of spitting blasts of frigid air at Link. Like other Like Likes, their hide is too tough to damage, but their bulbous, cyan tongue is extremely sensitive, and striking it leaves them vulnerable to attacks. Ice Likes intermittently reveal their tongues, swallowing Link if he is too close when they retract their tongues into their mouths. If they swallow Link, they steal one of his Shields or Weapons before spitting him out. They are vulnerable to Fire-based Weapons and Arrows, which stun them, allowing their tongues to be attacked. Ice Likes can also briefly be shocked by Electrical Weapons and Arrows. When defeated, they may drop Ice Like Stones and Ice Fruits, as well as any Weapons or Shields they have stolen.

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Ice Wizzrobes appear inside Vaati's Palace in . They will vanish and appear in a random location and attack with a ball of ice before vanishing again. Ice Wizzrobes appear as an ice variant to the standard green Wizzrobes and Fire Wizzrobes in . Like the others, they will teleport to random locations throughout the area in which they appear, shooting their ice attack before vanishing again. Ice Wizzrobes appear alongside their Fire Wizzrobe variants in . Like previous incarnations, they will randomly appear around the area and attack with a ball of ice before vanishing again. Ice Wizzrobes appear alongside dark Wizzrobes in . They are common in the Ice Cavern, but also appear in the Sky Temple. The ice beams they cast can freeze the Links on contact. They float at varying heights; those that float high above the ground can be reached by forming a Totem. They require at least two Sword strikes to defeat. As ice-based enemies, they are also weak to fire, and can be defeated by a single fireball either thrown or held with the Fire Gloves. Ice Wizzrobes can be found near ruins around the Gerudo Highlands and Hyrule Field regions in . They attack by using their Ice Rods to summon blasts of cold air or by summoning frozen monsters such as Ice Chuchus and Ice Keese. They also create blizzards to decrease the area's temperature, making it too cold for Link without cold-resistant Armor or Elixirs. Ice Wizzrobes, like their variants, will turn invisible after attacking, leaving ripples in the air with each footstep. Striking one in the head with an Arrow will stun it and give Link time to attack. Hitting it with a fire-based attack, such as with a Fire Arrow or a Flameblade, will immediately evaporate it. When defeated, Ice Wizzrobes drop their Ice Rods. Ice Wizzrobes are Wizzrobes that wield Ice magic. Similarly to their counterparts, they can create blasts of cold air and conjure Ice Monsters, along with generating Blizzards that cause a Freezing Climate. They wield Traveler's Swords with Sapphires Fused to them. When defeated, Ice Wizzrobes drop their Swords. Ice Wizzrobes are Wizzrobes who use Ice magic. They can be found on the higher levels of Hebra Mountain, over a pool of Cold Water. When in combat, they hover in the air, charge, and release an Ice blade that flies at their target. After firing their Ice attack, they teleport to another nearby location and repeat the process. When summoned as an Echo, they have an Echo cost of five. Other Appearances left Ice Wizzrobes appear as enemies in where they move to the beat of the music. Here, they act as medium- to long-range combatants for Cadence, Link, Yves, and Zelda, teleporting towards them whenever they are nearby and attempt to cast icy projectiles in their direction. the music. Here, they act as medium- to long-range combatants for Cadence, Link, Yves, and Zelda, teleporting towards them whenever they are nearby and attempt to cast icy projectiles in their direction. They appear for a total of seven beats between each teleport, taking two beats to fully appear and charging their attack on the third. On the fourth beat, they release their magic, letting it fly in a straight line on every single music beat until it makes contact with something. If any of the heroes or even monsters gets struck by the projectile, their bodies will become frozen within a block of ice for a few beats before breaking out of it, rendering them vulnerable to attack. After casting their spell, they will remain stationary until the seventh beat, raising their crystal orbs to the sky in order to teleport themselves away, fading until they finally disappear on the eighth beat. Once gone, they will remain invisible for five beats, or if the heroes are too far away, won't reappear at all until they return to the Ice Wizzrobe's last known location. Despite their appearance, they can still be attacked while fading in and out of teleportation. There is another, stronger version of the Ice Wizzrobe that only appears in the Wizzroboe boss fight if the boss is in its more powerful form. They also appear in Octavo's boss fight. Ice Wizzrobes appear in almost every single Stage. They are Wizzrobes that use their Ice Rods to freeze enemies. Some attacks are making a laser of Ice, or making a rain of Ice fall, which freezes any characters that hit the Ice falling. Ice Wizzrobes are particularly weak to Fire Rods or other Fire weapons, and their Weak-Point Gauge will appear after being attacked by Fire weapons. They will drop their Ice Rod if a player has not already gotten it, and will drop three pieces of Ice energy that can be used to replenish the Ice Rod's Ice.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Igneo Pebblits can be found in many areas in Eldin, often near Lava. is the family name of several female members of the Sheikah, a mysterious tribe that has served and protected the Royal Family of Hyrule for many generations. Many Sheikah of the name so far have been associated with and taken on the role of accompanying an incarnation of Princess Zelda, being like a bodyguard or attendant of sorts in some games. In addition, every Impa has given extensive information and guidance to the various incarnations of Link they encounter in their time. Biography thumb|left|x120px|Link aiding Impa from In , Impa appears in the game as an Old Woman, however she is only named in the game's manual. When Hyrule was under attack by Ganon's forces in , Princess Zelda ordered her old nursemaid Impa to secretly flee and find the one who could save them. Ganon soon found out and sent his men after Impa. Though she managed to stay out of their reach for a long time, she was eventually captured. However, she was saved by a strange boy who managed to chase away Ganon's henchmen. Knowing that this was the one she had been looking for, Impa told him the whole story and asked him to go save Princess Zelda. Manual; Page 3-4 thumb|left|x120px|Impa showing Princess Zelda to Link from In , Impa had resumed her normal duties. One day, Link came to her because he was worried about a strange mark that had appeared on his hand. Manual; Page 3-4 When Impa saw the mark, she was initially startled, but quickly regained her composure. She then took Link to a door in North Castle that only the members of her family knew how to open. In the room behind the door lay a princess of Hyrule from ancient times and before Link could ask any questions, Impa told the princess' story. Manual; Page 5-6 When she was done telling, she picked up six Crystals and a scroll lying on a stand next to the altar and gave them to Link. She explained that these items were handed down in her family for generations while waiting for the one who was chosen by destiny to save the princess. Manual; Page 7-8 Manual; Page 9-10 She implored Link to follow his destiny and save the princess, to which he agreed. Manual; Page 11-12 thumb|left|x120px|Impa escaping from Ganondorf with Princess Zelda from In , Impa was born and raised in Kakariko Village, the village of the Sheikah. Though Hyrule Castle became her new home, she still kept a watching eye over Kakariko, but most of her attention went to the young princess. Until Link came along, Impa was the only one who believed her visions. Link met Impa for the first time in Hyrule Castle, where she taught him "Zelda's Lullaby." She then helped him leave the castle. "" is a Main Quest in . Overview At New Serenne Stable, Link can encounter Cado and his Donkey looking out toward the North Hyrule Plain. He is relieved to see that Link has reappeared after going missing, but he then asks where Zelda is. Upon hearing Link's explanation, he is shocked to hear that she is still unaccounted for. Upon hearing that she is still missing, Impa declares that they must continue to search for her. She explains that when the Upheaval began, Geoglyphs appeared all throughout Hyrule, and she and Cado have been traveling to investigate them. He can also throw Items related to Fire below the Balloon, such as a Fire Fruit or a Ruby. After lighting a Fire in Impa's Hot-Air Balloon, she and Link will begin to float into the Sky. are recurring locations in . Inns go unnamed in . Features and Overview The only Inn in is the Happy Hearth Inn in Hyrule Town. Staying there costs Rupees, but Link will have his Life Energy restored and receive a Kinstone Piece as a gift for staying. The Happy Hearth Inn is also the location where the three Oracles can be found before they rent out Vacant Houses from Gorman. There are numerous Inns across Hyrule Kingdom in . Inns are typically found in major settlements, where they offer guests regular Beds ranging from free to 20 Rupees a night to restore Link's Life Gauge, or more expensive Beds which grant Extra Hearts in addition to restoring Link's Life Gauge. Inns that charge 40 Rupees for their expensive Beds will grant a single Extra Hearts whereas Inns that charge 80 Rupees per night come with additional services and grant two Extra Hearts. However, the Extra Hearts granted from Inns are not successive and can only restore to the level of Extra Hearts that they are intended to grant. If Link has any Extra Stamina while resting on an 80 Rupee charge, the active Stamina Wheel for his Extra Stamina will also be completely filled regardless of the original amount of Extra Stamina that he possessed. Stables also double as Inns, and each Stable offers Beds ranging from 20 to 40 Rupees. The Great Deku Tree's Navel and the unnamed Inn in Tarrey Town are the only Inns which do not charge Link to stay the night. However, they do not offer any expensive bedding options and cannot grant any Extra Hearts or Stamina. List of Inns Inns reappear in . They serve the same purpose as they did in , although some prices have since changed. List of Inns Other Appearances The Elde Inn appears in the Kakariko Target Practice Stage in .

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Inogo Bridge is the westernmost bridge that spans the Zora River in the Lanayru Great Spring. It features two large pillars on its northern end, marking the beginning of the path to Zora's Domain. During Divine Beast Vah Ruta's rampage, Rain will constantly fall on Inogo Bridge and the surrounding area. As Link travels through the Lanayru Wetlands, several Zora will direct him to meet with Sidon at Inogo Bridge. Once he reaches the Bridge, Sidon will call out to him from one of its pillars. Recognizing Link to be a Hylian, Sidon asks if he could speak with him. During their conversation, Sidon states that he has been searching for a Hylian to assist him in appeasing Divine Beast Vah Ruta, and he asks if Link would be willing to help him. If Link agrees, Sidon will give him an Electro Elixir to use, since the path is filled with Electric Monsters. Sidon then decides to scout ahead and jumps into the Zora River. Following their conversation, the "Reach Zora's Domain" Main Quest will begin.

, also known as , and Bug Parts, are a group of Enemies, Creature, and Item found in various games throughout the . With the exception of Shadow Insects, Bugs do not have plot-relevance; their role is usually limited to sidequests. Location and Uses left Generic, blue beetle-like Bugs can be stored in Bottles in . They can be found under small Rocks and inside Bushes or they can be purchased at the Medicine Shop for 50 Rupees. Each Bottle holds three individual Bugs which, when released, will scatter around for a few seconds, and then dig underground, never to be seen again. Their preferred breeding grounds are mounds of soft soil. These seemingly insignificant Bugs benefit Link greatly while he searches for Gold Skulltulas. If Link finds a mound of soft soil to drop them on, they will burrow into the soil and in so doing may reveal a Gold Skulltula. Since three Bugs appear every time they are released, this can be useful to increase or maintain Bug supply by releasing and re-catching Bugs in new Bottles. This trick can also be used for quick money in , as they can be sold to the Buyer for 50 Rupees per Bottle. Bugs take a similar role to their iteration in . If Link releases a Bottle of Bugs near a mound of soft soil, different items such as Rupees, Arrows, and Bombs will come out. This happens everywhere that patches of soft soil are found, with the exception of the Swamp Spider House, where Gold Skulltulas are released instead, much like in . left The Bugs of , Golden Bugs, are found all over Hyrule. A child in Hyrule Castle Town, Agitha, fancies these Bugs and sent invitations to 24 Bugs around Hyrule for a ball. Unfortunately, it seems none have arrived, and she asks for Link's help in bringing all the Golden Bugs to Agitha's Castle. She will reward Link generously upon finding and giving her the Bugs. Collecting them all leads to two Wallet upgrades, each with a higher maximum Rupee capacity. The collection of Golden Bugs is an optional Sidequest and is not required for completion of the game. There are 12 types of Golden Bugs, and a male (♂) and female (♀) of each type, for a total of 24 to bring back to Agitha for her Bug ball. Both male and female variations of a single Bug exist in the same region, relatively nearby, thus making the hunting for a pair easier. Bugs are a collectible item found in both the The Sky and on the The Surface in . At night, they can be sold to Strich, who is particularly fond of them, or used to upgrade Potions at the Infusion Shop. Insects are abundant on Bug Rock in the Thunderhead. At Bug Rock, Stritch runs a mini-game called Bug Heaven during the day, which involves catching specific Bugs within a certain time limit. Beedle owns a pet Bug called the Horned

them, or used to upgrade Potions at the Infusion Shop. Insects are abundant on Bug Rock in the Thunderhead. A small marsh can be found on the southwestern side of Irch Plain, at the edge of which is a Wagon that can be searched for Gems. During the "Silent Princess" Recovered Memory, Zelda and Link are seen taking Pictures of the Flowers on Irch Plain with the Sheikah Slate. She then spots a Silent Princess, which she explains is rare and endangered. Though she is visibly saddened, her demeanor changes when she notices a Tireless Frog nearby. She informs Link that Hyrule Castle has been conducting research on ingesting them. Despite not being in a controlled environment, she decides that Link would be perfect for the study, and she encourages him to eat the Tireless Frog that she has caught. After Link receives the "Captured Memories" Main Quest, he can recall this Memory on Irch Plain. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Irch Plain. In the marsh on the south end of the Plain, there is a large Tree with a Rock on top of it. If Link picks up the Rock, it will be revealed as a Natural Hiding Spot, and a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

They can often be seen walking along the sand or in Shallow Water, or hiding under Rocks. When approached, they will scurry away, but usually are not very fast and can be caught easily. Eating one raw will restore one Heart to Link's Life Gauge. They can also be roasted by a Fire to become Blackened Crabs or chilled by Ice to become Frozen Crabs. Cooking a dish with Ironshell Crabs will increase Link's defense when eaten. Ironshell Crabs, or other crabs, are required in a Cooking Pot to make a Crab Omelet with Rice, Crab Risotto, Crab Stir-Fry, and Salt-Grilled Crab. Any snail or crab can be used to make a Seafood Skewer. They also count as seafood when making Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. is a recurring character in . Biography Isha is a jeweler who owns and works at the Starlight Memories Jewelry Shop in Gerudo Town. According to Cara, Isha's real name is Jewel, but she goes by an alias to avoid the being a jeweler named Jewel. In the past, she and Ashai were involved in a love triangle with Aurie Taamu, but they both have remained single since then. Cara has also heard that Isha sleeps wearing nothing but Accessories. Despite claiming to do nothing special with her looks, Isha visits the Hotel Oasis once a week. When Link first arrives in Gerudo Town, he will find Isha wandering around in front of Starlight Memories. If Link speaks to her, she initially greets him, but she then realizes that she is pressed for time and should not have done so. If Link asks what the problem is, Isha explains that she has run out of the Flint she needs to make her Accessories. She then says that if someone would give her 10 pieces of Flints, she would offer a nice reward. However, she believes that no one would really do that for her. If asked about her Accessories, Isha explains that she uses Rubies, Sapphires and other Gems to make the Accessories and that each Gem has a unique power that transfers into the wearer. Unfortunately, without Flint, Isha cannot make any Accessory. At this point, Link receives the "Tools of the Trade" Side Quest. Isha then apologizes for having nothing to show him. Once Link has collected 10 pieces of Flint, he can return to Gerudo Town to offer them to Isha, much to her surprise. She thanks Link, but since he has been so kind to her, she offers to make an Accessory for him. Link is then able to choose if he wants the Ruby Circlet, Sapphire Circlet, or Topaz Earrings. When Link makes his selection, Isha remarks that she had a feeling that would be the one he picked, before she takes a moment to prepare his reward. After giving Link his Accessory, Isha offers him a special discount at Starlight Memories. However, she asks him not to inform her other customers of this deal.| When she finishes speaking, the Side Quest will be completed. Afterwards, Link can purchase a variety of jewelry Accessories from Isha at Starlight Memories. If asked, Isha will explain that wearing Gems grants a form of protection. She goes on to say that Sapphire offer Heat Resistance, while Rubies offer Cold Resistance. By crafting circlets and earrings with these Gems, she is able to channel their powers to protect their wearers. Since the Materials needed to make them are difficult to acquire, she needs her customers to bring them to her. While it will take time to craft, Isha guarantees Link will be satisfied with the result. She also claims that her Accessories can be enjoyed by both men and women, making them great gifts for others. Like most other

Link switches to wearing the Hero's Clothes after being gifted them by his Grandma. In the Second Quest, Link is instead gifted the invisible Hero's New Clothes, which he wears on top of his Pajamas. This allows Link to instead continue in his adventure with special dialogue addressing Link's blue clothing instead of his standard green. Upon first meeting Link, Medli will comment on the color of Link's clothing and the "crawfish" design on them. The Island Lobster Shirt is a piece of Armor introduced in The Champions' Ballad DLC pack as part of the "EX Treasure: Garb of Winds" Side Quest. It is a priceless relic that was once kept safely within the walls of Hyrule Castle, but was later stolen by Misko. Misko hints at the whereabouts of the Island Lobster Shirt in Misko's EX Journal 2 in the Deya Village Ruins, claiming that it rests at the mouth of the Menoat River. are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Items are anything that is stored within a character's Inventory, often usable multiple times. Items are separate from Objects, which are things that exist outside of Inventories. Items do not necessarily have to be visible within the Inventory to be considered Items. Some Items may also overlap with characters, enemies, or Objects. For instance, characters such as Child and the Deku Princess, enemies such as Bees and Bomblings, and objects such as Braziers also double as Items. Five different types of Items are utilized in . Within the Inventory, Link can select and use up to eight Items at any given time. Link also has access to six other Items which activate at contextually specific times, such as the Stepladder, which is used whenever Link approaches small gaps. Other Items of this type include the Raft, Book of Magic, Magical Key, and the Power Bracelet. Link's Inventory also contains a space for the Triforce Shard of the Triforce of Wisdom, which is used in the final battle against Ganon. The fourth set of Items are those displayed within the HUD. These are Rupees, Keys, and the Hearts in Link's Life gauge. Like the second set of Items, these are also used under certain conditions, such as when purchasing other Items or taking damage. Though they do not appear directly in his Inventory, Link can also obtain other Items such as the Sword, which is automatically equipped to Link. Items are found on Item Podiums in ; several of them are located in each Stage. They store Items for Link to obtain, since he may only hold one Item at once. Once Link takes the currently-stored Item, his previous Item will replace it. There are three main categories of Items in : traditional Items that Link can use to overcome obstacles in his adventure (appearing in the Items Screen), quest-related Items that are usually delivered or given to other characters to advance the story (appearing on the Quest Status Screen), and collectible Items such as Rupees and Kinstone Pieces. Several Items (the Smith's Sword, Small Shield, Boomerang, Bomb, and Bow) have different variations or upgrades that can be obtained, though most of them are optional and are not required to complete the game. is a recurring character in . Biography Ivee is a young Hylian woman who lives in Hateno Village. She can typically found sweeping the ground outside of the East Wind with her Broom. When it is Raining outside, Ivee will move from her usual spot to sweep underneath the canopy instead. Ivee stays outside until 9:00 PM, when she decides to turn in. At night, she sleeps on the second floor above the East Wind, along with her brother Azu and her mother Amira. Whenever Link passes by the General Store, she will call him over with a wave and a greeting. If it is their first meeting, she will bring up the nice weather to him. She then mention that the East Wind is open for business and urges Link to check the stock inside. After their initial encounter, Link can ask Ivee a couple of questions. Should Link inquire where he is, she will happily identify the East Wind again, assuring Link of the quality of their products. If Link decides to ask Ivee who she is, she will be shocked by the question before bringing herself to properly answer. She will continue to stumble over a formal greeting before going with an informal one. The next time he asks, she assures him that she will introduce herself as many times as he likes. If Ivee is finally able to get out the formal greeting she was trying to find before, she will be pleased pleased with herself. When Link leaves the conversation, she responds by asking him to return to the shop later. While Ivee is heading to her bed, Link will not be able to ask her any questions. If he speaks to her during this time, she mentions that even though the hour is late, the East Wind is still open. Even while asleep, she dreams of beckoning patrons into the General Store. Ivee has a Diary sitting on a side table next to her bed. Within, she has written down Recipes for three different meals. Like other residents of Hateno Village, Ivee has a unique reaction when Link speaks to her while carrying the Blue Flame. She recognizes the Flame as something Purah used to carry around. Ivee can be seen sweeping the exterior of the East Wind in Hateno Village. She now wears a large Mushroom hat.

is a recurring character in . Biography Izra is a Stable Worker at Wetland Stable. At night, he dozes near the center of the Stable, though he denies falling asleep. During the Rain, he flees inside the Stable, and he laments that the men visiting will track mud all over. When Link first arrives at Wetland Stable, he will find Izra investigating the banks of Hylia River. Since he is afraid of deep Water, he mutters to himself that he is unsure what to do. However, when he notices Link listening to him, he apologizes for being lost in thought. If Link asks, Izra explains that he can see a shape at the bottom of the River that he believes to be a Treasure Chest. Unfortunately, he has no way to reach the Chest, but he is so curious about it that he has been unable to sleep. After he finishes speaking, the "Riverbed Reward" Side Quest will begin. Link can pull the Treasure Chest out of Hylia River using the Magnesis Rune, much to Izra's surprise. When Link speaks to him before opening Chest, Izra will be amazed and urges him to open it. After Link does so, he asks what he found. If Link tells him that it was treasure, Izra will be disappointed, as he could have become rich and attracted many women. Alternatively, if Link tells him it was a Sword, Izra will brush it off, since it was not what he wanted. Ultimately, Izra will be able to relax now that he knows the contents of the Treasure Chest, and the Side Quest will be completed. During the day, Link can find Izra searching the Wagons and boxes at Wetland Stable for anything useful that has been left out. He suggests that one could investigate the destroyed Wagons on the roads to find something useful. He also tells Link to ask Ami for information about the area, remarking that he enjoys having a younger brother who can pull his weight.

The is a recurring location in . The Jail goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Situated near the middle of Windfall Island, the Jail is where alleged criminals on the island are sent. A long time ago, the thief that stole a Picto Box from Lenzo was imprisoned here. The thief later escaped the Jail by tunneling out, though the Picto Box was left behind. It is in the Jail where Tingle is imprisoned after being accused of being a troublemaker, though he claims that he is innocent . Link can press a Switch hidden behind a cluster of Vases to free Tingle, who will thank him by giving him the Tingle Tuner. In , Tingle will instead give Link the Tingle Bottle. Moreover, he gifts Link a Map with the location of his island, and tells him that if he ever needs help with reading charts to "just leave it to Tingle." Once Tingle is freed, Link can enter the cell and push the crate that is against the wall to reveal a small hole through which he can crawl. Inside the hole is the Jail Maze, a complex crawlspace riddled with dead-ends guarded by Rats who will activate Trapdoors, sending Link into the water where he first met the King of Red Lions. If Link successfully navigates the Maze, he will find a hidden room where the Picto Box is kept in a Treasure Chest. There are two Stone Tablets in this room; one explaining the culprit's story, while the other explains the controls of the Picto Box. Enemies The Jail is located within the Gerudo Shelter beneath Gerudo Town. It is guarded by Katta, a Gerudo Soldier.

is a recurring character in . Biography Jana is a young Hylian woman who lives at South Akkala Stable in the Akkala Highlands. Starting at 5:00 AM, she tends to the flowers in front of the Stable. She works until 9:00 PM, at which point she sits under a large Tree nearby. If it Rains, she will seek shelter under that same Tree. Upon first meeting Jana, she will be abrasive towards Link, and she asks him not to bother her as she is thinking about something. Link can speak to her younger sister, Gleema, to learn that Jana likes Armoranths. Upon remembering that this is a secret, Gleema says that Jana will be mad at her again. If Link talks to Jana while he has at least one Armoranth in his Inventory, she asks if he can give it to her. If he does, Jana thanks him and reveals that it is her favorite plant, and since he happened to have one, they could get along with each other. Jana then asks Link why he came to Akkala, as she believes there is nothing interesting in the Region. If Link responds that he is a traveler or just wandering, Jana will have a request for him. Gleema is a fan of Insects, which Jana does not understand. Supposedly, there is a type of Insect that Gleema wants to see, but she will not tell Jana what it is. Therefore, she asks Link if he could figure out what the Insect is, as Jana wants to know for Gleema's birthday. After this, the "Little Sister's Big Request" Side Quest will begin. After beginning the Side Quest, Link can ask Jana about Gleema. When asked about her sister during the day, Jana mentions that Gleema is looking for Insects. If it is nighttime when Link asks, Jana states that Gleema is probably asleep. She then reminds Link to find out what the Insect that Gleema wants to see is. When Link next speaks to Gleema, she shares that Jana hates dragonflies. Gleema recounts that she was once reading a book about Insects that contained depictions of a Warm Darner, a Cold Darner, and an Electric Darner. However, when she showed the dragonflies to Jana, she said they were creepy and got mad at her. When she remembers that this is a secret, Gleema realizes that Jana is going to get mad at her again. Gleema thinks the only reason Jana found the pictures creepy was because they were close up, and they would be much cuter in real life. Once Link returns to Jana, she is shocked to hear that Gleema wants to see the three different types of dragonflies. She realizes that the reason Gleema never told her about her wish was due to her hatred of dragonflies. Since it is for Gleema's birthday, Jana asks Link if he could find a Warm Darner, Cold Darner, and an Electric Darner for her. When Link has collected all three dragonflies, Jana

realizes that the reason Gleema never told her about her wish was due to her hatred of dragonflies. Since it is for Gleema's birthday, Jana asks Link if he could find a Warm Darner, Cold Darner, and an Electric Darner for her. When Link has collected all three dragonflies, Jana will nervously ask for them. Unfortunately, once she sees them, she is unable to get over her fear and instead asks Link to deliver them to Gleema on her behalf. After receiving the dragonflies, Gleema will excitedly run over to show them to her older sister, much to Jana's horror. After she manages to calm down, Jana decides to reward Link for his help. She then gives him a Silver Rupee. While she is fine with most Insects, she explains that she does not like dragonflies. She takes a deep breath to calm herself, after which the Side Quest will be completed. When Link approaches Jana after completing the Quest, she will recognize him. In the morning, she remarks that he is up early. At night, she encourages him to stay at South Akkala Stable if he needs somewhere to stay. She also makes comments on the weather, noting if it has cooled down or if it is Raining. When Link ends his conversation with her, she tells him to take care. Link is able to ask Jana several questions. If Link has already started the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, he is able to ask Jana about Hudson. She says that he mentioned building a town before he left for Lake Akkala. She informs Link that Lake Akkala is east of South Akkala Stable, and she encourages him to check it out if he is curious. Next, if Link asks Jana who she is, she states that she is the second eldest of her sisters. She works on the flower patch while her older sister Kaifa takes care of the livestock. Jana will also say what Gleema is doing. She mentions that, while she does not care about most Insects, there is a certain type that she is unable to stand. If Link chooses to ask about where they are, Jana tells him that they are at South Akkala Stable. East of the Stable, Jana says Link will be able to see both Lake Akkala and the Akkala Sea, but those are the only interesting attractions in the area. Jana remains working at South Akkala Stable with her family. Occasionally, Jana will stop and look at a picture depicting a Dondon. If Link speaks to her, she will mention the rumors about them and express skepticism, as she does not believe anything she has not seen for herself. However, if Link tells her the truth about Dondons, she will be pleasantly surprised and thank Link for telling her.

is a character in . Biography Jatora is one of six Koroks that can be found in the Great Hyrule Forest Depths during the Main Quest "Trail of the Master Sword". Both Jatora and Maheli are located between the Great Deku Tree's roots and an Ascend Access Point in Korok Grove. The pair initially left Korok Forest to take a walk with Tasho, Mopu, Nako, Mokka, and Raha, but they were unable to pass through the Lost Woods upon their return. They then entered the Depths through the Minshi Woods Chasm, hoping it could lead them back to Korok Forest. When Link speaks to Jatora, they recognize the roots in front of them belong to the Great Deku Tree, meaning that Korok Forest is directly above them. They then wonder whether the Great Deku Tree could suck them up through his roots and bring them to the Surface, before asking if that is silly.

is a recurring character in . Biography Jengo is a Goron miner who works for the Goron Group Mining Company at the Southern Mine in the Eldin Canyon. During the day, Jengo mines alongside Dorill and Greyson for Gems. At night, Jengo takes his break next to the Cooking Pot while Bohrin works the night shift. Jengo is focused on his work, so much so that he is startled when Link approaches him during this time. He prefers not to be disturbed until he is on his break. If Link keeps speaking to him, he informs him that it is not yet time for his break. When he is finished with work for the day, Jengo asks that Link wait until he sits down before they talk. During Jengo's break, Link is able to ask him questions. Should Link ask about Jengo, he will introduce himself himself. He explains that because he and the other Gorons are digging up Gems, Goron City is able to prosper. If Link asks about their location, Jengo explains that they are at the Southern Mine. If Divine Beast Vah Rudania has not been calmed, Jengo shares that the Goron Group Mining Company used to mine at the Death Mountain Summit before the Divine Beast appeared, forcing them to move to the Southern Mine. He tells Link to speak with Bludo, the boss of the Gorons, for more information. After the Divine Beast has been calmed, Jengo excitedly reveals that Bludo has instructed them to start mining again.

is a recurring character in . Biography Jerrin is a Hylian researcher who lives in the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab with her husband, Robbie. The focus of her research is Ancient Shrines. She previously worked as a research assistant to Purah at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab, but Impa had her sent to help Robbie instead. After arriving at the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab, she began to carry the Blue Flame from Tumlea Heights, and she also reworked Robbie's design for the Ancient Oven. Not long after, they ended up married. When the Ancient Oven's redesign was completed, Jerrin became jealous of Robbie's interactions with the machine, which Robbie referred to as "Cherry" after his first love. Though she knew her feelings were illogical, she was in tears when she finally admitted them to Robbie. The pair decided to restore Cherry's mechanical way of speaking, and Robbie instead began to refer to it as the Ancient Oven. Some time after this incident, Jerrin gave birth to her and Robbie's son, Granté. When Link first arrives at the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab, Jerrin will stand by as Robbie confronts him for trespassing. Afterwards, if Link tries to talk to Jerrin, she calls him suspicious and refuses to speak with him unless he proves that he knows Robbie. Due to trade secrets, she is wary of sharing information with Link. Once Link has confirmed his identity to Robbie, Jerrin will excitedly greet him with an imitation of Purah. However, she becomes concerned that it was too much for their first meeting. If Link agrees it was too much, Jerrin assures him that everything is fine. Alternatively, if Link tells that it was not too much, Jerrin is relieved that he is so friendly. Jerrin then asks Link what he needs from her. If Link asks who she is, she will properly introduce herself. She explains that she is an amateur scholar with a focus on Ancient Shrines. The topic reminds Jerrin that Link needs to go to the left eye of Skull Lake, as there is an Ancient Shrine there. She informs Link that the left eye is higher up than the right eye, where Kilton sets up the Fang and Bone. This initiates "The Skull's Eye" Shrine Quest. After Link completes the Shrine Quest, Jerrin will be able to tell that he visited Skull Lake. When Link is confused, Jerrin explains she has a magical Sheikah nose implant that enhances her sense of smell. At Link's silence, however, she reveals that she is joking. As Link appears to be humorless, she surmises that his visit to Zuna Kai Shrine did not go smoothly. She thanks Link for his report, but since the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab is short on funding, she is unable to give him a reward. Link can also ask Jerrin about Robbie, who she explains that he is a researcher of ancient civilizations who studied Guardians at Hyrule Castle 100 years ago. She also reveals that she and

the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab is short on funding, she is unable to give him a reward. Link can also ask Jerrin about Robbie, who she explains that he is a researcher of ancient civilizations who studied Guardians at Hyrule Castle 100 years ago. She also reveals that she and Robbie are married. This shocks Link, so Jerrin happily shares that they run the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab and have a son together. After hearing about Granté, Link can ask Jerrin about him. Jerrin asks Link if he has seen him during his travels. If Link says that he has, Jerrin will be relieved. She stills considers Granté to be a work in progress, and once he is done studying Armor, she hopes he will take over her own research. If Link says that he has not, Jerrin asks him to be nice to him if they ever meet. In subsequent conversations, if Link changes his answer about whether or not he has met Granté, Jerrin will notice the discrepency. Since the start of the Upheaval, Jerrin and Robbie have resided at Lookout Landing. Jerrin can be found in the Emergency Shelter, where she uses a Broom to clear away dust. When Link approaches Jerrin, she recognizes him, and she invites him to make use of the Emergency Shelter's services. However, she warns him not to kick up any dust, since she has spent a lot of time cleaning. In particular, she has noticed that the spot that she is cleaning gets incredibly dusty.

is a recurring character in . Biography Jiahto is a Zora historian who studies and preserves the history of Zora's Domain. He spends his days in the Sleeping Chamber examining the Stone Monument at its rear. If Link approaches Jiahto before calming Divine Beast Vah Ruta, he will find him lost in thought. When Link asks him what is wrong, Jiahto will initially believe him to a be a traveler. He explains that the Stone Monument contains the history of the Zora as told by King Dorephan, which he is rereading so he can record it in a Book. When Link expresses that Jiahto's plan sounds difficult, Jiahto will finally recognize him. He blames Link for stealing Mipha from the Zora. He proclaims that he will never be able forgive Link. No matter how Link responds, Jiahto accuses him of not understanding what he has done. He explains that not only did the the Hylians fail to stop Calamity Ganon, they also caused Mipha's death. Due to this, he refuses to forgive the Hylians for what happened. Despite his prior statement, after Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, Jiahto will admit to Link that he misjudged him. Now that he can see the Divine Beast aiming at Hyrule Castle, he is confident that Mipha will still be able to assist in defeating Calamity Ganon. Jiahto apologizes for not properly introducing himself earlier, and he describes his role as a historian to Link. However, he is concerned by the condition of the History of the Zora, Part Seven, as it has become deteriorated over time. He is worried that the rest of the Stone Monuments are in a similar condition. Jiahto reiterates his desire to transcribe their contents into a Book. Due to Jiahto's age, though, traveling to all 10 Stone Monuments will take some time for him. Therefore, he asks Link if he could find the 10 Monuments and relay their contents to him. If Link agrees, Jiahto is relieved that the Champion will be assisting him. He informs Link that one of the Stone Monuments details the location of a treasure, which he tells Link to keep should he find it. Jiahto expresses his belief in Link, after which the "Zora Stone Monuments" Side Quest will begin. During the Side Quest, Link can speak to Jiahto to have him share the location of one of the Stone Monuments that he has not read yet. If Link does so, Jiahto will randomly select one of the Monuments to share the location of. Once Link has read all 10 Stone Monuments, he can return to the Sleeping Chamber to inform Jiahto of what he has learned. After hearing the contents, Jiahto remarks that many of the details of the Zora have been recorded, and thanks to Link, he has been able to gather all of that information. He thanks Link for helping him and rewards him with a Diamond. After this, the Side Quest will be completed. If Link has

Jiahto remarks that many of the details of the Zora have been recorded, and thanks to Link, he has been able to gather all of that information. He thanks Link for helping him and rewards him with a Diamond. After this, the Side Quest will be completed. If Link has the maximum amount of Diamonds in his inventory, Jiahto will ask Link to return when he has free space. When Link speaks to Jiahto again, he will express his gratitude for reading all of the Stone Monuments. He feels responsible to ensure that King Dorephan's words are passed on for future generations. In addition, he promises to include a description of all Link did in his future Book, as well.

is a recurring character in . Biography Jini is a Hylian who resides at the Mounted Archery Camp in the Faron Grasslands. Alongside Straia, he is conducting an ecological study of the area. They were drawn to the Faron Grasslands when they heard of a Giant Horse living there that could not be found anywhere else. Due to monsters in the area, however, they have been unable to get close to it. When Link first approaches Jini, he recognizes him as a trained warrior. He then asks Link how confident he is fighting while riding a Horse. If Link claims to be confident, he asks if he would like to prove his skills. If Link is not confident, Jini will be concerned and asks if he wants to run some drills. Link can ask how he can prove himself, Jini introduces him to Horseback Archery. The goal is to shoot targets with Arrows while riding a Horse. With these drills, Jini claims that Link will be prepared to face off against mounted enemies. When Link agrees to attempt a drill, Jini remarks that such impulsiveness may save his life one day. However, if Link does not have a Horse with him, Jini tells him to find one before they can begin. He instructs Link to return to the nearby Highland Stable to retrieve his Horse, if he owns one. Jini asks for 20 Rupees in order to run a Horseback Archery drill,| which he guarantees is worth twice as much. While he lis happy running drills, he requires payment in order to meet his own needs. After completing a drill, Jini will call Link back to the Mounted Archery Camp. If Link hit less than 11 Balloons, he suggests trying to shoot while the Horse is trotting instead of galloping. There is no reward. Between 12 and 19 Balloons, Jini is not convinced of Link's skill and reminds him to keep his eye on the targets. As a reward, he gives Link 15 Arrows. When Link pops between 20 and 22 Balloons, Jini says he has the potential to be among the best archers and gives him the Knight's Bridle. Finally, if Link hits between 23 and 25 targets, Jini will say he has not seen someone so young with such talent in a long time. He does not believe that Link is actually over 100 years old and gives him the Knight's Saddle, as he no longer needs it. Once Link has received his reward, Jini asks if he would like to run another drill. If Link refuses, Jini reminds him not to be a stranger and to come back. If Link agrees, Jini says he made the right call and asks for 20 more Rupees. Once Link has paid, he needs to fix the Balloons that were destroyed on Link's previous run. After fixing up the Balloons, he is ready for Link to go again. Before running any drills, Jini will offer to sell Arrows or buy from

The , designated by the trial name Shape Rotation, is a location in . Entrance to the Shrine The Jiosin Shrine is a Shrine of Light on the Surface. It is located just outside the Hyrule Field Chasm in Central Hyrule. It corresponds to the Nisoij Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation The Jiosin Shrine focuses heavily on the precise use of the Ultrahand ability to manipulate the orientation of Objects. The starting room consists of a short hallway with a pit separating the hallway from the door to the next room and another room to the left from the Shrine entrance separated by a fence. The door across the pit cannot be reached because of its height and distance from the hallway where Link stands. A large Stone Slab in the room behind the fence can be used to cross the gap; however, it will not fit through the door that Link entered from. Link must use Ultrahand and rotate the Stone Slab in a position so it will fit through the X-shaped hole in the fence to reach the first room. Standing on either short end side of the Stone Slab will line it up with the hole when Link rotates, without needing to rotate the Stone Slab at all. The Stone Slab can then be laid across the gap to reach the door. The next area of the Shrine has two more fences separating rooms with large holes on either side. The room on the right side from the entry contains the large stone Block needed to progress. This Block appears as two cubes connected on the diagonal. Like in the previous room, the stone Block must be positioned using Ultrahand to fit through the hole in the fence. Standing at the back of the room and facing the fence, rotating the stone Block twice forward will allow it to be wiggled through the hole. However, rotating it two more times to the left will more cleanly line it up with the hole to fit through. An optional Treasure Chest can be obtained after getting the stone Block through this first hole. If Ultrahand is kept active from the previous hole, rotating the stone Block four times to the left will line up the stone Block with the hole in the ground which Link can use to climb up to the Treasure Chest, which contains a Hasty Elixir. The stone Block must be used a second time to reach the final room of the Jiosin Shrine, but it must first fit through another hole. Keeping the same rotation from the previous use of the stone Block through the hole, the following rotations will position the stone Block to fit through the fence: two right, two up, one left, two down. If the stone Block was used to reach the optional Treasure Chest, the order will instead be: two left, two up, one left, two down. Finally, in the room across the fence, rotating the stone Block

Block to fit through the fence: two right, two up, one left, two down. If the stone Block was used to reach the optional Treasure Chest, the order will instead be: two left, two up, one left, two down. Finally, in the room across the fence, rotating the stone Block twice up, once right, twice up, then twice right will allow Link to place the stone Block against the raised platform and climb on top of it to reach the end of the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Jiosin Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

The Jochi-iu Shrine, designated by the trial name Courage to Pluck, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Jochi-iu Shrine is situated on the North Akkala Foothill in Deep Akkala, between East Akkala Stable and the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab. It corresponds to the Ui-ihcoj Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of the interior of the Shrine.|The interior of Jochi-iu Shrine Jochi-iu Shrine opens into a great room that branches into three directions. On the right sits the end of the Shrine and a high ledge a high ledge with a Stone Chest can be found to the left. Directly opposite the entrance is a ramp that leads downward into a pit. Between the end of the Shrine and the downward ramp, there is a Concave Slot and a diode beside a floating Platform. A ledge below the Platform has an Electricity Generator and a broken circuit leading toward the diode. A bisected platform floats over the pit, housing a stack of Iron Boxes reminiscent of an Osiadan tower. A square-shaped Iron Box with a rimmed top design sits at the top of the tower holding an Ancient Orb. A metallic Treasure Chest also sits on a rear-side Iron Box on the fifth row from the bottom. In order to reach the end of the Shrine, Link must transport the Ancient Orb from the top of the tower to the Concave Slot near. This can be achieved through several means. The first method is to join two Iron Boxes from the tower and complete the circuit between the Electricity Generator and its diode. With the diode active, the floating Platform activates, moving between the floor of the room and the side of the tower. From the apogee of the Platform's path, Link can easily grab the Ancient Orb with Ultrahand and return to the Concave Slot. Alternatively, Link can destabilize the tower and force the Ancient Orb to fall toward him. Before the Orb falls into the pit below, Link can stop it with Recall and quickly grab it with Ultrahand to carry it to the Concave Slot. Regardless of the method that Link fills the Concave Slot, the portcullis to the end of the Shrine will permanently open for as long as Link is inside the Shrine, even if the Ancient Orb is removed. thumb|right|320px|alt= Screenshot of the bisected platform dumping its contents.|The platform beneath the tower giving way when Link stands on it The bisected platform holding the tower is prone to giving way, forcing its contents into the pit below under various conditions. The first condition is if Link attempts to stand on the platform or its contents. The second condition is if the Ancient Orb falls into the pit. If the Ancient Orb falls into the pit, the bisected platform will return to its original position and the tower will reset to its original configuration. Once the Ancient Orb has been used to activate the Concave Slot,

The second condition is if the Ancient Orb falls into the pit. If the Ancient Orb falls into the pit, the bisected platform will return to its original position and the tower will reset to its original configuration. Once the Ancient Orb has been used to activate the Concave Slot, the tower no longer resets with it at its top unless the Orb happens to fall into the pit. Following the Concave Slot's activation, the tower enters a second reset state. All previous conditions continue to apply, with one addition. The Treasure Chest located on the fifth row now forces the tower to reset if it falls into the pit, even if its contents are obtained. Similarly, regardless of whether the Treasure Chest has been opened or is sitting on stable ground, it will reappear on the tower as it resets if the Ancient Orb falls into the pit at any time. Finally, if both the Ancient Orb and the Treasure Chest are on safe ground and Link forces the bisected platform to dump its contents, the tower will not reset and both the Chest and Orb will remain in place. is a recurring character in . Biography Jogo is a Hylian man visiting Rito Village alongside his wife, Juney, for their honeymoon. The two of them are staying at the Swallow's Roost, where he can be found throughout the day. He wears a Snowquill Tunic and a pair of Snowquill Trousers. When Link first approaches Jogo, he asks if he has also come to stay in Rito Village. He is relieved to meet someone else who appreciates the town, admitting that he appreciates its simplicity. However, he regrets choosing it for his honeymoon, since Juney has been complaining about the cold and lack of activities. He fears that she will divorce him if he is unable to make amends with her. In order to make Juney happy, Jogo needs to make her Baked Apples. Unfortunately, he does not have the Flint he would need to start a Fire. Once he finishes speaking, "The Spark of Romance" Side Quest will begin. If Link speaks to Jogo with some Flint in his Inventory, Jogo will be able to smell it. He then asks Link if he would sell it to him. If Link agrees, Jogo will give him a Silver Rupee as payment. He is happy to be able to make Baked Apples for Juney. Since he will need to make more Baked Apples in the future, he asks Link to bring him Flint. After this, the Side Quest will be completed. Link can continue to sell Flint to Jogo so long as he has at least one in his Inventory. Depending on how many pieces of Flint Link has, Jogo will buy them in groups of one, five, 10, 30, 50, or 100. He repeats his claim that he needs more Flint to make for Baked Apples, explaining that Juney is obsessed with them. Jonsau Shrine, designated by the trial name Deep Force, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Jonsau Shrine can be found on Mercay Island in the Lanayru Wetlands. It corresponds to the Uasnoj Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation 320px|thumb|right|alt= A screenshot of Link using the Ultrahand Ancient Power to hold a water-resistant board underwater.|The solution to the Target Switch puzzle The entrance room to Jonsau Shrine features a pool with a structure above its center. Along the far wall, there is an entryway that is blocked by a portcullis. The pool's Water holds a spherical Float, and the structure above the pool bears a downward-facing Target Switch. This Target Switch can be activated by holding the Float below the Water with Ultrahand and releasing it to make use of the buoyant force, sending the Float into the Target Switch. Alternatively, the Target Switch can be activated with any strong force, such as being struck with a Bomb Flower. When activated, the Target Switch releases the portcullis, allowing entry into a hallway further into the Shrine. This hallway leads to another room with its own pool and structure with a downward-facing Target Switch. In this pool, there is a buoyant Board that can be used to activate the Target Switch and release the portcullis in this room. Link is then able to advance to the final room. 320px|thumb|right|alt= A screenshot of Link using a buoyant Float to bash through a Board blocking the rail structure in the final room.|Link using the Float to free the basket In the final room, there is a more complex structure set in a pool. This structure features a rail extending from the Water upward to a square platform with a hole in the middle. A basket set along this rail sits above the hole but is blocked by a wooden Board. By using the spherical Float in this pool, Link can dislodge the Board and send the basket falling down the rail. Link can then use the Float in tandem with the basket to ascend the rail platform, or use Recall to return the basket to its former position while he sits inside. Atop this platform, Link is able to walk over the gate barring access to the end of the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Jonsau Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Enemies Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Jora is a Hylian who travels the West Barrens of the Gerudo Desert alongside his friend, Dillie. The pair can be found under attack by two Bokoblins, during which time he states he is too pretty to die. If Link saves them, Jora will give him a Chilly Egg Pudding as a reward. Once he has been saved, Jora will express his excitement to find his future wife in Gerudo Town. He and Dillie will then begin to scout their surroundings. If Link speaks to Jora, he will explain that they are traversing the Gerudo Desert in order to find Gerudo Town. While he has been relying on Dillie for directions, Jora believes that they will be popular once they arrive. However, Dillie then reveals that he has been following Jora, at which point Jora asks when they decided he was the leader. Alternatively, if Link speaks to Dillie, he will try to cheer Jora up by reminding him that they will be in Gerudo Town soon. He offers to let Jora lead the way, but Jora is anxious about this. Jora is a member of the Zonai Survey Team.

is a character in . Biography Josha is a young Sheikah girl who resides at Lookout Landing. She notably refers to people by nicknames, such as calling Robbie "Goggles" or Link "Swordsman." Josha is a student of Purah's, and she is considered to be her favorite. Since the Upheaval, she has lead the Chasm Research and investigations into the Depths done by the Zonai Survey Team. However, she has not been allowed to visit the Depths herself due to her age. She has also contributed to the search for Zelda. Initially, Josha can be found looking into the window of the Research Lab on the Second Floor of Lookout Landing. When Link approaches, she begins to run toward him. If he walks out of her range, she will believe that she misidentified him. When she speaks to Link, she recognizes him and calls out for Purah, yelling that he has returned. Alongside Purah, Josha listens to Link's story about what happened Beneath Hyrule Castle, and she appears surprised afterwards. When Link speaks to her after starting "Crisis at Hyrule Castle", she sympathizes with Zelda, commenting on how scared she is thinking about being in her position. She then demands that Link go rescue Zelda.

Josiu Shrine, designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . In order to enter the Shrine, Link must first complete the Shrine Quest "The North Necluda Sky Crystal". Upon bringing the Mysterious Crystal from the nearby Sky Island to the Shrine, the entrance will appear.
