is a recurring character in . Biography Joute is a Hylian who travels with his Horse between Dueling Peaks Stable and Hateno Village. He carries a Wooden Shield and a Traveler's Sword. At both of his stops, he momentarily rests under a Tree before continuing his journey. If it Rains, he will seek shelter near Fort Hateno or the Equestrian Riding Course. Joute likes Horses more than he does people. In particular, he holds much affection for his Horse, referring to him as his "best horsey." He keeps track of his hunger as they travel together, and he makes remarks about needing to buff his Saddle. During the night, he is happy to be able to see the stars with his Horse. When it is Raining, Joute will inform Link that both he and his Horse dislike such Weather, so he tries to avoid it when he can. As he travels, Joute will have many Horse facts to share with Link, even if Link does not care to hear them. He tells Link that the secret to holding on to a Horse is to approach it from behind quietly and hop on quick. He recommends petting the Horse after getting on them "to let them know you care." If Link does catch a wild Horse, Joute to register it at a Stable, as they will give him a Saddle and Bridle. He also claims that Horses like Carrots and suggests buying them at Kakariko Village. Joute informs Link that Horses vary in the speed and power, so it is important for him to keep their strength in mind. He suggests that Link choose a Horse that suits his own needs. Since Horses will get tired if they run all the time, Joute advises Link to an eye on his Horse to make sure it is alright. Joute has a song to describe the different types of legendary Horses, the lyrics of which encourage the listener to go catch them. Though he describes it at slightly inaccurate, he believes it is a catchy tune. In order to make it work as a musical, he had to make it seems as though there were multiple of each legendary Horse. In general, Joute cares more about Horses than any local attractions. However, he does tell Link about the Equestrian Riding Course, which is in ruins. While it was once an important location, it is now suffering from an infestation of monsters. Joute will share that Horses are not the only Animals that will allow someone to ride them. While he does not think it would be worth it to ride anything else, he believes Link may be interested. He encourages Link to try to ride any Animal that looks mountable.

is a recurring character in . Biography Juannelle is a Hylian residing at Snowfield Stable in the Tabantha Tundra. She spends her days inside the Stable, where she writes in her journal. At night, she sleeps in one of the Stable's Beds. When Link first speaks to Juannelle, she explains that she has been all over Hyrule Kingdom in search of information. She has come to Hebra in search of a Stalhorse, but her efforts have been halted by the cold. If Link shows interest, Juannelle shares that she wants to see a Stalhorse with her own eyes. She thinks such a discovery would be a huge scoop. Since she is unable to go looking herself, Juannelle asks Link if he could take a Picture of one for her. If Link takes her offer, Juannelle will be pleased. She shares rumors that a Stalhorse can be found with Stalkoblins in the N. Tabantha Snowfield or near the North Lomei Labyrinth. She wishes Link luck in his search. After this, the "Stalhorse: Pictured!" Side Quest will begin. Once Link has a Picture of a Stalhorse, he can return to Snowfield Stable to show it to Juannelle. While the sight of a Stalhorse scares her, she is still pleased to receive a Picture of it. Now that she has the Picture, Juannelle is going to use it as inspiration to write an article. As a reward, she gives Link a Silver Rupee. She expresses her desire to work with Link in the future, at which point the Side Quest ends. When Link approaches Juannelle afterwards, she proclaims that she knows everything before asking if his name is Link. If Link confirms that he is, Juannelle states that she loves straightforward and honest answers. However, if Link instead instructs her to call him "Mr. Link," she reprimands him for acting coy. After confirming Link's identity, Juannelle offers to share information about the area with him. He is also able to wake her up at night to ask her questions, though Juannelle considers this to be rude. If Link asks about the Thyphlo Ruins, Juannelle explains that they are extremely dark, even during the day. She theorizes that there is a mysterious power behind the phenomenon. She believes that someone would become famous if they were able to find out what was hiding within the Ruins. Finally, she informs Link that they are located past Mount Drena in the direction of the Eldin Mountains. If Link asks about the far edge of the Hebra Mountains, Juannelle shares he story of an adventurer who attempted to journey to the northwestern corner of Hyrule Kingdom. However, before he was able to reach his destination, he was forced to turn back due to the cliffs and Updrafts. Juannelle asked the adventurer why he went so far out, and he told her it was because he wanted to know what was there. Juannelle is unable to understand his reasoning, as that would not be enough of a reason

forced to turn back due to the cliffs and Updrafts. Juannelle asked the adventurer why he went so far out, and he told her it was because he wanted to know what was there. Juannelle is unable to understand his reasoning, as that would not be enough of a reason for her to go out into the cold.

is a recurring character in . Biography Jules is a young Hylian woman who can be found in Gerudo Town. Jules visits many locations in the Town throughout the day, such as outside of the Jewelry Shop, Starlight Memories. If Link has not yet completed the "Tools of the Trade" Side Quest, Jules comments that she does not see any accessories on display and questions if the Shop is open or not. If the Side Quest is completed, Jules stands outside and decides that it is not her time to own jewelry, as she lacks the Materials needed and outright buying it from the store is expensive. If Link speaks to Jules while she is standing at Ardin's Stall, which sells a variety of Mushrooms, Jules will contemplate whether she should buy some Chillshrooms or some Sunshrooms. When the General Store is sold out, she buys into Ardin's lie that she is selling Mushrooms that only beautiful people can see. If Link speaks to her while she is in the center of Town or in The Noble Canteen, she will ask if Link's Gerudo Outfit is the clothing sold at Fashion Passion and mentions that she was thinking about buying some herself. She also asks if the clothes are comfy. Jules is suspicious that Link is a boy and asks if he is secretly in disguise. Link will react in surprise after having his cover blown, confirming her suspicions. She compliments Link on his ability to get into Gerudo Town without anyone noticing and assures him that she will keep the secret between them. Jules considers learning the Gerudo language while she is in Gerudo Town and again compliments Link that he makes a convincing girl. If Link speaks to Jules while she is in The Noble Canteen, she expresses how refreshing her drink is. Jules explains that all of the drinks made at The Noble Canteen are made from the Ice at the Northern Icehouse, which is the reason it is possible to have cold drinks in the middle of the Gerudo Desert. Jules comments that her drink is the Noble Pursuit, which is the signature product of the Canteen. If Link asks about the Icehouse, Jules explains that it is an underground Ice depository that harvests its supply from the Gerudo Highlands and stores it. If Link asks where it is, she tells him to go past the ruins to the north of Gerudo Town and he will find it. If Link warns Jules not to drink too much, she assures him that she is fine and is only going to have one more drink. Before the conversation ends, Jules struggles to remember the Gerudo word for "good-bye" until finally recalling that it is "sav'orq."

is a recurring character in . Biography Juney is a Hylian woman on her honeymoon in Rito Village. She spends her days sitting on the ledge between Kaneli's House and Teba's home. During the night, she sleeps at the Swallow's Roost. When Link first approaches Juney, she will be shocked to see another Hylian in such a remote location, and she asks if he is wandering around Hyrule in order to find himself. Juney explains that she is visiting Rito Village for her honeymoon, but she is not pleased with it. She believes that Gerudo Town or Zora's Domain would be more interesting, as Rito Village only makes her want to return home. Juney is angry at her husband, Jogo, for choosing this as their honeymoon destination. Though he has tried to apologize, Juney threatened to divorce him if he did not bring her a Baked Apple. After this, "The Apple of My Eye" Side Quest will begin. To complete the Side Quest, Link must bring a Baked Apple to Juney. When Link speaks to her with a Baked Apple in his Inventory, Juney will be able to smell it on him. She asks if she can have one, promising Link a present in return. If Link agrees, Juney will give him a Silver Rupee. Juney wishes Jogo would bring her Baked Apples more often, and she asks Link to bring her more in the future. This completes the Side Quest. After completing "The Apple of My Eye", Link can sell Baked Apples to Juney. She buys them in groups of one, five, 10, 30, 50, and 100. When Link agrees to sell to Juney, she promises that she will pay higher prices if he brings her more. If Link refuses, Juney will call him a cheapskate.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kabetta is the youngest of the Goron Blood Brothers, a group consisting of himself and his brothers Bayge and Heehl. Kabetta and his brothers are passionate about training in difficult feats of strength and endurance. However, he is more docile and meek than the rest of the Goron Blood Brothers. They all live in a house in southern Goron City, which has been left with a Sign saying they have gone to Gut Check Rock to train. Kabetta is involved in the "Test of Will" Shrine Quest at Mount Nabooru in the Gerudo Highlands. Kabetta and the other Goron Blood Brother have traveled to their ancestral training ground to train themselves to withstand the heat in Goron City. Kabetta and the others invite Link to partake in their challenge. If Link agrees, Kabetta will be inspired by his choice. The three Goron Blood Brothers will then step onto the platform, and the contest of endurance will begin once Link joins them. To complete the challenge, Link will have to outlast the Goron Blood Brothers on the platform. During the contest, Kabetta will have difficulty adjusting to the heat. Kabetta is the first challenger to collapse. After all three Gorons have collapsed, Link will be declared the winner. Once their first contest has been cleared, the Goron Blood Brothers then challenge Link to their contest f ultimate endurance, which Kabetta explains is the toughest challenge known to Gorons. He goes on to say that the next ring is even harder to withstand than the previous one. Passing this test is supposed to reveal an Ancient Shrine. While watching Link attempt the second challenge, Kabetta remarks that his soul is on fire. After Link has cleared the trial, Joloo Nah Shrine will rise from the ground nearby, which Kabetta is surprised by. If Link has yet to attempt the Gut Check Rock Challenge, Kabetta encourages him to try it out. If Link has already cleared the Gut Check Rock Challenge, Kabetta proclaims his respect for Link and resolves to beat it himself. Kabetta also appears at the base of the Gut Check Rock in northern Eldin Canyon, laying on the ground in exhaustion after failing his Gut Check Rock Challenge training. Despite his own failures, he encourages Link to attempt the Gut Check Rock Challenge for himself. During the "EX Champion Daruk's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, the Goron Blood Brothers will train at Darb Pond, since they heard Daruk did the same thing. The goal of the training is to stand on the Glowing Ring that has appeared on top of Darb Pond. However, Kabetta informs Link that they are unable to stand on Lava. He wonders whether Daruk actually completed this training, but he retracts that statement when he realizes it sounds like he is doubting Daruk. The Goron Blood Brothers then get together to strategize. After Link has passed through the Glowing Ring, Rinu Honika Shrine will

are unable to stand on Lava. He wonders whether Daruk actually completed this training, but he retracts that statement when he realizes it sounds like he is doubting Daruk. The Goron Blood Brothers then get together to strategize. After Link has passed through the Glowing Ring, Rinu Honika Shrine will rise from the ground. Kabetta is relieved by the disappearance of the Glowing Ring, as that means he will no longer have to attempt the training.

is a character in . Biography Kabok is a Hylian and a member of the Zonai Survey Team. During the Main Quest "The Dragon's Tears", Link is able to find Impa and Cado speaking to Kabok in front of Yamiyo Shrine, asking him if the Zonai Survey Team have discovered any new Geoglyph locations. He explains that the Zonai Survey Team have sent out Balloons in order to search for them, although their progress has been slow. He also notes that they could possibly use Skyview Towers as well, but worries that they are unsafe. Despite these challenges, Kabok assures that the Zonai Survey Team will support Impa's investigation.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kachoo is a Gerudo woman who manages the Kara Kara Bazaar Inn in the Kara Kara Bazaar. Recently, the Inn has been losing business due to the appearance of Divine Beast Vah Naboris in the Gerudo Desert, which upsets Kachoo. Kachoo assures Link that while the Divine Beast may be loud, the beds at the Inn are still comfy. After Link has calmed the Divine Beast, Kachoo is relieved that people will be able to sleep soundly at the Inn without the constant stomping. If Link speaks to Kachoo while wearing the Gerudo Outfit, she says claims the clothes look nice on him and that he could pass for a woman. Kachoo offers a regular Bed for 20 Rupees and a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. If asked, she explains that the Soft Bed is made from Cucco feathers and has been designed to leave its user full of energy when they wake up. The Kara Kara Bazaar Inn offers a mandatory wake-up shout, but Kachoo allows Link to choose when he receives it. She wishes Link a good rest before he goes to sleep. Kachoo will loudly greet Link when he wakes up. She tells him to be safe in his travels before he leaves.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Kaepora Pass is a road located in the Akkala Region. It starts in the Akkala Highlands at the East Sokkala Bridge, following the eastern edge of Hyrule until it reaches the East Akkala Stable in Deep Akkala. Along the way, it borders the East Akkala Plains and East Akkala Beach, and it passes through part of the North Akkala Foothill. At East Akkala Stable, it merges with the Shadow Pass. A small fork of the Kaepora Pass leads towards Tarrey Town on Lake Akkala, which is marked by a Sign. Another branch connects to the road north of the Torin Wetland. The Hylian traveler Lonni can be found on parts of the Kaepora Pass. Her journey on the Pass starts just north of Lake Akkala, and she travels to a small shack near the East Sokkala Bridge. Stamm also walks along Kaepora Pass between East Akkala Stable and Tarrey Town. Creatures Enemies Materials Creatures Materials

is a character in . Biography Kaffi is a traveler who can be found at numerous campsites throughout Hyrule. They are in search of Misko's treasure, which is rumored to be located in nearby Caves. When Link first encounters them at any camp, they are under attack from a Bokoblin. If Link helps them defeat it, they will thank him and reward him with Food. They then explain their reason for camping at that location and ponder aloud about leaving if they cannot find what they are looking for. After dealing with the Bokoblin and returning to their camp, they eventually disappear from a given camp until a Blood Moon resurrects the Bokoblins at their campsites. Kaffi can be found at the following locations in search of treasure:

is a recurring character in . Biography Kaifa is a young Hylian woman who works at South Akkala Stable as a Stable Worker. Her duty is to take care of the Stable's Cuccos and Highland Sheep. During Rain, she seeks shelter under one of the Trees behind the Stable. When Link first approaches Kaifa, she asks if he is a customer. Once Link has confirmed that he is, she will be relieved. Kaifa explains that a suspicious individual known as Kilton has been appearing all throughout Hyrule. He is supposedly the owner of the Fang and Bone, which she has heard only appears during the night. Due to the rumors, the nearby East Akkala Stable has hired security, and Kaifa warns Link to be careful. If Link speaks to Kaifa again, she becomes nervous and asks if he needs something. Link can ask her about Kilton again, and she admits that she does not feel secure, as the only man at South Akkala Stable is her father, Dmitri. She also thinks they should hire soldiers like the East Akkala Stable did. If Link asks Kaifa who she is, she will be thrown off guard. She then apologizes to Link. When he asks her a second time, she takes a moment before introducing herself. She explains that she is the eldest daughter at the Stable, but after that she is unable to continue. Link can ask Kaifa where they are, and she explains that they are at the South Akkala Stable. Due to the large number of Highland Sheep housed at the Stable, many customers refer to it as a Sheep Stable instead of a Horse Stable. While Kaifa is not good at raising Horses, she can do nothing to help the fact that they have had a lot of Highland Sheep births. Kaifa begins to shout as she wonders what is wrong with having a lot of Sheep. After a moment of silence, she apologizes to Link for her outburst. She will later claim that she does not care if the Stable is referred to as the Akkala Sheep Stable.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kairo is a Goron who travels the Mountain Road between Foothill Stable and the end of the Maw of Death Mountain. At the end of his trail, he stops to search for Gems before heading back. He used to work at the Goron Hot Springs, but he grew bored there and decided to travel the world as a Merchant. He carries a Traveling Pack on his journeys. Goron City is Kairo's hometown, and the reason he is so far away is to sell the Gems he has mined from Death Mountain. While he admits that the area can be dangerous at times, he claims there is an abundance of Gems to mine. He also mentions that he is friends with Yunobo, and he wonders how he is doing while he is away. Kairo considers himself to be more suited for the life of traveling Merchant, as he enjoys the scenery he sees along the way. He wants to see parts of the world he otherwise would not be able to in Goron City, such as cold locations, green Trees, and hills. He is interested in the Weather further away from Death Mountain, as there are no Magma Bombs falling from the sky. Since Link is a Hylian, Kairo warns him that he will need a way to protect himself from the Scorching Climate if he continues past the Maw of Death Mountain. He recommends the use of a Fireproof Elixir, but he is unable to remember any of the ingredients required beyond a Fireproof Lizard. He also warns Link about Magma Bombs, as getting hit by them would even hurt a Goron. Along his route, Kairo may be attacked by Fire Chuchus or other Monsters. If Link saves him, he may share his relief to live another day. He also has a chance to remark that he finds monsters to be scary. As a reward, he will give Link Hasty Steamed Mushrooms, a Sneaky Elixir, a Fireproof Elixir, or Rupees. Kairo sells a limited selection of Gems at a fairly low price. During Rain, Kairo will add rare Gems, such as Diamond, to his lineup. When Link buys from Kairo, he shows his appreciation for his business. As with all other Merchants, Kairo will buy Items from Link as well. He is grateful for any wares he is able to purchase from Link. Wares and Pricing Kairo is no longer a merchant but is still traveling in . He now travels with Zorona. According to Zorona, Kairo had such a bad sense of direction that it inspired Zorona to travel with Kairo. This works out well for the two of them, as Zorona is also a terrible cook and can rely on Kairo. Kairo partially blames the recent geographic changes surrounding Goron City for his poor direction, but Zorona constantly teases him nevertheless. Link can watch as Scorpis gives directions to Zorona and Kairo and then meet up with them as they travel

is also a terrible cook and can rely on Kairo. Kairo partially blames the recent geographic changes surrounding Goron City for his poor direction, but Zorona constantly teases him nevertheless. Link can watch as Scorpis gives directions to Zorona and Kairo and then meet up with them as they travel from Lookout Landing to Riverside Stable, to next to a tree on the path between Wetland Stable and Kakariko Village, and finally to just outside Gerudo Town. Along the way, Kairo often remarks how he wants to taste the Ring Ruins though Link will never meet up with the two in Kakariko Village. Later at Gerudo Town, Kairo will repeatedly demand for him and Zorona to be allowed in as he is under the assumption that another male friend of his was allowed. While it is never said who this friend is, it is likely Lyndae or Strade as both of these Gorons were allowed in during .

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Kakariko Bridge is a large, damaged stone brick bridge in West Necluda that spans Lake Siela. An oversized boulder is stuck in the eastern side of the Bridge, and many Rocks cover its surface. The Bridge serves as one of the means to enter Kakariko Village.The Hylian travelers Brokka and Bugut can be seen crossing it on their way to and from Kakariko Village. After Link has either completed the "Seek Out Impa" Main Quest or entered the Yiga Clan Hideout, a Traveler will appear at the northern entrance to the Bridge, waiting to ambush the Hylian Champion. A small patch of land beneath the Kakariko Bridge hosts a campsite. In this campsite, Link can find a lit Cooking Pot, which is flanked by a Roasted Bass and metal boxes that contain Arrows, Rupees, and cooked Food. A metallic crate sits atop some boulders in the waters east of the Kakariko Bridge. A metallic Treasure Chest hides behind two metallic crates in a small alcove north of the Cooking Pot and contains five Ice Arrows. A second metallic Treasure Chest containing an Opal can be found in the water beside these boulders. A wooden platform held aloft by Sky Octoroks appears due east of the Kakariko Bridge in Master Mode, bearing a metal Treasure Chest which contains a Boomerang. In the water on the western side of the Kakariko Bridge is a circle of rocky pillars. If Link throws a Rock into this circle, a Korok will appear. Creatures Enemies Equipment

(pronounced , ), also known as Kakariko Town, and the Peaceful Village, is a recurring location in . Kakariko Village goes unnamed in . Its geographical and historical situation seems to change in each game. It may have been inspired by various towns in and, in turn, may have served as the inspiration for such future towns in the series – Mabe Village, Clock Town, Lynna City, Horon Village, Windfall Island, Hyrule Town, and various minor villages. Features and Overview In , Kakariko Village is the largest settlement. It is located in the western side of the Light World, just south of the Lost Woods. Here there are several Merchants, as well as villagers with vital information for Link. Kakariko Village has a number of businesses, including Dwarven Swordsmiths, Shops, a Fortune Teller, a tavern, and an inn. Kakariko Village is the home of Sahasrahla, the famed elder, and his family, and it is with the intention to find him that Link first travels there. Upon arriving in Kakariko Village, Link discovers that he has been blamed for the abduction of Princess Zelda, and that some villagers who believe him to be guilty will summon Soldiers to arrest him. Others are more sympathetic, and the family of Sahasrahla will provide him with clues as to his whereabouts. After Link retrieves the Master Sword from the Lost Woods, Kakariko Village is overrun by Soldiers who will attack Link at sight, forcing the villagers to remain inside their homes. It is also at this point that Link can free the Flute Boy's Bird sealed within the Weathercock located in the middle of Kakariko Village. After Link receives the Whistle from the Flute Boy in the Dark World, he can play the Instrument in front of the statue to reveal a small Bird within. With the Flute Boy's Bird awakened, Link can call it to be transported to specific places in the Light World any time the Whistle is played. Blind the Thief, the leader of a gang of thieves, once lived in Kakariko Village, where his home served as the hideout for his mischievous companions. However, when Link visits his home, the hideout turns out to be vacant except for a couple of Treasure Chests left behind. During Link's adventure to rescue the Maidens, he journeys to Kakariko Village's Dark World counterpart: the Village of Outcasts, a town notorious for its corrupt establishments as well as the many thieves roaming around. It is here that he finds Blind the Thief, who reveals himself to be the Boss of the Dark World's fourth Dungeon: Thieves' Town. Areas Inhabitants In , Kakariko Village is located in the northeastern portion of Hyrule, right next to Hyrule Castle Town and at the foothills of Death Mountain. The town is an entrance to a number of locations, such as the Shadow Temple, the Bottom of the Well, the Graveyard, and the Death Mountain Trail. The village's origins are elaborated upon during the game, explaining that it was

Hyrule Castle Town and at the foothills of Death Mountain. The town is an entrance to a number of locations, such as the Shadow Temple, the Bottom of the Well, the Graveyard, and the Death Mountain Trail. The village's origins are elaborated upon during the game, explaining that it was founded by the Sheikah, the guardians of the Royal Family of Hyrule. Moreover, it is revealed that the village was home to only those pertaining to the Sheikah tribe, although it was later opened up to the poor commoners by Impa, who was also born and raised in Kakariko. As such, she is often considered the leader of Kakariko Village, not only for having helped the commoners of Hyrule, but also for her great efforts in turning the village into a great city to equal the bustling metropolis of Hyrule Castle Town. Kakariko Village as seen in is one of the most prominent locations in the game due to it being Link's primary destination many times during his adventure through Hyrule. The town is home to many important attractions, such as the windmill, which is used to draw water up from the well, the village's only source of water. It is also the location of the Kakariko Graveyard, where the souls of the fallen Hyruleans, Hylian Royal Family, and Sheikah tribe members are said to rest. The small town also contains many buildings of interest, including a Potion Shop, a Shooting Gallery (still under construction in the earlier time period), and a Bazaar. Some notable residents include the Cucco Lady, the Carpenters, the Graveyard Boy and his family, and Dampé. Through various actions, Link will obtain numerous items from this village, including the Lens of Truth, a Bottle, a Hylian Shield, and several Ocarina Songs, such as the Song of Storms, Sun's Song, and Nocturne of Shadow. Areas Inhabitants In , Kakariko Village appears almost identical to its appearance. It is located in the westernmost part of Hyrule, located directly south of the Lost Woods, and north of the desert. There are numerous shops, merchants and buildings in the town, and it even has its own Weather Vane, located in the same position as the Weathercock in . While the village is almost exactly alike to its predecessor, there are still some locations worth noting. The Milk Bar is located to the south, where Link can purchase Milk; it is also the basis for a bottle sidequest later on. There is a smaller shop located in the northern part of the village, where Link can purchase Shields, Scoot Fruit, and Foul Fruit. A Street Merchant can also be found in the village, slightly to the west of the Weather Vane. Other notable items Link can receive here are empty Bottles, the Smooth Gem, the Pegasus Boots, the Bug Net, and the Bee Badge. Link can also take part in the Fortune's Choice Mini-Game, which is found on the east side of town. Gramps is found in the western region of the village, and teaches Link about using the StreetPass feature to battle Shadow Links. Kakariko Village's Lorulean counterpart is Thieves' Town, which is home to the Thieves' Hideout and is where Link will find the portrait of the Sage Osfala. Kakariko Village has three Lost Maiamais hidden in it. One can be found on top of the roof with a rock on it - this requires a Cucco and the Power Bracelets to reach. Another is behind the Cucco Lady's house, in the patch of sand. It requires the Sand Rod to unearth it. The final one is in the tree in the southwest of town, and must be knocked down with the Pegasus Boots. Areas Inhabitants In , Kakariko Village is a settlement in the West Necluda region of Hyrule, north of the Dueling Peaks. One hundred years ago, during the Great Calamity, it avoided damage from the Guardian's assault. It contains several houses, gardens, and a selection of stores, including High Spirits Produce, a general store where travelers can purchase locally grown food and supplies; Shuteye Inn, which allows travelers to rest and regenerate Hearts; The Curious Quiver, a store that specializes in Arrows; and Enchanted, a boutique that sells Armor. Link is told to go to Kakariko Village after completing the four Ancient Shrines located on the Great Plateau, when the Old Man reveals himself to be the former King of Hyrule and informs Link of the events that transpired 100 years ago. The , also known as the Graveyard, and , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview In , Kakariko Village Graveyard lies behind Kakariko Village. During young Link's time, the gravekeeper Dampé oversees the Graveyard at night to promote his Heart-Pounding Gravedigging Tour Minigame, while in the daytime, a little kid roams around the graves instead. While Dampé is not out patrolling, he is sleeping inside his hut, which is located in the east corner of the graveyard. Within it Link can find the Gravekeeper's Diary, which talks about a treasure that he found while digging around. Poes of many fallen Hyruleans, Royal Family members, and the Sheikah tribe who founded Kakariko rest in the graveyard, and it is said that the latter watch over the spirits in their eternal slumber. The gravestones that have flowers in front of them can be pulled back to reveal a secret room or underground chamber. These often contain a Treasure Chest with a few Rupees, and one contains a Treasure Chest with a Hylian Shield. At the back of the graveyard rests the two famous Composer Brothers: Flat and Sharp, whose tombstones are separated by the Royal Family's Tomb. This tomb, which can only be opened by playing "Zelda's Lullaby" on the Ocarina, houses the Composer Brothers' "Sun's Song" as well as a poem to go along with said melody. After Link becomes an adult, he returns to the graveyard only to discover that Dampé has passed away. Link reads the Gravekeeper's Diary inside his hut, which beckons anyone who reads the text to come to his grave to receive the treasure he found seven years ago. The young hero can uncover Dampé's grave on the west side of the graveyard to race the deceased gravekeeper and receive the Hookshot from him. Even farther back, in a ledge high above the graveyard, is a small, concealed room with several torches and a sealed door decorated with the Sheikah symbol. Link can only access this chamber once he has learned the "Nocturne of Shadow" from Sheik, and uses it to travel to the area's Triforce Warp. By using Din's Fire in the middle of the room, the torches will light up, opening the sealed door and granting access to the Shadow Temple. thumb|right|300px|King Zora's tomb in In , the graveyard is also located behind Kakariko Village, accessed by entering the gate behind Renado's Sanctuary. is a recurring character in . Biography Kalani is a Gerudo child who lives in Gerudo Town. She and her sister, Makure, reside at the Arrow Specialty Shop Stall that their grandmother Danda manages. During the day, Kalani will stand in front of the Arrow Specialty Shop, where she encourages customers to buy from her grandmother. Even as she sleeps, Kalani will attempt to attract customers. She recommends each type of elemental Arrow, saying that Bomb Arrows go "BOOOOOM!!!", Shock Arrows go "BZZBZZT!!!", Ice Arrows go "CRAAAAACK!!!" and Fire Arrows go "BOOSH!!!". If Link buys all of the Arrows at the Shop, Kalani asks if he is a good person, since her grandmother told her that people who spend a lot of Rupees are good people. While Kalani running around Gerudo Town, she tells Link that she does not have time to greet people and that the Rito, Frita, will be gone if she does not hurry. If Link speaks to Kalani while she is staring at Frita, she comments about what a "big vure" she is. As the sun sets, Link can find Kalani and the other three children in Gerudo Town speaking to each other as a group. After Link completes the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Dalia will be late joining the group. During this time, Kalani asks the others if they have heard what happened to her crops. Makure comments that Dalia has not stopped crying. Pearle declares she will never forgive the person who destroyed Dalia's crops. Once all of the children are gathered together, Kalani asks them if they are in love. Makure then responds that she wants to attend Ashai's class when she grows up so she can get married. Pearle then comments that Ashai is unmarried, but she does not know what that word means. Lastly, Dalia says that she heard being in love is the sweetest thing in the world, but she does not think she can handle something sweeter than berries. At the end of the day, Kalani and Makure return to the Arrow Specialty Shop to sleep.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview Link can encounter Kaneli in the Flight Range hut, where he is searching for a volunteer. He explains that after he retired as chief of Rito Village, he decided to assist Rito warriors who are training at the Flight Range. While the Blizzard ended up damaging the training equipment, Kaneli decided to take it as an opportunity to create a new course. The new course focuses on agility by having participants pass through Floating Rings, which Kaneli hopes will result in the warriors becoming for confident in their flight. Since the course was just finished, however, no one has tried it yet, though Kaneli wishes someone will come soon. At this point, "Kaneli's Flight Training" will begin. When Link speaks to Kaneli again, he will be honored that he is volunteering to attempt Flight Training. Kaneli explains that Link must pass through as many Floating Rings as he can before time runs out, and if he strays too far from the Flight Range, he will be disqualified. He challenges Link to try and pass through 15 Floating Rings for his first attempt, promising a reward if he can do so. If Link agrees to start Flight Training, Kaneli will show him to his position. At the start of the Mini-Game, Kaneli will count Link down. The Floating Rings can be found situated around the Flight Range's central pillar. After 30 seconds have passed, Kaneli will call Link back to the hut. If Link passed through at least 16 Floating Rings, Kaneli declares not only has he passed, he set a bar for the Rito to aspire to. As a reward, he gives Link a Purple Rupee. Kaneli also offers the Flight Training advanced course to Link, believing he needs more of a challenge. He invites Link to come again, but if he does so, he will need to pay a fee. Afterwards, "Kaneli's Flight Training" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring location in . Kaneli's House goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Kaneli's House is the highest House in Rito Village, located at the end of the wooden path that twists around the spire. It is next door to Teba's Home. Link can find Kaneli, the chief of the Rito, inside at all hours of the day. When Link first speaks to Kaneli in his House, he will begin to welcome him to Rito Village. However, he is caught off guard when he recognizes the Sheikah Slate Link has, which he asks him about. Once he realizes that Link is capable of boarding the Divine Beasts, Kaneli asks him to stop the rampage of Divine Beast Vah Medoh. Agreeing to do so begins the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest. After Link has calmed Divine Beast Vah Medoh, he must return to Kaneli's House to tell him the news. As a reward, Kaneli has prepared a Treasure Chest, the contents of which he allows Link to take. Inside is the Great Eagle Bow.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kaneli is the chief of Rito Village. He once was a Rito warrior and Teba's mentor. He resides in his House at the top of Rito Village. When Link first approaches Kaneli, he will take note of the Sheikah Slate that he is carrying. He introduces himself to Link and asks if he is truly has a Sheikah Slate. If Link confirms it is, Kaneli will reason that he must be a Champion like Revali, and therefore capable of boarding Divine Beast Vah Medoh. However, realizing that it has been 100 years since the Champions died, he surmises that Link must instead be one of their descendants. Despite this, he still asks Link to listen to his request. If Link agrees to hear him out, Kaneli will be grateful. Since Link has the blood of a Champion, Kaneli asks him to deal with their issues with Divine Beast Vah Medoh. Only Champions are capable of stopping the rampage of a Divine Beast. This information was lost on Teba and Harth, who went to confront Medoh on their own and were defeated. Though Teba is unharmed, Kaneli fears that he is planning another attack on the Divine Beast. He asks Link to seek out Teba and try to stop Divine Beast Vah Medoh together. After this conversation, the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest will begin. During the Main Quest, Kaneli is capable of answering questions for Link. If Link asks who Teba is, Kaneli explains that he is a warrior who lives next door to hime. Alongside Harth, Teba went to confront Divine Beast Vah Medoh, but Harth ended up injured and was forced to retreat. Their defeat only made Teba more determined, and Kaneli repeats his fear that Teba plans on facing Divine Beast Vah Medoh alone. As the Divine Beast is still flying, Kaneli hopes that Teba is well. He suggests that Link speak to Teba's wife, Saki, to learn of his whereabouts. If Link asks about Revali, Kaneli explains that he was a warrior from Rito Village who died 100 years ago. Stories claim that Revali was able to fly as though he were the Wind, and he was capable of wielding a Bow twice his size. King Rhoam recognized Revali's skill and appointed him pilot of Divine Beast Vah Medoh. Unfortunately, Revali fell during the fight against Calamity Ganon. Kaneli wonders what could have been capable of killing such a strong warrior. Finally, Link can ask Kaneli about Divine Beast Vah Medoh. He will ask Link if he noticed the giant bird in the sky, and he explains that this is Divine Beast Vah Medoh. He continues to share that the Divine Beasts were made by the ancient Sheikah ages ago in order to fight Calamity Ganon. However, during the Great Calamity, they were turned against the people of Hyrule by Ganon himself. Though this happened a century ago, the Divine Beasts have made a sudden return and started

that the Divine Beasts were made by the ancient Sheikah ages ago in order to fight Calamity Ganon. However, during the Great Calamity, they were turned against the people of Hyrule by Ganon himself. Though this happened a century ago, the Divine Beasts have made a sudden return and started attacking people. Kaneli is concerned that this could foretell the return of Calamity Ganon. After Link has successfully calmed Divine Beast Vah Medoh, he must return to Rito Village to share the news with Kaneli. He is pleased to see that the Divine Beast has taken up residence atop Rito Village. According to legend, the light of the Divine Beasts is capable of destroying Calamity Ganon. In the meantime, Divine Beast Vah Medoh will serve as a protector for Rito Village, and Kaneli declares that both it and Link will live on in legend. Kaneli decides that he needs to reward Link. He implores Link to take the contents of the nearby Treasure Chest for himself, proclaiming he will get more use out of it. Inside the Chest, Link will find the Great Eagle Bow. If Link has not yet acquired the Master Sword, Kaneli will liken his accomplishments to that of the Hylian Champion from 100 years ago. According to Kaneli, the only thing he lacks to achieve that same greatness would be the Master Sword. If Link has the Master Sword, Kaneli will recognize it as such. He then wonders whether Link is indeed the Hylian Champion. Once he finishes speaking, the Main Quest will be completed. Afterwards, Link is able to keep asking Kaneli questions. If he asks about the Master Sword, Kaneli shares the legend that it was used by the Hylian Champion against Calamity Ganon. He tells Link that the Master Sword is a precious gift from his ancestors, and he warns him to never lose it. When Link asks about the Great Eagle Bow, Kaneli explains that it is the finest Bow in the land and made using traditional Rito crafting, and he goes on to share that it was once used by Revali. None of the Rito are capable of using the Bow to its full potential due to it being difficult to handle. Since Harth knows it well, Kaneli encourages Link to speak to him for more details on the Great Eagle Bow. Finally, if Link asks about Divine Beast Vah Medoh again, Kaneli explains that it is an ancient Sheikah weapon with the power to seal evil, once piloted by Revali. He will then repeat the legend of the Divine Beasts' ability to ravage the Ganon as well as his desire to see it go down in legend. If Link requests that Kaneli tell him about Revali, Kaneli explains that the Rito recently uncovered The Diary of Revali, which was very exciting for them. is a recurring character in . Biography Kanny is a Hylian Merchant who travels on Horseback. He follows a portion of the Hilltop High Road between Serenne Stable and Snowfield Stable, at which point he continues on to Rito Stable. He wears a Snowquill Tunic and Snowquill Trousers, and he carries an Emblazoned Shield and a Traveler's Sword. On his way to Rito Stable, Kanny will invite Link to accompany him. Once there, he plans on selling off the last of his stock. He also demonstrates a familiarity with Serenne Stable, referring to it as his stomping grounds and explaining it is where he finds the best Mushrooms. Some of his Mushrooms are also sourced from Snowfield Stable. While Kanny is appreciates the Snow, he dislikes the cold. Even though the road between Rito Stable and Snowfield Stable is cold, Kanny relies on it to keep his products fresh. After he crosses into the Tabantha Tundra, he remarks that the wind that comes from the Hebra Mountains is cold enough to freeze him to his Horse. Kanny also harbors a dislike for the Weather when it is Snowing, as he believes it would be easy to become lost in such conditions. However, he is unable to sit idly by while people need to buy from him. He congratulates Link for making to the Great Hyrule Forest, and he explains that he will need protection from the cold if he goes any further north. Kanny believes that Link appears to be good with a sword, but he wonders how good he is with a Shield. He suggests that Link check out the cabin on the Hebra East Summit if he is interested in Shield Surfing. He remarks that many young people are into Shield Surfing, which he relates to as a way to forget about the cold. As a Merchant, Kanny specializes in selling Mushrooms. When it is Raining or Snowing, Kanny offers rare Mushrooms. If Link agrees to buy from Kanny, he urges him to take his time as he browses. He thanks Link for every purchase he makes. Like other Merchants, Link can sell his own belongings to Kanny. He will thank Link each time he sells to him. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring character in . Biography Kapson is an elderly Zora and a retired priest of Hylia. He can initially be found inside the Sleeping Chamber in Zora's Domain. When Link first speaks to Kapson, he will be happy to see a traveler and begin to welcome him to Zora's Domain. He recognizes Link after a moment, at which point he expresses anger at him for the death of Mipha during the Great Calamity. He informs Link that many of the elderly Zora still remember Mipha, and as a result, they hate him for what happened to her. However, Kapson claims to hate Link's actions, not Link himself, and he believes that Link can be forgiven. Kapson informs Link that he has retired from his role as a priest. Ever since his retirement, Kapson has found that his life has become boring. He worries that he will soon pass away. Therefore, he asks Link to introduce him to any engaged couples he meets, as he would like to officiate one more wedding. During the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, Hudson will ask Link to find a priest to officiate his wedding among the Zora. Link can then return to Zora's Domain to inform Kapson of this opportunity. Since Akkala is not far from their current location, Kapson decides to leave for Tarrey Town right away. He is eager to be able to work again. He invites Link to come visit him once he is settled in. At this point, he then departs from Zora's Domain. Kapson will officiate Hudson and Rhondson's wedding in Tarrey Town. Once the ceremony begins, Kapson asks Hudson if he is willing to take Rhondson as his wife, which Hudson agrees to. Next, Kapson asks the same question of Rhondson, with the added stipulation that she name their children in accordancw with the Bolson Construction naming guidelines. Rhondson objects, claiming that these are not traditional vows. After being convinced, Rhondson will take the vow. Kapson then asks the gathered crowd to help him greet the newly married couple. He wishes them happiness as they begin their lives together. Once he arrives in Tarrey Town, Kapson will take charge of its Tarrey Town. Kapson's Inn does not charge any Rupees for a stay and does not offer any superior bedding options, though he will wake Link up at his preferredtime of day. If Link speaks to Kapson while atop any of the furniture in his Inn, he will pray to Hylia that she smites him for his insolence.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Kara Kara Bazaar is a small oasis in the Gerudo Desert, found in the middle of the path to Gerudo Town. It is a resting stop while exploring the hot Gerudo Desert. Link is not hurt by Temperature while here. The Kara Kara Bazaar contains one Recovered Memory, one Main Quest, one Side Quest, three Treasure Chests, an Inn, and three unnamed General Stores. Link's seventh Recovered Memory, "Blades of the Yiga", can be found at the Kara Kara Bazaar as part of the "Captured Memories" Main Quest. During the Memory, Zelda is attacked by several Yiga Clan members before Link jumps in to rescue her from them. Vilia can be found at the Kara Kara Bazaar, where she serves a role in the "Forbidden City Entry" Main Quest. Vilia is a Hylian woman who dresses in traditional Gerudo clothes, which Link must obtain in order to sneak into Gerudo Town. Link must find Vilia by asking around at Kara Kara Bazaar about them. Ripp, a Gerudo soldier at the Bazaar, tells Link that she saw a Hylian woman at the Kara Kara Bazaar Inn. After Link asks around at the Inn, Shaillu tells him that there is a Hylian woman who likes to relax on the roof. Vilia can be found atop the roof there, where she offers to sell a Gerudo Outfit to him for 600 Rupees. The two Quests that are at the Kara Kara Bazaar are the "An Ice Guy" Side Quest, given by Guy, and "The Eye of the Sandstorm" Shrine Quest, given by Nobiro. A Hylian Merchant named Robsten can be found at the Bazaar. Before Link calms Divine Beast Vah Naboris, a Goron named Strade sits near the small pool of Water in the center of the Kara Kara Bazaar. In addition, Beedle, Kyra, and Lukan sometimes travel through the Bazaar. During the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, Hudson has Link search for a Gerudo tailor with "son" in their name. A Gerudo woman named Rhondson who meets these requirements is found at Kara Kara Bazaar, just outside of the Inn. Rhondson has been searching for love, but has not been successful. Upon speaking to Rhondson, she comments that Akkala is far away, but admits that she needs to get away from a village full of other women. She then thanks Link for the information and sets off for Tarrey Town. There is a Treasure Chest hidden in the water containing a Silver Rupee and a Treasure Chest buried in the ground behind the Inn containing a Purple Rupee. Link can befriend the Hylian Retriever here by feeding it four pieces of edible Material, causing it to lead Link to a Treasure Chest containing a Knight's Bow. Areas Emri's General Store Emri's General Store is a small Fruit Shop. Wares and Pricing Maike's General Store Maike's General Store sells Monster Parts and a variety of Roasted Food. The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Kara Kara Bazaar Barracks are located in Kara Kara Bazaar, an oasis in the Gerudo Desert. They are a makeshift tent set up by the male Merchants who have been denied entry to Gerudo Town. While Benja attempts to figure out a way inside, Robsten and Nobiro wait for him at the Barracks. After the "Forbidden City Entry" Main Quest has been completed, Benja returns to the Barracks, having been unable to find a way into Gerudo Town. The Kara Kara Bazaar Barracks feature a Campfire at their front, which Benja and Robsten sit near at night. There is also a small observation post on the back of the Barracks, where Nobiro watches the Great Cliffs. The first time Link speaks to Nobiro, he shares a rumor that the Sandstorm over the Great Cliffs stops for a few hours each day, but he has yet to see this happen. He has heard that there is an ancient treasure hidden in the Sandstorm, so he has been waiting for the storm to clear. Suddenly looking at Link, Nobiro realizes he does not know who he is. Afterwards, "The Eye of the Sandstorm" Shrine Quest will begin. Equipment Emri and Maike have moved their General Stores in front of the Kara Kara Bazaar Barracks. Saula has also set up Fashion Passion between the two Stores.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Kara Kara Bazaar Inn is an Inn located in the Kara Kara Bazaar in the Gerudo Desert. It is managed by the Gerudo Kachoo. During Divine Beast Vah Naboris's rampage, Kachoo will complain that it has caused the Inn to lose business. Although the stomping is loud, she encourages Link to stay in one of their comfortable Beds. She is also relieved once the Divine Beast has been calmed, as patrons can now sleep without being disturbed. Link can pay 20 Rupees for a regular Bed, but he can also get a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. The Soft Beds used by the Inn are made using Cucco feathers and have been designed to leave their users full of energy. Choosing this Bed will provide Link with temporary Hearts after Sleeping. The Kara Kara Bazaar Inn also offers a mandatory wake-up shout, which Link can choose to happen in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Kachoo will shout a Gerudo greeting at Link when he awakens. She wishes Link safety on his travels before bidding him farewell. While Divine Beast Vah Naboris is active, Konora will reside at the Inn. She has been unable to return to Gerudo Town, as she is afraid of getting zapped by the Divine Beast. The Rumor Mill: Volume 7 is found on one of the top bunks in the Kara Kara Bazaar Inn. It details various secrets of the Royal Family of Hyrule hidden in Hyrule Castle. There is also a Poster on the wall of the Inn, which depicts the recipe for a Chilly Fruit Pie. The poster lists the ingredients as Goat Butter, Cane Sugar, Tabantha Wheat, and a Hydromelon. During the "Forbidden City Entry" Main Quest, Shaillu mentions that there is a Hylian woman who likes to relax on the roof of the Kara Kara Bazaar Inn. There, Link can encounter Vilia, who asks if he needs anything from her. Though she does not know anything about a man sneaking into Gerudo Town, if Link calls her beautiful, she realizes her style of clothing would look nice on him. She offers to sell Link the Gerudo Outfit for 500 Rupees. Afterwards, Link can return to the roof to speak to Vilia, who can sell him more clothes or change him into the Gerudo Outfit. Shaillu's General Store At the front of the Kara Kara Bazaar Inn, Shaillu runs a General Store specializing in Arrows. She suggests that, if Link wants to buy something else, he should check out Gerudo Town. However, she realizes that, as a man, he would not be allowed inside. Link is also able to sell Items to her. The Kara Kara Bazaar Well is a location in . Features and Overview The Kara Kara Bazaar Well is situated outside of the Kara Kara Bazaar Inn, which is part of the Kara Kara Bazaar in the Gerudo Desert. A Ladder can be found inside its rim, which allows Link to Climb in and out of its interior. The Well's inner chamber is covered by a shallow layer of Water, and it features a tunnel on its southern wall that connects to the Oasis Source. As part of the Side Quest "Lost in the Dunes", Link finds Ponthos trapped within the Oasis Source. By breaking the piles of Hard Sediment within the Cave, Link can reveal the tunnel leading to the Kara Kara Bazaar Well's underground chamber. This allows Ponthos to escape using the Well's Ladder and return to Kara Kara Bazaar. Creatures Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Karin lives in the Village Chief's House in Hateno Village with her parents, Reede and Clavia. She spends her days walking back and forth throughout the Village. When Link speaks to Karin during the day, she will begin to argue with him, but she becomes embarrassed once she realizes she is addressing the wrong person. If Link asks if she was speaking to him, Karin explains that she thought he was either Azu or Sefaro. However, she encourages him to listen to her anyway. Karin explains that she saw a young girl outside of the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. Unfortunately, when Karin tried to tell an adult about what she saw, she was told that the only people who live there are an old man and woman. Despite this, Karin still asserts that she saw a Sheikah girl. She laments that people never listen when kids have something to say. Due to Azu and Sefaro playing spies, Karin has heard a lot about the girl, but they have yet to catch sight of her. In her sleep, Karin will occasionally mention the girl. During Rain, Karin will stay inside the Village Chief's House. She sits on the floor as she reads a Book. It contains a story about a prince who encountered something strange on his way to the castle. Karin will follow Link around if he passes by while carrying the Blue Flame. Seeing it up close, she says that it looks like a star. She also asks Link where she can get one.

is a recurring character in . Biography Karsh is a Gerudo woman who travels between Woodland Stable and Foothill Stable by way of the Ternio Trail. She carries a Gerudo Scimitar and a Gerudo Shield. At the beginning of conversations, she will often introduce herself to Link and tell him to remember her name. Originally, Karsh is from the Gerudo Desert. She was a guard for Gerudo Town, where she was a master archer. Back then, she was able to stop Monsters from attacking with a single Arrow. Karsh left Gerudo Town in search of a man, but she has not had much luck in her quest. Though Karsh started her journey some time ago, she has not yet given up hope. She notes that the Gorons have a similar level of endurance to her, and she wonders whether she will meet her match amongst them. All Karsh wants is to be with the man she was born to marry, and she does not care what race he could be. During her journey, Karsh has met men of many different races and learned how people live outside of Gerudo Town. She likes the Gorons in particular and wishes her skin was as tough as theirs. Karsh knows many things about Eldin. She has heard that the Mountain Road becomes even hotter than the Gerudo Desert, and she regrets not bringing clothes that are appropriate for such conditions. She also warns Link of the Magma Bombs that make travelling to Goron City dangerous. In addition, she has heard that the Goron Hot Springs are supposed to be good for one's skin, which she remarks that visitors will need, since they will be torn apart by monsters on the way there. While Karsh dislikes Rain, she considers it a good excuse to start conversations with people. If Karsh encounters any enemies on her journey, she will draw her Gerudo Scimitar to fight. When Link saves her, Karsh will be grateful for his assistance. She may also complain about having to deal with monsters. To thank Link for helping her, she gives him an Energizing Elixir, a Fireproof Elixir, or Rupees.

is a recurring character in . Biography Karson is a Hylian resident of Hateno Village in East Necluda. He has recently finished his trial period for Bolson Construction, making him an official employee. Initially, Karson can be found attempting to demolish the abandoned house in Hateno Village alongside Hudson. He tells Link that the former owner of the house left to serve at Hyrule Castle and never returned. When Link comments that this seems like hard work, Karson claims that he would not want it any other way. If Link offers to buy the house, Karson will direct him to his boss, Bolson. Karson admits to Link that he was hired by Bolson Construction due to his name ending in "-son." At Link's confusion, Karson explains that Bolson Construction has a policy of only hiring people whose names end in "-son." he claims that Bolson has been considerig expanding his business, but he does not know where he is going to find enough people fitting the name requirement. Once Link offers to buy the House from Bolson, Karson will cease work and sit underneath a Tree nearby, awaiting Bolson's orders. He appears relieved to receive a break. He will admits to Link that he finds construction work to be hard, which is why he idolizes Hudson's ability to work quickly. He then reveals that he overheard Link's deal with Bolson, and he asks if he is serious about buying the House. When Link confirms that he is, Karson will be surprised, especially since Link appears to be younger than him. If Link claims that he will not buy the House, Karson is still impressed that he considered it, and he wonders how much demolition he will have to do in order to make that kind of money. Despite Link's answer, Karson decides to keep working hard to build his own place in the world. After Link completes the purchase of his House, Karson will thank him for doing so. He is impressed someone so young was able to spend so many Rupees. Due to this, Karson has received a sizable bonus. With it, he plans on getting a meal with his girlfriend, Sophie. Karson will take note when Hudson leaves for Akkala. If Link asks where he went, Karson reveals that he is in search of new and creative ways to expand the business Bolson Construction. Though he wants to help him, Karson believes he still has much to learn. Karson still has many things he hopes that Hudson will teach him, and so he hopes they will meet again soon. Throughout the "Hylian Homeowner" Side Quest, Karson will assist Bolson in renovating Link's House. After all of the renovations are complete, Bolson has Karson help him install the rest of the Furniture into Link's House. The two of them will then proceed to take a break. During the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, Hudson will ask Link to invite Bolson and Karson to his wedding in Tarrey Town.

Karson considers her to be a beauty, and he is impressed that she makes all of the clothes that she sells. He shares that his girlfriend Sophie also works at an Armor Shop, but her father is the one who actually makes all of the clothes. However, he realizes he has gotten on a tangent. During the wedding ceremony, when Bolson rebukes Rhondson's claim that the vows are not traditional, Karson argues that she likely did not mean traditional in the way he is thinking. He is also seen applauding once the couple has been declared married. Afterwards, he and Bolson will return to Hateno Village. After returning to Hateno Village, Karson will wonder what it is that Rhondson likes about Hudson. He theorizes that it could be Hudson's silky hair or his chiseled physique. Karson is now a member of Hudson Construction, and he is well-known to have played a major role in building Lookout Landing. He resides at Lookout Landing, where he can initially be found finishing its construction. When Link first arrives in Lookout Landing, Karson can be seen using a Stone Axe, made from a Wooden Stick and a Stone, to chop Logs near the incomplete Lookout Landing Well. At first, he claims to be too busy to speak, but he stops when he realizes Link is the one who approached him. He is relieved to see Link is safe, and he wonders were he has been since he disappeared. He then tells Link to meet with Purah, before once again expressing how happy he is to see him. If spoken to again, Karson predicts that Purah will lose her composure when she sees Link due to how worried she was when he and Zelda went missing. Should Link try to use Ultrahand to lift the Board on top of the Lookout Landing Well, Karson will yell at him not to touch it. He advises Link to stay away from the Well until it has been completed. After Link has met with Purah, Karson reveals that he is figuring out the logistics of building a Mini Stable for Lookout Landing, since he believes it would be useful for Lester. Although it will take him time to complete it, Karson tells Link he will be able to make use of it once it is done. He is

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Karusa Valley is located in the Gerudo Desert. The Yiga Clan Hideout is located at its eastern end, and as a result, they have left decorations in the Valley. This includes Traveler's Guardian Deities that have been defaced with the Yiga symbol. Many large cliffs hang over the Valley from the Gerudo Highlands. During the day, the southern parts of of Karusa Valley are subject to intense Heat, requiring Link to have at least one level of Heat Resistance while traversing it. At night, the Valley becomes a Freezing Climate, and Link will require one to two levels of Cold Resistance depending on his elevation. Sho Dantu Shrine is situated within the Karusa Valley, though it is initially buried beneath the ground. Its location is marked by a Pedestal and Luminous Stone Deposits, and a nearby Stone Tablet directs its reader to offer "a shining blue stone." If Link places a Luminous Stone on the Pedestal, the Ancient Shrine will rise from the ground, allowing him to enter. During the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Gerudo soldiers will direct Link to Karusa Valley so he can infiltrate the Yiga Clan Hideout. left|40px A total of seven Korok Seed Puzzles can be found within Karusa Valley. Five of them are Food Offerings marked by Traveler's Guardian Deities on the cliffs hanging over the Valley, into which Link must place Mighty Bananas. The sixth Puzzle is a Flower Trail located at the Valley's entrance. The final is a Natural Hiding Spot, taking the form of a Rock on the cliff with a large hole in it. When Link solves each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Enemies Materials

Kass is a character in . Biography Kass is a minstrel who travels throughout Hyrule in search of the "Ancient Songs". He has left his family and his hometown of Rito Village to fulfill the final wish of his teacher, the Court Poet. This journey is documented in Kass's Journal, which can be found in a hut on Washa's Bluff. When Link first encounters Kass, he recognizes the Sheikah Slate that he is carrying, though he excuses himself for prying. If Link asks if he is a Bird, Kass is shocked to hear that he has never seen a Rito before. He then introduces himself to Link and asks if he has heard of the "Ancient Songs". He goes on to explain that the "Ancient Songs" are dedicated to the Ancient Hero who defeated Calamity Ganon 10,000 years ago. During his journey, Kass can be found at several Stables throughout Hyrule Kingdom. There, he plays a version of "Epona's Song" that harmonizes with the regular "The Stables" theme. At these Stables, he offers to sing an "Ancient Song" for Link that recounts the previous sealing of Calamity Ganon, which was taught to him by the Court Poet. After singing the Song for Link, Kass thanks him and welcomes him back to listen to it again. At Wetland Stable, Kass asks Link if he has seen the nearby Kaya Wan Shrine, as he knows a lot about Ancient Shrines. He reveals that he learned about them from the Court Poet, as he was a member of the Sheikah tribe that often accompanied Zelda as she surveyed ruins. Kass recounts that the Court Poet was always happy when he shared these memories with him. Upon meeting Link at Foothill Stable, Kass informs him that there are many theories about the origin of the Song he plays at Stables. He heard from the Court Poet that it was a Song played by the Ancient Hero to call his Horse companion. He encourages Link to come back and listen to it. At Gerudo Canyon Stable, Kass is impressed that he made it so far, as even he struggled to make it there by flying. He recounts that the Court Poet, who served the Royal Family of Hyrule, was forced to flee Hyrule Castle when the Great Calamity struck. He imagines that it was a much more dangerous journey than his own. When spoken to at Rito Stable, Kass confesses that he is homesick. He admits that he had to leave his wife, Amali, and their children behind when he set out on his journey, and he hopes they are doing well. However, he reveals that he is unable to return until he fulfills his promise to the Court Poet. When Link asks about his promise, Kass begins to explain, but he then decides now is not the time to reveal his promise. He tells Link that after he learns all of the "Ancient Songs", he shares his promise with him in Rito Village. Kass

promise to the Court Poet. When Link asks about his promise, Kass begins to explain, but he then decides now is not the time to reveal his promise. He tells Link that after he learns all of the "Ancient Songs", he shares his promise with him in Rito Village. Kass can also be found in several locations in the wild. Hints for these locations can be found in Kass's Journal, which documents all of the "Ancient Songs" that he knows of. At each of these locations, Link receives a Shrine Quest or a Side Quest after listening to an "Ancient Song" from Kass. They are as follows: In his Journal, Kass pledges to continue his journey until he can pass the "Ancient Songs" on to the Champion. Once Link solves the riddles in each of the "Ancient Songs", Kass returns to Rito Village, where he performs with his bandoneon next to Akh Va'quot Shrine. The final page in Kass's Journal also changes, revealing that he is pleased to have shared all of the "Ancient Songs" with Link, fulfilling his promise to the Court Poet. During the day, he is joined by his daughters, Notts, Kotts, Genli, Cree, and Kheel, who sing along as he plays. Through his Song, he wishes that the peace they have will last forever. When visited at night, Kass reveals that he has a Song that he would like Link to listen to. He warns Link that he will take some time explaining himself, and he asks if he is fine with this. If Link agrees to listen, Kass thanks him and says that he wishes to talk about his teacher, the Court Poet. Kass informs Link that his teacher was a Sheikah poet who lived in Hyrule Castle before the Great Calamity struck. During this time, the Court Poet fell in love with Zelda, who he was close in age with. Unfortunately for him, Zelda was in love with her knight, Link, which made the Court Poet jealous. However, Kass claims that something changed after the Great Calamity, as the Court Poet believed so deeply that Link would return to defeat Calamity Ganon that he wrote a Song. Kass then plays that Song for Link, entitled the "Song of the Hero". After finishing the Song, Kass continues his story, explaining that the Court Poet witnessed Link sacrifice himself for Zelda while fleeing the Calamity. Once Impa explained what happened, the Court Poet decided to begin collecting the "Ancient Songs" in the hope that he could pass them down to Link upon his return. Turning back to Link, Kass asks him if he accepts the "Song of the Hero" from the Court Poet. When Link agrees, Kass thanks him for doing so. He recalls that the Court Poet often spoke of Zelda's beauty, and he expresses a desire to meet her and write a Song worthy of her. He once again thanks Link for lending his time to him. is a recurring character in . Biography Katta is a Gerudo Soldier who can be found in the Royal Palace of Gerudo Town. She guards one of the entrances to Riju's Bedroom upstairs, and she carries a Gerudo Spear. When Link initially tries to go past, she stops him and tells him that he cannot enter without permission. After Link has recovered the Thunder Helm from the Yiga Clan Hideout, Katta will allow him to pass. She comments that Link must be special to have permission to enter Riju's Bedroom. Katta is in charge of guarding the Jail in the Gerudo Shelter.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kayden is a Zora who runs the Seabed Inn in Zora's Domain. He is married to his childhood friend, Kodah, and the two of them have a daughter, Finley, together. When Kayden is first approached by Link, he will recognize him from his visits to Zora's Domain 100 years ago. However, he does not stay on the topic for long, and he will return to his duties tending to the Seabed Inn. After Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been appeased, Kayden will ask Link where he has been for the past 100 years. He will also begin to inform Link about of his marriage to Kodah, but he cuts himself off to remain professional. He appears to be relieved that the Rain has ended. Through the Seabed Inn, Kayden offers a place for Link to rest. The Seabed Inn is capable of providing a regular Bed or a Water Bed for guests to sleep in. If Link asks about the Water Bed, Kayden explains that it is a Bed made of Water, which makes it cool and comfortable. If Link decides to stay at the Inn, Kayden asks him what time he wants to wake up. After Link chooses the time, Kayden tells him to sleep well. Once Link wakes up, Kayden notes that he appears to have had a good sleep. If Link utilized the Water Bed, Kayden will also add in the hope that he enjoyed it.

is a recurring location in . Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain is located on Piper Ridge in the Tabantha Frontier. As its name implies, it is home to the Great Fairy named Kaysa. The Great Fairy Fountain is surrounded by a shallow pool of Water, and a nearby path leads off of Piper Ridge. According to rumors, the shadow of Tabantha Tower points towards the Fountain in the afternoon. Initially, Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain will be closed. Link can hear the voice of Kaysa from inside, begging him to listen to her story. If he agrees, Kaysa explains that her Fountain used to receive many offerings of Rupees from travelers, but her power has dwindled now that they have stopped visiting. To restore her power, Kaysa requests that Link make an offering to her. Depending on how many other Great Fairy Fountains have been opened, Kaysa will ask for 100 Rupees, 500 Rupees, 1,000 Rupees, or 10,000 Rupees. When Link makes the offering, Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain will bloom as her power is restored. As a reward for helping her, Kaysa will enhance Link's Armor, so long as he brings her the necessary Materials. The degree to which she can do so depends on how many other Great Fairy Fountains have been opened. After hearing rumors about Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain, Toren set out in search of it, but he has been unable to progress past the Tabantha Bridge Stable. As part of the "A Gift for the Great Fairy" Side Quest, he asks Link to make an offering to the Fountain on his behalf. If Link agrees to his request, Toren will give him 500 Rupees. Once Link has opened the Fountain, Toren will be jealous that he got to see Kaysa in person, but he is glad that his offering has been made. Toren does not give Link a reward, believing that being able to see Kaysa is enough. Creatures Materials Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain is located on the hill above Outskirt Stable in Hyrule Field. The path up to it has been blocked by Fallen Debris, making the Fountain inaccessible by Horse.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kazul is a Hylian traveler who rides on Horseback between Riverside Stable and Wetland Stable. He carries an Emblazoned Shield and a Traveler's Sword. On his journey, Kazul will occasionally comfort his Horse. As he travels, Kazul will give Link advice and warnings. On his way to Riverside Stable, Kazul informs him that Kakariko Village is about the same distance from their current location. He also suggests that Link bring a Horse and a Map if he is also going to Riverside Stable. Kazul tells Link to head to Akkala if he is looking for adventure, directing him towards Skull Lake. If Link does go to Akkala, Kazul suggests that he stock up on supplies near the base of Death Mountain. While he is stopped, he will quietly tells Link about the Fang and Bone, which sells special wares at night. He encourages Link to visit the Fang and Bone should he ever find himself at Skull Lake, as it would be an interesting experience. In addition, Kazul will warn Link to be careful if he enters Hyrule Castle in search of treasure, since he has never been anywhere so dangerous. However, he has heard of a secret entrance to Hyrule Castle, which is located through the inlet behind the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins. He reminds Link that this is simply a rumor, and Kazul even suspects it could have been a story that was spread to catch thieves. Kazul also knows of a secret cave on the west side of the Castle, but none who have entered have returned. Kazul recommends that Link sell off any extra Gems he has because they are worth a fair amount of Rupees. If Link does this enough, Kazul explains that he will be able to afford pricier gear. Kazul is a member of the Zonai Survey Team.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Keese are bat-like creatures that inhabit Dungeons and Caves, similarly to their real-life counterparts. Following their debut in , they have since become a staple of and have appeared in the majority of games with the exception of , where Keese are absent and are instead replaced by the similar Aches. Keese often exist in clusters in the places where they are found. They fly around the screen erratically, not heading towards anything in particular, and stop to rest for a short amount of time on a neighboring wall or rock face. In some games, such as and , Keese move about the screen only when Link is within close proximity, otherwise they remain still. Later games, such as and , introduce Keese with a slightly more active attack strategy, targeting Link, but pausing above him before striking, providing an opportunity for him to strike. As small and commonplace creatures, Keese are relatively weak and can be dispatched with a variety of weaponry, from Swords and Boomerangs to Arrows and Bombs. Keese are known to inhabit various forms in adapting to their surrounding environment. Notable variants include Fire Keese and Ice Keese, which are enveloped in fiery and icy mist, respectively. Less common forms include Keese Swarms, Shadow Keese, Electric Keese and Dark Keese. Vires, when defeated, will also split into a pair of Keese, which may or may not be fought. Keese inhabit Dungeons in . They resemble blue bats, and commonly appear in small to medium-sized groups. Keese flutter through rooms in a random path, stopping only periodically to rest. They are also the only enemies that are encountered in the game's side-scrolling chambers, where they can be found resting against the walls before taking flight. Keese can be defeated by any weapon in Link's arsenal, including the Sword, Bow and Candle. As they are very small enemies, the Boomerang will also defeat them as opposed to stunning them. Vires will split into two red Keese when defeated. These Keese are fought in the same manner as the common variety. Keese never drop any items when defeated. 30px|left Keese inhabit Caves and tunnels in the Light World of Hyrule in . Unlike their previous incarnation, Keese remain still along Cave walls and crevices, but take flight when Link draws close. Keese in have a more direct flight pattern than previous appearances, soaring in a curving arc as opposed to random flight, before resting again on the next wall. They are also encountered less frequently in groups, though they can still occasionally be found huddled together. They are weak enemies and can be defeated by any means of attack. In the Game Boy Advance version of , Keese also appear as enemies in the Palace of the Four Sword. The Dark World counterparts of Keese are Chasupa, which behave identically but are significantly stronger. Keese often appear in small groups in Caves and Dungeons in .
