are recurring Enemies in . Keese Swarms go unnamed in and . Characteristics Keese Swarms lay hidden in bushes in The Swamp and the Lost Woods in . They consist of a single, large red Keese followed by a trail of purple, shadowy copies it leaves in its wake. If the Links disturb its hiding spot, the Keese Swarm will rush out and begin circling them. Trapped within the swarm, the only way to escape is by defeating the red Keese, which will try to keep a certain distance between itself and the Links. The heroes may assume the Long or Wide Formation, putting the outermost Link within reach of the Keese. Once the Keese is defeated, the trail is destroyed along with it, leaving behind a ring of Green Force Gems, while the Keese itself will drop a Blue Force Gem. Keese Swarms are clusters of Keese which can be seen flying over large swaths of land such as the Ancient Lab Ruins. They patrol their territories in search of prey, including Hylians such as Link. When the colony spots Link, its members will approach him before simultaneously swooping down at him. If at least one Keese in the colony is defeated or hit with the Stasis + Rune, the remaining Keese will cowardly fly off. Unlike in Four Swords Adventures, they are a real swarm as opposed to one Keese with a trail. Keese Swarms are groups of Keese which can be encountered flying out of Caves. When a Swarm spots Link, they will fly toward him before lunging, which deals one and a half Hearts of damage to Link's Life Gauge.

The number in parentheses is how many of the three Treasure Chests at the end of the Level contain a Keese Wing; each of the Links may open just one Chest. Hinox Mine, "Don't pop any balloons!" (1) Den of Flames, "Avoid the volcanic rocks!" (1) Fire Temple, "Clear within the time limit!" (1) Fire Temple, "Only Bombs-no swords!" (2) They can also be won in the Coliseum and Daily Riches, or purchased from the Street Merchant for 500 Rupees each. Keese Wings are one of the Materials used to make the Energy Gear Outfit. In , Keese Wings are commonly dropped by Keese when defeated. As is the case with other Monster Parts, they can be combined with critters in a Cooking Pot to make all kinds of Elixirs. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Gray Dye or exchanged for Mon at the Fang and Bone. There are three variations of Keese Wings, which are Fire Keese Wings, Electric Keese Wings, and Ice Keese Wings, which come from the relating variation of species. Three Keese Wings, as well as three Rushrooms, are needed to upgrade each piece of the Climbing Set to level ★. Keese Wings return as Items in . Keese Wings are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Kenyo is a Hylian child who resides at Tabantha Bridge Stable. During the day, he runs around the Stable. At night, he sleeps in one of the Stable's Beds. During the Rain, he and Ena sit together inside. When Link speaks to Kenyo, he will shout "BOOM BOOM! BAM BAM!" at him. If Link responds in kind, Kenyo will yell "BOOM-BAM!" If Link expresses confusion, Kenyo informs him that there is a ghost under that Tabantha Great Bridge that makes loud noises. He encourages Link to listen for the noises, only to realize that they have stopped. He then theorizes that the Boom-Bam Ghost is taking a nap. While it is Raining, Kenyo wonders if the Boom-Bam Ghost likes such weather. Even in his sleep, he mutters about the ghost.

is a recurring character in . Biography Keye is a Zora child who resides within Zora's Domain. During the day, he plays near Mipha's Statue in the Zora's Domain Square. At night, he and his brother, Tumbo, rest in the Sleeping Chamber. When Link initially speaks to Keye, he will ask who he is. If Link responds that he is a Hylian, Keye will not be very impressed. If Link is unable to answer, Keye will accuse him of copying how he speaks. Upon getting a closer look, however, he realizes that Link is a Hylian. Knowing that Link is a Hylian, Keye then asks if he came from far away. He starts to tell Link the reason for his question, but he decides not to continue, since his father, Fronk, told him not to talk to strangers. Afterwards, if Link tries to ask him what is wrong, Keye will claim that it is not the business of a Hylian. After Link has calmed Divine Beast Vah Ruta, he can find Keye standing in front of Mipha's Statue with Laruta. When Link asks what he is doing, Keye explains that he is practicing to use a spear. He does a jump to demonstrate his abilities, but he laments that he is unable to reach the Statue's pedestal. In frustration, he admits to having seen the pedestal somewhere else before. He thinks there may have been a similar pedestal at Veiled Falls, and he wants to be able to jump high enough to pierce it. Once Mei has returned to Zora's Domain, Keye tells Link that he hopes he will help his family if something happens to them again.

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview West of the Dueling Peaks in West Necluda, Link can find a large Fallen Ruin on the southern bank of Squabble River. Inside, he can find a Steward Construct offering to serve as a guide. When spoken to, it explains that it was tasked with guiding visitors to a Shrine of Light before the Ruin fell to the Surface, and it is thankful that it can still do so. The Steward Construct gives Link a riddle to reveal the Shrine, which states "Give keys born of water to the three altars. The sacred shrine will appear." Following this interaction, "Keys Born of Water" will begin. Within the Fallen Ruin, Link can find several Frost Emitters. By activating a Frost Emitter while it is facing the Water of Squabble River, he can then create square sheets of Ice. These sheets can be resized by leaving them out in the daylight or by exposing them to the nearby Campfire while it is lit. Once a sheet is appropriately sized, Link can then use Ultrahand to slot it into one of the three altars. When an altar has a sheet of Ice in its groove, it will sink into the ground. After all three altars have slotted sheets of Ice, the Jochisiu Shrine will appear on top of the Fallen Ruin, and "Keys Born of Water" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring character in . Biography Kheel is a Rito child who lives in Rito Village. When Link initially arrives at the Village, she can be found with her mother, Amali, on the platform near Akh Va'quot Shrine. At night, she and her sisters sleep inside their home. When spoken to, Kheel laments that it is currently too dangerous to leave Rito Village, as she wants to sing with her sisters at Warbler's Nest. Angrily, she calls Divine Beast Vah Medoh a jerk, which causes Amali to chastise her for using such language. Kheel then tries to defend herself. After Link has appeased Divine Beast Vah Medoh, he can encounter Amali searching for Kheel. She turns to Link and explains that she has been unable to locate her daughter. She theorizes that she may have gone to Warbler's Nest to practice her singing. However, she is worried that Kheel may not have been able to travel so far on her own. Once she finishes speaking, the "Find Kheel" Side Quest will begin. At Warbler's Nest, Link will find Kheel upset that her sisters did not come to rehearse their song for the elder, Kaneli. She is afraid that they will be laughed off stage if they perform as they are. Since Link is a "scary-looking" Hylian, Kheel asks him if he could return to Rito Village to remind her sisters of their rehearsal. She warns that it might be tough to convince her sister Genli, as she is probably in the Kitchen yelling for Salmon Meunière or something similar. She complains that Genli does not want to sing, which makes her a pain to deal with. When she finishes speaking, the "Recital at Warbler's Nest" Shrine Quest will begin. Once Link has retrieved all of Kheel's sisters, she thanks him for his help and asks if he wants to know what song they are singing. According to Kaneli, the song was performed at Warbler's Nest in the ancient past. Kheel explains that Warbler's Nest is the big stone platform with the pillars behind them. The lyrics to the song do not make sense to her, but the line, "When wind convinces the rocks to sing, open the monk's door will swing," appeals to her. Kheel asks Link what he thinks it means and wonders what a Monk is. If Link does not already have one, Kheel will give him a Korok Leaf as a reward for helping her. Kheel suggests swinging the Korok Leaf in the directioin of Warbler's Nest, as doing so makes a fun noise. The order of the notes in Kheel and her sisters' song correspond to the rocks surrounding the Pedestal. When Link manages to unearth the Voo Lota Shrine, Kheel turns and shouts for her sisters to look. Kheel's sister Notts says they should tell their mother about the phenomenon. Kheel agrees and bids Link goodbye. She counts her siblings off and they take to the sky. Back in Rito Village, Link will find

unearth the Voo Lota Shrine, Kheel turns and shouts for her sisters to look. Kheel's sister Notts says they should tell their mother about the phenomenon. Kheel agrees and bids Link goodbye. She counts her siblings off and they take to the sky. Back in Rito Village, Link will find Kheel singing on the platform near Akh Va'quot Shrine with her sisters. She reveals that Kaneli was surprised when she told him about Voo Lota Shrine. She remarks that Ancient Shrines must also like playing hide-and-seek. Once Kass returns to Rito Village, he will join Kheel and the rest of his daughters by playing his bandoneon as they sing. Kheel is happy that "Poppy" is back and they are all going to sing together. Due to the blizzard in Rito Village, Kheel has temporarily taken over the Brazen Beak Armor Shop.

is a recurring character in . Biography Khini is a Stable Worker at East Akkala Stable in the Akkala Highlands. Throughout the day, he stands in front of the Stable and welcomes travelers. When Link speaks to him, Khini offers to sell him an Akkala Bun, which he promises will increase Link's energy. If Link agrees to take one, Khini explains that he will need to eat it immediately, since the ingredients go bad quickly. When Link agrees to eat it at the East Akkala Stable, Khini then asks for 10 Rupees as payment. Once Link has payed for the Akkala Bun, Khini tells him to close his eyes and open his mouth. He then walks Link through the process of chewing and swallowing the Bun. On occasion, eating one will grant Link extra Stamina. Afterwards, he asks Link what he thought about it. If Link did not receive extra Stamina, Khini will notice and remarks that this is odd. Either he, he encourages Link to visit him again in the future.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kiana is a Hylian woman who lives in Lurelin Village. From 5:00 AM to 3:00 PM, Kiana can be found standing next to a clothes line outside her home, humming to herself as she works. When Link first speaks to her, she asks if he is a traveler. She explains that Lurelin Village is a small, proud fishing town. Her husband, Sebasto, is a fisherman, and she believes her sons Kinov and Zuta will follow in her footsteps one day. Turning to Kinov, Kiana asks him what she should make for dinner. Kinov requests Seafood Paella because he likes the way his mother makes it. Kiana decides to go along with his suggestion. However, she admits to Link that she is missing two ingredients for this recipe: Goat Butter and a Hearty Blueshell Snail. Since she is so busy with housework, Kiana is unable to shop for the ingredients herself. Therefore, she asks Link if he could retrieve them for her. If Link agrees, Kiana informs him that she will be waiting. After she finishes speaking, the "What's for Dinner?" Side Quest will begin. Once Link has the ingredients that Kiana needs, he can return to Kiana to give them to her. If Link agrees to hand them over, Kiana will take the ingredients and start Cooking. To thank Link, she gives him a Purple Rupee. She also invites Link to eat with her family, since he was able to find the ingredients she was missing. Afterwards, she gives Link a Seafood Paella of his own to eat, encouraging him to dig in. This completes the Side Quest. Starting at 5:00 AM, Kiana stands in front of the clothes line, where she begins to debate what she should make for dinner. From 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM, Kiana sits at a Cooking Pot next to her home, which she welcomes Link to use. As her family begins to gather to eat, she reveals that she made Seafood Paella for dinner. If it ever Rains while she is still outside, Kiana will run to her house with her hands on her head. At 9:00 PM, Kiana will walk into the house next to her own to put her sons to bed. She watches over Kinov and Zuta as they sleep, where she warns Link to be careful not to wake them. She goes to sleep in her house at 10:00 PM.

is a character in . Biography Kiimo is a member of the Zonai Survey Team who resides at Lookout Landing. He can be found in the Emergency Shelter, where he reads the Newspaper published by the Lucky Clover Gazette. When Link first approaches Kiimo, he will read aloud an article about the appearance of Shrines of Light throughout Hyrule. He then comments that he must be reading an older story. Should Link speak to Kiimo againm he is able to ask him about the information in the Newspaper. If Link asks about current events, Kiimo shares the story of the Extreme Cold Snap in Hebra, and he notes that any visitors to Rito Village should prepare Cold Resistance. If Link asks about others stories, Kiimo reads a story that describes the dangers of a Blood Moon. This reminds him of a researcher who went to investigate the effects of the Blood Moon at Monster forts, and he wonders how he has been. If Link decides to leave Kiimo alone, he expresses his admiration for the Lucky Clover Gazette, as well as an interest in becoming a journalist.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kilton is a Hylian Monster fanatic who owns the Fang and Bone traveling shop where he sells Monster-related wares. He can only be encountered during the night, when the Fang and Bone appears. Initially, the Fang and Bone can only be found at Skull Lake. When first spoken to, Kilton will be startled by Link's sudden appearance, though he becomes disappointed when he realizes he is simply a Hylian. Link asks who he is, Kilton introduces himself and asks if came because he heard rumors of a Monster Shop. He further explains that he is still preparing for the grand opening of the Fang and Bone. To prove his point, he provides Link with his business card, which advertises the Fang and Bone. However, he requests that Link return the card to him because it is the only one he has. Kilton then hesitantly asks Link if he is interested in Monsters. I Link affirms that he likes them, Kilton then asks how much he likes them. If Link claims to adore them, Kilton interjects and states that he loves Monsters more than Link does. After taking a moment to calm himself, Kilton apologizes to Link for his outburst. He explains that he loves researching Monsters so much that he decided to open the Fang and Bone, which is dedicated to them. Kilton informs Link that he travels all over Hyrule, though he is unsure where he should visit next. During his musings, he discusses the benefits of visiting Kakariko Village, Hateno Village, Rito Village, Zora's Domain, Lurelin Village, and Tarrey Town. Thinking about it excites Kilton so much that he decides to take off from Skull Lake. Before he leaves, he tells Link that he is sure they will meet again in a village during the night. Kilton, along with the Fang and Bone, will then disappear. Following this encounter, Link can find Kilton on the outskirts of all the villages he mentioned starting at 9:00 PM. The spots where Kilton appears are marked by a Sign. During their second meeting, Kilton will once again be surprised to see Link. He announces that the Fang and Bone is officially open for business. Since it is Link's first time shopping at the Fang and Bone, Kilton decides that the first thing they will do is convert his Monster Parts in Mon. If Link asks what Mon is, Kilton explains that he loves Monsters so much that he turned them into money. Kilton explains that if Link brings him Monster Parts, he will give him Mon in exchange. The Fang and Bone is the only business that accepts Mon, which Kilton considers to be exclusive. With Mon, Link is able to purchase Monster gear, which Kilton created based on his research. Kilton also reveals that he is constantly developing more Monster gear, so he reminds Link to check out the Fang and Bone between his adventures. He then encourages Link to start exchanging Monster

exclusive. With Mon, Link is able to purchase Monster gear, which Kilton created based on his research. Kilton also reveals that he is constantly developing more Monster gear, so he reminds Link to check out the Fang and Bone between his adventures. He then encourages Link to start exchanging Monster Parts with him. On subsequent visits, Kilton is able to smell Monsters on Link before he turns around. He will be surprised to see Link once he turns to face him, at which point he welcomes him to the Fang and Bone. When Link leaves, Kilton will hope to see him again in the future. If Link is still at the Fang and Bone after 5:00 AM, Kilton will realize that it is time for him to leave. Kilton is the subject of the "A Shady Customer" Side Quest. At the East Akkala Stable, Hoz shares that he has heard rumors about Kilton and the Fang and Bone and that his activities have made the people of Akkala uncomfortable. He asks Link to share the appearance of any suspicious individuals he sees, especially if he spots Kilton. To satisfy Hoz, Link must take a Picture of Kilton with the Camera to show him. When Link shows him the Picture, Hoz will chuckle before remarking that Kilton is strange. He thanks Link for showing it to him, as he believes it will help him hunt Kilton down. After defeating Calamity Ganon, Link is able to ask Kilton about certain Monsters, which Kilton is happy to talk about. He decides to talk about the big ones, specifically Stone Taluses, Hinoxes, and Molduga. Kilton is aware of how many of each of the Monsters reside in Hyrule. Kilton is currently pursuing these Monsters, but he is unable to get near them due to their size. He asks Link to find and defeat all of the members of these giant Monster species. He plans on analyzing the scent of their fluids that will stick to Link's body during their battle, which will allow him to learn about their habits, behaviors, and other qualities. He tells Link that he is counting on him. Once Link has defeated all of the members of a Monster type, Kilton will be able to smell it on him. To reward Link for his assistance, he will gift him a Medal of Honor. He claims that as long as Link has his Medal of Honor, he will always be with him. He reassures Link that he will no longer have to suffer in silence, empathizing with his pain for having to kill a Monster. While Kilton considers destroying Monsters to be "soul-crushing work," he recognizes that it must be done. Even after collecting the Medals of Honor, Link can continue to ask Kilton about the giant Monsters. Despite sharing Link's pain, Kilton will excitedly praise him for being able to defeat them all. Due to Link's assistance, Kilton was able to learn about the structure and diet of Stone Taluses,

Even after collecting the Medals of Honor, Link can continue to ask Kilton about the giant Monsters. Despite sharing Link's pain, Kilton will excitedly praise him for being able to defeat them all. Due to Link's assistance, Kilton was able to learn about the structure and diet of Stone Taluses, the Food preferences between different types of Hinoxes, and the size limits of Molduga. He once again thanks Link for his help. At some point, Kilton passed his old Shop over to his brother, Koltin. Upon completion of the Side Adventure "The Hunt for Bubbul Gems!", he will take up residence in Tarrey Town.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kima can be found at the Southern Mine in Eldin. He wears a Flamebreaker Helm over his head to protect himself from the Scorching Climate. He spends his days searching near the edges of the Mine. When Link first speaks to him, Kima remarks that that he appeared at the perfect time. He admits that he has just returned from Goron City, but he forgot to bring any souvenirs for the trip. While he wants to catch some Fireproof Lizards to bring back, hw has been having trouble due to their speed. Judging that Link appears quick, Kima asks if he could bring him 10 Fireproof Lizards in exchange for a piece of Fireproof Armor. If Link refuses to help him, Kima resolves to try harder, even though he has bad knees. If Link agrees, Kima informs him that he may be able to find the Lizards around the Southern Mine. After he finishes speaking, the "Fireproof Lizard Roundup" Side Quest will begin. Once Link has gathered enough Fireproof Lizards, he can return to Kima to trade them. When Link agrees to give them to Kima, he will be given Flamebreaker Armor as a reward. Noticing Link's apparent disappointment, Kima realizes that he was expected his Flamebreaker Helm instead, and he explains that he can buy his own in Goron City. He directs Link north, which is where he can find Goron City. Kima remarks that it is useful to have extra souvenirs on hand. If Link has more Fireproof Lizards, Kima offers to buy three of them for 20 Rupees. With both Fireproof Lizards and Monster Parts, Kima states that he will be able to make Fireproof Elixirs. When he finishes speaking, the Side Quest will end. Link can return to the Southern Mine to sell Fireproof Lizards to Kima. If Link agrees to sell to him, Kima will give him a Red Rupee in return. He then informs Link that he can make Fireproof Elixirs by Cooking Fireproof Lizards and Monster Parts together. If Link refuses to sell, Kima will be disappointed, but he tells Link to come back if he changes his mind.

, also known as Marks of the King, are Items in . Location and Uses King's Scales are scales taken from Kings of the Zora. As part of the "Clues to the Sky" Main Quest, Link is required to shoot a King's Scale Fused to an Arrow through a tear-shaped ring of floating stones on Floating Scales Island. To do so, he must ask for them from Dorephan within the Pristine Sanctum. Dorephan will give him a set of five, offering to replenish the supply need be. Unlike most Materials, King's Scales cannot be sold at Shops nor to Traveling Merchants.

is a recurring location in . The King's Tomb goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The King's Tomb is located in the Graveyard and to the southwest of the Mido Town. The King's Tomb can be easily spotted as being a lone cross in the middle of the entire Graveyard. Error of Ruto Town tells Link of a secret tunnel to the south of King's Tomb that leads to the Island Palace. The King's Tomb may be found at the peak of Mount Hylia. It consists of a Tombstone under which King Rhoam was buried, following his death during the second Great Calamity. Similarly to Wagons, the King's Tomb can be searched once to obtain a Material. Possible candidates include a Flint, an Amber, or an Opal. While under the guise of the Old Man, King Rhoam can be found standing next to his own Tomb. He will comment on the Plateau's beauty, and, should Link not have a Warm Doublet, give him one for the trouble of making it there. Equipment Other Appearances (Valiant Comics) In the , the Old King's Tomb is one of the many places that Link and Princess Zelda must cross to reach the Island of Hyron. After Zelda reveals to Link that she wishes to reach the Island of Hyron to obtain the Magic Flute that will warp her and the Triforce of Wisdom far away from Ganon's grasp, the young hero comments that they will have to cross through the King's Tomb on their way to the island.

are recurring characters in . Biography thumb|left|250px|Princess Zelda is interrogated by her brother and the evil magician about the Triforce. The King of Hyrule was the last in a long line of Kings who wielded the entire Triforce, a practice that began sometime following the events of . In the backstory of , it is revealed that there was once a great and wise King of Hyrule that governed the land with the strength of the united Triforce as his command. However, the King too was human and, anticipating his death, he hoped to find someone with the innate qualities that were fitting of a worthy possessor of the Triforce for if it were to fall in the wrong hands, evil would befall Hyrule. Unfortunately, he was unable to find any such person during his lifespan and, since his own son did not fit this archetype for being worthy to possess the one true Triforce, the King elected to split the relic into its three parts, leaving the Triforce of Power and the Triforce of Wisdom within the kingdom. The Triforce of Courage, however, shared a different fate than that of its counterparts. In secret, the King spirited this piece of the Triforce away to the distant and dangerous Valley of Death, where he concealed the relic within the deepest sanctums of the Great Palace that was set at the head of the valley, guarded by many powerful Monsters handpicked by the King himself. The King cast a magical barrier over the entire Valley of Death, one that would not grant entry to the valley until six special Crystals were restored to their respective statues in six other palaces that lay across Hyrule. He also secretly cast a spell over all of Hyrule, one that would, at some point in time when a worthy person was born and came of age, cause the symbol of the Triforce to appear on the back of the hand of this special individual, marking him as the King’s chosen person to reclaim the Triforce of Courage. Soon after this, the King’s time was drawing to a close, and before he died, he confided what he had done only to his daughter, Princess Zelda, choosing to not tell any of the secrets of the Triforce to his son. thumb|left|250px|The evil Magician casts the sleeping curse upon Princess Zelda I upon her refusal to divulge her father's secret After the King’s death, the Prince of Hyrule hoped to claim the Triforce, but he was angered and dismayed to find that he would only inherit it in part. He searched the kingdom high and low for the third piece, but was unsuccessful. After being told by a mysterious Magician that the king had told Princess Zelda about the Triforce's whereabouts, the Prince confronted his sister, but she refused to tell him of the king's secret even after threatened of being put into an eternal sleep. Angered, the magician decided to cast the spell on the princess against

Once Agahnim ceased these disasters using his magic, the king named him his chief advisor. The King of Hyrule is first shown as a skeleton sitting on his Throne in Hyrule Castle during 's intro. He is said to have been killed by Agahnim. When Link wishes upon the Triforce for all of Ganon's destruction to be undone, he is seen resurrected beside his daughter, Zelda, and the six Maidens. her for saving him and asks what has happened while he was gone. He is distressed when he hears that Zelda has been in dangerous situations while mending Rifts, but he is also proud of her. Two Soldiers enter the Throne Room to check on the King, but they become hostile when they notice Zelda. The King informs them that the intruder is actually Zelda. The Soldiers still believe that Zelda is responsible for creating Rifts, which the King disputes. He sends Zelda to rest in her Room, promising to clear her name in the meantime. While Zelda rests, Tri shares the details of their journey so far with the King of Hyrule and Impa. When she wakes up, Impa relays a message from the King to meet him in the Throne Room. Zelda can find him waiting for her there with Impa, Minister Lefte, General Wright, and Lueburry. The King greets Zelda upon seeing her and begins their meeting. He wants to plan their next steps toward restoring peace to Hyrule. Tri suggests that there is a greater force creating the Echoes they have faced, which the King believes is the figure that attacked Zelda in the Still World. Suddenly, a Soldier arrives with news that three large Rifts have appeared. Shocked, the King asks where they are. Upon hearing that they are at Eldin Volcano, the Faron Wetlands, and Holy Mount Lanayru, he wonders if there is a connection to the Prime Energy. He explains that the Prime Energy is a source of power left behind by the Golden Goddesses, which the Royal Family of Hyrule has passed down legends of. He also shares another legend, which states that a priestess and a hero will appear to defend the Prime Energy from evil. Tri identifies Zelda as the priestess, and the King deduces that Link is the hero. As a result, the King commands Zelda to mend the Rifts and work with Link to defeat their enemy. He is saddened that Zelda will have to take on such a burden, but he offers to support her as best he can. The King then issues orders to Minister Lefte and General Wright. Lefte is to work with Lueburry to research and monitor Rifts, while Wright and his Soldiers are to fight off Monsters. The King then tells Impa to provide Zelda with special garments. Zelda returns to the Throne Room wearing the Royal Travel Attire, which the King claims is an heirloom of the Royal Family. At the end of their conversation, he asks Zelda to protect Hyrule. The Main Quests "Lands of the Goddesses" and "Rescuing the Hero Link" then begin. If Zelda speaks to the King during this time, he tells her that she is the only one who can mend the Rifts. The King of the Zora is a title belonging to multiple characters in . Biography The former King of the Zora, King Zora, is deceased by the time of . He was the husband of Rutela, and he created the Zora Armor. His grave is part of the Kakariko Village Graveyard. After Link is given the Zora Armor by Rutela, she asks him to pass on a message to her son, Ralis. She asks him to be brave and become the King of the Zora. At first, Ralis lacks confidence in his ability to lead the Zoras, so he remains in Kakariko Village. After he gives Link the Coral Earring, however, he decides to return to Zora's Domain to rule. Following this, Ralis can be found in the Domain, and the Zoras begin making plans for his coronation once peace returns to Hyrule. For the past 10,000 years, it has been the responsibility of Kings of the Zora to manage the Water level of East Reservoir Lake. This is the result of a promise the King of the Zora made to the King of Hyrule at the time. By the time of , King Dorephan has been the King of the Zora for at least 200 years. He and his wife, the Queen, had two children: Mipha and Sidon. As the Great Calamity drew near, he gave his permission for Mipha to become a Champion and pilot Divine Beast Vah Ruta. On the day of Calamity Ganon's revival, Vah Ruta was taken over by Waterblight Ganon before Mipha could reach it, and she died inside her Divine Beast. Shortly before the beginning of , Divine Beast Vah Ruta reactivated and began spreading Rain over the Lanayru Great Spring, threatening to wash Zora's Domain away. As part of the Main Quest "Divine Beast Vah Ruta", King Dorephan asks Link to help calm the Divine Beast. When Link returns to Dorephan after defeating Waterblight Ganon, he commends him for his efforts in saving the Domain. As a reward, Dorephan gives Link the Lightscale Trident that once belonged to Mipha. He also acknowledges Sidon's role in stopping the Divine Beast, claiming he will be a worthy heir when the time comes for him to be King. The History of the Zora, Part Three mentions another King of the Zora from the past, who was known for his love of the Zora and his Queen. When a horde of Lizalfos approached Zora's Domain from the Zodobon Highlands, he led his forces despite not being a talented fighter. Fearing for his life, the Queen wove one of her scales into his armor to protect him. He was attacked by the Lizalfos general, but he was saved when the Queen's scale reflected the sunlight and blinded the general. This allowed the King to defeat the Lizalfos army and save the Domain. reveals more information about Kings of the Zora that was not present in . When a King wishes to abdicate his title, he must cleanse himself in the Pristine Sanctum and offer one of his scales to its Throne, symbolizing his abandonment of the earthly world. Dorephan continues in his role of King of the Zora from . After being attacked by the Sludge Like, Dorephan secluded himself in the Pristine Sanctum to recover. At the end of his encounter with Link during the Main Quest "Clues to the Sky", Dorephan considers passing on his title to his son, Sidon, due to his age. After Link and Sidon defeat Mucktorok as part of the Main Quest "Sidon of the Zora", Dorephan decides it is time for Sidon to inherit his Throne. Although Sidon finds this sudden, Dorephan admits that he has been thinking of this for a while. Sidon also marries his fiancée, Yona, making her the Queen of the Zora. Afterwards, Sidon stands above the Zora's Domain Square and proclaims himself the new King. He and Yona ask the Zora to help Link during his Search for Princess Zelda. Other Appearances As established in , King Dorephan is the King of the Zora prior to the Great Calamity. The former King of the Zora was Qia's father, and he was responsible for leading the Zora in the Lanayru Wetlands. Like other leaders of Hyrule, he was presented with an Envoy Mask upon forging an alliance with Rauru and Sonia. Lago served as his bodyguard. When the Imprisoning War begins, the Forbidden Construct arrives in the Lanayru Wetlands and kills the King of the Zora. As a result, Qia becomes the Queen of the Zora earlier than anticipated. Due to Grimtorok's presence in the Lanayru Wetlands, Qia is forced to fight them and their Sludge Monsters soon after her father's death. Ashamed that he failed to protect the King, Lago temporarily renounced his role as a soldier.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kinov is a Hylian child who lives in Lurelin Village. He spends his day by his mother Kiana's side, following her around as goes about her day. At night, he sleeps in his home with his brother, Zuta. The first time Link speaks to Kiana, she will turn to Kinov to ask him what he wants for dinner. Kinov responds that he wants Seafood Paella, since he likes how she makes it. When Kiana decides to go with his suggestion, Kinov celebrates. During the day, Kinov will express his desire for his mother to make Seafood Paella for dinner. While Kiana is preparing their dinner, Kinov complains that he is hungry. When his entire family is gathered to eat, Kinov proclaims that Kiana's food is the best. If Link tries to speak to him while he is heading into his home for the night, Kinov informs him that he has to sleep.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kish is a Hylian and the owner of the Woodland Stable at the edge of the Eldin Canyon. He can be found at the front of Woodland Stable. If Woodland Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Kish will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Kish explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Kish then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Kish instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Kish suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Kish to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Kish tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Woodland Stable, Kish will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Kish thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Kish will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Kish asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Woodland Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Kish asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Kish will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Kish insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Kish refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Kish starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Kish gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from

to name her Epona. Kish gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Kish gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside Woodland Stable, Kish once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by Woodland Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Kish tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Kish wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay. Kish continues to manage Woodland Stable.

The , designated by the trial name Upward and Forward, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Kitawak Shrine is located on top of the East Gerudo Mesa in the Gerudo Highlands. It corresponds with the Kawatik Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation The entrance to the Kitawak Shrine is a short floor that opens way to an abyss below. Across from the entrance there is a floating platform with a short segment jutting out toward the entrance. At the ledge across from this segment there is a slab connected to the ledge by a hinge. This hinge holds it at an angle, preventing Link from crossing the gap. Along the floor there is a Stone Slab, which can be merged to the hinged slab to weigh it down and create a bridge to the floating platform. To the left of the floating platform, there is a spire with a Gear at its top standing between the platform and another floor along the wall. By merging a Stone Slab to the Gear, Link can create a rotating bridge to this floor. Along the right side of the platform, there is a pair of ramps cutting through the floor to a slightly lower level that holds a second Stone Slab. Beyond this side of the platform, there is a hinged seesaw in the gap leading to a higher level. On this higher level, there is a Shock Switch beside a second, hinged slab. This slab is held downward by the hinges holding it over an enclosed lower area with a platform controlled by the Shock Switch. This platform sits beneath the end of the hinged slab, and will raise to push the hinged slab when the Shock Switch is activated. This effect remains until the Shock Switch is manually deactivated. By merging one of the previous Stone Slabs onto the hinged slab and activating the Shock Switch while standing at the end of the Stone Slab, Link can propel himself in the air to reach the end of the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Kitawak Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

are recurring locations in . Features and Overview The Kitchen is a building located within Rito Village. It features the Village's only Cooking Pot, which rests above a Campfire in the center of its floor. Genli and Amali both frequent the Kitchen. When Link first arrives in Rito Village, Genli can be found in the Kitchen during the day. When spoken to, she will ask who Link is and if he came to stop Divine Beast Vah Medoh. At night, he can encounter Amali standing by the Cooking Pot, and she wonders if Link has anyone to Cook for. She goes on to explain that when she makes dinner for her family, she thinks about their future, but these dark thoughts disappear after she eats. Amali encourages Link to use the Cooking Pot to make Food for himself. After completing the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, Link can find Kheel at Warbler's Nest. She complains that her sisters have forgotten about practicing for their recital, and she asks Link to help retrieve them. Kheel believes that Genli may difficult to convince, as she is likely in the Kitchen demanding Salmon Meunière. This begins the "Recital at Warbler's Nest" Shrine Quest. True to Kheel's prediction, Genli can be found at the Kitchen, refusing to sing until she eats Salmon Meunière. Her other three sisters have all left to gather ingredients to make it for her. When Link locates Notts, Kotts, and Cree, they will each give Link an ingredient on the condition that he return to the Kitchen to make Salmon Meunière for Genli. If Link approaches Genli with Salmon Meunière in his Inventory, she is able to smell it and asks if he would give some to her. Should he agree, Genli will immediately eat it. After being reminded of her promise, Genli will leave the Kitchen to join her sisters. Once "Recital at Warbler's Nest" has been completed, Amali can be found in the Kitchen at all hours of the day. While she is here, she will speak to Link about her husband and daughters. Equipment There is a Kitchen located within the Emergency Shelter.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Knight's Bows are Bows that were once favored by the Hylian Knights who defended Hyrule Castle. Their metal construction grants them a superior durability, and they are known to be reliable while firing. Commonly, they are used by many Enemies in the Gerudo Desert and Tabantha Frontier. The following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Knight's Bow when they are scanned with the amiibo Rune: Series Princess Zelda amiibo Series Link (Archer) amiibo Being made of metal, Knight's Bows will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped outdoors during a Thunderstorm. In addition, they sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. They also do not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Knight's Bows belong to the Knight's Gear equipment archetype. Many of the Weapons in this grouping were used by the Hylian Knights prior to the Great Calamity. Knight's Bows are set to reappear in .

The is a recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Knight's Bridle is a type of Bridle that can be obtained by Jini at the Mounted Archery Camp. It is given when Link breaks 20-22 targets during the Horseback Archery Mini-Game. Before the Great Calamity, the Knights of Hyrule gave these Bridles to their Horses. Despite claiming that they provide additional armor to a Horse's head and neck, it is purely cosmetic. The Knight's Bridle belong to the Knight's Gear set of Horse Gear. Workers at Highland Stable, South Akkala Stable, Outskirt Stable, and Woodland Stable are able to equip Link's Horses with the Knight's Bridle. However, they are unable to be placed on Epona or the Giant Horse. The Knight's Bridle, alongside the Knight's Saddle, is obtainable by interacting with the Pony Points Ledger after collecting a total of 23 Pony Points from Stables. Afterwards, Link is able to speak to any Stable owner to have it equipped to his current Horse.

In the present, they are commonly used by adventurers due to their ease of use and high attack power. The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Knight's Saddle is a type of Saddle that is given to Link by Jini. are recurring Items in . Knight's Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Knight's Shields are mid-tier Shields once favored by the Knights of Hyrule who guarded the Royal Family of Hyrule. They belong to the Knight's Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons manufactured for Knights. They boast a great defense and Durability, comparable to that of even the strongest Enemy Shields. Though their metal construction makes them Durable, their weight makes it so they require more skill to wield. They can be found around the northern half of Hyrule Kingdom, wielded by Enemies in the Hebra Mountains and Eldin Mountains. There are a few notable exceptions, however, including a Treasure Chest in Gerudo Canyon Pass. Another Treasure Chest is located near Aquame Bridge leading to the Coliseum Ruins. It can be obtained as a reward from Selmie for completing the Shield-Surfing Mini-Game with a time between 1:45 and 2:00. Finally, Russ sells a Knight's Shield on Trilby Plain for 300 Rupees. If Link buys it from him, he will call it a sturdy Shield, which reminds him of the rumored Durability of the Hylian Shield. The , also known as the Dye Shop, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Kochi Dye Shop is located in Hateno Village. It is the only Shop of its kind in Hyrule. Sayge operates the Dye Shop itself, while his wife, Senna, greets visitors outside. At night, their son Sefaro sleeps in one of the Shop's Beds, muttering about a Sheikah girl. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Sayge can use Hateno Dyes to change the color of Link's Armor. The procedure costs 20 Rupees, but Link must provide five Materials of matching color as well. In the past, the Kochi Dye Shop would be able to prepare these Materials themselves, but the increased number of Monsters has made their collection difficult. As a result, the Shop started allowing customers to bring their own Materials, with the addition of a service charge. As is tradition in Hateno Village, Link's entire outfit will be Dyed at once. Sayge is also able to restore Link's Armor to its original appearance. When Link decides to Dye his Armor, he will be transported to the nearby platform, where Sayge prompts him to either choose a Hateno Dye color or change his Armor. If Link is wearing Armor that cannot be Dyed, Sayge will warn him of this fact. After selecting a Dye color, Sayge then asks for five Materials that match. He then asks Link for his 20 Rupee payment. Once everything has been finalized, Sayge thanks Link and instructs him to stay still, at which point he drops him and his Materials into the basin below. When Link leaves the basin, his entire outfit will have been Dyed. Sayge will also offer to redo the Dye if Link dislikes it. Equipment Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Kodah is a Zora who resides at Zora's Domain. She is one of the owners of the Seabed Inn, the other being her husband Kayden. She spends her days tending to the Inn. Kodah knew Link prior to the second Great Calamity, affectionately referring to him as "Linny." She asked Link to choose between herself and Mipha. Since then, she married Kayden, and they had their daughter Finley together. When Divine Beast Vah Ruta began its rampage, Kodah banned Finley from going to the Bank of Wishes. When Link first approaches Kodah, she will begin to welcome him to the Seabed Inn. Recognizing Link, she asks if he is "Linny" and does not wait for an answer before proclaiming that he is. After Link speaks, Kodah only becomes more certain, remarking that it has been a long time since they last saw each other. Since she thought both Link and Mipha had fallen to Calamity Ganon, Kodah begs Link to tell her where he has been and what he has been doing since the Great Calamity. Embarrassed, Kodah apologizes for making a ruckus, as she is an adult. She asks if it has really been a century, because to her it feels like yesterday. Kodah states they have both been through a lot and that they should catch up sometime soon. When Link speaks to Kodah again, he will be able to ask her questions. If Link asks about Mipha, Kodah will be shocked to hear that he forgot about her. She explains that Mipha was a princess, in addition to being King Dorephan's daughter and Sidon's older sister. As the Zora Champion, she was beloved by her people, and she could also heal their wounds. 100 years ago, Mipha piloted Divine Beast Vah Ruta against Calamity Ganon, which led to her death. If Link asks Kodah who she is, she calls him terrible and introduces herself. She apologizes to Link for asking him to choose between herself and Mipha 100 years ago. Now, she is married to Kayden and has a daughter named Finley. If Link again questions the name "Linny," Kodah reveals that it is the nickname she gave him a century ago. Though much time has passed, she still remembers that he is Link, the Hylian Champion who fought against Calamity Ganon with Mipha. Kodah warns Link that the council of elders is angry about what happened, believing that Link stole Mipha away from them. However, Zora such as Kodah who are around 100 years old know what it was like back then and do not believe that, since Link and Mipha are the ones who have held back Calamity Ganon. When spoken to after Link has appeased Divine Beast Vah Ruta, Kodah notices that the Rain has stopped and wonders if it means that Divine Beast Vah Ruta has ended its rampage. Kodah then notices Link standing nearby and apologizes, asking if he needs something. Kodah is present when

Ganon. When spoken to after Link has appeased Divine Beast Vah Ruta, Kodah notices that the Rain has stopped and wonders if it means that Divine Beast Vah Ruta has ended its rampage. Kodah then notices Link standing nearby and apologizes, asking if he needs something. Kodah is present when King Dorephan and Sidon thank Link for appeasing the Divine Beast. Afterwards, Kodah thanks Link for appeasing the Divine Beast. After the Rain stops, Kodah is unable to find her daughter Finley, even after searching everywhere. Once Sasan has arrived in Zora's Domain, Kodah remarks that he is not what she expected. Finley's taste in men reminds her of someone else.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kohm is a Gerudo who manages the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Northwest Booth in Gerudo Town. Her daughter, Frelly, trains the Sand Seals and manages the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth. When Link speaks to Kohm, she introduces herself, reasoning that Link is the Hylian that Frelly was talking about. Kohm explains that they rent out Sand Seals and that their business is thriving. While it seems unlikely, their business is actually thriving, which is aided by the fact that customers can easily learn how to ride Sand Seals. The only thing Link will have to do is stand on his Shield, and the Sand Seal will pull him through the Gerudo Desert. Kohm also explains that due to their training, their Sand Seals are easier to ride than wild Sand Seals. She tells Link to let her know when he needs a Sand Seal. The next time Link visits Kohm, she tells him that he will need a Sand Seal in order to cross the Gerudo Desert. She offers to rent him one for 20 Rupees. If Link asks how to "set seal," Kohm explains that he will only need to guide his Sand Seal. She claims that the best way to learn is through experience. Whether Link refuses or accepts Kohm's offer, she will notice his Sand Seal puns and wonder if that is how people speak outside of Gerudo Town. If Link chose not to rent a Sand Seal, Kohm reminds him that he would be wise to take one if he travels outside of Gerudo Town. After hearing Link's puns, Kohm will begin to incorporate them into her speech. She says that a Sand Seal is the best way to cross the Gerudo Desert, claiming that Link will "seal" what she means. When Link asks about riding Sand Seals this time, she states that he will "seal" how easy it is to learn. If Link decides to rent a Sand Seal, Kohm says it was great "sealing" him. If Link refuses, Kohm reminds him that the Gerudo Desert "stretches as far as the eye can seal."

is a recurring character in . Biography Koko is a little girl residing in Kakariko Village with her younger sister Cottla and their father Dorian. She has a tendency to speak about herself in the third person. Early in the morning at around 5:00 AM, Koko will go to Kakariko Village's graveyard and begin to cry, but is startled out of it when Link comes close. The girl will deny crying, saying her mother needs her to be strong. Link can ask her about her mother and Koko will tell him that she has passed away and that she is resting in the graveyard. She understands that her father is not being truthful about what happened, but she realized it on her own. If Link decides not to ask about her mother, Koko can explain that her family is reacting to her mother's absence in different ways and asks that Link not tell her sister that he saw her. At around 8:00 AM, Koko will leave the grave site to meet with the rest of her family at the base of a specific Tree, growing at the fork in the road that leads up to the East Hill. Once she reaches the spot and sits down with her sister Cottla, Koko explains that her mother was very fond of the Tree. Once Link has had his first meeting with Impa, Dorian will also join them at the Tree. At 11:00 AM, the family parts ways and Koko goes to the public kitchen to Cook Food for her sister. Link can speak to her and she will declare that dinner is Veggie Cream Soup. While she claims that the dish is healthy, she admits that she only knows that through hearsay. Koko tells Link how he can make the dish. However, Koko quickly realizes that she is missing an ingredient and panics. Whether or not Link agrees to help Koko, just speaking to her begins the Side Quest, "Koko's Kitchen". Once the Side Quest is completed, Koko will have another problem at the Cooking Pot. If spoken to, she will be debating on what to make before settling on Hot Buttered Apple, a Recipe of her mother's that she and her sister enjoy. Koko goes over the ingredients out loud, then realizes that she is once again short one. Disappointed in herself, she guiltily calls herself a bad daughter that cannot take her mother's place. Again, just the act of hearing Koko's problem begins the Side Quest, "Cooking with Koko". When this Side Quest has been finished, Koko will have another dilemma ready for Link to solve. She will be contemplating what new meal to make and decides on a favorite of Dorian's, Tough Meat-Stuffed Pumpkin. The girl claims this meal is good for a boost of energy. Once more, Koko lists the ingredients needed and finds herself lacking. Although she admits she could use other meat, she wishes to use her mother's recipe. Dorian used to hunt to replenish their

Her opinion on it has matured with the passage of time, but when mourning her mother she still takes shelter, albeit under the Tree in the graveyard.

, also known as the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Kolami Bridge is located in the Tabantha Frontier between Strock Lake and Tanagar Canyon. Kolami Bridge is a long, thin strip of logs tied together across a long gap. Along the Bridge, Wind Gusts blow hard sometimes east and sometimes west. Link can use the Paraglider to glide down the west wind to Strock Lake quickly, or use the east wind to glide across Tanagar Canyon. Down under the Bridge, although there are many Enemies, there are some Luminous Stone Deposits for Link to harvest. Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds Materials Other Appearances Located in the Tabantha Frontier Stage, the Bridge to Rito Village spans a wide gap overlooking Tanagar Canyon. True to its name, it leads to Rito Village to the north. It is made out of Snow-covered logs tied together by ropes. An Outpost is located just southeast of it. During the Scenario "Revali, the Rito Warrior", a Bow-wielding Rito Captain destroys it with a Bomb Arrow to cut off access to Rito Village, forcing the Warriors to take an alternate route north. After traveling through the west side of the Stage, the Warriors can jump down to the plateau below the Bridge, which is inhabited by a group of Ice-Breath Lizalfos and an Ice Moblin. On this plateau is a Wooden Box and a Cracked Wall blocking an Updraft that the Warriors can ride up to the north side of the Bridge, which connects to the Outpost in front of Rito Village guarded by Revali. The south end of the Bridge to Rito Village can be visited in its destroyed state in the Challenges "Anti-Ice Training: I" and "Mountain Rescue". Its north side and the plateau below it can be accessed during the Challenges "Fairy Fountain: Deep Snows" and "Fierce Gale of the Rito". The "Winged Escort" Challenge allows Teba to cross the Bridge in its intact state, thus allowing access to both its north and south sides, and, by extension, the plateau below it. All Challenges lack the Cracked Wall on the plateau, leaving the Updraft exposed and readily usable.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Kolomo Garrison Ruins are located in Hyrule Field. They sit on a small plateau that juts into the neighboring Lake Kolomo. They are the remains of the Kolomo Garrison, which was destroyed during the second Great Calamity. If Downloadable Content pack is installed, a metallic Treasure Chest containing Majora's Mask can be found buried in a pile of debris at the southern corner of the Ruins as part of the "EX Treasure: Ancient Mask" Side Quest. A Korok can be found by lifting a Rock hidden under a pile of leaves in the Garrison Ruins. Creatures Enemies Equipment As in , the Kolomo Garrison Ruins are located at the the south end of Lake Kolomo in Hyrule Field. As shown in the "Zelda and Sonia" Memory, neither the Kolomo Garrison nor the Kolomo Garrison Ruins existed in the Era of Myth. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests

Koltin's Stall is a location in . Features and Overview Koltin's Stall is a Shop run by Koltin, who will trade various Armor and Monster Parts to Link in exchange for Bubbul Gems. Initially, Koltin's Stall can be found in front of the Pico Pond Cave. There, Koltin and his brother Kilton are looking for a Bubbulfrog so that Koltin can acquire and eat a Bubbul Gem in order to become "a Satori". Link can speak with them to begin the Side Adventure "The Hunt for Bubbul Gems!". When Link brings a Bubbul Gem to Koltin, he will receive the Bokoblin Mask in exchange. After this, Koltin will take his Stall and leave to search for more Bubbul Gems, and Kilton will ask Link if he can continue to help Koltin realize his dream. He will also tell Link that he plans to settle in Tarrey Town, should he need any clues as to Koltin's whereabouts. This will begin the Side Adventure "The Search for Koltin", during which Link must find Koltin's Stall at night at any of its locations in Hyrule. Once Link finds Koltin and speaks with him, the Side Adventure will be complete. Link will then be able to give Koltin Bubbul Gems in exchange for his rewards, which is classified as an Additional Adventure known as "Bubbul Gems". Link can also speak with Koltin at each of the Koltin's Stall locations to obtain hints on where to look for Bubbulfrogs that he has not yet found. However, Koltin can only provide the locations of five preset Caves for each location he can be found, totaling to 35 out of the 147 Caves. After Link turns in all 147 Bubbul Gems to Koltin and receives Koltin's Fabric, Koltin will complete his transformation into "a Satori". Link can then visit Tarrey Town and speak with Kilton, informing him of his brother's fate. Kilton will thank Link for telling him, and say that he will take Koltin's Stall to Koltin's "favorite place". After this, Koltin's Stall can be found at any time of the day next to the Cherry-Blossom Tree on Satori Mountain, with a few Blupees nearby. Koltin's Stall Locations Koltin's Stall only appears at night between 9:00 PM and 5:00 AM. Koltin's Stall Rewards Koltin's rewards are available in a set order, and each Item must be traded for before the next becomes available.

Koltin is a character in . Biography Koltin is the brother of Kilton. He trades various Armor and Monster Parts to Link in exchange for Bubbul Gems, believing that consuming them will allow him to become "a Satori". Koltin can initially be found at Pico Pond Cave with Kilton, looking for a Bubbulfrog to obtain a Bubbul Gem from. When Link first speaks with Kilton, Koltin will emerge from the Cave entrance, telling his brother that while he has found a Bubbulfrog, he is unable to catch it. The two of them ask Link for his assistance, and Koltin promises to give him a "treasure" in exchange for a Bubbul Gem. This begins the Side Adventure "The Hunt for Bubbul Gems!". After Link obtains a Bubbul Gem and gives it to Koltin, he will give Link the Bokoblin Mask, completing the Side Adventure. Koltin will then eat the Bubbul Gem, but he finds that doing so does not transform him into "a Satori". He instead feels a strange sensation, indicating that he is on his way to becoming "a Satori", but he will need to consume a large quantity of Bubbul Gems at once to accomplish it. Speaking to Kilton, he then says that he has decided to travel across Hyrule to acquire more Bubbul Gems. Kilton, seeing that Koltin has made up his mind, tells him that he will give Koltin his full support. Koltin then tells Link that he is about to set out on his journey, and asks Link if he will give him any other Bubbul Gems he finds. Koltin then leaves, and Kilton tells Link that he will be in Tarrey Town, but he will listen for any news of his brother if Link needs help finding him. This begins the Side Adventure "The Search for Koltin". In order to complete this Side Adventure, Link must find and speak to Koltin in his Stall at any of its seven locations across Hyrule. As part of the Additional Adventure "Bubbul Gems", Link can continue to bring Koltin Bubbul Gems in exchange for rewards. Koltin will also be to sense the locations of nearby Bubbulfrogs for Link, but this is limited to five preset Caves per Stall location. Once Link has given Koltin all 147 Bubbul Gems, he will give Link Koltin's Fabric and ask him to show it to Kilton. Then he will fully transform into "a Satori", taking on the appearance of a Blupee before running away and vanishing. Link can then visit Kilton in Tarrey Town and tell him what happened to Koltin. Kilton will give Link his thanks and say that he will move Koltin's Stall to his brother's "favorite place". He will also tell Link to keep Koltin's Fabric, saying that it is what Koltin would have wanted. Koltin's Stall Locations Koltin's Stall only appears at night between 9:00 PM and 5:00 AM.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Komo Shoreline is located along the Faron Sea on the southern end of the Faron Grasslands. A large cliff from Ibara Butte hangs over the Shoreline and forms a natural stone tunnel, where several Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits can be found. On occasion, a strong Wind from the Faron Sea sweeps over the beach. Several shallow pools of Water are situated throughout the Komo Shoreline. One Treasure Chest can be found on Komo Shoreline. It is located in the tide pool on the western end of the Shoreline. When Link opens the Chest, he will receive a bundle of five Ice Arrows. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Konba is a Hylian man who can be found camped at the Footrace Check-In. He operates the Foot Race Mini-Game. When approached, Konba notices that Link looks tough and challenges him to a friendly race. If Link declines his offer, Konba will be disappointed, as he finally thought that he found a worthy opponent. Alternatively, if Link accepts, Konba will introduce stakes to their race. Link can refuse Konba's stakes, which causes him to say he will never get anywhere in life with such an attitude. If Link decides to go along with it, Konba will leave to set up the Foot Race. Once Konba returns, he explains that the objective of the Foot Race is the pair of Big Flags on top of Mount Rhoam. However, he reminds Link that it is a Foot Race, not a "hoof race," and he will be disqualified if he rides a Horse. After explaining this, he will begin the Foot Race. If Link reaches the Big Flags before Konba does, he will be shocked to see that he lost. Back at the Footrace Check-In, he reluctantly rewards Link with a Purple Rupee. However, if Konba finishes the Foot Race before Link, he will gloat and cheer for his victory. When they return to the Footrace Check-In, Konba tells Link that he did well, but he will have to try harder if he wants to beat him. After finishing a Foot Race, Konba will ask Link if he wants to start another one. If Link agrees, Konba will become excited and explains that the rules are the same as before. If Link refuses, Konba will be disappointed, but he encourages Link to use his traveling as a chance to build his leg muscles. He also invites Link to come back to the Footrace Check-In if he ever wants to race again.

is a recurring character in . Biography Konora is a Gerudo who can first be found inside the Kara Kara Bazaar Inn. She lives in Gerudo Town, but she is stuck at the Kara Kara Bazaar because of the threat posed by Divine Beast Vah Naboris and its Lightning. When Link first speaks to Konora, she comments that the Divine Beast seems to get closer every day. Konora wonders how long it will be until she can return to Gerudo Town. If Link asks about the Divine Beast, she explains that she is talking about the giant thing roaming around the Gerudo Desert. According to Konora, it has been creating sandstorms and will blast Lightning at anyone who comes near. She is too afraid of getting struck by Divine Beast Vah Naboris's Lightning to travel back to Gerudo Town. If Link asks about Gerudo Town, Konora explains that it is a large, lively town to the southwest made up almost entirely of Gerudo. However, she tells Link that he cannot enter Gerudo Town because men are not allowed inside. Konora wishes that a hero would do something about the Divine Beast Vah Naboris. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Konora can be found sitting in The Noble Canteen in Gerudo Town. If Link speaks to her, she explains that she forgot where she lives because she has been gone so long. After a long pause, she yells that she is not joking. Konora is found amongst Cherry-Blossom Trees which she deems as romantic. She wonders if Link could be the voe she is destined to fall in love with, but can tell from the look on his face that this is not the case. Nevertheless she still believes to find the voe of her dreams in a place as magical as this. She proceeds to tell him about the magical creature called a Satori, which can be found near such trees and loves fruits. After Link summons the Lord of the Mountain, Konora will note that she felt an unusual sensation in the air, but she seems not to have actually seen the spirit.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Kopeeki Drifts are a field of Snow located on the eastern side of the Tabantha Frontier. An abandoned tent can be found on the northern end of the Drifts, as well as many small Snowballs. Gee Ha'rah Shrine is situated in the Kopeeki Drifts Cave on the southern end of the Kopeeki Drifts, but its entrance is blocked by a pair of Giant Stone Doors. To access the Ancient Shrine, Link must roll a Snowball into the Doors from the top of the Drifts, which will break them open. One Treasure Chest can be found on the Kopeeki Drifts. When Link opens the Chest, he will receive a Knight's Shield. Creatures

The is a recurring location in . The Kopeeki Drifts Cave goes unnamed in . Overview The entrance to the Kopeeki Drifts Cave can be found on the southern edge of the Kopeeki Drifts on the Tabantha Frontier. However, it is initially blocked by a pair of Giant Stone Doors. By rolling a Snowball from the top of the Kopeeki Drifts, Link is able to open the Doors and access its interior. Since the Cave is located in a Freezing Climate, Link will require at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit it without taking damage. Areas The Kopeeki Drifts Cave is a Cave in the Tabantha Frontier, and it is located at the southern edge of the Kopeeki Drifts. It is situated within a Freezing Climate that Link needs at least two levels of Cold Resistance to avoid taking damage from. The Cave's interior is much larger, and it is filled with Cold Water that will damage Link if he falls into it. Link is also unable to Climb the walls around the Cold Water, since they are made of Ice. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Korne Beach is located along the Necluda Sea in East Necluda. It stretches south along the Necluda Sea before shifting west, turning into Clarnet Coast. There are many small patches of Palm Trees along the beach which sport Palm Fruit. Kilton will open the Fang and Bone is a shop run by Kilton during the night. During the day, only a Sign appears without Kilton. Around the middle of the beach, there is a spot with many rocks. Underwater near these rocks is a metallic Treasure Chest containing a Red Rupee. Link can raise the chest out of the water with his Magnesis Rune. South of this chest, there is another chest underwater that holds an Amber. Farther out in the water, there are 2 chests that have sunk below the water. One of these chests holds a bundle of 5 Shock Arrows while the other holds an Opal. Another chest can be found behind the Fang and Bone underwater. This chest encloses a Purple Rupee. East of this chest in the water is another chest. This chest contains a Topaz. Farther north of this chest is another chest. This chest holds a Purple Rupee. The final chest can be found right before Korne Beach turns west into Clarnet Coast. The chest is buried in the sand near a cluster of Palm Trees. This chest holds an Amber. A Korok can be found hiding in a Rock Circle a small distance from the water. There are 3 gaps that need to be filled with rocks. The rocks can be found in their own smaller circle formations around the bigger circle. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Korok Forest is located at the center of the Lost Woods in the Great Hyrule Forest. In order to access the Forest, Link must follow the direction of the Wind in the Lost Woods. The Great Deku Tree is known to be the protector of Korok Forest, and it is also home to a variety of Koroks. The primary feature of the Forest is the Pedestal of the Master Sword, which houses the Master Sword when it is not in use. Keo Ruug Shrine is also situated at the base of the Great Deku Tree. An Ogre Tree east of the Pedestal serves as the exit to Korok Forest, returning Link to the entrance of the Lost Woods when he steps into its mouth. 100 prior to the events of , Link entered the Korok Forest at around the age of 12 or 13 and pulled the Master Sword from its Pedestal. After Link fell on the day of the Great Calamity, Princess Zelda returned the Master Sword to its Pedestal, hoping that he would find it again after his Slumber of Restoration. She attempted to leave a message for the Great Deku Tree to relay to Link, though he insisted that it would be better for Link to hear her words directly from her. The events of Zelda and the Great Deku Tree's conversation can be seen during Recovered Memory "The Master Sword", which Link recalls as part of the Main Quest "The Hero's Sword". In preparation for Link's inevitable return to Korok Forest, the Koroks prepared a series of Korok Trials to help guide him to the Ancient Shrines in the Lost Woods. Eventually, the Trials became rites of passage for young Koroks. These Trials can be found by following the Signs or Bean Lamps throughout Korok Forest. The Goddess Statue of Korok Forest in located within the Great Deku Tree's Navel. When Link first enters Korok Forest, he will be directed towards the Pedestal of the Master Sword. If he attempts to pull the Master Sword, he will receive a vision of several Recovered Memories, and the voice of Princess Zelda reminds him that he is the hope of Hyrule. The Great Deku Tree then awakens, recognizing Link from 100 years prior. He informs Link that he once wielded the Master Sword, though he warns him that he may currently be too weak to do so now. After speaking to the Great Deku Tree, The Main Quest "The Hero's Sword" will begin. When Downloadable Content pack is active, the Side Quest "EX Trial of the Sword" will take place at Korok Forest. As part of this Side Quest, Link will be able to access the Trial of the Sword from the Pedestal of the Master Sword. Areas Creatures Materials Equipment As in , Korok Forest is located within the Great Hyrule Forest, north of Hyrule Castle. It is surrounded by the Lost Woods, which are impenetrable. The only way for Link to first access Korok Forest is by Ascending through an Ascend Access Point in the Great Hyrule Forest Depths's Korok Grove. When Link emerges at Korok Forest, he finds the Great Deku Tree in a sickly state. The air carries a Gloom fog, rendering the Koroks within catatonic. In order for Link to restore the Forest to normal, he must enter the Great Deku Tree's Navel and descend into the Deku Tree Chasm within. Gloom Spawn, the source of the illness, can be found below. By defeating the Gloom Spawn and the Phantom Ganon that appears afterward, Link can restore Korok Forest to normal. Areas Creatures Materials Equipment Other Appearances In , Korok Forest first appears in the Scenario, "Freeing Korok Forest." In the first battle, Korok Forest could be seen from above from Divine Beast Vah Medoh. In the second battle, Link and Zelda destroy the Malice swamp blocking the way to Korok Forest, and defeat Astor, who was in Korok Forest. Link was also able to get the Master Sword there.

The is an archetype of Weapon in . Location and Uses Korok Gear is weaponry crafted by the Koroks to be used by Hylians. The exception to this is the Korok Leaf, which is a naturally occurring leaf. All other forms of Korok Gear are made from the sturdy of wood of Trees that grow within the Korok Forest. Every piece of Korok Gear will float when they are dropped in Water, which is due to their plant-like compositions. This also means they will burn and eventually disintegrate when they are exposed to a Fire or a Scorching Climate. They do not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, and they cannot be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. is a location in . Features and Overview Korok Grove is a large grove in the Great Hyrule Forest Depths. It is only accessible from the southeast, near Minshi Grove. Korok Grove corresponds to Korok Forest on the Surface. A secluded portion of the Korok Grove sits inside the roots of the Great Deku Tree and can only be accessed by descending from the Deku Tree Chasm in the Great Deku Tree's Navel. Inside, there is a spacious chamber where a Gloom Spawn lurks, hurting the Great Deku Tree. When it is defeated, a Phantom Ganon will appear to challenge Link. Upon its defeat, the Gloom infecting the Great Deku Tree will disappear, and its climate will return to the normal conditions of the Korok Forest. With the threat removed, three Koroks will descend from the Deku Tree Chasm to thank Link and tell him that the Great Deku Tree wishes to speak to him. A trail of Mighty Bananas runs from the Ramobnukas Lightroot into the Forest Coliseum further in the Great Hyrule Forest Depths. It is revealed to be a trap set by Yiga Footsoldiers to kill Link when he sets foot into the Forest Coliseum. Areas Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses In the Downloadable Content Pack for , obtaining the Korok Mask is the objective of the "EX Strange Mask Rumors" Side Quest. As part of the Quest, Link must read the Super Rumor Mill V1 at the Woodland Stable. According to Traysi, the Korok Mask is inhabited by a spirit. She has also heard that it occasionally shakes and makes noises when worn, which she theorizes may be due to hidden friends nearby. Finally, Traysi shares that it is supposedly hidden in the hollow of a Tree in a forest that makes people lose their way. The Korok Mask can be found in a Hidden Chest south of the pair of stationary Torches at the Lost Woods' entrance. It is located in the mouth of an Ogre Tree. After obtaining the Korok Mask, Granté will begin selling it for 50 Rupees. When worn, the Mask shakes when a Korok is hiding nearby. The Korok Mask can be found in the Forest Coliseum in the Great Hyrule Forest Depths. When Link enters the Coliseum, he will be greeted by two Yiga Footsoldiers, who release a Black Hinox to attack him. Once Link defeats the Black Hinox, a shroud of Gloom over a Treasure Chest clears, allowing him to collect the Korok Mask. Other Appearances

Korok Seeds are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Korok Seeds are given by Koroks when they are found throughout Hyrule. They possess a distinct smell. When Link receives his first Seed, he is asked to return it to the Korok Hestu. Korok Seeds are actually the beads used in Hestu's Maracas. When first found, Hestu asks Link to retrieve his Maracas from a group of Bokoblins nearby. After Link returns them, Hestu realizes the Seeds were taken by the other Koroks as part of a prank. In exchange for Korok Seeds, Hestu will add one slot to Link's Weapon, Bows, or Shields stashes. Link can fully upgrade his inventory with only 441 Korok Seeds. If all 900 Seeds are returned to Hestu, he will reward Link with a "gift of friendship".
