is a character in . Biography Kosi is a Hylian handyman in Lookout Landing's Emergency Shelter. He wears a pair of Soldier's Greaves, and he can be seen working to restore a Soldier's Helm. When Link first approaches Kosi, he decides to talk through his work, claiming that it requires his attention. He explains that as a result of the Upheaval, all Weapons have become decayed, and he has been unable to repair them. If Link asks about the decay, Kosi reveals that their Weapons were attacked by Gloom right before the Upheaval. Due to the chaos brought brought by the Upheaval, Kosi has given up on trying to understand what has happened. At the end of their conversation, Kosi allows Link to take the nearby Traveler's Sword and Boko Reaper. Should Link speak to Kosi again, he says that he has been attaching things to the ends of Weapons.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kotta is a Gerudo Soldier who can be found in the Barracks in Gerudo Town. She carries a Gerudo Spear. The first time Link speaks to Kotta, she expresses disbelief that the Thunder Helm was stolen. Before she can continue, she is interrupted by Liana, who yells at her for speaking of their problems to outsiders. Upset that she is in trouble again, Kotta blames Link. After Link has started the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Kotta is afraid she will have to go searching on a Sand Seal again, as she gets sick while riding them. If Link approaches Liana, he will hear her asking Leena and Kotta if they have seen Barta. Leena reveals that Barta told them two days ago that she was going to investigate the Yiga Clan Hideout, and she has not returned since then. Liana is afraid that Teake will make them run 100 laps around the Gerudo Desert once she hears that they lost Barta. Kotta asks what they should do about this, to which Liana snaps that she is thinking about it. Once Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Link can return to the Barracks to find that Kotta is anxious about Barta being in trouble again. When he approaches Liana, she will be shocked to hear that Barta has yet again failed to return to Gerudo Town. Kotta explains that she went to investigate the Gerudo Great Skeleton in the southwest of the Gerudo Desert. Leena reminds Liana that a Molduga lives in that area, so she did not think Barta would even approach. Kotta agrees, adding on that the Heat in that part of the Desert would make it difficult for Barta to last with their gear. This only angers Liana further, as she believes they let Barta walk into a dangerous situation. She resigns herself to the fact that Barta, Leena, and Kotta are never going to change. Afterwards, "The Search for Barta" Side Quest will begin. When Link speaks to Kotta while the Side Quest is active, she shares a rumor about a fairy living in the Gerudo Great Skeleton. She thought Barta would be interested in this, but since a Molduga lives in the area, she never thought she would actually investigate it alone. Once Barta has returned to the Barracks, Kotta notes that she seems to feel guilty about the mess she caused. However, she is jealous that someone who is all over the place like Barta is still popular with men. Kotta is a member of the Sword Troops.

is a recurring character in . Biography Kotts is a Rito child who can be found in Rito Village. She is the second-eldest daughter of Kass and Amali, the younger sister of Notts, and the older sister of Genli, Cree, and Kheel. At night, she sleeps in her home alongside her sisters. When Link first arrives in Rito Village, he can find Kotts in Kaneli's House. She admits that she is scared of the "bird monster" in the sky, and she asks if Link is also scared. If Link claims not to be scared, Kotts is shocked and wonders if he could be a Champion. Alternatively, if Link tells Kotts that he is scared, she will become hopeless, since he is bigger than her. She gets the idea to feed Fish to Divine Beast Vah Medoh until it is too full to eat her. However, she becomes concerned that it will try to eat her when she goes to feed it the Fish. Finally, if Link is confused about what she means by "bird monster," Kotts tells him to talk to Kaneli. She promises to hold his hand if the story gets too scary for him. When she leaves Kaneli's House for the day, Kotts remarks that she has to return to her home quickly or else she might be eaten by the Divine Beast. After calming Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Link can find Kotts' sister, Kheel, at Warbler's Nest. She complains that Kotts and the rest of their sisters promised to rehearse with her, but none of them showed up. She asks Link to return to Rito Village and remind her sisters about their rehearsal, as she thinks they will listen to a "scary-looking Hylian" over herself. This starts the "Recital at Warbler's Nest" Shrine Quest. Link can find Kotts at the ponds in front of Rito Village, where she is fishing for Hearty Salmons. When Link reminds her about her rehearsal, she is confused at first. However, when she realizes what he is talking about, she explains that she forgot due to her focus on catching Fish. Afraid that Kheel will kill her, Kotts gives Link a Hearty Salmon so he can make Salmon Meunière for Genli in the Kitchen. She hopes that Genli will feel like singing after she eats it. Before she leaves the pond, Kotts wants to try to catch some more Fish. In the meantime, she encourages Link to try and find the rest of her sisters. She shares that Notts like places that are high and Cree is at The Slippery Falcon. Once Link has gathered all of the ingredients, she tells him to go to the Kitchen to make Salmon Meunière in the Cooking Pot. Once all of the sisters have been gathered, Link can return to Warbler's Nest to find them all singing together. Kheel explains that they are practicing a song passed down in Rito Village that was sung at Warbler's Nest in ancient times. When Link speaks to Kotts,

the Cooking Pot. Once all of the sisters have been gathered, Link can return to Warbler's Nest to find them all singing together. Kheel explains that they are practicing a song passed down in Rito Village that was sung at Warbler's Nest in ancient times. When Link speaks to Kotts, she will accidentally mess up the song. Promising not to mess it up again, she promises to perform it for Link. If Link agrees, the sisters will sing for him. After Link uncover Voo Lota Shrine, Kheel will excitedly point it out to Kotts and her other sisters. Kotts notices that it is an Ancient Shrine, which Kaneli told them about. Notts says that they should inform their mother, to which Kotts declares that the last one to reach Amali is an unhatched egg. The five sisters will then fly back to Rito Village. Back in Rito Village, Link can find the sisters singing together near Akh Va'quot Shrine. Kotts actually wants to catch Fish, but she is afraid Kheel will get mad at her if she does not practice. She sings about Fish, and she asks Link if there were any inside the Ancient Shrine. Finally, if Link says he has not gone inside yet, Kotts tells him to bring her back some ancient Fish. After they finish singing, Kotts hopes she will have time to catch Fish tomorrow. After Kass returns to Rito Village, he will join his daughters by playing the bandoneon as they sing. Kass claims that they refuse to leave him alone for the whole day. Kotts reveals that her father taught her to catch Fish by dive-bombing them. However, she has trouble getting out of the Water afterwards, since she does not know how to Swim. She also encourages Link to Swim right up to Fish and grab them. Due to the blizzard in Rito Village, Kotts has temporarily taken over managing the Swallow's Roost Inn.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Koukot Plateau is located on the southern side of the Gerudo Canyon in the Gerudo Highlands, forming part of its walls. It is bordered to the south by South Koukot Plateau, and the Koukot Plateau Path wraps around its eastern side. At the center of Koukot Plateau is a small Monster Stronghold, centered around a single Campfire. In this campsite is a Treasure Chest containing a Knight's Bow. A second Chest can be found on the southeastern side of the Plateau, and it has a Purple Rupee inside. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on top of Koukot Plateau. On the eastern side of the Plateau, Link can find a Cube Pattern. Once the Pattern has been completed, a Korok will appear, which then proceeds to give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

Koume is a recurring character and Boss in . Biography Koume, along with her sister, Kotake, are twin Gerudo witches who possess Fire and Ice powers, respectively. Koume and Kotake collectively have the power to combine to form Twinrova, a witch with both Fire and Ice powers. Because of her fire-based powers, Koume is weak to Kotake's ice powers, a property that is transferred to Twinrova upon their fusion. Together, Koume and Kotake acted as surrogate mothers for Ganondorf, raising him to be evil in the hopes of fostering his role as the Demon King, Ganon. Koume and Kotake operated in secret, using the Spirit Temple as a hideout. Nabooru learned of this and attempted to enter the Spirit Temple to steal their treasure and potentially thwart their plans. Because of the small passages in the Spirit Temple, Nabooru is unable to navigate it and so enlists Link's aid to steal the Silver Gauntlets from within. However, as Link retrieves the Gauntlets, Koume and Kotake discover Nabooru and capture her with the intent of brainwashing her with their evil Magic. When Link reenters the Spirit Temple seven years later, he is greeted by Koume and Kotake, who force him to battle an Iron Knuckle as punishment for intruding upon their hideout. After defeating the Iron Knuckle, it is revealed that Koume and Kotake outfitted Nabooru with Iron Knuckle armor and forced her to defend the Spirit Temple against her will. After Nabooru comes to her senses, Koume and Kotake decide to brainwash her once more and magically transport her elsewhere. They then retreat deeper into the Spirit Temple, waiting for Link to follow them. Koume and Kotake mock Link as he enters the Spirit Temple's boss chamber, claiming that he is there to offer himself as a sacrifice for Ganondorf. Prior to their fight with Link, Koume swears to burn Link to the bone. After Link deals enough damage to the duo, Koume tells her sister that it is time to get serious, prompting them to launch their Double Dynamite Attack, fusing into Twinrova. When Link defeats Twinrova, Koume and Kotake separate, resolving to come at Link more seriously. However, Kotake notices a halo floating above Koume's head, leading to an argument between the two as they both float toward the sky. Before they disappear completely, Koume and Kotake threaten to return and haunt Link from beyond the grave. Koume is the Terminan counterpart of the Koume from Hyrule in . Koume resides in the Southern Swamp with her sister, Kotake. At some point prior to Link's arrival, Koume was attacked by the Skull Kid while she was picking Mushrooms in the Woods of Mystery. She was left there, injured and unable to return home. Upon seeing Link inside the Woods, she will ask him to give her something to restore her energy. However, if Link tries to speak to Koume in the Woods of Mystery as a Deku, Goron, or Zora, Koume will instead pretend to be dead. If

is a recurring character in . Biography Koyin works at the Hateno Pasture in Hateno Village, tending to animals such as Highland Sheep and Hateno Cows alongside Dantz. Prior to Link arriving in Hateno Village, Koyin left a note on the Village's Bulletin Board asking for help with the Monsters on Hateno Beach. When Link first meets her, she is angrily talking to herself and holding a stick in her hand. Should Link decide to speak to her, Koyin is immediately aggressive toward him. If Link decides to end their conversation, she calls him a creep and says to cut it out. If Link keeps speaking to her, she asks what he wants. Noticing he seems confused, she tells him not to act clueless. However, Koyin eases up once she decides that Link seems to be harmless, and she explains that she has been on edge due to all the monsters in the area. She goes on to reveal that they come from Hateno Beach to steal her Highland Sheep, so much so that she is afraid she will run out if nobody stops them. After she finishes talking, "The Sheep Rustlers" Side Quest will begin. When Link speaks to Koyin again, she expresses her hatred for the monsters that live on Hateno Beach. If Link asks about the monsters, Koyin complains that they attack anything that moves, and she claims to have attacked them with a Farmer's Pitchfork. While she wanted to follow them back to their Monster Stronghold, she decided she was not prepared to fight seven monsters at once. If Link asks Koyin about Hateno Beach, she will tell him to follow the winding road to reach it. Due to how well-known it is, Koyin believes that Link will be able to find it on a Map, as well. When Link decides to stop talking to her, Koyin sighs and apologizes for being defensive. After Link has defeated the monsters on Hateno Beach, he must then return to Hateno Beach to inform Koyin. She notes that her flock is calmer and asks Link if he was the one to exterminate the rustlers. Should Link admit that he was, she will say that she thought he would be the one to do so. If he simply bids her farewell instead, she stomps her foot and refuses to let him leave the conversation without hearing her out. Koyin rewards Link with 10 bottles of Fresh Milk, though it does not feel like enough to her. She is pleased that she will be able to sleep soundly without having to worry about her Highland Sheep at night. She also shyly invites him to come talk to her at anytime. After this, the Side Quest will be completed. Koyin's message on the Bulletin Board will turn into one thanking Link for his help. When Link speaks to Koyin, she greets him, though she sourly wonders what is so good about their day. However, she acknowledges that her life could be worse

this, the Side Quest will be completed. Koyin's message on the Bulletin Board will turn into one thanking Link for his help. She states that Link has saved her flock, as the Highland Sheep have been eating and sleeping better in addition to providing more milk. is a recurring character in . Biography Krane is a Goron who stands watch at the western entrance to Goron City. He wears a Forehead Protector and carries a Cobble Crusher. When Krane first meets with Link, he greets him as "Master Link." If Link asks how he knew who he was, Krane appears confused, before he expresses his hope that Link made it past the Magma Bombs without injury. He admits that not many tourists have visited Goron City since the Magma Bombs started falling, so he has been addressing guests as the Hylian Champion to pass the time. He explains that Link was the name of the Hylian who fought alongside the Goron Champion, Daruk. Krane directs Link to Bludo if he wants to know more. Krane then asks what has brought Link to Goron City. If Link speaks to him again and answers that he is visiting for a different reason, Krane will notice the change and become confused. When told that Link is there for a Divine Beast, Krane admits that he does not know much about that. He believes that Bludo would know something about it. The next time Link tells him that he is there for a Divine Beast, will mishear him as saying he is there for a "diving feast," which he does not know about. However, he adds that Bludo has been driving away a lizard monster with his Cannons, referring to the Divine Beast Vah Rudania. He tells Link that Bludo lives in the deepest part of town. If Link gives this answer to Krane after calming Divine Beast Vah Rudania, Krane complains that it so much chaos. He is grateful that Yunobo was able to bring peace back to Goron City. Next, if Link says that he is there for pleasure, Krane says that he reasons do not matter and welcomes him to Goron City. Due to the Scorching Climate surrounding the City, Krane has not seen many Hylians as of late. He considers it their loss, though, and he encourages Link to enjoy his visit. If Link tells Krane a second time that he is there for pleasure, Krane wonders whether he is equipped for the heat. He informs Link that there are goods in Goron City that could help him adjust, such as Fireproof Armor from Ripped and Shredded or Fireproof Elixirs. Finally, Link can tell Krane that he is in Goron City for business, which causes Krane to recall that it used to be easy to find Gems in town, even though the Gorons find them disgusting. Though it sounds outlandish to him, Krane shares that there are people who buy them for high prices. In fact, he claims that it is the main source of income for Goron City. If Link again tells Krane that he is there for business, Krane shares that he heard there are many valuable Gems on Death Mountain. Since no one goes there anymore, Krane believes that anyone who goes there

he claims that it is the main source of income for Goron City. If Link again tells Krane that he is there for business, Krane shares that he heard there are many valuable Gems on Death Mountain. Since no one goes there anymore, Krane believes that anyone who goes there to dig up Gems would not face much competition. During the "EX Champion Daruk's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Krane can be found on the northern shore of Lake Darman. He paces back and forth, talking about Daruk to himself. When spoken to, he asks Link how he is dealing with the Scorching Climate, warning him that it will not cool down when the sun sets. He is surprised that a Hylian has made it so far, and he asks if he is visiting Daruk's turf. When Link asks, Krane explains that he is also following in Daruk's footsteps. He has heard that Daruk fought a huge Monster at this location, and he wonders what it looked like.

The , designated by the trial name Bridging the Sands, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Kudanisar Shrine is a Shrine of Light on the Surface. It is located near the entrance to Karusa Valley in the Gerudo Desert. It corresponds to the Rasinaduk Lightroot in the Gerudo Desert Depths. Themes and Navigation The Kudanisar Shrine is composed of one gigantic room separated into segments. A river of Quicksand flows throughout the Shrine of Light, pushing to crushers made with Spikes. Boards can be found floating across the surface of the Quicksand, acting as platforms for Link to rest on as he crosses the river. In the first segment, Link is caged in the entrance, and must cross over the gate to enter the rest of the Shrine. In the main portion, there are Vehicles made from Sleds, Steering Sticks, and Fans. Beyond the gate and directly across from the entrance, there is a raised platform that houses the end of the Shrine. However, it is barred by a portcullis controlled by a Concave Slot. On the opposite side of the platform from the Concave Slot, there is a Floor Switch and a Tilted Platform, which sits underneath a dispenser in the ceiling. By pressing the Floor Switch, the dispenser will drop an orb, which will immediately be pushed to the other side of the Shrine by the Tilted Platform. The orb lands inside a caged area guarded by Soldier Constructs. This caged area can be entered by using Ascend while standing underneath the horizontal grates surrounding it. Inside, there is another Floor Switch that controls the portcullis to the chamber and two more Vehicles that Link can escape with. By returning the orb to the Concave Slot, Link can find a Statue of Rauru and Sonia. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Enemies Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Kula is a Korok that resides in the Korok Forest. He can be found wandering around in front of Great Deku Tree. Upon approaching Kula, he will recognize Link as the hero and welcome him to Korok Forest, noting that he is much cooler than he thought he would be. To ensure that Link is prepared to be the hero, Kula reveals that he has prepared a trial for him. He then asks Link if he wants to accept his trial. If Link agrees to attempt the trial, Kula will cheer and ask to be shown a rod with the power of Ice. He explains that these rods can be used to freeze monsters and are known to be carried by Ice Wizzrobes. Kula believes that if Link were to wield one of them, he would become both stronger and cooler. When he finishes speaking, the "A Freezing Rod" Side Quest will begin. Once Link is in possession of an Ice Rod, he can return to Korok Forest to show it to Kula. If Link does not have it equipped, Kula instructs him to do so. When Kula sees the Ice Rod, he will be impressed by it. As thanks, he gives Link a Silver Rupee. Kula will also accept seeing a Blizzard Rod, for which he will give Link a Gold Rupee. After this, the Side Quest will be completed. After Link has obtained the Master Sword, Kula will be excited. He advises Link that if the Master Sword is unable to be used, then he could use a rod instead. He says there are more types of rods than Ice Rods, such as Fire Rods, Meteor Rods, Lightning Rods, and Thunderstorm Rods. If Link speaks to Kula with the Master Sword equipped, Kula will ask to see it. Should Link agree to his demands, Kula will become excited and shout. After seeing it, Kula remarks that it is cool, and he thanks Link for letting him see it. While he is happy to have seen the Master Sword, he tells Link to leave and save Princess Zelda with it. If Link refuses to show Kula the Master Sword, he will be disappointed.

Kumamayn Shrine, designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Kumamayn Shrine is located on the southern chain of Sky Island in the Necluda Sky Archipelago, which is within the East Necluda Sky. In order to enter the Shrine, Link must first complete the Shrine Quest "The Necluda Sky Crystal". Upon bringing the Mysterious Crystal from the nearby Flux Construct III to the Shrine, the entrance will appear. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of the interior of the Shrine.|The interior of Kumamayn Shrine Kumamayn Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Kumamayn Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Kurakat Shrine can be found among a set of Zonai Ruins that have fallen onto Quatta's Shelf in the Lanayru Great Spring. It corresponds to the Takaruk Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Kurakat Shrine Kurakat Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Kurakat Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

The , designated by the trial name Alignment of the Circles, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Kyokugon Shrine is a Shrine of Light found at the end of the Great Plateau Foothill Cave. It corresponds to the Nogukoyk Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation 320px|thumb|right|The interior of the Shrine The entrance to the Kyokugon Shrine features a large stairway leading into a grand central chamber. Within this chamber, there are several levels that contain a total of 10 Concave Slots along the floor. Near the base of two staircases in this chamber, there are a total of four Ancient Orbs, which are meant to be placed in the Concave Slots. Magic-powered Torches along the walls feature a unique symmetry pointing both downward and upward, indicating that the solution to the Shrine's puzzle can be found on the ceiling. Along the ceiling, there are four glowing ripples that rest above four of the Concave Slots, showing which ones must be filled. 320px|thumb|right|The answer to the puzzle Once the Ancient Orbs have been placed within their respective Slot, a portcullis leading to the rear chamber of the Shrine will open. A Statue of Rauru and Sonia can be found in this chamber. Additionally, to the right side of this room, there is a caged side chamber with a Treasure Chest and a fifth Ancient Orb that sits outside it. Along the ceiling of this room, there is a fifth ripple sitting above a seemingly normal spot in the floor. However, a disguised Stone Box conceals the fifth Concave Slot. After placing the final Ancient Orb in its Slot, Link can release the portcullis to the caged chamber. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

The , designated by the trial name Combat Training, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Kyononis Shrine is a Shrine of Light situated at the edge of the Central Square in the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins. It corresponds to the Sinonoyk Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|250px|alt= The Training Construct inside of the Kyononis Shrine|Link engaging the Training Construct in battle The Kyononis Shrine consists of three chambers. Its purpose is to teach and challenge Link's combat abilities with a Training Construct placed at the center of the middle chamber. If Link approaches the Training Construct, it will awaken and a portcullis will fall behind him, preventing him from leaving the Shrine until he completes a combat trial. A Mysterious Voice will then call to Link, telling him to follow its instructions. It teaches Link to perform Side Hop, Backflips, Perfect Guards, and Charged Attacks against the Training Construct. This Construct cannot be destroyed until Link is prompted to perform a Charged Attack. While Link is tasked with Side Hopping and Backflipping, he is required to strike the Training Construct with a melee Weapon, though this is not required to advance beyond the Perfect Guard test. When Link completes the Charged Attack test, the Training Construct will be defeated. The Mysterious Voice will acknowledge his skill, opening all of the portcullises in the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found in the rear chamber. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Enemies Equipment Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Kyra is a Gerudo who can be found traveling the Gerudo Desert. In particular, she goes back and forth between the Kara Kara Bazaar and Gerudo Town. Her goal is to find her dreams while wandering the world. At Kara Kara Bazaar, she stops to eat a snack. When Link talks to Kyra without wearing the Gerudo Outfit, she mutters to herself to stay calm, remember her training, and greet a man like anyone else. She then introduces herself to Link while stuttering nervously. Kyra tells Link that she is wandering the world in search for her dreams, and she wonders if he has a place in them. If Link tells Kyra that she is his "dream girl," she rejects this and remembers that her grandmother warned her not to waste her time on men who use such phrases. If Link claims to simply be taking a walk, Kyra decides she can stop wasting her time with him. If Link talks to Kyra again, she is upset that he is disrupting her "personal journey of learning and discovery." Kyra asks Link once more if he thinks he is a part of her destiny. If Link calls her his "dream girl" this time, she says that her grandmother was right about men, telling Link to leave her alone. If Link rejects her, Kyra wonders what the point of talking to him is. Kyra's interactions with Link change if he is wearing the Gerudo Outfit. In Gerudo Town, she compliments his outfit and says that it must drive men wild. Kyra goes on to say that she is the perfect age to travel, but she has barely explored the Gerudo Desert because she prefers being around the familiar. However, Kyra recommends that Link travel the world so that he might meet a nice man. While staying at Gerudo Town, Kyra thinks that if men were allowed inside, they would be able to share their adventures with its inhabitants. However, she also notes that younger Gerudo women like the law, as it gives them an excuse to leave and see the world. While Kyra sometimes wishes men could enter Gerudo Town, she acknowledges that there are advantages to keeping them banned. She thinks that the outside world is interesting, but if she had heard about it from a traveler, she never would have left Gerudo Town to experience it for herself. Kyra regrets not learning to Sand Seal surf when her grandmother told her to. She has trouble walking through the Gerudo Desert on her own, and she dreams of meeting someone that she can ride with. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been appeased, she warns Link that the Desert can still be dangerous, and it can be easy to avoid threats with a Sand Seal. Kyra appreciates Kara Kara Bazaar, often wishing to be there when she is in Gerudo Town. However, since she would have to walk there, she does not feel like

warns Link that the Desert can still be dangerous, and it can be easy to avoid threats with a Sand Seal. Kyra appreciates Kara Kara Bazaar, often wishing to be there when she is in Gerudo Town. However, since she would have to walk there, she does not feel like making the journey. When she arrives in Kara Kara Bazaar, she remarks that there is no better place to relax, as it has cool Water and green plants. She tries to visit as much as she can. While she is there, she resolves to start living her daydreams. On her way back to Gerudo Town, Kyra tells Link that the best way to avoid the Heat is with a Hydromelon. When she was younger, she would never leave Gerudo Town without them. On occasion, she also remarks that she feels as though she is being baked by the sun. If Link saves Kyra from being attacked by Enemies, she will thank him, noting he is stronger than she thought. As a reward, she gives Link a Chilly Elixir.

is a recurring character in . Biography Laflat is a Zora who serves as the chief secretary for the Zora royal family. As Link enters Zora's Domain, she can be seen inspecting Mipha's Statue for damage in the Zora's Domain Square. When Link approaches her, Laflat cautiously asks if he is a Hylian. Despite how he answers, she will then introduce herself and her role to him. After a moment, she asks if Link is curious about Mipha's Statue. If Link claims that he is, Laflat explains that the statue depicts Mipha, the former Zora Champion. According to her, Mipha was both kind and beautiful, and she was capable of healing wounded soldiers. Though they are old now, these soldiers still remember and love Mipha. Laflat tells Link to speak to them if he wants to know more. After Link speaks with King Dorephan, Laflat can be found near the Throne Room gazing out at Ploymus Mountain. If Link approaches her, she asks him to confirm his identity. When Link wonders why she wants to know, Laflat reveals that Sidon left Zora's Domain shouting that he would stop Divine Beast Vah Ruta with Link the Hylian. She then asks Link if he plans on ascending Ploymus Mountain in search of Shock Arrows. If Link confirms this, Laflat reveals that she has a request for him. She explains that there is a monster called a Lynel that lives on top of Ploymus Mountain. Laflat needs a Picture of this Lynel or a similar one. She then asks Link if he can get this Picture for her. If Link accepts her request, Laflat will be relieved they settled things so quickly. She further explains that there is an individual in Zora's Domain who is encouraging others to jump into the East Reservoir Lake from Shatterback Point. Laflat is afraid that, if he continues pressuring people, someone may end up injured. She needs the Picture to show the rest of Zora's Domain how scary the Lynel is, in hopes that hearing of its description will deter them from approaching Ploymus Mountain. When she finishes speaking, the "Lynel Safari" Side Quest will begin. Once Link has a Picture of a Lynel, he can return to Zora's Domain to show it to Laflat, who asks him how his mission is coming along. When Link informs her that he has a Picture, Laflat requests that he show it to her. Upon seeing the Lynel, she will at first scream in shock, but will quickly compose herself. She believes that anyone who sees this Picture would avoid visiting Ploymus Mountain. Laflat thanks Link, revealing her plan to tell the children of Zora's Domain about the Lynel. As a reward, she gives Link a pair of Zora Greaves. She informs Link that they were once made by skilled craftsmen on behalf of an ancient Zora king, but they are now fairly common. After the East Reservoir Lake was finished, the Zora Greaves were made to give to visiting

a reward, she gives Link a pair of Zora Greaves. She informs Link that they were once made by skilled craftsmen on behalf of an ancient Zora king, but they are now fairly common. After the East Reservoir Lake was finished, the Zora Greaves were made to give to visiting Hylians as a sign of friendship. However, when the number of Hylians visiting Zora's Domain dwindled, Laflat's father was forced to close his Armor Shop. The pair she gave Link was the last one left in his stock room. She explains that wearing them could help a Hylian Swim like a Zora, which is why they would be wasted on her. After she is done talking, the Side Quest will be completed. Laflat can be seen in the crowd of Zora congratulating Link after he calms Divine Beast Vah Ruta. Afterwards, she tells Link that all of the Zora, including Mipha, are grateful for his help.

is a recurring character in . Biography Laine is a Gerudo Soldier who guards the Northwest Gate of Gerudo Town. She stands at her post all day carrying a Gerudo Spear. When Link tries to enter Gerudo Town without wearing the Gerudo Outfit, Laine will stop him from passing by. While it is safe inside, she is unable to let a man enter due to Gerudo Town law. Laine suggests that Link goes back to the Kara Kara Bazaar if he seeks shelter. Laine is impressed that Link approached Gerudo Town from the northwest, and she asks if he passed through the Sandstorm over the West Barrens. If Link claims that he did, Laine will deny it and say that it is impossible. If Link says he did not, Laine does not find that surprising. She goes on to explain that a Gerudo Sandstorm has the "temperament of a raging stallion." She goes on to explain that the ancients used these Sandstorms to their advantage and hid treasure in them. If Link approaches Laine while wearing the Gerudo Outfit, she warns him to avoid Sandstorms. She explains that it is very easy for one to lose their sense of direction, and even Gerudo get lost in such circumstances. She remarks that the Sandstorms have made the Gerudo Desert a perfect hiding place for bandits and treasures. When Link asks about the treasure, Laine admits that she does not know all the details. However, she tells Link about the Swordswomen Statues, which are scattered across the Gerudo Desert. She has heard rumors that they point to the hiding place of an ancient treasure, though Laine herself dismisses this as superstition. Even if it was true, Laine considers the threat of the dangerous Monsters in the Sandstorms mean it is not worth the risk. After Laine is finished speaking, Link receives "The Silent Swordswomen" Shrine Quest. During the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Link is able to ask Laine about Karusa Valley. She points him past the West Barrens, and she claims that even though he is unable to see it, Karusa Valley is in that direction. Due to the length of the Valley, Laine suggests that he take a Sand Seal. After Link has calmed Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Laine will comment that the Sand-Seal Races will be starting up again. She remarks that it has been too long since she has seen the Sand-Seal Racing champion, Tali, show her talent. She considers going to the Sand-Seal Rally once she finishes her shift. If Link asks about the Sand-Seal Races, Laine tells him that he can find the Sand-Seal Rally by looking for a gate with red fabric past the other side of Gerudo Town. Since it is located outside of Town, both men and women are able to participate. Laine explains that the Sand-Seal Race is traditional Gerudo competition. Even with the Divine Beast gone, Laine warns Link that there are still Monsters and Sandstorms to be careful of.

Even with the Divine Beast gone, Laine warns Link that there are still Monsters and Sandstorms to be careful of. Due to the danger, she reminds Link to tread lightly as he travels the Gerudo Desert.

is a recurring character in . Biography Laissa is a Rito who lives in Rito Village. She spends her days pacing around the home that she shares with her sister, Bedoli. When Link initially speaks to her, Laissa asks what he is doing in Rito Village and calls him crazy. If Link expresses confusion, she points out Divine Beast Vah Medoh, which is circling the Village. She explains that it has put Rito Village is disarray. Laissa is so angry about it that she would try to bring it down herself, but she restrains herself since she is not a soldier. During "The Ancient Rito Song" Shrine Quest, Bedoli directs Link to Laissa to learn the second half of the song. When she hears that Bedoli forgot the rest of it, Laissa remarks that her memory is the worst. Laissa agrees to help Link, but only if he can recite the half that Bedoli taught him. If Link is able to accurately repeat the first half of the song, Laissa will honor her promise to teach him the second half. The lyrics describe a heart shining upon an incomplete path, but a warm Fire is able to stir its soul. She remarks that the second half is profound. Afterwards, Link is able to ask Laissa to sing the entire song for him at any time. If Link decides to listen, Laissa remarks that being asked to sing on the spot makes her want to do so less, but she agrees nonetheless. Laissa then proceeds to sing the whole song. She comments that the lyrics are deep and make one think.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Akkala is the largest lake in the Akkala Region. It is located in the Akkala Highlands, where it is fed by the Akkala Falls. The western shore of Lake Akkala is flanked by the Torin Wetland. A peninsula cuts into Lake Akkala, connecting Tarrey Town with the rest of the Akkala Highlands to the east. The southern side of the Lake contains underwater ruins, which hide three metallic Treasure Chests. The Treasure Chests contain five Ice Arrows, a Silver Bow and a Silver Shield. Another Treasure Chest can be found in the waters beneath the middle waterfall of the Akkala Falls, containing a Gold Rupee, valued at 300 Rupees. A second Gold Rupee can be found in a Treasure Chest that rests in the water north of Tarrey Town. A Raft can be found on the northern bank of the Lake. Near this Raft is a sunken wagon, which serves no purpose. Ore Deposits and Luminous Stone Deposits can be found along the banks of Lake Akkala. Kilton's shop, the Fang and Bone, can be found underneath the land bridge connecting to Tarrey Town after 9:00 at night once Link has met Kilton at Skull Lake. Creatures Enemies

Lake Darman is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Darman is a medium-sized lake of Lava in northeastern Eldin Canyon. It is supplied by an inflow of Lava from Death Mountain's moat. From there, the Lake extends to the larger Darunia Lake west, followed by the Golow and Goronbi Rivers, and finally Goronbi Lake. Across from a small island at the northern tip of the Lake, two Torches can be found on the shore alongside four Rusty Broadswords and two Rusty Claymores that are embedded in the ground next to it. The island's main feature is its lone Rock Octorok that can convert the Rusty Gear into Traveler's Gear, Soldier's Gear, Knight's Gear, or Royal Gear. , also known as Lake Ferona Springs, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Ferona is a large Hot Spring lake in southern Eldin Canyon. The Lake sits at the bottom of a mountainous gorge that surrounds it. Its water is generally shallow, but has numerous areas that are deep. Lake Ferona is partially an extension of Lake Intenoch to the east. The road that paves through Eldin bridges the gap between the two Lakes. As a Hot Spring, the water is warm and will gradually recover Link's health as he stands or swims in it. Several Luminous Stone Deposits can be found around the Lake's shore. Creatures

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Floria is the largest known body of water that exists in the present day on the Surface. It is inhabited by a large range of flora and aquatic creatures. Most of the Lake is composed of large submerged underground caverns which can be explored through the use of the Water Dragon's Scale and the bomb-like Froaks. Link first discovers the entrance to Lake Floria after completing Farore's Silent Realm. He obtains the Water Dragon's Scale, allowing him to swim underwater, and makes his way up to the top of the canopy of the Great Tree, where he meets the Kikwi Hermit known as Yerbal. He reveals the location of the entrance to Lake Floria. The Lake is inhabited by the squid-like Parella tribe, who are protected by the Water Dragon Faron. She was entrusted with a part of the Song of the Hero and protects Farore's Flame. However, shortly before Link arrived, Lake Floria was invaded by Ghirahim and his force of aggressive beasts known as Cranioc, and Faron was injured as a result. Near the Lake is the Ancient Cistern, a water-themed dungeon where Link can obtain the Whip and Farore's Flame. Animals Enemies Treasures Goddess Cubes Lake Floria is located in West Necluda. It is fed by the 10 Waterfalls that make up the Floria Falls to the north. Another Waterfall from Rassla Lake flows into Lake Floria from the south. The Lake itself feeds into the Floria River, which runs westward. Lake Floria is bisected by the Floria Bridge, which connects the Faron Highroad between the eastern Ebara Forest and the Sarjon Woods in the west. The Dragon Farosh is frequently seen flying over Lake Floria, creating Updrafts and Winds as she does so. She flies down from Riola Spring in the north, weaving under Floria Bridge before descending into Rassla Lake. She then emerges from Rassla Lake and flies back into Riola Spring. In addition to this, a Stone Talus can be found on a cliff on the northern edge of the Lake. It will initially be dormant, but if Link approaches it, it will stand up and begin to attack him. Numerous Treasure Chests, including floating Wooden Chests, sunken Metal Chests, and Stone Chests on standing rocks, are found across Lake Floria. In total, these Treasure Chests contain one Giant Boomerang, one Silver Bow, one Soldier's Shield, 20 Arrows, 10 Fire Arrows, 15 Shock Arrows, two pieces of Flint, three Opals, one Topaz, and six Purple Rupees. , also known as the Great Lake, is a recurring location in . It is the largest body of water in Hyrule and is commonly guarded by the Zora people. Lake Hylia is usually home to an underwater temple that is guarded by the Zoras. Lake Hylia goes unnamed in and . Features and Overview Lake Hylia is located in the center of Hyrule in . Level 1 can be found on a island in the northeastern part of the Lake. Level 4 can be found on another island in the southwestern area, which can only be accessed with the Raft. In the Second Quest, Level 5 can be found in the southwestern island instead. Enemies In , Lake Hylia is located in southeast Hyrule and has a network of small caves coming off it. The lake itself is fed from Zora's River, which in turn flows from Death Mountain. In both its Light and Dark World incarnations, the lake is filled with Zora who will attack Link upon sight. In the center of the lake is an island featuring the Pond of Happiness that is inhabited by Venus, the Queen of Fairies, who will upgrade Link's ability to carry Bombs or arrows in exchange for Rupees. Outside the pond is a warp tile that grants access to the Ice Palace located in the Dark World's Ice Lake, which has several ice platforms across the lake. In addition, the Ice Rod item is found in the Ice Cave on the northeastern side of the lake, as well as the Golden Bee, a Bottled insect that can be unleashed to attack foes. Areas Enemies Shop thumb|right|Lake Hylia's Shop There is a Shop inside a cave in the northwest section of Lake Hylia. It is identical in appearance to the Secret Store, and like its Death Mountain counterpart, it sells the same wares as the Hero Essentials Shop. Additionally, all three of them are run by identical Hooded Shopkeepers. A Sign directing people to it can be found near the Bridge east of Link's House. Banners resembling Shields mark the cave the Shop can be found in. The only other building in this immediate area is a Fortune Teller's Shop. Wares and Pricing In , Lake Hylia is located in the southern region of Hyrule and is home to the sunken Water Temple, which is used by the Zoras to worship the water spirits. The lake is made up of various islands, with the largest one bearing a lone tree as well as the Triforce Warp for the "Serenade of Water." It is connected to Hyrule Field and has an underwater tunnel that serves as a shortcut to Zora's Domain, although it is blocked by ice once Link turns into an adult. All of the lake's water comes from Zora's Fountain, passing through Zora's River, then Gerudo Valley, and eventually reaching Lake Hylia. As such, it is possible to reach the lake by floating down the river from Gerudo Valley. Also on

is blocked by ice once Link turns into an adult. All of the lake's water comes from Zora's Fountain, passing through Zora's River, then Gerudo Valley, and eventually reaching Lake Hylia. As such, it is possible to reach the lake by floating down the river from Gerudo Valley. Also on the shore of Lake Hylia are two Scarecrows named Pierre and Bonooru, the latter of which helps Link obtain the Scarecrow's Song. Other notable features of Lake Hylia include the Lakeside Laboratory, where various experiments are conducted to discover the lake's mysteries, and the Fishing Pond, where Link can fish for an unlimited time for just 20 Rupees. Link first visits the lake as a child while looking for Princess Ruto, where he finds Ruto's Letter encased in a bottle at the bottom of the lake. Later, after the young hero turns into an adult by pulling the Master Sword from its pedestal, Link returns to find the lake almost drained of its rich waters. He discovers that the lake has been drained as a result of Morpha's curse. With the help of Princess Ruto, Link sinks to the bottom of Lake Hylia using the Iron Boots and the Zora Tunic to reach the Water Temple and defeat Morpha. Once Ruto awakens as the Sage of Water, the lake is filled with water again, returning it to its normal state. Furthermore, Link can stand on a stone tablet above the Water Temple's entrance and shoot an arrow at the sun as it rises to have the Fire Arrows appear on the small, lone island. Areas Enemies thumb|right|300px|The uppermost waterfall of Lake Hylia in In , Lake Hylia is the first stage of Whereabouts of the Wind, the first level of the game. The Links land in this area after they are flung away from Hyrule Castle by Vaati's tornado, and are awakened by the voice of Kaepora Gaebora, who tells them that they must rescue Princess Zelda and the six Maidens. Lake Hylia differs from previous games as instead of a singular, large lake, it consists of a series of small lakes and rivers, as well as giant waterfalls and cave tunnels. It is here that the young heroes also meet Tingle for the first time, who is trapped under a stone beneath the lakeside's wooden bridge. The lake leads to a cave entrance, where four dark barriers must be broken with the Four Sword in order to yield passage to the Cave of No Return. Lake Hylia is an area in , located in eastern Hyrule. It connects to two other areas: Lon Lon Ranch to the west and Minish Woods to the south. The water enters the Lake by a river from Veil Falls to the north. To the south is the Minish Woods and to the west is Lon Lon Ranch. Stockwell, the shop-owner from Hyrule Town, owns a house here where his dog Fifi lives alone. Moreover, Waveblade, one of the Blade Brothers, houses a tree,

by a river from Veil Falls to the north. To the south is the Minish Woods and to the west is Lon Lon Ranch. Stockwell, the shop-owner from Hyrule Town, owns a house here where his dog Fifi lives alone. Moreover, Waveblade, one of the Blade Brothers, houses a tree, ready to teach Link sword techniques. David Jr. is also found here. One of Lake Hylia's most notable features is the Temple of Droplets, a frozen Minish-sized temple which serves as the fourth Dungeon of the game. After Link completes the Fortress of Winds and receives the Ocarina of Wind, he warps to the Wind Crest located in Lake Hylia and speaks to the nearby Forest Picori, who compliments Link for finding him. Upon hearing that Link is seeking to enter the Temple of Droplets, the Minish tells him that only one Minish, Librari, was able to find a way into it and directs him to the Royal Hyrule Library in Hyrule Town where Librari lives in semi-retirement. After speaking to the Minish at Lake Hylia, the Royal Hyrule Library opens to the public, allowing Link to enter and speak with Librari. The Minish located at Lake Hylia is also a possible target for Kinstone Fusion. If Link successfully fuses Kinstone Pieces with him, the vines covering a tree in the Western Wood will clear, allowing Link to enter the tree and obtain the Piece of Heart inside. Areas Enemies thumb|right|300px|Lake Hylia covered in Twilight in In , Lake Hylia is located on the side of Hyrule and is part of the Lanayru Province. The lake is home to Lanayru's Spirit Spring, Fyer's Cannon Rides, and Falbi's Flight-by-Fowl. The Lakebed Temple rests at the bottom of the lake, where Zoras patrol the entrance to the temple due to it being a sacred place for their people. Lake Hylia is again fed by Zora's River, which travels all the way from the throne room of Zora's Domain. The only ways to access Lake Hylia are by playing Falbi's Flight-by-Fowl game, playing Iza's Rapids Ride game, jumping down from outside the South Gate of Castle Town, or Warping there. Despite this, many of Hyrule's citizens come to Lake Hylia to send prayers to Lanayru. When Link first visits Lake Hylia, it is covered in Twilight and has been mostly drained due to Zora's Domain being frozen, which stopped the water from flowing into the lake. After Link and Midna thaw Zora's Domain with the Molten Shard from Death Mountain, the water flow returns and fills up the lake, allowing the young hero to visit Lanayru at his Spring and obtain the Vessel of Light to collect the Tears of Light of the Lanayru Province. Collecting 15 Tears of Light will make the last Shadow Insect appear in the middle of the lake, which is actually an oversized monster known as Twilit Bloat. Twilit Bloat's defeat allows Link to collect the last Tear of Light, abolishing the Twilight and returning light to the

Lanayru Province. Collecting 15 Tears of Light will make the last Shadow Insect appear in the middle of the lake, which is actually an oversized monster known as Twilit Bloat. Twilit Bloat's defeat allows Link to collect the last Tear of Light, abolishing the Twilight and returning light to the province. Later on in the game, Link must visit the lake once again to meet with Auru at the tower situated on the side of the area. Auru hands Link a memo to give to Fyer so that the young hero will be able to reach Gerudo Desert and thus reach the Mirror Chamber. When Link must visit the City in the Sky in search of a Mirror Shard, he must bring Fyer the broken Sky Cannon that is found beneath the Sanctuary in Kakariko Village. For a fee of 300 Rupees, Fyer will repair the Sky Cannon, allowing Link to visit the dungeon at any time from the Sky Cannon's new position at Lake Hylia. Lake Hylia is also home to three Pieces of Heart as well as a mini-game hosted by Plumm known as Fruit Pop Flight Challenge. Areas Lake Hylia appears in , located southeast of Hyrule Castle. It features the House of Gales, the second dungeon in the game, on an island at its center, located where the Pond of Happiness was in . Link cannot reach the dungeon until he has obtained the Flippers from Oren, Queen of the Zoras, which she gives to him as thanks for returning her stolen Smooth Gem. He also cannot enter it without renting the Tornado Rod from Ravio. Lake Hylia's counterpart in Lorule is dubbed Lorule Lake, with a fiery maze at its center known as Turtle Rock serving as analogous to the House of Gales in Hyrule. Gaining access to the dungeon requires Link to come to the aid of three turtles that are trapped in various predicaments across the lake; doing so prompts their mother to thank him by allowing him a ride atop her back, which Link can use to reach the dungeon's entrance. Lake Hylia also features a hidden cave that houses Mother Maiamai, a character who will upgrade any one item that Link has purchased from Ravio for every ten Lost Maiamais that the hero finds and returns to her. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Intenoch is a large Hot Spring lake in southeastern Eldin Canyon. The Lake is part of a river that flows toward the northeast of a deep gorge that surrounds the Lake. It is partially an extension of Lake Ferona to the west, another Hot Spring lake. The two Lakes are split by the road that paves through Eldin. Unlike Lake Ferona, whose water levels varies between shallow and deep, Lake Intenoch is mostly deep water. As a Hot Spring, the water is warm and will gradually recover Link's health as he stands or swims in it. Broca Island is the Lake's sole landmark, which lies at the far northeastern end of the Lake. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Kolomo is a body of Water located northeast of the Great Plateau in Hyrule Field. Lake Kolomo surrounds the Kolomo Garrison Ruins on three sides and features a small island in its center, where a Stone Talus (Luminous) resides. Prior to the Great Calamity, Zelda and Link walked along the Lake's shoreline while making preparations to head to Goron City to work on Divine Beast Vah Rudania to make it easier for Daruk to pilot it. Consequently, Lake Kolomo is the site of the Recovered Memory, "Resolve and Grief", which Link can recall by visiting the Lake after talking to Impa and receiving the "Captured Memories" Main Quest. A Monster Encampment is situated on the southeastern shore of the Lake. A total of five Bomb Barrel are around the camp. At the center of the camp is a Campfire, where a few Roasted Bass have been cooked. Three Iron Boxes are in the camp as well and can be broken to receive Rupees, Arrows, Roasted Bass, and Blackened Crab. A short distance south of the main camp is a Cooking Pot, along with a Wooden Box that holds Acorns, Apples, and more Arrows. In ancient Hyrule at the time of King Rauru's rule, Zelda drank tea with him and Queen Sonia at a gazebo overlooking Lake Kolomo, as seen in the "Zelda and Sonia" Memory. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Saria is a small body of water in the southwestern section of the Great Hyrule Forest. It is the end section of the Korok Trial and Shrine Quest "Trial of Second Sight". Link must use a Raft provided to cross the Lake in order to transport a Treasure Chest to a small island in the center of the Lake and place it inside the Tree living on the island. Once Link does this, the Kuhn Sidajj Shrine appears on the far side of the Lake. Areas Creatures Equipment Creatures Materials Treasure Chests

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Siela is located in West Necluda, northeast of Dueling Peaks. It is fed by a waterfall that starts at the base of the Phalian Highlands, and passes under the Kakariko Bridge. A Raft sits at the bank on the northeastern shore near the base of the waterfall. A metal crate containing Arrows and Rupees sits atop the rocks protruding from Lake Siela east of Kakariko Bridge. Link can use Magnesis near the Raft to retrieve a metallic Treasure Chest containing 10 Arrows at the bottom of the river. A second metallic Treasure Chest containing an Opal can be found underwater on the eastern side of the Kakariko Bridge, near the boulders protruding from the Lake. In the northwestern corner of the Lake, there is a small island with several Rocks on it, and to the south of this island is a circle of rocky pillars. If Link throws a Rock into this circle, a Korok will appear. Northwest of the small island there is a circle of Lily Pads, and jumping off of a nearby cliff into this circle will cause another Korok to appear. Creatures Enemies

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Sumac is located north of the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab and south of Mount Lanayru in East Necluda. Lake Sumac is a small lake with an island in the center, and on the small island, a large Tree grows tall. On the south-eastern edge of the lake, a Raft floats tied to a pole in the water. Link can cut the rope and use the raft to float across the lake. On the top of the giant Tree that grows on the island, a Korok can be found hiding underneath a rock. When Link picks up the rock, the Korok will appear and gift Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Totori is located on the Tabantha Frontier. It is a large body of Water with several spire-like islands, the largest of which bears Rito Village. One of these islands contains a group of Luminous Stone Deposits. Several wooden bridges hang over Lake Totori, connecting the Village to Rito Stable and the rest of Hyrule. Fish reside in the shallower parts of the Lake, as well as in ponds on its islands. There are also many Updrafts stemming from the Lake's surface, which can be Link can glide on using his Paraglider. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Lake Totori. The first is an Offering Spot on the island northwest of Rito Village, which requires Link to place an Apple in the missing spot. The second Puzzle is a Race starting on the island directly west of the Village, ending on the island to the Village's southwest. Once Link solves each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Materials Equipment Other Appearances During the "Flight Training at Lake Totori" Quest, it is revealed that the Rito previously did glide training on Lake Totori, but they were forced to stop after running out of supplies. When they receive new Materials, the warriors are able to resume their practice, which Teba witnesses and is inspired by.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lake Totori South is located between Lake Totori and Cuho Mountain on the Tabantha Frontier. It is a wooded area filled with Cedar Trees and a shallow pool of Water, and an unnamed road passes along its northern end. Another feature of Lake Totori South is a set of ancient ruins, which are believed to be Zonai Ruins. A Black Hinox sleeps at the center of Lake Totori South. It will initially be asleep, but if Link disturbs its rest, it will wake up and begin to attack him. In addition to this, a Monster Stronghold built around a large Tree can be found on the eastern side of Lake Totori South. The Stronghold features a Cooking Pot with a Campfire underneath it. A Treasure Chest containing five Shock Arrows is situated at the top of the camp. As part of "The Ancient Rito Song" Shrine Quest, Link will find a Pedestal on Lake Totori South. As the sun passes behind the pillar upon which Rito Village is built, a beam of light in the shape of a Heart will be projected onto the Pedestal. If Link holds a lit Torch or ignites a Campfire on the Pedestal during this time, Bareeda Naag Shrine will rise from the ground nearby. Enemies Creatures Materials

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lakeside Stable is a Stable located on the south side of Lake Floria in West Necluda. The Shai Utoh Shrine is located behind it, in a cave with a bombable wall, providing a convenient Travel Gate to the stable when activated. The Stable is run by Anly, who mans both its Horse services and lodging. As with all other Stables, Beedle can occasionally be found here selling his wares. Meeshy and Letty may stop here on their travels. One of the stablehands, Cima, is a nervous wreck due to lightning frequently striking the stable, and asks Link to investigate it through the "Thunder Magnet" Side Quest. Shay and Kampo can be found out front. A Hylian Retriever can be befriended with raw meat, who will lead Link to a Treasure Chest containing a Forest Dweller's Spear. is a character in . Biography Lammz is a member of the Zonai Survey Team. He travels with a Donkey along the path between Proxim Bridge and the Big Twin Bridge, passing through the Dueling Peaks along the way. When spoken to, Lammz questions Link, asking him if he is headed in the same direction. He then explains that a Chasm has appeared on the other side of Proxim Bridge at the Outpost Ruins, which emits a dangerous substance called Gloom that will sap Link's strength if he touches it. Lammz comments that if investigating Chasms and Gloom was not part of his research as part of the Zonai Survey Team, he would never go near them, and he doubts anyone else would willingly do so. Since the Chasm goes down to the Depths, Lammz advises Link to avoid falling in it. Lammz notices that Constructs are hanging around the Zonai Ruins that fell from the Sky and fighting with Monsters. He wonders if he could find some way to get them to finish each other off, assuming that it would make his work easier. He also wonders why Constructs and Monsters fight each other. Lammz also informs Link about the Big Twin Bridge leading to Dueling Peaks Stable, explaining that Fallen Debris had landed on top of Big Twin Bridge and destroyed it as a result. He warns Link that although disaster measures have been put nearby, it is still not completely safe. During the morning, Lammz remarks on Link's high energy. During nighttime, Lammz comments that Link must have lots of energy, since he can walk all night with no rest. When it Rains, Lammz will use a large Tree or a Fallen Debris as shelter. When spoken to, he expresses his lack of energy because of his research, commenting that he would rather crawl into a Soft Bed than Sleep outside. He considers Sleeping at a Bed at Inns, mentioning that upon waking up, he will feel far more energetic and refreshed. If Link saves Lammz from Enemies, he will note Link's skills, claiming he would ask him to be his bodyguard if he could. Afterwards, he rewards Link with a Meal to show his gratitude.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lanayru Promenade is located in East Necluda. It has been left in ruins after the Great Calamity with several walkways being either flooded or destroyed. The Lanayru Road - East Gate and Lanayru Road - West Gate serve as exits for the Promenade, and Lanayru Road runs along its northern wall. The walls of the Lanayru Promenade feature large stylized carvings that depict Loftwings. These carvings are identical to the ones found in the Sky Keep from and appear in smaller form on similar ruins across Hyrule. Multiple Ore Deposits can be found throughout the Promenade. A Raft can be used to navigate the Water. After being freed from Malice, Naydra will fly through the Lanayru Promenade at 6:00 AM and 6:00 PM. Several Updrafts will appear around it that Link can travel with using his Paraglider. Eleven Treasure Chests can be found in the Promenade. The total contents of these Chests are: five Bomb Arrows, ten Shock Arrows, five Fire Arrows, five Ice Arrows, a Meteor Rod, a Soldier's Broadsword, a Knight's Broadsword, two Opals, and two Purple Rupees. Two Koroks can also be found in the Promenade. One is hiding under a Natural Hiding Spot on top of the central fountain, and the second can be revealed by diving into a Circle of lily pads in the Water. When Link finds them, they will each give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials While still in ruins, the Lanayru Promenade remains relatively unchanged after the Upheaval aside from some Fallen Debris and newly exposed Cave entrances. Three new Koroks can be found hiding around the Promenade: one in a Tree with an Acorn Jar, one beneath a Natural Hiding Spot under the large staircase, and one near another Tree at the end of a Flower Trail.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lanayru Range is located atop Mount Lanayru, south of the Spring of Wisdom and east of Madorna Mountain. Its only feature of note are two pillars of Ice on its northern end, which cannot be melted. Several Cedar Trees are also situated on the Range. Being part of a Freezing Climate, Link will take damage while on the Lanayru Range unless he has two levels of Cold Resistance. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on the Lanayru Range. On its west side is a chunk of Ice, which Link must melt using Fire. When this is done, Leaves with Fairy Dust will appear. If Link interacts with the Leaves, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lanayru Road is an unmarked road that passes through East Necluda and Mount Lanayru. It starts at the Lanayru Road - West Gate, runs along the northern side of the Lanayru Promenade, and continues under the Lanayru Road - East Gate before ending on the western side of the Naydra Snowfield. The Lanayru Road South Cave is named after it. Lanayru Road returns in . A new Cave, the Lanayru Road East Cave, now bears its name. Other Appearances Lanayru Road is a Stage added in the Downloadable Content pack. It is the only Stage that is split into two halves, which are inaccessible to one another. The portion the Champions run along is quite tight, being a nearly straight line forwards with a small base in the middle. The portion King Rhoam goes across is much wider, going under a covered portion of the landscape. During the Scenario "EX The Princess and the King", the location is being raided by Monsters.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lanayru Road - West Gate is located between East Necluda and the Lanayru Great Spring. It is the crossroads leading from Kakariko Village, Rabia Plain, and the Lanayru Promenade. The area is full of long Grass, and Ore Deposits can be found on the sides of the surrounding cliffs. During the second Great Calamity, the Lanayru Road - West Gate suffered damage with the rest of the Lanayru Promenade. After the Main Quest "Seek Out Impa" has been completed, a Traveler can be found at the Lanayru Road - West Gate. The first time Link meets this Traveler, they recount that a year prior, they saw a something floating in the sky that was glowing, and they were unable to look away. They were then bathed in light and woke up in Bed, and they ask Link what he thinks about it. Initially, they thought it was a nightmare, but then they realized that they were not in their Bed. They claim that the Bed was full of a strange liquid, and the room was empty except for a glowing device in the corner. When they touched the device, they were overwhelmed with a sense of familiarity, and then they came to at the Lanayru Road - West Gate. Again, they ask Link what he thinks about their story. After Link responds, the Traveler reveals that they know he is the Hylian Champion. The Traveler reveals that they are a Yiga Footsoldier, and they then attack Link. When Link encounters this Traveler again, he will find them grumbling. If Link speaks to them, they comment that the Weather is going to be nice tomorrow. No matter Link's response, the Traveler then says that he will not be alive to enjoy it. At this point, the Traveler reveals that they are a Yiga Footsoldier and proceeds to attack Link once more. Creatures Enemies Materials Korok Seeds

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lanayru Sea was a treacherous ocean that had receded long before the events of . Due to rapid climate change, an area of the Lanayru Sea would later become the Lanayru Sand Sea, and eventually Gerudo Desert. During the events of , Link is tasked to retrieve an Ancient Sea Chart in order to navigate the waters lost to time. In , the Lanayru Sea is a body of Water on the eastern end of the Lanayru Region. It is part of Hyrule's eastern coast, bordered by the Akkala Sea to the north and the Necluda Sea to the south. It is also located along the edges of the Lanayru Great Spring and Mount Lanayru. The Water from the Lanayru Sea feeds into Lanayru Bay. Climates Areas Areas Other Appearances

The is a recurring location in . The Lanayru Wetlands Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Lanayru Wetlands Well is north of the Millennio Sandbar in the Lanayru Wetlands. It is surrounded by several Ruined Houses, which were part of an unnamed Hylian settlement that was destroyed by Guardians during the Great Calamity. Equipment The Lanayru Wetlands Well returns in , still being a part of the Lanayru Wetlands. Link is now able to access the Well's interior, made easier by the Ladder present inside of it. This inner chamber consists of a large room, within which is a small pool of Water, as well as an Ore Deposit and a Luminous Stone Deposit. Inside the Lanayru Wetlands Well, a Traveler equipped with a Traveler's Sword and a Hunter's Shield can be seen practicing with a Dummy. When spoken to, they share a myth that the wailing of the dead can be heard by placing one's ear to a Well. If Link claims that he already knew this, the Traveler is impressed before declaring that Link will soon be dead himself. Alternatively, if Link states that he has not heard of this, the Traveler encourages him to listen closely, at which point they say that the wails will be Link's. In both scenarios, the Traveler reveals themself to be a Yiga Footsoldier and proceeds to attack Link. Should Link return later and talk to the Traveler again, they will be surprised that he came back even after their threats, after which they battle Link once more. The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lantern Falls are located in Kakariko Village. They are a pair of two Waterfalls that flow downwards from Lantern Lake, pooling beneath Impa's House. They are the only place where Sanke Carps can be found, as they are bred for their colors by the people of Kakariko Village. left|40px There is one Korok Seed Puzzle within the Lantern Falls. It takes the form of a Circle of Lily Pads on the northern side of Impa's House. If Link jumps into the Circle, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures

is a recurring character in . Biography Laroba is a Gerudo who travels between the East Akkala Stable and the South Akkala Stable via the Shadow Pass. She carries a Gerudo Scimitar and a Gerudo Shield. Laroba left the Gerudo Desert in search of a man to marry. To further this goal, she sizes up every man she meets to gauge his eligibility. Since they are all different ages, sizes, and races, she has difficulty making a decision, though she acknowledges that she likely appears creepy to them. She discourages Link from pursuing her, though, claiming he is too young. During her journey, Laroba has enjoyed meeting people from all over the world and getting to hear their perspectives. In particular, she appreciates that she can meet a variety of people in Akkala, such as Zora, Gorons, and Rito. She is glad that they are able to meet with each other, as they were more isolated in the past. She also encourages Link to talk to the people he meets, no matter what they look like. On occasion, Laroba remarks that Gorons are hardy or that Hylians are good folk. She also likes those who can Cook, although she is curious about other travelers. Recently, Laroba had a conversation with Naddon, a Goron who also travels the Shadow Pass. He thought she was pretty, and he liked how her hair shined like a stone. Laroba often gives Link tips when it comes to using Bows. For example, she informs Link that he should aim for the heads of monsters and the eyes of Guardians. She encourages him to keep practicing his aim. She reminds Link to always stock up on Arrows, especially since life can always throw him for a loop. In addition to keeping an eye on his Quiver, Laroba also advises that Link carry extra Bows in case his current one snaps. Laroba claims to take care of her own Bow, despite the fact that she does not visibly carry one. If Link ever finds himself in a battle, Laroba suggests that he should decide if he fights or runs based on the condition of his Weapons. She also shares a rumor she heard about a rare set of arrows that are hidden deep in Hyrule Castle. Laroba proposes that Link set a goal to reach on his Map, occasionally checking to ensure he is on the right path. In addition, she points out Skull Lake on his Map, explaining that he can encounter the Fang and Bone there at night, if he has the stomach for it. Laroba is troubled when it Rains, proclaiming that she will never get used to it. However, she also considers it a way to cool off when she gets too flushed while staring at a man. If Laroba is threatened by an Enemy, she will flee in terror. While she is in danger, she can claim that her stomach is tied in knots or that she has had enough mortal peril.
