is a recurring character in . Biography Laruta is a Zora child who can be found in Zora's Domain. For most of the day, spends her time with Tona and Tula outside of the Sleeping Chamber, where they talk about Sidon. Starting at 4:00 PM, she begins to run around the entrance to the Throne Room while singing the "Champion Festival Song". At night, she sleeps in one of the Chamber's pools. When Link first speaks to Laruta, she sings part of the "Champion Festival Song". Noticing Link, Laruta asks who he is. If Link responds that he is a Hylian, Laruta will become excited. If Link claims to be a swordsman, Laruta will be impressed with him. Despite how he responds, Laruta still believes that Sidon is much cooler. The next time Link approaches Laruta, she will introduce herself and ask if he wants to talk. If Link asks about the "Champion Festival Song", Laruta explains that she loves to sing, especially the song from the Champion Festival. She then asks if Link wants to hear it. If Link agrees to listen, Laruta will recite the song for him. If Link declines her offer, Laruta will be upset. Next, if Link asks about Prince Sidon, Laruta claims that he is handsome and what every girl dreams of. When Link leaves their conversation, Laruta says goodbye to him. Laruta is among the Zora present when King Dorephan thanks Link for appeasing Divine Beast Vah Ruta. Afterwards, she can be found standing in front of Mipha's Statue in the Zora's Domain Square. When spoken to, she will start humming part of the "Champion Festival Song". However, she stops when she recognizes Link as the Hylian who helped Sidon, calling him handsome. Although, she believes that Sidon is even more handsome. Due to Link's appearance, Laruta decides to keep speaking with him.. If Link once again asks about the "Champion Festival Song", Laruta will respond the same as before, including singing the song for him. When she finishes singing, Laruta states that she does not understand the meaning of the song, even though she plans on singing it at the next Champion Festival. She explains that Trello is in charge of organizing the Festival, but he has not started preparing yet. Laruta wonders what is wrong with him, theorizing that he forgot this was his responsibility. Once she finishes speaking, "The Ceremonial Song" Shrine Quest will begin. If Link asks Laruta about the "Champion Festival Song" after completing the Shrine Quest, Laruta will yet again remark that Trello is in charge of the event. She has heard that Dento is going to create a replica of the Lightscale Trident that was used by Mipha.

is a recurring character in . Biography Lashley is a Gerudo Soldier who guards the Southeast Gate of Gerudo Town. She wields a Gerudo Spear. If Link tries to enter Gerudo Town without a disguise, Lashley will stop him from entering and tell him that men are forbidden. When spoken to, she will reiterate that men are not allowed inside and tell him to leave. When Link speaks to Lashley while wearing the Gerudo Outfit, she tells him that it is dangerous to wander around the Gerudo Desert because of the Divine Beast Vah Naboris. While the Lookout Post is between them and the Divine Beast, she does not believe it is enough to protect them. If Link asks about the Divine Beast, Lashley explains that it was said to be a god who protected the Gerudo Desert, but it suddenly appeared and began to wander aimlessly. She claims that everyone is afraid that it will wander into Gerudo Town, but the chief, Riju, is doing everything she can do to avoid this. Lashley also shares a rumor that Naboris shoots those who come near it with Lightning, and she hopes that it does not come their way. Even though the Lookout Post is safe from the Lightning, there are many monsters in the area, so Lashley warns Link against visiting. If Link asks about the Lookout Post, Lashley points in its direction and explains that it is where Divine Beast Vah Naboris is monitored from. Lashley then asks if Link is planning to go to the Lookout Post. Though it appears close, Lashley claims that it is actually far away, and she recommends that Link should ride a Sand Seal to get there. She repeats her warning about the monsters surrounding the Lookout Post. When Link ends their conversation, Lashley tells him not to worry, as it is safe in Gerudo Town. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Lashley claims that she was worried about Riju setting out on her own, but she now sees that she is capable. She mentions hearing that Riju fought alongside a Hylian woman, remarking that she must have been strong. Lashley claims not to have seen this Hylian from her post, and she wonders where she could have gone. When spoken to again, Lashley expresses her disbelief that the Divine Beast is actually gone. While it only caused problems for the Gerudo, Lashley had been watching it for quite some time. She admits that she feels somewhat lonely now.

is a recurring character in . Biography Lasli is a member of the Sheikah Tribe living in Kakariko Village. Her job is to call attention to the local Armor Shop called Enchanted, which is owned by her sister Claree. She continues this job even when it is Raining. Previously, Lasli was dating a man named Jarod, but he passed away after a monster attack. Since then, she has been struggling to cope with her grief, and her only respite has been seeing the Sunset Fireflies. However, due to the danger posed by wandering around at night, she has been unable to visit them as of late. When Link initially approaches Lasli, she immediately begins to fawn over him, saying he is her type. She takes note of the Sheikah Slate he has with him and has to pause to realize what that means. Her outburst startles Link, but she reels back to point out that he must be quite important. Lasli awakens and leaves home at 5:00 AM each morning. She will remark on how Link seems to be wide awake so early. She mentions that she is going to work and that Link can join her if he is looking for clothing. At 9:00 PM, Lasli will run for home, worried about her grandmother, Nanna, chastising her. Once she is home, she will take a seat and remove her umbrella. Link can speak to her and she will tell him how she used to catch Sunset Fireflies at night. However, she cannot go out anymore due to the Monsters and the Yiga, which causes Lasli to lament her misfortune. If Link is already inside the house when Lasli first comes home, she is frightfully startled at first. Then she realizes who it is and relaxes. If Link enters her home late at night, Lasli will call him rude, but she stops when she notices his Sheikah Slate. She realizes that Link must be the hero from the stories her grandmother told her about the Great Calamity. She is surprised by how young Link appears, as she imagined he would be much older. She admits that people her age have difficulties understanding the scope of the Great Calamity. Noticing the expression on Link's face, Lasli realizes that he also lacks an understanding of what happened. Though she has a hard time believing it, she claims that there are many things that are hard to understand. If Link has yet to meet with Impa, Lasli tells him to go see her for an explanation. Once Link has had his first meeting with Impa, he can visit Lasli in her home at night, which causes her to remark on his kindness. She tells him of how much she enjoyed the nighttime of the Village, but recalls that now she cannot go out late. Lasli wishes that she could do something about her situation. Later on, she will remark on how pretty the Fireflies were that evening. She admits she used to be

tells him of how much she enjoyed the nighttime of the Village, but recalls that now she cannot go out late. Lasli wishes that she could do something about her situation. Later on, she will remark on how pretty the Fireflies were that evening. She admits she used to be good at catching them when she was younger. After Link completes both "Find the Fairy Fountain" and "Flown the Coop", he can speak to Lasli in her home. She laments that due to how dangerous the roads have become at night, she is forced to come home without searching for Sunset Fireflies. She admits that she misses spending time with them at night, and her nights now seem dull without them. She wishes that the Sunset Fireflies would come visit her. When she finishes speaking, the "By Firefly's Light" Side Quest will begin. To fulfill Lasli's request, Link must releases five Sunset Fireflies in her home at night. Once Lasli sees them, she will stand up and express her excitement. She thanks Link for bringing them, offering him a Purple Rupee as a reward. Watching them fly around, she remarks that they way they glow is pretty. If Link comments that she is also pretty, Lasli will giggle and thank him. Alternatively, if Link reminds her of their short lifespan, Lasli will become frustrated and call him unromantic. After this, the Side Quest will be completed. During "The Stolen Heirloom" Shrine Quest, Dorian and Cado both mention that Lasli visited Impa's House before the Sheikah Heirloom was stolen. If Link asks Lasli about what she does at night, she will be unimpressed, believing he is flirting with her. At night, Lasli will sneak out of Kakariko Village, nervously speaking to herself the whole time. If Link speaks to Lasli as she starts to leave Kakariko Village, she quietly calls him a stalker and remarks that that she will have to visit "him" later. She then states that it is dangerous for her to be alone at night, so she decided to return to Enchanted. If Lasli catches Link following her, she claims her stalker to be Jarod and tells him to stop following her. As Lasli returns to Enchanted, she tells Link to leave her alone. When Lasli is back at Enchanted, she accuses him of being a stalker and tells him to leave before she calls for Dorian. If Link catches Lasli in the Kakariko Village Graveyard, she will be shocked by his sudden appearance. She realizes that she is unable to keep her secret any longer, which she claims not even Claree knows about. She admits that she came to visit Jarod, who was the love of her life. When Link asks where the Sheikah Heirloom is, Lasli will initially be confused, asking if he is referring to the object kept in Impa's House. When Link asks if she stole it, Lasli will be outraged by such an accusation. She questions if he was following her because he

life. When Link asks where the Sheikah Heirloom is, Lasli will initially be confused, asking if he is referring to the object kept in Impa's House. When Link asks if she stole it, Lasli will be outraged by such an accusation. She questions if he was following her because he thought she was a suspect. When Link nods, she calls him awful. When Link speaks to Lasli for a second time, she starts to talk about Jarod's death, recalling that he promised to always protect her before he was attacked by a Monster. If Link again asks if she stole the Sheikah Heirloom, she will berate him for talking about it while she is vulnerable. She also wonders how she could have stolen it when so many people, including Dorian, are always guarding it. If Link expresses sorrow for her loss, Lasli will begrudgingly thank him, but she reminds him to be more sensitive towards strangers.

is a recurring Enemy in . Lava goes unnamed in , , and . Characteristics Lava is molten rock that is usually in the form of thick, fiery liquid that ranges from red to orange to yellow. In most Zelda games, it will cause Link to lose health if he falls in, and it will sometimes force him to start the room over in a few 3D games. In some games such as , Link is able to walk on Lava and will be constantly taking damage; however, wearing the Goron Tunic will significantly reduce the amount of damage taken. The same also applies to , but whether Link is able to walk on Lava and whether he takes damage by doing so varies depending on the form he is in. Link as a Hylian boy is able to walk on Lava while constantly taking damage. Deku Link and Zora Link will restart a room if they fall into Lava, whereas Goron Link is completely immune to Lava. Notably, in , Link will lose two Hearts at once if he falls into Lava before being returned to the beginning of the room. However, if wearing the Zora Armor, this damage is multiplied by 10, making Lava an instant-death hazard for Link. Lava also appears in some Dungeons as red tiles in , but like Water, it cannot be walked on and is thus harmless. The Stepladder, however, can be used to walk over water and lava. In , falling into lava will automatically count as a death and will take away one of Link's lives. Lava appears in the Cave of Flames in . It will damage Link if he falls into it. He can traverse Lava using Updrafts as well as unstable rocky platforms that must occasionally be flipped over with the Cane of Pacci. Lava appears at Death Mountain and under the surface of Hyrule. Lava can be found atop the Eldin Volcano. Other Appearances Lava can be found within the Gerudo Ruins. When touched by one of the heroes, they lose half of a Heart and are reset back to their position before they fell into the Lava. Damage from Lava can be mitigated by the Goron Locket, and a combination of the Goron Locket and the Zora's Flippers allows the heroes to swim in it.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Laverra Beach is a location found within the Faron Grasslands, running from the western side of the mouth of the Menoat River bordering the Faron Sea. It is a predominately sandy beach with the occasional patch of gravel, with segments of rocks and grass to the west and cliffs to the north. A Lizalfos base lies just off the shore. Four Treasure Chests can be found off the shore of Laverra Beach. Three of these are wooden and can be found floating near the Lizalfos camp, and by the eastern end of the beach. The fourth is metal and lies on the ocean floor towards the central point of the beach. Several Luminous Stone Deposits can be found along the norther cliff face. Link can find five Koroks along Laverra Beach. One can be found be completing the star shaped pattern of rocks at the eastern end of the beach, a second by examining a moving patch of green light towards the beaches centre, a third under a rock Link can access by blowing up a weak portion of the cliff to the right of a Luminous Stone Deposit, a fourth up a palm tree at the beaches centre, and a fifth under a rock on a ledge towards the top of the cliff to the west. Creatures Enemies Materials Creatures Enemies Materials Zonai Devices Korok Seeds

is a recurring character in . Biography Lawdon is a Hylian and the owner of the Wetland Stable in the Lanayru Wetlands. He can be found at the front of Wetland Stable. If Wetland Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Lawdon will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Lawdon explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Lawdon then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Lawdon instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Lawdon suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Lawdon to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Lawdon tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Wetland Stable, Lawdon will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Lawdon thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Lawdon will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Lawdon asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Wetland Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Lawdon asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Lawdon will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Lawdon insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Lawdon refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Lawdon starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Lawdon gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling

Epona. Lawdon gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Lawdon gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside Wetland Stable, Lawdon once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by Wetland Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Lawdon tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Lawdon wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

are recurring Objects and a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Leaves with Fairy Dust go unnamed in . Location and Uses Leaves with Fairy Dust are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. They come in two varieties. The first is Fairy Dust (Fixed Position), which is stationary and found at the top of tall, steep objects like Trees, roofs, or Big Flags. These types are sometimes frozen in Ice, which must be melted before they can be reached. The second type is Fairy Dust (Moving), which travels in a loop around a central point. This loop may be a simple circle or a more complex shape, and the cluster may or may not pause at various points in this circuit. If Link interacts with the Leaves with Fairy Dust while standing close to them, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. List of Leaves with Fairy Dust A total of six Leaves with Fairy Dust can be found in Akkala. A total of 30 Leaves with Fairy Dust can be found in Central Hyrule. A total of three Leaves with Fairy Dust can be found in Eldin. A total of four Leaves with Fairy Dust can be found in Faron. A total of 13 Leaves with Fairy Dust can be found in Gerudo. A total of 19 Leaves with Fairy Dust can be found in Hebra. A total of 16 Leaves with Fairy Dust can be found in Lanayru. A total of 15 Leaves with Fairy Dust can be found in Necluda. Leaves with Fairy Dust return in , operating in the same manner as they did in . Fairy Dust (Moving) works the same as it did previously. Instances of Fairy Dust (Fixed Position) are now sometimes suspended in the air, requiring Link to construct a platform in order to reach them. In addition, Arrow Sign Intersections involve following Arrow Signs toward hidden Leaves with Fairy Dust. When Link interacts with these Leaves, a Korok will appear to give Link a Korok Seed.

is a recurring character in . Biography Ledo is a Zora who lives in Zora's Domain. He an apprentice of Dento who has been tasked with repairing the Domain. Ledo can first be encountered near the Moor Garrison Ruins, where he will call out to Link. He directs Link to where he is swimming in the Water. When Link approaches him, he apologizes for disturbing him. Ledo introduces himself, and he explains that he had no choice but to speak to Link once he realized that he was a Hylian. He asks Link to take a moment to listen to what he has to say. If Link agrees to hear him out, Ledo thanks him. He points out Lanayru Tower to Link, asking that he follow the Zora River towards it until he reaches Inogo Bridge. Noticing that Link appears confused, Ledo promises that it will be worth it if Link does so. He explains that prince of the Zora, Sidon, is searching for a strong Hylian. Since this request is from a member of the Zora royal family, Ledo reasons that that there must be a reward for fulfilling it. Therefore, he asks Link to meet Sidon at Inogo Bridge. Once Link arrives at Zora's Domain, Ledo can be found conducting repairs on the entrance. If Link did not meet him at the Moor Garrison Ruins, he will introduce himself. If they have already met, Ledo will recognize Link and thank him for coming. He then asks Link to meet with King Dorephan in the Throne Room. After Link has spoken to King Dorephan, Ledo will reiterate that Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been causing trouble for the citizens of Zora's Domain. Due to this, Ledo and Fronk have been tasked with repairing the Domain, but they have been running out of supplies. When Link asks about this, Ledo explains that the Domain's upkeep requires a large amount of of Luminous Stones. He reveals that many of them can be found in Upland Zorana. If Link could bring him 10 Luminous Stones, Ledo claims that it would aid his efforts. Once he finishes speaking, the "Luminous Stone Gathering" Side Quest will begin. When Link has collected 10 Luminous Stones, he can return to Zora's Domain to give them to Ledo. He then proceeds to count out all 10 of them. As a reward, Ledo will give Link two Diamonds. He calls Link a lifesaver, promising to trade give one Diamond if he ever brings him 10 Luminous Stones again. After Link has completed the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" Main Quest, Ledo can be seen among the Zora gathered to celebrate in the Throne Room. When spoken to later, he will express his gratitude towards Link. If Link has not received "Luminous Stone Gathering" yet, Ledo remarks that Zora's Domain is still suffering from Divine Beast Vah Ruta's rampage. Link is able to ask Ledo questions while he speaks to him. If Link inquires about Luminous Stones, Ledo explains that

will express his gratitude towards Link. If Link has not received "Luminous Stone Gathering" yet, Ledo remarks that Zora's Domain is still suffering from Divine Beast Vah Ruta's rampage. Link is able to ask Ledo questions while he speaks to him. If Link inquires about Luminous Stones, Ledo explains that they were one of the many Materials used to construct Zora's Domain. Supposedly, the reason Zora's Domain was built in the Lanayru Great Spring was because Upland Zorana is a reliable source of Luminous Stones. If Link asks about Fronk, Ledo reveals that they are both Dento's apprentices. He claims that they both work hard to better their craft, and part of their training is the repair of Zora's Domain. When Link ends their conversation, Ledo will return to his work.

is a recurring character in . Biography Leekah is a young Hylian woman who can be found either at Rebonae Bridge, near Woodland Stable, or near Horwell Bridge. While there, she likes to watch the Hylia River. Whenever Link encounters her, she will be under attack by a Bokoblin. If Link saves Leekah, she gives him Foods or ingredients as a reward. When gifting it to him, she may remark that he deserves it more than the guy she planned to give it to. She might also claim that she is scared of what would have happened to her if Link did not show up. After Link saves Leekah for the first time, she informs him that she likes watching the Hylia River flow by. When she watches the Water, she finds it hard to believe that the Great Calamity ever happened. When she is inevitably attacked by Monsters, she is reminded to return to the nearest Stable. On subsequent rescues, Leekah expresses disdain that she is unable to take a walk and watch the Hylia River without needing to be saved. She then decides to return to either Wetland Stable, Woodland Stable, or Riverside Stable. She may also remark that it is typical that her day out would be ruined. Should Link fail to save Leekah, she will eventually pick herself up off the ground. When she does so, she claims that her head hurts, and she wonders why she thought it would be a good idea to take this road. She may also be angry, accusing Link of standing by while she got beat up. When she arrives at a Stable, Leekah will stand at its entryway. If Link previously saved her, she claims to feel less anxious when he is around. Leekah has heard that ladies 100 years ago were able to walk alone without feeling threatened, but she is unable to imagine that. If Link did not save her, Leekah will be irritated and wonder what she should do now.

is a recurring character in . Biography Leena is a Gerudo Soldier who can be found in the Barracks of Gerudo Town. She carries a Gerudo Spear. The first time Link can speak to her, he will find her going through a list of supplies she needs for a trip into the Gerudo Desert. After Link has started the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Leena will be concerned that Barta may have been captured by the Yiga. However, she assures herself that Barta must have instead gotten lost in the Sandstorms near Karusa Valley. When Link speaks to Liana, she notices that she has not seen Barta for some time. Leena explains that she left for the Yiga Clan Hideout two days ago, and she wonders what happened to her. Angered, Liana asks why she let Barta go by herself, which Leena apologizes for, explaining that she thought she would be careful. Liana is upset that they now have to retrieve both the Thunder Helm and Barta. She expresses concern about Captain Teake finding out about what happened. Once Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Link can speak to Leena to find that she is once again concerned about Barta. When he approaches Liana, she will be shocked to hear that Barta has disappeared for a second time. Kotta reveals that she went to investigate the Gerudo Great Skeleton, though Leena claims she tried to stop her. Liana notes that they clearly did not succeed, but Leena explains that she did not think Barta would actually go due to the Molduga living in the area. When Kotta furthers this point by bringing up the extreme Heat, which only causes Liana to call them idiots. She tells them that Barta would not realize if she was walking towards danger. She resigns herself to the fact that Barta, Kotta, and Leena will not change, but she wonders why she has to get into trouble so often. After witnessing this exchange, "The Search for Barta" Side Quest will begin. When spoken to afterwards, Leena will be upset that Liana is angry at her again. She recalls that she has been in trouble like this before with Teake, claiming that she was mad at her then, too. However, she repeats that she tried to stop Barta this time, since she told her to equip herself for the Heat in the area. Link tells her to try harder next time, but this only angers Leena. When Barta returns to the Barracks, Leena notes how impressive it is that she was able to cross the Gerudo Desert. She wonders how strong Barta must be to do so.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link returns to Rito Village after completing the "Tulin of Rito Village" Main Quest, he will be able to find Teba in his Home. Since he gave his Great Eagle Bow to Tulin, Teba plans to craft a new one for himself. He offers to make an additional one for Link, but he needs a Swallow Bow, five bundles of Wood, and three Diamonds in order to do so. Following their conversation, "Legacy of the Rito" will begin. Once Link has collected the necessary Materials, he can return to Teba to craft the Great Eagle Bow. Before he does so, he asks if Link is certain, since Diamonds can be difficult to acquire. When Link gives his permission, Teba will accept the Materials, promising to make a worthy Bow. He assures Link that Harth, the finest craftsman of the Rito, considers his work to be masterful. Upon finishing the Great Eagle Bows, Teba will give one to Link. Teba then tells Link that if his Bow ever breaks, he can bring him the Materials again to have a new one made. Afterwards, "Legacy of the Rito" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview In the Tobio's Hollow Cave, Link can find a Tattered Notebook at an abandoned campsite. It describes a legend surrounding a treasure that the Zonai hid in the Cave, which goes, "Throw the Zonai spear with a wing from the pedestal, through the ring. Should your aim be true and right, you'll be blessed with dispelling light." However, the writer was unable to throw a Zonaite Spear through the Glowing Ring, and so they left the Notebook behind in the hope that the person that finds it would have better luck. After reading this passage, "Legend of the Soaring Spear" will begin. When Link stands on the pedestal inside the Tobio's Hollow Cave, a Glowing Ring will appear above the nearby spring. In order to throw a Zonaite Spear through the Ring from the pedestal, Link must Fuse a Monster Wing to its end. This will allow the Zonaite Spear to fly farther after being thrown. Once he has successfully thrown a Zonaite Spear through the Glowing Ring, the Utojis Shrine will appear inside the Cave. Following this, "Legend of the Soaring Spear" will be completed. Objectives

Lenalia is a recurring character in . Biography Lenalia is the chamberlain for Zelda in Ancient Hyrule, and the author of the 13 Ancient Tablets found on Small Islands throughout the Sky. In her writings on these Tablets, she describes some of her service to the Royal Family of Hyrule during the events surrounding the Imprisoning War, including the steps taken by Zelda and Mineru to aid Link. She expresses great care for the members of the Royal Family, even protesting when Zelda tries to ride a large Construct built by Mineru. In The Latest Trend, Lenalia writes about how Zelda inspires a seamstress in Ancient Hyrule to create mushroom-patterned clothing, creating a new fashion trend. Lenalia was unable to procure samples of these patterns for herself. Lenalia also writes about the sightings of a fake Zelda about the castle, though its identity as a Phantom Ganon is not known. Troubled by these sightings and what they could mean, Lenalia struggles to sleep at night. Other Appearances Lenalia is quick and dependable in spite of her laid-back behavior. This has led to her becoming a trusted attendant to Rauru. She takes an interest in spiritual things and is always seen carrying her notebook around. She wears the same style of dress as Zelda, who she serves as a chamberlain.

is a recurring character in . Biography Leop is an older Hylian who lives in Hateno Village. He diligently stands outside The Great Ton Pu Inn, welcoming visitors and imploring them to stay. He can be found at the base of the Inn's stairs at most hours of the day and night, greeting Link if he approaches. However, Leop will retreat inside if it begins to Rain. According to Leop, The Great Ton Pu Inn is the best place in Hateno Village to rest. He suggests travelers speak with Prima, the Inn's proprietor, if they wish to stay. When spoken to again, he will encourage Link to spend some time at the Inn. When Link speaks to Leop while carrying the Blue Flame, he asks if Purah is unable to get around on her own anymore. Realizing he has not seen Purah in some time, he wonders if the rumors he heard about her are true. If Link confirms that Purah is doing well, Leop will be relieved, as the people in Hateno Village tend to get worried easily. Alternatively, if Link has difficulty answering him, Leop shares the rumor that Purah's granddaughter has been visiting her, believing Link to have given it away. He is unable to think of any other reason that a child would be staying at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. Leop can be seen walking through Hateno Village.

is a recurring character in . Biography Lester is a Hylian man who works at Rito Stable on the Tabantha Frontier. He spends his days sitting by the Cooking Pot outside of the Stable. When Link first speaks to Lester, he admits that he enjoys spices. In particular, he likes the spiciness of Curry Rice. While he has the Hylian Rice he needs in order to make it, he has run out of Goron Spice. However, he is unable to leave Rito Stable to acquire it. Therefore, he asks Link to bring him Goron Spice if he ever has some. If Link agrees, Lester will thank him, as Curry Rice keeps him warm. The "Curry for What Ails You" Side Quest will then begin. After obtaining Goron Spice, Link can return to Rito Stable to give it to Lester. Once Lester has confirmed its authenticity, he offers to buy it from Link for 50 Rupees. If Link agrees to this deal, Lester will be relieved that he can make Curry Rice to keep warm. He then gives Link a Purple Rupee. Lester asks Link to bring him more Goron Spice if he has it, offering him Hylian Rice in return. He also shares that by Cooking other ingredients with Goron Spice and Hylian Rice, Link can make a variety of curry dishes. When he finishes speaking, the Side Quest will be completed. If Link speaks to Lester afterwards, he will recognize him and ask if he has any Goron Spice to trade for Hylian Rice. If Link agrees to the exchange, Lester is expresses his joy to be able to make Curry Rice, at which point he gives Link his Hylian Rice. If Link refuses, Lester claims he will not force him to do anything, noting that he looks like he needs a good meal. Lester previously worked at Rito Stable, but it was forced to close due to the Extreme Cold Snap in Hebra. He felt adrift after losing his job, but then Purah asked him to tend to the Horses at Lookout Landing, which he accepted. After the construction of the Mini Stable, he serves as its operator. When Link arrives at Lookout Landing for the first time, Lester can be found tending to the Horses. Lester recognizes Link, stating that his appearance will cause a stir. Should Link need something, Lester tells him to talk to Scorpis. If Link speaks to him again, Lester remarks that there has been a stir in Lookout Landing since his arrival. After Link has spoken to Purah, Lester comments on how much the residents have fussed over him. He then explains that he is currently unable to register Horses for Link. If Link asks about registering Horses, Lester informs him that Stables are able to transport registered Horses to each other. is a recurring character in . Biography Letty is a Hylian who travels the Faron Highroad between Lakeside Stable and Lurelin Village. She carries a Hunter's Shield and a Traveler's Sword. During her journey, she rests at the table inside Lakeside Stable and at the Fishing Resort. Letty has been known to suffer from mood swings, which has led others to describe her as "temperamental". When Link speaks to her, she may greet him differently depending on her mood. She also has difficulty discerning and managing her emotions. If she notices that she is treating Link poorly, she will become embarrassed and apologize. As she travels, Letty shows an interest in Lover's Pond. She has heard that it is south of their location in Atun Valley, recalling that she saw it on a Map once. Though she is surprised that it is shaped like a heart, she does not know what else she would have expected. Letty has considered visiting Lover's Pond to find a life partner. Aside from Lover's Pond, Letty will tell Link about other geographical features. While she is in Lurelin Village, she shares that he can take a Raft from their current location to Eventide Island. She has also heard of the Palmorae Ruins near Lurelin Village, but she does not know much about them. She suggests he check out Highland Stable, west of Lakeside Stable, but she warns him that he is likely to encounter Monsters on his way there. Letty will often talk about Food to Link. Her reason for visiting Lurelin Village is to try the Fish and fruit there, which she has heard are delicious. Due to how fatty the Fish are, she believes that grilling them would enhance their flavor. She also informs Link that, while meat dishes can recover Hearts, Fish dishes can grant special effects to those that eat them. Finally, she asks Link if he has has success at Cooking with Fish and fruit, or if he has ended up with Dubious Food. If she encounters any foes during her travels, Letty will draw her Traveler's Sword to protect herself. When Link saves her, she may remarks that she thought she was a goner. She can also comment on her bad luck. As a reward, she will give Link Rupees. Alongside Totsuna, Letty is visiting Kakariko Village to see the Ring Ruins. She expresses annoyance that Totsuna is always asleep or tired despite wanting to see the Ruins.

is a recurring character in . Biography Liana is a Gerudo Soldier who can be found in the Barracks of Gerudo Town. She carries a Moonlight Scimitar and a Gerudo Shield. When Link first approaches Liana, she asks what an outsider is doing in the Barracks. She informs him that they are on high alert, and she suggests that he instead check out the market. If Link asks what happened, Liana begins to explain, but she quickly realizes that she should not tell an outsider anything involving their security. She mentions that she could tell him if he had permission from Captain Teake. If Link speaks to Liana after meeting with Riju, she notices that she has not seen Barta recently and wonders where she is. Leena explains that Barta went to scout out the Yiga Clan Hideout two days ago, but she does not know what happened to her. Angered, Liana asks why she let Barta go by herself, which Leena apologizes for. Liana is upset that they now have to retrieve both the Thunder Helm and Barta. She is fearful that, if Teake were to find out, they would be punished with 100 laps around the Gerudo Desert. Kotta asks what they should do, causing Liana to yell that she is thinking about it. After Link has completed the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, he can return to the Barracks to find Liana yet again shocked that Barta failed to return. Kotta explains that she went to investigate the Gerudo Great Skeleton, and Leena claims that she tried to stop her. Liana points out that this did not work, since Barta is clearly not with them. Leena and Kotta reveal that they did not think Barta would actually go, due to the Molduga and the intense Heat in the area. Liana is only angered further by this, reminding them that Barta walks into danger unknowingly. She resigns herself to the fact that Barta, Leena, and Kotta will not change. However, she still wonders why Barta gets herself into trouble so often. After witnessing this exchange, "The Search for Barta" Side Quest will begin. If Link speaks to Liana during the Side Quest, he can overhear her scolding Kotta and Leena. She is scared of what will happen if Riju finds out what has happened. She then mutters to herself that she needs to do something before anyone else finds out. After Barta returns to the Barracks once again, Liana commends Link, revealing that Barta told her about how he helped her. She compares him to a Champion, claiming that if he were a Gerudo, she would want him as part of her troop. Liana is relieved that the situation has been resolved before Teake could punish her for it. As a reward, she gives Link a Silver Rupee, telling him to buy something nice at the market. With this, the Side Quest will be completed. If Link talks to Liana after calming the Divine Beast Vah Naboris,

the situation has been resolved before Teake could punish her for it. As a reward, she gives Link a Silver Rupee, telling him to buy something nice at the market. With this, the Side Quest will be completed. If Link talks to Liana after calming the Divine Beast Vah Naboris, she admits that she dismissed Link's abilities too quickly. After completing "The Search for Barta", she may also remind him to use his reward and enjoy Gerudo Town.

The , also known as , , , , the , , the , and , is a recurring element in . It is a meter that measures Link's current amount of health in Hearts. Uses The Life Gauge measures Link's current amount of health, represented in the form of Hearts (with the exception of , where Link's health is instead represented by square segments). Whenever Link takes damage, either by an enemy attack, a hazard, or by falling from a high altitude, Link will lose a certain amount of Hearts or part of a Heart equal to the damage taken. In earlier games, the Life Gauge's Hearts are in fractions of two. Starting from , Hearts are in fractions of four. When Link loses all of his Hearts, the game ends with a Game Over. Link's Life Gauge can be replenished by picking up recovery Hearts. The Gauge can also be replenished by drinking recovery Potions, using a Fairy, visiting a Great Fairy, or by resting while Sitting or Sleeping. In many games, Link can also instantly be revived and some or all of his Hearts restored provided he has a Bottled Fairy or a Potion with the effect. In most multiplayer games, such as and , the Links each have their own Life Gauge. The Life Gauge is shared in single-player campaigns, as well as in , wherein the Links all share the damage taken. In most games, but not all, Link's Life Gauge starts with three Hearts. The Life Gauge can usually be increased by obtaining Heart Containers, which add an additional Heart to the Life Gauge for every Heart Container acquired. In some games, Link can also temporarily increase his maximum health through the use of items or equipment. The maximum total of Hearts the Life Gauge can have varies by game. Often it is also possible for Link to gain a Defense upgrade against enemy attacks, thereby taking less damage than normal. This may either take the form of wearing certain equipment, using items, or by receiving permanent upgrades. In some games, Link's unit of health is actually smaller than the increment displayed, which is rounded up to half or quarter of a heart. This results in some attacks not affecting the Life Gauge until enough damage has incurred. This is shown in when using the Red Mail against Bees, in when taking damage from Fire in the Fire Temple, and in the when being eaten by a Like Like. Link's Life Gauge is known as Life or Life Hearts in . Link's Life can be extended to a total of 16 Hearts. When Link is full on Life Hearts, he can throw his Sword. The is a recurring character in . Biography The Light Dragon is a Dragon Spirit known for flying in the upper areas of the Sky. It is the form that Zelda takes after swallowing her Secret Stone of Time and undergoing the process of draconification, losing her mind and sense of self in the process. She does this in order to infuse the Master Sword with her Light powers and restore it back to its former glory, all so that Link can reclaim it in the future. Upon her transformation, she shed 11 Dragon's Tears that landed throughout Hyrule. Ancient Hyruleans were able to view Zelda's Memories by interacting with these Tears, and they drew the Geoglyphs surrounding them. As she flies, the Light Dragon passes over each of these Geoglyphs in chronological order. Several Dragon Parts can be obtained from the Light Dragon. Shards of Light Dragons Spike can be found along her back, while Light Dragon's Scales, Light Dragon's Talon, Shards of Light Dragon's Fang, and Light Dragon's Horns can be obtained from striking various spots of her body. All of these Materials grant Link a healing effect when they are Fused to his Weapon or Shield. The Light Dragon can first be seen after Link Skydives from the Room of Awakening for the first time. As Link explores the Great Sky Island, the Light Dragon repeatedly flies back and forth behind the Temple of Time. After the Decayed Master Sword disappears when Link places it into the Light above the Altar, the Light Dragon flies through the clouds and reveals Hyrule below. Once Link has viewed all 11 of Zelda's Memories from the Dragon's Tears as part of the Main Quest "The Dragon's Tears", the Light Dragon will appear and shed a 12th Tear on Rist Peninsula. This Dragon's Tear allows Link to witness "Tears of the Dragon", wherein he can see Zelda's transformation into the Light Dragon. Once he successfully holds on, the Light Dragon will take Link higher into the Sky. The fur holding the Master Sword in place recedes, and Link is able to claim it once again. is a recurring mechanic in . Overview Lightning can be seen during the opening of . As Link sails through a Thunderstorm, his boat is struck by Lightning and destroyed. Lightning occurs during Thunderstorms, striking sporadically. Any metallic Weapons, Shields, or Bows, including those equipped by Link or an Enemy, will spark during Thunderstorms and eventually attract a Lightning strike on their position (which will deal extreme damage to Link if he does not either remove the offending equipment before the strike happens or equips the Thunder Helm to neutralize the strike). Other metallic Objects will also attract Lightning, requiring Link to keep his distance to avoid being hit by a Lightning strike. Lightning occurs during Thunderstorms, striking sporadically and functioning in the same way as it did in . Lightning also appears in the cloud cluster around the Thunderhead Isles. Thunder and King Gleeoks shoot beams of Lightning at Link that electrocute him if he is not wearing Armor with Shock Resistance or the Lightning Proof Added Effect. These Lightning beams will still harm Link with or without either of these Added Effects. When Thunder or King Gleeoks are badly damaged, they cause Lightning to strike the ground, creating Updrafts at their impact site. Other Appearances In the "Watchers of the Triforce" Scenario, Phantom Ganon makes use of Lightning to attack the Hyrulean Forces. The Lightning can be protected against through the power of the Sages. When a Warrior is struck by Lightning, they lose one quarter of a Heart.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Lightning Temple 2F is accessible from the Lightning Temple 1F's Room of Ascension. It leads to the Room of Light and Flame, which features a Battery inside a cage that cannot be opened from the outside. There is also a light-sensitive Switch attached to a Statue above the Room of Ascension. By redirecting a Light Beam from the Room of Natural Light through the Lightning Temple 5F to this Statue, Link can move it to reveal a Floor Switch that opens a stairway to the Room of Offered Light on the Lightning Temple 3F.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Lightning Temple 4F is accessible by a stairway above the Room of Ascension. There are two light-sensitive Switches attached to Statues on the floor. Additionally, there is Light Beam obscured by Stone Blocks and rotating semi-circular walls. By using Recall to align the semi-circular walls and either Fuse or Ultrahand to move the Stone Blocks, the Light Beam can be carried to the first of the two Statues. When activated, the Statue will move and cause a portcullis to descend, allowing Link to walk through to the stairway. This also opens the path for the Light Beam to reach the second Statue, which moves to reveal a Floor Switch when activated. This Floor Switch opens a pathway to a southwestern chamber filled with traps, which leads to the Room of Light and Shade. A Battery can be found behind a gate controlled by a light-sensitive Switch in the corridor leading to the Room of Light and Shade. By carrying a Light Beam from the Room of Light and Shade, Link can access the battery. Enemies Treasure Chests

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Lightning Temple 5F is accessible by riding the Updraft from the Room of Ascension. Four Statue equipped with Mirrors can be found on Rails in the central chamber of the floor. A ledge on the southwest side of the room gives way to the Room of Natural Light. By carrying a Light Beam from the Room of Natural Light and positioning the Statues to redirect it, Link can activate Statues equipped with light-sensitive Switchs on the Lightning Temple 2F and Lightning Temple 6F. This opens paths into the Room of Offered Light and the Room of Light and Flame, respectively. Enemies

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Lightning Temple B1 is a winding pathway found directly across the entrance to the Lightning Temple 1F. It is the lowest floor of the Lightning Temple, and its dark halls are filled with traps such as falling floors, Flame Balls, and Flame Fountains. Riju will not be able to accompany Link throughout the floor while some of these traps are active. Floor Switches throughout the floor are capable of deactivating these traps, allowing Riju to safely travel through the floor. At the end of the Lightning Temple B1 is the Room of Hopeful Light, which connects the floor to the Room of Ascension. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests

, also known as Glowing Roots, and Roots That Dispel the Darkness, are locations in . Features and Overview Lightroots are the roots of giant Trees found in the Depths. Link can activate them to illuminate a small portion of the Depths. When activated, they reveal the surrounding area on the Purah Pad's Map and become available for use as Travel Points. Standing under their light also reverses the effects of Gloom on Link's maximum health as though he were on the Surface. Each Lightroot has a corresponding Shrine of Light on the Surface. The names of each Shrine of Light are anadromes of each Lightroot, with their names spelled in reverse.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Lightscale Tridents are a variant of the Zora Spear. They belong to the Zora Gear equipment archetype, which is a group of Weapons created by the Zora. A Lightscale Trident was given to the Zora princess Mipha on the day she was born. Even though Mipha preferred to use her healing abilities, it is said that she was talented with this Spear as well. When she came of age, Seggin was the one who taught her to fight with her Trident. King Dorephan later had the story of the Lightscale Trident written on the History of the Zora, Part Four, one of the Stone Monuments found throughout the Lanayru Great Spring. When Mipha did not return after the Great Calamity, the people of Zora's Domain mourned her. They tried to send the Lightscale Trident down Zora River in an attempt to put her Spirit to rest. However, the Trident began to glow, and Mipha's voice was heard. She told the Zora that she was one with the Lightscale Trident, and they should forget their grief and focus on remembering her. As a result, the Zora celebrate the Champion Festival and honor the Lightscale Trident on the anniversary of the Great Calamity. However, if Link speaks with Trello while the Shrine Quest "The Ceremonial Song" is active, he will admit that the Champion Festival uses a replica of the Lightscale Trident instead of the real one. This replica, the Ceremonial Trident, is nearly identical to the Lightscale Trident, but it is not as strong or durable. Link can obtain Mipha's Lightscale Trident after taming Divine Beast Vah Ruta and saving Zora's Domain from flooding. King Dorephan will gift the Trident to him as a reward and symbol of their friendship. After the cutscene, Link can collect the Lightscale Trident from inside a Stone Chest in the Throne Room. If the Lightscale Trident breaks, Dento will remake it if Link approaches him at the Hammerhead. To do so, he requires a Zora Spear, a Diamond, and five pieces of Flint. If the Lightscale Trident is not in Link's possession but still exists elsewhere, Dento will be aware of its presence and instead recommend that Link locates it. The Lightscale Trident is made of metal, and therefore it can conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if it is equipped during Thunderstorms. It will also sink if it is dropped in Water, but it can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate. Finally, it will not burn if it is exposed to a Fire or a Scorching Climate. Lightscale Tridents as they appear in return in . Dento describes them as formidable Weapons that have been passed down by generations of Zora. Unlike other Weapons, they have not Decayed as a result of the Upheaval. Sidon now wields a Lightscale Trident, which he uses in battle. are recurring Enemies in . Like Likes go unnamed in . Characteristics Like Likes are voracious and gelatinous, tube-like creatures notorious for sucking up their prey into their wide mouths and robbing them of their Shields before spitting them out. Like Likes will suck in and engulf Link, after which they will spit him out without his equipment. In most games, they will relinquish the stolen Shield if they are slain quickly enough. While Like Likes will steal most Shields, unique equipment like the Mirror Shield usually cannot be eaten by these enemies. They often reside in wet and dark places, but can also occasionally be found in dry areas. Like Likes are often harmless and will not hurt Link, while in other games they will inflict minimal damage as they spit him out. Link can fight Like Likes with his Sword, Bow, Boomerang and most other items. In later games, a Bomb can be tossed into the Like Like's mouth as it tries to suck Link in. While the Hookshot can be used in some games to stun or damage them, it does not work in all games, and instead may pull Link into the Like Like's mouth and risk losing his equipment. While Like Likes most commonly prey on Shields, other varieties of Like Likes exist with a penchant for eating other items. These include Rupee Likes, which eat Rupees; Force Likes, which eat Force Gems; Deku Likes; and Life Likes, which simply drain Link of his Hearts. The Pikit is a similar kind of enemy that also steals Shields. Like Likes inhabit Dungeons in . On the First Quest, they appear in Level 4, Level 6, and Level 9. On the Second Quest, they appear in Level 5 as well as Level 6 and Level 9. Like Likes frequently appear in small groups, often in small spaces with other enemies, making them more difficult to avoid. While slow, they move in random and erratic patterns. They will only eat Link's Magical Shield, after which they will release him and his Shield reverts back to an ordinary Shield. If Link is caught by a Like Like, he can use his Sword to quickly attack it from inside before it can steal his Shield. Like Likes will not attempt to steal his basic Shield, and will never drop any items when defeated. Like Likes appear in the Game Boy Advance version of . They appear as enemies in the Dark World in their tube-like form. Groups of Like Likes appear near the Shield Shop to the east of the Pyramid of Power, as well as in the Palace of the Four Sword. These incarnations of Like Likes are similar to those in other 2-D games; they move in slow, random paths, but will usually try to target Link when he is nearby. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lindor's Brow is a wooded mountain on Hyrule Ridge. It is mostly covered by Cedar Trees, creating a forest inhabited by many woodland Creatures. Upland Lindor is located on the western foothills, and the two make up the northern border of Ludfo's Bog. The peak of Lindor's Brow is made up of three large and separate rocks, which Link can walk between. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Lindor's Brow. The first is a group of Leaves with Fairy Dust that are situated on top of a dead Cedar Tree. The second is a Race that starts on one of the rocks that makes up the mountain's peak, and it ends directly to the southeast. Whenever Link solves one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Lindor's Brow returns and is now one of the many locations for the game's new Skyview Towers, namely Lindor's Brow Skyview Tower. The landmark itself also features a corresponding cave, Lindor's Brow Cave, where a Gloom Spawn dwells and Maag No'rah Shrine rests. Areas

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Linebeck Island is located in the Lanayru Wetlands. It is a small island surrounded by Shallow Water, and there is a large Tree at its center. The Island is connected to Mercay Island and an unnamed island by wooden bridges. Off the southwestern shore of Linebeck Island, Link can find a Treasure Chest in the Water. When it is opened, he will receive a Purple Rupee. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Linebeck Island. It is a Natural Hiding Spot that takes the form of a Rock on top of the Tree. is a recurring location in . It is Link's place of residence in several games in the series. It is usually located somewhere within the kingdom of Hyrule. Features and Overview Link's House is located in a somewhat central location of Hyrule, with Hyrule Castle nearby in the north in . It is a simple building, containing basic, wooden furniture, and is home to both Link and his uncle. Next to Link's bed, which is situated in the house's northwest corner, are three Pots that each contain a recovery Heart. A Treasure Chest located in the southeast corner of the house contains the Lantern, which will likely be the first item that Link collects in his quest. Link is the protagonist of . He has appeared across many incarnations throughout the series, usually depicted as an ordinary boy or young man who becomes a legendary hero by saving the world through feats of courage. He is often the holder of the Triforce of Courage, a sign of his being chosen by the Golden Goddesses. He is typically seen wielding a sword and shield, most often the Master Sword and Hylian Shield. Specific incarnations of Link may be distinguished by titles such as the Hero of Time in and the Hero of Winds in . All incarnations of Link possess the spirit of the hero and are thereby destined to fight evil. Before the princess is kidnapped by Ganon, she commands her nursemaid, Impa, to find someone courageous enough to save the kingdom. While wandering the land, the old woman is surrounded by Ganon’s henchmen, though a young swordsman named Link appears and rescues her. After hearing Impa’s plea, he resolves to save Zelda and sets out to reassemble the scattered Shards of the Triforce of Wisdom, to become powerful enough to defeat Ganon. Link located the eight underground labyrinths, defeats several guardian Monsters, and retrieves the Triforce Shards. With the completed Triforce of Wisdom, Link is able to infiltrate Ganon’s hideout and defeats him with the Silver Arrow. Link picks up the Triforce of Power from Ganon’s ashes and returns both pieces of the Triforce to Princess Zelda, restoring peace to Hyrule. In , Link is from Suthorn Village in southern Hyrule. When he was a child, he and several other children from Suthorn Village were pulled into a Rift. While they were able to return, Link and the other children lost their ability to speak. Unlike all the other children who had returned, Link kept his memories of what happened inside the Still World. From his experience Link gained the ability to sense when new Rifts opened, which he used to fight off Monsters that would appear from them and help people who would be taken by the Rifts. Link fought with the hope that in doing so he might eventually regain the ability to speak. Link saved a Sheikah man named Lueburry from Monsters in Suthorn Forest, and after hearing his story, Lueburry entrusted Link with the Sword of Might that he had created using Might Crystals from the Still World. Lueburry also gave Link the blue hood and cloak that he wears. When Link set off to defeat Ganon in the Suthorn Ruins, Lueburry provided him with the Bow of Might and Bombs of Might as well. At the beginning of , Link faces off against Ganon. At first he seems to be victorious, but then Ganon's Trident creates a Rift that pulls him into the Still World. Abilities Link is depicted throughout the series as an impressive swordsman. He usually begins his adventure as an average boy with little to no swordsmanship skills. When trouble arises, however, Link demonstrates a natural aptitude for the ways of the sword and is able to best his enemies easily: in , Link goes to Orca to learn how to wield a sword in order to help Tetra from the Forest of Fairies. It is further noted by Orca himself that Link's ability to use a sword is firmly present in his veins. As the game progresses, Link becomes known for his swordsmanship as well as his ability to quickly adapt to a wide variety of items and skillfully wield them, such as the Boomerang, the Bow, and the Grappling Hook, among others. In some games, Link can learn advanced sword techniques and complicated move-sets: in , the Blade Brothers teach the young hero various sword skills by using Tiger Scrolls, and in , the Hero's Spirit shares his knowledge of the sword by teaching Link seven Hidden Skills to help him become more powerful and save Hyrule. Additionally, Link is portrayed as having an excellent physical condition, performing backflips easily as well as being able to best others in sumo-wrestling, as seen in . However, despite this, Link is usually defenseless without a sword or an item. easily as well as being able to best others in sumo-wrestling, as seen in . However, despite this, Link is usually defenseless without a sword or an item. This is depicted in , where Link loses his sword after being launched into the Forsaken Fortress and must use his stealth abilities to get it back: if he is spotted by an enemy, he quickly surrenders due to his inability to fight back. Although in some games Link is easily able to pick up large stones or push blocks many times his size, other games require him to use special bracelets or gauntlets to further increase his strength, such as the Power Bracelet or the Titan's Mitt. As seen in , , and , Link is capable of using magic spells such as Din's Fire provided that he possesses a Magic Meter, which is usually granted to him by a Great Fairy. Link is also talented in playing a wide variety of instruments. This is first shown in the original , in which the young hero plays the Recorder to open up secret entrances or transport him to various parts in the overworld. Since then, Link has competently played other instruments such as the Ocarina, a pan flute, a guitar, the drums, and a Harp, all of which play a major role in each of the respective games in which they appear. Not only is Link a proficient instrument player: he is also adept in using a conductor's baton to conduct other players. After receiving Rauru's arm in , Link gains the ability to use the mysterious powers of the Zonai, such as Ultrahand and Recall. are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Lizalfos brandish swords and have little armor in . They are very agile, for they are able to jump far out of Link's attack range, as well as capable of leaping over the young hero's head to deliver a strike from behind. They first appear in Dodongo's Cavern, where two pairs act as the Dungeons's Sub-Bosses. Despite having to face off against a duo, Link does not have to fight both simultaneously. One engages the young hero, while the other watches from afar. Befitting their tendency to fight in pairs, after one Lizalfos sustains enough damage, the two switch roles with one another. They are seldom encountered, only appearing as regular enemies later in the Spirit Temple and in certain other Dungeons in . A related enemy known as Dinolfos appear later in the game as well. Lizalfos come in two varieties in . One variety uses an axe blade affixed to their tails, and the second variety makes use of a skull mask. They are easily defeated with Bomb Arrows or Hidden Skills such as the Back Slice and the Mortal Draw. In addition, Wolf Link is able to leap at and bite at their throats. Lizalfos appear in parts of Hyrule Field in Lanayru Province in addition to numerous Dungeons, including the Lakebed Temple, the Temple of Time, the City in the Sky, Hyrule Castle, and the Cave of Ordeals. Dynalfos, similar but much larger and more heavily armored enemies, appear in the Temple of Time and the City in the Sky. They are considerably more dangerous opponents than Lizalfos, capable of dodging the Ending Blow and blocking many other attacks. A winged variety of Lizalfos called Aeralfos also appear later in the game. Lizalfos are first encountered in the Earth Temple as regular enemies in . Besides being adept defenders, Lizalfos are very nimble and can swiftly dodge sword strikes, and they can harm Link by blowing streams of fire and by mashing him with the maces found on the tips of their tails. In addition to the Earth Temple, the saurian creatures can be found at the Lanayru Shipyard, the Pirate Stronghold, and the Volcano Summit. An efficient way to slay a Lizalfos is to use strong attacks that make them fall on the ground such as the Spin Attack. After this happens, Link can use the Fatal Blow to kill them. Defeating a Lizalfos will make it drop a Lizard Tail, which can be collected as Treasure. A stronger variant known as Dark Lizalfos appear in the Fire Sanctuary and Sky Keep. The mask was made by the owner of the Fang and Bone store.
