They are highly valued as ingredients in Elixirs due to their ability to continue wriggling after being severed from their body. Lizalfos Tails can be exchanged for 12 Mon at the Fang and Bone or sold for 28 Rupees. They can also be used to make Green Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop. Great Fairies can use Lizalfos Tails to enhance the Soldier's Set and Zora Set. Lizalfos Tails are dropped by standard Lizalfos. They can be Cooked into Elixirs and used for Upgrading pieces of Armor. They may also be Fused to Weapons to grant them whip-like properties. Lizalfos Tails are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Lizalfos Talons are Monster Parts that are dropped by all types of Lizalfos and Stalizalfos upon their defeat. They can be combined with critters in a Cooking Pot to make an Elixir. They can also be sold to Kilton at the Fang and Bone for Mon or given to the Kochi Dye Shop to make Gray Dye. The Zora Set requires five Lizalfos Talons, as well as five Hyrule Basses, to upgrade each piece to their second tiers at a Great Fairy Fountain. Lizalfos Talons are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lockup is a series of dungeon cells found under the northeastern side of the Hyrule Castle Underground. The Lockup Back Room is located at its far end. The Lockup's entrance is guarded by a Decayed Guardian and marked Luminous Stone Deposits. The portcullis is placed over a small pool of Water, allowing Link to lift it with Cryonis to gain entry into the Lockup. It is also possible for Link to enter from the side of the cliff bearing the Lockup, placing him inside a cell opposite a Glowing Eyeball. If defeated, the Glowing Eyeball will release its control on a wooden Lever Switch placed between the two cells, consequently opening the parallel cells. As the Lever Switch is broken, the third cell on the left-hand side can only be accessed through a cracked tile wall between the second and third cells. A second Glowing Eyeball connected to a mass of Malice occupies the switch between the fourth row of cells. The left-hand side hosts a cracked tile wall that connects to the Water Pump Room and the West Passage. Inside the Lockup, Link can find a Wooden Box, which can be broken open for supplies. Areas Enemies Sub-Bosses Equipment Treasure Chests As in , the Lockup composes part of the Hyrule Castle Underground in Hyrule Field. It remained largely intact during the Upheaval, though it is now more difficult to navigate with several broken portcullises that obstruct its pathways. The Lever Switches inside the Lockup are broken and can only be activated by merging them with an Item or Object and then moving them with Ultrahand. The northern Lever Switch controls the northernmost pair of cell doors. The middle Lever Switch is completely broken and cannot be used to open the four central cell doors. However, two of the cells are already open and the remaining closed cells can be entered from their adjacent cells instead. The southern Lever Switch controls the two southermost cell doors can can be activated in the aforementioned way. The southeasternmost cell leads to the West Passage and a break in Hyrule Castle Corridors that once connected it to the Water Pump Room. It now instead leads into the Hyrule Castle Chasm. The Lockup Back Room is no longer accessible from here, and must instead be entered by breaking through the Hard Sediment on its roof. Enemies Equipment Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

The is a recurring location in . The Lockup Back Room goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Lockup Back Room is spacious side chamber at the far end of the Lockup, which is part of the Hyrule Castle Underground. It was initially used for the Test of the Royal Guard, a combat trial to determine those worthy of becoming royal knights. Following the destruction of Hyrule Castle, it stands occupied by a lone Stalnox. If Link enters the chamber, the portcullis at the entrance will close behind him, forcing him to face the Stalnox. Once it has been defeated, the portcullis will lift back up. Enemies Sub-Bosses Treasure Chests The Lockup Back Room returns in . In this game, the Stalnox is gone, with Gloom Spawn located where it used to be. The gate is also sealed, meaning Link will have to bomb the ceiling to make an entrance to the room rather than entering via the same means as in . Once the Gloom Spawn and Phantom Ganon are defeated, the Royal Hyrulean Fabric can be obtained from the chest in the center of the room. Enemies

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lomei Labyrinth Island is a Labyrinth located in the Akkala Sea off the shore of the North Akkala Beach. Three Guardian Skywatchers patrol the top of the Labyrinth walls. Atop the Labyrinth walls, strong winds impede Link from easily Paragliding to the northeast. Upon entering, Link hears a voice telling him that he shall receive a blessing at the end of the Labyrinth and he is given the "Trial of the Labyrinth" Shrine Quest. In a pyramid across the courtyard, Link can see the Ancient Shrine behind a portcullis. To navigate the maze, Link must use Magnesis to move Iron Boxes and must use Fire to burn Thorns that block his path. Throughout the Labyrinth, Link will encounter Guardian Stalkers, Fire Chuchus, Electric Chuchus, and Keese. Link can find several Treasure Chests containing a Silver Rupee, a Ruby, an Opal, and a Royal Broadsword. Link can also find a Great Flameblade, a Thunderstorm Rod, a Torch, a Knight's Broadsword together with a Knight's Shield, a Knight's Halberd, and a Knight's Bow hidden within the maze. Once Link reaches the end of the Labyrinth, he will discover the Tu Ka'loh Shrine and the Shrine Quest will be complete. In addition, an Updraft can be found blowing from a shaft in front of the Shrine; jumping down said shaft brings Link to a vast chamber with four Decayed Guardians, two Guardian Stalkers, a Treasure Chest containing a Diamond Circlet and, in DLC Pack, a Treasure Chest containing the Travel Medallion. The Decayed Guardians in this chamber will not activate until the Diamond Circlet is collected, at which point all four activate simultaneously. If Link returns to this chamber after collecting the Diamond Circlet, they will simultaneously activate upon entry. The Guardian Stalkers activate when approached. Areas Enemies Master Mode Equipment Treasure Chests

, also known as Ingo's Ranch, is a recurring location in . The ranch belongs to Malon and her father Talon, and is most famous for selling Lon Lon Milk. Features and Overview The Lon Lon Ranch is the home of Talon, Malon, Ingo, and Epona in . It is located in the center of Hyrule and is owned by Talon. It is a small farm, with one house area and a barn to keep horses and cows safe. It also has a paddock that can exercise the horses daily. The ranch raises Cuccos, horses, and cows. They make a profit by selling off the famous Lon Lon Milk that the cows make to the people of Hyrule. Young Link can win a Bottle full of Lon Lon Milk from Talon after winning Talon's Chicken Game. A storage tower at the back of the ranch, directly behind the paddock, houses a Piece of Heart, as well as two cows. A Secret Grotto can also be found to the left of the paddock as child Link only. When Link first visits the ranch as a child, Malon introduces him to Epona, a young horse. The farm girl goes on to teach Link "Epona's Song", and Link can play this melody to beckon Epona to him, but he cannot yet ride the horse. Seven years later, Link returns to the ranch to find that it has been taken over by Ingo with the help of Ganondorf and has been renamed to Ingo Ranch. As a result, Talon was kicked out of the ranch, and Malon is forced to obey Ingo's orders or else the horses will be mistreated. For a fee of 10 Rupees, Link can ride the horses in the ranch. For an additional fee of 50 Rupees after riding once, he can race Ingo for the chance to keep the horse (namely, Epona, as she is the fastest). After losing, he will challenge Link again, this time wagering Epona. Upon being defeated yet again, he keeps his promises and hands over Epona to Link; however, he closes the gates of the ranch, intending to prevent the young hero from leaving the ranch. Link easily jumps over the gate by using Epona, and when he returns to the ranch, he finds that it has returned to its normal state. After losing the horse he had set aside for Ganondorf, Ingo turns the ranch over to Malon, and becomes a much happier and much more humble person after the experience. Malon also informs Link that her father will be returning to the ranch soon, and thanks Link for all that he has done. Link can speak to Malon to take part in a small obstacle course and test his skills by using Epona. The goal is to complete two laps around the racetrack in the fastest time possible while jumping the set fences without missing one. If Link beats the obstacle course record, Malon will reward him by delivering a cow to

a small obstacle course and test his skills by using Epona. The goal is to complete two laps around the racetrack in the fastest time possible while jumping the set fences without missing one. If Link beats the obstacle course record, Malon will reward him by delivering a cow to his house in Kokiri Forest, so that he can easily obtain free Lon Lon Milk at any time. Inhabitants Lon Lon Ranch can be found in The Field in . Upon arriving to the field, Link encounters a girl named Malon standing all alone. She tells the young traveler that she was running errands, but just as she was about to head back to her home, it started raining; furthermore, the castle guards were moving all the cannons and even aimed their bows at her. Helpless, she asks the four Links if she can accompany them until she gets back to Lon Lon Ranch with her father, Talon. Unlike , the ranch has no cows or horses to be seen, and there are no buildings except for the house in which the two farm owners live. As thanks for saving his daughter, Talon allows Link to use his horse to make his journey through the fields much easier. Link can grab one of the carrots that are encased in a crystal ball and throw it on the ground to make the horses magically appear, which the young hero will mount automatically. Lon Lon Ranch is an area located in eastern Hyrule in . It connects to five other areas: the Eastern Hills to the south, Hyrule Town to the west, Lake Hylia to the east, North Hyrule Field to the northwest, and Veil Falls to the north. Malon and her father, Talon, live at the Lon Lon Ranch along with their Cows. After Link fails to cross Castor Wilds, Malon and Talon will be locked out of their home. In order to reach Lake Hylia, Link must shrink himself to the size of a Minish, enter the Ranch house, break a Pot containing their Spare Key, and return it to them. As thanks, Talon will grant Link free passage through his Ranch. Located on the Ranch is a tree that can be rammed with the Pegasus Boots to create a Minish Portal and a cave that leads to a Chest containing 50 Rupees and Ankle, who will fuse Kinstone Pieces with Link. Link can also fuse Kinstones with Elsie, one of the cows, if he is in Minish form. Link can also buy Milk from Malon and Epona in Hyrule Town. Enemies Inhabitants Though it is never seen, Lon Lon Ranch is mentioned in the description for the Lon Lon Ranch Fabric.

Lonni is a recurring character in . Biography Lonni is a Hylian who travels between South Akkala Stable and a small shelter southeast of Tarrey Town, walking along the Torin Wetland on her way. While she is east of the Wetland, she follows the Kaepora Pass. She carries a Hunter's Shield and a Traveler's Sword. Often, Lonni is confused for a Gerudo or Merchant by other travelers, which confuses her. Like many Gerudo, Lonni is traveling in search of love, but she feels that her love of Monsters has been scaring away potential candidates. When Link talks to her, she will be surprised, as she believes she is not as interesting as a Gerudo or a Monster. As she walks, she will occasionally claim that she needs to find someone to date. Lonni is familiar with a variety of Monsters. For example, she informs Link that most Octoroks will drown if they are dropped in Water, the only exception being the Water Octorok. She also shares directions to the East Akkala Stable, though she warns Link that he would encounter strong Monsters on his way there. In particular, Lonni appreciates Stalnoxes. She hopes that she will find someone who loves Monsters as much as she does, so they can talk about Stalnoxes all night. When she is near the East Akkala Plains, she claims to have heard about a large Monster in the area, referring to the nearby Stalnox. However, she does not have enough information to track it down. She occasionally remarks on this Stalnox, stating that she gets so excited when she thinks about it that she starts to shake. Aside from Monsters, Lonni is also interested in the Great Fairy that can be found in Akkala. She shares a rumor that the Great Fairy can bring someone happiness with a single glance. She has also heard that she can enhance people's clothes. In addition to this, she also has learned that a lot of treasure was left behind in Hyrule Castle, though she is more excited about the Monsters that have taken up residence within it. While she travels, Lonni will remark on the Weather or the time. Her favorite time of day is the morning. During the night, she remarks that it is a good time to encounter Monsters. If it Rains, she will run for shelter, commenting that the Weather is bad. Once she is safe, she claims that she does not mind having to hide out, since it gives her a chance to meet someone in a romantic setting. If Lonni is attacked by Monsters or Maraudo Wolves, she will run away in fear. During the attack, she states that while she loves Monsters, she hopes they will be struck by Lightning so she does not have to deal with them. If Link saves her, she will be relieved. She may also wonder if this could be a destined encounter between them. In addition, she might claim that this was the last day of

she hopes they will be struck by Lightning so she does not have to deal with them. If Link saves her, she will be relieved. She may also wonder if this could be a destined encounter between them. In addition, she might claim that this was the last day of her journey. As a reward, she gives a Meal or Rupees. Lonni continues to carry a Traveler's Sword and a Hunter's Shield. During the "The All-Clucking Cucco" Side Adventure, Lonni can be found up a hill by a large Tree near South Akkala Stable, waiting in line to consult the All-Clucking Cucco, thinking of what to ask it. Once she notices Link, she asks him if he is also waiting for the Cucco's prophecy, and states that allegedly, the Cucco's words always come true. Afterwards, she offers Link to take her place in line, as she needs time to organize her questions first. When it Rains, Lonni comments that despite frequently traveling, she is not used to getting lots of Rain, and hopes she does not get sick from it. Once the Yiga Footsoldiers reveal themselves, Lonni immediately flees. After Link defeats the Yiga Footsoldiers, Lonni will temporarily stay by the Cooking Pot of South Akkala Stable, talking to Falmark. When Link approaches Lonni, she reflects that, despite that the All-Clucking Cucco was a hoax, she realised that only she is entitled to her decisions in life. Finally, she reveals her plan of going to Hebra in the northwest of Hyrule, and remarks that she and Link may meet again if their paths happen to cross. After the Extreme Cold Snap in Hebra has stopped, Lonni will be found traveling between Snowfield Stable and the Lucky Clover Gazette. When Link interacts with her, she will instantly recognize him, glad to see him looking well, and reveals that she is training in Hebra to get stronger, claiming that training in the Cold Weather is the best way to do so. Lonni claims that allegedly, a Geoglyph is located somewhere in the Tabantha Tundra to the north of Snowfield Stable, as well as a lack of Roads and a Frost Gleeok, unsure how long she would live if the Frost Gleeok would notice her. Lonni warns Link about Snowballs out in Hebra, informing that whether he gets hit by one rolling down a hill, or if an Aerocuda hits him with one, the impact could be deadly. Lonni believes that even if Link does survive, he would still be too embarrassed to tell anyone what happened. Lonni also warns Link about exploring Caves in Hebra, as they could sometimes contain Monsters inside, explaining that she once walked into a Cave, only to be greeted by a Bokoblin ambush. When Lonni arrives at a Campfire near the Bridge of Rito Village at the Lucky Clover Gazette, she claims that fighting Monsters also requires knowledge, not just strength and skill. She then reveals that she reads the Newspaper everyday to learn information on fighting

be greeted by a Bokoblin ambush. When Lonni arrives at a Campfire near the Bridge of Rito Village at the Lucky Clover Gazette, she claims that fighting Monsters also requires knowledge, not just strength and skill. She then reveals that she reads the Newspaper everyday to learn information on fighting Monsters, and advises Link that a trivial piece of information may save his life. Lonni asks Link if has seen a Hinox, a Monster that has a large eye, and claims that they will chase after any Enemy they catch sight of. She wonders if she is able to be use their eyeballs as Weapons, as eyeballs from other Enemies that she obtained are also useful as Weapons. Lonni warns Link that Monsters have set up a Monster Fort nearby. Ever since she heard about it, she has been dreaming about going in there and defeating all of the Monsters, however, she worries she might be defeated if she physically tries to do so, therefore, she has to train up and learn combat strategies first, such as assessing the Enemies' moves, or the timing of her attacks. During the Cold Weather, Lonni will seek shelter under a hut or a Deserted House at the Tabantha Village Ruins until the Weather changes. If Lonni encounters an Enemy, she will fight back. If Link interacts with her during the fight, she will appreciate Link for helping, although advises him to be careful as well. After Link defeats the Enemy, she thanks him, despite believing that she could have handled it on her own. She then proceeds to reward him with a Meal.

is a location in . Features and Overview Lookout Landing is a fortified settlement located in the center of Hyrule Field, next to a Skyview Tower. It is built at the site of 's Sacred Ground Ruins. It is the base of operations for the Zonai Survey Team. In the northwestern corner is the Lookout Landing Well. Areas Mubs' General Store Alongside the Lookout Landing Armor Shop, Mubs also runs a General Store. Like the Armor Shop, the Store starts out small, with only Apples and Arrows in stock initially. As the parts of "Regional Phenomena" are completed, new items are added to Mubs' stock. Additionally, after completing the Side Adventure "A New Signature Food", the Store will start selling Hateno Cheese instead of Fresh Milk. Wares and Pricing Bargainer Statue Creatures Equipment Inhabitants Materials

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Lookout Landing Armor Shop is an Armor Shop ran by Mubs in Lookout Landing. She also runs a parallel General Store with everyday goods instead of Armors. When Link completes one of the four "Regional Phenomena" Main Quests, the Lookout Landing Armor Shop and Mubs' General Store both are expanded with the help of Lookout Landing's Carpenter Karson Initially, Mubs will only have the Hylian Armor Series in stock. With the expansion of the Shop, Mubs will have the room for four more Mannequins, which she will add progressively to display the new Armor she is able to acquire. The Snowquill Tunic is made available at the Shop after Link has completed the Main Quest "Tulin of Rito Village". After the completion of "Yunobo of Goron City", Link will be able to buy the Flamebreaker Armor. The last two spots are reserved for two Armor pieces sold at the Kakariko Village Armor Shop Enchanted. Mubs will add both to her stock once Link has completed the "Gloom-Borne Illness" Side Quest. Jambo can be found checking out the displays the Shop throughout the day. He is very passionate about Clothes, and when a Stone Tablet falls into Lookout Landing he considers selling it in order to buy more outfits. He often comments on the pieces on display while talking to Link. When the Shop's stock is expanded, he worries someone else might snatch the new arrivals before him. If Link buys one of the new products, Jambo expresses his regret at not selling his ore to afford the Armor. Before Link completes "Gloom-Borne Illness", Jambo mentions wanting to get his hand on the Radiant Shirt or the Stealth Chest Guard, but laments that they are only available in Kakariko Village. Wares and Pricing

is a location in . Features and Overview The Lookout Landing Well is a Well on the northeastern side of Lookout Landing. Though it is mostly featureless, there is a Cracked Wall on its southwestern side that rushing Water flows out from. Breaking the Wall reveals a passageway small enough for Link to Crouch through, at the end of which is a second chamber. This chamber is visible through a grate in the Emergency Shelter. When Link first arrives in Lookout Landing, the Lookout Landing Well will still be under construction. If he tries to move the Board blocking its entrance, Karson will stop him, as he is worried about Link falling in. Should Link try to do so again, Karson believes he is interested in the Well, and he promises to be done with it soon. After Link has spoken to Scorpis and opened the Emergency Shelter, the Lookout Landing Well will be complete and Link is able to explore it. Upon starting the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?", Fera will leave her current location to visit the Lookout Landing Well. When Link meets her there, she comments on how interesting newly-built Wells can be and declares that she likes it. From this point on, Link must visit Fera in the Lookout Landing Well to inform her of any new Wells he has discovered. Fera will remain in the Well even after her Side Quest has been completed, where she will be contemplating which of the Wells in Hyrule to see first. Materials Treasure Chests

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lookout Post is a small Gerudo outpost located on the East Barrens of the Gerudo Desert, directly south of Gerudo Town. The Gerudo soldier, Sudrey, has been stationed at at the Post with the purpose of monitoring Divine Beast Vah Naboris. Due to the Lookout Post's proximity to the Divine Beast, it will initially be covered by a Sandstorm. Link can avoid Naboris's Lightning attacks by hiding inside the Post. Two Ladders can be found on the exterior on the Lookout Post, which lead to the roof and a wooden platform. Link is also able to sleep in the Bed inside the Post. During the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Riju asks Link to meet her at the Lookout Post for their fight against the Divine Beast. When Link arrives, the Sandstorm will have shifted away from the Post. Sudrey directs Link to the wooden platform on top of the Post, where Riju is waiting for him. While speaking with Link, Riju will go over their plan for facing Divine Beast Vah Naboris. She also asks Link to retreat to the Lookout Post if he needs to stop fighting. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Sudrey decides to remain at the Lookout Post for the foreseeable future, citing the presence of Monsters throughout the Gerudo Desert. Inside the Lookout Post, Link can come upon a Stone Chest with a Golden Bow inside. Creatures

is a character in . Biography Loone is a Hylian woman who resides at the camp on Puffer Beach. When Link first encounters her, she will be sitting at the Cooking Pot next to an Ancient Orb. If Link speaks to Loone, he will overhear her telling the Ancient Orb how smooth and gorgeous its skin is, referring to it by the name Roscoe. Noticing that Link is watching them, Loone teases Roscoe for being shy. She encourages Roscoe to show himself off. Realizing that Link appears to want something, Loone becomes fearful that he is after Roscoe. She assures Roscoe that she will never let someone take it, claiming to be in love with it. Quietly, Loone admits that she lied to Roscoe. Much more loudly, she proclaims that she wants to see Guardians. In particular, she wants to see Guardian Skywatchers, Guardian Scouts, and Guardian Stalkers. She specifies that she wants to see active ones, not like the ones on Puffer Beach that have ceased functioning. She admits that if she were to ever see them, she may abandon Roscoe. However, she soothes Roscoe's worries, saying that getting close to a Guardian would be too dangerous. She decides that seeing them in person is simply a dream. After this, the "Guardian Slideshow" Shrine Quest will begin. When Link speaks to Loone again, he can hear her repeating her desire to see Guardians to Roscoe while she comforts him. If Link has taken Pictures of all three Guardians, he can show them to Loone. She begins to tell Link to not bother her and Roscoe, but she stops once she sees the Picture of the Guardian Skywatcher. Loone is shocked to see the Picture, stating that the beauty of the Guardian Skywatcher makes her feel alive with terror. When she sees a Guardian Scout, she calls it adorable, noting that it appears vicious for its small size. Now that Link has shown her two types, Loone begins to realize that Link must have a third Picture. Seeing the Guardian Stalker Picture, Loone has trouble believing it, and she exclaims that it is "exhilaratingly scary." After seeing all three Pictures, she remarks that it was a joy. Loone demands the Sheikah Slate from Link, as she wants to look at the Pictures everyday. When Link refuses, Loone will be disappointed, but she resolves herself to burn the Pictures into her mind. When Link asks if he can take Roscoe, Loone allows it, claiming to be over it. After seeing the Pictures, Loone is now obsessed with Guardians, and they are all she can see when she closes her eyes. Afterwards, Loone will stand by the broken down Guardian Stalker near her camp. When Link speaks to her, she states that he has inspired her imagination. Since she saw Link's Guardian Pictures, she has spent her time daydreaming. She also claims to not remember Roscoe.

is a recurring character in . Biography Lorn is a Gerudo woman who manages Lorn's Fruit Stand in Gerudo Town, where she sells a variety of Fruits. At night, Lorn's daughter Dalia sleeps in the Stall at her side. As Link passes by Lorn's Fruit Stand, she will advertise her wares. If Link speaks to Lorn, she claims that her Fruits fresh, juicy, and perfect for eating. She may also claim that her Fruits are just as sweet as her daughter. When Link ends his conversation with Lorn, she tells him that Dalia loves Fruitcake, so she tries to make it occasionally. However, she has difficulty finding the Tabantha Wheat, Cane Sugar, and Goat Butter needed to Cook it. Lorn suggests that Link make Fruitcake for himself, if he has the ingredients. Like other General Stores managers, Lorn will buy Items from Link. During this, she may comment that Link has many things that Dalia would like. When she makes a purchase, Lorn will be grateful towards Link, especially if she believes Dalia will like it. She can also comment that it is fun to see what foreigners carry with them. When Link stops selling, she tells him to come back in the future.

The , also known as the Deep, Dark Forest, is a maze-like area of a confusing forest that has made several appearances throughout . Its layout is usually designed to make anyone who enters to become irreversibly lost, and the only way to exit the forest is by navigating it in specific directions. In certain games, it is said that if people wander in the forest for too long, they can turn into a monster such as a Skull Kid, a Stalfos, or a Deku Scrub. Features and Overview Its first appearance, in , is as a simple-looking cross-section of dead Trees. However, once Link enters it, he finds that exiting the forest in any direction (except east) will cause him to simply appear back at the same spot. The only way to clear the forest is to follow a specific pattern through it. This special pattern is revealed when Link pays an Old Woman for information. She tells him that the proper directions to escape the forest are north, then west, then south, then west again. Successfully navigating through the Lost Woods leads Link to the Graveyard. In , the Lost Woods are more like a maze than a puzzle. Many notable things can be found here. Most importantly, it is the location of the legendary Master Sword, which is held in the Sacred Grove located in the northwestern portion of the woods filled with Animals. Several Fake Master Swords can also be found, resulting in a humorous line if Link picks one up. When Link first enters the Lost Woods, it is covered in a thick fog that makes it hard to navigate; however, once the young hero retrieves the Master Sword after acquiring the three Pendants of Virtue, the mist will disappear. A secret hideout for a gang of Thieves is located in the eastern portion of the woods, with a Piece of Heart found in a secret entrance under a bush. Other Thieves run amok in the forest, bumping into Link in an attempt to steal his Rupees, Bombs, and Arrows. The Magic Mushroom can also be found here scattered throughout the woods. If picked up and given to Syrup the witch, Link can receive the Magic Powder. In , the Lost Woods are laid out like a map, with each screen having something unique about it. Also, the goal in these Lost Woods is to stay inside, rather than to escape; if Link takes the wrong doorway, he will be warped back to the Kokiri Forest. By following the music of "Saria's Song", Link can navigate through the hollow trees and get to the Sacred Forest Meadow, which is located in the northernmost portion of the Lost Woods and Saria's "secret place". The Forest Temple is located here. Alternative methods can also be used to determine if a path leads to another part of the woods or back to the Kokiri Forest. The main method is to simply analyze the holes in the trunks. If

the Lost Woods and Saria's "secret place". The Forest Temple is located here. Alternative methods can also be used to determine if a path leads to another part of the woods or back to the Kokiri Forest. The main method is to simply analyze the holes in the trunks. If there is gradually increasing light in the center of the tree trunk (as if it were a tunnel out), it will lead back to the Kokiri Forest, but if it is a flat wall of blackness, it will continue through the woods. The Lost Woods is home to the only Moblins in , as well as many Business Scrubs, Mad Scrubs and the only collection of average Deku Scrubs in the game, the Deku Community. Hidden within the Lost Woods is the Forest Stage, where Link can be rewarded with item upgrades by showing off specific Masks in front of Deku Scrubs. Moreover, scattered throughout the woods are two portals that lead to Goron City and the upper part of Zora's River near the Sleepless Waterfall. It is said that those who become lost in the woods will become Stalfos. The Skull Kids that inhabit the forest are implied to be children who were lost as well. The Lost Woods is a place that can only be explored in the beginning of . The Lost Woods is where Link must chase down the Skull Kid to retrieve his Horse, Epona, back. Link travels into the Lost Woods in search of his lost friend, Navi. While searching, he was knocked off his Horse by the Skull Kid, giving him the opportunity to steal the Ocarina of Time and Epona before Link woke up. Once Link falls into the Sealed Room, he will not be able to return to the Lost Woods again for the rest of . The Lost Woods are also where the Skull Kid encountered the Happy Mask Salesman, whom he stole Majora's Mask from. The Lost Woods are situated in northwestern Holodrum in , connecting to the Tarm Ruins. Near the Lost Woods, there is a Deku Scrub in a cave. If Link has obtained Guru-Guru's Phonograph, the Deku Scrub will say that he likes the song and tell him to go in some specific directions in the Lost Woods. If he does this he will find the Noble Sword (or, if he already has the Noble Sword in a linked game, the Master Sword) in a pedestal. This is the final part of the Trading Game. In , the Lost Woods appears as the first Stage in The Dark World level. It was originally known as the Forest of Light, and under the White Maiden's control, until a thick cloud of darkness covered northwestern Hyrule and corrupted it into its present state. The cursed woodland is covered in bones and skulls, giving it a look closely resembling the Skeleton Forest from . It is populated primarily by Deku Scrubs, who all swear allegiance to Ganon. The Links arrive to the forest to search for the Dark Mirror, which is believed to be hidden away in a temple in the heart of the woods. They eventually make their way through the wood, and find themselves at Kakariko Village where they continue their search. According to the Deku Scrubs, those who wander and become lost in the forest turn into Deku Scrubs, mirroring the myth how the Lost Woods in turns people into Stalfos. They also mention that Ganon's darkness will cause the Lost Woods to spread all over Hyrule's forests, turning them into Lost Woods as well. In , Link must navigate the Lost Woods to reach the Forest Sanctuary to open a path to the Forest Temple by performing a song with Gage using the Spirit Flute. When he first enters the woods, Link is sent back to the entrance, and must speak with the residents of the nearby Whittleton to find out how to navigate them. He learns that by following the directions that certain Trees point (save the fourth one), he will make it to the Forest Sanctuary. Once the Lost Woods are solved for the first time, they disappear. In , the Lost Woods houses the Master Sword, much like in . To obtain the Master Sword, Link must retrieve all three Pendants of Virtue. When Link enters the northwest area of the Lost Woods, he is met with eight Poes in an area with pathways going in all four directions. One Poe offers to bring him deeper into the Lost Woods if he can follow the correct one; all the Poes then shuffle their places and fly off in different directions. If Link goes in the proper direction, he will soon be met again by the Poes. Two of them test him by attempting to mislead the hero and instruct him to go in the direction that they did not. Next, three Poes will attempt to mislead Link in the same manner. If Link successfully follows the Poes' instructions, he will be lead to the Sacred Grove housing the Master Sword. If he takes a wrong direction, he will find himself starting over back at the first area with Poes, though there will be one fewer Poe trying to mislead him. By using the Hint Glasses, Hint Ghosts can be found in these areas of the Lost Woods and will point Link in the correct direction for a Play Coin. Once Link obtains the Master Sword, Sahasrahla will telepathically speak to Link, telling him to use the newly-obtained Sword to destroy the Barrier at Hyrule Castle. Light then returns to the forest, clearing out the fog, and Link will no longer have to

the correct direction for a Play Coin. Once Link obtains the Master Sword, Sahasrahla will telepathically speak to Link, telling him to use the newly-obtained Sword to destroy the Barrier at Hyrule Castle. Light then returns to the forest, clearing out the fog, and Link will no longer have to follow the Poes through the Lost Woods to reach the Sacred Grove. The Lost Woods also houses several Maiamais and a Piece of Heart. The Lost Woods is a fog-infested forest in . It serves as the only means of entry to the Korok Forest in the Great Hyrule Forest, connecting to the Korok Forest via an isthmus surrounded by the impassable Lake Mekar. Travelers who enter the Lost Woods may find themselves lost in the dense fog that covers the landscape, which will return them to the entrance of the Woods. To successfully navigate the Lost Woods, Link must carry a lit Torch through the fog. One can be obtained at the Woods' entrance, where a pair of stationary Torches can be found, along with one that can be picked up. Following the trail of embers that come from the Torch will lead Link to the entrance to the Korok Forest. Despite this, it is possible to navigate the Lost Woods without the assistance of a Torch if one knows the path. Due to its nature, the Lost Woods protects the Master Sword from intruders. The Lost Woods are filled with a unique type of Tree known as Ogre Trees. Near the entrance, Link can find a stone Treasure Chest in one of the Ogre Trees's mouths containing a Forest Dweller's Spear. Another stone Treasure Chest holds an Opal. During the "EX Strange Mask Rumors" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link must read the Super Rumor Mill V1. It claims that the Korok Mask can be found in the hollow of a Tree in a forest that makes people lose their way. South of the pair of Torches at the Lost Woods' entrance, Link will find the Korok Mask in an EX Treasure Chest in the mouth of an Ogre Tree. Creatures Enemies Materials The Lost Woods are now covered in fog that makes them completely impossible to navigate. The fog disperses after Link cleanses the Korok Forest of Gloom by defeating the Gloom Spawn and Phantom Ganon within the Deku Tree Chasm, allowing him to travel through the Lost Woods normally. After obtaining all three Pendants of Virtue, Link enters the Lost Woods and, while speaking telepathically with Sahasrahla, the young hero begins to have his doubts about whether or not the Master Sword will select him as its bearer. Link then finds the Master Sword and seizes it from its Pedestal, readying himself to have his final battle with Agahnim and rescue Princess Zelda. Afterward, Link is ambushed by several Ball and Chain Troopers, although he easily defeats them with a single Spin Attack from the Master Sword. Link decides to lie down and rest in the Woods, only to be awoken by Princess Zelda via telepathy. Although the young hero tells Princess Zelda that he must rest, Princess Zelda reminds him that only a single night remains until Agahnim casts his final incantation on her and causes the entrance to the Dark World to open and overwhelm Hyrule with its evil. With this in mind, Link leaves the Lost Woods and heads to Kakariko Village to prepare himself. (Himekawa) Although not appearing in the main story, the Lost Woods do appear in the bonus chapters. The Lost Woods is a dangerous place where people will get lost if they lose sight of the exit. Nobody is allowed in there but Link and Saria; they enter it in an attempt to retrieve a Mask. The Forest is dangerous and, according to Skull Kid, those that get lost will eventually lose all hope and become faceless Skull Kids. It is also home to the Baga Tree, an evil opponent of the Deku Tree that is possessed by a bug (most likely Gohma) and is eager to kill Saria and Link as an act of vengeance on the Deku Tree for "Ignoring the rules of the Forest" and allowing Link into the Kokiri. Strangely the forest appears to be home to only Skull Kids, Wolfos, and Moblins (under complete command of the Bagu Tree) that wish to reclaim the forest for their own with no Deku Tree at all. The forest is accessible also from Hyrule Field (as seen in Skull Kid's memory). In , the Lost Woods is an area that is placed within a randomly-generated location within the Forest biome in Hyrule. Upon entering Lost Woods, Link, and Zelda will be sent back to the initial screen if they take the incorrect exit. In order to reach its center, the Lost Swamp, the heroes must take the exit closest to the initial position of the enemy on the screen that is different from the rest, or follow the vibrations generated from Tingle's Dowser, which rumbles the most when the hero is next to the correct exit. The center of the maze is the Lost Swamp, which contains a dungeon where the player fights Gohmaracas,

the enemy on the screen that is different from the rest, or follow the vibrations generated from Tingle's Dowser, which rumbles the most when the hero is next to the correct exit. The center of the maze is the Lost Swamp, which contains a dungeon where the player fights Gohmaracas, one of the four monsters that the heroes must defeat in order to break Octavo's seal on Hyrule Castle. The Lost Woods is also the location of Tingle's House, where Tingle gives the heroes the Tingle's Dowser, which can help guide them through the Lost Woods by causing the Nintendo Switch to rumble when the heroes are close to treasure or near the correct path to the Lost Swamp, giving light rumbles when the heroes are near the incorrect exit but strong rumbles when they are next to the correct exit. It is also the location where the heroes can meet Yves, a friendly Deku Scrub, who resides in the same tree hut as Tingle and joins the heroes on their quest to stop Octavo after they give Tingle 20 Deku Seeds. On the initial screen of the maze is a Cave where Cadence can be found inside with a special item, with the item varying depending on how many times the heroes' have encountered her outside of seeing her at Link's House. If it's the first time the hero has found her in a cave, she gives them the Lute, allowing them to travel to previously activated Sheikah Stones. The Song "Lost Woods - Combat" plays in the Lost Woods whenever combat is initiated. Enemies Minibosses The Lost Woods is the setting of the "Freeing Korok Forest" Scenario in . After the Rito Champion, Revali, defeats the monster outposts surrounding Korok Forest, Link, Impa, Zelda, and the four Champions go through the Lost Woods. However, they think they might have gotten lost. Hestu then appears and guides them, only to figure out that the entrance to Korok Forest has been blocked by Malice. After defeating the Hollows of the four Champions inside the Lost Woods, the entrance to Korok Forest is made clear.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lover's Pond is a Heart-shaped pond located atop Tuft Mountain in East Necluda, directly to the west of Lurelin Village. According to legend, the Lover's Pond is said to show people to their soulmate. Following this legend, many individuals throughout Hyrule search for the Pond, hoping to find their soulmates. When Link arrives at Lover's Pond, he will find Wabbin and Perda standing at either of its ends. They have both come to find their true love, but Wabbin's hesitance is frustrating to Perda. If Link speaks to Wabbin, he states that he is working up the courage to speak to Perda. He goes on to explain that he became lost on his way to Lover's Pond, but when he opened his eyes, he saw Perda and fell in love with her. Wabbin has always wanted to confess to the girl of his dreams by giving her a Blue Nightshade, but he does not have one. This begins the "A Gift of Nightshade" Side Quest. After Link gives Wabbin a Blue Nightshade, Wabbin will initially be excited, but he soon becomes nervous and asks Link to deliver it to Perda on his behalf. Once she receives the Blue Nightshade, Perda will become suspicious. She then confronts Wabbin, who becomes fearful and wonders if she dislikes the Flowers. Perda explains that Blue Nightshades are her favorite Flower, and she accuses Wabbin of being a Yiga spy. However, after Wabbin reveals his intentions, Perda is convinced that their meeting is the result of destiny and demands that Wabbin speak his piece. At Wabbin's confusion, Perda gives examples of how a man should ask out a woman. Wabbin, believing that Perda is asking him out, accepts her request. To reward Link for his assistance, Wabbin gives him a Red Rupee. Perda is angered that Wabbin would give him so little, so Wabbin gives Link a Silver Rupee. Perda then thanks Link, wishing him luck in finding his own true love. A metallic Treasure Chest can be found at the bottom of Lover's Pond. Using the Magnesis Rune, Link can pull the Chest from the Water. When it is opened, Link will receive a Throwing Spear. Creatures Materials

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Lucky Clover Gazette is a Newspaper company owned by Traysi. After the Extreme Cold Snap caused by the Upheaval drove customers away from Rito Stable, most of its residents left and sought a home elsewhere while Traysi bought the place from Galli at a dubious price. She enlisted the Rito Penn and her sisters Juannelle and Douma to serve as its staff. At the Lucky Clover Gazette, Penn offers for Link to apply to work there, explaining how the Gazette came to be and promising to put in a good word for him with his boss. Traysi overhears this and yells at Penn to be quiet for her investigation into Zelda's disappearance and to stop gossiping about how she obtained the site. After recognizing their guest as Link, she asks Penn to leave so that they may talk in private. When Link and Traysi are alone, she explains that she was asked by Purah to use her Newspaper to help search for Zelda. As a result, the Lucky Clover Gazette received too many reports back to keep up on the investigation. She asks Link to help Penn visit every Stable across Hyrule and offers to give Link the Froggy Armor in exchange for helping, beginning the "Potential Princess Sightings!" Side Adventure. Materials Equipment

The Lucky Treasure Shop is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Lucky Treasure Shop is a Shop run by Cloyne in Lurelin Village. It hosts the Treasure-Chest Game Mini-Game. Cloyne also keeps a variety of Books on the Shop's shelves, which is noted to be unusual for places where gambling is done. On days with Rain, Armes mentions that he goes to the Lucky Treasure Shop to gamble. During Rain, Numar also asks Link if he could fund his visits to the Shop, requesting a payment of 100 Rupees. He will often lose Rupees while playing, but if he wins, he will give Link 1,000 Rupees. The Hylian text on the Sign of the Lucky Treasure Shop reads "CHANCE" and "ALL OR NOTHING", reflecting the game of luck. Inhabitants Korok Seeds Inhabitants

is a recurring character in . Biography Lukan is Gerudo who can be found traveling throughout the Region of Gerudo. In particular, she travels between Gerudo Town and the Gerudo Canyon Stable, stopping at Kara Kara Bazaar along the way. She carries a Gerudo Shield and a Gerudo Scimitar. When Link first meets Lukan, she notes that he looks like a regular traveler, but she is unsure. Lukan admits that she is a Gerudo Soldier in disguise as a Merchant. Asking Link if he has heard of the Yiga Clan, Lukan explains that they have been causing trouble in Gerudo Town, and some of them have disguised as travelers to ambush people. The reason that Lukan herself is disguised is so she can catch them when they try to attack her. She believes that, since they were bold enough to infiltrate Gerudo Town, they will likely strike travelers as well. If Link speaks to Lukan at the Gerudo Canyon Stable, she says that the Yiga Clan is bound to attack if anyone at the Stable lets their guard down. Lukan will spend her time carefully watching for suspicious people who may be Yiga. Sometimes, Lukan be found sitting inside the Stable, though she claims that it is a bad place to rest due to the danger of the Yiga Clan. As the day breaks, Lukan notices that the Heat is starting to increase. During the day, she remarks that it is "broiling." In the evening, she will be relieved that the weather is cooler. At night, she comments on how cold it is. In the Gerudo Desert, Lukan tells Link not to go near the Divine Beast Vah Naboris, or else he will be struck by its Lightning. She then proclaims that the Gerudo know better than to go near the Divine Beast. Lukan has heard that Riju, the chief of the Gerudo, might be doing something about Naboris, but that it is still smart to stay away until then. Lukan also tells Link that Naboris has caused many problems since it showed up. She continues to say that everyone avoids the Divine Beast, and she tells Link should get somewhere safe before its Lightning strikes him. If Link speaks to Lukan again, she is surprised that he is still there, saying not to blame her if he is struck by Lightning. After the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest has been completed, Lukan informs Link that the Gerudo Desert is still dangerous. She tells him to make sure he is well-equipped before he journeys the Desert. She also warns Link about the dangers of sandstorms in the Gerudo Desert, and she tells him to avoid them if he values his life. If Link speaks to Lukan at the Kara Kara Bazaar or Gerudo Town, she claims that she has been watching her surroundings and that there is no one suspicious in the area. In Gerudo Town, she is paranoid that the last of the Yiga could attack at any

his life. If Link speaks to Lukan at the Kara Kara Bazaar or Gerudo Town, she claims that she has been watching her surroundings and that there is no one suspicious in the area. In Gerudo Town, she is paranoid that the last of the Yiga could attack at any moment. She will also tell Link that the Gerudo soldiers have been working to root out all surviving Yiga Clan members, and she is doing her part as well. When Lukan is attacked by enemies while traveling, she will draw her Gerudo Scimitar to defend herself. If Link saves her, she will thank him. As a reward, she will give Link Chilly Mushroom Risotto.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Lulu Lake is a small lake in the Lanayru Great Spring. It is located east of Mikau Lake and on a higher ridge. The Lake is one of the shortcuts to the top of Ploymus Mountain, being accessible by Swimming up its Waterfall while wearing the Zora Armor. East of the Lake is the History of the Zora, Addendum 2. Before Divine Beast Vah Ruta is calmed, Lulu Lake will be constantly under the effect of its Rain. Prior to the Great Calamity, Lulu Lake was the site where Mipha faced part of her Divine Beast Tamer's Trial in order to become a Champion. During the Main Quest "EX Champion Mipha's Song", which is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack, Link is tasked with repeating this Trial, which involves Swimming through the Glowing Rings along the Lake's Waterfall. In Master Mode, a wooden platform carried by Sky Octoroks will appear above Lulu Lake. On it is a Metal Chest containing a Silver Bow. Creatures Enemies Materials Creatures Other Appearances During the Quest "Scouting the Training Ground", Sidon decides to host his Waterfall-climbing class at Lulu Lake, and he wants to inspect it without disturbing the Lynel on Ploymus Mountain nearby. With Stealth-boosting Materials, Sidon confirms that the Lake is a good fit for his class, but he needs someone to defeat the Lynel beforehand. In the Quest "Duel on Ploymus Mountain", Urbosa is tasked with clearing out the Lynel, which allows the Zora to move forward with their class. As part of the Quest "Training at Lulu Lake", Sidon is finally able to start his Waterfall-climbing class, but he needs speed-boosting Materials for his students. Using the Materials, Sidon's students are able to master climbing Waterfalls, and their eager attitudes inspire him to work even harder with his own training.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Luminous Stones can be found by breaking Luminous Stone Deposits, which can be identified by their glow during the night. They are also dropped by Stone Taluses (Luminous) upon their defeat. The Kochi Dye Shop can use Luminous Stones to make Navy Dye. Three of them are also required to buy one piece of the Radiant Set at the Gerudo Secret Club. If Link speaks to Ledo at Zora's Domain, he will explain that he needs more Luminous Stones in order to continue his repairs. He will ask Link to gather ten Luminous Stones for him, which will initiate the "Luminous Stone Gathering" Side Quest. Upon delivery, Ledo will reward Link with two Diamonds. Afterwards, Link can bring him ten Luminous Stones at any time in exchange for one Diamond. The Radiant Set requires Luminous Stones the be upgraded to its first, second, third, and fourth tier at a Great Fairy Fountain. Luminous Stones are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

is a recurring location in . Overview Lurelin Village is a seaside town located at the western end of the Faron Highroad in East Necluda. Many of its Houses are simple wooden huts, which have been built around the Palm Trees indigenous to the area. The residents also make use of wooden platforms and Docks, one of which is located along a freshwater pond on the western end of the Village. There is also a small pasture within Lurelin Village where Hateno Cows are kept, and Yah Rin Shrine can be found on a cliff overlooking the Village. Lurelin Village subsists itself by catching Fish, which is an industry most of men Village's men participate in. During the Great Calamity, Lurelin Village avoided being overtaken by the Guardians' assault due to its distance from Hyrule Castle. As a result of this, it has gained popularity as a resort location in modern times. Like other settlements in Hyrule, Lurelin Village features a Goddess Statue, which is located west of the Fishing Resort. There, Link can exchange four Spirit Orbs for a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. Three Side Quests are also available at Lurelin Village, those being "Sunken Treasure", "What's for Dinner?", and "Take Back the Sea". When the "Captured Memories" Main Quest is active and "Find the Fairy Fountain has been completed, Pikango can be found painting in Lurelin Village. When spoken to, Pikango is able to identify the eighth Picture in Link's Album as the cloisters of Hyrule Castle. Excluding those used in the Treasure-Chest Game, a total of five Treasure Chests are hidden in Lurelin Village. The first in a metal Chest south of Yah Rin Shrine that can be found by befriending the local Hylian Retriever, and it contains a Star Fragment. The other four Treasure Chests are also made of metal, but they have been submerged in the Village's bay. In all, these Chests contain a bundle of five Fire Arrows, two Ambers, and one Purple Rupee. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzles can be found within Lurelin Village. It takes the form of an Archery Puzzle, marked by an Apple in the Palm Tree above Rozel and Numar's House on the western end of the Village. When Link shoots the Apple with an Arrow, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Areas Creatures Materials Equipment After a pirate attack, Lurelin Village is badly damaged, forcing its inhabitants to seek refuge elsewhere. Link later drives off the pirates and rebuilds the village with Bolson's help. Lurelin seems to have a lot of fishing related phrasing, as seen with Tauro. Areas Other Appearances

The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . Location and Uses The Merchant Boat is located at the end of the longest Dock in Lurelin Village. It is a General Store run by Mubs, focusing on selling Fish that can be found in the surrounding Necluda Sea. The Merchant Boat itself carries Mubs' supplies, including extra Armored Porgies and Mighty Porgies. There is also a Jar and Wooden Box at the end of the Dock, which can be broken for supplies. As Link approaches the Merchant Boat, Mubs advertises the price and quality of her wares. To buy an Item from the Merchant Boat, Link must stand in front of it and interact with it. When Link makes a purchase, Mubs will thank him for his business. If Link buys the entirety of Mubs' stock of an Item, she promises to procure more in the future. If Link stands on any of the products, Mubs will yell at him to stop. At the end of their conversations, Mubs invites Link to come back. Wares and Pricing After completing the "Village Attacked by Pirates" Side Quest and the "Lurelin Village Restoration Project" Side Adventure, Link can find Garini at an empty dock in Lurelin Village. He has lost his boat and cannot open his store. Once Link has brought him a new boat from Tenoko Island, Garini will be able to set up his shop. To thank Link for saving the village and helping restore it, Garini lets him have anything he wants from the store for free. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Luto's Crossing is a bridge that spans over the Zora River and Ruto Lake in the Lanayru Great Spring. It connects the path to Zora's Domain to Ruto Mountain. Prior to Divine Beast Vah Ruta being calmed, Rain will constantly fall over Luto's Crossing. When Link passes through Luto's Crossing during the "Reach Zora's Domain" Main Quest, Sidon will call out to him from Ruto Lake. He reveals that he has been waiting for Link, since he knew he would have to cross the bridge. Due to their proximity to Zora's Domain, Sidon decides to Swim ahead and meet Link there. However, their conversation is interrupted by a Blue Moblin attacking Link from behind, which Sidon warns him of. In Master Mode, wooden platforms suspended by Sky Octoroks will appear above Luto's Crossing. On one of this platforms is a Treasure Chest, which contains a Frostspear. Enemies Enemies

is a recurring character in . Biography Lyndae is a Goron traveler who can be found in Gerudo Town. At all hours of the day, he sits near the entrance to the Royal Palace, and he carries a Traveling Pack. Despite being a man, he has been allowed entry to Town. When Link speaks to Lyndae during the day, he incorrectly pronounces sav'otta as "sabotta", which is a Gerudo greeting meaning "good morning". Lyndae explains that one must really bite their lip to get the "V" sound out clearly. One of the Gerudo children made fun of him for not being able to get it right. No matter what he does, he feels that it sounds the same. At night, Lyndae will struggle to greet Link with "sav'saaba," which is the Gerudo word for "good evening." Lyndae feels that Gerudo words are hard to remember. He also remarks that Gerudo Town truly is full of women and that it smells nice. At this moment, Lyndae recalls the rule against allowing men into Gerudo Town, and he wonders why he was let in. After Link calms the Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Lyndae can be found sitting with Strade, a fellow Goron. When Link speaks to him, Lyndae is finally able to pronounce his greetings correctly. However, he still struggles with pronouncing "sav'saaba," instead saying "sav'saava" and "sab'saava." Lyndae also expresses how shy he felt being surrounded by women before Strade came to Gerudo Town. However, he admits that he still feels shy around Strade.

Lynels, also known as Fire Cats, are recurring Bosses, Enemies, and Sub-Bosses in . Described as "half man, half horse", they resemble a cross between Lions and centaurs. Characteristics Lynels appear in red and blue variations in , with the blue one dealing twice as much collision damage and taking 6 hits to kill instead of 4 with the wooded sword. They can be found around Death Mountain. Lynels fire beam projectiles at Link, which cannot be blocked with the Wooden Shield, only with the Magical Shield. When defeated, red Lynels may drop either a Heart, a Fairy or one Rupee, while blue Lynels may drop either a Heart, one Rupee, four Bombs or a Clock. Lynels appear on Death Mountain in where only 3 are found by the east bridge near Ganon's Tower. They shoot fireballs at Link, which can only be deflected with the Red and Mirror Shields. They can only be damaged with the Magic Hammer, Silver Arrows, a Spin Attack from the Master Sword, or an attack from any of its upgrades. Lynels appear in red and blue variations in . They also shoot fireballs at Link. A Golden Lynel appears in the Tarm Ruins during Winter after talking to the golden-robed Old Man. Defeating the Golden Lynel alongside the other Golden Monsters rewards Link with the Red Ring. Lynels appear in red and blue variations in . Lynels appear in two variations in , a white-maned type found on Death Mountain and a black variant with an orange mane that is found in the Treacherous Tower. They attack by breathing a long stream of fire that takes three hearts, which can only be blocked with the Hylian Shield. thumb|left|200px|Link using a Perfect Guard against a Lynel In , Lynels are a strong and intelligent type of Monster that have resided in Hyrule since ancient times. They come in five different variations: the standard red-maned Lynels, Blue-Maned Lynels, White-Maned Lynels, Silver Lynels, and the Master Mode exclusive Golden Lynels. Lynels exclusively use Weapons of the Lynel Gear equipment archetype, of which they are the sole source. The only exception to this is the Lynel encountered in the Coliseum Ruins, which carries a Flameblade when encountered as a Silver Lynel. They are capable of wielding Lynel Crushers and Lynel Spears with a single hand, despite them being two-handed Weapons when held by Link. They can also be equipped with Arrows, Fire Arrows, Ice Arrows, Shock Arrows, or Bomb Arrows. After spotting Link, Lynels will refrain from attacking and stare him down for 30 seconds, regardless of whether or not he is wearing the Lynel Mask or Majora's Mask. The Lynel on Ploymus Mountain is an exception to this, attacking Link as soon as it spots him if he is not wearing either of the aforementioned masks. This allows Link a chance to escape before the battle begins. While Link is in view during this time frame, the Lynel will begin to attack if he draws or swings

this, attacking Link as soon as it spots him if he is not wearing either of the aforementioned masks. This allows Link a chance to escape before the battle begins. While Link is in view during this time frame, the Lynel will begin to attack if he draws or swings a Weapon, aims a Bow, uses any Runes, or gets too close. Additionally, if they have no Weapon drawn, they will follow Link if he is far away. If a Lynel loses track of Link and spots him again, it will go back to staring him down for 30 seconds. However, this only happens if Link has not already engaged in battle with it. Lynels will begin to attack Link without a stare-down if they have taken damage from him, are struck or recoiled by a Shield, mounted, or attacked by Wolf Link. They only stop attacking once Link has left their vicinity. Lynels have a variety of attacks, both ranged and melee, such as shooting Fire balls, body slamming, dashing, and trampling. Lynels also have the ability to teleport, doing so to either briefly flee from battle or to give chase after Link. This teleportation is only used when they get stuck on uneven terrain or they are too far away from their territory. Link can perform a Perfect Dodge or a Perfect Guard on most of their attacks, leaving them vulnerable for counterattacks. He can also utilize the Updrafts created by their Fire attacks to Paraglide up and shoot at their head with a Bow, stunning them and inflicting double damage. Every kind of Lynel is resistant to all elemental attacks and the effects granted by them. The only exception to this is Urbosa's Fury, which does not abide by this rule. Unlike most Enemies, Lynels are unable to be knocked back when struct, not even with the Spring-Loaded Hammer. This also means that they never drop their Weapons until they are defeated. Link can temporarily Mount Lynels either by sneaking up from behind, jumping on while they are stunned, or using the Paraglider to drop onto them from above. They can also be mounted after they perform one of the two dashing attacks. The first is when they charge at Link, and the other is when they sprint towards Link followed by swinging their Weapon. This swinging attack takes the form of a horizontal strike with a One-Handed Weapon or smashing the ground with a Two-Handed Weapon. While mounted, Link can repeatedly attack the Lynel up to five times with any Weapon without it losing any Durability. If Link's Stamina runs out, though, he will be thrown off and lose a quarter of a Heart. Unlike the Creatures that Link can mount, Lynels cannot be soothed and tamed. Link can buy a Lynel Mask for 999 Mon from Kilton's Fang and Bone shop after completing three Divine Beasts. It can be used to disguise Link and temporarily avoid being attacked by Lynels. Majora's Mask can also be worn to deceive Lynels. These pieces of Armor will only work for a short amount of time, as the Lynel will eventually see through the disguise and attack Link. Drops Lynels reappear in , acting the same as they did in with minor exceptions. If Link runs out of Stamina and falls off a Lynel he mounted, he will be dealt its base damage rather than a quarter of a Heart. If Lynels happen to be next to any Zonai Devices or any Object created with Autobuild, they will destroy them by roaring. They are also immune to the effects of Dazzlefruits. In addition to attacking Link if he draws a Weapon at moderate range, Lynels will do so if he draws a Bow at any distance. Performing the Earthwake will also cause them to attack. If Link does not have a Bow equipped, Lynels will still attack him if he attempts to draw one while facing them. When angered like this, Lynels will skip their 30-second stare down state and proceed to attack. If Link is not on the ground when these 30 seconds pass, they will skip roaring and immediately start attacking via Arrows. ground when these 30 seconds pass, they will skip roaring and immediately start attacking via Arrows. If Link leaves the Floating Coliseum, the Lynels will stop attacking until he returns. Lynels are quadrupedal Monsters regarded as the most fearsome in all of Hyrule. They wield a Lynel Sword. One can be found in the Eternal Forest by following the hoof marks on the ground that start near the Waypoint in the center of the area. After it has been encountered once, it can be reencountered later without the need to follow the hoof prints. A dark version of a Lynel appears in Null's Body. When summoned as an Echo, they have an Echo cost of six, or five if Tri is Lv. 11. Their cost is the highest of any other Echo that Princess Zelda can summon. When an Enemy Lynel spots Zelda, it will start growling and then attack. Lynels attack by dashing followed by a swipe, using Spin Attacks, and a double slash. These attacks deal five Hearts of damage, although the double slash only deals two and a half Hearts. Lynels are also capable of jumping on top of Trees. Zelda cannot use Bind on them. Lynels cannot be frozen, set aflame, electrocuted, stunned by ReDead screams, or sent flying by Tornandoes. If they fall into Water deep enough to reach their heads, they will drown. are Items in . Location and Uses Lynel Bows are Bows used by regular Lynels, particularly in the Gerudo Highlands and Lanayru Great Spring. They become scarce as Lynels tier up. However, in Master Mode, Blue-Maned Lynels will use them instead, but they will still disappear with Blue-Maned Lynels. The only exception is the Lynel on Ploymus Mountain, which is always a regular Lynel. Therefore, it may become the only source of Lynel Bows in the world as the game goes on. Lynels make these Bows from rough metal. They can fire multiple Arrows at a time, most commonly three, but occasionally one can be found that fires five Arrows at once. Lynel Bows are part of the Lynel Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created and utilized by Lynels. They are known to reflect the vicious nature of Lynel Gear and are ideal for taking down fast-moving targets. Being made of metal, Lynel Bows conduct Electricity and will attract Lightning if equipped during a Thunderstorm. They will also sink if dropped in water, but can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, they do not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate.

They're heavier than horse hooves and can be used in a Cooking Pot with critters to make Elixirs. The Kochi Dye Shop also accepts Lynel Hooves as an ingredient for Black Dye, but they can also be exchanged for Mon at the Fang and Bone. The is a recurring Item} in . Location and Uses The Lynel Mask is a piece of Armor that can be purchased from Kilton at the Fang and Bone for 999 Mon shop after freeing three Divine Beasts. It cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy, nor can it be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. When worn, it grants Link the Disguise Added Effect, allowing him to blend in with Lynels, though they are smart enough to eventually see through his disguise and attack. The Lynel Mask does not prevent other Enemies in the same area from attacking Link. It also makes quiet Lynel sounds as Link moves around. While wearing the Lynel Mask, Link adopts a new idle pose to match that of a Lynel. The Lynel Mask returns in , functioning the same as it did in with the exception of the Lynels in the Floating Coliseum, as they are scripted to attack Link without provocation. It can be obtained from Koltin's Stall for four Bubbul Gems after trading a total of 33 Bubbul Gems for the prior rewards. Subsequent Lynel Masks can be purchased from Cece for 4000 Rupees. Other Appearances The Lynel Mask is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and is only obtained by completing the Quest "Mystery Meal for the Merchant". It was crafted by the Fang and Bone's owner.

are recurring Items in . Lynel Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Lynel Shields are Shields favored by Lynels for both their defensive and offensive capabilities. While they are primarily useful as Shields, their edges are capable of dealing slash attacks that do 7 damage while deflecting. They belong to the Lynel Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created by and for Lynels. Regular Lynels predominately use Lynel Shields, however Blue-Maned Lynels in Master Mode will use them instead. They can become scarce as Lynels tier up, but since the Lynel on Ploymus Mountain will always remain a regular Lynel, it will always be a source of Lynel Shields. Being made of metal, Lynel Shields will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms. They will also sink if they are dropped in water. However, they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune, and they will not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Lynel Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Lynel Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Lynel Swords.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mabe Prairie is located northeast of the Mabe Village Ruins in Hyrule Field. It is bordered by the Romani Plains and the Applean Forest to the north and the Sacred Ground Ruins to the west. Several remains of Fallen Guardians can be found throughout the Prairie, which can be searched for Ancient Materials. Creatures Enemies Materials Mabe Prairie features a nameless lake, which sits east of Lookout Landing. A number of Hyrule Restoration Materials can be found along the roads of the Prairie, though Fallen Debris now litter the field and Monster Outpost now plague the Prairie's roadside. Certain travelers can be seen crossing the roads of Mabe Prairie, such as the Goron Naddon and the Hylian Meeshy. Meeshy will divulge rumors about Misko's treasure in the local area, pointing to the Barbarian Armor in Crenel Peak Cave, the Climbing Gear in North Hyrule Plain Cave, and the Rubber Armor in the Whistling Hill Cave. She also tells Link about Great Fairy Tera, who may Enhance his Armor but is said to be hiding north of Woodland Stable. The traveling Hylian merchant Cormus can also be seen riding his Wagon. Beside the road west of Rebonae Bridge, Link can find Addison attempting to set up a Signboard for Hudson Construction. Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment Materials Treasure Chests Zonai Devices

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Mabe Village Ruins are located roughly in the center of Hyrule Field. They are the remains of Mabe Village, a trading hub prior to the second Great Calamity. As they were destroyed during the Great Calamity, the Ruined Houses in the Ruins are now devoid of life. They were likely the second settlement that was destroyed during the Great Calamity, following Hyrule Castle Town. Any possible survivors are speculated to have crossed Horwell Bridge and waded through Squabble River to retreat to Fort Hateno in the Necluda Region. The Mabe Village Ruins are bordered by Mabe Prairie to the northeast, the Ranch Ruins to the southeast, and Passeri Greenbelt to the west. Two Fallen Guardians can be seen in the Ruins. These can be searched for Ancient Materials. A broken Wagon that can be searched for Gems is situated at the southeastern edge of the Mabe Village Ruins. After the fall of Hyrule Kingdom, the bandit Misko stole Tingle's Tights from Hyrule Castle and hid them among the Mabe Village Ruins. In Downloadable Content pack, Misko's EX Journal details this event and hints the location of the stolen treasure. In the "EX Treasure: Fairy Clothes" Side Quest, Link can find and retrieve the Tights from a metallic EX Treasure Chest in the ground beneath the Fallen Guardian in the south of the Ruins. This Treasure Chest must be retrieved from the ground with the Magnesis Rune. Atop the keep on the western side of the Mabe Village Ruins, Link can find a stone Treasure Chest that contains a Silver Rupee. Another stone Treasure Chest containing a bundle of 10 Ice Arrows can be found in the Ruined House at the center of the Ruins. A third stone Treasure Chest containing a bundle of 10 regular Arrows sits beside the small pond at the southern portion of the Village Ruins. A dried well sits in the western portion of the Mabe Village Ruins, around which Link can find Barrels and metal crates. A single Korok Seed Puzzle is located in the Mabe Village Ruins. It takes the form of a Rock on the eastern side of the Ruins. When Link picks the Rock up, it will be revealed as a Natural Hiding Spot, and a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Equipment The Mabe Village Ruins remain uninhabited by Hylians in . Fallen Debris dots the outskirts of the Ruins, and the interior of the Mabe Village Ruins Well is now accessible. The rock on the east side of the Ruins has also cracked open, providing an entrance to the Ranch Ruins Cave. Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment Materials

The is a recurring location in . The Mabe Village Ruins Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Mabe Village Ruins Well is situated within the Mabe Village Ruins in Hyrule Field. It was part of Mabe Village 100 years before the events of , which was destroyed by Guardians during the Great Calamity. The Mabe Village Ruins Well returns in , and it is still part of the Mabe Village Ruins in Hyrule Field. Link is now able to enter the Well, where he will find a pool of Water and an abundance of Cave-exclusive Creatures.
