is a recurring character in . Biography Maca is a Korok that lives in the Korok Forest. He can be found outside the entrance to the Great Deku Tree's Navel, where he can provide Link with information about the Forest and Master Sword. As Link passes Maca, he will advertise their services. If Link asks about the Korok Forest, Maca proclaims that its highlights are the Great Deku Tree and the Pedestal of the Master Sword. He then quietly remarks that the Great Deku Tree likely is not happy to have been turned into a tourist trap. Maca explains that the Koroks decorated the Great Deku Tree's Navel for Link, including an Inn and General Stores. Moving on to the Pedestal of the Master Sword, Maca states that it is where the Master Sword rests. Since the Pedestal is located in the center of Korok Forest, Maca claims that standing on it will give one a sense of most of the paths located within. In addition to this, he informs Link that he can use the Bean Lamps to navigate the Korok Forest as well. Should Link ever find himself lost in the Korok Forest, Maca tells him to return to the Pedestal to reorient himself. Next, Link can ask Maca about the Master Sword. Maca tells Link that the Master Sword may lose power if overused, but it will regenerate over time. He suggests only using it for fighting evil, as opposed to trivial matters like opening bottles or cans. Should Link want to know more, Maca directs him to the Great Deku Tree. Finally, when Link asks about leaving the Korok Forest, Maca questions why he would want to leave such a perfect place. However, he then reveals that he is joking, and he understands that Link would need to leave the Forest to save Hyrule. Maca tells Link that past the Sign east of the Pedestal of the Master Sword, he will find an Ogre Tree. If Link enters its mouth, he will be taken back to the entrance to the Lost Woods. The Koroks set this up because they do not like traversing the Lost Woods. At this Ogre Tree, Link will find a Stone Tablet bearing a note from Maca, wherein he assures the reader that they will not be eaten by the Tree.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Madorna Mountain makes up the southern border of Mount Lanayru, and it is located directly to the west of the Lanayru Range. The Mountain has three peaks, upon each of which is a Cedar Tree. Ore Deposits and a Rare Ore Deposit can be found on its western end. The Mountain is part of a Freezing Climate, meaning Link needs to have at least two levels of Cold Resistance to avoid taking damage. At the beginning of the "Secret of the Cedars" Shrine Quest, Clavia points out the Cedar Trees on Madorna Mountain to Link, explaining that she found a note that says "When the three summit trees become one, turn your back to them and head toward the sea. A trial encased in stone awaits you there." Clavia suggests that Link attempt to follow the instructions himself, since she is unable to leave Hateno Village. When Link walks towards Afromsia Coast after lining up Madorna Mountain's Cedar Trees, he will find Tahno O'ah Shrine in a blocked off cave. left|40px There is one Korok Seed Puzzle on top of Madorna Mountain. It takes the form of a Race that starts on the Mountain's central peak. After reaching the end of the Race on the western peak, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Magda is a Hylian who resides on the Floret Sandbar. Magda planted a maze of Flowers surrounding the Hila Rao Shrine, where she regularly tends to them. Because of her investment in her garden, she becomes upset if people step on or harm the Flowers. When Link first speaks to Magda, she proclaims that she is pleased with how the Ancient Shrine looks now, and while she welcomes him to look at the Flowers, she also warns him to be careful not to step on them. If Link steps on the Flowers before interacting with Magda, she will yell at him to stop. She then explains that she was the one who planted the Flowers, and she tells him to be careful not to cause them harm. After either of these exchanges, the "Watch Out for the Flowers" Shrine Quest will begin. The first time Link steps on the Flowers, Magda will be angered, saying that they are screaming in pain. If Link disrupts the Flowers a second time, she will yell at him to treat them carefully, as they are living beings. If he does so a third time, Magda will become despondent, saying that she has told him to stop so many times that she has lost count. She cannot comprehend how Link does not understand. Suddenly, she shouts in anger before taking off. While running through her garden, Magda rants at Link about his trespasses before falling on her face. She then resolves to make Link understand the "flowers' rage," at which point she attacks him. When Magda attacks Link, she will remove three of his Hearts. Her attack him will leave him with a minimum of a quarter of a Heart. If Link has less than three Hearts when she attacks, she will not cause any damage to him, instead knocking him out. Following this, the process of angering Magda will start over. After Hila Rao Shrine has been activated, Magda will notice that it has changed in color, believing this to be because it is pleased with her Flowers. When spoken to again, she will ask if he has been stepping on the Flowers recently. Magda is recruited by Princess Zelda to help restore the flowers on the Floret Sandbar. To this end, Magda and Princess Zelda borrowed several farming tools from Izra at the nearby Wetland Stable; however, Princess Zelda went missing during the Upheaval and the farming tools were never returned. Izra, accompanied by Link, travels down the Hylia River in search of the missing tools, and learns the truth from Magda, who has continued tending to the flowers in the princess's absence. Izra is satisfied knowing the tools are still being utilized, but accidentally volunteers himself to assist Magda, who forcibly puts him to work. Should Link step on or otherwise damage Magda's flowers after this point, she will chide him, quoting what she believes the flowers would say in increasingly desperate and aggressive ways;

knowing the tools are still being utilized, but accidentally volunteers himself to assist Magda, who forcibly puts him to work. Should Link step on or otherwise damage Magda's flowers after this point, she will chide him, quoting what she believes the flowers would say in increasingly desperate and aggressive ways; however, she will no longer attack him.

, also known as , are recurring Items in . Location and Uses In , the Magical Rod allows Link to shoot projectile beams. The beams are similar to a Wizzrobe's and travel across the screen. According to the game manual, it is the same wand that Wizzrobes use to attack. In the first quest, the Magical Rod is found in Level 6. In the Second Quest, it is found in Level 8. The Book of Magic can be found to increase the power of the Magical Rod. After obtaining it, the Magical Rod's attack leaves a fiery blaze, similarly to the Candle, when it makes contact with an enemy or wall. This also allows the Magical Rod to be used in lieu of the Candle to light up pitch dark rooms. In , the Magic Rod is used to expel blasts of magical energy in the form of fireballs, which can be used to burn Objects or Enemies. It is the main item of Turtle Rock. It is primarily used as a weapon and for lighting unreachable Braziers, as well as for melting Ice. The Magic Rod is vital to defeating the Dungeon's boss, Hot Head. The Magic Rod is one of the most powerful weapons in , doing twice as much damage as even the Koholint Sword. There are some enemies the Magic Rod does less damage against, or cannot damage at all, such as Crows, Takkuri, and Stalfos. The Magic Rod is also notable as the only item other than the Magic Powder that can kill a Cucco and a Mutt. Magic Rods are Weapons that were created by an ancient magician by awakening the latent power of Gems. Magic Rods normally act as a simple melee Weapon with low attack power, but by Fusing it with Gems such as Rubies the Magic Rod will take on the elemental properties associated with the Gem, and will do so more effectively than other Weapons that are Fused with Gems. Other Appearances The Magic Rod is a class of Weapon used by Link in . It is associated with Fire. It can shoot wide-ranged projectiles and conjure pillars of flames to juggle enemies. The Rod is also capable of changing shape, such as forming a flamethrower, transforming into a larger staff to emit flame-based energy beams, and transforming into a fiery battleaxe. An 8-Bit version of the Magical Rod from , called the 8-Bit Magical Rod?, appears as the Lv.★ form of Lana's Spear. It was added to the game with the Pack DLC in . , also known as , , and , are recurring traps in . Magma Bombs go unnamed in , , and . Characteristics In , Magma Bombs fall from the sky during volcanic eruptions on Death Mountain when Link is a child. When this happens, the ground will tremble and Magma Bombs will descend shortly after. There are two types of Magma Bombs that will fall: a series of sporadically-placed rocks and Magma Bombs which will fall directly onto Link. These can be deflected by using any Shield. During the battle with Onox, he will shake the room so that a barrage of Falling Rocks will fall and harm Link. In , Magma Bombs fall from the sky during Link's first visit to Death Mountain, including the Molten Shard. They can be avoided by looking at their shadows to see where they will land and by listening for the whistling sound they make as they approach the ground. Magma Bombs tend to explode when making contact with the ground. Once Link has quelled Fyrus's rage in the Goron Mines, the Magma Bombs will stop falling permanently. In , Falling Rocks fly out of the active volcano in the Isle of Ember. Link must avoid them while climbing to its summit in order to enter the Temple of Fire. In , when visiting the Fire Realm for the first time, Magma Bombs fall around and on the Spirit Tracks. Link must use the Cannon in order to blast them out of the rails. When Link arrives to Goron Village, he finds out that several paths are blocked by the debris. Link must then get Mega Ice to the Village in order to open these paths. On his way to the Fire Sanctuary, Link must avoid more Magma Bombs. Cragma, the Boss of the Fire Temple, also uses Magma Bombs as one of its attacks. In , a volcanic eruption takes place when Link first arrives at Hyrule's Death Mountain, causing Great Balls of Fire to continually rain down around Link. Occasionally, a Great Ball of Fire will burst into several Green Rupees when it smashes into the ground, while sometimes it will spawn a Deadrock instead. Great Balls of Fire will no longer threaten Link once he reaches the summit of Death Mountain, but will resume falling if he returns to the Mountain's lower portions. In , Volcanic Rocks only appear in the third stage of Blazing Trail and during the "Avoid the volcanic rocks!" Drablands Challenge in the Den of Flames and the Dragon Citadel. The Links must avoid the falling rocks while traversing these Levels; being hit by one will burn them as well as causing damage. In , Magma Bombs fall from Death Mountain and explode around the Eldin Region. This is caused by the rampaging of the corrupted Divine Beast Vah Rudania. Due to the Magma Bombs, a rock slide seals the entrance to the vault where Bludo's painkillers are kept, trapping Yunobo inside. Once Rudania is

Magma Bombs fall from Death Mountain and explode around the Eldin Region. This is caused by the rampaging of the corrupted Divine Beast Vah Rudania. Due to the Magma Bombs, a rock slide seals the entrance to the vault where Bludo's painkillers are kept, trapping Yunobo inside. Once Rudania is freed from Calamity Ganon's corruption, the Magma Bombs stop. Magma Bombs are fired at Link by Moragia on Death Mountain in . is a character in . Biography Maheli is one of two Koroks that can be found between the Great Deku Tree's roots and an Ascend Access Point in Korok Grove during the "Trail of the Master Sword" Main Quest, the other being Jatora. Originally, the pair left Korok Forest with Tasho, Mopu, Nako, Mokka, and Raha to take a walk. When they found that they were unable to return through the Lost Woods, they instead descended through the Minshi Woods Chasm to try and find a way back from the Depths. Initially, they can be seen humming to themself as they think. When Link speaks to Maheli, they explain that they cannot figure out how to reach the Surface from their current position. They theorize that by jumping very high, one would be able to reach Korok Forest, but it would still be impossible to pass through the ceiling.

is a recurring character in . Biography Maike is a Gerudo merchant who runs a General Store in the Kara Kara Bazaar. She sells Monster Parts and Roasted Food. If Link speaks to Maike during the day, she will attempt to say "good morning" in the Hylian language, and she explains that the appropriate word in the Gerudo is sav'otta. At night, she will try to say "good evening" in Hylian, and she likewise explains that the Gerudo say sav'sabba instead. She also incorrectly says "welcome" as "well come" and explains that they say vasaaq in Gerudo. Maike reveals that her younger sister, Estan, runs a butcher shop Stall in Gerudo Town, and that her should visit her since she knows Hylian well. However, Maike quickly realizes that as a man, Link would not be allowed to enter Gerudo Town to do so. During the "Forbidden City Entry" Main Quest, Link can ask Maike if she has seen anyone suspicious in Kara Kara Bazaar. Maike will be unable to recall someone of that description, and since she spends all her time at her General Store, she is unsure how she would be able to spot a Merchant. She suggests that Link ask one of the Hylian Merchants who are camping at Kara Kara Bazaar instead. If Link walks near her wearing the Gerudo Outfit she will remark that the outfit suits him. When Link speaks to her, she will again tell him about Estan. Maike calls Estan cute, and she encourages Link to say hello to her. When Link buys Maike's wares, she will attempt to thank him in a way that would be familiar to Hylians. If Link speaks to her after buying all of her stock, Maike will thank him for shopping. Like other proprietors of General Stores, Link can sell his own Items to Maike. When Link does so, she will be appreciative of whatever she buys from him. Afterwards, she invites him to come back in the future.

are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Main Quests are a variety of quest accessed from the Adventure Log. Most are related to the main story of , though only three, ("Follow the Sheikah Slate", "The Isolated Plateau", and "Destroy Ganon") are actually require completion to beat the game. Main Quests are generally longer and more extensive than Side or Shrine Quests. There are 15 Main Quests in the base game, with an additional five added in Downloadable Content pack, for a total of 20. Main Quests return in , functioning the same as in . Main Quests are Quests with a larger scale than Side Quests, that relate to progression of the game's main story. There are a total of eighteen Main Quests.

is a recurring Item, Object, and Boss in . Location and Uses Majora's Mask serves as the main villain that Link must stop and defeat within the game of same name, rather than Ganon. It is first introduced after the Happy Mask Salesman removes the curse that was placed on Link by Skull Kid. The Happy Mask Salesman explains that Majora's Mask is an ancient, powerful artifact that was used by an ancient tribe for its bewitching rituals, but Majora's Mask's wicked power became so great that it was sealed away to prevent a great catastrophe. However, since the ancient tribe vanished, no one accurately knows the true nature of its power. The Happy Mask Salesman fears the great devastation that could befall Termina if Majora's Mask is not quickly taken back from the Skull Kid. When the Skull Kid donned Majora's Mask, it transformed a world into the land of Termina out of a combination of the evil within the Mask and the Skull Kid's memories and delusions. For the vast majority of the game, the Majora's Mask is worn by Skull Kid on the Clock Tower, drawing the Moon to Termina. Although the Skull Kid is unaware, Majora's Mask is gradually beginning to take complete control of his mind, with his once harmless pranks becoming malicious acts of pure evil. Prior to the game's events, Skull Kid used the power of Majora's Mask to prank and curse others around him, such as Kafei. After the Guardian Deities are called, Majora's Mask abandons Skull Kid and enters the Moon so that it can push it through the Guardian Deities' blockade and complete its destructive path. Link then proceeds to follow Majora's Mask into the Moon. Once inside, he finds four Moon Children wearing the Boss remains and one lonely child under a Tree wearing Majora's Mask itself. If Link gives all his non-transformation Masks to the four children, the child wearing Majora's Mask will give him the Fierce Deity's Mask. He will then take Link to the Final Boss room. It will come in three increasingly powerful forms, the mask itself, Majora's Incarnation and Majora's Wrath. After the young hero and Tatl defeat Majora's Mask in a clashing battle, they return to the land of Termina where the Happy Mask Salesman informs them that the evil inside the Mask has disappeared for good. Majora's Mask is last seen as the Happy Mask Salesman departs with it in his hands. In the bad ending of the game, Majora's Mask can be seen for a brief moment before the screen fades to black. An image of Majora's Mask appears on Floor Switches, Shock Switches, and Blocks, replacing the Crest of the Gerudo from . is a recurring character in . Biography Makure is a Gerudo child who lives in Gerudo Town. She resides at the Arrow Specialty Shop Stall, which is run by her grandmother, Danda. During the day, Makure runs around near the Arrow Specialty Shop. When Link speaks to her, she is surprised that someone is visiting Gerudo Town. She then explains that she was pretending to be a Horse. If Link asks why, she questions if he knows about "Horsey Fatback". She explains that "Horsey Fatback" is a huge animal that walks around the Gerudo Desert, referring to the Divine Beast Vah Naboris. She then comments that if you get close, it makes loud sounds like "BZZBZZ," referring to the power of Lightning that Naboris possesses. Makure believes that the Divine Beast is good, saying that he is only in a bad mood because others believe he is bad. Makure can sometimes he found looking out at the Gerudo Desert from the steps of the Royal Palace, stomping and claiming that she can see Divine Beast Vah Naboris. While she sleeps at the Arrow Specialty Shop, she dreams of stomping. In the evenings, Makure will gather with the other three children who reside in Gerudo Town. These are her sister Kalani, Pearle, and Dalia. After completing the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Dalia will be late to their meetings. During this time, Kalani asks the other two if they heard what happened to Dalia's crops. Makure notes that, since then, Dalia has not stopped crying. Pearle proclaims that she will never forgive the person who wronged Dalia. Once all four children are present, Kalani will ask them if they are in love. Makure then responds that she wants to attend Ashai's class when she grows up, that way she can fall in love and get married. Pearle then comments that, according to her mother, Ashai herself is unmarried, and she wonders what that means. Lastly, Dalia says that she heard being in love is the sweetest thing in the world, but does not think she can handle something sweeter than berries. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Makure will be sad that the Divine Beast has left the Gerudo Desert. She blames the people of Gerudo Town for making it leave, since they always said it was bad. While standing on the steps of the Royal Palace, Makure will be able to see Divine Beast Vah Naboris on Spectacle Rock, and she wonders if it has finished stomping. During "The Undefeated Champ" Shrine Quest, Makure can be seen among the crowd gathering at the Southeast Gate as Shabonne announces the Sand-Seal Race.

is a recurring character in . Biography Malanya is the god who watches over the Horses of the world. He makes his home in the Faron Region in Malanya Spring, near the Lake of the Horse God. While he has a strange sense of humor about reviving Horses, he will not harm those who truly care for them. When first visited, Malanya is found trapped inside the bud of his Spring. He begs Link to listen to his story. If Link agrees, Malanya introduces himself and asks if he has ever lost one of his Horses. Malanya claims that if his power is restored, he will be able to help Link. In order to regain his power, Malanya requires 1,000 Rupees. His hand will appear from inside the bud, and he will ask Link to hand over his Rupees. If Link agrees to the payment, Malanya will thank him. Malanya Spring will then open, and Malanya's power will be restored. Malanya himself then emerges from the Water, and he remarks on how free he feels. He recognizes Link as the one who set him free. Malanya then properly introduces himself to Link, explaining he presides over the Horses of the world. Since Link helped, Malanya believes he should grant Link a reward. Malanya considers eating him for a meal, which causes Link to take on a defensive stance. However, Malanya reveals that he is joking. Malanya explains that if one of Link's Horses is killed, he will be able to revive it. This only works on Horses that have been registered at a Stable. He warns Link that if he believes the Horse's death was by his own hands, he will be subject to his wrath. Claiming to be joking once again, Malanya takes a look at Link's Horses. On subsequent visits to Malanya Spring, Malanya will recognize Link when he emerges from the Water. He asks Link why he has returned, and he takes a look at Link's Horses to ensure their wellbeing. Should Link not have any dead Horses, Malanya claims that all seems well. If Link has a high bond with one of his Horses, Malanya notes that they have an extraordinary friendship. He reminds Link that his Horses care for him, just as he does for them. Alternatively, if Link does not have any Horses registered when he speaks to Malanya, he will be shocked. Malanya cannot imagine going through life without a Horse, but he supposes this is how Link lives his life. He is unable to do anything to help those who have decided to avoid Horses. However, if Link ever does befriend a Horse that later dies, Malanya tells him to come see him. If one of Link's Horses has died, Malanya will be able to tell. In anger, he threatens to end Link. He quickly calms down, revealing this to be another joke, and he asks Link if he would like the Horse to be revived. If Link agrees, Malanya will ask

him. If one of Link's Horses has died, Malanya will be able to tell. In anger, he threatens to end Link. He quickly calms down, revealing this to be another joke, and he asks Link if he would like the Horse to be revived. If Link agrees, Malanya will ask him to choose among his deceased Horses. Depending on how Link's Horse died, Malanya will have differing reactions to Link's request. If Link's Horse died to a Guardian, Malanya will be moved by how well it served its master. However, Malanya becomes angry that Link was not able to control his Horse well enough to save its life. Malanya then claims to be joking, and he asks Link if he is certain he wants to revive this Horse. If Link's Horse died due to an explosion, Malanya will be saddened by its manner of death. While he does not want to cast unwarranted doubt on Link, he wonders if he actually killed his Horse. However, Malanya decides this could not be, and he asks Link again if he wants to revive the Horse. If Link's Horse was killed by him, Malanya will be shocked. He asks Link if he only wants to revive his Horse so he can kill it again, and he accuses Link of thinking of Horses only as tools that can be discarded. Malanya claims that if he were a Horse, he would kick Link in the chest. After claiming to be joking again, Malanya asserts that Link likely struck his Horse on accident, and he asks for confirmation that Link would like to revive his "temporarily betrayed" friend. If Link's Horse died in any other manner, Malanya will call it an accident, which he assures Link happen sometimes. He claims that the Horse knows that its death was not Link's intention, and he asks Link if he is certain that this is the Horse he wants to revive. When Link once again confirms his decision to revive his Horse, Malanya will then attempt to bring it back. He will then wave his hands in the air and spin his head, after which the selected Horse will appear nearby. After this, Malanya proclaims that he was successful in reviving the Horse. In the future, Malanya reminds Link to take good care of his Horses, as they are supposed to be partners. He warns Link that he will regret it if he is careless with them. Malanya claims that he is only joking for now. At the end of their conversation, Malanya will collapse and fall back into his Spring. When Link makes another visit to Malanya Spring, Malanya will be shocked that he has come back to revive another Horse. He explains that he only helped Link for free the first time due to the fact that he freed him, but he is too busy to always be available to him. However, Malanya reveals that if Link were to bring him something, he would continue to revive

revive another Horse. He explains that he only helped Link for free the first time due to the fact that he freed him, but he is too busy to always be available to him. However, Malanya reveals that if Link were to bring him something, he would continue to revive his Horses. At Link's confusion, Malanya reveals that he needs Endura Carrots, which he has only eaten once. When Link hands over an Endura Carrot, Malanya will agree to revive one of his Horses. After the Upheaval, Malanya has relocated his Spring to Akkala, on a peninsula within Bloodleaf Lake near East Akkala Stable. Initially, he will stay inside Malanya Spring, but he will leave when Link gives him an Endura Carrot. After receiving the Endura Carrot, Malanya will grant Horse-related wishes for Link in exchange for food. In addition to resurrecting dead Horses in exchange for a Roasted Endura Carrot, Malanya now offers to enhance a Horse's stats if given certain Meals. However, he cannot enhance the stats of Epona, the Giant Horse, or Giant White Stallion, claiming it does not want their abilities enhanced. Each trait can be upgraded to five stars at maximum, at which point Malanya claims the Horse will become too powerful if he continues. Malanya is also featured on the Horse-God Fabric, unlocked at five Pony Points. He also delivers messages to those who sleep in a Malanya Bed, unlocked at seven Pony Points. Upgrades Malanya will accept Meals regardless of their specific ingredients or whether they grant any Added Effects. Other Appearances In , Malanya appears in one variation of the Great Fairies' Weak Point Smash, where he summons an army of Horses to trample the enemy. In the "Shimmering Horseshoe" Quest, it is revealed he joined the battle at the request of the four sisters, and receives a horseshoe pendant as an offering in return. He is also mentioned in the "Lushify the Spring" Quest as appearing pleased by having more visitors due to added plants around the Great Fairy Fountains.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Malanya Spring is a Great Fairy Fountain located east of the Horse God Bridge in the Faron Grasslands. It is surrounded on most sides by Ibara Butte. A shallow pond can also be found on the Spring's edges, which contains Lily Pads. When Link first finds Malanya Spring, it will have shriveled up into a bud. Malanya's voice can be heard from inside, asking Link to listen to his story. If Link agrees, Malanya explains that he can help with the pain of losing a Horse companion, but he needs 1,000 Rupees to restore his power. Should Link give the Rupees to Malanya, the Spring will bloom. From then on, Link can visit Malanya Spring in order to revive deceased Horses. During the "EX Ancient Horse Rumors" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link reads the Super Rumor Mill V3 and learns that the Ancient Bridle can be found at a Spring "where a horse spirit resides". Subsequently, Link can find a Hidden Chest submerged in the Water near Malanya Spring, which he can pull to the surface with Magnesis to receive the Ancient Bridle. Creatures Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Malena is a Gerudo who can be found in Gerudo Town. During the night, she enters the Barracks, where she will beg the Gerudo soldiers to help her. At night, she sleeps at the Hotel Oasis, whispering in her sleep about a cure. Malena is originally from Gerudo Town, but she left after marrying her husband, Platt. With their marriage, Malena believed that she had finally found happiness. However, he soon became sick with a rare disease. After discovering that he could be cured with Molduga Guts, she returned to Gerudo Town to ask for help, since she would never be able to defeat a Molduga by herself. When Link speaks to Malena, she explains her plight to him. When she asked the Gerudo Soldiers for help, they denied her. Malena does not blame them for avoiding a beast as dangerous as a Molduga, and she theorizes it would be foolish to expect others to help a stranger in need. She is disappointed that she has been forced to return to Gerudo Town because of her circumstances. If Link ends their conversation at this point, she shares that Molduga live in areas of extreme Heat, which even the Gerudo cannot stand without the proper gear. Malena warns Link to be careful if he travels to those areas. If Link asks about Molduga, Malena explains that it is a Monster so savage that even other Monsters do not go near it. She mentions that one can be found in the Toruma Dunes and at the Southern Oasis. She comments that Molduga are sensitive to vibrations, and they will attack anything that approaches them. Unable to approach it or use someone as bait, she wonders what she is supposed to do. After speaking to her, the "Medicinal Molduga" Side Quest will begin. When Link speaks to Malena again, she repeats her assertion that no one would face a dangerous Monster like the Molduga on her behalf. However, she states that Molduga Guts are the only thing that is capable of curing Platt, and she refuses to give up on him. After obtaining Molduga Guts, Link can return to Malena, who will recall that Platt was the first man who ever called her beautiful. Due to how much she loves him, she needs Molduga Guts to cure him, but she laments that she cannot obtain them on her own. Malena is worried that she is running out of time to save her husband. Link can then offer his Molduga Guts to her, which she is surprised by. When Link confirms he is giving them to her, she becomes overjoyed and thanks him. As a reward, she gives Link a Gold Rupee. Now that she has Molduga Guts, Malena cries that she will be able to save Platt. Malena then begins to walk away, and the Side Quest is completed. As she is leaving, Malena will again thank Link for providing her with her husband's cure if

gives Link a Gold Rupee. Now that she has Molduga Guts, Malena cries that she will be able to save Platt. Malena then begins to walk away, and the Side Quest is completed. As she is leaving, Malena will again thank Link for providing her with her husband's cure if he talks to her. She reveals that she is preparing to return to him as soon as possible. Malena then realizes that she never learned Link's name. If Link responds that he is just a traveler, she compliments him for his modesty, and she hopes that she can someday raise a daughter to be like him. If Link shares his name, she mentions that it sounds like a man's name. She then tells Link that she might name her daughter after him, should she ever. She again thanks Link for his assistance, claiming she will never forget him. After completing "Medicinal Molduga," Malena temporarily returns to Hotel Oasis. When Link next leaves Gerudo Town, she will disappear, and she can never be encountered again from this point on.

is a recurring character in . Biography Manny is a man who resides alone in Hateno Village, often spending his days people-watching in front of The Great Ton Pu Inn. At night, he stands in front of the door to his house. When Link first approaches to Manny, he will find him mumbling to himself. If spoken to, he explains that he is checking out the people who pass him by, which is what he does everyday. He then asks Link if he is staying at the Inn. Should Link respond that he has, Manny states that it makes no difference to him. Alternatively, if Link claims no to have done so, Manny will be confused. Whatever his response, Manny will declare that his loitering is actually a profession. If Link agrees his this, Manny will be pleased. If Link responds that this is weird, Manny calls him weird in response. Manny claims that Hateno Village has been peaceful lately, but he is aware that life outside the Village can be dangerous. Therefore, he says that he has put himself in charge of making sure no suspicious individuals come by, but he accidentally reveals that he is watching for "beauties." Should Link claim that this job sounds difficult, Manny will agree with him. However, if Link comments on his mistake, Manny will sigh. Either way, he claims that his actions can be explained by seeing Prima, the proprietor of The Great Ton Pu Inn. He then quietly remarks that she does not know who he is. Frustrated by this Manny decides to give her a gift. He asks Link if he knows what Prima would like, but he claims he is doing so on behalf of a friend of a friend. After he finishes speaking, the "A Gift for My Beloved" Side Quest will begin. Following this conversation, Link is able to ask Manny questions. If Link asks if he knows Prima, Manny scolds him for not referring to her casually, but he then inquires whether he has been to the Inn. He reveals that Prima serves as the clerk for The Great Ton Pu Inn. He then repeats his desire to give her a gift. If Link questions Manny's loitering, he defends himself, claiming that he is preventing suspicious people from entering Hateno Village. He believes that this is an important service for the Village. After talking to Prima, Link can return to Manny to share what he learned. While Manny is surprised, he is also jealous that Prima spoke to Link. He tries to be calm, but he then shouts and demands that Link tell him what she likes. When he learns that Prima supposedly wants 100 Restless Crickets, he remarks how coincidental it is, since he also loves Restless Crickets. However, he is concerned about catching 100 of them, so he asks Link to help him by collecting 10. Once Link has 10 Restless Crickets, he must return to give them to Manny. He quietly reveals that

Crickets, he remarks how coincidental it is, since he also loves Restless Crickets. However, he is concerned about catching 100 of them, so he asks Link to help him by collecting 10. Once Link has 10 Restless Crickets, he must return to give them to Manny. He quietly reveals that he has yet to catch a single Cricket. Manny then asks Link to hand over his Crickets. He is impressed that Link actually has them, as he thought he was being messed with. After confirming that there are 10 Restless Crickets, Manny gives Link a Silver Rupee. He resolves to catch the rest of the Restless Crickets, at which point he will use them to ask Prima on a date. With this, the Side Quest will be completed. Afterwards, Link will have more questions he can ask Manny. if Link asks Manny if he is still checking people out, he will stumble through his words, claiming he is looking out for beauties, tourists, and suspicious individuals. Since he mentioned beauties, he brings up Prima, claiming that no one else could be as beautiful as her. He also claims to have heard that Zelda was beautiful, as well, and while she may have been able to compare to Prima, he thinks this only speaks to how pretty they both are. Following these statements, Link can ask Manny about Zelda, and he is shocked that he does not know about her. He explains that she was "swallowed up" by the Great Calamity, and he attributes the peace in Hyrule Kingdom to her sacrifice. After hearing this, Link can ask him about the Great Calamity, and Manny wonders whether he has been sleeping in a cave for the past 100 years. He has heard that is was a serpent or a black fog, but since he never saw it himself, he tells Link to make inquiries about it with the older residents of Hateno Village. If Link speaks to Manny while carrying the Blue Flame, he recognizes it as Purah's and wonders how she is doing. Changing the subject, he brings up how many beautiful women reside in Hateno Village, bringing up Prima as an example. He claims that Purah herself was likely just as beautiful when she was younger.

Not to be confused with Dungeon Map, Mini-Map, or Map of Hyrule. are recurring Items in . They often show detailed representations of places Link can explore. There are mainly World and Dungeon Maps used for exploring their respective areas, but certain Maps exist that serve other purposes. Location and Uses left|50px|Link's Map icon in Maps are obviously used for navigation, but their uses have become increasingly elaborate as The Legend of Zelda series has progressed. They have been used in every game with the exception of and . Maps detail the layout of the Overworld or a Dungeon and often show Link's current location. As with Dungeon Maps, World Maps are often blank until an area is explored or a full Map of an area is obtained. In many Legend of Zelda titles, Maps can only be viewed on a subscreen, but in , a very simplistic mini-map could be viewed in the HUD. This is similar to the Map used during gameplay of . The mini-map mechanic did not return until , in which it only shows the area Link is currently traveling and his position in accordance to the Map, as well as where he entered from. The mini-map returned in every console title until . and displayed Maps on the top screen of the Nintendo DS with the ability to move them to the touchscreen to write notes and draw paths. Despite their similarities, World Maps and Dungeon Maps often have distinct differences. World Map Full World Maps have been available during gameplay since . Oftentimes, key locations will be marked on World Maps, such as Towns and Link’s next destination. In and every game since , it often possible to magnify an area of the World Map to get a keener look at the layout. When Warping is possible, some of the titles in the series would display the World Map to show where Link can warp to. The World Map is not always used only for navigation; in and , the World Map is used for selecting different stages. The World Map of allowed Link to place light Beacons to guide the way to a chosen destination. There are diverse methods of obtaining and using World Maps throughout the series. Dungeon Map left Dungeon Maps are found in Treasure Chests inside Dungeons. Once obtained, a Dungeon Map will allow Link to see every room of every floor in the Dungeon it was found in.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Marari-in Shrine is located at the back of the Eventide Island Cave in the Necluda Sea. It corresponds with the Ni-iraram Lightroot in the Depths. Initially, the Shrine of Light's entrance will be blocked by bars. After Link defeats the Monster Forces occupying the Eventide Island Cave during the "Seeking the Pirate Hideout" Side Quest, the bars will disappear, allowing him to access the Shrine. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Marari-in Shrine The Marari-in Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Marari-in Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

Marbled Gohmas are Bosses in . Characteristics Marbled Gohmas are four-legged, insectoid Monsters that are protected by rocky armor. Their Legs are covered in the Gloom Rocks that Marbled Rock Roast is mined from. Like all Gohmas, they have a single Eye that acts as their weakness. One Marbled Gohma created and spread Marbled Rock Roasts throughout the Eldin Region. After this Marbled Gohma is defeated in the Fire Temple, three Marbled Gohmas can be fought in Boss Rematches throughout the Depths. The first is east of the Takaruk Lightroot in the Necluda Sea Depths, the second is east of the Uasnoj Lightroot in the Lanayru Wetlands Depths, and the final one is near the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm in the Gerudo Highlands Depths. If Marbled Gohma is not defeated in the Fire Temple, Link fights it at Gloom's Origin during the War in the Depths of Hyrule. It appears after Colgera and before Mucktorok. When defeated at Boss Rematches in the Depths, Marbled Gohmas drop a Marbled Gohma Leg and unlock a Treasure Chest containing a Huge Crystallized Charge. Marbled Gohmas attack primarily by flinging explosive Gloom Rocks at Link, which can be destroyed by Yunobo's Power of Fire before they detonate. If Link is sufficiently close, Marbled Gohmas will try to stomp on him, which will also produce a small shockwave. As their Eyes are too high up for Link to reach and are protected from Arrows, Link must use Yunobo's Power of Fire to break their Legs. After breaking any two Legs, they will collapse to the ground, letting Link climb up their body to hit their Eyes. Alternatively, Link may use his Ascend ability to travel through their bodies, or use Recall on the Gloom Rocks to stun them with the explosion. Link must be sure to retreat when the bodies of Marbled Gohmas begin to shake, as he will otherwise take damage as they throw him off. At half health, Marbled Gohmas will try to cage Link with their Gloom Rocks, preventing him from outrunning the blasts and ensuring that he will take damage if he does not use Yunobo's Power of Fire in time. In the Fire Temple, when at half health, the Marbled Gohma will cling to the ceiling and attack from above. While it can now be knocked down by breaking only one Leg, its position means that Link must angle Yunobo so he rolls up the walls and into a Leg in order to create an opening for attack. He must then repeat the process of hitting its eye until it is defeated.

Before it was destroyed, the Maritta Exchange was the hub of trade between inhabitants of the Hebra and Tabantha regions to the west, and those of Hyrule to the east. The Maritta Exchange Ruins Well is located within the Ruins' southern corner, and a large Monster Stronghold also stands at their center. Areas Enemies The Maritta Exchange Ruins return in . The is a recurring location in . The Maritta Exchange Ruins Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Maritta Exchange Ruins Well is located among the Maritta Exchange Ruins in Hyrule Field. Prior to the Great Calamity, which occurred 100 years before the events of , it was part of the Maritta Exchange. In , the Maritta Exchange Ruins Well returns, still being situated in Hyrule Field. It now features an interior that Link is able to access. However, its entrance is initially blocked by brown Hard Sediment, which can be easily broken. is a recurring character in . Biography Marot is a young Zora woman who resides in Zora's Domain. She is the proprietor of Marot Mart, which includes the Coral Reef General Store and the Hammerhead. The latter of those businesses is operated by her grandfather, Dento. As Link passes by Marot, she will welcome him to Marot Mart. When he speaks to her, she will explain the services that Marot Mart provides. After this introduction, she will ask if there is something else that Link needs. If Link asks about Marot Mart, Marot claims that it refers to the combination of the Coral Reef and the Hammerhead. She then proceeds to sing the jingle for Marot Mart, which she considers to be cute. Should Link ask about Marot Mart a second time, she will repeat the theme song for him. If asked about the Coral Reef, Marot informs him that is has been in business for more than 100 years. She describes its proprietor, Cleff, as a serious individual, but she is amused that his sister Tona is in love with Sidon. Finally, if Link inquires about the Hammerhead, Marot reveals that her grandfather is in charge of it. She claims that he was responsible for fixing the Lightscale Trident, which once belonged to Mipha.

is a recurring character in . Biography Marta is a Gerudo Soldier who can be found in the Barracks of Gerudo Town. She wields a Gerudo Spear. When Link first enters the Barracks, he will find Marta training with a practice dummy alongside Smaude. If Link speaks to her, she reveals that this training was instigated by Babi, who is watching the two of them. However, since the Yiga thieves were able to slip past her and steal the Thunder Helm, she does not feel like she can complain. After Link receives Teake's permission to learn about the theft from the soldiers, Babi refuses to allow him to speak to Marta and Smaude, claiming they are in the middle of training. After Link has recovered the Thunder Helm, Marta will be relieved that they can finally take a break. However, she expresses concern that Babi has special training ready for them after they repair their Gerudo Spears. Marta also feels that Babi is working too hard, and she hopes that she never becomes as intense as her.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Martha's Landing is located between the Faron Grasslands, the Faron Sea, the Necluda Sea, East Necluda, and West Necluda. The Komo Shoreline sits to the west of Martha's Landing and the Aris Beach sits to the east. It is a long, irregular shaped beach with many Palm Trees. A fork from the Faron Highroad ends in the northern part of the Landing, and the entrance to the beach is marked by a natural stone archway. A nonfunctional Guardian sits along the shore, which Link can search to obtain Ancient Materials. On the eastern edge of Martha's Landing, there is a small section of beach that extends into the Water. In the middle of this section, a Stone Talus sits embedded in the ground, but it will emerge if Link approaches it. Far up in the middle of the beach near the cliffs, a metallic Treasure Chest containing a bundle of five Fire Arrows is buried in the sand. Link can pull this Chest from the ground using the Magnesis Rune. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle is located on Martha's Landing. Next to the aforementioned Stone Talus, an incomplete Rock Pattern can be found. When Link fills in the missing Rock, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed as a reward. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring location in . Master Kohga's Room goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Master Kohga's Room is located at the back of the Yiga Clan Hideout in the Gerudo Highlands. The Room has two entrances, the first being accessible through the Yiga Clan Hideout Hall. The second entrance is a false wall made of metal that leads to the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm. Link must use the Magnesis Rune in order to open it. Several Traveler's Guardian Deities which have been covered with the crest of the Yiga are posed throughout the Room. During the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, a Yiga Blademaster will stand guard at the front entrance to Master Kohga's Room. To bypass the Blademaster, Link can either lure them away using Mighty Bananas or fight them. However, this is rather difficult since the Blademaster will whistle for backup and is able to kill Link in one hit. Afterwards, Link passes through Master Kohga's Room in order to reach the giant pit. When Link returns to the Yiga Clan Hideout during the "EX Champion Urbosa's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, the Hideout's front entrance will be blocked off. As a result, he must use the outdoor entrance into Master Kohga's Room in order to infiltrate the Hideout. Just outside the Room, Link can encounter Mina and Mils, who warn him that the Yiga have returned to their Hideout. After obtaining the Sacred Orb, Link must once again pass through Master Kohga's Room to throw it into the Chasm in order to reveal an Ancient Shrine. Equipment Treasure Chests In , Master Kohga's Room has been repurposed as a storage room for the Yiga Clan Hideout. While wearing the Yiga Clan Attire, Link can speak to the Yiga Footsoldiers and Yiga Blademaster in the Room, who are part of the Distribution Division. If Master Kohga has been defeated, the Blademaster will tell Link to ignore any such rumors.

is a recurring character and Boss in . Characteristics Master Kohga is the leader of the Yiga Clan, an opposing Clan to the Sheikah who hunt Link on a ceaseless mission. Master Kohga is a respected figure of authority, but he spends most of his time napping and loafing around. He loves Mighty Bananas the most. Master Kohga is known to possess many secrets about the Sheikah. Link meets Master Kohga during the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest outside of the exit of the Yiga Clan Hideout, near the edge of the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm. Initially, he berates Link for invading his napping spot. However, Master Kohga will then recognize the Sheikah Slate he is carrying, which causes him to realize that Link is the hero he has been looking for. He comments on his luck, as Link wandered right into the Yiga Clan Hideout while all of his scouts are looking for him. Master Kohga introduces himself to Link, and he tells him to prepare himself before he attacks. The fight against Master Kohga consists of three phases, each of which utilizes his control over magnetism and levitation. In the first phase, Master Kohga conjures up a rock above him to hurl at Link. Striking Master Kohga from afar as he levitates in the air, such as with a Bow, Remote Bomb or thrown Weapon, will break his focus and cause the rock to fall on his head. This temporarily stuns Master Kohga, partially burying him in the ground and allowing Link to attack him unopposed. In the second phase, he levitates above the large pit nearby and conjures up two rocks that spin around him. Link must hit Master Kohga when one of the rocks is directly above his head, causing it to once again fall on his head and stun him. In the third and final phase, he conjures up a fortified boulder to attempt to crush Link. Link must use Magnesis to gain control of the boulder and push it back towards Kohga. This will stun Kohga once again and give Link the opportunity to finish the fight. In all phases, he is protected by a blue shield which disappears when he goes offensive in the first two stages but remains permanently during the third. Ancient Arrows act like normal arrows when Master Kohga is hit with one, and he and his boulders cannot be stopped with Stasis at any time. He is the only notable Sheikah to display this, as even Monk Maz Koshia can be placed under Stasis. Master Kohga is also the only enemy that's immune to Urbosa's Fury, and takes only 10% of the normal damage done by any attack. After defeating Master Kohga, he will use his last bit of energy to perform his "secret technique", which backfires and causes him to fall down the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm. After defeating Master Kohga, he will use his last bit of energy to perform his "secret technique", which backfires and causes him to fall down the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm. While falling down the Chasm, Master Kohga is heard yelling that he shall be remembered and the Yiga Clan will track Link to the ends of Hyrule Kingdom. As a reward for defeating him, Link will receive a Treasure Chest containing the Thunder Helm. Master Kohga somehow survived his fall down the pit at the Yiga Clan Hideout to find himself in the Depths, and has since been plotting his revenge against Link. He plans to use Zonai Technology to create weapons that will win him favor with Ganondorf. He is first found in the Great Abandoned Central Mine in the Central Hyrule Depths after Link receives Autobuild, and he will challenge Link to a fight so he can have it for himself. In his first battle, Master Kohga deploys a buggy with a spiked ram while attempting to drop Boulders on Link. Shooting Master Kohga will eject him from the buggy and bury him in the ground. Link can then attack with impunity until he recovers. Additionally, his Boulders can be sent back at him with Recall. He will eventually add a set of wood panels that prevent him from being hit from the front and the side, but he remains vulnerable from behind. At low health, he will add a pair of Rockets that will allow him to charge at high speed, but this can be turned against him by getting him to charge into a wall. In his second fight, Master Kohga employs an airplane with Flame Emitters on its underside, which he will try and attack Link with. These will later be replaced with a far more dangerous Cannon. The arena contains an array of Zonai Devices that will allow Link to gain enough altitude to shoot Master Kohga off his Vehicle. At low health, he will project a screen that will block frontal shots. In his third fight, Master Kohga attacks Link from a Headlight Raft, aided by two Yiga Footsoldiers with Duplex Bows. Several Vehicles in the nearby area will allow Link to close the distance with Master Kohga and strike. At low health, he will begin throwing Boulders and project his energy screen. In his fourth and final fight, Master Kohga attacks Link with the Ultimate Weapon, a modified Crafter Construct rebuilt by the Yiga Clan. While riding the Ultimate Weapon, he battles similarly to the Seized Construct, with the same attacks and electric fence weakness. Knocking him into the fence will knock him off the Ultimate Weapon, stunning him and letting Link attack him with impunity until he recovers. Alternatively, he can just attack the Construct, which will eventually defeat Kohga as well. The , also known as the Blade of Evil's Bane, the Legendary Sword, the Sword of Legend, the Master Sword of Resurrection, the Sword that Seals the Darkness, and the Sacred Sword, is a recurring legendary Sword in the . Overview The Master Sword was originally crafted by the goddess Hylia as the Goddess Sword, and was later forged into the Master Sword by the Goddess's chosen hero and its spirit, Fi, who bathed it in the three Sacred Flames located across the land that would become the Kingdom of Hyrule. Din's Flame, in particular, imbued the sword with the Power to Repel Evil, a power augmented after the Sword received the blessing of Zelda, which transformed the blade into the true Master Sword. Although not always, it is the only weapon that can defeat Ganon in the games it appears in. The Master Sword is often seen to choose or accept its master by its own will, always a hero who has gone through great trials that test his courage, wisdom, and power to prove him worthy of wielding it. This may be the conscious choice of the sword's spirit, Fi, who sleeps eternally within the sword and only assists her heroic master. Appearance When the Master Sword was originally introduced in artworks of , the Sword's grip was red and its cross-guard yellow (in-game, both the grip and guard are red). However, in its pedestal, the Master Sword has a purple grip and blue guard. Its most conventional appearance was clearly defined in , with the purple grip and purple guard, though in subsequent games and the re-release of , the purple has become more blue or indigo. In , the grip and guard are royal blue as opposed to a deeper color. For the rest of the games, the Master Sword is merely a bastard sword with a narrow and a wide, shallow that runs almost the entire length of the blade, although in some appearances it has no fuller at all. The Triforce can be seen engraved in the lower part of the blade and yellow gemstone is embedded in the cross guard. It is seen in and that the state of the gem and the cross guard are indicative of the sword's awakening and power. When Link acquires the unawakened Master Sword in and the first form of the Master Sword in , the gem in its cross guard is dark and the guard is retracted toward the grip. Once the Master Sword has been restored to its full power in both games, its cross guard regains its winged form and the gem its yellow color. Abilities The Master Sword's classic ability is the power to vanquish evil. Infused with the sacred flames provided by the Golden Goddesses and blessed with Hylia's power, the sword is effective even against evil ones possessing the Triforce. However, in order to keep the power to repel evil intact, two Sages, known as the Sage of Earth and the

to vanquish evil. Infused with the sacred flames provided by the Golden Goddesses and blessed with Hylia's power, the sword is effective even against evil ones possessing the Triforce. However, in order to keep the power to repel evil intact, two Sages, known as the Sage of Earth and the Sage of Wind, are in charge of praying to the gods and thus infuse the Master Sword with the gods' power (in case of The Wind Waker) Should something happen to these Sages, the Master Sword will weaken and lose its might to combat evil. The sacred blade is also capable of destroying magical barriers and breaking curses that involve powerful, dark magic. In addition, it has the ability to lock away the remains of a demon. The Master Sword can also unleash Skyward Strikes by channeling heavenly energy. Even when low on power, the Master Sword can unleash Skyward Strikes through the use of lightning when it strikes the blade. Only a true hero that is "pure of heart and strong of body" is capable of wielding the sacred blade, and as such, those with tainted hearts can't even touch this sword. If a hero who is too young to bear the title that comes with the Master Sword withdraws this blade from its pedestal, the Master Sword will seal away the hero's soul and awaken him when the bearer comes of age to wield it, as seen in Ocarina of Time. However, if someone that is weak attempts to draw the Master Sword from its pedestal, they will lose their life. The Master Sword also acts as a key to gain entrance to the Temple of Light. If the Master Sword is retrieved from its pedestal in the Temple of Time, the portal to the Sacred Realm will open, eventually leading to the Triforce. Additionally, the bearer of the sword can travel through time to some extent by simply thrusting the Master Sword into the Pedestal of Time. The hero is able to travel backwards and forwards through the seven years of his life that were lost when he was kept in the Sacred Realm until he was old enough to hold the sword. When in the Twilight, the Master Sword itself can be infused with the power of the Sols from the Twilight Realm, allowing it to cut through the dark fog that exists in the realm. Even in its final form, it is seen in that the Master Sword can be further improved by smithing or magic means. However, after its task is accomplished and the sword returned into its pedestal, it will revert back its original shape. ending Location and Uses The Master Sword does not appear in , as the original game had the Magical Sword, its precursor. not appear in , as the original game had the Magical Sword, its precursor. However, a sword closely resembling it can be seen on an artwork referring to in . is the Master Sword's debut in the Zelda series. It is the legendary blade that rests in the Lost Woods of northwestern Hyrule in a pedestal with ancient Hylian inscribed on it. The ancient text says the hero with three symbols of virtue will wield it on cataclysm's eve, reading: "The Hero's triumph on Cataclysm's Eve wins three Symbols of Virtue. The Master Sword he will then retrieve, keeping the knights' line true." In order to defeat the evil wizard Agahnim that has taken over Hyrule Castle, Link must obtain the Master Sword. However, before the young hero can wield it, he must first acquire the three Pendants of Virtue that are scattered throughout the land. After doing so, he retrieves the sacred blade from the Pedestal of Time within the Lost Woods. With it, he is able to destroy the electrical barrier that Agahnim had placed in the upper floor of Hyrule Castle. With the Master Sword in hand Link manages to defeat Agahnim twice in the game and, eventually, Ganon. With Hyrule safe from evil, Link places the Master Sword back in its pedestal, never to be used again. The Master Sword is twice as powerful as the Fighter's Sword and has a longer reach. When at full health, the Master Sword will also fire a Sword Beam when swung. In , the Master Sword can also break Signs. During the course of the game, Link can actually upgrade the Master Sword. Its first upgrade is the Tempered Sword, which is acquired when the Dwarven Swordsmith is reunited with his partner on the outskirts of Kakariko Village. In the tempered shape, the Master Sword is two times stronger than its standard form, has a glowing orange blade and makes a deeper swing sound as opposed to the usual slash sound. Its second and last upgrade is the Golden Sword, acquired by giving the Master Sword or Tempered Sword to the Cursed Fairy in the Mysterious Pond of the Dark World within the Pyramid of Power. In the golden shape, the Master Sword is four times stronger than its standard form, killing almost any enemy in one hit, has a golden blade and green hilt, has the ability to break jars and skull jars (in the GBA remake), and also make a deeper swing sound than the tempered form. Moreover, Link can obtain the magic of the Bombos and Ether Medallion by holding the Master Sword up into the sky next to certain inscriptions around Hyrule. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of the Shrine The Mayachideg Shrine consists of three rooms, with the first being a descending chamber with three levels and ramps connecting them. At the top level, there is a Weapon supply spot. On the middle level, there are two round pedestals with Homing Carts placed on them and two plates of Spikes nearby. At the bottom level, there is a lone Soldier Construct, a second Weapon supply spot, and a portcullis blocking Link's way deeper into the Shrine. When the Soldier Construct is defeated, the portcullis will raise and allow entry. The second chamber consists of a large room with a complex four-level structure at its center, guarded by several more Soldier Constructs. Throughout this room, there are additional pedestals with more Homing Carts and Zonai Devices. is a recurring character in . Biography Maypin is a Hylian Merchant who specializes in selling Insects. He travels from the gateway near Koukot Plateau to the Gerudo Desert Gateway, stopping at Gerudo Canyon Stable along the way. Maypin wields a Traveler's Sword and a Wooden Shield, and he is always seen with his Donkey. When Maypin reaches one of the endpoints of the path he takes, he will stop for a moment to investigate the road ahead. Near Koukot Plateau, he states that the Monsters ahead are too dangerous to risk. At the Gerudo Desert Gateway, he claims that the Sand from the Gerudo Desert is difficult for him and his Donkey to traverse, so he has no choice but to turn back. As he walks away from the Gateway, he also reveals that there is too much competition for him at the Kara Kara Bazaar for it to be worth the trip. Despite this, he is interested in making sales in the Gerudo Desert, but he has yet to find a pack Animal that will not get stuck in the Sand. Maypin is knowledgeable about Elixirs that can be made with Insects, especially those that make journeying through the Gerudo Desert easier. He will inform Link that these Elixirs can be made with only Insects and Monster Parts. Should Link's plans include a trip into the Gerudo Desert, Maypin tells him to prepare Spicy Elixirs and Chilly Elixirs. Due to the Heat during the day and the Freezing Climate at night, Maypin believes only Gerudo women would be prepared for both. He suggests using Chilly Elixirs for traversing the Gerudo Desert during the day, but a Spicy Elixir is the better choice for the nighttime. Should Link only have the supplies to make one Elixir, Maypin states that it should be a Chilly Elixir, since the Heat in the Gerudo Desert is worse than the cold Temperature at night. If Maypin encounters Enemies while he is traveling, he will run away in fear. After Link defeats the Enemy, he will be relieved. Afterwards, Maypin may thank compliment Link's fighting ability. He also has a chance to express concern for his Donkey and the cargo it carries. For saving him, Maypin will give Link Enduring Veggie Rice Balls or Rupees as a reward. As Maypin walks, he will advertise his Insects to passing travelers. If Link asks to see what Maypin is selling, he reveals that his only wares are Warm Darners and Cold Darners. When Link makes a purchase from Maypin, he will be grateful. Like other Merchants, Link can also sell his own Items to Maypin. After paying for Link's Items, he will either thank him or ask if he needs something else. Wares and Pricing Maypin operates a traveling Wagon, from which he sells goods. Initially, he can be found stopped outside of Woodland Stable. When Link talks to Maypin at Woodland Stable, he expresses his joy at finally owning a Towing Harness. Noticing that Link

ask if he needs something else. Wares and Pricing Maypin operates a traveling Wagon, from which he sells goods. Initially, he can be found stopped outside of Woodland Stable. When Link talks to Maypin at Woodland Stable, he expresses his joy at finally owning a Towing Harness. Noticing that Link has been staring, Maypin accuses him of being jealous of his Towing Harness. However, he claims he understands, since a Towing Harness allows a Horse to drag a Wagon. Doing so has always been his dream as a Merchant. He claims he does most of his business in Akkala, inviting Link to speak with him should they run into each other again. If spoken to again, he suggests that Link acquire Pony Points from Stables to he can receive one himself. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring character in . Biography Mayro is a Hylian who resides at the Foothill Stable in Eldin. He can be found inside, where he admires a painting displayed on its wall. During the night, he sleeps in one of the Stable's Bed. When spoken to, Mayro claims that he wishes he had the skill to make such a painting. Turning to face Link, he asks if he has also come to admire the painting, and he reveals that he could stare at it for hours. He has heard the the owner of Foothill Stable, Ozunda, was the one who created it. In particular, he appreciates Death Mountain in the background and how the Stable blends into the background. By looking at the painting, Mayro is able to deduce that it depicts the Stable from the south. Following this conversation, the "A Landscape of a Stable" Shrine Quest will begin. If Link returns to Mayro after finding the Tah Muhl Shrine, he realizes that there is an Ancient Shrine on the painting's left-hand side. Despite how often his looks at the painting, he has never noticed it before. He believes this is because it is an unusual place for a Shrine, and he wonders who would go out of their way to visit it. He is then surprised to hear that Link has already visited it, and he rationalizes that there are some people who simply want to travel the world. When spoken to again, he hopes he will one day be able to paint as well as Ozunda does. Mayro now wears a Mushroom-Themed Outfit. As a result of the Extreme Cold Snap and Blizzard in Hebra, Mayro can initially be found sheltered inside Snowfield Stable. When spoken to, he notices that Link's Armor must keep him warm, and he states that the Blizzard may be life-threatening to those without Cold Resistant Clothes. He also comments that, although his Mushroom-Themed Outfit is perfect for almost every scenario, a Blizzard is not one of them. He informs Link that he is able to buy the Snowquill Set at Rito Village, but the bridge crossing over to Rito Village has collapsed. If Link talks to Mayro without any Armor equipped, he will be shocked to see Link doing so. After Link has defeated Colgera, Mayro can be seen traveling along Westbound Road between Tabantha Bridge Stable and the Lucky Clover Gazette. If Link has spoken to Mayro before, he will immediately recognize him and ask if he is also looking for Misko's Treasure. He assumes that Link is heading to the Tabantha Frontier, and he explains that a piece of Misko's Treasure is supposedly hidden in a Cave somewhere in Tabantha Frontier. While he has not been able to find the Treasure, he has become knowledgeable of the Region. He also explains that he went to Foothill Stable in Eldin so the Treasure-Hunting Brothers could tell him where the Treasure is, after which he returned to the Tabantha Frontier. Despite

Tabantha Frontier. While he has not been able to find the Treasure, he has become knowledgeable of the Region. He also explains that he went to Foothill Stable in Eldin so the Treasure-Hunting Brothers could tell him where the Treasure is, after which he returned to the Tabantha Frontier. Despite walking through various Roads, Mayro has not found a single Cave that could hold Misko's Treasure, and he considers expanding his search. However, he worries that he may ruin his Mushroom-Themed Outfit whilst doing so. If Link saves Mayro from Enemies, he thanks him. Afterwards, he rewards Link with a Meal as a sign of his gratitude. Like many Cece Fans, if Link talks to Mayro whilst wearing no Armor, Mayro will try avoid talking to him until he puts them back on.

is a recurring character in . Biography Mazli is a Rito who guards the entrance to Rito Village. He carries a Feathered Spear, and he patrols closer to Rito Village than his fellow guard, Gesane. Upon meeting Link, Mazli claims that he would like to show him around, but now is not a good time. If Link asks where he is, Mazli responds that he is in Rito Village, but they are not in welcoming mood. To learn more, Mazli directs Link to the rest of the Village's inhabitants. When asked what is going on, Mazli faces the sky toward Divine Beast Vah Medoh, explaining that it showed up a while back and shot down the Rito warriors who flew up to check it out. Although it is said to have once been a divine being that protected the Village, it does not seem very divine to him. Mazli is thankful it only shoots at anything flying in the sky, but it is still demoralizing for the Rito to have to fly so low to the ground. When Link leaves, Mazli allows him to do so. If Link speaks to Mazli again, he will recognize him and state that there are no new happenings. After starting the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, Link can ask Mazli is he knows Teba. Mazli claims that Teba has left Rito Village. He directs Link to Gesane, who might know where Teba is. After Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been appeased, Mazli asks Link if he has come to see the Divine Beast. Vah Medoh has been perched above Rito Village, and it has not moved since then. Mazli is surprised that the spire there can support its weight. During the "EX Champion Revali's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link can encounter Mazli along the edge of Tanagar Canyon. When asked why he is there, Mazli explains that Kaneli told him to keep watch on Dinraal, the Dragon that appears in the Canyon. Due to the frequency in sightings of Dinraal, the citizens of Rito Village have become worried it will cause them trouble. He does not blame them for being worried, since Divine Beast Vah Medoh left them all on edge. While everything seems fine, Mazli plans on continuing his watch to be sure. He recalls that Dinraal flies through Tanagar Canyon every night, and he finds the way its horns glow to be captivating. As Dinraal passes by, Mazli comments that he believes it to be friendly due to how tranquil it is. He then points out the glow of its horns to Link, once again stating that it is captivating. However, Mazli is still fearful of Dinraal's size, even though he knows it will not hurt him. After Link has unearthed Shira Gomar Shrine, Mazli notices that Dinraal's horns have stopped glowing and wonders what it means.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Meadela's Mantle Cave is situated on the northern side of Meadela's Mantle in the Gerudo Highlands. It features an underground river, at the end of which the Gerudo Highlands Skyview Tower's supports can be found. Billson's Records are located within the Meadela's Mantle Cave. While constructing the Gerudo Highlands Skyview Tower, Billson sought shelter in the Cave in order to avoid a Blizzard, and he consequentially decided to use it for storage. Predicting that Hudson Construction may need to return to the Cave, Billson decided to leave Hyrule Restoration Materials inside. Creatures Materials

Several different variations of Meat and Mushroom Skewers can be made by using different Ingredients: Chilly Meat and Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Chillshrooms. Enduring Meat and Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Endura Shrooms. When eaten, they completely refill and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Meat and Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Stamella Shrooms. They can be eaten to restore a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Meat and Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Rushrooms. Eating these skewers will boost Link's Stealth for a short period. Spicy Meat Skewer: Made by adding spicy ingredients. When eaten, they'll grant Link one level of Cold Resistance temporarily. Tough Meat Skewer: Made by adding tough ingredients. They'll increase Link's defense when he eats them. Other Appearances The recipe for Zesty Meat Skewer is earned by completing the Quest "Cooking for the Common Cold". It is made using two Spicy Peppers, two Raw Meats, and two Raw Bird Drumsticks. However, it can be lowered to one of each ingredient through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warriors will take 50% less damage from Ice.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Meat Stews are Meals that are made by Cooking either Raw Meat or a Raw Bird Drumstick with Tabantha Wheat, Goat Butter, and Fresh Milk in a Cooking Pot. When eaten, they will heal some of Link's Hearts. These stews are mainstay dishes, containing hearty Meats that leave people satisfied throughout Hyrule. By adding a fifth Ingredient to Meat Stew, Link can make one of the following variations: Chilly Meat Stew: Made by adding chilly Ingredients. Link can eat these stews to gain one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Meat Stew: Made by adding electric Ingredients. Link gains one level of Shock Resistance when he eats them. Enduring Meat Stew: Made by adding an enduring Ingredient. Consuming them will completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Meat Stew: Made by adding an energizing Ingredient. If one of these stews are eaten, Link's Stamina Wheel will be partially refilled. Hasty Meat Stew: Made by adding a hasty Ingredient. When eaten, they'll boost Link's movement speed. Hearty Meat Stew: Made by adding a hearty Ingredient. Eating them will heal all of Link's Hearts and increase his maximum Hearts. Mighty Meat Stew: Made by adding mighty Ingredients. If they are eaten, they will increase the power of Link's attacks. Sneaky Meat Stew: Made by adding sneaky Ingredients. When eaten, Link will gain a temporary boost to his Stealth. Spicy Meat Stew: Made by adding a spicy Ingredient. Eating these stews will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Meat Stew: Made by adding tough Ingredients. Eating these stews will increase Link's defense.

Link can add additional ingredients to the recipe for Meaty Rice Balls, which can result in the following variations: Chilly Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding chilly ingredients. When eaten, they grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding electric ingredients. Link can eat them to gain one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding enduring ingredients. They can be eaten to completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding energizing ingredients. Eating them will refill part of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding hasty ingredients. Eating these rice balls will temporarily increase Link's movement speed. Hearty Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding hearty ingredients. When eaten, they will heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him temporary Hearts. Mighty Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding mighty ingredients. If eaten, Link gains a boost to the power of his attacks. Sneaky Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding sneaky ingredients. Eating them will provide Link with a boost to his Stealth. Spicy Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding spicy ingredients. Consuming them will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Meaty Rice Balls: Made by adding tough ingredients. They increase Link's defense when they are eaten. Like in , Meaty Rice Balls can be made by Cooking a bundle of Hylian Rice with Meat.

They are usually found in Goddess Cube Chests, or can be purchased from Beedle after upgrading the Wallet. Medals either passively boost Link's abilities or alter the results of things appearing in the Overworld. They consume one space in the Adventure Pouch as a result.
