is a recurring character in . Biography Medda is a Hylian who resides in Hateno Village with his daughter, Aster. During the day, he tends to the field behind his house. At night, he watches over Aster as she sleeps in her Bed. While doing this, he eventually falls asleep in his chair. When Link speaks to him, Medda correctly guesses that he is a traveler. While he does not believe that there is much to see in Hateno Village, he encourages Link to enjoy himself. If Link presses him, Medda admits that there are certain things that make the Village interesting, such as the only Dye Shop in Hyrule. He also points out Mount Lanayru, which is located to the north. When Link inquires about Mount Lanayru, he shares a rumor that it is the location of the Spring of Wisdom, which was used by Zelda for purification. Due to how special it is, he believes that the Royal Family of Hyrule may have left treasure at the Spring. At least, this is what he would have done. Due to the dangerous Ice surrounding Mount Lanayru, Medda believes that no one will be able to access this treasure. Should Link have the time, Medda suggests that he explore Mount Lanayru. After this, "The Spring of Wisdom" Shrine Quest will begin. Following this conversation, Link is able to ask Medda questions. If Link asks about the Spring of Wisdom, he explains that it was the site of a ceremony performed by princesses from Hyrule Castle. While he is unsure of the details, Medda decides that it does not concern the people of Hateno Village. Next, if Link asks about Mount Lanayru, Medda claims that it is the most famous mountain that can be seen from Hateno Village. He then repeats his statements about it being a hiding place for treasure, but he is unsure if this is useful information. Finally, if Link asks Medda what he is doing, Medda explains that it is his responsibility to tend to this field, and he sometimes harvests more than he needs. When this occurs, he sends his extra produce to the East Wind, the General Store operated by Pruce. When asked this same question while inside his home, Medda admits that he enjoys watching Aster while she is asleep. He remarks that Link would understand if he were a parent, but he admits that doing so leaves him tired in the morning. Lastly, if Link asks this question while it is Raining, Medda explains that he is checking the Water level of the reservoir behind his house, because his crops could drown otherwise. Medda has a habit of speaking and singing to himself. As he works, Medda will sing about Mount Lanayru and attendants. While Medda is returning to his home, he yawns, and he will then mutter about finishing his work and watching over Aster as she sleeps. He also sings as a way to motivate himself to keep working, particularly during

As he works, Medda will sing about Mount Lanayru and attendants. While Medda is returning to his home, he yawns, and he will then mutter about finishing his work and watching over Aster as she sleeps. He also sings as a way to motivate himself to keep working, particularly during Rain. In all these scenarios, when he notices Link nearby, he is embarrassed that someone overheard him. He tells Link to wait until he has settled down if he wants to talk, since he cannot walk and talk at the same time. If Link speaks to Medda while carrying the Blue Flame, he recognizes that it belongs to Purah. He directs Link to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab, which is located on the eastern edge of Hateno Village.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Medingo Pool is a small pool of Lava in southeastern Eldin Canyon. It is situated right beside the Mountain Road paving the way toward the Southern Mine and Goron City. The Pool is connected by a narrow strait that flows from Darb Pond north. The Pool and the Road are patrolled by a Guardian Stalker. On an isolated shore is a giant skull that conceals a Korok inside, who will give Link a Korok Seed for finding them. Enemies Medingo Pool has been drained of Lava, revealing a Igneo Talus. Several fiery rocks that burn Link if he stands on them can be found around the Talus. Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Korok Seeds

is a recurring character in . Biography Meeshy is a Hylian adventurer. She travels on the Faron Highroad between Highland Stable and Lakeside Stable. Meeshy is a novice adventurer, so she is careful when it comes to pushing herself too hard. Mush of her information about the surrounding area comes from other adventurers or studying her Map. During her journey, she will often refer to her Map for guidance. If it Rains, she will be worried that her Map will get wet. At night, she looks out for Shooting Stars. As she travels, Meeshy will occasionally mention the Faron Woods to Link. She advises Link to reference his Map if he journeys through the Faron Woods, since they can be difficult to navigate. She has also heard of Dracozu Lake, which she refers to as "Mouth of the Dragon." In addition, she considers the ancient Zonai Ruins to be romantic, even though she would never visit them. Finally, Meeshy shares rumors that the Spring of Courage is located within the Faron Woods, but she believes visiting it would be too risky for someone of her skill level. As she approaches Lakeside Stable, Meeshy expresses an interest in the Floria Falls that flow into Lake Floria, and she likes the idea of going behind a Waterfall. While Meeshy is at Lakeside Stable, she informs Link that he could continue following the Faron Highroad east to Lurelin Village. However, she warns him that he would be at risk of Monster attacks if he went this way. When she leaves Lakeside Stable, Meeshy shares that her plan is to go to Highland Stable through the Faron Woods. Meeshy claims to have had bad encounters with Monsters in the past, stating that they seem to be drawn to her. As she approaches Highland Stable, she will begin running to avoid the Monsters in the area. Near Lakeside Stable, she claims she was so scared of these Monsters that she sees them in her dreams. When she is attacked by Enemies, Meeshy will run away in fear. If Link speaks to her during this time, she will wonder what she should do and wish the Monsters would disappear. After Link defeats the Enemy, she will be relieved. She tells Link how scared she was, and she is grateful that he was there to help her. As a reward, Meeshy will give Link Food and Rupees. Meeshy can be found in various different locations throughout Hyrule.

is a recurring character in . Biography Meghyn is a Hylian who travels Hyrule Kingdom searching for Hearty Truffles with her sister, Nat. When Link encounters them, the sisters will be under attack by a pair of Bokoblins. Meghyn and Nat can be found in the Ginner Woods, along the Ternio Trail south of Foothill Stable, and in the Sarjon Woods. While she is being attacked, Meghyn will run away in fear. After the Bokoblin has been defeated, she will be relieved. When spoken to, she she thanks Link for his help by giving him Food, Materials, or Rupees. Afterwards, she states that Nat's idea to search for Hearty Truffles is the reason they got in danger. If Link speaks to Meghyn again, she claims that she never wanted to go hunting for Hearty Truffles, blaming Nat for their predicament. After both Bokoblins have been defeated, she is surprised that she and Nat have survived. She recalls that the Bokoblins appeared out of nowhere. She harbors some resentment towards Nat, who refuses to let them return home without Hearty Truffles. If Meghyn was knocked unconscious by a Bokoblin, she continues to blame Nat. Alternatively, if Link saves Meghyn while Nat is still in danger, Meghyn will be concerned for her sister. While they are scouring for Hearty Truffles, Meghyn remarks that she wants to go home. She recalls that she told Nat it would be risky to go hunting. She claims that Nat becomes unreasonable when she thinks about Rupees. Nat tells Meghyn to return to their search, reminding her that they will not return home until they find Hearty Truffles. With a sigh, Meghyn agrees with her. When Link speaks to Nat, she tells him about her and Meghyn's journey and reasoning behind searching for Hearty Truffles, claiming there is no reward without a risk. Meghyn becomes angered by this, standing up and telling Nat not to make it sound as though they only care about Rupees. She reminds Nat that whatever money they make is not worth it if they do not survive to spend it at home. Nat argues back, stating they will either practice fighting or find Hearty Truffles, and she considers both of these scenarios to be a win. Meghyn becomes despondent, claiming that Nat will be the death of her. After Link has completed the Side Quests "Cave Mushrooms That Glow", "The Captured Tent" and "Who Finds the Haven?", Meghyn and her sister Nat part ways to go explore the world on their own in search of more mushrooms. Meghyn becomes a Wandering Merchant, and she can be found traveling between the Lucky Clover Gazette and the Tabantha Great Bridge. Wares and Pricing

is a recurring character in . Biography Mei is a Zora woman who resides in Zora's Domain. However, when Link first arrives in Zora's Domain, she will be absent. Her job is catching Fish, which she then sells at the Coral Reef. Mei is the wife of Fronk and the mother of Tumbo and Keye. Fronk describes Mei as lively and cheerful, a trait he believes she passed down to Tumbo. On the day Divine Beast Vah Ruta started its rampage, Mei left Zora's Domain to catch Fish in Zora River. However, the Rain that the Divine Beast spouted caused the River to swell, leading Mei to be swept downstream. Mei can be found on the islet to the west of Hylia Island in Lake Hylia, singing to herself as she swims. When Link speaks to Mei, she will greet him. After this, she comments on the Weather at Lake Hylia. If Link asks what she is doing, Mei explains that she is catching Fish to sell at the Coral Reef, the General Store in Zora's Domain. Following this, Link can ask about Zora's Domain, and Mei explains that they are far away from it. However, she is having fun catching the rare Fish in Lake Hylia. After the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" Main Quest has been completed, Link will find Fronk worrying about Mei. When Link asks him what is wrong, Fronk confesses that he is concerned for Mei, who has yet to return. He recounts that Mei left to go fishing when Divine Beast Vah Ruta began rampaging. He regrets allowing her to leave, fearing that something terrible could have happened to her. When Link offers to search for Mei, Fronk will be grateful for his help. After this, the "A Wife Washed Away" Side Quest will begin. In Lake Hylia, Mei will be singing about how big her catch is. When Link approaches her, she mentions she has caught a lot of Fish today. Following this, Link asks Mei if she knows Fronk, to which she questions if something is wrong with him. After a moment, Mei realizes that she has been away from Zora's Domain for too long, and she begins to cry and apologize to Fronk. Determined to return home immediately, Mei gives Link the five Staminoka Basses that she has caught. Once this has been done, she will leave Lake Hylia. When she leaves, the Side Quest will be completed. Upon returning to Zora's Domain, Mei can be found swimming in a pool of Water in the Sleeping Chamber. She recounts to Link that Fronk scolded her for being gone so long. Due to this incident, Mei has been temporarily banned from leaving Zora's Domain, which she accepts as fair. Despite being bored because of this, Mei is happy that Fronk is looking after Tumbo and Keye, so all she has to worry about is having fun. While Mei wants to work, she has decided to let Fronk take care of their family, since

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mekar Island is a small island located in Lake Mekar. Mekar Island sits directly west of Korok Forest and the Lost Woods. Mekar Island is devoid of life, hosting only a dead Tree in its center. Piles of bones are scattered across the islands. If Link steps on the Island at night, a large group of various Stal enemies will rise and attack him. Enemies In , Mekar Island reappears in the same location as with some slight changes. An Electric Wizzrobe inhabits the island and the large group of Stal Enemies no longer appears at night. An Iron Treasure Chest and a Campfire can be found next to the dead Tree in the center. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mellie's Plum Garden is located in Kakariko Village. It is located just east of Steen's Swift Carrot farm, down the slight decline. It houses a total of nine Plum Trees. The Plum Trees in Mellie's Plum Garden were all planted by Impa on the day Mellie was born, despite the fact that it was Raining. The Garden is considered to be an heirloom of Kakariko Village, and Impa gifted it to Mellie to take care of. Mellie has tended to the Trees all her life and considers them an extension of herself. As such, she forbids trespassers from entering. If Link enters Mellie's Plum Garden while she is present, she will yell at him to stop. On subsequent entries, she reminds him that he is not allowed in her Garden, claiming that something could happen to her if he continues to trespass. If only a few Trees have been destroyed, Mellie notices that there are not as many as there were before, but she believes she could be imagining things. Should all of Mellie's Plum Trees be destroyed, Mellie will be horrified, stating that her life has lost its meaning. When her Trees are destroyed during Rain, Mellie remarks that it is fitting her life would end while it is Raining, since the same Weather was present on the day of her birth. During the "Flown the Coop" Side Quest, one of Cado's Cuccos can be found in Mellie's Plum Garden. To retrieve it, Link must wait until Mellie leaves the Garden at night. At this time, he will be able to enter without being yelled at. Creatures Creatures Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Mellie is an elderly Sheikah woman who resides in Kakariko Village. During the day, she watches over her Plum Garden. At 5:00 PM, she leaves the Garden to Cook dinner in the Common Cooking Area. At 8:00 PM, Mellie returns to her home next to Olkin's Pumpkins, where she and her husband Olkin reside. It was Raining on the day that Mellie was born, and it was also the day that Impa planted the Garden's Plum Trees in Kakariko Village. Impa eventually gave the Garden to Mellie. Due to this, the plums are special to Mellie, so she watches over them. According to Mellie, Plum Trees represent endurance and prosperity, and thus are the "silent guardians" of Kakariko Village. A Sign outside of the Garden warns against trespassers. If Link enters Mellie's Plum Garden, while she is watching, she yells at him for the intrusion. Afterwards, she explains to Link that she has been caring for the Plum Trees her whole life, and they have become a part of her. She believes that she will die when the Garden does, so she has raised the Trees with as much love as she can. Mellie has vowed to take care of the Garden so long as she is alive, and she refuses to allow Link to mess with them. When Link trespasses into Mellie's Plum Garden again, she will remind him that he is not allowed to enter. She is concerned that something would happen to her or her Plum Trees, so she begs Link to leave them alone for her sake. In anger, she will call him a "rascal" and a "darn whippersnapper." If Link destroys a Plum Tree, Mellie will again yell at him to stop. If he speaks to her when only a few have been destroyed, Mellie notices that there are fewer than there were before. When all Mellie's Plum Trees, Mellie once again lectures him about their importance, afterwards she realizes that it is not time for such things. Should Link trespass into the Garden after the Trees have all been destroyed, Mellie will notice they are gone after she scolds Link. Following both of these scenarios, Mellie expresses her sadness, and she claims that when her Plum Trees died, so did her life's meaning. Additionally, if Link destroys the Trees while it is Raining, Mellie recounts that this was the Weather the day she was born, and it is therefore fitting for it to Rain on the day her soul was to die. In the evening, Mellie can be found at the Common Cooking Area, where she Cooks dinner for herself and Olkin. Olkin is a fan of her Cooking, particularly the Fortified Pumpkins that she uses. When Link speaks to Mellie during this time, she explains that Olkin's rivalry with Steen stems from his hatred of Carrots, although she does not understand his pettiness. As she walks back to her home, Mellie remarks that night came quickly,

, also known as are a recurring mechanic in . Overview List of Memories After undergoing a century-long rejuvenation process in the Shrine of Resurrection, Link's Memory is fragmented. Throughout the events of , Link slowly regains his Memory as certain locations or objects spark his recollection. There are a total of 18 Memories and they can be Recovered in any order. Link can view the Memories again in the Sheikah Slate's Adventure Log after recovering them. The majority of Link's Memories are Recovered by visiting the locations shown in the 12 photos found on the Sheikah Slate's album. These photos were captured by Zelda 100 years ago. In addition, Link recalls a Memory during each of the four Divine Beast Main Quests and recalls a Memory after obtaining the Master Sword. After visiting the 12 locations from the photos in the Sheikah Slate album and regaining the Memories associated, Impa will show Link a picture that depicts the location of his final Memory of his past with Princess Zelda. Recovering this final Memory completes the "Captured Memories" Main Quest. Zelda then tells Link through telepathy that he has Recovered all of his Memories of him and Zelda and that it is time to defeat Calamity Ganon. Completing the "Captured Memories" Main Quest will also unlock a post-credits scene after defeating Calamity Ganon. Downloadable Content pack adds five EX Recovered Memories that take place before the other Recovered Memories. Link is able to visualize the first four EX Recovered Memories after listening to a Song that is sung by Kass to honor one of the Champions that piloted a Divine Beast when Link completes a Main Quest related to the Trials that Champion faced. Link remembers the final EX Recovered Memory after listening to the Champions' Ballad, the Unfinished Song by Kass's teacher that Kass later completes. 125 additional Voice Memories were added to the Zelda Notes feature of the Nintendo Switch App for copies of . These Voice Memories explore Zelda's inner thoughts as she travels across Hyrule while training to develop her divine sealing powers to stop the Great Calamity. List of Memories Like in , Link is tasked with gathering 12 Memories. To view them, Link must find the Dragon's Tears, which are hidden within the Geoglyphs found throughout Hyrule. A majority of these Memories take place shortly after the Founding of the Kingdom of Hyrule in the Era of Myth, and they depict Zelda's experiences after traveling to the distant past using the power of a Secret Stone. List of Memories

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Menoat River starts directly underneath the Lake Tower and feeds into the Faron Sea, south of Lake Hylia. At the head of the River is Cora Lake. The Menoat River then curves south through Harfin Valley and the Parache Plains for a short time, before finally ending at the Faron Sea. During the "EX Treasure: Garb of Winds" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link is tasked with reading Misko's EX Journal 2 to find the location of the Island Lobster Shirt. The Menoat River is mentioned in this Journal, as it describes the Shirt being at the location "where the Menoat River was born." left|40px A Circle of Lily Pads can be found near the beginning of the Menoat River. If Link dives into this Circle, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mercay Island is an Island located in the Southwestern Sea of the World of the Ocean King. It is the home of the Temple of the Ocean King as well as Mercay Village, a port town located on its southeastern coast. It has recently been victim to various disasters such as earthquakes and increased Monster sightings. After losing Tetra to the Ghost Ship, Link finds himself lost on Mercay Island's southwestern beach. He is awoken by Ciela, a curious Fairy who offers to help him find the Ghost Ship with the help of her "grandfather", Oshus. With Oshus's guidance, Link and Ciela find Linebeck and embark on their journey to chase the Ghost Ship to rescue Tetra. Mercay Island is divided into two halves where people have taken root. Oshus, Lapelli, and Apricot reside on its western half, which hosts farmland and a beach. A stone bridge connects this settlement to Mercay Village. However, this bridge is prone to breaking every time a significant earthquake strikes the Island and people are forced to take the dangerous Mountain Passage to the north instead. Despite Oshus's warnings, Link and Ciela steal their way into Oshus's Storehouse near Oshus's House and retrieve his Sword in order to reach the port when an earthquake destroys the bridge to Mercay Village. Due to the recent earthquakes, Boulders have fallen into Lapelli's garden. He asks for Link's help to remove them and rewards him with a single Green Rupee for his efforts. After receiving a dirty look from Link for such a cheap reward, he offers information on where Link can find a Big Green Rupee in the North Woods. The road north of Oshus's House features several Monsters as well as a Boing Statue. The Boing Statue teaches Link how to perform a Somersault and tells him to perform it on the Big Tree beside it. Doing so will cause a Red Rupee to fall from the Big Tree. A group of five Fellable Trees block the entrance to the Mountain Passage along this road. Mercay Village sits at the end of the Mountain Passage. In addition to its port it features the Mercay Island Shop, the Mercay Tavern, the Shipyard, and the Treasure Teller. The North Woods sit between Mercay Village and the Temple of the Ocean King. In these Woods, Link can find the musician Freedle and the Mercay Bomb Caverns. After Linebeck is rescued from the Temple of the Ocean King: 1F, Gazpacho successfully repairs the bridge connecting the Island. is a recurring character in . Biography Merina is a Gerudo Soldier who guards the North Gate of Gerudo Town with Dorrah. She wields a Gerudo Spear. When Link tries to enter Gerudo Town without a Gerudo Outfit disguise, Dorrah and Merina will stop him from passing through. When Link speaks to Merina, she notices that Link is a "voe," or a man, and warns him that men are not allowed into Gerudo Town. When Link speaks to her again, Merina again scolds him and reiterates that only "vai," or women, are allowed. When Link finishes speaking to her, she exclaims that all men must leave at once. If Link asks what "voe" means, Merina explains that it is the Gerudo word for "man." Similarly, she reveals that "vai" in the Gerudo word for "woman." After either of these explanations, she will find it ridiculous that Link is trying to enter Gerudo Town without knowing the difference between "voe" and "vai." When Link speaks to Merina while wearing the Gerudo Outfit on, she comments that they do not see many Hylian women around and welcomes him to Gerudo Town. Merina also explains that only women are allowed inside Town walls, and she invites Link to take his time there. In this scenario, when Link asks about the meaning of "voe" or "vai," Merina will politely teach him. She recommends that Link learn the Gerudo language if he plans on entering Gerudo Town. Before finishing speaking, Merina also recommends that Link order a Noble Pursuit at The Noble Canteen, calling it the best drink she has ever had. If Link approaches her again, she vows to keep all voe out of Gerudo Town. If Link speaks to Merina after calming the Divine Beast Vah Naboris, she is grateful that Riju has brought peace back to the Gerudo Desert. Due to this, she is excited to return to living her life.

is a recurring unseen character in . Mestro goes unnamed in . Biography One century prior to the events of , Mestro built and was the proprietor of Wetland Stable. He was also the first chairman of the Stable Association, which was established in anticipation of the Great Calamity. Mestro's grandson, Mastro, is the leader of a traveling band known as the Stable Trotters. If Link jostles Breezer too much during the Side Adventure "Serenade to Kaysa", Mastro will remark that he thought he would be reunited with his grandfather. At Wetland Stable, Violynne will tell Link how Mestro inspired Mastro to be bring happiness to others, thereby causing him to form his band.

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Meteo Wizzrobes are a stronger variant of the Fire Wizzrobe. They attack by using their Meteor Rods to conjure 3 Fireballs as well as by summoning flaming monsters such as Fire Chuchus and Fire Keese. They are also able to increase the area's temperature, making it too hot for Link without heat-resistant Armor or Elixirs. The Meteo Wizzrobe, like other Wizzrobes, will become invisible after attacking, leaving ripples in the air with each footstep. Striking it in the head with an Arrow will stun it and give Link time to attack. Hitting it with an ice attack, such as with Ice Arrows or a Frostblade, will immediately evaporate the Wizzrobe. Upon defeat, Meteo Wizzrobes drop their Meteor Rod. Instead of a Meteor Rod, Meteo Wizzrobes now carry a Magic Rod that has been Fused to a Ruby. Link can defeat them in one hit by Fusing Ice-type Materials to an Arrow, such as Ice Fruits or White Chuchu Jelly. Other Appearances Meteo Wizzrobes appear as Powerful Foes in the Downloadable Content pack for .

is a recurring character in . Biography Mezer is a Hylian Merchant. He works as a wandering butcher, selling Meat during his journey. He travels between Dueling Peaks Stable and the abandoned Monster Stronghold to the west, passing along the Squabble River and through the Dueling Peaks on his way. For equipment, Mezer carries an Emblazoned Shield and a Traveler's Sword. Due to the Meat he carries with him, Mezer smells like Raw Meat. When Link speaks to Mezer, he will often notice that he appears to be hungry. He will then offer his wares to Link, stating that it can rectify his problems. He also gives Link advice about Cooking with Meat, such as grilling it with the Rock Salt that he sells. This recipe will result in Salt-Grilled Meat, Salt-Grilled Prime Meat, and Salt-Grilled Gourmet Meat. Mezer may also notice that Link wants to speak to someone. While he is willing to talk with him, Mezer warns Link that he only talks about Meat. He then asks Link if he is interested in buying. In addition to this, if he believes that Link appears to be lost, he offers directions to Dueling Peaks Stable and Kakariko Village. Mezer himself typically frequents Stables. Finally, if Link appears to be tired, Mezer tells him to go to Dueling Peaks Stable, but he offers to sell him Meat if he does not have the strength to make it there. While Mezer is resting at the abandoned Monster Stronghold, he will feel as though he is being judged by Link. He claims that he finds being alone in the wilderness peaceful, even if it can be considered a wasteland. He then states that if Link has time to judge him, then he has time to buy Meat from him as well, and doing so would cheer him up. This continues at Dueling Peaks Stable, where he does not appreciate Link judging where he is sleeping for the night. In reality, Mezer would like to sleep in a Bed, but he does not make enough selling Meat to afford one. If Mezer is attacked by Enemies while he travels, he will draw his Traveler's Sword to defend himself. During his fight, Mezer claims that one needs to be tough to fight Monsters, and he attempts to ward off his attackers. After the Enemies have been defeated, he will try to calm himself down. When Link saves him, he will be relieved that both he and his wares are safe, and he may comment that his Meats likely attracted the Monsters. As a reward, Mezer gives Link Food and Rupees. When it Rains, Mezer will take note. He will take refuge under the cliffs of the southern Dueling Peak. Despite this, he is still determined to keep selling Meat. During Rain, Mezer will add Raw Gourmet Meat to his list of wares. As Mezer travels, he will advertise his wares to passerby. He claims to sell the best Meats, offering his customers their Rupees

of the southern Dueling Peak. Despite this, he is still determined to keep selling Meat. During Rain, Mezer will add Raw Gourmet Meat to his list of wares. As Mezer travels, he will advertise his wares to passerby. He claims to sell the best Meats, offering his customers their Rupees back if they are dissatisfied. If Link agrees to browse his wares, Mezer will promote his Raw Prime Meat and Raw Bird Thigh. When Link makes a purchase, Mezer will thank him and encourage him to return. He may also repeat his motto, which is "If you want meat, you want Mezer!" When Link stops buying, Mezer asks if he wants anything else, since it would be a waste if his Meat went bad. If Link buys all of his stock, Mezer informs him that he has nothing left to sell. However, he still allows Link to view the Meats he will have when he restocks. Like other Merchants, Link can sell his own Items to Mezer. When Mezer makes a purchase, he will thank Link and ask if there is anything else he needs. When their business is concluded, Mezer thanks Link and wishes him well. Wares and Pricing Mezer can initially be found at the Bedrock Bistro, where Cooke is upset with him for wasting either a Marbled Rock Roast or regular Rock Roast, depending on if Link has completed the "Yunobo of Goron City" Main Quest. Speaking to him will start the "Meat for Meat" Side Quest. Upon completing the Quest, Mezer will thank Link for helping and introduce himself as a meat lover. He will give him a Large Zonai Charge as a reward. He then asks if Link has heard rumors about a mysterious beast, which he wants to try eating. He tells Link that the two are now friends before he departs to search for the creature. The beast Mezer is looking for turns out to be a Dondon. After this, Mezer can be found walking along the Faron Highroad, where he will tell Link about his continued search for a Dondon. Due to its size, he offers to split the beast with Link if he finds it. However, he notes that if the creature he is searching for is endangered, he will not try to eat it. Passing Sarjon Bridge, Mezer will stop under a ruined Wagon for a while before continuing. If Link talks to him, he will apologize that he does not have Food to share and mention the way to Lurelin Village. At the fork in the trail, he turns down the path to Martha's Landing. Reaching the water, he will turn around and head back the way he came. When close to the Dondon sanctuary, he will remark that he can smell them nearby and talk excitedly about meat.

is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses Midna's Helmet is a piece of Armor that Link can wear on his head. It is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack. The bandit Misko stole it from Hyrule Castle, along with several other treasures. During the "EX Treasure: Twilight Relic" Side Quest, Link is tasked with reading Misko's EX Journal 2 in order to learn the location of Midna's Helmet. In reading it, he discovers that the Helmet can be found at the ruins of a temple flooded by the Regencia River. At the Sage Temple Ruins, Link will find a Hidden Chest embedded in the ground, which contains Midna's Helmet. Once acquired, Granté will begin selling Midna's Helmet for 50 Rupees. Furthermore it cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop or enhanced by a Great Fairy.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mido Swamp is a small mire in the northeastern section of the Great Hyrule Forest. It is made of Bottomless Bogs, though there are several small islands and fallen Trees that can be used to travel through it. The Swamp is also surrounded by Ogre Trees. At the end of the Test of Wood Mini-Game, Link must pass through Mido Swamp. If Link falls into the Swamp, he will drown and be sent to the beginning of the Trial. "The Test of Wood" Shrine Quest requires Link to complete the Mini-Game in order to access Maag Halan Shrine, which is located at the end of the Swamp. Following the Shrine Quest, Link will be able to play the Mini-Game again with a time limit of five minutes. After Link passes through Mido Swamp, Damia will end the Mini-Game. Enemies A small grove of Trees bearing Golden Apples can be found north of the Swamp. To the northwest, a small passage unaffected by the Lost Woods's fog is filled with Brambles. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Treasure Chests

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Mighty Bananas can be found growing in the tropical forests of West Necluda and on Eventide Island. They are also sold by Emri in Kara Kara Bazaar and dropped by regular Hinox. Eating one raw heals half of a Heart. When Cooked, the resulting Meal provides Link with the Attack Up Added Effect. This is due to the high amount of protein and calories present that they contain. Mighty Bananas exposed to Fire become Roasted Mighty Bananas. They can be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Yellow Dye. Mighty Bananas are one of three foodstuffs favored by the Sheikah, with the others being Swift Carrots and Fortified Pumpkins. They are the clear obsession of the Yiga Clan, as the Yiga Clan Hideout contains many Mighty Bananas. In addition, all Yiga Footsoldiers and Yiga Blademasters drop them upon their defeat. The Yiga Blademasters patrolling the Yiga Clan Hideout will also deviate from their path to eat Mighty Bananas that are left on the ground. Monk Maz Koshia will also stop fighting and eat them should Link drop some during their fight. Mighty Bananas are required to make Fried Bananas in a Cooking Pot. They can also be used in Fruit-based Meals: Mighty Bananas are required to make Fried Bananas in a Cooking Pot. They can also be used in Fruit-based Meals: Mighty Bananas are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Characteristics Mighty Carp can be found swimming in the Water of the Akkala Highlands and Lanayru Great Spring. There is a compound in its liver that promotes muscle growth. Like other carps, they can be exposed to Fire to become Roasted Carps or chilled by Ice to become Frozen Carps. Link can eat one to restore a single Heart, but they can also be Cooked into a dish that will increase the damage he deals when eaten. As is the case with otherFish, Mighty Carp can be used to make a Fish Skewer, a Fish and Mushroom Skewer, and Salt-Grilled Fish. They also count as seafood when making Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Mighty Lynel Bows are Bows wielded by Blue-Maned Lynels within Hyrule. In Master Mode, though, White-Maned Lynels use Mighty Lynel Bows instead of their Blue-Maned counterparts. They will become rare as Enemies tier up, but the Blue-Maned Lynel in the First Gatehouse of Hyrule Castle will always remain the same. Therefore, it can become the only source of Mighty Lynel Bows later in the game. Mighty Lynel Bows are a type of Lynel Gear, a series of Weapons that are created by Lynels. The bowstrings of Mighty Lynel Bows are noted to be made of a metal so tough that regular Hylians have trouble drawing them. When they are drawn, however, they can fire three arrows at once. Since they are made of metal, they conduct Electricity and will attract Lightning if equipped during Thunderstorms. Mighty Lynel Bows also sink if they are dropped in water, but can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, they do not burn if when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate like wooden Weapons do.

are recurring Items in . Mighty Lynel Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Mighty Lynel Shields are Shields made by Lynels. They have been reinforced by both armor and many blades. Compared to Lynel Shields, they are stronger in both defense and offense, and they are capable of tearing through armor when deflecting (dealing 13 damage). They are part of the Lynel Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created by Lynels. Blue-Maned Lynels use these Shields, however White-Maned Lynels in Master Mode will use these Shields. They become scarce as Lynels tier up, though the Blue-Maned Lynel in Hyrule Castle's First Gatehouse will always stay the same, making it a permanent source of Mighty Lynel Shields. Being made of metal, Mighty Lynel Shields conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during a thunderstorm, and will also sink if dropped in water. They can also be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune, and they will not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Mighty Lynel Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Mighty Lynel Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Mighty Lynel Swords.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Characteristics Link can find Mighty Porgies swimming in the waters of Necluda Sea and Lanayru Sea. They are also sold by the traveling merchant Chumin and at the fish market in Lurelin Village by Mubs. They can be eaten raw to restore one Heart to Link's Life Gauge. They become Frozen Porgies when exposed to Ice and Roasted Porgies when exposed to Fire. Meals made in a Cooking Pot with Might Porgies will temporarily increase Link's attack damage. Either a Mighty Porgy or an Armored Porgy can be used while Cooking to make Porgy Meunière and Seafood Paella. A porgy or a Hearty Blueshell Snail is needed to make Seafood Curry and Seafood Fried Rice. Mighty Porgies are among the fish that can be used to make a Fish Skewer, a Fish and Mushroom Skewer, and Salt-Grilled Fish. They're also among the seafood that can be used while making Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. Other Appearances Mighty Porgies can be sold for 10 Rupees.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Mighty Thistles can be found growing in the Faron Grasslands and West Necluda. Many Mighty Thistles grow around Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain near the Tabantha Tower. When Mighty Thistles are used while making a Meal in a Cooking Pot, the resulting dish will grant Link Attack Up when eaten, which increases the damage of his attacks. Mighty Thistles that make contact with Fire turn into Roasted Mighty Thistles. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Mighty Thistles can be used to create Orange Dye. is a recurring location in . Mija's Great Fairy Fountain goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Mija's Great Fairy Fountain is located southeast of Tarrey Town in the Akkala Highlands. As its name implies, it is home to the Great Fairy named Mija. The Fountain is surrounded by a shallow pool of Water and a small, unnamed forest. Several residents of Tarrey Town are aware of the Fountain's presence, though they are fearful to approach. Initially, Mija's Great Fairy Fountain will be closed. When Link approaches the bud, Mija will speak to him from inside, begging that he listen to her story. If he agrees, Mija explains that in the past, travelers would visit the Fountain and make offerings of Rupees, but her power has dwindled now that the offerings have stopped. In order to restore her power, she requests that Link make an offering. Depending on how many other Great Fairy Fountains have received offerings, Mija will ask for either 100 Rupees, 500 Rupees, 1,000 Rupees, or 10,000 Rupees. Should Link make a payment to Mija, her Great Fairy Fountain will bloom as her power is restored. Once the Fountain has been opened, Mija will be able to enhance Link's Armor, so long as he brings her the necessary Materials. The degree to which Link's Armor can be enhanced depends on how many other Great Fairy Fountains have been opened. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found at Mija's Great Fairy Fountain. It takes the form of a Flower Trail surrounding the Trees nearby. When Link reaches the end of the Flower Trail, a Korok will appear, giving him a Korok Seed as a reward. Creatures Materials Mija's Great Fairy Fountain is now located on the foothills of Mount Drena's northern peak, which is part of the Hebra Mountains.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mikau Lake is a part of the Lanayru Great Spring. It is a two-tiered lake that is bisected by a large Waterfall, located on a ridge to the west of Lulu Lake. It is considered by the Zora to be a shortcut to the top of Ploymus Mountain, and Link can Swim up its Waterfall while wearing the Zora Armor. Before Divine Beast Vah Ruta is calmed, it will be constantly Raining at Mikau Lake. 100 years before the events of , Mipha faced part of her Divine Beast Tamer's Trial to become a Champion at Mikau Lake, which involved Swimming through the Glowing Ring on its Waterfalls. During the Main Quest "EX Champion Mipha's Song", which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link is tasked with repeating this Trial for himself. A Wooden Chest containing an Opal can be found floating in the Water of Mikau Lake. In Master Mode, two platforms held in the air by Sky Octoroks appear above Mikau Lake. The one floating over the lower level bears a Metal Chest containing a Soldier's Bow. The higher platform also has another Metal Chest, though this one has a Windcleaver inside. Creatures Enemies Materials Creatures Materials

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Military Training Camp is the area surrounding Woodland Tower. The Camp is made up of multiple destroyed wooden towers sinking into a mire. The Camp is situated on a hillside southeast of Lake Mekar. The Camp is inhabited by Enemies that guard Treasure Chests. Areas Enemies The Military Training Camp remains in its location from , though the Woodland Tower is no longer present. The Monster Stronghold that was in the south of the Camp is also no longer visible. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests Korok Seeds Other Appearances The Military Training Camp can be unlocked after the Warriors give 5 Moblin Trophies, 50 Lizalfos Trophies, and 200 Bokoblin Trophies to complete the Quest "Entrance Test". By talking to Rubeo, one of its workers, the Military Training Camp can be used to level up all of the Warriors for a certain amount of Rupees. As the Warrior's level gets higher, so does the fee. Warriors can only be leveled up to the highest-leveled Warrior. For example, if Link has the highest level at level 30, then all the other Warriors can only be leveled up to level 30.

is a recurring character in . Biography Mils is a Hylian who hunts for treasure throughout Hyrule alongside his sister, Mina. The siblings will be under attack by a pair of Bokoblins when Link comes upon them. They can be encountered near the Exchange Ruins, in the Gatepost Town Ruins, and at the Rauru Settlement Ruins. Mils carries a Traveler's Sword and a Wooden Shield. While Mils is being accosted, he will draw his Traveler's Sword to defend himself. During this time, he resolves to give the Bokoblins a fight they will not forget. He may also wonder why this is happening to him. If Mina is knocked unconscious while Mils is fighting, he will be concerned for her. Alternatively, if Mils is the one knocked out, he will note that he was useless against the Bokoblins, and he considers whether he should have played dead. If Link saves Mils, he will be relieved. When spoken to, he may thank Link for his assistance. He might also wonder what would have happened had Link not helped them. As a reward, he will give Link Food and Rupees. After the Bokoblins have been defeated, Mils will thank Hylia that Mina is safe, and he recalls that it was dangerous to go treasure hunting at their current location. While Mils searches for treasure, Mina will direct him to hurry, which Mils apologizes for. When Link speaks to Mils during this time, he states that any treasure at their current location already belongs to him and Mina, and he discourages Link from searching on his own. However, he then remarks that nobody in their right mind would be searching for treasure there to begin with. Mina is the one who decides where they search, but Mils only wants to return home. Hearing him speaking, Mina orders Mils to keep searching for treasure. After this, Mils grumbles to himself about family. As Link speaks to Mina, she warns him to stay away from Hyrule Castle, since it is surrounded by Guardians. Mils joins their conversation and claims that people who are spotted by Guardians do not live long afterwards, which makes him nervous. Mina remarks that he should focus on finding treasure, or else she will give him something to worry about. Mils then grumbles about family. During "EX Champion Urbosa's Song," which is a Main Quest exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Mils and Mina can be encountered at the back entrance to the Yiga Clan Hideout, outside of Master Kohga's Room. They came in search of the Sacred Orb, which the Yiga Clan stole from the Gerudo. When spoken to, Mils is surprised that so many members of the Yiga Clan remain, as he had heard they were defeated by a traveling swordsman. He has been able to determine that the Sacred Orb is located on the second floor of the Yiga Clan Hideout Hall. However, Mils believes that infiltration would be too dangerous, as an important part of being a great treasure

he had heard they were defeated by a traveling swordsman. He has been able to determine that the Sacred Orb is located on the second floor of the Yiga Clan Hideout Hall. However, Mils believes that infiltration would be too dangerous, as an important part of being a great treasure hunter is staying alive. When Link exits the Yiga Clan Hideout with the Sacred Orb, Mils will be shocked that he was able to steal it. He claims that when the Yiga Clan find out, they will chase Link for the rest of time. When Link throws the Sacred Orb into the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm, he and Mina will run to the edge of the pit. If Link speaks to Mils, he angrily asks what Link was thinking.

is a recurring character in . Biography Mimo is a Rito who can be found at the top of Koholit Rock on Eventide Island. He does not appear until the "Stranded on Eventide" Shrine Quest and Korgu Chideh Shrine have been completed. Mimo operates the Paraglider Course Mini-Game. When Link first approaches him, Mimo asks what he is doing so high up. If Link answers that he is seeking adventure, Mimo reasons he must be drawn to heights. Mimo claims that this is something they have in common, since Koholit Rock is the only place where he can hear the Wind. Alternatively, if Link responds that he is in search of treasure, Mimo tells him that the only object in their vicinity is the Ancient Shrine. Mimo then explains that he came to Eventide Island to find freedom. Mimo wants to live free and unrestricted as the Wind does, and he asks Link if he wants to live the same way. If Link responds that he does, Mimo starts to feel a connection with him. While Link must use his Paraglider to fly, Mimo believes he is still capable of undergoing his Paraglider Course. If Link asks about the training, Mimo explains that he wants to find the freedom of the Wind by copying its movements. To achieve this, he has created the Paraglider Course, which involves flying through Floating Rings that are suspended in the air. Mimo promises that Link will be enriched if he undertakes this training. When Link seems unsure about participating, Mimo asks to be left alone so he can hear the Wind's voice. However, if Link decides to attempt the Paraglider Course, Mimo will be happy. To set up the Paraglider Course, Mimo requires a payment of 20 Rupees. Once paid, Mimo tells Link to wait on Koholit Rock while he makes his preparations. On his return, Mimo apologizes for taking so long, but he informs Link that the Paraglider Course is ready for Link to fly through. Mimo recommends that Link start out with the route to their left, as the Wind is calmer in that location. However, he claims the Wind will welcome Link regardless of what direction he takes. After this, the Mini-Game will begin. Once Link either lands on the ground or flies through all of the Floating Rings, Mimo will come and retrieve him. If Link passed through less than 20 Floating Rings, Mimo admits that he may have overestimate Link's skills, but he thinks practice could help him improve. After reaching between 20 and 24 Floating Rings, Mimo states that Link is not yet one with the Wind, but he still gives him a Red Rupee as a reward. If Link passes through 24 to 29 Floating Rings, Mimo claims that he handles his Paraglider well, giving him a Purple Rupee. When Link flies through between 30 and 49 Floating Rings, Mimo states that even a Rito could not have scored so well, and he gives him a Silver

If Link passes through 24 to 29 Floating Rings, Mimo claims that he handles his Paraglider well, giving him a Purple Rupee. When Link flies through between 30 and 49 Floating Rings, Mimo states that even a Rito could not have scored so well, and he gives him a Silver Rupee as a reward. Finally, if Link passes through at least 50 Floating Rings, Mimo suggests he may be a Rito in disguise, and he rewards him with a Gold Rupee. After Link finishes the Paraglider Course, Mimo asks if he wants to try another round. If Link agrees, Mimo reminds Link before he leaves that he will be there to pick him up if he gets tired. If Link refuses, Mimo accuses him of being like a Cucco, but he still looks forwards to seeing Link again. When Link returns to Mimo, he recognizes him and asks if he is interested in training again. Mimo has partnered with Branli to run Branli's Bird-Man Flight Research at Koholit Rock on Eventide Island. For 20 Rupees, Link can participate in their study, which involves steering a Zonai Wing into the middle of a target in the sea. If Link agrees to participate, Mimo will set up the Mini-Game. The first time Link participates, Mimo also explains the rules at Branli's behest. During subsequent attempts, he will explain everything again upon request. If Link lands outside any of the circles, he will not receive any reward. Mimo will give him a tip for controlling the Wings. If Link lands within the second ring of the circles, Mimo will compliment him before giving him a Purple Rupee. If Link manages to land in the smallest circle at the center of the target, both Mimo and Branli will be overjoyed. Mimo praises Link's skill with the Wing and reward him with a Silver Rupee.

is a recurring character in . Biography Mimos is a Hylian who can be encountered on Ebon Mountain. He constantly wanders around the broken-hearted pond at its peak. When Link first approaches to Mimos, he asks if he is also searching for his soulmate. If Link responds that he is, Mimos reveals that he shares the same goal. Alternatively, if Link acts confused, Mimos tells him not to be shy, since this is the only reason anyone would climb Ebon Mountain. Mimos himself has been waiting on the Mountain for a while. Despite how Link answers, Mimos reveals that nobody else has shown up yet. He believes he is at Lover's Pond, but he wonders if he could be at the wrong place. If Link speaks to Mimos again, he asks where his soulmate is, and he theorizes that his loneliness may be a sign to put himself out there more. Should Link tell Mimos to believe in himself, Mimos thinks that Link is trying to cheer him up. He says that Link should not worry about him, as his mother always said that he could do anything he puts his mind to. He then asks about Link, stating that putting all of one's faith in a legend will not attract women. If Link tells Mimos to try another pond, Mimos asks if he truly thinks that will help. While it is Raining, Mimos will remark that Link must be desperate for love, since he came out in such bad Weather.

is a recurring character in .} Biography Mina is a Hylian woman who hunts for treasure with her brother, Mils. The siblings can be found near the Exchange Ruins, in the Gatepost Town Ruins, and at the Rauru Settlement Ruins. When Link encounters them, they will be under attack by a pair of Bokoblins. Mina carries a Traveler's Sword and a Hunter's Shield, which she uses to defend herself. While she is fighting, Mina remarks that the Monsters came out of nowhere and accuses Mils of failing to keep watch. She also demands that Link help them. If Mils is knocked unconscious by his attacker, Mina will complain and call him an idiot. If Mina was knocked out by a Bokoblin, she will be ashamed and claim she must be losing her edge. Once the Bokoblins have been defeated, Mina will be relieved. The first time Link saves her, she insists that she was not in danger. On subsequent rescues, Mina complains that she would be seen as rude for not rewarding him, even though she never asked for his help. She may also remark that Link uses his sword well and thank him. She rewards Link with either Food or Rupees. When this is done, she resolves to defeat the Monsters by herself next time. Afterwards, she will remarks that she and Mils are lucky to be alive. Following the Bokoblins' defeat, Mina will supervise Mils as he searches through the rubble. The first time that Link speaks to Mina, she claims that the ruins they are at was once a major population center, but that changed when Monsters ran the people out of town. As a result of this, she believes a lot of treasure has been left behind, which is why she and Mils search for it. If Link has spoken to Mina before, she tells him to look elsewhere for treasure. As the conversation continues, Mina warns Link to stay away from Hyrule Castle, as it is surrounded by dangerous Guardians. Mils chimes in, saying that once a Guardian spots you, you do not have long to live. Mina becomes annoyed, reminding Mils to keep searching for treasure before she gives him something to be nervous about. Mils then complains about family. When Link speaks to Mils, he says that any treasure at their current location belongs to himself and Mina, though he claims that nobody in their right mind would be searching to begin with. Since Mina decides where they scavenge, however, he has no choice but to follow her orders. Mina then reprimands Mils for wasting time talking, instead instructing him to find treasure. After this, Mils complains about family. During the "EX Champion Urbosa's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Mina and Mils can be found at the rear exit of the Yiga Clan Hideout, outside of Master Kohga's Room. When Link approaches Mina, she explains that they are after the Sacred Orb, which the Yiga Clan stole from

Urbosa's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Mina and Mils can be found at the rear exit of the Yiga Clan Hideout, outside of Master Kohga's Room. When Link approaches Mina, she explains that they are after the Sacred Orb, which the Yiga Clan stole from the Gerudo. However, she is now considering abandoning this idea while she has the chance. She then becomes scared that the Yiga are planning on throwing the Sacred Orb into the giant pit in their Hideout. When Link exits the Yiga Clan Hideout with the Sacred Orb, Mina is shocked that he was able to sneak it past the Yiga Clan guards. Mineru is a recurring character in . Biography Mineru is the Sage of Spirit and, alongside her younger brother Rauru, one of the last remaining Zonai in Hyrule. During the Era of Foundation, the Zonai king Rauru founded Hyrule Kingdom with Sonia, a Hylian priestess. Like Rauru, Mineru inherited a Secret Stone from her ancestors. However, by the time of Rauru's reign, he and Mineru were the only Zonai remaining, the rest having perished. During Rauru's reign, while the kingdom flourished, Mineru danced while Rauru sang at a celebration, as recorded on an Ancient Tablet by Lenalia, a royal chamberlain. Mineru frequently spent so much time reading Books that she would forget to eat. She also researched and created Constructs, particularly one that could hold her Spirit if her body failed. It is not clear if Mineru was solely responsible for the invention of the Constructs, but they were at the very least created while she and Rauru were alive. thumb|left|250px|alt= Closeup shot of Mineru.|Mineru when meeting Zelda in her study After Zelda arrived in the Era of Foundation, Rauru believed Mineru might be able to assist Zelda return to her home era. Upon meeting Zelda, Mineru expressed interest in the Purah Pad and held onto it for research, intending to restore its travel functionality. Mineru posited that the Secret Stone Zelda found allowed her to travel through Time. Though she sensed Zelda had both Light and Time powers, the Secret Stone only amplified the Time power. However, since Zelda lacked full control over her Time power to return home, Mineru thought of another method, remembering stories of the forbidden act of Draconification: "To swallow a secret stone is to become an immortal dragon... one blessed with eternal life." However, since the act was forbidden because it would cause one to lose their sense of self, Mineru discounted this as a way to help Zelda. Rauru suggested that Zelda learning to hone her power with Sonia could help solve the problem instead. While living in the past, Zelda visited Mineru with Lenalia. Mineru showed them her greatest Construct, and Zelda wanted to try riding it. Although Lenalia objected, Zelda nevertheless rode upon its shoulders, which amused Lenalia. Some time later, after Ganondorf slew Sonia and stole her Secret Stone to become the Demon King, Rauru gathered with Mineru, Zelda, and the leaders of the Gerudo, Goron, Zora and Rito tribes at the Forgotten Temple. Knowing they would have to face the Demon King, Mineru offered support from her and the others to Rauru. The four leaders received their Secret Stones and became Sages, and alongside Mineru (the Sage of Spirit) and Zelda (the Sage of Time) swore to serve Rauru. thumb|right|320px|alt=Zelda rushing to Mineru's side.|Mineru after being poisoned by Gloom The Sages confronted Demon King Ganondorf, but failed to stop him, so Rauru sacrificed himself to seal Ganondorf for millennia. thumb|right|320px|alt=Zelda rushing to Mineru's side.|Mineru after being poisoned by Gloom The Sages confronted Demon King Ganondorf, but failed to stop him, so Rauru sacrificed himself to seal Ganondorf for millennia. Although she and the other Sages survived, Mineru was gravely damaged by his Gloom in the battle and knew that her body would not last much longer. Resting in her study, Zelda brought her the Decayed Master Sword that had traveled through time. When Zelda told her that the Master Sword could heal itself over time, Mineru replied that it would take an impossibly long time to do so. Mineru initially objected to Zelda's suggestion of draconifying herself to bathe the sword in sacred power, but upon Zelda's insistence agreed to do what she could to assist Link in the far future, acknowledging that she bore some responsibility as a Zonai. Wanting to be ready for the future, Zelda and Mineru created a plan to raise the Temple of Time into the Sky so that it would be safe for Link in the distant future. Lenalia also asked Mineru to raise the Ancient Tablets so that they would be preserved for the future. Mineru herself wrote information on the Sages and a clue on where to find Zonai Relic on Stone Slabs at what would later become the Ring Ruins. Mineru's Spirit entered the Purah Pad, which Zelda gave to the care of a Steward Construct before swallowing her Secret Stone to become the Light Dragon. The other Sages, possibly including Mineru elevated the Temple of Time and the land surrounding it, creating the Great Sky Island, as well as raising Lenalia's Ancient Tablets. Mineru's Spirit then remained dormant in the Purah Pad for millennia. Mineru originally intended to awake as soon as Link found the Purah Pad and guide him to a pre-built Crafter Construct. Mineru thus waits for Link to discover the Zonai Relic stored on Dragonhead Island, so that Link can take it to the Construct Factory and build a new body for her. Upon doing so, she guides him to complete the new Construct. When Mineru's Construct is complete, she guides Link to the Spirit Temple in her new Construct body with the goal of recaliming her Secret Stone of Spirit. Although the path through the Depths contains many Monsters and obstacles, they make use of Mineru's Construct to overcome them. is a character in . Biography Mino is a member of Squad One of the Monster-Control Crew, which is led by Hoz. He attacks a Monster Stronghold south of the Hyrule Garrison Ruins with the rest of his squad during the Side Adventure "Bring Peace to Hyrule Field!". If Link tries to speak to him, he will say that he is on duty and cannot chat. He wields a Wooden Mop, which he fights with during battle. When "Bring Peace to Hyrule Field!" is completed, Mino will travel with the rest of his squad to Fort Hateno, starting the Side Adventure "Bring Peace to Necluda!".

is a recurring character in . Biography Mipha was the princess of the Zora, a friend of Link, and one of the Champions. She is described as being kind and soft spoken. She has a gift for healing, known as Mipha's Grace. She was the only daughter of King Dorephan and the elder sister of Sidon. When Mipha was born, Dento crafted the Lightscale Trident for her. When she grew older, she began to take lessons from the royal guard of the Zora, which led to them becoming fond of her. In particular, Seggin loved Mipha as though she were his own daughter, and he taught her how to use her Lightscale Trident. Her skills with the Trident were described as being in a class of their own. She also received tutelage from Muzu, who she was close with. Mipha met Link when he joined a group of Hylian diplomats visiting Zora's Domain at the age of four. She was surprised by how energetic he seemed and impressed he was talented enough to best adults at swordsmanship. Due to his recklessness, Mipha would heal his bruises with her Grace. She found the way he looked up at her to be adorable. As part of King Rhoam's excavations, Divine Beast Vah Ruta was discovered at Zora's Domain. When she heard of this news, Mipha rushed to go see it. Witnesses claimed that Mipha had a sparkle in her eyes when she saw the Divine Beast, which Mipha claims is due to finding it cute. She then spoke to Vah Ruta as though they were friends. Mipha found it interesting to imagine the person who piloted the Divine Beast for 10,000 years ago, and she wondered who would do so next. As a Hylian, Link grew up faster than Mipha did. When he returned to Zora's Domain with the Master Sword, Mipha was proud of him, but she was concerned by how rarely he spoke and smiled. When she asked how he was, Link shook his head at her, and Mipha felt as though he were looking past her. Zelda came to Zora's Domain, where she asked Mipha if she would be the Champion of Divine Beast Vah Ruta. Mipha was overjoyed and, feeling a sense of duty to stop Calamity Ganon, agreed to Zelda's request. Not only did she feel compelled to defend Zora's Domain and the rest of Hyrule against Calamity Ganon, Mipha also wanted to help Link. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Mipha kneeling to speak with a young Sidon atop Veiled Falls. Princess Zelda stands behind them.|Mipha speaking to a young Sidon at Veiled Falls During the "Champion Mipha's Song" EX Recovered Memory, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack, Mipha and Zelda can be seen standing together on top of Veiled Falls. pack, Mipha and Zelda can be seen standing together on top of Veiled Falls. She asks Zelda who her fellow Champions are, and Zelda describes Daruk, Revali, and Urbosa to her. Looking down the Waterfall, Mipha sees Sidon paddling in the Water, and she yells for him to Swim up to them. Zelda believes he may be too young to do so on his own, but Mipha states that she will have to leave him to pilot Divine Beast Vah Ruta. At the top of the Waterfall, Mipha kneels beside Sidon and tells him that, if anything happens to her, it will be his duty to protect Zora's Domain. Sidon smiles in response. Mipha expresses her belief in him before asking if he would like to try Swimming up the Waterfall again. In order to become a Champion, Mipha was tasked with undertaking a Divine Beast Tamer's Trial to prove she was worthy of taming a Divine Beast. This Trial included Swimming through a Glowing Ring in the Lanayru Sea, fighting Guardians in Upland Zorana, and Swimming through Glowing Rings on the Waterfalls of Mikau Lake and Lulu Lake. For the first Trial, she kept a note describing when the Glowing Ring would appear, which she would often repeat to herself. The next time Link visited Zora's Domain, Mipha told him about the Lynel on Ploymus Mountain, which had been causing trouble for the Zora. Link immediately left for Ploymus Mountain, and Mipha followed after him. Link tried to convince Mipha to leave the fight to him, but their arguing led to the Lynel ambushing them. He then defeated the Lynel with the Master Sword, which fascinated Mipha. Inspired by his strength and desire to help others, Mipha realized that she was in love with Link. This event would later be documented in the History of the Zora, Part Seven. Zelda also notes that Mipha had the easiest time mastering her Divine Beast. Due to Muzu's dislike of Hylians, Mipha never told him about her feelings for Link. Despite this, she still prepared Zora Armor for Link, which is traditionally given by Zora princesses to the man they will marry. She considered giving it to him during his next visit to Zora's Domain, but she had doubts about doing so. She took hope from a legend about a Zora princess falling in love with a Hylian swordsman. Since she and Link would be on their own, she planned on riding Divine Beast Vah Ruta's trunk together during the sunset. thumb|left|250px|A screenshot of Mipha healing Link's wounds while they sit on Divine Beast Vah Ruta.|Mipha and Link on Divine Beast Vah Ruta Their meeting can be seen during "Mipha's Touch," which is the 10th Recovered Memory. She appears dismayed to hear the Zelda failed to unlock her sealing power at the Spring of Wisdom. Revali flies into the air to investigate, discovering that Calamity Ganon has emerged from below Hyrule Castle. To reach Divine Beast Vah Ruta during the Great Calamity, Mipha swam through the Lanayru Wetlands and up Zora River. By the time she arrived, Vah Ruta had already been overtaken by Waterblight Ganon. When they did, the Trident began to glow, and Mipha's voice was heard. She told them to stop grieving and crying over her, instead, they should focus on remembering. Due to this, the Zora began to celebrate the Champion Festival on the anniversary of the Great Calamity. Mipha's Statue was also erected in her honor in the Zora's Domain Square. Since her death during the Great Calamity, Mipha's spirit has been trapped within Divine Beast Vah Ruta. When Link enters Vah Ruta during the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" Main Quest, Mipha's voice can be heard. She is happy that the day has finally arrived to free her Divine Beast. She directs Link to Ruta's Guidance Stone, where he can obtain a Map. Once all of the Terminals are active, Mipha tells Link to start the Main Control Unit, though she warns him not to let his guard down. is a location in . Features and Overview Mipha Court is a park that is situated on top of Ploymus Mountain in the Lanayru Great Spring. It consists of a fountain surrounded by three pools of Water, one of which flows down into a Waterfall that eventually leads to Zora's Domain. A walkway with flowing Water leads up to Shatterback Point, where Mipha's Statue has been enshrined. It utilizes the same architectural style that other pieces of Zora construction do. The Mipha Court Security Report can be found on a Table next to an unlit Campfire, which is located on the northeastern side of the park. Prior to defeating Mucktorok in the Water Temple, a stream of Sludge will fall on the Court, and several piles can be found surrounding the park's Water. The creation of Mipha Court is detailed in the Learnings of the Zora, Part Six. After Link defeated the Lynel that previously inhabited Ploymus Mountain, Water began to flow from the area. As a result, the Zora decided to construct a park on the Mountain. They considered multiple names while clearing the grounds, such as "Zora Park" and "Ploymus Park". When the Zora asked Sidon for an idea, he suggested Mipha Court in honor of his sister, Mipha. They agreed with this name, and work on the park continued. After Sludge began falling in the Lanayru Great Spring, Sidon took up residence in Mipha Court, where he uses his Power of Water to purify the Water flowing toward Zora's Domain. This has resulted in Mikau Lake and Lulu Lake being clean of Sludge. At the beginning of the Main Quest "Sidon of the Zora", Yona suggests that Link visit Sidon. When Link first arrives at Mipha Court, he will find Gaddison and Rivan guarding Sidon as he purifies the Water. Sidon is happy to be reunited with Link, To help Link in the Search for Princess Zelda, Sidon directs him to meet with Jiahto at Toto Lake. He also invites Link to visit him at Mipha Court whenever he wants. When Link returns to Mipha Court after completing the Main Quest "Clues to the Sky", he finds Sidon in a discussion with Yona. He is trying to convince her to leave due to danger in the area, but Yona insists that she needs to talk to him. After Link updates Sidon about his progress, Yona states that the two of them should continue their investigation together. However, they are soon after attacked by the Sludge Like, and Link and Sidon must work together in order to defeat it. Following this, Yona is able to help Sidon overcome his fear of losing her, and he departs Mipha Court with Link. Yona and her attendants, Chroma and Khira, take over purifying the Water for him. They are used to activate or remove Sun Switches and subsequently reveal chests and open doors by reflecting light onto them. Mirrors will reflect light from an open light source above, or from light coming from another Mirror. The cobra-shaped Mirrors can be turned around by pushing or pulling the handles on their sides, which will redirect the light to another direction. On the fourth floor is a large, circular mirror hanging from the wall and tilted downward. Link must use multiple cobra Mirrors and direct their reflected light onto this Mirror, which will shine a spot of light onto the floor below it. Link can then use the Mirror Shield to reflect this light onto a Sun Switch, activating a lift that will lower him down to the boss room door. In , Mirrors appear in the Stone Tower Temple. Like the Mirrors in , they are used to reflect light from Link's Mirror Shield, but function a little differently. Instead of instantly reflecting light beamed onto them, the Mirrors will absorb the light reflected onto their surface. When Link lowers his shield, the Mirrors will then beam the absorbed light ahead. Link can then use these beams of light to reflect it elsewhere using his Mirror Shield, which can be used to remove Sun Blocks. The longer Link reflects light onto a Mirror, the longer it will beam it back before it fades. In , Mirrors appear throughout the second half of the Earth Temple. They are used to reflect light and remove walls and stone statues that bare a swirl symbol. The Mirrors are in the shape of scorpions, and a few can be pushed or pulled to bring them closer to a light source and to redirect the flow of light. Some Mirrors require that Link shine light onto them with the Mirror Shield, or Medli with her harp. In the later part of the temple, Link must use multiple Mirrors to direct a continuous flow of light, so that Link and Medli can use the light to illuminate the eyes of a Sun-Moon statue in the chamber. The is a recurring Shield in . It is a powerful Shield that allows Link to reflect Light Beams or Magic from one place to another. Location and Uses In , the Mirror Shield is the strongest Shield that Link can obtain and is found in Turtle Rock. It is better than the previous two shields, known for its ability to stop beams, such as those fired by Laser Eyes, and attacks from enemies such as Lynels, and it can even reflect Wizzrobe projectiles. However, it cannot stop the beams of a Beamos. It is very large, with only half of Link's body being visible behind it during gameplay. It cannot be stolen by Pikits, but in , it can be still eaten by Like Like. Because of this, a shop in the Dark World will sell a replacement Mirror Shield if Link loses it in this version of the game. In , the Mirror Shield is found in Eagle's Tower. Because the Shield can protect its user from Fire, Wind and lasers from Beamos, it is essential for getting to the last Dungeon, Turtle Rock, as it is used to pass through Fires. The Mirror Shield is also unable to be eaten by Like Likes. In , the Mirror Shield is the final shield that Link acquires in his adventure. It is found in the Spirit Temple on a ledge that can only be reached after defeating an Iron Knuckle in the Adult Link portion of the temple. Unlike the Hylian Shield, the Mirror Shield has a polished surface, allowing it to reflect light. This allows Link to solve the light puzzles in the Dungeon, by reflecting beams of light at Sun Switches. Otherwise, the Mirror Shield acts the same except for the fact that it also destroys the projectiles spat at Link by Octoroks, Deku Scrubs, and Business Scrubs, instead of reflecting them. The Mirror Shield is also unable to be eaten by Like Likes. It can somewhat reflect one of Ganondorf's light magic attacks. The Mirror Shield also plays an important part in defeating Twinrova, the boss of the Spirit Temple. When Koume and Kotake are separate, the Mirror Shield can be used to reflect - and in turn, direct to the other sister - the fire or ice beam that a sister will fire at Link to cause damage. When in their combined form, the Mirror Shield can absorb Twinrova's energies, and after three of the same type of energy is absorbed, a beam of that element is fired that can stun Twinrova temporarily for a quick few slashes. The original version of the Mirror Shield resembled the real-world symbol, but this was changed in later releases and remakes to the Crest of the Gerudo because of Nintendo's policy of avoiding real-world religious imagery. Comparison of the two different versions of the Mirror Shield In , the Mirror Shield appears depicted as a decagonal shield with a picture of an unhappy or screaming face upon it.

is a recurring character in . Biography Misa is a Rito woman who owns The Slippery Falcon in Rito Village. She is assisted by her son Fyson before he leaves for Tarrey Town, and she wants him to take over the General Store one day. Misa can always be found at the back of The Slippery Falcon, and she welcomes Link when he walks inside. When spoken to, she will repeat her greetings to Link. She then asks what he needs from her. If Link asks about The Slippery Falcon's stock, Misa explains that they provide everything from self-defense Items to Cooking ingredients. She encourages Link to buy her ingredients, and she allows him to read her Recipe Book to learn how to use them. When Link makes a purchase at The Slippery Falcon, Misa will thank him. If he buys the entire stock of one product, Misa promises to replace it soon. Like other vendors, Link can also sell his own Items to Misa. When she buys one of Link's Items, she gladly gives him his Rupees and thanks him. At the end of their conversation, Misa encourages Link to return.
