is an unseen character in . Biography Misko is a bandit who has left their treasure hidden across Hyrule. Link never meets or sees Misko, and they can only be learned about through their treasure. When Link tries to talk to Prissen and Domidak at the Dueling Peaks Stable, they will be discussing a lead on Misko's treasure, before stopping when they notice Link is listening to them. If Link persists on discussing the treasure, Domidak will confirm they are looking for Misko's treasure, but he will not tell Link about the lead for free. If Link pays 100 Rupees that Domidak asks for, he will share a riddle that describes a "little twin" stepping over a "little river". Domidak explains that Misko hid the location of the treasure using a riddle, and he mentions that the person he had heard the riddle from can eventually be linked to an underling of Misko. Learning the riddle begins the "Misko, the Great Bandit" Side Quest. If Downloadable Content Pack is installed, Misko's EX Journal will appear in the Outpost Ruins. The Book was written by Misko to note down the locations of eight Treasure Chests containing priceless relics that they stole from Hyrule Castle. Obtaining the stolen relics is the goal of four Side Quests: "EX Treasure: Ancient Mask," "EX Treasure: Fairy Clothes," "EX Treasure: Twilight Relic," and "EX Treasure: Phantasma." If Downloadable Content Pack is installed, Misko's EX Journal 2 will appear in the Deya Village Ruins. In this Book, Misko wrote down clues to where they had hidden six more Treasure Chests containing priceless relics that they had stolen from Hyrule Castle. Retrieving the relics that Misko stole is the goal of four Side Quests: "EX Treasure: Merchant Hood," "EX Treasure: Garb of Winds," "EX Treasure: Usurper King," and "EX Treasure: Dark Armor."

, also known as , are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . They are among the most common enemies throughout the series, having appeared in the majority of games, and are prolific in Ganon's army. Early in the series, Moblins originally resembled anthropomorphic bulldogs, but beginning in , have increasingly acquired more pig- and -like features. In all of their appearances, Moblins are characteristically depicted as using spears or javelins as their main weapon. They are abundant in forests but also occasionally appear inside mountains and dungeons. In the 2D Zelda games, Moblins are often depicted as common foot soldiers encountered early in the game. In the 3D console Zelda games, Moblins are instead depicted as elite enemies capable of performing powerful attacks who may engage in full combat with Link. These Moblins usually require more careful or precise attacks to defeat. While Moblins have changed little aside from their visual appearance throughout the series, some variants of the standard Moblin have also appeared. These include the Club Moblin, exclusive to ; the Spear and Bow Moblins, which specialize in spears and Bows, respectively; and the Shield Moblin, which carry large Shields. In , , and , both bulldog- and pig-like Moblins appear. To differentiate between the two, the pig-like Moblins in those games are known as Boarblins. The King Moblin and Great Moblin are two notable Moblins that have appeared in the series. Other related species with similar names include the Bokoblin, Miniblin, Bulblin and Big Blin. Moblins attack by swiping, stabbing, or crushing Link with their spears, which can inflict varying amounts of damage depending on the attack. These attacks also lowers the Moblin's defense, provided if Link can find a safe opening to strike back. Moblins have immense reach with their spears, but their wide swings mean that two or more Moblins in proximity are likely to injure or even kill each other or other enemies. If disarmed, a Moblin proceeds to unleash mighty, lightning-fast punches until it gets its spear back. These attacks send Link flying as he is hit. Moblins may also punch Link in certain instances followed by a spear attack, such as when Link raises his Shield. Link, however, will not sustain any damage from this punch. Moblins are also adept at handling a frontal assault by defending with their spears, so attacking from the sides or back is recommended. If Link strikes the rear-end, the Moblin will comically cry out and briefly hop around, due to the pain inflicted in a delicate place. Notably, Moblins are afraid of explosives, and will flee in terror if Link takes out a Bomb while engaged with a Moblin. They will return to the fight once the Bomb explodes. Here, a group of Moblins raid Rauru Town in hopes of trying to find out the location of the Potion of Power and thus revive their master, Ganon. After Link, Princess Zelda and Kevin defeat all of the Moblins and save a woman's son from the grasp of the Moblin leader, the woman rewards the heroes with a map that helps them on their quest of retrieving the Potion of Power before Ganon's minions get to it. Although a Moblin also appears in "Once Upon a Time Machine" and "The Trojan Dragon" episodes, it only plays a minor role. In both of these episodes, Simon Belmont of the Castlevania series bumps into this foe while walking through the woods in Hyrule. These Moblins do not seem to be as clumsy as the ones portrayed in the Zelda animated series. The Legend of Zelda (Valiant Comics) thumb|right|120px|A Moblin in the Legend of Zelda comic The Moblins in the appear to be modeled after their artwork depiction in . Unlike the cartoons, these foes play a very minor role in all of the comic's issues. A Moblin makes an appearance in "Assault" with a slightly more significant role. In this story, a Moblin goes to inform Ganon that Link managed to defeat a pack of his fellow fiends to get past his outpost. Ganon punishes the Moblin for failing to capture the young hero and says that only he is allowed to destroy Link. They are also briefly seen in "Missing in Action", To the First Power, and Queen of Hearts. In , Moblins continue to serve under Ganon's orders and try to eliminate Princess Zelda on her quest to obtain the three items necessary to free Link from the Crystal. They always appear in groups, right behind Ganon, willing to attack as soon as the evil wizard commands them. At one point in the book, if Zelda enters Madame Grusha's fortune-telling hut, she will discover that the fortune-teller is actually a Wizzrobe in disguise who commands the Moblins to attack and kill the princess. However, Zelda easily defeats both the Moblin and the Wizzrobe with the use of her Bow. Once Link and Zelda find the Spear stuck in one

fortune-telling hut, she will discover that the fortune-teller is actually a Wizzrobe in disguise who commands the Moblins to attack and kill the princess. However, Zelda easily defeats both the Moblin and the Wizzrobe with the use of her Bow. Once Link and Zelda find the Spear stuck in one of the trees of the forest, Ganon and his gang of Moblin begin to quickly approach the heroes, but with the help of Zelda's friend Greenbeard, they are able to obtain the Spear and stop the Moblin right on their path. With the defeat of Ganon at the hands of Link, the Moblins disappear as well. See also: Moblin Boss and Nilbom the Tailor The Moblins in not only serve Ganon, but also a Moblin Boss who commands them to destroy Link in order to satisfy their master. These creatures play a much bigger role in this book, being capable of disguising themselves as humans and thus trick Link into thinking that they are there to help him. Both Princess Zelda and Link are first attacked by a gang of Moblins as they are walking through the woods. Although they defeat the first few monsters quite easily, Zelda runs out of Arrows for her Bow and ultimately gets knocked out by a rock thrown at her by one of the Moblins. Link goes after her but trips and tumbles to the ground, and just as he is about to be killed by a Moblin, a tall, dark man known as Charles saves him by commanding the Moblin to leave. Later on in the book, if Link chooses to go through the Midoro Swamp on his way to the Town of Ruto, he will once again get ambushed by a group of Moblins; however, with the help of the Golden Whistle, he is able to weaken them with its high-piercing sound. One of the Moblins then offers Link a Magic Potion in exchange that the young hero stops whistling. Once Charles of Moria runs away to the Midoro Swamp with the Triforce of Wisdom in hand, Link will follow him there only to find that Charles, who is actually Ganon in disguise, has an army of Moblins that quickly surround Link. Just as the Moblins are drawing in to attack the young hero, Link uses his Sword to slash Charles's Necklace in two, thus defeating the false Morian knight. The Moblins, now with their leader gone, all suddenly scatter away into the clearing. Moblins are known as Moblin Spearthrowers in . They are common soldiers of Ganon's army and appear throughout the lands of Koridai. Lupay enslaves Koridians and turns them into Moblins by replacing their souls with Rubies. Moblins are known as Spear Throwing Moblins in . They are common soldiers of Ganon's army and appear throughout the lands of Gamelon. In , Moblins appear as large ogre-like monsters carrying large spears. They do not throw their spears when they see Princess Zelda and instead walk in a random path.

known as Spear Throwing Moblins in . They are common soldiers of Ganon's army and appear throughout the lands of Gamelon. In , Moblins appear as large ogre-like monsters carrying large spears. They do not throw their spears when they see Princess Zelda and instead walk in a random path. They are described as being "stupid and slow." They are encountered in the Forest of Ogbam and its surrounding areas. (Himekawa) Moblins make an appearance in the , being summoned by the Twinrova witches alongside some Lizalfos to try and slow Link down. Moblins also appear as minions of the Baku Tree, alongside some Wolfos, with Mido stumbling upon one after declaring himself to be the true hero. Moblins appear as a Sticker in . Sticker Information |} Moblins appear as medium-strong enemies, closely based on the Wooden Shield and Metal Shield Moblins of . Wooden Shield Moblins are simply referred to as Moblins, whereas the Metal Shield variant are called Shield Moblins. Both types are equipped with spears that they use to powerfully attack their opponents. They often try to belly flop onto their enemies, either by charging their spear and furiously spinning forward, or by simply jumping towards them. Their fall creates a small shock wave which interrupts any actions currently being done by Warriors if they are unable to dodge it. Aside from the design of Shield, the two variants are otherwise identical with little difference between them. In , Moblin appears as a Spirit with no trait. In , Moblins are strong enemies that pose a threat to Cadence, Link, Yves and Zelda both at close range and at a distance. They carry spears, which they will throw at the heroes while moving to the beat of the music. Their beat pattern involves them moving on every other music beat, always crouching before hopping on the next beat as they make their way towards them. When they get close enough, they will pause on one beat to aim their spear, throwing it on the second beat and letting it land on the third. Once it lands, they will try to retrieve their weapon until it is either destroyed or picked up by another Moblin. After they lose their spear, they will try to attack the player head on. There are a total of four variants of Moblin, with Red Moblins, Black Moblins, and Purple Moblins being their stronger counterparts. Regardless of species, all of their spears can be picked up by the heroes at any time with the glove, and throwing it will do double the Moblin's attack damage against any enemy, but at the cost of taking two beats to land. Moblins appear as recurring Bosses in multiple Scenarios. Defeating them is often a main objectives of missions they appear in. Moblins can be encountered as Powerful Enemies in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Moblin Arms are detached Moblin bones that continue to move after being separated from the body. They are dropped by Stalmoblins after being defeated by Link. They can be used as two-handed Weapons, but are very brittle and will easily break. Moblin Arms are made of bone, which means they will not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during a Thunderstorm, can not be picked up using the Magnesis Rune, and will not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will also float if dropped in Water. Moblin Arms reappear in . Other Appearances

They can be used in a Cooking Pot with critters to make Elixirs. The Kochi Dye Shop can also use Moblin Fangs to make Gray Dye, and Kilton at the Fang and Bone accepts them in exchange for Mon. The Fireproof Armor set needs four Moblin Fangs to upgrade each of its pieces to their second tier at a Great Fairy Fountain. Moblin Fangs are dropped by Moblins upon their defeat. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Moblin Horns are dropped by Moblins and Stalmoblins upon defeat. They are useful as Ingredients in creating various Elixirs. The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Moblin Mask is a piece of Armor that can be purchased from Kilton at the Fang and Bone shop for 199 Mon after freeing one Divine Beast. It cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy, nor can it be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. When worn, it grants Link the Disguise Added Effect, allowing him to blend in with Moblins. However, the Moblin Mask does not prevent other Enemies in the same area from attacking Link. It also makes quiet Moblin sounds as Link moves around. While wearing the Moblin Mask, Link adopts a new idle pose to match that of a Moblin. The Moblin Mask returns in , functioning the same as it did in . It can be obtained from Koltin's Stall for two Bubbul Gems after completing "The Hunt for Bubbul Gems!" and "The Search for Koltin". Subsequent Moblin Masks can be purchased from Cece for 4000 Rupees. Other Appearances The Moblin Mask is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and is obtained when the Warriors complete the Quest "Cold Desert Nights". The mask was made by the merchant of Fang and Bone to replicate an actual Moblin.

is a recurring character in . Biography Modar is a Goron who resides at the Tanagar Canyon Course in Tanagar Canyon. He wears a Helmet on his head, and he carries a Mallet. Modar operates the Boom Bam Golf Mini-Game. He invented the Mini-Game after rolling down a hill, making him the only person to play it. Despite this, he claims that it is famous and anyone who plays it is unable to get enough. When Link first speaks to Modar, he is surprised to see a Hylian and reasons that he must be tough. Due to this, he asks Link if he is interested in trying out Boom Bam Golf. If Link refuses to play Boom Bam Golf at any time, Modar will be disappointed, but he welcomes Link to come back in the future. If Link asks what it is, Modar is shocked that he has never heard of it. However, after explaining that he only invented it a few days ago, Modar realizes that it makes sense for Link to be unfamiliar with it. He explains that the goal is to hit the Ball into the hole at the end of the Tanagar Canyon Course, which is marked by a Big Flag. Link will score higher the fewer tries it takes him to achieve this, and it costs 20 Rupees to participate. To send the Ball a great distance, Modar suggests using two-handed Weapons, such as Hammers. To move the Ball a short distance, Modar says to use one-handed Weapons, but he must be careful not to break them. If the Ball is knocked off the Tanagar Canyon Course, Modar will inflict a one-stroke penalty from Link, and it will be returned to its previous location. Modar will keep track of Link's strokes, but he must hit the Ball into the hole in less than 20. He tells Link that the further he can hit the Ball along the Course, the better it will be for his score. Finally, Modar explains that any movement from the Ball counts as a stroke, at which point he realizes that the rules are not as simple as he thought. He then asks Link if he will play Boom Bam Golf. If Link agrees to play Boom Bam Golf, Modar will be excited. Before they can start, he asks Link to pay the fee of 20 Rupees. Once Link does so, Modar will take a moment to set up the Mini-Game. After this, the Mini-Game will begin. When Link speaks to Modar during the Mini-Game, he assumes that he wants to stop playing. If Link refuses to give up, Modar states that Boom Bam Golfers never say die. Similarly, if Link leaves the Tanagar Canyon Course, Modar calls out and warns him that the game will end if he goes any further. Should Link ignore this and continue to leave the Course, Modar will disqualify him, telling him that he should have said something if he wanted to stop playing. If

leaves the Tanagar Canyon Course, Modar calls out and warns him that the game will end if he goes any further. Should Link ignore this and continue to leave the Course, Modar will disqualify him, telling him that he should have said something if he wanted to stop playing. If Link does not reach the goal in 20 strokes, Modar will cut him off. He is saddened to see someone accumulate 20 strokes, especially since he was rooting for Link. After Link completes a round, Modar will bring him back to the beginning of the Tanagar Canyon Course to tally his score. If it took Link 11 or more strokes to reach the goal, Modar will be disappointed, saying that Boom Bam Golf is not that hard. He tells Link not to give up and encourages him to keep practicing. If Link hits the Ball into the goal in six to 10 strokes, Modar states his belief that he can do better. He assures Link that it takes time to become good at something, and he gives him a Red Rupee as a reward. If Link reaches the goal in four to five shots, Modar remarks that he is becoming a heavyweight. He tells Link to keep trying to set the Boom Bam Golf record, giving him a Purple Rupee as a reward. Finally, if Link reaches the goal in three or less strokes, Modar will be impressed, saying he could be a professional if there were Boom Bam Golf leagues. While he cannot recall his exact score, Modar believes it was close to Link's. He thinks that Link is the type of player who could make Boom Bam Golf popular, and he encourages him to keep playing. He gives Link a Silver Rupee as a reward. After giving Link his reward, Modar believes that Link looks like he wants to play Boom Bam Golf again. If Link refuses, Modar will be disappointed, but he is pleased that Link was able to see the majesty of the Mini-Game for himself.

is a recurring character in . Biography Moggs and his wife Monari are Hylians who reside in Tarrey Town. They move to Tarrey Town after Fyson opens the Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch), and they live in the House behind Ore and More. He owns two Hylian Retrievers, which can be found behind his home. During the day, he walks throughout Town. At night, he sleeps in one of the Beds in his House. When Link first speaks to Moggs, he is pleased to see someone so young visiting Tarrey Town. If Link asks who he is, he introduces himself. He explains that he is retired, and he came to Tarrey Town after hearing a rumor about it. He is glad he did so, and he has even noticed that his Hylian Retrievers seem happier. He invites Link to speak with him at any time. When Link speaks to Moggs again, he asks him to stay and chat with him. If Link asks about his family, Moggs explains that his son who has left to travel the world. While their home feels empty without him, Moggs believes it has brought him closer to Monari. Before Link has completed the "A Parent's Love" Side Quest, Moggs states that he hears Hagie and Ruli fighting during the night. He has considered listening in from behind their House, but he does not want to be nosy. After the Side Quest has been completed, Moggs claims that he has not heard Hagie and Ruli arguing lately. He states that with every obstacle they face together, their relationship grows stronger. Following this conversation, Link can ask Moggs about Monari, who he claims is likely wandering around Tarrey Town. He claims that she is great at Cooking, and he especially likes her Mushroom Skewer. He suggests that Link speak with her if he has the time. If Link asks about his pets, Moggs claims to be talking about the Hylian Retrievers behind his House. He has noticed that they enjoy the clean air of Akkala, which makes him glad that they moved. When Link speaks to Moggs after 9:00 PM, he explains that he is going to Bed and asks to be excused. He may also invite Link to talk to him the next day.

is a character in . Biography Mokka is one of several Koroks who appear in the Great Hyrule Forest Depths during the Main Quest "Trail of the Master Sword". They are located at the northern end of Minshi Grove. Previously, Mokka left Korok Forest to go on a walk with Tasho, Mopu, Nako, Raha, Jatora, and Maheli, but they found they were unable to pass through the Lost Woods upon their return. As a result, the group decided to enter the Minshi Woods Chasm to try and reach Korok Forest from the Depths, leaving Tasho behind on the Surface. When Link speaks to Mokka, they point out that the Fog on the ceiling is the same one found in the Lost Woods, and they take it as a sign that they are close to Korok Forest.

, also known as Innards of a Molduga, are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Molduga Guts can be obtained by defeating Molduga, which can be found under the sand in the Gerudo Desert. They can be used in a Cooking Pot along with critters to make Elixirs. In addition, they can be sold to Kilton at the Fang and Bone in exchange for Mon or used as an ingredient for Green Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop. When spoken to, Malena explains to Link that her husband is sick and the only cure is Molduga Guts. After, Link receives the Side Quest "Medicinal Molduga". Upon delivery of Molduga Guts, Malena will reward Link with a Gold Rupee. The Radiant Set requires Molduga Guts to be upgraded to its third tier at a Great Fairy Fountain. Location and Uses After Link has completed the Side Quests "WANTED: Hinox", "WANTED: Molduga", "WANTED: Stone Talus", "Unknown Huge Silhouette", "Unknown Sky Giant", ane "Unknown Three-Headed Monster", he is able to talk to Gralens about Molduga in the Emergency Shelter. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Molida Island is an Island in the Southwestern Sea in . The southern portion of the Island is populated, whereas the northern territory is a wild grove. The Wayfarer's Words can be found scattered throughout the Island, which many of the inhabitants find to be a nuisance. The Shovel can be found in a cave on the Island, which is required for finding a safe route through the foggy passage in the Northwestern Sea. Molida Island also bears the Temple of Courage, which can be found on the back of the isle. To access it, Link needs a Salvage Arm from Eddo on Cannon Island, as Link needs the Sun Key, which is hidden underwater. Before Link can return to Molida Island with the Salvage Arm, a Giant Eye Plant will appear and guard the Island. Molida Island is also where Link will find the Shooting Range, which is unlocked after clearing the Temple of Courage. In addition, three small portions of land east of the Island can be accessed by blowing up a Wooden Box, or by making a ropebridge between the wooden box and the stone sign, retrieving the Cucco within with the Grappling Hook, then using the Cucco to fly there. With the help of the Shovel, a Treasure Map can be unveiled from the ground at the roots of a tree on the second small island. On the smaller island to the left of the treasure map, there is a smaller island that has a Big Red Rupee which can be obtained by using the shovel in the middle of the island. Two Big Green Rupees can be found in patches of dirt inside the Old Wayfarer's hideaway. A third Big Green Rupee can be found by digging just under the Tree south of Romanos and Maronie's house. Areas Enemies Inhabitants Molida Island is located in the Lanayru Wetlands in . It is surrounded by the Shallow Water of the Wetlands, though it is still connected to Kincean Island to the north by a wooden bridge. Molida Island itself is uninhabited, and it is only covered by a few Trees. One Treasure Chest can be found on Molida Island. Link can come across it underneath the bridge connecting to Kincean Island. When the Chest is opened, Link will receive an Opal. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

is a recurring character in . Biography Molli is a young Rito child who lives in Rito Village. She is the daughter of Harth, and since she is close in age to Tulin, their families spend a lot of time together. During the day, she sits on a ledge on the north end of the Village. At night, she sleeps in the House that she shares with her father. When Link approaches Molli, he will find her talking about a Bird. If spoken to, she asks Link if he wants to hear a story. Should Link state that he loves stories, Molli reveals that she does as well. Her story begins with her Grandpa stopping at a big Cedar Tree on top of a mountain and looking to the northwest. When he did so, he saw a huge white Bird, which he started flying towards. Drawing close to the Bird, he saw something in its stomach. When Link prompts Molli to reveal what the Bird swallowed, Molli admits that she gets tired during this part of the story and does not remember. However, she states that she knows the location of the Cedar Tree where her Grandpa stopped. She points out the Cedar Tree on Talonto Peak. Molli tries to recall what the Bird swallowed, and she laments not being able to hear the story from her grandfather. After this, "The Bird in the Mountains" Shrine Quest will begin. If Link speaks to Molli while the Shrine Quest is active, she asks if he wants to hear the story again. If Link agrees, Molli will repeat the story for him. Afterwards, Molli resolves to find out for herself what the Bird swallowed when she grows up. After locating Mozo Shenno Shrine and completing the Shrine Quest, Link can return to Rito Village to share his findings with Molli. When Link reveals that he found an Ancient Shrine, Molli is shocked to hear that the Bird was actually the Biron Snowshelf in the Hebra Mountains. She then recalls that her Grandpa was always a prankster. When Link speaks to Molli again, she will thank Link for helping her rediscover the ending to her Grandpa's story. Now, she is capable of reciting the entire story on her own, and she asks Link if he would like to hear it. At the end of her story, Molli reveals that her Grandpa saw an Ancient Shrine in the Bird's stomach. She then describes how the hero who found the Shrine defeated the bad guys and saved the princess, living happily ever after. Following this, Molli is proud to have told the story all by herself. If Link speaks to Molli while she is walking to her ledge, she tells him that she is busy. Despite this, she promises to tell him a story if he follows her. If Link speaks to Molli while she is returning to her House for the night, she says that it is time for her to go to sleep

is a recurring character in . Biography Molo is Hylian who is a regular at the Woodland Stable. During the day while the Weather is clear, he sits out at the Stable's patio drinking from a mug. When it Rains, he will instead sit at the table inside. At night, he sleeps in one of the Beds inside the Stable. If Link wakes him up, Molo asks who he is and why he would disturb him at such a time. When Link speaks with Molo, he complains that he is unsure of what to do. If Link ends their conversation, Molo thanks him for nothing. Alternatively, if Link asks what his issue is, Molo explains that the only way to move forward in life is to be rich and admired. Molo believes that the only way to achieve this is to steal the abandoned treasure and Weapons inside Hyrule Castle, though he does acknowledge how dangerous this would be. If Link encourages Molo to enter Hyrule Castle, he will be inspired to do so. However, if Link tells him not to try, Molo states that he is unable to let a rumor of this magnitude go to waste. Molo has heard that one can enter Hyrule Castle through the Docks He is also interested in the Ancient Shrine that is supposedly nearby, referring to Saas Ko'sah Shrine. Of the people Molo knows who have gone to Hyrule Castle, none have returned, which he believes is due to them being too busy now that they are rich. Once he has formulated his plan to enter the Castle, he thinks he will be able to live a comfortable life. Once again, Molo can be found outside of Woodland Stable, where he sits by the Cooking Pot. When Link approaches Molo, he will disappointed by the cooling of Eldin Canyon ever since Death Mountain stopped erupting. If Link asks about this, Molo complains that the cooled Lava created the New Road, which is easier to traverse than the Mountain Road. He is more interested in the Mountain Road that is supposedly full of Monsters, but he claims he is not strong enough for such a journey. While Kilton and Koltin are still at Woodland Stable, Molo expresses an interest in using Koltin's Stall to travel to Death Mountain. He thinks that the balloon could be the solution to his dilemma about which road to take. If Link ends their conversation, Molo wonders who owns the balloon.

is a recurring character in . Biography Monari is an elderly resident of Tarrey Town, which is located on Lake Akkala. She and her husband, Moggs, move in after Fyson opens the Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch). Their House is located behind the Ore and More Jewelry Shop. During the day, she walks around the center of Tarrey Town. At night, she sleeps in one of the Beds inside her House. Monari and Moggs have a son together who has recently left to travel the world. Due to this, the pair moved to Tarrey Town with their Hylian Retrievers after hearing a rumor about it. Though their House feels empty without their son, Moggs believes his absence has brought him and Monari closer together. Upon first meeting Monari, she greets Link and asks who he is. After Link responds, Monari questions if he came to Tarrey Town to purchase a holiday home. Whatever Link's response is, Monari warns him to be careful, as there seem to be many strange people living in Akkala. When Link speaks to Monari again, she asks if he needs something from her. If Link asks about the strange things she has seen, Monari claims to have seen strange plants and guys with ugly faces outside of Tarrey Town. She also mentions Mija's Great Fairy Fountain southeast of Tarrey Town, but after speaking about it with Moggs, she came to the conclusion that one should not disturb things that they do not understand. While speaking with Moggs, Link can ask him about Monari. He claims that she is great at Cooking, and he particularly enjoys her Mushroom Skewer. After this conversation, Link can ask Monari about this, and she claims that Moggs was exaggerating her skills. While she knows the basics of Cooking, Monari believes her real talent lies in baking. She learned her skills from her grandmother, who ran a sweet shop for the Royal Family of Hyrule. However, Monari claims that Link does not appear to need sweets, instead saying he needs to eat a lot of Food to put meat on his bones. If Link asks Monari about her baking skills again, she claims that her grandmother taught her how to make Carrot Cake and Pumpkin Pie. At Link's prompting, Monari reveals that she also knows how to make Monster Cake. While Monari considers it easy to make, needing only Tabantha Wheat, Cane Sugar, and Goat Butter, she has found that the final ingredient, Monster Extract, is difficult to obtain as of late. Despite its disgusting appearance and smell, Monari claims that Monster Cake is a very filling meal. After hearing this, Link can ask Monari to repeat the recipe for Monster Cake. At 9:00 PM, Monari will return to her House for the night. If Link speaks to her, she may tell him that she has to get ready to go to sleep, suggesting that he do the same. Alternatively, she might say that she has to go to Bed, since she

At 9:00 PM, Monari will return to her House for the night. If Link speaks to her, she may tell him that she has to get ready to go to sleep, suggesting that he do the same. Alternatively, she might say that she has to go to Bed, since she struggles during the day if she does not sleep well.

is a character in . Biography Mondi is a Hylian who guards the eastern entrance of Lookout Landing. He carries a Stone Spear that he created himself, which consists of a Long Stick with an attached Stone. If Link attempts to enter Lookout Landing for the first time from the east, Mondi will be shocked to see him. He explains that since he and Zelda vanished at the beginning of the Upheaval, people have been worried about their whereabouts, and Purah has been particularly upset. Mondi tells Link to meet with Purah in the Research Lab so that she knows he is safe. If Link speaks to Mondi after he has already entered Lookout Landing, Mondi urges him to meet with Purah. After Link has met with Purah, Mondi will greet Link the next time he speaks to him. He shows off his Stone Spear, explaining that he made it himself in order to fight off Monsters after the metal Weapons decayed.

is a recurring character in . Biography Monkton is an retired Stable Worker at Snowfield Stable. During the day, he paces around the interior of the Stable. At night, he sleeps upright in one of the chairs inside the Stable. When Monkton was a child, there were not many kids who lived around Snowfield Stable. His only friends were Harry and Mary, whom he would explore with. Monkton was told to avoid the North Lomei Labyrinth by the adults at the Stable. Despite this, Monkton convinced Harry to enter the Labyrinth to test his courage, but he never saw him again. After this, Monkton realized that the adults were right when they said that the Labyrinth is dangerous. The adults also warned Monkton to avoid the ruins of the Forgotten Temple in the Tanagar Canyon, as it was also supposedly dangerous However, Monkton still took Mary to investigate the ruins. Unfortunately, Mary slipped and fell into the Canyon, and Monkton never saw her again. That day, Monkton realized that curiosity could also be the cause of tragedy. When Link approaches him, Monkton asks if he would like to listen to a story. If Link inquires about the story, Monkton claims that he has been reminiscing on his childhood recently. Even in his old age, Monkton is still heartbroken over losing Harry and Mary. After listening to both stories, Monkton tells Link that he overcame his grief over Harry and Mary as he grew older. He then states that two of their descendants are located in the stall next to Snowfield Stable, revealing that both Harry and Mary were Horses. While he may no longer grieve for them, Monkton is still plagued by his memories of Harry and Mary, thinking about them even while he sleeps.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Monster Bridle is a type of Bridle that can be purchased at the Fang and Bone for 399 Mon. These Bridles were handmade by the shop's proprietor, Kilton, though he had a more monstrous Horse in mind when he made them. The Monster Bridle is a piece of Monster Horse Gear, which is a set of Horse Gear. It can be equipped onto Horses at either the Highland Stable, Outskirt Stable, South Akkala Stable, or Woodland Stable. Like other Bridles, Monster Bridles are unable to be worn by Epona or the Giant Horse.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Monster Cakes are a variety of Cake made by Cooking Tabantha Wheat, Cane Sugar, Goat Butter, and Monster Extract together in a Cooking Pot. Being made with Monster Extract, the amount of Hearts they restore to Link will be random when they are made. The Monster Extract will also randomize the strength and duration of any status effects the Cake has. It is said that once one has a taste, they will never forget the sweetness of Monster Cake. The second Castle Library Book details the recipe for Monster Cake, describing it as a secret recipe of the Royal Family of Hyrule and the favorite of an unnamed chancellor. The book instructs its reader to stew Monster Extract, Tabantha Wheat, Cane Sugar, and Goat Butter together for a short while. However, it warns that these Cakes make one's head fuzzy and may motivate someone to plan evil schemes. Monster Cake is one of two Meals Link can give to Gotter as part of the "A Royal Recipe" Side Quest. At first, he likens the Cake to biting into a Chuchu. However, realizing that would be disgusting and dangerous, he instead claims it stimulates the brain like being pummeled by a Hinox. He calls it an elegant dish, saying he never thought he would taste something so thrilling. As thanks, Gotter will give Link a Silver Rupee. Once the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest has been completed, Link can eavesdrop on Ruli and Hagie during the night in Tarrey Town. Ruli laments that their daughter, Hunnie, is sick and will only eat Cake, and she wonders whether anything can be done. No matter how much searching they have done, Hagie notes they have not been able to find a Cake that can please her. Ruli states that she would sell her soul to Monster for a Cake to cure Hunnie. This initiates the "A Parent's Love" Side Quest. During this Side Quest, Link can give Ruli a Monster Cake for Hunnie. She thanks Link for the gift, noting its pungent smell. However, she decides not to complain, since this could be the Cake that heals Hunnie. Ruli decides to have her daughter eat it right away. After this is done, Hunnie will begin to run around and play. Ruli thanks Link, noting that Hunnie's health has returned. As a reward, she will give Link a Gold Rupee. By adding a fifth Ingredient, several different variations of Monster Cake can be made: Chilly Monster Cake: Made by adding a chilly Ingredient. Eating them will grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Monster Cake: Made by adding an electric Ingredient. Eating them will grant Link one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Monster Cake: Made by adding an enduring Ingredient. Link's Stamina Wheel will be completely restored and overfilled if he eats these. Energizing Monster Cake: Made by adding an energizing Ingredients. Eating these Cakes will restore a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty

Since Monster Extract is used in their recipe, the amount of Hearts restored to Link is random each time they are made. The strength and duration of any status effects will also be random. Monster Curries are considered an unusual take on curry, since their use of Monster Extract mean they do not rely heavily on spices. Link can add more Ingredients when making Monster Curry, which can result in the following variations: Chilly Monster Curry: Made by adding chilly Ingredients. If these curries are eaten, Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Monster Curry: Made by adding electric Ingredients. If eaten, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Monster Curry: Made by adding enduring Ingredients. Link's Stamina Wheel will be restored and overfilled if he eats them. Energizing Monster Curry: Made by adding energizing Ingredients. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Monster Extracts are sold by Kilton at the Fang and Bone during the night. It can also be acquired as a reward for rescuing Chabi, who is searching for the Fang and Bone. Though it can't be eaten, dishes made in a Cooking Pot with Monster Extract will have their effects randomly affected (increased or decreased). It is also one of the ingredients that can be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Purple Dye. Using Monster Extract while Cooking will result in monstrous meals. These include Monster Cake, Monster Curry, Monster Rice Balls, Monster Soup, and Monster Stew. Other Appearances Monster Extracts can be obtained by completing the Quests "Fang for Your Buck", "A Rumor about Skull Lake", "Cold Desert Nights", and "Visiting a Special Shop", and can be used for Cooking Monster Cake, Monster Curry, and Monster Stew. They can also be commonly sold for three Rupees and specifically to Bena the Merchant for seven.

are recurring Items in . Monster Fangs go unnamed in and . Location and Uses Monster Fangs are Monster Parts dropped by Bokoblins and Moblins. Bokoblin Fangs are worn-down and blunt, whereas Moblin Fangs are sharp. Both types of Fang can be used to Cook Elixirs at a Cooking Pot, sold at the Fang and Bone for Mon, or used to Enhance Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. List of Monster Fangs List of Monster Fangs Monster Fangs are an Ingredient that can be combined with another Ingredient to make Potions or Unfortunate Smoothies. When used in a Potion, they may greatly boost the effect of the other Ingredient used. Monster Fangs may be dropped by certain Monsters upon defeat. The following table lists the Smoothies that are created by combining each Ingredient with a Monster Fang. Other Appearances

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Monster Forces are large groups of Monsters that have gathered in select areas throughout Hyrule. They consist mostly of Bokoblins and Moblins, with some Forces featuring a Boss Bokoblin that directs Bokoblins' attacks. Several sets of Monster Forces are the focus of the Monster-Control Crew's subjugation. List of Monster Forces Akkala Sea Monster Forces Akkala Span Monster Forces Eventide Island Foothill Monster Den Monster Forces Fort Hateno Monster Forces Hyrule Castle Ja'Abu Ridge Fort Monster Forces Lake Darman Monster Den Monster Forces Lurelin Village Monster Forces Menoat River Monster Forces South Tabantha Snowfield Monster Forces Windvane Meadow Monster Forces Other Appearances Monster Forces are hostile Forces comprised of Monsters. They are found in the "Ganondorf's Return" and "A New Disturbance" Scenarios, led by a King Dodongo, a Gohma and a Manhandla in the former and the Boss Blin as well as a Gohma in the latter.

The , also known as the Stage, is a location in . Features and Overview The Monster Gallery is a stage located in Tarrey Town. It is a grassy display area located next to the Break-a-Part Shop, with a wooden platform located in front. Once Link completes "The Hunt for Bubbul Gems!" Side Adventure, Kilton will appear near the Gallery. After the "Mattison's Independence" Side Adventure has been completed, Hudson will join him. By speaking with them, it is revealed that Kilton wants to use the Monster Gallery to teach people about the various types of Monsters found throughout Hyrule, but he lacks reference materials to show Hudson. By presenting him with a Picture of a Monster, Hudson will be able to create a Monster Sculpture depicting its subject, which Link can place in the Gallery using Ultrahand.

Monster Guts are recurring Items in . Location and Uses In , Monster Guts can be found in Treasure Chests and by defeating Enemies. 10 of them can be used to brew a Purple Potion at the Witch's House. In , Monster Guts are bronze-rarity Materials awarded for completing the following Levels and Drablands Challenges of the Volcano. The number in parentheses is how many of the three Treasure Chests at the end of the Level contain Monster Guts; each of the Links may open just one Chest. Blazing Trail, no challenge (1) Blazing Trail, "Evade the Wallmaster!" (2) Hinox Mine, "Clear within the time limit!" (2) Den of Flames, no challenge (2) They can also be won in the Coliseum and Daily Riches, or they can purchased from the Street Merchant for 250 Rupees each. Monster Guts are one of the Materials used to make the Energy Gear and Goron Garb Outfits. List of Monster Guts List of Monster Guts Monster Guts are an Ingredient that can be combined with another Ingredient to make Potions or Unfortunate Smoothies. When used in a Potion, they may greatly boost the effect of the other Ingredient used. Monster Guts are rarely dropped by certain Monsters upon defeat. 11 Monster Guts can be found in a Treasure Chest on Hebra Mountain. The following table lists the Smoothies that are created by combining each Ingredient with Monster Guts. Other Appearances List of Monster Guts

are recurring Items and classes of Items in . Location and Uses Monster Horns are instruments of animal bone carried by Bokoblins. They can be stolen from Red Bokoblins by using the Whip. Link can also win them by making between 20 to 27 cuts in the Clean Cut mini-game at Bamboo Island. The Moonlight Merchant will occasionally sell Monster Horns for 100 Rupees. In his home at night, Rupin will occasionally buy Monster Horns for 30 Rupees. Monster Horns are necessary for Upgrading the following Items at the Scrap Shop: Monster Horns can be found by opening Treasure Chests or by defeating Enemies in . In exchange for 10 Monster Horns and 100 Rupees, the Witch will brew Link a Yellow Potion. Alternatively, Link can sell Monster Horns to the Witch for five Rupees apiece. Monster Horns are a class of Materials dropped by most Monsters in . When Fused to Weapons and Arrows, they increase attack power significantly. Other Appearances Monster Horns are Materials which are dropped by Miniblin Captains in and .

, also known as , and Enemy Camps, are recurring location in . Monster Outposts go unnamed in . Features and Overview Monster Encampments are small camps occupied by Monsters. They may have watchtowers to spot nearby Enemies and prey, and may be home to Outpost Chests. More complex versions of Monster Encampments known as Monster Strongholds also appear, which are depicted as either multistory structures or skull-shaped rocks. Monster Outposts are small Monster camps, commonly found in the Depths. Monster Outposts in the Depths typically surround Zonaite Deposits, where they are mined by the occupants. Skull-shaped rocks and multistory structures are a more advanced type of Monster Outpost known as Monster Strongholds. Monster Outposts appear throughout Hyrule. They are typically inhabited by Moblins and Boarblins, though Outposts atop Eldin Volcano are also occupied by Lizalfos. At the heart of each Outpost there is an Outpost Chest that will only unlock once all of the Monsters connected to the Outpost have been defeated. Monster Outposts will eventually repopulate and their Outpost Chests will be refilled after a period of time.

, also known as Monster Materials, are a recurring class of Items in . Location and Uses Monster Parts are a type of Material dropped by Monsters when they are defeated. Higher-ranking Monster Parts can be dropped by higher-ranking Enemies. For example, Bokoblin Horns can be dropped by all Bokoblins, but Bokoblin Guts will only be dropped by Blue Bokoblins or higher. Materials dropped from Creature that can deal damage to Link, like Boars or Wolves, are not considered Monster Parts. Monster Parts can be sold to Shop and Merchants all around Hyrule for varying prices. Rarer Monster Parts will sell for higher amounts of Rupees. Kilton, the proprietor of the Fang and Bone, accepts Monster Parts in exchange for his currency, Mon. All Monster Parts can be Cooked with Lizards and Insects to make Elixirs, and their duration will vary based on the part included. If Cooked by themselves, Monster Part will only create Dubious Food. List of Monster Parts Armor Upgrades Several Armor Enhancements also require Monster Parts in order to be completed by a Great Fairy. Monster Parts return in . List of Monster Parts Other Appearances List of Monster Parts

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Monster Rice Balls are a Meal that can be made by Cooking Hylian Rice, Rock Salt, and Monster Extract together in a Cooking Pot. Due to Monster Extract being used in their making, the amount of Hearts restored to Link, as well as the strength and duration of any status effects, will be random. The unique aroma of Monster Rice Balls is disliked by many people. By incorporating additional Ingredients to the recipe, several different variations of Monster Rice Balls can be made: Chilly Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding chilly Ingredients. They can be eaten to grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding electric Ingredients. If eaten, Link will be granted one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding enduring Ingredients. When eaten, they will completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding energizing Ingredients. They will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel when eaten. Hasty Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding hasty Ingredients. Link can eat them to gain boost to his movement speed. Hearty Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding hearty Ingredients. These rice balls will heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him Extra Hearts. Mighty Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding mighty Ingredients. When these rice balls are eaten, Link will receive a boost to his attack power. Sneaky Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding sneaky Ingredients. Eating one will increase Link's Stealth. Spicy Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding spicy Ingredients. Eating them will increase Link's Cold Resistance by one level. Tough Monster Rice Balls: Made by adding tough Ingredients. Link will gain a boost to his Defense when he eats these.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Monster Saddle can be purchased from Kilton at the Fang and Bone for 299 Mon. Kilton made it himself, though it was intended for a more Monster-like Horse. Despite their strange appearance, they are still useable for Horses. The Monster Saddle is part of the Monster Horse Gear set, which is a group of Horse Gear. Link can equip his Horses with the Monster Saddle by speaking to specific workers at either Highland Stable, Outskirt Stable, South Akkala Stable, or Woodland Stable. As is the case with other Saddles, they are unable to be utilized by Epona or the Giant Horse.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Monster Soups can be made by Cooking Monster Extract, Tabantha Wheat, Fresh Milk, and Goat Butter together in a Cooking Pot. Due to Monster Extract being required to make them, the amount of Hearts restored to Link is random each time these soups are made. The same also applies to the strength and duration of any status effects. Since Monster Extract is used as a base, the soup is distinctly gamy. By adding more Ingredients, Link can create several different variations of Monster Soup: Chilly Monster Soup: Made by adding chilly Ingredients. These soups will grant Link one level of Heat Resistance when eaten. Electro Monster Soup: Made by adding electric Ingredients. Eating them will grant Link one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Monster Soup: Made by adding enduring Ingredients. Link can eat them to completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Monster Soup: Made by adding energizing Ingredients. When eaten, a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel will be refilled. Hasty Monster Soup: Made by adding hasty Ingredients. They can be eaten to increase Link's movement speed. Hearty Monster Soup: Made by adding hearty Ingredients. Eating these soups will heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him Extra Hearts. Mighty Monster Soup: Made by adding mighty Ingredients. Link can consume these soups to increase the power of his attacks. Sneaky Monster Soup: Made by adding sneaky Ingredients. When eaten, Link will receive a boost to his Stealth. Spicy Monster Soup: Made by adding spicy Ingredients. If they are eaten, Link will gain one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Monster Soup: Made by adding tough Ingredients. By eating them, Link can gain a boost to his Defense.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Monster Stews can be made by Cooking any Meat, any Seafood, and Monster Extract together in a Cooking Pot. Their default version can be made either by using seafood without status effects, such as Hyrule Basses or Sanke Carps, or by using seafood with contradictory effects. The Monster Extract used in this recipe causes the amount of Hearts healed to Link's Life Gauge to be random each time it is made. The same principle applies to the strength and duration of any status effects. These stews are known to be savory, despite the ingredients used. By using certain types of seafood or adding more ingredients, Link can create several variations of Monster Stew: Chilly Monster Stew: Made by using Chillfin Trouts or other chilly ingredients. When eaten, these stews will grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Monster Stew: Made by using Voltfin Trout or other electric ingredients. Eating these stews will grant Link one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Monster Stew: Made by using enduring ingredients. When eaten, they will completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Monster Stew: Made by using Staminoka Basses, Bright-Eyed Crabs, or other energizing ingredients. Eating them will refill a part of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Monster Stew: Made by using hasty ingredients. Link can eat these stews to receive an increased movement speed. Hearty Monster Stew: Made by using Hearty Bass, Hearty Salmons, Hearty Blueshell Snails, or other hearty ingredients. These stews heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him temporary Hearts when eaten. Mighty Monster Stew: Made by using Mighty Carps, Mighty Porgies, Razorclaw Crabs, or other mighty ingredients. Link will gain a boost to his attack power if he eats them. Sneaky Monster Stew: Made by using Stealthfin Trouts, Sneaky River Snails, or other sneaky ingredients. By eating them, Link's Stealth will be increased. Spicy Monster Stew: Made by using Sizzlefin Trouts or other spicy ingredients. They can be eaten to grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Monster Stew: Made by using Armored Carps, Armored Porgies, Ironshell Crabs, or other tough ingredients. Consuming these stews will increase Link's defense. Other Appearances The recipe for Monster Stew is earned by completing the Quest "Mystery Meal for the Merchant". It is made using six Raw Gourmet Meats, six Razorclaw Crabs, and six Monster Extracts. However, it can be lowered to four of each ingredient through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warriors will have 50% less total Hearts and a 15% boost to all other stats.

, also known as , are recurring locations in . Monster Strongholds go unnamed in . Features and Overview Monster Strongholds are encampments scattered throughout the Eldin Volcano in the Eldin Province in . They are usually inhabited by Bokoblins who live in crude tents, though Moblins can also appear. Monster Strongholds typically have towers occupied by Bokoblin sentries who watch for intruders and alert the inhabitants when one is spotted. These towers can be toppled with Bombs, dispatching the sentries atop them. After Eldin Volcano erupts, Bokoblins occupy the entire mountain, converting it into one massive Monster Stronghold. Monster Strongholds can be found east of Volcano East, outside the entrance to the Thrill Digger Area, and east of the Temple Entrance. Later in the game, all of the Monster Strongholds are abandoned, so Kortz decides to take residence inside one of the huts, while Merco can be found outside, wondering what Bokoblins eat. Monster Strongholds are distributed throughout Hyrule in . They come in many forms, but the most common are wooden platforms surrounding Trees and large skull-shaped rocks. Strongholds may contain Barrels, Bomb Barrels, and Treasure Chests. Outpost Chests are commonly found in skull-shaped Monster Strongholds and can only be opened when all Enemies in the Stronghold are defeated. Monster Strongholds appear throughout Hyrule and are often guarded by Aerocudas. Additional types of Monster Stronghold also appear, with various purposes. Battle Taluses function as mobile Monster Strongholds, while larger Monster Forts are stationed in various areas and provide protection from all sides. Pirate Ships are used by Monsters to assail Hyrule's waterways and are protected from ground assaults due to their positions in water. Other Appearances

is a character in . Biography Monte is a Hylian who has been tasked with guarding the entrance to the Emergency Shelter in Lookout Landing. He carries a Traveler's Spear. When Link first enters the Emergency Shelter, Monte will welcome him and introduce himself. If Link asks him about the Emergency Shelter, Monte explains that it was previously used by the Royal Family of Hyrule as a place to hide. Now that it is being used by the residents of Lookout Landing, they have been fixing it up and stockpiling supplies, and Monte considers it to be cozy. If Link asks about Monte, he explains that it his job to open and shut the entrance to the Emergency Shelter. At the end of their conversation, Monte advises that Link be careful when Climbing the Shelter's Ladder, musing that it would be easier to navigate Lookout Landing if one could Ascend through the ceiling.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Moor Garrison Ruins Well is situated among the Moor Garrison Ruins in the Lanayru Wetlands. The Well's interior allows Link to access parts of the Moor Garrison Ruins that have been buried. Its first chamber consists only of a slope leading downward to a partially-flooded archway. By Ascending from this point, Link can reach a second chamber that features two prison cells. Inside of the cells are destroyed pieces of Furniture, as well as Wooden Boxes and a Barrel that can be broken open for Materials. Along the northern wall of this chamber are a set of bars, through which the above-ground portion of the Moor Garrison Ruins can be seen. Creatures Treasure Chests

is a character in . Biography Mopu is a Korok who appears below the Minshi Woods Chasm in Minshi Grove during the "Trail of the Master Sword" Main Quest. They originally left Korok Forest to go on a walk with Tasho, Nako, Mokka, Raha, Jatora, and Maheli, but the group were unable to return through the Lost Woods. With the exception of Tasho, the Koroks then descended into the Minshi Woods Chasm in an attempt to reach Korok Forest from the Depths. When Link speaks to Mopu, they ask if he is also searching for a way to reach Korok Forest. If Link asks about Korok Forest, they explain their situation to him. They then point Link in the direction that their fellow Koroks went. Should Link speak to Mopu again, they claim that Koroks are able to see well in the Darkness, and they once again tell him which direction Korok Forest is located in. Alternatively, if Link claims he is busy, Mopu is shocked and warns him to be careful.

is a recurring Boss in . Characteristics Moragia is a three-headed, draconic Monster composed of Lava and Gloom Rock. In order to keep its form together, it draws power from the heat and Gloom rising from the Death Mountain Depths. Moragia is fought at the very top of Death Mountain during the Main Quest "Yunobo of Goron City". It emerges as Link and Yunobo approach Death Mountain Crater while searching for Princess Zelda. As a result, they are unable to look for her until it has been defeated. To combat Moragia, Link must use the nearby Zonai Devices to construct an airplane, which he can then fire Yunobo from like a cannonball using his Power of Fire. Each head requires only one shot to destroy, but they will try to shoot Link's aircraft down with Magma Bombs as he approaches. Other Appearances Moragia appears during the Scenario "The Behemoth in the Crater". As part of the Scenario, the Knight Construct and Calamo fly to the peak of Death Mountain in order to confront Moragia. The Knight Construct can use the Zonai Devices found in the Stage and the basic light beam attack to deal damage to it.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Moshapin Shrine can be found within the Lake Intenoch Cave in Eldin Canyon. It corresponds to the Nipahsom Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Moshapin Shrine The Moshapin Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Moshapin Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

are Enemies in . Characteristics Moth Gibdos are flying Gibdos that appeared in the Gerudo Desert alongside the Sand Shroud. Their resemblance to Insects is more prominent than in regular Gibdos, with mothlike wings, antennae, and a tail-like abdomen. Moth Gibdos fly above Link, preventing him from reaching them with standard blades, making them difficult to strike without Bows or Spears. Moth Gibdos occasionally spit clouds of acid at him. Like their standard counterparts, while highly resistant to physical attacks due to their tough skin, they are vulnerable to Electricity, Fire, Ice, and Water-based attacks, which will cause them to turn white and temporarily disable their resistance to physical attacks. Additionally, concentrated light will kill them outright.

The , also known as the Forgotten Temple Statue, is a recurring character in . The Mother Goddess Statue goes unnamed in . Biography The Mother Goddess Statue is the largest and oldest Goddess Statue in Hyrule Kingdom, and she can be found at the rear of the Forgotten Temple. By speaking to her, Link is able to exchange groups of four Spirit Orbs for either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. After Link completes all 120 Ancient Shrines in , the voice of a Monk will speak to him and offer him a reward at the Forgotten Temple. This starts the Side Quest "A Gift from the Monks". At the foot of the Mother Goddess Statue, Link will find three Stone Chests that contain the Cap of the Wild, the Tunic of the Wild, and the Trousers of the Wild. The Mother Goddess Statue returns in , being one of six Great Goddess Statues. She has since been toppled over, though the entrance to a new room in the Forgotten Temple has appeared behind her. Her counterpart, the Cliff Bargainer Statue, can be found in the Depths below her position. At the beginnings of the Side Quests "Goddess Statue of Courage", "Goddess Statue of Power", and "Goddess Statue of Wisdom", the Spring of Courage Statue, the Spring of Power Statue, and the Spring of Wisdom Statue all ask Link to check on the Mother Goddess Statue, claiming they can no longer sense her presence. Upon hearing that she has fallen over, the Great Goddess Statues task Link with offering their respective Dragon's claw at their springs so they can send a portion of their power to the Mother Goddess Statue. After completing all of these Side Quests, "The Mother Goddess Statue" will begin, wherein Link must check back on the Mother Goddess Statue. Upon his arrival, the Mother Goddess Statue will give Link the White Sword of the Sky as a sign of her gratitude. She then instructs him to go and bring peace to the world. After restoring the Mother Goddess Statue, Link will be able to give her four Lights of Blessing in exchange for either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. She will also enhance his bond with any given Sage in return for four Sage's Wills. In addition if Link has broken his White Sword of the Sky, she will give in another, given that he offers her Dinraal's Claw, Naydra's Claw, and Farosh's Claw first.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Motsusis Shrine can be found at the center of the South Lomei Labyrinth in the Gerudo Highlands. In order to reach the Shrine of Light, Link must navigate the maze and reach its innermost room. The Shrine corresponds to the Sisustom Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Motsusis Shrine The Motsusis Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Motsusis Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

are a recurring mechanic in . They are Animals or Enemies whose movements are manually controlled for the purposes of Transportation, combat, or playing Mini-Games. Some Mounts can be summoned with a special Call like Epona's Song. In some games, Link can knock Enemies off their Mounts and use them himself. In other games, he can only use his own. Epona is the most frequently recurring of Link's personal Mounts. Beyond that, using a Cucco to fly is the most frequently recurring form of Animal-based transportation in . Appearances In , Link revives the Flying Rooster. It then follows the hero around Koholint Island. Picking up the Flying Rooster causes Link to fly just above the ground, allowing him to retrieve the Bird Key in Tal Tal Heights. When Link completes Eagle's Tower, he can no longer use the Flying Rooster, as it has gone to live in the Henhouse. In , when Link jumps off a ledge carrying a Cucco as a child or adult, he will glide slowly downward. Link can use this technique to gather the Cucco Lady's Cuccos in Kakariko Village for a Bottle. Lone Cuccos at Zora's River and Gerudo Valley can be used to obtain Pieces of Heart nearby. Adult Link can mount the saddled Horses at Lon Lon Ranch. A Horse canters when its rider digs their heels into its sides. It gallops when whipped. Link can whip his Horse up to 6 times in succession to maintain a gallop. The number of remaining whippings is represented by a meter of Carrots which regenerate over time. A galloping Horse can jump over fences, but only if approaching the fence head-on. Link's primary Mount is Epona. Epona is able to jump over taller fences than regular Horses. Link wins Epona from Ingo by beating him in two horseback races. He escapes Lon Lon Ranch on Epona's back by making her jump over the outer fence. After this, he can Call her at any time by playing Epona's Song. Epona can also jump across the broken Bridge over Gerudo Valley. Link needs her in order to play at the Horseback Archery Range and to hunt Big Poes, who only appear while Link is on horseback. Link can draw his Bow while on horseback, but cannot use his other Weapons. He is also invincible while mounted on Epona. Princess Zelda and Impa ride a white Horse out of Castle Town as Ganondorf purses them on a black stallion. Phantom Ganon rides an identical stallion. In , Link rides a young Epona without a saddle, which he was unable to do in . Skull Kid steals Epona from him in the Lost Woods. Link must retrieve her from Romani Ranch in order to jump the fences in Termina Field barring the entrances to the Great Bay Region and the Ikana Region. Link also needs her in order to race the Gorman Brothers at the Gorman Track. During the "Protect the Milk!" event, Link defends Cremia's Carriage} against

from Romani Ranch in order to jump the fences in Termina Field barring the entrances to the Great Bay Region and the Ikana Region. Link also needs her in order to race the Gorman Brothers at the Gorman Track. During the "Protect the Milk!" event, Link defends Cremia's Carriage} against the masked Gorman Brothers as they attempt to attack the Carriage on horseback. One of the Bombers in West Clock Town uses a Cucco to glide away from Link when playing Hide-and-Seek. The Sub-Boss Gekko mounts a Snapper. and In , Link mounts one of the three Animal Companions to traverse the Nuun Highlands. Each Animal Companion has an attack move as well as a special ability. Ricky the Kangaroo can leap up cliffs and over holes, Moosh the Bear can fly, and Dimitri the Dodongo can swim against currents and up waterfalls. In , Link mounts all three Animal Companions, but as in , he can only summon the one whose Flute he owns (Ricky's Flute, Moosh's Flute, Dimitri's Flute). Their special abilities are needed to traverse Holodrum Plain (Ricky), Mt. Cucco (Moosh), Sunken City (Dimitri), and Natzu (whichever one Link can Call). In , Link also uses a Flying Cucco (similar to the Flying Rooster from ) to reach the eastern summit of Mt. Cucco where the Spring Banana Tree is located. In The Field stage, the Links instantaneously mount Horses when one of them picks up a Carrot. The Horses are needed to jump fences and can also trample Enemies and Grass. They disappear after a certain amount of time unless the Links pick up another Carrot before then. Horses also appear in the Bucking Broncos Mini-Game. In , Link mounts Epona to herd Goats at Ordon Ranch. Epona disappears when a band of Bulblins mounted on Bullbos attack Ordon Village. Their leader, King Bulblin, rides Lord Bullbo. Epona reappears in Kakariko Village after throwing off a pair of Bulblin riders. Link subdues his frenzied Horse and regains the ability to Call her with Horse Grass and later the Horse Call. Link can draw his Bow and swing his Sword while mounted on Epona. Unlike previous games, he is not invincible while mounted and can even be knocked off Epona by attacks. Likewise, Link can knock Bulblin riders off their Bullbos. When King Bulblin kidnaps Colin, a mounted battle ensues between him and Link. Link then defeats King Bulblin in a joust. Later on, Link again mounts Epona to fend off mounted Bulblins attacking the Wagon carrying Telma and Ilia to Kakariko Village. As part of the final battle, Link fights Ganondorf on horseback. Ganondorf summons Phantom Riders to attack Link. Bulblins always ride two to a Bullbo— one steers the creature while an archer sits behind. In Gerudo Desert, where Link cannot Call Epona, he can instead ride Bullbos and use their charging ability to destroy the wooden fences in the area. Cuccos can once again be used to glide to otherwise unreachable places. In particular,

Bullbo— one steers the creature while an archer sits behind. In Gerudo Desert, where Link cannot Call Epona, he can instead ride Bullbos and use their charging ability to destroy the wooden fences in the area. Cuccos can once again be used to glide to otherwise unreachable places. In particular, Link uses the Golden Cucco to cross the gorge in Faron Woods in order to reach the Sacred Grove. The Flight-by-Fowl Mini-Game features Cucco-gliding as well. After Wolf Link kills the Twilit Carrier Kargarok's Shadow Bulblin rider, Midna can mount the beast and steer it up Zora's River with Wolf Link in its claws. The same is true for the giant Kargarok used to play the Fruit Pop Flight Challenge. Bullbo-riding Bulblins occasionally attack the Spirit Train. Mounted Miniblins ride Armos. Adults in Skyloft mount Loftwings to travel between the floating islands of the Sky. Loftwings are bound to their riders for life. Link's Loftwing is a rare Crimson Loftwing. Link uses it to travel not only to the other islands of the Sky but to the Columns of Light and to the inside of the Thunderhead. Link can ride several unique Mounts. These include Horses, Deer, and even Bears. However, only normal Horses can be registered at Stables. Any other kind of Mount is unable to be registered. Attempting to register them will prompt unique responses from the Stable Workers. Link cannot use any Mounts in the Gerudo Desert. Link can also Mount Lynels, although they cannot be tamed.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Daphnes is located on the western side of Hyrule Field. It shares its northern border with a nameless lake, at the center of which grows the Ancient Tree Stump. The two locations are connected by a makeshift wooden bridge. Near the bridge, Link can find a Ruined House with three Barrels, containing Apples, Hylian Shrooms, and a Chuchu. The Kaam Ya'tak Shrine sits at the mountain's southern base. Prior to the second Great Calamity, the Ruined House on Mount Daphnes was inhabited by Hylians. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Mount Daphnes. It is an Offering Spot located on its eastern peak, and it is marked by a Stone Statue. If Link places an Apple in the Offering Spot, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Mount Daphnes is littered with Fallen Debris, and some Ruins Rubble can be seen falling from the Sky onto the mountain. The mountain is surrounded by small-scale Monster Strongholds, with the largest sitting at its northern base. Several Bomb Barrels, Wooden Boxes and a couple Barricades appear in this Stronghold. At the southwestern base of the mountain, there are multiple sets of Hyrule Restoration Materials and the Mount Daphnes Well, which doubles as a Chasm connecting to the Central Hyrule Depths. Brigo can be found exploring the area with his Donkey while searching for a Chasm that is rumored to be nearby. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Drena is located between the Great Hyrule Forest and the Hebra Mountains. It features two peaks, the northwestern one being part of the Hebra Mountains, while the southeastern one is part of the Great Hyrule Forest. Between the two peaks, an unnamed path leads to the Drenan Highlands. In the north, Mount Drena is the subject of a Freezing Climate, as is the top of its southeastern peak. Creatures and Materials more common to cold areas are found in the northern half of the mountain. In the south, their more temperate counterparts are present. Dinraal flies above Mount Drena while entering the Tanagar Canyon at 1:00 AM. She creates a gust of Wind as she flies by, but she cannot be reached at her distance. Two Monster Strongholds are situated around the northwestern peak. The southern Stronghold features a Cooking Pot. Creatures Materials Enemies Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Faloraa is located in the northwestern corner of the Faron Grasslands. It comes to a peak on its northern end, from which it slopes down into the Grinnden Plains and Zokassa Ridge. A sparse gathering of Cedar Trees cover the mountain. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Mount Faloraa. It takes the form of a group of Leaves with Fairy Dust on top of the Cedar Tree at the mountain's peak. When Link Climbs the Cedar Tree and interacts with the Leaves, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Floria is located along the southern edge of East Necluda. It has three peaks, two of which are Angel Peak to the west and Breman Peak to the east. On its northern side, a small Waterfall flows out into a branch of the Squabble River. Wind will also pass along the southern side of the mountain as Farosh flies through Riola Spring. During the Side Quest "Misko, the Great Bandit", Domidak tells Link that Misko's treasure can be found in a cave above a river. This cave is located above the Waterfall on the north side of Mount Floria. When Link breaks the rocks blocking the entrance, he will be able to access the treasure inside. The Treasure Chests inside contain a total of one Opal, one Amber, two Sapphires, and one Luminous Stone. Behind another bombable wall is an additional Treasure Chest containing a Flameblade. The Barrels nearby can be broken open for Roasted Bird Drumsticks and Seared Steaks. Finally, three Toasted Hearty Truffles and a Soldier's Spear can be found on the ground of the cave. left|40px Three Korok Seed Puzzles are located on Mount Floria. The first is a Natural Hiding Spot, which takes the form of a Rock on the mountain's central peak that Link must pick up. The second is another Natural Hiding Spot, this time on top of a large Tree on a ridge above Misko's cave. The final Puzzle is a Flower Trail, beginning to the west of Breman Peak and ending to the south. When Link solves each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Equipment Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Granajh is located at the southern end of the Gerudo Highlands. It contains two peaks, a main one at its center and a shorter one to the south known as Daval Peak. A wooden Ruined House can be found near the mountain's central peak, which contains a Campfire, three Barrels, and the Mountain Peak Log. Several shallow pools of Water and Fallen Guardians can be found on the mountain's southern foothills. Since Mount Granajh is situated within a Freezing Climate, Link will require at least two levels of Cold Resistance to traverse it without taking damage. According to the Mountain Peak Log, an unnamed individual came to Mount Granajh after reading about an Ancient Shrine that could be found there. However, they were unable to find the Shrine, and they were forced to leave after running out of rations. After reading the Mountain Peak Log, Link will receive the "Secret of the Snowy Peaks" Shrine Quest. The Log hints that one must cast a "cold shadow" onto the Pedestal located on the side of Daval Peak. Using a nearby pool of Water, Link can cast the shadow from a Cryonis block onto the Pedestal. Alternatively, Link can hold up one of the Snowballs surrounding the Ruined House so that its shadow will touch the Pedestal. Using either method will cause Suma Sahma Shrine to emerge from the ground nearby. left|40px Five separate Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Mount Granajh. The first is a Natural Hiding Spot, disguised as a Rock on a stone pillar at the mountain's central peak. The second is another Natural Hiding Spot west of the center peak. The third and fourth Puzzles are groups of Leaves with Fairy Dust, hidden within a blocks of Ice located to the south and southwest of Daval Peak. Lastly, a Rock Pattern can be found on the foothills south of Daval Peak. Whenever Link completes one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials In the years following the events of , all of the Snow covering Mount Granajh has melted, resulting in the Weather and terrain to be consistent with the rest of Gerudo Canyon. The Deserted House that was previously on the mountain has been dismantled, with only a small remnant of it foundation remaining. A Hylian named Rahdo resides on top of Mount Granajh, where he is conditioning himself to endure the Gerudo Region's extreme Temperatures. When Link speaks to Rahdo, he will be challenged to a Contest of Endurance. Accepting the challenge will begin the Side Quest "Cold-Endurance Contest!", which requires Link to endure the Freezing Climate on Mount Granajh from 8:30 PM to 4:30 AM while not wearing any Armor. During this Contest, Link can equip warm Elemental Weapons, build a Campfire, or eat Spicy Foods to endure the cold. If Link wins, he will be rewarded with a Silver Rupee. If Link speaks to
