is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Gustaf is located in Hyrule Field. Along the northern side of the mountain, several Ruined Houses that make up an unnamed Hylian village can be found. A grass trail cuts the center of the mountain and continues onto a land bridge over the Regencia River, which eventually leads to the West Hyrule Plains. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Mount Gustaf. It is located along the northern base of the mountain, and it is a Rock that is hidden behind a bombable wall. After Link destroys the wall, he can pick up the Rock to reveal that it is a Natural Hiding Spot, and a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Mount Gustaf is set to reappear in .

The Mount Gustaf Well returns in , still situated in Hyrule Field. Link is now able to access its interior, which consists of two chambers. The first is a large room with a pond of Water along its western wall. The entrance to the second chamber is to the south, inside of which are four Ore Deposits. Creatures Enemies Materials

, also stylized as Mt. Lanayru, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Lanayru is a large mountain located on the southern end of the Lanayru Region in Hyrule. It is considered a sacred site and is home to the Spring of Wisdom at its peak. Unique Ice spikes can also be found on Mount Lanayru at higher elevations. The mountain has a decree, which states, "No one is allowed, under the age of seventeen. For only the wise are permitted a place upon the mountain." Due to being a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least two levels Cold Resistance in order to traverse most of Mount Lanayru. Prior to the second Great Calamity, Link accompanied Zelda as she ascended Mount Lanayru on her 17th birthday so she could pray at the Spring of Wisdom. However, she failed to awaken her sealing power at the Spring. The end of their journey can be seen during the "Return of Calamity Ganon" Recovered Memory. Link must journey to Mount Lanayru as part of "The Spring of Wisdom" Shrine Quest. Upon reaching the summit, Link will find Naydra, the Spring of Wisdom's guardian, possessed by Malice. While freeing Naydra, the Dragon will fly around Mount Lanayru, requiring Link to utilize Updrafts in order to approach it. left|40px Three Korok Seed Puzzles can be found near Mount Lanayru's peak. The first two are Leaves with Fairy Dust that can be uncovered by melting two separate Ice blocks to the northwest. The third Puzzle is to the northeast, where a Rock Pattern must be completed. Once Link completes each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed as a reward. Climates Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Areas Other Appearances

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Nabooru is a large protrusion of the Gerudo Highlands, serving as one of the walls of the Gerudo Canyon. It stands opposite to the Koukot Plateau, though they are connected by two natural archways. The Koukot Plateau Path also connects to Mount Nabooru at several points. Several Ore Deposits are located along its edges. On the southern end of Mount Nabooru, a Stone Talus (Luminous) can be found embedded in the ground. It is initially dormant, but it will begin to move and attack Link if he approaches it. The "Test of Will" Shrine Quest takes place on Mount Nabooru. To start the Quest, Link must speak to the Goron Blood Brothers on the western side of the mountain, who reveal that they are partaking in a contest of endurance at their ancestral training grounds. Bayge, Heehl, and Kabetta invite Link to participate in their contest. This involves standing on one of their heated platforms without passing out. After Link wins the contest, the Brothers allow him to try the "contest of ultimate endurance," which is a much hotter platform. Bayge also shares a rumor that an Ancient Shrine will appear when someone completes this challenges. If Link is able to pass the Trial, Joloo Nah Shrine will rise from the ground nearby, completing the Shrine Quest. Two Treasure Chests are located on Mount Nabooru. The first is a metallic Treasure Chest on the south end of the mountain, which is embedded in the ground and requires the Magnesis Rune to remove. When Link opens the Chest, he will receive a Moonlight Scimitar. The second is a stone Treasure Chest that it is concealed by a bombable wall on the northeast corner of the mountain, and it contains an Amber. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Mount Nabooru. At the mountain's southern tip, there is an abandoned well with a metal Boulder chained to it. Using Magnesis, Link can place the Boulder in the well. This causes a Korok to appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Inhabitants Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Rhoam is located on Hyrule Ridge, wrapping around the northwestern end of Ludfo's Bog alongside Upland Lindor. The Seres Scablands are situated directly to the mountain's south. An unmarked path connects the peak of Mount Rhoam to the Footrace Check-In nearby. There is a small pond on top of Mount Rhoam, which is fed by a Waterfall north of the mountain's peak. A single Updraft near the peak allows Link to ascend part of the mountain with little effort. Many of the patches of Grass higher up on Mount Rhoam are differently colored than that elsewhere on Hyrule Ridge, being closer to red or brown. During the Foot Race Mini-Game, Link is tasked with reaching two Big Flags on Mount Rhoam before Konba. While competing in the Race, Chuchus and Electric Chuchus will pop out of the ground in front of him, and a Bomb Barrel will explode. If Link manages to reach the goal before Konba, he will receive a Purple Rupee as a reward. A Monster Stronghold has been settled on the southern foothills of Mount Rhoam. After defeating all of the Monsters inside, Link will be able to open its Treasure Chest, which contains a Knight's Claymore. In Master Mode, wooden platforms held afloat by Sky Octoroks can be found above the pond on Mount Rhoam. The Chest on these platforms is made of metal, and it contains an Edge of Duality. Three additional Treasure Chests are hidden on Mount Rhoam. In the mountain's pond, Link can find both a wooden and a metal Chest, the latter of which must be pulled from the Water using the Magnesis Rune. They contain a bundle of five Shock Arrows and a Knight's Shield, respectively. The third Chest is made of stone, and it is hidden on the western foothills of the mountain. Link can retrieve a Purple Rupee from inside. left|40px There are a total of two Korok Seed Puzzles on Mount Rhoam. The first is a Natural Hiding Spot, which takes the form of a Rock on the mountain's peak that Link must pick up. The second Puzzle is also a Natural Hiding Spot Rock, situated on top of the Waterfall north of the peak. Whenever Link solves one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Along the way, a Rito Captain informs them of a White-Maned Lynel atop the mountain, and Zelda states it would be dangerous for them to Paraglide on the Updrafts before defeating it. Once this is done, one Warrior

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Mount Taran is located in East Necluda. It is home to the Tawa Jinn Shrine and the three Giant Brothers. There are three Pedestals with Concave Slots, in addition to a Stone Tablet that instructs Link on how to complete "The Three Giant Brothers" Shrine Quest. On and around the mountain are a few patches of marshland surrounded by what appear to be giant ribs of some long-dead creature. Three of the marshlands (Hanu Pond, Uten Marsh and Rabella Wetlands) contain a Hinox, each of whom has an Ancient Orb on their necklace. Areas Other Appearances As part of the "Mount Taran's Solitary Masters" Quest, Link wishes to observe the Spear masters that are said to live on Mount Taran. When he sneaks up there, he discovers that the Spear masters are a pair of Hinoxes, though he is still able to improve his skills by watching them.

The is a recurring location in . The Mountain Road goes unnamed in and . Features and Overview The Mountain Road begins at the Maw of Death Mountain and ends at the top of Death Mountain. The fork of the Ternio Trail that heads towards Foothill Stable leads into it. The Southern Mine, Goron City, and the Abandoned North Mine are located along it. Stolock Bridge and the Bridge of Eldin both connect parts of the Road. The beginning of the Mountain Road is marked by the first of the Death Mountain Markers. The rest of the Markers are found along the Road. Near Medingo Pool, the Mountain Road enters a Scorching Climate. In order to progress further, Link will either need to drink a Fireproof Elixir or equip parts of the Fireproof Armor set. Past the Bridge of Eldin, Link will require another level of Flame Guard before he can continue. An Igneo Talus can be found in the middle of the Mountain Road as it passes through Goronbi Lake North, just under Gortram Cliff. During the "Divine Beast Vah Rudania" Main Quest, the part of the Mountain Road past the Bridge of Eldin will be filled with Sentries as Link and Yunobo attempt to approach Divine Beast Vah Rudania. Their progress along the Road will be impeded by Black Moblins, which Link must defeat in order to make use of Bludo's Cannons. Dayto and Kairo can both be found on the Mountain Road. They travel between Foothill Stable and the end of the Maw of Death Mountain. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Other Appearances The Mountain Road appears as part of the Death Mountain Stage. During the Movies "Reaching Vah Rudania" and "Daruk's Wishes", Daruk can be seen leading Zelda, Impa, Link, and Terrako along the Mountain Road.

is a recurring character in . Biography Moza is a Hylian woman who can be found near Ishto Soh Shrine in the Gerudo Highlands, where she is surrounded by Garbage Dumps. She carries a Pot Lid and a Soup Ladle, the latter of which she swings at the Cooking Pot in front of her. Inside her Cooking Pot is a burnt piece of Raw Gourmet Meat. When Link first approaches Moza, she will be confused and ask who he is. After Link expresses the same confusion, Moza introduces herself and explains she is training in isolation to complete her "ultimate dish". When Link tries to ask about her smoke signal, Moza insists that he is mistaken and that she is in the middle of Cooking. Upon being informed that it is burnt, Moza admits that she has failed. Moza sighs and confesses that whenever she tries to Cook, she never ends up with edible Food, but she does not know why her "ultimate recipe" is failing. If Link asks Moza to teach him a recipe, she will be excited by the prospect. She then describes her three recipes to Link and asks which he wants to learn. Moza's first recipe is her "lavish meat dish." The first step is to prepare the meat, and once this is done, add Gems to the Cooking Pot. When Link calls this recipe gross, Moza claims that Cooking meat with shiny Gems is the only way to create a lavish dish. Moza's attempts always result in Rock-Hard Food, though she is unsure where the rockiness comes from. Moza's second recipe is her "ancient meat dish." After preparing the meat, she tells Link to add an Ancient Material from a broken Guardian. When Link calls the recipe gross, Moza retorts that the only way to make an ancient meat dish is to include an ingredient with historical value. While she always ends up with Dubious Food, Moza does not see how her recipe could be dubious. Finally, Moza's last recipe is her "ultimate survival dish." After defeating a Monster, Moza instructs Link to Cook with the Monster Parts he has harvested. When Link calls the recipe gross, Moza insists that he needs to be able to eat anything so he can survive in the wild, and this sentiment was the inspiration for her dish. While the result is always Dubious Food, Moza believes this is a sacrifice she needs to make in order to achieve her goal. She is unable to see what is dubious about Cooking with Monster Parts. After explaining a recipe, Moza states that Cooking is complicated, since she messes up her recipes even when her ingredients are perfect. If Link refuses to listen to her recipes, Moza claims that they are special. When Link returns to speak to Moza, she believes he has come back to hear about her recipes.

is a recurring character in . Biography Muava is an elderly Gerudo woman who can be found sitting by the Goddess Statue near the Southeast Gate of Gerudo Town. In her youth, Muava travelled across Hyrule, and she was considered to be a beauty by Hylian men. Having heard rumors of Lover's Pond, she searched for it in the hope of finding her true love. However, she never found it, and she eventually became old and was no longer sought after by men. When Link first approaches Muava, she will begin to greet him, but then she wonders how a man was able to enter Gerudo Town. Link reacts with surprise, and Muava states that while he might be able to fool everyone else in Gerudo Town, she is not so easy. She assures Link that she will not share his secret, since she does not care what he does. Since he came all the way to the Southeast Gate, however, she asks if he would like to talk with her. If Link asks about the nearby Goddess Statue, Muava tells him that it has been there since before she was born. She explains that nobody visits it anymore because they do not "believe in that stuff anymore," comparing it to how people avoid her now as well. Muava believes that someone needs to keep the Goddess Statue company, which is what she decided to do. If Link asks Muava if she has ever left Gerudo Town, she recounts her past as a traveler to him. Noticing that Link appears sad, Muava tells him not to be, since it was a long time ago and she chased her dreams. Muava enjoys talking to Link, commenting that it is nice to speak with a man again. Before Link ends their conversation, Muava advises him to live his life to the fullest. When Link returns to Muava, she refers to him as "Mr. Cute Voe."

is a recurring character in . Biography Mubs is a Hylian who resides in Lurelin Village. She runs the Merchant Boat General Store on a Dock, where she sells Fish and other supplies. The Merchant Boat itself carries some of her storage, including extra Armored Porgies and Mighty Porgies. When Link first speaks to Mubs, she welcomes him to the Merchant Boat and remarks that she has never seen him before. During the day, she says that her fresh Fish are perfect for hot Weather. She also claims that she restocked her Fish that morning. In the evenings, she asks Link if he is shopping for his dinner. At night, she inquires if Link wants a midnight snack. At the end of their conversations, Mubs invites Link to return to the Merchant Boat. If asked, Mubs tells Link that he can make a purchase by standing in front of her stock and interacting with it. Whenever Link makes a purchase from the Merchant Boat, Mubs will thank him for his business. If Link buys the entirety of one Item, Mubs promises to restock soon. If Link stands on Mubs' products, she yells at him to stop. Like other General Store managers, Link can sell his own Items to Mubs. When Mubs buys an Item from Link, she will be grateful and encourage him to sell more. After selling to Mubs, she will thank him for his business. Due to Pirates invading Lurelin Village, Mubs was forced to flee the Lurelin Village Store. After arriving in Lookout Landing with Garini, she opened a new General Store with the goal of raising enough Rupees to return home. When Link passes by Mubs, she will recognize him as a newcomer to Lookout Landing. She welcomes him, explaining that despite her General Store looking thrown together, she offers a variety of goods. If Link asks about her hometown, she explains how she was forced to leave. Although she is concerned about Lurelin Village, she is dedicated to selling as much as she can for now.

Mucktoroks are Bosses in . Characteristics Mucktorok is a small Octorok-like creature, not much larger than a regular Octorok, which can create and control Sludge. It uses this Sludge to make a shark-like monster similar to a Gyorg, which it rides in battle. One Mucktorok is the source of the Sludge that is polluting the Lanayru Region. After this Mucktorok is slain in the Water Temple, three Mucktoroks can be found at Boss Rematches throughout the Depths. The first is located west of the Abandoned Tarrey Mine in the Akkala Highlands Depths, the second is located near the Uinoj Lightroot in the Lanayru Wetlands Depths, and the final one is near the Uoyoyuik Lightroot in the Central Hyrule Depths. If Mucktorok is not defeated in the Water Temple, Link fights it at Gloom's Origin during the War in the Depths of Hyrule. It appears after Marbled Gohma and before Queen Gibdo. When defeated in the Depths, Mucktoroks drop Octo Balloons, Octorok Eyeballs, and Octorok Tentacles. They will also unlock a Treasure Chests containing Huge Crystallized Charges the first time they are defeated. Mucktorok hides in its Sludge shark, and it attacks with a combination of charging attacks, waves of Sludge, and a Sludge beam. The Sludge shark resists most forms of attack, but Sidon's Power of Water or any Water-based attack will wash away the Sludge and expose Mucktorok. It will attempt to flee when it is vulnerable, but it can be stunned with an Arrow when it does so. At half health, Mucktorok will begin spraying Sludge around the arena to slow Link down and make it harder for him to dodge its attacks. The Sludge projectiles can also damage Link if he takes a direct hit. Additionally, Mucktorok will begin jumping between puddles of Sludge when it is exposed and will continue to spray Sludge while doing so, making it harder to hit.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Muddle Buds are a type of Flower that can be found throughout the Depths. They can be manipulated with the Ultrahand and Fuse Ancient Powers. When thrown, struck by a Weapon, Enemy, or Object, shot by an Arrow, or Fused to a Weapon, Shield, catches on fire or fired Arrow, they burst into a large cloud of purple powder, which will cause nearby Enemies to become hostile to one another. If only one Enemy is present in the immediate vicinity, it will attack Link instead. The purple powder is harmful to Link, dealing a minor knock back effect and a quarter Heart of damage. Muddle Buds do not attract Lightning nor conduct Electricity. When Fused to a Weapon or Shield, a Muddle Bud will be consumed after only one use unless it is Fused to a Weapon that is part of the Korok Gear, in which case it can be used continuously. Addison may give Link a Muddle Bud as a random reward for helping him stand up one of his Signboards. Other Appearances Muddle Buds are Materials that can only be used as Camp supplies.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Mushroom Omelets are Meals made by Cooking any Mushroom, a Bird Egg, Goat Butter, and Rock Salt together in a Cooking Pot. The regular version can be made either by using Hylian Shrooms, which offer no status effects, or by using multiple mushrooms with differing effects. Eating a Mushroom Omelet will heal some of Link's Hearts. The fluffy texture is considered to be a highlight of Mushroom Omelets. Either by using certain mushrooms or through the additional of more Ingredients, Link can create several variations of Mushroom Omelet: Chilly Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Chillshrooms or other chilly Ingredients. Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance if he eats these omelets. Electro Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Zapshrooms or other electric Ingredients. When eaten, Link will be granted one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Endura Shrooms or other enduring Ingredients. Link's Stamina Wheel will be completely restored and overfilled when he eats these. Energizing Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Stamella Shrooms or other energizing Ingredients. Eating these omelets will refill part of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Rushrooms or other hasty Ingredients. Consuming these will increase Link's movement speed. Hearty Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Hearty Truffles, Big Hearty Truffles, or other hearty Ingredients. When eaten, all of Link's Hearts will be healed and he will gain Extra Hearts. Mighty Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Razorshrooms or other mighty Ingredients. By eating these omelets, Link's attack power will be increased. Sneaky Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Silent Shrooms or other sneaky Ingredients. Eating them will boost Link's Stealth. Spicy Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Sunshrooms or other spicy Ingredients. Link will gain one level of Cold Resistance when he eats these omelets. Tough Mushroom Omelet: Made by using Ironshrooms or other tough Ingredients. When eaten, they will boost Link's Defense.

Spicy Mushroom Rice Balls: Made by using Sunshrooms or other spicy Ingredients. Link can eat them to gain one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Mushroom Rice Balls: Made by using Ironshrooms or other tough Ingredients. When eaten, Link's Defense will be boosted. Other Appearances

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Mushroom Risotto can be made by Cooking any Mushroom, Hylian Rice, Goat Butter, and Rock Salt together in a Cooking Pot. The default version of Mushroom Risotto can only be made either by using Hylian Shrooms, which offer no status effects, or by using multiple Mushrooms with differing effects. Ivee lists the Ingredients as one bundle of Hylian Rice, one serving of Goat Butter, a few Hylian Shrooms, and a little bit of Rock Salt. She also notes that the Hylian Shrooms can be substituted for a Hearty Salmon, which would result in Salmon Risotto. Several different kinds of Mushrooms can be used when making Mushroom Risotto, which can result in the following variations: Chilly Mushroom Risotto: Made by using Chillshrooms or other chilly Ingredients. If eaten, Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Mushroom Risotto: Made by using Zapshrooms or other electric Ingredients. When eaten, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Mushroom Risotto: Made by using Endura Shrooms or other enduring Ingredients. Link's Stamina Wheel will be completely replenished and overfilled by eating these. Energizing Mushroom Risotto: Made by using Stamella Shrooms or other energizing Ingredients. Eating them will replenish part of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Mushroom Risotto: Made by using Rushrooms or other hasty Ingredients. If eaten, Link's movement speed will be increased. Hearty Mushroom Risotto: Made by using Hearty Truffles, Big Hearty Truffles, or other hearty Ingredients. These meals will heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Mighty Mushroom Risotto: Made by using Razorshrooms or other mighty Ingredients. Consuming these meals will boost Link's attack power. Spicy Mushroom Risotto: Made by using Sunshrooms or other spicy Ingredients. They grant Link one level of Cold Resistance when consumed. are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Mushroom Skewers are Meals that can be made by Cooking any Mushrooms in a Cooking Pot. In order to cook the regular version of this dish, Link must use either only Hylian Shrooms or multiple, different Mushrooms with varying effects. If Link consumes a Mushroom Skewer it will restore at least one of his Hearts. The skewers are known for their colorful presentation. Using certain Mushrooms when making Mushroom Skewers can result in the following variations: Chilly Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Chillshrooms. They can be eaten to grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Zapshrooms. Eating them will give Link one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Endura Shrooms. Link can eat them to completely refill and overfill his Stamina Wheel. Energizing Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Stamella Shrooms. By eating them, a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel will be refilled. Hasty Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Rushrooms. When eaten, they will increase Link's movement speed. Hearty Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Hearty Truffles or Big Hearty Truffles. Eating these skewers will heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him Extra Hearts. Mighty Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Razorshrooms. If these skewers are eaten, Link will gain a boost to his attack power. Sneaky Mushroom Skewer: Made by using Silent Shrooms. Other Appearances Only one variation of Mushroom Skewer, the Electro Mushroom Skewer, is found in , and its recipe is earned by completing the Quest "Who's Shocked by Lightning?". It is made using four Zapshrooms. However, it can be lowered to three through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". Preparing this meal before a battle reduces the damage the Warriors take from Lightning attacks by 50%.

is a recurring character in . Biography Muzu is one of the elders on the Zora council. He was also in charge of teaching Mipha, which lead to him being close to her. Even before the Great Calamity, he harbored a disdain for Hylians. Afterwards, his hatred grew, as he felt that they were responsible for the devastation caused by the Great Calamity and Mipha's death. When Divine Beast Vah Ruta began its rampage, the Zora came to the decision that they would need the help of a Hylian to shoot Shock Arrows at it. To further this goal, Muzu was placed in charge of procuring Shock Arrows. When Link first enters the Throne Room of Zora's Domain, Muzu will watch him. He is silent until King Dorephan asks for Link's help in calming Divine Beast Vah Ruta, citing disgust at the thought of receiving assistance from a Hylian. Both King Dorephan and Sidon admonish him, with Sidon reminding Muzu that they already came to the conclusion that their only choice was to seek the aid of a Hylian. In anger, Muzu reminds King Dorephan how the Hylians misused the Sheikah's Ancient Technology and caused the death of Mipha. Muzu once again protests when King Dorephan gifts the Zora Armor to Link. He argues that it is too important to give to a Hylian, since it is tradition for Zora princesses to present this Armor to those they are engaged to. Though Link is a Champion, Muzu believes that he did not have a romantic relationship with Mipha. In frustration, Muzu storms out of the Throne Room, still unable to understand King Dorephan's reasoning. With Muzu gone, King Dorephan is unsure how they should proceed, since he was in charge of gathering the Shock Arrows for their plan. Sidon decides to resolve their issues with Muzu, running after him to the Zora's Domain Square. King Dorephan asks Link to join them, as he believes he may be able to assist Sidon. After this encounter, the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" Main Quest will begin. Sidon and Muzu can be found arguing in front of Mipha's Statue in the Zora's Domain Square. When Link approaches, Muzu remarks that he came for nothing, as he does not wish to speak with him. Sidon then explains to Muzu that Link was the one who Mipha was in love with. However, Muzu vehemently resists the notion, stating that Mipha could not have fallen in love with a Hylian. He states that his position is clear, since Link does not remember Mipha even when looking at her Statue. His words cause Link to look up at Mipha's Statue, which unlocks the "Mipha's Touch" Recovered Memory. After the Recovered Memory, Muzu notices that Link is shaking and asks what is wrong. When Link claims to remember Mipha, Muzu refuses to believe him, noting how convenient his timing is. He demands that Link show him proof of his relationship with Mipha, promising to share the location of the

the Recovered Memory, Muzu notices that Link is shaking and asks what is wrong. When Link claims to remember Mipha, Muzu refuses to believe him, noting how convenient his timing is. He demands that Link show him proof of his relationship with Mipha, promising to share the location of the Shock Arrows if he is able to do so. When Link equips the Zora Armor, Sidon will tell Muzu to look at what he is wearing. Upon seeing that the Zora Armor fits him perfectly, Muzu is initially confused. Sidon explains that the fact that it fits Link is proof that it was intended for him. He claims that the reason Mipha never told him was due to his hatred of Hylians. Muzu is shocked that Mipha would have feelings for Link. He takes a moment to silently gaze up at Mipha's Statue. Though he dislikes it, he recognizes that their only choice is to accept Link's help in saving Zora's Domain. As such, he decides to tell Link where he can find Shock Arrows. He points towards Ploymus Mountain, explaining that on Shatterback Point, there is a Monster that shoots Shock Arrows. Sidon realizes that he is referring to the Lynel, claiming that it would be a quick way to gather Shock Arrows. Muzu estimates that Link will need at least 20 Shock Arrows in order to face Divine Beast Vah Ruta. If Link speaks to Muzu again, he repeats that the Shock Arrows can be obtained from the territory of the Lynel on Ploymus Mountain. However, he warns Link that if he goes there, he cannot guarantee his survival. When Link returns to the Throne Room after appeasing Divine Beast Vah Ruta, the residents of Zora's Domain gather to show their appreciation. During this time, Muzu apologizes for his behavior and acknowledges Link's noble intentions, claiming that all of the Zora are grateful for his help. He concedes that the older generation of Zora misunderstood Hylians. Muzu hopes that Link will be able to forgive him one day. After "Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been completed, Muzu can be found on the northern bridge from Zora's Domain. He again claims that he misunderstood Hylians, as even without fins and gills, Link was able to stop Divine Beast Vah Ruta. He states that he should have expected such from the one who Mipha loved, congratulating him for his work. Muzu wishes that Link will find it in his heart to forgive him. During the "EX Champion Mipha's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Muzu and Tottika appear on a cliff in the Akkala Highlands, overlooking the gap between Ankel Island and Tingel Island. When Link speaks to him, Muzu reveals that they have been sent to watch over the site of one of Mipha's Trials, as the signs from when she first attempted them have now returned. He recounts a note that Mipha kept, which states that the path to the Trial is revealed as

speaks to him, Muzu reveals that they have been sent to watch over the site of one of Mipha's Trials, as the signs from when she first attempted them have now returned. He recounts a note that Mipha kept, which states that the path to the Trial is revealed as the sun rises. Mipha would also repeat these words about her Trial. Once Link causes Kee Dafunia Shrine to rise from the Lanayru Sea, Muzu will be impressed that Link was able to figure out Mipha's riddle. He believes that this must have been the reason that Mipha fell in love with Link. Now that the Trial has been completed, Muzu orders Tottika to prepare for their trip back to Zora's Domain. After "EX Champion Mipha's Song" has been completed, Muzu will be commend Link for overcoming the same Trial that Mipha did. He understands how Link was able to win Mipha's affection, and he states that he is impressed.

is a character in . Biography Mylle is a Hylian member of the Zonai Survey Team. She has been tasked with researching Shrines of Light, which she prefers to Chasm Research. She cane be found in the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins, where she investigates the Kyononis Shrine. When Link approaches Mylle, she will be surprised by him. She is concerned by her proximity to the Hyrule Castle Chasm, which has left her on edge. She is also concerned that the Kyononis Shrine could be dangerous, and she warns Link to be careful. If Link asks her about Chasms, Mylle explains that they appeared as a result of the Upheaval, and the two in the area are the Hyrule Castle Chasm and the Hyrule Field Chasm. Having heard that members of the Zonai Survey Team became sick from Chasm Research, Mylle is happy to focus on Shrines of Light. If Link asks about Shrines of Light, Mylle recalls that their appearance ended up on the front page of the Newspaper. While it is known they came from the ancient past, their origins remain a mystery. Since Shrines of Light and Chasms could be dangerous, the Zonai Survey Team has been dedicated to investigating them. Mylle is inspired by the Monster-Control Crew's search of Hyrule Castle, and she wants to put in the same long hours that they do. She wants to finish her research and return to Lookout Landing and wonders what is moving around the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins. When Link opens the Shrine she is surprised about its new entrance.

The is an Item in . Location and Uses The Mystic Robe is a piece of Armor torso gear. It can be obtained by trading a total of seven Bubbul Gems to Koltin. When worn, taking damage will cause Link to lose Rupees instead of Hearts. For every quarter of a Heart that Link would take, he will instead lose 10 Rupees. However, there is a limit to how much damage will be converted into Rupees at once. At one level of Defense Up, up to three Hearts-worth of damage will be converted, six Hearts at level two, and nine Hearts at level three. Once this threshold has been passed, Link will take any remaining damage. In addition, the Mystic Robe is unable to mitigate any damage dealt by Gloom. Dye Options

is a recurring character in . Biography Myti is a Hylian Stable Worker at the Outskirt Stable. During the day, she can be found standing next to the Stable's Cooking Pot, and she asks Link if he would like to use it. If Link inquires about the Cooking Pot, she will explain that since the Stable does not serve Food, guests are expected to prepare their own. If Link declines the offer, she will instruct him to speak to Embry for assistance and Trott for directions. If it begins to Rain, Myti will take shelter under the Stable's roof, and she instructs that Link to do the same. If Link inquires about the Cooking Pot while she is inside, she will suggest that he stay the night, as the Cooking Pot cannot be used in such Weather. In the evening, Haite joins Myti at the Cooking Pot for dinner. At night, Myti will head into Outskirt Stable and sit at the table. If Link attempts to speak to her, she will tell him to talk with her later. Around midnight, she will fall asleep while sitting. If Link chooses to listen to her, she will talk about vegetables in her sleep. She will sleep there until 6:00 AM.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Nabi Lake is located in West Necluda. It is formed after Hylia River splits at the Floret Sandbar. Nabi Lake is flanked by South Nabi Lake, and the area to the west is known as West Nabi Lake}. Along the Lake's western front is an unoccupied platform, and several small islets can be found within its Water. Three Treasure Chests are found on Nabi Lake. The first is a Stone Chest on one of the islets on the north side of the Lake, which contains an Amber. A second Metal Chest containing an Opal can be found embedded in the ground along the Lake's western bank. In order to retrieve it, Link must use the Magnesis Rune to pull it from the ground. Finally, another Metal Chest can be found submerged near the islet in the southern portion of Nabi Lake, and it contains a Silver Rupee. left|40px Nabi Lake has one Korok Seed Puzzle. On the small islet on its south side, Link can find a Rock that serves as a Natural Hiding Spot. When he picks the Rock up, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

, designated by the trial name The Ability to Rewind, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Nachoyah Shrine is located above the Room of Awakening on the Great Sky Island. After Link enters the Temple of Time and receives the Recall ability from Zelda, the Spirit of Rauru guides him to the Nachoyah Shrine to receive the Great Sky Island's fourth Light of Blessing. In order to enter the Shrine of Light, Link must interact with the Nachoyah Shrine's entrance. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Nachoyah Shrine The Nachoyah Shrine is heavily built around the use of the Recall ability. The first segment contains a Current of water that pushes Rafts along. One of the Rafts falls from a Waterfall, which makes for a ride up onto the ledge above once it is Recalled. On the second segment, there is a large, toothed Gear running through a pool of water beside a ledge with a Treasure Chest. In this area, there are also large clock-like hands running in opposite directions to each other that control a portcullis leading to the end of the Shrine of Light. This portcullis will only descend when both hands are positioned identically. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Nachoyah Shrine. By interacting with the Magical panel in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Nack is a Hylian farmer who lives in Hateno Village. During the day, he can be found tending to his garden near the Village's entrance. At 9:00 PM, he returns to his House north of his field, which he shares with Nikki, Nebb, and Narah. Once there, he sleeps in his Bed until 5:00 AM. When Link first speaks to him, Nack will offer directions to points of interest in Hateno Village. If Link asks about a "strange place," Nack believes he is talking about the Kochi Dye Shop operate by Sayge, whom he refers to as "Mr. Toothy." Though he acknowledges that Sayge is masterful at Dyeing clothes, he is also considers him to be strange. If Link asks for directions to a "very strange place," Nack will point him towards the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. He is suspicious about the research that its director, Purah, conducts, as he does not know how it is supposed to keep Hyrule Kingdom safe. In addition, he states that Purah does not like kids much, which has lead to the children of Hateno Village taking an interest in her. Finally, if Link asks for a place to rest, Nack claims The Great Ton Pu Inn is a typical choice for travelers. However, he also mentions the model houses created by Bolson Construction behind the East Wind. Nack is interested in the new Houses, and he wishes he could sleep in one. When Link speaks to Nack while carrying the Blue Flame, he recognizes it as belonging to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. He then admits that he does not mind Purah, since he believes the ultimate goal of her research is to help the people. of Hyrule Kingdom. If Link speaks to Nack again, he says to hurry and bring it to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. While he does not know what they are researching, he believes it will be beneficial for the people of Hyrule Kingdom.

is a recurring character in . Biography Naddon is a Goron traveler who carries a Traveling Pack. He can be found walking along the Shadow Pass in the Akkala Highlands, stopping at East Akkala Stable and South Akkala Stable along the way. While on the Shadow Pass, Naddon asks Link if he has met his brother, Boldon. He explains that Boldon is big-hearted and does not get caught up on small issues, and he wonders where he is traveling currently. Should Link ever meet Boldon, Naddon asks that he talk with him. Recently, Naddon met Laroba, a Gerudo woman who also travels along the Shadow Pass. He thought she was pretty, and he appreciated how shiny her hair was. Naddon is knowledgeable about Gems. He suggests that Link mine them from Ore Deposits, since the rare ones sell for many Rupees. Naddon himself sells more rare Gems that he finds in Ore Deposits and Treasure Chests, as dislikes their taste. At East Akkala Stable, he reveals that he eats the Rocks he does not need, but he realizes that a Hylian like Link would rather sell them. Often, Naddon makes remarks about eating while he travels. He claims that Rocks are an important part of the Goron diet, which leads to him debating whether to sell or eat rare ones. Naddon also considers Rocks to be delicious, but he prefers to sell Gems instead of eating them. Despite the difficult journey to Goron City, Naddon suggests that Link visit, claiming there are many good Shops. Naddon also talks about the Goron Hot Springs, which are located along the Mountain Road leading to Death Mountain. Due to the danger if the Mountain Road, however, Naddon warns Link about attempting to visit. Despite this, he has still heard of travelers making the journey to the Springs, though he still considers it to be risky for non-Gorons. During Rain or a Thunderstorm, Naddon will run to seek shelter. He also remarks that his current situation seems to be hopeless. When Link speaks to him after he escapes the Rain, he makes a rumbling sound, though he claims that it came from the Lightning. When Naddon is attacked by Enemies, he will run away in fear. During this time, he will be annoyed by their appearance. He can also become so tired from panting that he becomes thirsty. Once Link has defeated the Enemies, Naddon will be relieved. He thanks Link for his assistance, often complimenting him. As a reward, he gives Link Food and Rupees.

is a character in . Biography Nako is a Korok who can be found in the Great Hyrule Forest Depths during the Main Quest "Trail of the Master Sword". They are situated near the Zonai Ruins within Minshi Grove, which are directly below the Minshi Woods Chasm. Nako left Korok Forest to take a walk alongside Tasho, Mopu, Mokka, Raha, Jatora, and Maheli. After being unable to pass through the Lost Woods, the group attempted to return to Korok Forest by entering the Depths through the Minshi Woods Chasm, although Tasho stayed on the Surface. However, Nako has become scared of the Depths and now regrets heading underground.

is a recurring character in . Biography Nali is a Gerudo woman who resides in Gerudo Town. During the day, she can be found in the center of Town, occasionally speaking to Pritana. At night, she sleeps in her House next to the Barracks, which she shares with Pritana. During Pritana's conversation with Nali, Pritana says she cannot believe that Riju's Thunder Helm was stolen by thieves. Nali then recalls that the Thunder Helm was favored by Urbosa, and she explains that it has been passed from chief to chief for generations. Pritana feels sorry for Riju due to how young she is. Nali has heard that the Gerudo guards suspect a group of assassins stole the Helm. With this, Pritana reasons that this must be why the Barracks have been noisy lately. While Nali is walking around the Gerudo Town market, she asks if Link if he is a Hylian. She claims to be impressed whenever a Hylian is able to cross the Gerudo Desert. Following this, Nali asks if Link is also shopping, revealing that she is searching for Mighty Bananas. If Link asks about Mighty Bananas, Nali explains that they are full of protein and calories and that eating them grants power. Though they are often available at the Kara Kara Bazaar, not many of them are available. Quietly, she admits that she is unable to ride a Sand Seal, which means it is difficult for her to make the journey, but she asks Link not to tell anyone. Nali has also heard a rumor about a group that only eats Mighty Bananas, which depletes their stock in the Gerudo Desert. If Link speaks to Nali after she wakes up in the morning, she comments that it is strange to see a tourist in Gerudo Town and explains that the Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been deterring outsiders. She wishes there were more "brave vai" like Link who are willing to make the journey. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Nali will be more energetic in the morning. She explains that she was never able to sleep well between the Divine Beast's stomping and Pritana returning home late at night. However, with Vah Naboris's rampage coming to an end, she explains that she wakes up feeling refreshed now. When Link approaches Nali during the night, she informs him that he will freeze if he leaves Gerudo Town wearing the Gerudo Outfit. Though she would like to invite him to stay at her House, she is already sharing her room with Pritana. Instead, she suggests checking out the Hotel Oasis, as there may still be rooms available. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Pritana will note to Nali that the Divine Beast has gotten quiet. Hearing this, Nali realizes that she has not felt any rocking or shaking as of late. Pritana then wonders if this is due to the Thunder Helm being returned to the Royal Palace.

is a recurring character in . Biography Nanna is an elderly Sheikah woman who resides in Kakariko Village. During the day, she can be found sitting under the Tree at the Village's southeastern entrance. Her House is the one closest to this entrance, and it is where she sleeps at night. In the past, Nanna trained under her mentor, Purah, researching Ancient Technology at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. During this time, she found Purah to be strange. When Link first arrives in Kakariko Village, he will find Nanna injured and sitting on the ground. If Link approaches her, she explains that she has twisted her ankle. She manages to stand on her own and is embarrassed that a visitor found her in such a condition. Nanna then notices the Sheikah Slate on Link's belt and hesitantly asks where he found it. Once Link explains, she states that carrying the Slate means that he is the hero of legend. She admits that not many people remember those legends, but she assures Link that her people have been waiting for him. Nanna then directs Link to Impa, the leader of the Sheikah. If Link asks where to find Impa, Nanna will give him directions to Impa's House, which is located below Lantern Falls. Before he goes, Nanna expresses how honored she is to meet him, though she believes he is used to such praise due to how long he has lived. Once Link has spoken to Impa, Nanna hears that the Sheikah Slate is not fully functional, and she claims that her mentor Purah should be able to help. If Link asks about her mentor, Nanna explains that Purah researched the Sheikah Slate alongside Zelda, and she directs him to Hateno Village in the east to find her. She also warns Link that Purah is odd. Afterwards, she wishes Link well on his journey. When Link speaks to Nanna afterwards, she tells him that the Sheikah Slate was cherished by Zelda, and it contains many of her Memories. She believes that if Zelda knew it was in Link's possession, she would be happy. At 6:00 PM, Nanna returns to her House, where her granddaughter Lasli watches over her as she sleeps in her Bed. If Link wakes her up before speaking to Impa, Nanna will be embarrassed of her condition and apologize, mentioning how her mentor warned her. Despite her weakness, she offers what aid she can give and will repeat her information on Purah. When woken after the Sheikah Slate upgrade is complete, she comments how Link looks exhausted, and she encourages him to sleep at the Shuteye Inn.

is a character in . Biography Nappin is a Hylian and a member of the Zonai Survey Team. He can be found laying in one of the Beds in the Emergency Shelter. Prior to Link's arrival in Lookout Landing, Nappin explored Chasms for Josha and got sick because of Gloom. By eating a Sundelion, he was able to start recovering, but he has stayed in Bed to avoid being asked to return to Chasm Research. Despite his admiration for Josha, Nappin is unable to bring himself to return to seeing Chasms. Deon, who can initially be found on the Bed next to Nappin, complains about his sleep talking.

is a recurring character in . Biography Narah is a a young Hylian girl who resides in Hateno Village. She lives with her family in the House northeast of the Village's entrance. During the day, she and her brother, Nebb, can be be found running in front of the East Wind, the Well, and the Kochi Dye Shop. When Link approaches Narah she tells him that she likes to run. In addition, she also likes to talk, and she demands that Link ask her questions. Link can ask Narah three different things: who she cares about, what she enjoys doing, and what things she likes. Whenever she answers one of Link's questions, she will ask to keep the conversation going. Once the conversation is done, Narah will cheerfully bid him goodbye. If Link asks Narah who she cares about, she responds that she loves her mother, Nikki, but she is unable to interrupt her when she is talking with Amira at the Well. However, Narah has discovered that she can talk to Nikki if she sneaks up to her from behind. If Link asks what she likes to do, Narah tells him how she enjoys catching Insects. She teaches Link her technique for doing so, which is crouching down and approaching quietly. Finally, if Link asks Narah what she likes, she shares her love of Gems and Rupees. If Link has a Gem in his Inventory, Narah will notice. When Link asks what has her attention, she tells him to sell his Gem so he can be rich. Narah will also notice if Link does not have any Gems. At 8:00 PM, Narah and Nebb will run back to their House. When Link approaches Narah, she tells him that she is unable to talk. She sleeps in one of the Beds in the House's loft. During Rain, she will take shelter inside her House. When Link speaks to her, she says that she likes Cooking. When Link walks near Narah while carrying the Blue Flame, she begins to follow him around out of curiosity. If Link speaks to her, she calls it pretty and decides that she likes it. She then asks Link where he can get one of her own.

is a recurring character in . Biography Nat is a Hylian woman who can be encountered at several locations throughout Hyrule. She and her sister, Meghyn, are hunting for Hearty Truffles. They can be encountered in the Ginner Woods, along the Ternio Trail south of Foothill Stable, and in the Sarjon Woods, where they will be under attack by a pair of Bokoblins. When attacked by a Bokoblin, Nat will run away in fear. If Link speaks to her at this time, she will be panicking about what to do and whether Meghyn is alright. When Nat wakes up after being knocked unconscious by a Bokoblin, she complains about how she and Meghyn were ambushed. Should a Bokoblin knock Meghyn unconscious, Nat will shout and beg her to wake up. Once Link defeats the Bokoblins, Nat will be relieved. If Link approaches her, she asks if he is a "wandering do-gooder," giving him Food or Rupees as a reward. She then resolves to return to hunting for Hearty Truffles. After the situation has been resolved, she explains to Link that she and Meghyn are searching for Hearty Truffles, and she acknowledges that it is dangerous for them to do so. However, when she thinks about the taste of Hearty Truffles, she decides to ignore the warnings. Nat and Meghyn then begin to scavenge for Hearty Truffles at the base of a nearby Tree, with Nat trying to calm herself with breathing techniques. When Link approaches Nat, she explains that Hearty Truffles are capable of soothing one's fatigue and restoring their health. She once again admits that it is dangerous for her and Meghyn, recalling that they have been attacked before. Despite this, she believes that they will receive a great reward for the risks they take. Meghyn then stands, reminding Nat that they should value their lives more than any Rupees they could make. Nat argues that they will be fine, as they will either practice fighting or find Hearty Truffles. Meghyn asserts that Nat will be the death of her. When Link speaks to Meghyn, she recounts telling Nat that their Hearty Truffle-hunting location would be dangerous, but she was unable to convince her due to her desire for Rupees. Nat then snaps at Meghyn to continue their hunt, as they will not return home until they find Hearty Truffles. Meghyn sighs, but she ultimately agrees that Nat is right.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Natak Shrine is located within the Sokkala Sky Archipelago in the Akkala Highlands Sky. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Natak Shrine The Natak Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Natak Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Natie is a Korok who runs the Spore Store, a Mushroom Shop located within the Great Deku Tree in Korok Forest. In anticipation of Link's arrival, Natie has been gathering Mushrooms for him. They welcome Link to make a purchase or sell his Items. If Link asks where they are, Natie explains that they are technically inside the Great Deku Tree's stomach, which they warn him not to think too hard about. Alongside Natie, two other Koroks set up Shops for Link inside the Great Deku Tree, which he allowed them to do. Noticing that Link is bigger than them, Natie realizes that he may feel cramped. Despite this, they encourage Link to enjoy his shopping. When Link buys one of Natie's Mushrooms, they will thank him and encourage him to eat it. They will also be grateful that they thought to pick Mushrooms for him. If Link buys all of one type of Mushroom, Natie thanks him and promises to collect more. If Link buys all of Natie's stock, they will be surprised by how much he likes Mushrooms. They promise to forage for more, but in the meantime, they offer to buy his Items. At the end of their conversations, Natie encourages Link to sell any of his Items to them, even if it is not a Mushroom. When Link asks to sell to Natie, they ask what he wants to sell. Natie encourages Link to sell to them, showing interest in what he has to offer. When Natie makes a purchase, they may try to ask him to keep selling. They also promise to take care of their Items they bought from Link. Finally, after buying one of Link's Items, Natie will occasionally remark that he smells nice.

are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Natural Hiding Spots go unnamed in . Location and Uses Natural Hiding Spots are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. They come in five common forms: Rocks in the Open, under large stone slabs, Rocks under Boulders, behind Cracked Walls, and Rocks under Leaves. The most common of the six are Rocks in the Open, where all Link needs to do is lift the Rock. The large stone slabs and Boulders must be moved out of the way through use of Stasis or Octo Balloons to reveal the Rock. Rocks hidden under a Pile of Leaves must be burned out using Fire, revealing the Rock afterwards. Natural Hiding Spot Rocks can also be found behind Cracked Walls, which Link must destroy using a Remote Bomb. Another type of Natural Hiding Spot involves picking up Items that are out of place. When any of these Puzzles are completed, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Natural Hiding Spots are Korok Seed Puzzles in . They come in five different forms: Rocks in the Open, Rocks in Ice Blocks, Rocks under Boulders, a Rock under Bramble, and Rocks under Leaves. Whenever Link picks up a Rock that is part of one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Naydra's Claws can be obtained by shooting the claws of Naydra as it flies by. Naydra can be found on Mount Lanayru, from which it will fly down to either the Lanayru Promenade or Lanayru Bay. When Cooking with Naydraw's Claws, the resulting meal will always be Dubious Food. Naydra's Claws can be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Light Blue Dye. Two Claws, as well as five Courser Bee Honeys, are needed to upgrade the Tunic of the Wild to its second tier at a Great Fairy Fountain. One can also be used to upgrade the Fierce Deity Armor to its second tier.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Naydra's Scales can be collected from the Dragon Naydra, who rests atop Mount Lanayru. After defeating Malice Naydra and freeing the Dragon, Link will be able to strike her anywhere on her body and retrieve a Scale. The first time that Link strikes Naydra, she will yield a Scale regardless of where she was struck. To subsequently obtain a Scale from Naydra, Link must strike the main portion of her body. A Scale can also be found in a Treasure Chest beneath a stone slab above the northern entrance to the Library at Hyrule Castle. Link must place a Scale inside the Spring of Wisdom to complete the Shrine Quest "The Spring of Wisdom". Doing so will yield the way to Jitan Sa'mi Shrine. Cooking with Naydra's Scales will add 90 seconds to the Meal's Added Effect and guarantee a critical dish. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Light Blue Dye. Naydra's Scales are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Naydra's Scales are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain:

is a recurring Dragon Spirit in . Characteristics Naydra is one of three roaming Dragons in Hyrule Kingdom, the others being Dinraal and Farosh. While she cannot be defeated, she does not actively try to harm Link. However, if Link gets too close, he will be frozen by the icy aura surrounding her body. Link can prevent himself being frozen by wearing either a full Snowquill Set that has been enhanced twice by a Great Fairy, or Zant's Helmet. Naydra will drop different Materials if Link shoots her with a Bow. Depending on what part of Naydra is hit, she will drop either a Shard of Naydra's Horn, Shard of Naydra's Fang, Naydra's Claw, or Naydra's Scale. Naydra's Scale can be offered at the Spring of Wisdom to reveal the Jitan Sa'mi Shrine. Naydra, unlike the other dragons, does not roam Hyrule at first. She is first encountered as Malice Naydra at the Spring of Wisdom. After Link has purified Naydra of the Malice, Naydra roams the Lanayru and East Necluda Regions. However, Naydra will not appear if Link is too close to her spawn point. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Naydra Snowfield is located on the western end of Mount Lanayru, just past the Lanayru Road - East Gate. It is a grove of Cedar Trees, and it is also the starting point of the path leading to the Spring of Wisdom. Several of Luminous Stone Deposits are situated in the northeast corner of the Snowfield. Since Naydra Snowfield is within a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least one level of Cold Resistance in order to traverse it without receiving damage. is a recurring character in . Biography Nazbi is a Hylian who travels the Hilltop High Road between Snowfield Stable and Tabantha Bridge Stable with his Horse, Dauntless. The pair stop at Serenne Stable along their journey. Nazbi carries a Fisherman's Shield and a Traveler's Sword. Nazbi is a treasure hunter and adventurer. His purpose in tracing the Hilltop High Road is to search of the Dragon's Road, which is said to be near the Tanagar Canyon. Since the Hilltop High Road is long and winds like a Dragon, Nazbi wonders if it could be the Dragon's Road. As he travels, he often wonders about the Road aloud to himself. Even though he may encounter danger, Nazbi is determined to find the Dragon's Road. Nazbi pledges to continue his search for Dragon's Road as long as Dauntless is strong. He thanks Dauntless for this, declaring that they are equal partners. In addition to the mystery of Dragon's Road, Nazbi wants to solve the riddle pertaining to Rito Village, which is supposed to be west of the snow fields. However, considering how long his bucket list is, he does not think he will be able to get to it. Despite being an adventurer, Nazbi has difficulty coping with cold Temperatures. He attempts to work himself in order to keep warm, but this strategy has little success. He will still encourage Dauntless to face the cold. When he stops at Snowfield Stable, Nazbi is unable to stop his teeth from chattering due to the cold. When he is caught in the Rain, Nazbi will be disappointed. After finding shelter, he wonders when the Rain will end. Nazbi will occasionally share knowledge of the area with Link. For example, he has heard of a "forest where the master lives" south of Serenne Stable. He is also interested in the Foot Race in Upland Lindor, and he suggests that Link try it out. Nazbi initially claims that he is too busy adventuring to try it himself, he will then admit he has become reliant on Dauntless for transportation.

is a recurring character in . Biography Nebb is a young Hylian child who resides in Hateno Village. He and his family live in the house northeast of the Village's entrance. During the day, it is his duty to watch over his sister, Narah, while their mother Nikki is at the Well. The two of them can be found running in front of the East Wind, the Well, and the Kochi Dye Shop. As he runs, he wonders about the world and makes noises imitating Weapons. At night, he sleeps in one of the Beds in the loft of his House, where he dreams about fighting. The first time Link speaks to him, Nebb asks if he is from outside of Hateno Village. Since Link looks like he can use a Bow and sword, Nebb asks if he is strong. Regardless of Link's answer, Nebb decides to ask for his help in making his dream come true. He explains that his deceased grandfather was a lover of weaponry, but he passed away before seeing all of the Weapons he wanted to. Therefore, he asks Link to show him Weapons so he can describe them to his grandfather when they meet again. When Link agrees, Nebb will be excited. For his first request, he tells Link to bring him a Traveler's Sword. Once their conversation is concluded, "The Weapon Connoisseur" Side Quest will begin. Throughout the Quest, Nebb will also ask Link for a Fire Rod, a Moblin Club, a Duplex Bow, a Windcleaver, an Ancient Battle Axe+, a Frostspear, and an Ancient Short Sword. Whenever Link brings a Weapon, Nebb will give him either a Red Rupee, a Purple Rupee, a Silver Rupee, a Gold Rupee, or a Diamond. He claims that these rewards were given to him by his grandfather to pass onto the one who could show him these Weapons or teach him how to fight. Whenever Link returns to Nebb during the Side Quest, he will remind him of the Weapon he wants to see. After showing Nebb the final Weapon, he once again thanks Link, stating that his grandfather must be happy. With this, the Side Quest will be completed. When Link speaks to Nebb later on, he asks what he wants. If Link asks to play with him, Nebb explains that he is unable to due to needing to look after Narah. He notes that his mother is always busy talking with Amira at the Well, and he reasons that adults must have difficult lives. If Link remarks that he appears busy, Nebb attributes it to being in charge of Narah. During Rain, he will take shelter in his House, where he practices hitting a wooden dummy with a stick. At 9:00 PM, Nebb and Narah return home for the night, with Nebb telling Link that he will be going to sleep soon. If Link carries the Blue Flame in front of Nebb, he becomes interested and follows him around. When Link speaks to him,

wooden dummy with a stick. At 9:00 PM, Nebb and Narah return home for the night, with Nebb telling Link that he will be going to sleep soon. If Link carries the Blue Flame in front of Nebb, he becomes interested and follows him around. When Link speaks to him, he will be curious and ask what it is.

is a recurring Region in . Features and Overview Necluda is a Region of Hyrule, situated just east of the Faron and south of Lanayru. Necluda is divided into three sections: East Necluda, the Necluda Sea, and West Necluda. Fort Hateno is located on the border separating the East and West portions of the Region, while the Necluda Sea features landmarks such as Eventide Island and Tenoko Island. The Region is primarily inhabited by Hylians and Sheikah, though the Gerudo treasure hunter Flavi can be found in Lurelin Village and Koroks can be found hiding all throughout the area. According to the Sheikah Slate's Album, some areas of the Faron Tower Region are actually part of Necluda, such as Lurelin Village in East Necluda and Floria Bridge, Lake Floria, and Lakeside Stable in West Necluda As a result, Necluda has the most surviving villages of any Region, as Hateno Village, Kakariko Village, and Lurelin Village are all found within its borders. During the Great Calamity 100 prior to the events of , Link and Princess Zelda were responsible for the mass destruction of Guardian Stalkers near Fort Hateno in Necluda. This, along with the Hylian defenses at Fort Hateno, prevented Guardian forces from traveling toward Hateno Village. This event can be seen in the Recovered Memory "Zelda's Awakening".
