is a location in . Features and Overview The Necluda Sky Archipelago is located between the East Necluda Sky and West Necluda Sky. It spans from a lone Sky Island with a pool of Water above the Phalian Highlands to a chain of Sky Islands above Mount Taran and Mount Dunsel to the south. It contains the Zonaite Forge Island in its northern range. The southern chain of Sky Islands are littered with Decayed Constructs and Air Platforms. In the southeast of the Archipelago, there are two Sky Islands which are tied to the Shrine Quest "The Necluda Sky Crystal" and the Kumamayn Shrine. The western one of these Sky Islands features a Tilted Platform and a Zonai Ruin. A mechanism can be found on the eastern Sky Island which is composed of two Stone Slabs, two Springs, a Lattice, and a Stake. North of this mechanism is a large circular arena. South of the Tilted Platform, there is a Device Dispenser. Areas Device Dispenser Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests Zonai Devices

is a recurring character in . Biography Nekk is a Rito who resides in Rito Village. Alongside Huck, he operates the Brazen Beak, an Armor Shop that sells the Snowquill Set. When Link enters the Brazen Beak, Nekk will advertise his wares. If Link speaks to Nekk, he welcomes him and asks what he needs. Whenever Link makes a purchase, Nekk thanks him for doing so. If Link purchases his entire stock, Nekk remarks that he is going on a shopping spree. Afterwards, he congratulates Link, but he states that he has nothing else to offer him. He then remembers hearing about a Dye Shop somewhere, and he realizes Link could buy another Snowquill Set to have it in another color. Like other Shop owners, Link can sell his Items to Nekk. Throughout the process, he encourages Link to continue selling to him and take his time choosing. Whenever Nekk purchases an Item from Link, he will be grateful and ask if there is anything else he would like to sell. Once Link finishes selling, Nekk will thank him for his business.

is a recurring character in . Biography Nell is a Hylian traveler who can be encountered one the western side of the Akkala Bridge Ruins. While there, he can be seen defending himself against a Blue Moblin. He carries a Traveler's Sword and a Wooden Shield, and he wears a tattered piece of cloth that can be found on Soldier's Armor. While he is under attack, Nell will draw his Traveler's Sword to defend himself. When spoken to during his battle, he goads the Blue Moblin. He also states that Monsters do not belong at the Akkala Citadel Ruins. Once the Blue Moblin has been defeated, Nell will be relieved. If Nell was knocked unconscious, he complains that Link watched as he was beat up, but he still warns him to be careful while traveling. If Link saved him, he may state that he is impressed by how easily he was able to defeat the Moblin. He also has a chance to say that he was overwhelmed facing the Monster, comparing his own fighting skills with Link's. As a reward, he gives Link Food or Arrows. The first time Link speaks to Nell, he is saddened that he will have to turn back after traveling so far to reach the Akkala Citadel Ruins. Turning to face the Ruins, Nell explains that the Akkala Citadel was constructed long ago in order to protect the Akkala Region. While it was thought to be the impenetrable, the army retreated there during the Great Calamity after losing the Royal Family of Hyrule. Despite their best efforts, the Guardians destroyed the Akkala Citadel, which Nell attributes to the fall of Hyrule as a whole. When Nell discovered that he had an ancestor who died at the Akkala Citadel, he decided to travel there in order to pray for them. However, upon reaching the Akkala Bridge Ruins, he found that the Akkala Citadel Ruins were still swarmed with active Guardians, making it impossible for him to continue. He warns Link that he has never heard of someone who was able to escape a Guardian after it spotted them. While he does not think Link would be reckless, Nell still warns him to be careful while traversing the Akkala Highlands. After subsequent rescues, Nell will look out over the Akkala Citadel Ruins from the edge of the Bridge Ruins. When Link speaks to him, he comments that the scale of destruction from the Great Calamity can be seen in the ruins of massive structures and cities throughout Hyrule Kingdom. Though he wishes he could get a closer look at the Citadel, he does not want to risk his life, and he warns Link to be careful if he decides to go there.

is a recurring character in . Biography Nellie is an elderly Gerudo woman who resides in Gerudo Town. She resides in the House across from the Gerudo Secret Club with her granddaughter, Risa. While she is awake, she frequents the Stalls in the center of Town. If Link speaks to Nellie, she finds it interesting to see a "Hylian vai" and greets him. At 11:00 PM, Nellie can be found in front of Lorn's Fruit Stand. When spoken to, she recounts that her grandmother often told her never to eat Hearty Durians while drinking. While she does not know the reason why, she believes there must be a good reason due to how often her grandmother repeated it. At 5:00 AM, she leaves to look for a drink and snacks. After visiting Lorn's Fruit Stand, she oserves Ardin's General Store, which sells Mushrooms. If Link speaks to her, she says that her mother taught her that Food made from Mushrooms help relieve strong headaches. For that reason, Nellie always makes Fragrant Mushroom Sauté for herself whenever she is tired. She then explains how to make the dish by Cooking Goron Spice with any Mushroom. When Ardin's entire stock is sold out, Nellie is initially hesitant to believe that she is selling Mushrooms that only beautiful people can see. If Link claims he can see them, Nellie admits that she thought Ardin was lying so her customers would not know she was out of stock. While she does not care if she can see them or not, she believes she would have been able to see them when she was younger. If Link admits he cannot see them, Nellie reasons that if someone as beautiful as him is unable to, then Ardin must be lying. At 10:00 AM, Nellie leaves the market to sleep in her Bed, as she wants to avoid the Heat of the day. If Link speaks to Nellie while she is sleeping in her home, she irritably asks what he wants and says that she prefers to sleep until night falls. After Nellie wakes up at 5:00 PM, she wonders how people tolerate the Heat, as she likes the night more, before deciding to wake herself up with a drink. She then goes to The Noble Canteen, where she remarks that drinking is the only way she can wake up. She stays there until 11:00 PM, before leaving for Lorn's Fruit Stand.

is a Stable in . Features and Overview New Serenne Stable is a Stable situated on the North Hyrule Plain in Hyrule Field. It is a successor to Serenne Stable, having moved to its current location after the road west of Carok Bridge was diverted. The Stable is run by Sprinn, who employs Zumi. With the closure of Rito Stable, Ariane now works at the Stable as well. Akrah and Onya can be found at the Stable, where they talk about a rumored beast and a legendary weapon. Their brother Garshon initially sits outside the Stable, but he later leaves due to their constant arguing. Dophi reads the Lucky Clover Gazette's Newspaper at the Cooking Pot. A Recipe for Bright Tomato Mushroom Stew can be found on the southwest interior wall of the Stable. Cado can be found on the north side of the road passing by the Stable with his Donkey. He stands guard over Impa, who is investigating the Geoglyph in the North Hyrule Plain just north of his position. He explains that Impa may have important information about Zelda's whereabouts. This begins the "Impa and the Geoglyphs" Main Quest. During the Side Adventure "Potential Princess Sightings!", Penn can be seen standing in front of New Serenne Stable. Areas Creatures Materials Equipment Treasure Chests

is a recurring Set Bonus in . Overview Night Speed Up is a Set Bonus that, between the in-game hours of 9:00pm and 4:00am, mimics the running speed increase provided by a level two Speed Up Effect. This increases Link's running speed by 20%. It does not increase Link's Climbing speed or Swimming speed. Night Speed Up can be stacked with a level one Speed Up effect. In , Night Speed Up can be obtained from the following Armor Sets: Dark Series Stealth Attire (★★) Tingle's Outfit The Night Speed Up Set Bonus can be found on the following Armor Sets in : Dark Series Stealth Attire (★★) Tingle's Outfit Yiga Clan Attire (★★)

is a recurring character in . Biography Nikki is a Hylian woman who resides Hateno Village. She and her family reside in the House northeast of the Village's entrance, where she sleeps in one of the Beds on the first floor. During the day, Nikki meets with Amira at the Well, where the two of them gossip with each other. Should Link attempt to talk to her, she will shrilly accuse him of eavesdropping on their conversation. Trying to speak to Amira instead will get Nikki to shoo him away. In order to listen to their conversation, Link must hide behind the Well. When he does so, he will overheard Nikki saying that one of her children saw a child at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. While Amira wonders if Purah adopted a child, Nikki claims that she does not seem the type to do so. Nikki has an idea of who the girl is, but she is quick to dismiss the thought. At 9:00 PM, Nikki leaves the Well in order to start preparing for the next day, and she advises Link to do the same. At 5:00 AM, she wakes up to go to the water trough. Nikki claims she is going to work, but she becomes incredibly irritated if Link appears to be following her. If Link speaks to Nikki while carrying the Blue Flame, she yells at him to put it away, since it is not a toy.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Ninjis Shrine can be found in the southern part of the Lost Woods within the Great Hyrule Forest. It corresponds to the Sijnin Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Ninjis Shrine The Ninjis Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Ninjis Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Nobiro is a Hylian who resides at the Kara Kara Bazaar. At all hours of the day, he can be found on the lookout post at the Kara Kara Bazaar Barracks, even sleeping on the stool nearby. While he is awake, he looks out at the Great Cliffs. When Link first approaches Nobiro, he shares a rumor that the Sandstorm over the Great Cliffs stops for a few hours everyday, but he has never been able to witness this for himself. He has heard that an ancient civilization hid their treasure in the Sandstorm. Due to this, Nobiro has been waiting for an opportunity to find the treasure, though he has begun to suspect he was given a bad lead. Finally turning to Link, Nobiro realizes that he does not know who he is. After this, "The Eye of the Sandstorm" Shrine Quest will begin. If Link speaks to Nobiro again, he remarks that a treasure being hidden by a Sandstorm sounds like the beginning of a good adventure. He recounts that rumor that the Sandstorm stops for a few hours every day, claiming that the only times he is not watching it is when he falls asleep. Once again, he turns to Link and asks who he is. While Nobiro sleeps, he mutters about tomorrow being the day that the Sandstorm will stop. After Link completes the Dako Tah Shrine, the Sandstorm that concealed it will permanently disappear. Nobiro will be surprised by this and point it out to Link. At night, he tries to prevent himself from sleeping by talking. As part of the Monster-Control Crew, Nobiro has been tasked with guarding the interior of Hyrule Castle from thieves, due to the treasure and Weapons that are located inside. He can be found in the Observation Room, and he carries a Soldier's Spear. Nobiro can be seen looking into the Reception Room, and he compares Hyrule Castle to a maze. When he sees Link, he apologizes for not noticing him, and introduces himself and his job. Although he admits to being lost, Nobiro allows Link to venture inside Hyrule Castle, citing the fact that it is where he is from. However, he warns Link that Monsters can still be found on the premises.

are recurring Objects and Items in . Location and Uses The Noble Pursuit is a featured cocktail at The Noble Canteen that many customers seek out. Furosa, the owner of The Noble Canteen, describes it as having a light, sweet taste and providing a cooling sensation. It is made using Ice from the Northern Icehouse, and so is refreshing. However, Furosa considers Link too young for her Shop and refuses to sell to him. After completing the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Link can find Pokki collapsed outside the Misae Suma Shrine. She laments that, if she is to die here, she was unable to have one more sip of a Noble Pursuit. This begins the Shrine Quest "The Perfect Drink". Back in Gerudo Town, Link can ask Furosa for a Noble Pursuit. Not only has The Noble Canteen run out of Ice, Furosa also refuses to sell the drink to Link due to its strength. When Link explains that the Noble Pursuit is for Pokki, Furosa reveals that she can't retrieve the Ice herself since her legs are not in shape. Link offers to get the Ice for her, which relieves Furosa. Furosa offers to meet him at the entrance of the ruins between the Icehouse and Gerudo Town. Once Furosa receives her Ice, she proclaims that she will be able to make the ultimate Noble Pursuit. She asks Link to pass a message along to Pokki that the best Noble Pursuit ever is waiting for her. She believes that when Pokki hears this, she will come running. At Misae Suma Shrine, Link can inform Pokki of the Noble Pursuit that Furosa has prepared for her. When she finds out it is supposedly the "best Noble Pursuit ever", she immediately takes off for Gerudo Town. This completes the Shrine Quest. The Noble Pursuit is a drink that Link can Cook by placing a Hydromelon, a Palm Fruit, and Voltfruit, and Rock Salt into a Cooking Pot. They are also sold at the The Noble Canteen for 20 Rupees. Noble Pursuits that are purchased will restore four Hearts when consumed, and they sell for 22 Rupees. Other Appearances thumb|Icon for Noble Pursuit from Noble Pursuit boosts the Warrior's damage by 7% and is made using three Palm Fruits, three Hydromelons, three Voltfruits, and three Rock Salts.

is a recurring character in . Biography Nobo is a Hylian woman who resides at East Akkala Stable. During the day, she sits near the Stable's Cooking Pot. At night, she sleeps in one of the Beds inside the Stable. According to Pitar, she has a lot of information to share with her fellow travelers. When Link passes by Nobo, he can hear her talking about a "sacred article." If he approaches her, she realizes that she does not recognize him, remarking that he looks like someone who has traveled all over the world. Should Link ask who she is, Nobo introduces herself, explaining that of all the places she has traveled, she likes Akkala the best. As a result of this, she is familiar with several points of interest in the Region, and she asks Link if there is something he wants to know. If Link asks Nobo about the surrounding area, she explains that the Spring of Power is located to the west of the East Akkala Stable. She then recites a legend, which says that one must offer a "sacred article" to the Spring of Power. She then wonders if this was part of the ritual that Zelda would perform. After hearing this, "The Spring of Power" Shrine Quest will begin. If Link asks about areas that are further away, Nobo explains that there is a home that looks like a lighthouse to the north, but no one was home when she visited. After the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest has started, Link can ask Nobo if she knows Hudson. While she is unfamiliar with him, she claims to have heard clanging sounds from Lake Akkala, which is south of their current location. At night, Link is able to wake Nobo up to ask her questions, though she will be annoyed when he does so. During Rain, she runs inside to sit at the table. Nobo can be found at Woodland Stable.

is a recurring location in . goes unnamed in . Features and Overview North Dueling Peaks is located along the northern slope of the Dueling Peaks in West Necluda. It is bordered by Mable Ridge to the north. A Ruined House with a Cooking Pot can be found on the southern end of North Dueling Peaks. The Stone Talus (Senior) is situated on the western slope of North Dueling Peaks. It will initially be dormant, but it will stand up and attack Link if he approaches it. A small Monster Stronghold can also be found on the northern side of North Dueling Peaks. It surrounds a Campfire with a Seared Steak roasting over it. The Treasure Chest at this Stronghold contains a Luminous Stone. Two additional Treasure Chests can be found on North Dueling Peaks. The first is located in the Ruined House, and it contains an Iron Sledgehammer. The second Chest is south of the Stone Talus (Senior), and a Purple Rupee can be retrieved from inside. left|40px A single Korok Seed Puzzle is situated on North Dueling Peaks. It is an Offering Spot located at its very southern end, near the Ruined House. When Link places an Apple in the empty Spot, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

The is a location in . Features and Overview The North Gerudo Sky Archipelago is a series of several Sky Islands that surround Starview Island. They are situated in both the Gerudo Highlands Sky and the Tabantha Frontier Sky. The Archipelago is part of both a low-Gravity environment and a Freezing Climate, the latter of which requires Link to have at least two levels of Cold Resistance to avoid taking damage. A Small Island below the North Gerudo Sky Archipelago bears an Ancient Tablet, which contains An Ancient Ghost Story. If Link steps onto the center of the Island, it will break away and fall toward the Vatorsa Snowfield below. The Sky Islands surrounding Starview Island begin beneath it and eventually wrap around it as they rise in elevation over it. They are heavily guarded with Soldier Constructs, which sit atop Air Platforms. These Sky Islands come to a point in the northeast where a small ruined building housing a lone Treasure Chest can be found. Areas Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests Zonai Devices

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview North Hyrule Plain is located in the northwestern corner of Hyrule Field, directly bordered by the Breach of Demise to the south. The Hilltop High Road also runs along its western side. The Royal Ancient Lab Ruins can be found on the Plain. left|40px There are a total of two Korok Seed Puzzles on North Hyrule Plain. The first can be solved by rolling a Boulder down into a hole in the southeastern area of the Plain. The second is a Cube Pattern on the Plain's east side. Once each of these Puzzles have been solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials As in , the North Hyrule Plain is located in Hyrule Field. To the north it borders Salari Hill and Irch Plain, and to the west and south it borders Lindor's Brow, Ludfo's Bog and the Breach of Demise. To its east sit the Regencia River and Carok Bridge. Following the Upheaval, a Geoglyph has appeared in the Plain. Fallen Debris now litter the landscape as well, and a lone Fallen Ruin has fallen in the Geoglyph's path. The Sinakawak Shrine and North Hyrule Plain Cave also appeared after the Upheaval. At some point, the Serenne Stable moved south to North Hyrule Plain after a new road was built west of Carok Bridge, adopting the name of New Serenne Stable in the process. A Battle Talus has planted itself beside the road atop the hill west of the Royal Ancient Lab Ruins in the Plain. North of the Royal Ancient Lab Ruins, the Plain features a wetland biome. An unmarked stone road leads north from the Ruins into this biome. There is a Monster Outpost here with a lit Cooking Pot. Beside the largest pond of water, there is a Busted Wagon that can be searched for Materials. In order to uncover clues about the missing Zelda's location, Impa and Cado traveled here to investigate the newly-formed Geoglyph. To view the Geoglyph as a whole, Impa borrowed a Balloon from Purah. However, a strong wind tore her contraption apart as she took to the air and she was left with no means to repair it. thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of Link and Impa in a Balloon.|Link and Impa in her Balloon As part of the "Impa and the Geoglyphs" Main Quest, Link can help her reassemble her aircraft with the Ancient Power Ultrahand. Upon Link doing so, Impa will thank him and offer a ride in the aircraft to view the Geoglyph. When a Fire is lit inside the contraption, Impa and Link will fly into the Sky above the Geoglyph. Despite feeling a sense of vertigo, Impa recounts Kakariko Village's written records related to the Geoglyph and Dragon's Tears. She asks for Link's help with investigating what the Dragon's Tears are and suggests using their vantage point to identify it. This Dragon's Tear can be found in the left eye of the

a sense of vertigo, Impa recounts Kakariko Village's written records related to the Geoglyph and Dragon's Tears. She asks for Link's help with investigating what the Dragon's Tears are and suggests using their vantage point to identify it. This Dragon's Tear can be found in the left eye of the Geogylph. When it is examined, Link's Recall Ancient Power activates and the Dragon's Tear rises into the air and shows Link the "Where Am I?" Memory. After Link views this Memory, Impa appears beside him and asks him of what he saw. Upon hearing the details of the Memory, she muses that they must all be related to Zelda's disappearance. She then invites him to the Forgotten Temple in Tanagar Canyon where they may find out more information, beginning the Main Quest "The Dragon's Tears". Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials Equipment Zonai Devices Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

The is a location in . Features and Overview North Hyrule Plain Cave is located beneath North Hyrule Plain. Its primary entrance overlooks the Regencia River, while a secondary entrance can be found as a Hole northeast of New Serenne Stable. Gladis stands in front of the eastern entrance and informs Link that they are there because Koltin asked them to retrieve Bubbul Gems from Bubbulfrogs. The North Hyrule Plain Cave is a rising tunnel covered with Wet Walls. The entrance descends into a room with a pool of Water fed by two Waterfalls surrounding a rock overhang. By Ascending onto this rock, Link can access the next level of the Cave. This level splits into a ramp on the western side of the tunnel and a river on the eastern side. The river is fed by a third Waterfall. Beyond this Waterfall, the walking path and the river switch sides, with a natural bridge across the river between another Waterfall. thumb|right|320px|The palanquin holding Misko's Treasure The right-hand-side pathway leads up into the final chamber of the Cave where a Bubbulfrog and an exit in the ceiling can be found while a fifth Waterfall along the river hides a chamber with a palanquin placed by Misko. The chamber hidden by the fifth Waterfall is visible thanks to the Brightcaps that grow around its entrance. The final chamber is home to a Bubbulfrog, a natural spring in the wall, and a skylight exit in the ceiling of the Cave. Creatures Enemies Materials Treasure Chests

The , also known as the Enormous Maze, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The North Lomei Labyrinth is a large Zonai Ruin located in the northeastern Hebra Mountains. It is a giant stone maze, with its western corner serving as its main entrance. At the center of the Labyrinth sits Qaza Tokki Shrine. During his childhood, Monkton was warned by the adults not to visit the North Lomei Labyrinth due to its danger. Wanting to test his Horse Harry's courage, he sent him into the Labyrinth. Harry never returned from the maze. Upon entering the North Lomei Labyrinth, Link will hear the voice of Qaza Tokki, who promises him a reward for completing the maze. Hearing this starts the "Trial on the Cliff" Shrine Quest. By following the pathways through the Labyrinth, Link is able to reach Qaza Tokki Shrine, thereby completing the Shrine Quest. Throughout the North Lomei Labyrinth, Link can find nine separate Treasure Chests. In total, these Chest contain an Edge of Duality, a Knight's Shield, a bundle of five Ice Arrows, a Topaz, a Ruby, a Sapphire, a Diamond, a Silver Rupee, and a Gold Rupee. Areas Enemies Equipment Areas

The , also known as the , or the Northern Mining Site, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Abandoned North Mine is a disused quarry to the northwest of Goron City in Eldin Canyon. It is denoted as Death Mountain Marker #6. The Mine is situated within Darunia Lake, consisting of a shore and several small islands scattered across the Lava. Updrafts created by the Lake's Lava can be used to reach these islands by carrying Link while using the Paraglider. The Mine's northernmost island has a crag known as the Vault. Due to the intensity of the Scorching Climate surrounded the Abandoned North Mine, Link needs at least two levels of Flame Guard to traverse it without taking damage. A number of Cannons belonging to Bludo have been stationed around the Abandoned North Mine, which are operated by striking their levers to move them and inserting a Remote Bomb into their compartments to detonate them. These Cannons can be used to destroy debris and some of the Monster Strongholds surrounding the Mine. A rail track connecting the Mine and the Isle of Rabac begins at its southern shore. A Mine Cart can be found stationed nearby. A rubble of stones on the east islands can also be blown away using a Cannon, revealing an Ore Deposit and a Rare Ore Deposit underneath. The Abandoned North Mine was once used by the Gorons to mine for Gems, which they would then trade for Rupees. However, Divine Beast Vah Rudania's rampage caused a strong Scorching Climate to form around the Mine, and the Goron Group Mining Company was forced to stop working. Since then, more Lava and Monsters have appeared in the area. Prior to Link's arrival in Goron City, Yunobo had went to the Abandoned North Mine to find painkillers for Bludo. However, he became trapped in the vault after one of Divine Beast Vah Rudania's Magma Bombs caused a landslide. As part of the "Divine Beast Vah Rudania" Main Quest, Link must retrieved Yunobo from the Abandoned North Mine. Areas Enemies The North Mine is now used by YunoboCo. It hosts YunoboCo HQ, as well as several locations associated with the company. Areas

The is a location in . Features and Overview The North Necluda Sky Archipelago is a group of Sky Islands located above Kakariko Village and the surrounding areas in the West Necluda Sky. In the south of the Archipelago, there are two Sky Islands which are tied to the Shrine Quest "The North Necluda Sky Crystal" and the Josiu Shrine. A gyroscopic mechanism can be found on the northern Sky Island which can be controlled with Ultrahand to manipulate a curved Sky Island between them. The central Sky Islands features a Tilted Platform and a Device Dispenser. The eastern Sky Island features a plaza with several Zonai Devices. An Island that Glows in the Night Sky can be found in the northeast of the Archipelago. Atop this Sky Island, there are several Luminous Stone Deposits and a single Rare Ore Deposit. Areas Device Dispenser Creatures Enemies Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests Zonai Devices

The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview N. Tabantha Snowfield is located in the Tabantha Tundra, along the northern border of Hyrule. It is a flat expanse that is covered by Snow, surrounded by the Hebra Mountains and Mount Drena. The North Lomei Labyrinth is also accessible through the Snowfield. Sha Gehma Shrine is situated in the northern part of the Snowfield, in addition to two abandoned Monster Strongholds. As part of a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance in order to traverse the N. Tabantha Snowfield without taking damage. During the "Stalhorse: Pictured!" Side Quest, Juannelle directs Link to the N. Tabantha Snowfield, claiming to have heard rumors about Stalhorses being found there. Two Treasure Chests are located on the N. Tabantha Snowfield. One is a metal Chest inside the northernmost abandoned Monster Stronghold, which holds a Kite Shield. The other is also a metal Chest, this time situated in the northwestern corner of the Snowfield, and it contains a Forest Dweller's Bow. left|40px A total of three Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on the N. Tabantha Snowfield. The first is an Archery Puzzle, marked by a Pinwheel on a hill in the Snowfield's northwestern corner. The second is a Jar in a felled Cedar Tree on the eastern side of the Snowfield, which Link can destroy using Archery or Remote Bombs. The third Puzzle is a Rock Pattern on a hill west of the North Lomei Labyrinth. Whenever Link solves one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Northern Icehouse is an underground Ice depository north of Gerudo Town, which is used to store Ice brought to the Gerudo Desert from the Gerudo Highlands. The Ice is then used to make the drinks at The Noble Canteen in Town, including their famous Noble Pursuit. The House is managed by a Gerudo soldier named Anche. Since Anche goes to sleep early, Ice can only be taken from the Icehouse during the day. As part of "The Perfect Drink" Side Quest, Link offers to retrieve Ice from the Northern Icehouse for Furosa, the proprietor of The Noble Canteen. Once Link reveals that he is at the Icehouse on Furosa's behalf, Anche allows him to take a block of Ice, though she warns him to be careful of the Gerudo Desert's Heat. Should Link allow the Ice to melt, Anche will allow him to take another block. After the Side Quest is completed, Link will be able to partake in the Carry the Ice! Mini-Game at the Northern Icehouse. When Link speaks to Anche, she asks if he is willing to deliver Ice to Furosa again. She claims that she is unable to leave the Icehouse due to the amount of Monsters in the area, promising that Furosa will reimburse him for his work. Link must also pay 50 Rupees in order to take the Ice. At the end of the ruins between the Northern Icehouse and Gerudo Town, Furosa will reward Link with either a Silver Rupee or a Gold Rupee. If Link attempts to melt a formation of Ice inside the Northern Icehouse or if she detects any Fire inside the Icehouse, Anche will scold him for damaging her supply of Ice before kicking him out. Materials Equipment

is a recurring character in . Biography Notts is a young Rito child who lives in Rito Village. She is the eldest daughter of Kass and Amali, making her the oldest sister of Kotts, Genli, Cree, and Kheel. When Link first arrives in Rito Village, Notts will frequent Revali's Landing to practice her singing. While she is there, she sits on the southern edge of the platform. If Link speaks to her, she will try to sing, but she admits that her voice has not been the same since Divine Beast Vah Medoh showed up. She also apologizes for disappointing Link if he came to listen to her sing. Before she goes to sleep for the night, she hopes the Divine Beast will be gone when she wakes up. After the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest has been completed, Link can encounter Notts' youngest sister, Kheel, at Warbler's Nest. If he speaks to her, she complains that Notts and her other sisters have forgotten to attend their rehearsal, as they are supposed to perform a song for Kaneli soon. Noticing that Link is a "scary" Hylian, Kheel asks him to search for her sisters and remind them of their rehearsal. After she finishes speaking, the "Recital at Warbler's Nest" Shrine Quest will begin. When Link speaks to Genli in the Kitchen during the Shrine Quest, she will demand Salmon Meunière before she leaves to sing. Notts, Kotts, and Cree have all left to gather ingredients to make Salmon Meunière for her, but they have not returned yet. Notts can be found singing on a ledge overlooking Akh Va'quot Shrine. She explains that her song is entitled "Return of the Bird-Wrangling Hero," and she thanks Link for listening. When Link reminds her of her promise to Kheel, she claims that she did not forget, as she was busy gathering ingredients for Genli's Salmon Meunière. Since she finished early, she decided to start practicing until the others were ready. However, she feels bad about making Kheel wait, so she gives Link her Tabantha Wheat so he can make Salmon Meunière for Genli. Though Genli claims she cannot sing while hungry, Notts believes she is using that as an excuse. At the end of their conversation, she wishes Link luck. If Link speaks to Notts again, she promises to go to Warbler's Nest once her other sisters are there. She shares that Cree is at The Slippery Falcon and Kotts is at the entrance to Rito Village. Once Notts is at Warbler's Nest, she remarks that her singing sounds better due to practicing at rehearsal. She then asks Link if he wants to hear the song she has been singing. If Link agrees, the sisters will recite their song for him. When Voo Lota Shrine emerges from the ground, Kheel will turn and point it out to her sisters. Notts decides that they should tell their mother, Amali. Kotts declares that the last one to reach her will be an unhatched egg,

agrees, the sisters will recite their song for him. When Voo Lota Shrine emerges from the ground, Kheel will turn and point it out to her sisters. Notts decides that they should tell their mother, Amali. Kotts declares that the last one to reach her will be an unhatched egg, and the sisters will fly back to Rito Village. After returning to Rito Village, Notts can be found practicing with her sisters near Akh Va'quot Shrine. She sings when Link approaches, thanking her audience for listening to "Return of the Bird-Wrangling Hero." After Kass returns to Rito Village, he plays his bandoneon along with their singing. Notts begins to sing a new song, which she calls "Birds of a Feather." If Link speaks to her again, she explains that the song represents how happy she is that her father has come home.

is a recurring character in . Biography Numar is a Hylian who resides in Lurelin Village. During the day, he patrols the beach near the town's western gate. At night, he sleeps in the Village Head's House, which he shares with Rozel. He carries a Fishing Harpoon. The first time Link speaks to him, Numar says he is unfamiliar and asks if he is sightseeing. If Link is confused by this, Numar explains that they receive many visitors searching for the Lover's Pond, where they hope to find their true love. He then suggests that Link visit. If Link claims not to be a sightseer, Numar once again explains Lover's Pond, but since Link looks like he is popular with the ladies, he says that he probably does not need to go there. When spoken to again, Numar wonders if the people who climb Tuft Mountain to reach Lover's Pond have found love. During Rain, Numar takes shelter under the umbrellas next to his House. Since he is unable to go fishing during such Weather, he considers going to "test" his luck instead. When Link asks what he means, Numar explains that Cloyne operates a Treasure-Chest Game, which he considers to be fun. Lately, Numar has begun gambling on the Treasure-Chest Game at the Lucky Treasure Shop, but he has not been successful so far. Due to this, he asks Link to lend him 100 Rupees, promising to repay him 1,000 Rupees if he wins. If Link agrees, Numar asks if he is certain, since he will not be able to pay him back if he loses. When Link affirms his decision, Numar is confident he will be able to make their Rupees back, saying to come back the next day to hear the results. If Link refuses his offer, Numar will be saddened that he will have to ask someone else for help. When Link approaches Numar on the same day, he tells him not to rush, as he will not know the outcome until tomorrow. If Numar loses the Mini-Game, he confesses this to Link and claims to be broke. If Numar wins, he will excitedly share the news with Link. As he promised, he gives Link 1,000 Rupees. Afterwards, Numar admits that he will not stop gambling, and he encourages Link to try the Treasure-Chest Game for himself. The next time Link speaks to Numar while it is Raining, he thanks Link for helping him before. However, he reveals that he has once again run out of Rupees. Like before, he asks Link for 100 Rupees, promising 1,000 Rupees in return. Numar returns to the Village Head's House at 10:00 PM every night. When Link approaches him, he says he will be going to sleep and to come back tomorrow. At night, he sleeps in the Bed on the right side of the House.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Nutcakes are a kind of Cake that can be made by Cooking either an Acorn or a Chickaloo Tree Nut together with Tabantha Wheat, Cane Sugar, and Goat Butter. Eating them will restore some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. These Cakes have a pleasant texture and a simple sweetness, both of which come from the use of nuts. At The Slippery Falcon in Rito Village, Link can find Misa's Recipe Book, which contains a Recipe for Nutcake. Misa first instructs the reader to purchase Tabantha Wheat, Goat Butter, and Cane Sugar from her General Store. She then says to throw them into a Cooking Pot with nuts of one's choice, though she prefers Acorns. Link can add a fifth Ingredient when making Nutcake, which can result in the following variations: Chilly Nutcake: Made by adding a chilly Ingredient. When eaten, Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance. Electro Nutcake: Made by adding an electric Ingredient. If eaten, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Nutcake: Made by adding an enduring Ingredient. Consuming them will completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Nutcake: Made by adding an energizing Ingredient. These Cakes can be eaten to refill part of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Nutcake: Made by adding a hasty Ingredient. Link can eat them to have his movement speed increased. Hearty Nutcake: Made by adding a hearty Ingredient. When eaten, all of Link's Hearts will be healed, and he will gain Extra Hearts. Mighty Nutcake: Made by adding a mighty Ingredient. When consumed, Link will gain a boost to his attack power. Sneaky Nutcake: Made by adding a sneaky Ingredient. Eating these Cakes will provide a boost to Link's Stealth. Spicy Nutcake: Made by adding a spicy Ingredient. Eating them will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Nutcake: Made by adding a tough Ingredient. They can be eaten to increase Link's defensive abilities.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The O-ogim Shrine can be found along the northern wall of the Lanayru Promenade in the Lanayru Great Spring. It corresponds to the Migo-o Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of O-ogim Shrine The O-ogim Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of O-ogim Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Oaki is a young Korok who can be found on the northwestern edge of Korok Forest. He is close with Tasho, who refers to him as their "little Oaki." According to Tasho, he can will sometimes because nervous. Recently, Oaki has decided to partake in the Korok Trials, which he has insisted on challenging without Tasho. Link can first encounter Oaki in the Lost Woods, where he is trembling and repeating that he is not scared. If Link speaks to him, Oaki will be frightened by his sudden appearance. He tells Link to leave him alone, as he will be attempting the Korok Trial on his own. Should Link speak to Oaki once more, he will still be scared, and he reminds Link that he should stop scaring him. When Link talks to Tasho, they ask him to follow Oaki during the Korok Trial so nothing bad happens to him. This begins "The Lost Pilgrimage" Shrine Quest. Once Link begins following Oaki, he will start his journey through the Lost Woods. As he walks, Oaki will express fear about his surroundings. However, he tries keep calm by reassuring himself or inspecting the scenery. He also comments about landmarks and his progression along the path. On certain occasions, Oaki will be startled by his surroundings, causing him to turn around. After passing through a giant fallen Tree, Oaki becomes scared that someone else is around. Thinking he sees a ghost, he will run back down the path, but he eventually realizes that he only saw a shadow. If Oaki spots Link, he will at first confuse him for a ghost. When he realizes that it is Link, he becomes angry about being following, as he wanted to do the Korok Trial on his own. Since he was not by himself, Oaki insists on restarting the entire Trial. Tasho will ask Link to follow Oaki during his next attempt. At the end of the path, Oaki will see Daag Chokah Shrine. When he finally reaches it, he will begin to cheer. Noticing Link, Oaki realizes that he is the hero. He brags that he was able to finish the Korok Trial on his own, claiming that this makes him brave. Since Link is there for the Ancient Shrine, Oaki encourages him to investigate, recalling that the Great Deku Tree claimed a Monk's blessing could be found inside. Afterwards, the Shrine Quest will be completed. If Link speaks to Oaki again, he states that he is the "real deal" now that he has overcome the Korok Trial. With the Korok Trial completed, Oaki can be found sitting at the edge of the Lost Woods with Tasho. He claims that he is grown up now, which Tasho is proud of. If Link approaches Oaki, he shares that the pathway to Daag Chokah Shrine is marked by the trail of Flowers. Tasho chimes in, confirming Oaki's statement. Alternatively, if Link approaches Tasho, they congratulate Oaki for overcoming the

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Oakle's Navel is a deep basin located near Mount Rozudo in West Necluda. Hot-Footed Frogs and various Fish live in the waters alongside a Water Octorok. Five Ore Deposits are also dotted around the edge of the lake. A Korok can be found by diving into the plant circle from the above cliff. Slightly above the water, while still remaining in the depression, sits a grassy platform with the Trees that contribute to the site's namesake. It can be accessed via a tunnel connecting to Marblod Plain. Creatures Enemies Materials Areas

are a recurring mechanic in . Objects go unnamed in . Overview Objects are anything that is not stored within a character's Inventory. Objects are separate from Items, which are things that exist inside the Inventories. Some Objects, such as Braziers, may also overlap with Items. There are many Objects scattered throughout Hyrule for Link to interact with in . Some, such as Lilies and Minish Portals, are seemingly innocuous and naturally occurring Objects that will grant Link access to new areas while Minish-sized. Others, such as Crimson Cyclones, Elastic Mushrooms, and Tornadoes, help him to traverse more dangerous areas of Hyrule, including Dungeons. A number of staple Objects in appear in as well, including Vases and various Switches. Metal Objects can be interacted with via Magnesis, while many others can be frozen and launched with Stasis. Most interactable Objects have a unique weight value. Objects can be used in unique ways in . Many Objects can be Fused to Link's equipment to form new Weapons and Shields with additional effects. Objects can also be bonded together with other Objects and Items with the Ultrahand ability. Certain Objects can be Learned as Echoes, allowing copies of them to be summoned at any time using the Tri Rod for an Echo cost that depends on the Object. Other Appearances (Himekawa)

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Observation Room is a surveying spot positioned due north of the Hyrule Castle Gate, overlooking the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins. Initially, it is entirely inaccessible from all sides, as Malice blocks all apertures connecting to the Observation Room. If Link destroys the Glowing Eyeball in the adjacent Reception Room, his way into the Observation Room will be cleared. The interior of the Observation Room is decorated with a lone, avian statue flanked by two stairs leading to an upper level where the viewing platform is. To access the balcony, Link must destroy the Glowing Eyeball in the Room. Prior to the Great Calamity, King Rhoam would address his subjects from the Observation Room. When Calamity Ganon overtook Hyrule Castle, all of its windows ended up covered in Malice. On the Observation Room balcony, Link can find a Treasure Chest containing three Ancient Arrows. left|40px Two Koroks can be found on the balcony of the Observation Room through the use of Archery. The first will appear if Link shoots the coat of arms located on the balcony from below. The second is marked by a Pinwheel, which causes a Balloon to appear when Link approaches. Both of these Koroks will give Link a Korok Seed for finding them. Enemies Equipment The Observation Room survived the Upheaval, though the winged Statue inside was toppled in the process. This unveiled a hidden hatch that leads to the Royal Hidden Passage, a tunnel that leads to the Guards' Chamber and the Emergency Shelter. Nobiro was tasked to protect the Observation Room from any thieves. With Calamity Ganon's Malice now gone, the western doorway is now open and leads to the Guards' Chamber, the grounds below the First Gatehouse, and a broken hallway giving way to the Hyrule Castle Chasm. Octo Balloons are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Octo Balloons are Monster Parts dropped by Octoroks. Link, while using a Cooking Pot, can cook Octo Balloons with critters such as Lizards, Frogs, Insects or Fairies to make Elixirs. They can also be purchased for 20 Rupees from Beedle at the Dueling Peaks Stable and Highland Stable or in Lurelin Village at the Merchant Boat. They can be sold to merchants or exchanged at the Fang and Bone for one Mon apiece. Octo Balloons can also be used as an ingredient for Purple Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop. Octo Balloons can be dropped and used to lift Objects such as a Barrels or stone slabs. They can thus be used to solve simple puzzles or lift non-metallic Objects. Sky Octoroks use this property to lift wooden platforms, creating aerial fortresses for other Enemies. During the "Balloon Flight" Side Quest, a young girl named Shamae living at the Woodland Stable requires Link to use at least two Octo Balloons to lift a Barrel into the sky. If Link is able to do this for her, she will give him a Star Fragment as a reward. Octo Balloons are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Octo Balloons are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances A new type of Moblin appears wearing a basket full of Octo Balloons that are tethered to three Sky Octoroks. When the Sky Octoroks are deflated, the Moblins will use the Octo Balloons to heal and reinflate them.

The Kochi Dye Shop accepts Octorok Eyeballs as an ingredient for Yellow Dye, or they can be exchanged at the Fang and Bone for Mon. Octorok Eyeballs are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Octorok Eyeballs grant a homing quality to Arrows when they are Fused together. They can also be exchanged for Mon at the Fang and Bone or used for Light Blue Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop. Octorok Tentacles are once again dropped by Octoroks in . Due to their acidic taste, they are inedible, though they are highly valued for their utility in Cooking Elixirs with critters in Cooking Pots or Portable Pots. Each time the figure is scanned, a Treasure Chest will appear that has a small chance to contain one of the pieces. is a recurring character in . Biography Offrak is a Goron child who resides in Goron City. During the day, he rolls around the City, shouting as he does so. At night, he rests at the Protein Palace, a General Store operated by Aji. The first time Link speaks to Offrak, he tells him to "buy something." If Link asks what he means, Offrak reveals that he has a Fireproof Elixir he could sell him. On subsequent encounters, Offrak asks Link if he needs a Fireproof Elixir. If Link agrees that he needs a Fireproof Elixir, Offrak will mutter that everything was worked out. He then offers to sell Link a Fireproof Elixir for 60 Rupees. Should Link decline, Offrak will become angry at him, saying not to come back when he is on Fire. Alternatively, if Link agrees to the deal, Offrak will cheer that he made a sale. Afterwards, he tries to persuade Link to buy another. During the night, Link can wake Offrak up, who will be surprised to receive a customer. If Link refuses to buy a Fireproof Elixir, Offrak angrily asks why he would wake him up.

The , also known as the Woodcutter's House, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Old Man's Cabin is a small cabin based in the southwestern region of the Great Plateau. The Old Man's Diary can be found inside, which contains the Recipe for Spicy Meat and Seafood Fry. If Link prepares the dish for the Old Man, he will be rewarded with the Warm Doublet. If the Armor is not obtained either by giving the Old Man the dish or by visiting Mount Hylia, a Treasure Chest containing it will appear inside the Cabin. As Link progresses through the Plateau, the Old Man's Diary will update accordingly. A Cooking Pot can be found outside the Cabin, as well as Barrels including a giant Barrel in which Link can hide. A Korok can be found hiding atop the roof of the Old Man's Cabin. Creatures Equipment Inhabitants Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests Creatures Enemies Equipment Inhabitants Korok Seeds Materials

Old Maps are Items in . Location and Uses Old Maps are Key Items that can be found in Treasure Chests. There are 31 Old Maps that can be found on Sky Islands in the Sky. They mark locations in the Depths, signifying points of interest which hold Treasure Chests containing rare pieces of Armor and Equipment. The treasures that Old Maps point to can be obtained regardless of whether the Old Maps were found first. If Link has already found the contents of a Treasure Chest linked to an Old Map, no location will be given and he will be told that he has already found the associated treasure. If Link obtains any Old Maps prior to unlocking the Depths layer of the Map, their locations will not be marked on the map until he reaches the Depths and unlocks the Map layer. List of Old Maps

is a recurring character in . Biography Oliff is a Hylian traveler who can be found along the Koukot Plateau Path in the Gerudo Highlands. Previously, he was traveling through the Gerudo Canyon with his friends Sesami, Flaxel, Canolo, and Palme. However, the group was attacked by Monsters on their journey and ended up separated. Oliff carries a Traveler's Sword and a Fisherman's Shield. Sesami managed to arrive at Gerudo Canyon Stable, but he is still worried about Oliff and their other friends. He asks Link to let his friends know he is waiting should come across them. This begins the "Missing in Action" Side Quest. During the Side Quest, Link can find Oliff on the northern side of the Koukot Plateau Path, near Joloo Nah Shrine. He will be under attack by a pair of Blue Bokoblins, but he attempts to defend himself with his Traveler's Sword. If Link saves Oliff, he will compliment his fighting ability. He then introduces himself, explaining that while he is capable of fighting, he was caught off guard by the Bokoblins and intimidated by their numbers. Without Link, he believes he would have been in danger, and he is grateful that he arrived. When Link tells Oliff that Sesami is at Gerudo Canyon Stable, he will be relieved to hear he is safe and decides to meet up with him. At Gerudo Canyon Stable, Oliff says that he is relieved to see Sesami again, but he also feels weak in the knees. He decides to continue training, as he was inspired by Link's swordsmanship. He likens Link's skill to that of the Hylian Champion, who he claims saved Hyrule during the Great Calamity. Realizing he was rambling, Oliff excuses himself, but not before thanking Link once more. When Link speaks to Sesami after saving Oliff, Canolo, and Flaxel, he will be grateful that they are safe, giving him a Gold Rupee as a reward. He claims that the entire group contributed to the reward. Sesami then reveals that he, Oliff, and the others have decided to stop traveling together, since caring for one another is an emotional liability. After Link leaves the Gerudo Canyon Stable, Oliff will no longer appear there. Oliff has become a part of the Monster-Control Crew. He can be found at the south end of the bridge outside of the Hyrule Castle Gate, and he wields a Rusty Halberd. When Link approaches Oliff, he becomes aware of his presence and turns to face him. Believing that Link came out of the Hyrule Castle Chasm, Oliff is ashamed that he did not see him leave. Despite not being as strong as Link, he is determined to protect Hyrule Castle and its treasures. If Link has already started "Crisis at Hyrule Castle", Oliff will direct him to meet with Hoz at the First Gatehouse. He believes that Hoz will also be surprised to see Link. is a recurring character in . Biography Olkin is a Sheikah man who lives in Kakariko Village. He and his wife, Mellie, live in the House near the Common Cooking Area. Olkin manages Olkin's Pumpkins, the field in which he grows Fortified Pumpkins. This is where he sells his Pumpkins, since they are unable to be sold at High Spirits Produce due to his rivalry with Steen. Their animosity originates from the fact that Olkin dislikes Carrots. When Link first meets Olkin, he will remark on how unusual it is to have a visitor so young. After a moment of hesitation, Olkin jumps into a defensive position and startles Link, wondering if he is perhaps a member of the Yiga. Olkin then relaxes and admits it was a joke. He explains that the Yiga are a group who have sworn their allegiance to Calamity Ganon, and he notes that they have become more active since the Sheikah Towers rose from the ground. However, he assures Link that he can tell he is not affiliated with them. To make it up for scaring Link, Olkin gives Link a Fortified Pumpkin as a gift. He claims that Fortified Pumpkins are a specialty of Kakariko Village, and he invites Link to visit Olkin's Pumpkins if he wants more. In the morning, Olkin will head to Olkin's Pumpkins to begin tending to his crops. When Link approaches him during this time, he assumes that he is interested in buying a Fortified Pumpkin, and he asks him to wait until he gets there. If Link speaks to him while he is in his field, Olkin asks if he enjoyed the Fortified Pumpkin that he gave earlier. He reveals that eating them makes one stronger, which is why he asks Mellie to Cook them for dinner. When Link asks what he means by Cooking, Olkin explains that using Fortified Pumpkins will result in Food that increases one's Defense, and he encourages Link to experiment. If Link ends their conversation, Olkin brings up Steen's belief that "the best defense is a good offense," instead claiming that "the best offense is a good defense." Selecting a Fortified Pumpkin in the field prompts Olkin to ask if he would like to purchase it for 20 Rupees. If Link decides to buy it, Olkin will compliment his eye for quality and thank him. When Link buys all of the Fortified Pumpkins in his field, Olkin is happy that someone is finding use from them, and he promises that the next harvest will be even better. If Link comes by Olkin's Pumpkins while Olkin is away, he will note how nice the Fortified Pumpkins are, but he realizes Olkin will be mad at him if he takes it without paying. In the evening, Olkin and Mellie meet at the Common Cooking Area for dinner. Mellie makes their meals using Fortified Pumpkins, which Olkin considers to be delicious. He also likes her Cooking better than Carrots. At night, Olkin can be found

mad at him if he takes it without paying. In the evening, Olkin and Mellie meet at the Common Cooking Area for dinner. Mellie makes their meals using Fortified Pumpkins, which Olkin considers to be delicious. He also likes her Cooking better than Carrots. At night, Olkin can be found running around Kakariko Village. If Link stops Olkin to talk, he will be surprised that someone else is out so late. He explains that the reason he is awake is because great Defense can be achieved through training one's legs. He also states that training is the way to learn the "secret art of defense." When Link asks what he means, Olkin points out Ta'loh Naeg Shrine nearby, where the swordsman Ta'loh Naeg was enshrined. Supposedly, overcoming the trial inside will allow one to master the "secret art of defense," but no one in Kakariko Village knows what this trial is. Olkin believes that the trial will eventually come to him, so he trains to stay prepared. If Link chooses to end their conversation, Olkin will bring up Steen again, asserting that the strongest people are those who master Defense. At 3:00 AM, Olkin will stop running and return to his House. When he is at home, Olkin will still comment on Steen's opinions, judging him for his "nonsense." While he is sleeping in his Bed, he will murmur about how Fortified Pumpkins are superior and how he wishes to protect Mellie.

Ollie is a recurring character in . Biography Ollie is a Sheikah and the innkeeper of the Shuteye Inn in Kakariko Village. He is notably timid, often stuttering as he speaks with Link. Ollie often falls asleep while standing at the Inn's front desk. However, he will be startled awake when Link approaches him. After regaining his senses, Ollie tells Link about the Shuteye Inn's services, offering a regular Bed for 20 Rupees and a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. If Link asks about the differences between the Beds, Ollie explains it is stuffed with premium Cucco feathers, which will result in him feeling more energized than usual if he sleeps in it. Once Link selects a Bed option, Ollie asks what time he wants to wake up. When this is done, Ollie will go along with his choice, but he is unsure if he will be awake at that time. If Link decides to leave instead, Ollie will be disappointed. After Link sleeps at the Shuteye Inn, Ollie will wish him a good morning. Out of habit, he also says this at noon and at night, but he realizes his mistake a corrects himself.

is a recurring character in . Biography Olu is a Gerudo woman who resides in Gerudo Town. At all hours of the day, she can be found right outside of the Hotel Oasis. Olu works for the Inn, clapping her hands and advertising the Hotel to passing visitors. If Link speaks to Olu, she will excitedly greet him. She then encourages him to relax at the Hotel Oasis. Olu recommends the Hotel's Spa Plan and cites it as the number one way to feel relaxed and beautiful. To learn more, she directs Link to Romah, the innkeeper. At night, Olu informs Link that it is bad for his skin to stay up late. She tells Link that he should partake in the Hotel Oasis's Spa Plan, which she claims is famous all over the world. She promises it will be able to heal his mind and body better than any other method could.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Omelets can be made by Cooking a Bird Egg in a Cooking Pot. When eaten, they will heal some of Link's Hearts. These dishes are common in Hyrule, as making them only requires one to fry an egg until it is plump. Link can add several Ingredients to Omelets, which can result in the following variations: Chilly Omelet: Made by adding chilly Ingredients. When consumed, Link will gain one level of Cold Resistance. Electro Omelet: Made by adding electric Ingredients. By eating these, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Omelet: Made by adding enduring Ingredients. Consuming them will completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Omelet: Made by adding energizing Ingredients. They can be eaten to refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Omelet: Made by adding hasty Ingredients. Link can eat them to receive a boost to his movement speed. Hearty Omelet: Made by adding hearty Ingredients. Eating them will heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Mighty Omelet: Made by adding mighty Ingredients. They grant Link a boost to his attack power when eaten. Sneaky Omelet: Made by adding sneaky Ingredients. Eating them will boost Link's Stealth. Spicy Omelet: Made by adding spicy Ingredients. When eaten, they will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Tough Omelet: Made by adding tough Ingredients. If eaten, Link will receive a boost to his defense. Other Appearances

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview At South Akkala Stable, Link can find Parcy repeatedly striking a Rare Ore Deposit in an attempt to break it. When he approaches her, she becomes defensive, claiming that she will be the one to take the Gems from inside. She asserts that the reason she has not broken it open yet is because her hands are sweaty, and her grip is therefore not as firm. Sensing that Link does not believe her, Parcy angrily challenges him to smash the Rare Ore Deposit in only one swing, promising him all of the Gems inside if he can do so. Due to her own strength with her sword, Parcy does not think Link is able to do so. Following their conversation, "One-Hit Wonder!" will begin. Using a Hammer-type Weapon or a Bomb Flower, Link will be able to destroy the Rare Ore Deposit in a single strike. Parcy is annoyed, claiming that she was only joking when she told him to break it. She notes that while she was only using her arm muscles, Link used his "brain muscles" as well. Parcy congratulates Link, and she allows him to keep the Gems as she promised. Afterwards, "One-Hit Wonder!" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring character in . Biography Onya is a Hylian resident of Serenne Stable. He and his brothers, Akrah and Garshon, debate the extinction of the Leviathans with each other. Onya believes that they went extinct because of an ice age. When Link approaches the brothers, Akrah states that while they know where Leviathan Bones are located, they have been unable to access them to prove their theories. Noticing that Link appears to be an adventurer, Akrah asks him to retrieve Pictures of the Leviathan Bones on their behalf. As a reward, he promises Link 300 Rupees. If Link agrees, the "Leviathan Bones" Side Quest will begin. Onya wishes to see a Picture of the Hebra Great Skeleton, which is located within a cave in the Hebra Mountains. If Link promises him that he will do his best, he reasons that Link would not survive such a journey. When Link brings Onya a Picture of the Hebra Great Skeleton, Onya will be shocked by the quality of the image. He claims that it is the proof needed to show that the Leviathans went extinct during an ice age. If Onya is the final brother Link shows a Picture to, he will be amazed that he was able to bring them Pictures of all three sets of Leviathan Bones. He then gives Link a Gold Rupee as a reward. Afterwards, he says that he will continue to analyze the Picture that Link gave him in order to research his theory. Following the Side Quest, Onya will continue to debate the Leviathans' extinction with his brothers. He states that Link's Picture has given him confidence in his ice age theory. At night, he shivers in his sleep. During Rain, Onya and his brothers will move inside the Stable. He says that he finds joy in discussing the extinction, but he quietly wonders when Akrah will leave. Onya and his brother Akrah now reside at New Serenne Stable, where they argue about what goals to pursue next. He wants to find a legendary weapon, and he thinks that the rumored beast is just a story.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Opals can be found by breaking Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits. They are also sold by Kairo, who travels along the Mountain Road between Foothill Stable and the Maw of Death Mountain. The Kochi Dye Shop accepts Opals as an ingredient for Light Yellow Dye. Opals are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Opals can be found primarily by breaking Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposit. They also rarely appear by breaking Jars on the Great Sky Island. When Fused to Weapons, Opals increases their power by one. They also turn Weapons into Elemental Weapons that fire orbs of Water with every swing. Opals are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Opal Earrings are a type of Accessory, being Earrings that can be clipped onto Link's ears. They can be purchased at the Starlight Memories Jewelry Shop in Gerudo Town for 200 Rupees and eight Opals. When worn, they provide one level of Swim Speed Up. Opal Earrings can be enhanced by a Great Fairy at a Great Fairy Fountain. However, they cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Enhancing Enhancing Other Appearances The Opal Earrings are a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and they are obtained by completing the Quest "The Hope of Central Hyrule". Unlike most other pieces of Attire, they cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Oren Bridge is a bridge that spans the Zora River in the Lanayru Great Spring. It is located along the path to Zora's Domain. Before Divine Beast Vah Ruta is calmed, its Rain will constantly fall over Oren Bridge. When Link passes over Oren Bridge during the "Reach Zora's Domain" Main Quest, Sidon will call out to him from the Zora River to share that he is halfway to Zora's Domain. He warns Link that he will encounter more Monsters as he continues onward, but he believes that he is capable of making it through. Equipment

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Orsedd Bridge is a decayed wooden bridge that spanning the Hylia River in Hyrule Field. A metallic Treasure Chest containing an Opal can be found in the waters of the Hylia River just south of the Bridge. In Master Mode, a second metallic Treasure Chest containing a Royal Guard's Spear can be found atop a platform held aloft by Sky Octoroks beside the Bridge. A Korok can be found by breaking the Pot dangling from a chain underneath the Bridge. Creatures Enemies As in , Orsedd Bridge spans the Hylia River in Hyrule Field.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Otutsum Shrine is situated on the northern side of the Risoka Snowfield in the Gerudo Highlands. It corresponds to the Mustuto Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Otutsum Shrine The Otutsum Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Otutsum Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Outpost Ruins are located east of the Great Plateau in Hyrule Field. The remains of three Fallen Guardians can be found scattered throughout the Ruins, which can be searched for Ancient Materials. Link can also find several Barrels and Wooden Boxes around the Ruins, which contain Arrows and Apples. 100 years ago, Hyrule Outpost was the most populous of all other outposts in Hyrule Field, with its citizens mostly consisting of Hylians. As is the case with the East Post Ruins and the Gatepost Town Ruins nearby, the Outpost Ruins were previously used as a waypoint for those journeying to the Great Plateau, Lanayru, or the Gerudo Desert. During the Great Calamity, the Outpost was destroyed by a barrage of Guardians. Soldiers and civilians from Gatepost Town made their way through the Outpost while evacuating Hyrule Field, with any survivors making it to Necluda. If Downloadable Content Pack is installed, Misko's EX Journal will appear in the Outpost Ruins, atop a broken bookshelf in the corner of the southernmost structure. Its pages provide hints as to the current locations of several pieces of Armor that Misko had stolen from Hyrule Castle. Reading the Journal is is necessary for the "EX Treasure: Ancient Mask", "EX Treasure: Fairy Clothes", "EX Treasure: Twilight Relic", and "EX Treasure: Phantasma" Side Quests. A total of three Treasure Chests can be found among the Outpost Ruins. The first is a stone Chest at the center of the Ruins, containing a Traveler's Bow. A second stone Treasure Chest can be found in the building to the far east of the Ruins, and it contains a Red Rupee. The third Chest is made of metal and contains an Amber, and it can be found embedded in the ground on the southernmost building. Creatures Enemies As in , the Outpost Ruins are located in Hyrule Field.

The is a recurring location in . The Outskirt Hill Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Outskirt Hill Well is located on Outskirt Hill, which is situated in the southwestern corner of Hyrule Field. It is part of several ruins that were a Hylian settlement prior to the Great Calamity. Equipment The Outskirt Hill Well returns in , and it is still a part of Hyrule Field. Link is now able to enter its interior, which consists of a single narrow chamber illuminated by potted Brightblooms. The Well also includes two Barrels and a Cooking Pot with an unlit Campfire. A Note on the Table written by Aurie Taamu can be found nearby. Within, he details his view of the Gerudo Desert as a place where life thrives. He explains that he was able to increase his Hot Weather Attack against Monsters by consuming a Meal Cooked with Fire Fruits, though he had no Heat Resistance and collapsed soon after. Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Outskirt Stable is a Stable located at the northern fork of the Three-Way Intersection, which is in southwestern Hyrule Field. It is operated by Embry and employs Canni, Haite, Myti, Toffa and Trott, all of whom live there and have to follow a predominantly vegetarian diet. Inside the Stable, Link can find a Poster depicting a Recipe for an Energizing Honey Crepe, as well as the Rumor Mill: Volume 3 laying open on a table. The exterior of Outskirt Stable is surrounded by several Tree Stumps, and a Cooking Pot can be found near the entrance. Myti sits by the Pot during the day, where she explains that the Stable does not serve Food, though travelers are free to Cook for themselves. Canni can be seen tending to Horses, and she is one of the four Stable hands who will offer to customize Link's Horse Gear, provided it has a sufficiently high enough bond and is not too big. Beedle will regularly visit the Stable and the watchman and traveling salesman, Botrick will also stop by. Glendo, a Hylian traveler, will occasionally be seen passing by. Haite runs around the Stable during the day. When it Rains, he sits at one of the Stable doors and waits for the Rain to stop. During the "Captured Memories" Main Quest, Pikango appears at Outskirt Stable, where he is able to identify the scene in the 10th Picture of Link's Album as the Sanidin Park Ruins. When staying at Outskirt Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Embry explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Embry offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Embry will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Embry will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. During the "A Rare Find" Side Quest, Link is tasked with retrieving Raw Gourmet Meat for Trott, who is unable to gain enough energy from Outskirt Stable's vegetarian meals. Once Link brings a him a piece of Raw Gourmet Meat, Trott will reward him with a Silver Rupee. Following this Side Quest, Link can sell up to three pieces of Raw Gourmet Meat to Trott per day. Link can also obtain "The Royal White Stallion" Side Quest at Outskirt Stable by speaking to Toffa, who shares his wish to see the White Horse that he has heard about. When Link tames the White Horse and brings it to Toffa, he will reward him with the Royal Horse Gear, which consists of the Royal Bridle and the Royal Saddle. Lastly, Link can start the "My Hero" Side Quest by speaking to Aliza while she stands under the large Tree

When Link tames the White Horse and brings it to Toffa, he will reward him with the Royal Horse Gear, which consists of the Royal Bridle and the Royal Saddle. Lastly, Link can start the "My Hero" Side Quest by speaking to Aliza while she stands under the large Tree across the road from Outskirt Stable. Though she initially believes that Link is the legendary hero, she decides that she was wrong when she notices he is not carrying the Master Sword. When Link returns to Aliza after reclaiming the Master Sword, she will give him a Star Fragment that she wanted to give him. However, she is disappointed that Link is not her type. A Yiga Footsoldier may pass by the Outskirt Stable disguised as a Traveler. When Link speaks to the Traveler, they will reveal their identity as a Footsoldier and begin to attack him. If Link befriends the Hylian Retriever at Outskirt Stable, it will lead him to a metal Treasure Chest embedded in the ground among the Tree Stumps, which contains a Silver Rupee. Creatures Materials Equipment Inhabitants Outskirt Stable returns in . Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain is now located on Outskirt Hill above the Stable. Creatures Equipment Hyrule Restoration Materials Inhabitants Zonai Devices Treasure Chests Other Appearances

The is a recurring location in . The Outskirt Stable Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Outskirt Stable Well is situated between Outskirt Stable and Outskirt Hill in Hyrule Field. The Outskirt Stable Well reappears in , and it is still part of Hyrule Field. The Well's interior is now accessible by a Ladder located along its rim. The first chamber consists of a pool of Water. By Swimming through a nearby tunnel, Link can enter the second chamber, which consists of another shallow pool with two Luminous Stone Deposits along its shore. The Outskirt Stable Well is one of several Wells that Fera can be found in prior to beginning the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?". She rates the Well's Water quality as fair and its moss growth as extensive, in addition to confirming the presence of Brightcaps. Once her Side Quest has started, she leaves for the Lookout Landing Well. Creatures Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Ozunda is a Hylian and the owner of the Foothill Stable at the entrance to Eldin Canyon. He can be found at the front of Foothill Stable. Ozunda is also a painter by hobby. He is the artist behind a painting hung inside Foothill Stable's lodge, which depicts the Stable in its surrounding landscape. If Foothill Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Ozunda will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Ozunda explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Ozunda then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Ozunda instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Ozunda suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Ozunda to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Ozunda tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Foothill Stable, Ozunda will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Ozunda thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Ozunda will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Ozunda asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Foothill Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Ozunda asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Ozunda will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Ozunda insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Ozunda refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Ozunda starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Ozunda gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse.

Ozunda gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery.
