When Link wakes up, Ozunda wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

is a recurring character in . Biography Padda is a Gerudo Soldier who can be found in the Palace Courtyard. Her duty is to care of Riju's Sand Seal, Patricia. In addition to this, she also watches out for Riju while she is in Gerudo Town, and she worries whenever she leaves. She carries a Gerudo Shield and a Moonlight Scimitar. The first time Link speaks to Padda, she introduces Patricia as Riju's favorite Sand Seal, and she explains that Patricia is an oracle who offers wisdom in return for Fruit. If Link speaks to her again, she recalls that Riju used to visit everyday, but as of late, she has been too busy to allow herself to relax. Padda then apologizes for rambling on and encourages Link to offer Fruit to Patricia. While Patricia likes all types of Fruit, Padda reveals that she likes Wildberries the best. Padda has the ability to communicate with Patricia and understand her divine messages. When Link offers Fruits to Patricia, Padda will translate her responses for him. If Patricia does not like the Fruit, Padda will relay her message as "Seal the deal on your fortune by using more valuable fruit!" and comment that she could not avoid using Patricia's Seal pun. If Patricia likes the Fruit, Padda will translate for her, which includes information on Sand Seals, Sand Boots and Snow Boots, Heat, Moldugas, Farosh, the Statue of the Eighth Heroine, and Tera's Great Fairy Fountain. After every translation, Padda thanks Patricia for her wisdom. After Link calms Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Padda reveals that she can feel the stress lifting from Gerudo Town, which she is sure Riju feels as well. When Riju is sitting in the courtyard, Padda tells Link to behave. However, she only asks this because Riju has returned to her regular self, and Padda wants to protect her happiness. She then reminds Link that he can offer Fruits to Patricia to hear wisdom, even though Riju is present.

are Room Units in . Location and Uses Paddocks are Room Units that Link can purchase through Hudson Construction's Dream Home program for 400 Rupees. During construction, Link is able to use Ultrahand to rotate Paddocks and attach them to other Room Units. If a Paddock is left outside of Link's plot after Link's House is finished, Grantéson will store it for him. A Paddock is able to house one of Link's registered Horses. Once Link has chosen a Horse, Grantéson will contact the Stable Association to bring it to the Paddock. Link is also able to retrieve his Horse from the Paddock at any time.

The is a recurring location in . The Palace Courtyard goes unnamed in . Overview The Palace Courtyard is an area located within Hyrule Castle, on the first basement floor. The Minish Door appears within it once every one hundred years, serving as an entrance to the Elemental Sanctuary and a bridge between Hyrule and the Minish Realm. Link is first able to access the Palace Courtyard after obtaining the newly-forged White Sword from Melari. After searching the Castle, he and Ezlo discover the opened Minish Door that only they can see (due to Link being a child and Ezlo being a Minish sage) within the Courtyard. After Vaati transforms Hyrule Castle into Dark Hyrule Castle, Link and Ezlo emerge from the Elemental Sanctuary to find the Palace Courtyard bleak and withered, newly populated with the cursed stone forms of two Vassals and Minister Potho. The Palace Courtyard remains like this until Princess Zelda is able to use the Mage's Cap to undo Vaati's evil and restore Hyrule. The Palace Courtyard is located in the southwestern corner of Gerudo Town, and it is only accessible through the Royal Palace. A room off the side of the Courtyard contains a Sand-Seal Toy. It is the home of Patricia, Riju's pet Sand Seal, with Padda standing as her guard. Creatures After the Sand Shroud over Gerudo Town ends, Patricia will return to the Palace Courtyard.

are recurring Items in . Locations and Uses Palm Fruit can be found on Palm Trees in the Gerudo Desert and on the coast of East Necluda. They arere also sold in the Kara Kara Bazaar by Emri as well as by the traveling Merchant Chumin. Red Hinoxes also sometimes drop Palm Fruits upon their death. Palm Fruits can be eaten raw to restore one Heart. When it comes in contact with Fire, it will turn into Baked Palm Fruit, which heals one and a half Hearts. When Palm Fruit is cooked into a Meal, it will increase the Heart recovery provided.</ref> At the Kochi Dye Shop, Palm Fruit can be used to make Light Yellow Dye. Palm Fruits can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Palm Fruits reappear in . They are required to make Noble Pursuits: They can be used for other Fruit-based Meals: Other Appearances Palm Fruits can be bought from the Serenne Stable and are a reward for completing the Challenge Daily Drills: Gerudo for the first time. They are also a required ingredient for cooking the meal Noble Pursuit. Palm Fruits are Materials in .

is a recurring character in . Biography Palme is a Hylian who was previously traveling through the Gerudo Canyon with his friends, Sesami, Canolo, Flaxel, and Oliff. However, while the group was traversing the Koukot Plateau Path, they were ambushed by a group of Monsters and became separated. As part of the "Missing in Action" Side Quest, Sesami asks Link to direct his friends to his location at Gerudo Canyon Stable. Palme can be found on the Koukot Plateau Path near the archway connecting Koukot Plateau and Mount Nabooru, where he has been cornered by two Blue Bokoblins. If Link saves him, he will initially be shocked. When Link confirms that he defeated the Bokoblins, Palme will be grateful and say that he might be braver than Sesami. After hearing that Sesami is waiting at Gerudo Canyon Stable, Palme is surprised and wonders if he lied about his martial arts skills, but he eventually reasons that there must have been a misunderstanding. He then leaves for the Stable. At Gerudo Canyon Stable, Palme can be found sitting beside the Cooking Pot. Palme reveals that he asked Sesami why he did not rescue him, only for Sesami to start talking about the Master Sword to avoid the conversation. He realizes now that Sesami is a coward. To reward Link, Palme and his friends contributed to giving him a Gold Rupee. Deciding that connecting with others makes them weak, the group has decided to part ways from each other. If Link speaks to Palme after completing the Side Quest, he reveals that he considers himself more cowardly than Sesami, since he waited for someone else to help him instead of helping himself. This was why he decided to leave his friends, as he wants to learn how to stop relying on other people. He believes that once he learns this, he will be able to help others, much like how Link helped him. When Link next returns to Gerudo Canyon Stable, Palme, Canolo, Flaxel, and Oliff will have left.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Paraglider is first seen after Link activates the Great Plateau Tower and descends back to the ground. There, he is met by the Old Man, who is investigating the sudden appearance of Sheikah Towers across Hyrule. There, he explains to Link that the Great Plateau that they are on is entirely isolated from the rest of the world, as nobody can safely travel to and from it without a Paraglider such as his own. Upon being asked for the Paraglider, the Old Man agrees to give it to Link in exchange for the treasure resting in the nearby Oman Au Shrine. Upon completing the Shrine, Link is confronted by the Old Man, who then tells him that he must complete the three remaining Ancient Shrines on the Great Plateau before he hands over the Paraglider. The Paraglider consumes Link's Stamina when used, limiting the time in which he may glide through the air. If Link uses the Paraglider over a vertical draft caused by burning grass, he will be propelled upwards by the vent of wind. Link can also use the Remote Bomb Rune while gliding to attack enemies below. When Link's Stamina runs out mid-flight, he will automatically put away the Paraglider and fall to the ground. While having no Stamina, the Paraglider can be taken out for one second only once in order to break Link's fall. A slow-down effect will occur when Link aims with a Bow while airborne. The Paraglider is useful for performing this. While aiming, Link's Stamina will be drained quickly and Link can stop aiming by pulling out the Paraglider. Link uses a new Paraglider while among the islands in the Sky. Link can change the appearance of his Paraglider by finding different Paraglider Fabrics throughout Hyrule, and can also obtain special fabrics by scanning various amiibo. After Link completes the Side Quest "Photographing a Chuchu", Sayge offers to make him more Fabrics if he brings him the right reference material. The Paraglider is unlocked immediately after downloading the update. is a recurring character in . Biography Parcy is a Hylian traveler who resides at Riverside Stable. She can be found standing inside the Stable, where she mumbles about the Royal Guard's Series to herself. At night, she sleeps in one of the Stable's Beds. In the past, Parcy would enter Hyrule Castle in search of the Royal Guard's Series. However, when the Malice and Guardians surrounding the Castle increased, she was forced to stop before she could find any of the Weapons. When Link approaches to Parcy, she asks if he has ever been to Hyrule Castle. She then explains that she used to enter the Castle in search of the Royal Guard's Series. After she finishes speaking, "The Royal Guard's Gear" Side Quest will begin. If Link talks to Parcy again, she will ask if he wants advice for entering Hyrule Castle. Should Link agree, she explains that the best methods of entry would be to emulate the different peoples of Hyrule, offering "Goron," "Rito," and "Zora"-inspired ways. When Link asks to hear the Goron way, Parcy shares that it involves charging in through the Hyrule Castle Gate while carrying Food that restores Hearts and Stamina. As part of the Rito style, Parcy suggests that sailing in over the Hyrule Castle Moat via the Elma Knolls to the north. Lastly, if Link asks to hear the Zora style, Parcy points out the Waterfalls that feed into the Hyrule Castle Moat, saying that a strong Swimmer would be able to make it up them. Link can also ask for different methods of entry, which prompts Parcy to offer the "Gerudo" and "Sheikah" styles. When asked about the Gerudo, Parcy advises Link to charge into Hyrule Castle on a Horse, shooting Arrows at the Guardians' eyes to pass through without being harmed. If Link asks for the Sheikah style, Parcy will inform him that this style is her personal favorite, explaining that there are two ways to enter with this method. The first is to enter through the East Passage, which is marked by the Luminous Stone Deposits at its entrance and leads into Hyrule Castle's Library. The second is by way of entering through the Docks, which also lead into the Library. If Link wishes to enter with his own way, Parcy jokes that he should act like the hero 100 years prior and destroy all of the Guardians along his way. If Link declines Parcy's advice, she will tell him that it is dangerous, and while she does not recommend visiting, he should be prepared if he does. When Link returns to Parcy with a piece of the Royal Guard's Series, she will recognize it and ask to see it. Upon looking it over, she will thank Link for showing it to her. As a reward, Parcy gives him a Gold Rupee. Afterwards, the Side Quest will be completed. Following the Side Quest, Parcy wonders what other treasures could be hidden within Hyrule Castle. Link can continue to

see it. Upon looking it over, she will thank Link for showing it to her. As a reward, Parcy gives him a Gold Rupee. Afterwards, the Side Quest will be completed. Following the Side Quest, Parcy wonders what other treasures could be hidden within Hyrule Castle. Link can continue to bring pieces of the Royal Guard's Series to Parcy, all of which she recognizes. She then asks Link if he would trade it in exchange for a Topaz, Ruby, or Sapphire. If Link accepts, Parcy will be grateful and give him the promised Gem. If Link declines Parcy's offer, she will be upset and wish she had something better to offer. Should Link wake Parcy up while she is asleep, she will yell at him for his rude behavior. If Link wakes her while he is not wearing any Armor covering his torso, she will call him a creep.

is a character in . Biography Parga is a traveling merchant who operates Rolling Pastures, a Wagon-based Shop that sells edible Materials grown and raised on farms. Prior to traveling to Lookout Landing, Parga grew up in Hateno Village. By leaving her hometown for the first time, she gained a new perspective on how idyllic it was in comparison to the outside world. After Link completes the Side Quest "A New Signature Food", Parga will receive shipments of Hateno Cheese to sell in her store. While in Rain or in Thunderstorms, Parga will wear a brown, wide-brimmed leather hat. Parga will sometimes mention that she misses her brother. She explains that he is a chef who went to Riverside Stable with his friends to learn more about cooking, but that she has not heard from him in a while. Her brother seems to be one of the four cooks Link meets during the Side Adventure "Gourmets Gone Missing". Since she does not mention his name however, it could be Agus, Joute, Teli or Endai.

is a recurring character in . Biography Pasha is a young Gerudo woman who attends Ashai's classes in Gerudo Town. During the day, she attends the "Voe and You" class in the Relationship Classroom, and at night, she attends the Cooking Class in Ashai's House. Due to her tight schedule of attending classes and studying, Pasha is very often tired, and she will ask Link to speak to someone else if he approaches her. In the Relationship Classroom, Link can find Pasha sleeping in her seat. If he speaks to her, she will wake up startled and insist she was not sleeping. When she realizes that Ashai was not the one who woke her up, she scolds Link for scaring her. If Link continues their conversation, she repeats her claim that she was not asleep. Pasha then says that she has always dreamed of living an adventurous life and then finding her true love, with whom she would have a daughter and live happily. As a result of this dream, she considers her lessons to be important, which is why she cannot sleep through them. During the "Voe and You" class, Ashai asks her students three separate questions. First, she asks what they would do when a "handsome voe" approaches them on the street. Pasha is the first to stand up and share her solution, saying that she would wave casually yet remain prepared in case he is a distraction for a bandit ambush. Ashai praises Pasha for her answer, reminding the class that sometimes men only look suspicious due to being intimidated by a Gerudo. For her second question, Ashai asks the students what they would do if they encountered an injured man in the road. Pasha then responds that she would carry him to someone who could treat him. Yet again, Pasha praises this answer, though she states that she should check for non-visible injuries before moving someone. For her last scenario, Ashai asks what her students would do if they were approached by a man they were pursuing. In response, Pasha claims that she would pretend not to know his language. Ashai states that this method could inspire curiosity in a man, and she also believes it would be unlikely for him to know the other language. If Link speaks to Pasha while she is attending Ashai's Cooking Class, she shares that people prefer homemade Food. Pasha also explains that it can be better to create a quick meal with few Ingredients instead of something elaborate, which she believes is something to make a note of.

The is a recurring location in . The Passeri Greenbelt goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Passeri Greenbelt is a range of forests located in Hyrule Field. An unmarked Road leading to the Sacred Ground Ruins passes through the eastern section of the Passeri Greenbelt. A Korok can be found by examining the Leaves with Fairy Dust moving among the Trees in the west of the Greenbelt. A second Korok can be found by breaking the Acorn Jar in a nook on a Tree at the northern edge in the west of the Greenbelt. A third Korok can be found by popping the Balloon hidden at the top of a Tree in the northwest of the central section of Trees in the Greenbelt. Another Korok will appear after Link stands by a Pinwheel southeast of the center of the Greenbelt and destroys the Jar that appears to the south. Creatures Enemies Materials Ruins Rubble now litter the grounds of the Passeri Greenbelt. An unmarked road leading south from Lookout Landing passes through the Greenbelt and is used by travelers. A road leading from the Bottomless Pond beyond the Ranch Ruins toward Lookout Landing is guarded by Monster Outposts and a Monster Outpost. In the clearing to the west of the Hylia River, there are now Fallen Ruins atop a small mesa and a Skull-shaped Monster Stronghold sits at the base of the tallest Zonai Tower. Between the two Zonai Towers, Ruins Rubble will fall from a Sky Island in the Sky above. Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests Zonai Devices Other Appearances The Passeri Greenbelt appears as part of the Hyrule Field Stage. During the Quest "Hyrule Swordfighting Academy", a swordsmaster from the northern end of the Passeri Greenbelt wants to start a monster-fighting workshop. Link provides her with five Bokoblin Horns and 150 Bokoblin Trophies to build a classroom. After the swordsmaster builds the classroom, she offers Link to join the class. As a result, Link learns a One-Handed Weapon Bonus Combo. During the subsequent Quest "Keeping the Village Peace", some villagers ask the swordmaster to take care of nearby Lizalfos. Too busy to do it herself, she asks Link to take care of the Lizalfos for her. After Link gives her 100 Lizalfos Trophies as proof that he defeated the Lizalfos, the swordmaster spreads this news to the villagers. As a result, Link learns another a One-Handed Weapon Bonus Combo. During the Movie "In the Midst of Despair...", Zelda, Link, Impa, and Terrako watch as Calamity Ganon overtakes Hyrule Castle from the Passeri Greenbelt. From the Sheikah Slate, Zelda learns that they will soon lose the Divine Beasts as well, and she begins to cry about her failure to unlock her sealing powers. When one of her tears falls onto Terrako, it emits a Light that shoots into the sky before splitting into four pieces. Her faith is then renewed when she sees Divine Beast Vah Medoh and realizes that it is not

to cry about her failure to unlock her sealing powers. When one of her tears falls onto Terrako, it emits a Light that shoots into the sky before splitting into four pieces. Her faith is then renewed when she sees Divine Beast Vah Medoh and realizes that it is not too late for the Champions to be saved.

Patricia is a recurring Sand Seal in . Characteristics Patricia is a Sand Seal belonging to Riju, the chief of the Gerudo. She was given to Riju as a gift from her mother. Riju is known to dote on Patricia, such as adorning her with a ribbon. Patricia resides in the Palace Courtyard, which is located in the southwestern corner of Gerudo Town. Padda, who acts as Patricia's guard, can also be found in the Courtyard. Patricia is noted to be more agile and outgoing than the average Sand Seal, and she is always ready to take Riju Surfing. Much of the Fruit that Patricia eats is supplied by Lorn from her Fruit Stand. Patricia has the power to deliver divine messages, which has resulted in her being referred to as an oracle. If offered Fruit, Patricia will share her wisdom, though she can only be understood by certain individuals. Patricia likes Wildberries in particular, and she will share special messages if provided with them. Padda is capable of translating Patricia's messages, which often contain Sand Seal puns. When Link gives regular Fruit to Patricia, her prophecies will involve asking for higher quality Fruit, knocking out Sand Seals with explosions, Sand Boots and Snow Boots, and warnings about Heat. When offered Wildberries, Patricia reveals information about Molduga, Farosh, the Statue of the Eighth Heroine, and Tera's Great Fairy Fountain in the Gerudo Desert. When Divine Beast Vah Naboris became active, Riju took Patricia to investigate, though she decided to turn back when she encountered its Lightning and Sandstorm. However, Patricia was scared by a Monster on their way back, and she ended up fleeing directly towards Vah Naboris. As a result of this, Riju lost consciousness, but she was later rescued by Buliara. During the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Riju asks Link to meet her and Patricia at the Lookout Post. In order to approach Divine Beast Vah Naboris with Link, Riju Surfs with Patricia through the East Barrens. After Vah Naboris has been calmed, word of Patricia and Riju's part in doing so spreads throughout Gerudo Town. Riju will also begin to visit Patricia in the mornings in order to speak with her. As in her incarnation, Patricia has the power to deliver divine messages, which has resulted in her being referred to as an oracle. If offered Fruit, Patricia will share her wisdom. When fed Splash Fruits, Patricia provides strings of coordinates. Padda is capable of translating Patricia's messages, which often contain Sand Seal puns. When Link gives regular Fruit to Patricia, her prophecies will involve Sand Boots and Snow Boots, the Desert Voe Set, how to resist Freezing Climates, the location of the Statue of the Eighth Heroine, Sinkholes, the movement of Dragons, and requesting Splash Fruits. When offered Splash Fruits, Patricia provides the following coordinates: Other Appearances Riju uses Patricia as her attack method in . During the Scenario "Air and Lightning", Terrako summons Riju and Patricia to Divine Beast Vah Naboris to save

the Eighth Heroine, Sinkholes, the movement of Dragons, and requesting Splash Fruits. When offered Splash Fruits, Patricia provides the following coordinates: Other Appearances Riju uses Patricia as her attack method in . During the Scenario "Air and Lightning", Terrako summons Riju and Patricia to Divine Beast Vah Naboris to save Urbosa from Thunderblight Ganon. After Calamity Ganon is defeated at the end of "The Future of Hyrule", the two of them will be returned to their original time.

is a recurring location in . Paya's Room goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Paya's Room is located on the second floor of Impa's House in Kakariko Village. It features a Bed in the top right corner, and a Traveler's Guardian Deity can be found on a shelf on the opposite side of the Room. Paya's Diary rests upon a table at the foot of the Bed, which Link feels compelled to read. If Link examines the Diary while Paya is nearby, she will beg him not to read it. At 1:00 AM, Paya returns to her Room for the evening. Due to the frequency at which she prays for the protection of Kakariko Village, she loses track of time and does not rest until it is almost morning. When Link speaks to Paya while she is in her Room, she will be shocked by his presence and ask him to leave. Paya spends the entire night writing in her Diary. During "The Stolen Heirloom" Shrine Quest, Impa asks Link to accompany Paya for the rest of the day, since she is still scared due to the Sheikah Heirloom being taken. Afterwards, Link and Paya will end up in her Room, where she thanks him for helping her. She realizes that her fear will not help them reclaim the Heirloom, and she reveals what she knows about the day of the theft. Paya also believes that the thief may still nearby, and she warns Link to be careful of anyone he sees at night.

is a recurring character in . Biography Paya is a young Sheikah woman who lives in Kakariko Village. She resides in her grandmother Impa's House, where she has her own Room in the attic. She has a tattoo of the Crest of the Sheikah on her face to ward off evil, in addition to honoring her long Sheikah lineage. Her name is derived from the papaya-shaped birthmark she has on her left buttock. Paya is noted to become flustered when she speaks to boys. Prior to Link's arrival in Kakariko Village, Paya has been tending to the Sheikah Heirloom, which has been passed down in her family. Recently, she has begun hearing voices speaking about the Heirloom's destiny being realized soon, making her nervous. She wrote about her concerns in the Journal of Various Worries. Paya also started her Diary, where she writes her about her day and thoughts. Link first encounters Paya outside of Impa's House, where she is scrubbing the porch. When Paya notices Link, she will be shocked to be approached by a man and hide her face behind her hands. However, she soon spots the Sheikah Slate and, recalling the stories Impa told her, tries to remember his name. Paya assures Link that she has trouble speaking sometimes, and she then struggles to introduce herself. Once she says her name, Paya seemingly calms down, acknowledging that it should be easy to say her own name and apologizing. Since Impa has been waiting for Link's return, Paya urges him to go inside and see her grandmother. If Link speaks to Paya again, she will panic and hide her face in her hands again, mentioning how close he is before asking that he go inside. She will remain outside until Link and Impa have finished their conversation. Paya recounts their meeting later on in her Diary. She claims that she has never seen her grandmother as happy as she was when Link returned. Paya thought that Link looked like gallant hero, mentioning his pointed ears and blond hair. However, she does not know why her heart will not stop beating quickly. After the "Seek Out Impa" Main Quest has been completed, Paya will begin her daily schedule. From 8:00 AM to 7:00 PM, Paya will be cleaning the Sheikah Heirloom in Impa's House. At first, Paya is still incredibly shy around Link and refers to him with a title. Still, she is incredibly eager to help him in any way she can. At the end of their talk, Paya wishes Link good luck on his journey. If Link asks about the Sheikah Heirloom, she explains that it is an artifact that has been passed down in her family for generations. Paya admits that she does not know the meaning of the legend associated with the Heirloom, but she continues to contemplate it. If asked about Kakariko Village, Paya will speak about the history of the Sheikah, who have served the Royal Family of Hyrule for generations, but were

for generations. Paya admits that she does not know the meaning of the legend associated with the Heirloom, but she continues to contemplate it. If asked about Kakariko Village, Paya will speak about the history of the Sheikah, who have served the Royal Family of Hyrule for generations, but were scattered following the Great Calamity. When this happened, several members swore allegiance to the Yiga, and she warns Link that they will target him as an enemy. Paya tells Link that he can ask her for help if he needs it. Impa then speaks up, mentioning the Great Fairy Cotera who overlooks the Village. Paya shares that Cotera's Great Fairy Fountain can be found behind Ta'loh Naeg Shrine, and she believes Cotera would be happy to help him. Lastly, should Link ask Paya about herself, she immediately becomes flustered. After a moment of hesitation, she begins to tell him about how she got her name. If Link asks her where the birthmark is, Paya becomes embarrassed again and hides her face, struggling to tell him. Initially, Impa will interject, instructing Link to change the subject. Paya finishes by promising to tell Link where it is some day. Later on, Paya will struggle to answer Link's question. Impa will again insert herself into the conversation, revealing that the birthmark is on her left buttock. At 7:00 PM, Paya will leave Impa's House to polish the Traveler's Guardian Deities outside. She warns Link to be careful of traveling at night, since the roads can be dangerous. If Link approaches her at the statues, she will be surprised by his sudden appearance and ask how she can help him. If Link asks Paya what she is doing, she explains that the Deities are meant to guide individuals through life. She considers Link's path in life is admirable, and she believes that tending to the Deities will help him. Paya leaves the Traveler's Guardian Deities at 1:00 AM to return to her Room. In her Room, Paya will write about her day in her Diary. If Link tries to read Paya's Diary while she is present, she will frantically beg him not to. When Link speaks to Paya while she is entering her Room, she will be offended that he is there and ask him to leave. When spoken to at her desk, Paya will be surprised and wonder if Link needs something from her. If Link asks what she is doing, Paya will explain she is writing in her Diary. Should Link ask if she is tired, Paya reveals that she does so much work taking care of the Sheikah Heirloom and praying for Kakariko Village's safety that she loses track of time. Lastly, if Link asks about the Crest of the Sheikah on her face, Paya will be concerned that something is wrong with her face, but she then explains its significance to him. Lastly, if Link asks about the Crest of the Sheikah on her face, Paya will be concerned that something is wrong with her face, but she then explains its significance to him. Paya will sleep in her Bed from 6:00 AM to 8:00 AM, dreaming about Link. thumb|left|250px|Paya after the Sheikah Heirloom is stolen After the "By Firefly's Light" Side Quest has been completed, Paya can be found crying on the floor of Impa's House. When Link approaches her, she states that she only looked away for a second and wonders what she should do. If Link tells her to stay positive, Paya angrily asks how she is supposed to. Otherwise, if Link asks what is wrong, Paya reveals that the Sheikah Heirloom was stolen just when she discovered its secret. Paya then begins to sob, and Impa recites the legend of the Sheikah Heirloom. Believing Link to be the hero mentioned in the legend, Paya has been staying up all night to research the Heirloom. She eventually concluded that the Sheikah Heirloom is the key to revealing an Ancient Shrine. Before they could share this with Link, however, the Heirloom was stolen. Paya recounts she has been cleaning the Sheikah Heirloom every day, meaning it must have been stolen during the night. She claims that it is forbidden for outsiders to enter Impa's House, but she does not think any of the Village's residents would steal from them. This starts "The Stolen Heirloom" Shrine Quest. Paya feels violated that someone came into her home with evil intent, but she is grateful that Impa is safe. Since Paya is afraid the thief is possibly still nearby, Impa asks Link to stay by her side for the day. In Paya's Room that evening, she thanks Link for staying with her, but she now sees that being scared will not return the Sheikah Heirloom. According to Dorian and Cado, only the villagers were seen around the time of the theft. Paya says she will try to remember all she can about that night, but she warns Link that the thief could still be nearby. Feeling uneasy, she tells Link that not to approach if he spots any suspicious movements. After Link completes Lakna Rokee Shrine, he will find Paya depressed in Impa's House, blaming herself for the Sheikah Heirloom being stolen. However, when Link reveals that he was able to recover and use the Sheikah Heirloom, Paya will be happy. She prays that the old gods' protection will follow Link. When spoken to again, Paya will express some loneliness without the Heirloom, though she is still grateful that Link found it useful. When Link has calmed one Divine Beast, a third page will appear in Paya's Diary. In it, she admits that she is not great at interacting with men, but she claims she is now able to look Link in the eyes while speaking to him. Though she still gets embarrassed, Paya still naturally follows Link's gaze, which she blams on

will appear in Paya's Diary. In it, she admits that she is not great at interacting with men, but she claims she is now able to look Link in the eyes while speaking to him. Though she still gets embarrassed, Paya still naturally follows Link's gaze, which she blams on his "beautiful blue eyes." The fourth entry in Paya's Diary appears after two Divine Beasts have been calmed. Paya wonders if Link is in love with Zelda. She claims that she would give them her support if so, but the thought of doing so causes her heart to hurt. Concerned she is getting sick, Paya resolves to ask Impa for medicine the next day. Once three Divine Beasts are calmed, the fifth entry in Paya's Diary will appear. When Paya asked Impa for medicine, she only responded by smiling. She then went to Dorian and Cado to ask about her grandmother's actions, but they did the same. As a result, Paya was unable to get any medicine. The final entry for Paya's Diary appears once all four Divine Beasts have been tamed. After speaking with Impa, Paya now realizes that she is in love with Link. Despite the fact Link may not return her feelings, Paya is still grateful that she is able to experience them on her own. At any time, Link can speak to Paya while not wearing any Armor to cover his torso. When he does this, Paya will become incredibly embarrassed and hide her face, asking him to clothe himself. Paya is now the chief of Kakariko Village following her grandmother Impa's retirement.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Peak of Awakening is located in East Necluda. Lanayru Bluff is situated at its northern base, and several Ore Deposits are spread throughout the mountain. The top of the Peak of Awakening is a Freezing Climate, requiring Link to have at least one level of Cold Resistance to traverse it without taking damage. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on the Peak of Awakening. It is a Natural Hiding Spot, which takes the form of a Rock on top of the Peak. When Link picks up the Rock, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Pearle is a Gerudo child who resides in Gerudo Town. She and her older sister, Rotana, live in the House next to The Noble Canteen. According to Rotana, Pearle idolizes Urbosa, the Gerudo Champion. During the day, Pearle can be found running around the market of Gerudo Town. When Link speaks to her, she recognizes him as a "foreign vai" and excitedly greets him. However, she claims that she is currently unable to play with him. If Link asks what she is doing, she reveals that she is pretending to be Urbosa, who she considers to be an amazing person. She also claims that Urbosa saved Gerudo Town from an "evil ghost." Because of Urbosa's feats, Pearle has been inspired to patrol for Monsters every day. On occasion, Pearle stops to watch the Sand Seals at the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth. She comments that Sue, Nah and Zarashi are doing fine and look cute. Pearle can also be found standing at Spera's Stall, where she asks Link if there are Mushroom Rice Balls where he comes from. She explains that they can be made by Cooking Hylian Rice, Rock Salt, and Mushrooms together. Due to how busy Rotana has been with her research, Pearle considers making some for her. Afterwards, Pearle will ask Link if he is currently going somewhere. If Link confirms that he is, Pearle believes he is going to The Noble Canteen, which she refers to as the "cant-eenter." However, she admits that she is bothered by hearing their voices from her House. If Link claims not to be going anywhere, Pearle warns him to be careful of Heat during the day. In the evening Pearle and the other children in Gerudo Town gather together. Kalani asks the other three if they are in love. Makure then responds that she wants to attend Ashai's class when she grows up and get married. Pearle then recalls that her mother told her Ashai was unmarried, but she does not know what this means. Lastly, Dalia says that she heard being in love is the sweetest thing in the world, but she does not think she can handle something sweeter than berries. After Divine Beast Vah Naboris has been calmed, Dalia will start being late to their meetings. Kalani asks the other two if they have heard what happened to Dalia's crops. Makure then reveals that Dalia has not been able to stop crying. Finally, Pearle promises that she will never forgive the person who caused this. As Pearle returns to her House for the night, she asks Link if he is planning to go out. No matter how Link responds, she believes that he will be going to The Noble Canteen. She explains that due to living next door, she can hear the voices of its patrons, which annoys her and Rotana. After she has returned to her House, Pearle will ask Link if he wants to play. If Link accepts,

believes that he will be going to The Noble Canteen. She explains that due to living next door, she can hear the voices of its patrons, which annoys her and Rotana. After she has returned to her House, Pearle will ask Link if he wants to play. If Link accepts, Pearle admits that she cannot play with him, since she has to be home during the night. She claims that Rotana gets mad if she does not make it back in time, but she promises to play with Link in the future. If Link says that he was following Pearle, she recalls that the word for that is "stockings." Pearle says that Rotana taught her that word, and she admires how smart her sister is. Due to the noise from The Noble Canteen, Pearle does not sleep in her Bed at night, instead standing nearby and staring at her window. When spoken to, she recognizes Link as the "foreign vai" and greets him. She complains that she can hear everything the patrons of the Canteen are saying from her window. She vows that when she grows up, she is always going to speak quietly, even if she is having fun.

is a recurring character in . Biography Peeks is a Korok who resides in Korok Forest During the day, he can be found walking near the Pedestal of the Master Sword. At night, he circles the Cooking Pot inside the Great Deku Tree's Navel. When Link first speaks to Peeks, he will recognize him as the hero, wondering why he took so long to reach Korok Forest. If Hestu has not returned to the Forest yet, Peeks asks Link if he has seen him, since he left to look for Korok Seeds a while ago. He recalls that Hestu was planning to visit Kakariko Village, but since Hestu often becomes lost, Peeks reasons he could be anywhere. He asks Link to tell Hestu to come home should they meet. After Hestu returns to Korok Forest, Peeks reveals that he has prepared a Trial for Link. He wants Link to show him a Picture of a Blupee. If Link agrees to his request, Peeks will be grateful. He goes on to explain that while he does not know where they live, Blupees can be found all throughout Hyrule, and he promises a reward if Link is able to fulfill his request. After this, the "Legendary Rabbit Trial" Side Quest will begin. Once Link has a Picture of a Blupee, he can return to Korok Forest to show it to Peeks. When he sees the Picture, Peeks will be shocked at first, wondering if it is truly a Blupee. Afterwards, he remarks that it is more beautiful than he could have imagined, and he is content now that he has seen it. As a reward, Peeks will give Link a Silver Rupee. Should Link be in need of Rupees in the future, Peeks suggests shooting a Blupee with an Arrow, as this will cause them to drop Rupees. Peeks then expresses his joy to have seen a Blupee. With this, the Side Quest will be completed. If Link talks to Peeks after completing the Side Quest, he will wonder if the reason Blupees sparkle is due to them being full of Rupees. He then questions where they get their Rupees, theorizing that they may be the ones who make them.

is a recurring character in . Biography Pelison is a Goron child and the younger brother of Greyson. He initially resides at the Southern Mine in Eldin Canyon, playing with Axyl during the day. At night, he sits under the metal shack at the Mine, occasionally yawning. When Link speaks to Pelison in the Southern Mine, he happily greets him. If Link asks him what is going on, Pelison wonders why Greyson complains so much. If Link reveals that he does not know, Pelison becomes frustrated, stating that adults should always tell the truth. Should Link end their conversation, Pelison questions if he knows why adults are so secretive. After Link offers Greyson a job with Bolson Construction during the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, he will take Pelison and depart for Tarrey Town. Since both of their names end in "-son," a mandatory criteria of the Bolson Construction company's name policy, Hudson accepts them as workers. Upon his arrival in Tarrey Town, Pelison opens a Jewelry Shop called Ore and More, where he sells the Gems that his brother finds while removing the Town's boulders. When Link approaches Pelison at Ore and More, he recognizes him as Greyson's friend and asks what he needs. Link can then choose to speak with Pelison. If Link asks about Ore and More, Pelison explains that he decided to open the Jewelry Shop after finding all of the Gems in the boulders. He is unsure why so many Gems can be found at Lake Akkala, but he speculates that it is due to their proximity to Death Mountain. He then encourages Link to buy his wares. Next, Link can ask Pelison about Tarrey Town, which Pelison finds to be cold. However, he believes he may think so because Goron City has so hot. Lastly, Link is able to question Pelison about Greyson's whereabouts, to which he claims he is somewhere nearby. He notes that ever since they left the Southern Mine, Greyson has become much happier, which makes Pelison himself happy. At the end of "From the Ground Up", Pelison will be present at Hudson and Rhondson's wedding. He voices his support for the pair naming their children in accordance with Bolson Construction's guidelines. If Link purchases a Gem from Ore and More, Pelison may thank him for doing so. Alternatively, he remarks that Greyson will have to dig up more Gems to replace them. Link can also sell his own Items to Pelison. After Pelison buys Link's Items, he expresses his gratitude and encourages Link to keep selling.

is a character in . He is a Rito working as a reporter for the Lucky Clover Gazette. Biography Penn is first encountered at Lookout Landing after activating its Skyview Tower, where he congratulates Link for being the first person to use a Skyview Tower. He informs him that he is a reporter for the Lucky Clover Gazette, writing a story on this event, before returning to the headquarters of the Lucky Clover Gazette. Despite Link's renown, Penn does not realize his identity upon learning his name, believing him to only coincidentally share a name with the legendary swordsman. Penn is next found in the Lucky Clover Gazette headquarters, the site of the former Rito Stable. Link can talk to Traysi, who will pair them up to investigate the rumored sightings of Princess Zelda, though she decides to continue keeping Link's identity a secret from him. This begins the "Potential Princess Sightings!" Side Adventure, which consists of the following Side Adventures activated by meeting Penn at each Stable: "Princess Zelda Kidnapped?!" at Dueling Peaks Stable "White Goats Gone Missing" at Tabantha Bridge Stable "Gourmets Gone Missing" at Riverside Stable "The Missing Farm Tools" at Wetland Stable "The Beast and the Princess" at New Serenne Stable "The Beckoning Woman" at Outskirt Stable "Zelda's Golden Horse" at Snowfield Stable "The All-Clucking Cucco" at South Akkala Stable "For Our Princess!" at Foothill Stable "An Eerie Voice" at Highland Stable "The Blocked Well" at Gerudo Canyon Stable "Serenade to a Great Fairy" at Woodland Stable After all quests are completed, Penn will retire to Washa's Bluff, where a "famous bard" had once "perfected his craft". Penn can also be found at East Akkala Stable, where he notes there is potential for stories including "a god of horses" and "suspicious events at the nearby laboratory". However, since none of the stories involve sightings of the Princess, he decides to leave. The stable's analogous Side Quest, "The Gathering Pirates", is not part of the "Potential Princess Sightings" Side Adventure and is instead given by the stable worker Aya; however, the quest's internal name of Tribune01 follows the same patterns as those quests, indicating it may have initially been intended to involve Penn and the Lucky Clover Gazette.

is a recurring character in . Biography Pepp is a Korok who can be found inside the Great Deku Tree's Navel in Korok Forest. They have constructed a Bed for Link, where they encourage him to Sleep. Unlike other Inns, Link does not need to pay Pepp if he wants to Sleep in the Bed, since all they want is to help him rest. The first time Link approaches Pepp, they will be asleep in their seat, having a nightmare about being attacked by vegetarians. They then recognize Link as the hero, recalling that the Great Deku Tree told them he would come to Korok Forest one day. They explains that they have been waiting for his arrival for so long that they feared they would start growing roots. Pepp then officially welcomes Link to the Great Deku Tree's Navel and introduces him to the Bed they made. On subsequent visits to Pepp, they will have fallen back asleep, but they wake up again when Link speaks to them. If Link decides to end their conversation without Sleeping, Pepp is not surprised, but they are disappointed he does not appreciate the work they put into preparing the Bed. They then invite Link to come back whenever he desires, reminding him that the Bed is free. Should Link choose to rest at Pepp's Inn, they ask him to decide on a time to wake up. After Link selects a time, Pepp sends him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up in the morning, Pepp directs him to grab a meal from the Spore Store, which is located next door. In the afternoon, Pepp informs Link that they stood guard over him while he Slept. At night, Pepp will sleepily bid Link a good evening when he wakes up, warning him to be careful. They invite Link to come back and rest in their Bed whenever he needs.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Link can make Pepper Seafoods by Cooking Spicy Peppers with any type of seafood in a Cooking Pot. The default variation can only be made by using seafood that has contradictory effects to Spicy Peppers. When eaten, they will heal some of Link's Hearts. The seeds from the Peppers draw out the taste of this dish, in addition to providing a pleasant aroma. Only one variation of Pepper Seafoods can be made: Spicy Pepper Seafood: Made by using Hyrule Basses, Sanke Carp, or Sizzlefin Trouts. Eating these meals will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Pepper Steaks can be made by Cooking a Spicy Pepper with any Meat in a Cooking Pot. Their default version can be made by adding additional ingredients, such as Mushrooms or Vegetables, that provide effects that contradict the Spicy Peppers. Eating them will heal some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. The meat in these dishes is cooked in crushed peppers, which suppresses their gamy taste while highlighting their flavor. Only one variation of Pepper Steak exists: Spicy Pepper Steak: Made by using the original recipe. When eaten, these steaks will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Perda is a young, voe-crazed Gerudo who can be found at Lover's Pond on Tuft Mountain. When she lived in Gerudo Town, she was rather popular, with Pyra, Yaido, Sumati and even Barta discussing her departure. After learning from Ashai, Perda decided to go to Lover's Pond to find the voe of her dreams, where the only people she can see are Link and Wabbin, the former of whom Perda deduces to not be the one for her. After this, she complements the prospect of Wabbin being her true love, but wonders why he fails to act. Upon Wabbin asking Link to gift her the Blue Nightshade, she queries over what it is. Should Link dismiss her question, Perda will become offended and very defensive. When Link reveals it is from the other man, she does not take it with a grain of salt, and goes to confront Wabbin. This startles the nervous man, who submits to the Gerudo. The vai then proceeds to reveal it is her favorite flower, and gets suspicious as to how he obtained that information, asking if he is a spy of the Yiga The voe rapidly denies the allegation and admits it is also his favorite. Perda thinks this is destiny, and eggs him on to play his part. The young man is confused by this request, so the Gerudo elaborates. Wabbin is still confused, however. This prompts Perda to tell him exactly what to say. Wabbin complies with this direct confrontation. This time, it is Perda who is confused. Because of this, Wabbin thinks she is agreeing to the relationship, which greatly pleases him. He then proceeds to hand Link a Red Rupee. His now girlfriend is surprised at the pitiful reward. Out of fear, Wabbin then hands Link a Silver Rupee. This act pleases Perda, who thanks Link, and wishes him well in his hunt for love. Should Wabbin be spoken to again, he asks Link if his money can be returned, to the distaste of his lady. This scares Wabbin, who can only reply in an illiterate, monosyllabic manner. Perda is pleased with what has happened, and greets Link upon noticing him.

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Phantom Armor is a piece of Armor exclusive to The Master Trials DLC Pack. Obtaining it is one part of the objective of the "EX Treasure: Phantasma" Side Quest. The Armor was stolen from Hyrule Castle by Misko and a clue to its location can be found in Misko's EX Journal at the Outpost Ruins. The Treasure Chest that hides the Phantom Armor can be found buried in the southeast of the Sacred Ground Ruins. After obtaining the Phantom Armor, Granté will begin selling it for 50 Rupees. When worn, the Armor provides one level of Attack Up. The Phantom Armor cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy nor can it be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Phantom Armor, alongside the Phantom Helmet and Phantom Greaves, compose the Phantom Equipment.

Phantom Ganons are recurring Bosses in . Characteristics In , Phantom Ganon is the Boss of the Forest Temple. Once the battle starts, Phantom Ganon jumps into one of the six paintings around the room. Afterwards, it and two replicas will ride to the front of three paintings. The real one can be spotted by its lighter color. A purple vortex then appears revealing the real Phantom Ganon. As Phantom Ganon jumps out of the painting, Link can shoot it with the Fairy Bow. If the Arrow misses or is delayed, it summons an electric ball on the ground that scatters across the platform. This can be avoided by standing on one of the Triforce images on each corner of the platform. After three shots, Phantom Ganon leaves its horse, starting the second part of the battle. Phantom Ganon now attacks by shooting an energy ball from its staff at Link while hovering over the ground. Link can hit the ball back with the Master Sword or a Bottle. After enough hits, Phantom Ganon falls to the ground paralyzed, where it can be hit multiple times with the Master Sword. When its health is halved, Phantom Ganon can also attack by twirling his staff a few times and then charging at Link, dealing three hearts of damage. Once defeated, he is banished to the gap between dimensions by Ganondorf and Link receives a Heart Container as well as the Forest Medallion. In , Phantom Ganon appears in the Forsaken Fortress and in Ganon's Castle. It must be defeated by reflecting its blue orbs with the Sword or an empty Bottle. Once hit by a reflected attack, Link can attack Phantom Ganon with his Sword. He can also attack it by intercepting its Sword attacks. After defeating Phantom Ganon in the Forsaken Fortress, Link receives the Skull Hammer. During its fight in Ganon's Castle, Phantom Ganon is accompanied by four illusions of itself. It now also attacks by throwing dark energy balls, which splits into a group of small bursts of energy flying towards Link. These can be sent back at it with a Spin Attack. After just one hit, Phantom Ganon disappears, leaving its Sword behind with the handle pointing at the door Link must open to advance. Once the Light Arrows are found, they must be shot at Phantom Ganon once stunned in order to finally defeat it. Link can grab Phantom Ganon's Sword to attack; however, it must be held with both hands, leaving Link unable to use his Shield. After defeating Phantom Ganon in Ganon's Castle's labyrinth, Link must throw its Sword at the brick wall to gain access to the top of the Tower. In , Phantom Ganon first appears as the boss of Hyrule Castle. In order to defeat it, the Links must hit its energy balls back and forth with the Sword. Once stunned, it is vulnerable to slashes from the Sword. Phantom Ganon appears once again as the boss of the Temple of

Phantom Ganon first appears as the boss of Hyrule Castle. In order to defeat it, the Links must hit its energy balls back and forth with the Sword. Once stunned, it is vulnerable to slashes from the Sword. Phantom Ganon appears once again as the boss of the Temple of Darkness; however, it now summons clones to its aid. The real Phantom Ganon will throw green orbs that can be hit back, while the clones throw white balls that break when hit with the Sword. In , Windblight Ganon, Thunderblight Ganon, Fireblight Ganon, and Waterblight Ganon are all collectively known as Phantom Ganons. They are Calamity Ganon's creations that he sent out to the Divine Beasts, resulting in the death of the Champions. When Link tries to activate the Main Control Unit of a Divine Beast, these Phantom Ganons will appear, and they must be defeated in order to continue. When Link is victorious, a Heart Container will drop, and he will have access to the Main Control Unit. Link can also dress up as the Phantom himself with the Phantom Ganon Set after completing the "EX Treasure: Dark Armor" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack. The Phantom Ganon Set is comprised of the Phantom Ganon Skull, Phantom Ganon Armor, and Phantom Ganon Greaves. It is rumored that some believe this Armor Set is possessed by a dark entity resembling the Great King of Evil himself. Each piece of the set grants Stealth Up and has the same set bonus as the Radiant Set, increasing the attack power of the Bokoblin Arm, Moblin Arm, and Lizalfos Arm bone Weapons. The Phantom Ganon Set also disguises Link from all Stal enemies, save for Stalnox and Cursed Enemies. Ganondorf utilizes Phantom Ganons disguised as Zelda to sow confusion across Hyrule. Two waves of Phantom Ganons (a set of three followed by a set of five) are fought inside the Sanctum at Hyrule Castle during the Main Quest as a Boss. A Phantom Ganon also appears when entering the insides of the Great Deku Tree in the Korok Forest. If a Gloom Spawn is defeated, a Phantom Ganon will appear where the last arm is slain immediately afterwards. In the distant past, Ganondorf used a Phantom Ganon disguised as Zelda to distract Queen Sonia so that he could sneak up on her and kill her. Phantom Ganons can be equipped with a Gloom Sword, Gloom Club, or Gloom Spear, as well as a Demon King's Bow. While wielding a Gloom Club, they are capable of kicking Link. In between attacks, they will jump backwards and kick at Link if he is close to them. At low health, they will begin spreading Gloom around them to drain Link's maximum health and reduce his room to maneuver. When defeated, they will drop their Weapons and Dark Clumps. If they spot Link in a location they cannot reach, they will equip Demon King's Bows to attack from a distance. Attacks from a Phantom

spreading Gloom around them to drain Link's maximum health and reduce his room to maneuver. When defeated, they will drop their Weapons and Dark Clumps. If they spot Link in a location they cannot reach, they will equip Demon King's Bows to attack from a distance. Attacks from a Phantom Ganon's melee Weapon or the Demon King's Bow will destroy any Zonai Devices they come into contact with. The Phantom Ganons that appear from the Gloom Spawn are different from those at Hyrule Castle: Only one Phantom Ganon appears when a Gloom Spawn is defeated. If a Phantom Ganon loses sight of Link for a certain amount of time, it will perform a gloom spread attack. They cannot hear Link's noises (dashing, whistling, swinging a melee weapon, etc.). The same applies to the Gloom spawn. Other Appearances (Himekawa) Phantom Ganon appears in the first appearing in Chapter 2: "The Sage of the Forest: Saria", answering Ganondorf's call to guard the Forest Temple and strike down the Hero of Time. When Link and Mido walk by a painting of Ganondorf, Phantom Ganon attacks. Despite a good fight, Phantom Ganon is defeated when Mido throws Link the Bow, defeating the specter of the King of Evil and releasing Saria from the painting. In , Phantom Ganon appears as a Sticker. Sticker Information |} In , Phantom Ganon appears as a Giant Boss, and as the main villain of the Wind Waker series of Scenarios in Legend Mode. He had stolen Cia's dark magic and the Triforce of Power from Lana, creating a new dimensional rift that summons the world from the Era of the Great Sea. He is eventually defeated by Link, Lana, Tetra, King Daphnes, and Cia. In battle, Phantom Ganon wields his sword, which he uses for various spin attacks. He is able to vanish and reappear closer to enemy Warriors for a surprise spin attack, or alternately to create copies of himself to surround and attack the Warrior. His projectile attacks consist of raising both of his arms to create many homing energy balls, or to simply create a single white energy ball. The latter can be used to expose his Weak Point Gauge if bounced back at him by striking it. Phantom Ganon has no specific weakness to any item, and the only way to damage him is by reflecting his own attacks at him. After his health has been reduced to about half, he summons a second sword and switches his battle style to melee, using the two blades to violently hack at the enemy Warrior. He also lowers his hovering altitude, making himself reachable to attack, but will always shield himself similarly to Ganondorf if attacked at the front or the sides. His backside, however, will become vulnerable to attack. After striking his back enough times, he will fall to the ground, exposing his Weak Point Gauge. When defeated, Phantom Ganon will occasionally drop his Cape as a silver Material, and rarely, his Sword as a

at the front or the sides. His backside, however, will become vulnerable to attack. After striking his back enough times, he will fall to the ground, exposing his Weak Point Gauge. When defeated, Phantom Ganon will occasionally drop his Cape as a silver Material, and rarely, his Sword as a gold Material. Ganondorf makes use of Phantom Ganons to infiltrate both Hyrule Castle and Mineru's research stations in the Depths. One Phantom Ganon finds the Forbidden Construct beneath Tobio's Hollow and imbues it with Gloom. However, the Construct quickly absorbs the entire essence of the Phantom Ganon within itself as it awakens, destroying the Phantom Ganon double. Not particularly perturbed by this unexpected development, Ganondorf then used Monster Parts to create a second Phantom Ganon, which he successfully used in his plan to assassinate Queen Sonia. After becoming the Demon King, Ganondorf makes Phantom Ganon copies of his Demon King form to fight for him in the Depths. The first encounter against these new Phantom Ganons occurs during the Scenario "Purging the Shadows". Later, the Warriors encounter more Phantom Ganons during "The Demon King, Ensnared". Following the release of the update, after completing the main story, additional Phantom Ganons can be met as part of the Phantom Ganon Appearance mechanic. Before becoming the Demon King, the Phantom Ganons resemble Ganondorf's future shriveled form, while the Phantom Ganons he creates with his Secret Stone of Darkness instead resemble his Demon King form.

The are a recurring Item in . Location and Uses Phantom Greaves are a piece of Armor exclusive to Downloadable Content pack. Obtaining them is one part of the objective of the "EX Treasure: Phantasma" Side Quest. The Greaves were stolen from Hyrule Castle by Misko and a clue to their location can be found in Misko's EX Journal at the Outpost Ruins. The Treasure Chest that hides the Phantom Greaves can be found buried in the southeast of the Hyrule Garrison Ruins near a ruined Guardian Stalker. After obtaining the Phantom Greaves, Granté will begin selling them for 50 Rupees. According to its description, the Phantom Greaves look just like the Greaves supposedly worn by Phantoms that tormented heroes. When worn, the Phantom Greaves provide one level of Attack Up. The Phantom Greaves cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy nor can they be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Phantom Greaves, alongside the Phantom Helmet and Phantom Armor, compose the Phantom Equipment.

Obtaining it is one part of the objective of the "EX Treasure: Phantasma" Side Quest. The Helmet was stolen from Hyrule Castle by Misko and a clue to its location can be found in Misko's EX Journal at the Outpost Ruins. The Treasure Chest that hides the Phantom Helmet can be found buried near a wall on the first floor of the Coliseum Ruins. After obtaining the Phantom Helmet, Granté will begin selling it for 50 Rupees. The , also known as the , is a recurring Armor Set in . Location and Uses The Phantom Equipment was added in Downloadable Content pack. It is Armor Set composed of the Phantom Helmet, Phantom Armor, and Phantom Greaves. They're available through the Side Quest "EX Treasure: Phantasma", which can be obtained by reading Misko's EX Journal at the Outpost Ruins. They can be found at the following locations: The Coliseum Ruins The Sacred Ground Ruins The Hyrule Garrison Ruins Wearing the Phantom Equipment does not provide a Set Bonus, though wearing the full set will "scare" people Link encounters. They cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop nor can they be enhanced by a Great Fairy. Their design is based on Phantom Zelda from .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Phrenic Bows are a type of Bow passed down through the Sheikah tribe. They belong to the Sheikah Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Weapons created by the Sheikah. By concentrating before pulling the string, the user can enter a first person view that allows them to shoot distant targets as easily as those nearby. Phrenic Bows are most commonly found in Treasure Chests in and around Lake Hylia and West Necluda. There is also a Lizalfos that uses a Phrenic Bow at the skull rock base north of Sahasra Slope in the Lanayru Wetlands. Finally, they have a chance to appear in Treasure Chests that spawn when the Series Sheik amiibo is scanned with the amiibo Rune. Sheikah archers, such as Impa's bodyguard Cado, utilize Phrenic Bows in Kakariko Village. They have a wooden construction, and thus they will burn if exposed to a source of Fire or a Scorching Climate. As a result of this, however, they do not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity, and they will float if dropped in Water. They also cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Cado is equipped with a Phrenic Bow, which Link can take a picture of with the Camera Rune to add its entry to the Hyrule Compendium. Additionally, Link can find two more mounted inside of Cado's House, though their model is part of the environment and the Camera Rune does not register them. Phrenic Bows reappear in .

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview At the Gerudo Canyon Stable, Link will find Piaffe surrounded by Wooden Box, wondering if he is ever going to be able to clean them all up. When Link approaches Piaffe, he reveals that the Stable has been closed due to a lack of visitors and Zelda's order to stay away from the Gerudo Canyon Well. Although she promised to return to fix the Well's problem, she has yet to do so. If "The Blocked Well" Side Adventure is not yet completed, Piaffe apologizes for letting his sadness get to him, and he recommends going to Kara Kara Bazaar if Link needs a place to rest. If Link has already completed "The Blocked Well", he can inform Piaffe that Zelda was trying to prevent Monsters from attacking Gerudo Canyon Stable, Piaffe will be shocked. He recalls that Monster sightings in the area increased after the Gerudo Canyon Well was built, only ceasing after it was sealed, but he was too busy cleaning out the Stable to notice. He thanks Link for looking into it, resolving to thank Zelda the next time he sees her. At the end of either scenario, Piaffe decides to return to cleaning out the Stable, even though he is unsure how to deal with the scale of his mess. Afterwards, "Piaffe, Packed Away" will begin. When Link breaks all of the Wooden Boxes in Gerudo Canyon Stable, Piaffe will be shocked that they are all gone. Thanking Link, he admits that he was responsible for letting the Box pile up until the entrance was blocked. While he is eager to leave, Piaffe asks Link if he wants to be the Stable's final customer. He welcomes Link to the Stable, giving him a single Pony Point to commemorate being the last customer. Having completed his time as a Stable owner, Piaffe wishes Link will on his travels. He then decides to finish cleaning out Gerudo Canyon Stable, once again thanking Link for his assistance. Noticing the Empty Frames, Piaffe reveals that they were sent by the Stable Association. He removes their wrapping, claiming that they appear to be nicer than he predicted. He remarks that having art on the Stable's walls may make its final days seem less lonely. Afterwards, "Piaffe, Packed Away" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring character in . Biography Piaffe is a Hylian and the owner of the Gerudo Canyon Stable in the Gerudo Highlands. He can be found at the front of Gerudo Canyon Stable. At the entrance to the Gerudo Canyon, Piaffe left a Sign encouraging travelers to stop at his Stable before entering the Gerudo Desert. If Gerudo Canyon Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Piaffe will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Piaffe explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Piaffe then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Piaffe instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Piaffe suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Piaffe to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Piaffe tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Gerudo Canyon Stable, Piaffe will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Piaffe thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Piaffe will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Piaffe asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Gerudo Canyon Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Piaffe asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Piaffe will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Piaffe insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Piaffe refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Piaffe starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Piaffe gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He

Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Piaffe gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. Inside Gerudo Canyon Stable, Piaffe once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When Link wakes up, Piaffe wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Pierre Plateau is a section of highlands that is located in East Necluda. Pierre Plateau overlooks the Lanayru Road - West Gate to the north, and it is bordered by Bonooru's Stand to the south and the Phalian Highlands to the southeast. Ore Deposits can be found along the ridges of Plateau. left|40px A single Korok Seed Puzzle is located at the northern base of the Pierre Plateau. It is a Cube Pattern, which requires Link to use Magnesis on a metal cube and place it so the two cube structures match each other. When Link successfully does this, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Pikango is a traveling painter hailing from Kakariko Village. He can first be found in Kakariko Village, painting a picture of Impa's House. He asks if Link may be a traveler like him. Pikango explains that he travels Hyrule Kingdom to find incredible sights to paint. The reason he has returned to Kakariko Village is to search for the Great Fairy Fountain rumored to be there. However, since he has not lived in the village for many years, he is unknown and considered an outsider, meaning nobody will say any more on the subject to him. Still, Pikango is determined to find the Fountain and tells Link that he will inform him of any new leads. Even in the Rain, his determination only grows. At night, he will take refuge in the Shuteye Inn, dreaming of locating the Fountain. Once Link returns to the village, Pikango will tell him he knows where the Great Fairy Fountain is, but can't get far enough to see it. He asks Link if he will come with him to see it, and if Link obliges, he leads him up to the forest near Kakariko Village. Upon reaching the entrance, Pikango runs out of breath and tells Link to go ahead and see if he can find it. He also asks Link to take a picture of it if he does stumble upon it. When Link returns to show him the picture, Pikango admits he thought it would look more 'elegant', but still offers to reward Link for his help by telling him the location of one of the pictures on Link's Sheikah Slate.

are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Pinwheels & Balloons go unnamed in . Overview Pinwheels & Balloons are a type of Archery-based Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. They are marked by the presence of Pinwheels. When Link stands near a Pinwheel, several Balloons will appear. In some circumstances, these Balloons will move. After Link pops all of the Balloons with Arrows, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Pinwheels & Balloons operate in the same manner as they did in . Once Link has shot all of the Balloons with Arrows, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Piper Ridge is located on the southern end of the Tabantha Frontier. It is a large, rocky hill that borders the Tanagar Canyon. Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain is on a cliff on the Ridge's northern edge. A small path on the west side of the Ridge connects the main road to the Fountain. Ore Deposits, Rare Ore Deposits, and Luminous Stone Deposits can all be found throughout Piper Ridge. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Piper Ridge. The first is an Offering Spot, which is marked by Stone Statues in a cave on the east side of the Ridge. To solve it, Link must place an Apple in the empty basket. The second Puzzle is a Pinwheel on the peak of the hill. When Link stands near it, Balloons will appear nearby, and they must be shot using Archery. Once each of these Puzzles are solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Pirates' Ship used by the Piratians appears in Subrosia in . The Ghost Pirate Ship used by the Piratians appears in the Sea of Storms in . Tetra's ship makes an appearance very early in . It is seen pursuing the Helmaroc King, with Tetra gripped in its talons. The pirates use a large boulder fired from a catapult to attack the bird, causing it to drop Tetra on the summit of Outset Island's mountain. After being rescued by Link, Tetra returns to her ship, which had at this point docked at Outset. After some convincing from Quill the postman, she agrees to take Link to the Forsaken Fortress on board her ship. During the long voyage, Link is sent below-decks to see Niko, the lowest-ranking member of the crew. After Link completes his rope-swinging obstacle course, Niko gives Link the Spoils Bag. Upon their arrival at the fortress, Link is catapulted inside in a Barrel. Tetra's ship remains hidden behind a large rock while the pirates wait for Link. When they see Link being tossed into the sea by the Helmaroc King, the pirates presumably fled, mistakenly assuming that Link had drowned. Later in the adventure, Link arrives at Greatfish Isle, now cursed. Quill arrives to tell Link that Tetra's crew is seeking Nayru's Pearl, and the pirate ship is docked at Windfall Island. Link sails to Windfall, where the pirates are in the process of robbing the bomb shop. Link sneaks aboard their ship and steals a bomb bag to use at Outset Island. After the final battle with Ganon, Hyrule Castle floods, sending Link and Tetra back to the surface, where they are rescued by Tetra's loyal crew. They are pulled out of the water onto the deck of Tetra's ship. A map found in Tetra's room shows the three Triangle Islands, Dragon Roost Island, Forest Haven and Greatfish Isle connected by lines forming a Triforce around the Tower of the Gods. This, along with Tetra's search for Nayru's Pearl and her disbelief of Link possessing the Master Sword make some believe that the "legendary treasure" she is seeking is an artifact found in Hyrule Castle, possibly the Master Sword. Other pieces found in her cabin include a portrait of Tetra's Mother and two pieces depicting the Hero of Time and Hyrule as they appear in the opening cutscene. If Link speaks to Senza when they set out for sea, he will tell the young hero that he's seen a picture of someone wearing the same Hero's Clothes that Link wears in Tetra's cabin.
