is a recurring character in . Biography Pirou is an old Stable Worker who can be found at the Gerudo Canyon Stable. Link can speak to Pirou to begin the "Rushroom Rush!" Side Quest. When Link first speaks to him,Pirou asks him if he has any Rushrooms. He goes on to explain that he is tired of going at normal speed and that he used to eat Rushrooms every day when he was five years old. Pirou used to win every race thanks to Rushrooms, but now he feels out of energy 55 years later. No matter how many Rushrooms Pirou eats, he is too old to climb the cliffs where Rushrooms grow. Pirou says that he is in the market for Rushrooms, offering Link a Diamond for 55 of them. Pirou explains that Rushrooms grow all over the place and tend to grow on cliffs, which are common around the Stable. He says that he would be picking them himself if he was five years younger. Pirou tells Link to talk to him if he wants to do business. When Link returns to Pirou, he says that he thought Link would come back and asks him if he brought the Rushrooms. If Link does not have 55 Rushrooms in his inventory, Pirou will not accept them, stating that he has no use for a random number of Rushrooms. Once Link brings Pirou 55 Rushrooms, he tells him that he left the Diamond for him behind the Stable. Pirou also questions why Link went through all the trouble for a Diamond. After the Quest is complete, Link will find a Treasure Chest behind the stable containing the Diamond that Pirou promised to give him. Link can return to Pirou any time to exchange 55 Rushrooms for double the market value, which is a total of 330 Rupees. If Link talks to Pirou after the quest, Pirou claims that he knew Link would be back and can tell which people will be repeat customers. If Link sells Pirou another 55 Rushrooms, he will count them and exclaim that is what he likes to see. Pirou pays Link for the Rushrooms and tells him that he will happily buy another batch any time.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Pit Cave is located on the Great Sky Island's southeastern side, south of the Bottomless Cave. At the bottom of the Pit Cave, there is a Ranger Construct who warns Link about the dangers of the Great Sky Island's Freezing Climate near the top of the Cave. It will teach Link that he can avoid losing health in the Freezing Climate by preparing Food with Materials that have "warm-sounding names" and that only one effect gained from Food can be applied at a time. Near the entrance to the lower part of the Pit Cave is a Cracked Wall, which can be destroyed to reveal a chamber with a Rare Ore Deposit, which will always drop a Ruby when destroyed. This chamber connects to a fork in the central portion of the Cave. Creatures Enemies Materials

Pitar is a recurring character in . Biography In , Pitar is one of many people who have become a Cece Fan. He is held hostage in the Old Man's Cabin by the Yiga Clan and forced to make part of their uniforms. Not wanting the Yiga to get their hands on the Yiga Mask he made but unable to take it with him, he instead offers it to Link. After escaping, Pitar can be found traveling on the road to Martha's Landing. If spoken to, he will recognize Link and thank him for rescuing him from the Yiga Clan. He then mentions his search for Misko's treasure so that he can confess his feelings for Nobo in style. He knows the treasure is hidden somewhere in the area, but his search is impeded by how much ground there is to cover.

is a recurring character in . Platt goes unnamed in . Biography Platt is the Hylian husband of Malena, a Gerudo woman who can be found in Gerudo Town. She recalls that he was the first man who ever called her beautiful. The two became married recently, and Malena considers him to be the man of her dreams. However, he soon after fell sick with a disease that can only be cured by Molduga Guts. Malena returned to Gerudo Town seeking help from the Gerudo Soldiers, but none would risk their lives for her. When Link brings Molduga Guts to Malena during the Side Quest "Medicinal Molduga", she will be relieved that she is able to save Platt. Afterwards, she begins making preparations to return to him.

is a recurring character in . Biography Ploka is a Gerudo Soldier who, alongside Reeza, guards the front entrance to the Royal Palace of Gerudo Town at all times. Before Link first speaks to Riju in the palace, the Hylian reporter, Traysi, is seen speaking to Ploka. If Link speaks to Ploka, she mentions that between him and Traysi, many Hylians have come by the palace. Ploka then explains that she guards the palace and that it is the home of Riju, Chief of the Gerudo. She also warns Link not to distract her from her duty. If Link says that he is a Gerudo, Ploka finds the notion ridiculous and yells that he is too short, his hair is not red and he does not have abs. If Link asks for entry to the palace, Ploka yells that they are busy with an emergency, but quickly explains that Riju is in fact allowing visitors. Ploka warns Link that if he says anything rude to Riju, she will attack him with her Spear. If Link speaks to Ploka after speaking to Riju for the first time, she comments that the stolen Thunder Helm is a failure shared by every Gerudo soldier. She feels that only Gerudo should be allowed into the palace at the moment. After Link calms Naboris, Ploka comments that the Gerudo Desert is back to normal now. She also says that she thought Hylians were weak people, but admits that Link is not so bad. Also, as opposed to before, Ploka will enthusiastically welcome Link into the palace, as she considers Link one of the Gerudo. When Link bids farewell by saying "Sav'ork", Ploka corrects him and tells him to say "sav'orq" instead, as he is a friend to the Gerudo. She also mentions that he must work on his pronunciation.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Ploymus Mountain is a mountain in the Lanayru Great Spring which overlooks the East Reservoir Lake. It is inhabited by a lone Lynel, which has caused issues with the residents of Zora's Domain due to its tendency to loose Shock Arrows. In order to stop the flow of water coming from Divine Beast Vah Ruta, Sidon instructs Link to go to Ploymus Mountain and collect any stray Shock Arrows that the Lynel has shot. At Ploymus Mountain, Link can find a total of 31 Shock Arrows stuck to the bark of Cedar Trees, in the ground, and even in the rocks. He can get an extra 20 if he kills the Lynel. Ploymus Mountain is one of the locations that is affected by the constant Rain generated by Divine Beast Vah Ruta. Ploymus Mountain is also where the Zora, Laflat, directs Link in search of a Picture of a red-maned Lynel as part of the "Lynel Safari" Side Quest. During the "EX Champion Mipha's Song" Main Quest from Downloadable Content Pack, Ploymus Mountain is where the Mah Eliya Shrine rises from the ground after completing one of the Trials which requires Link to ascend the waterfalls at Mikau Lake and Lulu Lake. are recurring Enemies and Items in . They are cloaked spirits that freely roam Graveyards and other haunted locales about Hyrule and other lands. They carry a Lantern with them that serves as the container for that specific Poe Soul. Poes are spirits of the dead that became monsters because of an unresolved attachment to the mortal world. Characteristics As ghosts, Poes can disappear and reappear as part of their strategy, and can easily move through walls. Most Poes are known for being wicked, vengeful spirits, however some Poes are helpful and serve as guides, although not without their deceitful trickery. Poes can be defeated with merely the Sword in most games, however, they often have high health or defense mechanisms in place to hinder Link. The Bow can also be an effective weapon, and in some cases is the only weapon that can defeat them. When a Poe is defeated, its physical body disappears and its lantern is dropped and breaks, sometimes releasing its Poe Soul, which may be collected in certain games. These Souls are often important as sidequest items, or can be sold for Rupees. The Poe bears many similarities to Ghinis, and may serve as a replacement to them in console Zelda games since , as Poes behave similarly to them in that title. Poes have since developed separately from the Ghini, and now often employ different strategies and behavior. Poes are not common in the early 2D games, and Ghinis otherwise take their place in those games. Other variations of Poes have also appeared. The Big Poe is a much larger, and in some cases, stronger variant of the Poe. Prankster Poes of bear a close resemblance to Link. The Composer Brothers and Poe Sisters are notable Poes that appear in several games, the latter as mini-bosses. Jalhalla and the Big Poe of are a pair of Poe bosses. In , Poes appear at the Graveyard near the Sanctuary in the Light World, flying sporadically around the area and circling tombstones. They always tend to appear in large groups. Their behavior is similar to that of Ghinis. Much like the Ghini, they also have high health and endurance, and tend to take many hits before they are slain. Poes usually drop items, such as Magic Jars or Arrows when defeated. Their Dark World equivalent is the Hyu, which acts and appears in similar areas to the Poe. In , Poes take on the appearance of hooded wraiths with glowing eyes, and faces shrouded underneath their oversized cloaks. Their distinctive lanterns immediately identifies them, and is the only part of them that will not turn invisible. Targeting a Poe will cause it to temporarily become invisible, although they will reappear in even, predictable intervals. They attack by swinging their lanterns madly at Link. These Poes appear predominately in the Kakariko Graveyard, and rise from their disturbed tombstones, much like Ghinis of earlier games. A second kind of Poe with a square-shaped head also appears around Hyrule

although they will reappear in even, predictable intervals. They attack by swinging their lanterns madly at Link. These Poes appear predominately in the Kakariko Graveyard, and rise from their disturbed tombstones, much like Ghinis of earlier games. A second kind of Poe with a square-shaped head also appears around Hyrule Field when Link is an adult, and appears in the same spawn spots as Big Poes, except that they will only appear when Link is not riding Epona. These Poes do not disappear when Z-Targeted, and instead circle around Link and drop flames around him. All Poes will leave Poe Souls when defeated, which can be collected inside Bottles. These Souls can then be sold to the Poe Collector when Link is an adult for a sum of Rupees. The Poe Soul is a purple-flamed face with melancholy, which will disappear after a short while of inactivity. The aforementioned Big Poes are a variety that only appear in Hyrule Field when Link is an adult, and appear only when Link is riding Epona. These Poes can only be killed with the Bow, as dismounting Epona will make them vanish. Only ten Big Poes exist, and they drop unqiue Big Poe Souls when defeated, which can be sold to the Poe Collector for more Rupees and an empty Bottle as a reward after giving him all ten. There is also an individual Poe encountered in the Haunted Wasteland called the Phantom Guide. It is a helpful spirit that guides Link to the Spirit Temple through the wasteland, and is necessary to follow to avoid getting lost and starting over. It can only be seen with the Lens of Truth. The Composer Brothers are a pair of notable Poes that appear in the Kakariko Graveyard, and are fought as enemies if Link disturbs their tombstones before learning the "Sun's Song". After they are defeated, they reveal that they were the song's composers and left it inscribed in the Royal Family's Tomb. The Poe Sisters also appear as mini-bosses in the Forest Temple. These four Poes steal the fire in the central room and impede Link's progress, forcing him to hunt down each Poe Sister before ultimately facing the fourth sister in battle, Meg. In , Poes appear identically to those of . They carry lanterns with them which remain visible when they are Z-Targeted, and leave behind Poe Souls when defeated. Their Poe Souls can be sold to the Curiosity Shop for a sum of Rupees, though they have little else use aside from profit. Ordinary Poes appear in the Stone Tower Temple. As with , Big Poes also appear and drop Big Poe Souls when defeated. All Poes are encountered in the Ikana region and surrounding area. The Composer Brothers and Poe Sisters make a reappearance in , appearing around the Ikana region as well. The Composer Brothers were the composers of the "Song of Storms", and playing it to the brother Sharp after learning it from Flat will calm him

the Ikana region and surrounding area. The Composer Brothers and Poe Sisters make a reappearance in , appearing around the Ikana region as well. The Composer Brothers were the composers of the "Song of Storms", and playing it to the brother Sharp after learning it from Flat will calm him and revive the dried up Ikana River. The Poe Sisters are optional mini-bosses fought at the Spirit House, and defeating all four earns a Piece of Heart. In , a lone Poe named Allan appears inside a fenced tomb in Yoll Graveyard. Two Poe Sisters called Amy and Margaret serve as Minibosses for the Explorer's Crypt. In , Poes appear as translucent ghosts with mask-like facial features, who come in an assortment of colors, the most common being blue. Their bodies appear to be sack-like, as the tops of their heads are tied up in a knot. Poes will haunt an area slowly with a Lantern in hand until Link gets near, at which point they harass the young hero by following him and swinging their Lantern at him. Though Link can't harm a Poe directly, attacking them with Sword strikes will eventually knock the Lanterns from their hands. This makes the Poes chase Link aggressively, and if they catch up to him, they will jump into his body and possess him, temporarily reversing his movement controls. This lasts for approximately 10 seconds or until a light is shone on Link, then they exit his body and disappear, as if they had been defeated. If a Poe possesses Medli, it will immediately leave her body instead of reversing her controls. By shining light directly on a Poe for several seconds using the Mirror Shield (or Medli's Harp in the Earth Temple), it becomes opaque and corporeal, and begins to run frantically about the room in an attempt to avoid Link's now-effective attacks. Poes appear in the aforementioned Earth Temple and also inhabit the Ghost Ship, several floors of the Savage Labyrinth, and the Earth Temple Room of Ganon's Tower among other places. The Boss of the Earth Temple, Jalhalla, is composed entirely of Poes, and is said to rule over them. Fifteen Lantern-less Poes begin to panic when Link enters the Boss room and assemble themselves into Jalhalla; when the Boss is thrown into the spiked walls of the room, it splits apart into the remaining Poes, who run around the room briefly before reassembling. Using the Hurricane Spin is an effective strategy to defeat these Poes. In , four Poes also appear in the Arbiter's Grounds. Similarly to the Poe Sisters from , they steal the fire from the four Torches in the central room, thereby impeding Link's progress and must be defeated to retrieve the fire. They can only be seen and attacked as Wolf Link, and carry Poe Souls which can be ripped from them. The last Poe has the strategy of duplicating itself and encircling Link. Along with the Imp Poe encountered in Jovani's house, they

and must be defeated to retrieve the fire. They can only be seen and attacked as Wolf Link, and carry Poe Souls which can be ripped from them. The last Poe has the strategy of duplicating itself and encircling Link. Along with the Imp Poe encountered in Jovani's house, they are the only Poes required to be defeated in the game. In , Poes have a radically different look in comparison to their earlier incarnations. They resemble brightly colored puffer fish with body markings, and notably lack lamps. They appear aboard the Ghost Ship and attack by teleporting back and forth, periodically spitting a ball of blue fire at Link. They can only be struck when visible and will actively avoid Link's attacks. In , Poes are based on those from . They fly sporadically and circle around the general area. As ghosts, they are able to move through walls as well. Like the Poes of , they generally take several hits of the Sword to defeat. As enemies they appear in the secret passage connecting the Graveyard and the Sanctuary. A group of nine Poes also appear in the Lost Woods. They help guide Link to the resting place of the Master Sword, however, they also try to mislead him by moving in tricky formations and having Link follow the correct Poe through the woods. The Poes test him several times doing this. If Link fails and makes a wrong turn, he will have to start over from the beginning. After the Master Sword has been retrieved, they will no longer appear in the Lost Woods, and entering the woods will immediately bring Link back to the sword's resting place. In , Poes appear in Levels of The Ruins. They appear in four different colors: white, green, red, and blue. The white Poes can be attacked by any Link, however the colored Poes can only be attacked by the Link whose color corresponds with it. Some of the Poes also float at higher elevations, requiring that the Links form a Totem to reach it, with the top Link as the one who matches the target Poe. A Poe boss called the Grim Repoe is also battled in Palace Noir. When the Links enter its boss room, they first encounter three colored Poes and must defeat them to make Grim Repoe appear, however these Poes will actively flee from the Links, making fighting them difficult. In addition to these Poes, there are also Prankster Poes, Key Bandit Poes, and a Lantern Poe. Instead of being enemies as they traditionally are, Poes are Items that drift around the Depths, and serve as a secondary form of currency. They resemble blue will-o'-the-wisps. Link can collect Poes and trade them to Bargainer Statues for materials and rare equipment. is a recurring character in . Biography Link can first encounter Pokki after discovering the Misae Suma Shrine in the East Barrens. Link cannot enter the Ancient Shrine because Pokki is collapsed over the pedestal where he must place his Sheikah Slate to gain entry. If Link speaks to Pokki, she will claim that she is dying of thirst and, before passing, she would like one last taste of a Noble Pursuit. This gives Link the Shrine Quest, "The Perfect Drink", and he cannot enter the Shrine until he finishes the Quest. If Link speaks to Pokki after bringing ice to Furosa, he tells Pokki that there is a Noble Pursuit waiting for her in Gerudo Town. Pokki then stands up without any signs of dehydration and exclaims that she is leaving before running away toward town. After the Quest, Pokki can be found inside The Noble Canteen talking to the bartender, Furosa, about how great the taste of Noble Pursuit is, swearing to quit investigating the shrine in the process. After the "Riju of Gerudo Town" Main Quest is completed, Pokki can be found at the Sand-Seal Rental Shop East Gate Booth talking with Frelly. Link can eavesdrop to hear Pokki ask Frelly if any of her customers have seen ruins with large statues facing each other. Frelly comments on how there are a number of ruins throughout Gerudo Desert and asks if Pokki has a map or any other information to clarify which ruins she is talking about. Pokki complains that she used to have a map, but it was carried off by the wind and lost, and now the only thing she remembers is that the ruins are somewhere in the eastern desert. Frelly tries to think longer, but notices Link standing nearby and apologizes to Pokki stating that she needs to get back to work. This starts the Side Quest, "To the Ruins!" Pokki can then be found pacing nearby, pondering what she can do to get to the ruins. If Link speaks with her, she will ask him if he has ever seen the ruins she was talking to Frelly about. She asks if Link could take her to the ruins on a Sleigh Seal for a reward. If Link declines, she says it isn't a big deal since most Gerudo don't even know about the ruins. If Link agrees to take her, she'll wait by the East Gate to the town. Link can rent a Sleigh Seal from Frelly near the east gate.

is a recurring location in . Pondo's Lodge goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Pondo's Lodge is a House located on the Tabantha Frontier, directly east of Hebra Tower. Its sole inhabitant is Pondo, a Hylian man. A Cooking Pot and a Bed can be found inside the Lodge, the latter of which Link can Sleep in to restore his Hearts. Due to it being situated in a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit Pondo's Lodge without taking damage. From his Lodge, Pondo operates the Snowball Bowling Mini-Game. It costs Link 20 Rupees to play a single round. The first time Link scores a strike, Pondo gives him a Blizzard Rod as a reward. Otherwise, Pondo gives out a varying amount of Rupees as a reward, depending on how many pins were knocked over. In the time since , Pondo's Lodge has been destroyed, becoming a Deserted House.

is a character in . Biography Ponnick is a member of the Zonai Survey Team, who accompanies Robbie while he is investigating Hyrule Field Chasm. When Link approaches him, he reveals that Robbie instructed him to guide Link to his location. However, Ponnick did not bring enough Brightbloom Seeds to keep up with Robbie, and now he has lost him. He claims that Robbie was initially only visiting the Nisoij Lightroot nearby, but he kept walking past it, Ponnick then asks Link if he has any Brightbloom Seeds. If Link says that he does not, Ponnick impresses upon him the danger of exploring the Depths without Light. If Link claims to have Brightbloom Seeds, Ponnick will be relieved. Either way, Ponnick tells him that they can be found in Caves on the Surface, and he can throw them or shoot them on Arrows to cause them to bloom into Brightblooms. Before Link leaves, Ponnick once again expresses his sadness about not having enough Brightbloom Seeds.

The is a recurring location in . The Popla Foothills North Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Popla Foothills North Well is a stout stone Well, located on a ridge in the Popla Foothills. It has no roof. Prior to the Great Calamity that occurred 100 years before the events of , the Well was part of an unnamed Hylian settlement. Like in , the Popla Foothills North Well is situated on the Popla Foothills in West Necluda. The Popla Foothills Skyview Tower has been erected next to it. The Well now features an interior, which consists of a small pool of Water with two Boulders submerged in it. Nearby is a Cracked Wall, which Link can destroy to reveal a Zonai Ruin connected to that of the Popla Foothills Excavation Site. However, they are separated by two portcullises. When Link visits the Popla Foothills North Well after activating the Lookout Landing Skyview Tower, he can hear a voice calling for help from inside the Well. Once inside the Well, he can follow the voice past the Cracked Wall and into the Zonai Ruin. There, he finds Elmerson trapped between the two portcullises. He is shocked to see Link and asks for his assistance in escaping. When asked what happened to him, Elmerson explains that he became stuck after setting off a trap. He points out a Floor Switch on the other side of the portcullises, which he claims Link can use to free him. By entering the Popla Foothills Excavation Site and activating the Floor Switch, Link can rescue Elmerson, who gives him the Purple Rupee that he found within the trap's Iron Treasure Chest. The is a recurring location in . The Popla Foothills South Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Popla Foothills South Well can be found between the Popla Foothills and the Farosh Hills in West Necluda. Prior to the Great Calamity, which occurred 100 years before the events of , it was part of an unnamed Hylian settlement. Equipment Treasure Chests The Popla Foothills South Well returns in , and it is still part of West Necluda. Link is now able to access its interior, which features two chambers. The first contains a pool of Water and a small archway that leads to the second chamber. The second chamber contains dry land, as well as a potted Brightbloom next to a Note on the Table written by Aurie Taamu. It details the use of "bright" ingredients that produce the Glow Added Effect when Cooking, such as Brightcaps or Glowing Cave Fish. A Cooking Pot with an unlit Campfire beneath it is also nearby. are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Porgies are Ocean-dwelling Fish that increase Link's attack damage and Defense when Cooked into Foods. Two types of Porgy exist: Armored Porgies boost Link's Defense, and Mighty Porgies boost his attack power. Both types can be exclusively found in the Necluda and Lanayru Seas. Both types of Porgy are also sold at the Merchant Boat in Lurelin Village and by the traveling Merchant Chumin. Porgy Meunières and Seafood Paellas can be Cooked using either type of Porgies. Other Appearances Both Armored and Mighty Porgies can be sold at Shops for 10 Rupees.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Porgy Meunière can be made by Cooking either an Armored Porgy or a Mighty Porgy alongside Goat Butter and Tabantha Wheat in a Cooking Pot. The regular version can only be made in different ways. First, Link can utilize both types of Porgy when cooking. Second, he can use another ingredient that has a different effect than the Porgy used. When eaten, these meunières will restore some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. These dishes are popular among residents of coastal regions. Two different variations of Porgy Meunière exist: Mighty Porgy Meunière: Made by using Mighty Porgies. Eating these meals will grant Link a boost to his attack power. Tough Porgy Meunière: Made by using Tough Porgies. Link can eat them to increase his defensive abilities. Other Appearances The recipe for Porgy Meunière is earned by completing the Quest "Dish for a Diva". It is made using four Tabantha Wheat, four Goat Butters, and eight Armored Porgies. However, it can be lowered to three Tabantha Wheat, three Goat Butters, and six Armored Porgies through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warriors will take 10% less damage from Enemies.

Portable Pots are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Portable Pots are Zonai creations that can be found throughout Hyrule. They can be used as Cooking Pots to Cook Food anywhere, but they will only be able to Cook one Meal before being consumed. Portable Pots can also simply be bonded to Objects and other Zonai Devices with the Ultrahand ability. Unlike normal Cooking Pots, Portable Pots do not require an external source of Fire to work and can be used in Rain. Other Appearances Portable Pots appear at Camps in the Depths. Braton wears a Portable Pot as a helmet, which he can use while performing attacks. He received it from a Steward Construct at a Camp as a reward for performing well during battle. Braton often uses the Pot to eat Rocks out of.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Pot Lids are lids of large soup pots that can be used as Shields in combat. It is said that they smell of poultry, likely due to being used for Cooking. They are also considered to be quite Durable. They can often be found next to Cooking Pots at Stables or other settlements, such as Hateno Village and Kakariko Village. They can also be found in some Monster Strongholds, where they are wielded by Bokoblins, and rarely, Moblins. According to Daruk's Training Journal, Link once used a Pot Lid to defeat a Guardian by deflecting its laser after it began acting erratically during an experiment. Being made of wood, Pot Lids will burn and eventually disintegrate if they touch Fire or are equipped in a Scorching Climate. They will also float if they are dropped in Water, and they will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity. Finally, Pot Lids cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Pot Lids reappear in . Other Appearances Pot Lids can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Soup Ladles, the Lucky Ladle, or the Training Sword.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview After both "Riju of Gerudo Town" and "The Missing Owner" have been completed, Link can speak to Isha in front of Starlight Memories, who thanks him for saving Gerudo Town. To repay him for his assistance, she offers to craft the Arms of the Seven for him, which consist of the Scimitar of the Seven and the Daybreaker. Since she is the only one who knows how to craft them, she has chosen Link to wield them, and she asks if he wants them. If Link agrees to take on the Arms of the Seven, Isha reveals that their wielder must gather the supplies needed to craft them. In total, she needs four Diamonds, 10 pieces of Flint, a Gerudo Scimitar, and a Gerudo Shield, at which point she will be able to make them for him. After this conversation, "Pride of the Gerudo" will begin. When Link returns to Isha with all of the supplies, she will proceed to craft the Arms of the Seven for him. Afterwards, she will present him with the Scimitar of the Seven and Daybreaker, claiming to have poured her heart into making them. She also wishes Link luck on his journey. Isha reveals that she has only ever made the Arms of the Seven for one other person, that being Riju. She also claims that an ancestor of hers made them for Urbosa, the Champion of the Gerudo. Although Isha wants them to be taken care of well, she offers to make new ones of Link breaks or loses them. Lastly, she invites Link to visit her whenever he wants. Following this conversation, "Pride of the Gerudo" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring character in . Biography Prima is the clerk of The Great Ton Pu Inn and will greet customers as they come in, offering either a regular bed or a downy bed for the night. She is also the object of fellow villager Manny's affections. However, she appears to utterly ignore his existence. Once the Side Quest "A Gift for My Beloved" has begun, Link can approach Prima behind the counter. Although she is confused by his behavior, Prima attempts to keep a professional demeanor. Link can praise her establishment and she recommends that he return to the other side of the counter so she might set him up with a room. Once Link begins to ask about her interests for Manny, she becomes annoyed and blurts out a lie of wanting one hundred Restless Crickets. Should Link continue to pester her, Prima's irritation grows.

, also known as Ms. Zelda's House, is a location in . Features and Overview Princess Zelda's House was formerly Link's House in , but it has since come into Zelda's possession after she moved to Hateno Village. is a recurring location in . Princess Zelda's Study goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Princess Zelda's Study is a small room located in a tower structure connected to Princess Zelda's Room by a bridge. The bridge and the air encircling the Study is patrolled by a lone Guardian Skywatcher. The interior of the Study is filled with several Books, charts, and rotted plants. Prior to the Great Calamity, Zelda conducted her research on Ancient Technology and plants in this room. The "Father and Daughter" Recovered Memory can be accessed on the bridge connecting Princess Zelda's Study to the rest of Hyrule Castle. During this, King Rhoam confronts Zelda as she leaves her Study, eventually forbidding her from continuing her research. Following the return of Calamity Ganon, the Study was overtaken by Zelda's plants. Placed open-faced on the desk at the far end of the study Zelda's Research Notes, a Book detailing Zelda's findings on Ancient Technology, as well as the effort to pilot the Divine Beasts with the Champions at their helm. A singular Silent Princess can be found growing in the mound of rubble near the center of the room, an allegory of Zelda's love of research over her regal duties. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle is located at Princess Zelda's Study. At the tip of the spire on top of Princess Zelda's Study, Link can find Leaves with Fairy Dust. Interacting with them will cause a Korok to appear, which gives him a Korok Seed as a reward. Enemies Materials As in , Princess Zelda's Study is located west of Princess Zelda's Room within Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field. Equipment Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests Other Appearances Princess Zelda's Study can be seen on the day of the Great Calamity during the "Across Time" Movie. The box containing Terrako falls off of a shelf, and as Zelda awakens her powers, it is activated. Hearing Zelda's wish to protect everyone, it opens a Gate of Time, but it is interrupted by a Guardian breaking down the door. Terrako is able to dodge its laser and fall through the Gate, followed by several pieces of Malice.

, traditionally , is the eponymous character of . With the exception of , , and , an incarnation of Zelda or one of her alter egos has always been one of the central characters in the series. Physical traits Princess Zelda is often shown as a beautiful and elegant princess, with the exception of , where she is portrayed as an ordinary girl before the kingdom of Hyrule had been established. She is always either a child, teen, or young adult. Her hair color is depicted as blonde in most games of the series, as well as brown in and red in and . Her eyes are portrayed in different shades of blue throughout all the games, with the exception of her green eyes in . Her ears are always pointed, as is characteristic of all Hylians, although in some games her ears are shorter than in others. The dresses that she wears are long with determinate colors, such as different tones of pink, white, and blue. Most of her dresses are shown with the Hylian Crest, and in almost every game, she is seen wearing a tiara with either a red, pink, or blue jewel in it. In some games, she also wears long gloves. Princess Zelda is seen wearing makeup in most games, such as in and , and her hairstyle is characterized either with her hair down or with braids. She wears high heels, although in , , and she wears boots. She also occasionally wears sandals, such as in and . Each incarnation of Zelda has been shown at various ages depending on which title they appear in. They have appeared as a child, a teenager and as a young adult; for example, the Princess Zelda in is around 20 years of age, and the one in is depicted as 16 and 17 years old, depending on the time of flashbacks. Personality Zelda is depicted as a kind and benevolent ruler with a wisdom beyond her years and a deep love towards the people she watches over. She is a caring, gracious, and self-sacrificing person. Zelda's most prominent display of compassion and selflessness was when she saved the life of Midna, the Princess of the Twilight Realm, who had been nearly killed by the false King of the Twilight, Zant. Zelda's wisdom is her most valuable attribute. As a matriarch, it is imperative that she makes the wisest decision concerning the fate of Hyrule; in when Zant threatened her life and the lives of all of her subjects, she wisely surrendered to him. She upholds her responsibilities no matter the cost and is always willing to help her friends, such as in , where Zelda faces her duties as the goddess reborn and willingly remains in a deep sleep to keep Demise imprisoned within his seal. Above all, Zelda is known to be a forgiving person even towards those who have harmed her before, as seen in , where she asks Anjean to take care

Princess Zelda is one of the three most important characters of series, which is also why her name appears in the title of every game. Princess Zelda first appeared in the original , and has since been featured in every subsequent game, with the exception of . Each incarnation of the Princess is chosen by destiny to be the keeper of the Triforce of Wisdom in their respective eras, which is the main reason why they play such an integral role in the legends of Hyrule. Abilities thumb|250px|left|Princess Zelda calls upon the power of the Light Spirits in Throughout the series, Princess Zelda portrays various types of both magical and physical abilities, ranging from capably wielding a bow to telepathy, as seen in 's introduction when she pleads for Link's help. Early on in the timeline of the series, the original Zelda, while born as a Hylian, is the mortal incarnation of the Goddess Hylia. Carrying on this divine blood, her female descendants are always the of Hyrule throughout its history. Several princesses within the bloodline are also the possessor of the Triforce of Wisdom, imbued with the essence of the Goddess Nayru. The essence of Nayru affords each Zelda divine wisdom, allowing them to discern the wisest decisions, especially in situations concerning the welfare of Hyrule. It grants them myriad mystical abilities, including the ability to heal others, though there is a possibility that this could also be an effect of their bloodline passing down Hylia's own powers and, later, the Light Force. Each incarnation of Zelda uses their powers to keep evil in check. Many of her abilities as both a Sage and the wielder of the Triforce of Wisdom are widely illustrated in , one of them being that she has prophetic visions in her dreams. She also helps Link in their escape from Ganon's Castle by using her powers to magically remove the barriers blocking the exits. During the final battle between Link and Ganon, Princess Zelda uses her powers to restrain the King of Evil as Link delivers the final blow. Being the seventh Sage, she is the ruler of the rest of the six Sages, and it is with her guidance that the Sages seal Ganon in the void of the Evil Realm. Finally, with her powers as a Sage, she is capable of returning Link to his original time by simply using the Ocarina of Time. In , Princess Zelda aids Link in battling Ganondorf by borrowing the young hero's bow and using it to fire Light Arrows at the King of the Gerudo. This skill is again portrayed in the final battle of , where the princess yet again uses a bow and Light Arrows to strike Ganondorf while accompanying Link on his horse, and once more in the final battle against Malladus in . In one scene of , Princess Zelda is seen wielding a sword, although it is unknown if she possesses any true sword skills. As shown in , Princess Zelda is capable of communicating with the Light Spirits. Just as the princess and Link are about to be trampled by Ganondorf's ghostly army, Zelda calls upon the Light Spirits to aid her in her time of need, and the spirits grant her the Light Arrow to banish evil. In , Princess Zelda can possess a Phantom's body after Link strikes it with a powered-up sword or the Lokomo Sword. While in this state, the princess can help Link solve various puzzles as well as cross certain obstacles that the young hero cannot traverse by himself. Moreover, due to the Phantom's armor, she can also protect Link from attacks or use her strength to fight alongside Link and help him defeat enemies, as seen when fighting Geozards or Byrne. Naming Tradition and Law Origin It was revealed by that when the kingdom of Hyrule was established during the Era of Prosperity, the daughters of the Royal Family were often named Zelda after their ancestor, the mortal incarnation of the Goddess Hylia, from the events of . The Tragedy of "Princess Zelda I" left While she was not the first Princess Zelda in the history of Hyrule, she was the first in a long line of princesses to be named Zelda by law and not tradition after she was put into a deep sleep for many generations. Her brother, the Prince of Hyrule at the end of its Golden Era, who was partly to blame for her comatose state, decided that, in honor of his sister, every princess born into the Royal Family of Hyrule should be named Zelda. Biography 150px|left The Zelda in is the first Zelda appearing in the series, and the fourth Zelda chronologically in the Fallen Hero Timeline. After rescuing her father, Zelda learns that the force behind the Rifts is seeking out the Triforce, known as the Prime Energy. After helping close the Rifts on Eldin Volcano, the Faron Wetlands, and Holy Mount Lanayru, one of the three Golden Goddesses, Din, Nayru, and Farore, will appear before Zelda to grant her their Sanctions. is a recurring character in . Biography Prissen is a member of the Treasure-Hunting Brothers and can be found at the Dueling Peaks Stable with his twin brother, Domidak. When Link approaches them, he will overhear Prissen excitedly telling his brother about a hint toward the bandit Misko's treasure. Domidak is quick to quiet him when he notices Link listening in, but Prissen can't help boasting about how close they are to finding their latest target. His brother immediately chastises him and Prissen apologizes for his overzealousness. Domidak will try to throw Link off by saying Prissen is rambling to keep him off track of the treasure, but if Link is persistent, Prissen will recommend they just tell Link their information to get him to go away. His logic is that since the two of them are having such difficulty, Link is unlikely to find the treasure before them. Domidak agrees, but demands a fee of 100 Rupees out of Link, and Prissen praises him for his quick thinking. Once Link agrees and pays the fee, Prissen will praise Domidak once again for netting them some Rupees. Domidak will share their information as promised and Prissen continues to gush over his older brother's accomplishment. Once the conversation is over, the Side Quest "Misko, the Great Bandit" begins. Domidak will continue to ponder the riddle, thinking he's close to uncovering its meaning, and Prissen will naturally cheer him on. If Link tells them to keep up their work, Prissen rudely dismisses him and demands that his brother handle the issue. Link can let them both know that he already solved the riddle, even if the Side Quest has not yet been completed, but they do not believe him. Prissen goes on to declare that Link could not have found the solution before his brother. He immediately tells Domidak to get rid of him.

is a recurring character in . Biography Pritana is a Gerudo who can be found in Gerudo Town. When talking with Nali in the center of the Town, Pritana says she cannot believe that Riju's Thunder Helm was stolen by thieves. Nali replies that the Thunder Helm is a helmet that was Lady Urbosa's favorite and explains that it has been passed from chief to chief for generations. Pritana feels sorry for Riju and Nali comments that she heard the thieves are professional assassins. Pritana reasons that this must be why the barracks have been more noisy lately. If Link speaks to Pritana while she is not talking with Nali, she explains that she chats with Nali every day, but they never get tired of talking about the same things. Pritana feels like she could talk forever with her "vai friends." She also tells Link that the Gerudo Desert gets very cold at night, warning him that he will catch a cold or worse if he wears his Gerudo Outfit outside of the Town walls. Pritana recommends staying at the Hotel Oasis if Link does not have a warmer outfit, such as a Warm Doublet. Pritana will go home at certain times during the day, where she is found lying in bed muttering that she does not feel good. If approached when she gets out of bed and begins to leave, she will ask Link to be quiet, as she has a strong headache. During the night, Pritana can be found inside The Noble Canteen. If Link speaks to her, she says that he looks too young to drink there and asks how old he is. If Link says he is over 100 in reference to his Slumber of Restoration, Pritana pauses and then begins to laugh, complimenting Link's sense of humor and asking him to drink with her when he gets older. If Link ends the conversation instead, Pritana reaffirms that the drinks in the Canteen are only for adults.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Proxim Bridge is a stone bridge that spans the Hylia River It serves to connect the East Post Ruins in Hyrule Field to West Necluda. Unlike most other bridges, Proxim Bridge has stone Fire pits that line its walls. They can be rekindled as long as it is not Raining in the area. During the Great Calamity, any refugees from Hyrule Field would have passed over Proxim Bridge while attempting to evacuate to Necluda. Proxim Bridge is guarded by a Hylian named Brigo, who protects it from Monster due to it being an "important route." When asked, Brigo will give Link directions and insights into Kakariko Village, the Great Plateau, and Hyrule Castle. If Link stands on the Bridge's railings during Brigo's patrol, he will try to talk him down from jumping. When Link steps down from the railing, Brigo will be relieved and tell him never to do that again. Creatures Enemies Materials Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

is a recurring character in . Biography Pruce runs East Wind, the resident General Store of Hateno Village. He is usually busy behind the counter, sometimes neglecting to notice customers when they first come in. He takes a moment to make sure everything is in place before returning to the counter proper. When he is ready for business, he is open to conversation. Link can mention he is here to purchase items and Pruce will explain how to do so. Should Link ask Pruce about himself, he will be startled at first, then do so before mentioning his family. He will go on to mention that most of Hateno's villagers are friendly enough to speak with travelers. If Link asks to sell something, Pruce will be happy to oblige. Gaining anything makes Pruce quite happy, and although he is eager to buy, he assures Link that he is in no hurry. Lastly, when Link buys anything, he will thank him for his business. If he buys his entire stock, then Pruce may offer to restock the item eventually or state that Link has things going well for him. If it is late, Pruce will make note of the time. Despite this, the shop remains open. Once Link decides to leave the store, Pruce expresses the hope that he will return.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Puffer Beach is located on the southern end of the Faron Grasslands. The Beach features a large overhanging cliff from the Nette Plateau to the north, from which several Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits hang. Strong Winds occasionally sweep over the Beach from the Faron Sea to the south. Several tide pools and Fallen Guardians can also be found throughout the Beach. On the western end of Puffer Beach, Loone resides in a small campsite, which contains a Cooking Pot, two Barrels, and two Wooden Boxes. When Link first encounters Loone on Puffer Beach, she will be affectionately holding onto an Ancient Orb, which she has named Roscoe. A Pedestal with a Concave Slot can be found nearby. However, Loone refuses to hand over Roscoe, claiming that she is in love with it. She then admits, though, that she would give him up if she could see a variety of Guardians, though she considers this to be unlikely. Link will then receive the "Guardian Slideshow" Shrine Quest. When Link brings Loone Pictures of a Guardian Skywatcher, a Guardian Scout, and a Guardian Stalker, she will move on from Roscoe and allow Link to take it. If he places Roscoe in the Concave Slot of the Pedestal on Puffer Beach, Shoqa Tatone Shrine will rise from the Sand. Four Treasure Chests are located on Puffer Beach. The first can be found off the eastern end of the shore, and it contains a Silver Rupee. The second and third Chest are located in the western tide pool, and a bundle of five Bomb Arrows and an Opal can be found inside of them. The last Treasure Chest is within the eastern tide pool, and another Silver Rupee is located inside. left|40px A total of five Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Puffer Beach. The first is a Natural Hiding Spot, which takes the form of a Rock that is hidden under a Boulder on the western end of the Beach. The second is another Natural Hiding Spot Rock, this time located on top of the pillar near Loone's campsite. The third Puzzle is a group of Leaves with Fairy Dust that dart around the tide pool underneath the cliff. The fourth is a Circle of seaweed in the western tide pool, which Link must jump into. Lastly, a Cube Pattern can be found near a tide pool on the east end of the Beach. When Link solves each of the Korok Seed Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Puffshrooms are a type of Mushroom growing throughout the Depths. When thrown, struck by a Weapon, Enemy, or Object, shot by an Arrow, or Fused to a Weapon, Shield, or fired Arrow, Puffshrooms emit a smoke-like cloud of spores that blinds nearby Enemies to Link's presence. Affected Enemies can be Sneakstriked while the cloud is present. Link can also freely mount Lynels when they are caught in the spores. Due to the bitter powder they produce, they are inedible. When Fused to a Weapon or Shield, a Puffshroom will be consumed after only one use. However, if it is Fused to a Weapon that is part of the Korok Gear, it can be used continuously. Puffshrooms are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances Puffshrooms reappear as Materials in .

are recurring Objects and Items in . They occur sometimes as a visual element, sometimes as an item, sometimes as a breakable container, and sometimes as a combination of these. They appeared mainly as a recurring visual motif until , where physical pumpkins and their products became considerably more important. Location and Uses The first Boss in is Pumpkin Head, who, as its name suggests, is a spirit with a Pumpkin (specifically a ) for a head. This continues the theme of Pumpkins as a symbol of evil spirits seen in . Pumpkins feature prominently in as one of the main exports of Ordon Village. In Ordon Village, Link can find Pumpkins in the fields. These can be smashed to get Pumpkin Seeds, which are the primary ammunition for the Slingshot. The Scarecrows near Link's House also appear to have Pumpkins for heads. An Ordon Pumpkin is also found in a Treasure Chest in Snowpeak Ruins, although Yeta misremembered the chest as containing the Bedroom Key. When added to the Simple Soup, the Ordon Pumpkin converts it to Good Soup, which restores four Hearts as opposed to two. Pumpkins seem to be the primary agricultural product of Skyloftians in . One of the islands in the Sky, Pumpkin Landing, being dedicated to growing Pumpkins, as it is the home to a sizable (by game standards) Pumpkin patch and the Lumpy Pumpkin, a pub specializing in Pumpkin Soup. Even the decor of the establishment is Pumpkin-themed, as are the names of the father and daughter who staff it. Pumpkins can also be found on the main island of Skyloft in smaller patches. There is also a minigame in involving Pumpkins, that being Pumpkin Pull. As in , Pumpkins can be smashed, although they yield a variety of items, as Pots do. In , following "The Mayoral Election" Side Adventure, Mayor Reede of Hateno Village begins growing a new variety of Pumpkins named Sun Pumpkins. Other Appearances In , Ordon Pumpkins appear as destroyable objects that can be shot for extra points. They normally appear in clusters and mainly in stages that take place in Ordon Village. 64px|left In , Pumpkins appear as Plant-type Food. They are imbued with the Light Element. When consumed by a Companion Fairy in the Dining Room of the My Fairy mode, Pumpkins can increase the Fairy's Trust level and personality traits.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Link can make Pumpkin Pies by Cooking a Fortified Pumpkin, Tabantha Wheat, Cane Sugar, and Goat Butter together in a Cooking Pot. The default version can only be made by adding either a Fruit or a Vegetable with an effect that differs from Fortified Pumpkins. When eaten, they will restore some of his Hearts. Due to the sweetness of Fortified Pumpkins, these desserts are popular among children. Only one variation of Pumpkin Pie exists: Tough Pumpkin Pie: Made by adding no additional ingredients. By consuming these Pies, Link's defense will be temporarily boosted. Two variations of Pumpkin Pie exist: Sunny Pumpkin Pie: Made with Sun Pumpkins. By consuming these Pies, any Hearts Link has lost to Gloom will be restored. Tough Pumpkin Pie: Made with Fortified Pumpkins. By consuming these Pies, Link's Defense will be temporarily boosted.

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Pumpkin Stews are Meals that can be made by Cooking a Fortified Pumpkin, Tabantha Wheat, Goat Butter, and Fresh Milk together in a Cooking Pot. The only way to make regular Pumpkin Stew is to add ingredients to the Recipe that contradict the tough effect. Link can eat them to restore some of his Hearts to his Life Gauge. These Meals are favored in Kakariko Village. The Girl's Notebook, which can be found in Hateno Village, details the recipe for Pumpkin Stew. The author describes it as a secret recipe that will surprise the most knowledgeable of fathers, instructing the reader to start with some Fortified Pumpkins. Next, she suggests to add Tabantha Wheat for a "wheaty flavor", and then to let the Fresh Milk and Goat Butter simmer. The recipe is concluded by telling the reader they should now have Pumpkin Stew. Only one variation of Pumpkin Stew can be made: Tough Pumpkin Stew: Made by using the default recipe. When these Stews are eaten, Link will receive a boost to his defensive abilities. Two variations of Pumpkin Stew can be made: Sunny Pumpkin Stew: Made by using Sun Pumpkins. When these Stews are eaten, several of Link's Hearts damaged by Gloom will be restored. Tough Pumpkin Stew: Made by using Fortified Pumpkins. When these Stews are eaten, Link will receive a boost to his defensive abilities. Other Appearances The recipe for Pumpkin Stew is earned by completing the Quest "The Pumpkin Hunt". It is made using four Fortified Pumpkins, four Tabantha Wheat, four Fresh Milks, and four Goat Butters. However, it can be lowered to three of each ingredient through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warriors will recover health for every Enemy KO.

is a recurring character in . Biography Purah is the director of the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab, where she works with her assistant Symin. Her research and experimentation with an anti-aging Rune caused her to grow younger, but due to underestimating the Rune's potency she reverted to the body and mentality of a 6-year-old. Though she appears as a young girl, she is around 124 years old. She is the older sister of Impa and the oldest Sheikah alive, save for Monk Maz Koshia. When first approached by Link, she gives him a greeting and asks if he has come for the director of the Lab. If he says yes, she claims that Symin is the director and asks Link not to bother him long. She does take a moment to notice that Link appears to be a traveler on an adventure. Should Link say that he has spoken to the director, she pretends to be pleased and hopes that he remembers the Lab fondly. Once Link has been informed of her true identity, she confirms it. Purah asks him about any dreams he may have had during his Slumber of Restoration, calling him "Linky" and pointing out that he has not changed. She is happy to see him well, but his blank look helps her realize that he no longer recognizes her. Purah reveals that she was the one to originally take Link to the Shrine of Resurrection. She asks Link again if he cannot remember her and his response prompts her to pull out a notebook to take notes. Purah admits that she does this often and asks Link if he has any questions. Naturally, Link is confused by her appearance. At first, Purah claims his observation is rude, but realizes that he has a good point. She explains that it is due to a faulty experiment and asks him not to look into it in her Diary. She pushes the topic back to Calamity Ganon and Link's quest. Purah explains that she intends to help him by fixing the Sheikah Slate. If Link asks her to repeat what she said, Purah pulls out her notebook again to note it before telling him to pay attention. Should Link decide to refuse, Purah is at first annoyed, but then decides to give him the time to change his mind. Once Link agrees to Purah's help, she asks him to run a quick errand. Link seems to give her an odd look, and she asks if he thought she would help him for free. If Link admits that he did, she will take more notes. If he says he did not expect that, Purah decides that he is surprisingly considerate for his age. Purah explains the errand for him, stating that she requires their furnace lit to restore his Runes. She quietly wonders if people still use the same language that she does. Once she gives Link his task, he may ask her about a number of things. Should he

for his age. Purah explains the errand for him, stating that she requires their furnace lit to restore his Runes. She quietly wonders if people still use the same language that she does. Once she gives Link his task, he may ask her about a number of things. Should he ask about the ancient furnace, she will tell him where it is located. Questioning her about the Blue Flame itself will prompt her to give him advice on how to get it back to Laboratory. If he asks her who she is, she gives her name again and uses her catchphrase. However, she realizes that Link is looking for her true age and shoots down any hope of getting it from her, telling him not to ask her too many questions about herself. Whenever she is done answering a question, Purah will ask if Link has any others for her. Purah also mentions that there is a Torch nearby that Link can use in his task. Link can actually light the furnace before ever speaking to Purah. As soon they speak, Purah makes it clear that she is surprised to see him. At first, she tries out her new catchphrase on him, but realizes this is not the time. She finally asks Link if he was the one to bring the Blue Flame up to the Lab. Once Link admits to being behind it, Purah believes that he woke from his Slumber of Restoration in fairly good condition. Purah then introduces herself and reveals that she knows the Sheikah Slate is in need of repair. When Link confirms this, she is pleased that she predicted the issue, but informs the hero that she has a number of questions to ask first. She then moves into her usual dialogue. Once this is completed, she will add the Camera Rune and the Sheikah Sensor to the Sheikah Slate. Purah then asks Link to take a Picture of her. Link can ask her about the new Camera function, and she tells him how Zelda had once used it and how to create an image with it, before reminding him of her request for a self-portrait. Asking her about a Picture will prompt Purah to define it for him, mentioning the Hyrule Compendium and advising him take as many Pictures as possible. If he says he needs a moment to prepare the Camera, she tells him not to worry but makes it clear she is looking forward to it. When she sees the picture Link takes of her, Purah is very pleased with her appearance. For a moment, she is too overwhelmed to continue the conversation. Once she snaps out of it, Purah takes notice of Zelda's excessive use of the Camera and realizes that Link was likely with the Princess at each of the locations in the pictures. Before he sets out, the director asks him to return later with Ancient Materials, promising a reward for delivering them to either her or her companion in research, Robbie. After the Calamity, Robbie and Purah purposefully set up their labs in different places so that if one of them died, the other would still be around to help Link when he awoke. Purah will upgrade the Sheikah Sensor, Remote Bomb, and Stasis Runes in exchange for three Ancient Screws, three Ancient Shafts, and three Ancient Cores, respectively. Purah is the founder and leader of Lookout Landing, as well as the authority that the Zonai Survey Team reports to. She has also become a teacher to Josha. After Calamity Ganon was defeated, Purah and Robbie collaborated to create the Purah Pad, naming it after herself. She hoped that it would assist in Hyrule's recovery, and she gave their prototype to Zelda to use. Purah has written four volumes of her Diary, which she did to prevent all of her writings from being read by others. The volumes can be found in her Room at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab, Paya's Room at the Chief's Hall, the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab, and her Research Lab at Lookout Landing. Recently, Purah has returned her age to that of a 20 year-old, since she was frustrated when others treated her as a child. This is the age she was when she worked at the Royal Ancient Lab with Robbie, and as a result, she has had a dream about that time. She recalls that their experiments caused many explosions, but Zelda and Impa covered for them. Purah has also found it easier to reach high places and stay up late researching, and she notes that her skin is perfect. When Gloom began to seep up from Beneath Hyrule Castle, Purah established Lookout Landing so that she could observe it from a distance. After a stairway leading to the source of the Gloom was found, Zelda volunteered to investigate before Purah could ask her. Despite believing Zelda and Link to be qualified, Purah felt dread about sending them down there. Since the Upheaval started not long after they left, Purah feared that the two events were related. After Zelda and Link disappeared, Purah has been worried, and she mobilized the Monster-Control Crew to search Hyrule Castle for them. The is an Item in . Location and Uses The Purah Pad is a device created by the Sheikah researchers, Purah and Robbie, to be used by adventurers. It was developed after Robbie moved to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab to assist Purah with her research. Robbie is upset that it is not named after him, despite his contributions to its development. It has a thin, tablet-like design, with gold and crimson colorations. The back has a camera lens decorated with a Crest of the Sheikah, reminiscent of Purah's glasses. Instructions for the base features of the Purah Pad can be found in the Purah Pad Manual, in Purah's office at Lookout Landing. Robbie's Fabric's design is based on the Purah Pad's UI for the Hyrule Compendium. At the beginning of , the Purah Pad is in Zelda's possession. She uses it to capture photos of the Zonai Ruins Beneath Hyrule Castle. When she is transported through time to the distant past during the "The Awakening" Memory, the Purah Pad is brought with her. In the Era of Myth, Mineru studies the Purah Pad in an effort to adapt its Warping capability to the new setting. Due to its prominence in the "Mineru's Counsel" Memory, the Purah Pad is depicted by the Geoglyph at Trilby Valley. After the Imprisoning War, Mineru uses her powers as the Sage of Spirit to implant her soul into the Purah Pad. Zelda then entrusts the Purah Pad to a Steward Construct, to be given to Link in the future. Following his encounter with Ganondorf, Link awakens on the Great Sky Island. Upon reaching the Garden of Time, he speaks to the Steward Construct and receives the Purah Pad. Basic Functions The Purah Pad possesses features similar to that of the Sheikah Slate from . In addition to a modified version of the Map, Scope, Camera, and Hyrule Compendium, it also contains a Character Profiles section, which details important people in Link's journey, although this feature is unavailable until he encounters a character with an entry after completing the Great Sky Island. The Adventure Log is accessed via the Purah Pad as well. It can be used to Warp to activated Travel Points, after Link attempts to open the door at the back of the Temple of Time for the first time. The Purah Pad is also used on Terminals to activate Skyview Towers. It is then used after the first launch from each Skyview Tower to scan the surrounding terrain to create the Surface and Sky Maps. The Purah Pad is also used in various Side Quests across Hyrule. Many of them require Link to bring someone an picture of a specific subject, such as a Sinkhole, a lake at a certain time, or a view from a particular location. Map The Purah Pad's Map is comprised of three layers, the Sky, the Surface, and the Depths. The displayed layer can be switched with the Up and Down buttons on the D-Pad. The Sky

as a Sinkhole, a lake at a certain time, or a view from a particular location. Map The Purah Pad's Map is comprised of three layers, the Sky, the Surface, and the Depths. The displayed layer can be switched with the Up and Down buttons on the D-Pad. The Sky layer is unlocked by default, and the Surface and Depths layers are unlocked once Link reaches them for the first time. At the start of Link's adventure, only the Great Sky Island is fully mapped on the Purah Pad. Additional regions can be unlocked for the Surface and Sky layers by using Skyview Towers, while the Depths are mapped by activating Lightroots. The Map allows Link to place up to 6 Pins and up to 300 Stamps to mark any location. The Map and Mini-Map display Link's Map Coordinates, aiding in navigation. Additionally, the Map will show the current Temperature of the environment, or "ERROR" within a scorching environment. Certain icons on the map, such as the Pins or Link's current position, will still be visible when a different layer is shown, but take on an inverted or hollow appearance. When Link Warps or uses Ascend to leave the Depths, a flag-shaped marker is placed at his last location on the Depths Map. Repairs and Upgrades When Link initially obtains the Purah Pad, the Camera and Hyrule Compendium are unavailable. In order to restore both functions, Link must assist Robbie and Josha through the "Camera Work in the Depths" Main Quest. During this quest, Robbie is shocked to learn that Link hasn't made use of the Camera yet. When Link later speaks to Robbie next to Iayusus Lightroot, he will ask to see the Purah Pad for a moment, and upon closer investigation, Robbie realizes that the Camera and Hyrule Compendium are locked. He unlocks both features for Link, and directs him to use the Camera to take a picture of the nearby Statue That Points the Way. After the pair returns to Lookout Landing, Link shows Josha the picture in the Purah Pad's Album, completing "Camera Work in the Depths". Following this, Robbie will inform Link that he has some additional plans for improvements to the Purah Pad, and that as soon as he is finished assisting Josha with her study of the Depths, he plans to head back to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab so he can continue his own research. After the completion of "A Mystery in the Depths" and the start of the "Hateno Village Research Lab" Side Adventure, Robbie returns to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. There, Link can speak with him to receive the Sensor and use it to locate Mayahisik Shrine nearby. After Link has discovered the Shrine of Light and reported back to Robbie, "Hateno Village Research Lab" will be completed. Link has discovered the Shrine of Light and reported back to Robbie, "Hateno Village Research Lab" will be completed. Robbie then tells Link that he has more features planned for the Purah Pad, but that he needs more data to perfect them first. By speaking to Robbie after this, Link can begin the Side Adventures, "Presenting: The Travel Medallion!", "Presenting: Hero's Path Mode!", and "Presenting: Sensor +!". During these, Link must obtain certain data for Robbie, such as the locations of Shrines of Light. is a character in . Biography Purpen is Hylian who is part of Hoz's Monster-Control Crew squad. He wields a Soldier's Shield and a Boko Reaper, which consists of a Bokoblin Horn and a Tree Branch. He has searched all over Hyrule for an Intact Weapon that has not decayed as a result of the Upheaval, but he has yet to find one. During the search for Zelda and Link at Hyrule Castle, Purpen can be found within the First Gatehouse, where he examines a Soldier's Broadsword and a Soldier's Spear. He is disappointed that both of them are decayed, and he wonders whether any Intact Weapons remain in Hyrule. If Link asks about the Weapons, Purpen explains their weakened state, and he suspects that there may not be any Intact Weapons left in Hyrule. At the end of their conversation, he comments that decayed Weapons can be strengthened. Following the appearance of a figure resembling Zelda, Purpen notices there was a commotion above him and wonders if they could have found an Intact Weapon, though he does not think it is likely. As part of squad one he uses a Soldier's Shield and a Wooden Stick with an attached Bokoblin Horn during an attack on a Monster Stronghold south of the Hyrule Garrison Ruins. If Link talks to him during the fight, he shows great admiration for captain Hoz's Horse.

is a recurring character in . Biography Pyle is a Goron who lives in Goron City. Pyle stands near the western entrance of the City and directs travelers to the Armor shop Ripped and Shredded, which sells the fireproof Fireproof Armor. Pyle explains that ever since the Divine Beast Vah Rudania appeared, the climate has grown hotter and the shop has started selling the Fireproof Armor in response. He adds that he used to be a miner at Death Mountain, but was laid off when Vah Rudania's emergence forced the mining company to move and to cut down its employees. After Vah Rudania is freed from Calamity Ganon's control, Pyle jokingly makes fun of it and wants to start mining again at Death Mountain Summit. Link can also ask Pyle general questions about the area. He can be asked for directions to Bludo, the Goron boss of the City. Pyle runs the Rollin' Inn now that the former innkeeper, Tray, is retiring. He is still adjusting to the change from working at a clothing store to working at an Inn.

is a recurring character in . Biography Pyra is a Gerudo who can be found in Gerudo Town's bar, The Noble Canteen. If Link goes into the Canteen, he will find Pyra accompanied by two other Gerudo named Sumati and Yaido. If Link speaks to one of them, they talk to each other about a password for a secret place. They stop talking about it as soon as they notice that Link is listening and Sumati tells him to go away. Link can eavesdrop on them by going onto the opposite side of the nearby window in Rotana's house. If Link eavesdrops on them here before ever speaking to them while in The Noble Canteen, he will hear Yaido asking the others if they have heard of a rumor about Fashion Passion. Sumati replies that she has heard the rumor and Yaido responds by saying that she had asked Saula about it, but Saula wouldn't tell her anything. Pyra then mentions how suspicious it is that Saula will not give away any information. Once Link is eavesdropping on the Gerudo women after speaking to them directly, he will overhear Sumati referring to him as a little Hylian girl. Pyra says to forget about the girl and urges Yaido to tell them the password. Yaido reveals that she overheard Saula say the password is "GSC♦." Sumati quickly realizes that it must stand for "Gerudo Secret Club" before the conversation ends. The password they reveal allows Link entry to the Gerudo Secret Club. After Link calms Naboris, gains entry to the Gerudo Secret Club, and speaks to the Gerudo women again, Yaido will question where Perda is. Sumati says that she left in search of Lover's Pond and Pyra comments that it is rumored to be the perfect place to find true love. Yaido then proceeds to say something, but is interrupted when Sumati tells Link to go away. Link can eavesdrop on them again from the window in Rotana's house to hear them talk about Perda in more detail. While listening, Yaido wonders how Perda is doing and Sumati comments about how enthusiastic she was to find Lover's Pond. Yaido then talks about how quickly she left when she heard that Lover's Pond is in Faron. This surprises Pyra, who thought it was only a rumor. Sumati says that she does not know for sure, but Pyra and she conclude that Perda must have found true love because she has not returned yet. At the end of the conversation, Yaido contemplates if she should also travel to Lover's Pond.

Qia is a recurring character in . Biography Qia, the Sage of Water, was one of the Six Sages who fought alongside the first King of Hyrule, Rauru, during the Imprisoning War. She was a leader of the Zora, and she attained her status as a Sage after receiving a Secret Stone from Rauru. During the Memory "The Sages' Vow", Qia reports to Rauru that the last free village in the Gerudo Desert has fallen to Demon King Ganondorf. Within the Forgotten Temple, Rauru grants the remaining four Secret Stones to Qia, Agraston, Raphica, and Ardi, hoping to strengthen them before their battle with the Demon King. Her Secret Stone turns into a Secret Stone of Water, and she becomes the Sage of Water. Following this, the Six Sages swear a vow of loyalty to Rauru. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Qia in a flashback to the Imprisoning War. She is wielding a Lightscale Trident, and her Secret Stone is located on the back of her hand.|Qia during the Imprisoning War In flashbacks to the Imprisoning War, Qia can be seen wielding a Lightscale Trident. She appears wounded by Gloom during the Memory "The Imprisoning War". In attempt to distract Demon King Ganondorf, she throws her Trident at him, which Zelda sends backwards using Recall. Following this, Qia witnesses Rauru sacrifice himself to seal the Demon King. After the Imprisoning War, Zelda visited Qia at the Water Temple. Zelda informed her that Demon King Ganondorf would break from his seal one day, and she asked the Sage to ensure the Zora will help Link face him in the future. Qia swore that her successor would awaken when the Demon King returns and fight alongside Link. Later, in the Memory "Tears of the Dragon", Qia and the other three remaining Sages watch as the Light Dragon flies off into the Sky. thumb|right|320px|Qia appearing to Link and Sidon During the Main Quest "Sidon of the Zora", Link and Sidon repeatedly hear Qia's voice beckoning them to the Water Temple on Wellspring Island. When they reach the Temple, the Sage instructs them to fill the Water Vessels by spinning the four Water Wheels, which will allow them to wash away a large pile of Sludge. Once Mucktorok has been defeated, the Sludge covering the Secret Stone in the Water Temple will disappear. When Sidon touches the Stone, the two will be engulfed in Light, and Qia appears before them. She identifies herself as Sidon's ancestor, and she expresses pride in his Power of Water. The Sage reveals that Mucktorok was sent by Demon King Ganondorf to prevent Sidon from finding her Secret Stone. She then proceeds to tell Link and Sidon about the Imprisoning War and her promise to Zelda. After finishing her story, Qia reveals that, although Zora's Domain has been saved, the entirety of Hyrule is still threatened by Demon King Ganondorf. Therefore, she asks Sidon to fulfill her promise and help Link as the new Sage of Water. Other Appearances Qia

War and her promise to Zelda. After finishing her story, Qia reveals that, although Zora's Domain has been saved, the entirety of Hyrule is still threatened by Demon King Ganondorf. Therefore, she asks Sidon to fulfill her promise and help Link as the new Sage of Water. Other Appearances Qia is the princess of the Zora. After the Forbidden Construct awakens and kills her father, she reluctantly inherits the throne. She is considered to be a skilled Warrior, which serves as an inspiration to her people. She is recruited as part of the Scenario "Lanayru Defiled".

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Quarry Ruins are located in Hyrule Field, southwest of Hyrule and West Castle Town. The Quarry Ruins are a rocky terrain with very few Trees that were used to supply stones for Hyrule Kingdom prior to the second Great Calamity. The Katah Chuki Shrine sits in a nook along the southeastern side of the Ruins, beside the wall bordering West Castle Town. A Rare Ore Deposit can be found under a pile of bombable rocks in a crevice just before the peak of the hill in the north. There is also a ruined village to the southwest, along the path.
