is a Boss in . Characteristics Queen Gibdo is a massive, grotesque Gibdo who caused their infestation of the Gerudo Desert. Her wings are powerful enough to allow her to fly despite her large size. Unlike the Gibdos that she commands, she possesses eight limbs, typically using the first two pairs as arms while walking on the other four. One Queen Gibdo is responsible for the Sand Shroud affecting the Gerudo Region. After this Queen Gibdo is defeated in the Lightning Temple, three Queen Gibdos can be found in Boss Rematches throughout the Depths. One is located northwest of the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm in the Gerudo Highlands Depths, one is near the Korakut Lightroot in the Lanayru Wetlands Depths, and the final one is east of the Kawakarut Lightroot in the Gerudo Highlands Depths. If Queen Gibdo is not defeated in the Lightning Temple, Link fights her in Gloom's Origin during the War in the Depths of Hyrule. She appears after Mucktorok and before the Seized Construct. When defeated in the Depths, Queen Gibdos drop Queen Gibdo Wings. Defeating them unlocks a Treasure Chest containing a Huge Crystallized Charge. Queen Gibdo is fought twice, once outside the Lightning Temple and a second time within it. During the first battle, she will retreat when she has lost a quarter of her health. Queen Gibdo rapidly scuttles around the battlefield, trying to charge at Link or spit a stream of sand at him. Her attacks can be predicted by watching for her antennae to change color. She cannot be harmed unless Link uses Riju's Power of Lightning to hit her with a lightning strike, which will make her turn pale and become vulnerable in the same manner as other Gibdos. Doing so will also cause her to alter her attack patterns; she will generate sand tornadoes to attack at long range and conjure sandstorms to hamper Link's vision until she can recover. She will try to keep her distance from Link as best as she can despite her reduced speed in this state, but a second lightning strike will stun her and allow Link to attack with impunity until she recovers. At half health, Queen Gibdo activates four Gibdo Hives in the corners of the battlefield. These will generate an endless swarm of Gibdos and Moth Gibdos to assist Queen Gibdo as long as they remain intact, potentially causing Link to be overwhelmed by their sheer numbers. However, destroying the Hives will allow light to shine onto the battlefield, which will damage and eventually kill Gibdos that are exposed to it. Queen Gibdo herself will also generate more sand tornadoes while in her vulnerable state and will start flying around the battlefield in order to avoid Riju's lightning; while flying, she will also attack with an aerial sand stream that will try to track Link's movements.

The is a title belonging to multiple characters in . The Queen of Hyrule goes unnamed in and . Biography The Queen of Hyrule ruled over Hyrule Kingdom alongside her husband, King Rhoam. Together, they had a daughter, who they named Zelda in accordance with the naming traditions of the Royal Family of Hyrule. She was said to be naturally drawn to her sacred powers, which she described as overflowing. She also had a great affection for Horses. During her life, the Queen of Hyrule was a good friend to Urbosa, the chief of the Gerudo. After Zelda was born, the Queen brought her to Gerudo Town so she could meet Urbosa. Though Urbosa said that Zelda would grow up to be a beautiful queen like her mother, the Queen instead wished that she would find happiness in her life. Later on, Zelda would remember that the Queen often visited the Gerudo Desert despite her poor health. As she grew up, Zelda had a warm and loving relationship with the Queen of Hyrule. She told Zelda about her sealing power, which she claimed would one day develop within her. She also encouraged her daughter, saying that she could do anything and that all would end well. The Queen affectionately referred to her daughter as her "little bird." In her Voice Memories, Zelda recalls many memories of her mother. According to Zelda, she and her parents used to spend time together at the Hyrule Castle Gazebo. Once, the Queen and Zelda visited Hyrule Castle Town's Central Square, where the Queen bought her daughter a flower crown. She also brought Zelda to watch her pray at the Hyrule Cathedral. During a trip to Hopper Pond on the Great Plateau, a young Zelda excitedly showed her mother a Hot-Footed Frog she had seen, though the Queen hid her disgust to protect Zelda's feelings. The Queen was in possession of a coat made at the Brazen Beak, which eventually became part of Zelda's Winter Clothes. 10 years before the second Great Calamity, the Queen of Hyrule suddenly and unexpectedly passed away. She was unable to teach Zelda about her sacred powers before her untimely demise, since her training was meant to start the next year. Her death meant that King Rhoam was left alone to prepare Zelda for the resurrection of Calamity Ganon. Before the Calamity, Zelda would note that the Queen's Throne in the Sanctum had not been touched since her passing. In her Voice Memories, Zelda refers to another Queen of Hyrule, the founding Queen Sonia, on several occasions. She claims that the Hyrule Forest Park was founded when Sonia and her husband Rauru planted a Tree together. She also shares a theory that Rauru Settlement's name comes from it being Sonia's birthplace. Lastly, Zelda reveals that the sacred power passed down within the Royal Family can be traced back to Sonia. thumb|left|250px|alt= Sonia and Zelda at Lake Kolomo.|Sonia counseling Zelda Sonia is the first Queen of Hyrule, with she and her

theory that Rauru Settlement's name comes from it being Sonia's birthplace. Lastly, Zelda reveals that the sacred power passed down within the Royal Family can be traced back to Sonia. thumb|left|250px|alt= Sonia and Zelda at Lake Kolomo.|Sonia counseling Zelda Sonia is the first Queen of Hyrule, with she and her husband Rauru using the power of their Secret Stones to found Hyrule Kingdom. They are distant ancestors to Zelda, who they meet after she accidentally travels through Time to the Era of Foundation with a Secret Stone of her own. As a result, Sonia invites Zelda to stay with them at the Ancient Hyrule Castle while they look for a way for Zelda to return home. She becomes a mentor to Zelda in regards to her Time powers. Together, Sonia and Rauru would use their powers to create Shrines of Light, which sealed Monsters away from Hyrule. In the Memory "A Show of Fealty", Sonia and Rauru accept a vow of fealty from Ganondorf and welcome the Gerudo as part of their kingdom. However, Sonia is eventually ambushed and killed by Ganondorf outside of Ancient Hyrule Castle during "Sonia Is Caught by Treachery". He steals her Secret Stone and uses its power to become a Demon King. Sonia's grave can be found in the room behind the Mother Goddess Statue in the Forgotten Temple. After Link defeats the Demon Dragon, the Spirits of Sonia and Rauru appear, channeling their powers of Time and Light through him to restore Zelda from her Light Dragon form. Within her Voice Memories, Zelda often mentions her mother, the late Queen of Hyrule. When she was a newborn, the Queen and King Rhoam brought her to visit the Great Deku Tree in Korok Forest. A Cherry-Blossom bud bloomed on her forehead, and the Queen had a mixed reaction upon learning her daughter inherited her sacred powers. Zelda also recalls a time when her mother taught her how to make Garlands, during which she ended up crying in frustration. When she sees how Riju stepped up to lead the Gerudo after her own mother's untimely passing, Zelda is reminded of her devastation when the Queen died. Upon parting with the Golden Horse, Zelda recited a prayer for its Mane that she learned from her mother. Finally, Zelda promises both of her parents that she will restore Hyrule, and she asks Urbosa to pass along a message to her mother that she will be fine. Other Appearances The Queen of Hyrule from is mentioned in the "Urbosa, the Gerudo Chief" Narration as the reason Urbosa and Zelda already know each other. In the Movie "Determination, Zelda shows an ancient relic to King Rhoam, claiming that she found it while exploring with the Queen of Hyrule and that the two discussed its properties with one another. The Queen also makes a brief appearance in a flashback during the "Lullaby" Movie, which plays during "The Future of Hyrule" Scenario. After repairing Terrako, a young Zelda hurries to show the

it while exploring with the Queen of Hyrule and that the two discussed its properties with one another. The Queen also makes a brief appearance in a flashback during the "Lullaby" Movie, which plays during "The Future of Hyrule" Scenario. After repairing Terrako, a young Zelda hurries to show the Queen, but the memory ends before her face can be seen. Her dress appears similar to Zelda's Royal Attire. During the "EX The Princess and the King" Scenario, which is exclusive to the Downloadable Content pack, King Rhoam recalls his treatment of Zelda after her mother's passing, fearing what the Queen would think of him. During the Movie "The Aftermath of Survival", which plays after the Scenario has been completed, Urbosa claims that Zelda may be stronger than the Queen was. Sonia appears as the founding Queen of Hyrule in .

The Queen of the Zora, also known as the Zora Queen or the Queen of the Zoras, is a recurring title in . Biography The Queen of the Zora does not appear in , though she is mentioned in the History of the Zora, Part Four. She is the wife of King Dorephan and the mother of Mipha and Sidon. The History of the Zora, Part Three tells the story of a past Queen of the Zora. When a Lizalfos horde approached Zora's Domain from the Zodobon Highlands, the Queen feared for the safety of her husband, the King. To protect him, she wove one of her white scales into the armor she prepared for him. A ray of sunlight that reflected off the scale was able to blind the Lizalfos general, allowing the King to rally his forces and claim victory. This started the tradition of Zora princesses creating Zora Armor for their husbands-to-be. At the end of the Main Quest "Sidon of the Zora", Yona becomes the Queen of the Zora after marrying Sidon, who has inherited the title of King from his father. As the new leaders of the Zora, Yona and Sidon ask their people to assist Link as he continues the Search for Princess Zelda. Other Appearances Following the death of her father, the King, Qia succeeds him and becomes the Queen of the Zora.

are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Throughout , Link can obtain three types of Quests by exploring and interacting with characters. These are Main Quests, Side Quests, and Shrine Quests. Progress on all three types of Quests is tracked through the Adventure Log. Main Quests, Side Quests, and Shrine Quests all return in . Alongside these, a new type of Quest known as Side Adventures can be found as well. There are also Additional Adventures, which are multi-step Quests that are not tracked in the Adventure Log. In , Quests come in two varieties: Main Quests and Side Quests. Main Quests follow Zelda and Tri's efforts to fix Rifts across Hyrule, and Side Quests can appear based on Main Quest completion. Side Quests are shorter experiences that reward Zelda with various Items, such as Ingredients or Accessories. Both types of Quests can be tracked in the Adventure Log. Other Appearances In , Quests serve as the way to increase the effectiveness of a Warrior, replacing the Bazaar's Badge Market found in the original games. By using Materials, Link and the other Warriors will gain attributes such has extensions of their Light Combo, a new Strong Combo, Hearts, and more Special Attack bars. In addition, some Quests grant pieces of Attire for Link to wear. To unlock more Quests, Warriors must progress through the Story, complete certain Challenges, or finish other Quests. There are 376 Quests in total in the base game. Quests are split by the following within the Quest tab: Character-specific Quests, which benefit only one Warrior. These Quests are marked with the heads of the characters as depicted by the narration cutscenes, and are all found under their Warrior's name under the Quest search tab (e.g., all the Side Quests that benefit solely Link will be found under the tab "Link", and so on & so forth). Improve All Allies Quests, which as the name implies, benefits all Warriors. These Quests are marked with a heart icon. Sheikah Runes Quests, which lowers the cooldown of used Sheikah Rune abilities. They are individually marked with their specified rune (e.g. the Quest "Explosive Endeavours" is marked with the Remote Bomb logo). Divine Beasts Quests, which improve the vitality and functions of the Divine Beasts. They are individually marked with the specified Divine Beast. Unlock Services Quests, which open up Shops and Stables to shop for certain Materials if the need arises, as well as other vital specialized services. Shops have a Jar marker, and Stables have a horse head marker. The specialized services are: the Hylian Blacksmith Guild, marked with a hammer, helps Warriors by tinkering with weapons to make them stronger. the Military Training Camp, marked with a helmet, help lagging behind Warriors catch up with the currently highest leveled Warrior. and the Kochi Dye Shop, marked with a vial, changes the color of Link's clothes, with the Rupees depending on the dye. Improve Services Quests, which gives Link and co. discounts, as well as more services with

helmet, help lagging behind Warriors catch up with the currently highest leveled Warrior. and the Kochi Dye Shop, marked with a vial, changes the color of Link's clothes, with the Rupees depending on the dye. Improve Services Quests, which gives Link and co. discounts, as well as more services with the Blacksmith Guild, and additional dye options for the Dye Shop. These are marked with a building & an up arrow. Material Quests, giving Link more Materials, as well as monster-themed hats. They are marked with either monster icons or leaf icons. The latter can be completed multiple times as long as the player has the materials needed to make the trade Cooking Quests, allowing Link to come up with new recipes to use foodstuff Materials to make Food, giving bonus effects to Warriors in battle such as increased movement speed, a bigger window to initiate a Perfect Dodge, elemental damage reduction, etc. They are marked with a Cooking Pot. Battle Support Quests, which increase the carrying capacities of Apples and Weapons, as well as allowing Korok Seeds and Treasure Chests to be viewed in the Battle Info tab. Aside for "The Treasure Detector" which is marked with a treasure chest icon, all Battle Support Quests have their marker be Hestu's Maracas. Sheikah Sensor Quests, which help Link and co. use the Sensor to help find specific Materials in either combat missions or Shops/Stables if they are too few for a specific Quest. Like the Runes Quests, these quests are marked with the Sensor icon. And finally, Contribution Level Quests, which are region-specific quests that keep track of the completion rate of the Quests of that region of Hyrule, and are thus completed when all Quests in a specific region are completed. They are marked with a star icon. With the Downloadable Content pack, 54 additional Quests have been added to . 35 of these Quests can be found within the new facility, EX Royal Ancient Lab, marked on the map with a Ancient Screw with an "EX" next to it. These Quests are largely meant to help the lab grow and prosper. The Lab's Quests are arranged in a grid and operates similarly to how the Badge system from the original worked; completing one Quest can unlock the others that connect to it as long as the player has the Materials or the Rupees for it. The Quest icons also retain the previously established rules with what they entail. Quests from the EX Royal Ancient Lab grant access to new rewards added in , as well as the newly added Materials needed to complete them. Additionally completing them grants access to the Flail for Link, the Battle-Tested Guardian, and the Master Cycle Zero for Zelda.

, also known as , is a recurring trap in . Quicksand goes unnamed in . Characteristics Quicksand appears inside the Arbiter's Grounds. If Link steps into Quicksand, it will slowly pull him down and greatly slow his walking speed. If Link is pulled all the way down by it, he will lose one Heart of health and be taken back to the entrance of the room from where he came. Sinksand can be found in various places throughout Lanayru Province. As the name suggests, Link will sink into the sand unless he travels through it quickly. Link will spawn near the outside of the Sinksand after sinking. Some areas of Sinksand may be shallow with a hidden path underneath, allowing Link to cross safely. In the area where the Lanayru Mining Facility is located, Link can see shallow paths of Sinksand on his Map. To pass Sinksand quickly, Link can Dash across it to avoid sinking in it until his Stamina runs out. Stamina Potions can be useful for this, allowing Link to temporarily Dash across large stretches of Sinksand without his Stamina running out. Even with Stamina Potions, Link can never roll in Sinksand. Sinksand is often inhabited by Electro Spumes, an electrified type of Spume. They will shoot balls of electricity at Link as he tries to cross. Another enemy Link can encounter in Sinksand is the Ampilus. They have shells that allow them to traverse Sinksand without sinking. Link can take advantage of this characteristic by using the shells as platforms over the Sinksand after defeating them. Like Electro Spumes, they will attack Link by rolling toward him while he attempts to cross. Several Quicksand pits appear in the East Barrens.

is a recurring character in . Biography Quince is a hunter who can be found with Satty, his pet, at the Wetland Stable. He is usually staring at the eastern clouds. When first talked to, he becomes angry as Link is a man, saying that there are no women in the stable. If Link apologizes, Quince says that he does not want to hear it, saying that guys, along with the Zora prince, are the stable's only visitors. Link can ask about the Zora, and Quince will describe them to him and where they live. He also says that they wanted him to go to Zora's Domain because they needed a Hylian, although he is reluctant since he does not want to leave Satty behind. When told that he seems grumpy, he admits that he is disappointed that there are not many women at the stable, telling Link the clouds sour his mood as well. If Link tells him that he seems grumpy, Quince tells him to look to the clouds in the east, saying that rain sours his mood and that Satty cheers him up. Finally, if Link asks him about the stable, Quince once more says that it is filthy and only filled with men. He also talks about Sidon's previous visit to the stable, and says that he is only at the stable because of Satty. At this point, Link can ask about the Zora again, and Quince will give the same response as he does in other situations. At any time that Quince talks about Satty, Link can ask about him, and then he will tell Link about how they met if the hero chooses to listen. He will then proceed to tell him his story about finding the Lord of the Mountain when he went hunting, meeting Satty along the way who eventually protected him from the creature. Afterwards, he will inform link of the location of Satori Mountain, the place he had the encounter. He will also propose that Link find the Lord of the Mountain. If it is raining, Quince will stay or go inside, and wonder where the sun or any girls are when talked to. If Quince is talked to for the second time in a day, he will start by asking Link if he is only here to disappoint him again. Additionally, if Link disguises as a girl, Quince will try to flirt with him before realizing he is a man and saying that his clothes will not fool him. He sighs, and says that he should have known he would not meet any women at the stable. At 12:00 AM, Quince walks to bed, saying that he is hungry when talked to. When asleep, from 1:00 to 5:00 AM, he dreams about the Lord of the Mountain returning and telling Satty to run.

are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Location and Uses Races are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. They appear with a starting platform in the form of a Tree Stump with a leaf symbol in the center. If Link stands on the Stump, a yellow light shoots out of the stump, creating a ring of light somewhere within view, consisting of several small orbs that shrink in sequential order. A timer begins and challenges Link to get through the ring before it disappears. Link can reset the timer at any time before successful completion by standing on the Stump. If he makes it in the ring, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Races always challenge Link in ways involving Sprinting, Climbing, Gliding with the Paraglider, Shield Surfing, or Swimming. Races return in , and they can be operated in the same manner as in . In addition, two new Korok Seed Puzzles based on Races have appeared, all of which are started by standing on a Tree Stump. The first is Straight to the Target, during which Link must reach the Race's goal without touching the ground. The second is the Skydiving Challenge, wherein Link must Skydive to catch a glowing ball before it reaches the Surface. Two other new Korok Seed Puzzles, Ascend Challenges and Downclimbing, also utilize Tree Stumps. When any of these Korok Seed Puzzles are solved, a Korok will appear to give Link a Korok Seed.

The , also known as the , is a recurring Armor Set in . The Radiant Attire goes unnamed in . Location and Uses The Radiant Set is an Armor Set consisting of the Radiant Mask, Radiant Shirt, and Radiant Tights. All three pieces can be bought at the Gerudo Secret Club in Gerudo Town for 2400 Rupees and 9 Luminous Stones in total after "The Secret Club's Secret" Side Quest has been completed. Painted using Hateno Dye made from crushed Luminous Stones, the Radiant Set's skeletal markings glow when worn at night. The Radiant Set can be enhanced by a Great Fairy and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. If all three pieces of the set have been upgraded twice at a Great Fairy Fountain, wearing the set grants a "Disguise" Set Bonus against Stalkoblins, Stalmoblins, and Stalizalfos. The upgraded set also provides a "Bone Atk. Up" bonus, increasing attack power when wielding Weapons made of bone. Dye Options Enhancing Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances All three pieces of the Radiant Attire are acquired upon completing the "Deep Woods, Deep Shadow" Quest. Dye Options

are recurring Items in . Fashioned using Hateno Dye made from Luminous Stones, the Radiant Mask's skeletal markings glow when worn at night. The Radiant Mask can be enhanced by a Great Fairy and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Radiant Mask, alongside the Radiant Shirt and Radiant Tights, compose the Radiant Set. are recurring Items in . Radiant Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Radiant Shields are mid-grade Shields made by the Gerudo. They are presented to Gerudo Soldiers once they achieve the rank of captain, and they are considered to be a direct upgrade to Gerudo Shields. This is seen with Teake, the captain of the Gerudo guard, who carries one on her back. In addition, they are also known for their incredible Shield Surfing abilities. Their opulence is rivaled only by their capabilities in combat. They belong to the Gerudo Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created and utilized by the Gerudo. There are four Radiant Shields scattered throughout Hyrule, with a fifth added in Master Mode. One can be found inside the secret cave in the mountain east of the Sho Dantu Shrine, along with other pieces of Gerudo Gear. When scanned with the amiibo Rune, the following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Radiant Shield: Series Zelda amiibo Series Urbosa amiibo Selmie will comment on Radiant Shields if Link speaks to her with one equipped. She reveals that they are very rare, and she practically never sees them anymore. Unlike other shields, the Radiant Shield can Shield Surf on stone. Due to their metal compositions, Radiant Shields will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms. They also sink if they are dropped in Water. However, they can be manipulated with the Magnesis Rune, and they will not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Radiant Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Radiant Shields can be wielded by Urbosa in conjunction with Moonlight Scimitars.

is a character in . Biography Raha is a Korok who can be found near the entrance to Korok Grove during the Main Quest "Trail of the Master Sword". They left Korok Forest to go on a walk with Tasho, Mopu, Nako, Mokka, Jatora, and Maheli, although they found that they were unable to pass through the Lost Woods when they attempted to return. Following this, the group entered the Depths through the Minshi Woods Chasm, believing they could find a way back to Korok Forest. When Link speaks to Raha, they state that they plan on catching up with Jatora and Maheli, who went on ahead of them. They then explain that by continuing forward, Link will find himself directly below Korok Forest, and they hope there will be a way to reach it from there.

is recurring weather event in . Rain can often occur naturally, or it can be summoned with Items. Overview In , playing the "Song of Storms" on the Ocarina of Time will summon rain and trigger certain events, such as filling the Desert Colossus oasis. Rain and wind will appear even if the Song is played indoors. In , playing the "Song of Storms" on the Ocarina of Time will summon rain and trigger certain events. Rain and wind will appear even if the song is played indoors. Clock Town, the Swamp Fishing Hole and the Ocean Fishing Hole will experience rain on the Second Day from 7AM to 12AM. Rain will cause the Termina Loach to swim near the water's surface and the Goodta Goby to swim deeper underwater, making them easier to catch with standard lure and sinking lure respectively. In , after Zant injures Midna and Link must carry her to Princess Zelda, it is raining on the way to Hyrule Castle. Additionally, upon entering Hyrule Castle to battle Ganondorf, it is raining in the courtyard. Rain has no effect on Link. In , Rain will randomly occur in warmer Regions, and it makes surfaces become slick. This makes them difficult to Climb, as Link will periodically slip and fall. Rain will immediately extinguish any exposed Fires, with the exception of Blue Flames. Fires that are sheltered from the Rain are not affected. Empty shelters can be found alongside roads, and Link can create temporary shelters on Waterfalls using the Cryonis Rune, as Rain will not penetrate the blocks it creates. Zora's Domain and the surrounding region will permanently experience rain until Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been purged of Waterblight Ganon. Rain occurs during Thunderstorms. Rain is summoned by the croaking of Drippitunes, which are common in the Faron Wetlands. Other Appearances

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Rakakudaj Shrine is situated in the center of the Gerudo Canyon. It corresponds with the Jadukakar Lightroot in the Depths. Initially, the Shrine of Light has no entrance, although its Travel Point can be activated. As part of "The Gerudo Canyon Crystal" Shrine Quest, Link must bring a Mysterious Crystal up the Canyon's river to the Travel Point. Once he does so, it will grow in size and become the Shrine's entrance. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Rakakudaj Shrine The Rakakudaj Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Rakakudaj Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

The , designated by the trial name A Reflective Device, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Rakashog Shrine is located on the East Gerudo Sky Archipelago in the Gerudo Highlands Sky. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of the Shrine The entrance chamber of Rakashog Shrine is composed of a catwalk with two stairs to its sides. Ahead of the platform, there is a Mirror beneath a Light-sensitive Switch. A Light Beam projects onto the catwalk perpendicular to the Light-sensitive Switch. By redirecting the Light Beam with the Mirror onto the Switch, Link can activate the Switch and open a portcullis to enter the next room. The second room of the Shrine features a cell with a portcullis and a second Mirror. An opening in the left of the cell allows Link to pass a Mirror through it. Inside the cell, there is a second Light Beam pointing directly toward the center of the cell's floor and another Light-sensitive Switch along the right-hand wall of the cell. When the Switch is activated, the portcullis will lift and allow Link to enter the third room of the Shrine. The third room is divided into two levels. On the lower level, there sits a lone Mirror and a depression in the floor along the far wall with two ramps leading down to it. At the base of this depression, there is an upward-facing Light-sensitive Switch. When activated, the Switch will cause the portion of the floor it sits on to rise up toward the second level before looping back down to create an elevator platform. The second level contains another Mirror beside a Stone Box and the hallway leading to the fourth room. Along the far-side wall there is a small chamber with a Treasure Chest that is blocked by a portcullis controlled by a Light-sensitive Switch above it. This Switch can be activated by carrying a Light Beam from the fourth room to it. The fourth room consists of another ceiling-mounted Light Beam protected by Soldier Constructs. A divider separates the room into two halves. In front of the divider, there are two Mirrors, and a set of stairs can be found behind it. Along the wall behind the divider, there is a final Light-sensitive Switch holding a portcullis to the end of the Shrine. By chaining Mirrors, Link can carry the Light Beam to the Switch and reach the end of the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Rakashog Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Enemies Zonai Devices Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Ralera spends her daytimes sitting on a stool at the base of a tree, where she can watch over the windmills she and her husband, Rhodes, own. She has recently moved to Hateno Village from her hometown, Lurelin Village. Ralera is a newlywed who adores her husband and is more than willing to aid him in his work. While she enjoys the air of Hateno, she does mention that it is unlike the breeze she grew up with. Ralera is a carefree woman who enjoys chatting with passersby and will happily talk about things with Link. He can ask her about Lurelin Village and she will describe it for him as a fishing community past the Bridge of Hylia, which she herself had to cross with her husband. She takes a moment to reflect on how her father is doing, as she has not returned to the village after being married. Should Link ask what she is doing, Ralera explains how she watches the windmills for Rhodes's work during the day. She enjoys doing so, as she finds sitting there peaceful, and so is quite relaxed about the work. Sitting beside her is a Blue Flame Pedestal, which Link can point out. Ralera can tell him that the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab director lights these lanterns with a Blue Flame, but admits that she does not know much more than that. However, she does wonder if the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab still has a director at all, as she has not seen them. She encourages Link to visit the lab himself. At 9 o'clock in the evening, her shift at the windmills is over and she heads for home to get some sleep. While she rests, she sleep-talks about how Rhodes is currently watching over the windmills in her place, before waking up again at 5:00 in the morning to do her job. If Link talks to her while she walks to her stool, she tells him that she is going to work and that she can explain more once she sits down. According to her husband, Ralera was the one to suggest they go in shifts.

, also known as the Underground Cave of Ralis Pond, is a location in . Features and Overview Ralis Channel is located beneath Ralis Pond in the Lanayru Great Spring. It is a Cave that consists of Wet Walls and a channel of Water flowing southward. There are two entrances to Ralis Channel: a vertical entrance on the east side of Ralis Pond and a Cave entrance below the ledge south of the Pond. There are several spots inside the Channel where Link can form a boat from Objects, Zonai Devices, and Materials. Along the western wall of Ralis Channel, there are two Ore Deposits. Further north along this wall, there is a blocked chamber that can be cut open to reveal two Rare Ore Deposits and a Luminous Stone Deposit. The Joniu Shrine sits at the far end of the Channel. In order to gain access to the Shrine, Link must complete the Shrine Quest "The Ralis Channel Crystal" by bringing the Mysterious Crystal located near the Cave's southern entrance to the Shrine of Light at its back. Another Ore Deposit sits to the east of the Shrine. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Zonai Devices Treasure Chests

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Ralis Pond is located in the Lanayru Great Spring just to the south of Upland Zorana. The Water inside the Pond is not deep enough for Link to Swim in it, meaning he has to wade through it. In addition to this, Ralis Pond is surrounded by several Cedar Trees. Before Divine Beast Vah Ruta is calmed, the Rain that it generates will constantly fall over the Pond. As part of the Side Quest "The Giant of Ralis Pond", Torfeau asks Link to defeat the Blue Hinox at Ralis Pond. Once Link does so, Torfeau will be impressed and gives him a Silver Rupee as a reward. is a recurring character in . Biography Ramella is a Gerudo who came to the Eldin Region in search of precious Jewels. She can be found wandering around Goron City during the day. She tells Link that he can buy Fireproof Elixirs from Offrak in the city, which she herself uses to continue her work. At night, she can be found asleep in the Rollin' Inn, dreaming of Jewels. After Link has freed the Divine Beast Vah Rudania from Calamity Ganon's influence, Ramella will announce that since Death Mountain's eruptions have now ended, she has begun restocking on Jewels. She asks Link if he could bring her ten pieces of Amber, which she will buy at a higher price than at stores, initiating the Side Quest "The Jewel Trade". Ramella will offer to pay 500 Rupees for all ten Ambers, which is 200 more than is paid by stores. After Link has sold her the Ambers, Ramella will offer to buy more Jewels from Link at a higher price. She will ask for ten pieces of a randomly chosen Jewel each time. The Jewels she buys are Topaz, Ruby, Sapphire and Diamond; should Link have less than 10 of her requested Jewel, but try to sell anyway, Ramella} accuses him of trying to pull a fast one on her. This will deadlock her into wanting no other Jewel until 10 of the requested Jewel are provided, after which she will choose another random Jewel. Successfully selling 10 Jewels of a certain type will have her offer to buy 10 more for the same price. This can happen indefinitely provided Link still has enough of that type of Jewel. If Link speaks to Ramella while disguised (primarily the Gerudo Outfit, but the Snow and Sand Boots, and the Thunder Helm can be used in conjunction), a trade will not initiate. Ramella will instead claim she won't allow other Vai to get Jewels before her, considering disguised Link a business rival.

Raphica is a recurring character in . Biography Raphica was a leader to the Rito of Hyrule during the Era of Foundation. After Demon King Ganondorf began his attack, Raphica was summoned to the Forgotten Temple alongside Qia, Agraston, and Ardi by the King of Hyrule, Rauru. He granted each of them a Secret Stone and made them one of the Six Sages. Raphica's turned into a Secret Stone of Wind, and he became the Sage of Wind. Together, the Six Sages swore a vow of loyalty to Rauru. thumb|left|320px|Raphica during the Imprisoning War During the Imprisoning War, Raphica can be seen wielding a Great Eagle Bow. However, his strength was not enough to stand against Demon King Ganondorf, who soundly deflected all of Raphica's attacks. In order to distract Ganondorf, Raphica, Qia, Agraston, and Ardi throw their Weapons toward him, which Zelda reversed using Recall. Raphica and the rest of the Sages then witnessed Rauru sacrificing himself to seal the Demon King. After the end of the Imprisoning War, the Sage of Time, Zelda, met with Raphica at the Wind Temple. She warned him of Demon Ganondorf's inevitable return, and she asked for help from the Rito to defeat the Demon King when Rauru's seal is broken in the distant future. Raphica accepted her request, and he promised that a Sage of Wind from the Rito will awaken to fight alongside Link when the time comes. Throughout the Main Quest "Tulin of Rito Village", Tulin, Raphica's descendant, and Link hear the voice of Raphica beckoning them to meet him at the Wind Temple. After they defeat Colgera, Raphica's Secret Stone is revealed. When Tulin interacts with it, Raphica's Spirit appears before them, and he introduces himself as Tulin's ancestor. He reveals that he served Rauru as the Sage of Wind, as well as that Colgera was sent to prevent Tulin from awakening as a Sage. When Tulin expresses confusion, Raphica proceeds to relay the history of the Imprisoning War to him. Afterwards, he warns that although Rito Village has been saved, the rest of Hyrule is still in danger. As a result, he asks Tulin to honor the promise he made to Zelda and become the new Sage of Wind. Raphica then disappears. Other Appearances Raphica is the chief of the Rito who is fiercely loyal to his allies. He is a witty Warrior, although he can be seen as aloof by others. He is recruited alongside Vence as part of the Scenario "Shadows in the Snow".

is a character in . Biography Raseno is a Hylian member of Toren's Monster-Control Crew, Squad Two. He wears a tattered piece of Soldier's Armor, and he carries a Soldier's Spear. Initially, Raseno can be found past the Hyrule Castle Gate, where he is taking part in the Search for Princess Zelda. When Link passes through the Gate, Raseno tries to ward him off. He then recognizes Link and apologizes, before wondering if their search party is still needed. He directs Link to speak to Hoz, who is at the First Gatehouse. After he hears about a figure resembling Zelda being sighted, he urges Link to go meet with Purah.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Rassla Lake is located on the western side of Ubota Point in West Necluda. On its northern side is a Waterfall that flows into Lake Floria. The Dragon Farosh will fly into Rassla Lake after passing through Lake Floria. It will then leave the Lake and head north towards the Floria Falls. While Farosh is present at Rassla Lake, strong Winds and Updrafts will appear in the surrounding area. A total of five Treasure Chests can be found at Rassla Lake. Four metal Chests can be found at the bottom of Rassla Lake, requiring use of the Magnesis Rune in order to pull them to the surface. , also known as Kaepora Gaebora when in his owl form, is a recurring character in . Biography Era of Chaos During the Era of Chaos and shortly before the Kingdom of Hyrule was established by the royal descendants of the goddess Hylia's mortal incarnation, Rauru built the Temple of Time over the remains of the Sealed Temple that was located deep within the Faron Woods in the Faron Province. In doing this, he protected the Triforce from the chaotic Battle for the Sacred Realm being fought over its ownership at the time. Rauru named the temple after the Temple of Time from the legends of the events of about a hero who had wielded the Master Sword and traveled between two time periods. He chose to remain within the Temple of Light, situated in the center of the Sacred Realm, only leaving it in the form of the wise and watchful owl known as Kaepora Gaebora. Knowledge of the Sacred Realm passed onto the Sheikah tribe and Rauru's name faded into obscurity. After Link defeats Gohma in a failed attempt to save the Great Deku Tree, he leaves the Kokiri Forest and has his first encounter with Rauru, who awaits him in his owl form as Kaepora Gaebora at the edge of the woods. The owl gives him encouragement on the adventure the Great Deku Tree has tasked him with and advises him to visit Princess Zelda at Hyrule Castle before leaving with a promise that they will meet again. True to his word, Kaepora Gaebora often appears to tell Link about a new area whenever the young hero comes upon it, and he picks Link up and carries him twice when Link could not progress on his own. Once Link reaches the Spirit Temple, after navigating between the eras of his childhood and adulthood, Kaepora Gaebora compliments him on his growth and bids farewell after giving one final piece of advice on how to defeat the witches, Twinrova. When Link drew the Master Sword from the Pedestal of the Master Sword, Ganondorf entered the Sacred Realm and obtained the Triforce of Power from the Temple of Light. The Sacred Realm transformed into the Dark World, with the exception of the Chamber of Sages. The Master Sword kept Link in the safety of this chamber so that the boy could grow old enough to truly assume the role of the Hero of Time. Rauru speaks with Link for the first time after a period of seven years, informing him of what has transpired and his duties as the hero. After instructing him to awaken the other Sages, Rauru gives him the Light Medallion. Rauru contacts Link again after he frees the other five Sages. He tells Link to meet "someone" waiting at the Temple of Time before facing Ganondorf. This person turns out to be Sheik, who reveals himself as none other than Princess Zelda, the seventh Sage. The two take Zelda in while she searches for a way to return to her own time, and in doing so learn what the future of Hyrule Kingdom is like. They also learn from Zelda that a brave Knight named Link saves the Kingdom from a great evil. At some point, Rauru accepted Ganondorf and the Gerudo as subjects into the fledgling Hyrule Kingdom despite the Gerudo under Ganondorf ignoring prior invitations. Rauru understood that Ganondorf held Darkness within his heart and chose to keep him close in order to keep an eye on him. However, this plan backfired when Ganondorf created a Phantom Ganon that resembled Zelda to distract Sonia long enough to kill her and steal her Secret Stone. By using the Secret Stone to amplify his own powers, Ganondorf transformed into Demon King Ganondorf and summoned an army of Monsters to attack Hyrule Kingdom. This was the first act of the Imprisoning War wherein Rauru swore to stop Ganondorf at any cost. In order to increase Hyrule Kingdom's odds against Ganondorf's army, Rauru selected six individuals to hold Secret Stones. In accepting their responsibility to protect the land, these six people became the Six Sages. Zelda and Mineru already possessed Secret Stones and became the Sage of Time and Sage of Spirit, while an additional four were shared among leaders of the Rito, Zora, Gorons, and the Gerudo. Raphica became the Sage of Wind, Qia became the Sage of Water, Agraston became the Sage of Fire, and Ardi became the Sage of Lightning. While they prepared for their upcoming battle, Rauru mourned the late Queen Sonia. He also met with Zelda, who realized that the reanimated mummy she met Beneath Hyrule Castle was Ganondorf after watching him become the Demon King. Recalling the circumstances of her first encounter, she warned Rauru that despite their efforts, he would live on to the distant future where they would meet again. Despite their preparations, Rauru and the Six Sages are soundly defeated by Demon King Ganondorf. Following Rauru's imprisoning of Ganondorf underground, his people construct Hyrule Castle atop the Demon King to keep him sealed, the Castle remains intact and undestroyed for ages until it is damaged during the Great Calamity 100 years prior to the Era of the Wilds. Link and Zelda travel Beneath Hyrule Castle to investigate the Gloom seeping out from Ganondorf's body. After Link defeats the Demon Dragon, the Spirits of Rauru and Sonia appear to him. They channel their powers of Light and Time through Link to reverse Zelda's transformation into the Light Dragon and the damage done to Link's arm by Ganondorf's Gloom. With the defeat of Demon King Ganondorf and the future of Hyrule saved, Rauru and Sonia both fade into the afterlife. The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Rauru Settlement Ruins are a small collection of broken and dilapidated Ruined Houses located along the southern edge of Rauru Hillside in the Great Hyrule Forest. There is a small, unnamed Bottomless Bog that marks the western border of the Ruins. At their eastern exit, there is an abandoned Wagon that can be searched for Gems. Prior to the second Great Calamity, Rauru Settlement was growing in numbers, with a population mainly consisting of Hylians. However, an influx of Monsters in the area drove out its citizens, leaving it abandoned. Due to its proximity to Hyrule Castle, the Settlement was completely destroyed by Guardians. The Ruins were further desecrated by a landslide sometime later. The Rauru Settlement Ruins are one of the locations where Mina and Mils hunt for treasure. Their goal is to locate the treasure left behind when the Settlement's original inhabitants fled. When Link encounters them, they will be fighting off a pair of Blue Bokoblins. If Link saves them, they will give him Food, Materials, or Rupees as a reward. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests Areas

Features and Overview The Rauru Settlement Ruins Well is situated among the Rauru Settlement Ruins in the Great Hyrule Forest. 100 years before , it was part of Rauru Settlement, which was destroyed during the Great Calamity. The Rauru Settlement Ruins Well reappears in , still being located in the Great Hyrule Forest. Link is now able to access its interior. Most of its interior consists of a Bottomless Bog, which will cause Link to drown if he falls into it. However, several Boards are located within the Well. , also known as the Rabbit Hood, is a recurring Item in . Ravio's Hood goes unnamed in and . Location and Uses Ravio's Hood is a piece of clothing worn by Ravio in . It is worn to mask his identity as Link's Lorulean counterpart. Ravio removes his Hood after Link defeats Yuga Ganon, pleading for Hilda to give up her attempt to steal Hyrule's Triforce. Ravio's Hood is a piece of Armor introduced in the "EX Treasure: Merchant Hood" Side Quest from Downloadable Content pack in . It is a priceless relic that was once kept safely within the walls of Hyrule Castle, but was later stolen by Misko. Misko hints at the whereabouts of Ravio's Hood in Misko's EX Journal 2 in the Deya Village Ruins, claiming that it rests in the right hand of a dragon near Dracozu Lake. The Treasure Chest housing Ravio's Hood can be found embedded in the ground beneath the right hand of the dragon statue at the Spring of Courage. In order to retrieve it, Link must use the Magnesis Rune to pull it from the ground. Ravio's Hood is the same Hood worn by Ravio. When worn, it grants Link the Sideways Climbing Speed Up Added Effect, which increases his sideways Climbing speed. If Link sells Ravio's Hood, he can later purchase it from Granté at Tarrey Town for 50 Rupees. Ravio's Hood cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy, nor can it be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Other Appearances Ravio's Hood appears as part of Ravio's outfit in . In , the Rabbit Hood is also Fairy Clothing that Companion Fairies can equip in My Fairy's Salon.
