Any crab, a Sneaky River Snail, or a Hearty Blueshell Snail is needed to make a Seafood Skewer. They also count as seafood when making Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. Razorclaw Crabs are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Razorshrooms are found below Trees in the Great Hyrule Forest and on the Tabantha Frontier. They are also available to purchase at the Spore Store or from Ardin's Stall in Gerudo Town. They can be eaten raw to restore a half of a Heart, or they can be roasted by direct flames to become Toasty Razorshrooms. If one or more Razorshrooms are Cooked into a dish in a Cooking Pot, the resulting Meal will grant Link the Attack Up Added Effect, which temporarily increases his attack power. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Razorshrooms are one of the ingredients that can be used to make Crimson Dye. Razorshrooms, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Razorshrooms, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Razorshrooms are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances Razorshrooms are a type of Material in .

is a recurring character in . Biography Reagah is a Goron who can be found in the Hammerhead in Zora's Domain. He was originally recruited by Sidon to help calm Divine Beast Vah Ruta. However, Sidon deemed him too heavy to carry, so he ended up abandoning that plan. When asked by Link where he is from, Reagah describes Goron City and its Scorching Climate. and if he asks Reagah what Death Mountain is, he becomes shocked and tells Link that Gorons live there since they eat Rocks. Link can also ask him about his diet, and Reagah will say that Rocks are his favorite, although Gems taste terrible and are better sold or used as crafting Materials. Unlike many other Gorons, Reagah will not fight back against Link when attacked in any way. Reagah travels the southeastern road from Woodland Stable, where he eventually reaches the Maw of Death Mountain by way of the Ternio Trail. He excitedly greets Link, stating that he thought it would be nice to talk to someone. Reagah often mentions the Hot Springs in Eldin. If encountered at the Woodland Stable, he will tell Link about the Hot Springs near the Foothill Stable, stating that visiting Hot Springs every day is good for one's health. On the way to the Foothill Stable, he talks to Link about how Lanayru, despite having many bodies of Water, does not have any Hot Springs like the ones found in Eldin. On the approach to the Maw of Death Mountain, he says that there is a Hot Spring to heal Link's fatigue to the north. He will eventually walk into a Hot Spring and, if spoken to, comments on the soothing nature of the Water. Afterward, he will begin the walk back to the Woodland Stable, where he will briefly rest at a Tree. When encountering a Monster on the road, Reagah will flee rather than fight. If Link defeats the Monster, Reagah will thank Link, and reward him with either a Meal, or with Rupees.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Rebonae Bridge is a bridge that spans the Hylia River in Hyrule Field just northwest of the Wetland Stable. The Hylian traveler, Leekah, can be found on the Bridge being attacked by a Bokoblin, offering Link Food for saving her. She will also make a remark to Link if he rescues her after she is knocked out by the Bokoblin. In Master Mode, a wooden platform can be found suspended by Sky Octoroks. Atop this platform, Link can find a Metal Chest containing a Double Axe. A lone Rock can be found underneath the west side of the Bridge, a Natural Hiding Spot for a Korok. Creatures Enemies Normal Mode Master Mode Treasure Chests As in , Rebonae Bridge spans the Hylia River in Hyrule Field. Materials

The is a recurring location in . The Rebonae Bridge Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Rebonae Bridge Well is situated on the western side of Rebonae Bridge in Hyrule Field. Before the Great Calamity, it was part of a Hylian settlement that was ultimately destroyed by Guardians. Equipment The Rebonae Bridge Well returns in , and it is still within the limits of Hyrule Field. Link is now able to enter the Well, though the bottom half of the Ladder attached to its rim has broken off. The Well's interior consists of a small patch of dry land alongside a pool of Water. When Link first comes upon the Rebonae Bridge Well, a Smoke Signal will be coming from a lit Campfire inside of it. Upon investigating, he can find Dillie inside the Well, who is relieved Link is there to rescue him. He explains that he was trying to retrieve a personal belonging of his, but the Ladder broke when he tried to Climb out and trapped him inside. Dillie's friend, Jora, failed to notice his absence and abandoned him as a result. Now that Link is here, he considers reattaching the broken piece, though he cannot reach the point to reattach it. Following this conversation, the Side Quest "Fell into a Well!" will begin. Using Ultrahand, Link can fix the Ladder, allowing himself and Dillie to escape. Once they leave the Well, Dillie gives Link a Purple Rupee as a reward for saving him. He then departs for Foothill Stable, where he plans to meet with Jora and join the Zonai Survey Team. Afterwards, the Side Quest will be completed. Creatures Materials

is a recurring ability in . Overview Recall is an Ancient Power that allows its user to stop Objects in motion and reverse their trajectory. In Zelda's Memories from the Era of Foundation, both she and Sonia can be seen using Recall with the power granted to them by their Secret Stones of Time. During the Main Quest "Find Princess Zelda", an apparition of Zelda appears before Link when he touches the projection of her Secret Stone in the Temple of Time. She grants him the ability to Recall before disappearing. Link can use Recall to hit Objects or Enemies in the reversed path of his target. He can also use it on fallen pieces of Ruins Rubble to access Sky Islands directly above him. Recall only reverses the movement of the targeted Object, however, and if too much time has elapsed it may not be able to reverse all of its movement. The effects of Recall can be ended prematurely and will end on their own after enough time elapses. When this happens, the Object will resume its movement based on its new position. Other Appearances Like in , Zelda has the power to Recall Objects as a result of her Secret Stone of Time. She uses her ability during certain Weak-Point Smashes, wherein she reverses the trajectory of her Blade of Light to repeatedly damage the Powerful Enemy in front of her. She can also utilize it during Sync Strikes with Calamo, activating Recall to ensure his Boomerangs return to him. Lastly, her Unique Skills Temporal Toss and Temporal Counter both incorporate Recall to deal damage to Enemies. Sonia demonstrates Recall during her unique Sync Strike with Rauru. As part of this attack, she uses Recall to reverse the trajectory of his Spear of Light, dealing additional damage to the Enemies before them. During the Movie "Unsettling Rumors", Sonia suggests to Zelda that she will one day be able to use Recall on multiple Objects at once. As part of the Quest "The Queen's Suggestion", Zelda decides to master this skill, and she is able to learn how to reverse multiple Objects. This allows her to use Recall on her Light projectiles that appear at the end of certain combos, sending them backwards to perform a follow-up attack on Enemies.

The is a recurring location in . The Reception Room goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Reception Room is an interior room of Hyrule Castle. Each wall of the Reception Room has a doorway, making it a hub for Link as he explores. The northern doorway leads deeper into the Castle, though it is covered by rubble. The eastern door leads into the Hyrule Castle Corridors, towards the Dining Hall and Square Spiral Staircase. The western doorway also leads into the Hyrule Castle Corridors, though it is blocked by Malice. The southern exit of the Reception Room leads into the Observation Room. To access the Observation Room, Link must destroy the Glowing Eyeball in the Reception Room. This will clear away the Malice covering the doorway. Enemies As in , the Reception Room connects the Observation Room to the Hyrule Castle Corridors within Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field. Enemies

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview After Link views "The Master Sword's Power" Memory during the "Trail of the Master Sword" Main Quest, the Great Deku Tree notices that he is no longer carrying the Master Sword. Although Link does not know where it is, the Great Deku Tree is able to sense its power. From the Map, the Great Deku Tree is able to show Link where the Master Sword is currently located. However, he notices that it appears to be moving through the Sky. The Great Deku Tree urges Link to hurry, since the Master Sword is waiting for him. After this conversation, "Recovering the Hero's Sword" will begin. By following the Marker on the Map, Link can find the Master Sword embedded in the head of the Light Dragon. When he attempts to pull it out, the Light Dragon will suddenly roar and begin flying erratically. In order to keep his grip, Link will require at least two Stamina Wheels. If he manages to stay on the Light Dragon's head, she will calm down and bring him higher into the Sky. The fur around the Master Sword will loosen, and Link will be able to reclaim it. With its blade restored, Link then views the "Zelda's Wish" Memory. Following the Memory, Link disembarks from the Light Dragon at the Temple of Time on the Great Sky Island. At this point, "Recovering the Hero's Sword"s will be completed. Objectives

, also known as , are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Red Chu Jelly can be obtained in the Lakebed Temple, Hyrule Field, Snowpeak Ruins, and Caves. After defeating a Red Chu, Link can collect Red Chu Jelly in an Empty Bottle. Drinking it will have the same effect as Red Potions and restores eight Hearts. Red Chuchu Jelly can be obtained by killing Fire Chuchus, or by killing Chuchus with Fire Weapons. It can also be made from regular Chuchu Jelly by setting it on Fire. If struck with a Weapon, it explodes and releases a ball of fire that sets nearby Enemies on fire. Red Chuchu Jelly can be used to Cook Elixirs. Red Chuchu Jelly is also used to upgrade the Snowquill Set of Armor to its first and second tiers at a Great Fairy Fountain. Red Chuchu Jellies appear in . They can be Fused to Weapons and Shields or thrown to start Fires upon impact. Other Appearances

are locations in . Features and Overview The Red Pillars are a series of three buildings that can be found in the Gerudo Desert during the Sand Shroud. They are described on the Mural in the Underground Shelter to help lead Riju to the Sage of Lightning in the Lightning Temple. During the "Riju of Gerudo Town" Main Quest, Link must connect a Light Beam between all three Pillars. In the Red Pillar closest to Gerudo Town, Link is able to smash the Hard Sediment covering the origin of the Light Beam. Then, using the Mirror affixed to its ceiling, he can aim it towards the second Pillar. He can then use this Pillar's Mirror to aim the Light Beam towards the final Red Pillar. In order to aim the final Mirror towards the first Red Pillar, he must reattach the Poles to its lever. Once all three Red Pillars are connected via the Light Beam, a Battery will rise at their center.

is a character in . Biography Redhran is a Hylian and a member of the Zonai Survey Team. He is one of the researchers who can be found on the Digdogg Suspension Bridge, where he is investigating the Device Dispenser on the Bridge's east side. Redhran does not know what the Device Dispenser is, and while believes that it has a unique purpose, he is unsure what it is. He additionally informs Link that there are two other Device Dispensers located in Kakariko Village and Tarrey Town. He wants to discover the purpose of the Dispenser and be be known as the one who did so. If Link speaks to Redhran after using the Device Dispenser, he will be surprised. He initially tries to ask Link how it is used, but he instead decides to figure out on his own.

is a recurring character in . Biography Reede is the head of Hateno Village and can usually be found tending to the fields behind his home. When Link first approaches him, Reede notes that he must be an adventurer and introduces himself, asking Link what he thinks of the village. If Link agrees that it is peaceful, Reede says they are recovering from the Great Calamity at last. Link can admit that he is uncomfortable in Hateno and Reede will laugh, claiming that the village has grown. He ends the conversation by inviting the hero to stay for as long as he chooses. Link can return to Reede and ask him about a number of subjects. Asking about the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab leads him to direct Link to the hill where it sits. Reede mentions that a Sheikah tribe member conducts research there and never comes out. He also expresses concern over the occupants' wellbeing. Link can ask about the Calamity itself and Reede will describe the torturous event, noting that even now it is difficult to speak of. He advises Link to speak to the elders of the village to learn more about it, as Reede himself was not alive. Asking him about Hateno Village itself allows Reede to explain that the settlement was rebuilt, having only just survived the ruin of the Great Calamity. He mentions that many people now inhabit the village and they see a few travelers every-so-often.

is a recurring character in . Biography Reeza is a Gerudo Soldier who guards the front entrance to the palace in Gerudo Town at all times, alongside Ploka. If Link speaks to Reeza, she says that Riju, Chief of the Gerudo, is a kind person for allowing visitors during these tough times. If Link asks about the tough times she is referring to, Reeza snaps at Link that it is a Gerudo problem and is none of his business. Reeza allows Link into the palace, but warns him not to get in the Chief's way. When Link ends the conversation, Reeza tells Link not to be rude to Riju. If Link speaks to Reeza after speaking to Riju for the first time, she asks what makes Link so special that Riju trusts him to retrieve the Thunder Helm. She then warns him that the task is not simple, as the skilled Yiga thieves slipped past all of the guards. Reeza recommends that Link goes to the barracks to learn more, as the soldiers have been investigating the theft. After Link calms Naboris, Reeza talks about how much it stressed Riju and Buliara. She thanks Link for lifting that burden from them. If Link asks her to talk about Riju, she snaps at Link, demanding he call her by her full title, Lady Riju. She goes on to explain that Riju has a softer side, but can only let it show in private due to her expectations of leadership. If Link asks her to talk about Buliara, Reeza is offended that Link does not know about her. She then explains that Buliara is the best spear master in Gerudo Town and that she inspired her to train with the spear when she was young. When Link decides to say goodbye, Reeza says she hopes that Riju's ancestors are watching her.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Regencia River is an extensive River that separates Hyrule Field and Hyrule Ridge in Central Hyrule. It flows from the Hyrule Castle Moat. Near where it floods the Sage Temple Ruins, the Regencia River splits into a main branch and the distributary Tamio River. The River is spanned by both Carok Bridge and Manhala Bridge. A stretch of land connects Mount Gustaf to the West Hyrule Plains across the Regencia River. Additionally, a small branch of the River that connects it to Aquame Lake is spanned by the Gleeok Bridge. Korok Seeds The Regencia River reappears in .

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview During the "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" Main Quest, Purah asks Link to start investigating the strange phenomena that has appeared throughout Hyrule as part of the Upheaval, believing that it could help them locate Princess Zelda. After he has activated the Lookout Landing Skyview Tower and collected its Map data, Purah asks to see his Purah Pad. Using the Map, she directs him to the four Regions that have been reported issues, these being Hebra, Eldin, Lanayru, and Gerudo. She suspects that by investigating these phenomena, they can learn more about where Zelda could be. Josha claims to have heard that Zelda was sighted near Rito Village recently, which Purah thinks could be credible. After their conversation, "Regional Phenomena" will start. In order to complete "Regional Phenomena", Link must first finish the following Main Quests: "Tulin of Rito Village" "Yunobo of Goron City" "Sidon of the Zora" "Riju of Gerudo Town" During each of these Main Quests, Link will encounter an individual who appears to be Zelda causing the Region's disasters. As he awakens the Sages, their predecessors show him visions featuring an ancient Sage of Time that resembles Zelda as well. When Link solves the phenomena plaguing a Region, their leaders pledge to send reinforcements to Lookout Landing to help aid in the search for Zelda. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of the floating portion of Hyrule Castle during a Blood Moon. A figure that appears to be Princess Zelda stands on, the Sanctum visible behind her.|The impostor Zelda outside Hyrule Castle Once all four of these Main Quests have been completed, Link will be directed to return to Lookout Landing and report his findings to Purah. Upon his return, Link can hear rumors that Zelda has been seen near Hyrule Castle. He can then find Purah looking through the Telescope on top of her Research Lab. When spoken to, she commends him for solving the problems that the Regions were facing. She believes that the individual who resembles Zelda is related to the Upheaval, and although she has something to share with Link, she is interrupted by the sudden appearance of a Blood Moon. Looking back through her Telescope, Purah spots something and tells Link to look. When he does so, he can see Zelda outside of Hyrule Castle's Sanctum. Purah is shocked, but as the Blood Moon ends, Zelda disappears in a cloud of Gloom. After the Blood Moon ends, Purah reveals that she saw the person who resembles Zelda at Hyrule Castle, and instead of disappearing, it seems like she retreated inside. She declares that they must rescue her, but since Link is the only individual capable of reaching Hyrule Castle, he is forced to go after her alone. She asks him to come back safely with Zelda. At this point, "Regional Phenomena" will be completed, and "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" will continue. Objectives

are recurring Items in . Reinforced Lizal Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Reinforced Lizal Shields are Lizal Shields that have been strengthened with the addition of a different type of metal. Their edges are lined with spikes, which means they must be handled with care. Blue Lizalfos commonly use these Shields, though Fire-Breath Lizalfos, Ice-Breath Lizalfos, and Electric Lizalfos may also use them. They belong to the Lizalfos Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Weapons created and utilized by Lizalfos. Being made of metal, Reinforced Lizal Shields will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms, and they will also sink if they are dropped in Water. However, they can be picked up with the Magnesis basic Rune, and they will not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Reinforced Lizal Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Reinforced Lizal Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Lizal Forked Boomerangs.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Relationship Classroom is a room that can be accessed through the Barracks in Gerudo Town. The Classroom is located below the Royal Palace. During the day, Ashai teaches a class in the room entitled "Voe and You", which is designed to help young Gerudo women learn about interacting with men. Ashai sees her class as a way to prepare her students for the world outside of Gerudo Town. Ashai's three students are Pasha, Dina, and Risa. Traysi also observes lessons in the Relationship Classroom, where she notes how serious the Gerudo are. Ashai does not start her class until all of her students have arrived. Risa admits that she is only taking this class as a refresher, though she still studies. When spoken to inside the Relationship Classroom, Dina will ask Link what he thinks of her lipstick, as the color is supposed to bring good luck. If Link asks how that works, Dina sheepishly reveals that she was planning on learning that next. Alternatively, if Link compliments her, Dina says she can already feel it working. Should Link speak to Pasha, she will sit up and exclaim that she was not sleeping. However, when she realizes Link is not the teacher, she tells him not to scare her like that. Her dream is to travel the world before settling down with her true love to have a daughter, and she sees these classes as critical for achieving that goal.

, also known as Bases in the Depths, are locations in . Features and Overview Relay Bases are Yiga fortifications found throughout the Depths. All Bases are staffed by Yiga Footsoldiers piloting Vehicles, one of whom is tasked with keeping their storehouses secured. Upon this Footsoldier's defeat, the storehouse will be able to be opened, where Link can find two Stone Chests containing a Large Crystallized Charge and a Yiga Schematic. At least one Yiga Clan Notebook can also be found at every Relay Base. Sundelions and Mighty Bananas can occasionally be found at these Bases. Some Bases also have traps built from Zonai Devices that must be disabled or bypassed. Several Abandoned Mines have had smaller Relay Bases built on their premises. They are not actively patrolled by Yiga Footsoldiers and contain no Treasure Chests, though they do feature Yiga Clan Notebooks and abandoned Vehicles that Link can use. However, a Researcher can often be found nearby, who will reveal themself to be a Yiga Footsoldier and attack Link if spoken to. North of Great Abandoned Central Mine, there is an empty and run-down Relay Base with no Yiga Footsoldiers, storehouse, or Stone Chests. The only thing left is a Tattered Notebook. The text is damaged, but it seems to suggest that the Yiga posted there were warned by Master Kohga that something was going to happen. Relay Base Locations Abandoned Mines Other Relay Bases

is a recurring character in . Biography Rensa is found at the front of Dueling Peaks Stable. He welcomes Link and asks what he thinks of the Stable. Rensa tells the hero that although it may be hard to believe, the area was nearly destroyed about 100 years ago. Even so, Rensa cites the blessings of the Dueling Peaks as the reason everything is full of life again and the Wild Horses have returned. Rensa asks Link where he is heading and says that both Kakariko Village and Hateno Village are nearby. If asked about the Wild Horses, Rensa asks if Link did not see any Horses on his way here. He points out that there are still quite a few around, though certainly not as many as in years past. He informs Link that Horses in the wild are untamed, as no one has trained or cared for them. Rensa advises Link to let his brother Tasseren know if he manages to catch and tame a Horse so he can register it for him. Rensa's boys, Shibo and Darton, are incredibly knowledgeable about Horses, so he tells Link to feel free to pick their brains. When asked about Kakariko Village, Rensa says it is the Village where the Sheikah clan lives. He tells Link that some time ago the Sheikah had advanced techniques that were more powerful than anything anyone had seen, but because that power put them at odds with the king at the time, the Sheikah were scattered across the land. If Link leaves the Stable and follows the path straight to the north, he will find Kakariko Bridge. Crossing the Bridge and following the path will lead him to the Kakariko Village gate. When asked about Hateno Village, Rensa says it is a Village on the edge of Hyrule, and was largely unaffected by the events of the Great Calamity so the people are easygoing. Rensa tells Link that he has heard Hateno has a research center, but that folks tend to avoid Purah, the weird scientist who lives there. Rensa tells Link to head north until he reaches a fork in the road, then to follow the road to the east. He says it is a far distance if walked, but with a Horse Link should reach Hateno Village in under a day. After Link says goodbye, Rensa says that although everything in the area looks just as it always has, the effects of the Great Calamity still linger, and he warns the hero to be careful at night when monsters appear. If spoken to afterwards, Rensa notes that Horses are wild, so until Link calms them down it will be a crazy ride. Even so, Rensa claims there is no feeling quite like taming a wild stallion. Rensa then boasts that he took second place in the Hyrule Horse-Taming Competition. When he sees the look Link gives him, Rensa challenges the hero to a tame-off. If Link declines, Rensa asks if he would dare

so, Rensa claims there is no feeling quite like taming a wild stallion. Rensa then boasts that he took second place in the Hyrule Horse-Taming Competition. When he sees the look Link gives him, Rensa challenges the hero to a tame-off. If Link declines, Rensa asks if he would dare turn down a challenge from the second-greatest Horse tamer in the world. Rensa realizes there is not much he can do about that, however, and states it is only natural that the title of Hyrule Horse-Taming Competition Runner-Up would strike fear in Link's heart. Rensa claims that he himself would never run and hide, and tells Link to come back when he has the confidence to challenge his taming skills. However, if Link accepts the challenge, Rensa praises Link's competitive spirit. The only rule of the challenge is that Link has to bring a wild Horse back to the spot Rensa is standing in under two minutes, which is Rensa's record. This begins the "Wild Horses" Side Quest. Rensa advises Link that because Horses are skittish, it's best to approach them quietly. Rensa also asks Link that he not stray too far from the Stable, as he would not be able to record an accurate time. If Link fails to return with a Horse under the two-minute time limit, Rensa acknowledges the challenge of the task, but tells Link to not be discouraged, and that it took him years to place second in the competition. Once Link has caught a Horse and brought it back before time runs out, Rensa is amazed that Link could beat his record so easily. Rensa then admits that the only participants who actually competed in the Hyrule Horse-Taming Competition were his brother and himself. He gives Link the purse for winning the second Hyrule Horse-Taming Competition, which is a Purple Rupee. After Link's show of talent, Rensa guesses there is more competition out there than he originally knew about, and that maybe Hyrule is not all bad after all. If Link asks Rensa about Wild Horses after completing the challenge, Rensa will be surprised, as Link was the one to beat him, the man who placed second in the Hyrule Horse-Taming Competition.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Restless Crickets can be found almost anywhere in Hyrule by cutting Grass with any Sword or looking under Rocks. When found, they will hop away two or three times before flying away and disappearing unless Link is sneaking. They're sold by the traveling merchant Gartan and by Beedle at Dueling Peaks Stable and Outskirt Stable. Using a Restless Cricket in a Cooking Pot with Monster Parts will result in an Energizing Elixir, which will restore Link's Stamina when used. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop as an ingredient to make Green Dye. The Side Quest "A Gift for My Beloved" involves Link asking Prima what she likes on behalf of Manny. She will say crickets as an excuse, claiming that it's her dream to own one hundred of them. Upon hearing this information, Manny will ask Link to gather ten Restless Crickets for him while he collects the rest. Manny gives Link a Silver Rupee when the Restless Crickets are delivered. Restless Crickets can be found in the Grass on both the Surface and in the Sky. Other Appearances

The , also known as the Bed Chamber, is a recurring location in . The Restoration Room goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Equipment Korok Seeds The Restoration Room is located within the Shrine of Resurrection Cave on the Great Plateau. The Ancient Technologies within the Restoration Room have been stripped away to reveal rocky terrain with foliage growing off it and stalactites protruding down from the roof. A Hot Spring sits in its center, healing Link when he steps in it. A root grows out of the west wall of the Room above a small opening leading down to a Yiga base.

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview At the end of "The Sludge-Covered Statue", Yona asks Link to meet her after he visits Sidon. Afterwards, he will be able to find her tending to her patients in the Sleeping Chamber, alongside Chroma and Khira. When Khira informs her that Link has arrived, she will be glad to see him. Yona reveals that she wants to speak to him about his Zora Armor, which he previously left at Zora's Domain for repairs. While it is mostly complete, the last thing she needs is the scale of an Ancient Arowana. Since she does not know where to find one, Yona suggests asking Dento. She promises that she will be able to completely repair the Zora Armor if Link brings her one, reminding him that wearing it will allow him to Swim. After their conversation, "Restoring the Zora Armor" will begin. When Link speaks to Dento, he reveals that they may be found near Mipha's Statue, which is located at Mipha Court on Ploymus Mountain. He wonders whether the return of Ancient Arowanas could be related to the Upheaval. Link can also find Ancient Arowanas in bodies of Water on Sky Islands. Once Link has an Ancient Arowana, he can return to the Sleeping Chamber to give it to Yona. Now that she is able to repair the Zora Armor, Yona leaves for the Hammerhead. Upon her return, she claims to be honored to help restore the Armor. She then presents him with his Zora Armor. Yona wishes Link well on his travels, and she reveals that although the Zora Armor will help him Swim up Waterfalls, it will not work in Water tainted by Sludge. She hopes that the Armor will be helpful to his search for Princess Zelda, after which "Restoring the Zora Armor" will be finished. Objectives

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Revali's Landing is a flight platform in Rito Village. It is used by the Rito to travel between their Village and the Flight Range to the north. The crest of the Rito can be seen painted upon the Landing's floor. 100 years before the events of , the "Revali's Flap" Recovered Memory occurred on Revali's Landing. While visiting Rito Village with Zelda, Link can be seen watching Divine Beast Vah Medoh flying above him. Revali interrupts him by flying up using his Gale, which he then proceeds to gloat about. He then expresses his frustration about being forced to assist Link in the fight against Calamity Ganon, when he believes that he is capable of defeating it himself. Revali challenges Link to a duel to prove him wrong, and though he suggests Vah Medoh as a location, he uses it as an opportunity to mock Link for his inability to fly. Using his Gale once more, Revali flies off, wishing Link luck in sealing away Calamity Ganon. This Recovered Memory can be accessed during the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest. After Revali was killed during the Great Calamity, Revali's Landing received its name in his honor. While it is daytime, Bedoli visits Revali's Landing, where she paces. Prior to starting the "Recital at Warbler's Nest" Shrine Quest, Notts also visits the Landing, sitting on its edge. As part of the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, Saki directs Link to Revali's Landing as a path to reach the Flight Range. Creatures

is a recurring character in . Biography 100 years prior to the events of , Revali was the Champion of the Rito. He was known as the most skilled archer of all the Rito and could fire Arrows quickly. Revali had the ability to create an Updraft that allows him to soar into the air, later named Revali's Gale after him. He wielded the Great Eagle Bow, a Bow that is known for being too heavy for most Rito. However, Revali was able to make up for this with his strength and speed, thereby allowing him to wield it while flying. is a recurring character in . Biography Rhodes is a man who tends to the windmills with his wife, Ralera. They take shifts with Rhodes being awake at night, while his wife takes over during the day. Rhodes is a friendly man who will speak to Link if he wishes. Link can ask him about what he is doing, and Rhodes will describe his job for him. In response, Rhodes will return the question. Link can reply a few different ways: saying he is lost, that he is a thief, or that he is a traveler. Should he say that he is lost, Rhodes will laugh and say that everyone is lost to some extent. However, he then points him to the Ton Pu Inn so Link can have somewhere to stay the night. Rhodes will refer to him as the "lost boy" afterward. If Link says he is a thief, Rhodes takes it as a game. He will tease Link about it when spoken to again. When Link admits that he is a traveler, Rhodes is fairly uninterested as he does not consider the hero a threat. At 9:00 PM, Rhodes heads out to the Tree for his round of watching the windmills. Once 5 o'clock in the morning rolls around, he goes home to rest.

is a recurring character in . Biography Rhondson is a Gerudo from Gerudo Town who is first found in Kara Kara Bazaar in the Gerudo Desert. She is searching for the love of her life. When Link first speaks to her, Rhondson asks who he is and she is suddenly interested in Link when she notices that he is a man. She quickly loses interest in Link, stating that her mother would not approve of a delicate man like Link. Rhondson then introduces herself and explains that she is exhausted from searching for love. She expresses to Link that her mother constantly bothers her over not having found love. When Link points out that no male Gerudo exist, Rhondson explains that Gerudo women travel away from Gerudo Town to find their husbands. She goes on to say that she is a gifted tailor, but men do not appreciate her skills. Rhondson is also disappointed that there is no work for a tailor in the Gerudo Desert. Rhondson is stuck in her search for love and despite having dozens of skills, does not understand what men are looking for. She questions if there is anyone out there for her. If Link speaks to Rhondson while wearing the Gerudo Outfit, she compliments what a "cute vai" Link is and asks if he is seeking the love of his life as well. If Link says yes, she mutters that it is not the answer she expected and quickly wishes good luck to the both of them. In the Tarrey Town Side Quest, "From the Ground Up", Hudson has Link search for a Gerudo tailor with "son" in their name. Link then speaks to Rhondson, who meets these requirements. Rhondson comments that Akkala is far away, but admits that she needs to get away from a village full of other women. Rhondson thanks Link for the information and sets off for Tarrey Town. At the Town, she manages the Rhondson Armor Boutique and is soon engaged to Hudson. As Rhondson and Hudson take their vows during their marriage ceremony, Rhondson learns that they must vow to give their children names with "son" at the end in accordance with the Bolson Construction naming guidelines. Rhondson states that such a vow is not part of traditional marriage standards. Hudson questions her and the wedding guests express their agreement with the vow. Still uncertain, Rhondson accepts the vow. Rhondson and Hudson are then married.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Riju's Bedroom is the room in which Riju stays, at the top floor of the Royal Palace. Inside can be found Riju's Bed, the Chief's Diary, and one of each variety of Sand-Seal Toy: a Blue-Seal Toy, a Green-Seal Toy, and a Red-Seal Toy. When Link enters Riju's Bedroom at night, he will find her playing with her Red-Seal Toy. If Link approaches her, she will become embarrassed and tell him to ignore the Toys. She then scolds Link for entering someone's room so late at night. During Downloadable Content Pack, Urbosa's Diary can be found in Riju's Bedroom. According to Riju, it was discovered after Divine Beast Vah Naboris was calmed. When asked about the Diary, Riju explains that it is on the sofa in her room, and since Link was friends with Urbosa, she allows him to read it.

Makeela is a recurring character in . Biography Riju is the young Gerudo Chief, ruling over Gerudo Town after the untimely passing of her mother. Riju was her mother's only child, causing the duties of leading the Gerudo to fall to her. Riju resides in the Royal Palace, with her Bedroom being located on the second floor. At the time of , she is approximately 12 years old. Throughout her childhood, Riju's mother recounted many stories about the Champions and the Great Calamity to her daughter. One of these focused on Divine Beast Vah Naboris, which she referred to as a guardian Deity of the Gerudo. She holds a great deal of respect for her ancestor Urbosa, often remarking that among other ancestors, she must be looking down at them and working to keep them safe. Similarly, Riju admires Nabooru, one of the Sages who sealed Calamity Ganon when he was still a Gerudo. Riju also heard stories about Zelda placing Link into a Slumber of Restoration after he was defeated during the Calamity, as well as Zelda hiding the Master Sword in a forest. As evidenced by the Sand Seal design on her skirt and Sand-Seal Toys in her Bedroom, Riju loves Sand Seals. Prior to her death, Riju's mother gave her Patricia as a present. Despite Patricia's rugged appearance, Riju regularly dotes on her, and Patricia is always ready to go Sand-Seal Surfing with her. The red ribbon that Patricia wears was a gift to her from Riju. Riju keeps a journal known as the Chief's Diary, which she keeps in her Bedroom. She started the Diary shortly after the death of her mother, which Buliara informed her of. While Buliara told Riju that her mother was in a better place, Riju could not understand how it could be better if they were apart. After becoming the Gerudo Chief, Riju noticed that the people of Gerudo Town started acting nicer to her, but she still saw worry in their eyes. As a result, she wonders if she could be as great of a Chief as her mother was. When Divine Beast Vah Naboris reactivated and began roaming the East Barrens, Riju planned to investigate it, claiming that it seemed to be acting contrary to her mother's words. She approached the Divine Beast with Patricia, but she decided to turn back after encountering its Sandstorm and Lightning. However, Patricia was scared by a Monster, resulting in them turning directly towards Divine Beast Vah Naboris. The next thing Riju is able to recall was being rescued by Buliara. Afterwards, Riju concluded that the Gerudo would be in grave danger if Divine Beast Vah Naboris attacked them. Following Riju's encounter with Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Buliara refused to leave her side. This continued even after the Thunder Helm was stolen from the Royal Palace, which Riju fears happened due to her being unprepared to be the Gerudo Chief. "" is a Main Quest in . Overview During the "Regional Phenomena" Main Quest, Purah tasks Link with investigating strange occurrences throughout Hyrule in an effort to find Princess Zelda. After "Tulin of Rito Village", "Yunobo of Goron City", and "Sidon of the Zora" have all been completed, Purah will direct Link to visit Gerudo Town, since it is the only place he has yet to visit. Past the Kara Kara Bazaar, the entire Gerudo Desert will be covered by a Sand Shroud. When Link arrives in Gerudo Town, he will find that the Gerudo have fled to the Gerudo Shelter after their First Encounter with the Gibdos. There are two ways that Link can access the Shelter, The first is by using Ascend while in the waterways beneath Gerudo Town, and the second is by jumping into the hole under the Desk in the Relationship Classroom. In either scenario, the Gerudo Soldiers Ploka and Merina will detect his presence and attempt to apprehend him. However, the Gerudo Soldiers are stopped by Buliara, who informs them that he has received Riju's permission to enter both Gerudo Town and the Gerudo Shelter. She directs Ploka and Merina to inform all of those residing in the Shelter. After they leave, she reasons that Link must have an important reason to come visit during the Sand Shroud. She is shocked to hear that Zelda is still missing, though she is impressed that Link was able to make it to Gerudo Town through the Sand Shroud. She explains that after the Sand Shroud began, the Gibdos attacked the Gerudo and forced them to retreat to the Gerudo Shelter. As a result of this, the Gerudo are currently unable to assist in the search for Zelda. Buliara informs Link that Riju is currently training at the North Gerudo Ruins. Following their conversation, "Riju of Gerudo Town" will begin. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Riju at the North Gerudo Ruins during the Sand Shroud. is a recurring character in . Biography Rik is a Hylian traveler who makes his way between Wetland Stable and Kakariko Village. He is something of a worrywart, often worrying about people he knows and fellow travelers such as Link. Since he frequents Kakariko Village, he is aware of the feud between the Sheikah farmers Steen and Olkin, expressing concern about the conflict. Rik is a member of the Zonai Survey Team that can be found at Wetland Stable by the Cooking Pot. He is supposed to be on his way to Kakariko Village to investigate the Ring Ruins, but he has not left yet. He says he needs to go over the directions a few more times in case he gets lost, or he needs to eat before he leaves.

The , also known as Moza's Hideaway Restaurant, is a recurring location in . The Rikoka Hills Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Rikoka Hills Well is situated next to a pair of Ruined Houses on the eastern side of the Rikoka Hills. It is located within the boundaries of the Lanayru Wetlands. Equipment The Rikoka Hills Well returns in , and it is still part of the Lanayru Wetlands. It now has an underground chamber, which Link can access by the Ladder attached to its rim. The interior features a small patch of land and a shallow pool of Water. The Well has been turned into a restaurant by Moza, where she is able to transform Dubious Food and Rock-Hard Food into edible Meals for 10 Rupees. Although there is a Cooking Pot, Moza refuses to allow Link to use it. Smoke from the Campfire below Pot rises out from inside the Well. When Link first meets Moza, she reveals that her restaurant is not open to the public yet. As part of the Side Quest "The Ultimate Dish?", she offers to fix one of his Failed Dishes for him. Since it is his first time visiting, she gives him a discount of five Rupees. While Cooking Link's new Meal, Moza secretly adds Monster Extract, resulting in Monster Stew. Afterwards, "The Ultimate Dish?" will be completed. If Link comes back, Moza reveals that her restaurant is now officially open. Creatures

is a recurring character in . Biography Rima is an elderly Gerudo who can be found in Gerudo Town. Rima is always sitting under a tarp across from The Noble Canteen. Rima was the captain of the guard of Gerudo Town before she retired and was replaced with Buliara. If Link speaks to Rima, she comments that she feels like she has met Link before even though she has no Hylian acquaintances and has never left Gerudo Town before. Rima expresses disappointment that she cannot relax after retiring. Link asks what happened and Rima explains that a gang of thieves recently stole Riju's Thunder Helm from the Gerudo Town palace. She feels that it is especially unfortunate that the stolen object was a valued heirloom. Rima says that if she was still in charge, she would strictly discipline the guards. Rima is upset that the guards did not prevent the theft of the Thunder Helm and believes this never would have happened when she was captain of the guard. She also says that Buliara should have been on the front lines of another recent incident. Link again asks what happened and Rima explains that Riju's Sand Seal, Patricia, got scared by a monster and pulled Riju toward the Divine Beast Vah Naboris. Rima says that although Naboris strikes anyone who approaches with lightning, Riju managed to escape, prompting Buliara to stay at Riju's side at all times. If Link speaks to Rima during the night, she will sit up and complain about the noisy young ones at The Noble Canteen. Rima wishes she could fix their attitudes.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Ring Garland Shop is a Shop in Kakariko Village. It is operated by Koko, who can be found at the stand between 9:00 AM and 9:00 PM. She opened the Shop to sell Ring Garland souvenirs to tourists visiting the Ring Ruins. Each Ring Garland costs only five Rupees, as Koko wants to make many people happy with them. When Link purchases a Ring Garland, Koko will add extra love to it before allowing him to take it. After buying a Garland, Link will be unable to buy another until the next day.

Riogok Shrine, designated by the trial name Force Transfer, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Riogok Shrine is a Shrine of Light located in the northwestern corner of the Great Plateau, west of the Forest of Spirits. It corresponds to the Kogoir Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|Link moving the Lever Switch in the Shrine The entrance chamber of Riogok Shrine is divided into two separate chambers, each with its own Gear and separated by a portcullis. These Gears sit parallel from each other and both possess shafts with pinions pointed toward each other. These pinions are separated by a small gap, which can be bridged by merging a nearby Pole in the entrance to one of their fillets between the teeth with Ultrahand. A nearby Shock Switch controls the Gear to the right, which can cause the second Gear to move if the Pole has been positioned properly. When the second Gear moves, the portcullis to the second chamber will lift. Inside the second chamber, there is a second pole along the floor, a ladder leading to a lower level on the left, two stone slabs along a rail on the wall to the left, a recess in the wall along the back with a Treasure Chest, and a broken Lever Switch controlling a portcullis to a side chamber on the right. By merging the Pole onto the broken Lever Switch, Link can open the room to the right to find a third Pole, which is necessary to advance to the end of the Shrine. thumb|right|320px|A solution to the Gear puzzle One of the teeth on the second Gear is longer and thinner than the others. By merging a Pole to it, it can be used to push the bottom stone slab along the rail on the left. If the third pole is merged vertically onto the slab, it can be used to push the second slab upward to the end of the Shrine. Link can reach a Rauru and Sonia Statue by using Ascend on the stone slabs. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Riola Spring is located in West Necluda. It can be found to the south of Mount Floria, where it is the origin of one of the Waterfalls that make up the Floria Falls. It frequently Thunderstorms in the area, and the land that surrounds the Spring is composed of steep cliffs covered in long Grass and tropical Palm Trees. The remains of three flooded Zonai Ruin structures are also situated within the Spring. Farosh will often emerge from Riola Spring, creating Updrafts and Winds as she does so. She flies down the Floria Falls, doubling back towards Riola Spring after reaching Rassla Lake in the south. She then enters and exits Riola Spring one more time before departing for the skies. A total of ten Treasure Chests can be found at Riola Spring. Six of these are metallic Treasure Chests that have sunken below the Water, and two of them are wooden Chest trapped under Boulders in the Zonai Ruin structures. In all, these Chest contain one Soldier's Spear, one Phrenic Bow, 10 Arrows, five Fire Arrows, five Arrows, one Opal, and two Purple Rupees. left|40px Link can find two Korok Seed Puzzles at Riola Spring. One is a Race that starts at the Floria Falls, right at the base of the Waterfall that flows from Riola Spring. It ends at the top of the Waterfall, which Link must Swim up before time runs out. The second Puzzle is a metallic Boulder which must be placed into the easternmost Zonai Ruin using Magnesis. Whenever Link solves one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Materials Many Mighty Thistles can be found around Riola Spring. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Korok Seeds

is an Item in . Location and Uses Ripened Flint is a rare mineral that is indistinguishable from regular Flint. Gorons are only able to identify a piece of Ripened Flint by consuming it. It is described as having sharp edges and a "gravelly mouthfeel", and it leaves particulate between one's teeth. Gorons consider it polite to eat Ripened Flint by rolling it below their tongues as it dissolves. At the beginning of the Side Quest "Cash In on Ripened Flint", Gomo requests that Link bring him pieces of Flint so that he can taste Ripened Flint. is a recurring character in . Biography Ripp is a Gerudo soldier who guards the Kara Kara Bazaar. She sometimes patrols around the Bazaar. When Link first meets Ripp, she welcomes him to Kara Kara Bazaar and recommends resting in the Bazaar before heading to Gerudo Town. However, Ripp explains that Link will not be able to get into Gerudo Town due to him being a man. She recommends staying away from Gerudo Town anyway because of the storm caused by the Divine Beast Vah Naboris and tells him to be careful if he plans to travel there. If Link asks Ripp about Gerudo Town, she tells him that it is to the southwest and is the biggest town in the Gerudo Desert. She goes on to explain that Gerudo Town is famous for trade and that there is a law forbidding men from entering the city. If Link asks about the Divine Beast, Ripp explains that it was once the guardian deity for the Gerudo people, but suddenly started acting up. She says that there is nothing they can do to stop it because it is protected by a fierce sandstorm and lightning. Ripp says that it probably will not head toward the Kara Kara Bazaar, but she keeps an eye on it regardless. Link thanks Ripp for her vigilance, but she replies that it is only her job. Ripp also warns Link to be prepared for the Desert, explaining that it is very hot during the day and very cold at night. If Link speaks to Ripp while wearing the Gerudo Outfit, she comments that Link is the second Hylian she has seen wearing Gerudo clothing, referring to Vilia. Ripp thinks that the other Hylian looked more Gerudo and is puzzled why Gerudo clothing is so popular among Hylians. If Link speaks to Ripp while searching for the man who discovered a way into Gerudo Town, he asks Ripp if she has seen a merchant. Ripp says that she has seen many merchants, explaining that all of the male merchants gather at the Bazaar in hopes of gaining access to Gerudo Town. She says that they refuse to give up despite being strictly forbidden from entering the Town. Ripp then recalls a particular female merchant at the Inn who wore Gerudo clothes. She reasons that the merchant is probably still at the Bazaar because the Divine Beast is scaring people from traveling. Before Link leaves, Ripp offers to answer Link's questions any time because it is nice to have someone to talk to while on watch. After Link calms Naboris, Ripp says that the Desert is still full of monsters. Ripp also says that it is about time for someone to relieve her duties, muttering that she really wants to get back to Gerudo Town in time to relax at The Noble Canteen.

is a recurring Armor Shop in . Features and Overview Ripped and Shredded is the resident Armor Shop of Goron City. It is owned by Rogaro, who stands at the front desk at all hours. Pyle also works for the Armor Shop, directing travelers inside as they enter Goron City. Due to Divine Beast Vah Rudania creating a Scorching Climate in the Eldin Canyon, Ripped and Shredded has begun selling the Fireproof Armor Set. Ripped and Shredded's Armor pieces are supplied by Rohan, the local blacksmith, and they are crafted from Gems sourced from throughout the Eldin Canyon. If Link enters Ripped and Shredded not wearing any of the Fireproof Armor, Rogaro will urge him to buy his Armor. When Link expresses an interest in making a purchase at Ripped and Shredded, Rogaro states that the Fireproof Armor will help him stay cool in a Scorching Climate. After Link buys Armor, Rogaro will thank him for doing so. Should Link buy the entire Fireproof Armor Set, Rogaro claims he will have to procure a restock from Rohan. is a recurring character in . Biography Risa is a Gerudo who attends Ashai's relationship class. If Link speaks to Risa during the class, she explains that she is only taking the class to refresh her knowledge. During Ashai's relationship class, Ashai asks the class what to do in multiple different situations. Risa is always the third to stand up and answer, after Pasha and Dina; the former two provide practical answers, in contrast to Risa, who comes up with rather radical solutions. One example is what they'd do when a "handsome voe" approaches them on the street. Risa is the last to stand up and share her solution, saying that she would attack the man when he least suspects it. Ashai dismisses Risa's solution and tells her that would be illegal. Another is if they were to find an wounded voe when out and about. Risa determines that she'd take him back to her in a covert manor, and assist him in rejuvenation, seemingly forgetting that his entry into her house is forbidden under Gerudo law. Ms. Ashai considers it touching, but laments that is can be considered kidnapping. The final event posed on the class is being erratically engaged in conversation with a voe whom they had been attempting to have notice them. Risa deduces that she'd have use sheer physical force to have said voe agree to espousal. Their teacher is naturally taken aback and suggests that they discuss this answer later.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Rising Island Chain is the set of Sky Islands in the Hebra Mountains Sky. Its lowest Island is situated just above Hebra Peak, while its highest can be found below the Wind Temple. The Sky Islands advance to the northeast before they wrap back around to the southeast below the Wind Temple. The entire Chain features a unique architectural style in comparison to other Sky Islands. As a result, they also produce unique types of Ruins Rubble. In addition, the Islands feature several Flying Ships. Prior to the defeat of Colgera as part of "Tulin of Rito Village", the entire Rising Island Chain will be under the effect of a constant Blizzard. After Colgera is defeated, the Blizzard will dissipate above 0807 elevation. During the Main Quest "Tulin of Rito Village", Tulin claims he saw a figure resembling Zelda on the Rising Island Chain near Hebra Peak, who thereafter flew above the clouds. Soon afterwards, Link and Tulin receive permission from Teba to investigate the source of the Blizzard plaguing Hebra. As a result, they use the Rising Island Chain to reach the center of the storm. When they reach the area where Tulin saw Princess Zelda, he is distracted upon seeing a Flying Ship. The pair then hear the voice of the Sage of Wind calling out to them from the cloud above. While looking up, they see a flash of Lightning that illuminates the silhouette of the Wind Temple, and since the circumstances remind him of the "Song of the Stormwind Ark", Tulin wonders if it recounts a true story. Since Zelda is nowhere to be seen, Tulin decides that they should continue heading toward the Wind Temple. As Link and Tulin approach the Sky Island containing Kahatanaum Shrine, Tulin remarks that he has never been so high into the Sky. He also warns Link to be careful about the Freezing Climate. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Risoka Snowfield is located in the Gerudo Highlands. Kema Kosassa Shrine sits on the western side of the Snowfield at the foot of Mount Agaat. Areas Enemies Fallen Debris are now scattered across Risoka Snowfield, and a three-tiered Monster Stronghold has been constructed in it. As the external entrances to the lower two floors of the Stronghold are boarded up, Link can only enter it by climbing through the left eye hole of the top skull-shaped rock. Three Boulders can be found on the top floor of the Stronghold, accompanied by several Iron Boxes. An Ice Like is located on the second floor of the structure, guarding the breakable rocks blocking access to the bottom floor. Three Black Moblins rest around a Campfire on the bottom floor. The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Rito Stable is a Stable that is located in the Tabantha Frontier, not far from Rito Village. It is named for its proximity to the Rito of Rito Village. The Stable features a lumber yard behind the yurt, where several felled Cedar Trees can be found. The Stable's two Signs direct travelers to the Flight Range, Rospro Pass, and Rito Village. A Cooking Pot can be found in front of the Horses' feeding trough, and several Wooden Boxes and a covered Wagon sit near a lone Cedar Tree on the north side of the Stable. Inside Rito Stable, there is a Poster depicted a Recipe for Spicy Meat Stew. A copy of the Rumor Mill: Volume 2, which details rumors about the Master Sword, also sits open on the table. As with all other Stables, Beedle can be found either within or outside of Rito Stable, where he sells his wares. Before Link completes the relevant Side Quest, Shrine Quest, Rito Stable is one of the places that Kass stops on his journey, and he will offer to play an "Ancient Song" for Link while there. During the day, the Stable worker Ariane sweeps the grounds. Another worker, Lester, sits at the Cooking Pot with Ponthos. The travelers Kanny and Falmark both stop at Rito Stable on their journeys. Rito Stable is run by Galli, who mans both its Horse-boarding and Inn services. When staying at Rito Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Galli explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Galli offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Galli will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Galli will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. When Link speaks to Lester at Rito Stable, he claims that he wants to make Curry Rice, but he does not have the Goron Spice necessary to do so. As part of the "Curry for What Ails You" Side Quest, Lester asks Link to bring him the Goron Spice that he needs. Once Link has Goron Spice, he will be able to give it to Lester for a reward of a Purple Rupee. After completing this Side Quest, Link is able to continue trading Goron Spice with Lester, receiving Hylian Rice in turn. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Rito Village is a settlement located on an island at the center of Lake Totori on the Tabantha Frontier. The Village was built around a giant stone pillar, with a vertical construction that is suited to the Rito's ability to fly. A small grove of Cedar Trees can be found below the Village proper. Several bridges also connect Rito Village to Rito Stable nearby. Kaneli, who is knowledgeable about the history of the Champions, is the current chieftain. Due to the isolation imposed on Hebra by the Tanagar Canyon, very few travelers visit Rito Village. Before to the Great Calamity 100 years ago, Zelda visited Rito Village twice to ask Revali to become a Champion, due to Revali delaying in giving her a response. After Link was appointed as her knight, she once again traveled to Rito Village on official business, resulting in the events of the "Revali's Flap" Recovered Memory. When Calamity Ganon returned, the only known casualty from Rito Village was Revali. To honor both their Champion and the other lives lost on the day of the Calamity, the Rito named one of their flight platforms Revali's Landing. Prior to Link awakening from his Slumber of Restoration, Divine Beast Vah Medoh was reactivated, at which point it began circling the Village and shooting at the Rito. Wishing to protect their home, Teba and Harth attempted to face the Divine Beast, which resulted in Harth getting injured. When Link arrives in Rito Village, Teba will be absent, with Kaneli believing he is preparing for another attack on Vah Medoh. As part of the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh (Quest)" Main Quest, Kaneli asks Link to help Teba. Once Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been calmed, Revali will be able to guide it so it perches on top of the Village's spire, where it takes aim at Hyrule Castle. As a reward for saving Rito Village, Kaneli will allow Link to take the Great Eagle Bow, which is located in a Treasure Chest nearby. "The Bird in the Mountains" Shrine Quest, "The Spark of Romance" Side Quest, and "The Apple of My Eye" Side Quest can all be obtained at Rito Village. Additionally, after Divine Beast Vah Medoh is appeased, the "Find Kheel" Side Quest and "The Ancient Rito Song" Shrine Quest will become available. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles can be found in Rito Village. The first is a Balloon in a hole in its pillar, which Link must destroy using Archery. The second Puzzle is a Natural Hiding Spot, which takes the form of a Rock on a spire in the southwest corner of the Village. Whenever Link solves one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. is a recurring character in . Biography Rivan is a Zora who wields a Silverscale Spear and stands guard at the entrance of Zora's Domain with his daughter, Dunma. He is the son of Trello, whom he warns Link against seeing due to the prejudice older Zora have against Hylians. He is over 130 years old. When Link first encounters him, Rivan will reveal that they used to swim together when he was a child at the age of 30. During this time he was friends with Bazz and Gaddison, the three of them forming the Big Bad Bazz Brigade.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The River of the Dead is a body of Cold Water located on the western portion of the Great Plateau. It is fed by a Waterfall originating from Mount Hylia. Due to its altitude and the presence of Cold Water, the air around the River of the Dead is afflicted by a Freezing Climate, which requires Link to have at least one level of Cold Resistance to traverse the area without taking damage. The River flows west and leads off of the Great Plateau, ending in a Waterfall that feeds into the Regencia River. Just before this is a damaged wooden bridge, which spans the entirety of the River. To cross it, Link must use the Magnesis Rune to manipulate a nearby Metal Plate, laying flat against the bridge's planks. A Raft can be found at the end of a Dock near the River's center. Scattered on the riverbank are various Trees, patches of Grass, unlit Campfires, and Fallen Guardians. A Cooking Pot can be found in the remains of a Ruined House. There is a cave behind the Waterfall that feeds the River of the Dead which houses two Treasure Chests. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Riverside Stable is a Stable located along the Hylia River in Hyrule Field. It is operated by Ember, who manages the Stable's Horse-boarding services as well as its Inn. Inside, Link can find a Poster depicting a Recipe for Crab Stir-Fry. The Stable also features a short Dock with a Raft tied to its end. At the rear of the Stable are two small fenced off islands that act as pens for the resident Highland Sheep and Cuccos. The travelers Endai, Kazul, and Spoone all stop at Riverside Stable as part of their journeys. If Link saves Leekah at Horwell Bridge, she will flee to Riverside Stable for safety. While traveling back to Korok Forest, Hestu visits Riverside Stable, having gotten lost. After upgrading Link's Inventory four times, he will remember the way and depart from the Stable. Lastly, during the "Captured Memories" Main Quest, Pikango can be found at Riverside Stable, where he is painting the view of Death Mountain. When spoken to, he is able to identify the site of the second Picture in Link's Album, which is Lake Kolomo. When staying at Riverside Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Ember explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Ember offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Ember will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Ember will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. As part of the "A Royal Recipe" Side Quest, Gotter, a worker at Riverside Stable, asks Link to share with him Recipes from the Castle Library Books if he ever finds them. When Link makes either a Fruitcake or a Monster Cake for Gotter, he will try them immediately. He then rewards Link with a Silver Rupee. Parcy, a resident of Riverside Stable, will recount to Link that she once plundered Hyrule Castle in search of pieces of the Royal Guard's Series, though she was unable to find any. During "The Royal Guard's Gear" Side Quest, Link must bring a piece to Parcy, who gives him a Gold Rupee as a reward. When Downloadable Content Pack is active, a copy of the Super Rumor Mill V4 appears on the table inside Riverside Stable. As part of the "EX Royal Guard Rumors" Side Quest, Link is tasked with reading this Book to learn more about the location of the Royal Guard Set. From the Super Rumor Mill V4, Link discovers the specific locations in Hyrule Castle that the individual Armor have been hidden. It features a Ladder, which allows Link to easily access its interior. The Ladder leads into a small pool of Water, though the rest of the chamber is filled with several pieces of Lumber, Boards, and a Barrel. Due to its position under Hylia River, the walls are Wet Walls that Link is unable to Climb. From 5:00 PM to 10:00 PM, Tye will Sleep while leaning against the Riverside Stable Well. During Rain, he takes shelter under the Well's roof. The Riverside Stable Well is one of several Wells that Fera can be found in prior to beginning the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?". She rates the Well's Water quality as fair and its moss growth as extensive, in addition to confirming the presence of Brightcaps. Once her Side Quest has started, she leaves for the Lookout Landing Well. Materials Equipment

is a recurring character in . Biography Robbie is a Sheikah who researched Guardians at the Royal Ancient Lab before the Great Calamity. According to Purah, he was her subordinate as a researcher, though Robbie does not hold a high opinion of Purah's abilities as a researcher. Robbie and Purah worked together with Zelda on her expeditions to excavate ancient Sheikah technology, leading to the discovery of the Sheikah Slate. Robbie was responsible for restoring mobility to the Guardians. When Link was injured during the Great Calamity and subsequently saved by two Sheikah warriors, Robbie took Link to the Shrine of Resurrection along with Purah. Following the Great Calamity, Robbie fled to the northeastern reaches of Akkala, where he founded the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab and continued his research. Robbie and Purah purposefully set up their labs in different places so that if one of them died the other would still be around to help Link when he awoke. Robbie was easily able to destroy hostile Guardians near his lab because he had spent so much time researching them. About 40 or 50 years after the Great Calamity, Robbie created the first Ancient Arrows. When Robbie was 90, a woman named Jerrin traveled from Kakariko Village to assist him. They ended up getting married and had a son together, named Granté. In preparation of Link's fated standoff against Calamity Ganon, Robbie developed a machine that can generate Ancient Soldier Gear in exchange for Ancient Materials and Rupees. He dubbed the machine "Cherry", after his first love. Due to this, Jerrin becomes enraged whenever Robbie refers to the machine as Cherry and insists that he refers to her as the Ancient Oven instead. Around the time that Link awoke from the Slumber of Restoration, the Ancient Furnace outside the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab lost its Blue Flame, rendering Cherry inoperable. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Robbie posing with his finger pointing up at the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab.|Robbie posing Link first encounters Robbie after the Hylian Champion is caught examining Cherry inside the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab. Regardless of whether Link affirms or denies this, Robbie will begrudge the fact that he can't confirm that Link has truly returned without observing the scars on his body first. As he deems regaining control of the Guardians to be too difficult, he instead offers to equip Link with an arsenal to combat Ganon. is a recurring character in . Biography Robsten is a Hylian man who can be found at the Kara Kara Bazaar. Robsten is part of a group of traveling Hylian merchants, with Benja as their leader. He is stranded at the Kara Kara Bazaar because men are not allowed into Gerudo Town. When Link first speaks to Robsten, he asks whether Link is a merchant or a traveler. If Link says he is a merchant, he says that he is also a merchant and concludes that Link must also be stranded at the Bazaar. If Link says he is a traveler, Robsten just explains that he is a merchant. Robsten then continues to explain that his group wanted to sell their goods at Gerudo Town, but were not allowed in because they are men. Their leader, Benja, went to Gerudo Town to negotiate and figure out a way to get into the town. Robsten says that their leader has not come back yet, speculating that he is still figuring out a way to get inside. Robsten feels that Gerudo Town is so close, yet so far. He also comments that most travelers cannot get farther than the Town because of the Divine Beast Vah Naboris. If Link speaks to Robsten while wearing the Gerudo Outfit, he is shocked to see him and thinks he is a girl. Robsten then asks Link if he is there by himself, commenting that the Desert is dangerous. Robsten promises to be there for him if he is ever afraid. If Link speaks to Robsten while searching for the man who discovered a way into Gerudo Town, Robsten is expressing worry that their boss has not returned from Gerudo Town and speculates that he will not be coming back that day. When Link informs Robsten with Benja's news about the man who sneaks into Gerudo Town and travels between the Town and the Bazaar, Robsten is surprised and says that it must be true if his boss says so. Robsten claims to have never seen a sneaky guy around the Bazaar, but does recall seeing a pretty Hylian girl at the general store who dresses like a Gerudo. Robsten then wonders where she bought the Gerudo clothes and wonders if wearing them would allow him to sneak into Gerudo Town, but quickly dismisses the idea. After Link calms Naboris, Robsten sits beside Benja and says that he never figured out how to sneak into Gerudo Town.

Rock-Hard Food is a recurring Meal in . Location and Uses Rock-Hard Food is the result of an invalid Cooking Recipe. It appears when Link attempts to cook food containing Wood or Ores. Rock-Hard Food only restores a quarter of one of Link's Hearts and has no effects. Eating these Meals is noted to be difficult. Moza, the aspiring chef who can be found near Ishto Soh Shrine, has a recipe called the lavish Meat dish that will only result in Rock-Hard Food. She tells Link to prepare either bird Meat or steak and then to throw in some Ore. If Link calls the recipe gross, she scolds him for being rude and asks how else one is supposed to be a lavish Meat dish. However, Moza admits that the resulting Meal is always Rock-Hard Food, but she does not understand how it gets that rocky.

"Rock for Sale" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview At some point, a resident of Tarrey Town named Hagie chanced upon a Mysterious Crystal in the nearby Hudson Construction Site. Thinking it valuable, he took it with him intending to sell it to someone for a boon. However in spending more time with the Crystal, he grew disturbed by it and is now eager to sell it quickly. The Shrine Quest begins after Link expresses curiosity about the Crystal. Hagie explains how he found it and offers to sell it to Link for 100 Rupees. Link can agree to the price or haggle for something lower, to which Haggie offers to sell for 80 Rupees instead. Regardless of Link's answer, the Shrine Quest begins as Hagie's wife, Ruli, interrupts and scolds him for trying to sell junk to people. She dismisses the Crystal as a large piece of Flint and estimates it as no more than 50 Rupees in value. Though Hagie tries to reason with her that Link may have been willing to settle for a higher price, he falters at his wife's expression and caves. If Link denies the offer, Ruli continues to scold Hagie for damaging the spirit of Tarrey Town. However, if Link agrees to buy it, Hagie moves the Crystal behind his station and informs Link that he will accept no refunds on the deal. With a successful purchase, the Shrine Quest will be complete. Objectives

are Enemies in . Characteristics Rock Likes are Like Likes that can be found primarily in dark locations such as Caves and the Depths. They attack by spitting Boulders at Link. They have an outer layer of rocky armor that protects them from damage. Like other Like Likes, their bulbous, red tongues are extremely sensitive, but can only be damaged after their armor is broken. Rock Likes intermittently reveal their tongues, swallowing Link if he is too close when they retract them into their mouths. If they swallow Link, they steal one of his Shield or Weapons before spitting him out. If stunned in the few seconds they take to swallow the stolen item, they will drop it. Their armor can be destroyed by other rocky items such as the Boulders they spit, and by explosive items such as Bomb Flowers. With their armor destroyed, they closely resemble standard Like Likes, but retain the ability to spit Boulders. Like other Like Likes, Rock Likes eat Crabs, Fish, Frogs, Fruits, Insects, Lizards, Meats, and Mushrooms. When defeated, they may drop one or two bundles of five Arrows. They are guaranteed to drop a Like Like Stone, as well as any Bows, Shields, or Weapons they may have stolen. If they have not stolen any Equipment, they will instead drop an Iron Treasure Chest with contents varying based on the Rock Like's location. Rock Likes in the Depths may also drop one or two pieces of Zonaite.

, also known as , are recurring Enemies in the . Characteristics In , Rock Octoroks are Octoroks that adapted from water to land and have the ability to spit rocks. They sleep with rocks on their head as camouflage until it senses nearby prey and attack by spitting a rock. Link can deflect the rock back at them with a Shield to defeat them. In , Rock Octoroks primarily live in Eldin Canyon and Eldin Mountains, but they can also be found in Gerudo Highlands. They inhale massive loads of air and then spit out an explosive fire rock at their target. Getting too close to one causes it to take cover and hide underground with the rock on its head as protection. Link can defeat them by placing a Remote Bomb in its path while it inhales air and detonating the Bomb after the Octorok swallows it. If a Rock Octorok swallows a piece of Rusty Gear during the inhaling process, it will pause to crunch it in its mouth and, afterwards, shoot it back out as a clean counterpart. After being cleaned, there is a 50% chance that the item will be shot out as its corresponding item in the Traveler's Gear archetype, a 35% chance that it will be of the Soldier's Gear, a 10% chance that it will be of the Knight's Gear, and a 5% chance that it will be of the Royal Gear. The exact Weapon Bonus applied is randomly chosen based on the tier of Weapon Bonus and type of Equipment receiving it.
