are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Location and Uses Rock Patterns are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle found throughout Hyrule. When Link initially finds a Rock Pattern, its geometric pattern of Rocks will be incomplete. Typically, the missing Rock can be found in the direction of the empty spot. By finding Rocks nearby and placing them in any empty spots, Link will find a hidden Korok, which gives him a Korok Seed. List of Rock Patterns A total of four Rock Patterns can be found in Akkala. A total of 10 Rock Patterns can be found in Central Hyrule. A total of eight Rock Patterns can be found in Eldin. A total of six Rock Patterns can be found in Faron. A total of 14 Rock Patterns can be found in Gerudo. A total of eight Rock Patterns can be found in Hebra. A total of nine Rock Patterns can be found in Lanayru. A total of 10 Rock Patterns can be found in Necluda. Rock Patterns in operate in the same manner as they did in . Unlike in , Rock Patterns can be solved using Rocks that have been Fused to a Weapon or Shield, provided that Link positions them correctly. Whenever Link completes a Rock Pattern, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Rock Salt can be found by destroying Ore Deposits across Hyrule Kingdom. It can also be purchased from the Goron Gusto Shop, the Coral Reef, and the travelling merchant Mezer. Though it cannot be eaten, it can be used to make Meals in a Cooking Pot. It can also be an ingredient to make Peach Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop. Rock Salt is required in order to Cook Fish Pie, a Crab Omelet with Rice, Crab Risotto, Cream of Mushroom Soup, Cream of Vegetable Soup, Creamy Meat Soup, Creamy Seafood Soup, a Gourmet Meat and Rice Bowl, a Meat and Rice Bowl, Meat Pie, Monster Rice Balls, a Mushroom Omelet, Mushroom Risotto, a Prime Meat and Rice Bowl, Salmon Risotto, Salt-Grilled Crab, Salt-Grilled Fish, Salt-Grilled Meat, Salt-Grilled Greens, Salt-Grilled Gourmet Meat, Salt-Grilled Mushrooms, Salt-Grilled Prime Meat, Seafood Fried Rice, Seafood Paella, a Vegetable Omelet, Vegetable Risotto, Veggie Cream Soup, and Wheat Bread. Rock Salt is an Ingredient that can be combined with another Ingredient to make a Smoothie. When used in one, it usually imbues the Energy Recovery Added Effect, which causes the Smoothie to restore a portion of Princess Zelda's Energy. Rock Salt may be found by destroying Rocks. It can also be purchased in bulk in Goron City for 30 Rupees per piece. A portion of Rock Salt can be sold for 6 Rupees. As a reward for completing the Side Quest "Glide Path", Seko gives Zelda 10 pieces of Rock Salt, which he claims were his snack. The following table lists the Smoothies that are created by combining each Ingredient with Rock Salt. Other Appearances

are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Rocks under Boulders go unnamed in . Overview Rocks under Boulders are a type of Natural Hiding Spot. In order to solve the Korok Seed Puzzle, Link must remove the Boulder, which he can do by attaching Octo Balloons to it or hitting it while it is affected by Stasis. This reveals the Rock beneath the Boulder. When Link picks up the Rock, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Like in , Rocks under Boulders are a variety of Korok Seed Puzzle. Link can move the Boulder out of the way using Ultrahand, allowing him access to the Rock underneath. Picking up the Rock reveals a Korok, who gives Link a Korok Seed.

Rocks under Leaves are a recurring Korok Seed Puzzle in . Overview Rocks under Leaves are a variety of Korok Seed Puzzle that involves a Rock which is hidden beneath a Pile of Leaves. In order to access the Rock, Link must disperse the Leaves, which can be done by striking them with a Weapon or burning them with Fire. When Link picks up the Rock, it is revealed to be a Natural Hiding Spot, and a Korok will appear to give him a Korok Seed. As is the case in , Rocks under Leaves are a type of Korok Seed Puzzle in . After Link clears away the Pile of Leaves, he will be able to pick up the Rock. This causes a Korok to appear, who gives him a Korok Seed.

are recurring Items and Objects in . Rockets go unnamed in . Location and Uses A large metal Rocket can be found next to the counter in the Bomb Shop. Schematics pasted to the walls indicate that is meant to fly to the Moon, and could be powered by a large Bomb built into its base. Rockets are Zonai Devices in . When activated, they provide powerful propulsive force in the direction they face but burn out after a few seconds. Consequently, they are best used for devices that need a brief burst of speed or require a strong force to make them start moving. When Fused to a Shield, they allow Link to jet upward a considerable distance. When Fused to an Arrow, they will cause the Arrow to fly forward with considerable speed and accuracy. Other Appearances Rockets are one of many Zonai Devices that Warriors are able to use during combat.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses features two varieties of Rod: the Fire Rod, obtained from the Skull Woods, shoots fireballs, and the Ice Rod, which fires balls of Ice that freeze Enemies. allows Link to use the Rod of Seasons to change the current season. The Temple of Time contains the Dominion Rod, which can be used to animate specific Statues. features six varieties of elemental Rods, all of which are wielded by different varieties of Wizzrobe. The lower tier of Rods is composed of Fire Rods, Ice Rods, and Lightning Rods. Fire Rods shoot a single ball of Fire, Ice Rods release clouds of cold air that freeze Enemies, and Lightning Rods fire balls of Electricity. The higher tier is made up of Meteor Rods, Blizzard Rods, and Thunderstorm Rods. The Meteor and Thunderstorm Rods shoot three balls instead of one, and the Blizzard Rod releases three cold air clouds. Fire and Meteor Rods were crafted by an ancient magician, the Ice and Blizzard Rods are crafted from refined ice from Hebra Mountains and Hebra Peak respectively, and the Lightning and Thunderstorm Rods bear Gems charged with Electricity from Hyrule Ridge. Magic Rods are sold by Bargainer Statues in exchange for Poes. They bear more powerful effects when Fused with Gems. They were used by an ancient magician who used his skills to draw out the latent strength within Gems. Opal Magic Rods fire globules of Water, Ruby Rods launch balls of Fire, Sapphire Rods release clouds of cold air, Topaz Rods shoot orbs of Electricity, and Star Fragment Rods shoot orbs of Light. Amber and Diamonds are the only Gems that do not produce special attributes. The Tri Rod is a Key Item gifted to Princess Zelda by Tri. It can be used by Zelda to create Echoes of Enemies and Objects, which can be used in combat, for solving puzzles, and for traversing Hyrule. Other Appearances Rods are Items that can be wielded by all Warriors in , as well as by Wizzrobes. Located on the left bumper wheel with Apples, they are limited charge attack items that inflict conditions on Enemies, giving the Weak-Point Gauges of Elemental Enemies of the opposite element a cracked effect and making them drain faster. The Fire Rod lights Enemies and Bomb Barrels on Fire, and cracks the Gauges of Ice Enemies. The Ice Rod freezes Enemies in place and affects the Weak-Point Gauges of Fire Enemies. The Lightning Rod electrocutes Enemies and cracks Gauge of Enemies exposed to Water, Rain, or Elemental Enemies related to Water, such as Waterblight Ganon. Rods are obtained when their respective Wizzrobe is first slain. The Fire Rod is first obtained when the Warriors slay their first Fire Wizzrobe in the "The Battle of Hyrule Field" Scenario, and the other two are obtained from Ice and Electric Wizzrobes respectively. the Warriors slay their first Fire Wizzrobe in the "The Battle of Hyrule Field" Scenario, and the other two are obtained from Ice and Electric Wizzrobes respectively. They each need their own type of elemental energy as fuel for their attacks, and the amount of charges they have carries over into future battles. While they innately have three charges, completing the "The Research of Rods" and "It Takes Two" Quests both reward the Warriors with one additional charge to all Rods. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Rodai Lake is located on the southern foothills of Mount Floria in West Necluda. Its southwest edge is bounded by a pair of Waterfalls, which are part of the Floria Falls that feed into Lake Floria in the south. The remains of a single Zonai Ruin structure is situated upon the Lake's bed. When Farosh flies over the Floria Falls, strong Winds and Updrafts will appear over Rodai Lake. Five Treasure Chests can be found within Rodai Lake. Two of them are made of wood, and they are trapped inside the Zonai Ruin by a metal Boulder. One contains a bundle of five Arrows, while the other contains five Shock Arrows. Two metal Chests lie at the bottom of the Lake, one containing a Purple Rupee and the other another bundle of five Shock Arrows. Lastly, a stone Chest containing a Topaz can be found between Rodai Lake's two Waterfalls. Creatures Enemies Materials Areas

is a recurring character in . Biography Rogaro is the owner of the Armor shop Ripped and Shredded in Goron City. He sells the Fireproof Armor, and highly recommends it to Link if he intends on scaling Death Mountain. Rogaro states that the Armor he sells are intended for tourists, as Gorons do not normally wear clothes. If Link talks to Rogaro without any Fireproof Armor on, his eyes widen and he urges Link to quickly buy his gear, telling him that it is not a good time to talk or be casual. Like many other shop owners, Link can also sell items to Rogaro if needed. If Link tries to sell anything without any flame protection, Rogaro tells him to do so quickly.

is a recurring character in . Biography Rohan is a master Goron blacksmith who lives in Goron City. His smithy and house is located in the City's northeast. Rohan is strict and serious about his trade, and does not like to be disturbed while he is working or resting. He is known to supply the Flamebreaker Set of Armor sold at Ripped and Shredded. He is also the mentor of Fugo, who is training to become his successor. According to Fugo, Rohan had fought the Igneo Talus at Darunia Lake when he was young to grow strong, and he is said to have defeated every Igneo Talus in existence. For likely the same reason, he had sent Fugo to defeat the Igneo Talus at the Lake as part of his training. Rohan is able to reforge the Boulder Breaker if it breaks or is lost, requiring that Link brings a Cobble Crusher, five pieces of Flint, and a Diamond. Rohan also expresses skepticism of Link's inheritance of the sword, but accepts it for what it is.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Rok Woods are a large, wooded area south of the Skull Lake in Deep Akkala. The Rok Woods are filled with autumn-tinted Trees which hide a wide array of Creatures and Forest Octoroks. Ore Deposits can be found along the rock walls on the western side of the Woods. A Korok can be found underneath a Rock hidden under a Rock Slab to the west side of the Rok Woods. A second Korok can be found in the forest, under a Rock atop a large Tree near the center of the grove. Creatures Enemies

is a recurring character in . Biography Rola is a Hylian member of the Sheikah tribe who owns The Curious Quiver, a General Store in Kakariko Village. When Link first visits her, she mentions that she has not had a customer in a long while. She explains that this is due to the fact that not many of their younger villagers need a Bow. Rola is excited for the opportunity of a young new customer and implores that Link take his time browsing. When he bids her farewell, she admits that he lifted her spirits high enough to even miss her husband. Should Link come back at a later time with a Bow, Rola will have a Side Quest available for him, "Arrows of Burning Heat". Once Link completes the Quest, she will begin to fawn over him due to his skill in archery and has to remind herself to get back to business. Should Link complete the side quest without a bow, Rola becomes somewhat disheartened by Link's lack of consideration for her feelings, and comments men will always disappoint womankind. If Link decides to leave the conversation without selling her anything, she becomes disappointed. Still, she gives him the advice to sell Ore for some quick Rupees should he need them. In the Journal of Various Worries, Rola notes that Link seems good with a Bow, and that she hopes he will "nock an arrow" for her at some point. She signs the Journal entry with the pseudonym "Lonely Arrow Girl" to remain anonymous.

is a recurring Inn in . Features and Overview The Rollin' Inn is an Inn in Goron City. The front desk is staffed by Tray, while Volcon stands outside advertising the Inn. Since she is a visitor to Goron City, the Gerudo traveler Ramella Sleeps at the Inn at night, where she dreams about Gems. After Divine Beast Vah Rudania has been calmed, Volcon believes tourists will begin to stay at the Inn again. When staying at the Rollin' Inn, Link is able to Sleep in a regular Bed, which costs 20 Rupees, but he can also receive a Goron massage for 80 Rupees. The Inn's massages are done by applying pressure to a person's back while they lay on a rock hard Bed. While it may end up hurting Link, Tray insists that he will feel energized when he wakes up afterwards. Upon deciding to stay at the Rollin' Inn, Tray allows Link to choose when he will wake up. Once Link makes his selection, Tray will send him off to Sleep. Tray wakes Link up by asking if he Slept well. If Link chooses to have a massage, Tray will call in Volcon to tend to him. Volcon responds, assuring Link that he has him covered. When Link wakes up, he will receive a temporary Stamina Wheel. Tray will then ask if he enjoyed his massage. Inhabitants Inhabitants

is a location in . Features and Overview Rolling Pastures is a mobile Shop in the form of a Wagon operated by Parga and driven by her Horse. According to Parga, she traveled from Hateno Village with it to visit Lookout Landing, where she stops to rest and sell her wares. After Link completes the Side Adventure "A New Signature Food", Parga will begin selling Hateno Cheese in addition to her normal stock. When not stationed at Lookout Landing, Parga travels along the unmarked road south past the Hyrule Field Chasm, turns to the southeast at the Hyrule Garrison Ruins, turns east at Windvane Meadow's crossroads, and then stops to rest underneath the Tree south of the Teniten Shrine. After this, she turns around and returns to Lookout Landing. Wares and Pricing

is recurring a character in . Biography Romah is a Gerudo woman who manages Hotel Oasis in Gerudo Town. If Link speaks to her, she tells him that he would love what they have to offer. Aside from the usual 20 Rupee cost of a night at an Inn, Romah also offers an 80 Rupee Spa Plan. She encourages Link to stay at the Inn and rest for a while. Romah says that despite being very popular, she will allow Link to cut to the front of the line for the Spa Plan and then asks what she can do for him. If Link asks about the Spa Plan, Romah is surprised that he has never heard of it and claims that it will fill Link with energy and a feeling of resilience to danger. She also mentions that it will relax Link and leave his skin bright and smooth. During the Spa Plan, Romah may comment on how muscular Link is for a Hylian.

is a recurring character in . Biography Ronn is a Hylian traveler and Dragon enthusiast who travels along a portion of the Hilltop High Road from Serenne Stable to Snowfield Stable. He carries an Emblazoned Shield and a Traveler's Sword. Once Link talks to Ronn, he expresses his desperation to find one of the three legendary Dragons on Hyrule. He describes it as being very large, and he claims that their bodies block out the sun when they rise into the sky. Additionally, he also states that it is supposedly the length of two-hundred people lying down, from head to toe. While traveling along Rowan Plain, Ronn asks Link on what he is searching for on his journey, after which he reveals he is searching for Dragons. According to a legend that Ronn has heard, one of them remains near a Spring, but he is unsure whether or not this is true. When Ronn reaches the Tabantha Tundra, he asks Link if he has seen a Dragon, though he immediately dismisses him before he can give an answer. Afterwards, he wonders if anyone else has ever seen them. Upon entering Snowfield Stable, Ronn considers heading back to Serenne Stable to gather more information on Dragons. While on his way back to Serenne Stable, he tells Link that he prays every morning to see a Dragon. Another legend that Ronn has heard claims that he needs to obtain the blessing of Hylia before he can see a Dragon, but he dismisses this as a fairy tale. After staring up at the sky in hopes of finding a Dragon, Ronn starts to feel neck pain. Despite this, he does not want to risk missing out on them flying. Since he keeps hearing about Dragons, he wonders if they inhabit the sky or the ground. When it Rains, Ronn decides he will rest under any wooden shelter until the Weather changes. If Link saves Ronn from any Enemies while off horseback, he is unaware of Link's help as he was running away. Alternatively, he states that he initially thought that he had a good method of avoiding Monsters. He thanks Link and rewards him with a Meal. Occasionally, Ronn will shout the term "Dinayrosh", which are the names of Dinraal, Naydra, and Farosh combined. Ronn is a member of the Zonai Survey Team. He travels with a Donkey along the paths between Woodland Stable and Foothill Stable. When Link encounters Ronn, he describes that his passion is finding Geoglyphs, and he wonders about the circumstances in which they were made. He also states that there is a Geoglyph located near Thyphlo Ruins near the Eldin Mountains. He reveals that people can travel Eldin freely since Death Mountain has stopped erupting, although Ronn thinks that Climbing it would not be easy. When he leaves Woodland Stable, he mentions that he has heard of two Geoglyphs in Eldin, the one in Thyphlo Ruins and another nearby. However, he does not know exactly where they are,

freely since Death Mountain has stopped erupting, although Ronn thinks that Climbing it would not be easy. When he leaves Woodland Stable, he mentions that he has heard of two Geoglyphs in Eldin, the one in Thyphlo Ruins and another nearby. However, he does not know exactly where they are, and he suggests searching for them from the top of a hill. After walking past Trilby Plain, Ronn states that the Geoglyph nearby seems to refuse to show itself, and he wishes that he had wings like a Bird. Once Ronn arrives at Foothill Stable, he is disappointed by the fact that his colleagues from the Zonai Survey Team have not told him any news about Geoglyphs. When it Rains, Ronn will seek shelter under a hut or a Tree. Since Eldin it does not commonly Rain in Eldin, he hopes that the Geoglyph is still in good condition. If Link saves Ronn from Enemies, he asks Link if he has been hurt during battle, and he reveals that he is not injured. He thanks Link for his bravery and gives him a Meal as a reward.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Room of Ascension is the central hub for the Lightning Temple], located on the Lightning Temple 1F above the Room of Hopeful Light. At its center, it features a Terminal that controls an elevator. This elevator is inoperable at first because the four Batteries that power it are inactive. One of the Batteries can be found on the floor behind a gate. A path around this gate can be found to the side, obscured by Stone Blocks. Another Stone Block in the southeast corner blocks an Updraft, which can be used to ascend to other floors. Additionally, a spiral staircase that can be found in the southeast section of the Room leads up to the Lightning Temple 4F. By activating all four Batteries and returning to the Terminal, Link and Riju can ascend to the Lightning Temple 7F.

The Room of Light and Shade is a location in . Features and Overview The Room of Light and Shade is a room connected to the Lightning Temple 4F. There are two chambers to the Room. The upper chamber contains a central altar with a decorative bridge over a gap, as well as a hole in the chamber floor that leads to the one below. The altar's gap is obscured by a hatch controlled by a light-sensitive Switch in the lower chamber. This Switch is located behind a rotating wall, which must be stopped with an Object in order for a Light Beam located at the center of the chamber to be redirected to it long enough to activate. When activated, the Light Beam will continue upward into the higher chamber so that it can be redirected to another light-sensitive Switch, which blocks a Battery on the Lightning Temple 4F. Enemies Zonai Devices

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Room of Offered Light is a hidden chamber on the Lightning Temple 3F, and it is protected by a Statue equipped with a light-sensitive Switch on the Lightning Temple 2F. By redirecting a Light Beam from the Room of Natural Light and the Lightning Temple 5F to the Switch, Link can move the Statue to reveal a Floor Switch that opens the passageway to the Room of Offered Light. A Light Beam protrudes from the floor of the Room of Offered Light. There is also a light-sensitive Switch above a ledge in the northeastern portion. At the opposite end of the entrance, there is a Battery behind a gate controlled by the light-sensitive Switch. By redirecting light to the Switch, Link can open the gate and access the Battery. Enemies Equipment Zonai Devices

are a type of Items in . Location and Uses Room Units are structures created by Hudson Construction as part of their Dream Home program. After purchasing a plot, Link is able to buy Room Units from Grantéson, who will also store them on his behalf. A maximum of 15 Room Units can be used at once while constructing Link's House. If placed in storage, Weapon/Bow/Shield Stand Rooms will retain any Equipment currently displayed in them (as well as their specifics such as Durability and Weapon Bonuses), so the Equipment can be accessed again if brought out of storage. List of Room Units

is a recurring character in . Biography Rotana is a Gerudo archaeologist who lives in Gerudo Town. Link can begin the Shrine Quest, "The Seven Heroines", by speaking to her. If Link speaks to Rotana, he will catch her muttering something about a sandstorm to herself before she turns around and notices Link. When Rotana notices Link, she asks what a "Hylian vai" is doing there. If Link says he has to go, Rotana becomes upset that he is leaving already and thought he wanted to hear the legend of the Seven Heroines. Rotana mutters that she hoped someone would listen to her because her sister, Pearle, will not. If Link asks Rotana what she is doing, she introduces herself and says that she was just analyzing part of an ancient text that she discovered recently. Rotana feels that she can get recognition for this discovery and that Link arriving must be fate. Rotana offers to share her research with Link if he promises to keep it secret. If Link says he has to go, Rotana becomes upset, demanding that he listens and tells him about her research anyway. If Link instead promises to keep it a secret, she will simply tell him about her research. Rotana tells Link of a temple to the east near the entrance of Gerudo Desert. She tells Link that the temple is dedicated to giant statues of the seven heroines who once protected the Gerudo people. Rotana also tells Link of the ancient scripture that she discovered there, which serves as a clue for the Shine Quest. Rotana explains that this was all she has been able to decipher so far. She also explains that people once traveled in search of the heroines' blessing, but no one has ever found it. If Link asks about the blessing, Rotana says that she is not sure what it means yet. Rotana then explains that the heroines are said to each hold a different power, which include skill, spirit, endurance, knowledge, flight, motion and gentleness. Rotana thinks they all look the same, so she is unable to decipher which heroine holds which power without understanding the entire script. Rotana is also concerned about the Divine Beast Vah Naboris wandering the Desert and hindering her research, exclaiming that Naboris has "no respect for academia." Rotana also says that she knows the place referenced in the ancient script, but she needs to finish deciphering it. If Link asks where the place is, she reiterates that it is near the entrance to the Gerudo Desert, but adds that the nearby sandstorm is a problem. She also mentions that approaching the temple will be difficult with the Divine Beast around. When Link ends the conversation, Rotana wishes that her sister, Pearle, was more like Link and took interest in her research instead of obsessing over Lady Urbosa. If Link speaks to Rotana after completing the "The Seven Heroines", she is ecstatic that the Shrine that appeared at the temple must be

Link ends the conversation, Rotana wishes that her sister, Pearle, was more like Link and took interest in her research instead of obsessing over Lady Urbosa. If Link speaks to Rotana after completing the "The Seven Heroines", she is ecstatic that the Shrine that appeared at the temple must be a trial given to her by the Seven Heroines. She believes that she will be the star of the archaeological society after she completes the trial.

The , designated by the trial name A Balanced Plan, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Rotsumamu Shrine is a Shrine of Light on the Surface. It is located in the directly southeast of the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm in the Gerudo Highlands. It corresponds to the Umamustor Lightroot in the Gerudo Highlands Depths. Themes and Navigation The Rotsumamu Shrine is functionally one large hallway divided into four levels. The first level is the entrance, which holds a seesaw that works as an unstable ramp up to the second level. On the second level, there is another seesaw that leads to the third level and a nearby metallic Barrel that can be used as a counterweight. The third level features a weighted seesaw, held down by three Iron Boxes. A Stone Slab and another Iron Box can be found near this seesaw, which can be used to displace the weight of the three Iron Boxes. By ascending to the fourth level, Link can find a Statue of Rauru and Sonia. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

The Round Spiral Staircase is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Round Spiral Staircase connects the garden of Hyrule Castle to its interior. However, its exterior entrance is covered by Malice, blocking this route for Link. The Staircase can be accessed from the Hyrule Castle Corridors via the Water Pump Room. After defeating the Glowing Eyeball found there, Link can pass through the Staircase without any obstacles. The Hyrule Castle Courtyard is found at the top of the Round Spiral Staircase. A stone Treasure Chest can be found in the Round Spiral Staircase. From inside, Link can retrieve three Ancient Arrows. Enemies Equipment Treasure Chests As in , the Round Spiral Staircase is located within the floating section of Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field. It connects Hyrule Castle B2 to the Hyrule Castle Corridors on Hyrule Castle B3. Equipment

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Rowan Plain is a flat, grassy field west of Aldor Foothills, northeast of Serenne Stable and southeast of the Forgotten Temple. The field contains groups of Horses and is loosely surrounded by a ring of Trees. In the northeastern, southeastern, and southwestern sections of the Plain are Koroks, with one in each section. In the northeastern corner, Link must shoot an acorn into a log to reveal the Korok. In the southeastern corner, Link must climb on top of a destroyed building and subsequently examine the Fairy Lights there. In the southwestern corner, Link must jump three fences in a row while riding a Horse to reveal the Korok. In a group of Trees in the northwestern section of Rowan Plains rests a Stalnox. Creatures Enemies

The is a recurring location in . The Rowan Plain Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Rowan Plain Well is a Well that can be found on the eastern end of Rowan Plain in the Great Hyrule Forest. Prior to the Great Calamity, it was part of an unnamed Hylian settlement, which now consists of a single Ruined House. Link can encounter a Traveler near the Rowan Plain Well. When spoken to, they ask if he knows the way to the Gerudo Desert. If Link claims that he does, the Traveler will be relieved. However, should Link say he does not, they will be confused, as they thought they had seen him there before. No matter how Link responds, the Traveler reveals themself to be a Yiga Footsoldier, and they proceed to attack Link. Enemies The Rowan Plain Well returns in , and it is still located in the Great Hyrule Forest. At the start of the Upheaval, a Chasm opened beneath the Well, which allows Link direct access to the Great Hyrule Forest Depths when he Climbs into it. After Link has defeated Master Kohga at least three times during the Side Adventure "Master Kohga of the Yiga Clan", Mighty Bananas will begin appearing in the Deserted House next to the Rowan Plain Well. If Link tries to pick them up, he will hear the voice of a Yiga Footsoldier mocking him. A group of Yiga Clan members then appear and proceed to attack Link. Alternatively, should Link be wearing the Yiga Clan Attire when he interacts with the Mighty Bananas, the voice of a Yiga Footsoldier can be heard telling him off for interfering with their trap. Enemies Materials Equipment

The , also known as the , the Royal Tech Lab, or the Ancient Tech Lab, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Ancient Research Institute was a facility established for the sole purpose of researching Ancient Technology. It was placed on the North Hyrule Plain in Hyrule Field in proximity to Hyrule Castle, one of three known sources of Ancient Energy, to remain under the control of the Royal Family of Hyrule. After the thorough destruction of the Ancient Research Institute during the second Great Calamity, it was abandoned and became the Royal Ancient Lab Ruins. Robbie and Purah fled and formed their own individual laboratories in the two other known sources of Ancient Energy, the Akkala Ancient Tech Lab in the Akkala Highlands and the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab in Hateno Village, respectively. Other Appearances thumb|right|320px|The Royal Ancient Lab as seen in the Downloadable Content from The Royal Ancient Lab is seen in the "Road to the Ancient Lab" Scenario. Impa and Zelda, accompanied by Link, travel to the Royal Ancient Lab in order to request Purah and Robbie's aid in researching the newly-discovered Diminutive Guardian. Through their research, Purah and Robbie learn that the Guardian acts as an amplifier for Ancient Technology.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Royal Ancient Lab Ruins are located on the North Hyrule Plain, which can be found in the northwestern corner of Hyrule Field. They are the remains of the Ancient Research Institute that was destroyed during the second Great Calamity. Only parts its outer walls have been left behind, and the fact that it was so thoroughly ruined is believed to be intentional. Creatures Enemies Materials Korok Seeds As in , the Royal Ancient Lab Ruins are the remains of the Royal Ancient Lab situated in the North Hyrule Plain in Hyrule Field. The Royal Ancient Lab Ruins remain relatively untouched, though a few pieces of Fallen Debris now litter its grounds. A troop of Monsters has taken up patrol inside the Ruins. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Royal Bows are Bows that King Rhoam used to gift to the most talented archers in Hyrule. Both their combat ability and design are noted to be impressive. They are commonly found in Treasure Chests or in use by high-tier Enemies on the Tabantha Frontier and in the Hebra Mountains. When scanned with the amiibo Rune, the following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Royal Bow: Series Zelda amiibo Series Link (Archer) amiibo Due to their metallic composition, Royal Bows will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are outdoors during a Thunderstorm. They will also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. Finally, they will not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Royal Bows belong to the Royal Gear equipment archetype, which is associated with the Royal Family of Hyrule.

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Royal Bridle is a Bridle that can be obtained from Toffa by completing "The Royal White Stallion" Side Quest. Prior to the second Great Calamity, Zelda equipped her White Horse with the custom-made Royal Bridle and its counterpart, the Royal Saddle, as part of an attempt to bond with her Horse. Following the Great Calamity, Toffa's grandfather inherited the Royal Bridle and passed it down to Toffa. By registering the White Horse at a Stable and showing it to Toffa, the elderly man will gift Link the Royal Bridle and Royal Saddle and equip them onto the Horse. The Royal Bridle is a piece of Royal Horse Gear, which is a set of Horse Gear. It can be equipped to any Horse by speaking to specific workers at Highland Stable, Outskirt Stable, South Akkala Stable, or Woodland Stable. However, it is unable to be worn by Epona or the Giant Horse. The Royal Bridle is well-known for its craftsmanship and how much the Royal Family of Hyrule favored it. The Royal Bridle can be seen equipped to Zelda's White Horse during the special cutscene that plays after the credits for , but only if the "Captured Memories" Main Quest has been completed.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Royal Broadswords are one-handed Swords that deal 36 damage. They can be found in Hyrule Castle and are occasionally wielded by Silver Bokoblins and Golden Bokoblins. Before the Great Calamity, the Royal Family of Hyrule would award these swords to Hylian Knights who achieved remarkable feats. They balance strength and beauty elegantly, making them rare. When scanned with the amiibo Rune, the following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Royal Broadsword: Series Young Link amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link (Rider) amiibo Due to their metallic composition, Royal Broadswords will attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms, and they are capable of conducting Electricity. They also will not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They sink if they are dropped in the Water, but since they are magnetic, they can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. Royal Broadswords belong to the Royal Gear series of equipment, which was used by distinguished individuals in Hyrule. Other Appearances The Royal Broadsword appears as one of Link's Weapons in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Royal Claymores are part of the Royal Gear series. They are two-handed Weapons intended to be wielded by the Royal Family of Hyrule and the Royal Guard. Being struck by one of these Claymores is said to destroy one's body and their resolve. They have a base attack damage of 52. Royal Claymores are scattered throughout Hyrule. They can be found on the necklaces of Hinoxes. Stalnox can also drop Royal Claymores when they are defeated, particularly the one within Lockup. Other high-tier enemies, such as Silver Moblins, make use of them. Royal Claymores can also be found in the following locations: Woodland Tower Nero Hill Hyrule Castle Various Ancient Shrines Coliseum Ruins (If only three Divine Beasts have been completed) When the following amiibo are scanned with the amiibo Rune, they have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Royal Claymore: Series Young Link amiibo Series Link () amiibo If a Royal Claymore is equipped during a Thunderstorm, it will attract Lightning due to being made of metal. Similarly, they are capable of conducting Electricity. They can also be picked up using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate, and they will sink if they are dropped in Water. They are incapable of burning, which means they can be exposed to Fire and Scorching Climates without issue. Royal Claymores belong to the Royal Gear equipment archetype, an intricate set of Weapons designed for the Royal Family of Hyrule. Royal Claymores reappear as Weapons in . Other Appearances Royal Claymores are a Weapon used by King Rhoam.

are recurring Items in . Locations and Uses Royal Guard's Bows are a powerful type of Bows found within Hyrule Castle. A Royal Guard's Bow, spawns above the fireplace in Princess Zelda's Room. Another one spawns inside the Square Spiral Staircase. Royal Guard's Bows belong to the Royal Guard's Series equipment archetype, which is associated with the Royal Guard of Hyrule. Prior to the second Great Calamity, Royal Guard's Bows were made by the Sheikah using Ancient Technology to fight Calamity Ganon. Royal Guard's Bows make a trade between firepower and Durability, as they have a higher strength but has lower Durability. If Link speaks to Parcy at Riverside Stable, she will tell him about the Weapons once used by the Royal Guards of Hyrule Castle, expressing sadness she could never find any of them. This will begin "The Royal Guard's Gear" Side Quest. Royal Guard's Bows are one of the Weapons Link can bring Parcy. She will recognize it immediately, asking to see it. If Link allows her to, she will thank him and express a desire to find her own pieces of the Royal Guard's Series. Parcy will give him a Gold Rupee as a reward. Following this exchange, Link can trade Royal Guard's Bows to Parcy for a Topaz, a Ruby, or a Sapphire. Royal Guard's Bows are made of metal, and will therefore conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms. They will also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, they will not burn if they touch Fire or if they are exposed to a Scorching Climate. Royal Guard's Bows reappear in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Royal Guard's Claymores are part of the Royal Guard's Series, an equipment archetype that includes the Royal Guard's Sword, the Royal Guard's Spear, the Royal Guard's Bow, and the Royal Guard's Shield. The Sheikah used Ancient Technology to forge them. They were initially designed to help defend against the Great Calamity, but they found little use due to their low durability. All Royal Guard's Claymores are found in Hyrule Castle. They can be found in Lockup and the Guards' Chamber. When Link speaks to Parcy at Riverside Stable, she will tell him about the equipment belonging to the Royal Guards inside Hyrule Castle, and she laments that she could not find all of it. This will give Link "The Royal Guard's Gear" Side Quest. A Royal Guard's Claymore can be turned in for this quest in exchange for a Gold Rupee. Afterwards, Parcy will give Link a Topaz if he keeps bringing her Royal Guard's Claymores. Royal Guard's Claymores are made of metal, which means they will attract Lightning when equipped during a Thunderstorm and conduct Electricity. They also can not burn near a Fire or in a Scorching Climate, and they can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. However, they will sink if they are dropped in Water. Royal Guard's Claymores reappear in . Other Appearances The Royal Guard’s Claymore is a Weapon Link can use in .

are recurring Items in . Royal Guard's Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Royal Guard's Shields are found in Hyrule Castle, either abandoned or being used by the Enemies inside. They were created using the Ancient Technology of the Sheikah for use of the Royal Guards of Hyrule Kingdom. Though they have an incredibly high defense, a structural weakness led to their low Durability, making them impractical for combat. This is a common feature of the Royal Guard's Series, the equipment archetype to which Royal Guard's Shields belong. One Royal Guard's Shield can be found in the King's Study, which is within Hyrule Castle's Library. If Link wears a Royal Guard's Shield while talking to Selmie, she will be unimpressed to the point of yawning and calls them flimsy pieces of garbage that are worthless to serious Shield Surfers, due to their poor Durability making them unsuitable for Shield Surfing. As part of "The Royal Guard's Gear" Side Quest, Parcy wishes to see a piece of the Royal Guard's Series. If Link speaks to her while carrying a Royal Guard's Shield, she will recognize it and ask him to show it to her. Should Link agree, she will be grateful and give him a Gold Rupee as a reward. Afterwards, Link can trade Royal Guard's Shields with Parcy in exchange for a Topaz, Ruby, or Sapphire. Being made of metal, Royal Guard's Shields conduct Electricity and will attract Lightning if equipped during Thunderstorms. However, they will not burn like wooden Shields do when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will also sink if they are dropped in water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Royal Guard's Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Royal Guard's Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Royal Guard's Swords.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Royal Guard's Spears are Weapons that are part of the Royal Guard's Series. They were crafted by the Sheikah using Ancient Technology to fight the Great Calamity, and while they have a high attack power, a design flaw left them with low durability. They can be found in the interior of Hyrule Castle as they are intended to be wielded by the Soldiers who previously served as guards. In the Castle, a Royal Guard's Spear can be found hidden in the fireplace in the Dining Hall, and another can be found wielded by a Black Moblin. If Link speaks to Parcy at Riverside Stable, she will reveal that she wants to find the gear that belonged to the Royal Guards of Hyrule Castle. The Royal Guard's Spear is one of the Weapons Link can bring to her for a reward, which Parcy immediately recognizes. She will be grateful and give Link a Gold Rupee in return. Following this exchange, Link can continue to trade Royal Guard's Spears to Parcy for a Topaz, a Ruby, or a Sapphire. Royal Guard's Spears are made of metal, and they will therefore attract Lightning during Thunderstorms and conduct Electricity. If Link drops them in Water, they will sink, but they are incapable of burning when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They can also be manipulated using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate. Royal Guard's Spears reappear in . Other Appearances The Royal Guard's Spear is a Weapon Link can use in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Royal Guard's Swords are Weapons that are part of the Royal Guard's Series. They are replicas of the Master Sword made with Sheikah Ancient Technology to oppose the Great Calamity, but they were unsuccessful due to their low durability. They are commonly found in Hyrule Castle, both scattered about and being wielded by Enemies. The Royal Guard's Sword is one of several Items of the Royal Guard's Series that can be given to Parcy to complete "The Royal Guard's Gear" Side Quest. As a reward for completing the quest, Parcy will give Link a Gold Rupee. Afterwards, whenever Link speaks to Parcy while carrying a Royal Guard's Sword, she will ask for it in exchange for a Ruby. Since they are metallic, Royal Guard's Swords will attract Lightning if equipped during a Thunderstorm, and they are also capable of conducting Electricity. They can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune, which is useful since they will sink in Water. Finally, Royal Guard's Swords will not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Royal Guard's Swords reappear in . However, they have become decayed due to the Upheaval. Other Appearances The Royal Guard's Sword is a weapon Link can use in .

Royal Guard Boots are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Royal Guard Boots can be found as part of the "EX Royal Guard Rumors" Side Quest exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack. As part of this Quest, Link is required to read the Super Rumor Mill V4 at Riverside Stable. In this Book, Traysi claims that pieces of the Royal Guard Set can be found in the Dining Hall, near the Guards' Chamber, and on the second floor. They Royal Guard Boots are located in an EX Treasure Chest in the Dining Hall of Hyrule Castle. After they have been found, Granté will begin to sell them in Tarrey Town. They Royal Guard Boots are part of the Royal Guard Set, along with the Royal Guard Cap and Royal Guard Uniform. Wearing the whole set will decrease the amount of Stamina required to perform a Charge Attack. The Royal Guard Boots cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy, nor can they be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. The Royal Guard Boots are found in a Treasure Chest within the hidden King's Study. Enhancing Other Appearances

The are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Royal Guard Cap is obtained through the "EX Royal Guard Rumors" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack. During the Side Quest, Link is required to read the Super Rumor Mill V4, which is located at Riverside Stable. Within, Traysi claims that pieces of the Royal Guard Set can be found in the Dining Hall, near the Guards' Chamber, and on the second floor. The Royal Guard Cap can be found in a Hidden Chest in Champions' Hall, which is located on the second floor of the Sanctum of Hyrule Castle. After it has been found, Granté will begin to sell it in Tarrey Town. The Cap is part of the Royal Guard Set, along with the Royal Guard Boots and Royal Guard Uniform. Wearing all three pieces of Armor will decrease the amount of Stamina Link uses during a charge attack. The Royal Guard Cap cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy or Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Enhancing Other Appearances The Royal Guard Cap is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and it is obtained by completing the Challenge "King Rhoam's Training". Unlike most other pieces of Attire, it cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop.

The is a recurring Armor Set in . The Royal Guard Set goes unnamed in . Location and Uses The Royal Guard Set is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack. It is a set of Armor originally worn by members of the Royal Guard that can be found as part of the "EX Royal Guard Rumors" Side Quest. It consists of the Royal Guard Cap, the Royal Guard Uniform and the Royal Guard Boots. Wearing the full set confers the effects of Charge Atk. Stamina Up, Swim Dash Stamina Up, and Climb Jump Stamina Up, with the Inventory only displaying Charge Atk. Stamina Up. These reduce the Stamina cost of charge attacks and jumping while climbing by 50%, and the cost of dashing or spin attacking while swimming by 75%. The Armor Set does not apply any other effects. It cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop, nor can it be enhanced by a Great Fairy. Enhancing Other Appearances The Royal Guard Cap is acquired upon completing the "King Rhoam's Training" Quest. The Royal Guard Uniform is acquired upon completing the "King's Escort" Quest. The Royal Guard Boots are acquired upon completing the "A King Serves His People" Quest.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Royal Halberds are spears that were utilized by the Hylian Knights who guarded the Throne Room of Hyrule Castle. They were ornately designed by craftsmen on behalf of the Royal Family of Hyrule. In the present, they are used by high-tier variants of Enemies, particularly in the Gerudo Highlands and Tabantha Frontier. They also have a chance to appear in Treasure Chests that spawn after scanning the Series Link () amiibo with the amiibo Rune. Since they are made of metal, Royal Halberds will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. They can also be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. They are also unable to burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate, and they will sink if they are dropped in Water. Royal Halberds belong to the Royal Gear equipment archetype, a group of Weapons designed on behalf of the Royal Family of Hyrule. Other Appearances The Royal Halberd is featured as one of Link's Weapons in .

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Royal Hidden Passage is a series of tunnels and underground structures that lead from Hyrule Castle to the Emergency Shelter. It can be accessed via hatches located in the Observation Room and near the Guards' Chamber. Alternatively, the Passage can be accessed through the Emergency Shelter after one Region has been investigated for the "Regional Phenomena" Main Quest. A large cavern holds a Stalnox hidden beneath a pile of rocks. In the same area's Water-filled portion, a tunnel to the north leads to Hyrule Castle, while a tunnel to the south leads to the Emergency Shelter and Horned Statue. Numerous Ore Deposits, Rare Ore Deposits, and Luminous Stone Deposits can be found throughout the Passage. A Stone Tablet beneath the Observation Room entrance explains the origins of Hyrule Castle. The is a recurring location in . The Royal Palace's Throne Room goes unnamed in and . Features and Overview The Royal Palace's Throne Room is a part of the Royal Palace in Gerudo Town. It consists of the Palace's first floor, and it contains Riju's Throne and the pedestal for the Thunder Helm. During the day, Riju will sit on her Throne, which is constantly guarded by Buliara. The guards Bertri and Katta guard the interior of the Throne Roome. When Downloadable Content pack is active, Link is able to obtain the "Champion Urbosa's Song" Recovered Memory. This Memory begins inside the Royal Palace's Throne Room, with Zelda and her Attendant standing in front of Urbosas she sits upon the Throne. Urbosa accepts Zelda's request for her to be a Champion, explaining that their enemies, the Yiga, have been planning to steal their Thunder Helm along with resurrecting Calamity Ganon. She vows not to rest until the Calamity falls. On behalf of Hyrule, Zelda thanks Urbosa. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Riju sitting on her throne in the Royal Palace's Throne Room|Riju's introduction in the Royal Palace's Throne Room Riju greets Link when he first enters the Royal Palace's Throne Room. However, she takes note of his Sheikah Slate, calling it something interesting. Link approaches, but once he reaches the steps to Riju's Throne, Buliara demands he stop and declare his business. Believing that he is more than the average traveler, Riju halts Buliara's questioning and asks Link's name. She then asks what his purpose his coming so far to meet her. At first, Buliara does not believe that Link is capable of calming Divine Beast Vah Naboris, as all of the Champions that were capable of controling it died 100 years ago. However, Riju remembers her mother telling her a story of a fallen swordsman that the princess put into a deep sleep during the Great Calamity. Though the story always seemed more like a legend than history, the swordsman she heard of was also named Link. Riju points out that Link is carrying a Sheikah relic, which means he must be more than a simple wanderer to possess it. While Buliara can not recall a Hylian woman among the Champions, she quickly realizes that Link is actually a man. Since Link is a Champion and is there to help with Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Riju refuses to throw him out. Though the Divine Beast is dangerous, the Gerudo have been unable to find a way to calm it on their own. She believes that Link's role as a Champion will allow him to enter and tame Divine Beast Vah Naboris. Buliara interrupts, urging Riju to reconsider entrusting such a task to a stranger. Instead, she suggests he prove himself by retrieving the Thunder Helm. Riju likes this suggestion, explaining that the Thunder Helm is the only thing that can resist the lightning of Divine Beast Vah Naboris. Buliara sends Link to Captain Teake in the barracks to learn

a task to a stranger. Instead, she suggests he prove himself by retrieving the Thunder Helm. She is glad to see that Link is alright, and while she is still worried about the greater threat to Hyrule, she is relieved that the Gerudo will no longer be in danger from the Divine Beast. Behind Riju's Throne is two Treasure Chests, the contents of which Riju offers Link to show her appreciation. Inside are the Champion's Arms, the Scimitar of the Seven and Daybreaker, which are treasured by the Gerudo as belongings of Urbosa. Since Link was friends with Urbosa, Riju believes it is right for him to have them. After completing "Divine Beast Vah Naboris", Link can attempt to take the Thunder Helm from the Royal Palace's Throne Room. Buliara stops him, as his status as a hero does not give him permission to touch it. Riju instructs Buliara to calm down and asks Link if he desires the Helm. Despite the deeds Link has done for the Gerudo, Riju is unable to give it to him, but since Link is fighting the enemy of Urbosa, she offers to lend it to him. In order to earn the Thunder Helm, Link must gain the trust of the Gerudo. By solving the worries of Gerudo Town, Link will prove himself worthy. This begins "The Thunder Helm" Side Quest. Once Link has completed all of the Side Quests in Gerudo Town, Riju shares that she has heard of what he has done and offers her thanks. She declares Link a true friend of the Gerudo and allows him to take the Thunder Helm. More than anyone else, Riju believes Link will be able to use it to its fullest potential. This completes the Side Quest. Other Appearances The Royal Palace's Throne Room is located on the first floor of the Royal Palace in the Gerudo Town Stage. During the Movie "Return of the Chief", Zelda, Impa, Link, and Terrako manage to enter the Royal Palace's Throne Room after being unexpectedly attacked by the Gerudo. Master Kohga, who is disguised as Urbosa, attempts to kill Zelda, but he is stopped by the real Urbosa returning and using her Fury to electrocute him. Before fleeing, he summons several Yiga Footsoldiers to fight on his behalf.

The is a recurring location in . The Royal Palace goes unnamed in and . Features and Overview The Royal Palace is a feature of Gerudo Town, located along the southwest edge of the Town. A large rock spire rests on top of the Palace, which serves as the source Gerudo Town's Water. Riju, the chief of the Gerudo, inhabits the Palace, and her Bedroom takes up its entire second floor. Initially, Link is unable to access this part of the Palace. The left exit leads to a courtyard, where Patricia can be found, and the right exit leads to the Barracks and Relationship Classroom. Alongside Riju, several Gerudo guards patrol the Royal Palace. Ploka and Reeza guard the front entrance, while Bertri and Katta protect the stairs to Riju's Bedroom. Buliara acts as Riju's personal guard and protects her while she sits on her Throne. Before Link's arrival in Gerudo Town, the Yiga infiltrated the Royal Palace and stole the Thunder Helm, an heirloom of the Gerudo. This has caused the soldiers of Gerudo Town to go on high alert. Babi has also inflicted rigorous training on her soldiers as punishment for allowing the thieves to get by them. When Link approaches the Royal Palace, he can ask Ploka if he is able to go inside. While she wants to turn him away, Riju has allowed visitors to the Palace. Though he is allowed inside, Ploka threatens him should he anything rude to the chief. Her fellow guard, Reeza, thinks Riju allowing visitors in these tough times portrays her as a kind chief who puts her people first. However, she also warns Link against disturbing Riju. The first time Link enters the Royal Palace, he will be greeted by Riju, who wonders how he managed to enter. However, she takes note of his Sheikah Slate, calling it something interesting. Link appraoches, but once he reaches the steps to Riju's Throne, Buliara demands he stop and declare his business. When Link returns to the Royal Palace after recovering the Thunder Helm, Buliara will direct him to Riju's room on the second floor, which he has been granted special permission to enter. She threatens Link to be on his best manners, or else he will meet a bad end. Both Bertri and Katta will be shocked by this. At the top of the stairs, Riju tells Link she has been waiting for him and can sense the power of the Thunder Helm from him. When it was stolen, Riju felt as though a shadow had fallen over her, but now she sees Link's arrival in such a dark time as the work of Urbosa. Riju then puts the Thunder Helm on and asks how she looks, which triggers the "Urbosa's Hand" Recovered Memory. Though Riju notices Link's staring, she dismisses it and asks if she looks right. She tells Link to meet her at the Lookout Post before leaving. left|40px On top of the Royal Palace, Link can find Leaves with

The is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Royal Saddle is a Saddle that can be obtained from Toffa at Outskirt Stable by completing "The Royal White Stallion" Side Quest. Prior to the second Great Calamity, Zelda equipped her White Horse with the custom-made Royal Saddle and its counterpart, the Royal Bridle, as part of an attempt to bond with her Horse. Following the Great Calamity, Toffa's grandfather inherited the Royal Saddle and passed it down to Toffa. By registering the White Horse at a Stable and showing it to Toffa, the elderly man will gift Link the Royal Saddle and equip it onto the Horse. The Royal Saddle is a piece of Royal Horse Gear, which is a set of Horse Gear. The Royal Saddle can be equipped onto any Horse by speaking to specific workers at Highland Stable,Outskirt Stable, South Akkala Stable, and Woodland Stable. However, they are unable to be placed onto Epona or the Giant Horse. The emblem on the Royal Saddle is meant to symbolize its connection to the Royal Family of Hyrule. The Royal Saddle can be seen equipped to Zelda's White Horse during the special cutscene that plays after the credits for , but only if the "Captured Memories" Main Quest has been completed.

are recurring Items in . Royal Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Chief among metal Shields are the Royal Shields, whose Durability and defensive power outshine many others. Before the Great Calamity, these Shields were issued to the immediate guard detail of the Royal Family of Hyrule. hey belong to the Royal Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons associated with the Royal Family. Though they have an incredibly high defense, Royal Shields are considered collector's items due to their ornamentations. Being rare, there are only nine Royal Shields scattered across Hyrule Kingdom, with a tenth in Master Mode. Of these, six are held by Enemies. Some Royal Shields with consistent locations include: Within a Treasure Chest under Sarjon Bridge in Faron Woods Beneath a spiral staircase in Hyrule Castle The following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Royal Shield when they are scanned with the amiibo Rune: Series Toon Zelda () amiibo Series Zelda amiibo A Royal Shield can be obtained as a reward from Selmie for completing the Shield-Surfing Mini-Game with a time less than 1:30. When Link speaks to Selmie with a Royal Shield equipped, she will take note. She points out the one she has hanging up and claims it is the best Shield she has seen for Shield Surfing. Royal Shields are made of metal, and therefore conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if equipped during a Thunderstorm. They also sink if they are dropped in Water, and will not burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. The Magnesis Rune also works on them, allowing Link to pick up and manipulate them. Royal Shields reappear in . They can be Fused onto Weapons. Other Appearances Royal Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Royal Broadswords.

is a recurring character in . Biography Rozel is an old man living in Lurelin Village. He wakes up every morning at 5:00 AM and walks to one of the village's docks, although if it is raining, he stays inside or runs back in with his hands covering his head if it occurs during the day. Link can talk to Rozel as soon as he wakes up, and if he does, Rozel first either tells him to take his time looking around the village or to be careful if he plans to go out to sea. Additionally, Rozel may also comment on the weather. Next, Link can ask him many things about the village and the surrounding area. If he asks about the village, Rozel explains that it is a fishing village and then he used to be a fisherman as well when he was younger, and tells him that he should try some of its fish as they are delicious. When it is raining, Rozel also says that it is too dangerous to go fishing, and mentions the Treasure-Chest Game played by fishermen in Cloyne's shop. If asked about the ocean, Rozel tells him of treasure that still may be underwater, and that Link could probably find some if he looked hard enough. Link may also ask him about Eventide Island, and if he does, Rozel tells him that it is a big island to the east of the village, surrounded by some legends. If Link has visited the island, he can tell Rozel, who is then amazed at his accomplishment. Finally, Link can ask Rozel about nearby ruins, which Rozel says are east of the village at Palmorae Beach. He also tells Link about Garini, a young man who often visits the old site, and that he should go see the ruins as well as Garini knows much more about them. If it is raining, he also mentions that Garini also visits the ruins when it rains. Once Link says goodbye, he is told to come back if he has any more questions. He starts heading home at 10:00 PM, and if Link tries to talk to him at this time, Rozel says that he can talk to him tomorrow if he needs something.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Rubies are rare Materials occasionally obtained from breaking Ore Deposits. They are also dropped by various types of Stone Taluses, Silver Enemy variants and Yiga Blademasters when killed. They are sold at Ore and More in Tarrey Town and by Kairo at Foothill Stable. Rubies are said to contain the power of fire within them, granting warmth in colder temperatures when used in Armor. Link can sell Rubies for 210 Rupees in most Shops, though the merchant Ramella will occasionally pay more for them in groups of ten after completing the Side Quest "The Jewel Trade". Rubies are required to purchase the Ruby Circlet from "Starlight Memories" Shop. The description of the Snowquill Headdress reveals it is adorn with a Ruby. Rubies are used by Great Fairies to upgrade certain pieces of Armor. They are needed for all tiers of the Ruby Circlet and the Hero Set, while five are needed for the final tier of each piece of the Snowquill Set. Rubies can be found by destroying Rare Ore Deposits. They can be Fused to Arrows. Rubies are used by Great Fairies to Enhance the following pieces of Armor: Other Appearances Tingle may exchange a 2-Star Sticker with Dr. Bean for a Ruby, a Gold Gem, and a Topaz. It is also dropped by the Bell Bell Flower, and can be found in certain Treasure Chests in Gooey Swamp and the Fairy Garden, as well as by digging in the Auros Ruins. One can be found behind a Cracked Wall in Desma's Labyrinth.

is a recurring character in . Biography Rudi is a Hylian and the owner of the East Akkala Stable in Deep Akkala. He can be found at the front of East Akkala Stable. If East Akkala Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Rudi will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Rudi explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Rudi then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Rudi instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Rudi suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Rudi to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Rudi tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the East Akkala Stable, Rudi will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Rudi thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Rudi will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Rudi asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that East Akkala Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Rudi asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Rudi will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Rudi insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Rudi refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Rudi starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Rudi gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated

Link to name her Epona. Rudi gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Rudi gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside East Akkala Stable, Rudi once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by East Akkala Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Rudi tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Rudi wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Rugged Rhino Beetles can be found resting on Trees in Hyrule Field and the Faron Grasslands. Cooking one with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot will create a Tough Elixir, which will temporarily increase Link's Defense when consumed. The Kochi Dye Shop accepts Rugged Rhino Beetles as an ingredient for Green Dye. When Link speaks to Beedle with at least one Rugged Rhino Beetle in his Inventory, Beedle will notice and ask for it. In return, he offers Link a Tough Elixir. If Link accepts, Beedle will be happy, remarking that he is adding it to his collection. When Link speaks to Beedle afterwards, he claims to still be excited about the Beetle. He claims that if Link has another, he should give it to him tomorrow, as he is going to be focusing on his new Beetle for the rest of the day. If Link refuses, Beedle believes that he misjudged Link's character. Other Appearances

, also known as , are items in . They are the unit of Currency within most games, in circulation in the lands of Hyrule, the Dark World, Koholint Island, Termina, Labrynna, Holodrum, the Great Sea, the World of the Ocean King, New Hyrule, Skyloft, Lorule and Hytopia. They resemble hexagonal gemstones, come in many colors and sizes, and are most often stored within a Wallet. Location and Uses Rupees are most commonly acquired by defeating enemies, cutting tall grass or bushes, throwing Rocks, smashing Pots, rolling or dashing into Trees, winning mini-games or found inside Treasure Chests. They can also rarely be found simply lying around in the Overworld and in Dungeons and are sometimes given to Link as rewards for completing certain sidequests. In many games, it is possible for Link to sell certain Items, such as Treasures and Bugs, in order to obtain Rupees quickly and easily. In some games, it is also possible to gamble for Rupees as well. The amount of Rupees that Link can carry at once differs from game to game. In many games, Rupees are stored inside Wallets, in which Link can increase his carrying capacity by obtaining Wallet upgrades. Rupees are primarily used to purchase Items in Shops, play certain mini-games or progress through the game, usually by paying an important character a fee. The value of a Rupee is often denoted by its color, but the value of each color is inconsistent throughout the series. Generally, the greater the value of a Rupee, the harder it is to obtain, usually requiring more difficult tasks to do so. In and , , , , and , both size and color denote value. In , the value of a Rupee is specified through text rather than color because of the Game Boy's limited color palette. right|80px right|80px In , Rupees were originally called Rupies (singular: Rupy), while they were called Rubies in the game manual. They are referred to as Rupees in the Game Boy Advance release. Only two varieties exist in . The Rupee that flashes yellow and blue is worth 1, while the blue Rupee is worth 5. Link can hold up to 255 Rupees. Normally, they can only be found by killing enemies or stumbling across hidden rooms in Dungeons, where a large formation of yellow Rupees can be found. Defeating all enemies in a room will sometimes reward Rupees. However, in addition to this, Moblins hidden in Caves around Hyrule will gift Link Rupees when visited, uttering the iconic phrase "It's a secret to everybody." Alternatively, Old Men can be found in hidden Caves, who will force Link to pay Rupees to repair the entrance that he damaged to get inside. Link can also gamble his Rupees by playing Money Making Game, where he can choose to spend 10 Rupees on one of three slots to either gain or lose Rupees. Large formations of Blue Rupees can also be found hidden in certain Caves and Dungeons, such as the basement floor of the Palace of Darkness and Chris Houlihan's room, which brightly glisten. introduced the concept of being able to find Rupees by cutting grass and bushes, destroying Rocks and Pots, opening Treasure Chests, and dashing into Trees. The Shovel can also be used to dig for Rupees, most notably at the Treasure Field. It also introduced the ability to sell Items to gain Rupees; Link is able to sell Golden Bees to the Street Merchant for 100 Rupees each, as well as Fish for 21 Rupees in addition to Bombs and Arrows. As a small easter egg, paintings resembling can be found in certain buildings in Kakariko Village, and will occasionally produce Rupees when pulled. is a recurring character in . Biography Russ is a member of the Shield Breakers, a Shield Surfing gang, consisting of him and his friend Fin. He asks Link to buy from the selection of Shields he has, which are used for Shield Surfing. If Link purchases a Shield, he tells him about the Hylian Shield, which he thinks would be perfect for Surfing with. After discussing the Shield, he tells Link that there is a rumor of one being in Hyrule Castle. Wares and Pricing Russ and Fin went to Selmie's Spot the receive Shield Surfing training from her, but due to the blizzard over Hebra Mountains, they can't go outside though. When Link arrives there, he recommends he should return once the weather conditions improved, as Selmie might take other students by then. When spoken to again he advices Link to watch for flags in the vicinity, as they contain Flint and Wood which help create a Campfire. He wields a Wooden Shield. Wares and Pricing

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Rusty Broadswords are a type of Weapon known to break easily due to their age. They can commonly found in Hyrule Field and Eldin Canyon, where they either have been abandoned or are wielded by low-level Enemies. One spawns in a stone on a small island in a lake near the Temple of Time on the Great Plateau. They also have a chance to appear in Treasure Chests that spawn when the Series Guardian amiibo is scanned with the amiibo Rune. Rock Octoroks will inhale Rusty Broadswords when they are placed in front of them, spitting back out a cleaned counterpart. There's a 50% chance for a Traveler's Sword, a 35% chance for a Soldier's Broadsword, a 10% chance for a Knight's Broadsword, and a 5% chance for a Royal Broadsword. Rusty Broadswords are made of metal, so they can attract Lightning during Thunderstorms and conduct Electricity. They will sink in Water and can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. If they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate, they will not burn like wooden Weapons do. Rusty Broadswords belong to the Rusty Gear equipment archetype, which includes Weapons that have become deteriorated. Rusty Broadswords reappear as Weapons in . Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Rusty Claymores are two-handed Weapons known for their low durability. They are commonly found in Hyrule Field and Eldin Canyon, either abandoned or being used by Enemies. They also have a chance of appearing in Treasure Chests that spawn from scanning the Series Guardian amiibo with the amiibo Rune. If a Rusty Claymore is placed in front of a Rock Octorok, it will inhale the sword and then spit out its cleaned counterpart. There is a 50% chance for a Traveler's Claymore, a 35% for a Soldier's Claymore, a 10% chance for a Knight's Claymore, and a 5% chance for a Royal Claymore. Since they are made of metal, Rusty Claymores will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if equipped during a Thunderstorm. They are also unable to burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. Rusty Claymores are part of the Rusty Gear equipment archetype, which consists of Weapons that have been left exposed to the elements. Rusty Claymores return as Two-Handed Weapons that can be wielded by some Enemies. Other Appearances

is a recurring archetype of Weapon in . Location and Uses Rusty Gear consists of Weapons that were once used by Hylian Knights. Over time, lack of maintenance and exposure to the elements have decayed the quality of these Weapons, causing them to become brittle and lowering their Durability. If a piece of Rusty Gear is placed in front of a Rock Octorok while it is inhaling air, it will swallow the Weapon and pause to crunch it in its mouth. After this, it will shoot it back out as a cleaned counterpart. After being cleaned, there is a 50% chance that the item will be its corresponding item in the Traveler's Gear archetype, a 35% chance that it will be of the Soldier's Gear, a 10% chance that it will be of the Knight's Gear, and a 5% chance that it will be of the Royal Gear. As Rusty Gear is made from metal, all Weapons in this series sink when placed in Water, but they do not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will attract Lightning during Thunderstorms and conduct Electricity, and they can be manipulated through the Magnesis Rune. When scanned with the amiibo Rune, the Series Guardian amiibo has a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a piece of Rusty Gear. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Rusty Halberds are Weapons that can be found in the Great Hyrule Forest and Hyrule Field, particularly around ruins. They were potentially used by Hylian Knights, before they deteriorated due to exposure to the elements. Because of their rusted nature, they have a very low durability. Rock Octoroks will inhale Rusty Halberds that are placed in front of them, spitting out a cleaned counterpart. The Item has a 50% chance to be a Traveler's Spear, a 35% chance to be a Soldier's Spear, a 10% chance to be a Knight's Halberd, and a 5% chance to be a Royal Halberd. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Rusty Shields are old Shields that were once potentially used by the Knights of Hyrule. Though they still offer some defense, a majority of their usefulness has been lost to time. These Shields belong to the Rusty Gear equipment archetype, a series of deteriorated Weapons. They can commonly be found abandoned in Hyrule Field and East Necluda. If a Rock Octorok inhales a Rusty Shield, it will chew it before spitting out a cleaned counterpart. The Shield has a 50% chance to be a Traveler's Shield, a 35% chance to be a Soldier's Shield, a 10% chance to be a Knight's Shield, and a 5% chance to be a Royal Shield. Being made of metal, Rusty Shields will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. They will also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, unlike wooden Shields, Rusty Shields will not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate.
