is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Rutala Dam is the larger of two dams containing the East Reservoir Lake in the Lanayru Great Spring. It is located on the southern side of of the Reservoir, and it bears a large Dock that extends into the Lake itself. Rutala Dam is the origin point of Rutala River. Rain will constantly fall onto the Dam before Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed. During the Era of Prosperity 10,000 years before , Rutala Dam was constructed through a joint effort between the Hylians and the Zora in an effort to stem the floods that plagued Lanayru every 10 years. Prior to Link awakening from his Slumber of Restoration, Divine Beast Vah Ruta became active again and situated itself in the East Reservoir Lake, where it began spouting an endless amount of Rain. As a result, the Water level in the Reservoir grew, and the Zora became fearful that Rutala Dam could burst, endangering the lives of those both in Zora's Domain and in Hylian settlements downstream. Since they would need the help of a Hylian to stop the Divine Beast, Sidon left Zora's Domain in search of a one. After Link frees Vah Ruta during the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" Main Quest, Mipha will pilot the Divine Beast out of the East Reservoir Lake by passing under Rutala Dam. Creatures

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Rutala River is begins at Rutala Dam in the Lanayru Great Spring, and it eventually flows into and feeds the Lanayru Wetlands. A small Dock with a Raft at its end stretches out onto the River from Samasa Plain. Divine Beast Vah Ruta's Rain will constantly fall on Rutala River until it has been calmed. When Link calms Vah Ruta during the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" Main Quest, Mipha will pilot it out of the East Reservoir Lake and through Rutala River. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Rutala River. It is a Balloon that floats over the River south of the Zodobon Highlands. Using Archery, Link can destroy the Balloon, which causes a Korok to appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Rutile Lake is located on the western edge of Satori Mountain in Hyrule Ridge. It is surrounded by a dense forest, and several rocky outcroppings and Tree Stumps stick out from its Water. Whenever the Lord of the Mountain is present on Satori Mountain, several unique Creatures will appear around the Lake. Two metallic Treasure Chests can be found sunken in Rutile Lake. Using the Magnesis Rune, Link can pull them to the surface. The Chest contain an Opal and a Giant Boomerang. left|40px There are a total of two Korok Seed Puzzles on Rutile Lake. The first is comprised of two metal Boulders, which Link must use Magnesis to place in their corresponding Tree Stumps. The second is a stone Circle at the center of the Lake, and Link is required to throw a Rock into it. Once each of these Puzzles are solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Ruto Lake is located in the Lanayru Great Spring, directly to the northwest of Ruto Mountain and Ruto Precipice. Five small islands can be found within the Lake. It is the source of Water for the Zora River to the southwest, and it is covered by both Luto's Crossing and the Great Zora Bridge, the latter of which leads into Zora's Domain. Before Divine Beast Vah Ruta is calmed, its Rain will constantly fall over Ruto Lake. During the "Reach Zora's Domain" Main Quest, Sidon will call out to Link from Ruto Lake as he passes through Luto's Crossing. Knowing Link would pass by, Sidon reveals that he has been waiting for him. He then decides to go on ahead and meet Link in Zora's Domain, since they are close already. However, a Moblin approaches Link from behind, which Sidon warns him of. As part of the "Zora Stone Monuments" Side Quest, Link must inspect the Stone Monument on Ruto Lake's western coast. It is the History of the Zora, Part Three, which tells the Zora legend of the white scale. A total of four Treasure Chests are located within Ruto Lake. They are all made of metal, and three of them need to be lifted from beneath the Water using the Magnesis Rune. The first Chest can be found on a ledge below the Great Zora Bridge, containing an Amber. The second is submerged underwater west of the Stone Monument, and it contains a Silver Rupee. The third Treasure Chest, located in the middle of the Lake, has a Phrenic Bow inside. Lastly, the final Chest contains a bundle of five Ice Arrows. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Ruto Lake. It takes a form of a Rock Pattern on the southernmost island. When Link replaces the missing Rock, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Ruto Mountain is a part of the Lanayru Great Spring, located between Ruto Lake and Rutala River. It is bordered to the north by Ruto Precipice. The path to Zora's Domain connects to Ruto Mountain from Luto's Crossing, which then curves through the Mountain. Four small ponds can be found on top of the Mountain, as well as several Ore Deposits. There is a small campsite near the Mountain's peak, which contains a Campfire and a Cooking Pot. Until Divine Beast Vah Ruta is calmed, Rain will constantly fall on Ruto Mountain. As part of the "Zora Stone Monuments" Side Quest, Link must examine the four Stone Monuments that can be found on Ruto Mountain. The first is the History of the Zora, Part Four, which tells the history of the Lightscale Trident and is located south of Luto's Crossing. The second is the History of the Zora, Addendum 1 near the Mountain's peak, telling a story about King Dorephan. Next, the History of the Zora, Part Six, which recounts the history of Divine Beast Vah Ruta, can be found on the southeastern side of the Mountain. Lastly, a worn down copy of the History of the Zora, Part Seven is located on the northwestern side of Ruto Mountain. Four Treasure Chests can be found on Ruto Mountain. The first is a metal Chest embedded in the ground northwest of the Mountain's peak, and it contains a bundle of five Bomb Arrows. The next is made of stone and is buried underneath a pile of bombable rocks, and a Silver Rupee can be found inside. Due south, the last two Treasure Chests, which are metal, can be found submerged in a pond. They contain a Zora Spear and an Ice Arrow, respectively. left|40px There are a total of two Korok Seed Puzzles on Ruto Mountain. The first is a Natural Hiding Spot, taking the form of a Rock that Link can pick up on the Mountain's peak. The other is a group of Leaves with Fairy Dust that dart around a pond northeast of Luto's Crossing, which Link can examine. When each of these Puzzles are solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Other Appearances During the "Fish Out of Water" Challenge, the Warriors are tasked with rescuing a group of Zora Soldiers that were attacked by Monsters while crossing Ruto Mountain.

It is bordered by Ruto Lake to the west and the East Reservoir Lake to the east. The are a recurring location in . The Sacred Ground Ruins go unnamed in and . Features and Overview The Sacred Ground Ruins are an ancient site in Hyrule Field south of the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins where Hyrule's Royal Guards were honored by the Royal Family of Hyrule. At the center of the Sacred Ground Ruins, there is a symbol of a Triforce that bears the crests of Din, Farore, and Nayru in their respective Triforce positions. There is also a Wingcrest in the blank space of the Triforce. Prior to the second Great Calamity, Zelda and the Champions gathered here to honor Link's appointment as Zelda's personal knight. Consequently, the Sacred Ground Ruins are the site of the Recovered Memory, "Subdued Ceremony", which Link can recall by visiting the Ruins after speaking to Impa and receiving the "Captured Memories" Main Quest. In the "EX Treasure: Phantasma" Side Quest exclusive to DLC Pack, a Hidden Chest is added to the Sacred Ground Ruins. It holds the Phantom Armor and is lodged in the ground in the southeastern portion of the Ruins’ pool. The is a location and Object in . Features and Overview The Sacred Tree of the Zonai is a large Tree found atop the highest Sky Island on the Great Sky Island. It is located directly above the Room of Awakening. In the eponymous Voice Memory "Sacred Tree of the Zonai", Rauru reveals that the Sacred Tree shares a connection with the Zonai people, prospering when they do. However, with the decline of the Zonai, the Sacred Tree has been reduced to a hollowed Tree Stump. In the distant past, the Sacred Tree was the site of rituals for the Zonai. At some point, the Temple of Time was constructed to fulfill this purpose instead. However, Rauru believes that the Sacred Tree is still offering protection to them. By the time Link arrives at the Sacred Tree, Water has filled its interior. Its roots extend to the bottom of the Sky Island it rests on, piercing into the Room of Awakening below. Sage Avatars are characters in . Biography Sage Avatars are projections of a Sage's power, made possible via the possession of a Secret Stone. By swearing a Vow to Link, a Sage may allow their Sage Avatar to serve as a traveling companion to Link. Sage Avatars are nearly identical to their respective Sages, with the only difference being their translucent blue bodies and glowing white eyes. A Sage's Secret Stone can also be seen on Sage Avatars. After being upgraded, Sage Avatars receive a yellow-green sheen and their eyes glow yellow instead of white. While summoned, Sage Avatars will automatically attack Enemies that are acting aggressively towards Link. They also allow Link to call on a Sage's power, as if the actual Sage were present. Sage Avatars can be summoned and dismissed by interacting with their respective Vows in the Inventory. Even if they are active, Sage Avatars will not appear inside towns. With the exception of Tulin's Avatar, Sage Avatars will only accompany Link while he is traversing solid ground, and will be temporarily dismissed if he begins Climbing, Gliding, Swimming, or some other action that takes him away from solid ground. Sage Avatars will also attempt to move out of frame when Link is using the Camera. The damage of a Sage Avatar may be increased through two ways. If Link trades four Sage's Wills to a Goddess Statue, he can deepen his bond with a specific Sage, upgrading their Vow to a Solemn Vow. The respective Sage Avatar will then be permanently upgraded, gaining a visual tweak and increasing their base attack power. Sage Avatars will also be temporarily upgraded while Link is wearing the Divine Helm associated with that Sage's Element. This will cause the Sage Avatar to wear the same helm worn by the corresponding Sage from the Era of Myth. The Sage Avatar's base attack power will also be increased by the Divine Helm, stacking with the increase granted by a Solemn Vow. Avatar of Tulin, Sage of Wind Tulin's Sage Avatar attacks with a custom Great Eagle Bow, firing between one and three Arrows, with any shots following the first dealing a lower damage. The first, second, and third shots have a 30%, 45%, and 60% chance to land a Critical Hit on his target. Once he lands a Critical Hit, any subsequent shots of the volley will also deal double damage. The is a title belonging to multiple characters in . The Sage of Fire goes unnamed in and . Biography The Sage of Fire is one of the Six Sages that awaken whenever the Sacred Realm is threatened. An ancient Sage of Fire helped Rauru and the other Sages create the Temple of Time during the Era of Chaos. Once Link awakens from his seven-year seal, Rauru tasks him with helping awaken five new Sages, including the Sage of Fire. When Link arrives in Goron City, he is informed that Darunia, the Goron Chief, left for the Fire Temple in an attempt to save the rest of the Gorons from being eaten by Volvagia. Inside the Fire Temple, Darunia recognizes Link and reveals his plan to face Volvagia alone, despite not having the Megaton Hammer. While he does so, he asks Link to free the captured Gorons. After Link defeats Volvagia, Darunia appears before him in the Chamber of Sages, where he thanks him for helping save the Gorons. Darunia then reveals that he has awakened as the Sage of Fire. He grants Link the Fire Medallion, which he claims contains both the power of Fire and his friendship. As Link leaves, Darunia reminds him that they are now true brothers. Alongside the rest of the Six Sages, Darunia uses his power to construct the Rainbow Bridge, which allows Link to access Ganon's Castle. Later, Darunia appears in the Fire Room once Link has destroyed the Fire Barrier, and he urges Link to hurry. Once Ganon has been defeated, Darunia and the other Sages use their power to seal him in the Evil Realm. During the Credits, Darunia, Saria, Princess Ruto, Nabooru, and Impa gather together on Death Mountain. Saria can be seen sitting on Darunia's shoulders as the group overlooks Hyrule. The Sage of Fire is a member of the Six Sages. As a Sage, they were tasked by the Golden Goddesses with guarding the Mirror of Twilight in the Mirror Chamber. The Sage of Fire was present at the Failed Execution of Ganondorf, where they assisted the other Sages in activating the Mirror of Twilight to banish Ganondorf to the Twilight Realm. When Link and Midna find the shattered Mirror of Twilight, the Sage of Fire appears alongside the other Six Sages. The Sage of Fire asks Link and Midna to lsiten to them. The Sages claim that Ganondorf's power, which had been passed on to Zant, was able to shatter the Mirror of Twilight. They then reveal where the three Mirror Shards can be found: the Snowpeak Ruins, the Temple of Time, and the City in the Sky. However, the Sages also warn them of the power contained in the Mirror Shards. Once the Mirror of Twilight is repaired, the Sage of Fire and the remaining Sages appear once more, blaming themselves for Ganondorf's power taking over the Twilight Realm. They ask for Midna's forgiveness, acknowledging her as the true ruler of the Twili. As Link and

contained in the Mirror Shards. Once the Mirror of Twilight is repaired, the Sage of Fire and the remaining Sages appear once more, blaming themselves for Ganondorf's power taking over the Twilight Realm. They ask for Midna's forgiveness, acknowledging her as the true ruler of the Twili. As Link and Midna enter the Twilight Realm, the Six Sages disappear. The Sage of Fire during the Era of Foundation was Agraston. After receiving the Secret Stone of Fire, he became one of the Six Sages and swore a vow of loyalty to Rauru, the first King of Hyrule. He and his fellow Sages fought Demon King Ganondorf with Rauru during the Imprisoning War, where they witnessed Rauru's sacrifice to seal the Demon King. Following this, Zelda visited Agraston at the Fire Temple. She revealed that the Demon King would one day break free, and she asked Agraston to ensure that the Gorons would help Link fight him in the future. Agraston promised that a new Sage of Fire would awaken in the future to fight beside Link. Agraston's voice can be heard by his descendant Yunobo and Link during the Main Quest "Yunobo of Goron City", beckoning them to the Fire Temple. After the two of them defeat Marbled Gohma and interact with Agraston's Secret Stone, he appears before them and introduces himself. He reveals that Marbled Gohma was deployed by Demon King Ganondorf to prevent Yunobo from awakening as a Sage, at which point he relays the story of the Imprisoning War. Afterwards, he asks Yunobo to fulfill his promise to Zelda by taking up his mantle as the Sage of Fire. Initially, Yunobo is nervous, believing he is unable to live up to the former Sage of Fire's legacy. However, he realizes that he will be failing Hyrule if he refuses his destiny, so he accepts the Secret Stone and his title as Sage of Fire. To show off his new powers, Yunobo summons his Sage Avatar. Bumping his fist with Link, Yunobo makes the Vow of Yunobo, Sage of Fire, which allows Link to call on Yunobo's Sage Avatar. When Link approaches Gloom's Origin, Yunobo will appear to fight alongside him as the Sage of Fire. After the Demon King's Army is defeated, Yunobo will stay behind to battle another Marbled Gohma summoned by the Demon King, allowing Link to push forward. He later rejoins Link to fight Demon King Ganondorf, but he is soon after attacked by a wave of Gloom and rendered unconscious. In the post-Credits scene that plays after awakening all five Sages, Yunobo accompanies Zelda, Link, Purah, Tulin, Sidon, and Riju as Mineru shows them the Temple of Time. As Mineru disappears, the remaining Sages swear a vow of loyalty to Zelda and Hyrule, similar to the one their ancestors made. Other Appearances Agraston appears as the Sage of Fire alongside the other Six Sages in the Era of Foundation.

The is a title belonging to multiple characters in . Biography In the Era of Foundation, Ardi became the Sage of Lightning after receiving the Secret Stone of Lightning. Alongside the rest of the Six Sages, she swore a vow of loyalty to Rauru, the first King of Hyrule. Together, they faced Demon King Ganondorf as part of the Imprisoning War, and Ardi was a witness to Rauru sacrificing himself to seal the Demon King. Following this, Zelda visited Ardi at the Lightning Temple. She claimed that the Demon King would one day break free of his seal, and she asked Ardi to make sure that the Gerudo would help Link face him in the future. As a result, Ardi promised that a new Sage of Lightning would awaken. Throughout the Main Quest "Riju of Gerudo Town", Ardi's voice can be heard calling out to Link and her descendant Riju. Once the two of them defeat Queen Gibdo and interact with Ardi's Secret Stone, she appears before them and introduces herself. Ardi reveals that Demon King Ganondorf sent Queen Gibdo to prevent Riju from awakening as a Sage, at which point she relays the events of the Imprisoning War. In order to fulfill her promise to Zelda, Ardi asks Riju to take her Secret Stone and become the Sage of Lightning. After Ardi disappears, Riju states that fighting the Demon King sounds fun, and she accepts the Secret Stone and her new role as a Sage. As the new Sage of Lightning, she makes the Vow of Riju, Sage of Lightning to Link, wherein she promises to stand by his side. This allows Link to call on Riju's Sage Avatar and her Power of Lightning whenever he needs. As the Sage of Lightning, Riju and the other Sages appear at Gloom's Origin to fight Demon King Ganondorf. They are temporarily separated when another Queen Gibdo appears to battle Riju, with Link moving forward to face the Demon King. She returns during their fight to help Link, but the Sages are soon after incapacitated by Gloom. In the post-Credits scene that plays when all five Sages are awakened, Riju and her fellow Sages visit the Temple of Time with Link, Zelda, and Purah. Together, the Sages recite a similar vow to the one their ancestors made to Rauru, this time swearing to support Zelda and protect Hyrule. Other Appearances The Sage of Lightning initially appears as a Gerudo warrior clad in green. She can be seen fighting Rauru for unknown reasons. Later, she is given a Divine Helm in the shape of a camel and changes to wear white clothing. She wields the Scimitar of the Seven and the Daybreaker in battle.

The is a title belonging to multiple characters in . The Sage of Spirit goes unnamed in , , and . Biography The Sage of Spirit is a member of the Six Sages, who are chosen by a voice from the Sacred Realm whenever it is threatened. An ancient Sage of Spirit helped Rauru and the other Sages construct the Temple of Time during the Era of Chaos. When Link awakens from his seven-year slumber, Rauru tasks him with finding the new Sages and helping awaken them. When Link returns to the Spirit Temple as an adult, he faces a unique Iron Knuckle near the Temple's end. Upon defeating the Iron Knuckle, it is revealed to be Nabooru, who was brainwashed by Koume and Kotake. She is confused at first, but then Koume and Kotake reappear with the intent of brainwashing her again. Nabooru attempts to flee, but she is struck by spells and disappears. Once Twinrova has been defeated, Nabooru will appear before Link in the Chamber of Sages. She thanks Link for his help, noting how much he has grown since their encounter seven years prior. While she is regretful for carrying out Ganondorf's orders while she was brainwashed, Nabooru is eager to fight against him and get revenge now that she has awakened as the Sage of Spirit. Acknowledging Link as the Hero of Time, Nabooru grants him a piece of her power in the form of the Spirit Medallion. Alongside the other Six Sages, Nabooru creates the Rainbow Bridge, which allows Link to access Ganon's Castle. After Link destroys the Spirit Barrier in the Spirit Room, Nabooru appears and tells him to hurry. Upon defeating Ganon, Nabooru and the other Sages combine their power to seal him in the Evil Realm. During the Credits, Nabooru can be seen traveling to Death Mountain with Saria, Darunia, Princess Ruto, and Impa. The group looks over Hyrule together, and Nabooru and Ruto share a look with each other. The Sage of Spirit is one of the Six Sages that reside in the Mirror Chamber, where they guard the Mirror of Twilight at the command of the Golden Goddesses. The Sage of Spirit was present at the Failed Execution of Ganondorf, witnessing the murder of the Sage of Water and assisting in banishing Ganondorf to the Twilight Realm. After Link and Midna reach the Mirror Chamber, the remaining Sages appear before them, including the Sage of Spirit. Alongside the Sage of Forest and the Sage of Light, the Sage of Spirit explains that the Mirror of Twilight was shattered by Zant, who was using Ganondorf's dark power. Since Zant is not the true ruler of the Twili, however, he was not able to completely destroy the Mirror, and the Sages reveal that the Mirror Shards are located in the Snowpeak Ruins, the Temple of Time, and the City in the Sky. In , the Sage of Spirit is Mineru, whose power has been amplified due to her possessing the Secret Stone of Spirit. This has given her the ability to separate her own Spirit from her body. In the Memory "The Imprisoning War", Mineru can be seen collapsing as a result of her exposure to the Demon King's Gloom. As part of Princess Zelda's plan to assist Link in the distant future, Mineru imparts her Spirit in the Purah Pad, where she remains dormant for thousands of years. After he finds the Zonai Relic on Dragonhead Island, Mineru begins to speak to Link, guiding him to the Construct Factory as part of "Guidance from Ages Past". Once they arrive, Mineru formally introduces herself as the Sage of Spirit, and she requests that Link build a new body for her with pieces from throughout the Factory. Mineru's Construct allows her to fight alongside Link, and her next goal is to recover her Secret Stone from the Spirit Temple. Upon defeating the Seized Construct, Mineru's Spirit leaves the Purah Pad for the Secret Stone of Spirit, which embeds itself within her Construct. She then appears before Link and makes the Vow of Mineru, Sage of Spirit, wherein she swears to serve him as a Sage. This allows Link to summon Mineru's Constuct. As the Sage of Spirit, Mineru appears to fight alongside Link and any other awakened Sages when he faces the Demon King's Army at Gloom's Origin. However, they are separated when a magical copy of the Seized Construct appears, which Mineru stays behind to defeat. She later rejoins Link while he faces Demon King Ganondorf, but she and the other Sages are knocked out by a wave of Gloom. In the post-Credits scene, Mineru leaves her Construct body and guides Link, Zelda, Purah, and the other Sages through the Temple of Time on the Great Sky Island. When they reach the altar behind the Temple, Mineru expresses that she wanted to show them the view of Hyrule. She starts to fade away, and she realizes it is time for her to move on. The is a title belonging to multiple characters in . The Sage of Water goes unnamed in and . Biography The Sage of Water is a member of the Six Sages. Whenever the Sacred Realm is threatened, it sends out a call to awaken new Sages, including a Sage of Water. In the Era of Chaos, an ancient Sage of Water worked alongside the other Sages to create the Temple of Time. After Link is released from his seal in the Chamber of Sages, the Sage of Light Rauru tasks him with awakening the rest of the Sages. Inside the Ice Cavern, Sheik informs Link that Princess Ruto has gone to the Water Temple. At the Water Temple, Link will find Ruto, who recognizes him and asks for his help saving Zora's Domain. She offers to guide him to the locations within the Temple where he can change the Water level, at which point she swims away. However, she vanishes thereafter. After Link defeats Morpha, Princess Ruto will appear before him in the Chamber of Sages. She claims that Link's actions have saved Zora's Domain, and she wants to offer him her eternal love as a reward. She cannot, though, as she reveals she has awakened and the Sage of Water and must guard the Water Temple as a result. She encourages Link to continue his search for Princess Zelda, claiming that she can sense she is still alive. Ruto then gives Link the Water Medallion, which lends her power to him. Before he leaves, Ruto asks Link to thank Sheik on her behalf. Using her power as a Sage, Princess Ruto is able to help the other Sages construct the Rainbow Bridge, which allows Link to enter Ganon's Castle. Princess Ruto appears in the Water Room after Link destroys the Water Barrier, where she urges him to hurry. After Link defeats Ganon, the Sages combine their powers to seal him away in the Evil Realm. Princess Ruto can be seen during the Credits, where she overlooks Hyrule from Death Mountain alongside Saria, Darunia, Nabooru, and Impa. While doing so, Ruto shares a look with Nabooru. Alongside the other Six Sages, the Sage of Water was tasked by the Golden Goddesses to watch over the Mirror of Twilight. The Sage of Water was present at the Failed Execution of Ganondorf in the Mirror Chamber. They attempted to execute Ganondorf using the Dusk Claymore, but he was able to call on the Triforce of Power and killed the Sage of Water instead. Ganondorf was consequentially banished to the Twilight Realm. Afterwards, the remaining Sages can be seen mourning the Sage of Water. After being given the Secret Stone of Water by the King of Hyrule, Rauru, she and her fellow Sages swore a vow of loyalty to him. They joined him in fighting Demon King Ganondorf, witnessing his sacrifice to seal him. Sometime afterwards, Zelda visited Qia at

of Foundation's Imprisoning War. After being given the Secret Stone of Water by the King of Hyrule, Rauru, she and her fellow Sages swore a vow of loyalty to him. They joined him in fighting Demon King Ganondorf, witnessing his sacrifice to seal him. The , also known as the Sage of the Wind Temple, is a title belonging to multiple characters in . Biography The Sage of Wind was a Kokiri named Fado who served Daphnes Nohansen Hyrule from the Wind Temple during the Era without a Hero. During the Era of the Great Sea, he was killed by Monsters when Ganondorf escaped his seal under the Great Sea so that he could not use his sacred powers to restore power to the Master Sword. Though he was still bound to the Wind Temple out of a sense of duty, his Spirit could no longer perform the rite. When Link arrives at Gale Isle, Fado greets him and informs him of his condition. He then instructs Link to find another who carries the same Instrument that he does to awaken as a new Sage of Wind. Makar is chosen as the new Sage of Wind, and he travels alongside Link through the Wind Temple to defeat Molgera, the Boss plaguing the Temple. There, Makar and Fado play a duet conducted by Link's Wind Waker to restore the Master Sword's power in order to defeat Ganondorf. During the Era of Foundation's Imprisoning War, Raphica served as the Sage of Wind after receiving the Secret Stone of Wind. He and the rest of the Six Sages swore a vow to the first King of Hyrule, Rauru. Raphica fought Demon King Ganondorf alongside Rauru, and he witnessed his sacrifice to seal the Demon King in the Imprisoning Chamber. Afterwards, Zelda visited Raphica at the Wind Temple, requesting that he ensure the Rito would help Link in the future when the Demon King breaks free of his seal. In response, Raphica promised that a new Sage of Wind will awaken. In the distant future, Kurafiki's descendant Tulin and Link hear Kurafiki's voice drawing them toward the Wind Temple. There, they defeat Colgera, the source of a mighty Blizzard plaguing the Hebra Region. This Monster was sent by the Demon King to prevent a new warrior from finding Raphica's Secret Stone and awakening as the new Sage of Wind. When Tulin touches the Secret Stone, the Spirit of Raphica speaks to them to tell them the history of the Imprisoning War and the duty of the Rito to defeat Demon King Ganondorf. Tulin accepts this responsibility and awakens as the new Sage of Wind. Upon doing so, the Secret Stone attaches itself to Tulin's leg and grants him the power to create a Sage Avatar of himself. To assist Link along his journey, Tulin grabs Link's Right Arm and swears to fight alongside him, imparting the Magic of his Sage Avatar into Link and allowing him to summon a copy of Tulin at any time. This manifests as a Ring known as the Vow of Tulin, Sage of Wind. Tulin appears at Gloom's Origin to fight alongside Link as the Sage of Wind to fulfill his predecessor's promise. However, they are temporarily separated when Demon King Ganondorf summons

a copy of Tulin at any time. This manifests as a Ring known as the Vow of Tulin, Sage of Wind. Tulin appears at Gloom's Origin to fight alongside Link as the Sage of Wind to fulfill his predecessor's promise. However, they are temporarily separated when Demon King Ganondorf summons another Colgera. Tulin ultimately defeats this Colgera on his own and rejoins Link in the climactic battle to defeat the Demon King. Other Appearances Raphica from 's Era of Foundation is a Warrior in .

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Sage Temple Ruins are the half-sunken remains of the Sage Temple located along the Regencia River in Hyrule Field. Scattered around the Ruins are a number of Barrels, in which Link can find Hylian Shrooms and Apples. Two broken wagons can be found in the Ruins, which can be searched for Materials. Floating right in the northwestern corner of the area is a Raft. A metallic Treasure Chest containing an Opal can be found in the southernmost building in the Ruins. A stone Treasure Chest containing a Knight's Halberd can be found in the building at the center of the Ruins. In the "EX Treasure: Twilight Relic" Side Quest from The Master Trials DLC Pack, another metallic Treasure Chest containing Midna's Helmet can be found hidden among the rubble just south of the northwesternmost building of the Ruins. A Korok can be found underneath a Rock atop a broken wall in the center of the Ruins. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

is a recurring character in . Biography Sagessa is found at Dueling Peaks Stable. During the daytime, she sits beside the Stable's Cooking Pot, but typically spends her nights admiring the nearby Ancient Shrine, Ha Dahamar Shrine. She takes shelter inside the Stable when it Rains, and wishes it would stop for a while. While fleeing from the Rain, she warns Link that Lightning will strike metal objects, and advises him to watch himself if he's wandering around with a metal weapon. She mentions that the Sheikah in Kakariko Village wear clothing that allows them to work in the Rain, but laments that only Sheikah can wear it and won't sell the clothing to anyone else. If Link inquires about Kakariko Village, she will explain to him where it is located. If Link ignores her instead, she will remind him of the dangers of Lightning. Sagessa greets Link when he speaks to her, as many travelers do not pass through the area. Sagessa says it is sometimes easy to forget the world almost ended during the Great Calamity because of how peaceful it can be. Despite this, she notes that monsters still tend to wander around, and that the area near Hyrule Castle is especially dangerous. Sagessa tells Link that if he is going to be traveling he should know about Elixirs. If Link he explains that an Elixir can be made by cooking Bugs and other small creatures with Monster Parts. She notes that while most Elixirs do not restore health, they can still have different effects, like increasing speed or raising resistance to extreme Temperatures. Impressed that Link has made it so far without knowledge of Elixirs, Sagessa gives him a Hasty Elixir in case something happens to him, in order to ease her conscience. Since Hasty Elixirs increase running speed, Sagessa says she uses them to escape from monsters or when she needs to hurry. The Recipe is simple, so she usually has a rough stock of 10 on hand. If Link states that he already knows all about Elixirs while Sagessa is standing near the pond, she'll be surprised that he's leaving so soon and decides to spend her time admiring the Ancient Shrine. If Link tells her this during the day, she'll point out how only twins seem to run the Stable, and how this fact unnerves her. If spoken to again, Sagessa will repeat her information of Elixirs, but will not give Link another one. While walking between places at the Stable, Sagessa will complain about how hungry she is. If Link approaches the Apples near the Stable, Sagessa will tell him that anything lying around the Stable is free for the taking. She also comments on the crispness of the Apples and assures Link that Darton and Shibo will go pick more if the Apple supply runs out. After Link completes the Ha Dahamar Shrine near the Stable, Sagessa may meet him outside and say that although it only recently started glowing, the

also comments on the crispness of the Apples and assures Link that Darton and Shibo will go pick more if the Apple supply runs out. After Link completes the Ha Dahamar Shrine near the Stable, Sagessa may meet him outside and say that although it only recently started glowing, the Ancient Shrine has been there for about 10,000 years. She says there are so many that it sometimes feels like there is a Shrine behind every hill. She also says that though archaeologists get excited about finding Shrines, she has no time for mysteries and would rather leave that to younger people. Despite this, Sagessa notes that the glowing light does make the concept romantic. Sagessa can be found in the Haran Lakefront Well, practicing her singing. As part of the Side Adventure "An Eerie Voice", Link can find Penn at Highland Stable investigating a voice that resembles Princess Zelda echoing from Fural Plain. The voice had allegedly been stating "Leave the...rms" repeatedly. Upon entering the Haran Lakefront Well, Link can find Sagessa singing. She is confused when Link confronts her and explains that the song is actually about a Fox chasing storms. She states that she is not trying to cause any trouble, as she simply likes how her voice sounds in the Well. However, she also believes that it is not her fault if people had misheard her. Since people were throwing Weapons in the Well every morning, Sagessa was afraid they could be dangerous and has gathered them into a pile. She tells Link that he is free to use them if he is willing to, as she has no interest in them. When Link approaches her afterwards, she asks if he returned to visit her or if he is a Well enthusiast. She apologizes to him before returning to her singing. When spoken to again, she comments that she will continue to sing, and she states that practice is the only way she can improve.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Sahasra Slope Cave is a Cave that runs beneath the Sahasra Slope Skyview Tower on the Sahasra Slope. There are two entrances to the Cave: one northwest of the Sahasra Slope Skyview Tower and one to the southeast. Large portions of it are filled with Hard Sediment, which divide different sections of the Cave and produce Rocks and Rusty Claymores when broken. Three Ore Deposits can be found throughout the Cave, and a southern chamber hidden behind a Boulder holds three more Ore Deposits and a Rare Ore Deposit. The Cave's northeastern chamber is littered with Garbage Dumps created by the Monsters inside. It is necessary to enter the Sahasra Slope Cave in order to reach the interior of the Sahasra Slope Skyview Tower via Ascend, as the Skyview Tower's Doors are blocked by Long Sticks. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests

The , designated by the trial name Aid from Above, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Sahirow Shrine is situated on top of Corvash Peak in the Hebra Mountains. It corresponds to the Worihas Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation The entrance to the Shrine opens to a twisting hallway. Inside this hallway, there is a Sensor and a Trapdoor. If Link touches the Sensor's ray, it will trigger the Trapdoor, preventing him from walking across the hallway's floor. To avoid this, Link must successfully jump over the Sensor. This hallway continues to a longer stretch with several Sensors and a long Trapdoor floor. At the end of this stretch, there is a short platform that sits in front of three Sensors. To avoid these, Link can either take a running jump from the floor, or he can jump and Paraglide from the ledge. Beyond this hallway, there is a wall with a floating platform that moves along its top ledge. Link must Ascend to reach the top of this wall, which opens to a forked path. To the right, there is a head-height Sensor and a Trapdoor blocking the way to a small chamber. Link can crouch under this Sensor's ray to reach the chamber, which contains two Iron Boxes and a portcullis guarding a Stone Chest. This portcullis is controlled by the Sensor outside the chamber, and the Sensor must be triggered in order for it to be lifted. Link can open the portcullis from within the chamber by moving an Iron Box with Ultrahand into the Sensor's ray. thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of Link using Ascend in the arch near the end of Sahirow Shrine.|The answer to the Sensor laser puzzle To the left of the floating platform is a series of hallways. When Link enters the first hallway, a portcullis will fall and trap him in as Sensors move horizontally along the floor. Successfully passing this hallway will trap Link in the next one as the Sensors deactivate. The second hallway is much the same, though a pair of head-height Sensors will move along the hallway instead. In the third hallway, a large arch structure will move through the space instead. Several Sensors placed on the inside of this arch will create an impassable cage that Link cannot move through. Instead, Link must wait for the arch to approach and use Ascend on the ceiling of the arch to bypass the Sensors. Upon doing so, Link will have a clear pathway to the end of the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Sahirow Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Enemies Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Saki is a Rito woman who resides in Rito Village. She lives in Teba's Home with her husband Teba and son Tulin. Prior to Divine Beast Vah Medoh being appeased, Saki can be found staring out the window of Teba's Home. When Link approaches her, she will ask if he needs anything. If Link asks what is wrong, Saki will become dismissive and end their conversation. Should Saki be spoken to again, she claims it is not a good time. After starting the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, Kaneli will direct Link to Saki, as she may know where Teba is. When Link speaks to her, Saki admits that she overheard his conversation with Kaneli, and she claims to know Teba's location. She reveals that he went to the Flight Range, explaining that it is a training ground for Rito warriors. She believes that he intends to gather more Weapons there before facing Divine Beast Vah Medoh again. To get to the Flight Range, Saki tells Link to Paraglide from Revali's Landing. She reveals that the Landing was named after the Champion Revali, so that the events of the Great Calamity would not be forgotten. This initiates the "Revali's Flap" Recovered Memory. After the Memory concludes, Saki will become concerned for Link's well-being. Fearing she has said too much, Saki apologizes and informs Link he can talk to her if he does not understand anything. During this time, Link can ask Saki about Teba, whom she describes as impulsive. She claims that she tried to stop him from leaving to face Divine Beast Vah Medoh, but he did not listen to her. However, Saki has resigned herself to this, attributing it to Teba's status as a Rito warrior. Additionally, Link is able to ask Saki about Revali. She relates that he is a legend to the Rito who is idolized by all of the warriors. According to her, Teba wishes to make Tulin into a warrior as strong as Revali was. Whenever they play, she reveals that it actually involves Teba training Tulin at the Flight Range. However, she admits that she does not want Tulin to become a warrior. If Link returns to Saki after meeting Teba, she will be relieved and happy to hear he is still alive. As thanks, Saki gives him a bundle of 10 Bomb Arrows. She states that Teba left them with her in case she needed them, but she does not want them in an area where Tulin might play with them. After Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been calmed, Teba will join Tulin and Saki in their home. Teba credits Saki for helping him recover enough from his injuries to stand. Saki also told Teba that Link is a descendant of the Hylian Champion, which Teba believes. Similarly, Teba told Saki about his and Link's fight against the Divine Beast, including the fact that everything is back to normal now. She is grateful so

recover enough from his injuries to stand. Saki also told Teba that Link is a descendant of the Hylian Champion, which Teba believes. Similarly, Teba told Saki about his and Link's fight against the Divine Beast, including the fact that everything is back to normal now. She is grateful so have Teba home safely, and she does not know how to express her gratitude. After Teba and Tulin leave for the Flight Range, Saki will begin a daily routine, wherein she repeatedly walks between Teba's Home and The Slippery Falcon. When Link speaks to her, she states that Teba and Tulin are at the Flight Range. She would prefer if they stopped such dangerous training now that the Divine Beast has been appeased, but Teba still believes it to be necessary. Though Teba wants to make Tulin into a warrior, Saki still considers their son to be a fledgeling. Saki also thinks that Tulin is sweet, and she is scared of him losing his innocence.

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Sakunbomar Shrine can be found in the Lost Woods within the Great Hyrule Forest. It corresponds to the Ramobnukas Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Sakunbomar Shrine The Sakunbomar Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Sakunbomar Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Salmon Meunières are Meals that can be made by Cooking a Hearty Salmon with Tabantha Wheat and Goat Butter. Regular Salmon Muenières can only be made by adding another ingredient with an effect other than hearty. Eating them will restore several of Link's Hearts. The crispy skin of Hearty Salmons puts the texture of this dish into a class of its own. After calming Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Link can find Kheel on her own at the Warbler's Nest. She will ask him to retrieve her sisters for their rehearsal, but she claims that Genli may be difficult since she wants Salmon Meunière. When Link speaks to Genli, she explains that she cannot sing until she gets some Salmon Meunière. The rest of their sisters left to retrieve the ingredients, but Genli wonders what is taking them so long. Link can locate and help the sisters put together Salmon Muenière. Cree is found in The Slippery Falcon, where she will give Link the Goat Butter she bought. Kotts is found at the Fishpond in Front of the Village, fishing for Hearty Salmon. When reminded of her rehearsal, she gives Link the Hearty Salmon she caught. Finally, Notts is found on one of the ridges above Rito Village, and she will explain that she finished gathering her ingredients early and so began practicing. She gives Link her Tabantha Wheat. Returning to Genli, Link can make Salmon Meunière for her. If he gives it to her, she will eat it all. Afterwards, she decides to keep her promise to her sisters and attend the rehearsal. Genli thanks Link for the Salmon Meunière and asks him to attend their rehearsal. Only one variation of Salmon Meunière can be made: Hearty Salmon Meunière: Made by using the default recipe. When eaten, they heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him temporary Hearts.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Salmon Risotto can be made by Cooking a Hearty Salmon, Hylian Rice, Goat Butter, and Rock Salt together in a Cooking Pot. The only way to make regular Salmon Risotto is by adding a fifth ingredient that grants an effect other than hearty. Eating these Meals will heal some of Link's Hearts. This Risotto is known the be rich, as the rice permeates the light flavor of the Salmon. In her diary, Ivee details a recipe for Mushroom Risotto. However, at the end, she suggests substituting the Hylian Shrooms used with Hearty Salmon for a "fish-lover's dish". Link can only make one variation of Salmon Risotto: Hearty Salmon Risotto: Made by using the default recipe. When these meals are consumed, all of Link's Hearts will be healed, and he will gain temporary Hearts. Like in , Salmon Risottos are made by Cooking a Hearty Salmon with Hylian Rice, Goat Butter, and Rock Salt.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can make Salt-Grilled Crabs by Cooking any Crab together with Rock Salt in a Cooking Pot. There are two ways to make their default version. First, Link must use two different types of Crabs. Alternatively, another Ingredient can be added to the Meal with an effect that differs from the Crab used. Eating these dishes will restore some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. A majority of fishermen enjoy Crabs most when they are prepared in this way. Based on the type of crab used, Link can make the three following variations of Salt-Grilled Crab: Energizing Salt-Grilled Crab: Made by using Bright-Eyed Crabs. They refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel when eaten. Mighty Salt-Grilled Crab: Made by using Razorclaw Crabs. When consumed, they grant Link a boost to the power of his attacks. Tough Salt-Grilled Crab: Made by using Ironshell Crabs. Link's defensive abilities will be boosted by eating these Meals. Salt-Grilled Crab returns from . It can be made using the same Recipe, which involves Cooking any type of Crab with Rock Salt. Other Appearances

are recurring Meals in . Location and Uses Salt-Grilled Fish can be made by Cooking any Fish together with Rock Salt in a Cooking Pot. The default version can only be made either by using Hyrule Basses or Sanke Carp, both of which offer no status effects, or by using two Fish with contradictory effects. Eating these Fish will heal some of Link's Hearts. To make them, the whole Fish must be rolled in Rock Salt before it is grilled. Based on both the type of Fish used and whether any additional Ingredients are added, several different variations of Salt-Grilled Fish can be made: Chilly Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using Chillfin Trouts or other chilly Ingredients. Link will gain one level of Heat Resistance if he eats these fish. Electro Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using Voltfin Trout or other electric Ingredients. When eaten, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance. Enduring Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using enduring Ingredients. They can be eaten to completely replenish and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Energizing Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using Staminoka Basses or other energizing Ingredients. Consuming them will refill a portion of Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using hasty Ingredients. Link's movement speed will be increased by eating these meals. Hearty Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using Hearty Salmons, Hearty Bass, or other hearty Ingredients. When eaten, all of Link's Hearts will be healed, and he will gain temporary Hearts. Mighty Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using Mighty Carp, Mighty Porgies, or other mighty Ingredients. By eating this fish, Link will receive a boost to his attack power. Sneaky Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using Stealthfin Trouts or other sneaky Ingredients. If Link eats them, he will receive a boost to his Stealth abilities. Spicy Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using Sizzlefin Trouts or other spicy Ingredients. One level of Heat Resistance will be granted to Link if he eats them. Tough Salt-Grilled Fish: Made by using Armored Carp, Armored Porgies, or other tough Ingredients. They will grant Link a boost to his defense if he eats them. Salt-Grilled Fish return in , and their Recipe still consists of Cooking any type of Fish with Rock Salt. Their default version can be made by using a Hyrule Bass, a Sanke Carp, or an Ancient Arowana.

When consumed, they'll replenish part of Link's Stamina Wheel. Enduring Salt-Grilled Gourmet Meat: Made by adding enduring ingredients. Link's Stamina Wheel will be completely restored and overfilled when he eats these meats. Hasty Salt-Grilled Gourmet Meat: Made by adding hasty ingredients. These meals will grant Link a boost to his movement speed when he eats them. Spicy Salt-Grilled Gourmet Meat: Made by adding spicy ingredients. By eating them, Link will gain one level of Cold Resistance. Electro Salt-Grilled Gourmet Meat: Made by adding electric ingredients. If they're eaten, Link will receive one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Salt-Grilled Gourmet Meat: Made by adding mighty ingredients. By eating them, the power of Link's attacks will be boosted. Tough Salt-Grilled Gourmet Meat: Made by adding tough ingredients. Other Appearances The Recipe for Salt-Grilled Gourmet Meat is earned by completing the Quest "Relieving Meat Fatigue". is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Samasa Plain is located directly between Rutala River and Lanayru Bay in the Lanayru Great Spring. A tunnel connects it to Brynna Plain on the other side of a hill. The remains of an unnamed Hylian village can be found at the center of the Plain. Nearby, Rucco Maag Shrine is surrounded by a maze of spikes, though it can be safely navigated without taking any damage. Before Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, Rain will constantly fall on Samasa Plain. On the northern shore of Samasa Plain is a Dock with a Raft at its end stretches out onto Rutala River. A group of Lizalfos have set up a Monster Stronghold around the Dock. The Treasure Chest in this camp contains a bundle of five Ice Arrows. A second Treasure Chest is located on a hill on the south end of Samasa Plain. When it is opened, Link will receive a Silver Rupee. left|40px A total of three Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Samasa Plain. The first is a Rock Pattern in the southwestern corner of the Plain. The second is a Flower Trail that begins on Brynna Plain, ending on the other side of the hill that separates the two. Lastly, a Natural Hiding Spot that takes the form of a Rock under a Pile of Leaves. Once each of these Puzzles have been solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Sanctum is the highest structure in Hyrule Castle. On Link's Map, it is marked as the location of Calamity Ganon. Zelda has been holding him back within his Cocoon in the Throne Room, which is located on the first floor of the Sanctum, for the past 100 years. By entering the Throne Room, the final battle against Calamity Ganon will begin. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle is located in the Sanctum. Leaves with Fairy Dust can be found at the end of the spire on top of the Sanctum. When Link interacts with them, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Areas After luring Link to the Sanctum, Ganondorf summons two waves of Phantom Ganons as a boss. During the fight, the first floor of the Sanctum, the Throne Room, can be seen in pristine condition. Link is able to fight off the Phantom Ganons with the aid of the Sages, but the Demon King escapes after taunting them with a vision of his planned invasion of Hyrule. The room returns to its original state after the battle ends. Areas Enemies Bosses Equipment Treasure Chests Korok Seeds Other Appearances

The is a recurring location in . The Sanctum Observation Room goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Sanctum Observation Room is located on the third floor of the Sanctum of Hyrule Castle. From this vantage point, all of Central Hyrule can be seen. A hole in the center of the Room allows Link a view of the Champions' Hall below. Before the Great Calamity, those in the Sanctum Observation Room were able to see all the way down to the Throne Room. However, the top of Ganon's Cocoon has blocked this view. Unlike other parts of Hyrule Castle, the Sanctum Observation Room has avoided much of the damage caused by Calamity Ganon. As in , the Sanctum Observation Room sits above Hyrule Castle's Sanctum in Hyrule Field. Treasure Chests

are recurring locations in . Features and Overview Sand-Seal Rental Shops are a variety of Shop that exists only within Gerudo Town. Their purpose is to rent trained Sand Seals to people heading into the Gerudo Desert. The Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth is located near the Southeast Gate and operated Essa and Frelly, while the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Northwest Booth is situated near the Northwest Gate and operated by Kohm. The Shops' Sand Seals are trained by Frelly to be faster than their wild counterparts, and they also do not run away if their rider dismounts them. It costs Link 20 Rupees to rent a Sand Seal, although he can pay 50 Rupees to receive a Wooden Shield that he can use while Sand-Seal Surfing. The Sand-Seal Rentals Shops in Gerudo Town return in . They have also been renamed to the Sand-Seal Rental Shop East Gate Booth and the Sand-Seal Rental Shop West Gate Booth. However, due to the Sand Shroud covering the Gerudo Desert, they are not operational until the Main Quest "Riju of Gerudo Town" has been completed. Frelly is in charge of the East Gate Booth, while Essa manages the West Gate Booth. In addition to these two Shops, a new Sand-Seal Rental Shop run by Kohm can be found near the entrance to the Gerudo Desert.

page_title: Sand-Seal Rental Shop East Gate Booth
text: The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth is a Shop operated by Frelly in Gerudo Town. Another employee, Essa, works part-time feeding and cleaning up after the resident Sand Seals. The Rental Shop rents out Sand Seals to assist people in Surfing through the Gerudo Desert. Its sister shop, the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Northwest Booth is operated by Frelly's mother, Kohm. The Southeast Booth is marked by a large Sand-Seal Statue with the word "rental" written beneath it in Gerudo. The Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth charges 20 Rupees to rent a Sand Seal, though this price increases to 50 Rupees if Link does not have a Shield. Sand Seals allow Link to traverse the Gerudo Desert very quickly. According to Essa, Frelly trained all of the Sand Seals at the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth to be faster and to wait for their riders to return to them. A young Gerudo girl named Pearle likes to check on the Sand Seals in the later hours of the morning. Like Patricia, all the trained Sand Seals have names. At the Southeast Booth, they are named Sue, Nah, and Zarashi. Creatures Creatures

page_title: Sand-Seal Rental Shop West Gate Booth
text: The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Sand-Seal Rental Shop Northwest Booth is a Shop operated by Kohm in Gerudo Town. It rents out Sand Seals to the residents and visitors of Gerudo Town, which allow them to quickly traverse the Gerudo Desert via Sand-Seal Surfing. Its sister shop, the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Southeast Booth is operated by Kohm's daughter, Frelly. The Northwest Booth is marked by a large Sand-Seal Statue with the word "rental" written beneath it in Gerudo. Kohm charges Link 20 Rupees to rent a Sand Seal. If Link does not have a Shield, Kohm will offer to include a Wooden Shield in the rental, though the price increases to 50 Rupees. Due to the Sand Seals at the Rental Shop being trained, they are more obedient than their wild counterparts, as evidenced by the fact that they will not run away if Link dismounts from them. Creatures Creatures

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Sand Boots can be used to travel more quickly across sandy ground, such as the Gerudo Desert or beach areas. They can also be worn in Gerudo Town (in conjunction with the Gerudo Top and Gerudo Veil). To get the Sand Boots, Link must speak to Bozai, who can be found jogging around Gerudo Town. Link must wear the complete Gerudo Outfit to initiate a Side Quest called The Eighth Heroine. Link will temporarily be given Snow Boots for this quest. Once Link has ventured to the Gerudo Highlands and taken a picture of the Statue of the Eighth Heroine, he must show it to Bozai. Link will trade back the Snow Boots and be given the Sand Boots. After acquiring them, Granté will begin to sell the Sand Boots in Tarrey Town. The Sand Boots are not required to complete any Quests in the game, but Link will be able to access The Forgotten Sword quest after obtaining them. Dye Options Enhancing Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances The Sand Boots are a piece of Attire obtained when the Warriors complete the Quest "Surveying the Desert Ruins". It can only be worn by Link, and can be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. They are modified by Gerudo artisans to allow normal movement in sand. Dye Options

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Sanidin Park Ruins are located atop Safula Hill in the Hyrule Ridge. The Sanidin Park Ruins resemble a horseshoe. The Ruins feature two fountains and a pond. At the center of the fountain in the middle of the horseshoe design sits a statue of a Horse rearing. The Hylian traveler, Glendo, can be seen riding his Horse along the path in the Ruins. There, he points out how Hyrule Castle is visible from the Park Ruins, though the sight of it fills him with dread. Sanidin Park Ruins is the site of the Recovered Memory, "To Mount Lanayru", which Link can recall by visiting the Park Ruins after speaking with Impa and receiving the "Captured Memories" Main Quest. In the memory, prior to the second Great Calamity, Zelda and Link ride across Safula Hill to the Sanidin Park Ruins, where Zelda shows Link Mount Lanayru on the day before her 17th birthday, when she will be allowed to climb the mountain and pray at the Spring of Wisdom, the third and final Spring that Zelda must visit. Creatures Creatures

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Sanke Carp are a type of Fish found exclusively at the base of the Lantern Falls in Kakariko Village. They are a subspecies of Armored Carp that do not provide any special effects when Cooked. When consumed, Sanke Carp restore one of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge each. When exposed to Fire, Sanke Carp become Roasted Carps, while they can be chilled by Ice to make Frozen Carp. Similar to other fish, Sanke Carp can be used in a Cooking Pot to make a Fish Skewer, a Fish and Mushroom Skewer, and Salt-Grilled Fish. They also count towards seafood when making Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. Sanke Carp return in , possessing the same properties as they did in . In addition to spawning at the base of Lantern Falls, one Sanke Carp can be found in each Garden Pond when included in Link's House. Unlike other Materials and Animals, the Sanke Carp found in Garden Ponds will be respawned by Blood Moons if taken. Other Appearances

is a character in . Overview Sanson is a Goron employed by YunoboCo, and he wears a Helmet and wields a Pickaxe. He is responsible for leading YunoboCo's staff at the Hudson Construction Site. When Link speaks to Sanson, he initially claims that he is sworn to secrecy about the details of his job. However, he soon after reveals that the Hudson Construction Site has so many Zonai Devices and other valuables that it has been referred to as the "Zonai Treasure Trove". He states that YunoboCo's purpose at the Site to gather these Devices, and Hudson and the Zonai Survey Team collaborate in their development.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Sapphires are Materials in . They can be found by destroying Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits, or by defeating Stone Taluses, silver Enemy variants, and Yiga Blademasters. They are sold by Pelison at Ore and More and Kairo along the Mountain Road. They are imbued with the power of Ice, which is useful for making Heat Resistant Armor. Three Sapphires are needed to purchase the Sapphire Circlet from Starlight Memories in Gerudo Town. In addition, the merchant Ramella in Goron City will occasionally ask for Sapphires, which she will pay an increased price for. Sapphires are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Sapphires can be Fused to Arrows to create massive blasts of cold upon impact. Sapphires are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances Sapphires are Gems in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Sapphire Circlets are a type of Circlet Accessory that is worn as head Armor. They can be purchased in the Starlight Memories Jewelry Shop in Gerudo Town. They cost 800 Rupees and three Sapphires to buy. Alternatively, at the end of the "Tools of the Trade" Side Quest, one of the Accessories that Isha offers to make Link as a reward is a Sapphire Circlet. When worn, they provide Link with one level of Heat Resistance. Sapphire Circlets can be enhanced by a Great Fairy at a Great Fairy Fountain. However, they cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Enhancing Enhancing Other Appearances The Sapphire Circlet is a piece of Attire that can only be worn by Link, and it is obtained by completing the Quest "The Hope of Lanayru". Unlike most other pieces of Attire, it cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Sarjon Bridge is located in West Necluda northeast of Sarjon Woods. The Sarjon Bridge extends over the Floria River between two small waterfalls. Occasionally, travelers like Chumin walk along this bridge. On the northern side of the Sarjon Bridge, a Flower Trail can be found near a small pillar. If Link walks close to the flower, it will disappear and reappear closer to the Sarjon Bridge, eventually leading Link across the bridge. Once Link gets to the end of the Flower Trail, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Sarjon Bridge's stonework is carved with Zonai imagery and designs. The support columns are capped with abstract carvings with a similar shape and color pattern as Zonai Dragon Statues, most notably the head and mouth. Each "head" is also topped with a ridge of spiral crests, similar to the large sculpture at the Spring of Courage. Creatures

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Sarjon Woods are located in West Necluda between Guchini Plain and Floria River. The Sarjon Woods are mostly grown on a raised plateau with many layers each containing trees. The Sarjon Woods' Plateau is surrounded by Floria River on the north and east, and by a path on the west and south. One Korok can be found hiding in the Eastern Sarjon Woods. Below the plateau, a big tree sprouts out of the ground. Atop this tree is a Hidden Balloon, which Link can pop to make the Korok appear and obtain a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

, also known as the Strange Mountain, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Satori Mountain is located on the southern end of Hyrule Ridge. Many Ore Deposits, Rare Ore Deposits, and Luminous Stone Deposits appear throughout the Mountain. On top of the Mountain is a Cherry-Blossom Tree known as Mother Tree, which sits beside a small pond. Rutile Lake also rests on Satori Mountain's western foothills, and Mogg Latan Shrine can be found near its peak. Despite the Mountain's points of interest, travelers rarely make the journey to visit it. thumb|right|320px|alt= An aerial view of Satori Mountain's summit.|The Lord of the Mountain on Satori Mountain from Occasionally, the top of Satori Mountain will glow green. During this time, the Lord of the Mountain and a group of Blupees will appear near Mother Tree. A variety of Creatures will also appear on Satori Mountain and in Rutile Lake, which is supposedly a result of being called there by the Lord. The Stals that are usually present on the Mountain will remain dormant during this night. However, if Link disturbs the Lord of the Mountain, it will flee, which causes the green light to fade and all of the Creatures visiting the Mountain to vanish. In the past, Quince ventured to Satori Mountain, hoping to hunt the Creatures that gather there and sell their Meat. While there, he met a Hylian Retriever puppy, Satty, who he gave some of his jerky to. After Quince fell asleep, he awoke to the Lord of the Mountain nearby, which began to charge at him. However, he was saved by Satty, who jumped between him and the Lord. When the Lord of the Mountain recoiled, Quince took the opportunity to grab Satty and flee from Satori Mountain. As part of the "EX Ancient Horse Rumors" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack, Link reads the Super Rumor Mill V3 at Highland Stable. The Book details rumors about Ancient Horse Gear, claiming that the Ancient Bridle can be found underneath a cherry blossom Tree on a mountain. Near Mother Tree on Satori Mountain, Link will find a Hidden Chest embedded in the ground. Using Magnesis, he can free the Chest, which contains the Ancient Bridle. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Equipment Inhabitants Korok Seeds left|40px A total of 15 Korok Seed Puzzles are located on Satori Mountain. Each time Link solves one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear nearby as a result. It will then give him a Korok Seed as a reward for finding it. Their locations are as follows: A Natural Hiding Spot, taking the form of a Rock under a Pile of Leaves north of Rutile Lake. A Natural Hiding Spot, taking the form of a Rock hidden under a pile of bombable rocks north of Rutile Lake. A Flower Trail north of Rutile Lake. A Boulder that must be rolled into a hole south of the Mountain's peak. A Natural Hiding Spot, taking the form of a Rock underneath a Boulder south of the Stalnox. A Jar in a fallen Tree on the southern end of the Mountain, which Link must break using Archery. A Natural Hiding Spot, taking the form of a Rock in a Tree Stump east of the Mountain's peak. A Flower Trail starting at the Mountain's peak. A Race, which starts near the Mountain's Stalnox. Materials Treasure Chests Many Treasure Chests can be found throughout Satori Mountain. In total, these Chests contains one Opal, one Topaz, one Forest Dweller's Spear, one Forest Dweller's Bow, five Ice Arrows, one Purple Rupee, and two Silver Rupees. Satori Mountain has a counterpart in the Depths known as Blupee Burrow. This Burrow also houses a Cherry-Blossom Tree and is the only place in the Depths where Blupees can be found. Areas

is a recurring location in . Satori Mountain South goes unnamed in . Features and Overview is a cliff directly south of Satori Mountain's peak on Hyrule Ridge. It features several Cedar Trees. On nights when the Lord of the Mountain is present on Satori Mountain, unique Creatures will appear there. A Stalnox resides on Satori Mountain South. It will be dormant during the day, but at night, it will become active and walk around. Should Link approach the Stalnox, it will attack him. However, it will remain inactive whenever the Lord of the Mountain is on Satori Mountain. Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Satori Mountain South returns in . Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses

is a recurring character in . Biography Saula is a Gerudo who manages the Armor Shop, Fashion Passion, in Gerudo Town. If Link speaks to her, she compliments him for his Gerudo Top and encourages him to try out more colors. If Link asks about the different colors, Saula expresses surprise that he does not know and explains that dyeing clothing is popular for "young vai" right now. She goes on to tell Link about the Kochi Dye Shop in Hateno Village where he can dye his Armor. However, she states that not many get to travel there due to its large distance from Gerudo Town. Saula also states that it is hot and expresses her desire to get a cold drink at The Noble Canteen. Like most other store owners, Saula will also buy Items from Link. If he decides to say goodbye, she comments that the evening is nice and cool, and that at times like these she likes to grab drinks at the canteen. Through the doorway behind Fashion Passion is a curtain that conceals an entrance to the Gerudo Secret Club If Link attempts to enter, Saula stops him, telling him that the doorway is not for customers. Saula then whispers to Link and tells him to use the door on the side of the building if he is a member. Saula knows about the Gerudo Secret Club, and is likely a member, as suggested by Yaido if Link eavesdrops on the Gerudo in The Noble Canteen. Yaido reveals that she overheard Saula say that the password to enter the Gerudo Secret Club is "GSC♦."

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can make Sautéed Nuts by Cooking at least one Nut in a Cooking Pot. This can be either an Acorn or a Chickaloo Tree Nut. Eating these Meals will restore some of Link's Hearts. They are considered to be the perfect snack for busy adventurers. No variations of Sautéed Nuts can be made. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Sautéed Peppers are made by Cooking Spicy Peppers in a Cooking Pot. Since their only ingredient is Spicy Pepper, there is no default version of them, and only Spicy Sautéed Peppers can be made. Eating these Meals will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Savage Lynel Bows are Bows found in the Hebra Mountains and Hyrule Field. White-Maned Lynels, Silver Lynels, and Golden Lynels all use them when fighting. These Bows are part of the Lynel Gear equipment archetype, which is a group of Weapons created by Lynels. They are forged with a special steel found at the peak of Death Mountain, and they have the strength to pierce thick Armor. Being made of metal, Savage Lynel Bows will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. They also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, Savage Lynel Bows will not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate.

are recurring Items in . Savage Lynel Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Savage Lynel Shields are considered the ultimate Lynel Shield, known to be wielded by White-Maned Lynels. They are also used by Silver Lynels and Golden Lynels. Not only are they capable of defending the most brutal of attacks, they can also cut down powerful foes with a deflection (dealing 21 damage). They belong to the Lynel Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Weapons created by Lynels. As they are made of metal, Savage Lynel Shields will attract Lightning if they are equipped during a thunderstorm. They also sink if they are dropped in water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, they will not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Savage Lynel Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Savage Lynel Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Savage Lynel Swords.

a game in progress via a built-in battery was one of the most unique features from , and a save function has since been in every game to date. In most cases, the save function can be accessed at anytime during gameplay from the start menu. In addition to retaining the game data, the save function allowed for the player to name the protagonist of the story. Overview The option to save from appears after losing all Life energy. This same menu can also be accessed by pressing Up on the Control Pad and the A Button simultaneously on the second controller while the game is paused (doing so will warp Link back to the starting screen). included a save system similar to that of the first title. There were three save files, in which a player could enter their choice of name. The player could access the save menu by pressing A, B, Start, and Select Buttons, or by death in-game. can be accessed from the in , or by pressing the start and select (or plus and minus) buttons at the same time. Three save files are also available for use in the game. thumb|right|Link quicksaving at an Owl Statue in deviated from the standard saving system immensely. The ability to save from anywhere and anytime during gameplay had been removed. In , the player can save the game by playing the "Song of Time" to return to the start of the First Day. Players can also quicksave at Owl Statues, a temporary save that allows players to save their progress partway through the three-day cycle or just before entering a dungeon. In the Japanese version of the Nintendo 64 release (and its Virtual Console release), Owl Statues cannot be used to quicksave; this function was added in the international release of the Nintendo 64 release (at the expense of the game having two save files rather than three), and was also added to the Japanese release of in . In , the "Song of Time" no longer saves the game. Instead, Owl Statues permanently save the game; additionally, Statue Statues were added, which allow saving like Owl Statues but cannot be warped to with the "Song of Soaring". The game also has three save files, like the original Japanese release. saving system departed from the typical manner of series. Saving was automatically done upon the completion of a level throughout the game. Saving in is performed using the Save button from the Collection Screen. An option to Save Link's progress will also be given after certain events, such as clearing a Dungeon. introduces the ability to save Link's progress to any of the three Quest Logs at will, rather than having to copy a Quest Log beforehand. This ability was removed from subsequent games but returns in . Saving in works similarly to , using Bird Statues scattered throughout the map; however, these saves are permanent, rather than the temporary save states of the Owl Statues. Because

Saving in works similarly to , using Bird Statues scattered throughout the map; however, these saves are permanent, rather than the temporary save states of the Owl Statues. Because this is the one and only way to save in , the Bird Statues are much more numerous than Owl Statues were in , with some even found in dungeons. Once the credits finish, the option to create a Hero Mode file is offered, but this will save over the existing file. In , the player can choose which of the three files to save onto, as opposed to saving over the file that the game started on. This allows the creation of a Hero Mode file without deleting the existing progress. Also, an Autosave function is added. In , Link can save by using Weather Vanes. Once a sleeping Weather Vane is found, Link must talk to it in order to wake it up. Weather Vanes can be found in both Hyrule and Lorule. They are also seen flapping their wings and moving around in a panicked manner after Link has completed a large task, or has spent a considerable amount of time doing things since his last save, trying to indicate that now may be the time to save. In , saving is performed at a statue in the center of Hytopia Village, referred to as the Tri Force Hero Statue. The raised sword atop the Statue will shimmer when Link saves his journey's progress, similarly to a charged Skyward Strike. If Link proceeds to the Castle without saving first, then the Bearded Baron, who is standing nearby, will implore Link to "give thanks" to the statue. Link's progress is also saved automatically at the conclusion of each Level, whether the Links successfully complete the Level, lose all health, fail the Drablands Challenge, or are disconnected from a multiplayer game. If a Link intentionally leaves the game, he will simply return to Hytopia Castle without having his progress saved. Automatic saving also occurs after each completed battle in the Coliseum and after each completed Zone in the Den of Trials. is the only main series game that does not allow for multiple save files. In , Link can Save by using the Save button in the System screen. Link's progress is also periodically recorded by Autosaves after performing certain actions (such as receiving an item from a Treasure Chest or resting at a Campfire), approaching certain locations (such as Ancient Shrines or Stables) or every five minutes. In Normal Mode, Link is allowed to utilize one Save file and up to five Autosave files while in Master Mode Link is restricted to using one Save file and one Autosave file.
