Other Appearances In , the game can be saved by accessing a Tingle Tuner-like device found within Tingle's house. There are three save files which can be selected at the start of the game, with Tingle holding up the respective number of fingers for the file icon. In , Tingle has the ability to save his game in one of three files by accessing a save point, and tapping on a spinning, three-dimensional pig known as the Save Pig. Unlike the previous Tingle Series installment, the player can choose to save the game to any of the three files while playing. Once the game is completed, the file image icons will replace the three images of Tingle with the likes of Kakashi, Buriki, and Lion, respectively.

is a character in . Biography Sawson is a Hylian who works for Hudson Construction. He can be found at three different Skyview Towers: Ulri Mountain Skyview Tower, Gerudo Canyon Skyview Tower and Eldin Canyon Skyview Tower. He was sent there to fix them, but he ran into trouble and needs Link's assistance to get them working: at Ulri Mountain an Aerocuda has stolen the terminal, at Gerudo Canyon the elevator is broken and Sawson cannot reach the Tower, and at Eldin Canyon a piece of Fallen Debris has hit the Tower and jammed the doors. When the issue has been dealt with, Sawson can repair the Tower. He then thanks Link for his help. Once all three towers have been fixed, Sawson can be found bathing at the Goron Hot Springs. He is still grateful to Link for helping with the Towers, so he offers to share some information about other Hot Springs and their locations.

is a character in . Biography Sawtu is a member of Hoz's Monster-Control Crew squad and a Hylian. He carries a Rusty Broadsword and a Knight's Shield. During the search for Zelda and Link at Hyrule Castle, Sawtu can be found on top of the First Gatehouse. Having already completed looking around, he is awaiting new orders from Hoz, but he is hesitant to approach him when he seems on edge. In case Link wants to speak to Hoz, Sawtu allows him to go first. During the "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" Main Quest, Sawtu witnesses the figure resembling Zelda fly away from Hyrule Castle and disappear into Light, which he is confused by. The unit he belongs to goes to attack a Monster Stronghold south of the Hyrule Garrison Ruins as part of the "Bring Peace to Hyrule Field!" Side Adventure, where he uses a Rusty Broadsword and a Knight's Shield. When spoken to during the battle, he thanks Link for his support but wants to focus on the battle.

are recurring Items in . Scales go unnamed in . Location and Uses The Scale is the thirteenth item in 's Trading Quest. It is obtained from Martha the Mermaid, who promises Link one of her Scales from her tail in return of her missing Necklace. The Scale is pivotal to complete "The Mourning Mermaid", an unfinished Statue that Schule Donavitch sculpted in Martha's Bay. After placing the Scale onto the statue, it will move aside and reveal a cave where Link finds the final item in the Trading Sequence, the Magnifying Lens. Scales are Dragon Parts that fall from Dinraal, Farosh, the Light Dragon, and Naydra after their bodies or manes are struck. Imbued with elemental power in the case of Dinraal, Farosh, and Naydra's Scales and healing power for the Light Dragon Scales, they impart their power onto Weapons they are fused to, causing them to use Fire, Electricity and Ice for the elemental Dragons and to heal Link when he strikes an Enemy or Object for the Light Dragon. Arrows with the Scales of the elemental Dragons attached create large explosions of Fire, Electricity, and cold air respectively on impacting something. List of Scales

are Items in . Location and Uses Schema Stones are a type of Key Item used to obtain new Autobuild designs. They are primarily obtained from Steward Constructs in Abandoned Mines, with two exceptions; the Schema Stone for the Hot-Air Balloon Schematic is given by Josha as a reward for completing "A Mystery in the Depths", and the Beam Cycle Schematic is obtained from the Steward Construct in the Shrine of Resurrection. If Link speaks with a Steward Construct that can provide a Schema Stone prior to obtaining Autobuild, he will be instructed to travel to the Great Abandoned Central Mine before he can receive it. After the Steward Construct at an Abandoned Mine has provided Link with its Schema Stone, it will also supply Link with the Objects needed to assemble the Schematic. At most Abandoned Mines, the assembled Schematic can be used to more easily reach a Treasure Chest. List of Schema Stones There are a total of 12 Schema Stones.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses As part of the Champion's Arms, Scimitars of the Seven are commonly used alongside Daybreaker Shields. They belong to the Gerudo Gear equipment archetype, which is a series of Weapons created and utilized by the Gerudo. Prior to the Great Calamity, the Gerudo Champion Urbosa wielded a Scimitar of the Seven with a Daybreaker. They were created by a Gerudo jeweler. It is said that Urbosa's movements resembled a dance while she used the Scimitar in battle. During the EX Recovered Memory "Champion Urbosa's Song", Urbosa can be seen using her Scimitar to fight off a pair of Yiga Footsoldiers attacking Zelda. Riju will gift Link Urbosa's Scimitar of the Seven and Daybreaker after completing the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest. She believes that, since Link was friends with Urbosa, they should be in his possession. They can be found in a pair of Stone Chests behind Riju's Throne in the Royal Palace. If Link loses the Scimitar of the Seven, he can go to Buliara to replace it, though it will cost him one Diamond, five pieces of Flint, and a Gerudo Scimitar. Scimitars of the Seven are made of metal, and will therefore attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. This also means that they are capable of conducting Electricity. They will sink if dropped in the Water, but they can be picked up again using the Magnesis Rune. In addition, they will not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Scimitars of the Seven return in . They are one of the few Weapons to remain Intact after the rest Decayed as a result of the Upheaval. Paired with Daybreakers, they are considered part of the Arms of the Seven, which can be made using a technique known by a select few. Currently, Isha is the only individual who knows how to make them. Both pieces form a bond with their owners that can only be broken when they are permanently lost. Riju now dual-wields two Scimitars of the Seven, which Isha chose to make for her. Isha also claims that her ancestor was responsible for crafting Urbosa's Scimitar. Throughout the Main Quest "Riju of Gerudo Town", Riju utilizes her Scimitars to fight Gibdos with Link. Most notably, she uses them during the Gibdo invasions of Kara Kara Bazaar and Gerudo Town, in addition to combating Enemies in the Lightning Temple. Riju's Sage Avatar wields projections of her two Scimitars of the Seven, which will still count toward the Hyrule Compendium if Link takes a Picture of them. If Riju has been awoken as a Sage, she will appear to help Link during the War in the Depths of Hyrule, where she uses her Scimitars to fight the Demon King's Army. As part of the Side Quest "Pride of the Gerudo", Isha chooses to make a Scimitar of the Seven and Daybreaker for Link. Since Link will be carrying these Arms of the Seven,

War in the Depths of Hyrule, where she uses her Scimitars to fight the Demon King's Army. As part of the Side Quest "Pride of the Gerudo", Isha chooses to make a Scimitar of the Seven and Daybreaker for Link. Since Link will be carrying these Arms of the Seven, it is his responsibility to procure the supplies to create them. To make the Scimitar, she requires three Diamonds, five pieces of Flint, and a Gerudo Scimitar, the latter of which can be either Decayed or an intact Gerudo Scimitar✨. Once Link has brought Isha the necessary Materials, she will make a pair of Arms of the Seven for him. When she is done, she gives them to Link, claiming that they are a symbol of the Gerudo's gratitude toward him. If Link ever breaks his Scimitar, Isha offers to make a new one for him. However, she refuses to do so if his Scimitar can still be retrieved, since his bond with it has not been broken. In flashbacks to the Imprisoning War that took place during the Era of Foundation, the Sage of Lightning Ardi can be seen carrying her own Scimitar of the Seven and Daybreaker. Other Appearances Scimitars of the Seven are Urbosa's primary Weapons. When one is equipped, a Daybreaker will appear as her Shield. Additionally, Scimitars of the Seven are the default Weapons used by Urbosa in Movies and Narrations. For example, she draws her Scimitar in "Return of the Chief", uses it to attack Master Kohga and Sooga in "Slippery as a Banana Peel!", wields it when threatened by a Monster ambush in "A Song from the Past", and fights Thunderblight Ganon with it in "Rescue Across Time: Air and Lightning". Ardi uses the Scimitar of the Seven alongside the Daybreaker in battle.

The is a recurring mechanic in . Overview The Scope is a feature used to view landmarks at a distance and place Pins that are visible on the Map, Mini-Map, and when using the Scope. In , the Scope is a function of the Sheikah Slate, and it can be used whenever Link is on solid ground. It can be used to place up to five Pins. In , the Scope is used via the Purah Pad. Up to six Pins can be placed at any time. The Scope can now be used in midair, slowing time in a manner similar to when Link draws a Bow in the air.

are a recurring mechanic in . Scorching Climates go unnamed in , , and . Overview In , the Death Mountain Crater, Fire Temple, and Fire Room are all located within or contain a Scorching Climate. When Link is in a Scorching Climate, a countdown timer will appear. The amount of time Link has is eight seconds for every Heart in his Life Gauge. If this timer expires, Link will instantly die, although he is able to be saved if he has a Fairy. Wearing the Goron Tunic allows Link to traverse Scorching Climates without taking damage. The Volcano Summit, which is located on the upper portion of Eldin Volcano, is a Scorching Climate. In , a Scorching Climate appears in the Eldin Canyon and Death Mountain. It is the result of Divine Beast Vah Rudania's rampage, which has worsened the eruptions from Death Mountain. When in a Scorching Climate, Link will catch on Fire and begin to take damage. He will also have a pained expression on his face. However, this can be avoided by wearing pieces of Fireproof Armor or drinking a Fireproof Elixir, both of which grant the Flame Guard Added Effect. Additionally, Arrows drawn in a Scorching Climate will ignite and deal Fire damage when shot at flammable Objects or Enemies. If Link attempts to fire a Bomb Arrow in a Scorching Climate, it will immediately explode. Several of the Death Mountain Markers along the Mountain Road track the intensity of Eldin Volcano and Death Mountain's Scorching Climate. The Scorching Climate begins near Medingo Pool, only requiring one level of Flame Guard to traverse. At the Abandoned North Mine and past the Bridge of Eldin, the Scorching Climate intensifies, requiring two levels of Flame Guard for protection. In a Scorching Climate, Roasted Foods can be created by dropping their corresponding Materials onto the ground. Weapons, Bows, and Shields that are made of wood will also burn when exposed to a Scorching Climate, eventually disintegrating into ash. In , Eldin Canyon has cooled down with the dormancy of Death Mountain and no longer has a Scorching Climate. However, the Caves within these Regions still contain Scorching Climates. Additionally, parts of the Depths contain Scorching Climates, such as the Death Mountain Depths, Eldin Canyon Depths, and parts of the Eldin Mountains Depths. Waterfalls of Flowing Lava, which are located below Hot Springs on the Surface, are also surrounded by Scorching Climates. Lastly, Dinraal is surrounded by a Scorching Climate that moves with her. Like in , Link is required either equip a piece of Flame-Resistant Equipment or drink Fireproof Elixirs to safely navigate Scorching Climates. If Link brings out a Bomb Flower in a Scorching Climate, it will explode the moment he either drops or throws it, or when he Fuses it to an Arrow. However, this explosion can be prevented by dousing the Link in Water first. In , Scorching Climates are created by the presence of Lava in an area. A Scorching Climate is present on

explode the moment he either drops or throws it, or when he Fuses it to an Arrow. However, this explosion can be prevented by dousing the Link in Water first. In , Scorching Climates are created by the presence of Lava in an area. A Scorching Climate is present on Eldin Volcano in the area surrounding its Crater. This includes several Caves, such as the Crater Shortcut, the Rock-Roast Quarry, and the Lizalfos Burrow. Areas in the Still World that feature Lava, like the Stilled Eldin Volcano, Stilled Western Eldin Volcano, and parts of Eldin Temple, are also subjected to Scorching Climates. When Princess Zelda is idle within a Scorching Climate, she will sweat and fan herself, which is similar to reaction to the Heat of the Gerudo Desert. Unlike in other appearances, Scorching Climates do not cause damage to Zelda.

is a character in . Biography Scorpis is a Hylian member of the Monster-Control Crew charged with managing Lookout Landing. He guards the entrance to the Emergency Shelter. He wears a tattered Soldier's Armor chest piece, and he wields a Soldier's Spear. When Link first arrives in Lookout Landing, Scorpis will be shocked to see him. He asks Link where he has been, claiming that they have been hoping he would return. Although he is concerned about Zelda's whereabouts, Scorpis directs Link to meet with Purah in her Research Lab. After Link has done so, Scorpis will apologize for not greeting him properly and introduce himself. He tells Link to come to him if he has any questions, before he proceeds to open the Emergency Shelter. Banging his Soldier's Spear on the ground, Scorpis identifies himself and demands that the Shelter be opened. The Triforce-design in the stonework then lowers itself and moves out of the way. Scorpis explains that it was once a refuge for the Royal Family of Hyrule, but now it is used by the people of Lookout Landing. Afterwards, Link is able to ask Scorpis questions about Lookout Landing. When asked about recent events, Scorpis claims that the Cook in the Emergency Shelter, Burmano, has been struggling to come up with daily menus. He recalls that when it was his duty to serve as the Shelter's chef, he gave up and started making Baked Apples. If Link asks about Lookout Landing, he learns that it was originally established to study the Gloom that came from Beneath Hyrule Castle, but it has now become the central base in the search for Zelda. Previously, the only residents were researchers and Zonai Survey Team members, but new people have come to help since Zelda went missing. Lastly, if Link requests equipment, Scorpis offers the Emergency Shelter's Beds and Cooking Pot. He also suggests that Link visit Mubs's Shop for Armor and Materials. Should Link end their conversation, Scorpis claims that Hudson Construction is responsible for building new facilities.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Scout's Hill is located in Hyrule Field, along the western bank of the Hylia River just before it empties into Lake Hylia. Bosh Kala Shrine can be found at the Hill's northern base. A stone Treasure Chest containing a Sapphire can be found atop a stone pillar on the Hill's northern section. At the base of the pillar is a wooden crate holding Arrows. Some Ore Deposits are present near the Shrine, just to the west. A Korok can be found by lifting a Rock on top of the ruins at the Hill's peak. Another can be found by pushing a Boulder down into a hole on the northern half of the Hill. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment As in , Scout's Hill is located in Hyrule Field.

The , also known as the , is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Boomerang can be found inside the Forbidden Woods in . It now can lock onto up to five different targets, which is used in various puzzles involving Switches or for collecting multiple items at the same time. The Boomerang primarily stuns enemies, though it can kill Boko Babas in one hit. The Sea-Breeze Boomerang is obtained by scanning either the or The Legend of Zelda series Toon Link amiibo with the amiibo Rune. It is the Boomerang used by a hero during the Era of the Great Sea, and it consequently retains the scent of saltwater. Despite this, Link can obtain multiple Sea-Breeze Boomerangs from repeatedly scanning the Toon Link amiibo. Since it is made of wood, the Sea-Breeze Boomerang will burn and disintegrate if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. It will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity like metallic Weapons, and it will also float if it is dropped on Water. After Link throws the Boomerang, it will return to him after a short while. If he does not catch it when it does so, it will hit him and he will take damage. The Sea-Breeze Boomerang is a One-Handed Weapon that can be obtained from a Treasure Chest in the Hebra Canyon Mine. It can also be obtained by scanning either the or series Toon Link amiibo with the amiibo. Once it is obtained, it will then be available to buy from the Bargainer Statues in the Depths for 100 Poes.

, also known as , and , are recurring Items in . The Sea-Breeze Shield goes unnamed in , , and . Location and Uses right|thumb|200px|Link's Grandma presenting him with the family Shield from The Hero's Shield is the basic Shield received at the beginning of . It bears a resemblance to the Small Shield once used by the Link in . The Shield is sturdy and provides adequate protection against most attacks, although its flimsy appearance is mocked by Tetra. Despite this, the Hero's Shield will not burn upon contact with fire like most wooden Shields. The Hero's Shield is an heirloom belonging to Link's family. It is said that the family Shield was the legendary Shield used by the Hero himself. The Hero's Shield is given to Link by his Grandma before he leaves Outset Island to save his sister, Aryll. It is with sadness that Link's Grandma gives him the Hero's Shield, as it symbolizes his departure from the Island to face great danger. Link uses the Shield throughout a large portion of the game before obtaining the Mirror Shield in the Earth Temple, after which the Hero's Shield disappears from Link's Items Screen. The Hero's Shield is predominantly brown. The design of the Triforce is present in the very center of the Shield. There are long swirls surrounding it as well as three bolts at its corners. A winged creature with horns replaces the typical bird motif. The Hero's Shield from the Era of the Great Sea appears in . It is obtained randomly when 30th Anniversary series -themed Princess Zelda amiibo is used is scanned using the amiibo Rune. Multiple can be obtained through repeatedly scanning the Rune. It is said this Shield was the favorite of a hero who travelled the open seas. This Shield was apparently a family heirloom, passed down through generations. Being made of metal, the Hero's Shield will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if it is equipped during a Thunderstorm. It will also sink if it is dropped in Water. However, it can be picked up with the Magnesis Rune, and it will not burn like wooden Shields do when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Sea-Breeze Shields are Shields in . Like in , they can be obtained by scanning -themed Princess Zelda amiibo. One can also be found in a Treasure Chest in Tabahl Grove. Once obtained, they can be purchased from a Bargainer Statue for 120 Poes. Other Appearances Toon Link uses the Hylian Shield in battle. It also appears as a Sticker. The Sea-Breeze Shield is used alongside the Hero's Sword in . Toon Link uses the Sea-Breeze Shield in battle in .

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Seabed Inn is an Inn that is located in Zora's Domain. It is operated by Kayden, whose wife Kodah takes care of other tasks, such as beckoning customers from the Zora's Domain Square. The Inn consists of two rooms. The first room has a Cooking Pot over a Campfire, as well as several Jars. The second room bears the front desk where Kayden works, as well as the Inn's two Beds. After the "Divine Beast Vah Ruta (Quest)" Main Quest has been completed, Douma will begin to Sleep at the Seabed Inn during the night. Similarly, Sasan will stay at the Inn once the "Special Delivery" Side Quest has finished. The Seabed Inn offers two types of Beds to its customers: the regular Bed for 20 Rupees, and the blissful Water Bed for 80 Rupees. When asked about the Water Bed, Kayden explains that it offers a cooling effect that adds to the comfort one feels while Sleeping. This provides Link with an additional Heart and bonus Stamina when he wakes up. If Link chooses to stay at the Inn, Kayden offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or during the night. When Kayden wakes Link up, he will greet him. After Link uses the Water Bed, Kayden will hope that he enjoyed it. Equipment

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Seafood Curries can be made by Cooking Goron Spice, Hylian Rice, and either a Hearty Blueshell Snail, Armored Porgy, or Mighty Porgy in a Cooking Pot. The default version can be made by using two types of Seafood with differing effects. Eating these Meals will heal some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. Though this dish is filled with a lot of Seafood, the intensity of the Goron Spice makes it unsuitable for children. Depending on the type of Seafood used, three different variations of Seafood Curry exist: Hearty Seafood Curry: Made by using Hearty Blueshell Snails. When eaten, they will heal of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Mighty Seafood Curry: Made by using Mighty Porgies. By eating them, Link will receive a boost to his attack power. Tough Seafood Curry: Made by using Armored Porgies. Link can eat these curries to have his defensive abilities be increased. Seafood Curries can be made by Cooking either type of Porgy with Hylian Rice and Goron Spice.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Seafood Fried Rice can be made by Cooking Hylian Rice, a piece of Rock Salt, and either a Hearty Blueshell Snail or a Porgy in a Cooking Pot. To make the default version, Link must use two seafood Ingredients with contradicting effects. When they are eaten, Link will have some of his Hearts restored to his Life Gauge. These Meals are tastier when stronger Flames are used to cook them. Based on the type of seafood used, the three following variations of Seafood Fried Rice can be made: Hearty Seafood Fried Rice: Made by using Hearty Blueshell Snails. These Meals will completely heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him Extra Hearts. Mighty Seafood Fried Rice: Made by using Mighty Porgies. If eaten, Link will receive a boost to the power of his attacks. Tough Seafood Fried Rice: Made by using Armored Porgies. Link can eat them to receive an increase to his defensive abilities. Link can make Seafood Fried Rice by Cooking either type of Porgy with Hylian Rice and a piece of Rock Salt.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can make Seafood Meunières by Cooking Tabantha Wheat, Goat Butter, and any Seafood together in a Cooking Pot. The only exceptions to this are Hearty Salmons, Armored Porgies, and Mighty Porgies, as including these Fish will result in different Meals. The default version of Seafood Meunière can be made either by using Hyrule Basses or Sanke Carps, which offer no status effects, or by using multiple types of Seafood with differing effects. Eating these Meals will heal some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. The secret Ingredient to Seafood Meunière is a lot of love. When making Seafood Meunière, Link can make the following variations, based on both the type of seafood used as well as additional Ingredients: Hearty Seafood Meunière: Made by using Hearty Bass, Hearty Blueshell Snails, or other hearty Ingredients. When eaten, these will heal all of Link's Hearts and temporarily increase his maximum Hearts. Energizing Seafood Meunière: Made by using Staminoka Basses, Bright-Eyed Crabs, or other energizing Ingredients. By eating them, Link can refill part of his Stamina Wheel. Enduring Seafood Meunière: Made by using enduring Ingredients. Link's Stamina Wheel will be completely refreshed and overfilled if he eats them. Hasty Seafood Meunière: Made by using hasty Ingredients. They can be eaten to grant Link a boost to his movement speed. Spicy Seafood Meunière: Made by using Sizzlefin Trouts or other Ingredients. If Link consumes these meals, he will gain one level of Cold Resistance. Electro Seafood Meunière: Made by using Voltfin Trout or other spicy Ingredients. When eaten, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Seafood Meunière: Made by using Mighty Carp, Razorclaw Crabs, or other mighty Ingredients. Eating them will provide Link with a boost to his attack power. Tough Seafood Meunière: Made by using Armored Carp, Ironshell Crabs, or other tough Ingredients. Link's defensive abilities will be increased if he eats these. Sneaky Seafood Meunière: Made by using Stealthfin Trouts, Sneaky River Snails, or other sneaky Ingredients. These meals will provide a boost to Link's Stealth. Chilly Seafood Meunière: Made by using Chillfin Trouts or other chilly Ingredients. Consuming them will grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Seafood Meunières can be made by Cooking any type of Seafood, excluding Hearty Salmons and Porgies, with Goat Butter and Tabantha Wheat.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Seafood Paellas are made by Cooking a Hearty Blueshell Snail, Hylian Rice, Goat Butter, Rock Salt, and either a Mighty Porgy or an Armored Porgy together in a Cooking Pot. These Meals are considered top-shelf and are common in the birthday celebrations of fishermen. When Link speaks to Kiana in Lurelin Village, she will ask her son Kinov what she should make for dinner. Kinov responds that she should make Seafood Paella, to which Kiana agrees. However, since she is low on ingredients, she asks Link to retrieve and Hearty Blueshell Snail and Goat Butter for her. When Link returns with the ingredients, Kiana will ask for them. She tells Link she wll start Cooking and gives him a Purple Rupee as a reward. Kiana also invites Link to eat with her family since he brought her the ingredients, giving him Seafood Paella as well. Because the required ingredients are of contradicting effects, no variations of Seafood Paella can be made. Link can make Seafood Paella by Cooking any type of Crab, either kind of Porgy, Goat Butter, Hylian Rice, and Rock Salt together. Two variations of Seafood Paellas can be made: Mighty Seafood Paella: These can be made by using Mighty Porgies and Razorclaw Crabs. When eaten, these Paellas boost Link's strength. Tough Seafood Paella: These can be made by using Armored Porgies and Ironshell Crabs. When eaten, these Paellas boost Link's toughness against attacks. Other Appearances The recipe for Seafood Paella is earned by completing the Quest "Bounty of the Sea". It is made using three Fortified Pumpkins, three Tabantha Wheat, three Fresh Milks, three Fresh Milks and three Goat Butters. However, it can be lowered to two of each ingredient through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warriors will start the battle with three extra Hearts.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can make Seafood Rice Balls by Cooking any Seafood together with Hylian Rice in a Cooking Pot. Their default can be made either by using Hyrule Basses or Sanke Carps, which provide no status effects, or by using two types of Seafood with contradicting effects. When eaten, they will restore some of Link's Hearts. Though the flavor varies based on Ingredients, Seafood Rice Balls are known to never disappoint. By using certain types of Seafood or adding extra Ingredients, the following variations of Seafood Rice Balls can be made: Hearty Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using Hearty Bass, Hearty Salmons, Hearty Blueshell Snails, or other hearty Ingredients. By eating them, all of Link's Hearts will be healed, and he will gain temporary Hearts. Energizing Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using Staminoka Basses, Bright-Eyed Crabs, or other energizing Ingredients. They can be eaten to restore a part of Link's Stamina Wheel. Enduring Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using enduring Ingredients. Link's Stamina Wheel will be completely replenished and overfilled when he eats these. Hasty Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using hasty Ingredients. If consumed, Link will receive a boost to his movement speed. Spicy Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using Sizzlefin Trouts or other spicy Ingredients. Eating them will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Electro Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using Voltfin Trout or other electric Ingredients. When eaten, Link will gain one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using Mighty Carp, Mighty Porgies, Razorclaw Crabs, or other mighty Ingredients. They can be eaten to grant Link a boost to his attack power. Tough Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using Armored Carp, Armored Porgies, Ironshell Crabs, or other tough Ingredients. By eating them, Link's defensive abilities will be increased. Sneaky Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using Stealthfin Trouts, Sneaky River Snails, or other sneaky Ingredients. Link can eat them to receive a boost to his Stealth. Chilly Seafood Rice Balls: Made by using Chillfin Trouts or other chilly Ingredients. They can be consumed to offer Link one level of Heat Resistance. Like in , Seafood Rice Balls can be made by Cooking a bundle of Hylian Rice with any type of Seafood. Other Appearances The Recipe for Seafood Rice Balls is earned by completing the Quest "Fine Bites from Lurelin Village". It is made using four Stealthfin Trouts and four bundles of Tabantha Wheat. However, it can be lowered to three of each Ingredient through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Warriors' Sheikah Rune damage will increase by 35%.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Seafood Skewers are made by Cooking at least one Crab or Snail in a Cooking Pot. Link can make their default version can be made by utilizing Seafood that has contradicting effects. When eaten, they will restore some of Link's Hearts. The natural water in this Meal creates a delicious broth. To achieve a status effect from Seafood Skewers, several Ingredients of the same effect must be utilized. Hearty Seafood Skewer: Made by using any combination of Hearty Bass or Hearty Salmons with Hearty Blueshell Snails. They will heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him Extra Hearts when eaten. Energizing Seafood Skewer: Made by using Staminoka Basses and Bright-Eyed Crabs. Eating them will partially refill Link's Stamina Wheel. Mighty Seafood Skewer: Made by using any combination of Mighty Carp or Mighty Porgies with Ironshell Crabs. When eaten, Link will receive a boost to the power of his attacks. Tough Seafood Skewer: Made by using any combination of Armored Carp or Armored Porgies with Ironshell Crabs. Link will gain a boost to his defensive abilities when he eats these skewers. Sneaky Seafood Skewer: Made by using Stealthfin Trouts and Sneaky River Snails. By eating them, Link will receive a boost to his Stealth abilities. Link can make Seafood Skewers by Cooking any type of Crab or a Sneaky River Snail.

The is a recurring location in . The Second Gatehouse goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Second Gatehouse is a small building located along the path to the Sanctum, continuing from the First Gatehouse. Much like the First Gatehouse, it is flanked by two Guardian Turrets. If Link enters the Second Gatehouse, the portcullises at the entrance and exit will close and a White-Maned Lynel will descend from the ceiling. Upon its defeat, the portcullises will be raised once again. The conical spire roof of the Second Gatehouse has broken in places, giving Link access to the interior. Enemies Treasure Chests Korok Seeds As in , the Second Gatehouse is located along the Hyrule Castle Courtyard beneath the Sanctum within Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field. It connects Hyrule Castle 1F to Hyrule Castle B1. Enemies Sub-Bosses Equipment Treasure Chests Other Appearances The Second Gatehouse appears as part of the Hyrule Castle Stage.

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview During the "Find the Fifth Sage" Main Quest, Purah asks Link to search for clues as to the remaining Sage's whereabouts among ruins from the ancient past. In Kakariko Village, he can find Paya and Tauro looking up at the Floating Ring Ruin. Upon hearing that the Zelda who ordered them to stop was actually a Phantom Ganon, they are initially shocked, though Paya recalls that she seemed different than the real Zelda. Tauro realizes that the Floating Ring Ruin may be a threat to Demon King Ganondorf, and he decides that they should investigate as soon as possible. Paya agrees with Tauro, giving him permission to open the Floating Ring Ruin. Tauro is so excited that he begins using phrasing from Lurelin Village, which Paya notes. However, Tauro does not know how to access the Ring Ruin. Despite the Floating Ring Ruin being hollow, there is no entrance leading to its interior. As is the case with the other Ring Ruins, he believes that there could be a Ring Ruins Stone Slab with Zonai writing inside. First, he wants to confirm the existence of the Stone Slab, though he decides to inform the other members of the Zonai Survey Team. Afterwards, "Secret of the Ring Ruins" will begin. Using Ascend, Link is able to enter the Floating Ring Ruin and take a Picture of the Ring Ruins Stone Slab inside. Tauro will be confused having seen this, though he believes he imagined it. When Link shows his Picture to Tauro, he is shocked, calling over Paya and Calip to see it. As they examine the Picture, Tauro is able to decipher the words "Mineru" and southeast. Calip notes that Mineru could be the name of a Sage Although Tauro is excited, he notices that Paya appears to be thinking. She is able to translate more of the Zonai writing, referring to a Dragon land in the southeast. Once Tauro confirms it, she attributes her knowledge to studying the Zonai language. Fearing Paya is upstaging him, Calip points out that the Ring Ruins Stone Slab could be referring to the Zonai Ruins. Tauro praises Calip for this, which he appreciates. Looking back on what they have learned, Tauro determines that they can find out more by visiting the Zonai Ruins. He asks Calip to accompany him, which he agrees to. They plan to established their base camp near the Popla Foothills Skyview Tower. Tauro and Calip then depart for Faron. At the Popla Foothills Skyview Tower, Link can find Calip near a makeshift Tent. He welcomes Link to his base, revealing that Tauro has already left to see the Zonai Ruins near Dracozu Lake. If it is daytime, Calip expresses his hope to find more clues, though he claims he needs to rest before joining Tauro. At night, Calip is worried that Tauro has yet to return, wondering if he is caught up in his investigation. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Tauro using

Dracozu Lake. If it is daytime, Calip expresses his hope to find more clues, though he claims he needs to rest before joining Tauro. At night, Calip is worried that Tauro has yet to return, wondering if he is caught up in his investigation. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Tauro using a magnifying glass to examine a mural at the Zonai Ruins.|Tauro investigating the Zonai Ruins Among the Zonai Ruins, Link can find a Note on the Table written by Tauro, telling Calip to meet him inside a room revealed by rubble falling away. There, he encounters Tauro, who is examining a Zonai mural. He is happy to see Link, and he reveals that he has made a huge discovery. Tauro directs his attention to the mural, which he thinks may have been preserved due to Zonai Technology. He has been able to decipher some of the Zonai writing as well, which states to wear the "electric garb" found along the "forest serpent". This reminds Tauro of a Song that referred to the Dracozu River as a forest Dragon. Continuing his translation, Tauro states that a Zonai Charge must be offered to an Altar located at a "tail," and he believes that he can make more discoveries by uncovering the meaning behind this riddle. Tauro also points out a Treasure Chest in the room, which he has been unable to open. Using his Right Arm, Link is able to open the nearby Treasure Chest and receive the Charged Shirt. He can also find two similar rooms that are marked by Tall Dragon Pillars, within which he can find Treasure Chests containing the Charged Headdress and the Charged Trousers. Near the southwestern end of the Dracozu River, Link comes across one last room marked by a Tall Dragon Pillar. When he holds and drops a Zonai Charge or Large Zonai Charge on the Altar inside while wearing the entire Charged Set, the eyes of the Tall Dragon Pillars will begin to glow and their horns start to spark. All of them are simultaneously stuck by Lightning, and as the Sky above them clears, the Thunderhead Isles and Dragonhead Island will be revealed. Drawn by the Lightning, Tauro and Calip arrive at the Altar. They are shocked to find Link inside, though Calip is relieved that he is unharmed. Tauro asks Link if he knows what happened. He is impressed by Link's findings, though Calip laments that they are unable to visit the Sky Islands themselves. Since he needs to make a report to Purah, Tauro leaves Calip in charge of investigating the Zonai Ruins further. Though Calip is hesitant at first, Tauro's assurances convince him to stay. When Link reaches Dragonhead Island, he can find an interior chamber blocked by a Challenge Door. In order to open it, he needs at least 10 Hearts. Inside the chamber is the Zonai Relic, and when interacted with, he will hear the voice of Mineru telling him to follow the beam of light it emits.

page_title: Secret Treasure under the Great Fish
text: "" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link speaks to Sidon after completing the "Sidon of the Zora" Main Quest, he reveals that he can across a text about the Zora royal family that mentions a secret treasure. If Link expresses his interest, Sidon will recite the passage for him, which states "The great fish. The eternal guardian. A secret treasure awaits just beneath the stony form of its statue. Below the long bridge that reaches for the statue, leave your fears behind. Pass beneath two waterfalls to find your prize." Although Sidon is excited by the prospect, he warns Link that the treasure may already be gone. Despite this, he still encourages Link to search, since it may be useful to him. Following this conversation, "Secret Treasure under the Great Fish" will begin. Behind the Waterfall below the Great Zora Bridge, Link can find the entrance to the Cave Under Zora's Domain. Passing under the Waterfall in this cave, Link will come upon a secret chamber with a stone Treasure Chest, in which is the Vah Ruta Divine Helm. After Link obtains the Helm, "Secret Treasure under the Great Fish" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring character in . Biography Sefaro is a curious boy who spends his time with his friend Azu, spying on the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab in an effort to see a mysterious Sheikah girl rumored to be there. Despite his determination, neither he nor Azu have any luck in spotting the little girl. While he would like to go up to the Lab and get a definite answer, Azu reminds him that they are not allowed to get too close. It is getting to the point where Sefaro begins to doubt that the girl exists. If Link gets in the way of his line of sight, Sefaro will angrily demand that he moves. However, if Link shows interest in what he is doing, Sefaro will happily tell him why he and Azu are there before catching himself. Link can attempt to apologize for interrupting Sefaro's mission and the boy will huff at him in irritation. At 8 in the evening, Sefaro is forced to call it quits for the day and go home. Still, he is adamant about returning in the morning. While he sleeps, he continues to grumble and wonder about the rumored Sheikah girl.

is a recurring character in . Biography Seggin is a Zora and former sergeant who resides in Zora's Domain. He can first be found trying to withstand the electricity of a Shock Arrow, and he is later noted to be quite shock resistant for a Zora. When he notices Link, he's angered by his failure to save Mipha and expresses a desire to attack him. He claims that his training is so he can face Divine Beast Vah Ruta himself and avenge Mipha. If Link takes the arrow from him, he will angrily tell Link to take on the responsibility of appeasing the Divine Beast Vah Ruta. Despite this, he still prepares to attack Vah Ruta on his own on Zora Domain's eastern bridge. However, he gives up when he remembers his fortune that day warned him to be cautious of injury. Once Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, Seggin will be remorseful of his previous actions towards Link. He will ask Link to forgive him.

The is a Boss in . Characteristics The Seized Construct is a large humanoid Crafter Construct similar to the Construct built by Mineru to house her spirit, and according to her it was a prototype of her Construct body. It has since been stolen by Ganondorf to stop Mineru from reclaiming her Secret Stone of Spirit at the Spirit Temple, and now visibly emanates Gloom. Another Seized Construct appears at Gloom's Lair during the War in the Depths of Hyrule, which must be fought alongside any other story Bosses who were not defeated in their respective Temple. Otherwise, if Mineru has reclaimed her Secret Stone, she will handle it so that Link can go on to fight Demon King Ganondorf. If Mineru is the only Sage acquired at this time, she will explain that this Construct is a "magical copy" given that it has already been defeated. Unlike the other Main Quest bosses, the Seized Construct cannot be re-fought in the Depths after defeating it. It also cannot have a statue of it created by Kilton. Battle Attempting to fight the Seized Construct directly is all but pointless, as it possesses an enormous amount of health and takes no damage from arrows if they have not been fused with explosive items. Furthermore, if in the Spirit Temple, the entirety of the arena's floor is covered in Gloom that will inevitably drain all of Link's hearts. Instead, Link must pilot Mineru's Construct and knock the Seized Construct into the electric fences surrounding the arena. When pushed into the fence, the Seized Construct will always lose 1/8th of its health, with any additional hits before it gets back up dealing 1/16th. Several Spiked Balls and Cannons, as well as any Zonai Devices that Link might have in his inventory, can be attached to the construct's arms to enable it to attack at close quarters or long range. The Construct will similarly try to push Link and Mineru into the fence, and so they should wait for it to attempt an attack before closing in and retaliating. Upon losing half its health, the Seized Construct will grow two additional arms; it will also attach a Rocket to its back, two Fans to its lower arms, and two Cannons to its upper arms. It will immediately follow up by flying into the air before firing repeatedly. Link and Mineru can either focus on defending themselves until the Seized Construct lands, or counterattack with Cannon fire of their own. The Seized Construct will also attempt flying body slams, which will deal significant damage but can be baited in order to create further opportunities to knock it into the electric fence.

is a recurring character in . Biography Seldon is a man who owns the Ventest Clothing Boutique in Hateno Village. He is the father of Sophie and formerly managed the Shop, but has since left it in his daughter's care. In his free time, he offers Seldon's Village Tours for travelers visiting Hateno Village. He can be found pacing the road near the entrance to the village, awaiting visitors. Should Link refuse a tour, Seldon will make his disappointment clear with a sigh. If Link agrees to his offer, he will run across Hateno Village's thoroughfare, guiding Link to the various shops. As Seldon runs through the village, he has to urge himself forward and keep himself focused. The first place Seldon guides Link to is East Wind, the Shop opposite the Ventest Clothing Boutique. He then guides Link to the Kochi Dye Shop, a dyeing shop operated by Sayge. The third place Seldon directs Link to is The Great Ton Pu Inn, where Link can rest for the night. Completing the tour, Seldon brings Link to his own shop, welcoming him to visit when he has the time and stock up on Armor before visiting the Kochi Dye Shop. If spoken to again, Seldon will either tell Link that the tours will resume when he catches his breath, or that the tours are closed until he has had a rest. However, Seldon will not have the energy for another tour until the following day. At 9 o'clock in the evening, Seldon will head home for the day, assuring Link that he can give him a tour in the morning. He sleeps on the bottom half of a bunk Bed and tends to grind his teeth as he sleeps. If it rains in Hateno Village, Seldon will retreat to the interior of the Ventest Clothing Boutique and sit at the work station at the back of the store. Seldon is set to reappear in .

, also known simply as , are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Sell Prices are the amount of Rupees that Link can obtain by selling certain Items to Shops or Merchants. Link can sell certain Bottled items to the Buyer. Link can sell most Bottled items at the Curiosity Shop. After giving Kotake a Magic Mushroom to restock Blue Potion, Link can sell any additional Magic Mushrooms to Kotake for 20 Rupees each. Link can sell Spoils to Beedle. Link can sell Treasures to the Linebeck Trading Company. Link can sell some Adventure Pouch items to Peatrice at the Item Check in order to free up space. Sellable items include Bomb Bags, Quivers, Seed Satchels and all Shields except the Hylian Shield. Link can sell Treasures to the Witch. List of Sell Prices Other Appearances

, also known as the Lodge on the Summit, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Selmie's Spot is a small cabin located on the northern side of the Hebra East Summit in the Hebra Mountains. Shada Naw Shrine is located in a small cave nearby. Following her retirement from Shield Surfing, Selmie took up residence in the cabin, supposedly waiting for a worthy opponent to come find her. The walls of the House are decorated with a variety of Shields, and a Cooking Pot can be found over its fireplace. Link is also able to sleep in the cabin's Bed to restore his Hearts. Two Wooden Boxes, which can be broken open for Materials, have been placed behind the cabin. Since it is located in a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit Selmie's Spot without taking damage. From Selmie's Spot, Selmie operates the Shield-Surfing Mini-Game. She charges Link 20 Rupees per run. After Link completes the beginner course, Selmie allows him to take on the advanced course. As a reward for completing the advanced course, Selmie gifts Link the Shields that she has hung on her walls. Materials Equipment Korok Seeds Selmie uses the cabin to wait out the blizzard over Hebra Mountains with her Shield Surfing-pupils, Russ and Fin. It is decorated with a variety of different shields. If Link tries to interact with any of them, she scolds him for it. Materials Equipment

is a recurring character in . Biography Selmie is a Hylian and legendary Shield Surfer known as the Duchess of Downhill. She can be found at her residence, Selmie's Spot, in the Hebra Mountains. She is apparently a native of Hebra province and an experienced mountaineer in addition to her legendary shield surfing skill. At the stable she proposes to Link a mini-game at her snowy spot consisting of shield-surfing. According to Selmie's Notes in Hebra Trailhead Lodge at the foot of Rospro Pass, she is the owner of Hebra Trailhead Lodge as well which she set up as a safe place for travelers to rest and prepare before hiking up further into the mountain as the mountain can easily lead to the death of unprepared travelers. It is also implied that Selmie herself has retired from Shield Surfing. Selmie is shown to be quite popular with one shield surfer leaving a note in her notebook asking to marry her if he can prove he is a better shield surfer. The notebook also reveals she is the one who set up the flags on Hebra Mountains as guide posts for travelers to help them avoid getting lost. Though she is passionate about her sport she is realistic about the dangers of Hebra Mountains and even notes that being a shield surfer is a rough life style even refusing to pass Link to the next course if he answers too enthusiastically by saying shield surfing is his life as Selmie notes he is not ready and even notes its not an ideal way of life, though if he shrugs Selmie notes she'd probably give the same response as its not something that can easily be put into words showing her passion for the sport is a mature one. Her notes also suggest she has witnessed many shield surfers and mountain travelers meet a tragic end due to the harsh conditions and bluntly states the mountain will kill them before explaining the death toll and serious dangers of the mountain. She also encourages her fellow shield surfers to be safety conscious while surfing presumably due to have witnessed young shield surfers meet their end due to being reckless or lacking common sense (such as wearing warm clothing to handle the cold) due to their youth. It is implied that Selmie became tired of people dying needlessly because they where unprepared or unexperienced thus set up flags and the lodge as places to prepare and left her notes as a guidebook to newcomers. Upon talking to her, Selmie will make a remark about the shield Link is currently wearing on his back, though this will not happen for certain types, including the Hylian Shield, likely due to its extreme rarity. She also is apparently unfamiliar with Ancient Shields and Guardian Shields. She considers Royal Shields the best overall and even has one proudly on display above her fireplace, though she considers the Royal Guard's Shield too flimsy for serious shield surfers. Shield, likely due to its extreme rarity. She also is apparently unfamiliar with Ancient Shields and Guardian Shields. She considers Royal Shields the best overall and even has one proudly on display above her fireplace, though she considers the Royal Guard's Shield too flimsy for serious shield surfers. Apparently, they are a popular collector's item due to their rarity and historical significance as relics of the Great Calamity. She also notes the Gerudo designed the Gerudo Shield to make it surfable, which Selmie herself apparently finds somewhat surprising, indicating that she is unaware that Sand Seal surfing is the main form of transportation as well as a popular traditional sport among the Gerudo in Gerudo Desert. It's practically unheard of outside the desert as no Hylian shield surfers, including Selmie, mention or show awareness of it (ironically, Selmie would be one of the few Hylian shield surfers capable of entering Gerudo Town and renting a Sand Seal as she is a Hylian vai (woman) and would likely have little trouble learning how to ride a Sand Seal). She is however familiar with Gerudo made shields and even notes Radiant Shields are rare. She notes Steel Lizal Shields are stylish due to their radical design. Selmie decided to step down as a pro shield surfer and teach the next generation. As the Blizzard rages over Hebra Mountains, she waits it out with her pupils Russ and Fin. As Link visits their cabin in such extreme weather, she assumes he is also a shield surfer and wants to learn from her. When he confirms this, she declines taking on another student as her current ones would not receive as much training as they deserve. If he asks again she commends his attitude, but declines nonetheless. Should Link ask her what Shield Surfing is, she explains to him the basic idea of it. She also offers him a resting spot in the cabin and asks him to return once the Blizzard ends.

is a recurring character in . Biography Senna is a resident of Hateno Village where she greets people for the Kochi Dye Shop. She considers herself be be the hardest worker in greeting, though when it is not raining she admits the weather keeps it from feeling like real work. If it is raining, she says that she does not care and that the rain cannot prevent her from doing her job. She can be found in the front of the Shop, where she directs people to her husband, Sayge. She is a taciturn person, telling Link to leave her so she can return to greeting. At 9:00 PM, she goes to bed and will tell Link that she is done greeting and that he should to talk to her husband. While asleep, she snores loudly and tells herself to get better and more enthusiastic to make him proud before continuing her job at 5:00 AM.

The , also known as the , is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Sheikah Sensor is used to locate Ancient Shrines in . It can be unlocked either by activating any Sheikah Tower after leaving the Great Plateau or in the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab by repairing the Sheikah Slate. When Link is near an Ancient Shrine, the Sheikah Sensor will beep louder. It can be upgraded to the Sheikah Sensor + in order to detect objects other than Ancient Shrines. The Sensor is an upgrade for the Purah Pad used to locate Shrines of Light in . It is obtained by speaking to Robbie at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab during the "Hateno Village Research Lab" Side Adventure. When Link is moving in the direction of a nearby Shrine of Light, it will beep louder, and it will display a message indicating if the Shrine of Light is directly above or below Link. It can be upgraded to the Sensor + to be used to detect objects that have been registered in the Hyrule Compendium. Other Appearances

The , also known as the , is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Sheikah Sensor + is an upgrade for the Sheikah Sensor used to locate any unlocked Hyrule Compendium entries in . It can be obtained from Purah by bringing her three Ancient Screws during "Slated for Upgrades". Once it has been unlocked, Symin will ask to see the Sheikah Sensor +, and the "Sunshroom Sensing" Side Quest will become available. The Sensor + is an upgrade for the Sensor used to locate objects that have been registered in the Hyrule Compendium. It is obtained from Robbie at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab during "Presenting: Sensor +!" after registering at least five Monsters in the Hyrule Compendium. Other Appearances

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Seres Scablands are a large area of land located on Hyrule Ridge, nestled between the Tanagar Canyon and the West Hyrule Plains. They are bordered by Ludfo's Bog to the northeast, and the Hilltop High Road runs along their southern edge. Their terrain is rough, as evidenced by the many holes and crevasses throughout the landscape, and covered by an open woodland of Dragon's Bloods of various sizes. In the middle of the Seres Scablands, a Blue Hinox sleeps in a small field of grass. In Master Mode, it is replaced by a Black Hinox. The Hinox will initially be asleep, but if Link wakes it up, it will begin to attack him. left|40px There are a total of four Korok Seed Puzzles that can be found on the Seres Scablands. The first is a Balloon underneath one of the large Dragon's Bloods north of the Blue Hinox, which Link must use Archery to destroy. The second is another Balloon that can be found under a Dragon's Blood south of the Hinox. The third can be solved by interacting with the Leaves with Fairy Dust that dart around the east end of the Scablands. Finally, the fourth Puzzle is a Race found on a Dragon's Blood on the southeast end of the Seres Scablands, its endpoint being another large Dragon's Blood nearby. When Link solves each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Other Appearances The Seres Scablands are part of the Hyrule Ridge stage. During the "Questionable Escort Mission" Challenge, the Warriors encounter a lone Hylian Soldier while passing through the Seres Scablands.

is a recurring character in . Biography Sesami is a Hylian man who can be found at the Gerudo Canyon Stable. When Link initially meets him, Sesami asks him if he has seen his friends, named Oliff, Flaxel, Canolo and Palme. He explains that he was separated from them when some monsters jumped them at the Koukot Plateau. Sesami says that he ran away and did not stop until he made it to Gerudo Canyon Stable. Sesami is worried that the monsters got his friends and wishes he could have saved them, but he is not much of a fighter. Sesami believes that even with the sword of legend, he still could not slay the monsters. When Link asks what he means by this, Sesami tells him of a mythical sword that sleeps in the Great Hyrule Forest and speculates that a legendary sword must be really strong. Sesami questions for a moment if a sword like that could really make him into a "monster-slaying hero." Sesami quickly dismisses the thought that his friends are in danger and asks Link to let his friends know where he is if he happens to find them. After Sesami finishes speaking, Link receives the "Missing in Action" Side Quest where he must find Sesami's friends in order to complete it. Link can find Sesami's friends at the Koukot Plateau, where he must rescue them each from monsters. After rescuing Canolo, she immediately expresses anger toward Sesami, saying that he ran away as soon as the monsters showed up. After saving Flaxel, she is also very angry that Sesami was at the stable instead of saving her. After saving Palme, he wonders to Link why Sesami did not come to save him and questions if Sesami lied about mastering martial arts. After rescuing all four of Sesami's friends, they can be found at Gerudo Canyon Stable with Sesami. Sesami will tell Link that he is glad to see his friends are safe and thanks him by rewarding him with 300 Rupees. Before Sesami finishes talking, he tells Link that he is glad this happened because it helped him realize the importance of friendship. He reflects on what he learned, expressing to Link that while opening up to others makes a person more vulnerable, it is the only way to give life value. Sesami then bluntly reveals that he will be parting ways with his friends because caring for others is an emotional liability. In reality, Sesami has no idea what lesson to take away. If Link returns to Sesami, his friends will no longer be at the Stable. If Link talks to Sesami again, he tells him that he came at just the right moment and that Link should hear what he has been going through. Sesami tells Link that he has been unsure whether or not he should venture into the Gerudo Desert. When Links asks him why not do it, Sesami says that the Temperature in the Desert swings dramatically between the

moment and that Link should hear what he has been going through. Sesami tells Link that he has been unsure whether or not he should venture into the Gerudo Desert. When Links asks him why not do it, Sesami says that the Temperature in the Desert swings dramatically between the day and night. He explains that one's health would suffer without the right clothing. Sesami then says that even Horses do not like going into the Desert and adds that considering all of that with monsters in the mix, it is a nightmare of a place. Sesami once again brings up the legendary sword that sleeps in a forest, saying that he would be safe in the Desert with it. He goes on to explain that he thinks the legendary sword is in the Great Hyrule Forest in the Eldin Region and that the Fairies that live there will confuse those who enter the forest. Sesami says that he would love to see the legendary sword just once if it exists. He then jokes that he gets lost in the woods even without Fairies messing with him, so he could never make it through the Great Hyrule Forest.

, also known as Special Bonuses, are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Set Bonuses are a type of Added Effect that can only be obtained by wearing all three pieces of certain Armor Sets. Usually Set Bonuses will require all three pieces of the Armor Set to be enhanced at least twice by a Great Fairy, but some Armor Sets have their Set Bonus by default. While Set Bonuses replace the Added Effect name that is displayed in the Inventory, they do not remove the Effects provided by the individual pieces of the Armor Set, although some Set Bonuses may effectively nullify their benefits. One example of this can be found in the Froggy Armor's Set Bonus Slip Proof, which functions as an improved version of Slip Resistance. In , there are 15 different Set Bonuses, two of which are hidden in the Inventory. Set Bonuses in Hidden Set Bonuses in With the addition of several new Armor Sets, there are eight new visible Set Bonuses and one new hidden Set Bonus available in . With the removal of the Ancient Set and the Gerudo Set, the Ancient Proficiency and Heat-Resistant Set Bonuses are no longer available. This totals to 20 visible Set Bonuses and two hidden Set Bonuses. Set Bonuses in Hidden Set Bonuses in

The are a recurring group of characters in . Biography The Seven Heroines are known as the divine protectors of the Gerudo people. Massive Heroine Statues that stand in their honor can be found in the East Gerudo Ruins on the east end of the Gerudo Desert. People once journeyed from around the world searching for the Heroines' blessing. Each Heroine is said to have a unique power, which are skill, spirit, endurance, knowledge, flight, motion and gentleness. The statues of the Seven Heroines play a role in the Shrine Quest, "The Seven Heroines", given by Rotana in Gerudo Town. Link must solve a puzzle involving the statues to finish the Shrine Quest and reveal the Korsh O'hu Shrine. In addition to the Seven Heroines, there is also a rumor of an Eighth Heroine. Its Statue can be found in the northern Gerudo Highlands. The Seven Heroines have been worshiped by the Gerudo for a long time, and are said to have protected and guided the Gerudo in times past. Little is actually known about the Heroines, even by the Gerudo. There is a debate among the Gerudo between whether they should worship all seven as a group, or each one as individuals. Even the number is disagreed on, with some claiming there are eight, or even only one. Link and Rotana ultimately discover that the Eighth Heroine was in fact a voe and was subsequently barred entrance to Gerudo Town despite being the one to unite the Seven Heroines. Ashamed by their actions but unable to make amends, the ancient Gerudo built a hidden temple to honor him. "Seven Sages" is written on the statues of the Seven Heroines in Gerudo.

is a recurring character in . Biography Shabonne is a Gerudo who coaches Tali, the Sand-Seal Racing champion. She can be found with Tali at the Sand-Seal Rally in the Gerudo Desert. If Link approaches the nearby Ancient Orb, Shabonne scolds him and exclaims that only those who have proven themselves may touch it. If Link talks to Shabonne, she apologizes to him because Tali is not in the mood for autographs. If Link asks what happened, Shabonne explains that the Sand-Seal Race course is unusable with the Divine Beast Vah Naboris stomping around. She then rudely tells him that he can stand around, but that she would prefer he did it elsewhere. If Link asks about Sand-Seal Racing, Shabonne is surprised that Link has not heard of it and explains that it is a sport where people guide Sand Seals through arches on a race course. Shabonne says that the racer with the fastest time wins, but they cannot run any races with the Divine Beast around. If Link asks who Tali is, Shabonne is in disbelief that he does not know the Sand-Seal Racing champion and says that Tali could demonstrate her skills if it were not for the Divine Beast. If Link asks Shabonne who she is, she explains that she is the one who raised Tali into a racing champion. She goes on to say that it was not easy and that her relationship with Tali is great despite Tali's shyness. Shabonne asks Tali if that is right, and Tali responds with silence as usual. Shabonne is angry that the Divine Beast has upset Tali. She also comments that the cold Desert nights must be rough on Hylians and that the Gerudo are used to it. When Link returns to the Sand-Seal Rally after calming Naboris, the Sand-Seal Race will be open again. Link can speak to Shabonne or Tali to begin the Shrine Quest, "The Undefeated Champ". Shabonne tells Link that if he can beat Tali's record of 1:30, he can have a trophy. The trophy that Shabonne refers to is the nearby Ancient Orb needed to reveal the Ancient Shrine, which has been passed down by ten thousand years of Sand-Seal Racing champions. Shabonne charges Link 50 Rupees to race against Tali's record. When Link beats Tali's record and places the Ancient Orb into its pedestal, the Raqa Zunzo Shrine rises from the ground and the Shrine Quest is completed.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Shadow Hamlet Ruins are the remains of Shadow Hamlet in Eldin Canyon. They lie on the mountain range between the eastern side of Death Mountain's Lava moat, and the Shadow Pass of Akkala. The Shadow Hamlet Ruins consist of three Ruined Houses in varying states of decay, while the surrounding area is littered with Busted Wagons and scorched Trees. Two intact Barrels can be found inside the northern Ruined House. The roof of the Shadow Hamlet Ruins Well can be seen sticking up out of the dirt next to this House. Enemies Materials The Shadow Hamlet Ruins are the remains of Shadow Hamlet in Eldin Canyon. Much more foliage has grown throughout the Ruins, and the previously-buried Shadow Hamlet Ruins Well has opened up. Rocks and Spiny Bones now lie around the grounds, and a new structure has been built next to the western Deserted House, though it has become overgrown much like the surrounding buildings. The Barrels within the northern Deserted House remain in place. Areas Creatures Materials Equipment

The is a recurring location in . The Shadow Hamlet Ruins Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The roof of the Shadow Hamlet Ruins Well can be seen sticking out of the ground next to the northern Ruined House in the Shadow Hamlet Ruins. Prior to the Great Calamity, it was part of the Shadow Hamlet. The Shadow Hamlet Ruins Well is located in the Shadow Hamlet Ruins in Eldin Canyon. The Well's entire structure is now visible. Sparks drift out of its rim due to the intense Scorching Climate within it. In order to enter the Well without being set on Fire and taking damage, Link must have at least one level of Flame Guard active. The below-ground portion of the Well consists of one large chamber with two pools of Lava. The first is a large pool on the eastern side of the chamber fueled by two Waterfalls of Flowing Lava seeping from the roof, and the second is a smaller pool on the western side. Two Ore Deposits are located adjacent to the western Lava pool. Enemies Materials Treasure Chests

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Shadow Pass is a road in the Akkala Highlands connecting the South Akkala Stable to the East Akkala Stable that cuts through a dense forest. At the northern and southern sections of the forest, Link can find broken Guardians, which can be searched for Ancient Materials. Also at the northern end are the remains of a wagon, which travelers may take refuge under. On one of the sides of this wagon, Link can find a Rusty Shield. Chabi can be found in the Shadow Pass, defending herself from a Bokoblin. Similarly, the Gerudo and Goron travelers, Laroba and Naddon, can be seen walking through the Shadow Pass. The Hylian traveler, Pitar, can also be seen riding through the Shadow Pass on horseback. The northeastern section of the Shadow Pass's forest is situated on a lowered segment of land. Bokoblins have set up an encampment in this spot, atop of which rests a wooden Treasure Chest that contains a Purple Rupee, valued at 50 Rupees. The walls around this lowered area also feature Ore Deposits and Luminous Stone Deposits. A Korok can be found atop a large pine tree in the northwestern section of the forest. Creatures Enemies

is a recurring character in . Biography Shaillu is the manager of an Arrow shop inside the big building at the Kara Kara Bazaar. She sells every type of Arrow. Shaillu is always seen reading a book behind the shop's counter. When Link talks to her, her focus is broken from her book and she apologizes. Shaillu tells Link that if he is looking for something other than Arrows, he should look in Gerudo Town, but quickly remembers that men are not allowed there. If Link ends the conversation with Shaillu without asking for anything, she says that she is busy and asks Link to only speak to her if he needs something. If Link speaks to Shaillu while wearing the Gerudo Outfit, she comments that the clothes look good on him. If Link speaks to Shaillu while searching for the man who discovered a way into Gerudo Town, he asks Shaillu if she has seen a sneaky guy around. Shaillu is unable to recall someone of that description, but does know of a Hylian girl who likes to relax on the roof.

is a recurring character in . Biography Shamae is a little girl who works at the Woodland Stable. During the day with clear Weather, she can be found at the Stable's patio next to its Barrels. She tells Link that she has dreams of a land in the sky, and believes that people used to live there long ago. She desires to watch balloons float high into the sky and asks Link if he could help her realize her dream. She promises to give him a treasure she got from the sky, and instructs that he put some balloons onto one of the Barrels. This initiates the "Balloon Flight" Side Quest. Link completes her request by attaching an Octo Balloon to one of the Barrels and allowing it to fly high enough. Overjoyed, she confesses that her dream is to visit the land in the sky by balloon. She then gives him the promised treasure: a Star Fragment. In , Shamae still resides at Woodland Stable. Initially, Shamae can be found looking up at the Sky outside of Woodland Stable. When Link approaches her, Shamae welcomes him to the Stable and asks if he is also looking for things that fall from the Sky. If Link ends their conversation at this point, Shamae insists it is more fun to search on her own. If Link asks her about it, she claims that Fallen Debris will occasionally falls from a nearby Sky Island, and she is able to point out such an occurrence to him. Shamae believes this is the work of someone who lives in the Sky, and though she wants to go visit them, she is still too young to travel so far. When she grows up like Link, she wants to visit the Sky Island herself. When Link ends their conversation after this point, she states that they should meet on the Sky Island after she becomes an adult. She will also become annoyed if Link asks her about Fallen Debris again. Shamae then wonders if another piece of Fallen Debris will fall, once again expressing her desire to play in the Sky. While Kilton and Koltin are still at Woodland Stable, Shamae wonders if balloons like theirs could be used to travel into the Sky.

is a character in . Biography Sharce is a Hylian member of Toren's Monster-Control Crew, Squad Two. He wears a piece of Soldier's Armor and wields a Soldier's Spear. During the Monster-Control Crew's search of Hyrule Castle, Sharce can be found guarding one of the entrances. He initially recognizes Link, but he convinces himself he is wrong and refuses to let him pass. He explains that Hoz has ordered the area be off-limits to anyone who is not part of the Search for Princess Zelda, and he claims he will need his permission if he wants to pass by. Sharce reveals that Hoz can be found at the First Gatehouse. If Link tries to walk past Sharce, he will be stopped. Link is able to inform Sharce of the figure resembling Zelda during "Crisis at Hyrule Castle", though he does not believe him.

If Link shoots Dinraal's teeth with an arrow, a fang will drop onto the land, appearing as a glowing light. Like other dragon materials, Link can only make one fang drop with each encounter with the dragon. Using Dinraal's Fangs in a Cooking Pot will result in Dubious Food. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Crimson Dye. If Shards of Farosh's Fang are used in a Cooking Pot, the resulting meal will always be Dubious Food. The Shards can also be used as an ingredient to make Light Yellow Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop in Hateno Village. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Shatterback Point is a cape jutting out from Ploymus Mountain over the East Reservoir Lake in the Lanayru Great Spring. It is a popular diving spot, despite its dangers, and is often used by the Zora thrill-seeker, Gruve. To deter would-be divers, a Sign cautioning travelers was placed at its tip, and Laflat has begun searching for Pictures of the Lynel atop Ploymus Mountain to scare anyone whom Gruve may have goaded into diving. Shatterback Point is one of the locations that is affected by the Rain generated by Divine Beast Vah Ruta. Creatures

is a recurring character in . Biography Shibo can be found at the Dueling Peaks Stable with his family. He normally stands outside with his twin brother, Darton outside the Horse pen beside the Stable. When approached, he speaks with Darton about whether Link is interested in Horses. The two conclude that he must then be a customer to the Stable. The two offer to share their knowledge of Horses with Link. Shibo offers insight on how to catch Horses by sneaking up on them. Shibo will also inform Link that spotted Horses possess an even temperament and are easy to tame whereas single-color horses are wilder and more difficult to train. Shibo and Darton's father, Rensa, also gave the two advice on what kind of Horse is difficult to train, and which to start with. When asked about how to train a Horse properly, Shibo points out that a Horse will not be obedient at first and must be soothed at first and when it performs well. At night, Shibo will go inside the Stable to sleep. While asleep, Shibo will count spotted Horses. When he wakes up, Shibo will attempt to beat Darton to the Horse pen. Shibo and his brother Darton can be seen outside of Dueling Peaks Stable.

are recurring Items and Objects in . It is Link's primary protective defense used to deflect objects, guard from attack, and in some instances, reflect light onto other objects. As a common and recurring item in nearly every Zelda title, the Shield is not only a trademark of the series but completes Link's hero-like appearance, along with any Sword he happens to wield at the time. From defending Link to being the favorite snack of Like Likes, the design and function of the Shield greatly differs throughout the series. Location and Uses In , Link begins his adventure already equipped with a Shield. The Shield can be used to block non-magical projectiles if Link is facing them and not attacking. It can be replaced by the Magical Shield, which can be bought from certain Merchants found throughout Hyrule for 90-160 Rupees. If Link loses the Magical Shield to a Like Like, he will again equip his original Shield. The Shield cannot be eaten by Like Likes. In , Link starts with the Magical Shield and does not receive any other Shields throughout the game. While holding down, the Magical Shield covers the bottom half of Link's body. By default, the Magical Shield covers the top half of Link's body. The Reflect Spell can temporarily increase the power of the Magical Shield. The Shield is the first Item that Link obtains in . Link was separated from the Shield when he shipwrecked on Koholint Island, but was found and returned to him by Tarin. Tarin mentions that Link's name is inscribed on the back. In the artwork for the original and DX versions of , the Shield has the appearance of the Fighter's Shield from . However, in , it resembles the Hylian Shield. If the Shield is eaten by a Like Like, Link can buy an identical one at the Town Tool Shop for 20 Rupees. There are three types of Shields in . Shields can be freely equipped in the Equipment menu. Link can hold a Shield in front of him using the R button. While L-Targeting, Link is able to hold a Shield while moving. Attacking while brandishing a Shield will cause Link to perform a crouch stab. During the Child Era, Link cannot properly use the Hylian Shield due to its weight. As a result, using the R button will result in him ducking under the Hylian Shield instead of holding it in front of him. List of Shields adopts the shielding system from with a few differences. Only two Shields can be found, though each Mask transformation allows Link to defend himself. Link cannot freely switch between Shields. The Mirror Shield will completely replace the Hero's Shield. The main differences are that it is predominantly grey rather than brown, it features the shape of a Force Gem rather than the Triforce and the lobster is replaced by a Dove. introduces shields with limited durability; they are damaged when used strenuously. The level of damage sustained is indicated by the Shield Gauge. Shields can be repaired at the Scrap Shop or with a Revitalizing Potion. When the Shield Gauge empties, the shield is broken beyond repair, unless Link possesses an Revitalizing Potion+ at that moment. Like many items in , shields can be upgraded at the Scrap Shop, improving their durability but otherwise retaining their qualities. The Hylian Shield, obtained by completing the Thunder Dragon's Lightning Round, is indestructible and cannot be upgraded. Every shield in has a specific amount of damage it can take before breaking. This is laid out in the table below. In general, for a given tier of shield (i.e. basic, 1st upgrade, 2nd upgrade), the Sacred Shield derivative is the weakest, the Wooden Shield derivative is the second strongest (being 1.6 times as strong as the Sacred Shield derivative), and the Iron Shield derivative is the strongest (being 2.4 times as strong as the Sacred Shield derivative or 1.5 times as strong as the Wooden Shield derivative). For a given type of shield, the first upgrade is 1.5 times as strong as the basic shield, and the second upgrade is twice as strong as the basic shield. The damage dealt to a shield by an enemy attack or other damage source is proportional to the damage it would do to Link. Therefore, if a given attack does twice as much damage to Link as another attack does, it will also damage his shield twice as much. However, this does not apply to the increased damage attacks deal to Link in Hero Mode; shields take the same amount of damage from a given attack in Hero Mode that they do in regular gameplay.
