List of Shields In , Shields can be bought at any Shop for 50 Rupees. They will block most ranged attacks like Arrows and melee attacks from Enemies, but cannot block magical attacks and Lynels' fire breath. If Link is trapped by a Like Like, his Shield can be eaten. In this event, Link cannot retrieve his shield from the Like Like and will need to purchase a new one. The Shield is later replaced by the Hylian Shield found in Turtle Rock. left|Shield Icon from features several different pieces of equipment to use as protection. The diverse range of Shields available allows Link to deviate from the standard Sword and Shield dynamic. Many of these Shields follow a series of archetypes, such as "Boko," "Soldier's," and "Traveler's." Initially, Link can carry up to four Shields at a time in his inventory; however, he can obtain additional slots by giving Korok Seeds to Hestu. Hestu will upgrade Link's slots up to a full page, or 20 slots, of Shields. If Link takes another Shield while his inventory is full, he will drop the Shield or put it back if it came from a Treasure Chest. You can also obtain Shields from Selmie; however, she will turn you away if your inventory is full. Each Shield, including duplicates, occupies its own slot in the inventory. Each hit a Shield receives while Link is Blocking lowers it durability, breaking once it reaches zero. Performing a Perfect Guard prevents the Shield from taking damage, while simultaneously stunning the enemy or deflecting its projectile. The Lynel Shield and its upgrades can also be used to deal direct damage when used to guard. By using a Shield while aerial, Link is capable of Shield Surfing at the cost of the Shield's integrity (provided the Shield is being ridden on coarse terrain; if Link Shield Surfs on snow or sand, the Shield will not take damage). Several types of Shields appear in . They can be Fused with Materials and Objects as a means of enhancement. Along with many reuccuring shields from , the game also introduces a series of new shields, manily a new archetype - the "Zonaite" shields. Fusing these with Zonai Devices reduces the Battery usage of them when Blocking. Like in the last game, Hestu can upgrade the Shield Inventory in exchange for Korok Seeds. Levels of Shields In the Zelda universe, three common shields exist: the Wooden, the Durable, and the Mirror shields - from which the games, at their own discretion, add different variations and unique shields to the mix that operate differently as required by the individual games themselves. and both contain examples of all three varieties. Wooden Shields Related Articles: Wooden Shield, Ordon Shield, and Deku Shield 50px|right|The Deku Shield from 50px|right|The Ordon Shield from The Wooden Shield is often the first that Link acquires in his journey, as this type of shield is the closest and most readily available to Link at the time. Though not specifically noted, many of the games such as and incorporate wooden shields; they are noted by their adequate protection from rocks and arrows and weakness against fire, instead of by their rudimentary wooden makeup. In 3D The Legend of Zelda titles, the wooden shield's weakness to fire makes it a relatively risky choice to use under volcanic and high heat conditions because contact with fire will burn the shield, namely the Deku Shield and the Ordon Shield, away completely. Unlike the more durable Iron Shield in Skyward Sword, the Wooden Shield is resistant to electricity. In order to accommodate this aversion to fire, wooden shields can be replaced at many bazaars for a nominal price. Also, in , the basic shield has the same properties as most other basic, wooden shields, blocking most basic enemy attacks, but not such attacks as beams or fire, but it cannot be burned away. The Magical Shield of is the first form of this shield, and the Red Shield from and Hero's Shield of fame are prime examples of the impenetrability of these shields - even large boulders that rain down from the apex of Death Mountain do not leave a scratch on the surface of the Hylian Shield of . Contrary to the wooden shield, which often has a minimalistic art design on its facing side, these often impregnable shields commonly boast the Hylian Crest and the Triforce at their front. While the majority of these shields are metallic in construct, many in the series do not give any physical description beyond what they protect against. Mirror Shields Main Article: Mirror Shield right|50px|The Mirror Shield of right|50px|Mirror shield from Always having a smooth, reflective face, the Mirror Shield is usually the last, and sometimes even optional, shield variation Link can receive on his quest; this shield is an impregnable shield with one added function: the ability to reflect light. Its plot usability is determined by game; for example, incorporates a mirror shield that is required to beat the Spirit Temple, while presents the shield as a reward for completing a lengthy side-quest unrelated to the plot. The mirror shield is used almost exclusively to complete the dungeon it was found in, and rarely throughout the rest of the game, save certain side-quests and other small situations. Function Link has always used the shield to defend himself. Sometimes, the shield is even necessary to defeat specific enemies. However, the way the shield is utilized varies; depending on the game, Link is limited to defending either automatically or manually. Automatic 150px|right|Artwork of Link blocking an attack from In , Link automatically carries his shield, but it can only block projectile attacks as long he faces the direction of attack. Once again, in , the shield exclusively deflects ranged attacks. However, he doesn't only need to use it in the direction he's facing. As he charges his sword for a Spin Attack, Link can hold his shield on his right side (except when looking east, in which case he holds it on his left side), leaving that side guarded but his front open. Link, in , may use his shield against not only ranged attacks, but direct ones as well, which is crucial during combat with Iron Knuckles and Stalfos. However, this shield cannot defend against strikes from chain hammers, axes, clubs, and fireballs. The Reflect magic, one of the many spells Link can use in , increases the defensive powers of the shield, allowing it to bounce back projectiles. The shield of can also deflect both ranged and direct attacks, but as before, they are vulnerable to certain attacks. In and , Link's can protect against ranged and close-ranged attacks. Only in , however, can Link use the power of Wisdom Gems to augment the defensive powers of his shield. This method can be used to block debris shooting from Death Mountain. Now when targeting an enemy, Link automatically lifts his Shield in defense. However, he can't automatically reflect projectiles without use of the Shield Attack, a learned ability he can also use to open the defenses of enemies and stun them. To defend with the Shield in , the Wii Remote's Nunchuk must be thrust forward. The same motion is used to perform a Shield Bash, a move similar to the Shield Attack. If used just as an enemy's attack lands, the Shield Bash will act as a parry and temporarily stun them. Performing this parry does not decrease the Shield's durability. In , Link can perform a Deflect by pressing the 'A' button while guarding by holding 'ZL'. This move will bash enemies and even cause damage as a slash attack when used with any type of Lynel Shield. are recurring Items in . The Shield of the Mind's Eye goes unnamed in . Location and Uses Shields of the Mind's Eye are small Sheikah-made Shields found in both East Necluda and West Necluda. They also have a chance to appear in Treasure Chests that spawn when the Series Sheik amiibo is scanned with the amiibo Rune. Shields of the Mind's Eye were designed to decrease the wielder's blind spots without sacrificing too much in the way of defense. These Shields belong to the Sheikah Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created by the modern Sheikah. Being made of metal, Shields of the Mind's Eye will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. They will also sink if are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, they will not burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate like a wooden Shield does. Shields of the Mind's Eye reappear in . Other Appearances The Shield of the Mind's Eye can be wielded by Link in conjunction with the Prototype Ancient Short Swords. It is exclusively available as part of the purchase bonus for the game's Expansion Pass.

is a recurring character in . Biography Sho is a young Hylian living at the Tabantha Bridge Stable. He wakes up at 7:00 each morning and can be seen running around the stable, first going outside to look for bugs on the ground. At 11:00, he runs to the road next to the stable and waits for Beedle, who arrives at about 12:00. When he does arrive, Sho inspects his backpack, wishing he had a bug backpack and telling himself that he will buy a backpack when he is older. At 4:00 PM, when Beedle leaves, Sho does as well and continues to look for bugs in the same location as before. He stays there until 9:00 PM when he runs off to bed. If Link talks to him at this time, Sho expresses his disappointment since he did not find many bugs that day. Also, if Pikango has already left after Link recovered the memory "Zelda's Resentment," Sho always recognizes Link and tells him that Pikango says hello. At any time Sho is awake and it rains, he runs or stays inside, wanting to go outdoors and explaining how Thunderwing Butterflies only come out in the rain.

are Enemies in . Characteristics Shock Likes are Like Likes that are capable of spitting powerful balls of Electricity at Link. While preparing to spit Electricity at Link, the markings on their body glow bright yellow. Like other Like Likes, their hides are too tough to damage, but their bulbous, orange tongues are extremely sensitive, and striking them leaves Shock Likes stunned and vulnerable to attacks. Shock Likes intermittently reveal their tongues, swallowing Link if he is too close when they retract their tongues into their mouths. If they swallow Link, they steal one of his Shields or Weapons before spitting him out. Fire-based Weapons and Arrows stun them briefly, causing them to reveal their tongues for a few seconds before the Fire is extinguished. They can be frozen using Ice-based Weapons and Arrows. When defeated, they may drop Shock Like Stones and Shock Fruits, as well as any Weapons or Shields they have stolen. Gloom-Wreathed Shock Likes found within the Depths drop one to two pieces of Zonaite.

, also known as Stores, or are a recurring variety of location in . They sell a large variety of items or equipment that Link can purchase, often in exchange for Rupees, although there are some notable exceptions. There are many different types of Shop, and the goods that they sell tend to differ depending on these types. Features and Overview Merchants reside in hidden Shops across the Overworld in . The items available for purchase differ between each Merchant, as well as the items' prices. In , the Shop system is a lot more complex than in , introducing different types of Shops that specified in particular types of items. For example, the Magic Shop, which only sells Potions, and the Dark World Shield Shop, which only sells Shields. However, a few Shops still retain the same style as the ones run by the merchants in . also introduces the concept of selling items; Link is able to sell Golden Bees to the Street Merchant for 100 Rupees each. In the Game Boy Advance version of , there is an additonal Shop in the Village of Outcasts which sells Bees, Golden Bees and Fairies. List of Shops Although it has almost the exact same Shop system as in , does introduce Thievery. This allows Link to get any item for free by stealing it from the Town Tool Shop, but if he enters the Shop again, the Shopkeeper will kill him. This idea is only ever used again in , in which Link is able to steal from Trill's Shop. List of Shops As in , includes multiple Shops that each sell different items. One new addition is the Happy Mask Shop, which functions very differently from Shops seen previously in the series. Rather than buying the masks upfront, Link has to borrow them and then sell them himself, before paying the price of the mask back to the Shop's owner, the Happy Mask Salesman. Doing this will allow Link to borrow the mask again for free whenever he wishes. List of Shops The Shop system seen in is very similar to the one seen in , with a couple of new additions. The first of these is the Curiosity Shop, which sells stolen goods. Here, Link can purchase items that were stolen from other people, such as the Big Bomb Bag, which was stolen from the Old Lady from Bomb Shop by Sakon. Shrines are recurring locations and Objects in . Features and Overview Other Appearances Shrines are Objects that were introduced as part of the Downloadable Content update. Shrines appear within randomly-generated Dungeons in Story Mode and Dungeon Mode. They can be activated once by bumping into them. When activated, the Shrine may drop Items and/or produce an effect that persists until the character leaves the Dungeon, falls in battle, or defeats the Boss. Shrines may also be destroyed using a Bomb, Bombchu, Bomb Fairy or Red Puffstool. When destroyed, most Shrines will drop an Item depending on their type. Shrines originally appeared in Crypt of the NecroDancer, wherein they function similarly.

are locations in . Features and Overview Shrines of Light are sacred places created to purge Darkness. They were built before the foundation of Hyrule and were placed above where a demon was destroyed to prevent its reappearance. They appeared due to the Upheaval. Shrines of Light often act as trials that offer Lights of Blessing in return for reaching their ends. The Shrines of Light on the Surface have corresponding Lightroots in the Depths. These Lightroots appear in the same X and Y Map Coordinates as their Surface counterparts, and bear reversed names from their Surface counterparts. Shrines of Light in the Sky do not have matching Lightroots. There are a total of 152 Shrines of Light, with 120 found on the Surface and 32 in the Sky. In their default state, Shrines of Light have swirls of green energy that encircles a large stone at their centers. By touching a magical panel between the Dragon Statues on their fronts, Link is able to activate the Shrines of Light. When activated, Shrines of Light summon Travel Points and a portal to their interiors appears on the front of the stones at their centers. Link must enter these portals in order to claim the Lights of Blessing inside. The Travel Points summoned by the Shrines of Light can be Warped to with the Purah Pad. The Shrine of Resurrection is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Shrine of Resurrection is a Sheikah medical facility from the Era of Prosperity that utilizes Ancient Technology, and it is located within the Great Plateau. It has the ability to induce long-lasting states of sleep in its patients, which is meant to ease their healing process. One hundred years prior to the events of , Princess Zelda and Purah rediscovered the Shrine of Resurrection. Zelda was concerned that the previous Great Calamity has injuries so great that the Shrine was required, and she hoped that the upcoming Calamity would not be as severe. When the Calamity eventually occurs, Link is fatally wounded while defending Zelda from Guardians. She ordered two Sheikah soldiers to take him to the Shrine of Resurrection to recover. Once there, Purah and Robbie placed him in a Slumber of Restoration. At the beginning of , Link awakens from his Slumber within the Shrine's Restoration Room after hearing Zelda's voice call to him. He is guided to a Pedestal, where he receives the Sheikah Slate. Afterwards, the door to the chamber opens, leading to the Second Room containing a Terminal. Link can place the Sheikah Slate on this Terminal and open the entrance to the Shrine of Resurrection, leading to the Great Plateau. As part of the Main Quest "EX The Champions' Ballad", which is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack, Link must return to the Shrine of Resurrection to unlock a new power. When he places the Sheikah Slate back in its Pedestal, he will be verified as a Champion, and his Divine Beast Tamer's Trial will begin. This causes the One-Hit Obliterator will appear. The voice of Monk Maz Koshia then tasks him with clearing out groups of Monsters throughout the Great Plateau. If Link leaves the Great Plateau at any point during this trial, the One-Hit Obliterator will return to the Shrine of Resurrection. Later on, after Link completes the Divine Beast Tamer's Trials of the other Champions, Link must return to the Shrine of Resurrection again to undertake his last trial. This time, when Link places the Sheikah Slate in its Pedestal, the Restoration Room will begin to descend to the Final Trial. Areas Equipment Korok Seeds Treasure Chests The Ancient Technology within the Shrine of Resurrection has eroded away, replaced by a Cave system. The Shrine of Resurrection's counterpart in the Depths is the Secret Spring of Revival. The entrance to the Shrine is blocked by Vines hanging down from above. Though the chambers have eroded into rock and are now covered in foliage, the Restoration Room and Second Room resemble the terrain of their counterparts closely. Several Barrels and Wooden Boxes can be found where one of the Treasure Chests was located in . The Restoration Room now contains a small Hot Spring, and a crevice leading further down into the Cave has formed, marked by a large root. A Yiga Clan base has been built into the lower regions of the Shrine, marked by large flags bearing the Yiga emblem. A Steward Construct lies inside, inactive, while Mighty Bananas lie on a small podium in the middle of the base. When Link picks up the Bananas, a Yiga Clan member laughs and mocks the swordsman for falling for their trap, causing three Yiga Footsoldiers to appear and attack Link. Once Link defeats the Yiga Footsoldiers, the Steward Construct will reactivate, thanking him for his assistance when spoken to. It explains to him that it was taken from the Depths by the Yiga. It also chooses to continue its task of managing Schema Stones in the Shrine, as it has no way to return to its post. After explaining to Link that Zonaite was once mined and processed in the Depths, the Construct offers him the Schema Stone for the Beam Cycle. If Link has not unlocked Autobuild, the Steward Construct will instead advise him to visit the Great Abandoned Central Mine in the Depths before returning for his reward. Robbie agrees with this idea, stating that Terrako should be used in the activation. Since the Yiga Footsoldiers are able to bypass the rubble, Zelda asks them to carry Terrako to the Shrine of Resurrection, which Master Kohga allows them to do. A Yiga Footsoldier then disappears with Terrako. After defeating the Black Hinox and Electric Hinox blocking their path, the Yiga Footsoldiers are able to continue on to the Shrine of Resurrection. Once the Shrine of Resurrection has been activated, the Warriors will be able to access the Temple of Time. By gathering at the foot of the nearby Sheikah Tower, a Warrior will be transported directly to the Shrine. From there, they must leave the Shrine in order to assist the Hylian Captains. In order to fulfill future objectives, however, the Warrior must pass back through the Shrine of Resurrection to return to the Sheikah Tower.

are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Shrine Quests are a variety of quest accessed from the Adventure Log. Each one is linked to the discovery of an Ancient Shrine, some of which are inaccessible without involvement with the Shrine Quest. Some Shrine Quests, such as "The Silent Swordswomen" instead guide Link to an already-existing but difficult to access Ancient Shrine. In these cases, the Ancient Shrine can actually be completed without starting its respective Quest. Some Shrine Quests, such as "Into the Vortex", lead to a "blessing" Shrine that contains no puzzle nor Enemies, instead containing only a reward for reaching the Shrine. There are a total of 42 Shrine Quests to complete. List of Shrine Quests Except for "The White Bird's Guidance" and "The South Lanayru Sky Crystal", all Shrine Quests lead to a Shrine of Light which is designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing. These Shrines contain no puzzle nor Enemies, instead containing only a reward for gaining entry to the Shrine. There are a total of 31 Shrine Quests to complete. List of Shrine Quests

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Shuteye Inn is an Inn in Kakariko Village. It is located across from Impa's House and adjacent to the pond that surrounds the Goddess Statue. Ollie manages the Inn, often falling asleep at his desk and being surprised when a guest speaks to him. At night, Pikango will Sleep in the corner of the lobby, mumbling about his "journey on the horizon." The travelers Bugut and Brokka both stop at the Inn while visiting Kakariko Village The Shuteye Inn offers two Bed options: the regular Bed for 20 Rupees and the Soft Bed from 40 Rupees. The Soft Bed is stuffed with Cucco feathers, which is supposed to offer a more energizing Sleep to its users. If Link decides to Sleep at the Inn, Ollie will offer to wake him up at 5:00 AM, 12:00 AM, or 9:00 PM. After waking Link up, Ollie will instinctively wish him "good morning," regardless of the time. If Link decides not to stay, Ollie will be disappointed.

There are a total of 12 Side Quests in , two of which ("Deliver a Letter" and "Do You Love Me?") have multiple possible outcomes. In , Side Quests are optional Quests given to Link by various characters. They are denoted by a speech bubble icon containing an ellipsis. There are 76 Side Quests in the base game, seven Side Quests added in Downloadable Content pack, an extra Side Quest released through the update, and six Side Quests in Downloadable Content pack, giving a total of 90 Side Quests to complete. He is the son of King Dorephan, the current king of Zora's Domain, and the younger brother of Mipha, the fallen Champion of the Zora. His personality is noted to be cheerful and positive, and despite his status as royalty, he is respectful to everyone he meets. "" is a Main Quest in . Overview As part of the "Regional Phenomena" Main Quest, Purah asks Link to investigate strange happenings throughout Hyrule as part of the search for Princess Zelda. After both "Tulin of Rito Village" and "Yunobo of Goron City" have been completed, she suggests visiting Zora's Domain next, since Monsters are more active in the south. After Link cleans The Turning Tide during "The Sludge-Covered Statue", Yona asks why he has come to Zora's Domain. Upon hearing that he is searching for Zelda, she welcomes him to search for her in the Domain. She also suggests that Link visit Sidon, who is currently at Mipha Court on Ploymus Mountain. Once she leaves, "Sidon of the Zora" will begin. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Sidon at Mipha Court, which is covered in Sludge. He reveals that he was concerned when he heard that Link was missing and asks what happened to him. is a character in . Biography Sila is a Hylian member of the Zonai Survey Team. She eagerly wants to go on a survey mission, but she has been forced to wait on standby in the Emergency Shelter. As a result of her downtime, she has been studying the ZST: Three Big Ideas and copies of the Newspaper. When Link first approaches Sila, she can be seen reading a Newspaper. She comments on the Zonai Ruins that have appeared throughout Hyrule, and she expresses a desire to go out there and study them. She laments being stuck in Lookout Landing, claiming her studying is so that she will be prepared when she is finally called out into the field. She then reads aloud an article about the Extreme Cold Snap in Hebra, commenting that the Rito have been a focus in the Newspaper as of late. Sila reveals that some members of the Zonai Survey Team are hesitant to visit Hebra, but she claims that Freezing Climate can be avoided with Cold Resistance and the Beds at the Swallow's Roost Inn.

By the time takes place, the Silent Princess was feared to have gone extinct but was then spotted growing in the wild. The flower was said to have been a favorite of Princess Zelda, which is confirmed in the Recovered Memory Silent Princess. There is a legend if you swear your love on one, you will live a charmed life with your partner. However, they've been unsuccessful in their quest. are recurring locations in . Features and Overview There are a total of three Silos in Hyrule, all of which are located in Hateno Village. Two of these Silos, which can be found on the outskirts of the Village, are outfitted with windmills to grind flour. The third Silo, which is closer to the center of Hateno Village, has a Ladder on its outside leading to a loft. There are also several Barrels inside. The married couple Ralera and Rhodes take turns monitoring the Silos with windmills, ensuring that they are turning at the right speed. Ralera watches them during the day, while Rhodes watches them at night.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Silver Bokoblins are much more clever, powerful, and dangerous than the other three lower-tiered Bokoblins. Silver Bokoblins tend to use similar Weapons to the Black Bokoblins, including the Dragonbone Boko Clubs, Bows, and Shields. The Silver Bokoblin retains all the skills other Bokoblins have, like kicking and avoiding Remote Bombs. New to this Bokoblin is the faster reaction time and use of more powerful attack patterns. When first encountered, they tend to use a double slash attack and sometimes a slower single slash attack as well. They also use their jump and swinging attacks more often, lasting much longer than the weaker Bokoblins. Silver Bokoblins are much stronger than all other Bokoblin variants due to being influenced by Ganon's Dark Magic, only being outclassed by the Golden Bokoblins introduced during Master Mode. They carry stronger Weapons than other Bokoblins and may drop Bokoblin Horns, Bokoblin Fangs, Bokoblin Guts, Amber, Opal, Topaz, Rubies, Sapphires, and Diamonds when defeated. Drops Silver Bokoblins reappear in , acting mostly the same as they did in . However, they can now ram Link with their new Silver Bokoblin Horns. Other Appearances Silver Bokoblins are the strongest type of Bokoblin in . They have more health and do more damage, and first appear in the Scenario "Calamity Strikes". When defeated, they may drop Bokoblin Fangs, Bokoblin Horns, and Bokoblin Guts. At the end of a Battle, the Warriors will be awarded with a Bokoblin Trophy for each slain Silver Bokoblin.

are Enemies in . Characteristics Silver Horriblins are the strongest variety of Horriblin encountered, fighting the same way as their weaker relatives. Purple markings coat their bodies as a sign of Demon King Ganondorf's power, which has made their bodies tough and enhanced their Silver Horriblin Horns. Their hair is colored purple. Silver Horriblins cling to the roofs of Caves, Wells, as well as skeletons and the Desert Coliseums in the Depths. When struck while clinging to ceilings, they fall to the ground bouncing up and down in pain for a few seconds before standing back up. They are able to drown in deep Water. Bright Light from sources such as Dazzlefruits and Mirrors will cause Silver Horriblins to drop their Weapons, jump up in the air and flail their arms in an attempt to cover their eyes. With the Disguise effect from either the Horriblin Mask or Majora's Mask active, Silver Horriblins will remain passive so long as Link does not lose the Disguise effect or draw the aggression of another Monsters. While passive, they will approach Link and sniff him while tilting their heads around. They will back away from Link if he walks into them. If they are angered, they slam their fists down on the ground or ceiling and draw their Weapons. When killed, they may drop Horriblin Claws, Horriblin Guts, and Silver Horriblin Horns.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Silver Lizalfos are a strong variant of Lizalfos, surpassing both Blue Lizalfos and Black Lizalfos due to the influence of Calamity Ganon's dark magic. They have a high health of 864 and carry the strongest variants of Lizalfos Weapons. They attack Link by hitting him, spitting streams of water, and striking him with their tongue. Silver Lizalfos are capable of swimming and spitting water at Link from the water. Link can defeat Silver Lizalfos with any Weapon or Bow. When defeated, Silver Lizalfos may drop Lizalfos Horns, Lizalfos Talons, Lizalfos Tails, Amber, Opal, Rubies, Sapphires, and Diamonds. Drops Silver Lizalfos retain the same overall appearance as in . Their primary physical difference is the shape of their nasal horns, which resemble long, red scythe blades with red edges and golden swirling decorations. Other Appearances Silver Lizalfos may drop Lizalfos Horns, Tails, and Talons. At the end of a Battle, a Lizalfos Trophy will be awarded for each one defeated.

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Silver Lynels are a variant of Lynel under the influence of Calamity Ganon's dark magic, resulting in their status as the strongest of the Lynels. They are also known to be rare, and they stand out because of their purple stripes. Like White-Maned Lynels, Silver Lynels carry around the "Savage" set of Lynel Gear, though their Weapons tend to possess various bonuses. As Lynels, they are resistant to elemental attacks. Silver Lynels will often refrain from attacking for a short period of time after spotting Link, instead opting to stare at him. Using the Lynel Mask or Majora's Mask, Link can temporarily disguise himself, though they will eventually see through it and attack. They start their battles by roaring loudly and slamming their Weapons to the ground, which causes an explosion of Fire. When defeated, Silver Lynels drop Lynel Horns, Lynel Hooves, Lynel Guts, Topazes, Rubies, Sapphires, Diamonds, and Star Fragments. Drops Silver Lynels reappear in and drop Silver Lynel Saber Horns and Silver Lynel Mace Horns in addition to their previous drops of Lynel Hooves and Lynel Guts from . Other Appearances Silver Lynels are Powerful Foes who can appear in . In , Silver Lynels are Powerful Enemies.

are Items in . Location and Uses Silver Lynel Mace Horns are branching Monster Horns dropped by Silver Lynels upon their defeat, said to be as hard as Diamond. Though they are a valued Elixir Ingredient, their primary use is being Fused to Weapons, Shields, and Arrows. Weapons with Silver Lynel Mace Horns Fused to them will deal 51 additional damage when used on an Enemy, and will also be granted Crushing properties that allow them to break tough Objects such as Hard Sediment. They will, however, be unable to cut down Trees or Evermeans. Fusing one to a Shield will cause Link's Parries to damage destructible Objects and Enemies. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Sayge will exchange Silver Lynel Mace Horns for black Hateno Dye. Silver Lynel Mace Horns are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain:

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Silver Moblins are tall Monsters that can be found all over Hyrule. Due to Calamity Ganon's magic, they are a powerful variant of Moblin, surpassing even Black Moblins, but they are outclassed by Golden Moblins. When defeated, they may drop Moblin Horns, Moblin Fangs, Moblin Guts, Amber, Opal, Topaz, Rubies, Sapphires, and Diamonds. Drops Other Appearances Silver Moblins reappear as Powerful Foes in , first appearing in the Scenario "Relentless as a Waterfall". During Challenges and Scenarios added in the Downloadable Content pack, some can be seen wielding containers with Bomb Barrels during battle. A variant that utilizes Sky Octoroks is also introduced during Scenarios. Silver Moblins can be encountered as Powerful Enemies in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Simmered Fruits are Meals that can be made by Cooking a maximum of three different Fruits together in a Cooking Pot. There are two ways to make this dish's default version. First, either Apples, Palm Fruits, or Wildberries must be used without any status-altering Fruits. Alternatively, Link can use multiple Fruits with contradicting status effects. If consumed, Simmered Fruits will restore at least one of his Hearts. They have a sweet taste, and the Fruits are simmered until tender. Link can use certain Fruits, in addition to extra Ingredients, to make different variations of Simmered Fruits: Hearty Simmered Fruit: Made by using Hearty Durians or other hearty Ingredients. By eating them, Link can have all of his Hearts healed and his maximum Hearts temporarily increased. Energizing Simmered Fruit: Made by using energizing Ingredients. When eaten, they will refill part of Link's Stamina Wheel. Enduring Simmered Fruit: Made by using enduring Ingredients. Link can eat these fruits to completely restore and overfill his Stamina Wheel. Hasty Simmered Fruit: Made by using Fleet-Lotus Seeds or other hasty Ingredients. If Link eats them, Link's movement speed will be increased. Spicy Simmered Fruit: Made by using Spicy Peppers or other spicy Ingredients. When eaten, they will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Electro Simmered Fruit: Made by using Voltfruits or other electric Ingredients. They can be eaten to give Link one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Simmered Fruit: Made by using Mighty Bananas or other mighty Ingredients. These fruits will boost the power of Link's attacks when eaten. Tough Simmered Fruit: Made by using tough Ingredients. Eating these meals will increase Link's defensive abilities. Sneaky Simmered Fruit: Made by using sneaky Ingredients. When eaten, they'll increase Link's Stealth. Chilly Simmered Fruit: Made by using Hydromelons or other chilly Ingredients. Consuming them will grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Like in , Simmered Fruits can be made by Cooking up to three different types of Fruit together.

, designated by the trial name Unlit Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Siyamotsus Shrine is situated at the entrance to the South Lomei Castle Top Floor in the Gerudo Highlands Sky. Themes and Navigation Initially, the interior of Siyamotsus Shrine appears similar to a typical blessing Shrine of Light. There is a Treasure Chest in the center of the Shrine, and several small Trees bearing Fire Fruits can be found nearby. When Link approaches the end of the Shrine, however, the Statue will start moving away, revealing several unlit Torches. are recurring Creatures and Items in . Characteristics Sizzlefin Trouts can be found swimming in Hot Springs in the Eldin Canyon and Eldin Mountains. They are also sold at the Coral Reef in Zora's Domain by Cleff. It has a special organ that stores heat, which will grant Cold Resistance to Link when cooked into a dish. Eating one raw restores one of Link's Heart, but it can be exposed to Fire to make Roasted Trout or chilled by Ice to make Frozen Trout. As is the case with other Fish, Sizzlefin Trouts can be used in a Cooking Pot to make a Fish Skewer, a Fish and Mushroom Skewer, and Salt-Grilled Fish in a Cooking Pot. Sizzlefin Trouts are also among the seafood that can be used to make Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. Sizzlefin Trouts are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

Skull Lake, also known as the Skull-Shaped Lake, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Skull Lake is nestled in the upper region of Deep Akkala, just past Rok Woods and Tempest Gulch. As its name suggests, the Lake is mysteriously shaped like a Skull when viewed from above. The Left Eye is a tall pillar that juts toward the sky which Link is tasked with reaching the top of to access the Zuna Kai Shrine in "The Skull's Eye" Shrine Quest. Large purple flower-like plants can be seen in the depths of the water of the Lake. The Fang and Bone, a shop ran by Kilton that specializes in Monster-related wares, can be found on the "right eye" of the Lake at night. Once Link first meets him there, Kilton moves on to set up shop in other specific areas throughout Hyrule. A Raft can be found on the southwestern edge of the Lake, with a nearby Korok Leaf. Skull Lake is one of the locations that Link must travel to in the "[Xenoblade Chronicles 2]" Side Quest. If Link stands on the Left Eye at night and looks to the east, a Shooting Star will fall from the sky. Following this Shooting Star will reveal a Metal Chest containing the Salvager Vest. Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment Materials Treasure Chests Zonai Devices Other Appearances During the "A Rumor about Skull Lake" Quest, the Warriors wish to investigate rumors about a Merchant appearing at Skull Lake at night. When they do, they discover the Fang and Bone, where they are able to trade Monster Parts for 10 Monster Extracts and the Bokoblin Mask.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Before the events of , It was said that the Minish descended from the Sky to grant the Hero of Men and the Royal Family a magical sword, the Picori Blade, and great magical power, the Light Force. The Sky is a great expanse of air that exists above the land of Hyrule. It is normally blue during the daytime and black and Star-studded at night, with the Sky turning a burnt orange when an area of the land is engulfed in Twilight. Floating high in the Sky is the City in the Sky, an aerial city that houses the ancient Oocca. Link can reach it by launching himself out of the Sky Cannon. Areas Before the events of , a large horde of monsters led by Demise appeared from beneath the ground of The Surface world, and began leading a massacre against the people of the Surface. The monsters wanted only one thing, the ultimate power given to Hylia by the gods of old. To prevent the great power from falling into the hands of the demonic creatures, Her Grace gathered all the remaining humans on a plot of land and brought it up skyward. Centuries later, the civilization living above the clouds is living a peaceful life, with the protection of the Statue of the Goddess depicting Hylia, presiding over them. The Statue of the Goddess was built so that Hylia, could keep the Goddess Sword, Fi, and the Triforce hidden away from the mortals, and to keep them safe for the chosen hero of the goddess. The technology of the region has also greatly advanced since Skyloft was risen into the heavens, even surpassing the Surface's technology, with windmills that have the power to raise the sacred Light Tower, Beedle's flying Air Shop, and various lighting and furnishing. However, the people living there are known for their way to travel around the different Islands of The Sky, on large shoebill-like birds called Loftwings. Having a Loftwing is what separates children from adults in this little society. There are numerous islands in which Link is able to travel to with the help of his Loftwing, earning treasures and Heart Containers after locating the corresponding Goddess Cube from the surface. Also located in the sky is the Thunderhead, where the great spirit of the skies, Levias, resides, as well as the main location of the Isle of Songs. Areas Enemies Treasure Chests Goddess Cubes Goddess Cubes are mysterious cubes spread onto the world by the Goddess Hylia in order to assist her chosen hero. When Link uses the Skyward Strike on these cubes, it disappears from The Surface and beams into the sky, unlocking a Goddess's Treasure Chest. Development A distinctive aspect of is the lack of roads connecting in-game areas. The developers designed the different areas to possess distinctive gameplay styles and mechanics, which made developing roads between different areas difficult. The developers eventually decided not to include

beams into the sky, unlocking a Goddess's Treasure Chest. Development A distinctive aspect of is the lack of roads connecting in-game areas. The developers designed the different areas to possess distinctive gameplay styles and mechanics, which made developing roads between different areas difficult. The developers eventually decided not to include roads, since if they could make the gameplay in each area sufficiently dense then they wouldn't have to physically join them. They initially attempted to do this using a course selection similar to that of the , but they couldn't do it the exact same way and settled on the idea of a sky where Link would dive to the land below. According to the developers, after using the idea for some time in development, the pieces naturally fell together. The transportation, for instance, felt the most natural with a bird. In , Sky Islands appear in the Sky above Hyrule after the Upheaval began. After his encounter with Demon King Ganondorf Beneath Hyrule Castle, Link is taken to the Room of Awakening on the Great Sky Island to recover by Rauru. There, he begins to attain Ancient Powers he can use with his new Right Arm. After passing through the Temple of Time, he is able to Skydive back down to Hyrule on the Surface. Sky Islands can be found throughout the Sky. Many of them can be reached by using Recall on Ruins Rubble that falls from them. Alternatively, Link can launch himself into the Sky using Skyview Towers. Several Shrines of Light can also be found on Sky Islands, allowing for easy travel to the Sky once activated. Areas Other Appearances In , Cadence falls from the Sky when she is teleported to Hyrule.

Sky Islands, also known as Floating Islands, are recurring locations in . Features and Overview List of Sky Islands Sky Islands appear in the Floating Garden, Deception Castle, Dragon Citadel, and the Sky Temple Stages. Sky Islands appear throughout the Sky in . Zonai-style architecture can be found atop them, and they are covered with unique yellow-leafed Trees. The bottoms of these Sky Islands typically taper down to thin points supported by cores of ribbed stone. The earth surrounding some of these cores has eroded, leaving them exposed. Additionally, terrain and portions of structures from Sky Islands appear to have fallen to the ground below them as Fallen Debris and Fallen Ruins. Ruins Rubble will occasionally drop from Sky Islands, which Link is able to Recall to travel upwards into the Sky. List of Sky Islands Other Appearances The Skyloft Stage is made up of Sky Islands.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Skyshrooms are Mushrooms that grow near Trees on Sky Islands and near Fallen Debris on the Surface. When eaten, they restore one quarter of a Heart to Link's Life Gauge. They can be roasted in Fire or Scorching Climates to create Toasty Skyshrooms. Skyshrooms have no special effects when Cooking with them, and Weapons with Skyshrooms Fused to them cause Enemies to fly back when struck. Skyshrooms, among other Mushrooms, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Other Appearances Skyshrooms can be obtained as Materials in . As part of his Bouncing Slash Unique Skill, Calamo jumps onto a Skyshroom to launch himself into the air.

are locations in . Features and Overview Skyview Towers are towers built by Hudson Construction across Hyrule's Surface. Travel Points can be found outside the doors of each Skyview Tower, though they remain inactive until the Terminals inside are activated. Once activated, the Travel Points can be Warped to with the Purah Pad. After Link and Zelda disappear Beneath Hyrule Castle, Purah has to stop her work on surveying the land. Once Link returns and speaks to Purah at Lookout Landing, Purah activates the Skyview Towers and gives him a Paraglider while tasking him with the mission of traveling to all of them and Scanning both the Sky and Surface. There are a total of 15 Skyview Towers across Hyrule. Purah constructed them as a means to survey the surrounding areas where they are placed, similarly to Sheikah Towers. Unlike Sheikah Towers, Skyview Towers require a person to be shot into the Sky with a Purah Pad and a Paraglider in order to Scan the environment and return safely. Many of the Skyview Towers are malfunctioning when Link reaches them, and will need to be repaired by a nearby Hudson Construction worker before Link will be able to activate them. Once Link enters a Skyview Tower's cannon and Scans an area, both the Maps of the Sky and Surface will update, providing him with detailed location information. List of Skyview Towers

The is a recurring location in . The Sleeping Chamber goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Sleeping Chamber is located on the second level of Zora's Domain, behind the stairs leading up to the Throne Room. It has four pools of Water, which many Zora sleep in at night. Since the Zora do not have individual homes, the Sleeping Chamber serves as a communal resting space. Many Sneaky River Snails also appear at the edges of the Water, in addition to six Jars that Link can break for supplies. Two Zora can always be found in the Sleeping Chamber, these being Torfeau and Jiahto. Torfeau practices with her Zora Spear, while Jiahto will be examining the Stone Monument found at the rear of the Chamber. After "A Wife Washed Away" has been finished, Mei will spend her day swimming in the pool beneath the stairs, though she is bored by this. Initially, Kapson is also found inside the Sleeping Chamber. Due to his age, he would like one last chance to marry a couple, and so he asks Link to inform him of any engaged couples he encounters. During the Side Quest "From the Ground Up", Hudson will task Link with finding a priestly Zora to marry him and Rhondson. Kapson is interested in this, and he decides to leave Zora's Domain to officiate Rhondson and Hudson's wedding. In the back of the Sleeping Chamber is the History of the Zora, Part Seven, one of the 10 Stone Monuments scattered throughout the Lanayru Great Spring. The Monument has been worn down by the passage of time. After completing the Main Quest "Divine Beast Vah Ruta", Link can speak to Jiahto, who will have a request for him. In an effort to preserve Zora history, he wants Link to read all of the Stone Monuments and recount their contents to him. This begins the Side "Zora Stone Monuments". Once Link completes the Quest, Jiahto gives him a Diamond as a reward. Another Side Quest begins in the Sleeping Chamber after "Divine Beast Vah Ruta" has been completed, this being "The Giant of Ralis Pond". Torfeau asks Link to defeat the Blue Hinox that has taken up residence near Ralis Pond. Once this has been done, she will give him a Silver Rupee as a reward. Creatures Equipment

is a recurring character in . Biography Slergo is a Goron child who lives at Rohan's smithy. During the day, Slergo walks to the bridges crossing the lava pool in the center of Goron City, where he loiters for the rest of the day. Slergo is initially not very talkative to Link when first spoken to. However, when bidden good-bye as soon as he is greeted, Slergo becomes offended but then interested in Link's style. He decides then to appoint Link as his own student and is willing to answer him questions about the City. However, many of his answers are short and lacking. If Link asks all three questions to Slergo, he becomes excited to have such a curious student, and tells Link to ask him anything he wants, whenever he wants.

The is a recurring General Store in . Features and Overview The Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch) is a branch of Rito Village's The Slippery Falcon that is established in Tarrey Town as part of the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest. Wanting to start his own General Store separate from his mother Misa's, Fyson opened his new branch. It sells both Arrows and Ancient Materials, some of which Fyson collected on his journey to Tarrey Town. The Arrows at this General Store are usually cheaper than other Shops, as it sells Arrows for about 87% of the price compared to others. Whenever Link makes a purchase from the Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch), Fyson will thank him for his business. Should Link buy all of the General Store's Items, Fyson promises to restock soon. Wares and Pricing Wares and Pricing

are recurring Bosses in . Characteristics Sludge Likes are Like Likes coated in a thick layer of Sludge, with only their fangs and the insides of their mouths visible through it. Their hides are a light shade of grey, and the areas around their jaws are a vibrant magenta with white flecks. They have two rows of fangs. Unlike their weaker cousins, they are capable of movement, giving them a fearsome reputation. They ooze a protective coating of Sludge, which allow them to move through areas avoided by typical Like Likes. This coating can be dispelled with Sidon's Power of Water, Hydrants and Water-based Weapons, Shields, Arrows and Materials. Sludge Likes spew Sludge from their mouths in order to capture their prey, creating pools of it on the ground that impede movement. As with other Like Likes, their hides are too tough to damage even after their Sludge coating is dispelled, but their bulbous, purple tongues are extremely sensitive. However, Sludge Like tongues are also covered in a protective coating of Sludge, protecting them from damage unless the Sludge coating them has been dispelled. They intermittently reveal their tongues, allowing them to be attacked if their protective coating has been dispelled. Once their tongues are struck, they sprawl down on the ground, unable to attack for several seconds. After being stunned, they dig into the ground, reemerging nearby shortly after with a new protective layer of Sludge and firing a barrage of the substance into the air. One Sludge Like was summoned by a Phantom Ganon in the form of Zelda to attack King Dorephan of the Zora. During the "Sidon of the Zora" Main Quest, the Sludge Like that the Phantom Ganon summoned arrives in Mipha Court to attack Link and Prince Sidon. Sidon advises Link to use his Power of Water to clear the Sludge protecting the Like Like. Once defeated, Sludge Likes spew out a few last bursts of Sludge before retracting their necks into their bodies and turning black, bubbles covering their bodies before they explode into dark smoke, leaving behind an Iron Treasure Chest. Other Appearances Sludge Likes are Powerful Enemies that primarily appear in Battles taking place in the Lanayru Wetlands Stage. They have a protective coating of Sludge that increases the durability of their Weak-Point Gauge, but leaves them more vulnerable to Water-based attacks. One, which leaves behind a Stone Chest containing a Hydrant when defeated, appears during the Scenario "Lanayru Defiled".

are recurring characters in . Biography Only one Smithing Construct appears in , and it can be found in the Spirit Temple. It is a type of Steward Construct created by Mineru to discover the potential of Zonai Charges, and it is capable of crafting pieces of Zonaite into Weapons. While the Seized Construct is occupying the Spirit Temple, the Smithing Construct is in hiding. After Mineru is reawakened as the Sage of Spirit, the Smithing Construct will appear in the Spirit Temple. At Mineru's request, the Smithing Construct will give Link the Weapons it creates in exchange for Zonaite. Other Appearances Like in , Smithing Constructs are a type of Steward Construct. The first Smithing Construct is made at the end of the Quest "Enhancing our Weapons", having been created by Mineru to serve as a blacksmith for the Weapons Research Base. Following this, multiple Smithing Constructs are responsible for staffing the Base.

, also known as Papilio vulcensis, are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Smotherwing Butterflies can be found in areas of Death Mountain and Eldin Canyon with Scorching Climates, often on the edges of lava lakes. Beedle also sells them at East Akkala Stable and Wetland Stable. Using one in a Cooking Pot with Monster Parts will result in a Fireproof Elixir, which will grant Link a temporary resistance to Scorching Climates. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop as an ingredient to make Gray Dye. When upgrading Fireproof Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain, three Smotherwing Butterflies and three Moblin Guts are needed to upgrade each piece to its third tier. In addition, five Smotherwing Butterflies and two Hinox Guts are needed to upgrade each piece to its final tier. Other Appearances

, also known as , are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Clam Chowder is a dish made by Cooking Fresh Milk, Tabantha Wheat, Goat Butter, and a Hearty Blueshell Snail together in a Cooking Pot. Their regular version can only be made by including a fifth ingredient with an effect that contradicts that of the Hearty Blueshell Snail. If eaten, they will heal some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. The nutritious Hearty Blueshell Snails combine with the other ingredients to create a rich soup. There is only one variation of Clam Chowder that can be made: Hearty Clam Chowder: Made by using the default recipe. Eating this chowder will heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him temporary Hearts. Snail Chowder is a Meal made by Cooking a Sneaky River Snail, Fresh Milk, Goat Butter, and Tabantha Wheat.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Snow Boots allow Link to travel more quickly on Snow. They can be worn in Gerudo Town along with the Gerudo Veil and Gerudo Top. To obtain them, Link must wear the Gerudo Outfit and talk to Bozai outside Gerudo Town. By accepting The Eighth Heroine Side Quest, he will temporarily be given the Snow Boots. Once Link has completed the Side Quest, he will return the Snow Boots in exchange for the Sand Boots. Afterwards, Link can obtain the Snow Boots permanently by talking to Bozai again and completing The Forgotten Sword Side Quest. Once they are acquired, Granté will begin to sell the Snow Boots in Tarrey Town. Snow Boots can be both upgraded at a Great Fairy Fountain and Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Dye Options Enhancing Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances The Snow Boots are a piece of Attire obtained by completing the Quest "The Hope of Hebra", and they can only be worn by Link. are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Snow Octoroks live on Snow-covered land and can burrow through the Snow. They hide within the Snow and disguise themselves as a patch of Grass until someone comes within range of them, at which point they will spit Snowballs at their target. If Link gets too close to a Snow Octorok, it hides in the Snow to protect itself. Link can force them out of the Snow by attacking the grass on their head while they are hiding. Link can also perform a Perfect Guard with any Shield to deflect their Snowballs back at them. Other Appearances

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Snowfield Stable is a Stable that lies on the S. Tabantha Snowfield in the Tabantha Tundra, marking the northern end of the Hilltop High Road. Rin Oyaa Shrine can be found in a cave near, which makes a convenient Travel Gate to the Stable when activated. Snowfield Stable is operated by Varke, who runs both its Horse-boarding services and Inn. Harlow and Monkton are both employed as workers for the Stable. The Stable's Cooking Pot is owned by Darton, though he allows other travelers to us it. A Poster showing a Recipe for Spicy Mushroom Rice Balls hangs on the northern wall inside the Stable. Since Snowfield Stable is located within a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit without taking damage. As with all other Stables, Beedle can be found at Snowfield Stable selling his wares. Two other Merchants, Kanny and Yammo, also stop at the Stable. The travelers Ronn, Baumar, his Horse Bamboo, Nazbi, his Horse Dauntless, and Falmark all rest at the Stable during their journeys, as well. When staying at Snowfield Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Varke explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Varke offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Varke will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Varke will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. Juannelle, a resident of Snowfield Stable, has come to the Tabantha Tundra in search of information about Stalhorses, but she is unable to withstand the Freezing Climate. As part of the "Stalhorse: Pictured!" Side Quest, she asks Link to take a Picture of one on her behalf. Once Link returns with the Picture, Juannelle will reward him with a Silver Rupee. A total of three Hylian Retrievers reside at Snowfield Stable. When Link befriends the patterned Retrievers, they will lead him to a metal Treasure Chest southwest of the Stable, which contains a Star Fragment. If Link befriends the black Retriever, it leads him to another metal Chest north of the Stable, within which Link can find a Feathered Spear. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Snowfield Stable Well is a Well located behind Snowfield Stable on the Tabantha Tundra, which is part of the Hebra Mountains. It is part of a Freezing Climate, so Link will require at least one level of Cold Resistance to reach the Well without taking damage. However, its interior is instead a Stable Climate, meaning Link does not need any Cold Resistance once he is inside. The Well's underground chamber consists of a small pool of Water with four Ore Deposits and one Rare Ore Deposit along its shore. Creatures Materials

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Soldier's Bows are Bows designed for armed conflict, and they will therefore deal more damage than their civilian counterparts. They are used by Enemies across Hyrule, especially in Hyrule Field and the Faron Grasslands. The following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Soldier's Bow when they are scanned with the amiibo Rune: Series Princess Zelda amiibo Series Link (Archer) amiibo Series Revali amiibo Despite their upgrades, Soldier's Bows will burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate, and they cannot be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. Soldier's Bows belong to the Soldier's Gear equipment archetype, which is associated with the Hylian Knights from before the Great Calamity. Soldier's Bows appear in . Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Soldier's Broadswords are Weapons that Link can use to defeat Enemies, destroy Barrels and Jars, and cut down Trees. Soldier's Broadswords will usually deal 14, but that increases to 28 damage when they are thrown and broken. They were once brandished by those who once defended Hyrule Castle prior to the Great Calamity. They are considered a good and durable Weapon to use against Monsters. Link can find them commonly in Hyrule Field and the Faron Grasslands. A Soldier's Broadsword can be found planted in the ground of the cave located behind the Waterfall that feeds the River of the Dead. Scanning the following amiibo with the amiibo Rune has a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Soldier's Broadsword: Series Link amiibo Series Young Link amiibo Series Toon Link amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Toon Link () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link (Rider) amiibo Series Urbosa amiibo Soldier's Broadswords are made of metal, and they will attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. This also means that they will conduct Electricity. They will sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, Soldier's Broadswords will not burn near Fire or in a Scorching Climate. Soldier's Broadswords belong to the Soldier's Gear equipment archetype, which were all utilized by the Hylian Knights prior to the Great Calamity. A Soldier's Broadsword is part of an unnamed set of equipment used by Link in promotional media, alongside a Traveler's Bow and a Traveler's Shield. Soldier's Broadswords return as Weapons. Other Appearances A Soldier's Broadsword is Link's default Weapon. It is broken during the Movie "The Master Sword Emerges". An ancient version of the Soldier's Broadsword appears as a One-Handed Weapon. By default, Typhan wields a Soldier's Broadsword alongside a Shield. The Knight Construct is also able to fight with a Soldier's Broadsword.

They are heavy, and therefore difficult to use, but have a decent quality and durability. They are commonly used by Enemies in Hyrule Field and the Faron Grasslands, though they can also be found abandoned. Scanning the following amiibo with the amiibo Rune have a chance to drop a Treasure Chest containing a Soldier's Claymore Series Young Link amiibo Series Ganondorf amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Young Link () amiibo Series Daruk amiibo Due to being made of metal, Soldier's Claymores will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning when equipped during a Thunderstorm. To this end, they are known to be of decent quality and Durability. Soldier's Gear is primarily crafted out of iron, granting it an inability to burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will also conduct Electricity and attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, and they will sink if they are dropped in Water. Finally, they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Contradicting this, the Soldier's Bow and Soldier's Shield are constructed out of wood, meaning they are vulnerable to burning. They do not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning, they float when they are dropped in Water, and they cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. are recurring Items in . Soldier's Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Soldier's Shields are mid-grade Shield known to have once been used by the guards of Hyrule Castle. They belong to the Soldier's Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons intended for soldiers of Hyrule Kingdom. They boast a moderately high defense rating as well as a decent durability. They can be found almost anywhere throughout Hyrule Kingdom, though an easy spot is Snowfield Stable on the Tabantha Tundra. A Soldier's Shield is sold by Russ on Trilby Plain for 100 Rupees. She was born on the Surface and was a priestess before becoming queen. She is married to Rauru, and together the two founded the Hyrule Kingdom, though is possible that Hyrule may have been destroyed before the founding of their Kingdom. She possesses powers over Time and bears a Secret Stone that amplifies her powers. is a recurring character in . Biography Sophie is the daughter of Seldon, a lifelong citizen of Hateno Village. She manages the Ventest Clothing Boutique, the Armor Shop in Hateno Village. She is a meek girl who stands in the corner of the store with her posture hunched because it makes her feel more confident. When asked about the Ventest Clothing Boutique, she will recite a slogan for the Armor Shop. Even at night, Sophie will assure Link that they are open. Should Link decide to sell her something, she will take a moment before accepting anything he would like to give her. Sophie responds to anything sold to her politely and with enthusiasm. Sophie can be found in front of the Ventest Clothing Boutique in Hateno Village.

is a recurring character in . Biography Sorelia is a Hylian traveler making her way across Hyrule's wilderness with her husband Tye, whom she loves very much. They are searching for a Silent Princess blossom in the hopes of swearing their love over it and living a happy life together. While she knows the countryside is dangerous, Sorelia feared for her husband's safety and insisted on joining him in his quest. She believes that nothing can stand in their way as long as they have each other. Still, there are times when she worries that her presence is an unnecessary burden on Tye.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview After completing "Yunobo of Goron City", Link can find Fugo arguing with Rohan. He asks Rohan to allow him another attempt at making the Boulder Breaker, but Rohan refuses after he abandoned his training to indulge in Marbled Rock Roast. Fugo begs for a chance to finish his Boulder Breaker, saying that Rohan can forsake him as a student if he fails. However, Fugo needs a Cobble Crusher, five pieces of Flint and three Diamonds to do so, and he spent all of his funds buying Marbled Rock Roasts. Once Link listens to their conversation, "Soul of the Gorons" will begin. When Link has the necessary supplies, he can give them to Fugo, who will be grateful to him. Now that he is able to make a Boulder Breaker, Fugo asks Rohan to watch him do so. After he completes the Boulder Breaker, Rohan examines it and declares it is perfect. Fugo thanks Rohan for his praise, and now that Fugo has gotten his priorities straight, he decides to pass the forge on to him. Fugo is honored by this. Turning to Link, Fugo thanks him for providing the supplies he needed. As a reward, he gifts Link the Boulder Breaker that he just made. If it ever breaks, Fugo offers to make a new one for Link if he brings the supplies again. Afterwards, "Soul of the Gorons" will be finished. Objectives

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Soup Ladles are a wooden kitchen implement used for serving soup. They can be found in Hyrule Field and on the Tabantha Frontier. One in particular can be found by the Cooking Pot in the Shared Cooking Space of Hateno Village. As they are made from the wood of sturdy Trees, Link can use Soup Ladles to inflict a low amount of damage to Enemies. Due to their wooden composition, Soup Ladles will burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, and they do not conduct Electricity. If they are dropped in Water, they will float on its surface. Soup Ladles belong to the Daily Use Goods equipment archetype, which consists of Weapons that double as tools used in the daily lives of Hyrule residents. Other Appearances The Soup Ladle is an Item that serves as a relatively weak Weapon, accompanied by a Pot Lid and a Wooden Bow. Soup Ladles are One-Handed Weapons in . As a result, they can be wielded by the Knight Construct, Typhan, Lago, Vence, and Sholani. If Typhan's Weapon is a Soup Ladle, he will carry a Pot Lid with it as his Shield.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview South Akkala Stable is a Stable located in the Akkala Highlands. It is situated at the fork between Kaepora Pass and the Shadow Pass. Like other Stables, South Akkala Stable features a Cooking Pot available for use by travelers. Behind the Stable is a pen, which is where Highland Sheep and Cuccos are kept. Several Wooden Boxes have been left outside, which Link can break open for Materials. Inside the Stable is a poster, depicting a Recipe for an Egg Tart. South Akkala Stable is owned and operated by Dmitri, who manages its Horse-boarding services and Inn. His four daughters, Kaifa, Jana, Tenne, and Gleema, are also employed at the Stable. Kaifa's responsibility is to watch over the livestock, while Jana has been tasked with tending to the Stable's Flowers. Tenne is able to switch the Horse Gear or Mane of Link's Horses. Beedle can be found selling his wares at South Akkala Stable. The travelers Laroba, Lonni, Naddon, and Pitar all stop at the Stable during their journeys. Lastly, the Hylian traveler Rex currently resides at the Stable. When staying at South Akkala Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Dmitri explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Dmitri offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Dmitri will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Dmitri will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. When Link initially tries to talk to Jana, she will be dismissive of him. After giving her an Armoranth, she admits that her impression of him was wrong. As part of the "Little Sister's Big Request" Side Quest, Jana asks Link to find out what Insect her sister Gleema wants to see for her birthday. Upon hearing that Gleema wants to see dragonflies, which Jana hates, she requests that Link find a Cold Darner, an Electric Darner, and a Warm Darner. However, she is unable to take them, so she has Link deliver them to Gleema on her behalf. When she receives the dragonflies, Gleema is so happy that she runs over to show them to Jana, much to her sister's horror. After calming down, Jana gives Link a Silver Rupee as payment for his help. When Downloadable Content Pack is active, a copy of the Super Rumor Mill V2 can be found on the table inside South Akkala Stable. As part of the "EX Teleportation Rumors!" Side Quest, Link is tasked with reading the Book to learn the location of the Travel Medallion. The Super Rumor Mill V2 states that the Medallion is hidden in a labyrinth in northeastern Akkala. If Link befriends the Hylian Retriever inside South Akkala Stable's

part of the "EX Teleportation Rumors!" Side Quest, Link is tasked with reading the Book to learn the location of the Travel Medallion. The Super Rumor Mill V2 states that the Medallion is hidden in a labyrinth in northeastern Akkala. If Link befriends the Hylian Retriever inside South Akkala Stable's livestock pen, it will lead him to a metal Treasure Chest embedded in the ground on the eastern side of the pen. Using the Magnesis Rune, Link can pull the Chest from the ground and open it, at which point he will receive a Knight's Claymore. The is a location in . Features and Overview The South Akkala Stable Well is situated in the pen behind South Akkala Stable, which is located in the Akkala Highlands. It features an interior, which Link can access via a Ladder attached to its rim. The Well's underground chamber is mostly comprised of dry land, though there is a small pool of Water on its southeastern side. South Akkala Stable's missing Cucco can be found within the South Akkala Stable Well. According to the Stable Worker Kaifa, the Cucco hates being alone and will not produce Bird Eggs if she does not have a companion. Kaifa has also been woken up at night by the Cucco's squawking coming from the Well, but she dismisses it as a dream. If Link brings one of the Stable's other Cuccos into the Well, the missing Cucco will lay a single Bird Egg. When he returns later, the Cucco will have built a nest, which contains two Bird Eggs. Kaifa notes that the Cucco's squawking that wakes her up sounds happier, though she still thinks she is only dreaming it. The South Akkala Stable Well is one of several Wells that Fera can be found in prior to beginning the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?". She rates the Well's Water quality as good and its moss growth as limited, in addition to confirming the presence of Brightcaps. Once her Side Quest has started, she leaves for the Lookout Landing Well. Creatures Materials

The is a location in . Features and Overview The South Eldin Sky Archipelago is a collection of Sky Islands that can be found in the southern part of the Eldin Canyon Sky. There are two sets of Mine Cart Tracks that run through the Sky Islands beginning at the western Island then traveling through the southern Island before arriving at the eastern Island. In addition to being populated by Zonai Devices, a broken set of Mine Cart Tracks leads off of the north side of the western Island. Beneath the western Island, there is an unrelated set of three Sky Islands that are not counted as part of the South Eldin Sky Archipelago and instead simply belong to the Eldin Canyon Sky. The western and southern Sky Islands are guarded by Soldier Constructs, with one riding a Mine Cart between them. The southern Island is a three-tiered structure, with the entrance at its bottom floor. The middle floor is separated into several small rooms that house Decayed Constructs and Treasure Chests. These rooms are often separated by roots that must be cut or burned. The top level of this Island is a plaza with another set of broken Mine Cart Tracks that is pre-loaded with a Mine Cart and an intact set of Tracks beside it. There is a small cache of Zonai Devices nearby to help with the upward movement toward the eastern Island. A broken set of stairs leading to the middle level can be found on the north side of this Island. The eastern island consists of a single platform for loading and unloading Mine Carts. A set of stairs leads under a set of archways onto a small street that overlooks a Sky Island to its north. This northeastern Sky Island features a Tilted Platform at its center, the Kadaunar Shrine to its west, and a Device Dispenser to its east. The Tilted Platform points to a Sky Island to the southeast. This Sky Island features a small plaza with Barrels and Pots that house supplies. A smaller Sky Island sits directly beneath this one, with a lone Treasure Chest dangling from a Vine between them. Further southeast and lower in elevation there is a Small Island with the Account of a Celebration etched onto an Ancient Tablet. North and above from this plaza there is a small Sky Island that houses an Apple Tree. Finally, a Sky Island sits to the northeast and far below these clusters of Islands. This Island features a couple Air Platforms and a supply of Zonai Devices. Areas Device Dispenser Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Zonai Devices Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

The is a location in . Features and Overview The South Hyrule Sky Archipelago is a Sky Island due west of the Great Sky Island in the Central Hyrule Sky. Its islands lead from just south of the Hyrule Field Skyview Tower and curve clockwise on the Map, ending northwest of Hopper Pond over the Great Plateau. An additional star-shaped island can also be found floating over the River of the Dead. These islands lead to the Shrine Quest, "The South Hyrule Sky Crystal", which opens the way to the Jinodok Shrine. The highest island to the west at 1220 meters bears Luminous Stone Deposits and a Rare Ore Deposit. The island bearing the Jinodok Shrine also has a Tilted Platform to launch Link around and a Device Dispenser that produces Zonai Capsules. In the southeastern corner of the Plateau there is a Ladder, which can be used to access a series of Platforms nearby. Several of the Platforms hang over South Koukot Plateau. A Stone Talus (Luminous) can be found embedded in the center of South Koukot Plateau. It will initially be dormant, but if Link approaches it, it will rise from the ground and begin to attack him.
