The is a location in . Features and Overview The South Lanayru Sky Archipelago is a group of several Sky Islands that span the Lanayru Great Spring Sky, the Lanayru Sea Sky, and the Mount Lanayru Sky. Its westernmost Islands exist within a Freezing Climate, and Link will therefore require at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit them without taking damage. The westernmost Sky Island contains a pool, an Air Platform, and a pair of Vehicles. Several sets of Rusty Gear and Decayed Constructs that cannot be searched litter the Island. A Rail can also be found pointed south toward the Spring High in the Heavens. The South Lanayru Sky Archipelago advances higher and to the east toward Valor Island. The two Sky Islands directly to the east are guarded by Soldier Constructs and contain Vehicles to climb further into the Sky. A Sky Island to the east features a ruined building littered with Rusty Gear and Zonai Devices. East of Valor Island, there is a Sky Island with a Tilted Platform at the heart of its crossroads. The Shrine Quest for the Mayanas Shrine, "The South Lanayru Sky Crystal", can be found to the northwest of the Tilted Platform and a Device Dispenser can be found to its southeast. North of the crossroads is a small forest with multiple Decayed Constructs that can be searched for Materials. Air Platforms can be found surrounding the land containing the forest, and these lead along a chain of Sky Islands to a larger Island above. This larger Sky Island is a multi-story structure. Its top level is a flat landscape with hollow Tree Stumps. The level below it is a spacious cave obstructed by a tall wall of roots. Inside this cave, there are several Zonai Devices and a second wall of roots hiding a chamber where the Mysterious Crystal for "The South Lanayru Sky Crystal" can be found. By returning the Mysterious Crystal, Link can gain entry to the Mayanas Shrine. Areas Device Dispenser Creatures Enemies Equipment Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests Zonai Devices

The , also known as the Desert Labyrinth, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview In , the South Lomei Labyrinth is a maze located in east Gerudo at the foot of Daval Peak. There are two Koroks near the Labyrinth on mesas that overlook the area. A Guardian Stalker wanders an area to the south along with a nearby Decayed Guardian. Two Black Bokoblins patrol on top of the Labyrinth walls. Upon entering, Link hears a voice telling him that he shall receive a blessing at the end of the Labyrinth and he is given "The Desert Labyrinth" Shrine Quest. Link can see the Ancient Shrine beneath a gate on the floor that is located in the central corridor. To navigate the maze, Link must climb across walls to avoid touching the Pools of Malice along some of the labyrinth's floors and walls. He must also be careful of the Stalizalfos, Stalkoblins and Stalmoblins that can be found here in the night. Throughout the Labyrinth, Link can find several Treasure Chests containing a Silver Rupee, a Gold Rupee, a Gerudo Scimitar and a Gerudo Shield. He can also find a Golden Claymore and a Golden Bow trapped in some of the Malice. He can use Magnesis to retrieve them. Once Link reaches the end of the Labyrinth, he will discover the Dila Maag Shrine and the Shrine Quest will be complete. Enemies 's incarnation of the South Lomei Labyrinth is mostly similar to its counterpart. Pools of Gloom have appeared within the Labyrinth, and the Dila Maag Shrine has been replaced by the South Lomei Chasm, which leads directly into the South Lomei Depths Labyrinth. Far above the Surface Labyrinth is the South Lomei Castle Top Floor in the Sky. Once Link has read a tablet at the Labyrinth's entrance and reached its center, a mysterious voice will instruct him to reach the northern entrance to the Labyrinth of the sky, starting the "The South Lomei Prophecy" Side Quest. Materials Treasure Chests

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview South Nabi Lake is located in West Necluda. The main Nabi Lake can be found to its north, while a plain known as West Nabi Lake is found along its western bank. In the southwest part of South Nabi Lake, there is a small wooden Dock with a Raft at its end. A small island is located at the center of the Lake. A total of four Treasure Chests can be found on or within South Nabi Lake. The first is a Metal Chest containing an Opal, which is submerged in the Water next to the Dock. Another sunken Chest can be found between the Dock and the small island, this one containing a Soldier's Bow. Two additional Chests hidden in the Water can be found east of the island. One contains a Soldier's Spear, while the other houses an Amber. left|40px South Nabi Lake bears a single Korok Seed Puzzle. This takes the form of a Rock on the island in the center of the Lake, which serves as a Natural Hiding Spot. If Link picks up the Rock, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures

Features and Overview The South Nabi Lake Well can be found north of South Nabi Lake on West Nabi Lake, which is part of West Necluda. 100 years prior to the events of , it was part of an unnamed Hylian village. This village would eventually be destroyed by Guardians during the Great Calamity. The South Nabi Lake Well is a Well located on East Batrea Lake in West Necluda, and it is north of South Nabi Lake. The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview S. Tabantha Snowfield is located in the Tabantha Tundra. The Snowfield Stable is located at the center of the S. Tabantha Snowfield, surrounded by several groupings of Cedar Trees. It is bisected by part of the Hilltop High Road, which ends once it reaches the Stable. The Tanagar Canyon runs along the southern end of the Snowfield. Since the Snowfield is part of a Freezing Climate, Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance in order to traverse it without taking damage. One Treasure Chest can be found on the S. Tabantha Snowfield. It is a metal Chest northeast of Pondo's Lodge, and it contains a bundle of five Shock Arrows. left|40px There are a total of four Korok Seed Puzzles on the S. Tabantha Snowfield. The first is a grouping of Leaves with Fairy Dust that dart around the Snow north of Snowfield Stable. The second is a Jar located within a felled Cedar Tree, which Link must destroy using Archery. The third is a Natural Hiding Spot, taking the form of a Rock under a Pile of Leaves southwest of Snowfield Stable. Lastly, an Archery Puzzle can be found along the edge of the Tanagar Canyon south of the Stable, where it is marked by a Pinwheel. Whenever Link solves one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Areas Creatures Enemies Materials Areas Creatures Sub-Bosses Materials

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Southern Mine is a small quarry that sits along the Mountain Road in western Eldin Canyon. It is denoted by the third Death Mountain Marker. The Mine is staffed by several Gorons, who work in separate day and night shifts. Amenities for when the Gorons are not mining, including metal tents and a lit Cooking Pot, are set up for use between shifts. A number of Ore Deposits can be throughout around the Southern Mine, which can be broken to yield Gems. Since it is part of a Scorching Climate, Link requires at least one level of Flame Guard to traverse the Mine without being set on Fire. The Southern Mine is an operation by the Goron Group Mining Company. The Gems excavated by the Gorons here are sold throughout Hyrule, thereby fueling Goron City's economy. Originally, the Goron Group Mining Company used to mine at the Death Mountain Summit, but they relocated to the Southern Mine by Bludo's advisory when the Divine Beast Vah Rudania appeared. During the "Fireproof Lizard Roundup" Side Quest, Kima, a Hylian traveler visiting the Southern Mine, asks Link to help him find 10 Fireproof Lizards he can bring back home as a souvenir. Once Link has the Fireproof Lizards, he can give them to Kima, who gives him Fireproof Armor as a reward. One of the Goron miners, Greyson, expresses that he is tired of mining and desires a job where he could use his strength to make an actual difference. As part of the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest, he can be invited to move to Tarrey Town in Akkala to help Hudson demolish boulders. Greyson and his younger brother, Pelison, then depart from the Southern Mine. Creatures Other Appearances The Southern Mine is part of the Death Mountain stage. During "Daruk, the Goron Hero" Scenario, a horde of Monsters begin to attack the Southern Mine. This forces the Warriors to split apart and fight the Monsters separately. After the Igneo Talus has been defeated, a group of Fire Moblins will lay siege to the Southern Mine. As a result, some Warriors must stay behind to defend the Mine while others travel up Death Mountain. To aid them, several Goron Captains move to help with the Southern Mine's defense.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Southern Oasis Training Area can be found directly southwest of the Southern Oasis in the Gerudo Desert. It was founded by Riju after Zelda suggested the Gerudo Soldiers become more in touch with the Desert. Following the closure of the Lookout Post, Sudrey was placed in charge of the Training Area. As a result of the Sand Shroud over the Gerudo Desert, however, the Gerudo Soldiers have been unable to access the Southern Oasis Training Area. During the Sand Shroud, Link can find Teake and Sudrey arguing about reopening the Southern Oasis Training Area. Sudrey claims that it is important that the Training Area be reopened, but Teake believes it is important not to underestimate the danger of the Gerudo Desert. After the "Riju of Gerudo Town" Main Quest has been completed, Sudrey returns to the Southern Oasis Training Area. She begins to operate the Desert Race Mini-Game, which Link is able to participate in.

is a recurring location in . Southern Tal Tal Peak goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Southern Tal Tal Peak is a valley in the Lanayru Great Spring}. It is located between Tal Tal Peak to the north and Ja'Abu Ridge to the south. It is also bordered by the East Reservoir Lake, being the landing spot for two of its Docks. On its northern end is a pond, which is fed by a Waterfall from Tal Tal Peak. Another pond is located in the center of the valley. Before Divine Beast Vah Ruta is appeased, Southern Tal Tal Peak will be constantly subjected to the Rain that it generates. Within the pond at Southern Tal Tal Peak's center, a Stone Talus (Luminous) can be found embedded in the ground. It is initially dormant, but if Link approaches it, it will rise from the ground and begin to attack him. One Treasure Chest is located on Southern Tal Tal Peak, and it is within the pond on its northern end. When Link opens the Chest, he will receive a Gold Rupee. In Master Mode, a wooden platform suspended by Sky Octoroks appears over this pond. It carries two Metal Chests, containing a Frostblade and a Sapphire. Creatures Enemies Materials

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Compared to other types of weapons, Spears have low damage per hit but have a long reach and are reasonably fast. Their charged attack is a series of rapid jabs. Other Appearances (TV Series) The Spear is the only weapon that can defeat Ganon and destroy the Magic Scroll, which holds the spell to encase Link in a Crystal again. Zelda and Link find the spear stuck in the middle of the trunk. The young hero says he will cut the spear off, but Zelda stops him and asks if there isn't any other way, remembering the promise that she made to Greenbeard in which no one would hurt the woods as long as she lived. Just then, Link hears a band of Moblins heading their way. If Link decides to cut off the spear, Link will pick it up only to see that it is beginning to fade and turn into mist. The tree that had the spear stuck then starts to wither and die with its massive limbs falling onto the ground. As such, the heroes are now stuck between the advancing hordes of Moblins and the falling tree. The book ends with a Game Over as Zelda wishes she had kept her promise to Greenbeard and not let have Link cut the tree. If, however, Link does not cut off the spear, Zelda will mention she knows how to get the spear and steps back from the giant tree, lifting her arms. She calls upon Greenbeard and asks him to give them his spear to stop the gang of Moblins. The Moblins fall silent and stop in their path after a soft wind blows through the clearing, and just then the spear falls into Link's hand. As the Moblins run away, Ganon reveals himself near the cowering Moblin and steps forward. Link, getting ready to throw the spear, causes Ganon to stumble backward and asks how the heroes found the Spear. Ganon then begins to shoot fireballs at Link, who successfully dodges them. Zelda urges the young hero to use the sacred weapon, but he mentions he cannot get a clear shot. Using her bow, the princess fires an arrow at Ganon, which causes for his robe to get pinned to the tree trunk. Link takes this opportunity to hurl the spear, which lands on Ganon's hand and nails the Magic Scroll to the tree trunk. Injured, the evil wizard warns the heroes that it isn't over yet and quickly vanishes. With Ganon defeated, the pair then look at the spear, which begins to sink into the bark of the tree along with the Magic Scroll, causing for both of them to disappear into nothingness. is a recurring location in . It typically appears as a mountain with twin peaks. Features and Overview In , Spectacle Rock is found in northern Hyrule in the central western portion of Death Mountain. It is the location of Ganon's lair in the First Quest. In order to enter, Link must use a Bomb in the southern side of the base of its left peak to reveal the entrance. Areas In , Spectacle Rock is found in Death Mountain in the southwestern region of Hyrule and both of its peaks contain and are represented by caves on the map. Its eastern peak contains a cave where the Hammer is obtained after Link works his way east through its bottom level. Its western peak contains a cave that is initially covered by a rock that Link can destroy after acquiring the Hammer. Unlike the eastern peak's cave that is entered laterally, the western cave is underground where the opening is on top of the peak. A Magic Container can be found inside the cave. Enemies In , Spectacle Rock is located on top of Death Mountain in the Light World. Being Death Mountain's highest point, it is an obstacle blocking the path to its north that leads to the Tower of Hera. The center of the adjoining bridge between its peaks contains a cave that leads to lower elevations on Death Mountain. Its counterpart in the Dark World is buried under volcanic sediment, as its outline is visible. To get to the path north of Spectacle Rock in the Light World, Link must first travel to the Dark World and stand within the outline of its counterpart. Using the Magic Mirror within this area sends Link on top of Spectacle Rock in the Light World where he can find a Piece of Heart on its eastern peak. He can then leap down to the path north of it leading to the Tower of Hera. In , Spectacle Rock is based on the same location from . It appears as two large circular mesas in the east portion of the Gerudo Highlands. The northernmost mesa bears the Wasteland Tower, which is surrounded by a Bottomless Bog. Initially, the southernmost mesa will be vacant. After Link frees Divine Beast Vah Naboris during the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Urbosa will pilot it on top of the southernmost mesa of Spectacle Rock. There, it will take aim at Hyrule Castle, waiting for Link's attack on Calamity Ganon. As part of the "EX Champion Urbosa's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link is directed to return to Divine Beast Vah Naboris on Spectacle Rock. Once there, he is transported to the Illusory Realm, where he must face a recreation of Thunderblight Ganon. After defeating Thunderblight Ganon, Link will be returned to Spectacle Rock, where he will find Kass nearby. Kass reveals that he has been inspired to create a song in honor of Urbosa, which unlocks the "Champion Urbosa's

As part of the "A Picture for the Closed Stable I" Side Quest, Link must take a Picture of Spectacle Rock from above where multiple Sky Island formations create the shape of a smiling face, with Spectacle Rock itself appearing as the eyes. A Race Korok Seed Puzzle is present in the Spectacle Rock cliff face, with the Korok granting Link a Korok Seed once found. Various Stones and pieces of Tumbleweed can be found throughout Spectacle Rock, as well as a singular Boulder found in the elevated part of the northern mesa. is a location in . Features and Overview The entrance to the Spectacle Rock Cave is situated at the base of Spectacle Rock's northwestern formation in the Gerudo Highlands. It leads into a torus-shaped chamber with a pillar of rock in the center. The southwest side of this pillar bears Hard Sediment, which covers a small niche where a Bubbulfrog hides. Along the walls of the chamber, there are three Ore Deposits and a second deposit of Hard Sediment. Beyond the Hard Sediment is a tunnel with a Bottomless Bog along its floor. Three more Ore Deposits and a Rare Ore Deposit can be found within this tunnel. A stalactite at the end of the tunnel provides Link a spot to Ascend, leading to the western eye of Spectacle Rock. is a recurring character in . Biography Spera is a Gerudo who manages a Stall in Gerudo Town. She sells Cooking ingredients, including Rock Salt, Tabantha Wheat and Hylian Rice. Like many of the vendors in Gerudo Town, Spera is married to a man who lives outside of the town's walls and returns to the town in order to sell her wares. She and her husband are newlywed and seem to be close despite how little they see each other, with the two of them agreeing that voe from other places are tiny, and that the best meals are made with the best ingredients. While Spera runs the store her husband supplies the stock and does all the Cooking. Like most other store owners, Spera will also buy Items from Link, and when she does, she tells him that her husband will be pleased with the purchase. If Link speaks to Spera, she will make different remarks depending on the time of day. In the morning, she asks him if he has already eaten and wonders if people who are not Gerudo eat enough due to their small size. In the afternoon, she mentions her and her husband's views on fresh ingredients, and at night she will tell him that Gerudo Town never sleeps and that as a result her store is always open, meaning that she often cannot go home to her husband. Regardless of the time of day Spera will end their conversation by explaining that although they can get by with less sleep than most people, given how dangerous the desert can be it is important for Link to rest when he is tired. Spera will also apologise to Link that her shop does not samples of the ingredients, but guarantees that he will like the flavor. If Link buys all her stock she will give him thanks from both her and her husband.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Spiced Meat Skewers can be Cooked by combining Raw Meat and Goron Spice together in a Cooking Pot. By eating them, Link can replenish some of his lost Hearts. The Goron Spice covers up the scent of the Meat, which allows its flavor to shine. Link can add extra Ingredients while making Spice Meat Skewers, which results in the following variations: Hearty Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding hearty ingredients. Eating these Meals will heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him Extra Hearts. Energizing Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding energizing ingredients. Link's Stamina Wheel will be partially refilled if he eats them. Enduring Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding enduring Ingredients. When eaten, they completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding hasty Ingredients. They can be eaten to increase Link's movement speed. Spicy Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding spicy Ingredients. Link will gain one level of Cold Resistance when he eats these meals. Electro Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding electric Ingredients. If eaten, they grant Link one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding mighty Ingredients. Eating them will provide Link with a boost to his attack power. Tough Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding tough Ingredients. By eating them, Link's Defense will increase. Sneaky Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding sneaky Ingredients. Link's Stealth will be boosted when he eats them. Chilly Spiced Meat Skewer: Made by adding chilly Ingredients. When eaten, they will grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Like in , Spiced Meat Skewers can be made by Cooking a piece of Raw Meat with Goron Spice.

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Spiked Boko Bows are Bows used by Blue Bokoblins in the Faron Grasslands and East Necluda. They are Boko Bows that have been upgraded with Animal bone to increase their Durability and strength. Though they are sloppily made, they are light and easy to use. These Bows belong to the Bokoblin Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Weapons created by Bokoblins. Being made of wood, Spiked Boko Bows will burn if they touch Fire or if they are equipped in a Scorching Climate. They also float if dropped in Water, and they are incompatible with the Magnesis Rune. Spiked Boko Bows do not attract Lightning or Electricity like metal Weapons do during Thunderstorms. If scanned with the amiibo Rune, the Series Bokoblin amiibo has a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Spiked Boko Bow. Spiked Boko Bows appear in . They are often wielded by Bokoblins. Other Appearances Spiked Boko Bows are wielded by Blue Bokoblins and Black Bokoblins. They cannot be wielded by any Warriors.

are recurring Items in . Spiked Boko Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Spiked Boko Shields are Boko Shields that are made using slightly stronger wood and reinforced with Animal bones. They are commonly used by Blue Bokoblins in East Necluda and the Faron Grasslands. They belong to the Bokoblin Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created by Bokoblins. If scanned with the amiibo Rune, the Series Bokoblin amiibo has a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Spiked Boko Shield. Because of their wooden composition, Spiked Boko Shields will burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. However, they float if they are dropped in Water, and do not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms like metal Shields do. Finally, they are unable to be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Spiked Boko Shields appear in . Other Appearances Spiked Boko Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Spiked Boko Clubs.

The , also known as the Vessel of Spirit's Resting Place, is a recurring Dungeon in . Overview Entrance to the Temple Placed inside the Goddess of Sand, the temple is located in the westernmost area of the Desert Colossus in the Haunted Wasteland. It lies past the Gerudo Fortress. Constructed by the ancient ancestors of the Gerudo, it served as Nabooru's headquarters until Ganondorf rose to power, becoming a base of operations for the King of Thieves and his surrogate mothers. Unlike the other dungeons of the game, the Spirit Temple has two portions, each requiring a different age of Link. The Spirit Temple carries a theme of the relation between past and future, and the statues in the temple's entrance tell poems relating to such. The Spirit Temple is connected to the Arbiter's Grounds from . As an adult, Link finds the temple after following a ghost that guides him across the desert. However, when he enters the temple for the first time, he cannot make any progress due to the obstacles in front of him being beyond his tools. The west route can only be accessed through a hole too small for Adult Link, and the east route is blocked by a block too big for him. After exiting the temple, he finds Sheik and learns the Requiem of Spirit, which allows him to return to the area anytime regardless of his age. The young hero then goes to the Temple of Time and travels back to the past, and plays the new tune to start exploring the temple's western route as a child. Only after finding the proper tool can Link return to the Spirit Temple as Adult Link and explore it in the future. Themes and Navigation As a child, Link explores the western wing of the temple through a crawl space. This is the only time in this age that he encounters Nabooru, who asks him to fetch her the Silver Gauntlets. The puzzles mirror those seen in the first three dungeons (Child Link's period): In one room, a switch behind a fence must be pressed with the boomerang, another switch must be held with a statue, torches must be lit with a Deku Stick, etc. Upon defeating an Iron Knuckle and finding the Silver Gauntlets, Link has his final meeting with Kaepora Gaebora and witnesses Koume and Kotake abduct Nabooru. The adult portion of the temple is not accessible until after Link obtains the Silver Gauntlets. While wearing these, Link is able to explore the eastern wing of the temple as an adult by moving Marble Blocks. Now having a larger repertoire of items, he must solve several puzzles involving light until he ultimately finds the Mirror Shield behind an Iron Knuckle. With said shield acquired, Link's next objective is to find the Boss Key in order to access the whereabouts of Koume and Kotake. Before battling the bosses, Link must first battle a third Iron Knuckle, who is revealed to be a

ultimately finds the Mirror Shield behind an Iron Knuckle. With said shield acquired, Link's next objective is to find the Boss Key in order to access the whereabouts of Koume and Kotake. Before battling the bosses, Link must first battle a third Iron Knuckle, who is revealed to be a brainwashed Nabooru. Koume and Kotake abduct her a second time and Link gives chase to the boss room. After defeating Twinrova, it is revealed that Nabooru is the Sage of Spirit, and she gives Link the Spirit Medallion to aid him in his quest. In the version of Ocarina of Time, there are Wallmasters in several rooms of the dungeon. Some enemies, like Beamos, Red Bubbles and Stalfos are found in greater numbers, but there is only one Anubis now. There are more Silver Rupee puzzles, and there is a room with a spinning platform where a Stalfos is fought. Bombchus are used several times in the first half of the dungeon and, just like other Master Quest dungeons, Din's Fire and the Song of Time are also used. Instead of Lizalfos, Dinolfos are fought, and instead of White Bubbles, giant Green Bubbles are found. Armos are no longer found in the dungeon. It is generally thought that the Scarecrow's Song is required to progress, but there is a torch that can be hit with the Hookshot as well, although the red marker will not appear on it. It is also necessary to go through the first half of the dungeon backwards as an adult to make a chest with a Small Key appear; the key can only be collected as a child. There is a black Iron Knuckle in a room with two Gold Skulltulas; some stone thrones must be broken to collect them. New enemies include a Like Like, Fire Keese, several Gibdos, Leevers, the previously mentioned Dinolfos, and even a Club Moblin. The latter is found in an optional room where five of the non-warp songs (all but "Saria's Song") must be played, with some clues telling which one to play (Time Block for the "Song of Time", a sun for "Sun's Song", even a Lon Lon Ranch crate for "Epona's Song"), which in turn unlocks access to a Skulltula-filled room with a single Gold Skulltula. Enemies Entrance to the Temple The Spirit Temple is located in the West Necluda Depths. Its entrance is designed to resemble a Dragon, and its roof is shaped like an eye to match its counterpart in the Sky, Dragonhead Island. Statues of Owls can be found throughout the exterior of the Temple, including one guarding the entrance to the Temple. This Statue must be activated in order to gain entry into the Spirit Temple's interior where Mineru's Secret Stone rests. Only Mineru's Construct is capable of activating the Statue, requiring Link to visit the Construct Factory and assemble a Crafter Construct to act as Mineru's new body. Upon visiting the Statue with Mineru's Construct, she will activate the Statue, creating a

the Spirit Temple's interior where Mineru's Secret Stone rests. Only Mineru's Construct is capable of activating the Statue, requiring Link to visit the Construct Factory and assemble a Crafter Construct to act as Mineru's new body. Upon visiting the Statue with Mineru's Construct, she will activate the Statue, creating a Travel Point and lowering the platform bearing the Statue and Link into the depths of the Spirit Temple. Themes and Navigation The Spirit Temple's interior is composed of a single, large room that has flooded and is now home to a lake. Above the water, there remains a square stadium that leads to an enclosed shrine. This stadium is flooded with Gloom and Spiked Iron Balls dot its floor, making traversal to the shrine treacherous. The walls of the Spirit Temple are circular and tiered, with various slots for Crafter Construct. Various Poes can also be seen in some of these slots. A hallway leading north from the stadium is present, though it has caved in and cannot be used. Upon entering the stadium, a Seized Construct will ambush Link and Mineru, beginning the Boss fight. During this fight, the outside of the stadium will be sealed by a makeshift electrified gate, preventing escape. After the Seized Construct is defeated, the Gloom will disappear from the stadium, allowing Link to enter the shrine and reach the Secret Stone contained within. Within this shrine, the fragment of Mineru's Spirit will leave the Purah Pad to claim her Secret Stone and regain her power as the Sage of Spirit. After Mineru reawakens as the Sage of Spirit, a Mining Construct and a Smithing Construct will appear beside her to open Shops in the Spirit Temple. The Smithing Construct will sell various pieces of Zonai equipment while the Mining Construct will trade Ancient Blades in exchange for Zonaite as part of the "Ancient Blades Below" Side Quest. Areas Mining Construct's Shop Smithing Construct's Shop Enemies Materials

The is a recurring Shop in . Features and Overview The Spore Store is a Mushroom-themed Shop that can be found inside the Great Deku Tree's Navel in Korok Forest. After hearing from the Great Deku Tree that Link would return to Korok Forest one day, Natie opened the Spore Store, hoping it would help him if he ever became hungry. When Link enters the Spore Store, Natie will advertise their Mushrooms. Should Link make a purchase from the Spore Store, Natie will thank him for doing so. They also encourage Link to eat his newly acquired Mushrooms. If Link buys Natie's entire stock of a single Mushroom, they will promise to gather more. When Link purchases all of the Mushrooms in the Spore Store, Natie is shocked by how much he likes Mushrooms, and they resolve to go foraging soon. Wares and Pricing The Spore Store is a Shop operated by Natie. It is located directly in the center of the Great Deku Tree's Navel. Due to the infestation of Gloom that plagues the Great Deku Tree, it is initially closed and will only reopen once Link defeats the Phantom Ganon at the heart of the Great Deku Tree far beneath the Deku Tree Chasm. Due to the presence of the Deku Tree Chasm, the Spore Store moved to surround the Cooking Pot in the Great Deku Tree's Navel. Wares and Pricing

is a character in . Biography Spot is a unique Horse named for his beige coat and gray dappling. By default, his Mane is styled as a Mohawk Mane. Despite his wild temperament, Spot is also known to be meek and scared of wandering far away. Initially, Spot belongs to Lester, who recalls that they used to share Swift Carrots with each other. Prior to the completion of the Mini Stable at Lookout Landing, Spot ran away from Lester. During the "Spotting Spot" Side Quest, Link is tasked with locating Spot, who can be found on the Passeri Greenbelt southwest of Lookout Landing. When Link rides Spot back to Lester, he will be relieved to see he is safe. As a reward, Lester will give Link a Purple Rupee. Noticing that Spot seemed much happier as a Wild Horse, Lester decides to relinquish his ownership of him, though he invites Link to register him instead. If Link decides to register Spot at the Lookout Landing Mini Stable, Lester is relieved that they will be together. Once the registration fee is payed, Lester requests that Link take care of Spot. At this stage, Link is also able to change Spot's name.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview To unlock the "Spotting Spot" Side Quest, Link must have completed at least one "Regional Phenomena" Main Quest, completed the previous Side Quest "The Incomplete Stable", and be a registered Stable Association member. If Link speaks to Lester at Lookout Landing, Lester will be worried about his missing horse, Spot. Spot can be found just southwest of Lookout Landing near Passeri Greenbelt with other Horses. Like any Horse, Link can mount and ride Spot back to Lookout Landing and speak with Lester again to complete the Side Quest. Lester will reward Link with 50 Rupees and a Swift Carrot as thanks. He will also offer to let Link keep Spot and register him as his own Horse. Objectives

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Spring of Courage is an Ancient Hylian Ruin located at the northernmost part of the Zonai Ruins, which are hidden within the Faron Woods in the Faron Grasslands. It is surrounded by a giant Dragon statue, the mouth of which serves as the entrance to the Spring. A large Tree grows from the head of this statue. Inside is a large Goddess Statue known as the Spring of Courage Statue, which is surrounded by a low level of Water. When Link approaches the Statue, he will be able to exchange Spirit Orbs for Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels. The Dragon, Farosh, has served the Spring since ancient times. Prior to the second Great Calamity, Princess Zelda frequented the Spring of Courage in an attempt to unlock her sealing powers. In the Pagos Woods, Link can find Kass playing his bandoneon along the Faron Highroad. When Link approaches him, he offers to play an "Ancient Song," which describes finding an Ancient Shrine where a forest Dragon can be found. Listening to this starts "The Serpent's Jaws" Shrine Quest. When Link first arrives at the Spring of Courage, Hylia will speak to him through the Spring of Courage Statue, instructing him to offer Farosh's Scale to the Spring. If he does so, the doorway behind the Statue will open, allowing him access to Shae Katha Shrine. During the "EX Treasure: Merchant Hood" Side Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack, Link will learn from Misko's EX Journal 2 that they hid Ravio's Hood on the right hand of the Dragon statue surrounding the Spring of Courage. At this location, Link will find a metallic EX Treasure Chest, inside of which is Ravio's Hood. One additional Treasure Chest can be found at the Spring of Courage. At the entrance to the Spring, there is a metallic Chest that contains a Gold Rupee. left|40px In total, two Korok Seed Puzzles are located at the Spring of Courage. The first is a Cube Pattern on the Dragon statue's right hand, which must be solved by matching it to the Pattern on its left hand. The second Puzzle is a Rock on top of the large Tree, and Link can pick it up to reveal that it is a Natural Hiding Spot. Once each of these Puzzles have been solved, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Other Appearances

The , also known as the Goddess Statue of Courage, is a recurring character in . The Spring of Courage Statue goes unnamed in . Biography The Spring of Courage Statue is a large Goddess Statue found at the Spring of Courage in the Faron Grasslands. Like others of her kind, she is capable of exchanging four Spirit Orbs for a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. During "The Serpent's Jaws" Shrine Quest, the Spring of Courage Statue instructs Link to offer one of Farosh's Scales to the Spring. Once this is done, a doorway behind the Statue will open, allowing Link to access Shae Katha Shrine. The Spring of Courage Statue is a Great Goddess Statue situated in the Spring of Courage. By interacting with her, Link is able to exchange four Lights of Blessing for either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. He can also give her four Sage's Wills in order to deepen the bond he has with a single Sage. Her counterpart, the Wellspring of Courage Bargainer Statue, can be found below her position in the Depths.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Spring of Power is an Ancient Hylian Ruin located in Deep Akkala. A tunnel from the Ordorac Quarry serves as the entrance to the Spring. It features a large Goddess Statue known as the Spring of Power Statue at its center, which is flanked by two Trees. Waterfalls flow down from a ring on a higher level, which supply the Water for the Spring. When Link approaches the Goddess Statue, he will be able to exchange Spirit Orbs for Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels. The Dragon, Dinraal, has served the Spring of Power since ancient times. Prior to the second Great Calamity, Zelda would frequent the Spring of Power in an attempt to awaken her sealing powers. In the "Slumbering Power" Recovered Memory, Link accompanies Zelda as she visits the Spring of Power in an attempt to awaken her sealing power. In the middle of her prayer, she becomes frustrated that her power has remained dormant. She recounts that her father, King Rhoam, has been scolding her for researching Ancient Technology. Zelda curses Hylia, and she begins to cry as she wonders what is wrong with her. After receiving the "Captured Memories" Main Quest, Link can recall this Memory at the Spring of Power. At East Akkala Stable, Nobo will share a legend about offering a "sacred article" to the Spring of Power, which she believes could be part of the rituals Zelda performed. Listening to this begins "The Spring of Power" Shrine Quest. The first time Link enters the Spring of Power, Hylia will speak through the Goddess Statue, instructing him to offer Dinraal's Scale to the Spring. If Link does so, the door behind the Statue will open, allowing him to access Tutsuwa Nima Shrine. left|40px A single Korok Seed Puzzle can be found in the Spring of Power. On the ledge above the main level, there is a Rock that serves as a Natural Hiding Spot. When Link picks it up, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed as a reward. Materials Other Appearances

The , also known as the Goddess Statue of Power, is a recurring character in . The Spring of Power Statue goes unnamed in . Biography The Spring of Power Statue is a large Goddess Statue that can be found at the Spring of Power. When Link prays at the Statue, he will be able to exchange four Spirit Orbs for either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. When Link approaches the Spring of Power Statue during "The Spring of Power" Shrine Quest, she tasks him with offering Dinraal's Scale to the Spring. Once this is done, a doorway behind the Statue will open, allowing Link to access Tutsuwa Nima Shrine. The Spring of Power Statue is known to be one of several Great Goddess Statues located throughout Hyrule. She remains at the Spring of Power, where Link can give her four Lights of Blessing in exchange for a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. He can also offer four Sage's Wills in order to deepen his bond with a Sage.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Spring of Wisdom is an Ancient Hylian Ruin located at the peak of Mount Lanayru. A pathway up Mount Lanayru leads travelers directly to the Spring, which is surrounded by jagged Ice formations. It is a shallow pool of Water that flows into two small Waterfalls at either side of its entrance. There is a Goddess Statue at its center known as the Spring of Wisdom Statue, where Link can exchange four Spirit Orbs for either Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels. Due to being within a Freezing Climate, Link will take damage at the Spring of Wisdom unless he has two levels of Cold Resistance. Since ancient times, the Dragon, Naydra, has served the Spring. Prior to the second Great Calamity, the Spring of Wisdom was the final spring that Zelda visited, since those under the age of 17 are not wise enough to climb Mount Lanayru. On the day of her 17th birthday, Zelda visited the Spring of Wisdom. However, she failed to awaken her sealing power, and she and Link can be seen returning from this journey during the "Return of Calamity Ganon" Recovered Memory. In Hateno Village, Link can ask Medda about Mount Lanayru, who believes that the Royal Family of Hyrule could have a hidden treasure at the Spring of Wisdom. After listening to him, "The Spring of Wisdom" Shrine Quest will begin. When Link first arrives at the Spring of Wisdom, he will find Malice Naydra, a form of Naydra after she has been corrupted by Malice. Hylia speaks to him through the Spring of Wisdom Statue, revealing that she has been afflicted by an attack from Calamity Ganon. She tasks Link with destroying the Glowing Eyeballs and freeing Naydra. After Link shoots one of the Glowing Eyeballs on Malice Naydra, she will fly away from the Spring of Wisdom. Once Naydra has been purified, Link will automatically return to the Spring of Wisdom. As a final task, Hylia instructs Link to shoot Naydra with an Arrow. When he does so, Naydra will fly off, but not before dropping one of her Scales to the ground. Link is then told to offer Naydra's Scale to the Spring of Wisdom. Doing this will open the door to Jitan Sa'mi Shrine behind the Statue. After being freed, Naydra will appear above the Spring of Wisdom at 5:00 AM and 5:00 PM everyday. However, she will not do so if Link is at the Spring during these times. Areas Creatures Enemies Other Appearances As part of the "Inner Knowing" Quest, the Warriors are instructed to make an offering to the Spring of Wisdom. This offering includes 10 Stamella Shrooms, 10 Restless Crickets, 10 Staminoka Basses, 10 Energetic Rhino Beetles, and five Courser Bee Honeys. Once the offering has been made, a mysterious power will improve the Warriors' ability to execute Special Attacks.

The , also known as the Goddess Statue of Wisdom, is a recurring character in . The Spring of Wisdom Statue goes unnamed in . Biography The Spring of Wisdom Statue is a giant Goddess Statue that stands at the Spring of Wisdom on top of Mount Lanayru. She is capable of granting Link Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels in exchange for four Spirit Orbs. During "The Spring of Wisdom" Shrine Quest, the Spring of Wisdom Statue asks Link to free Naydra from the Malice afflicting her. After doing so, the Statue tells him to shoot her with an Arrow one final time. This causes one of Naydra's Scales to fall before Link, which can be placed into the Spring of Wisdom to open the door to Jitan Sa'mi Shrine. The Spring of Wisdom Statue is one of several Great Goddess Statues that can be found throughout Hyrule. When Link prays to her, he will be able to exchange four Lights of Blessing for either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. He is also able to deepen the bond he has with a single Sage by giving her four Sage's Wills. Her counterpart, the Wellspring of Wisdom Bargainer Statue, can be found in the Depths below her position.

is a recurring character in . Biography Sprinn is a Hylian and the owner of the Serenne Stable on the edge of the Great Hyrule Forest. He can be found at the front of Serenne Stable. If Serenne Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Sprinn will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Sprinn explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Sprinn then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Sprinn instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Sprinn suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Sprinn to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Sprinn tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Serenne Stable, Sprinn will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Sprinn thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Sprinn will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Sprinn asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Serenne Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Sprinn asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Sprinn will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Sprinn insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Sprinn refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Sprinn starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Sprinn gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated

Link to name her Epona. Sprinn gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Sprinn gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside Serenne Stable, Sprinn once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by Serenne Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Sprinn tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Sprinn wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay. Sprinn is now the manager of New Serenne Stable. If this is the first stable Link has visited, Sprinn will register him as a member of the Stable Association membership system and introduce it to him. In order to lodge there, Link has to talk to him on the inside counter. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and Malanya beds for 50 Rupees and at least 7 Pony Points. He wonders if the floating of Hyrule Castle could mark the end of the world. If it is raining, he thanks Link for coming despite the bad weather.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Squabble River is a lengthy river that stretches across the Necluda Region, beginning at some point where the Fir River meets the Cliffs of Quince, continuing until it confluences with the Hylia River just before the Proxim Bridge. The Squabble River passes under both Big Twin Bridge and Little Twin Bridge and through the Dueling Peaks, where it surrounds the Dueling Peaks Tower. Many enemy encampments can be found along the banks of the River, comprised mainly of Bokoblins. Keese and Stalkoblins will also spawn at night along the riverbank. In Hickaly Woods in a section of land south of the last bend in the Squabble River, a Stalnox will form at night. Many Treasure Chests are hidden along the riverbank and within the River itself. From west to east, the first Chest is underwater where the River meets Hylia River. Inside is an Amber. There is a Boomerang within the ruins on the north side of the River. The next two Chests are guarded by camps of Bokoblins and both contain Opals. There is an Amber, a Purple Rupee, and a Soldier's Spear within Chests that can be found inside the rocks circling Dueling Peaks Tower. There is also another Amber underwater in the northern section of the River surrounding the Tower. In Master Mode, there is a Sky Platform floating to the east of the Dueling Peaks Tower that holds a Chest containing a Shield of the Mind's Eye. Within the cliff face of the Dueling Peaks facing the river, there are two Chests that contain a Traveler's Bow and a Boomerang. There is an Opal under Big Twin Bridge, and in Master Mode, there are Sky Platforms over both bridges that contain a Soldier's Spear and a Soldier's Claymore. In addition, there are ten Arrows in a Chest in the northern section of Hickaly Woods. There is a Korok that can be found south of the Dueling Peaks Tower. Link must touch a yellow flower and follow the flower and touch it as it continually pops up across the River from stone to stone. Once Link follows the flower to the other side of the River, it becomes white and touching it causes a Korok to appear give Link its Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies

are recurring locations in . Features and Overview Animals Stables are yurt-like structures found throughout Hyrule Kingdom. They are characterized by their giant, Horse-shaped rooftop decorations. They are places where travelers, such as Link, can register and board Wild Horses that they have tamed. In addition, these travelers can seek lodging inside the Stable's main room. The owner of a Stable can instruct Link on how to capture Wild Horses, should he need to know. All Stables are connected through a network across Hyrule, allowing Link to call a registered Horse to any of the Stables he visits. To register a Horse, Link must first catch and domesticate a Wild Horse and bring it to a Stable before speaking to the Stable owner. It is not necessary to ride a Horse while speaking to the Stable owner to register it, as Link can simply bring the Horse near the Stable and speak to the owner. During the registration process, Link is able to view the Horse's qualities, which are based on Strength, Speed, Stamina, Temperament, and Bond to Link, as well as the Horse's headshot. He is also able to name his Horse at this point, provided the name fits within a nine character text limit. Stables only allow patrons to carry a maximum of five Horses, though Horses can be swapped at any time. Stables charge a fee of 20 Rupees each time a Horse is registered to fund their conservation efforts as well as cover the cost of a Saddle and Bridle, which, once paid for, will be automatically put on Link's Horse. After registering a Horse, Link is given the option to board it or to take it with him. Stables also serve as hubs for the various people of Hyrule, such as the merchant Beedle, or various characters who can provide Side Quests. List of Stables Although most of the Stables present in still remain, there have been some changes, including the addition of two Mini Stables. Serenne Stable relocated south to North Hyrule Plain after the road west of Carok Bridge was constructed. Due to a lack of customers caused by the Extreme Cold Snap in Hebra, Rito Stable was shut down and most of the residents had to leave. Traysi opportunistically purchased the Stable from Galli and converted it into the Lucky Clover Gazette. In addition, all Stables now give off a horseshoe-shaped Smoke Signal. List of Stables

Stable Bridles can be equipped to registered Horses.

are a recurring mechanic in . Stable Climates go unnamed in , , , and . Overview In , Stable Climates are areas that do not contain a Scorching Climate. Most of Hyrule is a Stable Climate, with the exception of the Death Mountain Crater, Fire Temple, and Fire Room. In , most of the Surface and the Sky consists of Stable Climates. The only place that does not contain a Stable Climate is the Volcano Summit, which is instead a Scorching Climate. Stable Climates are parts of Hyrule that do not feature Extreme Temperatures, such as Freezing Climates, Extremely Hot Zones, and Scorching Climates. When Link is in a Stable Climate, he will not take damage as he would in other environments. In , Stable Climates function the same as they do in . Link is able to enter Caves and Wells to avoid being damaged in hazardous environments. In , Stable Climates are locations where Princess Zelda will not be damaged by a Freezing Climate. They are also places where she does not react to Heat or Scorching Climates.

After switching the Horse Gear on his Horses, Link can return his Horses to Stable Gear by speaking to specific workers at Highland Stable, Outskirt Stable, South Akkala Stable, and Woodland Stable. Stable Gear is not the default Gear for Epona and the Giant Horse, who instead wear the Epona Gear and Giant Horse Gear respectively. are recurring Items and Objects in . Stakes go unnamed in . Locations and Uses Stakes appear in the Stake Garden. They can be pressed down with the Magic Hammer. When all 22 Stakes in the Stake Garden are pressed, they reveal a Cave containing a Piece of Heart. Stakes are a type of Switch made from Sheikah Ancient Technology. They require a great amount of force to activate, which can be done by striking them with Boulders or other heavy Objects. Stakes typically glow orange, but once they have been pressed, they will glow blue instead. The bases of Stakes are marked by Sheikah text that says "STAKESWITCH". They can be found in the Dunba Taag Shrine of Tanagar Canyon, the Gee Ha'rah Shrine of Kopeeki Drifts, and inside Divine Beast Vah Medoh. Stakes are Zonai Devices that have semi-solid bodies which, when used with Ultrahand, can merge into surfaces to anchor other objects onto those surfaces. They can be found inside Shrines of Light as well as on the ground on the Surface, in the Sky, or in the Depths. They can also be received in Zonai Capsule form from Device Dispensers. Stakes can only be stuck onto surfaces that Link can not manipulate with Ultrahand, such as terrain and buildings.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Stalizalfos are the skeletal remains of Lizalfos which emerge from the earth at night. They may have various Weapons such as Lizal Forked Boomerangs equipped, however, if they do not carry any Weapons, they will swipe their tails at Link or try to jab their tongue at him, the latter not even happening due to being undead. Like other Stal enemies, their bones are very fragile. Any attack Link dishes out will cause them to temporarily fall apart. The bones rebuild themselves without the head after a short period of time and walk toward the head as the head hops and rolls to the body so that they can rejoin. If Link destroys the head before the monster rebuilds itself, it is permanently defeated and both the body and head will vanish. If Link wears the Lizalfos Mask, Majora's Mask, or possesses the Stal Disguise Set Bonus by wearing the full Radiant Set or Phantom Ganon Set, Stalizalfos will not attack Link unless he attacks them. Drops Other Appearances Stalizalfos reappear in , first appearing in Freeing Korok Forest. Like in , they wield various Weapons to attack enemies with. Unlike , when a Stalizalfos is defeated, its head flies off and resumes the fight as a Cursed Lizalfos.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Stalkoblins are the skeletal remains of Bokoblins that emerge from the earth at night. They are capable of wielding a variety Weapons. If they lack any Weapons, they will either swipe at Link or dig up rocks to throw at him. Some can also be found riding Stalhorses. Stalkoblins are fragile and their bodies will easily collapse if struck, leaving their disembodied skulls to roll around. Shortly afterwards, their bodies will reform and run after their heads to reattach them. If a Stalkoblin's skull is present, the bodies of other Stalkoblins whose skulls have been destroyed will remain. These decapitated skeletons will simply jump and wave at the remaining intact Stalkoblins until their skulls have been detached, at which point they will attempt to take the skull for themselves. Stalkoblins will pick up the detached skulls of other Stalkoblins and throw them at Link to hurt him. They are usually resistant to Arrows, but if Link hits the Stalkoblin's skull, it kills them instantly. If they come into contact with a flame, their entire body will catch on Fire, in addition to any wooden implements they carry. The detached arms of Stalkoblins, known as Bokoblin Arms, can be picked up by Link and used as a Weapon. While detached, it will roll towards a common point with the other bones to reform the Stalkoblin's skeleton. If taken, Bokoblin Arms will remain animate when the rest of the skeletons they belong to are destroyed. When defeated, they may drop Bokoblin Fangs. Curiously, the Bokoblin Fangs will not drop from their skulls, but rather from their skeleton bodies. Link may pick up a detached Stalkoblin head and kick it further away from its body. If it lands in water deep enough to submerge it completely, the Stalkoblin will die. If Link wears the Bokoblin Mask, Majora's Mask, or possesses the Disguise; Bone Atk. Up Set Bonus by wearing the full Radiant Set or Phantom Ganon Set, Stalkoblins will not attack Link unless he attacks them. Drops Stalkoblins reappear in . Their behavior is the same as that of the counterparts, in that they will become active at night from 9:00 PM to 5:00 AM. During this time, Stalkoblins can emerge from the ground as Link traverses the Surface. At 5:00 AM, Stalkoblins will automatically be defeated. However, Stalkoblins in the Depths and Caves can become active regardless of the time, and they are not affected by the day. While they are inactive, Stalkoblins that the form of a pile of Bones. They can be occasionally found riding Stalhorses, particularly in the Depths. Stalkoblins usually have Weapons, which they use to attack Link. If they do not have Weapons, they are able to lunge or throw Rocks at him. Like other Stal Enemies, Link can defeat Stalkoblins by striking their heads or throwing a Dazzlefruit at them. If Link does enough damage to their bodies, their bodies will collapse and their heads will fall off. Once a

have Weapons, they are able to lunge or throw Rocks at him. Like other Stal Enemies, Link can defeat Stalkoblins by striking their heads or throwing a Dazzlefruit at them. If Link does enough damage to their bodies, their bodies will collapse and their heads will fall off. Once a body puts itself together, it will try to reattach any heads in the area. Upon defeating Stalkoblins, they drop Bokoblin Fangs and Bokoblin Horns. They also drop a Bokoblin Arm, which Link can use as a Weapon. Other Appearances Stalkoblins first appear in the Scenario "Freeing Korok Forest". Like in , they make use of various Weapons, usually of the Bokoblin Gear archetype, to fight the Warriors. Unlike in , if a Stalkoblin is defeated, its head flies off and resumes the fight as a Cursed Bokoblin. They may drop Bokoblin Fangs or Bokoblin Horns. At the end of a Battle, the Warriors will be awarded a Bokoblin Trophy for each defeated Stalkoblin.

are recurring locations in . Stalls go unnamed in . Features and Overview Stalls are the General Stores located in the center of Gerudo Town. All of the Stalls are managed by Gerudo women. According to Spera, many of the Stalls' proprietors are married and live outside of Gerudo Town, but they return to sell their wares. Arrow Specialty Shop The Arrow Specialty Shop is a small Arrow-based General Store managed by Danda. Danda sells Arrows, Fire Arrows, Ice Arrows, Shock Arrows, and Bomb Arrows. At night, Danda's granddaughters, Kalani and Makure, sleep by her side. Lorn's Fruit Stand Lorn's Fruit Stand is a small General Store in Gerudo Town managed by Lorn. At night, Lorn's daughter Dalia sleeps here. Emri, a fellow fruit merchant at the Kara Kara Bazaar, competes with Lorn. Ardin's Stall Ardin's Stall is a Mushroom General Store. She claims that the Gerudo keep their skin beautiful with the Mushrooms that she sells. As Link approaches the Stall, Ardin will greet him. When Link makes a purchase, Ardin will thank him and encourage him to use the nearby kitchen for Cooking. She also encourages him to eat many Mushrooms so he can grow bigger. If Link buys her entire stock, Ardin claims to be selling Mushrooms that only the beautiful can see. However, she admits the truth to Link and promises to restock soon. Both Jules and Nellie frequent Ardin's Stall. Jules will weigh the value of Chillshrooms against a Sunshrooms in the Gerudo Desert, which features Heat during the day and Freezing Climates at night. She also believes Ardin's claim to be selling Mushrooms only beautiful people can see. When Nellie is at Ardin's Stall, she recalls that her mother used to say that Mushroom dishes were good for dealing with headaches. As a result, she makes Fragrant Mushroom Sauté whenever she is tired, which she explains is made with Goron Spice and Mushrooms. Initially, she is hesitant to believe Ardin is selling Mushrooms that can only be seen by beautiful people. If Link claims he can see them, Nellie admits that she thought Ardin was lying to her customers while she was out of stock. While she does not care if she can see them, she claims she would have been able to when she was younger. If Link says that he cannot see them, Nellie confirms that Ardin was telling a lie. Wares and Pricing Estan's Stall Estan's Stall is a butcher General Store. It is located outside of the Hotel Oasis, to the right of the Arrow Specialty Shop. According to Maike in Kara Kara Bazaar, who runs a similar General Store, Estan is her little sister. As Link approaches the Stall, Estan will beckon him towards her. When Link makes a purchase from her, Estan will be pleased. If Link buys all of her stock, Estan will thank him for doing so. The Rito Frita is always standing by Estan's Stall. While she is enamored with how good the Food smells

Estan will beckon him towards her. When Link makes a purchase from her, Estan will be pleased. If Link buys all of her stock, Estan will thank him for doing so. The Rito Frita is always standing by Estan's Stall. While she is enamored with how good the Food smells and wants to try it, she is disappointed that there is no poultry available. Estan notices Frita staring at her Stall, and while she wonders if she has something against meat, she realizes that would be impossible. Wares and Pricing Spera's Stall Spera's Stall is a small General Store in Gerudo Town. It is located on the southern side of the market, near Ashai's House. Spera sells a Cooking ingredients, all of which are gathered by her husband. As Link approaches her Stall, she advertises how fresh her ingredients are. At night, she explains that Gerudo Town never sleeps, so she never closes her Stall. However, this means that she is so busy that she is unable to visit her husband often. When Link makes a purchase, Spera will thank him. If Link buys all of her stock, Spera will make plans to close the Stall. She thanks Link for buying everything. Pearle stops by Spera's Stall during the day. She explains that Mushroom Rice Balls are made by Cooking Hylian Rice, Rock Salt, and Mushrooms together. Since her sister Rotana has been busy researching the Seven Heroines, she considers making her some. Wares and Pricing In the wake of the Upheaval, a massive Sand Shroud erupted in Gerudo Desert, forcing the residents of Gerudo Town to take refuge in a Shelter beneath the Royal Palace. The Stalls had to be relocated to the Shelter as well, and although they are still open for business, the Sand Shroud makes it difficult to gather supplies, and as a result, some vendors don't have much products to sell. But once Link has completed the "Riju of Gerudo Town" Main Quest and stopped the raging Sand Shroud, vendors will be able to re-open their Stalls on the outside, and Link will have access to their full range of wares. They can all be found in the spots they occupied in , and almost all of them carry the same items. Arrow Specialty Shop The Arrow Specialty Shop is a Stall ran by Danda. In addition to common Arrow, she also sells Yellow, White and Red Chuchu Jelly, as well as Bomb Flowers. In the past her Stall only stocked Arrows, but she decided to adapt to the growing demand as people started attaching things to them. Fruit Store The Fruit Store is a small Fruit Stall ran by Lorn. In the shelter she has very limited supplies and can only sell Link one Voltfruit and one Hydromelon. Once the Sand Shroud has subsided, however, she will go back to the surface and add Palm Fruits to her wares. Her Stall will also be able to stock three of each Fruit at once. Ardin's

has very limited supplies and can only sell Link one Voltfruit and one Hydromelon. Once the Sand Shroud has subsided, however, she will go back to the surface and add Palm Fruits to her wares. Her Stall will also be able to stock three of each Fruit at once. Ardin's Stall Ardin's Stall offers a selection of Mushrooms, and her stock remains the same once she leaves the Gerudo Shelter. Wares and Pricing Estan's Stall Estan's Stall only opens once Link has completed "Riju of Gerudo Town". It is the only Stall not featured in the Gerudo Shelter during the Sand Shroud. Wares and Pricing Spera's Stall Spera's Stall was really impacted by the Sand Shroud. Her husband usually takes care of gathering her products, but she can't reach out to him from inside the Shelter, and she apologizes for having a very limited selection. Once it is safe to go back outside, she is able to see her husband again, and to stock her usage ranges of wares. Wares and Pricing

Treasure Chests The Stalry Plateau Cave is a small Cave in the Gerudo Highlands, and it is guarded by a Fire-Breath Lizalfos at its entrance. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Stamina Vessels permanently increases the amount of total Stamina available to Link. Link begins with one full Stamina Wheel, but he can increase the amount of Wheels he has by obtaining Stamina Vessels. Each Stamina Vessel provides a small amount of extra Stamina, with five Vessels needed for each additional full Wheel. Link can earn Stamina Vessels by choosing them over a Heart Container after trading in four Spirit Orbs to a Goddess Statue anywhere in Hyrule. Spirit Orbs are rewarded to Link at the end of every Ancient Shrine. Link can obtain up to 10 Stamina Vessels, allowing him to have three full Stamina Wheels. If Link instead uses his Spirit Orbs to achieve a maximum of 30 Hearts from the Goddess Statue, he will only have enough Spirit Orbs left to obtain a total of seven Stamina Vessels. By visiting the Horned Statue in Hateno Village, Link can exchange his Stamina Vessels for Heart Containers and vice versa. This is achieved by selling either a Stamina Vessel or a Heart Container to the Horned Statue in exchange for 100 Rupees. The Horned Statue then allows Link to buy one of either item at a higher price of 120 Rupees. This allows Link to change how he spent his Spirit Orbs at the total cost of 20 Rupees for each conversion. Stamina Vessels can be bought from Goddess Statues for 4 Lights of Blessing after "The Closed Door" Main Quest has been completed. They restore Stamina lost to Demon King Ganondorf's Gloom to Link's Stamina Wheel.

The , also known as the , is a recurring feature in . Overview The Stamina is displayed as a pie-shaped indicator that appears near Link whenever he is performing an action that requires great effort, such as climbing, sprinting, rolling, pushing, pulling, or carrying heavy objects, and performing a Spin Attack. Performing said actions depletes the Stamina Gauge, although some actions drain the meter faster than others: while dashing diminishes the stamina constantly, the Spin Attack decreases it in large portions. When Link's stamina is depleted, he will become tired and his movement will be slowed down dramatically for a few seconds until it replenishes. During this time, Link will also be unable to use items, including his Sword and Shield, leaving him defenseless against enemies. The Stamina Meter replenishes over time once Link stops performing strenuous actions, and it replenishes faster by standing still than by walking. Even if Link does not have the required stamina for a roll or spin attack, he can still perform one, making for perfect last-minute bursts of speed as the stamina meter runs out before reaching something such as a Stamina Fruit to refill the meter. If Link buys a Stamina Potion in the Skyloft Bazaar, he may halve the rate that his Stamina Gauge depletes for three minutes, or, if it is upgraded, the Stamina Gauge will not decrease at all for three minutes. Link's Stamina Gauge, upon reaching its last 1/4th, will drain at half speed for continuous actions such as running and climbing, but actions that drain Link's bar in portions (such as spin attacks and rolls) will have no change in the amount they drain. Because the stamina meter refills at a constant rate regardless of this, it is a common tactic to allow the meter to refill up to 1/4th before running again, as this effectively doubles the refill rate. While sailing the Lanayru Sand Sea on Skipper's boat, the motor's constraints appear identical to the Stamina Gauge, though it is shown in the shape of a boat's steering wheel. However, it acts exactly the same, the only differences being that the boat's motor depletes half as quickly as Link's stamina meter (and therefore depletes at a quarter of the speed when it reaches its last 1/4th of energy), and that the boat does not have any available actions that lower its meter in portions. 40px|left In , the Stamina Wheel measures Link's ability to sprint, swim, climb, glide, and use Charged Attacks. It functions nearly the same as it did in . Aiming a Bow while airborne slows time down and allows Link to aim and fire several Arrows in rapid succession, at the cost of the Stamina Wheel rapidly depleting. Unlike , the Stamina Wheel can be permanently extended via Stamina Vessels obtained by exchanging four Spirit Orbs to a Goddess Statue. Link can also receive temporary upgrades through certain recipes of Food and Elixirs. The Stamina Wheel can be extended to a maximum of

the Stamina Wheel rapidly depleting. Unlike , the Stamina Wheel can be permanently extended via Stamina Vessels obtained by exchanging four Spirit Orbs to a Goddess Statue. Link can also receive temporary upgrades through certain recipes of Food and Elixirs. The Stamina Wheel can be extended to a maximum of three full rings and two temporary rings acquired from food, with a total of five rings. But once used up, it will revert back to three rings. The Horned Statue, found in Hateno Village, can exchange Link's Stamina Vessels for Heart Containers and vice versa. This is achieved by selling either a Stamina Vessel or a Heart Container to the Horned Statue in exchange for 100 Rupees. The Horned Statue then allows Link can then buy either item at a higher price of 120 Rupees. Just like in , if Link depletes his entire Stamina Wheel, he will become exhausted until his Stamina recovers. Link is unable to swim without Stamina and will instead sink into the water only to appear on nearby land. Other Appearances Stamina is displayed as a bar on the HUD, which functions similarly to the Magic Meter where it decreases through the use of magic and special abilities like the Spin Attack, but also draining when when enemy attacks are successfully blocked with a Shield. It can be refilled by dealing successful blows against enemies, collecting Magic Jars, drinking Stamina Potions, or by consuming bottled fish, such as the Big Fish and Golden Fish.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Staminoka Bass are Fish that can commonly be found in the waters of Hyrule, or they can alternatively be purchased from the traveling merchant Bugut. Due to their naturally long lives, Food made by Cooking Staminoka Bass may restore Stamina. Eating one raw restores one Heart to Link's Life Gauge. They become Frozen Bass when exposed to Ice and Roasted Bass when burned by a Fire. All fish, Staminoka Bass included, are required to make a Fish Skewer, a Fish and Mushroom Skewer, and Salt-Grilled Fish in a Cooking Pot. Staminoka Bass are also among the seafood that can be used to make Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. Staminoka Basses can be found in bodies of Water on the Surface. Other Appearances

, also known as the Gerudo Jewelers, and , is a recurring Jewelry Shop in . Features and Overview Starlight Memories is a Jewelry Shop in Gerudo Town, owned by the jewelers Cara and Isha. The Accessories offered at the Jewelry Shop are crafted by Isha in a manner that channels the natural power of Gems, allowing their wearers protection against certain elements. Since these Gems are difficult to obtain, however, Isha requires her customers to bring them as part of their payments. The Accessories at Starlight Memories are also unisex, being able to be worn by both men and women. When Link first arrives in Gerudo Town, he will find that Starlight Memories is closed due to running out of Flint to work with. As part of the "Tools of the Trade" Side Quest, Link must bring Isha 10 pieces of Flint so she can reopened the Jewelry Shop. When Link delivers the Flint, Isha will thank him with a gift of either a Ruby Circlet, a Sapphire Circlet, or Topaz Earrings. She also invites Link to come back to the Jewelry Shop in the future, offering him a special discount if he does so. Following the completion of "Tools of the Trade", Link will be able to buy Accessories from Starlight Memories. Whenever Link makes a purchase, Isha might thank him for doing so. She can also wish for the Gems in his new Accessory to offer him protection. Isha may also comment that the Accessory suits Link.
