is a location in . Features and Overview Starview Island is a spherical Sky Island between the Gerudo Highlands Sky and Tabantha Frontier Sky. It sits among the North Gerudo Sky Archipelago in a low-Gravity field. Inside the Island, there are several floating platforms. Six of these platforms bear Updrafts, which can push Link higher inside the Island. Two more Updrafts sit at the bottom of the Island's interior. Atop several of these platforms, there are cranks attached to Mirrors, which can be rotated to redirect the faces of the Mirrors. The central platform is also controlled by a crank, which rotates three devices generating Light Beams. By moving one of the Light Beams to face north, Link can begin a chain of Light Beams throughout the Island's interior. There are two destinations for these Light Beams, both marked by light-sensitive Switches: one on a northeastern platform with a caged room housing a Treasure Chest, and another on a western platform marked by a Zonai-style arch. By activating the northeastern Switch, Link can open the caged room and access the Treasure Chest, and Link can cause the Mayasiar Shrine to appear by activating the western Switch. On a southeastern platform, there is a Device Dispenser that produces Zonai Capsules. Areas Device Dispenser Treasure Chests

The , also known as the Bronze Giant and the Eighth Heroine Statue, is a recurring location in . The Statue of the Eighth Heroine goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Statue of the Eighth Heroine is a Gerudo Ruin located on the northwestern end of the Gerudo Highlands. Several Updrafts and a pair of Ore Deposits can be found at its feet. It is of the same design as the statues of the Seven Heroines at the East Gerudo Ruins. The Statue is a monument to the Eighth Heroine, a protector of the Gerudo who is rumored to have existed, but she was removed from official Gerudo legends for unknown reasons. Myths about the Eighth Heroine and her Statue are considered to be folklore inspired by the Seven Heroines. According to Patricia, the Risoka Snowfield rests on the Statue's shoulders. Since the Statue of the Eighth Heroine exists in a Freezing Climate, Link requires at leas two levels of Cold Resistance in order to visit it without taking damage. As part of "The Eighth Heroine" Side Quest, Bozai tells Link to bring him a Picture of the Statue of the Eighth Heroine in return for his Sand Boots. To aid Link in his journey, Bozai gives him the Snow Boots. When Link brings back a Picture, Bozai will be shocked that the Statue actually exists. He states that he will not tell anyone else the location of the Statue. As he promised, Bozai then gives Link his Sand Boots. Areas Other Appearances During the "Surviving the Gerudo Highlands" Quest, a traveler wishes to visit the Statue of the Eighth Heroine to see if it has been damaged by the Great Calamity, but she needs warming Materials in order to avoid the cold. After the traveler receives the Materials, she embarks on her journey through the Gerudo Highlands.

is a recurring mechanic in . Overview begins with a telepathic message from Princess Zelda. The message beckons Link and/or his uncle to sneak into Hyrule Castle from the garden. However, this requires little actual stealth from him, as the soldiers are not actively looking for him or guarding the secret entrance. In , Young Link must sneak past the patrolling Soldiers in order to meet Princess Zelda in the courtyard of Hyrule Castle. The soldiers cannot be knocked out. Upon catching Link, they will quickly apprehend him and toss him in the dirt road to town. Before obtaining Gerudo membership at the Gerudo's Fortress, Adult Link must jump, run, hide, or knock down Gerudo patrols by any means necessary or land in a jail. Deku Link, at the suggestion of a Monkey, must sneak through the gardens of the Deku Palace to find the Bean Seller. improved on the Stealth Mission format by adding representation of line-of-sight with several dots in front of patrolling Deku; however, this only occurs at night, and so during the daytime the player cannot rely on these visual representations. This was removed in . Another expansion is that Link is required to sneak overhead to progress in addition to the usual run and cover technique. Link must infiltrate the Pirates' Fortress in Great Bay to retrieve four Zora Eggs, which the Gerudo Pirates have stolen. First, Zora Link must find a secret underwater passage hidden behind a wooden barricade. After gaining entrance to the Fortress, Link must avoid the patrols circling the cove on motorboats (if Link has already obtained the Stone Mask from Shiro, wearing it will make him invisible to the pirates, making this task much easier), while making his way over to a Switch, which he must activate with a Goron Pound while in Goron Link form. The switch opens up an underwater grate, which Link must then navigate through, avoiding traps and solving Puzzles. Once Link emerges from the passage, he must again avoid Gerudo Pirate patrols, although this time, he can knock the women unconscious with his weapons (the Stone Mask can once again come in handy while avoiding the guards). After getting past the guards, Link overhears a conversation between Aveil and one of her subordinates, after which, Link shoots an Arrow at a Bee hive, releasing the angry insects and scaring away Aveil and her guards. Link then retrieves the Hookshot from Aveil's quarters and scoops his first Zora Egg into an empty Bottle. Link then uses the Hookshot to explore the rest of the Fortress, while avoiding guards and gathering the rest of the stolen Zora Eggs. The Silent Realms in are a variation on the traditional Stealth Mission formula. Link must search for and obtain fifteen Sacred Tears in order to complete each Trial. During his search, numerous strategically-positioned Guardians will chase after him. However, every time he picks up a Tear, the Guardians become dormant and return to their original positions for 90 seconds, the countdown resetting with every new Tear. Even during this otherwise-peaceful period of time, creatures called Watchers patrol different areas of the Silent Realm, carrying searchlights. Some Watchers merely patrol along set paths; other Watchers wait in one spot until Link gets close to them, at which point they will begin to chase after him with their searchlights. If Link comes into contact with the light from a Watcher's searchlight, the countdown automatically ends, and the Guardians wake up. The same happens if Link comes into contact with an ebbing liquid called Waking Water. If a Guardian catches up to and hits Link, the Trial will end, and Link will have to start from the very beginning (except for having the locations of previously-obtained Tears marked on his map). Link has no access to any of his items or weapons whatsoever in the Silent Realms. Another stealth sequence in that sticks more to the traditional formula takes place around Eldin Volcano when Link descends to the Eldin Province to learn part of the "Song of the Hero" from Eldin. During his descent, the volcano erupts, allowing a large number of Bokoblins to take advantage of the situation and completely take over the mountain, setting up watch towers and searchlights. When Link lands, he is promptly captured and locked up, relieved of all of his items and weapons by the Bokoblins. At this point, Link must make his way stealthily around the mountain paths and collect his stolen items from Treasure Chests without being seen by Bokoblin guards or searchlights. All of the Chests are close by or directly under the light of a searchlight, which always remains stationary. If Link is caught, he is thrown in one of two cells in the area, depending how close he has gotten to the palace itself. He can easily escape by Wall Merging to slip through the bars. Snap Dragons and Zirros also appear near the Dark Palace, however, unlike the Lorule Soldiers, they are easily defeated. After saving Gulley, the soldiers disappear. Unlike the other games, stealth is now a new game mechanic used in . When Link obtains the Sheikah Slate, he is able to recognise how much noise Link is making; when walking, crouching or attacking. Stealth can be used to sneak up on monsters (which can then be attacked with a Sneakstrike for a significant damage bonus), Horses, or creatures, and is used sometimes on characters, for example following Oaki for The Lost Pilgrimage Shrine Quest. Certain factors - for example rain or tall grass - can also improve your stealth, as the rain will make your footsteps harder to recognize, and the tall grass will make you less visible. Link can also improve his stealth by using armor or food to make less noise coming from Link. There can be a maximum of level 3 Stealth boost, either by wearing a full set of stealth-up armor, or using more Materials in your food to grant a higher-level stealth boost. Sprinting will produce noise regardless of Link's level of Stealth Up. However, a more traditional stealth mission occurs in the Yiga Clan Hideout, when Link must defeat Master Kohga and obtain the Thunder Helm for Riju. The , also known as the , and the Stealth Series, is a recurring Armor Set in . The Stealth Attire goes unnamed in . Location and Uses The Stealth Set is an Armor set consisting of the Stealth Mask, Stealth Chest Guard, and Stealth Tights. Each piece of the Stealth Set can be purchased at "Enchanted," an Armor shop in Kakariko Village. The Sheikah designed this armor for stealth purposes, so each piece of the Stealth Set provides the Stealth Up effect. Wearing the entire set while every piece is upgraded at least twice provides the Night Speed Up set bonus, which increases Link's movement speed at night. However, this armor has lower defense when compared to other armor sets. Unlike regular Sheikah clothing, which cannot be purchased by folk of other races, the Stealth Set is available for all to purchase, such as Link or Bugut. Dye Options Enhancing Dye Options Enhancing Other Appearances In , Sheik wears a set of Stealth Attire, though the Stealth Mask headgear is replaced with Sheik Mask.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Characteristics Stealthfin Trouts can be found in bodies of Water in both the Great Hyrule Forest and Eldin Mountains, though they are plentiful within Lake Mekar. They are easy to find at night due to the fact that they glow in the dark. If Link eats a Stealthfin Trout, he will regain one Heart in his Life Gauge. They can also be burned by Fire to become Roasted Trout or chilled by Ice to become Frozen Trout. Cooking with Stealthfin Trout results in a meal that will temporarily increase Link's Stealth when eaten. Stealthfin Trouts, as well as other Fish, can be used in a Cooking Pot to make a Fish Skewer, a Fish and Mushroom Skewer, and Salt-Grilled Fish in a Cooking Pot. Stealthfin Trout are also counted among the seafood that can make Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. In order to upgrade the Stealth Set to its final tier at a Great Fairy Fountain, Link needs to gather ten Stealthfin Trouts and five Silent Princesses for each piece. Other Appearances

is a recurring Meal in . Location and Uses Link can make Steamed Fish by Cooking a Fish with any Vegetable, herb, or Flower in a Cooking Pot. There are two methods to make the default version of this Meal. The first way is to cook either Hyrule Basses or Sanke Carps with Hyrule Herbs, as none of these Ingredients provide any Added Effects. Alternatively, Link can use Ingredients with contradicting effects, which will cancel out. Link can heal some of his Hearts by eating these Fish. They are considered a refined dish. Based on both the type of Fish used and the kind of herb, Vegetable, or Flower used, Link can make several different variations of Steamed Fish: Hearty Steamed Fish: Made by using Hearty Bass, Hearty Salmons, Hearty Radishes, Big Hearty Radishes, or other hearty Ingredients. When eaten, they heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him Extra Hearts. Energizing Steamed Fish: Made by using Staminoka Basses or other energizing Ingredients. These Meals will refill some of Link's Stamina Wheel when he eats them. Enduring Steamed Fish: Made by using Endura Carrots or other enduring Ingredients. Link's Stamina Wheel will be completely replenished and overfilled when he consumes them. Hasty Steamed Fish: Made by using Swift Carrots, Swift Violets, or other hasty Ingredients. By eating them, Link will receive a boost to his movement speed. Spicy Steamed Fish: Made by using Warm Safflinas, Sizzlefin Trouts, or other spicy Ingredients. Consuming these meals will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Electro Steamed Fish: Made by using Electric Safflinas, Voltfin Trout, or other electric Ingredients. They can be eaten to give Link one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Steamed Fish: Made by using Mighty Thistles, Mighty Carp, Mighty Porgies, or other mighty Ingredients. If Link eats them, he will receive a boost to the power of his attacks. Tough Steamed Fish: Made by using Armoranths, Fortified Pumpkins, Armored Carp, Armored Porgies, or other tough Ingredients. Link's Defense will be increased by eating these meals. Sneaky Steamed Fish: Made by using Blue Nightshades, Silent Princesses, Stealthfin Trouts, or other sneaky Ingredients. When eaten, Link will receive a boost to his Stealth. Chilly Steamed Fish: Made by using Cool Safflinas, Chillfin Trouts, or other chilly Ingredients. Eating these will grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Steamed Fish returns in . Like in , it can be made by Cooking any type of Fish with a Vegetable, herb, or Flower. Other Appearances Steamed Fish appears in as an unlockable Recipe. The Recipe is unlocked after completing the Scenario "Road to the Ancient Lab". Steamed Fish reduces the damage Warriors take from Enemies by 5%. It is is made using two Hyrule Herbs and two Hyrule Basses.

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Steel Lizal Bows are Bows mostly found in the Hebra Mountains and Akkala Highlands, where they are used by Black Lizalfos, Silver Lizalfos, and Golden Lizalfos. Elemental Lizalfos such as Fire-Breath Lizalfos, Ice-Breath Lizalfos, and Electric Lizalfos also use them. The Lizalfos that wield them are known to be expert marksmen. While the metal reinforcements of Steel Lizal Bows increase their durability, they also end up adding weight. They belong to the Lizalfos Gear equipment archetype, a series of Weapons created and utilized by Lizalfos. Due to their metallic components, Steel Lizal Bows will attract Lightning if they are equipped during Thunderstorms and conduct Electricity. They also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, Steel Lizal Bows will not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Other Appearances Steel Lizal Bows reappear in , being wielding by the strongest variety of Lizalfos. Unlike in , they cannot be wielded nor picked up by players as Weapons.

are recurring Items in . Steel Lizal Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Steel Lizal Shields are Lizal Shields that have been reinforced with several metal shells. They belong to the Lizalfos Gear equipment archetype. Though they offer an incredible defense, their weight makes it so only a skilled soldier can bear them. They are commonly wielded by Black Lizalfos, Silver Lizalfos, and Golden Lizalfos. After Enemies tier up for the second time, they are also used by Fire-Breath Lizalfos, Ice-Breath Lizalfos, and Electric Lizalfos. If Link speaks to Selmie with a Steel Lizal Shield equipped, she will make note of it. She explains that their spike makes them worth major style points, and they make their riders look hard-core while Shield Surfing. Being made of metal, Steel Lizal Shields will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. They also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up and manipulated with the Magnesis Rune. Finally, they will not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Steel Lizal Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Steel Lizal Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Lizal Tri-Boomerangs.

is a recurring character in . Biography Steen is a member of the Sheikah tribe who resides in Kakariko Village with his wife Trissa, where he tends to his garden of Swift Carrots. When Link first approaches him, Steen asks if he needs help. After a pause, he notes that Link seems familiar to him. With another moment, Steen recalls the swordsman who attempted to halt the Calamity. Link tells him that he is that very same knight, which startles the older man, but Steen does not believe him at all due to the lack of the Master Sword. Should Link possess the Master Sword, Steen will be taken aback before deducing that it was all an elaborate joke. Steen thinks that the swordsman of old used Swift Carrots to train. However, he admits that this was something his grandfather told him. Steen tells Link to be more serious and eat Carrots to emulate the swordsman, gifting him with a Swift Carrot. He then goes on to tell Link that he can find more Carrots at his wife's store, asking Link to come to his home if he aspires to be strong. Should Link examine the field while Steen is working, he will ask the hero if he believes they are well grown. If Link agrees, Steen begins to boast and recommends that Link go to his family's store to get some. If Link should respond poorly, Steen becomes irritated with Link's lack of manners. When Link looks over the field while Steen is away, he will note how well taken care of the Carrots are. Steen claims that the Swift Carrots he grows are part of Kakariko's heritage. He will dismiss Olkin's claims about Fortified Pumpkins being the pride of the Village as rambling and considers Olkin hardheaded. Link can ask him to clarify and Steen will tell him about their rivalry. Despite their differing opinions, Steen and Olkin are on good enough terms to hunt together, though even then they're at odds. Steen has attempted to press his views onto Olkin, but to no avail. Link can also ask him for cooking tips and Steen will give him examples on how to use Swift Carrots effectively. Around 3 o'clock in the afternoon, Steen will hurry to the High Spirits Produce store to check on Trissa. When he gets there, he immediately begins to bombard her with questions about how she is doing. She brushes off his concern with a laugh. At night, Steen can be found in front of High Spirits Produce, practicing fighting with a stick that somewhat resembles a Tree Branch, but of better structure and quality. Should Link speak to him, he will offer to teach him the art of combat. If Link agrees, he once again compares Link to the swordsman of old. Steen explains that the Sheikah have developed a number of techniques, but that he may only share a few. Steen will help Link to master the moves Focus (or Targeting, Jump

teach him the art of combat. If Link agrees, he once again compares Link to the swordsman of old. Steen explains that the Sheikah have developed a number of techniques, but that he may only share a few. Steen will help Link to master the moves Focus (or Targeting, Jump Attack, and Sneakstrike. When asking about the Sneakstrike, Link gives Steen a look that causes him to quickly defend himself. Steen will explain crouching if Link expresses confusion about sneaking up on enemies. When Link bids him goodbye at the end of their session, Steen will admit his desire to take the trial of the Ancient Shrine above the Village. However, it seems no one knows how to enter the Shrine. At 3 in the morning, Steen will finally go home to rest and tells Link they can train the next night. Even in his sleep, Steen is competing with Olkin and his Fortified Pumpkins, dreaming of destroying the crop. In the morning at 6am, Steen will leave to tend to his field again, taking note of the weather and how his Carrots are doing. He mentions how his field always looks tilled in the morning; he is unaware that at night Olkin attempts to trample his crops.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Stone Pebblits are found all over Hyrule Kingdom, though they are mainly located within groups of ordinary Rocks, possibly in an attempt to catch Link off guard. Their appearance changes based on the type of terrain that they hide in. When Link gets close, they will rise out of the ground and move toward him, attempting to swipe at him with one arm. While ordinary Weapons will not work against them, they can easily be defeated by detonating Remote Bombs, or simply picking them up and tossing them away, at which point they will shatter. However, if held for too long, they will explode. This explosion does not deal damage to surrounding enemies, though it can harm Link for a base amount of 16 points of damage. The Boulder Breaker, Cobble Crushers, Drillshafts, Iron Sledgehammers, Stone Smashers, and strikes from either Ancient Arrows or Bomb Arrows will instantly destroy Stone Pebblits regardless of damage dealt. Stone Pebblits will also instantly die if they are submerged in water. Once killed, each one will drop a single piece of a random Ore or Flint. Stone Pebblits will slam their arms into Link to attack, dealing 16 base damage. Drops Other Appearances

is an Added Effect in . Overview Stormy Weather Attack is an Added Effect that, when in Thunderstorms, causes Link's charge attacks and combo finishers to generate an Electricity-based area of effect. In addition to the damage the Enemy will receive by default from the element, the area of effect has a bonus attack power of five, which can be increased by the Attack Up Effect. Level two increases the size of the area of effect by 50% for combo finishers and 33% for charge attacks, while level three increases the size of the area of effect by 100% for combo finishers and 66% for charge attacks. Level three is the maximum possible potency for this Effect. The following Materials and Armor pieces grant Stormy Weather Attack:

is a recurring character in . Biography Strade is a Goron who can be found in the Gerudo Desert. He is first found at the Kara Kara Bazaar, watching the sandstorm in the distance. Strade tells Link that sandstorms are common in the Gerudo Desert and that anyone who gets caught in one will get lost. He goes on to say that the sandstorm at the Great Cliffs is said to clear up for a few hours each day. Strade wants to visit the Gerudo Tower, but the sandstorm is in the way. He also wants to go to Gerudo Town, but has been told that it is too difficult to go there and is stuck at the Bazaar. Strade watches the sandstorm every minute of the day while awake. Because the sandstorm only clears up during the night between 9:00 PM and 4:00 AM when Strade sleeps, the Goron has never seen it die down. If Link wakes Strade up during the night, the Goron expresses a distaste for the cold nights of the Gerudo Desert. After Link calms the Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Strade can be found sitting in Gerudo Town next to the Goron Lyndae. Strade is confused why he was allowed into Gerudo Town, implying that he is male.

are recurring Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Strengthened Lizal Bows are upgraded Lizal Bows with a grip reinforced by metal. Their wooden body is made from flexible Trees that grow near Water, increasing their destructive power. They belong to the Lizalfos Gear equipment archetype, which includes all Weapons created by Lizalfos. They are commonly used by Blue Lizalfos on the Tabantha Frontier and in the Gerudo Desert, but they are also found in the hands of Fire-Breath Lizalfos, Ice-Breath Lizalfos, and Electric Lizalfos. While they do have metallic components, Strengthened Lizal Bows are considered wooden Weapons in the game. Therefore, they will burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They also float if they are dropped in Water, and they will not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms or conduct Electricity. Finally, they cannot be picked up using the Magnesis Rune. Strengthened Lizal Bows reappear in . Other Appearances Strengthened Lizal Bows reappear in , being wielded by Lizalfos and their semi strongest variants. Unlike , they cannot be picked up nor wielded by Warriors.

Overview Sub-Bosses usually protect an item within a Dungeon or other locations. Most of the time, they must be defeated to proceed within a Dungeon or area. A common characteristic that distinguishes a Sub-Boss from a regular enemy is a particular battle theme played during the encounter, which is different from the usual enemy theme. They may return later as common enemies, likely because Link will have new tools and weapons to defeat them more easily. They may come in groups, as in the case of common enemies. If they are fought in a room, the doors usually lock until they are defeated. Almost every Boss is eventually fought again as a Sub-Boss, as they no longer guard Heart Containers or Triforce fragments in their later appearances. is a recurring character in . Biography Sudrey is a Gerudo soldier who can be found at the Lookout Post in the Gerudo Desert. She was ordered by the Gerudo Chief, Riju, to monitor the Divine Beast Vah Naboris from the Post. If Link speaks to Sudrey, she says that a Hylian is a rare sight and warns him to stay away from Vah Naboris. If Link speaks to Sudrey after calming Vah Naboris, she explains that although the Divine Beast has been calmed, the monsters around the Gerudo Desert are still a problem. Sudrey continues to patrol the Desert from the Lookout Post to keep an eye on everything.

is a recurring character in . Biography Sumati is a Gerudo who can be found in Gerudo Town's bar, The Noble Canteen. If Link goes into the Canteen, he will find Sumati accompanied by two other Gerudo named Pyra and Yaido. If Link speaks to one of them, they talk to each other about a password for a secret place. They stop talking about it as soon as they notice that Link is listening and Sumati tells him to go away. Link can eavesdrop on them by going onto the opposite side of the nearby window in Rotana's House. If Link eavesdrops on them here before ever speaking to them while in The Noble Canteen, he will hear Yaido asking the others if they have heard of a rumor about Fashion Passion. Sumati replies that she has heard the rumor and Yaido responds by saying that she asked Saula about it, but Saula wouldn't tell her anything. Pyra then mentions how suspicious it is that Saula won't give away any information. Once Link is eavesdropping on the Gerudo women after speaking to them directly, he will overhear Sumati referring to him as a little Hylian girl. Pyra then says to forget about the girl and urges Yaido to tell them the password. Yaido reveals that she overheard Saula say that the password is "GSC♦." Sumati quickly realizes that it must stand for "Gerudo Secret Club" before the conversation ends. The password that they reveal allows Link entry to the Gerudo Secret Club. After Link calms Naboris, he gains entry to the Gerudo Secret Club and speaks to the Gerudo women again, Yaido will question where Perda is. Sumati says that she left in search of Lover's Pond and Pyra comments that it is rumored to be the perfect place to find true love. Yaido then proceeds to say something, but is interrupted when Sumati tells Link to go away. Link can eavesdrop on them again from the window in Rotana's house to hear them talk about Perda in more detail. While listening, Yaido wonders how Perda is doing and Sumati comments about how enthusiastic she was to find Lover's Pond. Yaido then talks about how quickly she left when she heard that Lover's Pond is in Faron. This surprises Pyra, who thought it was only a rumor. Sumati says that she does not know for sure, but her and Pyra conclude that Perda must have found true love because she has not returned yet. At the end of the conversation, Yaido contemplates if she should also travel to Lover's Pond.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Summerwing Butterflies can be found in the Great Hyrule Forest and less scorching areas of the Eldin Mountains. They can be caught by sneaking up on them or purchased from Beedle at the Kara Kara Bazaar, Snowfield Stable, and Tabantha Bridge Stable. Combining one in a Cooking Pot with Monster Parts will create a Spicy Elixir, which grants Link temporary Cold Resistance. They can also be used to make Red Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop in Hateno Village. are Items in . Location and Uses Sun Pumpkins are a new type of Pumpkin that were cultivated by Reede in Hateno Village. When eaten, they will restore half of a Heart to Link's Life Gauge. Cooking with Sun Pumpkins will result in a dish that grants Gloom Recovery, which can heal the effects of Gloom. After his daughter Karin noticed that other children in Hateno Village were not eating as many Vegetables, Reede decided to start breeding a new Vegetable that would appeal to them. Working with Nack, Reede's philosophy was to use the styling of Cece-Brand Designs, which is popular among the youth of Hateno. At the end of the Side Adventure "The Mayoral Election", Cece offers to help Reede with the development of his Pumpkins. Sun Pumpkins and Fortified Pumpkins can be used interchangeably when Cooking. In some cases, they can also be replaced by a Carrot. They are required for the following Meals: Like other Vegetables, Sun Pumpkins can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals:

, also known as Yellow Plants, and as a New Species, are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Sundelions are Flower Materials that grow in the sunlight on Sky Islands. They can also be found on the Surface next to Fallen Debris and Fallen Ruins that fell during the Upheaval. When used in Cooking, they grant Gloom Recovery to Link, which restores Hearts depleted by Gloom. Once thought to be extinct, the Zonai Survey Team have found Sundelions in the Southern Ring Ruin and are cultivating them in Mellie's Plum Garden. Due to them being difficult to procure, Ebah has been working to create an alternative to Sundelions for use in treating Gloom. Like other Flowers, Sundelions can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Sundelions are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Sunset Fireflies can be found flying around during the night, particularly noticeable by their glow. When combined with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot, the result will be a Sneaky Elixir, which will temporarily increase Link's Stealth when consumed. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop as an ingredient for Purple Dye. If Link enters Lasli's home during the evening, she will express remorse over being unable to gather any fireflies due to the roads being dangerous at night. After talking to her, Link will receive the Side Quest "By Firefly's Light", which requires him to obtain five Sunset Fireflies. Releasing the fireflies in front of Lasli will end the quest, and she will reward him with fifty Rupees. Five Sunset Fireflies, as well as five Blue Nightshades, are needed to upgrade each piece of the Stealth Set to its second tier at a Great Fairy Fountain. Sunset Fireflies can be seen on the Sky Islands during the night. Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Sunshrooms are a type of Mushroom that can found growing near Trees in Eldin Canyon and the Gerudo Highlands. They can be purchased from The Slippery Falcon and Ardin's Stall in Gerudo Town. They can be eaten as is to restore half a Heart to Link's Life Gauge, but they can also be Cooked into Food to restore greater health and provide Cold Resistance. When Sunshrooms are burned by Fire, they become Toasty Sunshrooms. In addition, Sunshrooms can be used as an ingredient at the Kochi Dye Shop to create Red Dye. After Link upgrades his Sheikah Sensor at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab, Symin will ask to see it. When Link speaks to Symin next, he decides to demonstrate how he can use Sheikah Sensor to find Items that are depicted in the Hyrule Compendium. He tasks Link with taking a Picture of a Sunshroom, pointing out that one can be found behind the Lab. This begins the "Sunshroom Sensing" Side Quest. Once Link returns with a Picture of a Sunshroom, Symin will ask to see it to confirm. He is pleased to see the Picture, and he then tasks Link to tune his Sheikah Sensor to his Hyrule Compendium Picture of the Sunshroom. He then asks Link to bring him three Sunshrooms using the Sheikah Sensor. After gathering three Sunshrooms, Link can return to Symin and hand them over. When Link does so, Symin thanks Link and gives him three Hearty Truffles as a reward. Another Side Quest, "Riddles of Hyrule," involves Walton telling Link riddles and having him bring the corresponding Item. For his third riddle, Walton will ask Link to find a Mushroom that warms one's bones and can be found in warmer areas. If Link places a Sunshroom on the leaf in front of Walton, he will cheer that Link figured out the riddle. The , designated by the trial name A Spinning Device, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Susuyai Shrine is a Shrine of Light on the Surface. It is located in the northwest portion of the Hyrule Garrison Ruins in Hyrule Field in the same spot where the Central Tower was located in . It corresponds to the Iayusus Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation The whole of the Susuyai Shrine consists of one large hallway with multiple obstacles throughout it. These obstacles serve to instruct Link on how to use Small Wheels in his Ultrahand constructions. The first obstacle has three Vehicles made from Small Wheels and Stone Slabs that continuously drive across the hallway and off the side into a pit. These Vehicles may injure Link and can continue to push him off the side unless he moves away. Ultrahand can be used to grab the Vehicles and move them out of their cycle so Link can walk across. Link may also simply dodge them instead. The second obstacle is a large rolling cylinder that spans the entire width of the hallway. Four Small Wheels and a lone Stone Slab sit nearby that Link can use to create a Vehicle that will drive fast enough to cross the cylinder. It is possible to simply run across the cylinder instead, as it rotates at nearly Link's exact walking speed. The third obstacle is a portcullis that locks Link out of the next room. The nearby lever will raise the portcullis when pushed, but must be continuously pushed for the portcullis to remain open. To keep the lever spinning while Link walks through the gate, Link may use Ultrahand to attach a Small Wheel to the lever and then activate it, which will push the lever as long as it runs. Alternatively, Recall may be used on the lever after it is pushed for some time, which will keep the lever spinning without Link pushing it. The final room has a large pit with a Rail spanning the gap. The room provides Link with two Small Wheels and a Lift hanging on the wire. Attaching a Small Wheel to the top of the Lift where it hangs on the wire will drag the Lift across the gap and carry Link with it. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found across the pit. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Suzuna joined the Monster-Control Crew for logistical support, like tending to Horses and making elixirs. As such, when Link meets her near Hyrule Field Chasm, he is gifted an Elixir. She also points him towards the location where Hoz assaults a Monster Stronghold with his squad. Since the new recruits didn't receive much training, she is worried about the mission and wishes that an experienced fighter supports them. When squad one successfully defeated the Monster Stronghold she moves away with the temporary camp. If Link talks to her during the night she mentions that it can't be eay to travel in darkness.

, also known as the Swallow's Roost Inn, is a recurring Inn in . Features and Overview Swallow's Roost is Rito Village's Inn, being located near the town's entrance. Cecili works at the Inn's front desk, welcoming visitors as the enter. Verla also works for Swallow's Roost, standing in front of the building an advertising Beds to passerby. The Hylian travelers Jogo and Juney, who are on their honeymoon in Rito Village, Sleep at the Inn during the night. When staying at Swallow's Roost, Link has the option to use either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Rito-down Bed for 80 Rupees. According to Cecili, Rito-down Beds are made using Rito feathers that leave their users energized, and she guarantees that they are more comfortable than the average Stable Bed. If Link decides to stay, Cecili then gives him the option to wake up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Link can obtain "The Spark of Romance" Side Quest by speaking to Jogo inside Swallow's Roost. As a result of the Blizzard over Rito Village, Kotts has temporarily taken over the Swallow's Roost. She offers a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Rito-down bed for 50 Rupees.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Swallow Bows are Bows favored among Rito warriors. They belong to the Rito Gear equipment archetype, which consists of Weapons that are made and used by the Rito. Engineered for aerial combat, the bowstring is able to be drawn faster than those of normal Bows. They can be found most commonly in Rito Village, but some are scattered around the Tabantha Frontier and Hebra Mountains, either in Treasure Chests or being used by Enemies. Scanning the Series Revali amiibo with the amiibo Rune has a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Swallow Bow. If the Great Eagle Bow is ever broken, Harth can remake it with five bundles of Wood, one Diamond, and a Swallow Bow. A Swallow Bow can be found on the table next to Harth. If Link tries to take it, Harth will start to scold him. When Link apologizes, Harth decides to let him keep it. Swallow Bows are made of wood, and they will therefore burn if they are exposed to Fire or equipped in a Scorching Climate. They will also float if they are dropped in Water, and they will not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms. Finally, Swallow Bows cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Swallow Bows reappear in . Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Swift Carrots are one of three foodstuffs favored by the Sheikah race, with the others being Fortified Pumpkins and Mighty Bananas. They are primarily and exclusively cultivated by the Sheikah farmer Steen, who grows 14 in his field in Kakariko Village, and has 12 stocked at his wife Trissa's shop, suggesting he keeps two of each batch to eat himself. They may also be found at the foot of Satori Mountain, or behind the Horses at the Highland Stable. Beedle sells them at the East Akkala Stable, as will the Merchant Giro. Some may also be purchased from Cambo as he leaves Kakariko Village, implying he bought some from Trissa, however this does not reduce her stock. Eating Swift Carrots raw will heal Link for half of a Hearts. Swift Carrots can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to create Orange Dye. Burning a Swift Carrot with Fire will turn it into a Roasted Swift Carrot. When cooked in a dish, the resulting food provides Link with temporarily superior speed. The Side Quest "Koko's Kitchen" requires Link to gather a Swift Carrot for Koko so she can make hasty Veggie Cream Soup. As a reward for delivery, Koko will give Link some of the soup she makes. According to Steen's grandfather, Link exclusively ate and trained with Swift Carrots. Swift Carrots and Endura Carrots can be used interchangeably when Cooking. In some cases, they can also be replaced by Pumpkins. They are required for the following Meals: Like other Vegetables, Swift Carrots can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Ten Swift Carrots are needed to upgrade both the Sand Boots and Snow Boots to their second tier at a Great Fairy Fountain. is a recurring hidden Added Effect in . Overview Swim Up Waterfalls is an Added Effect found on the Zora Armor that allows Link to climb up Waterfalls when Swimming near their base by pressing A. Upon reaching the top of the Waterfall, Link will launch up into the air and automatically open the Paraglider. Link's Stamina will immediately begin regenerating as soon as he starts swimming up a Waterfall. When A is pressed to begin climbing a Waterfall in , Link will dash to a set point at the base of the Waterfall and begin Swimming straight up. During the climb, Link will be unable to move sideways nor end the climb early, except by unequipping the Zora Armor. In , Link can begin climbing a Waterfall from anywhere at its base, or from midair by moving through it while wearing the Zora Armor. He also now has the ability to freely strafe sideways while Swimming up a Waterfall, and he can jump backwards out of the Waterfall at any time. If Link has not obtained the Paraglider, then he will begin falling straight down after launching above the Waterfall. Link can use Swim Up Waterfalls to exit the Ancient Zora Waterworks and Lake Hylia Whirlpool Cave via the Waterfall at their entrances. When doing so, there will be a short fade to black, followed by Link launching abnormally high above the Whirlpools.

, also known as , and , are recurring Items in . Location and Uses First appearing in , the Sword can be obtained in a Cave in the very first area of the game. Inside, Link finds an Old Man who tells him to take the Sword because it is dangerous to travel alone. The Sword has two additional color variants which appear when Link wears either the Blue Ring or the Red Ring. The Sword can damage almost every enemy, but it is one of the weakest items in the game. However, the Sword can be replaced by the White Sword and then the Magical Sword, which each deals twice the damage of its predecessor. A Sword that is designed like a is depicted on the Title Display of the game. It is not confirmed to be any of the Swords that can be obtained in the game. The Fighter's Sword is given to Link by his Uncle along with the Fighter's Shield as he enters Hyrule Castle. Link uses the Fighter's Sword until he obtains the Master Sword. During the credits, Link's Uncle is shown using the Fighter's Sword again. The Sword in is the first Sword that Link can obtain. It is from Link's previous adventures and has his name engraved on it. Link finds it on Toronbo Shores shortly after waking up after his crash on Koholint Island. By bringing 20 Secret Seashells to the Seashell Mansion, Link can replace it with the Level 2 Sword. By holding his Sword out, Link can move while he keeps facing the same direction. If Link then releases his Sword, he will perform a Whirling Blade attack, which deals more damage than a regular Sword blow. Link can also hit walls with his Sword to determine whether or not they can be destroyed using Bombs. and The Sword in is the Sword used by the Links. It changes appearance when certain Outfits are worn, such as the Sword Suit, the Sword Master Suit, the Dapper Spinner, the Hero's Tunic, Ninja Gi, the Spin Attack Attire and the Tri Suit. While wearing the Fierce Deity Armor, the Sword becomes the Fierce Deity Sword. In addition, the Sword becomes a Telescope while wearing Linebeck's Uniform, and a parasol while wearing the Lady's Ensemble. Its appearance resembles its design throughout the artwork of . Being made of metal, the Sword will conduct Electricity attract Lightning during Thunderstorms. It will sink if it is dropped in Water, but it can be picked up again and manipulated using the Magnesis Rune. It is also unable to burn when exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. is a recurring character in . Biography Symin is the assistant of Purah, the director of Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. When first approached, Symin offers Link a greeting and fawns over the shelves of research tomes in the Lab's possession. The assistant begins to wonder at the exact amount of books on hand, but is distracted by the sight of Link's Sheikah Slate. He requests to see the Runes on the Slate, which Link readily does. Although he examines all of the runes, he notes that Link appears to be missing some. After a moment, he realizes that he has not given Link his name and properly introduces himself. Before Link is able to return the favor, Symin correctly guesses his name. He explains that Impa informed him about Link ahead of time. Symin remembers that he must tell Link something important and turns to get Purah's attention. Link will ask Symin to clarify and the man realizes that he has not yet introduced Purah to him, motioning to the little girl in the room. He respects Purah greatly. He begins to explain the director's appearance, but realizes that maybe Purah should be the one to do so. Link can then ask Symin about either the Sheikah Slate or the Lab itself. Bringing up the Slate allows Symin to explain its history. He expresses his pleasure with the knowledge that Link will use it properly, knowing the results would be disastrous in the wrong hands. Asking about the Lab pushes Symin to excitedly explain the purpose of the building. Eventually, Symin realizes that he is likely boring Link with his speech. He decides to put his words in a way that expresses the usefulness of their research plainly by giving the possibility of Calamity Ganon's full sealing. Wares and Pricing Symin is now the teacher of the Hateno School. He was recruited by Zelda because of his experience dealing with children from being Purah's assistant. He gives Link the "Teach Me a Lesson I" and "Teach Me a Lesson II" Side Quests.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Tabahl Woods are a dense forest of Cedar Trees within the Lanayru Great Spring. The path to Zora's Domain snakes along their northern end before cutting through their center. The Tabahl Woods also feature several rocky areas, in which Ore Deposits are located. They are just north of the Zodobon Highlands, and the Bank of Wishes can be found on their eastern shore. The Zora River also curves around the eastern and northern borders of the Woods. Prior to Divine Beast Vah Ruta being calmed, its Rain will constantly fall on the Tabahl Woods. On the west side of the Tabahl Woods, a Black Hinox can be found asleep. It will initially be asleep, but if Link approaches it, it will wake up and begin to attack him. In addition to this, three Monster Strongholds are located within the Tabahl Woods. The first is located along the road on the north side of the Woods, and it contains many metal crates and Wooden Boxes. The second is located near the hill on the Woods eastern side, and it protects a cave with a Campfire and Roasted Basses. An abandoned Cooking Pot can also be found in another cave nearby. The final Stronghold is west of the Bank of Wishes, and when it is cleared, a Treasure Chest containing a Sapphire can be opened. Several other Treasure Chests are located in the Tabahl Woods. Two are found in the first Monster Stronghold along the road, containing a Purple Rupee and a Soldier's Bow. The hill on the west side of the Woods bears a cave, though its entrance is blocked by thorns. If Link burns the thorns with Fire, he will be able to access the stone Chest inside, which contains a Throwing Spear. left|40px A total of three Korok Seed Puzzles can be found in the Tabahl Woods. The first is a Circle in the pond on the south end of the Woods, which Link must throw a Rock into. The second is on the hill on their western edge, taking the form of a metal Boulder chained to a well. To solve it, Link must use the Magnesis Rune to place the Boulder into the well. The final Puzzle is a Rock to the north of the Black Hinox, which is revealed to be a Natural Hiding Spot when picked up. When each of these Korok Seed Puzzles are solved, a Korok will appear and give Link a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

The is a recurring location in . The Tabahl Woods Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Tabahl Woods Well is a stout stone Well that has no roof. It is located in the Tabahl Woods on an outcropping near Zora River, and it is part of the Lanayru Great Spring. An Iron is chained to the base of the Well. Korok Seeds The Tabahl Woods Well reappears in , and it is still situated within the Tabahl Woods in the Lanayru Great Spring. The Well's interior consists of two separate chambers. The first only features a small pool of Water. Along its western wall is a Boulder, which Link can move with Ultrahand to reveal the second chamber's entrance. This chamber is illuminated by a potted Brightbloom, and it contains two Barrels and a Cooking Pot with an unlit Campfire beneath it. There is also a Note on the Table nearby written by Aurie Taamu, wherein he recounts his failure to Cook with a Soldier Construct Horn that he received. Creatures Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Tabantha Bridge Stable is a Stable located on the eastern side of the Tabantha Great Bridge in Hyrule Ridge. It marks the southern end of the Hilltop High Road. The Shae Loya Shrine is just south of the Stable, providing a convenient Travel Gate to the Stable when activated. A Cooking Pot can be found to the right of the Stable entrance near another cluster of crates. The Stable features a single livestock pen, which is built around a Dragon's Blood Tree. Inside the Stable is a poster depicting a Recipe for a Hasty Elixir. Tabantha Bridge Stable is owned by Dabi, who manages both its Horse-boarding services and Inn. Banji, Chork, and Geggle are all employed as workers. The children Ena, Kenyo, and Sho live at the Stable. Throughout the day, Banji and Ena tend to the White Goats, inspects the Stable's cargo, and feeds the Horses. Beedle can be found outside Tabantha Bridge Stable, where he will sell his wares. The Merchant Yammo also stops by the Stable with her Donkey. The travelers Baddek, Nazbi, his Horse Dauntless, and Savelle all rest at the Stable as part of their journeys. If Link has completed the "Find the Fairy Fountain" Main Quest, Pikango can be found at Tabantha Bridge Stable during the "Captured Memories" Main Quest. When spoken to, he is able to identify the setting of the third Picture in Link's Album, which depicts the Ancient Columns. When staying at Tabantha Bridge Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Dabi explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Dabi offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Dabi will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Dabi will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. During the day, Geggle stands on the cliff near Shae Loya Shrine, looking out at a mural in the Gerudo Highlands. When Link asks what he is looking at, Geggle notes that the cliffs appear to be man-made. After speaking to him, the "Cliffside Etchings" Shrine Quest will begin. Toren, a resident of Tabantha Bridge Stable, has come in search of the Great Fairy Kaysa. He has heard that Tabantha Tower points towards Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain in the afternoon, but he has stopped at the Stable due to being unable to Climb the Sheikah Tower. As part of the "A Gift for the Great Fairy" Side Quest, Toren asks Link to make his offering to Kaysa on his behalf. If Link accepts, Toren gives him 500 Rupees, which are the entirety of his life savings. After Kaysa's Great Fairy Fountain is opened, Toren does not give Link a reward, believing

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Tabantha Bridge Stable Well is located behind Tabantha Bridge Stable on Hyrule Ridge. Link can enter its interior via the Ladder along its rim. Underground, the Well features four chambers. The first is a room with a pool of Water. The second is a room filled by a Bottomless Bog, and it also contains two Boards that Link can manipulate with Ultrahand to cross the Big. The third is a room with an unlit Campfire, and the final room contains a Treasure Chest. The entrances to the second and fourth chambers are initially blocked by Boulders, though Link can move them out of the way using Ultrahand. The Tabantha Bridge Stable Well is one of several Wells that Fera can be found in prior to beginning the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?". She rates the Well's Water quality as fair and its moss growth as extensive, in addition to confirming the presence of Brightcaps. Once her Side Quest has started, she leaves for the Lookout Landing Well. Creatures Materials Treasure Chests

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Tabantha Great Bridge spans the southern end of the Tanagar Canyon between Hyrule Ridge and the Tabantha Frontier. Due to the Wind from the Canyon, the Bridge has become worn, resulting in many holes and gaps throughout its structure. The remains of colorful flags cling to its railings. Tabantha Bridge Stable, which is located to the east of the Tabantha Great Bridge, is named after it. At 1:30 AM, Dinraal will fly beneath the Tabantha Great Bridge, creating an Updraft as she does so. Creatures Korok Seeds Other Appearances As part of the "Great Bridge Repairs" Quest, Merchants have become fearful of crossing the Tabantha Great Bridge due to it falling into disrepair. After providing 20 Raw Bird Drumsticks, 20 Sanke Carps, 35 Moblin Fangs, 20 Moblin Trophies, and one Stone Talus Trophy, repairs to the Bridge will be completed, allowing Merchants to transport their goods across it.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Tabantha Tundra is a vast snowy expanse covering a large portion of eastern Hebra Mountains, lying between the Pikida Stonegrove and the Tabantha Frontier in the west and Mount Drena in the east. The Tanagar Canyon and the roof of the Forgotten Temple is at the bottom of the cliff along the Tundra's southern edge and a bottomless chasm passes along the northern edge. A road between the Hebra Tower and the Great Hyrule Forest runs through the southern portion of the Tundra, passing the Snowfield Stable. The Tundra is extremely cold, requiring two layers of Cold Resistance at all times. Cold-Footed Wolves, Great-Horned Rhinoceros, and Tabantha Moose inhabit the Tundra throughout. The is a recurring location in . The Tabantha Village Ruins Well goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Tabantha Village Ruins Well is a stout stone Well located amidst the Tabantha Village Ruins on the Tabantha Frontier. It has no roof, and an Iron is chained to its base. The Well is located within a Freezing Climate, and Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance to visit it without taking damage. Prior to the Great Calamity, which occurred 100 before the events of , it was part of the original Tabantha Village. Korok Seeds The Tabantha Village Ruins Well returns in , and it is still located on the Tabantha Frontier. The Well's interior is now able to be entered, where Link can find a small cavern with thin patches of Ice on the floor. Three Icicles also hang from the ceiling, though they can be broken off by attacking them. The Ice patches can be melted or shattered to reveal additional sections of the Well's interior. The southern patch gives way to a chamber with two Bokoblins and a Treasure Chest frozen in Ice, as well as a Cooking Pot with an unlit Campfire beneath it. The northern patch leads to a chamber with two Ore Deposits and one Rare Ore Deposit. Both the Well and its underground chamber are part of a Freezing Climate, which Link requires at least one level of Cold Resistance to traverse without taking damage. Tadarok Shrine, designated by the trial name Fire and Water, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine Tadarok Shrine can be found at the end of the River of the Dead Waterfall Cave on the Great Plateau. It corresponds with the Koradat Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation thumb|center|320px|alt= An aerial view of Tadarok Shrine's entrance.|The interior of Tadarok Shrine Tadarok Shrine opens into a cubic chamber that holds a single Stone Box. There is a hallway with a small pool of Water opposite the entrance. Two Electricity Generators connected to Iron Balls via Chains sit at the edge of the pool while the Iron Balls sit underwater, carrying the Electricity into it. In order to bypass this Electricity, Link must either carry the nearby Stone Box into the Water to create a bridge, or pull the Iron Balls out and away from the Water to neutralize it. The hallway opens into a larger chamber with several features. To the left, there is a dispenser that releases Blocks of Ice. However, Flame Fountains mounted on the nearby wall quickly melt the Blocks. To save the Ice, Link can quickly pull the Ice away from the Fire, or intercept the flames by placing the Stone Block from the previous room between the Ice and the Flame Fountains. A Stone Chest sits atop a ledge in the corner opposite the Ice dispenser. Directly opposite the pool is a second pool at the bottom of an open chute. A third Electricity Generator sits at the base of this pool with its own Iron Ball connected via a Chain, electrifying the Water. A large Iron Box sits in the center of this pool, which Link can retrieve from the pool. As before, the Iron Ball can be moved out of the Water to neutralize it. To the right of the pool of Water, there is a pool of Lava. By placing the Stone and Iron Boxes into the Lava, Link can create a step-stone bridge to cross the Lava and reach a side chamber. In the side chamber, a second dispenser repeatedly drops large Wooden Boxes into the path of more Flame Fountains. This dispenser will not release any more Wooden Boxes if the Flame Fountains are blocked. Instead, Link must grab a Wooden Box after it has been set alight and carry it to a pool of Water across the floor before it burns away. After dousing the Wooden Box, Link can carry it over the pool of Lava to the central chamber. By attaching the various cubic Objects with Ultrahand, Link can create a makeshift bridge to rise through the open chute with Ascend. If Link has not moved the Iron Ball out of the Water at the bottom of the chute, he can place the Wooden Box in the pool as it will not conduct Electricity. As long as Link does not place the Wooden Box or the Ice in the way of the Flame Fountains

not moved the Iron Ball out of the Water at the bottom of the chute, he can place the Wooden Box in the pool as it will not conduct Electricity. As long as Link does not place the Wooden Box or the Ice in the way of the Flame Fountains along the wall of the chute, he can rise to reach the end of the Shrine. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Tadarok Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Enemies Treasure Chests

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Tal Tal Peak is located on the northeastern edge of the Lanayru Great Spring. It borders Southern Tal Tal Peak, which is a valley found along the side of East Reservoir Lake. Two Waterfalls flow from Tal Tal Peak. One ends in a pond on Southern Tal Tal Peak, while the other settles in the Akkala Highlands. Prior to calming Divine Beast Vah Ruta, Tal Tal Peak will be constantly under the effect of its Rain. A Monster Stronghold can be found on the north side of Tal Tal Peak. Once Link defeats all of the Enemy|Enemies in the Stronghold, he will be able to open the Outpost Chest inside, which contains a Silver Rupee. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles are located on Tal Tal Peak. The first is a Boulder on one side of the northern Waterfall, which Link must push into a hole on the other side. The second is a Flower Trail that starts on the western side of the Peak, eventually ending at its very top. When Link solves each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. is a recurring character in . Biography Tali is the Gerudo Sand-Seal Racing champion who is coached by Shabonne. She can be found with Shabonne at the Sand-Seal Rally in the Gerudo Desert. Tali never speaks while Link is talking to Shabonne. If Link speaks to Tali, Shabonne apologizes to Link because Tali is not in the mood for autographs. If Link asks what happened, Shabonne explains that the Sand-Seal Race course is unusable with the Divine Beast Vah Naboris stomping around. If Link asks who Tali is, Shabonne is in disbelief that Link does not know the Sand-Seal Racing champion and says that Tali could demonstrate her skills if it were not for the Divine Beast. When Link returns to the Sand-Seal Rally after calming Naboris, the Sand-Seal Race will be open again. Link can speak to Shabonne or Tali to begin the Shrine Quest, "The Undefeated Champ". Shabonne tells Link that if he can beat Tali's record of 1:30, he can have a trophy. The trophy that Shabonne refers to is the nearby Ancient Orb needed to reveal the Ancient Shrine, which has been passed down by ten thousand years of Sand-Seal Racing champions. Shabonne charges Link 50 Rupees to race against Tali's record. When Link beats Tali's record, she will finally speak and congratulate Link by presenting him with the grand trophy. Tali explains the legend behind the trophy to Link, which tells that the chosen one will be granted a new power when the trophy is offered unto the pedestal. After encouraging Link to place the orb into the pedestal, the Raqa Zunzo Shrine rises from the ground and the Shrine Quest is completed.

The Talonto Peak is a steep incline with a few small ledges leading up to the summit. At the top of the peak, a single Tree sprouts into the air, and a small ledge juts out over the side of the mountain. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Tama Pond is located east of Rito Village and west of Hebra Tower in the Tabantha Frontier. It is a small oval-shaped pond with a flat rocky terrain on the north side, and a small cliff on the southern side. Creatures Korok Seeds Tama Pond is a small body of Water located south of the Hebra Plunge in Tabantha Frontier. It is located on a small, Snow-covered plateau with Rocks and Fallen Debris on it, with a cliff bordering its southeast side. The Pond is stocked with Hearty Salmons and Trout. is a recurring character in . Biography Tamana is a timid, slightly forgetful woman who tends to a small Cucco farm in Hateno Village. Should Link approach her, she panics and threatens to call someone to remove him for trespassing. However, she is quick to apologize for her rash behavior, as she can see that Link is not a threatening person. She realizes that she is talking randomly and mentions that her husband dislikes this habit. Tamana finally brings herself to simply ask Link to leave, giving him a Bird Egg as an apology for her words. If Link hangs around to speak to her further, she is not sure if she asked him to leave. Should Link admit that she did, she wonders why. However, if Link says he does not believe she did, she becomes confused. Tamana then admits that she is often dropping eggs, despite having been on the farm for a few years. In a joking mood, Tamana decides to reward Link with another Bird Egg for "correctly guessing" that she is clumsy. She then pauses, wondering if she was the one to answer the question. Link admits that she did and she tells him the benefits of using the egg in recipes. She then realizes that she gave the Bird Egg away instead of taking it to the East Wind for sale, which happens frequently. Although she admits that she does not like to sell the eggs, she knows her husband would never agree. Link can keep trying to speak to her, but Tamana wonders if he has somewhere else to be. Tamana can be found still living in Hateno Village, while her husband, Thadd, has gone to Lookout Landing. She leaves her Cucco farm at 5:00 PM to keep watch at the Hateno gate at night, sweeping the path. If Link approaches her at night, she will initially startle before noting how handsome she finds Link. She gives him one of her Bird Eggs, but immediately tells him to forget everything that happened. Tamana is relieved of watch duty at 6:30 AM by her son, Teebo, after which, she returns to her Cucco farm.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Tamio River is located between Hyrule Ridge and the Tabantha Frontier, and it is surrounded by sheer cliffs on all sides. It branches due west from Regencia River past the West Hyrule Plains, passing under Jeddo Bridge. A Dock sticks out into the River north of Satori Mountain,, at the end of which is a Raft. South of Washa's Bluff, a small campsite with a Cooking Pot, Wooden Boxes, and Iron Boxes can be found on one of the River's beaches, and a nearby path leads up the cliffs. Tamio River sharply turns south after passing Washa's Bluff, where it ends not long after. Several small beaches are located along its edges. The Canyon also reaches the edges of the Great Hyrule Forest, Hyrule Field, and the Tabantha Tundra. It is spanned by the Tabantha Great Bridge on its southern end, where many windmills can be found. The Tanagar Canyon Course and the Forgotten Temple can both be found within Tanagar Canyon. The Dunba Taag Shrine is also within a crag near the Canyon's center. Lastly, many Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits can be found along the Canyon's walls. Every night, Dinraal will fly through Tanagar Canyon. This causes Winds and Updrafts to appear surrounding it. left|40px In total, 20 Korok Seed Puzzles are located within and on the walls of the Tanagar Canyon. The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Taobab Grassland is a savanna located in the Gerudo Highlands. It sits south of the Great Plateau and north of the Oseira Plains. The Taobab Grassland boasts several Trees, which are unique to the valley containing the Taobab Grassland, Oseira Plains, and the Nautelle Wetlands. The Taobab Grassland is the only location that Link can find the Giant Horse, which is necessary for completing the "Hunt for the Giant Horse" Side Quest. If Link speaks to Straia at the Mounted Archery Camp, he will direct Link to the Taobab Grassland and ask for its capture and retrieval for study. A Korok can be found by destroying a clay Jar dangling from a chain on a Tree's branch. A second Korok can be found by popping the Balloon at the top of a Tree in the southern reaches of the Grassland. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Tarrey Town is a settlement in the Akkala Highlands started by Bolson Construction. The site of Tarrey Town is initially an uninhabited, circular rock island in the northern section of Lake Akkala. Only a Goddess Statue sits near the center of the island, at which Link can trade Spirit Orbs for Heart Containers or Stamina Vessels. When Tarrey Town is complete, it contains six Houses, all built in Bolson Construction's signature style of brightly-colorful cubic modules arranged and stacked to create different shapes of homes. All Houses ring the central square in a hexagonal arrangement similarly to a cul-de-sac, with the backs of each house against the outer edge of the island. The center of the square has a fountain and the Goddess Statue is moved to the fountain's centerpiece. The Unity Bell is also part of the fountain. One of these Houses serves as an Inn for travelers, which remains unnamed. When Link initially comes upon the site, Hudson reveals his plans to build a village named Tarrey Town. However, with only a House built to store the supplies, Hudson feels there is not enough in the Town. As part of the Side Quest "From the Ground Up", Link will gather bundles of Wood for Hudson so he can construct more Houses. He also asks Link to help him recruit employees to work and manage Shops in the Town, including a Goron miner, a Gerudo tailor, and a Rito trader. Due to Bolson Construction's policy, all new employees must have names that end with "-son". After Hudson receives all the Wood he needs for building, he confesses that he has gotten engaged to the Gerudo tailor, Rhondson. For the ceremony, he asks that Link try to find a priest for them among the Zora. He also requests that Link invite Bolson and Karson of Bolson Construction on his behalf. Once all the guests have been gathered, the ceremony will take place in front of Tarrey Town's Goddess Statue. Kapson presides over Hudson and Rhondson's wedding ceremony. He starts by asking Hudson if he will take Rhondson as his wife, which he accepts. Next, he asks the same question of Rhondson, with an additional vow to name their children in accordance with Bolson Construction policies. Though Rhondson initially objects to its inclusion, she eventually agrees to abide by the guidelines. Kapson then declares Hudson and Rhondson officially married. Following the ceremony, Hudson will give Link three Diamonds as a reward for his help, and "From the Ground Up" will be completed. Throughout "From the Ground Up",Grantéson, Hagie, Hunnie, Moggs, Monari, and Ruli will all move into Tarrey Town. As a result of this, the Side Quests "A Parent's Love" and "Hobbies of the Rich" will become available. Since Grantéson is a Merchant, Link will be able to purchase rare Armor from him. One Treasure Chest can be found in Tarrey Town. By befriending one of the Hylian Retrievers behind Moggs and

of this, the Side Quests "A Parent's Love" and "Hobbies of the Rich" will become available. Since Grantéson is a Merchant, Link will be able to purchase rare Armor from him. One Treasure Chest can be found in Tarrey Town. By befriending one of the Hylian Retrievers behind Moggs and Monari's House, Link will be led to an Metal Chest buried in the ground, which contains a bundle of five Bomb Arrows. The town has grown in the time since , with Hudson's House now also being the main office for Hudson Construction, and the Slippery Falcon (Tarrey Town Branch) having been expanded into a full Shop rather than just a stall. In addition to this, the Hudson Construction Site has also been opened on the Torin Wetland. Areas

is a recurring character in . Biography Tasseren is a Hylian and the owner of the Dueling Peaks Stable in West Necluda. He can be found at the front of Dueling Peaks Stable. Tasseren and his brother Rensa had both competed in the Hyrule Horse-Taming Competition as the only contestants, with Tasseren winning first place. If Dueling Peaks Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Tasseren will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Tasseren explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Tasseren then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Tasseren instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Tasseren suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Tasseren to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Tasseren tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Dueling Peaks Stable, Tasseren will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Tasseren thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Tasseren will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Tasseren asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Dueling Peaks Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Tasseren asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Tasseren will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Tasseren insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Tasseren refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Tasseren starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Tasseren gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link

he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Tasseren gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Tasseren gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside Dueling Peaks Stable, Tasseren once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and Soft Beds for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the Soft Bed a special bed offered by Dueling Peaks Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Tasseren tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Tasseren wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

is a recurring character in . Biography Tauma is a Hylian woman who can be found reading a Book inside Hotel Oasis in Gerudo Town. She has a temper and is obsessed with keeping her skin smooth. If Link speaks to her, she asks if he is also there for the s Spa Plan. Tauma is annoyed by how long she has been waiting for the Spa. Before finishing speaking, she asks Link if he is getting in line. If Link speaks to Tauma again, she questions how long she will have to wait and says that she has read her Book so many times that she could recite the dialogue. Tauma complains that she came there to reclaim her youth, but feels like she only lost more of it waiting there. If Link tells Tauma that he received the Spa Plan when he did not, she knows that he is lying and comments that the Gerudo Desert heat has dried his skin. She goes on to explain that Romah's special skills leave people moisturized to perfection and expresses her hatred for lying. Tauma calms herself down in fear that she will create wrinkles between her eyebrows and loudly warns Link not to make her angry. If Link gets the Spa Plan and speaks to Tauma, she will notice and mention that he looks relaxed and that his skin looks shiny.

is a character in . Biography Tauro is an explorer, a researcher, and the leader of the Zonai Survey Team, originally from Lurelin Village in southeast Hyrule. He is very knowledgeable about the Zonai and can even read their language. Tauro is passionate about field research and making big discoveries. He spent a long time traveling solo, investigating ruins, before being selected by Zelda to lead the Zonai Survey Team. Tauro wears a leather vest with pockets, along with a leather hat and gloves. He can be seen with a jacket tied around his waist, just above his shorts. He does not wear a shirt under his vest, exposing his well-defined musculature, including his abs, suggesting that Tauro is strong and physically active. He also wears a feather in his hat, goggles, a necklace, a bracelet, an anklet, and sandals. Tauro is normally holding a magnifying glass to assist with his field research. Tauro inspired Dr. Calip to join the Zonai Survey Team. In his journal, Calip claims that Tauro is able to understand him in a way that others cannot. Calip admires Tauro and is jealous of his ability to focus, recalling that he once examined a Ring Ruins Stone Slab for an entire night. Calip transcribes a lesson from Tauro, who stated that a researcher should make as many discoveries in their lifetime as possible, regardless of whether or not their receive recognition for their achievements. After being chosen to lead the Zonai Survey Team, Tauro visits Kakariko Village, now led by Chief Paya, to study the Ring Ruins. Phantom Ganon, posing as Princess Zelda, ordered Paya and Tauro to stop their research on the Floating Ring Ruin. In Kakariko Village, Link can find Tauro in three different locations, depending on weather and the time of day. Between 12:00 AM and 10:00 AM, Tauro will be located at the top of the cliff near the Floating Ring Ruin. From 10:00 AM to 12:00AM, he will be observing the Ruin from the ground. During Rain, he can be found inside the Zonai Survey Team Base. If Link approaches him while not wearing any Armor on his torso, Tauro will ask him if he is feeling bold. The leader of the Zonai Survey Team then sympathises with Link, saying that he would run around in just his "unmentionables" if not for the decorum required in his field and around Paya. He adds that he would not bother so much with his outfit otherwise. After this, Tauro declares that he is glad to have found a kindred spirit in Link. When Link tells Tauro and Paya that the Zelda who ordered them to stop was actually a Phantom Ganon, they are initially shocked, though Paya recalls that she seemed different than the real Zelda. Tauro decides that they should investigate as soon as possible. Paya permits an excited Tauro to open the Floating Ring Ruin, but he does not know how.
