"" is a Side Quest in . Overview If Link visits the Hateno School during the day, he will find Symin preparing to teach his students a lesson about the Great Calamity. At the start of the lesson, he explains that several Great Calamities have occurred throughout the history of Hyrule, and 10,000 years ago, it was sealed away by a princess and the Ancient Hero. Aster interjects, claiming that this story is a fairy tale. Azu agrees, staring that legend is often blurred with history over time. Karin also wonders what the significance of events 10,000 years in the past could be. Lastly, Sefaro asks for proof of a Great Calamity from 10,000 years ago. Symin attempts to convince the students that a Great Calamity happened 10,000 years ago, but he realizes that he will need to find proof in order to do so. He claims that he should have had the foresight to borrow the Screen of the Ancient Hero from Impa's House, but it is too far for him to ask for it now. He believes that by seeing the Screen, his students would be able to conceptualize the Great Calamity. Following their conversation, "Teach Me a Lesson I" will begin. The Screen of the Ancient Hero can be found in Paya's Room on the second floor of Impa's House. Using the Purah Pad's Camera, Link can take a Picture of the Screen. Upon showing the Picture to Symin, he tells his class to look at it for themselves. Aster is impressed by how real it looks, while Azu is shocked that the legend was true. Seeing the Screen makes Karin feel as though it happened yesterday. Sefaro considers the Screen to be enough proof that the Great Calamity actually happened, and he urges Symin to tell them more. Before moving on with the lesson, Symin thanks Link and asks if he is willing to sit in on his lecture. If Link agrees to listen, Symin explains that Calamity Ganon was sealed away due to the efforts of the Divine Beasts and the ancient princess, the Ancient Hero was capable of defeating the Calamity and bringing peace to Hyrule. When Symin implies that Calamity Ganon yet again returned, Karin demands to know more. Symin reveals that 100 years ago, a Fortune Teller predicted that Calamity Ganon would return, and when the Divine Beasts were excavated, four Champions were selected as their pilots. Despite having both Princess Zelda and the hero Link, Hyrule was still threatened by Calamity Ganon, Sefaro asks if something happened. Symin reveals that Zelda was unable to awaken her sealing powers until after the Divine Beasts were overtaken and Link was injured, at which point she sacrificed herself to seal Calamity Ganon away for 100 years. Checking that his students are following along, Symin reveals that Link awoke from his Slumber of Restoration after 100 years, and from there, he reclaimed the Divine Beasts and helped Zelda seal Calamity Ganon. After finishing his story,

point she sacrificed herself to seal Calamity Ganon away for 100 years. Checking that his students are following along, Symin reveals that Link awoke from his Slumber of Restoration after 100 years, and from there, he reclaimed the Divine Beasts and helped Zelda seal Calamity Ganon. After finishing his story, Symin apologizes for becoming emotional, though he asserts that it truly happened. Standing from her chair, Aster realizes that they owe their lives to those who have fought against Calamity Ganon. Azu proclaims that he wants to be like the Ancient Hero. With his lesson completed, Symin is relieved to have successfully taught his students. He once again thanks Link for bringing him the Picture, giving him 10 stalks of Hylian Rice as a reward. Symin claims that the development of new vegetables in Hateno Village have lead to Hylian Rice being farmed less, which he is disappointed by. He quietly adds that his next lesson is on home economics and involves Hylian Rice dishes. Afterwards, "Teach Me a Lesson I" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview Following Symin's lecture on the Great Calamity, he decides to teach his students about Hylian Rice dishes. He invites Link to listen in on the lesson if he is interested. Symin starts his lecture by introducing home economics, claiming that Food is essential for survival. He then asks what will happen if Goron Spice, Hylian Rice, and Raw Meat are Cooked together. Azu clarifies that Goron Spice is the hot seasoning sold in Goron City. Karin correctly identifies that the result would be a type of curry, and Aster and Sefaro deduce it must be Meat Curry. Since his students were able to correctly guess the answer, Symin instead asks what can be made by Cooking Goron Spice, Hylian Rice, and Monster Extract together. Azu is confused by Monster Extract, and Karin and Aster recall that unless used for medicine, Cooking with Monster Parts is not possible. Sefaro believes that Symin is trying to give them a trick question. Symin tells the class to calm down, though he acknowledges that his lesson might be too advanced. He informs the students that the result of this Recipe would be Monster Curry, but he realizes that they will not believe him unless they see it. Unfortunately, he does not have any Monster Extract to make Monster Curry, especially since it can only be found in Tarrey Town to the north. After this, "Teach Me a Lesson II" will begin. Using a Cooking Pot, Link can Cook a serving of Monster Curry. When Link sits in on the next lesson, Symin is able to smell it from his Inventory. If Link agrees to share his Monster Curry, Symin invites the class to come sample it. Despite their concerns, the students find that Monster Curry is actually delicious. Symin assures his class that while Monster Parts can usually only be used when making medicine, Monster Extract can be used to make meals. Symin is relieved that his students finally understand what he was trying to teach them. He thanks Link for his assistance, claiming that this lesson has lead the children to mature. Aster tells Link that he made their history lesson fun, and Azu claims that his Monster Curry tasted great. Karin declares that she already thinks of Link as her teacher. Lastly, Sefaro states that he cannot wait for their next lesson. Due to Link's popularity with the students, Symin allows him to use the School's Field. Although space is limited, he gives Link permission to plant whatever he would like, and he directs him to speak with Uma to set it up. He quietly informs Link that he is planning a test for his students, and he hopes that he will join their classes again. Afterwards, "Teach Me a Lesson II" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring character in . Biography Teake is a Gerudo who is captain of the soldiers in the barracks in Gerudo Town. If Link speaks to her, she questions what he is doing in the barracks and tells him to leave because they are on high alert due to a recent theft. If Link speaks to her again, she warns him not to make the guards any more tense than they already are. If Link speaks to Teake after speaking to Riju for the first time, she initially tells him again to leave, but apologizes after Link explains that Buliara sent him. She continues to explain that the Thunder Helm was stolen by the Yiga Clan the other day and that the Yiga Clan Hideout is in Karusa Valley. Teake says that she was just thinking about requesting extra help and then proceeds to inform the soldiers to tell Link any information. Teake then tells Link to consider himself part of their unit. If Link speaks to Teake after recovering the Thunder Helm, she compliments Link's combat abilities and asks if he will join the Gerudo forces. If Link accepts her offer, she laughs, but says that she knows he is on an important quest. If Link passes on the offer, Teake is disappointed but understands because of the important quest that Link is on. Either way, Teake encourages Link to reconsider his answer after his quest.

is a recurring location in . Teba's Home goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Teba's Home is located near the top of Rito Village, right next door to Kaneli's House. It overlooks Revali's Landing as well. It houses Teba, Saki, and their son, Tulin. After Link starts the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, he will have to seek out Saki to learn the location of Teba. He can find her in Teba's Home, from where she was able to overhear his conversation with Kaneli. She informs Link that Teba left for the Flight Range. She points out Revali's Landing to him, explaining that he can get to the Flight Range from there. Saki explains that it is a memorial for the Champion Revali, which triggers the "Revali's Flap" Recovered Memory. After Link has calmed Divine Beast Vah Medoh, he will be able to find Teba, Saki, and Tulin in their Home. Saki and Tulin are both grateful to have Teba home safe and sound. Teba has promised to take Tulin flying as soon as he has healed from his injures. When Downloadable Content Pack is active, The Diary of Revali will appear inside Teba's Home. According to Kaneli, he entrusted it to Teba since he admires Revali. Teba then decided that it would be safest in his Home.

Teba is a recurring character in . Biography Teba is the most skilled Rito warrior in Rito Village. He resides in his Home with his wife Saki and his son Tulin. Teba is known to be prideful to the point of recklessness, and Saki describes him as impulsive. Like other Rito warriors, Teba idolizes Revali, and he wishes for Tulin to become a great warrior as well. Growing up, Teba was childhood friends with Harth. Since Tulin is close in age with Harth's daughter, Molli, their families have remained close. Teba was also mentored by Kaneli while training to become a Rito warrior. When Divine Beast Vah Medoh reactivated and began circling Rito Village, Teba and Harth went to face it, ignoring Kaneli's warnings. This resulted in Harth becoming injured, though Teba remained unscathed. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Teba repairing a Falcon Bow at the Flight Range. Text on-screen displays his name, along with the title "Rito Warrior".|Teba's introduction When Link speaks to Saki during the "Divine Beast Vah Medoh" Main Quest, she reveals that Teba is absent from the Village, as he is preparing for another attack on Vah Medoh at the Flight Range. At the Flight Range, Link can find Teba working on a Falcon Bow. He turns to face Link when he senses his approach. Realizing he does not know Link, Teba tells him to leave since he is busy. Upon speaking to Teba, he reiterates that he is busy and asks Link if he needs something. If Link claims that he can help him, Teba initially does not know what he is talking about. When Link clarifies that he can calm Divine Beast Vah Medoh, Teba is skeptical that of his story, and he asks Link for his name. After they introduce themselves to each other, Teba voices his suspicions that Kaneli had Link come to talk him out of facing Vah Medoh. When Link confirms this, Teba is annoyed, but asserts that he will not return to Rito Village until he defeats the Divine Beast. After Link reasserts his desire to help, Teba states that he is in no position to talk him out of it. He recalls Kaneli saying that the only way to stop Divine Beast Vah Medoh would be to enter it, which he believes to be impossible. Though Link tries to tell him that he is capable of doing so, Teba does not believe him, since only the Champions would be capable of entering a Divine Beast. Teba decides to instead focus on fighting Divine Beast Vah Medoh. He explains that if they approach the Divine Beast without a plan, they will be shot down by its Cannons.< Therefore, he wants to test Link's skills before they attempt their assault. To do so, Link must use the Flight Range's Updrafts to destroy five Targets within three minutes. If Link asks for a tip, Teba explains that using a Bow in midair is the same as using it on the ground. He

is a recurring gameplay mechanic in . Overview Temperature is briefly used within the Death Mountain Crater and sections of the Fire Temple to hinder Link's progression. When exposed to the Scorching Climate, a timer will appear and will cause Link to die unless he is revived by a Fairy. However, this can be prevented by wearing the Goron Tunic, allowing Link to stay cool indefinitely and survive the scorching heat. The amount of time Link has is eight seconds for every Heart in his Life Gauge when the timer appears. Link is incapable of entering places with high Temperatures like the Volcano Summit, but this time Link is slowly damaged catches fire instead being subjected to a timer. To stay cool when entering areas with high Temperatures, Link must obtain the Fireshield Earrings from Din's Silent Realm trial. Unlike in the previous games, Temperature is now a gameplay mechanic featured everywhere around Hyrule Kingdom, and Link can check the Temperature with a dial on the bottom-right screen or opening his Sheikah Slate and viewing the Map section with actual measurements. When exposed to extreme Temperatures, Link will begin to take damage, but can prevent this by going to a more temperate area, entering bodies of Water in Scorching Climates, equipping an elemental Weapon, wearing certain Armor, or eating Food with status effects. When the Temperature drops below , Link will experience a basic level of cold Temperature that will slowly damage him. When the Temperature drops below , Link will experience an advanced level of cold Temperature and will take damage more quickly. Certain bodies of water in Freezing Climates will cause Link to quickly take damage; no armor, elixir nor food can offer protection against this. Similarly, when the Temperature rises above , Link will experience a basic level of Heat, he will also slowly sustain damage. When the Temperature rises above , Link will experience an advanced level of Heat and take damage more quickly. Places that contain lava flows raise Temperatures significantly beyond normal Heat, the Sheikah Slate will malfunction and read "ERROR". Additionally, Link and any wooden equipment exposed to the environment will begin to catch fire. Temperature is present all throughout Hyrule and the Sky Islands above it. Some locations are too cold for Link to withstand without special Armor or other protective measures.

Features and Overview During the Era of Chaos, a group of powerful sorcerers known as the Dark Interlopers waged a Battle for the Sacred Realm against the people of Hyrule to seize the Triforce. To prevent the abuse of the Triforce, the Golden Goddesses sent the Spirits of Light to banish the Dark Interlopers into the Twilight Realm, a sort of parallel world that exists "behind" the Light World. The Sage of Light, Rauru, also decided to hide the Triforce within the Sacred Realm's Temple of Light. As the only entrance to the Temple of Light was through the ruins of the Sealed Temple, Rauru built a new Temple over the ruins to protect the entrance. thumb|center|The Temple of Time's interior from Inspired by the legends of a hero who wielded the Master Sword and traveled through Time in the distant Sky Era, he chose to borrow the name of the fabled Temple of Time and used the Master Sword to seal the entrance to the Sacred Realm as it could not be touched by evil hands and could only be drawn from the Pedestal of the Master Sword by those deemed worthy. The Master Sword was then sealed behind the Door of Time, which could only be opened with the three Spiritual Stones and the Ocarina of Time. The Kingdom of Hyrule was established by the descendants of the reborn Goddess Hylia to protect the secret of the Triforce's whereabouts, and Hyrule Castle was built close to the Temple of Time in order to keep watch over it. Centuries later during the Era of the Hero of Time, the Gerudo King Ganondorf learned of the existence of the Sacred Realm and pretended to serve the Royal Family of Hyrule in order to discover its entrance. Princess Zelda began to have ominous dreams warning her of Ganondorf's impending betrayal yet also promising a hero would appear in the form of a boy from the Kokiri Forest. When Link appears to her with the Spiritual Stone of the Forest, she recognizes him as the hero from her dreams and tasks him with the responsibility of collecting the Spiritual Stones to keep them out of Ganondorf's hands. However, Ganondorf notices their plan and begins to watch Link. After Link successfully recovers the remaining two Spiritual Stones, Ganondorf attacks and seizes Hyrule Castle, forcing Princess Zelda to flee with the Ocarina of Time. Link and Princess Zelda encounter each other once more as she is fleeing Hyrule Castle Town, where she throws the Ocarina to him in desperation. Taking the three Spiritual Stones and the Ocarina of Time to the Temple of Time, Link opens the Door of Time and draws the Master Sword from its Pedestal. However, because Link has the body of a child, he is not strong enough to wield the Sword, and so the Master Sword casts Link into a deep sleep to allow his body to grow. Ganondorf recognizes this as

Door of Time and draws the Master Sword from its Pedestal. The is a recurring character in . The Temple of Time Statue goes unnamed in . Biography The Temple of Time Statue is a Great Goddess Statue located within the Temple of Time Ruins. It is initially the only Goddess Statue available to Link, as it is the only one that can be found on the Great Plateau. After obtaining four Spirit Orbs, Link is able to exchange them with the Temple of Time Statue for either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. The Temple of Time Statue remains in the Temple of Time Ruins. If Link has four Lights of Blessing, he is able to give them to the Statue for either a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. He can also exchange four Sage's Wills to deepen the bond he has with one of the Sages. Her counterpart, the Great Abandoned Central Mine Bargainer Statue, can be found below her in the Depths. If Link tries to interact with the Temple of Time Statue before draining the entrance to the Great Plateau, the Great Abandoned Central Mine Bargainer Statue will speak through it, claiming to be trapped under the Water. After doing so, Link can encounter a Bargainer Statue, which directs him back to the Temple of Time Ruins. There, the Great Abandoned Central Mine Bargainer Statue speaks through the Temple of Time Statue once again, which starts the "A Call from the Depths" Side Adventure. The voice from the Statue instructs Link to drop its four Eyes into the Chasms across the Great Plateau and deliver them to its body, promising a reward for doing so.
