Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|alt= A screenshot of Teniten Shrine's interior.|The platform inside Teniten Shrine The entrance to Teniten Shrine opens into a spacious room with a raised half-pipe platform. To the left of the entrance is a rack stocked with five Rusty Halberds. When Link approaches the platform, a Training Construct atop it will awaken and a Mysterious Voice will speak to him. The Voice instructs him to throw a Weapon at the Training Construct. The Training Construct will then periodically take shots at Link with its Construct Bow. As the Mysterious Voice warns, only thrown Weapons will have any effect on the Training Construct. Sword Beams from the Master Sword will not affect it, nor will attacks from Bows. Materials thrown at the Training Construct will simply disintegrate, and the lasting effects such as the Fire given off by Fire Fruits will not affect it. When the Training Construct is struck with a thrown Weapon, the Mysterious Voice will congratulate Link and then warn him to watch the Enemy's movements. At this point, the Training Construct will begin moving from side to side atop the platform and continue to shoot at Link. When it is struck by a thrown Weapon for a second time, it will be defeated. The Voice will again speak and instruct Link to advance further into the Shrine as a portcullis near the end of the Shrine lifts. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Teniten Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Enemies Equipment Treasure Chests

The , designated by the trial name Rauru's Blessing, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Tenmaten Shrine is located within the Elma Knolls Well in the Great Hyrule Forest. It corresponds to the Netamnet Lightroot in the Depths. The Well's interior is covered in Darkness, which Link must navigate in order to reach the Shrine of Light. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Tenmaten Shrine The Tenmaten Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Tenmaten Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him. Treasure Chests

is a recurring character in . Biography Tenne is a young female Hylian Stable Worker who can be found tending the hay trough at the South Akkala Stable in the Akkala Highlands, within the Akkala Region of Hyrule. She is the daughter of the stable's manager, Dmitri, while the other stable hands Kaifa, Jana, and Gleema are her sisters. She is one of four female stable hands that allows Link to style the mane and change the equipment of the registered Horse he has currently withdrawn, though only if they have bonded with him completely. However, like the others, she refuses to do this for Epona or the Giant Horse.

Tenoko Island is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Tenoko Island is located in the Necluda Sea. Tenoko Island hosts Chaas Qeta Shrine, where Link can find Climbing Gear. Tenoko Island is also home to a lone Palm Tree bearing Palm Fruit, under which Link can find a Korok Leaf. A Raft can also be found on the eastern side of the Island. On the shores of Tenoko Island, Link may find Hearty Blueshell Snails. Mighty Porgy and Armored Porgy can be found swimming the waters around Tenoko Island. Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment Korok Seeds Materials Treasure Chests Creatures Korok Seeds Materials Zonai Devices

Tent Camps are locations in . Features and Overview Tent Camps are campsites composed of Tents found throughout Hyrule. They are predominately used by the Monster-Control Crew and Zonai Survey Team. There are a set of four campsites established by the Zonai Survey Team in Kakariko Village. Each is associated with one of the Ring Ruins that it is located near. The only exception is the Floating Ring Ruin, which does not have an associated Camp. Every Camp contains at least one Survey-Team Tent. Most of the Tent Camps have a Note on the Table and a Map of the Ring Ruins. The Tent Camp near the Southern Ring Ruin houses Cori, with Lourda visiting while in Kakariko Village. The Southern Ring Ruin Research Journal can also be found here. At the Nestled Ring Ruin, the Tent Camp is inhabited by Drenja. The one at the Large Ring Ruin is utilized by Saguru and Gordi, and the Large Ring Ruin Research Journal, a Ring Ruins Stone Slab, and a volume of Deciphered Slabs are located there as well. Lastly, the Tent Camp near the Eastern Ring Ruin is home to Ebah and Xalis, and the Eastern Ring Ruin Research Journal can be found there as well. List of Tent Camps

The Tent Camp of Central Square is a location in . Features and Overview The Tent Camp of Central Square is a Tent Camp for the Monster-Control Crew that wraps around the northern and eastern sides of the Central Square. It is stocked with five Tents, three Weapon racks, one Wagon, and three covered supply stations. The eastern side of the Camp hosts an unlit Cooking Pot while a lit Campfire sits outside the northern Tent. Despite its size, the Tent Camp is uninhabited. A Note on the Table authored by Hoz can be found beside the Campfire. It describes Purah's orders to the Monster-Control Crew to search for Zelda in the wake of the Upheaval, which has caused Hyrule Castle to float in the Sky. After Link reports Zelda's sighting to Purah as part of the "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" Main Quest, the entire Camp and its contents permanently disappear. Creatures Equipment Materials

The Tent Camp of the First Gatehouse is a location in . Features and Overview The Tent Camp of the First Gatehouse is a Tent Camp for the Monster-Control Crew that sits inside the Gatehouse. It serves as Hoz's base of operations as he searches Hyrule Castle for Zelda after her disappearance during the Upheaval. It contains two Tents and four Beds. A lit Cooking Pot sits between two Beds, beside a covered supply station. Two Wooden Boxes containing supplies sit on the northern side of the Camp. Purpen can be found in the Camp standing in front of a Weapon rack, surveying the Gloom damage to their Equipment rendering them all as Decayed Weapons. The remaining members of Captain Hoz's Monster-Control Crew, Squad One can be found in the surrounding area on the grounds of Hyrule Castle. After Link reports Zelda's sighting to Purah as part of the "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" Main Quest, Hoz and his Crew leave the Camp to patrol Hyrule Field to the south, leaving the Camp uninhabited. Equipment Inhabitants

is a recurring location in . Tera's Great Fairy Fountain goes unnamed in . Features and Overview Tera's Great Fairy Fountain is located beneath the tail of the Gerudo Great Skeleton in Gerudo Desert. As its name implies, it is home to the Great Fairy named Tera. Unlike other Great Fairy Fountains, it is not surrounded by a pool of Water, but it still features a variety of plants. When Link first finds Tera's Great Fairy Fountain, it will be closed into a bud. Tera speaks to him from inside, asking that he listen to her story. If Link agrees, she explains that her Fountain was once a spring, but travelers have stopped coming by to offer her Rupees, resulting in her power dwindling. She now requires Rupees in order to restore her power. Depending on how many other Great Fairy Fountains have been opened, Tera will ask for either 100 Rupees, 500 Rupees, 1,000 Rupees, or 10,000 Rupees. After Link gives his Rupees to Tera, her Great Fairy Fountain will bloom as her power returns. Tera will now be able to enhance Link's Armor. The degree to which she can do this depends on how many other Great Fairy Fountains have been activated. Creatures Materials Tera's Great Fairy Fountain has moved to the edge of the Military Training Camp in the Great Hyrule Forest.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Ternio Trail is a mountain path that paves through southeastern Eldin Canyon, between Eldin proper, Akkala, and northern Lanayru. The Trail begins with a fork in the road that splits between Eldin to the north, and Akkala further east. The Trail is characterized by its fir trees, which gradually turn more scarce the further the path goes into central Eldin. The Eldin split leads to the Foothill Stable, before continuing as the Mountain Road that eventually leads to Goron City and ultimately Death Mountain. The travelers Nat and Meghyn can often be found on the Eldin split hunting for Hearty Truffles. They are sometimes attacked by Bokoblins in the area. Enemies

is a recurring character in . Biography Thadd is a cautious villager who guards Hateno Village's gate. Upon seeing Link, he will brandish his Farmer's Pitchfork and warily ask who he is. Realizing that Link is a Hylian, he will apologize and give him directions to Hateno Village's General Store and Inn. If he is spoken to again, Thadd can answer a couple of questions. He will give a description of Hateno Village as a whole, though he is unable to give specifics. Thadd points out that the village is highly responsive to tourism. However, he advises Link against visiting the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab on the hill overlooking the village. Although Link can ask Thadd to show him the village, he will turn the hero down at once. He will apologize afterward for his behavior, stating that although his work is important, it is not difficult. Still, he will adamantly refuse to use his time giving Link a tour, directing him to Seldon instead. As night rolls in, Thadd continues to guard despite his sleepiness. He is at the village entrance no matter the hour, never sleeping. Thadd guards the Second Floor of Lookout Landing. He carries a Farming Hoe. Despite being very worried about the safety of his family, he left Hateno Village to help out in the search for Zelda. When Link first arrives at Lookout Landing, he will remark how Lookout Landing is not as quiet as it usually is. If Link approaches Thadd, he recognizes him. He then tells Link not to waste his time chatting, directing him to meet with Purah. After Link has spoken to Purah, Thadd can be found looking out from the Second Floor. He comments on how unusual Link is to be on the Second Floor and introduces himself. He explains the he is originally from Hateno Village, and he has been worried about his wife Tamana and son Teebo. When he looks at the Ring Ruins, he thinks about how Hateno Village is located beyond them, which makes him even more concerned for his family. When spoken to again, he explains that he came to Lookout Landing to help search for Zelda.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview On the north end of Goron City, Link can find Dugby near the Mine Cart Tracks, where he is struggling to move a Mine Cart. He recalls hearing that he can use the Mine Cart to reach the end of the Tracks, but he has been unable to make it move. Dugby suspects that Gorondia is located on the other side of the Tracks. If Link asks about Gorondia, Dugby will initially be shocked, but he explains that it is an ancient city where Gorons lived in the ancient past. Treasure, advanced technology, and strange vehicles can also supposedly be found there. He reveals that he wanted to ride in the Mine Cart to search for this treasure, but he has been unable to move it. Dugby warns Link not to share his secrets, after which "The Ancient City Gorondia!" will begin. Using Ultrahand, Link can place the Mine Cart on top of the Mine Cart Tracks. In order to get the Mine Cart to move, however, he will need to attach a Fan to the back. Once the Mine Cart is on the Tracks, Link is able to direct Dugby to sit in it. After activating the Fan, Link must ride with Dugby to YunoboCo HQ at the end of the Tracks. Upon disembarking from the Mine Cart, Dugby declares that he is going to search for Gorondia. Noticing that Link is still there, Dugby realizes he must want a reward, and so he gives him a Zonai Charge. He predicts that the treasure he finds will make him rich, and when that happens, he promises to hire Link. Dugby then rolls off, and "The Ancient City Gorondia!" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview During the "Sidon of the Zora" Main Quest, Sidon suggests that Link meet with Jiahto, believing that his research may provide a clue to Zelda's location. At Toto Lake, Link can find Jiahto examining an ancient Stone Slate. He is impressed with the writing, stating that it must have been left by the ancient Zora. Due to the central piece's absence, however, he is unable to decipher the entire text. Noticing Link's presence, Jiahto apologizes for not doing so sooner, and he proceeds to demonstrate his discovery to him. He explains that the Stone Slate's text appears to focus on the Sky, but he cannot completely translate it due to its broken state. Following their conversation, "The Broken Slate" will begin. The Stone Slate's missing piece can be found lodged in a pile of Sludge nearby. After cleaning the Sludge with a Splash Fruit, a Chuchu Jelly, or a Hydrant, Link can use Ultrahand to lift the missing piece and return it to its place. Jiahto will be shocked, and he thanks Link for restoring the Stone Slate. Now able to read the entire Stone Slate, Jiahto relays that if an Arrow with the mark of the king is shot through a "droplet" on the land of the sky fish, it will reveal the resting spot of the Watery Bridge. Jiahto believes that these are instructions as to how to reach the Sky, though he is uncertain about what they mean. Jiahto suggests consulting with Dorephan about the "mark of the king", as he may have already returned from his investigation. At this point, "The Broken Slate" will be completed, and "Clues to the Sky" will begin. Objectives

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Rauru as a Spirit outside the Temple of Time. Text on-screen displays his name, along with the title "Source of the Right Arm".|Rauru's introduction After receiving the Purah Pad from a Steward Construct, Link is told that Zelda is waiting for him in the Temple of Time on the Great Sky Island. However, when he tries to activate the Terminal to open the Temple's door, the Terminal turns red and denies him entry. While Link is examining his new Right Arm, Rauru appears behind him, explaining that he can only open the door once he has a sufficient amount of power. Rauru apologizes for startling Link, revealing that he was the original owner of the Arm and introducing himself. Rauru laments having to appear as a Spirit, since his physical form is gone. He reasons that the Right Arm should have enough power to activate the Terminal, but it appears to have lost this ability. To restore his Arm's Ancient Powers, Link must visit three of the Shrines of Light located on the Great Sky Island, Looking towards Ukouh Shrine nearby, Rauru assures Link that the Shrines are the key to fixing the Arm before disappearing. Afterwards, "The Closed Door" will begin. Whenever Link enters a Shrine of Light, Rauru will appear before him yet again. In the first Shrine, Rauru will explain that he was the original creator of the Shrines, and he believes they are capable of restoring the Right Arm's lost Ancient Powers. He then asks Link to show him his hand, granting him either Ultrahand, Fuse, or Ascend depending on the Shrine. Link must then use these abilities to reach the end of the Shrine of Light. Once Link has completed his first Shrine of Light, Rauru appears in front of him, commending him for passing its trial and restoring one of the Right Arm's abilities. Should Link two more Shrines, Rauru believes he will be able to enter the Temple of Time. He suggests Link mark the locations of these Shrine with Pins with the Purah Pad's Scope, allowing him to keep track of them as he explores. After completing Ukouh Shrine, In-isa Shrine, and Gutanbac Shrine and receiving the Lights of Blessing, Rauru returns to Link, telling him that he has successfully restored some of the Right Arm's Ancient Powers. He believes that Link is now capable of activating the Terminal in front of the Temple of Time. Now, when Link attempts to activate the Terminal in front of the Temple of Time, it will respond to his Right Arm and open the door. Once this is done, "The Closed Door" will be completed. Objectives

, also known as the General Shop, is a location in . Features and Overview The Curious Quiver is a General Store located by the southwestern entrance of Kakariko Village. It is run by Rola, primarily selling Arrows and Fire Arrows. Several Jars can be found at the building's rear. When Link enters The Curious Quiver, Rola will greet him. The first time he speaks to her, she remarks that it has been some time since the Store received a new customer, since not many of the younger residents of Kakariko Village use Bows. As a result, she is happy that Link is visiting, and she encourages him to browse her wares. On subsequent visits, Rola tells Link to grab any Item he wants to buy, but she also offers to make a purchase from Link. At the end of their conversations, Rola will be disappointed that he is leaving The Curious Quiver. If Link buys Arrows from The Curious Quiver, Rola will thank him, compliment his choice of product, and invite him to come back. When Link buys the entire stock of one type of Arrow, she comments that he is eager and promises to make more soon. After buying all of the Arrows in the Store, Rola will apologize to Link for being out of stock, though she still offers to buy Items off of him. At the end of their conversation, Rola deduces that Link must be a prolific archer due to how many Arrows he needs. She compares him to her estranged husband Cado, who used to be the best archer among the Sheikah, but she eventually realizes she is rambling. The "Arrows of Burning Heat" Side Quest can be initiated at The Curious Quiver. When Link speaks to Rola for a second time, she states that she knew he would be good with a Bow, and she asks if he could demonstrate something for her with it. If Link agrees, Rola asks him to light the stationary Torches around Kakariko Village's Goddess Statue. After Link confirms he will do it, Rola will be excited, and the Side Quest will begin. After Link lights the Torches, he must return to The Curious Quiver to tell Rola. Once he speaks to her, she reveals that she saw what he did and is impressed. Since she is so excited, she gives Link a Red Rupee as a reward. This completes the Side Quest. Equipment Wares and Pricing Wares and Pricing

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview There are two methods to start "The Death Caldera Crystal". The first is by activating the Travel Point in front of the Momosik Shrine. The second is by interacting with the Shrine of Light's respective Mysterious Crystal. In either scenario, Link will hear a Mysterious Voice, telling him to bring the Crystal to the Momosik Shrine in exchange for a Light of Blessing. Upon hearing the voice, a beam connecting the Mysterious Crystal to the Shrine will appear, and the Shrine Quest will begin. The Mysterious Crystal corresponding to the Momosik Shrine can be found in the Death Mountain East Tunnel, which is initially blocked by blue Hard Sediment. The Crystal is also a part of the Ore Deposit of an Igneo Talus, which Link must defeat before being able to bring it to the Shrine. At the Shrine, the Mysterious Voice will speak again, honoring its promise to give him a Light of Blessing. The Crystal will then expand in size, revealing itself to be the Shrine's entrance. Afterwards, "The Death Caldera Crystal" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview After Link views the Memory "Where Am I?" during "Impa and the Geoglyphs", Impa will appear nearby and ask him what is wrong. After hearing that Link was able to see a vision of the past, she theorizes that Princess Zelda could be connected to the Geoglyphs and their Dragon's Tears. Impa suspects they can find more clues by continuing to investigate the Geoglyphs, and she claims that ancient literature states they can find out more at the Forgotten Temple. Once this conversation is over, "The Dragon's Tears" will begin. At the entrance to the Forgotten Temple, Link can find Cado tending to Impa's Hot-Air Balloon. He is happy to see Link, and he reveals that once they arrived, Impa went further into the Temple to keep investigating. He plans to join her after he has moored the Hot-Air Balloon. By venturing into the Temple, Link can next meet Impa near the Mayausiy Shrine. She once again thanks Link for fixing her Hot-Air Balloon, and she claims that due to the Forgotten Temple's size, she is having trouble finding anything related to the Geoglyphs. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of the Floor Map depicting an ancient Hyrule|The Floor Map Past the Mother Goddess Statue is another smaller chamber, at the back of which Link can come across the Floor Map. Impa and Cado follow behind him, and Cado decides that they should see it up close. Impa notices that the walls surrounding the Floor Map depict the Geoglyphs, and the one after that which they saw on the North Hyrule Plain is located near Rito Village. Cado then points out that the locations of all the Geoglyphs are marked on the Floor Map. Impa is shocked that there were still secrets to find within the Forgotten Temple, and she states that they should go and investigate the remaining Geoglyphs. This worries Cado, who insists that she should rest before they leave again. Impa tells Link to look into any Geoglyphs he comes upon during his travels, since they could help lead them to Princess Zelda. Excluding the one found on North Hyrule Plain, a total of 10 Geoglyphs remain for Link to investigate. By finding their Dragon's Tears, he will be able to view one of Zelda's Memories from the ancient past. The locations of the Dragon's Tears and their respective Memories are as follows: After Link views the first 11 Memories from the Dragon's Tears, he will be startled by the Light Dragon roaring from above him. As she flies, the Light Dragon sheds another Dragon's Tear, which lands at the tip of Rist Peninsula. By examining the final Dragon's Tear, Link will be able to view "Tears of the Dragon". When the Memory ends, several Silent Princesses can be seen to have sprouted around where the Dragon's Tear landed. The Light Dragon roars once again, and Link watches as she flies away. As he does so, "The Dragon's Tears" will be completed.

be able to view "Tears of the Dragon". When the Memory ends, several Silent Princesses can be seen to have sprouted around where the Dragon's Tear landed. The Light Dragon roars once again, and Link watches as she flies away. As he does so, "The Dragon's Tears" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview At Selmie's Spot, Link can find Russ wondering where Selmie has gone. When Link approaches him, he initially thinks he is Selmie, who he states was a famous Shield Surfer in the past. He explains that he took her and his friend Fin on as students, but she left to make a new course after the Blizzard disappeared and never came back. Fin left Selmie's Spot to look for her at the Biron Snowshelf, while Russ is waiting at the cabin in case she returns. Since Fin has also failed to come back, Russ has been searching for his Smoke Signals to try and meet with him. After their conversation, "The Duchess Who Disappeared" will begin. Objectives

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview There are two methods to start "The Gerudo Canyon Crystal". The first is by activating the Travel Point in front of the Rakakudaj Shrine. The second is by interacting with the Shrine of Light's respective Mysterious Crystal. In either scenario, Link will hear a Mysterious Voice, telling him to bring the Crystal to the Rakakudaj Shrine in exchange for a Light of Blessing. Upon hearing the voice, a beam connecting the Mysterious Crystal to the Shrine will appear, and the Shrine Quest will begin. The Mysterious Crystal corresponding to the Rakakudaj Shrine can be found in between a couple of large rocks further south, near where Giro sets up camp after getting lost. When Link brings it to the Shrine, the Mysterious Voice will speak again, honoring its promise to give him a Light of Blessing. The Crystal will then expand in size, revealing itself to be the Shrine's entrance. Afterwards, "The Gerudo Canyon Crystal" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview There are two methods to start "The Gisa Crater Crystal". The first is by activating the Travel Point in front of the Ikatak Shrine. The second is by interacting with the Shrine of Light's respective Mysterious Crystal. In either scenario, Link will hear a Mysterious Voice, telling him to bring the Crystal to the Ikatak Shrine in exchange for a Light of Blessing. Upon hearing the voice, a beam connecting the Mysterious Crystal to the Shrine will appear, and the Shrine Quest will begin. The Mysterious Crystal corresponding to the Ikatak Shrine can be found in between two Ice Likes in the nearby Gisa Crater Cave. When Link brings it to the Shrine, the Mysterious Voice will speak again, honoring its promise to give him a Light of Blessing. The Crystal will then expand in size, revealing itself to be the Shrine's entrance. Afterwards, "The Gisa Crater Crystal" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Great Ton Pu Inn is an Inn nestled in the eastern portion of Hateno Village. It sits along the main pathway that leads up to the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab, across from the Shared Cooking Space. Bright blue banners along the building's exterior adorned with an image of a crescent moon mark its location. The Inn is owned and managed by Prima. Leop also works for the Inn, advertising it to travelers as they pass by. The traveler Worten resides at The Great Ton Pu Inn. During the day, he sits on the Inn's porch, and he Sleeps in one of the Beds at night. Teli, a traveling Merchant, also stops by the Inn while visiting Hateno Village. When Link visits The Great Ton Pu Inn, Prima will greet him. The Inn offers a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Sleeping in the Soft Bed provides a "restorative experience", granting Link an Extra Heart in addition to regenerating his Life Gauge. When Link decides to Sleep at The Great Ton Pu Inn, Prima will offer to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or during the night. After Link chooses how long to Sleep, Prima tells him to enjoy his stay. She will then ask if he Slept well. If Link chooses the Soft Bed, Prima will tell him he looks well-rested when he wakes. At the end of their interaction, Prima requests that he stay at the Inn again. Materials Equipment

page_title: The Hidden Treasure at Lizard Lakes
text: "" is a Side Quest in . Overview After completing the "Yunobo of Goron City" Main Quest, Yunobo and Bludo can be found speaking at the center of Goron City. Yunobo recalls that while he was wearing the Weird Mask, the other Zelda told him not to go near the Lizard Lakes. Hearing mention of the Lizard Lakes, Bludo remembers a nursery rhyme about them, which states, "One brother hunts what the other brother hides—two lizards fighting over what's inside." In his youth, Bludo tried to find the Lizard Lakes hoping to find treasure, but the eruption of Death Mountain forced him to stop. Having been reminded of the Lakes, Bludo wants to continue his search. He believes the most likely place to find them would be halfway up the north side of Death Mountain. He wants to go immediately, but his back pain suddenly flares up before he can do so. After witnessing this conversation, "The Hidden Treasure at Lizard Lakes" will begin. The Lizard Lakes are located on the northern side of Death Mountain. One is situated at the base of Lake Darman, while the other is at the base of Death Caldera. Between the two Lakes, Link can come upon the entrance to the Lizard's Burrow. A Stone Chest can be found at the end of the Cave that contains the Vah Rudania Divine Helm. Upon obtaining the Helm, "The Hidden Treasure at Lizard Lakes" will be completed. Objectives

"The Lake Hylia Crystal" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview "The Lake Hylia Crystal" can be started in two separate ways. The first is by activating En-oma Shrine's Travel Point in the Lake Hylia Whirlpool Cave. The second way is to examine the Mysterious Crystal on the Sky Island above the Whirlpool Cave in the Faron Sky Archipelago. In either scenario, Link will hear a Mysterious Voice tell him to bring the Mysterious Crystal to the Shrine of Light in order to receive a Light of Blessing. Dropping the Mysterious Crystal from the hole in the Sky Island will cause it to fall directly into the Lake Hylia Whirlpool Cave. From there, Link can bring it to the Shrine of Light. The Mysterious Voice states that it will now offer the Light of Blessing. The Mysterious Crystal then begins to float and grow, and after its green sheen disappears, it is revealed to be the entrance to En-oma Shrine. Following this, Link is able to enter the Shrine of Light. Objectives

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview There are two methods to start "The Lanayru Road Crystal". The first is by activating the Travel Point in front of the O-ogim Shrine. The second is by interacting with the Shrine of Light's respective Mysterious Crystal. In either scenario, Link will hear a Mysterious Voice, telling him to bring the Crystal to the O-ogim Shrine in exchange for a Light of Blessing. Upon hearing the voice, a beam connecting the Mysterious Crystal to the Shrine will appear, and the Shrine Quest will begin. The Mysterious Crystal corresponding to the O-ogim Shrine can be found behind a breakable rock wall in the Lanayru Road South Cave, which Link can pick up and bring to the Shrine. At the Shrine, the Mysterious Voice will speak again, honoring its promise to give him a Light of Blessing. The Crystal will then expand in size, revealing itself to be the Shrine's entrance. Afterwards, "The Lanayru Road Crystal" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview In either the Gerudo Shelter or Starlight Memories, Link can find Cara wondering where Isha has gone. When Link approaches her, she becomes distracted trying to determine his measurements. She explains that she makes Accessories, and it is important for them to fit perfectly on their wearers. Despite offering to make Accessories for Link, she reveals that the Jewelry Shop's owner, Isha, could make more for him. However, she has yet to return from searching for adornments in the Toruma Dunes, which is the home of a Molduga. At this point in the conversation, "The Missing Owner" will begin. In the Toruma Dunes, Link can find Isha cowering on a rock pillar as a Molduga circles her. She laments not paying attention to her surroundings, and while she is safe on the pillar, she is unable to leave without alerting it to her location. She quietly pleads for the Molduga to go away. Once the Molduga has been defeated, Isha will be shocked. She then asks Link if he was the one who killed it. After he confirms this, she is surprised to have met such a strong man, claiming that is must be fate. She introduces herself, inviting him to come to Starlight Memories and receive a reward from her. Though she is concerned he will not be able to enter Gerudo Town, Isha is certain that they will meet again. Now that it is safe to do so, she leaves for Gerudo Town. When Link returns to Gerudo Town, he will find Cara speaking with Isha. Upon noticing Link, Cara reveals that Isha told her that he saved her. She thanks him and gives him a Diamond as a reward. She is impressed that he was able to defeat a Molduga. Isha thanks Link for helping her return to Gerudo Town, and she expresses her shock that he is Riju's honored guest. For her own reward, she tells Link to talk to her when he has time, since it is more involved. Afterwards, "The Missing Owner" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link speaks to Seggin after completing "Sidon of the Zora", he reflects on Sidon's recent coronation, stating that Mipha would have been overjoyed if she had seen it. He recalls witnessing Mipha holding her Lightscale Trident in the moonlight, claiming it was beautiful. He wishes to see it once more, at which point "The Moonlit Princess" will begin. At Mipha Court on Ploymus Mountain, Link can use his Camera to take a Picture of Mipha's Statue during the night. Upon seeing the Picture, Seggin will be shocked by its accuracy. Happy to have seen Mipha in the moonlight once again, he gives Link a Zora Sword as a sign of his gratitude. If Link's Weapon Inventory is full, Seggin will ask him to make room. He then reveals that he used the Sword in the past, and he believes that it could still be useful to Link. Feeling relieved, Seggin declares his loyalty to Sidon and the Zora royalty. Afterwards, "The Moonlit Princess" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link initially visits the Mother Goddess Statue, he will discover that it has been knocked to the ground. After completing "Goddess Statue of Courage", "Goddess Statue of Power", and "Goddess Statue of Wisdom", Link will be directed to meet with the Mother Goddess Statue. Upon hearing this request, "The Mother Goddess Statue" Side Quest will begin. At the back of the Forgotten Temple, Link can find that the Mother Goddess Statue has been able to set herself upright. When he prays to her, she expresses her gratitude for helping the Spring of Courage Statue, the Spring of Power Statue, and the Spring of Wisdom Statue. As a reward, she gives Link the White Sword of the Sky. She then tells him to bring peace to the world. Afterwards, "The Mother Goddess Statue" will be completed. Objectives

"The Necluda Sky Crystal" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview Link can start "The Necluda Sky Crystal" in two ways. The first is by activating Kumamayn Shrine's Travel Point, and the second is by examining the Mysterious Crystal which is located on the shoulder of a nearby Flux Construct III. In either scenario, a Mysterious Voice will speak to Link, informing him that he can receive a Light of Blessing by bringing the Crystal to the Shrine of Light. After dislodging the Mysterious Crystal from the Flux Construct's shoulder, Link will be able to bring the Crystal to Kumamayn Shrine, where the Mysterious Voice honors its promise to him. The Crystal will then float above the Shrine of Light and grow in size, and as its green sheen fades away, it is revealed to be the Shrine's entrance. At this point, Link can now enter the Shrine, and the Shrine Quest will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview After completing "Sidon of the Zora", Link can find Khira scolding Chroma in the Throne Room of Zora's Domain. She condemns Chroma for acting without self-awareness, since everything they do reflects back on Yona. However, they are interrupted when Chroma notices Link nearby. Khira apologizes for failing to see him, though Chroma claims she was too absorbed in her lecture to do so. This enrages Khira, who reveals that the point of her lecture was because she failed to retrieve the Zora Helm they wanted to give Link, which they learned has been kept in a "sky fish". Chroma claims that she searched the Zora River for a Fish that had eaten the Zora Helm, but she was unable to find it. Khira informs her that the "sky fish" is likely a metaphor, and she believes she would have understood her had she listened to her guidance. In fear, Chroma asks Link to help her. Afterwards, "The Never-Ending Lecture" will begin. On Floating Scales Island, Link can come across an entryway on the northeastern side of its tail. At the end of this hallways is a Stone Chest, which holds the Zora Helm inside. Once he obtains the Zora Helm, "The Never-Ending Lecture" will be completed. Objectives

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Noble Canteen is a bar in Gerudo Town managed by Furosa. It is known for a cocktail called Noble Pursuit, which is popular among the Gerudo. Due to the Ice that the Canteen sources from the Northern Icehouse, the bar's drinks are known the be refreshing. Various Gerudo women can be found within the bar throughout the day. Nellie, Pritana, and Jules all visit the Canteen throughout the day. A poster on the Canteen's wall shows a Recipe for Chilly Mushroom Risotto, with the Ingredients being Rock Salt, a Chillshroom, Goat Butter and Hylian Rice. When Link first enters The Noble Canteen, Furosa recognizes that he is too young to partake in her drinks. Deltan can be found sitting inside The Noble Canteen, hunched over and complaining about men. Pyra, Sumati, and Yaido are also regular patrons of the Canteen, where they can be found discussing the Gerudo Secret Club's password. However, they end their conversation when they notice that Link is listening to them. By listening in from the window of the House next door, Link is able to hear the password. During "The Perfect Drink" Shrine Quest, Link must procure a Noble Pursuit for Pokki, who is stranded in the East Barrens. When Furosa hears about her situation, she reveals that she has run out of Ice and is unable to make the drink. After Link offers to fetch the Ice for her, Furosa decides to meet him at the end of the ruins between the Northern Icehouse and Gerudo Town. Once she has the Ice, Furosa is able to make a Noble Pursuit, and she asks Link to inform Pokki that it is waiting for her.. Upon hearing this from Link, Pokki will run back to The Noble Canteen. Back at the Canteen, Furosa invites Link to come back when he is of age.

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview Link has two methods by which he can start "The North Hebra Mountains Crystal". The first is by interacting with the Travel Point in front of the Sisuran Shrine, which is located at Hebra East Summit North. The second is by touching the Mysterious Crystal that corresponds to the Shrine. In both cases, a Mysterious Voice will speak to him, requesting that he bring the Mysterious Crystal to the Shrine of Light in exchange for a Light of Blessing. Afterwards, a beam will appear that connects the Shrine and the Crystal, and the Shrine Quest will begin. The Sisuran Shrine's Mysterious Crystal can be found embedded in the Ore Deposit of a Frost Talus that lies dormant nearby, which must be defeated in order to obtain the Crystal. From this point, he can bring the Crystal to the Shrine of Light by either carrying it or using Ultrahand. Once he does so, the Mysterious Voice speaks again to honor its promise. At this point, the Crystal expands in size, revealing that it is the entrance to the Sisuran Shrine. Link will now be able to enter the Shrine, and "The North Hebra Mountains Crystal" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview "The Northwest Hebra Cave Crystal" can be started via two separate methods. The first is by activating the Travel Point that correlates to Rutafu-um Shrine inside of the Hebra Mountains Northwest Cave. The second is by interacting with the Mysterious Crystal located nearby. In either scenario, a Mysterious Voice will speak to Link and instruct him to bring the Mysterious Crystal to the Shrine of Light, with the goal of receiving a Light of Blessing. Following this, a green light will appear that connects the Crystal and the Shrine, and "The Northwest Hebra Cave Crystal" will begin. The Mysterious Crystal that corresponds to Rutafu-um Shrine can be found submerged in a pool of Cold Water that is located in front of the Shrine. By standing on a platform that floats in Water, Link can use Ultrahand to lift the Crystal out of the pool. Alternatively, he can attach one of the Icicles inside of the Cave to the Crystal with Ultrahand, which he can then use to pull it to the shore. Upon bringing the Mysterious Crystal to Rutafu-um Shrine, it will grow in size, revealing the Shrine's entrance. Afterwards, the Shrine Quest will be completed, and Link will be able to enter the Shrine. Objectives

"The Oakle's Navel Cave Crystal" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview Inside Oakle's Navel Cave, Link will find a Mysterious Crystal propped up on a pedestal. When he attempts to pick it up, a Mysterious Voice will speak to him, offering a Light of Blessing if he can bring the Mysterious Crystal to the end of its beam. Following this, the wall behind the Mysterious Crystal will part, revealing a large cavern with Boulders rolling across it, and "The Oakle's Navel Cave Crystal" will begin. After exiting the cavern, Link will be in a tight corridor, where a large Stone Ball rolls towards him. After avoiding the Ball, he will be able to arrive at the location of Tokiy Shrine. The Mysterious Voice honors its promise. The Mysterious Crystal will then float above the Shrine of Light's exterior, growing and revealing itself to be the Shrine's entrance. Once its green coating fades away, Link is able to enter Tokiy Shrine. Objectives

"The Ralis Channel Crystal" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview There are two ways to activate "The Ralis Channel Crystal". The first is by examining the Mysterious Crystal found by the southern entrance to Ralis Channel. The second is by approaching Joniu Shrine at the end of Ralis Channel and activating its Travel Point. In either scenario, a Mysterious Voice will speak to Link, instructing him to bring the Mysterious Crystal to the Shrine of Light in order to receive a Light of Blessing. A beam of light will then appear, connecting the Crystal and the Shrine. To bring the Mysterious Crystal to Joniu Shrine, Link must use Ultrahand to construct a makeshift raft. He can propel it through Ralis Channel using either the Sail or the Fans found nearby. When Link successfully brings the Mysterious Crystal, the Mysterious Voice speaks again, honoring its promise to grant him a Light of Blessing. The Mysterious Crystal will then float above the Shrine of Light and grow in size, and when its green sheen disappears, it is revealed to be the Shrine's entrance. The Shrine Quest will then be completed, and Link will be able to enter Joniu Shrine. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview After the Extreme Cold Snap in Rito Village has ended, Link can find Gesane and Juannelle at the broken bridge near the Lucky Clover Gazette discussing reconstruction efforts. Although the Rito do not have the supplies to rebuild, Gesane has heard that the Hylians are skilled in such matters, and he asks Juannelle if she knows any carpenters. Juannelle believes that the individual who built Lookout Landing could help, but she can only remember that his name ends in "son". Gesane is impressed by his reputation, but he is unable to leave Rito Village as a guard. He plans to dispatch an emissary in his place, though he is unsure if anyone is available to leave. Afterwards, "The Rito Rope Bridge" will begin. At Lookout Landing, Link can find Karson, who claims he has nearly finished building in the area. Since he is soon to be out of work, he asks Link if he is aware of anyone who needs the assistance of a carpenter. Upon hearing about the Rito, Karson recalls hearing that their bridge fell apart during the Extreme Cold Snap, and he notes that it must have ended if they are trying to rebuild. Karson decides to offer his help, at which point he departs for Rito Village. When Link meets with Karson at the bridge, he can be seen informing Gesane and Juannelle that it is in worse condition than he anticipated. Gesane apologizes for the Rito's lack of building supplies, but Karson insists it is his fault for not bringing enough. If Link asks what happened, Karson and Juannelle claim they are short 20 bundles of Wood. Karson believes that could get more by chopping down the Cedar Trees nearby, but he compares it to taking on another project. Once Link returns with enough Wood, Karson is shocked and asks if he is certain he can have it. When Link affirms it is for him, Karson will thank him. Now that he has all of the necessary Materials, Karson invites Gesane to fix the bridge with him. While working on the bridge, Karson directs Gesane, which involves Gesane catching a plank that was falling into Lake Totori and accidentally sitting on a support beam. Karson himself puts the finishing touches on the bridge, which involves singing the Hudson Construction theme song. After finishing the bridge, Gesane is impressed. Karson admits that he was concerned about the end result, but he is relieved that it turned out well. He is certain that the new bridge could be hit by 10 blizzards at once and still not fall. Gesane believes that Rito Village will start to feel normal again, and as a reward, he gives Link a Silver Rupee. Karson decides to return to Lookout Landing, though he tells Gesane that he will be there if he ever needs help again. Gesane is grateful, offering the same invitation to Karson in return. Juannelle notes that the bridge has connected

and as a reward, he gives Link a Silver Rupee. Karson decides to return to Lookout Landing, though he tells Gesane that he will be there if he ever needs help again. Gesane is grateful, offering the same invitation to Karson in return. Juannelle notes that the bridge has connected the Hylians and the Rito both literally and metaphorically, which she thinks would be a good topic for an article. Once Karson leaves, "The Rito Rope Bridge" will be finished. Objectives

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview There are two methods to start "The Satori Mountain Crystal". The first is by activating the Travel Point in front of the Usazum Shrine. The second is by interacting with the Shrine of Light's respective Mysterious Crystal. In either scenario, Link will hear a Mysterious Voice, telling him to bring the Crystal to the Usazum Shrine in exchange for a Light of Blessing. Upon hearing the voice, a beam connecting the Mysterious Crystal to the Shrine will appear, and the Shrine Quest will begin. The Mysterious Crystal corresponding to the Usazum Shrine can be found hanging from the neck of the Hinox that patrols the interior of the Satori Mountain Foothill Cave. The Hinox will drop the Crystal upon its defeat, at which point Link will be able to pick it up and bring it to the Usazum Shrine. At the Shrine, the Mysterious Voice will speak again, honoring its promise to give him a Light of Blessing. The Crystal will then expand in size, revealing itself to be the Shrine's entrance. Afterwards, "The Satori Mountain Crystal" will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview The Side Quest begins when Link receives the final Light of Blessing from any of the 152 Shrines of Light. Rauru will call to Link and instruct him to visit the Temple of Time atop the Great Sky Island in order to receive a reward for his achievement. A Stone Chest will appear behind the Goddess Statue in the Temple of Time after this. This Treasure Chest contains the Ancient Hero's Aspect, which houses the Spirit of the Ancient Hero who battled Calamity Ganon over 10,000 years prior. The Side Quest is completed upon opening the Treasure Chest. Objectives

is a recurring General Store in . Features and Overview The Slippery Falcon is a General Store located in Rito Village. It is operated by Misa, who stocks the Store with both groceries and self-defense Items. Her son, Fyson, also helps around the Store, and Misa hopes he will take it over one day. Inside The Slippery Falcon, Link can find Misa's Recipe Book, which contains Recipes for Apple Pie, Nutcake, and Fried Bananas. When Link buys an Item from The Slippery Falcon, Misa will thank him for doing so. If he buys the entire stock of a single Item, Misa promises to restock soon. Should Link purchase all of the Items at The Slippery Falcon, Misa will thank him for his business. Wares and Pricing During the Extreme Cold Snap in Rito Village, Cree takes over running The Slippery Falcon while Misa is away. The blizzard has resulted in fewer customers coming to visit the General Store, in addition to a loss of merchandise to sell. Wares and Pricing

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview When Link first arrives in Zora's Domain, he finds that the Zora are recovering from a wave of Sludge the fell on them. Nearby, Yona can be found discussing the situation with Chroma and Khira. They reveal to her that they have run out of Splash Fruit while treating those affected by the Sludge and apologize. Yona insists that they do not need to apologize, and she is relieved that all of the Zora have survived thus far. However, she is disappointed that the Statue at the center of the Zora's Domain Square has remained covered in Sludge. Turning to Link, Yona apologizes for not noticing him sooner. She explains that Zora's Domain is currently suffering due to the Sludge falling from the Sky, which has covered much of the Lanayru Great Spring. In particular, she is saddened by the Statue being obfuscated by Sludge, since it is important to the Zora. Although they are busy cleaning up, Yona encourages him to make himself at home. Afterwards, "The Sludge-Covered Statue" will begin. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Yona at the Zora's Domain Square, which is afflicted by Sludge. Text on-screen displays her name, along with the title "Caretaker to the Zora".|Yona's introduction Using Splash Fruit, Chuchu Jelly, or a Hydrant, Link can wash away the Sludge over the Statue, revealing The Turning Tide. When Link returns to Yona, she will be relieved that he was able to wash the Statue. She explains that The Turning Tide has become a symbol of hope for the Zora, depicting Sidon and Link himself. Chroma wishes to be able to meet Link one day, noticing that the individual in front of her resembles the one depicted on the Statue. After Link introduces himself, Chroma reacts with shock, which causes Khira to scold her. Yona and Chroma both apologize for their behavior. Yona claims that she has heard about him ever since she arrived at Zora's Domain, revealing that she is Sidon's fiancée. She expresses how honored she is to finally meet him. After hearing that Link is searching for Princess Zelda, Yona invites him to investigate Zora's Domain as much as he needs to. She also requests that he visit Sidon, who can be found at Mipha Court. Before leaving with Chroma and Khira, Yona asks Link to meet with her when he has time. Following their conversation, "The Sludge-Covered Statue" will end, and "Sidon of the Zora" will begin. Objectives

"The West Necluda Sky Crystal" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview Link can start "The West Necluda Sky Crystal" in two ways. The first is by activating Ukoojisi Shrine's Travel Point, and the second is by examining the Mysterious Crystal on the northernmost Sky Island in the West Necluda Sky Archipelago. In either scenario, a Mysterious Voice will speak to Link, informing him that he can receive a Light of Blessing by bringing the Crystal to the Shrine of Light. Inside the cave where the Crystal is located, Link can find a Wing, a Cart, a Steering Stick, Batteries, and several Fans. Using Ultrahand, he can connect these Zonai Devices to create a gliding vehicle, which he can use to bring the Crystal to the Sky Island to the south. From there, Link will be able to bring the Crystal to Ukoojisi Shrine, where the Mysterious Voice honors its promise to him. The Crystal will then float above the Shrine of Light and grow in size, and as its green sheen fades away, it is revealed to be the Shrine's entrance. At this point, Link can now enter the Shrine, and the Shrine Quest will be completed. Objectives

"" is a Shrine Quest in . Overview After completing the Main Quest "Tulin of Rito Village", Link can find Laissa looking out west from Rito Village, trying to remember the location of something she saw. If he speaks to her, she will mention a Cave before greeting him. She recognizes Link as the individual who helped Tulin end the Extreme Cold Snap, and she explains that it is now easier for the Rito to find Caves to scavenge Food from. Laissa reveals that while she was looking for a white Bird, she saw a Shrine of Light inside of a Cave, but she cannot remember where it was. At this point in their conversation, "The White Bird's Guidance"s begin. Laissa mentions that that Cave was stocked with Mushrooms and Fish, and she reiterates that she found it while seeking out a white Bird. If Link asks about the Bird, Laissa explains that she was on Vah Medoh's Perch in the morning when she saw the white Bird sitting on the shadow of Rito Village's spire. She went to investigate, and though she lost track of the Bird, she found the entrance to a Cave instead. If Link asks about further details, Laissa is unable to remember any beyond the white Bird and the Shrine of Light inside. At 5:00 AM, the shadow of Vah Medoh's Perch will pass under a stretch of Snow shaped like a Bird, which is situated west of Rito Village. When Link reaches the Bird, he will find the entrance to the West Lake Totori Cave. After traversing through the Cave, he will reach the Wao-os Shrine, which completes "The White Bird's Guidance". Objectives

The is a recurring location in . The Three-Way Intersection goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Three-Way Intersection is a series of unnamed roads that meet each other in Hyrule Field. The northern path leads to Outskirt Stable, the southwestern path leads to the Digdogg Suspension Bridge, and the southeastern path goes around the Great Plateau. Along the southwestern path are the remains of a Hylian settlement that was destroyed during the Great Calamity. Botrick can be found along the Three-Way Intersection as he travels to Outskirt Stable. Beedle can occasionally also be found at the Three-Way Intersection. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment The Three-Way Intersection returns in . As a result of the Upheaval, numerous amounts of Fallen Debris and Fallen Ruins have landed around the Intersection. A pallet of Hyrule Restoration Materials can also be found nearby. Creatures Enemies Monster Outpost near Digdogg Suspension Bridge Materials

are recurring locations in . Features and Overview The Throne Room is located within Hyrule Castle in . King Daltus resides within it until he is turned to stone by Vaati, who takes his place. Minister Potho and Princess Zelda are also found here, the latter also having been turned to stone. When Vaati transforms Hyrule Castle into Dark Hyrule Castle, the Throne Room becomes an arena for Link to fight a Red Darknut. After it is defeated, the Throne can be pushed aside to reveal a staircase leading to a subterranean level of the Castle. The Throne Room is a single chamber inside Lorule Castle in . The Throne Room serves as the stage of the final battle of the game, where Link faces Yuga Ganon and Princess Hilda for the freedom of Princess Zelda and ownership of Hyrule's Triforce. After unlocking the main door at the end of Lorule Castle, Link is able to access Princess Hilda's offices, which contains a portal back to Princess Zelda's offices in Hyrule that now contain several Fairies. Link follows the same path from Princess Hilda's private office to the Throne Room, where he learns of Princess Hilda's duplicity and conspiracy with Yuga to steal Hyrule's Triforce to restore Lorule, which lost its own Triforce when Princess Hilda's ancestors destroyed it to stop the endless wars fought over it. After sharing this story with Link, Hilda steals the Triforce of Wisdom from Princess Zelda, who is contained in her painting nearby. She then summons Yuga Ganon, commanding him to take the Triforce of Courage from Link. The hero bests the beast, who captures Princess Hilda in a painting as well, and absorbs it to gain the Triforce of Wisdom. Yuga Ganon then attempts to take the Triforce of Courage again, but falls to the blade of the Master Sword, exploding in a burst of dark energy and releasing both Hilda and Zelda. The Throne Room makes up the first floor of Hyrule Castle's Sanctum. Even in its ruined condition, it is heavily decorated with banners, Statues, and carpets. The floor of the Sanctum is decorated with a circular pattern with the symbol of the Triforce engraved in the center. The Marks of the Goddesses are positioned in the center of each respective Triforce piece, while the Royal Crest sits in the negative space created by the triangles. The metal decoration above the Throne bears the symbol of the Triforce, in addition to a circular music scale depicting "Zelda's Lullaby". Following the Great Calamity, Princess Zelda used her newly-awakened sealing power to contain Calamity Ganon within the interior of the Sanctum, where he bides his time and gathers strength to escape her grasp. Inside the Throne Room, Link will find Ganon's Cocoon suspended from the ceiling. If Link enters without having defeated any of the four Blight Ganons, he will be forced to face them. They consistently appear in the order of Windblight Ganon, Waterblight Ganon, Fireblight Ganon, and then Thunderblight Ganon. If

Inside the Throne Room, Link will find Ganon's Cocoon suspended from the ceiling. If Link enters without having defeated any of the four Blight Ganons, he will be forced to face them. They consistently appear in the order of Windblight Ganon, Waterblight Ganon, Fireblight Ganon, and then Thunderblight Ganon. If Link defeated any of them prior to entering the Throne Room, they will not appear. Once all four have been defeated, whether in the Throne Room or their respective Divine Beasts, Link will hear the voice of Zelda. She apologizes for not being able to hold Calamity Ganon back any longer. A Guardian laser bursts out of Ganon's Cocoon, breaking it open and releasing Calamity Ganon. Due to Ganon's weight, the fall breaks the floor of the Throne Room, causing both of them to fall into the Astral Observatory. The Throne Room of Hyrule Castle can be seen in pristine condition. Enemies Bosses Treasure Chests Hyrule Castle's Throne Room is attacked by one of Ganon's Rifts which quickly grows and encompasses the surrounding Castle Town. Other Appearances

The , also known as , King Zora's Chamber, the , and the Mine Keep, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview King Zora's Throne Room is located in Zora's Domain. King Zora sits on his Throne within, protecting the entrance to Zora's Fountain and Lord Jabu-Jabu. Any visitors to Zora's Domain seeking counsel with King Zora must visit the raised platform at the center of the Throne Room to speak with him. In pursuit of the Zora's Sapphire, Ganondorf visited King Zora's Throne Room and made his way to Lord Jabu-Jabu in order to infect the Zora deity with a deadly parasite. After Link rescues Princess Ruto from Inside Jabu Jabu's Belly and kills the parasite, Barinade, Princess Ruto will take her place beside her father in the Throne Room. In the Adult Era, Ganondorf caused the waters of Zora's Domain to freeze over, consequently trapping King Zora in a formation of Red Ice inside his Throne Room. If Link defrosts him, he will offer Link a Zora Tunic as thanks. If Link already has a Zora Tunic, King Zora will off him a kiss instead. Inhabitants The Throne Room is located on the highest level of Zora's Domain, and it houses King Dorephan. In the Voice Memory "Audience with King Dorephan", Princess Zelda recalls a meeting she had with Dorephan in the Throne Room. Link first enters the Throne Room at the behest of Sidon. There, he meets Muzu and King Dorephan, the latter of whom recognizes him as the Hylian Champion. He tells Link about the troubles that Zora's Domain is facing because of Divine Beast Vah Ruta, asking him to work with Sidon to quell its rampage. As a show of his faith, King Dorephan gifts Link the Zora Armor. Angered by this, Muzu storms out of the Throne Room. Sidon will follow him in the hopes that he can change his mind. After Sidon leaves, King Dorephan sends Link after them both. thumb|right|320px|alt= Screenshot of Sidon and Link after freeing Vah Ruta.|Sidon shaking Link's hand After Link has calmed Divine Beast Vah Ruta, all of the Zora will gather in the Throne Room to congratulate him. As a reward, King Dorephan allows Link to take the contents of the Stone Chest nearby, which he claims was an Item cherished by Mipha. In the Chest, Link will find the Lightscale Trident. On behalf of all the Zora, King Dorephan thanks Link and Sidon. Sidon himself thanks Link, shaking his hand and cheering for him along with the rest of the Zora. When Link starts the "EX Champion Mipha's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content pack, Mipha's Diary will appear in the Throne Room. King Dorephan gives Link permission to read it, believing Mipha would forgive for doing so. Inhabitants Treasure Chests As in , the Throne Room sits at the highest level of Zora's Domain. When Link first arrives to the Domain, both King Dorephan and Sidon are absent from the

Throne Room. King Dorephan gives Link permission to read it, believing Mipha would forgive for doing so. Inhabitants Treasure Chests As in , the Throne Room sits at the highest level of Zora's Domain. When Link first arrives to the Domain, both King Dorephan and Sidon are absent from the Throne Room. Tula and Torfeau stand guard over its entrance while three Zora children play inside. Inhabitants Other Appearances The King's Hall, known as the Mine Keep in Adventure Mode Battles, is a Keep at the northeast corner of the Lake Hylia Stage. Being part of frozen Zora's Domain, it features Ice all over its rocky floor and walls. It has two entrances, one on its west side and another on its south. Both feature metal Gates with the Crest of the Zora emblazoned on them. A Sign sits next to the south Gate. Overlooking the north section of the Hall is King Zora's Throne, inaccessible to the Warriors. A frozen passage can be seen behind it. During the Ocarina of Time Scenario "The Water Temple", the King's Hall is the only Keep initially owned by the Warriors and is where they begin the Scenario. It is guarded by Goron Soldiers serving under the Hyrulean Forces. The Throne Room in Zora's Domain first appears the beginning of the Movie "The Looming Threat", wherein Zelda meets with King Dorephan. Dorephan refuses her request to recruit Mipha to pilot Divine Beast Vah Ruta, as he does not wish to risk her life when the knight wielding the Master Sword has yet to appear. However, their discussion ends early when a Zora Soldier arrives with news of a Monster attack. Later, during the Movie "Mipha's Wishes", another audience is held in the Throne Room. Having seen Mipha's power when piloting Vah Ruta, King Dorephan gives her permission to become a Champion. In the Zora's Domain Stage, Warriors are capable of approaching the Throne Room, though its entrances are blocked by fences.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Throwing Spears are Weapons balanced to be thrown farther than the average spear. They are capable of striking Enemies at a great distance. Commonly, they are found in Treasure Chests in West Necluda and Hyrule Field. Being made of metal, Throwing Spears will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm. They also sink if they are dropped in Water, but they can be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Throwing Spears will not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Throwing Spears reappear in . Other Appearances

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics Thunder Wizzrobes are a variant of Electric Wizzrobes. They attack by using their Thunderstorm Rods to cast three balls of electricity, to summon Electric Chuchus and Electric Keese, as well as to summon thunderstorms that will strike Link if he is wielding any metallic Weapon. Thunder Wizzrobes will turn invisible after attacking, however, they leave trails below them. Performing a headshot will stun them, giving Link time to attack. After defeat, they will drop their Thunderstorm Rods. Instead of a Thunderstorm Rod, Thunder Wizzrobes now carry a Magic Rod that has been Fused to a Topaz. Other Appearances Thunder Wizzrobes appear as Powerful Foes in the Downloadable Content pack for , fighting with stronger attacks, such as firing electric magic blasts in a spinning motion.

, also known as , are a recurring mechanic in . Overview In an endless night occurs when Ganondorf casts a curse across the Great Sea, resulting in a Storm that creates choppy seas and strong winds. Visibility is reduced as the world is cast in darkness. On Outset Island all of the residents will hide indoors as ChuChus and Miniblins have appeared across the island. The Ghost Ship will always appear in its pre-determined location. Thunderstorms occur in Akkala, Central Hyrule, Faron, Lanayru, and Necluda. Throughout the duration of a Thunderstorm, Rain will fall from the sky and Lightning will strike at random. Thunderstorms are also possible during Snow in places such as Mount Hylia. Any metallic Weapons, Bows, or Shields that Link has equipped will begin to spark during a Thunderstorm, eventually culminating in Link being struck by Lightning. In addition to this, metallic Objects, such as the metal blocks in Cube Patterns, will also attract Lightning. Initially, Thundra Plateau and Calora Lake will be permanently under the affects of a Thunderstorm. After solving the "Trial of Thunder" and "A Song of Storms" Shrine Quests and activating their respective Ancient Shrines, these Thunderstorms will subside. Thunderstorms occur throughout the surface of Hyrule. Whenever a Thunderstorm occurs on the surface, Rain will fall from the Sky and Lightning will strike sporadically. Certain sections of the Sky such as those in the south of East Necluda are permanently engulfed in Thunderstorms.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Thundra Plateau is located within Ludfo's Bog on Hyrule Ridge. The Plateau features a variety of Zonai Ruins, including pillars and Dragon-head statues. It is known for the frequency at which Lightning and Thunderstorms appear in the area. When Link first arrives at the Plateau, it will be constantly under the effects of a Thunderstorm, which can be observed from a distance. As Link approaches Thundra Plateau, he will hear the voice of Toh Yahsa, who instructs him to return the "four spirits" to their proper places to reveal an Ancient Shrine. This starts the "Trial of Thunder" Shrine Quest. Throughout Thundra Plateau and in the surrounding area, Link can find four colorful orbs, which he must place in the four corresponding slots on the Plateau. Once all four orbs have been placed in their slots, Toh Yahsa Shrine will rise from the ground at the center of the Plateau, completing the Shrine Quest. Creatures Enemies Equipment Areas Other Appearances As part of the "Preparing for Field Work" Quest, Zelda wishes to investigate an ancient relic that has been discovered on Thundra Plateau, but she needs Materials to help protect her from Electricity. After receiving the Materials, however, Zelda is unable to learn anything from the relic. During the "Stealth Mission" Quest, Urbosa needs Materials to keep her hidden while she investigates rumors of a Monster horde on Thundra Plateau. With the Materials, she determines that the shadows from Lightning strikes made there seem to be more Monsters than were actually present. Lastly, as part of the "Beyond the Wall of Thunder" Quest, a Rito Monster hunter needs Electricity-resistant Materials so she can face the Monsters on Thundra Plateau. Once she receives the Materials, she is able to reduce the number of Monsters residing on Thundra Plateau.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview Located in the northern portion of the Great Hyrule Forest, the Thyphlo Ruins are a large set of Zonai Ruins. They are surrounded by a murky Bottomless Bog and are shrouded in Darkness, making navigation impossible without a Light source. In addition to this, the Weather in the surrounding area is constantly overcast. The Ruins can be accessed from the Drenan Highlands by crossing the bridge on their western side. When Link first enters the Thyphlo Ruins, he will hear the voice of Ketoh Wawai telling him to find an Ancient Shrine hidden in the darkness. This starts the "Shrouded Shrine" Shrine Quest. Link can navigate the Ruins by following their unique Bird-shaped Torches, which will eventually lead him to a Pedestal featuring a Concave Slot. Nearby, he finds the Ruins' Hinox, which has an Ancient Orb hanging from its necklace. After taking the Ancient Orb and placing it in the Concave Slot, Ketoh Wawai Shrine will emerge from the ground. Eight separate Treasure Chests can be found within the Thyphlo Ruins. In total, these Chests contain three Ambers, three Opals, one Ruby, and one Star Fragment. Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials Equipment The Thyphlo Ruins reappear in . The dark fog present in has been cleared, making the Zonai architecture more visible. A puzzle can be solved here using the power of the four Sages, and rewards Link with the Dusk Claymore when solved. The ruins are now the landmark for the game's many Skyview Towers, namely Thyphlo Ruins Skyview Tower. The Gleeok Den is their counterpart in the Depths.
