are Items and Objects in . Location and Uses Time Bombs are Bombs that emit delayed explosions when they are struck. They can be found throughout the Sky Islands, near Zonai Ruins, and in some Supply Sites in the Depths. When struck, dropped, or thrown, Time Bombs blink blue for a few seconds before exploding, dealing significant damage to nearby Enemies. Their blasts can also activate other Zonai Devices in range. Cube-shaped Time Bombs can be found in Monster Encampments, Forts and Strongholds on the Surface of Hyrule. These Bombs can be thrown at Link by the Monsters inhabiting these locations. They blink red instead of blue before exploding.

Time Travel is a recurring mechanic in . Overview In , after retrieving the three Spiritual Stones and playing the "Song of Time" in the Temple of Time, Link can take the Master Sword and can prevent Ganondorf from obtaining the Triforce. However, because Link is too young to use the Sword, he is sealed in the Sacred Realm during seven years, thus awakening as an adult. After he rescues Saria in the Forest Temple, he can return to his childhood by putting the Master Sword back into the Pedestal of Time. From this point, he can freely travel through Time between his childhood and his adulthood. Certain tasks can only be performed as a child, and certain tasks only as an adult. Items such as the Slingshot can only be used by Link as a child, while items such as the Bow can only be used by Link as an adult. In , Link can play the "Song of Time" to go back in time up to the First Day to prevent the Moon from crashing into Termina. Link can also play the "Song of Double Time" in order to travel half day forward to the future. In , using the Harp of Ages given to him by Nayru, the eponymous Oracle of Ages, Link can travel between the present day and 400 years in the past. He can play the Tune of Echoes, Currents, and Ages to open Time Portals or independently flit between eras. If not enough Force Gems are collected by the end of the Stage, the Four Sword sends the four Links back in Time to when the Stage began. As Link is looking for the missing pieces of the Mirror of Twilight in , which is vital to gain access to the Twilight Realm, he finds a Portal that takes him to an ancient version of the Temple of Time. This portal is the Door of Time, the gateway between Hyrule and the Sacred Realm. When Link travels back to the future, the Dominion Rod he find inside the temple is affected in that its magic is inactive in the present, so he must to retrieve its magic in order to progress. In , while in the Lanayru Mine and Lanayru Desert, Link can hit Timeshift Stones to alter time within the immediate vicinity of the stone. When struck, the Timeshift Stones replenish the area in its range, reverting it back to how it looked in the past. Link also must use the Gate of Time to travel to Hylia's Realm, thousands of years prior to his own time. In , while Beneath Hyrule Castle with Link, Zelda travels back in Time to the era of Hyrule's founding using Rauru's Secret Stone. After Link opens the Door of Time at the Temple of Time, he gains access to a mirage of Zelda's Secret Stone which grants him the ability Recall. Recall allows Link to send an Object back through time to its original state.

era of Hyrule's founding using Rauru's Secret Stone. After Link opens the Door of Time at the Temple of Time, he gains access to a mirage of Zelda's Secret Stone which grants him the ability Recall. Recall allows Link to send an Object back through time to its original state. He uses this ability to save Hyrule, and ultimately to return a Draconified Zelda back into her human form. Other Appearances The primary conflict caused by Cia, the War Across the Ages, occurs when the Dark Sorceress opens the Gate of Souls. This allows monsters from across time to congregate in the era of , so that Cia may possess Link's soul. To counteract this, the Hyrulean Forces launch an assault on the Valley of Seers in an attempt to close the Gate of Souls. However, this is a trap set by Cia, as the Dark Sorceress ensnares the Warriors and steals the Triforce of Courage and Wisdom from Link and Sheik, respectively. With all three Triforce pieces in her control, she opens three Gates of Time connecting the current era with the Eras of The Sky, Hero of Time and Twilight, causing key locations from those eras to impose over the normal landscape. Afterwards, the Warriors divide and set out for these three splits in the hopes of sealing the respective Gates of Times. Once the Hyrulean Forces have done so and retrieved the Triforce pieces, they wish away the connection across time, sending home the allies that they employed in their journey.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Tingel Island is located in the Akkala Highlands. It sits above the Lanayru Sea, and it is situated to the north of Ankel Island, Knuckel Island, and Davdi Island. It is connected to Ankel Island by a makeshift bridge, and several Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits are located among its rocky terrain. Kah Mael Shrine is located in a small cave at the center of Tingel Island. However, the entrance is blocked by a stone slab. Link can use the Stasis Rune or Octo Balloons to remove the slab, which allows him to access the Ancient Shrine. On the northern end of Tingel Island is a campsite inhabited by Monsters. Within, there is a Campfire, a Barrel, a Wooden Box, and two metal crates. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on Tingel Island. It is a Flower Trail that starts on the western side of the Island, eventually ending at the peak of a hill. When Link follows the entire Flower Trail, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses Tingle's Hood is a piece of Armor that Link can wear on his head. It is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack. Alongside Tingle's Shirt and Tingle's Tights, it is part of the Tingle's Outfit Armor Set. When all pieces are worn together, Link's speed at night will be increased. Tingle's Hood was stolen from Hyrule Castle with other pieces of Tingle's Outfit by Misko. During the "EX Treasure: Fairy Clothes" Side Quest, Link is tasked with finding Misko's EX Journal to learn where it has been hidden. In the Journal, the Hood is said to be within the "ruins where trade flourished. At the Outpost Ruins, Link can find a Hidden Chest embedded in the ground, which contains Tingle's Hood. After obtaining Tingle's Hood, Granté will begin to sell it from 50 Rupees in Tarrey Town. Tingle's Hood is unable to be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop or upgraded at a Great Fairy Fountain.

is an Item in . Location and Uses Tingle's Shirt can be found as part of the Side Quest "EX Treasure: Fairy Clothes" exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack. It can be found inside a Hidden Chest buried in the ruins of the Castle Town Prison, which can be lifted from the ground with Magnesis. After obtaining it, Granté will begin to sell Tingle's Shirt in Tarrey Town. It's part of Tingle's Outfit along with Tingle's Hood and Tingle's Tights. Tingle's Shirt offers no additional effects on its own or as part of a set. It cannot be enhanced by a Great Fairy, nor can it be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop.

, also known as the , are a recurring Item in . Location and Uses The Tingle Tights are an Outfit in that can be crafted at Madame Couture's after Link has completed the Forest Temple. The Outfit dresses Link in Tingle's signature bodysuit, complete with his clock pendant, rosy cheeks, and facial hair and mole. Wearers of the Tingle Tights begin each Level with three balloons tied to their waists. These balloons save the wearer from losing Health or failing the "Don't fall at all!" Drablands Challenge when falling off ledges. This ability works up to three times per Level, as one balloon will pop after each fall. The ability also works for falling into Lava, but not for falling into Quicksand. Tingle's Tights are only available when Downloadable Content pack is active. After beginning the "EX Treasure: Fairy Clothes" Side Quest, Tingle's Tights can be found in the Mabe Village Ruins. They are part of Tingle's Outfit, along with Tingle's Shirt and Tingle's Hood. Wearing the full Armor Set will give Link the Night Speed Up Set Bonus.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Tireless Frogs are a type of Frog that can be found near ponds in the Lanayru Great Spring and Hyrule Ridge, but they only appear during the Rain. When Link approaches a Tireless Frog, it will run away. To circumvent this, Link can sneak up to them, stun them, or chase after them. Tireless Frogs can be combined with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot to make an Enduring Elixir, which will temporarily increase Link's Stamina when consumed. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Tireless Frogs can be used to make Crimson Dye. Other Appearances

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview After the Decayed Master Sword disappears at the back of the Temple of Time, the Light Dragon rises from the clouds beneath the Great Sky Island, revealing the Surface below. As Link looks down on Lookout Landing, he hears the voice of Zelda telling him to come find her. Upon hearing her voice, "To the Kingdom of Hyrule" Main Quest will begin. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of Purah outside of her Research Lab at Lookout Landing. Text on-screen displays her name, along with the title "Head of Lookout Landing".|Purah's introduction When Link dives from the Temple of Time, he will be able to land in the Water of the Bottomless Pond. From there, he makes his way to Lookout Landing in Hyrule Field. When he reaches the Research Lab, Josha will be shocked to see him and call out to Purah. At this, Purah runs out from inside the Research Lab, asking Link where he has been. While examining Link, she wonders if he is a ghost, though she quickly becomes distracted by his new Right Arm. Removing her goggles, Purah decides to take their encounter one step at a time and asks Link what happened. Upon hearing Link's retelling of the events Beneath Hyrule Castle, Purah reasons that they must have occurred at the start of the Upheaval. She also repeats his story of his time on the Great Sky Island. She is shocked that Link was able to come back to the Surface from the Sky. Recalling that Rauru was the name of the first King of Hyrule, Purah speculates they could be the same individual, but she is still confused. However, she believes that the mummy Beneath Hyrule Castle is related to the Upheaval. She also takes Link hearing Zelda's voice as a sign she is still alive, potentially even trapped Beneath Hyrule Castle. Now that Link has returned, Purah decides that they need his help investigating Hyrule Castle as part of the Search for Princess Zelda. Following their conversation, "To the Kingdom of Hyrule" will be completed, and the "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" Main Quest will begin. Objectives

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview After the "Riju of Gerudo Town" Main Quest is completed, Pokki can be found at the Sand-Seal Rental Shop East Gate Booth talking with Frelly. Link can eavesdrop to hear Pokki ask Frelly if any of her customers have seen ruins with large statues facing each other. Frelly comments on how there are a number of ruins throughout Gerudo Desert and asks if Pokki has a map or any other information to clarify which ruins she is talking about. Pokki complains that she used to have a map, but it was carried off by the wind and lost, and now the only thing she remembers is that the ruins are somewhere in the eastern desert. Frelly tries to think longer, but notices Link standing nearby and apologizes to Pokki stating that she needs to get back to work. This starts the Side Quest, "To the Ruins!" Pokki can then be found pacing nearby, pondering what she can do to get to the ruins. If Link speaks with her, she will ask him if he has ever seen the ruins she was talking to Frelly about. She asks if Link could take her to the ruins on a Sleigh Seal for a reward. If Link declines, she says it is not a big deal since most Gerudo do not even know about the ruins. If Link agrees to take her, she will wait by the East Gate to the town. Link can rent a Sleigh Seal from either the Sand-Seal Rental Shop East Gate Booth or the Sand-Seal Rental Shop West Gate Booth on the other of Gerudo Town. Objectives

are Items in . Location and Uses Toasted Big Hearty Truffles are a type of Roasted Food, and they are made when Big Hearty Truffles are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They have better nutrition and a greater aroma than a regular Big Hearty Truffle. Eating a Toasted Big Hearty Truffle restores four and a half Hearts to Link's Life Gauge. Toasted Big Hearty Truffles reappear in and are again a variety of Roasted Food. They can created by allowing Big Hearty Truffles to come into contact with Fire or a Scorching Climate. They are known for both their aroma and their nutrition. By eating a Toasted Big Hearty Truffle, Link will heal four and a half Hearts in his Life Gauge.

are Items in . Location and Uses Toasted Hearty Truffles are a variety of Roasted Food, and they can be made by exposing Hearty Truffles to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Their outsides are known to be crispy, while their insides are warm and gooey. Eating one restores three Hearts to Link's Life Gauge. Toasted Hearty Truffles reappear in and are again a variety of Roasted Food. Link can make them by dropping Hearty Truffles near Fire or in a Scorching Climate. Although they are known to be crispy and delicious, many consider Cooking Hearty Truffles into Food to be more effective. If Link eats a Toasted Hearty Truffle, he will regain three of his Life Gauge's Hearts.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Toasty Chillshrooms are a variety of Roasted Food. Link can make Toasty Chillshrooms by burning Chillshrooms with Fire or a Scorching Climate. They are noted to taste better after being toasted. Eating a Toasty Chillshroom will restore three-quarters of a Heart to Link. Toasty Chillshrooms return in and are again a variety of Roasted Food. Link can make them by dropping Chillshrooms near a Fire or in a Scorching Climate. When compared to regular Chillshrooms, Toasty Chillshrooms are known to taste better. If Link eats a Toasty Chillshroom, it will restore three-quarters of one of his Hearts.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Toasty Endura Shrooms are a type of Roasted Food, and they can be made by burning Endura Shrooms with Fire or a Scorching Climate. While they do not grant special effects, they are still considered to be delicious. When eaten, Toasty Endura Shrooms restore one and a half Hearts to Link. Toasty Endura Shrooms reappear in as a variety of Roasted Food. Link can make them by exposing Endura Shrooms to Fire or a Scorching Climate. They are widely considered to be delicious, despite providing no additional effects. Eating a Toasty Endura Shroom will heal Link by one and a half Hearts.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Toasty Ironshrooms are a type of Roasted Food, and they are made when Ironshrooms are burned using a Fire or a Scorching Climate. The exterior of Toasty Ironshrooms is noted to be crunchy. Eating one will restore three-quarters of one of Link's Hearts. Toasty Ironshrooms reappear in as a variety of Roasted Food. Link can make them by dropping Ironshrooms near Fire or in a Scorching Climate. Instead of being tough like a regular Ironshroom, the exterior of Toasty Ironshrooms are known to be crunchy and tasty. If Link eats one, he will restore three-quarters of a Heart.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Toasty Rushrooms are a type of Roasted Food. Link can make Toasty Rushrooms by burning Rushrooms with Fire or a Scorching Climate. Though the special speed-boosting abilities of Rushrooms are lost in the process of roasting, their taste is improved. They restore three-quarters of a Heart to Link when eaten. Toasty Rushrooms reappear in and are again a variety of Roasted Food. They can be made by exposing Rushrooms to Fire or a Scorching Climate. The process of creating Toasty Rushrooms improves their taste, although they lose their speed-boosting effects. When Link eats a Toasty Rushroom, will be healed by three-quarters of a Heart.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Toasty Silent Shrooms are a type of Roasted Food. Link can make Toasty Silent Shrooms by burning Silent Shrooms with Fire or a Scorching Climate. While they have lost their glowing properties, they are noted to be fragrant. When Link eats a Toasty Silent Shroom, he will heal three-quarters of a Heart. Toasty Silent Shrooms reappear in and are again a variety of Roasted Food. They can be made by allowing Silent Shrooms to come into contact with Fire or a Scorching Climate. Toasty Silent Shrooms are known to be delicious and fragrant, although they no longer glow in the dark. Eating a Toasty Silent Shroom will restore three-quarters of one of Link's Hearts.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Toasty Stamella Shrooms are a type of Roasted Food, and they are made by burning Stamella Shrooms with Fire or a Scorching Climate. Having lost the special properties of Stamella Shrooms, Toasty Stamella Shrooms are only capable of healing. They restore three-quarters of a Heart to Link when eaten. Toasty Stamella Shrooms reappear in and are again a variety of Roasted Food. They can be made by exposing Stamella Shrooms to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Due to the roasting process, they have lost their Stamina-boosting abilities and can only proving healing. If Link eats a Toasty Stamella Shroom, he can heal three-quarters of a Heart.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Toasty Sunshrooms are a type of Roasted Food, and they can be made by exposing Sunshrooms to Fire or a Scorching Climate. It is considered a good idea to keep at least one Toasty Sunshroom on hand for emergencies. They restore three-quarters of a Heart to Link when eaten. Toasty Sunshrooms reappear in and are again a variety of Roasted Food. They can be made by exposing Sunshrooms to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Many residents of Hyrule prefer to keep Toasty Sunshrooms on hand in the event of an emergency. When Link eats a Toasty Sunshroom, he will heal three-quarters of a Heart.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Toasty Zapshrooms are a variety of Roasted Food. Link can make Toasty Zapshrooms by burning Zapshrooms with Fire or a Scorching Climate. A completely roasted Toasty Zapshroom is considered to be delicious. When eaten, they restore three-quarters of a Heart to Link's Life Gauge. Toasty Zapshrooms return in as a variety of Roasted Food. They are made when Zapshrooms come into contact with Fire or a Scorching Climate. Toasty Zapshrooms are thought by many to be delicious. They can restore three-quarters of a Heart to Link's Life Gauge if they are eaten.

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Tobio's Hollow Cave is located west of Tobio's Hollow in East Necluda. Legends state that the Zonai placed a treasure within. The Cave consists of a passage that leads to a large central chamber containing a body of northeast-flowing Water, and a tunnel leading north from the central chamber to a Bubbulfrog. This central chamber contains a Zonai Technology pedestal that glows green when stood on, next to an abandoned campsite with an extinguished Campfire, a Tattered Notebook, and two Zonaite Spears. A column of rock with a ring-shaped hole in it is located on an islet in the Water. If a Zonaite Spear with a Wing Zonai Device or Monster Wing Fused to it is thrown through the ring while Link stands on the pedestal, Utojis Shrine will rise out of the ground within the chamber. Areas Creatures Enemies Equipment Materials

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Tobio's Hollow Chasm is a Chasm that is located on the northern end of Tobio's Hollow in East Necluda. Its interior is a long tunnel, which leads directly to the Construct Factory in the Faron Grasslands Depths. It is the only Chasm that is artificially created, and since it did not appear as a result of the Upheaval, no Gloom can be found in its vicinity. Originally, the structure that contains the Tobio's Hollow Chasm is embedded in the ground and covered by an Owl Statue. During the Main Quest "Guidance from Ages Past", the Zonai Relic guides Link to the Owl Statue, resulting in the structure rising from the ground. When he places the Zonai Relic on top of the pedestal inside, a platform will descend through the Chasm and into the Depths, eventually bringing him to the Construct Factory.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview As Link talks to Burmano in the Emergency Shelter for the first time, the latter immediately realizes the fresh face. He says he is also a newcomer and therefore in charge of Cooking. In order to Cook a fancy dish he needs an Apple but is out of them. If Link has one of them with him he asks for it, as he can detect it with his nose. If Link denies it, he agrees, but promises a Fruit and Mushroom Mix in exchange for an Apple. When given an Apple he Cooks said dish and explains the Cooking. This completes the Cooking and Burmano distributes his meal amongst Link and the other people, who loved it. Later Burmano is missing and Deon explains that he went to Hyrule Castle's Dining Hall in order to find a super-special Cooking. Objectives

is a recurring character in . Biography Toffa is an elderly man who works at the Outskirt Stable. He can be found near the eastern entrance of the Stable, muttering to himself. When Link first encounters Toffa, he will ask Link if he has seen a White Horse before telling him that it has been seen on the nearby Safula Hill. As Toffa's grandfather told him that the Royal Family of Hyrule once had a pure-white Horse that grazed on Safula Hill, he suspects that this white Horse may be a descendant of the Royal Family's Horse. He then asks Link to catch the white Horse and, after domesticating it and registering it at a Stable, to show it to him. If Link agrees, Toffa will thank him and task him with the Side Quest "The Royal White Stallion," although warning him of the Horse's elusiveness. If Link denies this request, Toffa will dejectedly say that it was likely a "wild-goose" chase. If Link returns with the white Horse before registering it at a Stable, Toffa will grow excited and urge him to register it and return immediately. Additionally, after seeing the white Horse, Toffa will begin to mutter about it. Upon returning with the white Horse after its registration, Toffa will exclaim with joy and gift Link the Royal Bridle and Royal Saddle as thanks and immediately equip it to the white Horse. Toffa explains that the Royal Bridle and Saddle were custom-made for Zelda's white Horse and that his grandfather claimed the sight of the Princess atop the Horse was indescribably beautiful. Afterwards, Toffa describes his fantasy of riding around atop the white Horse with a woman like the Princess.

Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|The interior of Tokiy Shrine The Tokiy Shrine is a simple Shrine of Light with the sole purpose of rewarding Link for reaching it. It bears a lone pathway in a void marked only by a Stone Chest. A Rauru and Sonia Statue can be found at the end of Tokiy Shrine. By interacting with the Terminal in front of the Statue, Link can receive a Light of Blessing to cleanse the corruption of Darkness from within him.

is a recurring character in . Biography Tokk is an elderly man who lives in a farmhouse just under the hill where the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab sits. He usually spends his time sitting on a stool out by an Apple Tree in his yard. Tokk is not a forthcoming man, often sighing when spoken to. Link can ask to speak to Tokk about a few different topics. Should the hero ask about the Great Calamity, Tokk wonders if Uma may have put him up to this. Although he sees no real reason behind Link's curiosity, Tokk relinquishes what he learned about the Calamity from his father. He tells Link about how Hyrule Castle was "contaminated" and how the Great Calamity wiped out nearly everything. Tokk is thankful that Hateno Village managed to survive the disaster due to its far-off location. Tokk also recalls that someone attempted to put an end to the Calamity, but he is quick to dismiss the entire topic as irrelevant. If Link asks about the place he is in, Tokk at first believes he is inquiring about the farm. However, he is quick to realize that Link likely means the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab above them and tells him that a member of the Sheikah tribe, Purah, is conducting research there. Link can ask who Tokk himself is, but the elder will humbly admit he is naught but an old man. At 5:00 AM, Tokk wakes up to go to his usual stool outside. He will not discuss anything until he has a seat. Should it rain while he is outside, he will sit inside until it stops. At 9:00 PM, he considers the day to be over and goes to bed.

is a recurring character in . Biography Before Link travels to Zora's Domain for the first time, Tona finds Link at the base of Zora River near Lanayru Tower. She is swimming in the Water and calls out to him. She encourages Link to meet Sidon at Inogo Bridge upstream. After Divine Beast Vah Ruta is freed, she can be found on the second level of the domain chatting with Tula and Laruta about Sidon, staying there from about 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM. When talked to, she thanks Link for helping Sidon and wishes that her older brother Cleff would be like him. Then, she walks up a flight of stairs to the start of a pathway leading to the edge of the domain. While she is talked to, she thinks about going to see Sidon, and then thanks Link again for his help. At 12:00 AM, she walks to the Sleeping Chamber and sleeps until 8:00.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Topazes can be found by destroying Ore Deposits and Rare Ore Deposits, as well as by defeating Stone Taluses (Rare). The travelling merchant Kairo and the store Ore and More both sell Topazes for differing amounts. They're a precious gem that are said to have the power of electricity. The jewelry shop Starlight Memories requires five Topazes as payment for the Topaz Earrings. In addition, the merchant Ramella in Goron City will occasionally ask for Topazes, paying more than the regular price. The Kochi Dye Shop also accepts Topazes as an ingredient for Yellow Dye. Topazes are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Topazes return in . They can be Fused to Arrows to charge them with Electricity. Topazes are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Topaz Earrings are a type of Accessory, specifically being Earrings that can be clipped onto Link's ears. They can be purchased at the Starlight Memories Jewelry Shop in Gerudo Town for 500 Rupees and five Topazes. Alternatively, at the end of the "Tools of the Trade" Side Quest, one of the Accessories that Isha offers Link as a reward are the Topaz Earrings. When worn, Topaz Earrings provide Link with one level of Shock Resistance. Topaz Earrings can be enhanced by a Great Fairy at a Great Fairy Fountain. However, they cannot be Dyed at the Kochi Dye Shop. Enhancing Enhancing Other Appearances

is a recurring character in . Biography Toren can be found at the Tabantha Bridge Stable, either sitting down at the table inside or standing near the stable outside. When approached, he will be lost in thought, thinking of the Great Fairy. When Link talks to him, he will snap out of it and tell Link of the Great Fairy Kaysa. He explains that he is on a journey to find her. Toren tells Link that beyond the Tabantha Great Bridge, there is a tower, that at the right time of day, will cast a shadow pointing to the Great Fairy's location. He tells Link that he's stuck at the stable, as he cannot climb the tower. Afterwards, he asks Link if he would be willing to make an offering of rupees to the Great Fairy for him, starting the side quest, "A Gift for the Great Fairy". Additionally, he gives Link 500 Rupees to offer to the Great Fairy Kaysa. Toren has become the captain of the Monster-Control Crew, Squad Two. He now wears a worn-out piece of Soldier's Armor. During the search for Zelda and Link at Hyrule Castle, Toren can be found alongside Hoz on top of the First Gatehouse. When Link is speaking to Hoz during the "Crisis at Hyrule Castle" Main Quest, Toren interrupts their conversation to point out a sighting of Zelda nearby. He witnesses the figure turn into Light and fly away, which he is confused by.

is a recurring character in . Biography Torfeau is a Zora and a guard of Zora's Domain who wields a Zora Spear. When the domain was under threat of being flooded, Sidon dispatched multiple Zora to find help, Torfeau being one of them. She meets Link by the Soh Kofi Shrine and directs him to the nearby Inogo Bridge, where Sidon waits for a Hylian to assist him in saving Zora's Domain. When Link makes it to Zora's Domain, Torfeau will recognize him and be relieved to hear he'll help them appease Divine Beast Vah Ruta. After Vah Ruta has been calmed, Torfeau will ask Link to defeat the Hinox at Ralis Pond. Agreeing to this unlocks the Side Quest "The Giant of Ralis Pond". When the Hinox is defeated, she will thank Link and give him 100 rupees.

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Torin Wetland is located in the Akkala Highlands. The marsh is peppered with Guardian remains and a few ruins among the Trees. Three of them are still active, though one is a Decayed Guardian, bereft of its legs. Defeating them at least once is the goal of the "Hobbies of the Rich" Side Quest that Hagie assigns Link. The travelers Stamm and Lonni can be found walking along the road through Torin Wetland. Luminous Stone Deposits can be found at the base of the cliff in the southern reaches of the Wetland. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Toronbo Beach is located along the northwestern shore of Eventide Island in the Necluda Sea. Several Palm Trees grow from its sands, and a Raft can be found at its southern end. If Toronbo Beach is the first part of Eventide Island that Link lands on, he will be stopped by the voice of Korgu Chideh, challenging him to offer the three Ancient Orbs on the Island to the Pedestals. All of Link's Items will be taken away, and the "Stranded on Eventide" Shrine Quest will begin. One of these Pedestals is located off the northern shore of Toronbo Beach. Using the Cryonis Rune, Link can carry an Ancient Orb from the Beach and place it in the Concave Slot. A small Monster Stronghold can be found in the center of Toronbo Beach. It contains two metal crates, which can be broken open for supplies, and a Campfire with Roasted Basses Cooking alongside it. There is also a wooden Treasure Chest that contains a Traveler's Sword. An additional metal Treasure Chest is located on the south end of Toronbo Beach. It is embedded in the ground, requiring Link to pull it up using the Magnesis Rune. When he does so, he will be able to open it and receive the Soldier's Shield inside. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Toronbo Beach returns in . The Eventide Island Chasm has opened on its northern end. A campsite has been set up by Sesami nearby, consisting of a Tent, a Cooking Pot, and an accompanying Campfire.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Toto Lake is a small lake in the Lanayru Great Spring, and it is located atop Upland Zorana. It feeds into South Lake Akkala through a Waterfall at its northeastern end. Partially submerged Zonai Ruins can be seen at the center of the Lake. Prior to Divine Beast Vah Ruta being calmed, Toto Lake will be subjected to its constant Rainfall. To honor Link following the Great Calamity}, the Zora Helm that he won for defeating the Lynel on Ploymus Mountain was placed in Toto Lake. In the Water of Toto Lake, a Metal Chest containing the Zora Helm can be found. To pull it to the surface, Link must use the Magnesis Rune. In Master Mode, a platform suspended by Sky Octoroks floats just above the Waterfall. Upon it is a second Metal Chest containing a Silver Shield. Creature Enemies Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Tottika is a soldier and guard for Zora's Domain. He wields a Silverscale Spear and guards the right-side stairs to King Dorephan's throne. Tottika tells Link about the existence of the Master Sword, and then adds that he wishes to become a great warrior worthy of being chosen by a weapon. When talked to after Divine Beast Vah Ruta is freed and the continuous rain ends, he thanks Link for his service. If talked to afterwards, he thanks Link again, saying that the elders will forgive him for Mipha's death and no longer look down on him. If Link attacks him with a melee Weapon, Tottika knocks him back without dealing any damage; if Tottika is attacked with Electricity, he staggers backwards as the Zora are weak to the element.

"" is a Main Quest in . Overview After Link views the "Critical Decisions" Memory during "Guidance from Ages Past", Mineru informs hims that Zelda undertook a forbidden process the restore the Master Sword for him. She directs him to meet with the Great Deku Tree for help finding it, as Zelda wanted him to. She assures Link that the Master Sword is the key to defeating Demon King Ganondorf. Afterwards, "Guidance from Ages Past" will be completed, and the "Trail of the Master Sword" Main Quest will begin. When Link returns to Purah to report Mineru reawakening as the Sage of Spirit, she is relieved to hear news about Zelda, though she is saddened that she had to restore the Master Sword all on her own. Purah believes that the Master Sword must be somewhere in the present day, and she tells him that the Great Deku Tree can be found within the Great Hyrule Forest. Whenever Link attempts to walk through the Lost Woods, he will be overcome by fog and automatically returned to his point of entry. If Link tries to enter the Lost Woods from their southeastern entrance, Peeks will stop him and explain that it is impossible to reach Korok Forest without getting lost. He also shares that a Chasm has opened in the Minshi Woods, which frightens him. At the Minshi Woods Chasm, Link will find Tasho, who explains that the Koroks they were walking with jumped into the Chasm thinking they could find a way back to Korok Forest. In Minshi Grove at the bottom of the Chasm, Link can meet Nako and Mopu. Nako has become frightened of the Depths. When Link approaches Mopu, they ask if he needs directions to Korok Forest. If asked for further details, they point Link to the north. Along the way, Link can meet with Mokka, who identifies that fog on the roof of the Depths as being from the Lost Woods. Lastly, at the center of Korok Grove, Link can meet Jatora and Maheli, who have figured out that they are beneath Korok Forest and are trying to find a way to the Surface. thumb|left|250px|alt= A screenshot of the Great Deku Tree in Korok Forest, which is covered in a red fog. Text on-screen introduces him as the "Deku Tree", ascribing him the title "Great Spirit of Korok Forest".|The Great Deku Tree's introduction If Link Ascends through the Ascend Access Point at the base of the Great Deku Tree, he will emerge within Korok Forest. He finds that the Great Deku Tree appears unwell, with Gloom seeping out of his mouth. Inside the Great Deku Tree's Navel, he will find the Deku Tree Chasm, at the bottom of which is a mass of Gloom Spawn. Upon defeating the Gloom Spawn, a Phantom Ganon will appear and begin to attack Link as well. Once the Phantom Ganon has been defeated, all of the Gloom will disappear from the Great Deku Tree. A group of three Koroks

the bottom of which is a mass of Gloom Spawn. Upon defeating the Gloom Spawn, a Phantom Ganon will appear and begin to attack Link as well. Once the Phantom Ganon has been defeated, all of the Gloom will disappear from the Great Deku Tree. A group of three Koroks descend before Link, who thank him for saving Korok Forest. They also inform him that the Great Deku Tree is waiting for him on the Surface. When Link stands before the Great Deku Tree, he thanks Link for helping him despite still feeling groggy. He thinks back to the last time they met with one another, which starts "The Master Sword's Power" Memory. After the Memory ends, the Great Deku Tree notices that Link is no longer in possession of the Master Sword. Hearing that Link has lost it, the Great Deku Tree reveals that he can sense the Master Sword. A glowing Marker appears on Link's Map, marking the Sword's location. However, he notices that it appears to be moving through the Sky. Following this conversation, "Trail of the Master Sword" will be completed, and "Recovering the Hero's Sword" will start. Objectives

Training Constructs are Enemies in . Characteristics Training Constructs are a unique type of Captain Construct. Their purpose is to train individuals who enter Shrines of Light. Like other Captain Constructs, they are capable of Fusing various Items and Objects onto their Weapons. Training Constructs are always inactive until Link approaches them. During combat with a Training Construct, a Mysterious Voice instructs Link to do various different attacks based on the Shrine he is in. In certain Shrines, the Training Construct will not move until its second phase. The Construct will try to shoot Link with its Construct Bow in some Shrines, but in others it will swing its Rusty Broadsword or Zonaite Sword at Link. In some Shrines, Link will have to throw a weapon at the Construct when it is on a high platform. It could be on the middle of the main room, where Link has to do Flurry Rushes and Spin Attacks to subdue it. In others, Link must shoot it from above with a Bow. In all Shrines, only the attacks that Link is learning will do damage.

are recurring Items in . Traveler's Bows go unnamed in . Location and Uses Traveler's Bows are weak ranged Bows commonly used by travelers for protection. Though they do not deal much damage, they can be used to attack Enemies at a distance. They are most commonly found in Hyrule Field and West Necluda, where they are either wielded by Enemies or hidden in Treasure Chests. The following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Traveler's Bow when they are scanned with the amiibo Rune: Series Zelda amiibo Series Link (Archer) amiibo Series Revali amiibo Being made of wood, Traveler's Bows are flammable, and they will therefore burn if exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. However, they are not magnetic, so they cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. They do not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, but they will float if they are dropped in Water. Traveler's Bows belong to the Traveler's Gear archetype of equipment, which are all said to be used to defend travelers throughout Hyrule. A Traveler's Bow is part of an unnamed set of equipment used by Link in promotional media, alongside a Soldier's Broadsword and a Traveler's Shield. Traveler's Bows are Bows in . Other Appearances Link uses the Traveler's Bow as his neutral special move in . Like in , when Link fires an Arrow, it lingers on the ground. Link can then pick it up and throw it at opponents or draw two Arrows, which deal double damage when loosed.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses A Traveler's Bridle is a Bridle and a piece of Horse Gear. It has a chance to appear in a pair of Treasure Chest that spawn when the Link (Rider) amiibo is scanned with the amiibo Rune. One Treasure Chest will contain the Traveler's Bridle, while the other Chest will contain the Traveler's Saddle. Once obtained, the Traveler's Bridle will appear in Link's Key Item Inventory. Link can have it equipped on his Horses by speaking to specific workers at Highland Stable, Outskirt Stable, South Akkala Stable, and Woodland Stable. However, they are unable to be equipped onto Epona or the Giant Horse. Though its design does not stand out, it is favored among peddlers and travelers for suiting any type of Horse. In his Recovered Memories, Link is shown to have a Traveler's Bridle and Traveler's Saddle equipped to his Horse before the second Great Calamity.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Traveler's Claymores are two-handed Weapons commonly used by aspiring adventurers. They are hefty enough to knock the Shield out of Enemies' hands. These Claymores can be found abandoned in Hyrule Field and West Necluda. They are also carried by the Swordswomen Statues in the Gerudo Desert. When scanned with the amiibo Rune, the following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Traveler's Claymore: Series Young Link amiibo Series Ganondorf amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Young Link () amiibo Series Daruk amiibo Traveler's Claymores, since they are made of metal, will attract Lightning when equipped during Thunderstorms and conduct Electricity. However, they will sink if they are dropped in Water. They can be picked up using the Magnesis Rune, and they will not burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. Traveler's Claymores belong to the Traveler's Gear archetype of Weapons, which is used for defense by the travelers of Hyrule. Traveler's Claymores appear in . Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Traveler's Saddle is a type of Saddle and Horse Gear. It can be obtained from a pair of Treasure Chests that appear when the Link (Rider) amiibo is scanned with the amiibo Rune. One of the Treasure Chests will contain the Traveler's Saddle, while the other Chest will contain the Traveler's Bridle. Once obtained, the Traveler's Saddle will appear in Link's Key Item Inventory. Link can equip it to any Horse he has a maximum Bond with by talking to specific workers at Highland Stable, Outskirt Stable, South Akkala Stable, or Woodland Stable. However, like other Saddles, they cannot be used by Epona or the Giant Horse. Traveler's Saddles were designed for comfort and hold strong throughout all sorts of Weather, which has lead to them being favored by travelers. In his Recovered Memories, Link is shown to have a Traveler's Bridle and Traveler's Saddle equipped to his Horse before the second Great Calamity.

are recurring Items in . Traveler's Shields go unnamed in . Location and Uses Traveler's Shields are simple, mid-grade Shields. They are beloved by many travelers and are used for protection against weak monsters and Creatures. The Traveler's Shield is also a part of an unnamed set of equipment used by Link in promotional media, alongside a Soldier's Broadsword and a Traveler's Bow. There are many places to find a Traveler's Shield, most notably at enemy camps on the beaches surrounding Hyrule Field and West Necluda. They are also given out by Selmie as a reward for completing the Shield-Surfing Mini-Game with a time between 2:30 and 2:45. The following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Traveler's Shield when they are scanned with the amiibo Rune: Series Link amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Toon Zelda () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Zelda amiibo Series Urbosa amiibo Being made from Wood, Traveler's Shields will start to burn if exposed to a Fire. Since they are not made of metal, they do not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning when equipped during a Thunderstorm, and can not be manipulated using the Magnesis Rune. When dropped into Water, Traveler's Shields will float. Traveler's Shields belong to the Traveler's Gear archetype of equipment, which are all said to be used to defend travelers throughout Hyrule Kingdom. A Traveler's Shield is part of an unnamed set of equipment used by Link in promotional media, alongside a Soldier's Broadsword and a Traveler's Bow. Traveler's Shields reappear in . Other Appearances Traveler's Shields can be wielded by Link in conjunction with Traveler's Swords.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Traveler's Spears are Weapons utilized by travelers to defend themselves from wild Animals. They are noted to be easy to hold and simple to use. They are commonly found in Hyrule Field and West Necluda. When scanned with the amiibo Rune, the following amiibo have a chance to spawn a Treasure Chest containing a Traveler's Spear: Series Link () amiibo Series Mipha amiibo Being made of metal, Traveler's Spears will conduct Electricity and attract Lightning when they are equipped during a Thunderstorm, though they will not burn when exposed to a Fire or a Scorching Climate. They can also be picked up using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate. Finally, they will sink if they are dropped in Water. Traveler's Spears belong to the equipment archetype known as Traveler's Gear, which is utilized for self-defense by travelers. Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Locations and Uses In , Traveler's Swords are a common, weak sword often used by travelers to defeat small Enemies. Though it is fairly durable, it is unreliable due to its low attack power. They are often found in Hyrule Field and West Necluda, either abandoned or in use by Monsters. Traveler's Swords can also be obtained by using the amiibo Rune to scan the following amiibo: Series Link amiibo Series Young Link amiibo Series Toon Link amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Toon Link () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link () amiibo Series Link (Rider) amiibo Series Urbosa amiibo During "The Weapon Connoisseur" Side Quest, Nebb in Hateno Village will ask Link to bring him several different Weapons to see. The first Weapon he asks for is a Traveler's Sword. As a reward for bringing him a Traveler's Sword, Nebb gives Link a Red Rupee. Traveler's Swords are made from metal and will therefore attract Lightning if they are equipped during a Thunderstorm, and they will also conduct Electricity. They are magnetic, which means they can be picked up and manipulated using the Magnesis Rune on the Sheikah Slate. If they are dropped in the Water, they will sink. Traveler's Swords art part of the Traveler's Gear archetype of equipment, which is known to be used by travelers for self-defense. Other Appearances

are recurring characters in . Biography Travelers are members of the Yiga Clan in disguise who can be found scattered along roadsides throughout Hyrule Kingdom after one of two possible conditions are met: either by completing the "Seek Out Impa" Main Quest, or by entering the Yiga Clan Hideout. They assume the appearance of both Hylian men or women who travel the roads of Hyrule Kingdom and call to Link whenever he is nearby to engage in conversation. If Link speaks to them, they will direct the discussion towards Link's demise before dropping their disguise and attacking as Yiga Footsoldiers. If Link speaks to Travelers after defeating Master Kohga, they will reference the fact that Kohga was slain by him and assail him in their late leader's name. Travelers will not seek shelter during a rainstorm, though they will run from other Enemies. They do not reward Link if he rescues them, only instead opting to resume their plan to assassinate him. Some Travelers will attempt to sell Link their Mighty Bananas, a fruit which all Yiga are obsessed with. If Link initially denies the offer to look at their wares, they will insist that he buys from them. Rejecting the offer a second time will anger the Traveler, prompting him to attack. These Travelers carry 99 Mighty Bananas at 99 Rupees per bundle. If Link purchases all of the Mighty Bananas, the Traveler will refer to him as a "banana fan" and announce that he has nothing left to sell. When the transaction is done, the Traveler will claim to hope to see Link again, only to admit his lie and attack. Other Appearances A character known simply as a Traveler appears in a bonus chapter of . He is a hero from a faraway land who came to Termina and met Majora, who takes on the form of a beast. The creature, believing that the warrior wants its magical armor so that he may have his heart's desire, intends to kill the Traveler. However, the Traveler produces a drum and begins playing it. Entranced by the music, Majora begins to dance for three days straight. Upon the completion of the third day, the creature dies from exhaustion. The Traveler then crafts a Mask from its armor.

is a recurring character in . Biography Tray is the innkeeper of the Rollin' Inn in Goron City, which he runs alongside Volcon. Tray manages the Inn's front desk, where he offers customers a bed for 20 Rupees or a bed and a Goron-style massage for 80 Rupees. Tray highly recommends the Goron massages, which Volcon gives, stating that it rejuvenates the body and admitting that he even sometimes falls asleep during it. Whichever option Link chooses, he can decide to sleep until morning, noon, or night, and if he decides to get a massage, he will regain all of his Hearts, along with three temporary Hearts if he does not already have 20 and a temporary Stamina Wheel. Since Tray does not go outside, he is not bothered by the Divine Beast Vah Rudania's Magma Bombs. When Link bids Tray farewell, he is told not to overwork himself. Tray is retiring from running the Rollin' Inn and is passing it on to the former Ripped and Shredded shopkeeper, Pyle.

is a recurring character in . Biography Traysi is a Hylian investigative journalist who can be found researching her next story in Gerudo Town. She is the author of the Rumor Mill, which she claims is Hyrule's leading news publication. Traysi traveled to Gerudo Town after hearing of the Town's recent troubles and even hints at her own experience with the Divine Beast Vah Naboris. Link can first encounter Traysi while she is speaking with the Gerudo guard Ploka. Ploka is denying Traysi access to the Gerudo Town palace, though Traysi vows to keep trying. If Link speaks to Traysi, she tells him that she is busy gathering information. If Link asks her about the information, she expresses disbelief if Link says he has never heard of it, claiming that he is lying. Traysi exclaims that she is an award-winning journalist and that Link cannot hide anything from her. If Link says that he has heard of the Rumor Mill, Traysi is relieved, unsure how she would react. Either way, she reassures confidence in herself and hopes that Link enjoys reading her publication. After continually being denied entry to the palace, Traysi becomes agitated and questions why Ploka finds her suspicious. After Link speaks with Lady Riju, Traysi can be found standing on the Town wall overlooking the Gerudo Desert and taking notes. When she notices Link, Traysi pauses and tells him she is investigating rumors of the Divine Beast Vah Naboris. Traysi reveals she is interested in writing about the Divine Beast and mentions how much money she could make by covering the story. When Link asks her about her progress, she notes that the two large humps on the Beast's back seem to be generating electric current. Traysi also notes that there may be an entrance underneath the Beast's tail, but warns that gaining access may be difficult due to the height of the entrance and the lightning around the Beast. She suggests it would be easier to access the Beast if someone were to trip the Beast by entangling its legs. Traysi then abruptly ends the conversation and suggests Link should gather his own information. Once Link has calmed the Divine Beast Vah Naboris, Traysi wanders around Gerudo Town in search of a new story. She decides to write a book about the Gerudo people. Traysi takes notes while speaking with several characters and offers to share bits of information with Link. Traysi mentions that the average Gerudo is about the same height as a Voltfruit tree and weighs as much as ten Hydromelons. While analyzing Ashai's relationship class, Traysi expresses surprise about the Gerudo peoples' serious demeanor. While interviewing the male Gorons, Strade and Lyndae, she remarks that male Gorons seem to easily enter Gerudo Town, even though males are forbidden. Traysi also notes that Lover's Pond can be a "double-edged sword" while chatting with Muava. Seven volumes of the Rumor Mill can be found scattered throughout Hyrule. Each volume covers a topic of local gossip,

remarks that male Gorons seem to easily enter Gerudo Town, even though males are forbidden. Traysi also notes that Lover's Pond can be a "double-edged sword" while chatting with Muava. Seven volumes of the Rumor Mill can be found scattered throughout Hyrule. Each volume covers a topic of local gossip, which are discussed and recommended by Traysi using a 1 through 5 star-scale rating. In the first volume, found in Kakariko Village's Armor Shop, Enchanted, Traysi covers the legend of Lover's Pond. She details a rumor of "The Sword that Seals the Darkness" hiding in a forest in her second volume which can be read at Rito Stable. The third volume can be found inside Outskirt Stable. In it, Traysi tells readers about Koroks that can be spotted all throughout the land. Star Fragments from "Falling Stars" are the topic of the fourth volume, located at East Akkala Stable. At Wetland Stable, the fifth volume covers recent sightings of the Dragons Dinraal, Farosh and Naydra. The sixth volume can be found at Lakeside Stable. In that publication, Traysi recalls a story about a hunter shooting an arrow at a Blupee, a glowing rabbit-like creature, only to find Rupees where the creature had been. At Kara Kara Bazaar's Inn, the seventh and final volume of the Rumor Mill details Hyrule Castle, including a secret room formerly used by King Rhoam as well as Princess Zelda's laboratory. In The Master Trials DLC Pack, Link can find two volumes of Super Rumor Mill EX, which details some of the items included in the DLC. The first volume can be found at Woodland Stable and discusses the Korok Mask.. The second volume, which mentions the Travel Medallion, can be found in South Akkala Stable. In The Champions' Ballad DLC Pack, Link can find two more volumes of Super Rumor Mill EX, which details some of the items included with the DLC. The third volume of the series can be found in the Highland Stable, while the fourth volume can be found in the Riverside Stable. In addition, Traysi plays a part in the "EX Champion Urbosa's Song" Main Quest of The Champions' Ballad. After activating the Monument at the East Gerudo Mesa, Link can find Traysi on a mesa in the East Barrens of the Gerudo Desert. If Link approaches her dressed as a man, she expresses surprise and asks if he is the "pretty gal" she saw in Gerudo Town. Link reacts in surprise and Traysi continues to compliment him for cleverly sneaking into Gerudo Town and promises not to report this gossip. Link then scratches the back of his head and Traysi goes on to say that she is tracking down some gossip and decides to tell Link about the rumor. Traysi explains that just when the Desert seemed calm after Naboris had settled, a mysterious type of Molduga appeared. gossip and decides to tell Link about the rumor. Traysi explains that just when the Desert seemed calm after Naboris had settled, a mysterious type of Molduga appeared. She says that the Gerudo soldiers attempted to fight it, but their weapons were ineffective. Traysi then wonders what kind of weapon would work against the Molduga. This Molduga, known as Molduking, is found right next to the mesa where Traysi stands. If Link speaks to Traysi again after defeating the Molduking, she says that she saw the fight and is surprised that Link was able to defeat it. Traysi then asks if she may write a report about Link. Link declines and Traysi says that he would have had a lot of female attention and fans. As a result, Traysi decides to investigate Gerudo Town for a more interesting story. According to Super Rumor Mill EX: Volume 4, Traysi reveals she hopes that the kingdom of Hyrule is one day restored in the hopes that a Royal Guard in shining armor will come and sweep her off her feet. Traysi has founded the Lucky Clover Gazette.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Treasure Octoroks are a type of Octorok that lives in sandy and snowy areas. They bury themselves in the sand or snow disguised as a buried Treasure Chest, jumping out if close enough. They then burrow back into the ground, digging away from Link. Their Treasure Chests are not magnetic, therefore, they cannot be pulled out with the Magnesis Rune. If struck with a Remote Bomb, they will pop out of the ground confused, leaving themselves open for an attack. When defeated, Treasure Octoroks leave behind several Rupees alongside their spoils. Treasure Octoroks are unchanged from their previous appearance. They cannot be pulled out with Ultrahand. Other Appearances

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link returns to Rito Village after completing the Main Quest "Tulin of Rito Village", he can find Tulin inside of Teba's Home. If spoken to, he reveals that there is something he wishes to discuss with Link. While helping Harth sort ancient literature, Tulin found a passage that described guiding the Water of three secret Hot Springs to their central point, which will reveal a hidden treasure. Tulin is reminded of the Sturnida Secret Hot Spring situated northwest of the Village, and although he is unsure about the other two, he is tempted by the prospect of treasure. Following this conversation, "Treasure of the Secret Springs" will begin. To find this treasure, Link must go to the North Biron Snowshelf Cave, which is located at the center off the Sturnida Secret Hot Spring, Goflam's Secret Hot Spring, and Sherfin's Secret Hot Spring in the Hebra Mountains. Inside, he will find a tall chamber, with several Cracked Walls located along its sides. There is also an Updraft emanating from a structure in the chamber's center, as well as an Owl Statue. Destroying three of the Cracked Walls will cause Hot Springs to flow into the chamber, raising the Water-level. Once all three are destroyed, the Owl Statue will move to the side, revealing a hidden chamber with a Stone Chest inside. Opening the Chest will grant Link the Vah Medoh Divine Helm and complete the Side Quest. Objectives

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Tree Branches are One-Handed Weapons that can be found near Trees or bushes. They are flammable and will catch Fire if exposed to open flames or a Scorching Climate. Tree Branches are also not made of magnetic materials and cannot be manipulated with Magnesis. They do not attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, and they do not conduct Electricity either. They will float in sufficiently deep bodies of Water. When thrown with the R Button, Tree Branches will leave Link's hand. On one of the central supports of the Bridge of Hylia, Link can find a Tree Branch serving as a Natural Hiding Spot. When he picks this Tree Branch up, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Two varieties of Tree Branches appear in . The type found in can be found on the Surface, while a new type made of lighter wood can be found on Sky Islands. Like in , they can be used as Weapons. Link can also Fuse Objects, Materials, and other Weapons to Tree Branches. Other Appearances The Tree Branch is a weak Weapon that is accompanied by a Pot Lid as a Shield and a Wooden Bow. This Weapon can be obtained as early as the first stage simply by chopping down a few Trees. Tree Branches return in as One-Handed Weapons. As a result, they can be wielded by the Knight Construct, Typhan, Lago, Vence, or Sholani. If Typhan is carrying a Tree Branch, his Shield will be an Old Wooden Shield.

is a recurring character in . Biography Trello is the father of Rivan and the grandfather of Dunma. Like many elderly Zora, Trello holds resentment towards any Hylians, including Link, for Mipha's death. He refrains from attacking Link due to having his hands full trying to figure out what to do about Divine Beast Vah Ruta. Once Divine Beast Vah Ruta has been calmed, Trello will respect Link instead of shaming him. Since retiring, Trello is in charge of the Champion Festival and bears the Ceremonial Trident. As part of the Shrine Quest "The Ceremonial Song", Trello can be approached by Link about the Ceremonial Trident. He reveals that the trident used in the Champion Festival is a replica of Mipha's Lightscale Trident. He admits that he dropped the trident off the bridge while taking it for Dento to examine. However, he does not care much for it since it is fake, and decides to ask Dento to make a new one.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Trilby Plain is a small clearing on the southwestern edge of the Eldin Canyon, located southeast of Woodland Stable. Trilby Valley is found directly to the east, with Zelo Pond between them. A hill with a large Tree on top of it can be found at the center of the Plain, and a shallow pond is placed at its base. On the northern end of Trilby Plain is a grove of Trees. On the southeastern edge of Trilby Plain are the remains of an unnamed village, consisting of burnt Ruined Houses, that was destroyed during the Great Calamity. Near Thims Bridge, a Sign offers directions to Hyrule Ridge, Zora's Domain, and Akkala. The Shield Breakers, a Shield Surfing gang, make their home on Trilby Plain. Fin resides at a campsite near Thims Bridge, which contains a Campfire. When Link speaks to him, he asks if he is there to Shield Surf. If Link claims that he is, he will automatically be transported to the top of the hill, where he will find Russ standing under the Tree. He sells a variety of Shields in order to fund the Shield Breaker. He encourages Link to Shield Surf down the hill, since he believes it is suited for beginners. In the ruined village, a Treasure Chest can be found in one of the Ruined Houses. When Link opens it, he will receive a Ruby. left|40px Three Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Trilby Plain. The first is a Race, which starts on top of the large Tree on the hill. It ends in the pond below, and Link must Shield Surf in order to reach it in time. The second takes the form of Leaves with Fairy Dust that move around the pond, which Link can interact with. The final Puzzle is a Cube Pattern in the ruined village, the two of which must be matched. When Link completes each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Other Appearances During the "Prince's Escort" Challenge, the Warriors are tasked with escorting Sidon across Trilby Plain.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Trilby Valley is an extensive valley on the southern edge of Eldin Canyon. It is largely a mountainous stretch of land consisting densely of rocky foothills and deep gorges. It is bordered by Trilby Plain and Zelo Pond to the west, and the Ternio Trail runs along its northern border. The painting in Foothill Stable depicts the Stable from the Trilby Valley. During the "A Landscape of a Stable" Shrine Quest, Link will be able to locate Tah Muhl Shrine on the northern end of Trilby Valley. However, activating this Quest is not required in order to access the Ancient Shrine. A total of three Monster Strongholds can be found in Trilby Valley, all of which are shaped like giant skulls. The northernmost Stronghold contains a Treasure Chest with a Knight's Bow inside. The second Stronghold is on the eastern side of the Valley, and its Chest contains a Silver Rupee. The final Monster Stronghold is on the southwestern side of the Trilby Valley, which also has a Treasure Chest containing a Silver Rupee. left|40px A single Korok Seed Puzzle is located within Trilby Valley. It is a Race that starts southeast of Tah Muhl Shrine, and it ends directly to the southwest. When Link completes the Race, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials Korok Seeds

is a recurring character in . Biography Trissa is an elderly Sheikah woman living in Kakariko Village with her husband Steen. She manages the General Store, High Spirits Produce. When Link first meets her, she welcomes him to the Village and claims they are blessed. Trissa explains that her goods are all local and fine choices for Recipes. She urges him to pick something out, but realizes he may need something else. Link can ask her about a few different things. If he wants her recommendation, she has some difficulty narrowing the selection down. However, she finally settles on the Swift Carrots that Steen grows. While she notes that the Village is known for them, she admits that Fortified Pumpkins are also a staple. Trissa would like to sell them, but knows that her husband's rivalry with Olkin would get in the way. She directs Link to Olkin's field for Fortified Pumpkins. Link can also ask her about Cooking and she will teach him how, directing him to the Cooking Pot outside. If Link decides to sell her something, she will either mention how much she enjoys free trade or say how lovely the item is. Trissa urges him to let her know if he would like to sell anything else, but also cautions him not to rush. Once Link is finished selling, Trissa notes how she does not leave Kakariko Village very often and is pleased that he was able to show her some interesting things. When Link is ready to leave, she will tell him to come back whenever he likes. Steen will drop by at about 4:00 PM to check in on her. While he fusses over her well-being, Trissa cannot help but laugh at him and tell him not to worry so much. If Link speaks to her at this time, she tells him that Steen has a tendency to focus only on her. Trissa asks Link to take his time browsing and to ignore her husband.

is a recurring character in . Biography Trott is a Stable Worker at Outskirt Stable whose job is to provide directions. Trott is a Horse enthusiast who dreams of owning his own Stable. When Link first meets him, he can be seen pacing around the front of the Stable, having grown weary from being overworked and not eating any Raw Gourmet Meat as a consequence of the predominantly vegetarian diet that the Stable Association enforces. To combat his weariness, Trott occasionally takes breaks by sneaking to the rear end of the Outskirt Stable and resting up against some wreckage. If Link speaks to him while he is resting, he will explain his situation and ask that Link keeps it a secret from Embry, his boss. By speaking to Trott, Link can listen to his woes and desire for Raw Gourmet Meat, beginning the Side Quest "A Rare Find". If Link returns with Raw Meat or Raw Prime, Trott will recognize its scent and inform him that he will accept nothing less than Raw Gourmet Meat. If Link has a Seared Gourmet Steak, Trott will smell the aroma of the Gourmet Meat but complain that the Meat is cooked as he prefers his Meat raw and full of juice. Upon returning with Raw Gourmet Meat, Trott will grow excited over its scent and offer to pay Link for sharing it with him. If Link agrees, Trott will give him a Silver Rupee in return and resolve to work hard now that his craving for Meat has been sated. Trott also offers to pay Link for any more Raw Gourmet Meat that he has on hand. After completing "A Rare Find", Trott's mood improves dramatically. He can be seen walking around and occasionally greeting and waving to guests. As Trott promised, he will still purchase Raw Gourmet Meat from Link for a Silver Rupee apiece. However, Trott will only accept three pieces of Raw Gourmet Meat per day and will tell Link to return tomorrow if offered any more. If Link attempts to give Trott Seared Gourmet Meat, he will complain about how its value has diminished and refuse to buy it from him. Additionally, if Link offers Meat to Trott without having any Raw Gourmet Meat in his Inventory, Trott will get upset and tell him to return when he actually has something to offer. Trott will not react to Icy Gourmet Meat. If Link speaks to Trott before giving him any Raw Gourmet Meat, he can ask Trott who he is to learn of his aspirations to own a Stable of his own. Link can also inquire about Raw Gourmet Meat to learn that migrations occasionally take place atop Satori Mountain, providing the perfect opportunity to hunt for Meat. At any point, Link can ask Trott for information about the Outskirt Stable and its direct surroundings. After completing "A Rare Find", Trott can also tell Link about ideal hunting areas, citing Satori Mountain and the Lord of the Mountain who

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview When Link speaks to Kodah after completing "Sidon of the Zora", she informs him that she and Finley found an Ancient Manuscript while organizing the Seabed Inn's bookshelf. The Manuscript states, "Long, long ago, at Tarm Point, a blessed stone was hidden away within a sacred shrine. It was a magnificent shrine that was overflowing with blessings." Kodah then declares that the Manuscript must lead to a secret. If Link agrees, Kodah states she knew an adventurer like him would understand. If Link disagrees, Kodah continues to insist that she is right. Kodah believes that the Ancient Manuscript was likely left behind by a distant ancestor of hers and that it may lead to treasure. Upon seeing it, Finley decided to try and find the treasure for herself, and she took Sasan with her. Although Kodah is certain that Finley will remain safe, she is worried about Sasan. After speaking to Kodah, "True Treasure" will begin. Inside Tarm Point Cave, Link can find Sasan wondering what he should do. He is shocked to meat someone else in the Cave, asking if Link is also in search of the treasure mentioned in the Ancient Manuscript. If Link has not yet spoken to Kodah, then Sasan reasons he just so happened to find the Cave. If Link did speak to her, Sasan explains that the Manuscript was left by her ancestors. After hearing about the Ancient Manuscript, Sasan and Finley decided to seek out the treasure together, though Sasan admits that he was uncertain. However, he believes that a Shrine of Light is the most likely place that a treasure would be hidden, and so he followed after Finley. When they arrived at Tarm Point Cave, though Finley swam ahead, and Sasan was unable to keep up with her. He also has not been able to use the nearby Raft due to the Cave's Water level fluctuating, and so he is unsure how to reach her. With the nearby Korok Fronds, Link can use Fuse to create a Korok-Frond Guster. He can then place the Raft in the Water and instruct Sasan to board. Link can then use the Korok-Frond Guster to navigate the stream. At the end of the stream, he will find Finley standing in front of a Shrine of Light, calling out to them. Once they reach the end of Tarm Point Cave, Sasan will thank Link. On the shore, Finley notices that Sasan appears to be pale and asks how he is. He insists that he is fine, apologizing for keeping her waiting. Finley looks up at the Yomizuk Shrine nearby, wondering if it is the one mentioned in the Ancient Manuscript. While Finley is disappointed that there is no treasure, Sasan claims that the memory of their journey is more meaningful. Finley agrees, stating that the memory they shared is the greatest treasure of all. Sasan thanks Link for helping him reach the Shrine of Light. As a reward,

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Tuft Mountain is located in East Necluda. Both Lover's Pond and Yambi Lake can be found on top of the Mountain, and its northern foothill is known as Temto Hill. In Atun Valley, a branch of the Faron Highroad forks off to the west of Tuft Mountain, after which it turns around and leads to its peak. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Tuft Mountain. The first is a Rock Pattern in the shape of a heart on its southern end, which Link must complete using a Rock nearby. The second Puzzle is a Rock on the Mountain's peak, and it is revealed to be a Natural Hiding Spot when it is picked up. When Link completes each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Before Link enters Zora's Domain to appease the Divine Beast Vah Ruta, Tula can be found singing and swimming in a pond near the Daka Tuss Shrine. She will call to Link and remark that he is a Hylian. She exclaims that his timing is perfect, since she has been ordered by Sidon to find a Hylian. She says that she has been searching nonstop, and was not floating and splashing in the Water for fun. Tula will turn and point at a Sheikah Tower, and tell Link that Sidon is waiting at Inogo Bridge on the other side. She expresses hope that Link will go and meet the Zora prince, but realizes he is probably taken aback by such a sudden request. Apologizing, she explains that for the Zora, this is their top priority at the moment. Tula asks for Link to grant her request, and tells the hero not to let Sidon know she was splashing and playing in the water. Tula is the president of Sidon's fan club. Thinking of Sidon "turns her to mush," though she expresses great distaste towards the Zora elders calling them a pack of geezers. Tula apologizes and encourages Link to speak with the prince, who she says is a man with magnificent ideas. After Link appeases the Divine Beast Vah Ruta, Tula can be seen running around Zora's Domain. When stopped she tells Link he is in her way and asks if he needs something. If Link asks about the "pack of geezers," Tula says the Zora elders intend to stop Divine Beast Vah Ruta without any outside help, even though it is impossible for the Zora to touch Shock Arrows for an extended period of time. However, Sidon had the idea to ask an outsider to shoot the shock arrows for them. Tula says Sidon has such bold ideas. If Link asks about the Divine Beast, Tula says that she means Divine Beast Vah Ruta in East Reservoir Lake. Tula brings up that the bad weather seems to have calmed down, wondering if Sidon has finally appeased the Divine Beast. After Waterblight Ganon is defeated, Tula and the other Zora watch as King Dorephan gives Link his thanks. She cheers with the other Zora after Sidon thanks the hero as well. After the ceremony, Tula can again be seen meeting with Sidon's fan club from between 8:00-8:30 AM to 8:00 PM, and then stands by the end of a flight of stairs on the second floor of the domain until 12:00 AM. For the rest of the day, she runs around in small circles near the same area. When talked to, she thanks Link for saving the domain and says that Mipha is finally able to rest.

Tulin is a recurring character in . Biography Tulin is a young Rito child who resides in Teba's Home in Rito Village. He is the only child of Teba and Saki, and he has the same white and gray coloration as his father. Teba believes that Tulin is of the age to become a warrior, while Saki still considers him to be a fledgling. The first time Link approaches Tulin, he will excitedly greet him. After Link responds, Tulin will commend him, recalling that his father taught him that "great kids are great greeters". Prior to Divine Beast Vah Medoh being calmed, he excitedly shares that Teba promised to play with him at the Flight Range soon. If asked about the Flight Range, Tulin points Link in its direction, expressing his wish for his father to come play with him soon. Whenever Link speaks to Tulin again, he will recognize him and talk about his father's promise. In his sleep, Tulin will mumble about Teba. Once Divine Beast Vah Medoh has been appeased, Tulin will happily inform Link that his father has returned home. While he is concerned that his father was injured, Tulin is excited by the prospect of flying with him soon. Tulin invites Link to come back later and play with him. thumb|left|320px|alt= A screenshot of Teba flying away from Rito Village, with Tulin riding on his back.|Tulin riding on Teba's back After Link obtains the Great Eagle Bow, Teba decides it is time for him to take Tulin to the Flight Range, expressing his desire for Tulin to become a warrior just like Revali. When Link tells him to take care, Teba stands and beckons Tulin to come with him, much to Tulin's excitement. As they prepare to depart, Tulin invites Link to come play with them at the Flight Range. Tulin then rides on his father's back to the Flight Range. At the Flight Range, Tulin stands at the edge of the platform overlooking the ravine. When Link speaks to him, he will eagerly greet him. After Link responds, Tulin reveals that his father told him about the hero and that he is good with a Bow, which he wants to know the truth of. If Link confirms his skills, Tulin is amazed and asks for a demonstration. If Link downplays his abilities, Tulin recalls that Teba said he was great, asserting that his father never lies. Tulin offers to count down for Link before the Flight Range Mini-Game starts, at which point Link will have to shoot as many Targets as he can in a limited amount of time. He promises to give Link a prize dependent on how many Targets he breaks. Should Link ask for further clarification of the rules, Tulin confirms that they are as simple as he said. If Link declines to participate in the Mini-Game, Tulin will be dejected. If Link agrees, Tulin begins his countdown, which marks the start of the Mini-Game. At the end of the Mini-Game,

Link ask for further clarification of the rules, Tulin confirms that they are as simple as he said. If Link declines to participate in the Mini-Game, Tulin will be dejected. If Link agrees, Tulin begins his countdown, which marks the start of the Mini-Game. At the end of the Mini-Game, Tulin will call Link back to the Flight Range's hut. If Link broke less than five Targets, Tulin will be unimpressed, telling Link to show him something cooler next time. Depending on how many Targets Link has shot, Tulin will compliment him. Then, on Teba's behalf, he will give Link a Red Rupee, a Purple Rupee, a Silver Rupee, or a Gold Rupee. In the time since , Tulin has noticeably grown. In the past, he would watch Link and his father Teba train at the Flight Range. He is now considered a young Rito warrior, and he has a unique Power of Wind that sets him apart for the other Rito. is a recurring character in . Biography Tumbo is a Zora who lives in Zora's Domain, where he can be found running around Mipha's Statue during the day. When he first meets Link, he is confused by his appearance, and explains that he's never met a Hylian before. He asks if he's seen his mother, Mei, on his journey. After Divine Beast Vah Ruta is freed from Calamity Ganon's control, Tumbo is seen catching frogs, and can give Link the "Frog Catching" Side Quest. When talked to, Tumbo explains that he is catching Hot-Footed Frogs so that he can sell them to make money while his mom is away. Then, Tumbo realizes that Link is just pitying him and asks Link to give him five Hot-Footed Frogs. When Link brings him the Hot-Footed Frogs, Tumbo is surprised and excitedly counts them. In return, Tumbo gives Link an Armoranth, which he picked as it was strange, but decides to give to him because it does not suit him. Afterwards, whenever Link talks to him, Tumbo either thanks him for the frogs or suggests he looks at the fish his mom caught at Marot Mart. Each day, he wakes up at 7:00 AM, until 4:00 PM when he runs up a ramp to his father, Fronk, who is working on a pillar nearby. At 8:00 PM, he runs to the Sleeping Chamber and falls asleep at 9:00, saying that he is getting sleepy.
