The , designated by the trial name Hidden Metal, is a Shrine of Light in . Entrance to the Shrine The Turakamik Shrine can be found on the western end of the Gerudo Canyon in the Gerudo Highlands, overlooking the Gerudo Canyon Stable. It corresponds with the Kimakarut Lightroot in the Depths. Themes and Navigation Inside Turakamik Shrine is a metal ball on a chain attached to an Electricity Generator. Connecting the ball to a second one will power a large Gear that Link can stand on to reach the next area. On the wall, two more metal balls on chains can be joined to each other. Doing this activates four moving platforms higher up the wall that Link can Ascend through. A third ball on a chain must be connected to a metal bar sticking out of the wall in order to open the door to the end of the Shrine. However, the chain is not long enough for the two objects to reach. Link can use Ultrahand to dislodge the metal axle of a second large Gear. He can also use Recall on the Gear to reverse its direction and stand on it to reach a Treasure Chest. Attaching the axle to the ball lets Link proceed to the end of the Shrine, where he can interact with the Terminal and receive a Light of Blessing. Treasure Chests

Kotake and Koume, collectively known as , are a recurring pair of Gerudo twin witches in . They are known as the Sorceress of Ice and the Sorceress of Flame, respectively. As the surrogate mothers of Ganondorf, they are among his more devoted servants. Biography In , Kotake and Koume are a pair of 400-year-old twin witches who secretly lead the Gerudo tribe, and are the surrogate mothers of Ganondorf. They maintain their long lives by using their powerful magic. They both have green, wrinkled skin and dress in black robes with white Gerudo patterns near the hems, with an obi-like belt around their waists. Kotake's association with ice is noted by a blue jewel on her forehead and blue slippers. The markings on her headband are in red with a blue border, whereas these distinctions are red on Koume to highlight her association with fire. They first appear outside the Spirit Temple just after child Link obtains the Silver Gauntlets. They kidnap Nabooru, who they subsequently brainwash and dress in an Iron Knuckle armor. After adult Link defeats her, he fights Kotake and Koume inside the boss room of the Spirit Temple. After being defeated, halos appear over their heads and they are absorbed by a column of light, presumably passing to the afterlife. Koume tends to act as the leader of the two, usually appearing first and deciding what their course of action should be. She is the first to introduce herself during the boss battle and is also the one who formulates the idea of combining with Kotake to form Twinrova. Characteristics thumb|right|Link reflecting Kotake's ice attack using the Mirror Shield The boss room where Twinrova is fought has four small platforms surrounding a larger central platform. Link must climb the central platform in order to trigger the battle. Kotake and Koume emerge from the smaller platforms before circling above him, then flying off in different directions. Kotake and Koume fight using magic bolts of the elements from which their respective powers are derived. Using the Mirror Shield, Link is able to redirect the attacks of one sister against the other. After taking a total of four hits, the pair will use their "Double Dynamite Attack" and merge into Twinrova, a single being with the combined powers of both witches. After the transformation, the Mirror Shield remains essential in winning the battle. Link is able to use it to absorb the power of both the fire and ice spells. He is required to collect three consecutive charges of one type of spell, which allows him to release the spell back at Twinrova. However, since Twinrova frequently alternates between fire and ice attacks, care must be taken to only block attacks of one type at a time. Blocking a fire attack followed by an ice attack, or vice versa, will cause all power currently stored in the Mirror Shield to dissipate. Once Twinrova is injured by the reflected attack, she collapses on one of the four outlying platforms,

only block attacks of one type at a time. Blocking a fire attack followed by an ice attack, or vice versa, will cause all power currently stored in the Mirror Shield to dissipate. Once Twinrova is injured by the reflected attack, she collapses on one of the four outlying platforms, allowing Link to attack with his Sword. After enough damage is dealt, Twinrova will be defeated, at which point she splits back into Kotake and Koume. The two witches intend to keep battling, but soon realize that they are already dead. They then enter a comical argument about whether they were twins or not due to Kotake claiming she was two decades younger than Koume while ranting about how they're not ready to die, before eventually threatening Link with coming back to haunt him. The sisters appear in , though in stark contrast to , they are not evil and help Link on his journey. and 90px|left In and , Kotake and Koume send Veran and General Onox to cause chaos and light two of the three flames needed to resurrect Ganon; the Flame of Sorrow and the Flame of Destruction. They appear as a disguised old lady to dissuade Link from his quest, revealing themselves when he reaches the final dungeon. In a Linked Game to either Seasons or Ages, they show up to taunt Link and his allies in Labrynna before leaving or rub the Flame of Destruction being lit in his face after he completes Unicorn's Cave. Once the flames are lit, the two kidnap Princess Zelda to light the final flame, the Flame of Despair, by sacrificing her. In a Linked Game, Link fights the sisters both individually and as Twinrova. After Link defeats Twinrova, she chooses to become the vessel for the ritual herself instead of Zelda, so that Ganon can return. Unfortunately for the pair, their sacrifice is in vain as it only allows a mindless, raging Ganon to come forth. Characteristics left|90px Twinrova casts magical projectiles at Link that he must deflect back at them. However, Link must use his Sword to deflect them rather than his Shield. The Mirror Shield, an upgrade that can only be attained in a Linked Game, can only protect him from their magic attacks. After the sisters have taken three hits, they fuse together and become Twinrova. Twinrova alternates between two phases of attack, which affect the room around her and Link. In her cold phase, the room's floor is covered with slippery ice and Twinrova materializes spiked ice crystals that she launches at Link and which ricochet off the walls. In her fire phase, parts of the floor become lava pits and Twinrova launches fireballs. Link must strike Twinrova with his Sword several times to stun her, and once stunned, he must use a Mystery Seed to actually damage her. thumb|left|250px|Koume and Kotake behind Ganondorf In , Koume and Kotake appear behind Ganondorf in the Memories "The Gerudo Assault" and "A Show of Fealty". is a recurring character in . Biography Tye is wandering the wilderness of Lanayru just South of the Wetland Stable. His wife Sorelia is traveling with him and the two have set up a ramshackle tent at the edges of the unnamed forest, where they also have a Campfire and a Cooking Pot. The campfire sends up a pillar of smoke that can be seen from far away, making them easier to locate. The couple are out searching for a Silent Princess flower, although neither have seen it in person, and the trip has cost them a few fruitless months of effort. Tye had originally been planning to go on his own, only for his wife to refuse to be left behind. Although he never intended for her to join him, her presence only brings him joy. Still, he has concerns over being able to properly protect her and has decided to redouble his efforts to keep her safe. Their goal is to pledge their love to each other with a freshly picked blossom so that they may live a happy life together. When Link first encounters them, they are always under attack by a group of Blue Bokoblins and require saving. Once the threat has been dealt with, the couple goes to rest at their small camp, with Sorelia taking the tent and Tye crouching just outside of it. It it here that they explain why they are risking their safety out in the countryside in spite of the danger.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Ubota Point is located along the southern end of West Necluda, bordering Martha's Landing, Aris Beach, and North Aris Beach. The Sarjon Woods and Lakeside Stable are both on its northern side. Rassla Lake, which feeds Water into Lake Floria, is also situated on the western side of Ubota Point. When Farosh flies into Rassla Lake, Updrafts and Wind will appear on the parts of Ubota Point surrounding the Lake. In addition to this, three Monster Strongholds can be found upon Ubota Point, with Treasure Chests containing a Double Axe, a Soldier's Claymore, a bundle of five Arrows, and a Topaz. Another Treasure Chest is situated on the southern end of Ubota Point. It is made of metal, and it contains a bundle of five Bomb Arrows. left|40px A total of five Korok Seed Puzzles are located on Ubota Point. The first is an Offering Spot for Hearty Durians on the west end of the plateau. The second is a Natural Hiding Spot, taking the form of a Rock in the Bottomless Bog west of Lakeside Stable. The third Puzzle is another Offering Spot, this time for Mighty Bananas located west of Rassla Lake. South of Rassla Lake is the fourth Puzzle is another Natural Hiding Spot Rock. Lastly, a Rock Pattern is situated on the plain on the east side of Ubota Point. Whenever Link solves one of these Korok Seed Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Ulri Mountain Skyview Tower is a Skyview Tower in the Akkala Highlands. The first time Link uses the the tower to launch himself into the Sky, he will Scan most of Akkala and the Akkala Sky on the Purah Pad, in addition to activating the Tower's Travel Point. When Link first arrives at the Tower, he will find Sawson looking up at something. Sawson explains that he was sent here to fix the Tower, but that an Aerocuda has stolen the terminal. Link needs to shoot an Arrow at the Aerocuda to get it to drop the terminal so he can get it back into the Tower, either by carrying it himself or by using Ultrahand. Sawson thanks Link for his help and gets the Tower working again.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Ulria Grotto is located in the southeast portion of the Akkala Highlands. It is a deep pit with a pond at its bottom, and it is surrounded on all sides by rocky hills. Ke'nai Shakah Shrine is located in a cave in the Grotto, though the entrance is initially blocked by bombable rocks. Many Ore Deposits and Luminous Stone Deposits are located along its walls. Due to its proximity to the Lanayru Great Spring, Ulria Grotto will be subject to Divine Beast Vah Ruta's Rain until it has been calmed. One Treasure Chest can be found within Ulria Grotto. It is made of metal and submerged below the pond's Water. Using the Magnesis Rune, Link can pull the Chest to the surface, where he can open it to obtain a bundle of 10 Shock Arrows. The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Tanagar Canyon Course is located within Tanagar Canyon on the Tabantha Frontier. It is directly north of the Tabantha Great Bridge. Modar lives on the Course, where he has set up a a small campsite with a Cooking Pot. The far end of the Course is marked by a Big Flag. Modar operates the Boom Bam Golf Mini-Game from the Tanagar Canyon Course. He invented the game after rolling into the Canyon, and he has so far been the only person to play. It costs 20 Rupees to play, but Link can receive a Red Rupee, a Purple Rupee, or a Silver Rupee as a reward, depending on how well he does. left|40px Only one Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on the Tanagar Canyon Course. It takes the form of Leaves with Fairy Dust on top of the Big Flag. When Link interacts with the Leaves, a Korok will appear, giving him a Korok Seed as a reward for finding it. Equipment

Ultrahand is a recurring ability in . Overview Ultrahand is an Ancient Power that Link obtains from Rauru in Ukouh Shrine. It allows Link to stick Objects together or move them. When Ultrahand is used, Link has the option to move Objects around or rotate them either vertically or horizontally. If Link moves an Object close to another one, he can bind them together with a green viscous substance. This substance can hold shape in Water, allowing Link to create transportation such as Rafts with Logs and Fans or Sails. Bound Objects can also be split apart into their constituent parts if Link wishes to reassemble them in a different way. Link can attach a maximum of 21 Objects to one another. When multiple Zonai Devices are connected to an Object using Ultrahand, triggering one Device will activate all of the attached Devices at once. This allows Link to use Ultrahand to build a wide variety of Vehicles. Other Appearances Ultrahand is an ability that can be utilized by Rauru. He demonstrates this ability during several of his Strong Attacks, where he uses it to manipulate his Spear of Light from a distance. Similarly, he uses it during his unique Sync Strikes with Mineru and the Knight Construct. Rauru also uses Ultrahand to hold Zonai Devices when he uses them. By completing the Quest "For the Children", Rauru unlocks Ultrahand as a Unique Skill. It has an attack power of 60. He can use Ultrahand against Enemies that have thrown Objects, allowing him to take control of their projectiles and damage the Enemies instead. This can be used as a Special Action to Counter certain Dangerous Attacks. Like the rest of Rauru's Unique Skills, its cooldown time is reduced when he is at a Site of Sacred Power.

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview At the end of the "Teach Me a Lesson II" Side Quest, Symin gives Link permission to cultivate crops in the School's Field. At the Field, Link will find Uma tending to it. When Link approaches her, she reveals that Symin has already spoken to her about planting whatever Link wants and she has already finished preparing the Field. Uma claims she is capable of a variety of Fruits and Vegetables by extracting seeds from them. However, she is inexperienced in raising Endura Carrots and Hearty Radishes, and such harvests may have a lower yield than other crops. At this point, the "Uma's Garden" Side Quest will begin. Uma then asks Link which crop he would like to grow. So long as Link has their grown counterparts, Link can ask Uma to plant Hylian Tomatoes, Wildberries, Hydromelons, Big Hearty Radishes, Hearty Radishes, Endura Carrots, Fortified Pumpkins, Sun Pumpkins, Swift Carrots, Hylian Rice, and Tabantha Wheat. Once Link makes his choice, Uma will take one of the crops from his Inventory. She explains that she will be unable to return it to him, but she can change out what she is growing if he wants something else instead. She also asks Link allow her to witness his first harvest. Lastly, Uma informs Link that it will take some time before his crops are ready, and sleeping in a Bed or waiting by a Campfire will not make them grow faster. After two in-game days, the crops at the School's Field will be ready to harvest. When Link returns to the Field, Uma will greet him. She thanks him for being patient, pointing out how delicious the newly grown crops look. is a recurring character in . She is an elderly woman residing in Hateno Village. Biography Uma spends her time during the day sitting on a stool by a large tree outside the local inn. She kindly greets Link and asks if he happens to be a traveler. If Link admits that he is indeed traveling, Uma will be surprised. She states that the village has become lively thanks to the peaceful state of the region. Link can ask her to explain and she will tell him that in earlier years, Hateno was no place for farming. She sadly recounts the devastation of Central Hyrule in the wake of Calamity Ganon. Speaking to her again allows Link to ask her about a number of topics, which she does not mind answering. Asking about the Calamity pushes Uma to reveal that she was not alive for the event, but was born in an age called the Age of Burning Fields. She explains that in time, the people and plants of Hateno recovered, but that Central Hyrule is still caught in the grips of Calamity Ganon. She believes that older people may be able to tell Link more. Bringing up Hyrule Castle allows Uma to tell Link of what the Castle used to be like and how courageous villagers would seek out glory there. Its current state depresses the old woman. Uma will relate how Hyrule Castle Town used to be a bustling wealth of diversity should Link ask about it, which also reminds her to tell the hero how he can find the fallen city on his map. It makes her wonder at the scale of the Calamity's devastation. Whenever she is finished answering a question, Uma will ask if Link would like help with anything else. She will bid him farewell when he decides to leave.

is a recurring mechanic in . Most commonly, items such as the Master Sword or the Arrows can be upgraded into stronger versions, such as the Golden Sword and Silver Arrows, respectively. Overview While the ability to replace weaker items with stronger variants is prevalent in nearly every Zelda game, some games such as feature more in-depth systems of upgrading, and it is often necessary to provide Treasures or Materials as the basic ingredients for the relevant upgrade. Common upgrades throughout the series include: the Magical Boomerang, Magic Hammer, the White Sword, the Mirror Shield, Blue Mail and Red Mail, Light Arrows and Roc's Cape. Several equipment upgrades, such as the Quiver and Bomb Bag are prevalent in games that require ammunition. Wallet upgrades are commonplace, as well. In , items and Potions can be upgraded in the Skyloft Bazaar to give them added advantages, like extra strength or durability. Gondo will enhance Link's equipment in the Scrap Shop, while Bertie improves Potions at the Infusion Shop. All upgrades are permanent and take a few seconds to complete. As Link progresses, he is able to upgrade more of his items. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Upland Lindor is located on the foothills of Lindor's Brow on Hyrule Ridge. The Footrace Check-In, a camp inhabited by Konba, has been set up on its western end. Maag No'rah Shrine is located on the eastern end of Upland Lindor, inside a cave that faces towards the Maritta Exchange Ruins. Alongside Lindor's Brow and Mount Rhoam, Upland Lindor wraps around the northwestern side of Ludfo's Bog. During the "EX Champion Revali's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link is tasked with shooting an Arrow at Dinraal's horn as it passes through Tanagar Canyon. When he does this, Shira Gomar Shrine will rise from the ground on the northern side of Upland Lindor. A Stone Talus (Luminous) is embedded in the ground on the northeastern side of Upland Lindor. It will initially be dormant, but if Link approaches the Talus, it will stand up and begin to attack him. Additionally, while Dinraal does not fly over Upland Lindor directly, it gets close enough while in the Tanagar Canyon to create Winds and Updrafts. left|40px Three separate Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Upland Lindor. The first is a Jar in a Tree's hollow north of the Footrace Check-In, which Link must destroy with either Archery or Remote Bombs. The second Puzzle is a Natural Hiding Spot, disguised as a Rock west of the Stone Talus (Luminous). The final is another Natural Hiding Spot, this time buried under a pile of rubble east of the Talus. If Link solves one of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. is a recurring character in . Biography Urbosa was the Gerudo Champion who piloted the Divine Beast Vah Naboris. She was also the Gerudo Chief in life, a title that would later be passed on to her descendant, Riju. She was capable of manipulating Lightning, which is a power known as Urbosa's Fury. Urbosa battled with the Scimitar of the Seven and the Daybreaker, collectively known as the Champion's Arms. It is said that Urbosa's movements resembled a beautiful dance when using the Scimitar of the Seven, and she greatly cherished the Daybreaker for its lightness and durability. Urbosa cares for Zelda like a sister with a strong core. According to the Gerudo child Pearle, Urbosa once saved Gerudo Town from an evil ghost. Urbosa was a close friend of the Queen of Hyrule. She takes up Diary writing after the Queen came to visit her in Gerudo Town. The queen tells her that her visit was important and wanted to introduce her to her newborn child, Zelda, whose smile immediately endeared Urbosa to her. She told the Queen of Hyrule that Zelda was sure to grow into a beautiful and dignified queen, similar to her mother. The Queen thanked her, but she said that beauty fades, and all she wants for Zelda is to find happiness. Urbosa noticed that the look she gave her infant daughter was that of a mother who unconditionally loves her child. Six years later, the Queen of Hyrule passed away, leaving Urbosa so heartbroken that she took a long time to return to her Diary. It had been so sudden that she was still in disbelief over it. She was haunted by the memories of the Queen and still had trouble containing her emotions. She noticed that during the Queen's funeral that Zelda kept her head high and never cried. While she commends that Zelda carried herself like a true princess, Urbosa was certain that she was very deeply aggrieved and worried for her. One year after the Queen of Hyrule's death, Urbosa decided to take a trip to Hyrule Castle and after speaking with King Rhoam, she visited Zelda. In Urbosa's Diary, she admits that she only came to the Castle out of concern for Zelda. The King allowed Urbosa to accompany Zelda to one of the springs for her training. Zelda prayed for hours on end in the freezing Water until it was sundown. Worried for the Princess, Urbosa tried to convince her to stop, but she eventually had to drag her out of the Water. For a long time, Zelda stared at her, but she eventually described the pressure she feels to awaken her power. All Urbosa could do was hold her close and listen, which she hoped could be enough. Nine years later, emissaries from Hyrule Kingdom came to visit Urbosa and asked if she would be willing to pilot Divine Beast Vah Naboris. The Gerudo were not comfortable with the risk this posed to their Chief, which Urbosa understood.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Uten Marsh is located in East Necluda between the Necluda Sea and Mount Floria. The Uten Marsh is a very shallow pond which only goes up to Link's legs, but Link is still able to use the Cryonis Rune in the Water. The marsh is dense with plant life and a few Trees grow throughout the area. In the middle of the Uten Marsh, the Hinox (Middle Kin) sleeps on a small area of land that the Water does not reach. This Hinox is part of a Shrine Quest called "The Three Giant Brothers", where three Hinox brothers each have a Ancient Orb hanging around their neck. Along with the Ancient Orb, a Dragonbone Boko Spear and a Dragonbone Boko Club also hang from the Hinox's neck. A short distance southwest from the sleeping area of the Hinox, a stone chest holding a bundle of five Ice Arrows can be found underneath a tree. is a recurring character in . Biography Varke is a Hylian and the owner of the Snowfield Stable in the Tabantha Tundra. He can be found at the front of Snowfield Stable. If Snowfield Stable is the first Stable Link has visited, Varke will welcome him and introduce him to the Stable. Since he does not recognize Link, he asks if he knows how the Stable system works. If Link says he does not, Varke explains that he can board Horses and summon them to any Stable. He also tells Link that he can tame a wild Horse and register it to make it his companion. While each person is limited to five Horses, they can be swapped in and out. Varke then asks Link if he knows how to catch a wild Horse. If Link does not, Varke instructs him to sneak behind a wild Horse and hop on. When the Horse starts panicking, Varke suggests that Link soothe it. Once it has settled down, Link will be able to bring it to Varke to register it. Any wild Horse that Link catches will take time to get used to being ridden, so Varke tells Link to gently redirect and calm his Horses when they veer off course. As Link continues interacting with is Horses in this way, his Horses will trust him and become more obedient. When spoken to at the front of the Snowfield Stable, Varke will welcome Link and ask if he wants to register or take out a Horse. When Link takes a Horse out, Varke thanks him for choosing their Stable. If Link tries to register a Horse without one present, Varke will call him a comedian, saying to "quit horsing around" and to find a Horse. When Link approaches the Stable with a wild Horse, Varke asks if he wants to register it or rest for a while. He explains that Snowfield Stable charges a registration fee of 20 Rupees. Once the Horse has been registered, Varke asks if Link wants to board it or take it with him. When attempting to register a Deer or Bear, Varke will scold Link and say they only register Horses. Varke insists that Stalhorses are monsters, and he will not board it in fear of it eating the other Horses. If Link tries to register the Lord of the Mountain, Varke refuses, believing they will all by cursed if he does so. When Link registers Epona, Varke starts to ask him to enter a name for his new Horse. However, he recognizes Epona as a Horse of legend, and he states that there is probably a law against renaming her. He forces Link to name her Epona. Varke gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. Epona. Varke gives Link several tips for taking care of Horses, such as instructions on how to tame a wild Horse. He informs Link that Horses instinctively follow the road, which is great for viewing the scenery. He also tells Link that if he is separated from his Horse, whistling will cause it to come running, but it will not be able to hear him if he is too far away. In addition, Varke gives instructions as to how to navigate a Horse that is scared of its surroundings and refusing to move. Inside Snowfield Stable, Varke once again welcomes Link and asks if he will be staying with them. He offers regular Beds for 20 Rupees and a soft Bed for 40 Rupees. When asked, he explains that the soft Bed a special bed offered by Snowfield Stable, and anyone who uses it will wake up feeling more energized. Before Link rests, Varke tells him to sleep well. When Link wakes up, Varke wishes him a good morning, day, or evening and hopes he enjoyed his stay.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Vatorsa Snowfield is a flat expanse covered by Snow in the Gerudo Highlands. It is bordered to the west by the West Vatorsa Snowfield, the two being separated by a natural stone archway. In the center of the Snowfield is a deep valley. On the eastern end of Vatorsa Snowfield, sitting at the base of Laparoh Mesa is Kuh Takkar Shrine. As part of a Freezing Climate, Link must have at least two levels of Cold Resistance to traverse the Snowfield without taking damage. At 7:00 PM, Farosh will fly over Vatorsa Snowfield from Gerudo Summit, causing an Updraft to appear underneath it. Three Monster Strongholds can also be found on the Snowfield. The westernmost Stronghold is multi-tiered structure made out of wood, and its two Treasure Chests contain a Silver Rupee and a bundle of five Bomb Arrows. The second is a small encampment on the slope leading into the valley, and it contains a Treasure Chest containing a Purple Rupee. The last Monster Stronghold is located at the end of the valley, and the Treasure Chest inside contains a Ruby. Several Treasure Chests can be found in the Vatorsa Snowfield. In total, these Chests contain one Forest Dweller's Spear, one Golden Claymore, 10 Shock Arrows, one Amber, three Opals, one Ruby, and three Purple Rupees. Creatures Enemies Materials

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Vegetable Curries are made by Cooking Hylian Rice, Goron Spice, and either a Fortified Pumpkin, Swift Carrot, or Endura Carrot together in a Cooking Pot. Their default version can be made by using multiple Vegetables with differing effects. Eating them will heal some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. These Curries are healthy, and their mild flavor and spiciness make them popular. Based on the type of Vegetable used, Link can make the following variations of Vegetable Curry: Enduring Vegetable Curry: Made using Endura Carrots. When eaten, these curries will completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Vegetable Curry: Made using Swift Carrots. By eating them, Link will receive a boost to his movement speed. Tough Vegetable Curry: Made using Fortified Pumpkins. They can be eaten to grant Link a boost to his defense. Link can make Vegetable Curry by Cooking either type of Pumpkin or Carrot with a bundle of Hylian Rice and Goron Spice.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can make Vegetable Omelets by Cooking a Bird Egg, Goat Butter, Rock Salt, and any Vegetable, herb, or Flower together in a Cooking Pot. Their default version can be made either by using Hyrule Herbs, which have no Added Effects, or by using Ingredients with contradicting Effects. Eating them will heal some of Link's Hearts to his Life Gauge. The use of eggs and chopped Vegetables adds to the nutritional balance of this Meal. Several different variations of Vegetable Omelets can be made, depending on the type of Vegetable, herb, or Flower used: Hearty Vegetable Omelet: Made by using Hearty Radishes, Big Hearty Radishes, or other hearty Ingredients. By eating them, all of Link's Hearts will be healed and he will gain Extra Hearts. Energizing Vegetable Omelet: Made by using energizing Ingredients. They can be eaten to partially refill Link's Stamina Wheel. Enduring Vegetable Omelet: Made by using Endura Carrots or other enduring Ingredients. When eaten, they'll completely restore and overfill Link's Stamina Wheel. Hasty Vegetable Omelet: Made by using Swift Carrots, Swift Violets, or other hasty Ingredients. These omelets will provide Link with a movement speed when he eats them. Spicy Vegetable Omelet: Made by using Warm Safflinas or other spicy Ingredients. Consuming them will grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Electro Vegetable Omelet: Made by using Electric Safflinas or other electric Ingredients. If eaten, they give Link one level of Shock Resistance. Mighty Vegetable Omelet: Made by using Mighty Thistles or other mighty Ingredients. Eating these omelets will provide Link with a boost to his attack power. Tough Vegetable Omelet: Made by using Fortified Pumpkins, Armoranths, or other tough Ingredients. They will grant Link a boost to his Defense when he eats them. Sneaky Vegetable Omelet: Made by using Blue Nightshades, Silent Princesses, or other sneaky Ingredients. By eating them, Link will receive a boost to his Stealth. Chilly Vegetable Omelet: Made by using Cool Safflinas or other spicy Ingredients. They can be consumed to grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Vegetable Omelets are made by Cooking any kind of Vegetable, herb, or Flower with a Bird Egg, Goat Butter, and a piece of Rock Salt. Other Appearances

The is a recurring Armor Shop in . Features and Overview The Ventest Clothing Boutique is an Armor Shop located in Hateno Village. It is managed by Sophie, a girl who stands quietly in the corner of the store. The Boutique notably sells two complete Armor Sets: the Hylian Armor Series and the Soldier's Set. It also features a side room, which functions as a joint kitchen and bedroom. The Ventest Clothing Boutique was formerly operated by Sophie's father, Seldon, but he has decided to give more responsibility to his daughter. While giving Link a tour of Hateno Village, the Boutique will be his final stop, and he invites Link to come shopping. If it is Raining outside, Seldon will run inside and sit at the work station located at the back of the store. When Link makes a purchase from the Ventest Clothing Boutique, Sophie will thank him for doing so. Inhabitants Wares and Pricing The Ventest Clothing Boutique reappears in . Several giant Mushrooms have sprouted up along its edges, and the large shirt displayed above the door has been replaced to feature Mushroom patterns. Sophie's sister Cece has taken over the shop and turned it into an exhibition for her brand. The only item on display is the Cece Hat, and it is not up for sale. The armor pieces that should be in stock have been put away to make room for the exhibit. They are stored in the personnel-only room to the side. The door is locked, but they can be seen from the main room through an opening in the wall. Once Link has completed "The Mayoral Election" Side Quest however, Cece agrees to put the old stock back in the main room. Link can buy the armor pieces on display from Sophie, while Cece offers her own selection of wares. Inhabitants Wares and Pricing

"" is a Side Quest in . Overview After completing two of the "Regional Phenomena" Main Quests, Link can find Mubs and Garini talking to each other at the Armor Shop in Lookout Landing. Garini is worried about Lurelin Village and wonders if he should go back, but Mubs does not want something to happen to him as well. Link then updates them on the situation. They are both relieved to learn everyone is safe, and Mubs gives him a Mighty Salt-Grilled Crab as a sign of their gratitude. Garini thinks he should probably go check on their shop, but he does not want to leave Mubs alone in Lookout Landing. She convinces him to go back home to help the others bring their village back on its feet. Afterwards, Garini will be gone and "Village Attacked by Pirates" will be complete. Objectives

The is a recurring location in . The Village Chief's House goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Village Chief's House is a House found in Hateno Village, serving as the home of Reede, Clavia, and Karin. The family sleeps inside at night, and it is also where they take refuge during Rain. Outside of the Village Chief's House is the town's Goddess Statue, at which Link can exchange four Spirit Orbs for a Heart Container or a Stamina Vessel. There is also a Campfire that Link can sit at to pass the time, as well as an Apple Tree. The four Jars next to the front door can be broken for supplies, as well. The Shed is located outside of the House, as well. In the loft, Link can read the Girl's Notebook, which details a recipe for Pumpkin Stew. Below the loft is a basket, which contains two Apples. Creatures Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Volcon is a Goron who stands outside of the Rollin' Inn in Goron City, where he directs travelers to the lodge. Volcon helps run the Inn alongside Tray, and gives Goron-style massages to its customers. If asked, Volcon explains the inn to Link and describes it as a distinguished Goron establishment with a lovely view of Death Mountain, although blocked by Bludo's house. Afterwards, he offers to massage Link as compensation and invites Link to stay at the inn. If Link says goodbye without saying anything, Volcon tells him to rest every now and then. After the Magma Bombs stop falling following the Divine Beast Vah Rudania's liberation, Volcon becomes hopeful that droves of tourists will start coming to Goron City and stay at the Inn. If Link attacks him repeatedly with a melee Weapon, Volcon will knock him back without dealing any damage.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Characteristics Voltfin Trout can be found swimming in the waters of Hyrule Ridge and the Tabantha Frontier. Like other fish, they can also be dropped by Octoroks, specifically Forest Octoroks near Thundra Plateau. Link can eat one raw to restore one Heart. Voltfin Trout exposed to Ice become Frozen Trout, while ones exposed to Fire turn into Roasted Trout. Cooking with Voltfin Trout results in Meals that grant Link temporary Shock Resistance. During the Side Quest, Walton will ask Link to bring him several Items that correspond to his riddles. The fourth riddle he tells asks for something with scales and a tail that will zap people, and refers to it as a shocking swimmer. When Link placed a Voltfin Trout on the leaf, Walton will cheer that he figured it out, and then move on to the next riddle. In a Cooking Pot, Voltfin Trout and other fish can be used to make a Fish Skewer, a Fish and Mushroom Skewer, and Salt-Grilled Fish in a Cooking Pot. They're also among the seafood that can make Fish Pie, Creamy Seafood Soup, Copious Fish Skewers, Glazed Seafood, Gourmet Meat and Seafood Fry, Meat and Seafood Fry, Monster Stew, Pepper Seafood, Prime Meat and Seafood Fry, Seafood Meunière, Seafood Rice Balls, and Steamed Fish. Voltfin Trout are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Voltfruits can be found growing from Cacti within the Gerudo Desert, and they can be be bought at Lorn's Fruit Stand in Gerudo Town. Red Hinoxes can also drop Voltfruits upon their deaths. When eaten, Voltfruits provide Link with half a Heart. Voltfruits exposed to Fire become Roasted Voltfruit. Meals made using Voltfruits give Link Shock Resistance. The Kochi Dye Shop accepts them as an ingredient for Orange Dye. A Voltfruit is needed in order to make Creamy Heart Soup. They can also be used in Fruit-based Meals: Voltfruits are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Voltfruits once again grow on Cacti in the Gerudo Desert. They are naturally insulated and known for their sweet taste. Voltfruits restore half of a Heart to Link's Life Gauge when eaten. Due to being insulated, they cause Foods Cooked with them to grant Link Shock Resistance. They can be used as an ingredient for Orange Dye at the Kochi Dye Shop in Hateno Village. Voltfruits exposed to Fires or Scorching Climates become Roasted Voltfruits. They have no special properties when Fused to Weapons, Shields or Arrows. A Voltfruit is needed in order to make Creamy Heart Soup or a Noble Pursuit. They can also be used in Fruit-based Meals: Voltfruits are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

page_title: Vow of Sidon, Sage of Water
text: The is an Item in . Location and Uses Link receives the Vow of Sidon, Sage of Water from Sidon after the two of them defeat Mucktorok in the Water Temple and Sidon awakens as the Sage of Water. The Vow of Sidon, Sage of Water allows Link to summon Sidon's Sage Avatar, which can be commanded to perform Sidon's Power of Water. Additionally, the Avatar will automatically pursue and attack nearby Enemies when Link is in battle. The Vow of Sidon, Sage of Water can be deactivated from the Inventory, preventing the Sage Avatar from appearing alongside Link. By speaking to a Goddess Statue and exchanging four Sage's Wills, Link can deepen his bond with Sidon, changing the Vow into the Solemn Vow of Sidon, Sage of Water.

page_title: Vow of Tulin, Sage of Wind
text: The is an Item in . Location and Uses Link receives the Vow of Tulin, Sage of Wind from Tulin after the two of them defeat Colgera in the Wind Temple and Tulin awakens as the Sage of Wind. Using his newfound power, Tulin holds Link's hand and swears to fight alongside him with a Sage Avatar. After imparting his power into Link, the Vow of Tulin, Sage of Wind manifests as a Ring on the little finger of Link's Right Arm, allowing Link to summon a Sage Avatar of Tulin as long as it is active. This Sage Avatar allows Link to use Tulin's Power of Wind at any time. It will also fight alongside Link if he is in battle, shooting Arrows from its Bow. The Vow of Tulin, Sage of Wind can be deactivated from the Inventory, preventing the Sage Avatar from appearing alongside Link. By speaking to a Goddess Statue and exchanging four Sage's Wills, Link can deepen his bond with Tulin, changing the Vow into the Solemn Vow of Tulin, Sage of Wind.

is a recurring character in . Biography Wabbin is a timid young man seeking love. He is found at the top of Tuft Mountain, near Lover's Pond. As part of the Side Quest A Gift of Nightshade, he wishes to speak to the Gerudo woman Perda, whom he has feelings for. He asks Link to deliver a Blue Nightshade to her, citing that he long ago decided he would give that flower to the girl of his dreams. As a reward for setting him up with Perda, Wabbin gives Link 20 rupees. His new girlfriend scolds him for his cheapness, and he gives Link another 100 rupees out of fear. Wabbin is found in the Jail in the Gerudo Shelter for violating the rule that only women are allowed in Gerudo Town.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Walnot Mountain makes up the southeastern edge of Mount Lanayru. The Solewood Range makes up its southern foothills, though it also borders the Lanayru Range to the north. The Lanayru Sea is located directly to the east of the Mountain. As a Freezing Climate, Walnot Mountain requires two levels of Cold Resistance to be traversed without taking damage. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found on top of Walnot Mountain. It is a Flower Trail starting on the peak west of the Mountain. When Link follows the Flower Trail to its end on Walnot Mountain, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Enemies Creatures Materials

is a recurring character in . Biography Walton can be found outside atop the Great Deku Tree in Korok Forest. When spoken with, he gives Link the "Riddles of Hyrule" Side Quest. Like in , Walton can be found on top of the Great Deku Tree in Korok Forest. When Link speaks to him, he will tell Link about a treasure-hunting game he organized for the other Koroks. However, he wants someone to test the game first to make sure the objects are hidden well. If Link agrees to test the game, the "Walton's Treasure Hunt" Side Quest will begin. After finding the first two objects and returning to Walton, Walton will ask Link if the objects were hard to find. If Link answers that it was easy, Walton will be unsurprised. After Link finds the final object, Walton will ask if it was hard again, and Link can answer in the same ways as before. Walton then lets Link keep everything he found.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Warm Darners can be found in open areas of the Akkala Highlands and Hyrule Field. They're also sold by Maypin and by Beedle at Gerudo Canyon Stable, Rito Stable, Serenne Stable, and Snowfield Stable. Combining one with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot will result in a Spicy Elixir, which grants Link temporary Cold Resistance. The Kochi Dye Shop accepts Warm Darners as an ingredient for Red Dye. The Side Quest "Little Sister's Big Request" requires Link to gather Warm Darners and other dragonflies for Jana as Gleema's birthday present. However, Jana will become disgusted by the dragonflies and asks Link to deliver them in her stead. Jana will give Link one hundred Rupees upon completing this quest. Several Warm Darners can be seen on the Sky Islands Warm Darners are required to Enhance the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Warm Safflinas are found in Hyrule Ridge and the Gerudo Desert. Many Warm Safflinas can be found near Tera's Great Fairy Fountain under the Gerudo Great Skeleton. Meals made in a Cooking Pot using a Warm Safflina will give Link Cold Resistance when eaten. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop to make Orange Dye. Like other Flowers, Warm Safflinas can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Three Warm Safflinas, in addition to five Red Chuchu Jellies, are needed to upgrade each piece of the Snowquill Set to its first tier. Like other Flowers, Warm Safflinas can be used in a Cooking Pot to make the following Meals: Warm Safflinas are required to upgrade the following pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain: Other Appearances

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Washa's Bluff is located in the Hyrule Ridge between Illumeni Plateau and Satori Mountain. It is a large oval shaped plateau similar to the nearby Illumeni Plateau. The terrain is very grassy and rough with many small ridges and cracks running through the earth. Along the bluff, many misshapen Trees sprout from the ground. In the southern area of the bluff, a gigantic misshapen tree sprouts out of the ground, and atop this tree, Kass can be found. Behind Kass, a small structure holds a table which Kass's Journal rests. If Link speaks to Kass, he will state that he knows a song that speaks of Washa's Bluff. If Link asks to hear the song, Kass will oblige and sing it for him. This starts the Shrine Quest Under a Red Moon. Completing this quest reveals the Mijah Rokee Shrine to Link. Creatures Enemies Materials Kass's shack can no longer be seen atop the tallest Dragon's Blood Tree in Washa's Bluff.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Water Octoroks are the only type of Octorok that appear in all of the Drablands prior to the Den of Trials. They are encountered in bodies of water and are most commonly found in water-themed areas, such as Riverside and the Flooded Zone of the Den of Trials. Water Octoroks hide underwater, staying in one spot with only their shadow and a small whirlpool visible; however, they will pop out of the water if any of the Links are near them. While above water, Water Octoroks shoot rocks at the Links, inflicting one Heart of damage upon impact. If the Links get close enough to strike a Water Octorok with their Swords, it will retreat back into the water where it cannot be attacked. If the Links are quick enough, they can strike a Water Octorok with their Swords after it shoots a rock and before it retreats into the water. Water Octoroks are defeated after two strikes with a normal Sword. The Links can also stun a Water Octorok by either firing a Gripshot at it or by using a Water Rod on its spot. The pillar of water created by a Water Rod will force it out of the water and leave it temporarily stunned on top of the pillar. If any of the Links fire a Gripshot at Water Octorok while wearing the Robowear, it will be defeated in one hit. If any of the Links shoot a Water Octorok with a Gust Jar, it will stun it and push it a short distance away. Additionally, the Links can blow Water Octoroks onto land with a Gust Jar, where they will stand still and continue to shoot rocks while vulnerable. The Links can also defeat Water Octoroks from afar with long ranged weapons, such as the Bow, Fire Gloves, and Boomerang. Water Octoroks are defeated after being shot with two Arrows, Sword Beams, or Fire from Fire Gloves. A hit from the Boomerang or the Magic Hammer will cause Water Octoroks to sink below the water, instantly defeating them. The Links can also detonate Bombs on land to instantly defeat them. Upon defeat, Water Octoroks may drop either a Green Rupee or a Blue Rupee. Water Octoroks are Octoroks commonly found in bodies of Water in West Necluda and Hyrule Field. They are now different from the regular Octoroks, being colored with a plant on their head. Like the other variants of Octorok, Water Octorok camouflage with their environment, staying submerged underwater in one spot, with only the plant on their head visible, and their blue color blending in with the water. Once Link gets close enough to a Water Octorok, it will spot him and begin to leap out of the water every few seconds to spit a Rock at him. Link can be hit with a Water Octorok's Rock while moving due to its ability to track his movements both horizontally and vertically, aiming its Rocks for the direction

it will spot him and begin to leap out of the water every few seconds to spit a Rock at him. Link can be hit with a Water Octorok's Rock while moving due to its ability to track his movements both horizontally and vertically, aiming its Rocks for the direction he is moving. Link will always be hit by its Rocks if walking or, if close enough, running in a straight line. While it is Raining, Water Octoroks will inflate like balloons and float above the water due to the drop in barometric pressure that occurs during rain, causing their internal Octo Balloon to inflate. Like with other Octoroks, Link can defeat Water Octoroks by guarding with any Shield to deflect their Rocks back towards them. If Link is close enough, the Rock will hit the Water Octorok after being deflected and instantly defeat it. A Perfect Guard will send the Rock flying back faster, allowing kills from a greater distance. Alternatively, Link can defeat Water Octorok by shooting them with any type of Arrow, even if they are below the Water's surface. Link can also cut the plant on a Water Octorok's head by shooting it with an Arrow or slashing it with a Sword, causing it to emerge and look around before retreating back into the Water. This leaves it vulnerable, giving Link an opportunity to shoot it while it is above the Water and not spitting a Rock. The plant will grow back shortly after being cut. Link can also defeat Water Octoroks by detonating a Remote Bomb in the Water or by using Urbosa's Fury, even if they are hiding underwater. The Stasis Rune can be used to suspend them in time. If Link gets close to a Water Octorok, such as with the Cryonis Rune or a Raft, he can hit it with any melee Weapon after it jumps out of the water. Despite having eight health points, Water Octoroks will die from any amount of damage dealt to them. They can be revived without the occurrence of a Blood Moon. Upon defeat, Water Octoroks may drop any combination of several types of Crabs and Fish, Octo Balloons, Octorok Eyeballs, Octorok Tentacles, or Snails. Other Appearances Water Octoroks are Octorok Enemies that often drop Octo Balloons, Octorok Eyeballs, or Octorok Tentacles upon defeat. Killing one also rewards the Warriors with an Octorok Trophy at the end of a Challenge or Scenario. Water Octoroks can be found as some of the main Enemies in Challenges such "Sidon vs. the Octoroks", and are always found in small bodies of Water such as ponds or puddles.

The is a recurring location in . The Water Pump Room goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Water Pump Room is located below Princess Zelda's Study and Princess Zelda's Room in Hyrule Castle. A Waterfall runs down its northern wall. Partway down the Room, Link can find a small side-room with a Lever. Pulling this Lever causes an Updraft to rise from the floor. A passageway in the Water Pump Room leads to the West Passage and Lockup. 100 years prior to the events of , the Water Pump Room was used to supply Water throughout Hyrule Castle. Since the Great Calamity, however, it has fallen into disrepair. Enemies Treasure Chests Korok Seeds As in , the Water Pump Room is located within Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field. It is situated within the portion of the Castle that was suspended in the Sky at the beginning of the Upheaval. The bottom of the Water Pump Room has also filled with debris, and only its upper levels are accessible. As a result of these changes, the Room is no longer connected to the West Passage and Lockup. Enemies Sub-Bosses Equipment Treasure Chests

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Water Reservoir is located on the western edge of West Castle Town in Hyrule Field. It was used to provide water to the townspeople of Hyrule Castle Town prior to the second Great Calamity. A large slate of Rock can be found in the northwestern part of the lake and covers a submerged Metal Chest containing five Bomb Arrows. A second Metal Chest containing a Silver Rupee sits in the south end of the Reservoir. Creatures Enemies The Water Reservoir is relatively untouched, though it is now home to only a single Iron Treasure Chest. Fallen Debris has landed near the eastern bank of the Reservoir, changing some of the nearby ground and foliage. Creatures Treasure Chests

The Water Temple is a recurring Dungeon and location in . Overview Entrance to the Temple The ancient temple lies deep under the vast Lake Hylia. Guarded by the Zoras, it is considered a sacred temple that is used to worship the water spirits. The Water Temple is accessible after the young hero finds the Iron Boots in Ice Cavern. Aided with the boots and the Hookshot, Link can access its entrance by shooting the target above the gate. Themes and Navigation The Water Temple contains the source of the curse that has frozen Zora's Domain. Various parts of the temple require Link to go underwater for substantial amounts of time, thus necessitating the Zora Tunic (though the Water Temple can be beaten without it by an experienced and resourceful player). Its enigmatic structure consists of various floors (four in total, one of them is a basement) and requires the use of playing Zelda's Lullaby at each of the special markings on the walls that manipulate the level of water, which give Link access to various parts of the temple from the hub room. Link will need to use all of his intellectual skills and cunning survival techniques to truly conquer this temple, as puzzles and obstacles are strategically varied: From the aforementioned water level manipulation, to swimming in presence of current flows, defeating enemy groups, climbing a waterfall with descending platforms, raise and lower pillars with a switch, etc.; the young hero will also come to confront his very own doppelgänger, Dark Link in the Water Temple. After defeating Dark Link, Link will find the Longshot which, once acquired, helps Link in the search for the Boss Key and enter the lair of the aquatic boss, Morpha. This temple is infamous to fans for its difficulty and necessity for constantly pausing the game in order to switch to the Iron Boots and back. When the game was remade for the 3DS, the temple was altered in order to be completed easily. The Iron Boots are now a click-on item, glowing markings appear on the wall to show the way, and the entire temple was made brighter. The Water Temple makes much use of Din's Fire in the version of the game. The Hookshot is also used more often than in the original version. The infamous "serpent-shaped" room now has Hookshot targets over the wall, making it easy to simply bunny-hop through the vortex-filled gauntlet. The map, compass, and even the Longshot are obtained very early in the dungeon. The Longshot gives access to a lot of new areas and makes most puzzles easier than before. Most rooms are blocked with gates, so puzzles must be solved to be able to access them. Boulders and most enemies are no longer found, except for two Spikes and nine completely new Stalfos. Two new features include a room with several Dodongos, plus several crates that are found throughout the dungeon. In the GameCube version of the , Link can complete the dungeon

to access them. Boulders and most enemies are no longer found, except for two Spikes and nine completely new Stalfos. Two new features include a room with several Dodongos, plus several crates that are found throughout the dungeon. In the GameCube version of the , Link can complete the dungeon with an extra Small Key remaining. This is because one of the doors that Link is meant to unlock with a key unlocks itself, specifically when defeating the Stalfos prior to Dark Link and causing the dragon heads to rise. The only way to reach this door and unlock it normally is by using glitches. In this glitch was fixed. Eiji Aonuma apologized for the design of the Water Temple in a 2009 interview. Due to the confusing layout and controls for the Nintendo 64 version of , several changes were in . The Iron Boots were changed into an item rather than a piece of equipment, the dungeon received glowing markings on various walls and corridors to mark where the player must go and to make changing the water level more clear, and an additional camera scene was added in the central tower of the dungeon to make the location of a commonly and easily missed Small Key more obvious. Enemies The Water Temple is a Level in . It is the fourth and last Level of the Riverside Area, and is preceded by Cove of Transition. Themes and Navigation thumb|right|320px|Stage 1 The Water Temple is a large, flooded palace filled with many pools. As it involves a lot of swimming and traversing Water, the Zora Costume and the Torrent Robe become very useful here. In Stage 1, the Links enter the Temple from its entrance, where further ahead and down a ramp is a large pool. The Links can find two Gripshots on ledges to the sides. By firing each Gripshot to the north of where they are found, the Links can attach themselves to fences, crossing a small portion of the pool and dropping down onto platforms. A Water Rod can be found on top of a tall platform in the middle of the pool, but cannot be reached at that point. Inside the the pool are two Shock Switches, which are guarded off by railings on particular sides; using the Gripshots, the Links can hit the right Switch from the left platform, and the left Switch from the right platform. Activating both Shock Switches at the same time causes a small platform to appear in the center of the pool. From there, one of the Links can fire the Gripshot at a Crank to the north; doing so will open the Crank and flood the room, allowing the Links to reach the Water Rod. The Link with the Water Rod then has to create pillars of water for the heroes to reach the Triforce Gateway on the north end of the pool. thumb|right|320px|The beginning of Stage 2 In Stage 2, the Links appear on a caged

allowing the Links to reach the Water Rod. The Link with the Water Rod then has to create pillars of water for the heroes to reach the Triforce Gateway on the north end of the pool. thumb|right|320px|The beginning of Stage 2 In Stage 2, the Links appear on a caged floor above a pool of Water. A Big Switch in the center must be pressed down by all three Links, which automatically opens a Crank in the northeast corner and floods the room, as Tektites, Water Tektites and Skullfish appear. The Links must swim onto small platforms to be able to attack them, or use the Water Rod to stun them. Optionally, by using the Water Rod from the northeast platform, or by forming a Totem there, one of the Links with a Gripshot can pull the Crank to drain the room, making the enemies easier to defeat. After all enemies have been defeated, a steel grate in the northwest corner rises, opening to passage. To continue through it, the room needs to be drained if it has not already been. The Links can then walk under the grate and come to a platform that can be reached using the Water Rod. Another Crank can be seen on the wall high above, which can only be opened by using the Water Rod and forming a full Totem on top of the pillar. Pulling this Crank floods the room again, allowing the Links to reach the Triforce Gateway and a Squiddy. thumb|right|320px|The beginning of Stage 3 In Stage 3, the Links find themselves trapped in a caged enclosure with a Water Octorok. Two of the Links can escape the enclosure by using the Gripshot on a panel on the cage wall, which will flip around and drop the Links outside. Those Links then stand on two Floor Switches, opening the cage door so the third Link can escape. Outside the cage, the Links enter a room with platforms at several elevations and Water at a low level. To the northeast is a locked gate leading to the Triforce Gateway, and in the northwest is another section of the room behind a fence wall. Nearby is a platform reachable only with the Water Rod, from which the Links can open another Crank, raising the Water level. The Links with Gripshots can then reach another cage panel by having the other Link lead them with the Water Rod, while avoiding rocks fired at them by nearby Water Octoroks. On the other side of the fence, the Links can find a Treasure Chest containing a Red Rupee, and a Raft that can be pulled toward another platform by using the Gripshot on a Stake. On this platform is a Chest containing a Key, and a Floor Switch that opens the cage door back to the main room. As the locked gate is now submerged underwater, the Links cannot use the Key just yet; two of them are required to turn the Crank again to

On this platform is a Chest containing a Key, and a Floor Switch that opens the cage door back to the main room. As the locked gate is now submerged underwater, the Links cannot use the Key just yet; two of them are required to turn the Crank again to lower the Water, after which the Links can board the Raft and use the Gripshot to transport themselves and the Key to where the Triforce Gateway is. thumb|right|320px|Battling Arrghus in Stage 4 Stage 4 is where Arrghus is fought in a pool. The Links first need to defeat its eyes, using several platforms around the pool's edge to get closer. Once they succeed, the platforms automatically retract and the pool is completely drained. At the bottom of the pool, they battle Arrghus proper, with several Pots containing Hearts and Energy Potions strewn around the floor. After Arrghus is defeated, a door opens in an alcove at the north end leading to the Triforce Gateway. Drablands Challenges Once the Boss of the Riverside has been defeated, the Water Temple can be replayed with the following Drablands Challenges: "Fewer Heart Containers!", "Clear with halved energy!", and "Transport the orb quickly!". In "Transport the orb quickly!", the Links are given a timer of 30 seconds in Multiplayer, or two minutes and 10 seconds in single-player. This timer can be increased by collecting Hourglasses or wearing Linebeck's Uniform. As dropping the orb in Water will cause it to respawn at an earlier location, it is advisable to place the orb on safe ground before using a Crank to flood a room. Magical Materials At the end of the Level, each of the Links can open one of three Treasure Chests. Two contain the same Material, and one contains another, more valuable Material. Enemies Treasure Chests The Water Temple is located on top of Wellspring Island in the Lanayru Great Spring Sky. Areas Enemies Bosses Treasure Chests Equipment Zonai Devices Other Appearances The Water Temple appears as part of the Lake Hylia Stage in . This stage is a part of Sheik and Impa's quest to close the Gate of Souls located inside the temple. An updated version of Dark Link's chamber appears, where Wizzro, disguised as Zelda, is fought. Though the Water Temple is never seen during , a Sign stating that the Real Escape Game was "Easier than the Water Temple" was used as a prop during photo shoots with the Master Sword at events.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Hero's Bows are considered Weapons. Weapons are a type of Item in . Weapons are Link's main way of defeating Enemies by dealing damage to them directly. Weapons have a set amount of durability and will break when this value reaches zero, dealing twice as much damage as they do so. Many of these follow a simple series of archetypes that often coincide with the names of Bows and Shields. For instance, Traveler's Claymores, Traveler's Spears, and Swords compose the Traveler's Gear archetype, alongside Traveler's Bows and Traveler's Shields. Each archetype possesses its own traits, such as boasting high offense at the cost of Durability as is the case with the Royal Guard's Series, or possessing special properties that react to Guardians, such as Guardian Gear which can reflect lasers from Guardians or easily pierce through their defenses. Separately from these archetypes, Weapons also follow behavioral patterns. There are several main types of weapons, with very few exceptions leaving these groups: One-handed Weapons, such as Swords or simple clubs, which have a medium attack rate and damage stat, can be charged at the cost of Stamina to release a spinning charge attack and can be used in tandem with Shields. One-handed weapons also include two subtypes: Boomerangs, which will fly in a straight line and then return to Link after flying a set distance whenever they're thrown, dealing extra damage. They otherwise perform as regular one-handed Weapons. Link can pick up the Boomerang on its way back, but if he fails to catch it or if it crashes into something, the Boomerang will fall to the floor normally. Rods, which do very little melee damage but are instead mostly used at range. When Link performs an attack or throw with them, an elemental effect will happen in a straight line. They come in three varieties, fire, ice and electric. The Korok Leaf has very similar behavior to Weapons in this category and uses wind, but is strangely considered a two-handed Weapon instead. Charge attacks become a bigger elemental blast instead of a spin. Two-handed Weapons, all larger Weapons like claymores and heavy hammers, which have a low attack rate yet high damage and cause Link to constantly spin whilst charging an attack, costing Stamina and dealing damage to any Enemies hit by the spinning Weapon, and then finishing with a powerful downwards slam once the charge is released. If Link takes another Weapon while his Inventory is full, he will drop the Weapon or put it back if it came from a Treasure Chest. Although he does not actually take the Weapon, it will still be identified if it was the first time Link had taken that Weapon. Each Weapon, including duplicates, occupies its own slot in the Inventory. Weapons can also randomly have modifiers when obtained from Treasure Chests or dropped by enemies, with descriptors such as "Durability Up" and "Long Throw" which denote effects such as increased durability or throwing distance. These Weapons exhibit a shimmering sound and have a golden sparkle when laying on the ground. Several Weapons appear in . Beyond existing Weapons, new ones can be made by Fusing multiple Weapons together, or Fusing certain Objects onto a Weapon. Additionally, most weapon archetypes now possess secondary attributes inherent to the archetype called Weapon Traits; for example, the Royal Series of weapons will deal bonus damage during a Flurry Rush. Weapon Information Each Weapon has a certain tier that can determine the range of Attack Strength, skill limit, and element the Weapon holds. Most Weapons and their higher tiers can be unlocked in Adventure Mode, mainly after obtaining A Rank in certain battles. The higher the tier of Weapon, the higher base attack strength the Weapon will have, the higher the amount of Skills the Weapon can hold, and the higher amount of Elements the Weapon attains. Weapons will also have a Star Rating associated with them. This star rating can range from 1 to 5 stars, with 5 being the rarest and 1 being the most common. The Star Rating determines how high or low the Attack Strength of the Weapon is boosted. Each Star Rating will boost the Weapons's base Attack Power by 10 percent. The tier determines the general range of Attack Strength, while the star rating determines the exact value. The chance of obtaining higher Star Rated Weapons can be raised by both using a Weapon with the skill "Stars+" or by making a "Weapon Star 1", "Weapon Star 2", or "Weapon Star 3" Potion in the Apothecary. All Weapons will have an Attack Strength based on the weapons star rating and tier. This value will never change, but can be added on to by adding Skills and leveling up the Warrior in the Training Dojo. The higher the value of the attack strength, the more damage the Weapon will be able to inflict. Each Weapon a Warrior obtains can hold from 1 to 6 Skills to help the Warrior in battle. Skills can boost the Weapon with Attack Strength, increase Enemy Drops, increase Item power-up duration, and more. Some Skills on Weapons are sealed, or locked, and can only be unlocked after defeating a certain number of Enemies with said Weapon. Sealed Skills are hidden and will only be revealed after either unlocking the Skill or appraising it in the Smithy. Sealed Skills can be appraised to reveal the Skill effect at the cost of Rupees. The price to appraise the Skill will scale depending on how many KO's needed to unlock the Skill at 10 Rupees per KO. Some Weapons will have a slot for a Skill, but no Skill will be inside. This open slot can

the Skill effect at the cost of Rupees. The price to appraise the Skill will scale depending on how many KO's needed to unlock the Skill at 10 Rupees per KO. Some Weapons will have a slot for a Skill, but no Skill will be inside. This open slot can be filled by fusing Weapons in the Smithy. If one Weapon has a Skill while another does not, the Skills can be transferred from one Weapon to another. Doing so will destroy the Weapon that originally had the Skill, and fill in the open slot on the other. All Weapons will also have an Element assigned to them. Depending on the tier, Weapons may have more than one Element which the Weapon will automatically switch between depending on which Element has a greater effect. The Weapons' Element can cause the Weapon to have different effects when used on the right enemy, or right battle. If the Weapons' Element is Fire and used in the correct situation, hitting an Enemy will cause it to explode when it hits the ground, dealing damage to Enemies around it. If the Weapons' Element is Water and used in the correct situation, an Enemy will continue to take damage for a short amount of time after being struck. If the Weapons' Element is Lightning and used in the correct situation, Enemies will take more damage when attacked in the air. If the Weapons' Element is Light and used in the correct situation, the Weapons' Attack Strength will become stronger when the Warrior consecutively hits a group of Enemies but will return to base attack when the Warrior stops attacking. If the Weapons' Element is Darkness and used in the correct situation, the Weapons' Attack Strength will become stronger when the Warrior consecutively hits a single Enemy but will return to base attack when the Warrior stops attacking. Weapon Usage Weapons can be used to defeat Enemies, cut Grass, and destroy Jars. Weapons can be used by Warriors in different combinations of moves to inflict damage upon Enemies. Depending on what buttons the player presses, the Warrior will do a different set of moves. Warriors will use regular attacks if the player presses the Y button, (Or the B button if the player chose the Zelda Style controls) or will use Combo Attacks if the player presses the X button. (Or the Y button if the player chose the Zelda Style controls) If the player presses the A button (Or the X button if the player chose the Zelda Style controls) the Warrior will use a Special Attack. Special Attacks are powerful attacks that Warriors can use once their Special Attack Gauge is filled. Warriors can raise their Special Attack Gauge by defeating many Enemies. Warriors can use different combinations after the player presses the Combo Attack button after pressing the Regular Attack button any number of times. If the player presses X alone, the Warrior will use a Strong Attack. Some combinations for Warriors' Weapons

raise their Special Attack Gauge by defeating many Enemies. Warriors can use different combinations after the player presses the Combo Attack button after pressing the Regular Attack button any number of times. If the player presses X alone, the Warrior will use a Strong Attack. Some combinations for Warriors' Weapons can only be unlocked after crafting a Badge in the Badge Market. Some Skills on Weapons will also improve the Attack Strength of certain combinations of moves. Throughout battles, Warriors can find patches of Grass growing in many places. A Warrior can cut the Grass by using any attack, which can reveal Rupees, Force Fragments, Magic Jars and Hearts. Each Grass cluster will only give the Warrior one Green Rupee, and the Force Fragments, Magic Jars and Hearts will be at their smallest form, with the Hearts only refilling one of the Hearts in the Warriors' Health, the Force Fragments only filling 33 percent of the Special Attack Gauge, and the Magic Jars only filling 20 percent of the Magic Gauge. In Keeps, Warriors can find multiple Jars lining the walls of the Keep which the Warriors can destroy with their Weapons. Tan colored Jars will reveal Rupees or Power-Ups for the Warriors Items when destroyed. Yellow colored Jars will reveal Force Fragment when destroyed. Green colored Jars will reveal Magic Jars when destroyed, and finally, red colored Jars will reveal Hearts when destroyed. Cadence, Link, and Zelda can use a variety of Weapons in . Broadswords, Spears, and Flails can be used by any of the three. Daggers are only used by Cadence and Zelda, though Link can use Short Sword, which are functionally identical. In addition, each character except for Yves has at least one special Weapon that only they can use. Most Weapons can be infused by a Great Fairy in exchange for Diamonds. Glass and legendary Weapons cannot be infused. When a Weapon is infused, it will gain a new attribute. Glass Weapons boast 3 points of damage, but will shatter and disappear if the owner takes damage while wielding them. Legendary Weapons have powerful properties such as multiple infusion effects, different special moves, or even armor-piercing capabilities. There is at least one legendary Weapon for each type of Weapon. For a list of all Weapons, see Weapons in . In , as in , playable Warriors can use different weapons. These can be found in-battle and can only be used by a certain Warrior. Each weapon can be upgraded seveal times to increase its attack power until it reaches Level 20. , also known as , are a recurring mechanic in . Overview Weapon Bonuses are advantageous modifiers randomly given to Items in Link's Inventory when they are first obtained. Despite their name, Weapon Bonuses are not exclusive to Weapons and can also be found on Shields and Bows. Modifier types There are several different types of modifiers granted by Weapon Bonuses, and they come in two "tiers" indicated by their color: white and yellow. Although some Weapons are set to have a minimum tier of Weapon Bonus, most are determined by the World Level– a given weapon starts out with no modifiers, then is guaranteed a white one, then a yellow one. This renders The following is a list of Weapon Bonuses per tier with their effects. Some Weapon Bonuses are only applicable to certain types of Weapons; there are also more specific restrictions expanded upon in the next section. Weapons obtained through amiibo are guaranteed the maximum value for their applicable modifier tier (white or yellow), but will display as white regardless of which one it actually received. Additionally, due to a bug, Shields dropped from amiibo chests which are meant to have the white Shield Guard Up bonus will apply that value to the durability and correctly display it as a Durability Up bonus. This means that Shields from amiibo cannot receive Shield Guard Up, and have two possible values for Durability Up. This does not apply to the second-tier Shield Guard Up+ bonus, though as mentioned this will display as white bonus. There are also two unused types of Weapon Bonus within the game, both of which would be yellow: Shield Surf Up, which multiplies the friction of a Shield when Shield Surfing by 0.2, and an unnamed bonus for Bows internally called AddZoomRapid, which gives any bow a zoom property similar to the Golden Bow or Phrenic Bow. is a recurring mechanic in . Overview left|400px|thumb|Map used for climates. Check "Field Map Areas" on the object map for more details In , several different types of Weather can be encountered throughout Hyrule. The Weather changes dynamically, with most locations subject to clear or overcast Weather as well as Rain and Thunderstorms. At lower temperatures (especially at higher elevations), Rain will turn into Snow. The current Weather is indicated by a forecast to the left of the Mini-Map. The Sheikah Slate's Map also displays the current Weather. Every four in-game hours, the Weather of a given area will change. While not part of the dynamic weather system, certain areas may have Winds or Raging Winds. Similarly, colder areas are known as Freezing Climates, where Snow and Cold Water is common. Eldin and the Gerudo Desert both suffer from excessive Heat, which is caused by their Scorching Climate and Extremely Hot Zones, respectively. Portions of the Gerudo Desert also feature Sandstorms. Hyrule Kingdom is divided into 94 small "map areas" that are linked to one of the twenty predefined "climates." The name of Link's current map area can be seen in the System menu while Saving. Climates have different appearance rates for each Weather type and may be shared across different map areas. are recurring locations in . Features and Overview In , the Well is located in the western part of Mabe Village, north of the Village Library. Link can only access it by clearing out the Grass atop the cliff in vicinity, then jumping down. A Piece of Heart can be found in the puddle of Water near a staircase leading out. If Link jumps down the Well while Marin is following him, she will fall on him. In , if Link has met the Photographer, the latter will appear and take a Photo of the moment for The Travels of Link, which he will call "Heads Up!". In , several Wells can be found in the ruins of villages destroyed during the Great Calamity. Many of them contain Korok Seed Puzzles, such as Natural Hiding Spots. All of these Wells were retroactively named in . In addition to these, the structure between the East Wind and a nearby Silo in Hateno Village is referred to as a Well. During the day, Amira and Nikki stand at the Well and talk with each other. When Link approaches them, they will accuse him of eavesdropping on their conversation. To listen to Amira and Nikki, Link must stand behind the Well. Nikki mentions that one of her children recently claimed that a young girl was seen at the Hateno Ancient Tech Lab. Amira remarks that this is strange, and she wonders if the residents of the Lab adopted a child. Nikki dismisses this, claiming that the director, Purah, does not seem the type to do so. She begins to speculate about who the girl could be, before deciding that her idea is impossible. List of Wells There are 58 total Wells scattered throughout Hyrule, 32 of which are returning from . They are most commonly found in the proximity of settlements, such as towns, ruins, or Stables. Link is now able to access the interior of Wells, where he can find many of the same Creatures and Materials that appear in Caves. The interiors of most Wells are Stable Climates, thereby preventing Link from taking Weather-related damage while he is inside. There are three Wells that double as Chasms, serving as entryways into the Depths. Fera, who is a fan of Wells, dreams of traveling to all 58 Wells in Hyrule. As part of the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?", she tasks Link with finding the locations of these Wells. In return, she pays him 10 Rupees for each Well he discovers for her. As a reward for finding all of them, she gives Link the All's Well. The structure in Hateno Village that was referred to as a Well in returns in . It is still the location where Amira and Nikki speak with each other during the day. List of Wells Several Wells appear within settlements in .
