is a location in . Features and Overview Wellspring Island is the largest Sky Island in the Lanayru Great Spring Sky. The Gravity in the area is low, resulting in Link jumping higher than usual. It is the origin of the Watery Bridge, which connects it to the Lanayru Great Spring below. The Water Temple is also located on top of Wellspring Island. After Link defeats Mucktorok in the Water Temple, Mei can be found on one of the eastern Sky Islands attempting to catch some Fish. She explains that she was led there by her heart and that due to the low Gravity, she is able to catch Fish simply by jumping around. The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The West Barrens are located in the Gerudo Desert. The West Barrens make up the entire northwest section of the Gerudo Desert. In the Shrine Quest, "The Silent Swordswomen", Link must follow a series of the swordswomen statues through the sandstorm in the West Barrens. This will point Link to the hidden Kema Zoos Shrine. The Barrens contains the West Gerudo Ruins. Kilton's shop, Fang and Bone, can be found in the West Barrens at night on a small platform near Gerudo Town. A Treasure Chest containing a Gold Rupee sits on a platform in the center of the ruins. Several skeletons of large creatures are scattered around the area.

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview West Castle Town is located on the eastern side of the Hyrule Castle Town Ruins in Hyrule Field. The landscape is destroyed and covered in deep Pools of Malice. A stone Treasure Chest containing a bundle of five Bomb Arrows can be found inside the bastion along the southern wall. A second stone Treasure Chest containing a bundle of five Fire Arrows can be found along the western wall east of the Katah Chuki Shrine. A third stone Treasure Chest containing another bundle of five Bomb Arrows can be found inside the bastion along the western wall. Another bundle of five Bomb Arrows can be found in a stone Treasure Chest inside the northwestern bastion. Atop the northernmost wall, Link can find a bundle of five Ice Arrows inside a stone Treasure Chest. A Korok can be found in a Natural Hiding Spot beneath a Rock at the southwestern wall along the road to the Quarry Ruins. Creatures Enemies Materials West Castle Town remains largely untouched, with some Fallen Debris littering its grounds. There are four Hyrule Restoration Material stations scattered among West Castle Town and additional Restoration Materials in the southeast as signs of a reconstruction effort. A ruined tower in middle of the road in the south has a Cracked Wall that can be destroyed to create a passageway. Ruins Rubble may occasionally fall from the Sky here, however there are no Sky Islands above West Castle Town. West Castle Town surrounds the Water Reservoir, located in its northwest. It has roads which lead to the Moat Bridge in the northwest, Passeri Greenbelt in the southwest, and the Central Square, Hyrule Castle Town Gate, and East Castle Town in its east. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The West Deplian Badlands are a series of barren landscapes in the Eldin Mountains range. They are located south of the Deplian Badlands and northeast of the Drenan Highlands. The West Deplian Badlands offer very little vegetation, though more plant life can be found along the slope to the West Deplian Badlands' east. At the top of this slope, there is a large monster camp. Two metallic Treasure Chests can be found at the top of this camp, containing a Ruby and a Sapphire. A Korok can be found underneath a Rock atop a spire of land at the base of West Deplian Badlands' northern slope. Creatures Enemies

The , also known as the , is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Northwest Gate is one of three gates that serve as an entrance to Gerudo Town. It is guarded by Laine, a Gerudo Soldier. Past the Gate is the Sand-Seal Rental Shop Northwest Booth, which is operated by Kohm. When Link speaks to Laine at the Northwest Gate, she will warn him against traveling the West Barrens during a Sandstorm, as travelers can easily become lost. She warns him that both thieves and priceless treasures are hidden in Sandstorms. After receiving permission from Teake during the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Link will be able to ask Laine about the Karusa Valley. She will point him towards the Valley from the Northwest Gate. Link can also ask about the treasure in the Sandstorm. Laine points out the nearby Swordswoman Statue, explaining that there are more of them throughout the Gerudo Desert. There are rumors that the Statues lead towards an ancient treasure, but she dismisses this as superstition. She also considers it too risky, considering the dangerous Monsters in the area. This begins "The Silent Swordswomen" Shrine Quest.

The are a recurring location in . Features and Overview The West Gerudo Ruins are located throughout the West Barrens of the Gerudo Desert. They are a scattered set of Gerudo Ruins, bearing the Gerudo architectural style distinct from the rest of Hyrule. Several of the Swordswomen Statues are situated within the Ruins. During the day, Link needs at least two levels of Heat Resistance in order to survive the intense Heat at the West Gerudo Ruins without taking damage. At night, the Ruins become a Freezing Climate, and Link will need at least two levels of Cold Resistance. In addition to this, the West Gerudo Ruins will initially be subject to the Sandstorm that sweeps over the West Barrens. During "The Silent Swordswomen" Shrine Quest, Link will pass through the West Gerudo Ruins while following the Swordswomen Statues in the West Barrens. Once Link reaches Kema Zoos Shrine, the Sandstorm will end. left|40px One Korok Seed Puzzle can be found among the West Gerudo Ruins. It takes the form of a Race on one of the southern Ruins. When Link completes the Race, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Enemies Materials Equipment

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The West Hyrule Plains are a series of plains located between Hyrule Field and the Tabantha Frontier. The Hilltop High Road cuts through the Plains, and they are connected to Mount Gustaf by a land bridge that crosses over the Regencia River. An unoccupied campsite can be found in a small marsh in the northern Plain. A Monster Stronghold has been established in the ruins in the southern Plain. Various Barrels and Wooden Boxes that contain Acorns and Apples can be found within this camp. South of these ruins stand several Stone Rings which face various directions. The traveling Rito bard, Kass, can be found atop a rock formation in the far southern reaches of the West Hyrule Plains. He is there in search of the source of the last "Ancient Song" that his teacher, the Court Poet, taught him. He offers to play the song for Link, the lyrics of which describe threading two Stone Rings with an Arrow to reveal an Ancient Shrine. This begins the Shrine Quest "The Two Rings". When Link is able to shoot an Arrow through two Stone Rings, Sheem Dagoze Shrine will rise from the ground. Another traveler, Chabi, can be found fighting against a Blue Bokoblin near her Tent, which is located on the West Hyrule Plains at a fork in the Hilltop High Road. If Link saves her, she will give him Monster Extract as a reward. A Yiga Footsoldier may pass through the West Hyrule Plains disguised as a Traveler. In addition to this, A Blue Hinox can be found resting in the southern Plain. If Master Mode is active, it is replaced with a Black Hinox. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Treasure Chests Korok Seeds

The is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The West Passage is a defunct tunnel system that is part of the Hyrule Castle Underground. The entrance of the West Passage is marked by several Luminous Stone Deposits, and it can be found near the Water of the Hyrule Castle Moat, west of the Hyrule Castle Gate. The entrance contains several Wooden Boxes and Barrels, an unlit Cooking Pot, and a lit Torch. A Cracked Wall separates the entrance and the Passage, which contains Mine Cart Tracks that Link can traverse on a Mine Cart. At the other end of the Tracks, Link will find another cavernous chamber. There is a Hot Spring here, and a sloped ledge above this Spring leads further into a tunnel that ends in a Cracked Wall made out of stone tiles. If destroyed, it will open up a passage to Lockup and the Water Pump Room. The second chamber of the West Passage was a Guardian excavation site, as evidenced by the five half-buried Fallen Guardians found throughout. A Bird nest with two Bird Eggs inside sits in front of the north Fallen Guardian. Inside the West Passage, Link can find a number of Wooden Boxes, which can be destroyed for supplies. While the majority of the Boxes yield Arrows or Apples, one next to the start of the Mine Cart Tracks with a Barrel on top of it can be destroyed for three or four Hyrule Herbs, both varieties of Carrot, either type of Radish, Swift Violets, Mighty Thistles, Armoranths, or Blue Nightshades. Enemies Materials Treasure Chests Korok Seeds As in , the West Passage composes part of the Hyrule Castle Underground in Hyrule Field. Due to the Upheaval, it has suffered several cave-ins. Its entrance is now partially blocked by a Cracked Wall, and the tracks are blocked by Hard Sediment. Creatures Enemies Materials Treasure Chests

is a recurring location in . West Vatorsa Snowfield goes unnamed in . Features and Overview West Vatorsa Snowfield is a flat field of Snow in the Gerudo Highlands. It is located directly west of the Vatorsa Snowfield, and the two locations are separated by a natural stone archway. The Snowfield is bordered by Gerudo Summit to the north and Meadela's Mantle to the south. A campsite with a Cooking Pot can be found in a cave on the eastern end of the Snowfield. Link requires at least two levels of Cold Resistance to traverse the West Vatorsa Snowfield without taking damage, since it is part of a Freezing Climate. After flying through Vatorsa Snowfield, Farosh will fly over West Vatorsa Snowfield as well. When this happens, strong Winds will pass through the Snowfield. A Stone Talus (Rare) is found on the Snowfield's eastern side. Several Enemies frozen in chunks of Ice can be found embedded in the ground on the western end of Snowfield, as well. It will initially be dormant, but if Link approaches it, it will rise up and begin to attack him. Many Treasure Chests are located on the West Vatorsa Snowfield. In total, they contain five Ice Arrows, five Bomb Arrows, one Topaz, one Ruby, and two Sapphire. left|40px There is one Korok Seed Puzzle on the West Vatorsa Snowfield. It is a Race that starts on Rutimala Hill nearby, ending on the western end of the Snowfield. If Link reaches the end of the Race (Object) before time runs out, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures Enemies Materials

The , also known as the Western Road, is a recurring location in . The Westbound Road goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Westbound Road is a pathway leading northwest from Tabantha Bridge Stable and the Hilltop High Road. It begins at the Tabantha Great Bridge, and it ends at the entrance to Rito Village near Rito Stable. Along the way, the Road passes between the Rayne Highlands, Piper Ridge, and Nero Hill, and it also crosses over Kolami Bridge and Kolami Bridge South. Several Ancient Hylian Ruins can be found along the Road. Creatures Enemies Materials The Westbound Road reappears in . As a result of the Upheaval, the Wide Hole has appeared along the Road.

The is a recurring location in . The Western Entrance goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Western Entrance is located on the western side of the Kara Kara Bazaar, along the road connecting it to Gerudo Town. The Western Entrance remains the same as its appearance in , save for the addition of Barricades along the road. At the beginning the Sand Shroud, the Western Entrance is guarded by the Voe Caravan Squad, who are attempting to win the favor of the Gerudo Soldiers. However, when Gibdos attack Kara Kara Bazaar during the "Riju of Gerudo Town" Main Quest, the Voe Caravan Squad abandons their post and hides in the Kara Kara Bazaar Inn, which results in Ripp firing them. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Wetland Stable is a Stable located in the Lanayru Wetlands along Hylia River; it rests north of the Dueling Peaks and northwest of the Riverside Stable. The Wetland Stable is operated by Lawdon, who runs both the Horse-tending service and the inn. Just outside the entrance, Yolero trains with his Master Torch, which he claims to be the legendary Weapon that is given to the chosen hero. Ami sits next to the Cooking Pot and reluctantly gives directions to the east, west, and north. If Link asks about the east, Ami replies simply with Zora's Domain; if he asks about the west, Ami tells him about Hyrule Castle and the fabled East Passage that leads directly into the Castle; if he asks about the north, Ami replies with Death Mountain. When Link tries to leave, Ami asks if he would like to know what is to the south. If Link says yes, Ami complains that he would like to know as well, but that he is never allowed to the leave the Wetland Stable. Inside the tent, Link can find a Poster depicting a recipe for an Electro Elixir, as well as the Rumor Mill: Volume 5 on a table. Behind the Stable sits the Kaya Wan Shrine. Hestu may also appear here while on his way back to Korok Forest. Quince can be found with his pet Hylian Retriever, Satty watching the east; the latter can be befriended to find a metal Treasure Chest containing an Opal in the woods nearby. As with all other Stables, Beedle can be found sitting just outside Riverside Stable's entrance, but he will retreat inside when it is Raining. Kass can be found playing his bandoneon in front, and he mentions the Kaya Wan Shrine nearby. He then asks if Link would like to hear a song about Calamity Ganon from 10,000 years ago. Cambo, Endai, Kazul, Rik, and Spoone stop at this Stable on their journeys. After Link saves Leekah at Rebonae Bridge, she will head to the Stable for safety. When staying at Wetland Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Lawdon explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Lawdon offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Lawdon will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Lawdon will greet him. By Sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. One of the Stable Workers, Izra, can be found looking into the Water of Hylia River next to the remains of an old Wagon. If Link speaks to him, Izra will point out a shape in the Water that he believes is a Treasure Chest. He has been trying to figure out

the Stable Workers, Izra, can be found looking into the Water of Hylia River next to the remains of an old Wagon. If Link speaks to him, Izra will point out a shape in the Water that he believes is a Treasure Chest. He has been trying to figure out how to pull it ashore with little luck, and he is so curious about its contents that he has been losing sleep. To complete the "Riverbed Reward" Side Quest, Link must pull the Treasure Chest up using the Magnesis Rune. Inside, he will find a Knight's Broadsword. If Link tells Izra that he found treasure inside, he will be frustrated that he lost his opportunity to become rich. Alternatively, if Link informs Izra that it was a sword, he claims he did not want the treasure. After this, the Side Quest will be completed, and Link will be able to keep his Knight's Broadsword as a reward. If Link has already completed "Find the Fairy Fountain", Pikango can be found painting Hyrule Castle at Wetland Stable during the "Captured Memories" Main Quest. He will be happy to see Link again and offers him help in identifying Pictures. In this location, Link is able to show him the twelfth Picture in his Album, which Pikango is able to identify it as a forest northeast of the Bottomless Swamp. The is a location in . Features and Overview The Wetland Stable South Well is situated in the woods behind Wetland Stable, being part of the Lanayru Wetlands. It was originally constructed by Ami to serve as the Stable's primary Well, but he was forced to abandon it when a Monster Outpost was established nearby. He then built the Wetland Stable Well as a replacement. The interiors of both Wells are connected by a tunnel and covered with a shallow layer of Water. Several Barrels and Wooden Boxes can be found within the two Wells. As part of the Side Quest "An Uninvited Guest", Ami wishes that someone would defeat the Blue Moblin in the woods, since he is afraid of it attacking Wetland Stable. By entering the Wetland Stable Well and exiting from the Wetland Stable South Well, Link can sneak up on the Monsters and dispatch the Blue Moblin. Once he does so, Ami will give him two Pony Points as a reward. Creatures Materials

The is a location in . Features and Overview The Wetland Stable Well is located behind Wetland Stable in the Lanayru Wetlands. Link is able to access its interior using the Ladder inside its rim, which consists of a small underground chamber consists of a pool of Water. It was built by Ami to replace the Wetland Stable South Well after a Monster Outpost was established nearby. The two Wells are connected to each other by a tunnel, within which are several Barrels and Wooden Boxes. During the Side Quest "An Uninvited Guest", Ami wants someone to dispatch the Blue Moblin in the Monster Outpost. After entering the Wetland Stable Well, Link can exit from the Wetland Stable South Well in order to sneak up on the Monsters. As a reward for defeating the Blue Moblin, Ami will give Link two Pony Points. The Wetland Stable Well is one of several Wells that Fera can be found in prior to beginning the Side Quest "Where Are the Wells?". She rates the Well's Water quality as fair and its moss growth as extensive, in addition to confirming the presence of Brightcaps. Once her Side Quest has started, she leaves for the Lookout Landing Well. Creatures Materials

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Link can make Wheat Breads by Cooking Tabantha Wheat and Rock Salt together in a Cooking Pot. Eating them will restore some of Link's Hearts. The scent of these soft, springy breads is known to be heavenly. Adding extra Ingredients to Wheat Bread can result in the following variations: Hearty Wheat Bread: Made by adding hearty Ingredients. If eaten, they heal all of Link's Hearts and grant him Extra Hearts. Energizing Wheat Bread: Made by using energizing Ingredients. Consuming them will partially refill Link's Stamina Wheel. Enduring Wheat Bread: Made by using enduring Ingredients. Link's Stamina Wheel will be completely restored and overfilled when he eats these breads. Hasty Wheat Bread: Made by using hasty Ingredients. When eaten, Link will receive a boost to his movement speed. Spicy Wheat Bread: Made by using spicy Ingredients. They can be eaten to grant Link one level of Cold Resistance. Electro Wheat Bread: Made by using electric Ingredients. One level of Shock Resistance will be given to Link when he eats them. Mighty Wheat Bread: Made by using mighty Ingredients. By eating these breads, Link's attack power will be boosted. Tough Wheat Bread: Made by using tough Ingredients. If consumed, they increase Link's defensive abilities. Sneaky Wheat Bread: Made by using sneaky Ingredients. Link's Stealth will receive a boost if he eats them. Chilly Wheat Bread: Made by using chilly Ingredients. Eating these breads will grant Link one level of Heat Resistance. Like in , Link can make Wheat Bread by combining and bundle of Tabantha Wheat and Rock Salt in a Cooking Pot. By default, the Recipe will only restore two Hearts, but this can be increased by adding extra Ingredients. On top of the variations found in , Wheat Bread can also come in a Rapid, Bright, Warding, Sticky, Scorching, Sunny, and Biting variants depending on the Ingredients used. Other Appearances The Recipe for Wheat Bread is earned by completing the Quest "Expert Cooking Lesson". It is made using five bundles of Tabantha Wheat and pieces of Rock Salt. However, it can be lowered to four of each Ingredient through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, the Cooking effects of other Foods will increase by 20%.

Another can be found by lifting a Rock on top of the largest tree at the base of the Hill in the southwest. Creatures Enemies Materials Whistling Hill reappears in . The is a location in . Features and Overview The Whistling Hill Cave is situated southwest of Whistling Hill in Hyrule Field. The Cave's entrance is initially blocked by Hard Sediment, which Link must destroy in order to access its interior. The entrance of the Cave is a downward tunnel which opens into a round chamber that forks in two directions. To the southwest is a small chamber that is blocked by more Hard Sediment. This chamber houses two Ore Deposits and a single Rare Ore Deposit. The path to the northwest is tunnel that is obstructed by roots which must be cut or burned in order to advance. This tunnel leads to a shaft housing a single Ore Deposit and a den of Stalkoblins. The Cave then continues to another chamber to the southwest. In this chamber there are two ledges that fork the Cave in two more directions. The northwest ledge hides a small chamber that houses an Iron Treasure Chest. The southeast ledge leads upward to another room with two Ore Deposits and a single Rare Ore Deposit. At the end of this room there is a collection of Hard Sediment blocking the way into another chamber with pools of Water on the floor and a Shock Like dangling from the ceiling. Behind this Shock Like there is another collection of Hard Sediment that blocks the end of the Cave where one Ore Deposit and one of Misko's caches of treasure can be found. Ascending from this cache site will bring Link to the Teniten Shrine just south of the Cave. Creatures Enemies Materials Treasure Chests

are recurring Bosses and Enemies in . Characteristics White-Maned Lynels are a white and black-colored variant of Lynels. They have existed in Hyrule since ancient times, though few witnesses of this breed survive afterwards. Like other Lynels, they will often refrain from attacking for a short period of time after spotting Link, instead opting to stare him down. However, they start their battle by roaring out loudly and slamming their Weapon down to causing a fiery explosion around them. Being a higher tier variant from the Blue-Maned Lynels, they are known to carry a stronger set of "Savage" Lynel Gear, which includes the Savage Lynel Sword, Savage Lynel Shield, Savage Lynel Bow, Savage Lynel Spear, and Savage Lynel Crusher. In Master Mode, White-Maned Lynels carry "Mighty" Lynel gear. However, the White-Maned Lynel that appears on the Great Plateau carries a Savage Lynel Crusher and Savage Lynel Bow. At the beginning of Link's eighth Recovered Memory, "A Premonition", several defeated White-Maned Lynels and Bokoblins are shown. Drops White-Maned Lynels reappear in . Other Appearances White-Maned Lynels are Powerful Foes that can be encountered in . White-Maned Lynels appear as Powerful Enemies in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses White Chuchu Jelly can be obtained by killing Ice Chuchus, or by killing Chuchus with ice weapons. It can also be made from regular Chuchu Jelly by using an Ice Rod or Blizzard Rod to freeze it or by dropping it into icy water. They are cool to the touch and can be squeezed to relieve stress. If hit by a weapon, the jelly will burst and release a cloud of ice that can freeze nearby enemies. Elixirs can be made with White Chuchu Jellies by being combined with critters in a Cooking Pot. The Kochi Dye Shop accepts White Chuchu Jellies to make White Dye, while Kilton at the Fang and Bone can exchange them for Mon. White Chuchu Jelly is used to upgrade the Desert Voe Set of Armor to its first and second tiers at a Great Fairy Fountain. White Chuchu Jellies return as Items in . They can be attached to Arrows in order to freeze Enemies. White Chuchu Jelly is used to upgrade the Desert Voe Set of Armor to its first and second tiers at a Great Fairy Fountain. , also known as , are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Goddess Sword is a Weapon that may be obtained at random within a Treasure Chest that appears after tapping "The Legend of Zelda" series Link amiibo with the amiibo Rune. It has 28 attack power and a durability of 45. The Goddess Sword houses the fire of the Goddess Hylia. It is said that a "heavenly breeze" kicks up around its wielder. Being made of metal, the Goddess Sword will attract Lightning if it is equipped during a Thunderstorm and conduct Electricity. It will also sink in Water, but it can be picked up and manipulated using the Magnesis Rune. If it is exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate, the Goddess Sword will not burn like a wooden Weapon would. The White Sword of the Sky is a Weapon that is obtained as a completion reward for the Side Quest "The Mother Goddess Statue". After the Side Quest is complete, Link may reobtain the Weapon by bringing the Mother Goddess Statue Dinraal's Claw, Naydra's Claw, and Farosh's Claw. The White Sword of the Sky may also be obtained at random within a Treasure Chest that appears after scanning a series Link amiibo, after Link has visited the Depths for the first time. The White Sword of the Sky has a base attack power of 24 and a max Durability of 45 (70 when Fused). It cannot naturally receive Weapon Bonuses and has no special properties.

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Wildberries are found growing on bushes in the Gerudo Highlands and Hebra Mountains, or they can be dropped by Hinoxes when defeated. They can be eaten raw to restore half of a Heart. If a Wildberry is roasted over a Campfire or dropped in a hot location like Death Mountain, it becomes a Roasted Wildberry, which doubles its healing properties to heal a full Heart of the Life Gauge. At the Kochi Dye Shop, Wildberries are one of the ingredients that can make Peach Dye. Wildberries are not required to upgrade any pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. As part of the Side Quest "The Mystery Polluter," Link must give Calyban 10 Wildberries in order to get her to stop polluting the Water trough in Dalia's garden. Once Link delivers the Wildberries, Calyban will help Dalia start a Wildberry garden in Gerudo Town, which completes the Side Quest. Wildberries are necessary to make a Wildberry Crepe in a Cooking Pot. Either a Wildberry or an Apple is needed to make Fruitcake. They can be used in other Fruit-based Meals: Wildberries are similar to their counterparts. They are still not used to upgrade any pieces of Armor at a Great Fairy Fountain. Wildberries are required to make Wildberry Crepes in a Cooking Pot. They can be used in other Fruit-based Meals: Other Appearances Wildberries are a Material in . They can be obtained by defeating generic enemy Rito units and their captains. Wildberries are used for completing Quests, to be used by the blacksmiths in the Hylian Blacksmith Guild to break Sealed Skills on Weapons, or to be used in specific Cooking recipes to make combat-boosting Food that call for their usage. Wildberries are Materials that can be obtained in .

are recurring Items in . Location and Uses Wildberry Crepes can be made by Cooking a Wildberry, Fresh Milk, Cane Sugar, Tabantha Wheat, and a Bird Egg together in a Cooking Pot. By eating them, some of Link's Hearts will be restored to his Life Gauge. The Wildberries in this Meal are noted to be sweet and tart, while the dough is thin and springy. Since Wildberry Crepes require five ingredients to be made, all of which lack any Added Effects, no variations can be made. Wildberry Crepes have the same Recipe that they did in , which involves Link Cooking a Wildberry with a bottle of Fresh Milk, Cane Sugar, a bundle of Tabantha Wheat, and a Bird Egg. Other Appearances The Recipe for Wildberry Crepes is earned by completing the Quest "Extreme Foraging". It is made using two Wildberries, two Bird Eggs, two bundles of Tabantha Wheat, two bottles of Fresh Milk, and two pieces of Cane Sugar. However, this can be lowered to one of each ingredient through the completion of "Hungry Hunches". When prepared before a Challenge or Scenario, Enemies will have a 20% higher chance of dropping Materials upon their defeat.

is a location in . Features and Overview Wind Temple 1F encompasses the deck and surrounding area of the Stormwind Ark. It features a Terminal that controls a hatch holding Colgera, the source of the Blizzard plaguing the Hebra Region. However, this hatch is blocked by five turbine-shaped Locks which must be activated with Tulin's Power of Wind. Only two of these turbine Locks can be found on Wind Temple 1F with the other three being on Wind Temple B1 and Wind Temple B2. There are three cabins on the deck, with two to the north and one to the south. The two in the north are blocked by portcullises. The northwest one can be opened by moving its Lever Switch with Ultrahand, while the northeast one needs to have something merged onto its broken Lever Switch before it can be moved. A turbine Lock can be found in the northeastern cabin. The second turbine Lock is located in the southern cabin, which can only be accessed by entering from Wind Temple B1's southwestern room below. A large pair of doors can be opened with Ultrahand atop the tower in the north of Wind Temple 1F. This leads to a room on Wind Temple B1 with a Basement Fan and a turbine Lock. Enemies Bosses Equipment Treasure Chests

is a location in . Features and Overview Wind Temple B1 is the middle segment of the Stormwind Ark. It can be accessed through open passages on each side of the Stormwind Ark, though some are guarded by portcullises that must be opened from the inside first. In the northwest room, there are four lasers that activate a Trapdoor and two pathways that each lead to different parts of the Stormwind Ark. Near the Trapdoor, there is a Ladder that leads to Wind Temple B2, though it cannot be entered unless the turbine on Wind Temple B2 has been activated. Beyond a frozen gap there is a path to Wind Temple 1F, though it is blocked by portcullises controlled by a large Gear. This Gear cannot be rotated unless something is merged onto it with Ultrahand. This leads to a blocked room in Wind Temple 1F that can only be opened by activating the turbine from the Wind Temple B1 side. The eastern side of Wind Temple B1 can be accessed by breaking the Ice spikes on the southeastern opening. It is separated in two portions by a toothed wheel which can be ridden with Recall to access the northeastern segment. In this part, there is a Lever Switch which opens the northeastern entrance as well as a set of disconnected Gear. These Gear can be connected with an Object such as a long Ice spike, opening the way to a turbine Lock. A second turbine Lock can be found by opening the large doors at the top of the tower on Wind Temple 1F and Skydiving down to Wind Temple B1. This Skydiving segment features a Basement Fan and seven lasers which will lock the door to the turbine if anything comes into contact with their beams. Enemies Materials Zonai Devices Treasure Chests

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Windvane Meadow is located in Hyrule Field. A Road between the Hyrule Garrison Ruins and Mabe Village Ruins runs through the Meadow in the north and a crossroads between the Hyrule Garrison Ruins, the Exchange Ruins, and a Road east towards the Whistling Hill runs through the southern portion of the Meadow. During the second Great Calamity, Windvane Meadow was flooded with Guardians that eradicated all Hylian life in and around the Meadow. The remains of a Guardian can be found in the northern part of the Meadow, which can be searched for Ancient Materials. A Monster Stronghold can be found by the crossroads in the southeastern portion of the Meadow. Wooden Boxes and Barrels containing Apples, Arrows, and Hylian Shrooms can be found at this Encampment. This camp also features a lit Cooking Pot. Windvane Meadow is the location where Calamity Ganon reforms into Dark Beast Ganon after being defeated in the Astral Observatory. To prevent Dark Beast Ganon from escaping and destroying Hyrule, Zelda summons Link to Windvane Meadow and erects a barrier of light to contain them both. She also bestows Link with the Bow of Light to aid him in his quest to Destroy Ganon. A stone Treasure Chest containing a Soldier's Claymore can be found in the aforementioned Monster Stronghold. It can only be unlocked after defeating all of the monsters in the camp. A Korok can be found by breaking the Jar shaped like an Acorn hanging from a broken wagon on the side of the northern Road that passes through the Meadow. Another Korok will appear after examining the Leaves with Fairy Dust moving around a small group of Trees in the east of the Meadow. Another Korok is can be found in a Natural Hiding Spot under a Rock in a rock formation, north of the Central Tower. A Korok can be revealed by breaking another Acorn shaped Jar hanging from a large Tree along the southern edge of the Meadow, north of Lake Kolomo. Following the Flower Trail that starts in the Meadow and leads west into a forest between the Meadow and the Exchange Ruins will reveal another Korok. Creatures Enemies Materials Equipment Windvane Meadow reappears in . Areas Creatures Enemies Sub-Bosses Materials Equipment Treasure Chests Korok Seeds Other Appearances The Windvane Meadow appears as part of the Hyrule Field Stage. During the Quest "Study the Blade", an unnamed character instructs Link to cut in Windvane Meadow to strengthen his skills with a sword. After Link collects five Restless Crickets, he notices that he can swing his sword quicker. As a result, he receives a bonus combo for one-handed Weapons.

is a character in . Biography Wingo is a Hylian. Although he is originally a volunteer for the search for Zelda and Link, he eventually becomes a member of Hoz's Monster-Control Crew squad. He carries a Rusty Broadsword and a Lizal Shield. Initially, Wingo can be found looking up at the First Gatehouse of Hyrule Castle, where he is participating in the search for Zelda. When Link speaks to him, he asks if he has come to help the search party. He explains that including himself, many of the searchers feel as though they owe Zelda, which motivates them to look for her. However, he has not been able to meet with Hoz due to his position on top of the First Gatehouse. He suggests that they should stay out of the way until they figure out how to help. Should Hoz not come down soon, Wingo considers climbing up the First Gatehouse to meet him. After Hoz gives the order to withdraw from Hyrule Castle, Wingo realizes he would be annoying if he tried to talk to him right now. After the apparition of Zelda disappears, he moves out with the squad to their next mission, a Monster Stronghold south of the Hyrule Garrison Ruins. While fighting, he uses a Lizal Shield and a Rusty Broadsword and doesn't want Link to distract him.

are recurring Creatures and Items in . Location and Uses Winterwing Butterflies can be found flying in Hyrule Ridge and the Tabantha Frontier. In order to catch them, Link must be sneaking, or else they will fly away. Alternatively, they can be purchased from Beedle at the Gerudo Canyon Stable and Tabantha Bridge Stable. When combined with Monster Parts in a Cooking Pot, the resulting food will be a Chilly Elixir. They can also be used at the Kochi Dye Shop as an ingredient to make Blue Dye. Winterwing Butterflies are blue-winged Butterflies with black bodies that can be found in Freezing Climates on the Surface and in the Sky. Beedle also sells them at Tabantha Bridge Stable. They produce Chilly Elixirs when Cooked with Monster Parts at a Cooking Pot or Portable Pot. They are known among Bug enthusiasts for the unique scales on their wings which cool the surrounding air. is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Wintre Island is a small island in the Lanayru Sea, and it is situated off of Tarm Point at the mouth of the Lanayru Bay. It is the only island in the Lanayru Sea, and rocky shoal is located on its western shore. Embedded in the ground on the northwestern side of Wintre Island is a metal Treasure Chest. Using the Magnesis Rune, Link can free the Chest, which contains a Silver Rupee. left|40px Two Korok Seed Puzzles can be found on Wintre Island. The first is a Flower Trail that starts on the northern side of the Island, eventually ending at its peak. The second Puzzle is a Rock Pattern on the southern side of the Island. When Link completes each of these Puzzles, a Korok will appear and give him a Korok Seed. Creatures

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Wizzrobes are undead wizards that cast beams of magical energy, and are so named because of the cloaks they often wear. While the appearance of Wizzrobes has differed in some games, in all their appearances, they possess the ability to vanish and teleport elsewhere, enabling them to engage Link through ambushes and surprise attacks. Wizzrobes have also appeared as Bosses or Sub-Bosses in certain games. Wizzrobes appear inside Dungeons in . They are encountered in Level 6 and Level 9. In the Second Quest, they also appear in Level 5 in addition to the other two. They resemble humanoids whose faces are entirely hidden in shadow by their hoods. Wizzrobes come in two colors, both with drastically different behaviors. Orange Wizzrobes teleport throughout the room, while shooting magical bolts at Link, before disappearing again. Blue Wizzrobes are a much stronger variant that take more hits to defeat, and attack by moving across the area while casting spells. They will occasionally vanish to swiftly change direction to another area. These Wizzrobes are far more dangerous than the weaker orange variety, especially in cramped rooms where Link can quickly become surrounded by them. Both of their magic can be blocked with the Magical Shield. They can be dispatched with the Sword; however, due to their nature of teleporting across the area, it is easier to attack them from a distance, such as shooting Sword Beams at them. When defeated, red Wizzrobes may drop either a Heart, one Rupee, four Bombs, or a Clock, while blue Wizzrobes may drop either a Heart, one Rupee, or a Fairy. Wizzrobes in appear in Misery Mire and Ganon's Tower. The Wizzrobes of Misery Mire wear green robes and brimmed hats. Unlike Wizzrobes from , they appear and disappear in one place, and cast spells at Link in between. Their teleportation spells are slow, however, as they will briefly appear transparent just before emerging and vanishing. They can only be attacked once they take physical form. A faster variety of Wizzrobe known as Purple Wizzrobes also appear in Ganon's Tower. Wizzrobes in appear similarly to their green incarnation, staying in one spot as they vanish and reappear. When one emerges, it first appears as a hat on the floor, indicating where it will appear. It then rises and fires an attack in Link's general direction before vanishing again. Unlike previous Wizzrobes, they cannot be harmed with the Sword, which will instead only repel them back. They can only be harmed by firing an Arrow at them with the Bow, which will defeat them in two hits; by planting a Bomb near them, which will defeat them in one hit; or by throwing an object at them, such as a pot or a stunned enemy, which will defeat them in one hit. Wizzrobes can also be stunned with the Hookshot or Boomerang, making it easier to defeat them with a Bomb. They appear in the Face Shrine. Wizzrobes come in three different

Wizzrobes with red hoods shoot Fireballs, while Wizzrobes with yellow hoods can both shoot fireballs and summon other enemies. Wizzrobes in appear identically to their appearance in , with three varieties; standard green Wizzrobes, Fire Wizzrobes, and Ice Wizzrobes. They appear in the Palace of Winds and Dark Hyrule Castle. Wizzrobes in retain their bird-like appearance, but are slightly smaller, wear cloth masks, and carry large scythes instead of wands. In spite of the aesthetic similarities, they take on a completely different role in the game. They appear only in the Temple of the Ocean King and do not use their traditional magic. Instead, they are invisible until right before they attack. They will sneak up to steal 15 seconds from the Phantom Hourglass with a swipe of their scythes. They appear as Skulls on the map on the top screen, which is the only way to track them without coming in range of their attacks. Defeating one earns Link 30 more seconds of the Sand of Hours. As of the Version 2.0.0 update, dark Wizzrobes can be found in the Den of Trials. Six types of Wizzrobe appear in . There are three base forms of Wizzrobe: Electric Wizzrobes, Fire Wizzrobes, and Ice Wizzrobes, which carry Lightning Rods, Fire Rods, and Ice Rods respectively. Three stronger variants of these Wizzrobes also appear. These more powerful Wizzrobes are: Thunder Wizzrobes which bear Thunderstorm Rods, Meteo Wizzrobes which carry Meteor Rods, and Blizzrobes which carry Blizzard Rods. Three kinds of Wizzrobes appear: Electric Wizzrobes, Fire Wizzrobes, and Ice Wizzrobes. Although a Wizzrobe makes a brief appearance in "He Also Serves," they play a more important role in "To the First Power" and, to an extent, in "Queen of Hearts." In "To the First Power," a Wizzrobe commands several of Ganon's minions to tie Link up after Zelda heads inside the Eagle Labyrinth to train against Ganon's minions. However, the Wizzrobe reveals to Link that he filled the Eagle Labyrinth with the most dangerous of enemies so that Zelda may not stand a chance up against them. Although Link confronts the Wizzrobe and tells him that capturing Zelda will do no good since he is the one that Ganon wants, the Wizzrobe confesses that he is not interested in following Ganon's orders anymore. He elaborates that he has gathered many other minions who feel the same way, and as soon

the Wizzrobe and tells him that capturing Zelda will do no good since he is the one that Ganon wants, the Wizzrobe confesses that he is not interested in following Ganon's orders anymore. He elaborates that he has gathered many other minions who feel the same way, and as soon as he destroys Link and Zelda, all of Ganon's minions will join his renegade army, leaving Ganon to fail. The story ends with the Wizzrobe kneeling in front of Ganon while the Prince of Darkness praises him since he could make use of a "deceitful and treacherous" man like him. The Wizzrobe in "Queen of Hearts" is in charge of securing the Magic Container that holds all of Queen Seline's magical powers. When Link and Seline make their way to where the magic container is, they are confronted by a Wizzrobe and a horde of Ganon's other minions. Link is then heavily injured and faints, and before the Wizzrobe can finish him off, Zelda appears and shoots an Arrow at the Magic Container, restoring Seline's powers and allowing her to easily defeat the Wizzrobe and the rest of the enemies. A Wizzrobe disguised as a Fortune Teller appears in . Known as Madame Grusha, she resides in the Town of Ruto. If Zelda visits Madame Grusha's hut, she will guess that Zelda has traveled far and that she is searching for three things. The Fortune Teller goes on to explain that she knows how to help the princess, but she cannot speak of it in their current location and asks that Zelda follow her into her inner sanctum. Following Madame Grusha will lead to Zelda's death, while deciding to not follow her will result in a fight between Zelda and the Wizzrobe, along with some Moblins. However, the princess manages to defeat both enemies and come out of the hut alive. In , Wizzrobes appear wearing blue cloaks and carrying wooden staffs. They walk around and occasionally cast blasts of magic, however unlike their canonical incarnations, they do not teleport at will. They appear in the Shrine of Illusion and the Shrine of Destiny. is a recurring Item in . Location and Uses In , Wood can be obtained from Woodcutting Trees throughout Hyrule or found at various settlements like Hateno Village or Stables. They can be chopped using any bladed Weapon or knocked down with Remote Bombs. Once a Tree is felled, Link can strike or blow up the fallen Log to create a bundle of Wood. Wood can be used to light Campfires, along with a flammable Weapon or a piece of Flint and a metallic Weapon. In addition, Wood is used during the "Hylian Homeowner" Side Quest to buy Link's House, as well as during the "From the Ground Up" Side Quest to construct Houses for Tarrey Town. are recurring Items in . Location and Uses The Wooden Bow is found inside a Treasure Chest on the bow of the Sandship after defeating LD-002G Scervo in . It can be aimed and drawn for a longer period of time to increase its overall strength. For a price, Link can Upgrade the Wooden Bow into an Iron Bow. Wooden Bows are weak Bows that are used by weaker Enemies in Hyrule Field and West Necluda. Though they are not well suited for battle, they are known to be useful for hunting small Animals. Being made from wood, Wooden Bows will burn if they are exposed to Fire or a Scorching Climate. If they are not put away or extinguished, they will eventually disintegrate. They also float if they are dropped in Water, which is useful for retrieving them. Finally, they do not conduct Electricity or attract Lightning during Thunderstorms, and they cannot be picked up with the Magnesis Rune. Wooden Bows reappear in . Other Appearances

are recurring Items and Objects in . Wooden Mops go unnamed in . Location and Uses In , a Wooden Mop can be found inside the Knight Academy in Skyloft. It is found leaning against the wall inside the Restroom. When examined, a message appears stating that it's used to keep the room clean. Wooden Mops are commonly used to clean up around households in Hyrule. Therefore, they can be found in villages such as Hateno Village and ruins within East Necluda and Hyrule Field. Despite their intended purpose, Wooden Mops have a sturdy construction, giving them some merit in combat. Being made of Wood, Wooden Mops will float when dropped in Water. They are also unable to conduct Electricity or attract Lightning when equipped during Thunderstorms, but they will burn when exposed to a Fire or a Scorching Climate. Wooden Mops belong to the Daily Use Goods equipment archetype, which consists of tools used for the upkeep of settlements throughout Hyrule Kingdom. Other Appearances

Wooden Shields, also known as Strange Boards, are recurring Items in . These Shields are usually unable to protect against Fire and magical attacks, and may even be burnt by them. The Wooden Shield is usually superseded by a stronger, metallic Shield. Location and Uses In , the Wooden Shield is the first Shield that Link can obtain. It can be upgraded to the Iron Shield and later the Mirror Shield through a Linked Game. Wooden Shields can be bought for 30 Rupees from the Horon Village Shop. In , the Wooden Shield is the first Shield that Link can get. Wooden Shields can be bought for 30 Rupees in the Lynna Item Shop, or from Business Scrubs for varying amounts of Rupees. In a Linked Game, Impa gives Link a Wooden Shield at the start of the adventure instead of the Wooden Sword, which he already has. In , Wooden Shields can be bought at Malo Mart in Kakariko Village or the Hot Spring Shop on Death Mountain. They serve as replacements to the one-of-a-kind and flammable Ordon Shield, the first Shield Link obtains. Wooden Shields are larger than the Ordon Shield and have metal trims, but are functionally identical and may also catch on fire. If it catches fire, the Wooden Shield can be saved by putting it away. Like the Ordon Shield, the Wooden Shield is able to block and subsequently catch Arrows, a feature that Hylian Shields are incapable of. In , the Wooden Shield is the only Shield available. In order to improve his defense, Link must use Neri's powers to improve the Shield's capabilities, such as blocking more projectiles and stunning enemies that run into the Shield. The Shield also appears in , known as the Shield of Antiquity, where it cannot be eaten by Like Likes. In , the Wooden Shield can be obtained from Owlan by talking to him after obtaining the Goddess Sword. It can also be bought from the Gear Shop at the Skyloft Bazaar for 50 Rupees. It is the most basic Shield in the game. It is weak to fire and will burn up if Link falls into lava. However, it is immune to electric attacks, making it useful in the Lanayru Desert. The Shield's special property is that it will not only block enemy Arrows, but also enable Link to collect any of them that are lodged into it; however, while a well-timed Shield Bash will protect it from most fire-based attacks, a flaming Arrow will make it start to burn. By trading Gondo some Rupees and Treasure, Link can upgrade the Wooden Shield at the Scrap Shop. Despite their increased durability, they still retain their weakness to fire. Upgrades Wooden Shields are simple Shields in . They have low defensive power, but they are known to be ideal for less-experienced fighters. They are able to withstand lighter attacks, but it is not recommended to block stronger blows with them. They are found either abandoned or wielded

is a recurring location in . Features and Overview Woodland Stable is a Stable located in Eldin Canyon, bordering Hyrule Field and the Great Hyrule Forest. Its name is derived from its proximity to the Great Hyrule Forest. The Stable sits beside Pico Pond, where Mirro Shaz Shrine can be found nearby. It features an outdoor seating area, in addition to a pen for livestock. Like other Stables, it has a Cooking Pot available for travelers to use. Inside the Stable is a Poster, which depicts a Recipe for Hasty Vegetable Curry. Woodland Stable is run by Kish, who mans both its Horse-boarding services and Inn. A worker at the Stable, Breen, is able to change the Horse Gear or Mane of Link's Horses. An elderly worker, Ashe, is able to tell Link about points of interest in the area. His granddaughter Shamae also lives at the Stable. The Hylian traveler, Molo, can be found sitting outside the Stable. Beedle is a visitor of Woodland Stable, where he offers to sell his wares to Link. The travelers Boldon and Karsh both stop at the Stable during their journeys. If Link saves Leekah to the southeast, she will return to the Stable for safety. While returning to Korok Forest, Hestu becomes lost at Woodland Stable. After upgrading Link's Inventory four times, he will remember the way and leave the Stable. Lastly, if Link has completed "Find the Fairy Fountain", he can meet Pikango at Woodland Stable during the "Captured Memories" Main Quest. When spoken to, he is able to identify the Sacred Ground Ruins in the first Picture of Link's Album. When staying at Woodland Stable, Link can choose to Sleep in either a regular Bed for 20 Rupees or a Soft Bed for 40 Rupees. Kish explains that the Soft Bed leaves its users feeling more energized when they wake up. If Link decides to stay at the Stable, Kish offers to wake him up in the morning, at noon, or in the evening. Once Link makes his choice, Kish will send him off to Sleep. When Link wakes up, Kish will greet him. By sleeping in the Soft Bed, Link will receive an Extra Heart when he wakes up. As part of the "Balloon Flight" Side Quest, Shamae asks Link to put Octo Balloons on a nearby Barrel to make it float. Once Link does so, Shamae will excitedly share her dreams about a land in the sky and flying on a giant bird. She then gives Link a Star Fragment as a reward. When Downloadable Content Pack is active, a copy of the Super Rumor Mill V1 will appear on the table inside Woodland Stable. As part of the "EX Strange Mask Rumors" Side Quest, Link is tasked with reading the Book to learn the location of the Korok Mask. From the Super Rumor Mill V1, he discovers that the Korok Mask is hidden in a Tree in the Lost Woods. If Link befriends Woodland Stable's Hylian Retriever,

the "EX Strange Mask Rumors" Side Quest, Link is tasked with reading the Book to learn the location of the Korok Mask. If Link befriends Woodland Stable's Hylian Retriever, it will lead him to a Metal Chest, which is buried beneath a Tree across the road. Using the Magnesis Rune, Link can pull the Chest above ground and open it, receiving a bundle of 10 Ice Arrows. The is a recurring mechanic in . Overview The World Level is the overall condition determining the quality of Items that appear in Treasure Chests and what Enemies appear through the Enemy Progression system. Some Enemies add a hidden value which is added to the overall World Level when they are defeated. Items and Enemies each have specific thresholds which cause them to be replaced by stronger counterparts when these thresholds are met. Some Enemies, such as the Lynel atop Ploymus Mountain, are unaffected by the World Level and will not change under any circumstances. Additionally, instead of changing into different Items, Item may instead receive stronger Weapon Bonus. The effects of the World Level are unrelated to Blood Moons and can be seen without one occurring. After 10 of a specific Enemy type and rank have been defeated, they will no longer yield any Experience. For example, the maximum amount of Experience that can be gained from defeating Fire Wizzrobe is 50. It is still possible to accumulate Experience points from the Ice-based equivalent Ice Wizzrobes and the more powerful Meteo Wizzrobes independently from this, however. The exceptions to this include Dark Beast Ganon and Monk Maz Koshia, who only award Experience the first time they are defeated. The Phantom Ganons also only award Experience when defeated for the first time in their respective Divine Beast, and Phantom Ganons fought in the Illusory Realm or inside the Sanctum at Hyrule Castle will not yield any Experience when defeated. In the base game, the maximum number of Experience points that Link can earn is 13,150. Including Downloadable Content, Link can earn a maximum of 16,700 Experience points. The maximum threshold for Enemy Progression sits at 6,285.7, which corresponds with the appearance of Golden Lynels in Hyrule. Though Enemies yield a set amount of Experience upon defeat and impact both Enemies and Items, the World Level conditions for growth are applied at different rates for Enemy Progression and Item} progression. A single Experience point contributes a total of 1.4% toward Enemy Progression and 1.2% toward Item progression, respectively. In order to initiate the first change to Enemies through the World Level, Link must exceed a total of 285.7 Experience yield. The minimum possible value that exceeds that total is equivalent to two Fire Wizzrobes (10), three Decayed Guardians (36), and two Silver Lynels (240). These collectively add up to a total of 286 Experience, resulting in the corresponding red-colored Bokoblins found throughout Hyrule to change into Blue Bokoblins. List of Enemy Experience Values List of World Level Thresholds The World Level system in functions in much the same way as in , with a few notable changes: Dungeon Bosses can technically only award experience for being defeated twice, instead of ten times(however, the in-dungeon versions can only be fought once, so they functionally cap at one defeat.) There is a new "Skill System" that awards bonus experience for performing certain actions during combat: Perfect Guards Hitting the enemy's weakpoint Flurry Rushes

only award experience for being defeated twice, instead of ten times(however, the in-dungeon versions can only be fought once, so they functionally cap at one defeat.) There is a new "Skill System" that awards bonus experience for performing certain actions during combat: Perfect Guards Hitting the enemy's weakpoint Flurry Rushes Defeating the enemy without taking damage The maximum skill experience for an enemy type is capped at its current kill experience, meaning that for most enemies, the maximum experience you can earn is 20 times the amount awarded for a single kill (10 defeats + 10 defeats-equivalent of skill experience.) The in-dungeon versions of the Bosses also receive a nerf to skill experience, so only 10% of the normal experience is awarded per action.

is a recurring character in . Biography Worten is a Hylian traveler who can be found resting at the Ton Pu Inn in Hateno Village. During the day he spends his time sitting on the Inn's balcony, enjoying the nice weather and drinking from a tankard. He is knowledgeable about many of the major areas throughout Hyrule, and is eager to share when Link speaks with him. If Link asks about Goron City, Worten tells him it is located to the north in the Eldin Region. He admits he did not make it all the way to the city because of the heat. When questioned about Gerudo Town, Worten mentions it is situated out west, in the Gerudo Desert. He describes how he was driven off by the gatekeeper, only to find out later that only women are permitted entry to the Town. He laments he would not have crossed the Desert had he known, and muses he might have gained entry if he were able to fool them into thinking he belonged. If Link inquires about other towns, Worten notes that Zora's Domain and Rito Village are not-to-miss places for those with a strong sense of adventure, but warns that neither are easy to reach due to distance and dangerous roads. Worten can be found upstairs in the Inn at night, heading inside at 9:00 PM and sleeping until 5:00 AM, or otherwise when it is raining.

is a character in . Biography Wortsworth is a Hylian member of the Zonai Survey Team. He is a scholar with a specialty in deciphering Ancient Hyrulean. Initially, Wortsworth can be found in the Emergency Shelter of Lookout Landing, where he will be engrossed with with research into Hylian, commenting that although the script has not changed, their language has evolved over time. Noticing Link, Wortsworth is able to identify him based on Purah's description. He introduces himself to Link, in addition to explaining what ancient Hyrulean is. Since he only has a few Books as reference material, Wortsworth does not have many results from his research. One day, he wants to have his research posted around the Zonai Survey Team Base in Kakariko Village. During Rain, Wortsworth worries about his documents becoming damaged.

is a recurring character in . Biography Yaido is a Gerudo who can be found in Gerudo Town's bar, The Noble Canteen. If Link goes into the Canteen, he will find Yaido accompanied by two other Gerudo named Pyra and Sumati. If Link speaks to one of them, they talk to each other about a password for a secret place. They stop talking about it as soon as they notice that Link is listening and Sumati tells him to go away. Link can eavesdrop on them by going onto the opposite side of the nearby window in Rotana's house. If Link eavesdrops on them here before ever speaking to them while in The Noble Canteen, he will hear Yaido asking the others if they have heard of a rumor about Fashion Passion. Sumati replies that she has heard the rumor and Yaido responds by saying that she asked Saula about it, but Saula wouldn't tell her anything. Pyra then mentions how suspicious it is that Saula won't give away any information. Once Link is eavesdropping on the Gerudo women after speaking to them directly, he will overhear Sumati referring to him as a little Hylian girl. Pyra then says to forget about the girl and urges Yaido to tell them the password. Yaido reveals that she overheard Saula say that the password is "GSC♦." Sumati quickly realizes that it must stand for "Gerudo Secret Club" before the conversation ends. The password that they reveal allows Link entry to the Gerudo Secret Club. After Link calms Naboris, gains entry to the Gerudo Secret Club and speaks to the Gerudo women again, Yaido will question where Perda is. Sumati says that she left in search of Lover's Pond and Pyra comments that it is rumored to be the perfect place to find true love. Yaido then proceeds to say something, but is interrupted when Sumati tells Link to go away. Link can eavesdrop on them again from the window in Rotana's house to hear them talk about Perda in more detail. While listening, Yaido wonders how Perda is doing and Sumati comments about how enthusiastic she was to find Lover's Pond. Yaido then talks about how quickly she left when she heard that Lover's Pond is in Faron. This surprises Pyra, who thought it was only a rumor. Sumati says that she does not know for sure, but her and Pyra conclude that Perda must have found true love because she has not returned yet. At the end of the conversation, Yaido contemplates if she should also travel to Lover's Pond.

, also known as , are recurring Items in . Location and Uses In , Yellow Chu Jelly oozes from Yellow Chus when they are defeated. It can be scooped up into an Empty Bottle and functions exactly like Lantern Oil, refilling the Lantern fully when used. are recurring Enemies and Bosses in . Characteristics Yiga Blademasters are the elite soldiers of the Yiga Clan. They can be found patrolling the Yiga Clan Hideout, and if they spot Link in the hideout, they will close all doors and exits while calling in back up. After Master Kohga is defeated, they will also start appearing randomly to attack Link. Yiga Blademasters attack with Windcleavers that send blasts of air at long distances. They can also use the Earthwake technique create fissures in the ground, which produce Updrafts that Link can use to Glide before a stone pillar emerges from them. A shot to the head with the Bow can stun Yiga Blademasters, opening them for attacks. When defeated, they flee, leaving behind their Windcleaver and Mighty Bananas. During the Side Quest "The Stolen Heirloom", Link must defeat a Yiga Blademaster in order to retrieve the Sheikah Heirloom that grants access to the Lakna Rokee Shrine. Drops Yiga Blademasters reappear in , acting similarly to how they did in . They now wield Eightfold Longblades with visible Gloom markings rather than Windcleavers. They can disguise themselves as Trees. If Link is wearing the Yiga Clan Attire, he is able to speak to Yiga Blademasters without being attacked. In addition, they are mentioned to be the overseers of the Yiga Clan's Depths operations. Other Appearances Yiga Blademasters appear in as Powerful Foes. They fight the same way as in , though their Weak-Point Gauges can be exploited with Sheikah Runes. They also speak, similar to the Yiga Footsoldiers, in instances such as when they are defeated in battle. After Astor uses the souls of some Yiga Footsoldiers to revive the four blights, Master Kohga and Sooga turn against him. The rest of the Yiga Clan then follow suit, using the Hyrulean Army to exact vengeance on Astor.

The , also known as the Gerudo Desert Hideout, is a recurring location in . Features and Overview The Yiga Clan Hideout is located in the Gerudo Highlands inside what remains of a Gerudo temple that was reclaimed as the secret base of the Yiga Clan and their leader, Master Kohga. It is hidden at the end of Karusa Valley in the Gerudo Desert. Link must infiltrate it in order to recover Riju's stolen Thunder Helm as part of the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest. The road to the Hideout through the upper half of Karusa Valley is dotted with Frog Statues wearing veils with the inverted Yiga Clan eye. Before entering the main Hideout, Link will find himself in a circular chamber full of Torches. From here, he is surrounded by several sets of stairs and cloth banners. He can burn the banners to reveal the objects and Enemies behind them. Behind one of the banners is the entrance to the main Yiga Clan Hideout. Once inside, Link will meet an imprisoned Gerudo soldier named Barta who gives Link a hint about the Yiga Clan's affinity for Mighty Bananas. Link must sneak past all of the patrolling Yiga Blademasters in the Hideout to reach the end. Through the doorway, if Link continues forward he will find a ladder that leads up to an upper walkway to the side a large room with several Blademasters guarding the area. At the end of the walkway, he will find a small room with a Treasure Chest containing a Topaz and a table with 18 Mighty Bananas, serving as plenty of stock for luring Blademasters. In the large room, Link will find more wooden platforms that he can burn to cause Mighty Bananas to drop. There is also a ladder which leads another set of central upper walkways in the room which gives Link a wider variety of sneaking strategies. Link may also hide under the Barrels present in the room to sneak by. There is a Treasure Chest containing a Silver Rupee on the central platform with a Yiga Clan symbol on it. There are also three large cloth banners hanging on the eastern wall. Link can burn them with Fire Arrows and will find two Treasure Chests each containing a Gold Rupee in a secret room behind the middle banner. Link can also find a ladder in this secret room which leads to a back entrance to the central upper walkways, with another Chest containing another Topaz above the doorway. Should a patrolling Blademaster spot Link, they will whistle loudly. This shuts all the doors, alerts all other Blademasters in the room, and summons two Yiga Footsoldiers with Duplex Bows. All Blademasters will drop the torches they were carrying, which can Link can pick up if he is in desperate need of a Weapon. Being spotted can happen in both rooms, meaning Link may fight up to seven Blademasters and four Footsoldiers in the Hideout, as there are two Blademasters

All Blademasters will drop the torches they were carrying, which can Link can pick up if he is in desperate need of a Weapon. Being spotted can happen in both rooms, meaning Link may fight up to seven Blademasters and four Footsoldiers in the Hideout, as there are two Blademasters in the first room and five in the second. The Blademasters' ranged Windcleaver attacks and the Footsoldiers' arrows function normally, but should Link be struck directly by a Blademaster's Windcleaver, he will instantly die regardless of how many Hearts he has, Defense granted by his Armor, any Fairies in his Inventory, or if he has obtained Mipha's Grace. He will be warned of the Yiga for underestimating them, given a Game Over, then sent back to the start of the Yiga Clan Hideout. Link can use Mighty Bananas to lure the Blademasters and sneak past them when they are not looking. After sneaking past the first Blademaster, Link will encounter another one in the next room guarding an open doorway. There is a Treasure Chest in this room containing a sapphire. Two Mighty Bananas can be found sitting on wooden platforms on the walls, which can be shot with arrows to make the bananas drop down and lure the Blademaster. Once Link successfully sneaks past the Blademasters and through the open doorway to the east, he will find himself in a small room with a Treasure Chest on the center platform containing Mighty Bananas. Link can also find three more Treasure Chests buried in the ground whichhe can retrieve using Magnesis. Two of the Chests contain a Topaz and the third one contains a Ruby. To proceed, Link must use Magnesis again on the eastern wall to reveal a secret exit. Through the secret exit, Link will find himself outside of the Yiga Clan Hideout in an open area with a large pit in the center. He is then face-to-face with the Leader of the Yiga Clan, Master Kohga. Master Kohga will demand to know who Link is before he realizes Link is the person he and his clan have been looking for and initiates a battle. After defeating Kohga, he will use his magic to perform his "secret technique," summoning a very large and spiked Yiga ball to try and crush Link. However, the ball rolls backwards and ends up making him fall into the large pit instead. While falling, Kohga is heard yelling that he shall be remembered and the Yiga Clan will track Link to the ends of Hyrule. Because of this, Yiga encounters in the Overworld will become more common. Another Treasure Chest will then appear containing the stolen Thunder Helm Link came for. It will give Riju the power to withstand Divine Beast Naboris' Lightning and protect Link so that he can enter Vah Naboris. give Riju the power to withstand Divine Beast Naboris' Lightning and protect Link so that he can enter Vah Naboris. Link and his allies then attack the Yiga trying to defend their base, and ultimately force Master Kohga and Sooga to flee.

The is a recurring location in . The Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm goes unnamed in and . Features and Overview The Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm is located behind the Yiga Clan Hideout in the Gerudo Highlands. It is a bottomless pit, and Link will void out if he falls into it. The hidden door leading to Master Kohga's Room can be found near the Chasm, though it can only be opened from the inside. During her Divine Beast Tamer's Trial 100 years prior to the events of , Urbosa was tasked with throwing the Sacred Orb into the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm. After Link infiltrates the Yiga Clan Hideout during the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, he will be able to pass through the door leading to the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm. There, he will be confronted by Master Kohga, who recognizes that he is Link and proceeds to fight him. After being worn out by their battle, Master Kohga summons a giant Spiked Boulder to crush Link, but he accidentally rolls himself over and falls into the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm. As he falls, Master Kohga swears that the Yiga will remember him and seek vengeance on Link. Following this, a stone Treasure Chest containing the Thunder Helm will appear at the edge of the Chasm. As part of the "EX Champion Urbosa's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, Link is tasked with emulating Urbosa's Divine Beast Tamer's Trial by throwing the Sacred Orb into the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm. To do this, he must steal the Sacred Orb from inside the Yiga Clan Hideout. He can find two treasure hunters, Mina and Mils, nearby, who are considering infiltrating the Hideout to take the Orb for themselves. After throwing the Sacred Orb into the Yiga Clan Hideout Chasm, the Kihiro Moh Shrine will rise from the ground. Both Mina and Mils are angry with Link for doing this, claiming they would have taken the Orb if he did not want it. The is a recurring location in . The Yiga Clan Hideout Hall goes unnamed in . Features and Overview The Yiga Clan Hideout Hall is a part of the Yiga Clan Hideout in the Gerudo Highlands. It is the Hideout's largest room, and it features the front entrance to Master Kohga's Room. A small storage room filled with Mighty Bananas can be found above the Hall. In addition to this, a series of scaffolding can be used to traverse its upper levels. When Link enters the Yiga Clan Hideout Hall during the "Divine Beast Vah Naboris" Main Quest, Yiga Blademasters will be on patrol. If one catches sight of Link, they will whistle loudly, alerting the rest of the Yiga to his location. Following this, the nearby exits will be closed, and a duo of Yiga Footsoldiers will appear to fight alongside the Blademaster, who abandons their Torch to draw their Windcleaver. Link must pass through the Hall in order to reach the giant pit at the Hideout's end. Once Master Kohga has been defeated, the Yiga will abandon their entire Hideout, including the Yiga Clan Hideout Hall. During the "EX Champion Urbosa's Song" Main Quest, which is exclusive to Downloadable Content Pack, the Yiga will return to their Hideout. After stealing the Sacred Orb from the Gerudo, they hid it in the Yiga Clan Hideout Hall's storage room. They have also returned to patrolling the Hall. In order to obtain the Orb for himself, Link must enter the Hall through Master Kohga's Room and sneak past the Yiga Blademaster guards. Three stone Treasure Chests can be found in the Yiga Clan Hideout Hall. The first is in the storage room filled with Mighty Bananas, and it contains a Topaz. The second is on top of the large pillar in the center of the Hall, and a Silver Rupee can be found inside. The final Chest is located above the doorway to Master Kohga's Room, and another Topaz can be found inside. Enemies Materials The Yiga Clan Hideout Hall is the site of the Yiga Clan Training Mini-Game.

are recurring Enemies in . Characteristics Yiga Footsoldiers are members of the Yiga Clan who follow their leader, Master Kohga. They are always hunting Link down, attempting to assassinate him and stop his quest to defeat Calamity Ganon. Yiga Footsoldiers can be found in various places throughout Hyrule Kingdom, usually appearing disguised as travellers, revealing themselves as Yiga Footsoldiers after Link speaks to them. After defeating Kohga, Yiga Footsoldiers might also appear out of thin air to ambush Link. They will sometimes attempt to entice Link by selling Mighty Bananas, only to attack him regardless. Yiga Footsoldiers will often teleport around the area, levitating and shooting Link with a Duplex Bow. If wielding either a Vicious Sickle or a Demon Carver, they will teleport above Link and Down Thrust into the ground with their weapon, telegraphing the attack with a glowing red ring of nine Hylian letters. These letters parallel the nine Sheikah letters preceding some of Monk Maz Koshia's attacks. While infiltrating the Yiga Clan Hideout, Yiga Blademasters will summon two Yiga Footsoldiers if Link is spotted. When defeated, Yiga Footsoldiers will teleport away, dropping their weapon and leaving behind a random amount of Mighty Bananas and Rupees. Drops In addition to their standard tactics, Yiga Footsoldiers may drive vehicles assembled from Zonai Devices. While these vehicles can be dangerous, they can be neutralized by knocking them over and their pilots cannot defend themselves if attacked directly. They also have improved disguises, allowing them to disguise themselves as inanimate things such as Trees and Mighty Bananas or even Princess Zelda. Unlike in Breath of the Wild, they are equipped with Eightfold Blades that have visible Gloom markings. They will not be hostile to Link if he wears the Yiga Set, as they will mistake him for a Yiga Clan member. Other Appearances Though Yiga Footsoldier's do not appear directly in , items resembling the attire worn by Yiga Footsoldiers known as the Yiga Clan Mask and the Yiga Clan Outfit appear as a Mii Headgear for all Mii Fighters and a Mii Outfit for Mii Swordfighters respectively. Mii Swordfighters disguised as Yiga Footsoldiers appear in Sheik's and Zelda's Classic Mode Routes, "Masquerade" and "Wisdom Prevails", with the latter appearance referencing the Yiga Footsoldiers' goal of assassinating Zelda in . Yiga Footsoldiers retroactively debut in , now having voice acting and are fought both in Gerudo Town and the Gerudo Desert, and several other scenarios. They appear as the weakest soldiers of the Yiga Clan. Two Yiga Footsoldiers are also seen kneeling before Astor in the Lost Woods. On top of that, there is a new variant that stands at about twice the size of a regular Yiga Footsoldier, called Yiga Captains. Each can switch between their Vicious Sickle and Duplex Bow at will and can sustain much more damage; they act as Keep Bosses. Later in the game, they are sacrificed to revive the Blight Ganons after they failed to kill the Champions, causing the Yiga Clan to join

Yiga Captains. Each can switch between their Vicious Sickle and Duplex Bow at will and can sustain much more damage; they act as Keep Bosses. Later in the game, they are sacrificed to revive the Blight Ganons after they failed to kill the Champions, causing the Yiga Clan to join their former enemies to take down Astor and later, Ganon. They disguise themselves as Hylian Soldiers during "The Yiga Clan Attacks!" and even slip into their old Sheikah professions to infiltrate the Royal Ancient Lab in an attempt to stop Robbie and Purah from learning the full results of analyzing Terrako.

, also known as , are recurring Items and Objects in . Yiga Masks go unnamed in . They are wooden Masks worn by members of the Yiga Clan which bear an upside-down Crest of the Sheikah. Location and Uses Yiga Masks are worn by all active members of the Yiga Clan over their face. It is held on by matte iron rivets in a cross shape which spans the rest of their head. This cannot be seen on Yiga Blademasters due to the fact that they wear a hood. Accompanying the Mask are two iron earrings: on Yiga Footsoldiers, they are straight; on Yiga Blademasters, they curve to resemble tusks; on Master Kohga, they appear as hooks. Most Masks are simple and oval-shaped, but Master Kohga's features six curving horns, three on each side, on the top portion of his Mask. On the west face of the central column in the Yiga Clan Hideout are 24 Yiga Masks, arranged in two six-by-two patterns. These cannot be interacted with and are purely cosmetic. is a recurring character in . Biography Yolero is a Hylian that can be found at the Wetland Stable in the Lanayru Wetlands. During the daytime, he practices swinging a Torch at a wooden dummy outside the Stable. If Link attempts to speak to him while he is practicing, Yolero will stop and ask if he is a wanderer. Regardless of Link's response, Yolero excitedly shares that he possesses the legendary Weapon known as the Master Torch, a Weapon that can only be wielded by the chosen hero. Upon revealing the name of his legendary Weapon, Yolero dismisses Link so that he can practice. Afterwards, Yolero will muse on his Weapon's magical properties, reciting a corrupted version of the Master Sword's alias, the Sword That Seals the Darkness, as the "flame that lights the darkness". He will also threaten to burn Link with the sacred light from his Torch for bothering him. Despite Yolero's claims, his Weapon appears to be a normal Torch. His younger brother, Ami, refers to his practice sessions as simply playing. If Link speaks to Yolero after obtaining the Master Sword, Yolero asks what the Weapon is called, remarking that it probably could not sustain a fire. If Link responds truthfully, Yolero remarks that it's an "off-brand knockoff" of his own Weapon.
